issues.body:
The current WriteToDo tool relies on "in-context" task tracking, which maintains the todo list solely within the LLM's conversation history (prompt context). This creates issues with "context rot," high token costs, and total memory loss between sessions.

This issue proposes deprecating WriteToDo in favor of a persistent task tracking system (e.g., a local tasks.json) that allows the agent to maintain state across restarts and manage complex dependencies.

### Proposed Solution

Implement a new set of tools backed by a persistent local file (e.g., .gemini/tasks.json) to replace WriteToDo.

1. New Tool Definitions
The agent should have access to specific CRUD tools rather than just "writing" a list:
task_add(description: str, priority: str, dependency_id: int)
task_list(filter: str) (e.g., "show only 'ready' tasks")
task_update(id: int, status: str)
task_complete(id: int)

2. Storage Backend
Tasks should be serialized to a local file  in the working directory.

Benefits
1. Persistence: The agent can pick up exactly where it left off after a restart.
2. Efficiency: We stop burning tokens passing the entire completed history back and forth. The agent only queries task_list when it needs to know what to do next.
3. Complexity: Enables multi-step reasoning where the agent can plan out 20 steps and execute them over several days.

Address concerns and suggestions in https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/issues/17035 
Doc [go/tracker-gemini-cli](http://goto.google.com/tracker-gemini-cli)

prs.title: fix(core): cap total_max_matches and clarify context overflow message
prs.body:
## Summary

Broad `SearchText` (grep/ripgrep) queries can overflow the context window (#17448). On current `main` several guards already exist a default 100-match cap (hard-enforced via a streaming break), per-line 2000-char truncation, a 64KB tool-output cap, and a hard block in `client.ts` that refuses to send a request estimated to exceed the remaining context. This PR closes the two gaps that remain.

## What was still missing

1. **`total_max_matches` had no upper bound.** The schema only set `minimum: 1`, so the model could pass `total_max_matches: 100000` and defeat the default cap, flooding the context.
2. **The overflow UI message was misleading.** The request is already hard-blocked, but the wording ("Sending this message... might exceed") read like a soft warning, and the actionable `/compress` guidance was hidden behind a "more than 25% of context used" condition so in the broad-search case the user saw a vague message with no next step.

## Changes

- Add `MAX_TOTAL_MAX_MATCHES = 5000` (`packages/core/src/tools/constants.ts`) and a `maximum: 5000` constraint on `total_max_matches` in both tool-family schemas (`default-legacy.ts`, `gemini-3.ts`). The framework now rejects oversized values before execution. Regenerated the tool-schema snapshot.
- The redundant custom range check is left to the JSON schema (single source of truth); a comment notes this in `ripGrep.ts` / `grep.ts`.
- Rewrite `handleContextWindowWillOverflowEvent` (`useGeminiStream.ts`): the message now states the request was not sent, formats token counts with separators, and always offers next steps (narrow the request, `/compress`, or start a new session).

## Related Issues

Fixes #17448

## How to Validate

- `npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- --run src/tools/ripGrep.test.ts src/tools/grep.test.ts src/tools/definitions/coreToolsModelSnapshots.test.ts`
- `npm test -w @google/gemini-cli -- --run src/ui/hooks/useGeminiStream.test.tsx`
- `npm run typecheck`
- Manual: ask the agent to run `grep_search` with `total_max_matches: 10000`  it is rejected with `params/total_max_matches must be <= 5000`, and the model retries with a valid value.

- [x] Added/updated tests (if needed)
- [ ] Noted breaking changes (if any) none; opt-in behavior, default unchanged

prs.title: docs(extensions): stop recommending an excludeTools form that never matches
prs.body:
## Summary

The extension docs tell authors to write `"excludeTools": ["run_shell_command(rm -rf)"]` and promise it blocks that command. It blocks nothing.

Extension `excludeTools` entries are collected into a `Set` in `Config.getExcludeTools()` and compared against each tool's whole name in `ToolRegistry` (`!possibleNames.some((name) => excludeTools?.has(name))`). An entry carrying arguments is never a member of that set of names, so `run_shell_command` stays enabled and no warning says the entry was ignored.

The `toolName(args)` syntax is real, but it is parsed by `mapToolsToRules` for `tools.allowed`, `tools.core` and policy rules, which split it into a tool name plus an `argsPattern`. Extension `excludeTools` never goes through that path.

## Changes

- `docs/extensions/reference.md`: the `excludeTools` entry now states that each value is matched as a whole tool name, shows the working form, and says what the `toolName(args)` form actually belongs to. Command-scoped restrictions point at a policy rule with `commandPrefix` and a `deny` decision.
- `docs/extensions/best-practices.md`: the security example uses `["run_shell_command"]`, with the same pointer for narrower rules, instead of a value that leaves the tool enabled.
- `packages/cli/src/commands/extensions/examples/exclude-tools/gemini-extension.json`: the shipped example uses the form that works.
- `packages/core/src/tools/tool-registry.test.ts`: a test pins the contract, so `run_shell_command(rm -rf)` and `run_shell_command(rm -rf *)` must leave the tool registered. It fails if the matcher ever starts accepting the parenthesised form without the docs being updated with it.

## Verification

- `npx vitest run packages/core/src/tools/tool-registry.test.ts` — 33 passed
- `npx prettier --check` on all four files — clean
- `eslint --fix --max-warnings 0` via the pre-commit hook — clean

Fixes #28962

prs.title: fix(core): omit null exit code in list_background_processes
prs.body:
## Summary
Hello maintainers, i was looking at minor issue which was not solved from a long time #29167 a small fix can resolve the issue.  list_background_processes was showing `(Exit Code: null)` to the model for any background process that was killed by a signal. Now the exit code only appears when there actually is one.

## Details

When a process is killed by a signal it has no exit code, so its `exitCode` is `null`. The formatter only checks `exitCode !== undefined`, so `null` got through and was printed as text.

The check now prints the exit code only when `typeof exitCode === 'number'`. This still keeps an exit code of `0`, which a simple truthy check would have dropped.

## Related Issues

Fixes #29167

## How to Validate

1. Start a long-running background process, such as `sleep 300`.
2. Kill it with a signal, such as `kill -TERM <pid>`.
3. Call `list_background_processes`. The entry should no longer say `Exit Code: null`.
4. Start a background process that exits normally, such as `true`. It should still show `(Exit Code: 0)`.
5. Run the core test suite. The new regression test should pass, and it should fail if you revert the fix.

## Pre-Merge Checklist

- [x] Added/updated tests
- [ ] Updated relevant documentation (not needed)
- [ ] Noted breaking changes (none)

## Summary

The workspace scan no longer logs `Warning: Could not read directory ... ENOENT` when a subdirectory disappears between listing its parent and reading it. The usual trigger is `.gemini/projects.json.lock`, which `ProjectRegistry` creates and releases through `proper-lockfile` while the scan runs.

- Scope is limited to the warning: the vanished folder still shows up as an empty entry in the tree, same as before

Fixes #28826

npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- src/utils/getFolderStructure.test.ts

Updates `esbuild` from 0.25.0 to 0.28.2
Release notes

Sourced from esbuild's releases.

v0.28.2

  • Fix tree shaking bug due to TypeScript import alias (#4507)

    This release fixes a bug that could cause esbuild to incorrectly tree-shake imports that are used in a TypeScript type alias under certain circumstances. Affected code uses a TypeScript-specific import assignment and looks something like this:

    import Base from './dep.js';
import Alias = Base.SomeType;

  • Fix CSS minification bug involving & (#4497)

    This release fixes a bug where esbuild's CSS minifier incorrectly removed a & when it was unsafe to do so. Here is an example:

    /* Original code */
.a .b {
  & .b:not(& .c) {
    color: red;
  }
}

    /* Old output (with --minify) */
    
.a .b{.b:not(& .c){color:red}}
    

    /* New output (with --minify) */
    
.a .b{& .b:not(& .c){color:red}}

    This should match <span class="a"><span class="b"><span class="b">yes</span></span></span> but not <span class="a"><span class="b">no</span></span>. The old output incorrectly matched both.

  • Avoid overwriting input files without --allow-overwrite (#4484)

    For example: esbuild input.js --outfile=input.js tells esbuild to overwrite input.js with the output of running esbuild on it. This was supposed to already be prevented by default, but it accidentally regressed in version 0.17.0 and apparently didn't have any test coverage. The error message was being printed but the input file was still being overwritten. Oops.

    This release puts the original behavior back. With this release, esbuild should now actually avoid overwriting input files unless --allow-overwrite is explicitly present. This is done by not writing out any files when a build error is encountered.

  • Fix incorrect code generated when using top-level await (#4498)

    Previously esbuild could generate code containing a syntax error in complex scenarios involving top-level await used in a dependency cycle. The problem was a missing async on one or more module wrapper closures. With this release, esbuild now uses a fixed-point iteration algorithm to correctly annotate all dependencies in the cycle as needing an async module wrapper.

  • Fix a minification bug with lowered logical assignment operators (#4508)

    This release fixes a bug that could cause esbuild to generate incorrect code for logical assignment operators when lowering them to an older target environment. Specifically the lowering process requires duplicating the left-hand side, but esbuild incorrectly failed to count the duplicate as a new usage when the left-hand side is an identifier. That then caused the minifier to believe that the left-hand side was only used once and could attempt to incorrectly inline an initializer into the first usage. This bug has now been fixed:

function foo() {

  bar(x ||= {})

Changelog: 2025

This changelog documents all esbuild versions published in the year 2025 (versions 0.25.0 through 0.27.2).

0.27.2

  • Allow import path specifiers starting with #/ (#4361)

    Previously the specification for package.json disallowed import path specifiers starting with #/, but this restriction has recently been relaxed and support for it is being added across the JavaScript ecosystem. One use case is using it for a wildcard pattern such as mapping #/* to ./src/* (previously you had to use another character such as #_* instead, which was more confusing). There is some more context in nodejs/node#49182.

    This change was contributed by @​hybrist.

  • Automatically add the -webkit-mask prefix (#4357, #4358)

    This release automatically adds the -webkit- vendor prefix for the mask CSS shorthand property:

main {

}

    /* Old output (with --target=chrome110) */

mask: url(x.png) center/5rem no-repeat;
    
}

main {
    
-webkit-mask: url(x.png) center/5rem no-repeat;
    
mask: url(x.png) center/5rem no-repeat;
    
}

Updates `express` from 5.1.0 to 5.3.0
Release notes

Sourced from express's releases.

v5.3.0

Highlights

🐞 Bug fixes

  • Fixed HTTP header conflict between Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding in res.send - by @​YuryShkoda in #4893

    Fixed the behavior of res.send() to prevent conflicts between Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding HTTP headers in responses. The Content-Length header in res.send() is now only added when a Transfer-Encoding header is not present, complying with the HTTP specification that states both headers should not coexist in the same response. ETag generation is unaffected by the presence of a Transfer-Encoding header - by @​cuishuang in #7459

  • Upgrade qs to ^6.16.0, which fixes CVE-2026-2391 (GHSA-w7fw-mjwx-w883), CVE-2026-82417 (GHSA-4mjr-xmp4-gh2g) and CVE-2026-82562 (GHSA-x5fp-wj9c-mxmx): arrayLimit bypasses in comma parsing and a denial of service via an attacker-controlled isBuffer - by @​davetashner in #7057 and #7478, and @​cyphercodes in #7305

  • Upgrade proxy-addr to ^2.0.8, which fixes CVE-2026-90711 - by @​lazerg in #7474

🚀 Improvements

  • Allow conditional revalidation for QUERY requests. req.fresh previously only validated freshness for GET and HEAD requests, so QUERY responses never returned 304 despite a matching validator. Since QUERY is a safe, idempotent, and cacheable method that supports conditional requests, it is now included in the freshness check - by @​Cherry in #7366

    // QUERY /reports with If-None-Match: "12345"
app.query('/reports', (req, res) => {
  res.set('ETag', '"12345"');
  res.send(results); // now responds 304 Not Modified
});

  • Improve HTML structure in res.redirect() responses when HTML format is accepted by adding <!DOCTYPE html>, <title>, and <body> tags for better browser compatibility - by @​Bernice55231 in #5167

  • When calling app.render with options set to null, the locals object is handled correctly, preventing unexpected errors and making the method behave the same as when options is omitted or an empty object is passed - by AkaHarshit in #6903

    app.render('index', null, callback); // now works as expected

  • Upgrade content-type to ^2.0.0, bringing a faster parser (~1.5x quicker Content-Type parsing/formatting in res.send()) along with a behavior change: res.send() now keeps any existing parameters when adding the charset and no longer throws on a Content-Type that fails to parse. type-is is upgraded to ^2.1.0 as part of the same change - by @​blakeembrey in #7234

    res.set('Content-Type', 'text/plain; foo=bar').send('hey');
// -> Content-Type: text/plain; foo=bar; charset=utf-8

  • The default error handler now logs the full error object instead of only its stack trace, so nested details such as Error.cause and library-specific properties (e.g. Sequelize's parent/original) are no longer swallowed - by @​Nitin-Mohapatra in #6464

  • Upgrade content-disposition to ^2.0.1, which changes the Content-Disposition header emitted by res.download(), res.attachment(), and res.sendFile(): file names that are valid HTTP tokens are no longer wrapped in quotes. This is equivalent per RFC 6266, but applications asserting on the exact header bytes should update their expectations - by @​blakeembrey in #7233

    res.attachment('user.html');
// before -> Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="user.html"
// after  -> Content-Disposition: attachment; filename=user.html

Release notes

Sourced from lycheeverse/lychee-action's releases.

v2.9.0

Summary

This release updates the default lychee version from v0.23.0 to v0.24.2.

The main reason for this release is compatibility with the new lychee 0.24.x release artifacts. Starting with lychee v0.24.0, the archive layout changed, and the lychee binary may now be packaged inside a subdirectory. lychee-action now detects that layout automatically, so users can upgrade without changing their workflows.

If you use:

uses: lycheeverse/lychee-action@v2

you will get the new version once the floating v2 tag has been updated. If you pin exact versions, update to:

uses: lycheeverse/lychee-action@v2.9.0

What’s new from lychee v0.24.x

Better diagnostics

lychee now reports line and column numbers for detected links. This makes broken link reports easier to act on, especially in larger documentation sites or generated reports.

Text fragment checking

lychee can now check URL text fragments, such as links containing #:~:text=.... This helps catch links that point to a valid page but no longer points to the intended highlighted text.

Sitemap support

lychee can now read sitemap.xml inputs. This is useful for checking published websites or generated documentation sites where the sitemap is the easiest source of URLs to validate.

JUnit output

lychee now supports JUnit output. This makes it easier to integrate link checking results with CI systems and test reporting tools that understand JUnit XML.

Redirect and remap visibility

lychee can now show redirects and remaps more clearly. This helps explain why a URL was checked as a different final URL and makes debugging link-checking behavior easier.

Multiple config files

lychee now supports multiple configuration files and expanded config handling. This is useful for repositories that split documentation, website, or package-specific link-checking settings.

Timeout handling

lychee can now accept timeouts explicitly. This gives users more control over how strict their link checks should be for flaky or slow endpoints.

prs.title: feat(core): allow agents to invoke other agents
prs.body:
## Summary

Subagents cannot call other agents. Listing an agent name in `tools` fails validation with "Invalid tool name", and there is no way to let a subagent call every agent. This PR allows both, with a depth limit on nesting.

## Details

- **Validation:** `isValidToolName` takes a new `allowAgentNames` option. The agent loader uses it, so agent names pass validation. Agents are resolved when the subagent runs, after every agent is registered.
- **Granting agents:** `LocalAgentExecutor.create` resolves each `tools` entry: tool first, then agent. An agent name grants that agent. `invoke_agent` grants every registered agent. A name that is neither a tool nor an agent shows a warning, so typos that the loader used to reject are still reported.
- **Scoped tool:** the subagent gets its own `invoke_agent` whose `agent_name` is an `enum` of the granted agents. The tool description lists those agents, because a subagent's system prompt does not. Calls to any other agent are rejected.
- **Unchanged defaults:** `*` and an omitted `tools` list still grant no agents. The generalist builds its list from the main registry, which contains `invoke_agent`, so it now leaves `invoke_agent` out. Without that, it could call every agent, including itself (the issue raised in review of #28738).
- **Recursion guard:** `AgentLoopContext` has a new `agentDepth` field. A subagent at depth `MAX_AGENT_DEPTH` (3) does not get the agent tool. Each level keeps its own `max_turns` and `timeout_mins`.
- **Tools of called agents:** a called agent resolves its own `tools` from the same registry the caller resolved from, the same as when the main agent calls it. The docs say that a caller's `tools` list does not limit the agents it calls.

## Related Issues

Fixes #22092

## How to Validate

1. `npx vitest run src/agents src/tools/tool-names.test.ts` in `packages/core`. New tests cover the loader, the scoped tool, granting by name, granting all, `*`, the unknown-name warning, nested context, the depth limit and the generalist.
2. Manual: add `.gemini/agents/coordinator.md` with `tools: [read_file, codebase_investigator]`, then ask the main agent to use `coordinator`. It should delegate to `codebase_investigator`.

## Pre-Merge Checklist

- [x] Updated relevant documentation and README (if needed)
- [x] Added/updated tests (if needed)
- [ ] Noted breaking changes (if any)
- [ ] Validated on required platforms/methods:

prs.title: fix(acp): truncate large shell and mcp tool outputs in acp mode (#30233)
prs.body:
## Description
Fixes #30233.

Currently in ACP (Agent Client Protocol) mode, tool execution output from shell commands and MCP tools is forwarded directly to the model (`convertToFunctionResponse`) without truncation. When tools return large outputs (e.g. huge logs, large directory trees, verbose MCP responses), this exhausts context window token budgets and can trigger HTTP 400/413 errors from the Gemini API.

This PR:
1. Extracts the shared output truncation logic from `ToolExecutor` into a reusable core utility `truncateToolOutputIfNeeded` in `@google/gemini-cli-core/utils/tool-utils`.
2. Refactors `ToolExecutor.truncateOutputIfNeeded` to delegate to `truncateToolOutputIfNeeded`, eliminating duplication while maintaining 100% backward compatibility.
3. Integrates `truncateToolOutputIfNeeded` into `AcpSession.runTool`, saving full outputs to disk and passing bounded previews with file path references to the model and conversation history.
4. Updates ACP `tool_call_update` client notifications to display the formatted preview and file path when output exceeds the truncation threshold.
5. Adds unit and regression tests in both `packages/core` and `packages/cli`.

## Testing
- Added unit tests in `packages/core/src/utils/tool-utils.test.ts` covering shell within threshold, shell exceeding threshold, MCP tool truncation, and hard byte cap.
- Added regression tests in `packages/cli/src/acp/acpSession.test.ts` verifying that large shell outputs in ACP mode are truncated, written to disk, and recorded with bounded response parts.

prs.title: fix(sandbox): improve permission denial detection and unsupported environment handling (#29338)
prs.body:
## Description
Fixes #29338.

This PR addresses sandbox compatibility and permission error handling across containerized and restricted execution environments in `@google/gemini-cli-core`.

### Issues Addressed
1. **Permission Denials Unrecognized**: POSIX sandbox denial detection previously missed common tool-level permission errors (`mkdir: cannot create directory`, `touch: cannot touch`, `chmod: changing permissions of`, `scandir`, `access`, and Python `[Errno 13]`). This prevented the CLI from identifying file permission denials and offering dynamic permission resolution.
2. **Unhandled Crash on Unsupported Environments**: When tool sandboxing was requested in environments without supported sandbox managers, `LocalSandboxManager` threw an untyped generic error rather than the canonical `FatalSandboxError` (exit code 44), causing an unhandled crash rather than graceful user diagnostic exit.

### Changes Made
- `packages/core/src/sandbox/utils/sandboxDenialUtils.ts`:
  - Extended `isFileDenial` keyword detection for `cannot create directory`, `cannot touch`, `changing permissions of`, and `errno 13`.
  - Added dedicated extraction regexes for `mkdir`, `touch`, `chmod`, `scandir`, `access`, Python `[Errno 13]`, and shell permission denied errors.
- `packages/core/src/services/sandboxManager.ts`:
  - Updated `LocalSandboxManager.prepareCommand()` to throw `FatalSandboxError` with actionable remediation guidance.
- `packages/core/src/sandbox/utils/sandboxDenialUtils.test.ts`:
  - Added 8 regression test cases covering all new permission denial formats and `FatalSandboxError` verification.

## How Was This Tested?
- Added regression tests in `sandboxDenialUtils.test.ts` for all permission error formats.
- Verified `LocalSandboxManager` throws `FatalSandboxError` with exit code 44 (`ExitCodes.FATAL_SANDBOX_ERROR`).

## Checklist
- [x] Code follows the style guidelines of this project.
- [x] Unit tests have been added to verify changes.
- [x] No breaking changes introduced.

prs.title: fix(core): unify exit codes mapping and fatal error hierarchy
prs.body:
## Description
This PR centralizes and unifies CLI process exit codes across `@google/gemini-cli-core`.

Previously, `ExitCodes` in `exitCodes.ts` was missing several fatal error codes that were hardcoded as raw numeric literals in `errors.ts` (`FatalSandboxError`, `FatalTurnLimitedError`, `FatalToolExecutionError`, and `FatalUntrustedWorkspaceError`). Furthermore, `FatalError` subclasses in `errors.ts` used raw magic numbers rather than referencing the canonical `ExitCodes` constant.

This change:
1. Adds the missing fatal exit codes (`44`, `53`, `54`, `55`) to `ExitCodes`.
2. Exports the strongly-typed `ExitCode` union for autocomplete and compile-time validation.
3. Refactors all `FatalError` subclasses to reference `ExitCodes.*`.
4. Adds a comprehensive unit test suite in `exitCodes.test.ts` to ensure 100% test coverage and prevent future regressions.

prs.body:
Fixes #30114, #30132

### Problem
When Gemini CLI is running in ACP mode (`gemini --acp`), if a `BeforeAgent` (or `AfterAgent`) hook denies a prompt or stops execution (`continue: false` / `AgentExecutionStopped` / `AgentExecutionBlocked`), the ACP stream consumer in `acpSession.ts` dropped these events in the `switch (event.type)` default block. As a result, the ACP client received an empty turn ending with `end_turn` and no message or explanation.

### Solution
- Handle `GeminiEventType.AgentExecutionStopped` and `GeminiEventType.AgentExecutionBlocked` in `acpSession.ts`.
- Emit an `agent_message_chunk` with the effective reason or `systemMessage` so the ACP client/IDE clearly sees why execution stopped or was blocked.
- Added unit regression tests in `acpSession.test.ts`.

prs.title: fix(core): preserve custom model alias generation settings (#30238)
prs.body:
Fixes #30238

### Problem
When configuring a custom model alias that points to or extends a model tier (such as `flash-lite`), `applyModelSelection()` compares the concrete resolved model (e.g. `gemini-2.5-flash-lite`) against the requested tier name (`flash-lite`). Because they are not string-equal, `applyModelSelection()` falsely treated normal tier resolution as an availability fallback and re-queried `modelConfigService.getResolvedConfig()` with the concrete model name, silently dropping the alias's custom generation parameters (such as `temperature` and `maxOutputTokens`).

### Solution
- Distinguish normal tier resolution from genuine availability fallbacks in `applyModelSelection()` by comparing `finalModel` against the target model resolved for the alias/tier.
- Preserve the alias's configured `GenerateContentConfig` across tier resolution.
- Added unit regression tests for custom aliases resolving tiers and genuine availability fallbacks.

prs.title: feat(acp): execute independent tool calls in parallel (#30235)
prs.body:
## Description
Fixes #30235.

In ACP (Agent Client Protocol) mode, all tool calls in a turn were previously executed sequentially using a serial loop, even when the model generated multiple independent, read-only tool calls. In contrast, the standard CLI scheduler batches contiguous parallelizable tool calls into concurrent waves.

This PR brings parallel tool execution parity to ACP mode:
1. Implements `partitionToolCallRequestsIntoWaves` in `@google/gemini-cli-core/utils/tool-utils` to partition incoming tool requests into waves using the core `isParallelizable` rules.
2. Sorts `UPDATE_TOPIC_TOOL_NAME` to the front so topic/context updates are established before dependent actions.
3. Executes contiguous parallelizable tool calls concurrently via `Promise.all` in `AcpSession.prompt()`, while strictly preserving sequential execution for non-parallelizable tools (`EDIT_TOOL_NAMES`, `wait_for_previous: true`).
4. Preserves the exact ordering of function responses returned to the model.
5. Adds unit tests for wave partitioning in `packages/core` and concurrency/ordering regression tests in `packages/cli`.

## Testing
- Unit tests added in `packages/core/src/utils/tool-utils.test.ts` verifying wave partitioning, edit tool isolation, and topic sorting.
- Concurrency and ordering tests added in `packages/cli/src/acp/acpSession.test.ts` verifying concurrent execution (`maxConcurrent = 2`), strict sequential execution across edit tools, and response order preservation.

prs.title: fix(a2a-server): handle rejection of fire-and-forget scheduler.schedule()
prs.body:
## Summary

`Task.scheduleToolCalls()` fire-and-forgets `scheduler.schedule()`, but that call legitimately rejects. The discarded promise became an unhandled rejection, which terminates the whole a2a-server process and takes down every other running task. This attaches a rejection handler.

## Details

`schedule()` rejects with plain `Error`s (`Tool call cancelled while in queue.` when the signal aborts while queued, `Operation cancelled` if already aborted), so `isAbortError` would not match them. The handler checks the task's own `abortSignal` instead:

- **Aborted:** expected, so log and ignore. The task's cancellation flow owns cleanup.
- **Any other failure:** log the error and call `cancelPendingTools()`. Without this, the calls pre-registered just before scheduling stay pending forever and `waitForPendingTools` hangs waiting for tools that will never run.

## Related Issues

Fixes #29034

## How to Validate

```
cd packages/a2a-server && npx vitest run src/agent/task.test.ts
```

Expected: all passing. Both new tests fail on `main`, where vitest also reports two `Unhandled Rejection` errors. The new tests assign a plain function to `schedule` rather than using `vi.fn`, because vitest attaches its own handler to promises returned by mocks and would hide the bug.

Full `packages/a2a-server` suite: 185 passing. `tsc --noEmit`, eslint and prettier are clean.

prs.body:
## Summary
Allow agents to call agents

Fixes #22092 
<!-- Concisely describe what this PR changes and why. Focus on impact and
urgency. -->

## Details
Fixes #22092 by letting subagents delegate to other subagents — or recurse into themselves — via their `tools:` frontmatter. This was blocked twice over: the agent loader rejected agent names as `Invalid tool name`, and the executor stripped every `Kind.Agent` tool from subagent registries, so even a name that passed validation would have had no effect. i`sValidToolName()` now takes an `allowAgentNames` option (checked after the MCP branch, so malformed names like `mcp__tool` stay rejected), and the executor resolves each `tools:` entry through the tool registry, then the agent registry, then warns instead of silently dropping it. Resolved agents get an `invoke_agent` tool whose `agent_name` is constrained to a JSON-schema `enum` of exactly those agents. A bare agent name grants that one agent, `agent_*` or `invoke_agent` grants all of them, and a self-reference enables recursion;` *` and an omitted `tools:` deliberately grant no agent access, so no existing definition changes behaviour — notably `generalist-agent`, whose list is built from `getAllToolNames()`. Recursion is bounded three ways: an agent at max depth is never handed the tool, `AgentTool.createInvocation` rejects nesting past `MAX_AGENT_DEPTH = 3`, and each level keeps its own `max_turns/timeout_mins`. Docs updated; 26 tests added across `tool-names`, `agentLoader`, `agent-tool` and `local-executor`, with the two pre-existing recursion tests still passing unmodified. Note that this introduces a deferred import cycle (`local-executor` → `agent-tool` → `local-invocation)`, which ESM resolves correctly and the tests exercise in both load orders — happy to switch to a dynamic import if preferred.

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

On **GitHub Mobile (Android)**, the live connection to a Copilot cloud sandbox session drops whenever the app leaves the foreground, and frequently cannot be restored without force-closing the app.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open a Copilot cloud session in GitHub Mobile on Android (mobile data + VPN).
2. Do any of: switch to another app, use split screen, tap **+** to attach a photo/file, or simply stay on the chat screen without sending a message for 2–3 minutes.

### Actual behavior

- The banner "Live connection unavailable. Session history is still readable." appears.
- Sometimes it reconnects on its own after a few seconds.
- Often **Retry** never succeeds; the only fix is to force-close and reopen the app.
- Battery optimization for the GitHub app is set to "Unrestricted"; no change.

### Expected behavior

- The client keeps the connection alive while idle in the foreground (e.g. heartbeat/keepalive).
- After returning from background or a file picker, it reconnects automatically, and Retry works without restarting the app.

### Environment

- GitHub Mobile, Android
- Copilot in the cloud (cloud sandbox) session
- After any disconnect, MCP tools return "MCP tool is not registered" for the rest of the session.

issues.title: MCP client declares the Tasks extension on tools/call but rejects CreateTaskResult

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server configuration, discovery, connectivity, OAuth, policy, and registry

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

The MCP client sends `io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks` in `_meta["io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities"].extensions` on every request, `tools/call` included. When a server answers with a `CreateTaskResult` (`resultType: "task"`), the tool call fails and `tasks/get` is never sent:

```
MCP request failed: expected CallToolResult from tools/call, got CreateTaskResult(CreateTaskResult { result_type: ResultType("task"), task: Task { task_id: "6c618e1b-c5f1-4b21-81e8-b68d05d39753", status: Working, status_message: Some("Working, 90s left"), created_at: "2026-11-18T02:56:24.271Z", last_updated_at: "2026-11-18T02:56:24.273Z", ttl_ms: Some(600000), poll_interval_ms: Some(30000) }, meta: None })
```

The [Tasks extension spec](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/ext-tasks/blob/main/specification/2026-07-28/tasks.md#capability-negotiation) says: "A client that has negotiated this extension MUST be prepared to handle either `CallToolResult` or `CreateTaskResult` in response to any supported request it issues."

### Affected version

1.0.113

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Add a stdio MCP server to `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json` that implements protocol 2026-07-28 and the Tasks extension:
   - `server/discover` returns:
     ```json
     { "resultType": "complete", "supportedVersions": ["2026-07-28"], "capabilities": { "tools": {}, "extensions": { "io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks": {} } }, "ttlMs": 0, "cacheScope": "public" }
     ```
   - `tools/list` returns one tool, `slow_probe`, with an empty input schema.
   - `tools/call` for `slow_probe`, when the request's `_meta["io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities"].extensions` contains `io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks`, returns:
     ```json
     { "resultType": "task", "taskId": "<uuid>", "status": "working", "createdAt": "<now>", "lastUpdatedAt": "<now>", "ttlMs": 600000, "pollIntervalMs": 30000 }
     ```
   - `tasks/get` returns the task as `working` until 90 seconds have passed, then `completed` with a `result` holding a `CallToolResult`.
2. Start `copilot` (with or without experimental mode) and ask it to call `slow_probe`.
3. The client's `tools/call` request declares the Tasks extension in `_meta`; the server returns the `CreateTaskResult` above.
4. The tool call fails with the error above. No `tasks/get` request reaches the server.

### Expected behavior

Either:
- the client polls `tasks/get` until the task completes and returns its result to the model; or
- if Tasks v2 isn't supported yet, the client stops declaring `io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks`, so servers return a normal `CallToolResult`.

### Additional context

- With the same server, Claude Code 2.1.322 (Tasks v2) and VS Code 1.146.0's default Copilot harness (Tasks v1) both complete the task.
- Same failure with experimental mode on.
- Related: #2538, which added experimental v1 Tasks support for `taskSupport: "required"` tools. This report is about the v2 extension, which the client declares but doesn't handle.
- OS: Windows 11 x64

### Describe the bug

A Copilot **cloud sandbox** session stopped accepting live connections right after a tool call finished, and has never reconnected since. Only read-only history is available.

- Task: `15847dc9-166e-46cf-98bf-84524cdb6ea1` (session `219a46af-55de-4302-b417-c03b1d6c00ce`)
- Copilot version in the sandbox: 1.0.109
- Session was long-running (~17h, ~8,300 events). A context compaction happened shortly before the disconnect, at roughly half of the 1M context window.

### Timeline (UTC, from the session events)

- 2026-11-22 07:32 — last normal turn ends (`session.idle`), PR merged successfully.
- 07:36–07:42 — a resume/reconnect happens: managed settings resolved, MCP servers loaded (`connected`), tools updated.
- After that: no further events. New user messages never reach the session.
- Task status API reports `state: idle` with no recorded errors.

### What the client shows

GitHub Mobile and github.com both show: "Live connection unavailable. Session history is still readable." Retry never succeeds. The session's menu only shows Pin / Rename / Copy link (Sharing settings / Archive / Delete are missing).

### Expected behavior

Per the cloud sandbox docs, a stopped session should resume from its snapshot with files and progress intact. Retry should reconnect, or the UI should report a concrete error.

The session was not archived or deleted by the user. Other new cloud sessions in the same repo/account work.

issues.title: Image generation is never available in `copilot --acp` sessions
issues.body:
### Describe the feature or problem you'd like to solve

The image generation tool (GPT Image 2.5 Flare) works in interactive Copilot CLI and in VS Code, but never in a session started with `copilot --acp`. ACP clients (I hit it in T3 Code) get a session without the tool, even when the user's `imageGeneration` setting is on and the account has the rollout.

From reading the bundled `cli-main.js` (1.0.114):

- The interactive CLI passes the user's `imageGeneration` setting through to the session.
- The ACP session config (`clientKind: "acp"`) sets `tools.availableTools` and `tools.excludedTools`, but not `tools.imageGeneration`.
- The session layer then falls back to `tools.imageGeneration.enabled ?? false`, so ACP sessions always have it off.

There's no `--acp` flag or ACP session parameter that turns it on, so the ACP client has no way to enable it either.

### Proposed solution

Have ACP sessions follow the same `imageGeneration` setting as interactive sessions (default on, when the account has access). Optionally, let the ACP client override it per session, for example through `_meta` on `session/new`, the way SDK hosts already can with `tools.imageGeneration.enabled`.

Generated images already come back as files in the project, which ACP clients can display, so nothing else should be needed on the protocol side.

### Example prompts or workflows

1. In an ACP client, ask: "Make a 512×512 PNG icon of a red planet and save it to `assets/icons/`." Today the agent says it has no image tool; in `copilot` in a terminal it works.
2. An orchestrating agent delegates "generate 6 portrait variants in this style" to a Copilot ACP session, then wires the files into the app.
3. Generate a favicon or OG image as part of a coding task, without leaving the ACP client for VS Code or a terminal.

### Additional context

- Copilot CLI 1.0.114, Windows 11, Copilot account with the `copilot_cli_image_generation_tool` experiment enabled.
- `~/.copilot/config.json` doesn't set `imageGeneration`, so it's at its default (true).
- Steps to reproduce:
  1. Run `copilot` in a terminal, ask for a small test image: it's generated.
  2. Start `copilot --acp` from an ACP client in the same folder with the same account and model, ask the same thing: the agent reports no image generation tool.
- Related: #4581 (image generation for developer assets).

issues.title: Avoid duplicate skill lookup for slash-invoked skills with disable-model-invocation

labels.name: area:plugins
labels.description: Plugin system, marketplace, hooks, skills, extensions, and custom agents

issues.body:
### Summary

A skill that is explicitly invoked with a slash command can execute and inject its instructions into context, while another lookup path reports `Skill not found`, creating misleading context noise.

### Reproduction

Use a skill with this frontmatter:

```yaml
---
name: implement
description: "Implement a piece of work based on a spec or set of tickets."
disable-model-invocation: true
---
```

The local skill is `C:\Users\omzig\.copilot\skills\implement\SKILL.md`; the relevant setting is line 4: `disable-model-invocation: true`.

Then run:

```text
/implement #1147
```

Observed behavior:

- The `/implement` workflow is recognized and its instructions are injected into context.
- A separate skill lookup reports: `Skill not found: implement`.
- The command can continue, but the error is misleading and makes it appear that the skill failed to load.

Environment: Copilot CLI 1.0.80 on Windows.

### Expected behavior

`disable-model-invocation: true` should prevent automatic/model-driven invocation. It should not make an explicit slash-command invocation unavailable. When the explicit command path succeeds, the runtime should not perform a second conflicting lookup or emit `Skill not found`.

### Suggested fix

Distinguish explicit slash-command invocation from automatic skill invocation. Resolve the command/skill once, honor `disable-model-invocation` only for automatic loading, and suppress the registry error when the explicit command path has already loaded the skill successfully.

This is primarily a context-quality issue: the implementation workflow works, but the duplicate/conflicting lookup adds noise and obscures the actual result.

issues.title: fetch_copilot_cli_documentation fails with ENOENT: README.md is declared in files[] but absent from released platform tarballs

labels.name: area:installation
labels.description: Installing, updating, versioning, PATH setup, and binary distribution

labels.name: area:tools
labels.description: Built-in tools: file editing, shell, search, LSP, git, and tool call behavior

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

The built-in `fetch_copilot_cli_documentation` tool is documented as reading the CLI's own `/help` **and README** to answer capability questions ([changelog 0.0.355](https://github.com/github/copilot-cli/blob/main/changelog.md), 2025-11-12: *"Enabled the CLI agent to read its own `/help` and README to answer questions about its capabilities"*).

The README half fails. Calling the tool emits a raw filesystem error into model context:

```text
ENOENT: no such file or directory, open 'C:\Users\<user>\.copilot\pkg\win32-x64\1.0.81-9\README.md'
```

The cause is self-contained and verifiable from the released artifact alone: **`README.md` is declared in `package.json` → `files[]`, but is not present in the released platform tarball.** The install therefore cannot contain it, and the tool reads a path that never exists.

```console
$ gh release download v1.0.81-9 --repo github/copilot-cli \
    --pattern "github-copilot-1.0.81-9-win32-x64.tgz"

$ tar -tzf github-copilot-1.0.81-9-win32-x64.tgz | grep -E "^package/[^/]+\.md$"
package/LICENSE.md          # <- README.md absent

$ tar -xzOf github-copilot-1.0.81-9-win32-x64.tgz package/package.json | grep '"README.md"'
    "README.md",            # <- but files[] declares it
```

So the packaging intent is intact and only the build output diverged from it — which is likely why this went unnoticed.

### Affected version

```
GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.81-9
```

Also verified absent in the released `1.0.80` and `1.0.81-0` platform tarballs, so this is not specific to one prerelease. A much older local install (`0.0.410`) **does** contain `README.md` (7,787 bytes), so it regressed at some point between the two.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install the CLI from a GitHub release (this is the channel the GitHub Copilot desktop app updates through).
2. Confirm the file is absent from the install:

   ```bash
   ls ~/.copilot/pkg/<platform>/<version>/*.md
   # LICENSE.md only
   ```

3. Dispatch any agent that has the tool and make it call it:

   ```bash
   copilot --allow-all-tools -p "Call fetch_copilot_cli_documentation and report exactly what it returned."
   ```

4. The response contains the `ENOENT ... README.md` error. The `/help` half returns normally, so the tool half-succeeds rather than failing cleanly.

### Expected behavior

Either the released platform tarballs contain the `README.md` that `files[]` already declares, or the tool degrades gracefully — returning the `/help` content it does have without surfacing a raw `ENOENT` path into model context.

### Additional context

#### Environment

```
copilot : GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.81-9   (installed via GitHub release / desktop-app update channel)
OS      : Microsoft Windows 11 Enterprise 10.0.26200.0
Arch    : AMD64
Shell   : PowerShell 7.6.5
Terminal: ConsoleHost
```

#### Why this is invisible to anyone testing via npm

The npm-published package for the **same version** does contain `README.md`, because npm injects it regardless of `files[]` — per [npm's `files` documentation](https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v11/configuring-npm/package-json#files):

> Certain files are always included, regardless of settings: … `README` & `LICENSE` can have any case and extension.

Comparing the two publish paths for `1.0.80`:

| Artifact for `1.0.80`                                | `package/README.md` |
| ---------------------------------------------------- | ------------------- |
| npm-published `@github/copilot-win32-x64` *(via mirror)* | present             |
| GitHub release `github-copilot-1.0.80-win32-x64.tgz` | **absent**          |

npm silently repairs the omission; the GitHub release tarball does not. So the defect only manifests on the **release-tarball install path** — which is the path the desktop app's updater uses. An `npm i -g @github/copilot` check would show the file present and suggest nothing is wrong.

*(The npm-side artifact was fetched through a corporate registry mirror rather than `registry.npmjs.org` directly, which is network-blocked here. The primary evidence above does not depend on it — the `files[]`-vs-tarball mismatch is verifiable from the GitHub release asset alone.)*

#### Impact

- A documented capability silently returns half its intended content, so the agent answers capability questions from `/help` alone and doesn't know the other half is missing.
- A raw filesystem path is surfaced into model context as an error string on every call.
- The tool takes no parameters, so there is no way for a caller to route around the broken half.

#### Scope not verified

Only `win32-x64` was unpacked and inspected. The other platform tarballs are built from the same `files[]` manifest so they are very likely identical in this respect, but that is an inference, not a measurement. The exact version where the file stopped shipping was not bisected — only bounded between `0.0.410` and `1.0.80`.

#### Suggested labels

`area:installation`, `area:tools` — filed unlabelled because an outside contributor has `push:false` / `triage:false` on this repo and cannot set labels or type.

issues.title: Bash tool drops non-ASCII characters due to LC_CTYPE=C in shell environment

labels.name: area:tools
labels.description: Built-in tools: file editing, shell, search, LSP, git, and tool call behavior

issues.body:
## Summary

The bash tool in Copilot CLI spawns shells with `LANG=""` and `LC_CTYPE="C"`. This causes all non-ASCII characters (Chinese, Japanese, Korean, accented Latin, emoji, etc.) to be silently stripped from command strings. File paths containing such characters become unresolvable, and file content written via heredoc or echo loses all multibyte characters.

## Environment

- Copilot CLI version: 1.0.49
- OS: macOS (Darwin)
- Shell: bash (spawned by Copilot CLI)

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open Copilot CLI
2. Run any bash command involving non-ASCII characters:

```bash
echo "ABC你好DEF" | xxd
```

**Expected:** `41 42 43 e4bda0 e5a5bd 44 45 46 0a` (UTF-8 bytes preserved)

**Actual:** `41 42 43 44 45 46 0a` — the Chinese characters are gone entirely.

3. Attempt to write a file to a path containing non-ASCII directory names:

```bash
echo "test" > "/path/to/中文目录/file.txt"
```

**Expected:** File created successfully.

**Actual:** Command hangs indefinitely. The shell appears to attempt resolving a corrupted path (with multibyte characters stripped) and never returns.

## Root cause

Running `locale` inside the bash tool confirms:

```
LANG=""
LC_COLLATE="C"
LC_CTYPE="C"
LC_MESSAGES="C"
LC_MONETARY="C"
LC_NUMERIC="C"
LC_TIME="C"
LC_ALL=
```

With `LC_CTYPE=C`, the shell treats all bytes above 0x7F as invalid and discards them during command-line processing. This affects:

- String literals in commands (echo, printf, heredoc content)
- File path arguments containing non-ASCII characters
- Variable assignments with multibyte content

The same operations succeed when run through Python (which manages its own UTF-8 encoding independent of the shell locale), confirming the filesystem and disk are fine.

## Suggested fix

Set `LANG=C.UTF-8` (or `en_US.UTF-8`) when spawning bash subprocesses. This preserves the benefits of a minimal locale (deterministic sort order, no locale-dependent formatting surprises) while correctly handling multibyte characters:

```bash
env LANG=C.UTF-8 /bin/bash --norc --noprofile -c "..."
```

Using `--norc --noprofile` already avoids loading user shell plugins. Adding a UTF-8 locale on top shouldn't introduce any slowness or side effects.

## Impact

This bug makes Copilot CLI effectively unusable for any task involving non-English file paths or content — which is common for users working in CJK languages, or anyone whose project happens to have non-ASCII directory names. The failure mode is particularly bad: commands silently produce corrupted output or hang forever, with no error message indicating the cause.

issues.title: Show context window size (tokens) in /model command alongside premium request multiplier

labels.name: area:context-memory
labels.description: Context window, memory, compaction, checkpoints, and instruction loading

labels.name: area:models
labels.description: Model selection, availability, switching, rate limits, and model-specific behavior

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, improvement, or new functionality

issues.body:
### Describe the feature or problem you'd like to solve

The `/model` command shows the premium request multiplier for each model but not the context window size (max tokens). There is no way to know, from within the CLI, how many tokens a model actually supports in Copilot.

### Proposed solution

Add the context window size (in tokens) to the output of `/model`, alongside the existing premium request multiplier.

**Current `/model` output:**
```
  claude-sonnet-4.6      ×1  (default)
  claude-opus-4.6        ×3
```

**Proposed `/model` output:**
```
  claude-sonnet-4.6      ×1    160k ctx  (default)
  claude-opus-4.6        ×3    160k ctx
```

The context window values should reflect what **Copilot actually makes available** (i.e. the `max_prompt_tokens` configured in its routing layer), not just the provider's theoretical max. This distinction matters because the effective context window Copilot exposes may differ from the provider's advertised limits — and today users have no visibility into this.

### Example prompts or workflows

1. **Choosing between models for a long session**: A developer about to start a large refactor touching 30+ files runs `/model` to pick the model with the largest effective context window, not just the cheapest in premium requests.

2. **Debugging degraded responses**: A user notices the model is repeating tool calls and re-reading already-processed files. Knowing they're at 160k/200k tokens (vs just "78%") helps correlate the degradation with the known "lost in the middle" effect at high context fill.

3. **Cross-client comparison**: A user switching between VSCode Copilot, Copilot CLI, and Claude Code wants to know if they get the same effective context window across clients. Today this is completely opaque.

### Additional context

- The data is likely already available in the API response from `api.githubcopilot.com/models` (the `capabilities.limits` field), so this should be low-effort to surface.
- Related issues: [#1688](https://github.com/github/copilot-cli/issues/1688) and [#1761](https://github.com/github/copilot-cli/issues/1761) both request configurable compaction thresholds — knowing the absolute context window size would make those features even more useful.

prs.title: Add opt-in connection token generation to the CLI container
prs.body:
A local SDK client needs a shared secret to connect to the headless CLI, even before a session has GitHub credentials. This change lets developers try the server without first creating a secret on the host.

Set `COPILOT_CONNECTION_TOKEN_GENERATE=true` to print a fresh random token at startup. `COPILOT_CONNECTION_TOKEN` remains exclusively for the secret itself; setting both variables is an error. Anyone with access to container logs can see the generated token, and restarting the container invalidates it. For shared deployments, supply a token through `COPILOT_CONNECTION_TOKEN`; the Kubernetes example reads it from a Secret using `secretKeyRef`.

The guide distinguishes the server's connection secret from each user's GitHub credentials and includes shell and PowerShell examples. Startup diagnostics flag GitHub-shaped connection tokens and Kubernetes service-link port conflicts.

issues.title: console: Go limits table shows 0 for every model when the allowance scene animation doesn't complete

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something is broken

labels.name: area/web
labels.description: Web app

labels.name: inference/go
labels.description: OpenCode Go

issues.body:
## What happens

On https://opencode.ai/console/go#limits the numbers in the models table (`Est. requests / 5 hr` and the bars) are rendered from the table's scene animation. When that animation doesn't run to completion, every cell renders `0` and the bars are empty — permanently, with no static fallback to the published values.

Deterministic repro of the stuck state:

1. Open https://opencode.ai/console/go#limits
2. In devtools → Network, block a single unrelated page resource (any one works, e.g. `faq-pointer-*.svg`) and reload.
3. Scroll to the models table.

Actual: every model shows `0` (or an empty cell) and empty bars. Scrolling does not recover it; only a reload with nothing blocked brings the numbers back.

DOM while stuck:

```js
const scene = document.querySelector('[data-scene="go-models"]')
scene.getAttribute('data-scene-state')   // "waiting" — never leaves this state
scene.getAttribute('data-scene-time')    // "0.000"
document.querySelector('tr[data-model] [data-layer="current-value"]').textContent // "0"
getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('[data-layer="bar"]')).opacity            // "0"
```

On a healthy load the same element goes `still` (3.400, server-rendered values) → `waiting` (0.000) → `playing` (counts up) → `complete` (3.400). The visible cells are `span[data-layer="current-value"]`; the bars get `opacity: 0` + a `clip-path` inset of 100%.

I also ended up in the same permanent `waiting` state in Edge when the tab was hidden while the page finished loading (link opened in a background tab, switched to it afterwards) — the table stayed at 0 until a reload with the tab focused. That one is not 100% deterministic: `visibilitychange` sometimes recovers it and sometimes leaves it in `waiting`.

The scene clock also advances `Math.min(0.1, dt)` per animation frame, so below 10 fps the reveal runs in slow motion instead of shortening: in a throttled renderer the 3.4 s scene took >20 s and most rows still read `0`. Background/hidden tabs, efficiency or power-saving modes, and software compositing all throttle rAF, so the table can look broken for seconds to minutes.

## Why it matters

People open this page to read exactly these two numbers. Right now they are only correct if a decorative reveal animation completes. An ad blocker or privacy extension that blocks any page asset, a tab that was hidden during load, or throttled rendering leaves the table showing 0 — which reads as "my Go allowances were cut to zero".

## Expected

The table should always render the published values. Suggestions:

- Render the final values by default and treat the count-up as progressive enhancement, or force the scene to `complete` whenever the reveal can't run (hidden document, reduced motion, failed/blocked subresource, or a timeout).
- Drive the animation from elapsed wall time instead of accumulating `min(0.1, dt)` per frame, so a low frame rate shortens the animation rather than stretching it.
- Don't let a failed subresource keep the start gate closed: one blocked asset currently leaves the scene in `waiting` forever.

## Workaround that works today

`prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` makes the scene report `still` and every row renders its final value immediately, no animation. In Edge: Settings → Accessibility → "Turn off animations"; on Windows: Settings → Accessibility → Visual effects → Animation effects → off.

## Environment

Microsoft Edge on Windows 11; also reproduced on headless Chromium via CDP (`Emulation.setEmulatedMedia`, `Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled`). The console page isn't in this repo, so no source pointer — the selectors above should be enough to find the component.

issues.body:
## Summary

OpenCode's TUI does not react to Shift+Tab (toggle plan mode) when running
inside Dolphin's embedded Konsole terminal panel, while the same shortcut
works in a standalone Konsole window.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.3.2
- OS: Linux 7.0.0-43-generic x86_64 (Ubuntu, kernel #43-Ubuntu SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC)
- Terminal: TERM=xterm-256color, COLORTERM=truecolor, KONSOLE_VERSION=251203 (embedded Konsole part in Dolphin)
- Shell: /bin/bash
- Install/channel: latest
- Active plugins: None found in config

## Reproduction

1. Open Dolphin (KDE file manager) and enable the embedded terminal panel (F4).
2. Run `opencode` in the embedded panel.
3. Press Shift+Tab to toggle plan mode.

## Expected Behavior

Shift+Tab toggles between normal mode and plan mode.

## Actual Behavior

Nothing happens; OpenCode stays in normal mode. No error message is shown.

## Additional Context

- The same shortcut works correctly when opencode runs in a standalone Konsole window,
  so the issue appears specific to the Dolphin-embedded Konsole part.
- It may be that the embedded terminal does not send the BackTab escape sequence
  (CSI Z / `ESC [ Z`) for Shift+Tab, or that the keybinding is consumed by Dolphin/Konsole.
- Frequency: reproducible consistently in the embedded panel.

issues.title: Namespaced forced choices remain qualified in flat provider requests
issues.body:
### Description

Flat provider adapters flatten namespaced tool definitions but keep a forced choice qualified. For `crm.lookup`, the request defines `crm_lookup` while the forced choice still names `crm.lookup`. The tool and choice names should agree. I reproduced this with local request compilation, without contacting a provider.

OpenAI Chat, Open Responses-compatible, Mistral Chat, Gemini, Bedrock Converse, Anthropic Messages, and Meta Responses share the mismatch. Native OpenAI Responses uses a separate namespace-aware path and is not affected. This is a public AI-library request compilation case; the built-in core session currently does not force namespaced choices.

### Plugins

None required.

### OpenCode version

v2 at b29dab3231d40e9c13b6d3732b4af5e7705cbf03; Bun 1.4.2.

### Steps to reproduce

From `packages/ai`, save the following as `repro-tool-choice.ts` and run `bun repro-tool-choice.ts`:

```ts
import { Effect } from "effect"
import { LLM, ToolChoice, ToolDefinition, ToolNamespace } from "./src/index.js"
import { Auth } from "./src/route.js"
import { compileRequest } from "./src/route/client.js"
import * as Chat from "./src/protocols/openai-compatible-chat.js"

const model = Chat.route.with({
  provider: "custom",
  endpoint: { baseURL: "https://example.invalid/v1" },
  auth: Auth.bearer("unused-test-key"),
}).model({ id: "test-model" })
const request = LLM.request({
  model,
  prompt: "Look up a customer",
  tools: [ToolNamespace.make({
    name: "crm",
    tools: [ToolDefinition.make({ name: "lookup", description: "Look up a customer", inputSchema: {} })],
  })],
  toolChoice: ToolChoice.named("crm.lookup"),
})
const compiled = await Effect.runPromise(compileRequest(request))
console.log(JSON.stringify({ tools: compiled.body.tools, tool_choice: compiled.body.tool_choice }, null, 2))
```

Expected: `tools[0].function.name` and `tool_choice.function.name` both equal `crm_lookup`. Actual: `crm_lookup` versus `crm.lookup`. No provider request is sent.

### Operating System

Ubuntu 22.04 on WSL.

### Terminal

Not relevant to request compilation.

issues.body:
### Description

Code Mode advertises `tools.opencode.session_move`. In a controlled test of the native ACP route reporting model identity “Argon” on November 17, that literal namespace spelling correlated with HTTP `429 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` after about 35 seconds. Changing only four occurrences of `tools.opencode.` to `tools["opencode"].` in the complete original request returned HTTP 200 in 6.1 seconds.

Controls containing `opencode`, `session_move`, or `tools.session_move` returned 200. Removing the actual tool definitions did not remove the failure. Both JavaScript spellings are valid; this is not a sandbox execution error.

Current `dev` still emits the dotted spelling. A local source/runtime reproduction at `70c7f452a5851ef6e36077ec15d339f9271ae5fa` confirms that catalog signatures and `search()` return it, while both spellings execute the same fixture tool with identical input. The reproduction plus existing tool-path tests pass: 46 tests, zero failures.

Would you accept a formatter change that consistently uses JSON-escaped bracket access in generated tool expressions, leaving canonical tool IDs and execution routing unchanged?

**Limits:** I have not repeated the provider requests on current `dev`. The provider-side failure may be historical or intermittent; these observations do not establish a quota, timeout, filtering or account-policy cause. A later HTTP 403 “service disabled” observation is separate, with no demonstrated causal connection.

Related but different: #53623 concerns models misreading tool instructions; #57711 concerns a hint being injected when Code Mode is denied. This report concerns a transport response changing when only an expression's spelling changes.

### Plugins

Current local reproduction uses `@opencode/codemode` directly with one fixture tool; no plugins or provider calls.

### OpenCode version

Current source reproduction: `dev` at `70c7f452a5851ef6e36077ec15d339f9271ae5fa`; the same dotted formatter is present in v2.3.2.

### Steps to reproduce

From `packages/codemode`, add this test and run `bun test <test-file>`:

```ts
import { expect, test } from "bun:test"
import { Effect, Schema } from "effect"
import { CodeMode, Tool } from "../src/index.js"

test("catalog spelling and equivalent invocation", async () => {
  const runtime = CodeMode.make({
    tools: { opencode: { session_move: Tool.make({
      description: "Fixture only",
      input: Schema.Struct({ directory: Schema.String }),
      output: Schema.String,
      execute: ({ directory }) => Effect.succeed(directory),
    }) } },
  })
  expect(runtime.catalog[0]?.signature).toStartWith("tools.opencode.session_move(")
  for (const expression of ["tools.opencode.session_move", 'tools["opencode"].session_move']) {
    const result = await Effect.runPromise(runtime.execute(`return await ${expression}({directory:"fixture"})`))
    expect(result).toMatchObject({ ok: true, value: "fixture" })
  }
})
```

This reproduces the current producer spelling and runtime equivalence, not the external provider response. The historical request comparison is described above without publishing private conversation contents.

### Screenshot

Not applicable: HTTP responses and source/runtime tests, no UI failure.

### Operating System

Windows 11, Bun 1.4.4.

### Terminal

Git Bash.


### Tested upstream
dev 70c7f452a5851ef6e36077ec15d339f9271ae5fa; local catalog/runtime repro and tool-path suite: 46 pass, 0 fail; no fresh provider refusal claim

### Description

When a slash command fails during an ACP turn, the whole `session/prompt`
request fails and the client only sees `Internal error: Internal service failure`.
The command's real message (usage help, goal-state guidance) never reaches the client.

Cause: `CommandExecutionError` (thrown by the server for command failures) is not
recognized in `packages/cli/src/acp/client.ts` `classify()`, so the fiber dies and
`fromUnknown()` in `packages/cli/src/acp/error.ts` renders the opaque string.

Also seen: over ACP a successful `/goal <objective>` produces no `session/update`
at all — re-setting a goal replaces it silently. The client has no way to know.

2.3.2

With an active goal, sending `/goal` again fails the same way instead of showing

issues.title: service: serve --service self-terminates after idle location-services eviction, cutting external clients without warning

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something is broken

labels.name: area/service
labels.description: Background service and server

labels.name: version/v2
labels.description: OpenCode 2.x

labels.name: platform/windows
labels.description: Windows

issues.body:
## Summary

The managed `serve --service` background process exits cleanly — no error, no signal-handling log, the log simply ends — shortly after its last per-directory "location services" entry is evicted. Observed three independent instances over three days with lifetimes of ~1 h, ~16.5 h and ~8.7 h; the time of death tracks the last directory/client activity rather than any fixed interval. After exit, `opencode service status` correctly reports `stopped`, so nothing about the termination looks abnormal from the outside — yet every attached external client loses its connection with no warning.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.3.2 (`@opencode-ai/cli`, npm install; also reproduced with the `opencode-cli` binary bundled in OpenCode Desktop 2.3.2)
- OS: Windows 11 Pro x64 (10.0.26200)
- Install channel: latest
- Service start path: both `opencode service start` (manual) and the desktop's auto-spawn (`v2 CLI background service starting { reason: 'missing' }`)

## What we observed (from `~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log`)

Three `serve --service` instances, each ending the same way — a `location services evicted` event for the last tracked directory, immediately followed by a `watcher stopped` cascade and then silence:

**Instance A** (started 2026-11-20 14:30 UTC via `service start`, dead ~15:38 UTC — ~68 min):

```
15:38:12.861  message="location services evicted" directory="G:\\code\\luyou\\fuwuqi" role=server
15:38:12.894  message="watcher stopped" path="...AGENTS.md" ...
15:38:12.904  message="watcher stopped" path="C:\\Users\\Nirn\\.config\\opencode" type=directory role=server
(process gone; `service status` → stopped)
```

**Instance B** (started 2026-11-21 05:08 UTC, dead ~21:39 UTC — ~16.5 h): last log lines are `GET /api/event` 200s — an SSE stream held ~35 min (`http.span=2091213`) — ending at 21:39:49, then silence.

**Instance C** (started 2026-11-22 09:07 UTC, dead ~17:50 UTC — ~8.7 h): last `location services evicted` for its final directories at 17:47–17:48, watcher churn until 17:50:54, then silence.

In all three cases the next `service start` spawned a fresh `serve --service`, confirming the previous process was fully dead (not merely unresponsive).

## Impact

External/long-lived clients that subscribe to `GET /api/event` (in our case the T3 Code orchestrator configured with a `serverUrl`) see `provider event stream closed unexpectedly` / `The OpenCode event stream was lost and could not reconnect`. Their bounded reconnect budget cannot outlive a dead process, so every silent eviction-to-exit cycle fails in-flight work. This is the same user-facing symptom class as #54181 and #65544, but reached by a different path: here nobody kills the service — it appears to exit on its own once it believes nothing references it.

## Expected behavior

Any of these would resolve the surprise:

1. A service that was explicitly started with `opencode service start` stays resident until `service stop` (independent of per-directory idle eviction); or
2. A `service set` key to opt out of the self-termination (e.g. `keep_alive` / `idle_ttl`) — currently only `port`, `hostname`, `password` are accepted; or
3. If the ephemeral "serve while needed" lifecycle is intentional, document it on the `service` commands so external supervisors/clients know to treat the process as per-demand.

## Workaround

A scheduled task running `opencode service start` every 5 minutes (idempotent — it is a no-op while the service is alive) keeps the endpoint up for clients that need a stable URL.

## Possibly related

- #54181 — watchdog kills unresponsive service; sessions 404
- #65544 — managed clients SIGTERM/SIGKILL externally supervised services
- #51852 — idle CPU spin tripping liveness probes
- #42271 — opposite complaint: idle daemon holding 700–800 MB RSS

labels.name: type/bug

issues.body:
### Description

Desktop on Linux/Wayland uses ~0.7–1.4 cores while completely idle, and typing lags 2–3 s per keystroke in the composer, a quote's comment box and the model picker. Chromium 155 on the same machine, same moment, uses 2%.

CPU does **not** drop when the window is fully occluded or resized to 1/6 area → JS on the renderer main thread, not raster.

Idle, nothing running (`/proc/<pid>/stat`, 12 s, no input):

| process | min | median | max |
|---|---|---|---|
| `renderer` (client-id=5, main window) | 17% | **21%** | 107% |
| `gpu-process` | 20% | **28%** | 32% |
| `renderer` (client-id=7, **no `--opencode-window` flag**) | 15% | **21%** | 50% |
| Chromium 155 `renderer` (same moment) | 0% | 2% | 6% |

Occlusion test, 15 s windows:

```
window visible on ws1      renderer 43.1%  gpu-process 29.9%  GPU engine 3.1%
window on ws9 (occluded)   renderer 46.0%  gpu-process 29.1%  GPU engine 2.3%
window resized to 760x480  renderer 34.6%  gpu-process 27.4%  GPU engine 1.9%
```

Main-thread CPU per second while a job streams: `8 5 6 5 8 9 39 25 24 8 25 22 29 26 58 35 14 25 68 61` — floor 5–9%, a 25–68% spike per streamed token.

`renderer.log` gets 37 `content-visibility` repaint lines inside the same 3 ms, then 6-line clusters each minute while streaming — looks like the timeline is re-laid-out per token.

### Plugins

opencode-idle-compaction, opencode-wallpapers, opencode-side-chat, blindfold, sysmon, session-rename, opendesign-keypool, mcp-reaper, i-have-adhd, agent-models

### OpenCode version

2.3.2 Desktop (Electron 44 / bundled Chrome 152.0.7977.167), channel latest

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open Desktop on Linux/Wayland, HiDPI display with fractional scaling (1.6 here).
2. Open 8–10 tabs, at least one long conversation (296 messages of markdown/tables/code).
3. Have a turn in progress (subagent or shell tool streaming).
4. Watch the `ai.opencode` processes idle; then type in the composer, in a quote's comment box, or open the model picker.

### Screenshot

_No response_

### Operating System

Linux 7.2.15-1-omarchy x86_64, Hyprland 0.56.2 Wayland, 3072×1920@120Hz scale 1.6, Intel Arrow Lake-P (i915)

### Terminal

Desktop app (Electron), `--ozone-platform=wayland`

---

Two more findings, both small:

**Second renderer, no window.** `renderer-client-id=7` (pid 414257) appears ~3 min after launch, carries no `--opencode-window=`, and holds 15–21% of a core on its own, unaffected by the main window's visibility.

**Model picker `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded`** — 42 in `renderer.log`, always with the model dialog open. Matches #65138, but it is not limited to `zoomLevel != 1`: this machine is at 100% zoom with only display fractional scaling. Measured on dpr 1.6:

```
left=123.456px -> rect.left=123.447265625  delta -0.0087  (loop continues)
left=250.75px  -> rect.left=250.7421875    delta -0.0078  (loop continues)
```

At dpr 1 and 2 `250.75px` rounds exactly; at 1.6 nearly every fractional position leaves a residual, so `o || s` is always truthy. An epsilon (`Math.abs(x) > 0.5 || Math.abs(y) > 0.5`) would cover fractional display scaling too.

issues.body: ### Description After updating from v2.3.0 to v2.3.2, opening the model selector and moving the pointer over models causes severe 1–2s UI freezes/stuttering. ``` `renderer.log` repeatedly logs on every hover/open: ```text [error] Uncaught RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded [error] Uncaught (in promise) RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded ``` **Cause** With non-100% app zoom (e.g. "zoomLevel": 1.1 in opencode.settings), the model dialog flyout positioning code recalculates an offset using: ``` const a = n.getBoundingClientRect() const o = a.left - parseFloat(n.style.left) const s = a.top - parseFloat(n.style.top) return o || s ? { left: i.left - o, top: i.top - s } : i ``` At zoomLevel: 1.1, Chromium quantizes getBoundingClientRect() to device pixels (1/1.1 increments), so a.left - parseFloat(n.style.left) produces a non-zero sub-pixel rounding residual (~0.09px). Because the o || s check has no epsilon tolerance, the reactive effect re-dispatches { type: "placed", position } continuously in an oscillation loop until the call stack overflows. **Workaround / Regression info** v2.3.0: Worked smoothly at 110% zoom (0 errors). v2.3.2: Reproducible 100% of the time at 110% zoom (Ctrl +). Workaround: Pressing Ctrl + 0 (resetting zoomLevel to 1) immediately resolves the freeze and eliminates all RangeError logs. Suggested fix: ignore sub-pixel deltas (e.g. Math.abs(o) > 0.5 || Math.abs(s) > 0.5) or guard the placed effect against insignificant position deltas. ### Plugins None ### OpenCode version 2.3.2 (Desktop app, Windows) ### Steps to reproduce 1. Open OpenCode Desktop v2.3.2 on Windows. 2. Zoom in once (`Ctrl +`, setting `"zoomLevel": 1.1` in `opencode.settings`). 3. Click the model selector at the bottom of the chat composer. 4. Hover the mouse pointer up and down over the model list so the right-side variant flyout opens. 5. Observe 1–2s freeze/stutter on hover and `Uncaught RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded` spamming in `renderer.log`. 6. Press `Ctrl + 0` (100% zoom) and repeat step 3–4 — the freeze disappears immediately. ### Screenshot ### Operating System Windows 11 (Windows_NT 10.0.26300, x64) ### Terminal OpenCode Desktop app (Electron)

issues.title: Previous message lands on the reply above the prompt instead of the prompt
issues.body:
### Description

Previous message (Ctrl+Alt+[) can land on the wrong place. When the prompt it jumps to was not on screen yet, the prompt first lands below the session header, and then moves about 1,000 px down as the rows above it finish rendering. The reader sees the middle of the reply before it instead of the prompt.

Measured in the desktop app: the rows between the session header and the prompt mount at estimated heights, and the reply above the prompt then grows from 44 px to 1,037 px when its deferred content renders. TanStack counts that reply as visible, because it is inside the viewport, but it sits under the sticky session header. `shouldAdjustScrollPositionOnItemSizeChange` in `packages/app/src/session/timeline/virtualizer.tsx` compensates only rows before TanStack's first visible row, so the growth pushes the prompt down.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open a session with a few prompts that have long replies, scrolled to the end.
2. Press Ctrl+Alt+[ (Previous message) twice.
3. The prompt shows briefly under the header, then the view shows the middle of the reply above it.

### OpenCode version

`dev` at `18be128acc`.

### Operating System

Windows 11 (every platform).

This pollutes the parent agent's context, wastes tokens, and distracts it from the actual task. Please consider restoring the ability to choose between foreground (synchronous) and background (asynchronous) execution. Background execution is useful for parallel tasks, but synchronous execution is equally important when the parent agent needs the result immediately. Let the agent choose how to execute subagents instead of forcing every subagent to run in the background.

prs.title: fix(app): refresh browsed directories and reopened files
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #52941

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Watch the immediate entries of directories when they are listed. Directory changes now invalidate loaded trees, including the workspace root, whose normalized path is empty. This avoids recursively watching the whole workspace.

Directory watches are bounded so they cannot degrade open tabs: they take from their own per-location budget (`MAX_CHILDREN_PER_LOCATION`), never evict file watches, keep a shorter one-hour expiry (`CHILDREN_TTL`) that is reset on every listing, and coalesce (`CHILDREN_COALESCE`) so churn such as a continuously written file re-lists a browsed directory at most once per 250 ms window. The native children watch also ignores content writes, since a directory's entries only change on creation, deletion, and renames. This addresses the review concerns about the shared watch budget and uncoalesced directory events.

Force a fresh read when opening a file: closed tabs stop watching, so their cached content can be outdated.

No public API change or feature flag; this restores expected refresh behavior.

- Core suite: 7,960 passed, 28 skipped; app unit suite: 2,869 passed.
- Native filesystem/watch tests: 38 passed after rebasing onto current `dev`.
- Verified the native children watch on Linux: content writes and appends to a file emit no directory events, while creates still do.

- Official TypeScript checks passed in core, app, and gui-plugins. The separate E2E typecheck still reports existing fixture/Vite declaration errors outside the added case.
- Confirmed the new regressions fail without the fixes. Manually verified desktop updates on Ubuntu 24.04; the reporting user also tested and confirmed the fix.
