prs.title: fix(browser): open the browser in a project its server has only just started
prs.body:
The browser pane now attaches to a project that its server has only just started. The first `attach` to such a project is refused, because its plugins are still loading, and the pane took that answer for a server with no browser: "The browser couldn't open".

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant P as Pane
    participant S as Server
    P->>S: attach
    Note over S: starts the project, plugins still loading
    S-->>P: 400 rpc.unavailable
    Note over P: before: browser.pane.unsupported
    loop until the project lists its plugins, 10 s at most
        P->>S: plugin.list
        S-->>P: none yet
    end
    P->>S: attach
    S-->>P: attached
```

- **When a project is cold:** the app updated and restarted its server, or the server had evicted the idle project and started it again for this `attach`. One week of my desktop logs has 17 of these, 5 within 4 s of an app start and 12 mid-run: each `browser.pane.unsupported` pairs with an `attach` 400 at most 513 ms after `location services booted`.
- **What it cost:** the pane stayed unsupported until a `plugin.updated` or `server.connected` woke it. In the logs its next `attach` came 0.8 to 2.6 s later, and once not within 3 minutes. Meanwhile the pane said the browser could not open and `available(session)` was false.
- **The fix:** on `rpc.unavailable` before the handshake, the pane waits until the project lists its plugins, then attaches once more. This is the client-side wait `AGENTS.md` asks for under Plugin Loading, the same poll as `waitForPlugins` in the CLI.

```ts
const loaded = client.plugin.list({ location: { directory: session.location.directory } }).pipe(
  Effect.repeat({
    until: (plugins) => plugins.data.length > 0,
    schedule: Schedule.spaced("100 millis").pipe(Schedule.upTo({ duration: "10 seconds" })),
  }),
  Effect.ignore,
)

Deferred.await(connected).pipe(
  Effect.andThen(attach),
  Effect.catchIf(
    (error) => attachmentFailure(error) === "unavailable" && selectBinding(machine.state, binding)?.status === "connecting",
    () => loaded.pipe(Effect.andThen(attach)),
  ),
)
```

- **A server with no browser:** it lists its plugins at once, so it is unsupported one round trip later, as before.
- **A slow project:** one that takes more than 10 s to load its plugins ends unsupported, and `plugin.updated` wakes it as today. A server that started every open project at once took up to 6 s in the logs.
- **Idle eviction:** an attachment the server accepted and then dropped still suspends. Attaching again would start the project the server just evicted.
- **Tests:** the stand-in server of `electron-open.test.ts` now starts cold. It refuses `attach` and lists no plugin until its third answer to the plugin list, and the test checks that the pane was refused once and listed three times.
- **Flag:** none, this is a fix.

prs.body:

### Type of change

### What does this PR do?

Adds `opencode.session.interrupt`, a Code Mode tool (with `full_codemode` on) that interrupts any session by ID and stops everything under it:

- interrupts the session's running turn
- cancels its background jobs: shell commands, subagents, Code Mode scripts, media generation

prs.title: fix(ai): flatten tool namespaces once, before provider adapters
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/52088

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [x] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Flat protocols (everything but native OpenAI Responses) flatten namespaced tools to `namespace_name`, but a forced tool choice kept its qualified name, so the request forced a tool it never declared. Reported and reproduced by @vladislav-miroshnikov in the issue.

```diff
 "tools": [{ "type": "function", "function": { "name": "crm_lookup" } }],
-"tool_choice": { "type": "function", "function": { "name": "crm.lookup" } }
+"tool_choice": { "type": "function", "function": { "name": "crm_lookup" } }
```

The cause was structural: every adapter called `flattenToolRequest` itself and then read a mix of the original and flattened request, so any field it forgot (here the forced choice) stayed namespaced. This PR flattens once, before any adapter's `body.from` runs:

```text
Protocol.make(protocol):
  if the protocol has no native namespaces:
    body.from(request) = adapter's body.from(flattenRequest(request))
flattenRequest: tools, tool updates, past tool calls and the forced choice use flattened names
adapters: receive a flat request; never see namespaces
```

- **One flag:** `Protocol.namespaces`, forwarded by `gateway-protocol`. Only OpenAI Responses sets it, so it keeps sending namespaces natively.
- **Every request path is covered:** `compileRequest`, wrapper protocols, and callers that run `protocol.body.from` directly all go through `Protocol.make`. Wrappers flatten twice, which is a no-op the second time. The exported lower-level builders (`OpenAIChat.fromRequest`, `MistralChat.fromRequest`, `OpenResponses.fromRequest`/`fromRequestWithAdapter`) now document that they expect a flattened request. xAI Responses compaction still lowers unflattened history, as on `dev`.
- **Adapters:** the 9 `flattenToolRequest` calls are gone; they read `request` directly and pass their tools through `flattenTools` (a no-op on a flat list) only to type them. The core AI SDK bridge (`packages/core/src/aisdk.ts`) is a hand-built route, so it calls `flattenRequest` itself, and gets the choice fix too.
- **Forced choice:** matched against real namespace paths (including namespaces a tool update adds), so `crm.lookup` → `crm_lookup`, a dotted leaf follows `flattenTools`' naming, and an unrelated `foo.bar` isn't matched to a top-level `foo_bar`.
- **Tool updates:** a marker that redefines a namespace drops the tools it leaves out, which only the namespace shows. `flattenRequest` names those as explicit removals, so Anthropic Messages no longer tracks declared tools across updates to work them out.

**Trade-offs**
- `ProviderShared.flattenToolRequest` is public, so it stays as a deprecated wrapper over `flattenRequest`, removed in the next minor.
- A protocol that wraps OpenAI Responses' `body.from` must forward `namespaces`, like it already forwards `toolUpdates`; forgetting it only flattens, which every provider accepts.
- `shared.ts` imports `foldTools`/`withdrawnTools` from `tool-updates.ts`, which imports `flattenTools` back. Both are only used inside functions, so the cycle is safe at load time.

Source: 14 files changed, 105 insertions(+), 55 deletions(-) (`packages/ai/src`, `packages/core/src/aisdk.ts`).

### How did you verify your code works?

- `compile.test.ts`: a direct `OpenAIChat.protocol.body.from` call flattens tools, history and the forced choice; a forced `crm.lookup` compiles to `crm_lookup` on every flat protocol (fails on `dev`); a dotted leaf follows `flattenTools`; `foo.bar` isn't matched to `foo_bar`; a namespace added by a tool update on Anthropic is matched.
- Existing tool-update tests cover namespace redefinition removals on Anthropic, which now come from `flattenRequest`.
- `packages/ai` tests pass (2285/2285), `packages/core` AI SDK bridge tests pass, `bun run check` passes.

### Screenshots / recordings

N/A

- [x] I have tested my changes locally
- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

prs.title: perf(core): cut redundant remote file and search round trips
prs.body:
## Before

Remote workspace file writes, edits, and root searches paid extra round trips on every call:

- `write` read the existing file once and then read its first 3 bytes again inside `writeTextPreservingBom` (3 round trips).
- `edit` read the file, read 3 bytes for BOM, wrote the file, and re-read the whole file after writing even on remote workspaces where no formatter runs (4 round trips).
- `glob` and `grep` at the remote workspace root always ran an extra `stat` before spawning `rg` (2 round trips).

## After

- `write` carries BOM state from its initial read into `commit` (**3 → 2** round trips; omitted `knownBom` keeps the header probe).
- Remote `edit` carries BOM state and skips the redundant post-write re-read when no formatter runs (**4 → 2** round trips; local edits keep re-reading in case a failing formatter mutates disk).
- Remote workspace-root `glob`/`grep` invoke `rg` directly and fall back to `pathType` on failure (**2 → 1** round trips; local and non-root searches keep preflight validation).

| `packages/core` targeted unit tests | 93 passed (10 new counting cases RED → GREEN) |
| `packages/core` `bun typecheck` | Passed |

prs.title: refactor(desktop): simplify deep links and open sessions by id
prs.body:
## Summary

Simplifies Desktop deep links, adds `opencode://session/<id>` and brings back `opencode://new-session`.

Before this, main ran a multi-window delivery/acknowledgement state machine and the renderer re-dispatched links as an `opencode:deep-link` DOM event, but nothing in the app listened for it since the `open-project` / `new-session` handlers were removed in #43789. Links were delivered and then ignored.

Now:

- **One pending link.** Main holds at most one link; a newer link replaces one not yet taken. The launch link is captured at the top of the entry module (argv on Windows/Linux, early `open-url` on macOS) so it isn't lost before the layers load.
- **Pull, not push.** Renderers call `AppTakeDeepLink` once on startup and again on each `DeepLinkReceived` event. The first app window to take a link gets it. This replaces `AppReadyDeepLinks`, `AppAcknowledgeDeepLinks`, `DeepLinksOpened` and the deep-link machine.
- **`opencode://session/<id>`** opens the session as a tab. The renderer looks it up on the local server first, then each other connected server in list order, and opens it on the first that has it. It waits for the local server, hydrated tabs and plugin servers before looking.
- **`opencode://new-session?directory=<path>&prompt=<text>`** opens a new session draft on the local server in that directory, with the optional prompt in its composer (not sent). It registers the directory's project first; a directory the server can't resolve shows the usual "Request failed" toast and opens nothing.
- **Console return** (`opencode://console/authorized?window=<id>`) keeps working: it only focuses the originating window and never queues.
- **Retired:** `open-project` (already unhandled).

Both parsers now live in `src/shared/deep-links.ts` with tests.

Not behind a feature flag: deep links only act when an external `opencode://session/...` link is opened, and the previous link handling was already a no-op.

Known limits (agreed as edge cases): servers are checked sequentially, so a slow remote delays later ones; a session found nowhere only logs a console warning.

## Recording

Cold launch with `opencode://session/<local id>` opens the local session:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/29ce0fe7-a5b4-49e9-82e0-1dd1148297bb

App running on Home: a link to a session that only exists on a second server ("Remote box") opens it; a local session link opens a second tab; an unknown ID opens nothing:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5893ee40-53ee-41aa-8c83-77deece26f45

Recorded from a local build with an isolated profile, a local service and a second `opencode serve`. Links were sent via second-instance argv (the macOS `open-url` path feeds the same `receive`). Captions are recording-only overlays.

## Validation

- `bun run check`
- `bun typecheck` and `bun run typecheck:tsc` in `packages/desktop`
- `bun test` in `packages/desktop`

prs.title: feat(core): take execute's options on a first line of raw code for Lark models
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Replaces https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/65602 and https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/65714, which tried the same thing in `packages/ai` and with one shape for every model.

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Same goal as https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/65602: with `full_codemode`, `execute` has optional `timeout` and `background`, so GPT gets it as a JSON function and has to JSON-escape its code. This PR keeps `execute` a raw-text custom tool for models that take Lark grammars by putting the options on an optional first line of the code. The difference is where that happens: here the `execute` tool owns the line, and `packages/ai` and `packages/schema` don't change.

```text
Lark model + full_codemode:  execute = { code }            + Lark grammar   "// @options: {...}" line in the code
other models:                execute = { code, timeout?, background? } as JSON   (unchanged)
no full_codemode:            execute = { code } as plain text                   (unchanged)
```

- `CodeModeTool.create` takes an `optionsLine` switch. With it and `full_codemode`, `execute` declares `{ code }`, `freeform: { type: "lark", grammar }` and a description line explaining the options line.
- The session context sets it when the selected model lists `lark` in `capabilities.freeform`. `Tool.snapshot` caches the two forms separately.
- When `execute` is called, `Tool.snapshot` moves a leading `// @options: {...}` line into `timeout` and `background` before hooks run, so `execute.before` and the job runner see fields as they would from JSON. Keys `execute` doesn't take are dropped, as they are from JSON input. A line that isn't valid options, or has no program after it, fails the call with a message saying how to write it, the same way an invalid JSON field does.
- The stored tool call keeps the model's exact text, and the existing freeform replay sends it back unchanged.
- The TUI Scripts tab and the app's background list name a script by its first line of code, so they skip the `// @options:` line.

Compared with https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/65602:

| | https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/65602 | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Where the line is parsed | OpenAI adapter in `packages/ai` | `execute` in core, before hooks |
| `packages/ai` / `packages/schema` changes | `optionsPrefix`, generated description, stream hold-back, replay re-encoding | none |
| Replay | options re-encoded as compact JSON | the model's exact text |
| Streamed tool input | shows parsed fields | shows the raw code with the line (core only uses the finished input) |
| Execute's schema | the same for every model | depends on whether the model takes Lark |

The trade-off is the last row: plugins that read `execute`'s definition see `{ code }` for GPT and `{ code, timeout, background }` for Claude. Hooks on a call still see the fields either way.

### How did you verify your code works?

- Live with `openai/gpt-6.2-sol` and `full_codemode` (24 runs): `execute` went out as a Lark custom tool every time. Asked to run in the background, the model wrote `// @options: {"background": true}` and got a job (4/4); asked for a 10 minute timeout, it wrote `{"timeout": 600000}` (4/4); on tasks that need no options it left the line out (4/4). The same runs with `// @exec:` behaved the same, so the clearer name costs nothing.

- `codemode-execute-options.test.ts`: the Lark form of `execute`, and parsing of the options line (CRLF, leading spaces, unknown keys), and errors for invalid JSON, invalid values and a line with no program after it.
- `tool-registry.test.ts`: through `Tool.snapshot`, a Lark model's `execute` takes `{ code }` and `// @options: {"timeout": 5000}` reaches the job runner as `{ timeout: 5000 }` and an invalid line fails the call; other models keep the JSON fields; without `full_codemode` nothing changes.
- `packages/tui` `session.test.ts` and `packages/app` `session-background.test.ts`: script labels skip the options line.
- `tool-execute.test.ts`: the compiled requests send a custom Lark tool to GPT and a JSON tool with `timeout` and `background` to Claude.
- Core test suite: 7,949 pass. The 3 failures are shell tests that also fail on `dev` with macOS bash.
- `bun typecheck` in `packages/core` and `bun run check` pass.

prs.title: fix(core): stop an automation's timed-out shell command instead of backgrounding it
prs.body:
**A scheduled automation's shell command no longer wakes the session that created it when it runs past its timeout. The call now fails instead.**
An automation can run a small script on a timer with no model involved. When that script's shell command ran past its `timeout`, the command was moved to the background as if a model had run it, and its output later landed in the creating session as a new message, starting a model turn for nothing. A model's shell commands are not affected.

🔍 **Origin:** seen in real use: a script checking a remote process every 30 s with a 15 s `ssh` timeout. One slow `ssh` posted its `RUNNING` output into the session as a background result.

❌ **Before**
1. The automation's script runs `shell({ command, timeout: 15000 })`, and the command takes longer.
2. ❌ At 15 s, the command moves to the background and the script gets a shell ID back.
3. ❌ When the command ends, its output is posted into the creating session, and its model wakes.
4. ❌ While the command runs, it counts as blocking the creating session, so pressing "move to background" there takes it over too.

✅ **After**
1. Same script, same slow command.
2. At 15 s, the command is stopped and the call **throws** `Command timed out after 15 seconds`, with the output so far. A script that doesn't catch it fails the run, which is retried and pauses after 3 failures, as before. A script that wants to handle it can catch it.
3. Nothing is posted to any session, and the command never blocks one, so "move to background" can't reach it.

```diff
  shell call times out
- -> move to background -> post result to the session when it ends
+ -> called by an automation's code? stop the command, fail the call with what it printed
+ -> otherwise unchanged: move to background, post result when it ends
```

**How the shell tool knows:** each tool call an automation's code makes now carries `context.automation = { id }`. This is a new optional field on the tool call context plugins already receive. Nothing reads it except the shell tool, which uses it to choose the path above. It also gives a later change a place to send background work back to the automation that started it, instead of to a session.

📊 **Proof**

| Case | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Automation command runs past its timeout | ❌ moved to background, result posted to the session | ✅ stopped, the call throws "timed out" |
| "Move to background" pressed while an automation command runs | ❌ takes the command, result posted later | ✅ not affected |
| A model's command runs past its timeout | ✅ moved to background | ✅ unchanged |

Both new shell tests run a program through the same Code Mode runner automations use, and both fail without the change. A third test checks that an automation names itself on each tool call.

👀 **Read:** `tool/plugin/shell.ts`, the `context.automation` branch: the command runs as a plain process with no job, the same way an automation's own shell action does. `finished` is the existing "read the result" code, moved out of the job so both paths share it. The automation code description now says a timeout throws, and `openapi.json` is regenerated for it. The rest is routine.

<details><summary>Checks run</summary>

- `bun run script/test.ts test/tool-shell.test.ts -t automation` (packages/core): 2 pass; both fail with `shell.ts` from `origin/dev`
- `bun run script/test.ts test/automation.test.ts`: 47 pass
- `bun run script/test.ts test/tool-shell.test.ts`: 103 pass, 11 skip, 2 fail; the 2 ("conditional substitutions respect once/always") fail the same way on `origin/dev` locally
- `bun typecheck` (packages/core): no errors
- `bun run generate` in packages/protocol and packages/client: only `openapi.json` changed

</details>


---

Public API: adds optional `automation: { id }` to the plugin tool context; a timed-out shell call in automation code now throws (backwards compatible)

prs.title: fix(core): delete blobs a week after they were written
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

None.

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Blobs are no longer kept forever. The blob store now deletes each blob a week after it was written, whatever stored it, the same way tool output already cleans up its files. Video job records keep their 24-hour lifetime.

```text
before: video record deleted 24 h after the job finished; its videos in <data>/blobs kept for good
after:  video record deleted 24 h after the job finished (unchanged)
        any blob deleted 7 days after it was written
```

Nothing ever removed a blob before, and every video the agent tool made is stored twice (blob plus the copy in the project), so `<data>/blobs` only grew. With video headed for on-by-default that adds up quickly.

The store owns the lifetime rather than the video jobs, so it also catches blobs no job accounts for: a download interrupted mid-write, or a record that couldn't be read. On start and then hourly, `BlobStore` lists `<data>/blobs/blob_*` and removes files older than `RETENTION` (7 days) with the existing `FileRetention.cleanup`, by modification time.

Trade-off: a client that kept a blob ID gets 404 from `GET /api/experimental/blob/:id` after a week. Copies the agent tool saved into a project are untouched. The blob route's description says so.

prs.title: feat(core): add agent instructions and use them for Plan mode
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/62628. That loop came from Plan re-adding its reminder as a synthetic after each compaction, which woke the session again. This PR removes that code path, and after compaction the rules sit in the system prompt with no new message. The review bot ran the issue's mock-model repro with a 3,000-token context limit: on `dev` it never exits (1,873 requests in 40s), and with this PR it exits after 3 requests (title, one compaction, the answer).

Related: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/62554 (this removes the one-off Plan reminder it lists; the other one-off prompts are unchanged).

The revert case below relies on https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/63667, which is merged.

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [x] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Agents get an `instructions` field: text that's added to the default prompt while the agent is selected, without replacing the prompt like `system` does. Plan mode now uses it in place of its own reminder machinery.

Today a plugin can't add rules for one agent without trouble. Plan injects "you are in Plan mode" reminders as synthetic messages and repairs them on every request after compaction or a revert (https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/42652). The internal orchestrator agent adds its rules to the system prompt in a context hook, so every agent switch rewrites the start of the prompt and loses the cache, and the rules aren't stored with the session.

Core already has the right mechanism: instruction sources, which are stored per session, shown once in the system prompt, and sent as an update at the next step when they change. This adds one source, `core/agent`, built from the selected agent:

```text
agent has instructions → value { id, name, text }
agent has none         → removed

shown as               → "You are the Plan agent. Follow these
                          instructions while you are the Plan agent:"
                          + the agent's text
first step             → that, in the system prompt
switch in              → that, as an update before the next prompt
switch away            → "You are no longer the Plan agent. Stop
                          following the instructions you were given as
                          the Plan agent. Keep following anything the
                          user asked for."
switch between two     → one update: leave note + new agent's text
plugin edits the text  → "Your instructions as the Plan agent changed..."
```

Compaction, reverts, forks and storage all come from the existing instruction state. The source is last in the list because it changes most often.

`plan.ts` now sets `instructions` and drops the event subscription, the per-request repair hook and the reminder bookkeeping (about 60 lines). Its permissions and the error rewrite for blocked edits stay.

What changes for Plan, beyond the plumbing:

- The leave text is now core's note instead of Plan's "You are NO LONGER in Plan mode...". Both texts name the agent because the leave note only works reliably when the agent's own text was introduced under its name. I tested this on 13 models, through every way notes reach a model (native system message, developer message, user-turn `<system-update>`):
  - With no leave note, models kept refusing to edit after switching to build about as often as when still in Plan (5/200 went ahead).
  - Plan with this wording: 236/240 went ahead after switching (12 models including Sonnet 5.5 and Opus 5.5; the 4 misses were Muse Ember, which misses 2-3 in 20 with every wording I tried). Still in Plan, 1/200 went ahead.
  - An agent whose text doesn't name it ("Always reply in French"): with the raw text and a generic note, 59/100 dropped the rule when it was in the system prompt (Claude Haiku 5.5, GPT-6 Luna and Gemini 3.5 Flash Lite 0/10). With this wording, 97/100.
  - The leave note says what still applies. When the user had added their own rule while in the agent ("start every answer with Note:"), "...no longer apply. Do not keep following them." made models drop it too (kept 57/100 and 68/100); this wording keeps it (90/100 and 100/100) while still dropping the agent's rule (93/100 and 98/100).
  - An XML-tag label didn't work as well: routes that put notes in the user turn escape `<` and `>`, and Muse Spark then treated the escaped tag as injected text.

  Plan's enter text is unchanged apart from the header and the `<system-update>` wrapper, since it's now system content.
- The rules arrive as a system message (or in the system prompt), not as a user-role synthetic. In the timeline that shows as the standard "Instructions updated: core/agent" row.
- Switching away and back before the next step now sends nothing. Plan used to send both reminders.
- Sessions that are already in Plan when this ships still have the old reminder in history and get the rules once more as an update. That happens once per session.

The field is plugin-only for now. Agent config files have their own schema, and config already uses `instructions` for a list of file paths, so exposing this there needs a naming decision first.

### How did you verify your code works?

New runner scenarios under `agent instructions` in `session-runner.test.ts` use real agents and `switchAgent`: starting in an agent, switching in, switching to an agent without instructions, switching away and back, switching between two agents, a plugin editing the text, compaction, reverting past the switch in, and reverting between switching in and out. All pass, and the system prompt stays byte-identical across switches.

- `bun run check` from the root.
- Ran every core test file that touches history, compaction, forks, reverts, instructions, agents or Plan (179 files): 3,141 pass. The 33 failures are in shell, integration, provider and image test files and fail the same way on unchanged `dev` on my machine.
- Regenerated the client (`AgentInfo.instructions`).

### Screenshots / recordings

Not a UI change; the timeline row is the existing instruction notice.

### Checklist

- [x] I have tested my changes locally
- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR


---

Fixes #62628

Related: #62554

Public API: adds optional `instructions` (string) to Agent.Info (schema, plugin agent editor, client AgentInfo, OpenAPI); backwards compatible

prs.title: feat(app): support key chords in shortcuts
prs.body:
## Summary

Shortcuts can be key chords: a sequence of key presses separated by spaces, such as `mod+k mod+c` or `g i`. This is the second of three stacked PRs, based on the `@opentui/keymap` engine PR.

- **Keymap.** Each binding parses into strokes. A chord whose first key types a character only starts outside text fields, so typing is never taken. A chord that starts with a modifier works anywhere. Escape cancels a pending chord and Backspace removes its last key.
- **Next-key panel.** While a chord is pending, a panel near the bottom of the window lists the keys that continue it and the command each runs.
- **Labels.** Chords show one keycap per stroke, for example ⌥G ⌥S, in Settings, the palette and tooltips. `parseKeybind` and `matchKeybind` still only match single-stroke combos.
- **Recording in Settings > Shortcuts.** A key saves as soon as it is pressed, as before. The row just saved then shows **+**. Clicking it records one more key onto the shortcut, up to 4. Backspace while adding drops that key; with nothing before it, Backspace still unbinds the shortcut.
- **Conflicts** now include prefixes. A chord is rejected when it starts, or is started by, another shortcut. For example ⌘K ⌘J is rejected because ⌘K opens the palette.

prs.title: feat(core): take execute's options on a first line of its code for every model
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Third option next to https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/65602 and https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/65709, so all three can be compared. Only one should merge.

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Same goal as the other two: with `full_codemode`, `execute` has optional `timeout` and `background`, so GPT gets it as a JSON function and has to JSON-escape its code. Here `execute` takes only `code` for every model, and the options always go on an optional first line of that code.

```diff
 without full_codemode:  execute({ code })
-with full_codemode:     execute({ code, timeout?, background? })
+with full_codemode:     execute({ code })   // first line may be: // @exec: {"timeout": 300000}
```

- `execute` keeps its single `code` field, so it stays a raw-text custom tool wherever the model supports freeform input, and JSON `{ code }` everywhere else. No grammar.
- With `full_codemode`, the description explains the line. When `execute` is called, `Tool.snapshot` moves the line into `timeout` and `background` before hooks run, so `execute.before` and the job runner see fields. Keys `execute` doesn't take are dropped. A line that isn't valid options, or has no program after it, fails the call with a message saying how to write it.
- Without `full_codemode`, nothing changes: the line isn't mentioned and stays a comment.

Compared with the other two:

| | https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/65602 | https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/65709 | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `execute`'s shape | `{ code, timeout?, background? }` | `{ code }` for Lark models, JSON fields for others | `{ code }` for every model |
| Where the line is parsed | OpenAI adapter in `packages/ai` | core, before hooks | core, before hooks |
| Files touched outside codemode and `tool.ts` | `packages/ai`, `packages/schema`, `model-request.ts` | `session/context.ts`, the snapshot cache key | none |
| Grammar | Lark | Lark | none |

The trade-offs: every model, Claude included, sets options through the line rather than JSON fields, and without a grammar nothing forces the line's format; a bad line fails the call with instructions instead. A Lark grammar can still be added for models that take it, since the tool keeps one field.

### How did you verify your code works?

- `codemode-execute-options.test.ts`: `execute` takes only `code` with and without `full_codemode`, and the line is parsed with CRLF, leading spaces and unknown keys, with errors for invalid JSON, invalid values and a line with no program after it.
- `tool-registry.test.ts`: through `Tool.snapshot`, `// @exec: {"timeout": 5000}` reaches the job runner as `{ timeout: 5000 }` and an invalid line fails; without `full_codemode` the line is a comment.
- `tool-execute.test.ts`: the compiled requests send GPT a custom text tool and Claude a JSON tool with only `code`.
- Other core tests that touch `full_codemode` pass, except 2 shell tests that also fail on `dev` with macOS bash.

prs.title: feat(ai): carry optional fields on a first-line options comment in freeform tools
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Since https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/65266, full Code Mode `execute` has optional `timeout` and `background` fields, so `packages/ai` stopped sending it as an OpenAI custom tool and GPT got a JSON function instead. In our Terminal-Bench audits, JSON-escaped code makes gpt-6.2-sol fall into endless whitespace after an escaped `\"` in about 23% of trials, and cut programs short at unescaped quotes. Raw-text `execute` had none of these.

A `text` freeform tool can declare `optionsPrefix`. That allows optional fields next to its one required string. On OpenAI Responses and Chat, such a tool goes out as a custom tool with a Lark grammar: an optional first line `<prefix> <JSON object>`, then the source. One generated line is added to the description, naming the syntax and the fields.

- Parsing: if the first line matches the prefix and holds a JSON object, the input is `{ ...options, code: rest }`. Otherwise the whole text is the code; a bad line is just a JS comment. Core validates the result as usual.
- Replay: a call with options is written back as the options line plus the code, and parses back to the same input.
- Streaming: text that could still be an options line is held until the first newline (or the end), then sent as JSON fields.
- Other providers, non-freeform tools, and freeform tools without extra fields send the same requests as before. Without `full_codemode`, `execute` still goes out as plain `text`.
- Core changes: `execute` declares `optionsPrefix: "// @exec:"`. The capability check keeps the options line only for models that list `lark`; otherwise the tool falls back to plain text (single field) or JSON (with optional fields).

### How did you verify your code works?

- `bun test` in `packages/ai` passes. Added tests for parsing with and without options, malformed lines, an options line followed by code, CRLF, streaming on Responses and Chat, identical history replay, and unchanged behavior for Anthropic.

- Working on a paired machine meant prefixing every file path and shell `workdir` with `gpu:`, and every path on that machine prompted as `external_directory`.

✅ **After**

- `SessionRunner` (`SessionCwd.make`) and `SessionShell` (`SessionCwd.current`) bind the session's `cwd` when `machines` is enabled. If a session's `cwd` names a removed machine, tools fail loudly with `Machines.NotFound` instead of falling back to the home computer.
- Paths inside a remote `cwd` skip `external_directory` prompts (checked with that environment's own path rules) while keeping machine-scoped resources and rules (`gpu:…`).

+ const cwd = yield* SessionCwd.make
  ...
+ const activeCwd = yield* cwd.current(sessionID)
  const outcome = yield* steps.attempt({ ... })
+   .pipe(Effect.provideService(Environment.CurrentWorkingDirectory, activeCwd))

prs.title: feat(core): add Claude Agent as a web search provider
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Related: #64996, #10704, #63487, #63784

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [x] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Adds an opt-in websearch provider, `claude-agent`, served by the Claude Agent plugin while it's connected. It runs Claude Code's WebSearch, which Claude plans include, so any model can use opencode's `websearch` tool without a search API key or Console credit. It's never the default: you select it with `"websearch": { "provider": "claude-agent" }`.

#64996 asked for this and was closed because handing Claude its own WebSearch would break session continuity when you switch to a non-Claude model. This PR avoids that problem: Claude Code's built-in tools stay off for chats. The search runs behind opencode's own `websearch` tool, so results are stored as ordinary tool output that every model can read.

How it works:
- Each search is a one-off Haiku run with only WebSearch allowed, no transcript and thinking off. It's closed as soon as the results arrive and times out after a minute. A model has to run the search because WebSearch returns page contents encrypted. Haiku is the cheapest.
- Searches use the provider's connection settings (baseURL, headers and so on) and the account folder the chats used last (`configDir`).
- Copies of one page (`/de/...` locale folders, `hl`/`authuser` variants, `.md.txt` mirrors) are listed once, under the shortest URL. Claude's summary rides on the first result.

This was reviewed and merged first in the beta repo, Tarquinen/opencode-claude-agent#9. This PR ports that code into core, with the tests adapted to core's plugin test harness. Docs are in `websearch.mdx`, `claude-agent.mdx` and the spec.

- `bun test test/plugin/provider/claude-agent test/plugin/websearch.test.ts test/websearch.test.ts test/tool-websearch.test.ts test/config/websearch.test.ts`: 160 pass, 0 fail. The new tests cover de-duplication, offering the provider only while connected, searching with only WebSearch and no session persistence through the configured base URL, and following the last-used account folder.

prs.title: fix(core): reuse each ChatGPT account's client and fix adding a second account
prs.body:
Every time someone logged out of Sign in with ChatGPT and signed back in, OpenCode registered a brand new client with OpenAI, so each re-login added another "OpenCode" entry to the user's ChatGPT connected apps. And adding a second ChatGPT account while one was connected failed on OpenAI's page with `3p_login_workspace_scope_denied` (https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/56298), because OpenCode reused the connected account's client.

OpenAI's token-sharing guide says each issued client belongs to one ChatGPT account and workspace, that apps should keep a profile per account that survives logout, and that signing in to the same account again reuses its client while a different account registers a new one. This does that.

```text
                         before      after
add a second account B   error       new client for B
remove A, sign in again  new client  reuses A's client
sign in again, remove A  reuses A's  reuses A's client (when A's token is dead)
```

How "Sign in with ChatGPT" picks a client now:

```text
a working ChatGPT account is saved → register a new client (this is Add account)
only expired ones, or none saved   → reuse the last account's client, with id_token_hint + login_hint
"Use a different ChatGPT account"  → always register a new client
```

- After a verified sign-in I save a profile in plugin storage, keyed by the issued client ID: the ID token's `sub`, its email, and the ID token itself (for `id_token_hint`; the guide says an expired hint is fine since it only identifies the account). I also remember which client was used last. Logout deletes the credential but not the profile.
- When a refresh gets `invalid_grant` (the "Connect again" case), I record that client as expired, so signing in again reconnects it instead of registering a duplicate. A successful sign-in clears it.
- A reauthorization that comes back as a different account (`sub` mismatch) is rejected instead of overwriting the profile, and points to "Use a different ChatGPT account".
- Connections made before this change seed the last client from the credential on load.
- "Use a different ChatGPT account" only shows once an account is known. Both methods save the credential under `chatgpt-token-sharing`, so nothing else that checks the method ID changes. The app's first-sign-in welcome also fires for the new method.

No public API change. Entries already duplicated in someone's ChatGPT settings don't merge; they have to remove extras by hand.

## Verification

- `bun test test/plugin/provider-chatgpt.test.ts` in `packages/core`: 29 pass. New tests cover adding an account while one is connected (registers fresh), reconnecting an expired account (reuses its client), reusing the last profile with both hints after logout, the new-account method, and when it appears.
- `bun typecheck` and `bun run typecheck:tsc` in `packages/core`, `bun typecheck` in `packages/app`: pass.
- Not covered by a test: recording an expired client from a real refresh (the token URL isn't injectable through the method), and rejecting a mismatched account (needs a real token exchange). Not tried live against OpenAI.

prs.title: fix(ai): zstd-compress ChatGPT sign-in requests again
prs.body:
ChatGPT sign-in requests are now zstd-compressed again, as intended. The default moves from core into the AI package and is decided by URL, the way the Codex client does it.

**What was broken.** Core's OpenAI and ChatGPT plugins set `encoding: "zstd"` for ChatGPT sign-in only when no custom `baseURL` was configured. Since https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/59296 (Oct 26), models.dev gives every provider its own URL, so that check always saw a "custom" URL and the default never applied. ChatGPT requests have gone out as plain JSON since then, which is the case https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/54664 is about (503s on uncompressed bodies over ~1 MiB).

**Now.** `providers/openai.ts` compresses Responses requests with zstd when the resolved `baseURL` is the ChatGPT backend:

```text
https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex   → zstd       (ChatGPT sign-in)
https://api.openai.com/v1 (API key)     → plain JSON (unchanged)
anything else (proxy, gateway)          → plain JSON
```

**Sign in with ChatGPT** (token sharing, `chatgpt.ts`) also gets zstd, set by its plugin: it sends to `api.openai.com/v1` over HTTP only, and the ~1 MiB 503s in https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/54664 were reported on this path. Its URL is the regular API's, so the plugin sets it, and skips it when config sets its own `baseURL` (read from config only, via the new `configuredBaseURL()`, so the catalog's URL doesn't count).

API-key requests stay uncompressed: OpenAI's regular API takes zstd but rejects bodies that compress more than about 100x, and the Codex client doesn't compress them either. `settings.encoding: "none"` still turns it off. Chat Completions, media and WebSocket messages are unchanged. The two plugin checks in core are removed.

OpenAI's `/responses/compact` rejects compressed bodies with a 415 (checked live against `api.openai.com`), and the Codex client doesn't compress compaction requests, so `ResponsesCompaction` now always sends plain JSON.

Recorded tests compare request bodies as text, so `@opencode/http-recorder` and the AI tests' `handlerLayer` decode `gzip` and `zstd` request bodies before storing or matching them. https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/65697 has the identical change; whichever merges second rebases cleanly.

### Verification

- New `packages/ai/test/provider/openai-encoding.test.ts` checks the wire header: zstd for the ChatGPT backend (with and without a trailing slash); plain JSON for `api.openai.com`, a proxy, Chat Completions, compaction, and `"none"` on the model's options. It fails on `dev`.
- `test/plugin/provider-chatgpt.test.ts`: Sign in with ChatGPT gets `zstd` with the catalog's `baseURL` set, as models.dev sets it; it fails on `dev`.
- AI suite (2,284), core plugin tests, http-recorder suite and `bun run check` pass.
- Not tested live: a ChatGPT sign-in, since I don't have one here. The ChatGPT backend decoding zstd is what the original default and the Codex client rely on.

prs.title: fix(core): hold event watches like timers while automations are off
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Setting `automations: false` treated timers and event watches differently. A timer stays active, records `disabled` and checks again hourly, so it comes back on its own. A watch kept its stream open until the next event arrived, then paused as `failed` and needed a manual resume.

Watches now behave like timers:

- A watch whose directory has automations off stays active, records `last_outcome: "disabled"` and is checked again after an hour, like a timer.
- An open watch closes within one scheduler pass (30 seconds) instead of on its next event, which also lets its directory unload.
- When automations are back on, it reopens on its own from now. Its cursor is cleared, so events from while it was off don't run.

prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

No linked issue.

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [x] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

`CHANGELOG.md` on `dev` stops at v2.3.0. The v2.3.1 and v2.3.2 notes exist only on their release tags, because the PRs the release workflow opened to bring them back to `dev` were never merged: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/64548 (v2.3.1) and https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/64567 (v2.3.2). They also can't simply both merge. v2.3.2 was cut from a `dev` commit that didn't have v2.3.1's notes yet, so its changelog skips v2.3.1 and the two PRs conflict.

This PR does what both would have done together:

- adds the v2.3.2 and v2.3.1 entries above v2.3.0, copied unchanged from the `v2.3.2` and `v2.3.1` tags
- sets the package versions to 2.3.2, as the v2.3.2 release commit does

It touches the same 35 files as the `v2.3.2` release commit and nothing else (versions and the changelog only). The next release computes its version from npm, so this doesn't change how it bumps. Once this merges, https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/64548 and https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/64567 can be closed.

- Compared the new entries with `git show v2.3.1:CHANGELOG.md` and `git show v2.3.2:CHANGELOG.md`.
- Checked that the changed files match `git diff --name-only v2.3.2^ v2.3.2`, and that `bun.lock` only changes version lines.

prs.title: fix(app): stop restyling every timeline row when one changes height
prs.body:
Every mounted timeline row was restyled on almost every frame while scrolling through history or streaming a reply, and on each focus change in the timeline. Two CSS rules caused it. ## Discovery | Before (`dev`) | This PR | | --- | --- | | ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/26723d41-ec7d-4cab-ab63-b6c7ab856e44) | ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8b4becae-df8f-40d5-b01e-02371bfdfbcf) | - One headless Chrome trace per side: 4 s of middle-button autoscroll up through unvisited history of a real session. This is noisy discovery evidence. The strobe blocks under Results are the measurement. - Chrome's invalidation tracking named the trigger: the inline `height` write on `[data-timeline-virtual-content]` scheduled a `:has()` invalidation on the scroll root, which invalidated its whole subtree. ## Cause ```mermaid flowchart TD A["A row is measured, or a reply grows"] --> B["The virtualizer writes the content height inline"] B --> C{"Does a selector read [style] inside :has()?"} C -- "yes: markdown.css" --> D["Chromium rechecks each :has() anchor above the write"] C -- "no" --> G["Only that element is restyled"] D --> E{"Does the anchor's rule style another element?"} E -- "yes: timeline focus ring" --> F["Everything inside the scroll root is restyled: every row"] E -- "no" --> H["Only the anchor is restyled"] ``` - **Trigger (#64545):** `markdown.css` matched `:has(> pre:not([style*="background"]))`. With `style` inside a `:has()` argument, every inline style write in the document is a change that `:has()` can depend on. - **Blast radius (#65192):** the timeline's focus ring was `[data-slot="session-timeline-scroll"]:has(…) ~ [data-slot="session-timeline-visible"]::after`. When the rule after `:has()` styles another element, Chromium invalidates the whole subtree of the anchor. Here the anchor is the scroll root. - The ring rule alone also restyled every row on each focus change in the timeline: a click, or the first key press after one. ## Change - **Code blocks:** the wrapper of a highlighted `pre` records `data-code-painted` when it is built. The rule reads that attribute instead of `style`. ```css /* before */ [data-component="markdown-code"][data-code-kind="shell"]:has(> pre:not([style*="background"])) { … } /* after */ [data-component="markdown-code"][data-code-kind="shell"]:not([data-code-painted]) { … } ``` - **Focus ring:** the ring is the scroll root's own `::after`, so `:has()` stays on the element that it styles. The box, colour, radius and stacking are the same. ```css /* before */ [data-slot="session-timeline-scroll"]:has(> .scroll-view__viewport:focus-visible) ~ [data-slot="session-timeline-visible"]::after { … } /* after */ [data-slot="session-timeline-scroll"]:has(> .scroll-view__viewport:focus-visible)::after { … } ``` | Focus ring before | Focus ring, this PR | | --- | --- | | ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3d86c1c6-7820-4f6f-b285-9567c38514a7) | ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0b4d2a75-9709-492f-b44b-161459f12871) |
Standalone reproduction: elements restyled, counted from Chrome's UpdateLayoutTree events ```html
``` | Rules | `content.style.height = …` | Focus change on the viewport | | --- | ---: | ---: | | All four, as on `dev` | 1,685 | 1,686 | | Code rule fixed only | 1 | 1,686 | | Ring fixed only | 3 | 3 | | Both fixed (this PR) | 1 | 3 | | `dev` without the fourth rule | 3 | 3 | - The fourth rule stands for the app's other `:has()` rules. Without one, a page does not show the problem. - Either fix alone stops the restyle on a height write. The code rule also stops Chromium from rechecking `:has()` on every inline style write.
## Results strobe compares `stream.bench.ts` "stream a reply" and `timeline.bench.ts` "scroll history" against `origin/dev`. Its block for each follows. --- _Added by the opencode bot (AI-generated)._ Related: #54291

prs.title: feat(ai): gzip requests to api.anthropic.com by default
prs.body:
Requests to `api.anthropic.com` are now gzip-compressed by default. Closes https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/65170.

Every step resends the whole transcript, so long sessions upload hundreds of KB per tool call. Only ChatGPT sign-in had a default encoding (`zstd`); every other provider sends plain JSON.

```diff
 POST https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages
+content-encoding: gzip
-62 KB request body
+13.7 KB request body
```

The default lives in the AI package's Anthropic provider (`providers/anthropic.ts`), so it applies to anyone using `@opencode/ai`, not just OpenCode. It turns on when the resolved `baseURL` is Anthropic's own (`https://api.anthropic.com/v1`, trailing slash ignored). That has to be a URL comparison rather than "no `baseURL` given", because OpenCode passes the models.dev catalog URL explicitly. It stays off when:
- the `baseURL` points anywhere else, since a proxy or gateway may not decode gzip
- an `encoding` is set: `http.encoding` in the package, or `settings.encoding` in OpenCode config (`"none"` turns it off), which lands on the model's options and wins over the route default

Zen and Anthropic-compatible providers use other URLs and stay uncompressed.

Recorded tests compare request bodies as text, so `@opencode/http-recorder` (and the AI tests' `handlerLayer`) now decode a `gzip` or `zstd` request body before storing or matching it. Cassettes stay plain JSON and don't depend on the encoding.

### Verification

- `opencode run` on this branch with `anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5` and the default models.dev setup: every request to `https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages` went out with `Content-Encoding: gzip` (checked with Bun's fetch trace), and the session completed.
- Live against `api.anthropic.com` with a 62 KB prompt: gzip returns 200, the model read the whole body (a code at the end came back) and input tokens matched the uncompressed request (24,799). zstd returns 400 and br 415, so gzip is the only option. Prompt caching is unaffected: an uncompressed request wrote 16,820 cached tokens, and later gzip requests read all 16,820.
- New tests in `packages/ai/test/request-encoding.test.ts` check the wire header: gzip for the default URL with and without a trailing slash, plain JSON for another `baseURL`, an explicit `"none"`, and `"none"` on the model's options. The default-URL test fails without the change.
- `bun typecheck`, the AI suite (including the Anthropic recorded tests, which failed on the compressed bodies before the recorder change), the http-recorder suite and `bun run check` pass.


---
<!-- opencode-github-bot:pr-section -->
_Added by the opencode bot (AI-generated)._

Related: #60487

Public API: @opencode/ai Anthropic provider defaults http.encoding to "gzip" for api.anthropic.com (backwards compatible; "none" opts out)
<!-- /opencode-github-bot:pr-section -->

prs.title: fix(app): remove the focus rings around the timeline and composer
prs.body:
The timeline and the composer drew a focus ring around their whole frame at moments nobody navigated to them: after a click in the transcript followed by a key, when the app moved focus there, and still there on returning to the window.

### Before and after

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Click in the transcript, then press ↑ | ![Ring around the whole timeline](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c02459ff-f467-462c-8502-fe94991368c4) | ![No ring](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/32ef79fe-b3d3-46c3-a6f0-fad86079206c) |
| Then start typing | ![Ring around the composer](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/87ab74be-fa2a-4cb8-8212-7164c53f23d3) | ![No ring](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a98b5fec-5ece-473f-9516-56a36c644ec7) |

### Why they showed

- Chromium matches `:focus-visible` on whatever has focus once a key without Ctrl/Alt/Meta is pressed, and on every focused text field. A click in the transcript focuses the whole scroll area, so the next arrow or PgDn ringed it.
- The composer drew its ring on every focus that was not a direct click, which includes typing from elsewhere and focus the app restores.
- Focus rescue forced a ring whenever the last input was any key, Ctrl and Alt included.

### What changes

- Scroll areas (the timeline, Home's list) still take focus for keyboard scrolling, and draw no ring.
- The composer and Home search no longer draw a frame ring. Focus shows as the caret and the field's focused background.
- Focus rescue rings the control it lands on only when Tab or an arrow key moved focus last:

```ts
const NAVIGATION = new Set(["Tab", "ArrowUp", "ArrowDown", "ArrowLeft", "ArrowRight", "Home", "End"])

const useKeyboard = (event: KeyboardEvent) => {
  if (event.ctrlKey || event.altKey || event.metaKey || !NAVIGATION.has(event.key)) return
  keyboard = true
}
```

- `field-focus.tsx`, which tracked the fields' ring state, is removed with its callers' ring arguments. The composer keeps one flag that tells a press from other focus, so a new editor still restores the draft's caret.
- Every other control keeps the browser's `:focus-visible`.

### Trade-off

- Tab onto the timeline or into the composer no longer draws a ring. The composer shows its caret. The timeline shows nothing until focus moves to a control inside it.

### Tests

- The composer keeper in `e2e/regression/composer.spec.ts` now asserts that no ring shows however focus arrives.
- `focus-rescue.spec.ts` gains a case for focus that no key moved, which fails on the old rule.

Supersedes #65650, which replaced the browser's rule on every control to the same end.

prs.title: fix(session-ui): open a group of long Code Mode scripts without freezing the timeline
prs.body:
Opening a long run of Code Mode scripts folded into one `Used 46 Execute` group froze the app for about 15 s. Each script opens by default inside a group, and the six that walked a source tree listed all of their 19,039 calls. ### Discovery From `strobe bench --check` and `strobe record --bench` on an export of the session (single launches: discovery evidence, not results): - `main.work` 14,708 ms to open and close the group, `main.style` 11,703 ms of it. - Kobalte's `Collapsible.Content` reads its animation and size on every open and close: 63 forced style passes per open and close. - `markdown.css` matched a shell code block with `:has(> pre:not([style*="background"]))`. A `style` attribute inside `:has()` makes Chromium recheck every `:has()` above each element whose inline style changes. The timeline positions its rows inline, so the virtualizer's scroll adjustment after the open restyled the whole timeline a second time (3,314 then 3,673 elements). Dropping that one rule in the page removed the second pass. - Every open decoded all 19,039 calls through `Schema` and gave each finished call a six-element `TextShimmer`. ```mermaid flowchart LR click[Click Used 46 Execute] --> rows["46 scripts x every call\n19,039 rows"] rows --> forced["Kobalte content: forced style\nper collapsible"] forced --> resize[Virtualizer resizes the row] resize --> has["inline style change\n+ :has([style]) rule"] has --> again[Whole timeline restyled again] ``` ### Changes - **Latest calls first:** an Execute lists its latest 10 calls. A `+N more` button above them reveals 50 earlier calls per press, and focus moves to the first call when the button goes (`tool-renderer.tsx`). - **Decode what shows:** counting, the failed call and the subtitle read the raw list; only shown calls are decoded (`current-tool-state.ts`). - **Plain collapsible content:** `Collapsible.Content` mounts with the open state, without Kobalte's presence and measuring. Nothing in the app animates collapsible content (`collapsible.tsx`). - **No `[style]` in `:has()`:** the shell code block's toolbar background is matched from the toolbar after the code (`markdown.css`). - **Shimmer only when live:** a call or Execute title that never ran while shown renders plain text. ### Before and after The same opened group, scrolled up the same distance: before, one script's thousands of calls fill the view; after, each script lists its latest calls, with `+76 more` above the rest. | Before | After | | --- | --- | | ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dff7699f-6ee0-47a7-9aeb-07c76de505b5) | ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a292de4e-c3de-4cc5-a7d9-2c39f15df85c) | ### Results | One launch each, the real 46-script session | Before | After | | --- | --- | --- | | `main.work`, open and close | 14,708 ms | 222 ms | | `main.style`, open and close | 11,703 ms | 87 ms | | Click to frame, open | ~14,200 ms | 137-153 ms | | Click to frame, close | — | 27-31 ms | The block below is the committed `open a group of scripts` case in `packages/app/perf/timeline.bench.ts` (`fixtures/scripts.ts` rebuilds the session's 46 scripts and 19,039 calls). prs.title: fix(app): eliminate model picker layout thrash on open, scroll, and select

### Discovery Opening, scrolling and selecting in the desktop model picker were profiled with strobe on a 92-model, 19-provider catalog (`strobe bench --check --why always`, `exp_bcc754`). These are single attribution recordings of `dev`: they show where the time goes, they are not a timing verdict. - **Open** (`rec_a48088`): 9 forced style recalculations and 5 forced layouts per open. The flyout measured its row twice in one task, `solid-prevent-scroll` read `clientWidth` right after the dialog mounted, and Kobalte's `ariaHideOutside` set `aria-hidden` on each of the ~160 `` elements of the icon sprite, one timer each. - **Scroll** (`rec_c5e24a`): 154 forced style recalculations and 33 forced layouts in a one-second scroll. Three scroll handlers each read layout after the one before had written styles. - **Select** (`rec_675e12`): the pick updated Recent before the dialog closed, so the closing list reconciled its rows and measured itself again. ```mermaid flowchart TB subgraph Before["Before: every scroll event"] direction LR S1["fadeHeaders
reads 19 headers, writes styles"] --> S2["MenuScroll.measure
reads sizes (forced layout), writes thumb"] S2 --> S3["SearchList.edges
reads sizes (forced layout), writes fade"] end subgraph After["After: every scroll event"] direction LR A1["onListScroll
hit test and header rects, then changed styles only"] --> A2["SearchList.edges
arithmetic on cached sizes"] A2 --> A3["MenuScroll.position
arithmetic on cached sizes, one transform"] end ``` ### What changed - **Icon sprites** (`ui/src/icons/registry.ts`, `ui/src/icons/icon/icon.tsx`): both sprites sit in one host `
`. A modal dialog now hides that one element instead of every symbol. - **Dialog** (`ui/src/context/dialog.tsx`, `ui/src/overlays/dialog/dialog.tsx`): Kobalte's scroll lock is off for mouse and trackpad, where the shell's body does not scroll; it stays on for touch devices. The fallback search for a text field to focus runs only when nothing else takes focus. - **Scrolling** (`ui/src/components/menu-scroll.tsx`, `ui/src/forms/search-list/*`): `MenuScroll` and `SearchList` cache their sizes when the list lays out, and a scroll event reads `scrollTop` once. A list's own `onScroll` runs before the thumb and the fades are written. The bottom fade's custom properties are registered as non-inherited, so changing them does not restyle the rows. `SearchList` takes `topFade={false}` for a list that draws its own header fade. - **Model picker** (`app/src/providers/models/select-dialog.tsx`): a pick closes the dialog before it updates the selection. The flyout is placed once per task and again when it lays out, instead of twice in a row. Header label offsets are cached until the rows change, and styles are written only when their value changes. Each row reads whether it is selected through `createSelector`, and models are sorted once, not on every keystroke. ```ts // One measure per task: ArrowDown claims the old row, highlights the new one and scrolls it into view first. pendingPlace = { attempt: effect.attempt, id: effect.id } if (placeScheduled) return placeScheduled = true queueMicrotask(flushPlace) ``` ### Not in scope This does not explain or fix the multi-second freezes some people see when opening the picker. On a small page the picker never takes seconds, before or after this change; that cause is still being investigated and looks to be outside the picker. ### The bench `packages/app/perf/model-picker.bench.ts` (open, scroll and select with 96 models from 19 providers): `strobe bench packages/app/perf/model-picker.bench.ts --base origin/dev --head .` ### Results Strobe's block for the paired comparison against `dev` follows. Reading it: - Opening the picker and selecting a model each cost less main-thread work. Scrolling costs slightly less: its interval only just clears zero, so treat it as a small gain. - Every verdict is marked "warned": other work ran on the measured CPUs in every block of the run. - `interaction.p95` and `frames.interval.p95` were refused for open and select, because one open or one pick gives too few inputs and frames for a percentile. - The run was stopped after the last series decided, so that series has no attribution block. - The comparison ran on commit `537bb420fb`, before `dev` was merged in. That merge brought #65634, which caches the `MenuScroll` sizes on `dev` too, so the scroll difference against today's `dev` is probably smaller than the block shows. The bench's provider and model names were also changed to placeholders afterwards; the counts are the same. strobe · exp_be8bd9 · packages/app/perf/model-picker.bench.ts · generated ![39% less main-thread work (Open model picker), better in 8 of 8 pairs; 12% less main-thread work (Scroll model picker), better in 10 of 12 pairs; 31% less main-thread work (Select a model), better in 8 of 8 pairs.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5fa88a1e-08f5-4e54-824f-ea575e120b0e) ### 12–39% less main-thread work **Open model picker:** Main-thread work per 388 ms run ![−39%](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3f99e4af-3d61-4e46-9e21-dea7df327989) per pair (medians 76,511 → 48,971 µs), better in 8 of 8 pairs, likely −51% to −26%; **unsteady case**: its work grew each run. **Scroll model picker:** Main-thread work per 1 s run ![−12%](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a39a0f01-7cf4-478b-9d67-e5f43659a139) per pair (medians 130,595 → 115,238 µs), better in 10 of 12 pairs, likely −24% to −0.2%, perhaps by under 2%; **unsteady case**: its work grew each run. **Select a model:** Main-thread work per 368 ms run ![−31%](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a4118f28-aea5-4e32-9627-595d181643ef) per pair (medians 52,940 → 39,092 µs), better in 8 of 8 pairs, likely −45% to −19%; **unsteady case**: its work grew each run. **Stopped early:** the results cover only the pairs that finished.

prs.title: perf(ui): bake the activity spinner into a 90 fps APNG
prs.body:
Brings back the precomputed APNG from #42952 for Soft Radar. Each spinner is one element whose mask is a 90 fps APNG. The browser's image decoder advances the frames, so a spinner does no style, script or animation work on the main thread. This follows #65634, which reduced the spinner to one CSS `steps(36)` transform animation per instance. ```mermaid flowchart LR R[spinner-radar.ts
dots + radarOpacity] -->|bun run generate:spinner| G[script/generate-spinner.ts] G --> C["spinner-frames.css (generated)
--spinner-frames: 162-frame APNG, 15×15
--spinner-grid: rounded-dot SVG
--spinner-still: reduced-motion SVG"] C --> S["<span data-slot=spinner-dots>
mask: grid
::before mask: frames"] R -.->|spinner-radar.test.ts decodes every frame| C ``` ### Changes - **APNG frames** (`script/generate-spinner.ts`, `spinner-frames.css`) - 162 frames at 90 fps (11.1 ms each), looping forever: as smooth as #42952. Browsers stretch frames of 10 ms or less to 100 ms, so 90 fps is the fastest rate that plays as written. - Each dot owns a 3×3 block of texels, so smoothing never blends a neighbour's level into a dot. - Every spinner shows the same image, so all spinners share one loop and stay in phase with no script. `Spinner` no longer calls `syncSpinPhase`; `Loader` and the titlebar still use it. - **Two masks on two boxes** (`spinner.css`) - The grid masks the element and the frames mask its `::before`. - Chromium stops advancing an animated image that is a layer in a `mask-composite: intersect` stack, so the two masks can't share one element. - Reduced motion swaps the `::before` mask to the still pose. - **Drift guard** - `spinner-radar.test.ts` checks that the committed `spinner-frames.css` matches what `generate-spinner.ts` builds now: the frames, grid and still pose. If someone changes the radar and forgets to regenerate, CI fails. - Comments in `spinner-radar.ts` and `spinner.tsx` explain the regeneration step and the history: #42952 → #58010/#58578/#61562 → #65634 → this PR. ```css [data-slot="spinner-dots"] { mask-image: var(--spinner-grid); } [data-slot="spinner-dots"]::before { background-color: currentColor; mask-image: var(--spinner-frames); } ``` ### Spinner | #65634 strip (top) vs APNG (bottom), dark and light, 12–96 px | |---| | ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/26df0fbb-575a-49b1-b1b8-eb7ab40808ab) | ### Benchmarks (Strobe, origin/dev #65634 → this PR) | Case | `main.work` origin/dev | this PR | Change | Verdict | |---|---:|---:|---:|---| | Scroll menu, 20 subagents, quiet (`exp_3c2bd0`, 8 pairs) | 1,111 ms | 548 ms | −51% | less | | Scroll menu with live events (`exp_f9adfe`, 7 pairs) | 1,711 ms | 1,211 ms | −29% [−34 … −22] | stopped, no verdict yet | | One running session at idle (`exp_54fdb1`, 2 pairs) | 272 ms | 15.5 ms | −94% [−95 … −94] | stopped, no verdict yet | - **Style recalculation:** `main.style` 547 → 101 ms (quiet), 670 → 193 ms (live), 117 → 3.7 ms (idle). - **Frame time:** p95 is unchanged at 6.1 ms in all three cases. - **Stopped runs:** two runs stopped before a verdict because other benches had the machine's bench slot. prs.title: fix(app): open ~ file links in the server's home folder
prs.body:
Clicking a file link like `~/Downloads/clip.mp4` in a message showed "File not found", because the app treated `~` as a folder inside the workspace. Agents write home paths like this often, so now `~` expands to the server's home folder, which the app already loads from the server.

```diff
 [clip](~/Downloads/clip.mp4)
-  → <workspace>/~/Downloads/clip.mp4 → "File not found"
+  → /Users/me/Downloads/clip.mp4 → opens in the side panel
```

- `createPathHelpers` (the app's `Files.resolve`) expands `~` and `~/…` using the server's reported home folder. A path under the workspace still comes out relative. `~user/…` is left alone.
- The file link handler treats home paths as absolute, so a `~` link inside a document isn't resolved against that document's folder and skips the workspace search.
- The link-exists check, which used to always say no for `~`, now checks the expanded path. Inline-code paths like `~/notes/a.md` become clickable when the file exists.

Until the server reports its home folder, `~` paths behave as before.

Checks: new cases in `packages/app/src/workspaces/files/path.test.ts` and `packages/gui-plugins/src/file/resolve-link.test.ts`; `bun test src/workspaces/files` (app, 74 pass), `bun test src/file` (gui-plugins, 196 pass), `bun typecheck` in both. I didn't click through it in the running desktop app.

prs.title: fix(tui): complete directory arguments with a forward slash
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #56109

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

`expandDirectory()` appended `path.sep` when it inserted a directory argument, but the values it works from are built with `/`: `directoryAutocompleteResultValue()` joins with `/`, and the `@` branch of the same function already appends `/`.

On Windows that produced `name/\`. The next completion round splits the argument on `/` in `directorySearch()`, so `name/\` resolved to a directory literally named `\`, matched nothing, and the second Tab reported "No matching directories" instead of walking into `name/`.

This appends `/` instead of `path.sep`. The trailing-separator check stays because a bare `~` or `..` comes back from `directoryAutocompleteExactValue()` with no separator, while a listed entry already ends with `/`. Only `/` is appended, so a POSIX directory name that literally contains `\` keeps it.

Typing a Windows backslash path (`/cd c:\code`, #61739) is a different code path, because `directorySearch()` never splits on `\`. Not touched here.

prs.title: fix(app): show focus rings only during keyboard navigation
prs.body:
Focus rings showed at random: around the whole timeline, around the composer after the app moved focus there, and still there after returning to the window. Rings now show only while the keyboard is moving through the app.

### Before and after

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Type, then the app moves focus to the composer | ![Ring around the composer](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2de0ed25-e800-4734-82eb-4f11559e4f6f) | ![No ring](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/eac1cd24-d30f-4ac8-9f78-d522026833b0) |
| Tab into the composer | Ring | ![Ring around the composer](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a60a637d-9c43-4f7a-87ce-848bbfd98835) |

### Why the rings were random

- Chromium matches `:focus-visible` after any key without Ctrl/Alt/Meta, typing included, until a mouse click moves focus to another element. Click in the timeline, press ↓ or PgDn, and the whole timeline rings.
- Focus a script moves inherits that state, so after typing a prompt anything the app focused got a ring.
- The composer ringed on every focus that was not a direct click, and focus rescue forced a ring when the last input was any key, Ctrl and Alt included.

### The rule

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> pointer
  pointer --> moving: Tab, arrow, Home, End
  moving --> keyboard: focus moved to another element
  moving --> pointer: key press ended, focus stayed
  pointer --> keyboard: Enter, Space or arrow on a focused control
  keyboard --> pointer: pointer press
```

- Typing, shortcuts, lone modifiers, Escape, keys in a text field or on a scroll region, leaving and returning to the window, and focus the app moves itself never change the mode.
- Focus the app moves shows a ring only if the mode is already on.
- Enter or Space on a clicked control shows its ring, as Chromium and Fluent do.
- Settings › Appearance › **Always show focus rings** rings every focus, a click included.

### How

- `packages/ui/src/context/keyboard-mode-machine.ts` is the pure transition. `keyboard-mode.tsx` feeds it key, pointer and focus events and marks the focused element, through shadow roots, with `data-focus-visible`.
- Styles read the mark instead of the pseudo-class:

```css
/* before */
[data-component="home-session-row"]:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--v2-border-border-focus); }

/* after */
[data-component="home-session-row"][data-focus-visible] { outline: 2px solid var(--v2-border-border-focus); }
```

- Tailwind's `focus-visible:`, `group-focus-visible:` and `peer-focus-visible:` keep working, redefined in one line:

```css
@custom-variant focus-visible (&[data-focus-visible]);
```

- `base.css` removes the browser's own ring, and `bun run lint` now fails on a raw `:focus-visible` (`script/check-focus-rings.ts`).
- The composer and Home search draw their frame ring from the same mark, so they no longer decide for themselves.

### Why a mark on the element, not a flag on the root

Cost of one mode switch (the first Tab, or the first click after Tab), with the app's stylesheets in the session story:

| Elements on the page | Flag on `<html>` | Mark on the focused element |
|---|---|---|
| 1,300 | 19 ms | 0.1 ms |
| 8,000 | 137 ms | 0.1 ms |
| 25,000 | 419 ms | 0.1 ms |

A root flag re-styles the whole page, because the base ring rule has no class or attribute to narrow it. The mark touches one element, and a mouse-only user never triggers a write.

### Tests

- `focus-ring.spec.ts` gains "shows rings for keyboard navigation and operation only", which fails on the old behaviour.
- "leaves no ring on the review toggle after a pointer click" is removed: a lone Shift can no longer ring anything, which the "a lone Shift" case in `keyboard-mode-machine.test.ts` and the new story test prove.
- Tests that used `locator.focus()` or a lone Shift to stand in for keyboard arrival press Tab first.

### Notes

- No flag: this fixes existing behaviour.
- The ring bookkeeping in `field-focus.tsx`, `overlay-focus.tsx`, `dialog.tsx` and `focus-rescue.tsx` no longer affects what shows. Removing it is a follow-up.
- Screen readers are not detected. "Always show focus rings" is the route for anyone who wants rings on every focus.
