issues.body:
### What happened?

I pasted a 3.3 MB HAR export as a single prompt. It arrives as one markdown paragraph: 33k lines, no blank line anywhere, one 2.2 MB line of inline base64. pi aborted with

```text
FATAL ERROR: Ineffective mark-compacts near heap limit Allocation failed - JavaScript heap out of memory
```

That session has not opened since. Every attempt aborts the same way and prints only the V8 abort trace; nothing lands in `crashes.json`, so `/bug` is not reachable either. `pi --export` on the same file still finishes in well under a second, so the session data itself is intact.

Laying out that one paragraph is superlinear. I rendered prefixes of it through `sessionEntryToContextMessages` -> `UserMessageComponent` -> `Markdown` in a standalone script with `--max-old-space-size=4096`:

| chars | heap |
| --- | --- |
| 1.0M | 32 MB |
| 1.2M | 569 MB |
| 1.4M | 2395 MB |
| 1.6M | OOM |

Same text with one blank line every 2000 lines: 271 MB. Same text without the 2.2 MB line: 28 MB.

Disclosure: the wording above was drafted with an AI. I ran the repro and the measurements myself.

[repro-redacted.v2.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/35259950/repro-redacted.v2.zip)

### Steps to reproduce

1. Unzip the attached `repro-redacted.v2.zip` and open the `repro-redacted.v2.jsonl` inside (3.4 MB). Personal data and URLs were replaced, the base64 payload is `x` of the same length, and the paragraph structure is untouched: 33,013 lines with no blank line, the same 2.2 MB line.
2. `pi -ne --session repro-redacted.v2.jsonl`
3. After about 18 s it aborts at the V8 heap limit for this machine (about 4 GB, Node v26 default). No extensions loaded.

I could not build a smaller input: below about 1.5M characters in one paragraph it renders slowly instead of aborting.


### Expected behavior

Opening a session should never abort. An entry that cannot be rendered should show a placeholder such as "message too large to display", and a single oversized paragraph should be laid out in chunks or capped at some size.

This is not a request for paste folding in core. The point is narrower: the transcript is rendered before any extension can step in, so one huge message takes the whole session with it. A `context_edit` omit does not help, and entries are append-only, so editing the jsonl by hand was the only way back in.



### Version

pi 1.6.0 (npm), Node v26.13.1, Windows 10.0.26300. I only tested this on Windows.

issues.title: Reasoning items are replayed after a mid-session model switch, so GPT-6.2 drops them every turn (prefix_mismatch)

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What happened?

A session that started on a non-Responses model and switched to `codex/gpt-6.2-sol` mid-conversation starts getting `input_transformations` back that remove earlier reasoning items with `reason: "prefix_mismatch"`. The count only grows — 1 → 5 in one session, 1 → 63 in another — and the same item ids are removed again on every subsequent turn. Context compaction does not clear it.

I found this by scanning all 6173 session files on my machine: only two sessions have any `openai_input_transformations` diagnostic. Both were on gpt-6.2-sol, both had started on a different model, and both began reporting 8–10 turns after the switch. Nothing similar on the Anthropic side over the same period.

It doesn't break output (those items are unusable to the new model anyway), but every later request re-sends payload that the upstream is guaranteed to discard, and the per-turn notice is noise on a long session.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start a session on a non-Responses model with some tool calls (mine were on `deepseek-v4.1-flash`).
2. Switch that same session to a GPT-6.2 model (Responses API).
3. Keep working for roughly 10 turns.
4. Read the session JSONL: assistant messages carry `diagnostics[].type = "openai_input_transformations"` with `reason: "prefix_mismatch"`, and the number of removed items grows over turns.

I did not validate under `pi -ne`: these are my normal working sessions with a few extensions loaded, so from the records alone I can't rule extensions out. The code path below looks like core, but that is my reading, not a tested claim.

### Expected behavior

After a model switch, Pi should stop replaying reasoning items that the new upstream can't accept, instead of sending them every turn and having them removed again.

`openai-responses-shared.js:234-236` pushes any stored `thinkingSignature` back into `input` unconditionally, while `:273-274` drops tool-call item ids for cross-model / cross-api history. That id change is itself an edit in front of those reasoning items, which is what `prefix_mismatch` means in the OpenAI docs ("you insert or edit content before the reasoning item"). So Pi rewrites the prefix and then keeps resubmitting the items it invalidated.

Not planning to send a PR — reporting only.

### Version

1.6.0

issues.title: 0.99.x: terminal color query replies leak into the prompt and BEL opens the external editor (mintty on Windows, ConPTY)

labels.name: bug

labels.name: inprogress

issues.body:
### What happened?

On startup pi opens the external editor. The prompt contains `;0;rgb:0000/0000/0000;1;rgb:d4d4/2c2c/3a3a;…`.
The query runs regardless of theme.

**Versions:** 0.99.x are affected. 0.87.1 is fine. Windows Terminal is fine.
**Terminal:** mintty on Windows, native node.exe, `TERM=xterm`, `EDITOR=vim` (I am using GitBash for Windows environment)

## Cause

0.87.1 sent a single `ESC]11;?BEL` query. 0.99.x sends OSC 10, OSC 11, OSC 4 for indices 0–15, and DA1 (`ESC[c`) as the end marker (`TERMINAL_COLOR_QUERY` in `packages/tui/src/tui.ts`). In this terminal:

1. The DA1 reply arrives first, before any color reply. `consumeTerminalColorResponse` then drops the pending query, so later replies are no longer consumed.
2. The OSC replies arrive without their `ESC]4` prefix, in fragments (`;0`, `;rgb:0000/0000/0000`, `BEL`, `;1`, …). The reply regex cannot match them anyway.
3. `StdinBuffer` splits non-escape input into single characters, so they land in the editor as text. Each stray BEL is Ctrl+G and opens the external editor.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run pi under GitBash (Windows).
2. The prompt contains `;0;rgb:0000/0000/0000;1;rgb:d4d4/2c2c/3a3a;…`.
3. External editor opens, containing the prompt.

### Expected behavior

Prompt is empty and external editor is not opened at the startup. Worked in 0.87.1.

0.99.0, 0.99.1, 0.99.2,
1.0.0 (tui-mode regular; see my comment below)

issues.title: zai thinking handler sends disabled for forced-thinking models (glm-5.3/5.3-flash), leaking reasoning into output
issues.body:
## Bug: forced-thinking Z.AI (GLM) models leak reasoning into the answer when thinking is toggled off

### Summary
When the user sets the thinking level to `off` (so `options.reasoningEffort` is `undefined`), the `zai` thinking-format branch in `openai-completions.ts` unconditionally sends `thinking: { type: "disabled" }`. For **forced-thinking** Z.AI models whose `thinkingLevelMap.off === null` (e.g. `glm-5.3` and `glm-5.3-flash`), the API does not honor `disabled` — the model keeps thinking and folds its mandatory reasoning into the `content` field, which pi then renders as the final answer. The reasoning appears in the output instead of being separated into a thinking block.

### Affected models
In the built-in `zai-coding-cn` catalog:
- `glm-5.3` — `thinkingLevelMap.off = null`, `supportsReasoningEffort = true`
- `glm-5.3-flash` — `thinkingLevelMap.off = null`, `supportsReasoningEffort = true`

(These force thinking per the GLM-5.3 docs: `thinking.type` only supports `"enabled"`.)

Models that work fine, e.g. `glm-5.2` (`thinkingLevelMap.off = "none"`, and the API genuinely supports disabling thinking), are unaffected because `disabled` is honored there.

### Root cause
`packages/ai/src/api/openai-completions.ts`, the `zai` branch (around line 857):

```ts
if (compat.thinkingFormat === "zai" && model.reasoning) {
    const zaiParams = params as ...;
    zaiParams.thinking = options?.reasoningEffort ? { type: "enabled", clear_thinking: false } : { type: "disabled" };
    ...
}
```

Unlike the `deepseek` (line 908) and `openrouter` (line 922) branches, the `zai` branch has **no** `model.thinkingLevelMap?.off !== null` guard before sending `disabled`. For forced-thinking models (`off === null`) it should keep thinking enabled.

### Reproduction
1. Select `glm-5.3` or `glm-5.3-flash` (provider `zai-coding-cn`).
2. Toggle the thinking level to `off` (or otherwise leave `reasoningEffort` undefined).
3. Send a prompt that the model reasons about.
4. The streamed response contains no `reasoning_content` field; instead the model's reasoning text is returned inside `content` and shown as the answer.

### Expected
For models that cannot disable thinking, pi should send `thinking: { type: "enabled" }` (so the API returns `reasoning_content`, which pi routes into a hidden thinking block) rather than `disabled`.

### Suggested fix (mirrors deepseek/openrouter)
```ts
if (compat.thinkingFormat === "zai" && model.reasoning) {
    const zaiParams = params as ...;
    const forcedThinking = model.thinkingLevelMap?.off === null;
    zaiParams.thinking = (options?.reasoningEffort || forcedThinking)
        ? { type: "enabled", clear_thinking: false }
        : { type: "disabled" };
    ...
}
```

issues.title: pi-durable: permanently delete a conversation from storage
issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

Add a way to permanently delete a conversation from pi-durable storage, e.g. `harness.deleteConversation(id, ctx)`: it refuses (or aborts first) while a run is active, then removes the conversation's entries, docs, inbox items and scheduler state from the store.

### Why?

We host pi-durable for end users (SQLite storage, one harness per process). When a user deletes a conversation we can drop our own index row and files, but the message history stays in the durable store forever: in 1.2.0 the store is append-only and the only removal I could find is for inbox items (`removeInboxItem`). So "delete" only means "nobody can look it up any more", which is a weaker privacy guarantee than users expect, and the store only ever grows.

Deleting rows from the SQLite file ourselves would depend on the internal schema and break on upgrades.

### How? (optional)

A storage-level `deleteConversation` implemented by each backend, plus a harness method that checks the live run state, evicts the conversation from memory (rooms/subscriptions get a terminal "deleted" signal), and calls it. Tombstoning the id so a later `submit`/`entries` fails with a clear "not found" error would keep callers honest.

issues.title: Single-$ inline math corrupts shell-variable examples in chat rendering — differently in prose vs code blocks; renderLatex not exposed as a setting

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
# Single-`$` inline math corrupts shell-variable examples in chat rendering — differently in prose vs code blocks; `renderLatex` not exposed as a setting

## Environment

- pi 1.6.0 (also verified in 1.5.2), macOS arm64, default markdown settings
- Verified mechanically by capturing the rendered terminal bytes (`rex capture`) and comparing against the stored session JSONL (stored bytes are always clean — this is purely a render-layer issue)
- Affects both user-typed messages and assistant messages. Tool output panels are unaffected (plain text path).

## Summary

The transcript markdown renderer applies single-`$` inline math, and it does so through **two different code paths with different rules**:

1. **Prose (inline text):** pairs like `$foo$` are consumed as math — delimiters vanish, content is re-rendered as Unicode math. Observed: `the $foo$ variable here` renders as `the foo variable here`.
2. **Fenced code blocks:** a *separate* tokenizer pairs `$...$` only when the content "looks math-like" (contains `_`, `=` etc.), ignoring the trailing-whitespace guard that the prose path applies. Observed: `$MY_VAR_1    # x = y $MY_VAR_2 says` renders as backtick-wrapped text with all inner whitespace collapsed:

```text
`MY_VAR_1 # x = y`MY_VAR_2 says
```

The damage persists after the message completes and when scrolling back.

## Controlled experiments (all captured from the rendered screen)

| Channel | Content | Rendered |
|---|---|---|
| prose | `the $foo$ variable here` | `the foo variable here` (delimiters consumed) |
| prose | `the $foo and $bar here` | intact (trailing-space before closer) |
| code fence (any language) | `# valid math shape: $foo$ end` | **intact** |
| code fence (any language) | `# trailing space: $foo and $bar end` | intact |
| code fence (any language) | `# shape C: $MY_VAR_1    # x = y $MY_VAR_2 says` | **mangled** (backticks, collapsed spaces) |

The fence language is irrelevant: the same content mangles identically in `bash`, `sshconfig`, an unknown language, and an untagged fence — so the trigger is the *content*, not the language.

## Tokenizer-rule observations (from user-message tests)

- Left-to-right pairing.
- Prose path: a closing `$` preceded by whitespace does not close; the pairing shifts to the next candidate (e.g. `not$sure$ how$many $signs$you want` renders as `notsure how$many signsyou want`).
- Code path: no such whitespace guard — it pairs across trailing spaces — but requires math-looking content (underscores, equals) to fire at all.

## Source analysis (pi-tui 1.6.0, the version pi 1.6.0 declares as dependency)

`dist/components/markdown.js` defines `tokenizeInlineLatex` with guards that **reject** the code-block mangle shape (trailing whitespace before the closer, SCREAMING_SNAKE identifiers followed by word characters, currency `$5`) — i.e. the shipped pi-tui guards would have prevented the code-panel corruption. The rendered behavior differs, so the code-block path appears to use a different tokenizer than the pi-tui marked extension (the pi binary also bundles a micromark/remark-style parser with an `inlineMath` construct and a boolean math option). Worth checking whether the transcript code-panel/streaming path was supposed to run through pi-tui's `tokenizeInlineLatex` and instead bypasses it.

## Setting request

pi-tui's Markdown component accepts `renderLatex` (`renderLatex !== false` gate in both the inline and block renderer cases), but pi does not expose it:

- `settings.md` documents only `markdown.codeBlockIndent` and `markdown.mermaid`
- Setting `"markdown": { "renderLatex": false }` in `~/.pi/agent/settings.json` is **silently ignored** (verified: `$foo$` still consumed in prose after restart)

Please expose it as `markdown.renderLatex: false` (or equivalent) so users who work with shell examples can turn math rendering off. Coding agents emit `$ENV_VAR` constantly; the current workaround is instructing the agent to keep one `$` per line.

Related: #7264 (LaTeX math rendering feature).

labels.name: possibly-openclaw-clanker
labels.description: User has activity on openclaw/openclaw

issues.body:
## Human explanation
What looks like an upstream? tool call failure when using Codex, leads to a broken session:


Repeatedly entering "continue" won't recover the session - it seems like the latest message corrupted things. 

`Error: No tool call found for function call output with call_id call_KXHLl4OkJLqXnzhwMKjeCdHX.`

## LLM-written analysis
### What I saw
- Session: `<local session log>`
- Tool call for `call_KXHLl4OkJLqXnzhwMKjeCdHX` appears inside an assistant message that ends in `stopReason:"error"` with `errorMessage:"terminated"` (line 193 in the session file).
- Subsequent resume attempts (`continue`, `continue?`) produce OpenAI errors: `No tool call found for function call output with call_id call_KXHLl4OkJLqXnzhwMKjeCdHX` (lines 195, 197, 200).
- The call_id appears only 4 times total (tool call + 3 error messages); no tool_result entry exists in the session log.

### Why it fails
- `convertAssistantMessage()` skips tool calls if `stopReason === "error"` (`packages/ai/src/providers/openai-codex-responses.ts:350`).
- `convertToolResult()` always emits `function_call_output` (`packages/ai/src/providers/openai-codex-responses.ts:365`, `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-codex-responses.ts:377`).
- If a tool result is still emitted (from pending tool execution or replay) but the tool call is omitted from the converted history, the Codex request contains a `function_call_output` without a matching `function_call`. OpenAI rejects this with the error above.

### Expected
- Do not send `function_call_output` unless the corresponding `function_call` is included in the converted request context.

### Repro
1) Resume the session above.
2) Send `continue`.
3) Observe the OpenAI error about missing call_id.

### Notes
- This is an OpenAI validation error triggered by a pi-side message conversion/state mismatch; retries will repeatedly resend the same invalid request.

issues.title: Windows: Git for Windows outside Program Files is never found; bash tool falls through to the System32 WSL launcher

### What happened?

Git for Windows is installed at `G:\Programmi Aggiuntivi\Git`. `getShellConfig()` only probes `%ProgramFiles%` and `%ProgramFiles(x86)%`, then takes the first `bash.exe` from `where`, which is `C:\Windows\System32\bash.exe`. 3. Run pi and enter `!git --version`.

### Expected behavior

pi uses `<root>\bin\bash.exe` from the Git install whose `git.exe` is on PATH, before the generic `bash.exe` PATH lookup.

1.6.0 (same logic on `main`)

Fix ready: after the Program Files probes, take each `git.exe` from `where` (`<root>\cmd`, `\bin`, `\mingw*\bin`) and use `<root>\bin\bash.exe` only if `<root>\usr\bin\bash.exe` also exists. `shellPath`, the Program Files probes and the WSL fallback stay as they are. issues.title: gemini-4-neon stops in mid stream

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
### What happened?

Zooko here - human, no AI-generated content in this post. I observed the new gemini-4-neon model frequently just stops in the middle and doesn't resume. I asked my AI to diagnose it, and it positively identified the cause: OpenRouter normalizes `"MALFORMED_RESPONSE"` into OpenAI's generic `finish_reason: "stop"` while still sending `native_finish_reason: MALFORMED_RESPONSE"`. Pi looks only at `choice.finish_reason` and ignores `choice.native_finish_reason`, so pi treats this as a clean finish, does not retry or anything, and everything halts. My AIs proposed fix is, when `finish_reason` is `"stop"`, then inspect `native_finish_reason`, and if it is one of the list of reasons that OpenRouter is known to collapse to `"stop"`, then treat it as an error.

Say "lgtm" and I'll ask my AIgent to follow up with a link to our patch, or a PR, or whatever your CONTRIBUTING.md tells him to do. :-)

### Steps to reproduce

Okay this part is me cutting and pasting from my AIgent. I'm not gonna manually retype this in just for this submission:

1. Mock or receive an OpenRouter `openai-completions` SSE chunk with `choices: [{ index: 0, delta: {}, finish_reason: "stop", native_finish_reason: "MALFORMED_RESPONSE" }]` (as OpenRouter sends for Google's `MALFORMED_RESPONSE`, e.g. generation `gen-1795329502-PRW2udFdd5eiaknmbgWZ`).
2. Observe `streamOpenAICompletions(...).result()`.
3. `stopReason` is `"stop"` and `errorMessage` is `undefined`, so `AgentSession` ends the turn instead of auto-retrying.

### Expected behavior

Likewise, this is cut-and-pasted from my bot:

In `packages/ai/src/api/openai-completions.ts`: when `choice.finish_reason === "stop"` (or `"end"`) and `choice.native_finish_reason` is a known upstream failure (such as `MALFORMED_RESPONSE` / `MALFORMED_FUNCTION_CALL`, or `UNEXPECTED_TOOL_CALL`, `RECITATION`, `SAFETY`, etc., as in `google-shared.ts`), map it to `stopReason: "error"` with an `errorMessage` (e.g. `Provider native_finish_reason: MALFORMED_RESPONSE`) and preserve `rawStopReason`.

In `packages/ai/src/utils/retry.ts`: include `provider native_finish_reason: malformed_response` (and `malformed_function_call`) in `RETRYABLE_PROVIDER_ERROR_PATTERN`, alongside `provider finish_reason: error` (commit `a00a5048df`), so Pi automatically retries transient malformed-response stops.

I have verified this root cause across all 9 empty OpenRouter stops in our session (9/9 had `native_finish_reason: "MALFORMED_RESPONSE"` from Google, while normal stops have `"STOP"`). Happy to submit the PR with unit tests in `packages/ai/test/` once approved.

### Version

_No response_

issues.title: Truncate oversized/malformed path arguments in built-in file tool errors (read/edit/write)

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### Summary
When a model suffers a decoding glitch and leaks reasoning text into a file tool's `path` argument (while still producing syntactically valid JSON), the built-in `read`, `edit`, and `write` tools in `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` (`1.1.0`) do not bound/validate `path` or truncate it in error messages. As a result, multi-kilobyte malformed paths are echoed verbatim into `toolResult`, polluting the conversation context.

### Current behavior (`@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent@1.1.0`)
- **`read`** (`packages/coding-agent/src/core/tools/read.ts`): `ops.access(absolutePath)` / `ops.readFile(absolutePath)` propagates Node's raw `ENOENT` / `ENAMETOOLONG` error message verbatim, echoing the entire `absolutePath` back into `toolResult`.
- **`edit`** (`packages/coding-agent/src/core/tools/edit.ts`): `catch` interpolates the full raw `${path}` into `Could not edit file: ${path}. ${errorMessage}.`.
- **`write`** (`packages/coding-agent/src/core/tools/write.ts`): runs `mkdir(dir, { recursive: true })` and `writeFile(absolutePath, content)` without validating `path`, which can either create nested directories named after leaked text (when the leaked text contains `/`) or propagate raw `ENAMETOOLONG`/`ENOENT` errors containing the full path.

### Production impact
In a production session using `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent@1.1.0`:
1. An upstream model emitted a syntactically valid `read` tool call whose `path` argument contained ~3.8 KB of leaked reasoning text (including repeated JSON-like closing tokens).
2. `read` failed with `ENOENT` and echoed the entire ~3.9 KB path verbatim into `toolResult`.
3. Leaving thousands of characters of malformed `path` in `toolResult` amplified in-context recurrence across subsequent turns (21 malformed tool calls total, 17 of them on `read`, up to 4.7 KB) and subsequently triggered upstream provider usage-policy refusals on later turns.

### Suggested fix
1. Reject clearly malformed `path` arguments before filesystem operations in `read`, `edit`, and `write` (e.g., containing NUL/control characters or newlines, exceeding a reasonable length bound, or having path segments exceeding `NAME_MAX` / 255 bytes).
2. Truncate `path` when formatting filesystem errors (e.g., show a short prefix + total length) so oversized arguments are never echoed verbatim into `toolResult`.

issues.title: isContextOverflow treats 429/5xx/quota errors as overflow; codemode marks still-running calls as cancelled

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
Two small things we patch locally on 1.6.0 (both patches originally from n8n-io/nod, Apache-2.0); filing them in case you want them upstream.

1. `pi-ai` `dist/utils/overflow.js`: `NON_OVERFLOW_PATTERNS` only excludes "rate limit" / "too many requests" / Bedrock throttling. An error such as `429 Too many tokens, please wait`, `insufficient_quota: token limit exceeded`, `usage_limit_reached ... too many tokens` or a 5xx whose body says "prompt is too long" matches an overflow pattern, so `AgentSession` starts a compaction on a rate or quota limit. We add to `NON_OVERFLOW_PATTERNS`:

```js
/^(?:[\w -]+ API error \((?:401|402|403|404|408|409|410|429|5\d\d)\):|(?:401|402|403|404|408|409|410|429|5\d\d)(?:\s|:|$))/i,
/\(HTTP (?:401|402|403|404|408|409|410|429|5\d\d)\)(?: \(transport cause: [^)]+\))?(?: \[request phase: [^\]]+\])?\s*$/i,
/\b(?:insufficient_quota|quota_exceeded|usage_limit_reached)\b/i,
/\b(?:tokens? per (?:minute|day)|[tr]p[md])\b/i,
```

413 stays an overflow.

2. `pi-coding-agent` `dist/extensions/codemode/execute.js`: when a script fails or ends while tool calls it started are still running, those calls are reported as `cancelled`, but they may have already taken effect (e.g. a sent message). We track pending calls, wait for them within the script's remaining deadline (not after an abort), report a still-running one as `outcome unknown`, and append "Some tool results are still unknown. Check the outside state before repeating an action." so the model does not repeat a write.

Happy to open a PR for either if useful.

issues.title: A prompt accepted during switchSession runs on the disposed session

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
### What happened?

A prompt that arrives while pi is replacing a session is accepted and then runs on the old session after it has been disposed. The window is the time pi spends awaiting `session_shutdown` handlers inside `ctx.switchSession`. In RPC mode the prompt gets `{"disposition":"started"}`.

That run is live. It sends provider requests and executes tools. None of it is rendered or saved, and the prompt never reaches the replacement session.

The only sign is a "This extension ctx is stale" error from any `before_provider_request` handler that reads `ctx`. That is how I noticed it: the errors showed up after an extension command reopened a session with `ctx.switchSession`.

### Steps to reproduce

Two files, no API key needed: https://gist.github.com/nertzy/1728c161ae8dddc3db0b5205d9fe5116

Run `node repro.mjs`. It starts pi with `--no-extensions -e stale-run.ts` in RPC mode against a local fake Anthropic endpoint.

The extension has a 200 ms `session_shutdown` handler, a 500 ms `before_agent_start` handler, and a `/reopen` command that calls `ctx.switchSession`. The host sends one prompt when the shutdown handler starts. The fake endpoint asks for a tool call on every request, so the old session keeps looping until the script kills pi after 3 seconds.

```text
[ext] session_shutdown begin
[host] prompt sent during session_shutdown
[ext] session replaced
[host] prompt response: {"disposition":"started"}
[server] request AFTER the session was replaced
[ext] tool executed
...
provider requests from the replaced session: 11
tool executions from the replaced session:   10
stale-ctx extension errors:                  11
prompt saved in a session file:              false
```

### Expected behavior

The prompt is either rejected or carried into the replacement session.

A disposed session sends no provider requests and runs no tools.

### Version

1.5.2 (the same code is on main at d917b3e)

issues.title: Agent SDK advertises one same-name tool and executes another

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What happened?

The Agent SDK can advertise one definition for a tool name and execute another. With two tools named `shared`, the first request shows the second tool's description, but its call executes the first tool. The next request shows the first description. A model can therefore call the advertised interface and get different behavior.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Instantiate `Agent` with `initialState.tools` set to two tools named `shared`. Give them distinct descriptions and return values.
2. Use a mock `streamFn` to record `getCurrentTools(context.messages)` and return a `shared` call on the first request.
3. Compare the first declaration, the tool result, and the declaration on the next request.

This runs against the SDK directly with no CLI extensions or live provider. Related request-preparation mismatch: #10685.

### Expected behavior

Resolve each tool name consistently before sending the request and use the same selection for the declaration and execution.

I'm willing to implement a fix for this issue.

### Version

`@earendil-works/pi-agent-core` 1.5.1 at `4ea883792`. The same declaration and lookup code is present on main at `9c4652688`.

labels.name: untriaged

issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

Provide a clean way to patch and rerun a syntax-failed inline codemode script without resending the full source.

### Why?

Fixing a one-character syntax error (e.g., a missing `)`) in a long inline codemode script currently requires rewriting the entire script. On scripts hundreds of lines long, this burns thousands of output tokens for a trivial fix.

### How? (optional)

Pi already persists the source of syntax-failed `codemode` calls in `PI_SESSION_FILE` (session JSONL). Even without modifying Pi, the model can technically hack around this today by reading the failed call from `PI_SESSION_FILE` via `tools.bash`, patching it, and running it with `AsyncFunction`.

A cleaner way to submit a small patch against the failed source and execute it as a new call (leaving the original call unchanged) would avoid that workaround.

Would an extension be the preferred place for this?

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): resolve api keys by provider
prs.body:
Hey Mario, I found a bug when switching models mid-flight. I know you have high standards for PRs, so I've tried my best to make it high quality and slop free - please let me know if anything is missing or needs improvement :)

Model used: gpt-5.2-codex-high

## Summary
- resolve API keys using the provider argument to prevent model-switch 401s mid-run
- add regression test for provider-specific key resolution
- update coding-agent changelog

## Why (Human-written, verbatim)
- When switching models from opus 4.5 to codex, I got an error, interrupting first request to the model; I suspected that the access token was not adequately refreshed. It was annoying, so I asked codex to fix it for me :) The aim of this change is to ensure that you can seamlessly switch to/from OpenAI models without getting any errors.

## Proof (LLM-generated)
- The session log shows a `model_change` to `openai-codex/gpt-5.2-codex`, then an Anthropic `401 invalid x-api-key` error on the next assistant message. That’s the failure that triggered this fix.
- Session log: `<local session log>` (lines 694-699)


## Analysis (LLM-generated)
- Turn start snapshots `config.model` (provider stays Anthropic for the in-flight turn).
- `/model` immediately updates `agent.state.model` and writes the `model_change` entry.
- The LLM call resolves the API key via `getApiKey(config.model.provider)`.
- SDK `getApiKey` ignored its provider argument and read `agent.state.model`, so it returned the new provider’s key.
- Result: Anthropic request sent with Codex key → 401. Deterministic mismatch, not token expiry.
- The session log ordering reflects this: `model_change` to Codex, then an Anthropic tool call, then the Anthropic 401.

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): reject input on a session being replaced (#12243)
prs.body:
Fixes #12243

## Problem

A prompt arriving while `session_shutdown` handlers await inside `switchSession` / `newSession` / `fork` is accepted and runs on the outgoing session after it has been disposed. The run is live (provider requests + tool executions), but nothing is rendered or saved, and the prompt never reaches the replacement session. In RPC mode it is acknowledged with `{"disposition":"started"}`.

The window is exactly the `await emitSessionShutdownEvent(...)` in `teardownCurrent`: `AgentSession` had no "disposed/replacing" state, so `prompt()` kept starting runs until the later synchronous `dispose()`.

## Fix

- `AgentSession` gains a `_disposed` flag with `isDisposed` and `beginSessionReplacement()` (flag-only, no teardown).
- `AgentSessionRuntime.teardownCurrent()` and `dispose()` set it **synchronously before the first await**, closing the shutdown-handler window for every replacement path (resume / new / fork / import all route through `teardownCurrent`).
- `prompt()`, `steer()`/`followUp()` (via `_queueUserInput`) reject with a clear error once disposed — RPC mode surfaces this as an error response instead of `started`.
- `_startRun()` re-checks the flag, covering the narrow race where a prompt's preflight awaited across the start of a replacement.

`reload()` is intentionally unaffected: it reuses the same `AgentSession` object, so flagging it would break the reload.

## Tests

Added 3 regression tests in `test/agent-session-concurrent.test.ts`:
- replacement window rejects `prompt`/`steer`/`followUp`, session stays idle
- `dispose()` rejects subsequent prompts
- prompt whose preflight awaits across the start of replacement never reaches `_startRun`

Verification:
- `agent-session*` suite: 12 files, 47 passed (18 pre-existing skips)
- RPC/print suites: 7 passed; extension/interactive: 20 passed
  - `interactive-mode-suspend.test.ts` has 2 failures, confirmed pre-existing on base by stashing this change
- `tsc --noEmit` and Biome pass; full pre-commit check suite passed

## What would you like to be added?

Could the built-in Web Shell served by `qwen serve` support opt-in custom panels? I'd like to keep using the official page and add a view of my own without forking or rebuilding Web Shell, or hosting a separate React app. One supported extension point—for example, a custom tab in the existing right panel—would be enough to start. I use the built-in page as a workspace for a long-running agent. Chat is useful for instructions and discussion, but some information is easier to scan and revisit in a dedicated view: a release dashboard with progress and blockers, a table of task runs, or a view for reviewing saved memories. The embeddable Web Shell already offers React customization points for an app that hosts it. This request is specifically about the standalone page served by `qwen serve`. The built-in auto-memory browser in [#13396](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/issues/13396) and [PR #14230](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/14230) is a related use case, not a replacement for a way to add domain-specific views.

issues.title: proposal(managed-agent): Widen Action parking beyond the first increment (stateless Harness Phase 4 follow-up)

labels.name: type/feature-request
labels.description: New feature or enhancement request

labels.name: category/core
labels.description: Core engine and logic

labels.name: scope/session-management
labels.description: Session state and persistence

issues.body:
Follow-up to #18115, which shipped the first increment of Action parking (stateless Hosted Harness Phase 4, design in #18047). That increment parks only the waits that cold recovery already accepts, so most real Sessions still stay resident while a tool approval or question is pending: Sessions with Hooks or MCP, child Sessions, Turns started by wake inputs (monitor, loop, automation, channel), a wait that coexists with background work, extension command-step approvals, image-only Prompts, and `uncaptured` batches, whose most common source is a `run_shell_command` approval on a Workspace Shell profile.

This issue tracks widening that coverage in stages. The detailed design is in `docs/design/2026-11-22-managed-action-parking-coverage.md` (with a `.zh-CN.md` version), to be submitted as a docs PR.

## Principle

A frozen Turn is identical, to the journal, to a process SIGKILLed at the wait point. **Park coverage therefore never exceeds cold-recovery coverage.** Each stage first makes cold recovery accept the wait shape, then relaxes park eligibility in the same change. As a side effect, each stage also fixes crash recovery for that shape. For example, a monitor-started Turn waiting for an approval is today settled as a crash when its Harness dies, instead of continuing to wait.

No new configuration key is added. Everything stays behind `qwen.managed-agent.action-parking.enabled`, which remains default-off until the parent design's measurement gate (§7) passes. A stage that changes the seal certificate shape adds a writer-grant capability bit, and the Harness sends the new shape only when it sees that bit. A seal refused after the freeze is an irreversible teardown failure, so the safety net must not be "mixed versions are unsupported".

Each stage below lists **checks before starting**. Unless marked confirmed, these are conclusions drawn from reading the code, not yet confirmed by tests. Their outcome can change the stage's scope or approach, so confirm them with a test before implementing the stage.

## Stages

| Stage | Scope | Surface | Depends on | Size |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | Shared eligibility function + refusal reasons | Harness | — | S |
| 1 | Image-only Prompts; extension command-step approvals | Harness | 0 | S |
| 2 | Background work + Action; wake-started Turns | Harness + Store | 0, 3b | M–L |
| 3 | Child Sessions | Harness | 0, relay budget gap closed | M |
| 4 | Hooks; MCP | Harness (G3 producer/recovery) + Broker alignment | 0, Phase 2 MCP parking (for MCP) | L |
| 5 | Shell before dispatch | Harness (G3) + possibly Broker | A separate G3 extension design | L |

The order is a code-level estimate, not a measurement. Before starting Stage 3 or later, use the refusal counts from Stage 0 to see each wait shape's share of real load, and reorder by that share. For example, Stage 5 should move up if Shell-profile deployments dominate.

### Stage 0: one eligibility function for parking and cold recovery

- **What:**
  - Fold the Session-shape terms cold recovery requires before resuming an approval continuation (no Hooks, no MCP, a tool owner) into one function that both `actionParkCandidate` and the cold-recovery entry points (takeover load and resident redrive) call. The journal-state terms (continuation lookup, original Prompt) are already shared helpers. Terms where parking is stricter than recovery (lineage, wake ownership, command step, grant capabilities) stay park-only, each with its own reason; later stages remove them one by one. #18115 already lists this fold as a follow-up.
  - Return a typed refusal reason for every waiting Turn that cannot park. Today `actionParkCandidate` returns `undefined` without a reason, and a wait whose continuation was never captured (Hooks, MCP, Shell profile, unsupported tool, oversize plan) does not register at all, so it is invisible to eligibility.
- **How:**
  - The continuation producer returns its refusal reason instead of `undefined`. Every durable wait registers; one that can never park registers with that reason, and an extension command-step wait registers as `command_step`.
  - Count refusals by reason per suspension attempt in `suspensionStats`, beside the other Phase 1 counters.
  - Every later stage changes only its own term of this function plus its producer or recovery arm.
- **Done when:** Park and recovery behavior is unchanged, all call sites use the shared function, and refusals are counted by reason.
- **Note:** `suspensionStats` is read only in process today, by tests. Exposing it to operators is a separate prerequisite shared by every Phase 1 measurement, and the reordering before Stage 3 and open question 3 depend on it.

### Stage 1: Harness-only relaxations that recovery already supports

- **Image-only Prompts.**
  - Today's gate, `hostedOriginalPromptText`, joins only text parts. The resumed driver, however, already reads the full input, attachments included, from the durable `managed-input` resource through `readHostedInput`.
  - Change: replace the gate with "original input is readable": for a `hosted-harness` source, text or attachments are non-empty; other sources still require text.
  - Checks before starting:
    - Confirmed by a test in #18151: after a text-plus-image Prompt parks, is cold-loaded and is allowed, the history handed to the model on resume still holds the original image, so the text-plus-image Prompts that park today need no tightening.
    - The consumers of the run option `prompt: text` accept an empty string.
- **Extension command-step approvals.**
  - The takeover arm already recovers them (`extensionsCommandStepTakeover`, which allows a Hook catalog). Eligibility simply has not been opened.
  - Change: admit `plan.commandStep` when its `configRevision` equals the current extension configuration revision. The Hooks relaxation applies to command-step plans only.
  - Check before starting:
    - Confirmed by a test in #18151 for Workspace Sessions: the decision-delivery load carries the takeover flags and takes the parked Turn over.
    - A bare load never answers a parked command step (R9-1 guard).
    - An extension configuration change during the park ends in a typed terminal decline, not an endless retry.

### Stage 2: certificate extensions in the control plane

- **Background work + Action.**
  - Today the Store refuses a seal that carries both the 3b background hold and `parkedTurn`.
  - Change: accept both on the seal. When a background terminal reaches the staged-wake path, unpark the Session's `hosted_action_parked` Turn row in the same transaction, so that the coordinator reattaches immediately instead of waiting for `retry_after`. The notification stays pending until the Turn settles, so the Session reloads at most once per background terminal.
  - The park CAS never reads the background field, and neither certificate infers the other.
  - Check before starting: the wake-recovery load is a passive takeover load (`passiveRecovery`), so it enters the approval recovery arm and rebuilds the waiter.
- **Wake-started Turns** (monitor, loop, automation and child-result notifications first; channel and `pr_event` as a later sub-step).
  - These Turns have no coordinator-held `ma_turn` row. Today the pump settles an attempted wake input at `await_action` as a crash.
  - Harness: the pump resumes such an input through the approval-continuation driver. This piece is worth shipping on its own because it fixes crash recovery.
  - Store: `parkedTurn` gains `owner: 'wake'`, backed by a nullable `wake_seal_parked_owner` column. The wake-recovery scan also loads heads whose wake-owned park has reached `wake_seal_parked_until`.
  - Unpark: decision delivery loads the Session as today. Cancellation and approval-mode changes set `wake_seal_parked_until` to now in their own transaction, and the next scan loads the Session.
  - Check before starting:
    - Where the cancel entry point for wake-started Turns is today, and its transaction boundary. This decides whether setting `wake_seal_parked_until` can share the cancel's transaction.
    - The decision-delivery load is a passive takeover load.
    - If the writer that cleared a certificate then crashes, the existing wake recovery of "committed inputs no writer owns" picks the Session up.

### Stage 3: child Sessions

- A child Turn is already a coordinator-dispatched `ma_turn` row, and `ChildResultRelay` treats `RUNNING` as a wait, so the park CAS applies unchanged. Children have no live approval poll, so their certificate carries no approval revision.
- Change: drop the `lineage` term of eligibility.
- Check before starting:
  - The Phase 1 relay attempt-budget gap is closed. Today, session-message delivery, child-result delivery and automation fires may still charge cold-open waits against their attempt budget. If the gap is still open, close it first as part of this stage.
  - The mount handback of a child's single-question batch (`questionChild`) works after cold recovery.
  - `MESSAGE_TURN_WAIT_MS` does not settle anything wrongly during a long park.
- Note: the parent Turn stays resident inside its `agent` call, so this stage frees only the child's resident. Parking a parent that waits on a child is a separate proposal (see "Not in scope").

### Stage 4: Hooks and MCP (G3 evidence extensions)

- **Hooks.**
  - PreToolUse and PermissionRequest outcomes are already durable as `hook_execution` records, with a reader that replays them without rerunning (`orderedHookInput`).
  - Producer: the continuation records the Hook occurrences completed before the wait.
  - Recovery: `resumeSavedNativeBatch` and the takeover arm accept Hooks Sessions. Completed occurrences are read back, never rerun, and an occurrence with a record but no result declines.
  - Takeover: skip `answerResumedTurnCalls` when a recoverable native continuation exists, because it would destroy that continuation.
  - Check before starting: a resumed park does not refire SessionStart or UserPromptSubmit.
- **MCP.**
  - Park only when Phase 2 `qwen.managed-agent.runtime-broker.mcp-parking.enabled` retains connections and the catalog. Otherwise the tool definitions rediscovered after a cold load may differ from the saved ones, and a parked Turn could not resume, which is worse than staying resident.
  - The continuation records the MCP configuration revision and catalog pin.
  - Every earlier MCP call in the batch must have a committed result. A dispatched MCP call is never replayed.

### Stage 5: Shell before dispatch

- This is the highest-value item for Shell profiles, where most approvals are `run_shell_command`. G3 requires its own positive continuation evidence for Shell before dispatch.
- Check before starting: whether Shell execution has native-file-style prepare with `dispatch = false` and exact-key replay. If it does not, the Broker must gain them first, and the stage grows substantially.
- Either way, write a separate G3 extension design before implementing. Shell after dispatch keeps its refusal.

## Not in scope

- **v1/v2 approvals:** not supported. They exist only in waits written before the upgrade and disappear on their own.
- **Plans over 64 KiB:** not supported for now. The Stage 0 refusal counts show how often they occur.
- **Parent-waits-on-child parking:** a different wait with no Action. It is required for zero residency across a child-Session tree and needs its own proposal.
- **Public Workspace Shell profile + MCP Sessions:** Phase 1 never suspends them.
- **Handing back the parked Turn's Runtime membership:** parent design open question 2.

## Acceptance criteria (per stage)

- A wait outside the stage's conditions behaves exactly as before, and existing results are unchanged.
- For the same journal state, park eligibility and cold recovery agree, covering both the opened shape and its excluded neighbors.
- "SIGKILL during the wait → new Harness generation → decide" and "park → cold load → decide" give the same journal outcome. For each of decision, cancellation, mode change (where applicable) and expiry, one cold recovery completes the original Turn with unchanged Action, Prompt and batch identities; Allow executes exactly once and Deny zero times.
- At least one real-process "park → new Harness generation → decide" case on MySQL 8.4 runs in the required CI tier. H2 results do not substitute.
- `action-parking.enabled` is turned on in a deployment only after the parent design's §7 measurements are complete.

## Open questions (none of them blocks development)

Each question is implemented with the default below first and revisited after measurement. None of the later adjustments needs a protocol or schema change.

1. **Latency of cancelling, or changing the approval mode of, a parked wake-started Turn.** These take effect only on the next wake-recovery scan (2s by default).
   - Default: rely on the scan alone. Ordinary parked Turns are already redispatched by the dispatch sweep (1s), and the parent design treats an immediate kick after commit as a latency optimization, not a correctness requirement.
   - Revisit if the measured latency is unacceptable: add a direct load kick after the commit, which is a single extra call.
2. **Minimum park duration for Sessions with frequent background terminals** (Stage 2).
   - Default: none. This is tuning, not correctness, and the feature is default-off.
   - Revisit if measurements show repeated park-and-reload churn: add a Harness eligibility constant. The certificate and the control plane are unaffected.
3. **Share of Shell before dispatch and of plans over 64 KiB in real load.**
   - Affects only whether Stage 5 and oversize plans are worth doing, and when. Stages 0–4 are unaffected.
   - Answered by the Stage 0 refusal counts once `suspensionStats` is exposed to operators.

Related: #17527 (stateless Hosted Harness design), #18047 (Action parking design), #18115 (first increment), #17953 (Phase 3b), #17749 (Phase 2 MCP parking).

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

#18115 已交付审批停靠（无状态 Hosted Harness 第四阶段，设计见 #18047）的首个增量。它只停靠冷恢复今天已经接受的等待，所以在工具审批或提问等待期间，大部分真实 Session 仍然常驻。仍常驻的情况包括：带 Hooks 或 MCP 的 Session、子 Session、由 wake 输入（monitor、loop、automation、channel）启动的 Turn、与后台任务同时存在的等待、extension command-step 审批、纯图片 Prompt，以及 `uncaptured` 批次。`uncaptured` 最常见的来源是 Workspace Shell profile 下的 `run_shell_command` 审批。

本 issue 跟踪分阶段扩大停靠覆盖面。详细设计见 `docs/design/2026-11-22-managed-action-parking-coverage.zh-CN.md`（另有英文版），将以文档 PR 提交。

## 原则

冻结后的 Turn 对 journal 来说，等同于进程在等待点被 SIGKILL。**因此停靠覆盖面永远不超过冷恢复覆盖面。** 每个阶段先让冷恢复接受这种等待形态，再在同一改动里放宽停靠资格。附带的好处是同类等待的崩溃恢复也一起修好了。例如今天一个等审批的 monitor Turn 遇到 Harness 崩溃，会被按崩溃结算，而不是继续等待。

不新增配置项。所有改动都在 `qwen.managed-agent.action-parking.enabled` 之后，这个开关在父设计 §7 的测量门槛通过前保持默认关闭。改变 seal 证书形态的阶段增加一个 writer grant 能力位，Harness 只在看到该位时才发送新形态。冻结之后 seal 被拒是不可逆的 teardown 失败，所以不能拿"不支持混跑"兜底。

下面每个阶段都列有**开工前检查**。除标明已确认的以外，这些检查项是读代码得出的结论，还没有被测试证实。它们的结果可能改变该阶段的范围或做法，所以实现该阶段之前要先用测试确认。

## 阶段

| 阶段 | 范围 | 改动面 | 依赖 | 规模 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | 共享资格函数 + 拒绝原因 | Harness | — | 小 |
| 1 | 纯图片 Prompt；extension command-step 审批 | Harness | 0 | 小 |
| 2 | 后台任务 + 审批；wake 启动的 Turn | Harness + Store | 0、3b | 中到大 |
| 3 | 子 Session | Harness | 0、relay 预算缺口已关闭 | 中 |
| 4 | Hooks；MCP | Harness（G3 生产者/恢复）+ Broker 对齐 | 0、第二阶段 MCP parking（MCP 需要） | 大 |
| 5 | 派发前的 Shell | Harness（G3）+ 可能的 Broker | 单独的 G3 扩展设计 | 大 |

上面的顺序是代码级估算，不是测量结果。开始第 3 阶段及之后的工作之前，用阶段 0 的拒绝计数查看各类等待在真实负载中的占比，按占比调整顺序。例如 Shell profile 的部署若占多数，第 5 阶段应提前。

### 阶段 0：停靠与冷恢复共用一个资格函数

- **做什么：**
  - 把冷恢复在恢复审批 continuation 之前要求的 Session 形态条件（无 Hooks、无 MCP、有工具 owner）合成一个函数，供 `actionParkCandidate` 和冷恢复入口（接管加载与常驻 redrive）共同调用。journal 状态条件（continuation 查找、原始 Prompt）本来就是共享的辅助函数。停靠比恢复更严的条件（lineage、wake 所有权、command-step、grant 能力位）保留为停靠专属条件，各自带一个原因，由后续阶段逐项删除。#18115 已把这次合并列为后续工作。
  - 对每个不能停靠的等待中 Turn 返回带类型的拒绝原因。现在 `actionParkCandidate` 拒绝时只返回 `undefined`，不说明原因；而且 continuation 没被捕获的等待（Hooks、MCP、Shell profile、不支持的工具、超大计划）根本不会登记，资格判断看不到它们。
- **怎么做：**
  - continuation 生产者返回拒绝原因而不是 `undefined`。每个持久化等待都登记；永远不能停靠的等待带着这个原因登记，extension command-step 等待以 `command_step` 登记。
  - 在 `suspensionStats` 中、与第一阶段其他计数并列，按每次挂起尝试统计各原因的拒绝次数。
  - 之后每个阶段只改这个函数里属于自己的一项，再加上对应的生产者或恢复臂。
- **完成标准：** 停靠与恢复行为不变，所有调用点都使用共享函数，拒绝次数按原因计数。
- **说明：** `suspensionStats` 目前只在进程内由测试读取。把它暴露给运维是第一阶段所有测量共有的前置工作；第 3 阶段之前的顺序调整和开放问题 3 都依赖它。

### 阶段 1：冷恢复已支持、只需改 Harness 的放宽

- **纯图片 Prompt。**
  - 现在的闸门 `hostedOriginalPromptText` 只拼接文本 part。但恢复后的 driver 本来就会通过 `readHostedInput` 从持久化 `managed-input` 资源读回完整输入，包括附件。
  - 改动：把闸门换成"原始输入可读"：`hosted-harness` 来源的输入，文本或附件非空即可；其他来源仍要求有文本。
  - 开工前检查：
    - 已由 #18151 中的测试确认："文字 + 图片"Prompt 停靠、冷加载、Allow 之后，恢复时交给 model 的历史里仍有原图，所以今天已允许停靠的"文字 + 图片"Prompt 不需要收紧。
    - 运行选项 `prompt: text` 的消费方接受空字符串。
- **extension command-step 审批。**
  - 接管臂已经能恢复它们（`extensionsCommandStepTakeover`，允许带 Hook catalog），只是停靠资格还没放开。
  - 改动：当 `plan.commandStep` 的 `configRevision` 等于当前 extension 配置修订时放开。Hooks 的放宽只适用于 command-step 计划。
  - 开工前检查：
    - 已由 #18151 中的测试确认（Workspace Session）：决定投递时的加载带接管标志，并会接管停靠的 Turn。
    - 裸加载绝不回答停靠中的 command-step（R9-1 守卫）。
    - 停靠期间 extension 配置被修改时，结果是带类型的终态拒绝，而不是无限重试。

### 阶段 2：控制面的证书扩展

- **后台任务 + 审批。**
  - 现在 Store 会拒绝同时携带 3b background hold 和 `parkedTurn` 的 seal。
  - 改动：seal 接受两者同时存在。后台终态进入 staged-wake 路径时，在同一事务里解除该 Session 中 `hosted_action_parked` 的 Turn 行，让协调器立即重新接回，而不是等到 `retry_after`。通知在 Turn 结算前保持挂起，所以每个后台终态最多导致一次重载。
  - 停靠 CAS 不读取 background 字段，两份证书互不推断。
  - 开工前检查：wake 恢复加载是被动接管加载（`passiveRecovery`），因此会进入审批恢复臂并重建等待者。
- **wake 启动的 Turn**（先做 monitor、loop、automation 和子结果通知；channel 与 `pr_event` 作为后续小步）。
  - 这类 Turn 没有协调器持有的 `ma_turn` 行。现在 wake 泵遇到停在 `await_action` 的已尝试 wake 输入，会按崩溃结算。
  - Harness：wake 泵改为通过审批 continuation driver 恢复这类输入。这一部分单独上线也有价值，因为它修好了崩溃恢复。
  - Store：`parkedTurn` 增加 `owner: 'wake'`，对应新增可空列 `wake_seal_parked_owner`。wake 恢复扫描额外加载 wake 所有、且已到 `wake_seal_parked_until` 的 head。
  - 解除停靠：决定投递照常加载 Session。取消和审批模式变更在各自的事务里把 `wake_seal_parked_until` 设为当前时间，由下一次扫描加载 Session。
  - 开工前检查：
    - wake 启动的 Turn 现在的取消入口在哪、事务边界是什么。这决定设置 `wake_seal_parked_until` 能否和取消放在同一个事务里。
    - 决定投递时的加载是被动接管加载。
    - 如果清除证书的 writer 随后崩溃，既有的"无 writer 持有的已提交输入"wake 恢复能接住该 Session。

### 阶段 3：子 Session

- 子 Session 的 Turn 本来就是协调器分派的 `ma_turn` 行，`ChildResultRelay` 把 `RUNNING` 当作等待，所以停靠 CAS 无需改动。子 Session 没有 live 审批轮询，证书里不带审批修订号。
- 改动：从资格条件里去掉 `lineage` 这一项。
- 开工前检查：
  - 第一阶段遗留的 relay 尝试预算缺口已关闭。目前 session-message 投递、子结果投递和 automation fire 可能仍会把冷启动等待计入尝试预算。如果缺口仍在，先在本阶段内把它关闭。
  - 子 Session 单问题批次的挂载交还（`questionChild`）在冷恢复后工作正常。
  - 长时间停靠期间，`MESSAGE_TURN_WAIT_MS` 不会错误地结算任何东西。
- 说明：父 Turn 仍停在 `agent` 调用里常驻，所以这一阶段只释放子 Session 的常驻进程。"父等子"的停靠另行提案（见"范围外"）。

### 阶段 4：Hooks 与 MCP（扩展 G3 证据）

- **Hooks。**
  - PreToolUse 和 PermissionRequest 的结果已经以 `hook_execution` 记录持久化，并且有不重跑、直接重放这些记录的读取方（`orderedHookInput`）。
  - 生产者：continuation 记录等待之前已完成的 Hook 发生。
  - 恢复：`resumeSavedNativeBatch` 和接管臂接受带 Hooks 的 Session。已完成的发生只读回、不重跑；有记录但没有结果的发生则拒绝恢复。
  - 接管：存在可恢复的原生 continuation 时跳过 `answerResumedTurnCalls`，否则它会破坏这个 continuation。
  - 开工前检查：恢复停靠的 Turn 时不会重新触发 SessionStart 或 UserPromptSubmit。
- **MCP。**
  - 只有第二阶段的 `qwen.managed-agent.runtime-broker.mcp-parking.enabled` 保留了连接和目录时才停靠。否则冷加载后重新发现的工具定义可能与保存的不同，停靠的 Turn 无法恢复，比保持常驻更糟。
  - continuation 记录 MCP 配置修订和目录 pin。
  - 批次中排在前面的 MCP 调用都必须已提交结果。已派发的 MCP 调用绝不重放。

### 阶段 5：派发前的 Shell

- 对 Shell profile 来说这是价值最高的一项，那里的审批大多是 `run_shell_command`。G3 要求派发前的 Shell 有自己的正面 continuation 证据。
- 开工前检查：Shell 执行是否像原生文件那样，支持 `dispatch = false` 的 prepare 和按精确 key 重放。如果不支持，需要先补 Broker，这一阶段的工作量会明显变大。
- 无论结果如何，实现前都要单独写一份 G3 扩展设计。已派发的 Shell 维持拒绝。

## 范围外

- **v1/v2 审批：** 不支持。它们只存在于升级前写入的等待里，会自然消失。
- **超过 64 KiB 的计划：** 暂不支持。阶段 0 的拒绝计数会显示它们出现的频率。
- **"父等子"停靠：** 这是另一种等待，没有 Action。它是子 Session 树实现零常驻的必要条件，需要单独提案。
- **公开 Workspace Shell profile + MCP 的 Session：** 第一阶段从不挂起它们。
- **停靠期间交还 Turn 的 Runtime 成员资格：** 见父设计开放问题 2。

## 验收标准（每个阶段）

- 不符合该阶段条件的等待，行为与之前完全一致，既有测试结果不变。
- 对同一 journal 状态，停靠资格与冷恢复的判断一致；测试要覆盖新放开的形态和仍被排除的相邻形态。
- "等待中 SIGKILL → 新一代 Harness → 决定"与"停靠 → 冷加载 → 决定"的 journal 结果一致。对决定、取消、模式变更（如适用）、到期这四种情况，各自通过一次冷恢复完成原 Turn，Action、Prompt、批次身份都不变；Allow 恰好执行一次，Deny 零次。
- 必跑 CI 层级里至少有一个基于 MySQL 8.4 的真实进程用例："停靠 → 新一代 Harness → 决定"。H2 结果不能替代。
- 父设计 §7 的测量完成后，才能在部署中打开 `action-parking.enabled`。

## 开放问题（都不阻塞开发）

每个问题都先按下面的默认做法实现，测量后再回头调整。之后的调整都不需要改协议或数据库结构。

1. **停靠中的 wake 启动 Turn，取消或改审批模式的延迟。** 这两类操作要等下一次 wake 恢复扫描（默认 2s）才生效。
   - 默认：只靠扫描。普通的停靠 Turn 本来就靠分派扫描（1s）重新分派，父设计也把"提交后立即触发一次加载"当作降低延迟的优化，而不是正确性要求。
   - 如果测得的延迟不可接受：在提交后直接触发一次加载，只是多一次调用。
2. **后台终态频繁的 Session 是否需要最短停靠时长**（阶段 2）。
   - 默认：不设。这只关系到调优，不关系到正确性，而且功能默认关闭。
   - 如果测量显示反复停靠、重载：在 Harness 资格判断里加一个常量。证书和控制面都不受影响。
3. **派发前的 Shell 和超过 64 KiB 的计划在真实负载中的占比。**
   - 只影响第 5 阶段和超大计划值不值得做、什么时候做。第 0 到 4 阶段不受影响。
   - 在 `suspensionStats` 暴露给运维之后，由阶段 0 的拒绝计数回答。

相关：#17527（无状态 Hosted Harness 设计）、#18047（审批停靠设计）、#18115（首个增量）、#17953（第三阶段 3b）、#17749（第二阶段 MCP parking）。

</details>

issues.title: cli: pasting a search term (Ctrl+V) in /resume and /settings search boxes is silently ignored
issues.body:
### What happened?

When filtering sessions in `/resume` (after pressing `/` to focus the search input) or filtering settings in `/settings` (after pressing `↑` to focus the `Search settings…` box), pasting a single-line keyword via terminal paste (for example `登录` or `语言`) does nothing: the search box stays empty and the list is not filtered. Typing the exact same characters directly filters both dialogs as expected.

### What did you expect to happen?

- When the `/resume` or `/settings` search box is focused, pasting a single-line search term should insert the sanitized text into the search box and filter the list.
- Multi-line pastes should continue to be rejected so large multi-line clipboard contents do not accidentally turn into a search query.
- Pasting while focus is still on the session list or settings list (list mode) should continue to be ignored rather than implicitly switching into search mode.

### Client information

- OS: Windows 11 (win32)
- Qwen Code version: 0.28.3 (`main` at `18ac669a3a`)
- Node.js: v24.20.0

### Anything else we need to know?

The shared search-input printable-character check currently rejects all paste events unconditionally (to prevent multi-line pastes from silently seeding a query), and neither the `/resume` search handler nor the `/settings` focused search-box branch has a single-line paste handler.

prs.title: fix(core): correct usage token accounting across the dashboard and /stats
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Token usage in the daemon status dashboard and in the cross-session statistics view now comes from the per-request usage ledger, placed on the local day each response actually happened, instead of from session summaries that carry a resumed conversation's replayed history and attribute all of it to the day the session last ran. For a model/session covered by ledger evidence, its record entry is replaced instead of added again; legacy inputs without session metadata retain the bounded day/model fallback, not a universal event join. Independent models and sessions, and records without ledger overlap, keep session-based attribution. A missing `runScoped` flag or an id absent from known ledger roots does not prove a replay copy: provenance-ambiguous legacy records are preserved rather than deleting potentially independent spending. Undercounting an unseparable part of a mixed-coverage model is an explicit tradeoff. Reasoning tokens are counted once in the output breakdown, so input plus output equals the reported total. What a run persists is now only what that run itself spent, including when an interactive session resumes another conversation, and the read side keeps every run instead of collapsing them to the last one. Session counts, duration, tool calls, changed lines, skills and the per-project breakdown still come from session records over the same whole-day window, which the ledger deliberately does not carry.

## Why it's needed

On one real heavy history the dashboard reported roughly twice the tokens actually consumed for the current day, five times for seven days and seven times for thirty days; the cross-session view was 2.06x over seven days and 6.25x over thirty days, with average latency inflated too because the request denominator was inflated. Two causes dominated. A resume replays the stored conversation's telemetry into the live metrics, and those cumulative counters were then persisted as if the current run had spent them — a seven-minute resume of a long conversation was billed 45.7M tokens across 506 requests, and every further resume appended another full copy. And every token was attributed to the day the session ended, so a session that ran across three days landed entirely on one day: one session contributed 335M tokens to "today" while only 1.07M of them were actually spent that day. Separately, the output tile added reasoning tokens that chat-completions providers already include in their output count, so the breakdown did not sum to the hero total.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Open the daemon status Usage tab and toggle Today / 7D / 30D. The token totals, request count, input, cached and reasoning counters should equal an independent scan of the per-request ledger for the same window, and input plus output should equal the hero total. Each covered day's heatmap cell should equal that day's ledger tokens. Then open the cross-session statistics view, move to the Activity and Efficiency tabs, and cycle the range with `r`: the token total, session-independent counters, cache hit rate, average latency and per-model request counts should match the same ledger scan, and the period-over-period delta should compare only completed local days on both ledger-backed sides: the displayed window may include a partial today, but the comparison excludes that partial day on both sides rather than scaling or comparing it with full days. A single partial Today view shows no delta. To check the persist side, resume a long conversation and quit without sending anything: no usage record should be written. Run two turns of the same conversation in separate processes: both runs should survive a subsequent read, each carrying only its own spend. Note that the ledger lives under the runtime base directory, so when comparing against a frozen copy both the home and the runtime directory must be pinned, otherwise the UI reads the live, still-growing ledger.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Measured against an independent ledger scan on the same history. The "before" arm is the base revision's source driven directly; the "after" arm is this branch.

| Surface / window | Before | After | Ledger truth |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Cross-session stats, 7 days | 23,344,200,119 | 11,335,405,437 | 11,335,405,437 |
| Cross-session stats, 30 days | 253,761,756,717 | 40,624,370,019 | 40,624,370,019 |
| Dashboard output tile, today | 7,208,898 | 4,952,378 | 4,952,378 |
| Persisted record for a 400-response resume plus one live request | 401 requests / 400,000,005 input | 1 request / 5 input | 1 request / 5 input |
| Read side, two real runs of one conversation | 1 record / 30,778 tokens | 2 records / 72,818 tokens | 2 records / 72,818 tokens |

On a frozen copy of the ledger, all three dashboard windows matched the oracle exactly (`ALL_RANGES_EXACT=true`, zero day mismatches), as did the cross-session view's tokens, requests, average latency and cache hit rate.

Rendered in a real terminal from this branch's bundle (PTY capture, cross-session tabs): Activity for 7 days showed `Tokens 11492.1m` and `Sessions 28` against an oracle of 11,492,141,679; Activity for 30 days showed `Tokens 40781.1m` and `Sessions 389` against 40,781,106,261 / 389; Efficiency for today showed `Cache Hit Rate 97.2%`, `Avg Latency 5.7s` and per-model requests 943 + 108 + 21 = 1072 against 97.2% / 5,698 ms / 1,072. Two real headless runs of one conversation, the second resuming it, produced records of 3 requests / 42,040 tokens and 2 requests / 30,778 tokens — the second did not re-bill the first.

A real Chromium session against this branch's daemon now covers the previously open browser gap. With two ledger rows and deliberately matching session records, Today rendered hero `1,100`, input `1,000`, output `100` and cache `60%`; 7D rendered `3,300`, `3,000`, `300` and `60%`, with the daily-session series labelled `runs ended per day`. The route independently returned the same numbers, and the browser emitted no page errors. A separate real PTY lifecycle used only a local mock model: one 5,000-token request in A, resume B with 10,000 stored tokens, one 7-token request in B, then `/exit`. The final file contains exactly two run-scoped records, A=5,000 and B=7. The stored 10,000 never entered either record, and exit code was 0.

Every new guard is mutation-witnessed: reverting it turns the corresponding test red, and the existing history reduces byte-identically to before (2,065 raw records, both arms returning 2,043 records / 379,387,040,763 tokens with identical per-session keys).

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### Environment (optional)

Local build and bundle, real Chromium and PTY capture, real headless and interactive CLI lifecycles against isolated temporary homes. Final focused suites: core 1168 passed, cli 165 passed, Web Shell 13 passed. The complete llm suite has 129 passes and three relaunch-provenance failures that reproduce identically on the base commit; its two exit-usage cases pass. Build, typecheck, lint and format gates are clean.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: summary windows now select whole local days, because day buckets cannot be split by hour, so the boundary day is counted in full instead of only the hours after a rolling cut-off; on the fallback path this is measurable and confined to that one day. The per-project token column stays record-derived — the ledger has no project dimension — so it now visibly disagrees with the corrected totals above it. A conversation that spans the upgrade keeps only its run deltas, so pre-upgrade activity for that id can be undercounted; undercounting an ambiguous overlap was chosen over double counting.
- Freshness and performance: `/stats` reuses aggregate tables only for completed local months and always re-reads the current and future month files, so every append is visible on the next open while completed months are parsed once. Concurrent opens also share pending reads. When a provider omits a total, it is synthesized according to the auth-aware reasoning/output convention rather than unconditionally adding thoughts. The period comparison uses only the completed local-day prefix, with the same number of disjoint complete days before it, so a partial today and DST-hour transitions cannot manufacture a change. Daemon requests retain their intentional 60-second source cache.
- Ledger scope on purpose: this daily/monthly source contains user-turn responses, not persistent telemetry for the internal `prompt_suggestion`, `forked_query`, `speculation` and `side-query:*` helpers. Those calls remain in live/session metrics, so the ledger is deliberately not an exhaustive bill for every internal compaction, memory or routing call.
- Not validated / out of scope: Windows and Linux. The session-count and per-project tiles remain incomplete for sessions that never persist a usage record — on the reference history the ledger knows 633 sessions in seven days while the record file knows far fewer — which needs a ledger-backed session census and persisting usage at session end, both left as follow-up.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. One optional record field marks run-scoped writes; every reader that filters on the record version keeps working, existing history is neither rewritten nor migrated, and the dashboard payload shape is unchanged.

Design document: [English](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/fix/usage-dashboard-accounting/docs/design/2026-11-19-usage-dashboard-accounting.md) · [简体中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/fix/usage-dashboard-accounting/docs/design/2026-11-19-usage-dashboard-accounting.zh-CN.md). Both versions are complete and synchronized, and they record two first-pass findings that did not survive an independent check: a claimed session-identity divergence that the ledger disproved, and a proposed "sum the segments" dedup change that would have been a 3.1x regression on existing records.

## Linked Issues

No issue to close. Builds on the per-request ledger introduced for #4479 and on the session-swap telemetry transaction from #9833.

## 这个 PR 做了什么

Daemon 状态用量面板与跨会话统计视图的 token 用量，现在取自逐请求用量台账，并落在每次响应**实际发生**的本地日上，而不再取自会话摘要——后者携带被恢复会话重放的历史，并把全部用量归到会话最后活动的那一天。被台账证据覆盖的模型 / session 条目会被替换，而不是再次相加；缺乏 session 元数据的旧输入则保留有界的 day/model 回退，不宣称全局逐事件连接。独立模型和 session，以及没有台账重叠的记录，沿用会话原有归属。缺少 `runScoped` 标记、或某个 id 未出现在已知台账根中，都不能单独证明它是重放副本：无法分辨重放还是独立消费的旧记录会保留，而不是因日期与模型相同就删除潜在的真实消费。混合覆盖模型中无法安全拆分的部分仍按保守少算处理。输出明细中的推理 token 只计一次，因此输入加输出等于上报总量。一次运行落盘的用量现在只包含它自己花掉的部分，包括交互模式下 resume 到另一个会话的情形；读侧也会保留每一次运行，而不是收敛到最后一次。会话数、时长、工具调用、变更行数、技能以及按项目的明细仍取自同一个完整日窗口的会话记录——台账有意不携带这些。

## 为什么需要

在一份真实的重量级历史上，面板对当日报告了约两倍的实际消耗、7 天约五倍、30 天约七倍；跨会话视图 7 天为 2.06 倍、30 天为 6.25 倍，平均延迟也虚高，因为请求数这个分母被灌大了。主因有两个。其一，resume 会把已存会话的 telemetry 重放进实时指标，而这些累计计数随后被当作本次运行的消耗落盘——一次对长会话的七分钟 resume 被记为 506 个请求、45.7M token，且此后每次 resume 都再追加一份完整副本。其二，所有 token 都按会话结束日归属，于是跨三天运行的会话整体落在一天上：某会话向「今日」贡献了 335M token，而当天实际只花掉 1.07M。另外，输出 tile 还叠加了 chat-completions 类 provider 本已计入 output 的推理 token，导致明细之和不等于 hero 总量。

## 评审测试计划

### 如何验证

打开 Daemon 状态的用量页，切换 Today / 7D / 30D。token 总量、请求数、输入、缓存与推理计数应等于对同一窗口的逐请求台账所做的独立扫描，且输入加输出应等于 hero 总量；每个被覆盖天的热力图格应等于该天的台账 token。然后打开跨会话统计视图，切到 Activity 与 Efficiency 页，用 `r` 循环区间：token 总量、与会话无关的各计数、缓存命中率、平均延迟以及逐模型请求数都应与同一次台账扫描一致，且环比两侧都只比较已完成的本地日：展示窗口可以包含未过完的今天，但比较会排除那一部分，不与完整日比较，也不按比例估算。只有不到一天的 Today 视图不显示环比。验证持久化侧：恢复一个长会话后不发送任何内容直接退出，应当不写入用量记录；在两个进程中各跑同一会话的一轮，后续读取应保留两次运行，且各自只带自己的消耗。注意台账位于运行时基目录下，因此与冻结副本对照时必须同时钉住 home 与运行时目录，否则界面读到的是仍在增长的真实台账。

### 证据（修前与修后）

以同一份历史上的独立台账扫描为准。「修前」臂直接驱动基线版本的源码，「修后」臂为本分支。

| 表面 / 窗口 | 修前 | 修后 | 台账真值 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 跨会话统计，7 天 | 23,344,200,119 | 11,335,405,437 | 11,335,405,437 |
| 跨会话统计，30 天 | 253,761,756,717 | 40,624,370,019 | 40,624,370,019 |
| 面板输出 tile，今日 | 7,208,898 | 4,952,378 | 4,952,378 |
| 400 条历史响应的 resume 加一次真实请求的落盘记录 | 401 请求 / 400,000,005 输入 | 1 请求 / 5 输入 | 1 请求 / 5 输入 |
| 读侧，同一会话的两次真实运行 | 1 条 / 30,778 token | 2 条 / 72,818 token | 2 条 / 72,818 token |

在台账的冻结副本上，面板三个窗口全部与 oracle 精确一致（`ALL_RANGES_EXACT=true`，0 个日不符），跨会话视图的 token、请求、平均延迟与缓存命中率同样精确一致。

用本分支 bundle 在真实终端中渲染（PTY 抓屏，跨会话页）：Activity 的 7 天显示 `Tokens 11492.1m`、`Sessions 28`，oracle 为 11,492,141,679；Activity 的 30 天显示 `Tokens 40781.1m`、`Sessions 389`，oracle 为 40,781,106,261 / 389；Efficiency 的今日显示 `Cache Hit Rate 97.2%`、`Avg Latency 5.7s`，逐模型请求 943 + 108 + 21 = 1072，oracle 为 97.2% / 5,698 ms / 1,072。两次真实 headless 运行同一会话（第二次恢复它）分别产出 3 请求 / 42,040 token 与 2 请求 / 30,778 token——第二次没有把第一次再计一遍。

真实 Chromium 连接本分支 daemon，已补上了此前唯一缺失的浏览器验证。两条台账记录配两条等值会话记录时，Today 显示 hero `1,100`、input `1,000`、output `100`、cache `60%`；7D 显示 `3,300`、`3,000`、`300`、`60%`，按日会话序列明确标为 `runs ended per day`。独立 HTTP 读取返回同样数字，浏览器无 page error。另一组真实 PTY 生命周期全程只访问本地 mock 模型：A 发一次 5,000-token 请求，resume 带有 10,000 存量 token 的 B，再发一次 7-token 请求，最后 `/exit`。最终文件恰好有两条 run-scoped 记录：A=5,000、B=7；存量 10,000 没有混入任一记录，退出码为 0。

每个新增守卫都做了变异见证：还原它会让对应用例转红；而存量历史的归约结果与之前逐字节一致（2,065 条原始记录，两臂都返回 2,043 条 / 379,387,040,763 token，逐会话键相同）。

### 测试平台

|     OS     | 状态 |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |  ✅  |
| 🪟 Windows |  ⚠️  |
|  🐧 Linux  |  ⚠️  |

### 环境（可选）

本地 build 与 bundle、真实 Chromium 与 PTY 抓屏、隔离临时 home 上的真实 headless 及交互式 CLI 生命周期。最终触及套件：core 1168 passed、cli 165 passed、Web Shell 13 passed。完整 llm 套件 129 passed，另有 3 条在 base 上同样失败的 relaunch provenance 用例；退出用量两条用例通过。build、typecheck、lint、format 门禁全部干净。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：汇总窗口现在取整个本地日，因为日桶无法按小时切分，因此边界日被完整计入，而不是只计滚动截点之后的那几个小时；在回退路径上该影响可测量且只限那一天。按项目的 token 列仍是记录口径——台账没有项目维度——因此它现在与其上方已修正的总量存在可见的不一致。跨越升级时点的会话只保留运行增量，因此该 id 在升级前的活动可能被少算；对有歧义的重叠，选择少算而非重复计算。
- 新鲜度与性能：`/stats` 只复用已结束本地月份的聚合表；当前月及未来月份始终重新读取，因此每次追加都会在下一次打开时可见，而已结束月份只需解析一次。并发打开也共享未完成读取。如果 provider 未报 total，则按其 auth-aware 的 output 是否含推理进行合成，不无条件叠加 thoughts。环比只比较已完成本地日的前段及其之前等长、互不相交的完整日，因此未过完的今天和 DST 跨时制不会制造虚假变化。daemon 请求仍保留有意的 60 秒数据源缓存。
- 台账的范围是有意选择：其按日/按月内容只含用户回合回复，不持久化 `prompt_suggestion`、`forked_query`、`speculation` 与 `side-query:*` 内部 helper 的 telemetry。这些调用仍留在 live/session 指标中，因此台账刻意不是涵盖每次内部压缩、记忆或路由调用的完整账单。
- 未验证 / 范围外：Windows 与 Linux。对于从未持久化用量记录的会话，会话数与按项目 tile 仍不完整——参考历史上台账知道 7 天内有 633 个会话，而记录文件知道的远少于此——这需要台账口径的会话普查以及在会话结束时落盘用量，两者都留作后续。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：无。新增一个可选记录字段标记按运行写入；所有按记录版本过滤的读取方继续可用，存量历史既不重写也不迁移，面板载荷形状不变。

设计文档：[English](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/fix/usage-dashboard-accounting/docs/design/2026-11-19-usage-dashboard-accounting.md) · [简体中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/fix/usage-dashboard-accounting/docs/design/2026-11-19-usage-dashboard-accounting.zh-CN.md)。两版完整同步，并记录了首轮两项未通过独立复核的发现：台账证伪的「会话身份分叉」，以及会在存量记录上造成 3.1 倍倒退的「分段求和」去重提案。

## 关联 Issue

无需关闭的 issue。构建在为 #4479 引入的逐请求台账与 #9833 的 session-swap telemetry 事务之上。
