issues.body:
# tui/src/tui/ session, transcript, compaction files: 15 verified defects from R14 (baseline bc58781ba)

## How to read this document (terms used below)

- **R<number>** — review unit, one area of the codebase; this document is about R14.
- **L<number>** — one of twelve review lenses (themes) applied to every unit; the table below names each lens.
- **P0 / P1 / P2** — priority rank: P0 highest, P2 lowest. It orders the work, not the severity of a finding.
- **Stage D** — the verification step: every cited line was opened at the baseline, the reachability was traced, and severity was re-scored. **Stage E** — the drafting step that produced this report.
- **Baseline `bc58781ba`** — the exact commit every quote refers to; re-check before acting if `main` has moved.
- **Confirmed** — a verifier opened the cited line, traced a reachable path and kept the finding; rejected and uncertain findings are not here.
- **Public** — this issue contains only findings cleared for a public report; security-class findings are handled through a separate private channel.
- **needs-test** — the written proof is static; a focused test named in the finding would settle the remaining question. No test was run in this audit.
- **Cell** — one audit cell: a review unit crossed with one lens; finding IDs keep the cell number, so a gap in numbering means a candidate was rejected, marked duplicate or routed to the private index.
- **NOT READ** — a scope marker in a cell: that region was not opened, so no claim is made about it.
- **not-applicable / sampled-rescan-passed** — negative-check outcomes: the lens did not apply to that cell, or a sampled rescan found no new signal.
- **Refs #N / UPSTREAM REFS** — existing tracked issues related to the theme or to the exact code site; they are cross-links, never a claim to close or fix those issues. A 500-issue open/closed sweep found no exact duplicate of these findings at the same file and line.
- **CALL PATH, TRIGGER, MECHANISM, IMPACT, EVIDENCE, FIX, REGRESSION CHECK** — copied verbatim from the verified finding file. CALL PATH = how a user reaches the code; TRIGGER = the condition that fires it; MECHANISM = what the code actually does; IMPACT = what the user sees; EVIDENCE = the supporting lines; FIX = recommended change; REGRESSION CHECK = the test that should be added.

Unit R14 (P1 — highest priority is P0, then P1, then P2), history, resume, compaction, prompt assembly. Confirmed unique findings: **15** — **15 public** in this draft and **0** withheld as private-advisory or held. Finding IDs keep their original cell numbers; a gap means the candidate was rejected, marked duplicate or routed to the private index.

No finding in this unit is withheld as a private security advisory or held item.


## Coverage

- Unit R14 at baseline `bc58781ba`. The full analysis, verbatim quotes and verification notes are in the following comments.
- 15 confirmed public findings. No test, build or product run happened in this audit.

## Findings (condensed)

The verbatim quote, full mechanism, evidence, verifier note and regression check for each finding are in the following comment(s).

### R14-L2-01 — mcp connecting count includes non connecting rows

Severity: minor · Location: ``crates/tui/src/tui/session_boot.rs:391`` · Upstream refs: none

**Trigger:** MCP boot prediction still active (app.mcp_initializing true within MCP_BOOT_PREDICTION_HORIZON) after a snapshot has arrived that contains only Disabled/Connected/NeedsLogin/Failed server rows and no server in the in-flight `connecting` set.

**Mechanism:** `from_parts` sets `phase = Booting` whenever `initializing` is true (session_boot.rs:224), independently of whether any row is actually Connecting. `row_from_snapshot` (session_boot.rs:449-481) returns `Some` rows for Disabled (449-454), Connected (455-460) and NeedsLogin/Failed (461-471) servers; only lazy enabled-but-unconnected servers get `None`.

**Impact:** During the boot prediction window, with a snapshot already carrying connected or disabled servers and no in-flight names, the posture-bar chip reads e.g. `MCP · 3 connecting` when three servers are already connected or disabled.

**Fix:** In the `phase == Booting` fallback, do not derive the count from `self.servers.len()`. Since the line-381 branch already returns when any row is Connecting, the only legitimate remaining source is the unknown-name case: use `let count = self.unnamed_connecting;` and keep the `if count > 0` guard.

### R14-L2-02 — remaining count includes deduplicated references

Severity: minor · Location: ``crates/tui/src/tui/context_inspector.rs:584`` · Upstream refs: none

**Trigger:** `app.session_context_references` contains more than `MAX_REFERENCE_ROWS` (12) unique references plus at least one duplicate key that is skipped by the `seen` set.

**Mechanism:** The loop builds a deduplication key and `continue`s before the row-limit check (lines 576-582), so duplicate records never increment `rendered`. When the cap is hit, `remaining` is computed as `references.len() - rendered`: the total record count minus the number of *unique* rows rendered.

**Impact:** The context inspector overstates the number of hidden references whenever the reference list contains duplicates — e.g. 25 records with 15 unique and 10 duplicates render 12 rows but claim "13 more" instead of "3 more".

**Fix:** Track the number of distinct keys seen, e.g. increment a `unique_total` counter only when `seen.insert(key)` returns true, and compute `remaining = unique_total.saturating_sub(rendered)`.

### R14-L2-03 — tool hint skipped when active tools fill cap

Severity: minor · Location: ``crates/tui/src/tui/context_inspector.rs:643`` · Upstream refs: none

**Trigger:** `app.active_tool_details` contains at least `MAX_TOOL_ROWS` (8) entries, so the active-tools loop reaches the cap.

**Mechanism:** The early `return` exits the whole function before the trailing block at lines 656-670, which is the only place that emits `MessageId::CtxInspVHint` (the "press <key> for details" affordance) whenever `rendered > 0`. The other exit paths — the final-history loop at 647-654 and the `rendered == 0` branch at 656-657 — both fall through to that block.

**Impact:** In a busy session with eight or more active tool entries, the context inspector prints the eight rows but omits the key hint that tells the user how to inspect full tool details — precisely the case where the list is truncated and the hint is most useful.

**Fix:** Replace the `return` with a `break` out of the active-tools loop; the subsequent `take(MAX_TOOL_ROWS.saturating_sub(rendered))` becomes a no-op and control reaches the shared hint block. If the intent is to stop listing further rows entirely, move the hint emission into a helper called on every exit path.

### R14-L4-01 — delete session default location error swallowed

Severity: minor · Location: ``crates/tui/src/tui/session_picker.rs:615`` · Upstream refs: none

**Trigger:** sessions directory resolution fails (unreadable/inaccessible CODEWHALE_HOME, permission change) while a saved session is selected and the user confirms delete with 'y'.

**Mechanism:** `SessionManager::default_location()` returns `std::io::Result<Self>` (session_manager.rs:2719). At line 615 the failure is discarded by `.ok()?`, converting the error into a bare `None`.

**Impact:** The user confirms a destructive delete; nothing is deleted and the UI shows no explanation, so the user cannot tell whether the action was dropped, is still pending, or succeeded. The cause (directory resolution failure) is lost with no durable trace.

**Fix:** Replace `.ok()?` at 615 with an explicit match that sets `self.status = Some(tr(self.locale, MessageId::SessionsDirectoryFailed).into_owned())` (mirroring load_preview at 944) before returning `None`, and include `{error}` in a delete-specific message so the cause is preserved.

### R14-L8-01 — replay hardcodes update plan success

Severity: major · Location: ``crates/tui/src/tui/history.rs:939`` · Upstream refs: none

**Trigger:** A saved session containing an `update_plan` tool call whose tool result was an error is restored from disk (session resume, agent focus, /accept export, or ui/apply replay).

**Mechanism:** The replay constructor at history.rs:939 sets `ToolStatus::Success` unconditionally. The enclosing function accepts `messages: &[Message]` (history.rs:790), which carries tool results, but the plan arm never consults them.

**Impact:** After a session is reloaded, a plan update that actually failed renders with a success header and glyph; the failed tool result is dropped from the transcript. A user reviewing the restored session cannot tell the plan step failed, and no log records it — the #6559 false-success / typed-status-dropped class.

**Fix:** In the `update_plan` arm, find the matching `ToolResult` in `messages` by call id and derive status from it (`success == false` or absent/err result -> `ToolStatus::Failed`; confirmed success -> `ToolStatus::Success`), mirroring tool_routing.rs:986-1000. Keep the tolerance for legacy payloads, but do not hardcode terminal success.

### R14-L8-02 — discard syncsession error return ok done

Severity: major · Location: ``crates/tui/src/tui/conversation_mode.rs:239`` · Upstream refs: none

**Trigger:** A mode change is accepted while `EngineHandle::send` fails, e.g. the engine receiver is closed during shutdown or a session-sync task has stopped.

**Mechanism:** Line 239 binds the `send(...).await` result to `_`; there is no `?`, `map_err`, branch or tracing on the Err path (lines 239-252). Line 253 returns the localized "mode set" string unconditionally.

**Impact:** The user is told the mode was set, but the engine's session state was never synchronized. Subsequent turns can run with the old mode/prompt, and no log explains the discrepancy.

**Fix:** Propagate the sync result: `engine.send(...).await.map_err(|e| { tracing::warn!(error = %e, "conversation mode session sync failed"); tr(locale, MessageId::ConversationModeSetFailed).into_owned() })?;` and roll back or flag `install_conversation_mode` when sync fails, so `Ok(done)` is only returned after a confirmed sync.

### R14-L8-03 — discard request and json errors without log

Severity: minor · Location: ``crates/tui/src/tui/prompt_suggestion.rs:457`` · Upstream refs: none

**Trigger:** The bounded suggestion endpoint returns a transport error, timeout, or malformed/non-JSON body.

**Mechanism:** Both failure branches bind the error as `Err(_)` and return `None`; the error value is discarded and no `tracing` event is emitted. The only `debug!` calls bracket the operation: "generating prompt suggestion" at line 436 and "prompt suggestion generated" at line 472.

**Impact:** Repeated suggestion failures are indistinguishable from "no suggestion produced" in diagnostics. A misconfigured or unreachable suggestion endpoint silently degrades with no structured trace, so post-hoc inspection cannot tell whether the feature is broken or simply idle — the #6559 missing-log / no-receipt class.

**Fix:** Bind and log the cause in both branches, e.g. `Err(e) => { debug!(error = %e, "prompt suggestion request failed"); return None; }` and the same for `response.json()`.

### R14-L8-04 — malformed attrs default into valid context cell

Severity: minor · Location: ``crates/tui/src/tui/history/archived_context.rs:19`` · Upstream refs: none

**Trigger:** A saved assistant message contains an `<archived_context>` tag whose `level` attribute is non-numeric (e.g. `level="abc"`) or whose other attributes are missing/malformed.

**Mechanism:** `parse::<u8>().ok()` converts an unparseable level to `None`, then `unwrap_or(0)` yields level 0; every other attribute falls back to the empty string via `unwrap_or_default()`. The function still returns `Some(HistoryCell::ArchivedContext)` at lines 32-40, so a malformed tag is rendered as a normal context cell with label `Context L{level}` (render line 76) rather than being rejected or flagged as unparseable.

**Impact:** Corrupted or hand-edited archived-context metadata is presented to the user as a well-formed durable receipt, with no warning and no log of the failed attribute parse. This is a small instance of broken input looking like valid output — the #6559 typed-code-dropped / malformed-as-success class — limited to transcript display.

**Fix:** Return `None` (fall back to ordinary assistant prose) when a required attribute such as `level` fails to parse, or carry an explicit `malformed` flag and render an honest warning label; in either case log the offending attribute at `debug!` level.

### R14-L9-01 — deserialize full http response without byte cap

Severity: minor · Location: ``crates/tui/src/tui/prompt_suggestion.rs:460`` · Upstream refs: none

**Trigger:** the configured provider endpoint returned by api_url(base_url, "chat/completions") replies with a large JSON body to the follow-up-suggestion POST. The request asks for max_tokens:64 (:426), which caps generated tokens but does not bound the HTTP response body; a misconfigured, compromised or hostile endpoint can send arbitrarily many bytes within the 10-second timeout (:445).

**Mechanism:** `response.json().await` buffers and deserializes the entire HTTP response body into a `serde_json::Value` before any size check runs. The only length guard, `s.len() <= 200` at :468, applies to the extracted suggestion string after the full body has already been allocated and parsed.

**Impact:** A misconfigured or hostile provider endpoint (base_url is operator-supplied config) can make a best-effort UI feature allocate and parse an arbitrarily large JSON document in the TUI process. On a memory-constrained host this stalls or OOMs the session — the "cap applied after full read/deserialize" failure mode named in #6554.

**Fix:** Before deserializing, read the body with `let bytes = response.bytes().await` and reject with `None` when `bytes.len()` exceeds a fixed ceiling (e.g. the 64 KiB response ceiling referenced by sibling #6554 findings), then `serde_json::from_slice(&bytes)`.

### R14-L12-01 — ignore locale hardcoded english unavailable reason

Severity: minor · Location: ``crates/tui/src/tui/conversation_mode.rs:70`` · Upstream refs: #7071 (CLOSED)

**Trigger:** non-English `app.ui_locale` plus an unavailable conversation mode whose table entry has no `reason`, or whose `reason` is English text supplied by an extension.

**Mechanism:** `display_reason` declares a `Locale` parameter but discards it (`_locale`) and returns the raw string unchanged. `resolve` feeds it either a mode-supplied string or the hardcoded English literal `"This mode is unavailable."`.

**Impact:** a Zh-Hans/Ja/etc. user switching to or launching an unavailable conversation mode sees a half-localized error — localized prose wrapped around "This mode is unavailable." or an extension's English reason.

**Fix:** change `display_reason` to accept `Option<&str>` and use its `locale`: return the supplied reason when present, otherwise `tr(locale, MessageId::ConversationModeUnavailableDefaultReason).into_owned()`; update `resolve` to call `display_reason(locale, mode.reason.as_deref())` and apply the same to the `"unavailable"` fallback at :115. Extension-supplied free text cannot be translated by the TUI and should be treated as untranslatable data, not as a localized message.

### R14-L12-02 — hardcoded english tool status prefix bypass tr

Severity: minor · Location: ``crates/tui/src/tui/history.rs:1782`` · Upstream refs: #7304 (CLOSED)

**Trigger:** non-English `locale` with an exploring/tool cell holding more than one entry whose header does not already show the label (`header_shows_label == false`), so the compact branch paints the prefix.

**Mechanism:** `render_with_locale` receives `locale` and localizes the very same `ToolStatus` values elsewhere in the function — via `tool_status_label(status, locale)` at :1685 and `tr(locale, MessageId::WorkflowCount*)` at :1745-1762. The compact branch instead substitutes a six-word hardcoded English map, and `render_compact_kv` paints `prefix` as a visible label beside the entry.

**Impact:** a non-English user sees tool-status words in English ("live", "done", "loaded", "stopped", "issue", "failed") inline on compact tool cards while every surrounding line is localized. Narrow, visible locale drift with no functional break.

**Fix:** replace the match at :1783-1788 with `tool_status_label(entry.status, locale)`, coerce the returned `Cow<'static, str>` to `&str` when calling `render_compact_kv`, and remove the six literals. This matches the :1685 call site and needs no new message ids.

### R14-L12-03 — char truncation splits grapheme cluster — session_picker

Severity: minor · Location: ``crates/tui/src/tui/session_picker.rs:2090`` · Upstream refs: none

**Trigger:** a session title (or other truncated text) whose grapheme clusters contain multiple Unicode code points — a ZWJ emoji sequence, an emoji with a skin-tone modifier, or a base letter with a combining mark — and whose display width exceeds the picker column so the cut lands inside such a cluster.

**Mechanism:** the whole-string guard uses `UnicodeWidthStr::width` (`text.width()`, correct display columns), but the actual cut iterates `text.chars()` and accumulates per-char widths. A grapheme cluster spanning several code points is therefore decidable mid-cluster: a trailing ZWJ or combining mark can be emitted without its partner, or a modifier can be dropped.

**Impact:** a user with an emoji/CJK-accented session title that crosses the column budget sees a corrupted picker entry (dangling ZWJ modifier, separated accent, or a family emoji reduced to one person). Cosmetic, confined to narrow-width columns, with full title still stored and shown in the detail view.

**Fix:** mirror `history.rs::truncate_text` — iterate `text.graphemes(true)`, sum `codewhale_tui_kit::ui_text::text_display_width(grapheme)`, keep whole graphemes under the `max.saturating_sub(3)` budget, then append `"..."`. If a shared helper is preferred, call the existing `ui_text::truncate_line_to_width` used by `launch_resume_confirm.rs:158`.

### R14-L12-04 — char truncation splits grapheme cluster — transcript

Severity: minor · Location: ``crates/tui/src/tui/transcript.rs:1342`` · Upstream refs: none

**Trigger:** a tool-group transcript line wider than `max_width` whose span content contains a multi-codepoint grapheme (ZWJ emoji sequence, emoji + skin-tone modifier, or base + combining mark) positioned so the display-width cut falls inside the cluster.

**Mechanism:** the initial width check uses `UnicodeWidthStr::width` per span (:1325-1328), but the truncation loop walks `span.content.chars()` and sums `UnicodeWidthChar::width(ch)`. Because a grapheme may be several code points, the budget can be exhausted between a base character and its combining/ZWJ/modifier partner; the loop emits the base and stops before the partner, then appends `"..."` (:1358-1360).

**Impact:** a user with an emoji or accented label inside a tool-group line at a narrow terminal width sees a malformed glyph in the transcript — a separated accent, a lone skin-tone modifier, or a partial emoji sequence. Cosmetic, confined to the rail-prefixed tool-group path, and the full text remains available in the underlying cell.

**Fix:** replace the inner `for ch in span.content.chars()` loop with `for grapheme in span.content.graphemes(true)` and use `codewhale_tui_kit::ui_text::text_display_width(grapheme)`, appending the whole grapheme (or breaking before it) as `history.rs::truncate_text` does; keep the `"..."` suffix and style bookkeeping unchanged.

### R14-L12-05 — char truncation splits grapheme cluster — context_menu

Severity: minor · Location: ``crates/tui/src/tui/context_menu.rs:691`` · Upstream refs: none

**Trigger:** a context-menu title, description, or label containing a multi-codepoint grapheme (ZWJ emoji, emoji + skin-tone modifier, base + combining mark) whose display width exceeds the available column so the cut lands inside the cluster.

**Mechanism:** `trim_to_width` computes display width with `UnicodeWidthStr::width` for the early return (:671) but performs the actual cut by iterating `text.chars()` and summing `UnicodeWidthChar::width(ch)` (:691-698 in the multi-column branch, :677-684 in the `max_width <= 3` branch). A grapheme made of multiple code points can be split: the base is emitted and a ZWJ/combining/modifier partner is dropped, then `"..."` is appended (:699).

**Impact:** a user whose context-menu entry label or description contains an emoji sequence or accented character at a narrow menu width sees a malformed glyph. Cosmetic and narrow (menu column budget), with the underlying entry text unchanged and selectable.

**Fix:** iterate `text.graphemes(true)` and sum `codewhale_tui_kit::ui_text::text_display_width(grapheme)` in both branches of `trim_to_width`, appending whole graphemes; or delegate to the existing `ui_text::truncate_line_to_width` helper used by `launch_resume_confirm.rs:158`.

### R14-L12-06 — hardcoded english auth required label

Severity: minor · Location: ``crates/tui/src/tui/session_boot.rs:498`` · Upstream refs: none

**Trigger:** any non-English UI locale with at least one MCP server in `McpServerBootState::NeedsLogin` during session boot, or any other MCP surface that calls the shared helper.

**Mechanism:** the shared label builder hardcodes the English words "auth required" and takes no `Locale`. The locale-aware announcement that consumes it localizes its neighbouring states through `tr(locale, MessageId::ExtensionsStateConnected)` (:313) and `tr(locale, MessageId::PhaseFailed)` (:326 and :350), so only this one state label remains English in an otherwise translated line.

**Impact:** non-English users see "◆ auth required" embedded in a translated boot-status line, and on every other MCP surface that reuses the helper. Cosmetic locale drift with no functional effect — the user still sees the server names and the `/mcp` affordance.

**Fix:** add `MessageId::McpAuthRequiredState` to the localization catalog, change the helper signature to `mcp_auth_required_state_label(locale: Locale) -> String` returning `format!("{} {}", codewhale_tui_kit::glyphs::ATTENTION, tr(locale, MessageId::McpAuthRequiredState))`, and update every caller (including :319) to pass the locale. Compose the glyph in code as today; only the words move to `tr`.


---

Suggested labels: bug, needs-triage, area:tui, area:state, reliability, area:localization

issues.body:
# tui/src/tui/views/, widgets/, work_surface/: 7 verified defects from R13 (baseline bc58781ba)

## How to read this document (terms used below)

- **R<number>** — review unit, one area of the codebase; this document is about R13.
- **L<number>** — one of twelve review lenses (themes) applied to every unit; the table below names each lens.
- **P0 / P1 / P2** — priority rank: P0 highest, P2 lowest. It orders the work, not the severity of a finding.
- **Stage D** — the verification step: every cited line was opened at the baseline, the reachability was traced, and severity was re-scored. **Stage E** — the drafting step that produced this report.
- **Baseline `bc58781ba`** — the exact commit every quote refers to; re-check before acting if `main` has moved.
- **Confirmed** — a verifier opened the cited line, traced a reachable path and kept the finding; rejected and uncertain findings are not here.
- **Public** — this issue contains only findings cleared for a public report; security-class findings are handled through a separate private channel.
- **needs-test** — the written proof is static; a focused test named in the finding would settle the remaining question. No test was run in this audit.
- **Cell** — one audit cell: a review unit crossed with one lens; finding IDs keep the cell number, so a gap in numbering means a candidate was rejected, marked duplicate or routed to the private index.
- **NOT READ** — a scope marker in a cell: that region was not opened, so no claim is made about it.
- **not-applicable / sampled-rescan-passed** — negative-check outcomes: the lens did not apply to that cell, or a sampled rescan found no new signal.
- **Refs #N / UPSTREAM REFS** — existing tracked issues related to the theme or to the exact code site; they are cross-links, never a claim to close or fix those issues. A 500-issue open/closed sweep found no exact duplicate of these findings at the same file and line.
- **CALL PATH, TRIGGER, MECHANISM, IMPACT, EVIDENCE, FIX, REGRESSION CHECK** — copied verbatim from the verified finding file. CALL PATH = how a user reaches the code; TRIGGER = the condition that fires it; MECHANISM = what the code actually does; IMPACT = what the user sees; EVIDENCE = the supporting lines; FIX = recommended change; REGRESSION CHECK = the test that should be added.

Unit R13 (P1 — highest priority is P0, then P1, then P2), dashboards, cards, selection and state projection. Confirmed unique findings: **7** — **7 public** in this draft and **0** withheld as private-advisory or held. Finding IDs keep their original cell numbers; a gap means the candidate was rejected, marked duplicate or routed to the private index.

No finding in this unit is withheld as a private security advisory or held item.

## Coverage

- Files scanned: all 35 paths in the unit manifest were covered by at least one of the twelve theme scans; per-cell detail was recorded during the audit.
- Files read: every signal-matched production region was opened and quoted by the capturing and verifying agents; the exact per-theme counts and regions are in those cell files.
- Files not read: full sequential line-by-line reads of all files were not performed. Each cell records its own `NOT READ` scope; no claim is made beyond the matched regions.
- Themes applied: all twelve, L1–L12 — bugs, logic, edge cases, error handling, security, ordering, process lifecycle, fail-closed behaviour, resource limits, durable writes, async blocking, platform and Unicode. Each theme section below names its lens and its related tracked issue.
- Baseline: `bc58781ba` for every quote and every verification.
- Negative checks: not-applicable 2/12 cells, sampled-rescan-passed 10/12 cells.
- needs-test items: none in this unit. No test or product run happened in this audit.

## Related upstream issues

These are cross-links found in a sweep of 500 open and closed issues; none is a duplicate at the same file and line.

| Issue | State | Title |
|---|---|---|
| #7071 | CLOSED | zh-Hans and other locales: common TUI strings hardcoded English |

## Contents

| finding id | final severity | theme | one-line problem | confirmation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| R13-L11-01 | minor | L11 | blocking file read in render | static |
| R13-L11-02 | minor | L11 | blocking directory scans in async view construction | static |
| R13-L11-03 | minor | L11 | blocking source read in async view open | static |
| R13-L12-01 | minor | L12 | hardcode english header despite locale | static |
| R13-L12-02 | minor | L12 | hardcode english empty state ignores app locale | static |
| R13-L12-03 | minor | L12 | char count truncation splits grapheme in dock tab | static |
| R13-L12-04 | minor | L12 | hardcode english save pager in localized view | static |

## Planned-work issue card

- **Status:** verified at baseline `bc58781ba`; not fixed in code by this audit.
- **Ways to help without Rust (do these first):**
    - Reproduce or confirm a finding on the baseline by following its `TRIGGER` in the exact file listed below; report whether you see the described result.
    - Review the `IMPACT` wording for accuracy and add a real-world example where you have seen this happen.
    - Check the related tracked issue listed under each theme and report whether this finding is already covered there.
    - Improve the documentation or user-facing message for the locale and wording findings.
    Exact files for this unit:
    - `crates/tui/src/tui/views/fleet_detail.rs`
    - `crates/tui/src/tui/views/fleet_list.rs`
    - `crates/tui/src/tui/views/fleet_setup.rs`
    - `crates/tui/src/tui/views/skills_manager.rs`
    - `crates/tui/src/tui/work_surface/terminal.rs`
- **Ways to help with Rust:** add the regression test named in `REGRESSION CHECK`, make the minimal fix described in `FIX`, then run the focused test.
- **Local test command:** `scripts/dev-test.sh <path-from-LOCATION>`; the script maps a source path to the fastest crate test and refuses a green run when a filter matches nothing. Each finding also has its own `LOCAL TEST` line.
- **Done-when:** every finding here has a regression test that fails without the fix and passes with it; the focused area test is green; no compiler warning is silenced and no error is hidden to make a test pass; `scripts/preflight.sh --check` is green for the area you touched.
- **What maintainers already hold:** stage-D verification for every finding (quote opened at baseline, reachability traced, severity re-scored), the dedup decision, the private-advisory routing and this draft. Nothing has been fixed in code by this audit.
- **How to claim:** claim a finding by commenting on this issue with its finding ID; one finding per PR keeps the change reviewable. The maintainer resolves conflicts with `main` so contributors never rebase around our churn.


## Theme L11 — Async blocking and budget discipline

Refs: #6553 and the #6149 blocking-call rule.

### R13-L11-01 — blocking file read in render

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| FINAL SEVERITY | minor |
| FINAL CONFIDENCE | 9 |
| VENUE | public |
| LOCATION | `crates/tui/src/tui/views/fleet_list.rs:579` |
| FINGERPRINT | `crates/tui/src/tui/views/fleet_list.rs:579:blocking-file-read-in-render` |
| DUPLICATES | none |
| UPSTREAM REFS | none |
| CONFIRMATION | static |
| VERIFIER | stage-d-verifier |
| DATE | 2026-11-22 |

QUOTE — copied from the verified finding file (baseline `bc58781ba`; code lines are verbatim):

```text
    fn entry_summary(&self, entry: &FleetEntry) -> String {
        if entry.legacy {
            return "legacy format — open for details".to_string();
        }
        // Read the file to summarize operator + members. Parsing errors are
        // already shown on the row. Paths stay out of the primary row — they
        // belong in receipts after an explicit write/select/delete.
        let Ok(text) = std::fs::read_to_string(&entry.path) else {
            return "unreadable".to_string();
        };
```

**CALL PATH:** async UI loop (ui/event_loop.rs sole terminal.draw emitter) -> ui/frame.rs:1691 app.view_stack.render -> views/fleet_list.rs render -> :542 self.entry_summary(entry) -> :579 std::fs::read_to_string(&entry.path)

**TRIGGER:** open the Fleet list and leave it on screen; every rendered frame re-reads each visible fleet TOML from disk on the Tokio UI thread to build the second summary line.

**MECHANISM:** `FleetListView::render` calls `self.entry_summary(entry)` once per visible entry at line 542. `entry_summary` executes a synchronous `std::fs::read_to_string` at line 579. The view is rendered by `app.view_stack.render` (ui/frame.rs:1691) from the sole `terminal.draw` emitter in the async UI event loop (ui/event_loop.rs:2163). No `spawn_blocking`, `tokio::fs`, or caching wraps the read — the result is recomputed and discarded on every frame.

**IMPACT:** Each frame blocks a Tokio worker for one file open/read/close per visible fleet row. With a fleet list that fills the screen, or a workspace on a slow/network filesystem, this multiplies into repeated multi-millisecond stalls inside the UI draw path, delaying event ingestion, cancellation and rendering responsiveness. This is the "sync work inline on Tokio / std::fs in async" class of #6553 / #6149; no data is lost, so severity is minor.

**EVIDENCE:** Call site confirmed at fleet_list.rs:542 inside `render`; sole draw emitter at ui/event_loop.rs:2163; view-stack render at ui/frame.rs:1691. Contrast with the same unit's router_setup.rs:362-371, where config file IO is explicitly moved into `tokio::task::spawn_blocking` with the comment "keep that file IO off the UI runtime (#6149)" — the same discipline is absent here. **MECHANISM:** `save()` lives on `FleetDetailView`, which stores `locale` (line 100, set from `app.ui_locale` at 164) and localizes other messages via `tr(self.locale, MessageId::...)` (e.g. 513, 550, 563). Yet the success notice (678-683), the stale-source reason (674) and the failure pager title/body (686-689) are English literals. The locale is available (`self.locale`) but not used for these user-visible strings.

**IMPACT:** A non-English user who saves a Fleet detail sees an English result message and an English error/notice pager ("Save failed", "Nothing was written ... Fix the issue and save again.") in an otherwise localized interface. Wording drift only; the save itself succeeds or fails correctly.

**EVIDENCE:** fleet_detail.rs:35 imports `tr`/`MessageId`/`Locale`; line 100 stores locale; 513/550/563/750/1093 use `tr(self.locale, ...)`. The three hardcoded strings are at 674, 678-683, 686-689. A test at 2251 asserts `title == "Save refused"`, pinning the English literal; no locale variant is tested.

**FIX:** Route these through `tr(self.locale, MessageId::...)` — add MessageIds for the saved/failure/stale-source messages, using named placeholders for `{name}`, `{scope}`, `{path}`, `{err}`, as done in fleet_setup.rs (2462 uses `.replace("{path}", ...)`).

**REGRESSION CHECK:** Add a test that calls save() under Locale::Fr or Locale::ZhHans for ok/stale/err paths and asserts the message/title/body are localized rather than the English literals.

**CORRECTION:** none

**VERIFICATION (reviewer's own check):** Opened fleet_detail.rs at bc58781ba. Lines 672-690 read `fn save(&self) -> Option<ViewAction> { if !self.source_unchanged() { return Some(self.stale_source_action("Save refused")); } ... Ok(path) => ... message: format!("Saved Team `{}` ({}) — wrote {}", ...) ... Err(err) => ... title: "Save failed".to_string(), content: format!("Nothing was written.\n\n{err:#}\n\nFix the issue and save again.")`. `FleetDetailView` stores `locale: Locale` (line 100) set from `app.ui_locale` (164) and already localizes other messages via `tr(self.locale, MessageId::...)` (513, 550, 563, 750, 1093), so the locale is present but unused for these result strings. A test at 2251 asserts `title == "Save refused"`, pinning the English literal; no locale variant is tested. Reachable when a non-English user saves a Fleet detail (ok/stale/err). Wording drift only; the save itself behaves correctly — `minor` ("wording/locale drift without data loss"). Quote present and mechanism traced; confidence 9 stands.

**LOCAL TEST:** `scripts/dev-test.sh crates/tui/src/tui/views/fleet_detail.rs` — run after adding the regression test named above.

issues.body:
# tui/src/commands/: 8 verified defects from R12 (baseline bc58781ba)

## How to read this document (terms used below)

- **R<number>** — review unit, one area of the codebase; this document is about R12.
- **L<number>** — one of twelve review lenses (themes) applied to every unit; the table below names each lens.
- **P0 / P1 / P2** — priority rank: P0 highest, P2 lowest. It orders the work, not the severity of a finding.
- **Stage D** — the verification step: every cited line was opened at the baseline, the reachability was traced, and severity was re-scored. **Stage E** — the drafting step that produced this report.
- **Baseline `bc58781ba`** — the exact commit every quote refers to; re-check before acting if `main` has moved.
- **Confirmed** — a verifier opened the cited line, traced a reachable path and kept the finding; rejected and uncertain findings are not here.
- **Public** — this issue contains only findings cleared for a public report; security-class findings are handled through a separate private channel.
- **needs-test** — the written proof is static; a focused test named in the finding would settle the remaining question. No test was run in this audit.
- **Cell** — one audit cell: a review unit crossed with one lens; finding IDs keep the cell number, so a gap in numbering means a candidate was rejected, marked duplicate or routed to the private index.
- **NOT READ** — a scope marker in a cell: that region was not opened, so no claim is made about it.
- **not-applicable / sampled-rescan-passed** — negative-check outcomes: the lens did not apply to that cell, or a sampled rescan found no new signal.
- **Refs #N / UPSTREAM REFS** — existing tracked issues related to the theme or to the exact code site; they are cross-links, never a claim to close or fix those issues. A 500-issue open/closed sweep found no exact duplicate of these findings at the same file and line.
- **CALL PATH, TRIGGER, MECHANISM, IMPACT, EVIDENCE, FIX, REGRESSION CHECK** — copied verbatim from the verified finding file. CALL PATH = how a user reaches the code; TRIGGER = the condition that fires it; MECHANISM = what the code actually does; IMPACT = what the user sees; EVIDENCE = the supporting lines; FIX = recommended change; REGRESSION CHECK = the test that should be added.

Unit R12 (P1 — highest priority is P0, then P1, then P2), command contract, config and session mutations. Confirmed unique findings: **9** — **8 public** in this draft and **1** withheld as private-advisory or held. Finding IDs keep their original cell numbers; a gap means the candidate was rejected, marked duplicate or routed to the private index.

## Coverage

- Files scanned: all 129 paths in the unit manifest were covered by at least one of the twelve theme scans; per-cell detail was recorded during the audit.
- Files read: every signal-matched production region was opened and quoted by the capturing and verifying agents; the exact per-theme counts and regions are in those cell files.
- Files not read: full sequential line-by-line reads of all files were not performed. Each cell records its own `NOT READ` scope; no claim is made beyond the matched regions.
- Themes applied: all twelve, L1–L12 — bugs, logic, edge cases, error handling, security, ordering, process lifecycle, fail-closed behaviour, resource limits, durable writes, async blocking, platform and Unicode. Each theme section below names its lens and its related tracked issue.
- Baseline: `bc58781ba` for every quote and every verification.
- Negative checks: not-applicable 7/12 cells, sampled-rescan-passed 5/12 cells.
- needs-test items: none in this unit. No test or product run happened in this audit.

## Related upstream issues

These are cross-links found in a sweep of 500 open and closed issues; none is a duplicate at the same file and line.

| Issue | State | Title |
|---|---|---|
| #6555 | CLOSED | [audit] Durable writes not crash-atomic (tmp+rename without fsync) |
| #6559 | OPEN | [audit] Fail-open paths, swallowed errors, and false-PASS gates |
| #7071 | CLOSED | zh-Hans and other locales: common TUI strings hardcoded English |
| #7328 | OPEN | Provider failures: diagnostic log has no cause, typed code dropped |

## Contents

| finding id | final severity | theme | one-line problem | confirmation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| R12-L10-01 | minor | L10 | export file success receipt before directory fsync | static |
| R12-L11-01 | minor | L11 | blocking updater output on ui task | static |
| R12-L11-02 | minor | L11 | blocking workspace scan on ui task | static |
| R12-L12-01 | minor | L12 | hardcoded english config reply allow shell | static |
| R12-L4-01 | minor | L4 | config load error returned as unknown setting | static |
| R12-L4-02 | minor | L4 | unreadable command file silently dropped | static |
| R12-L8-01 | minor | L8 | import apply report write failure silent | static |
| R12-L9-01 | minor | L9 | read to string uncapped command file load | static |

## Planned-work issue card

- **Status:** verified at baseline `bc58781ba`; not fixed in code by this audit.
- **Ways to help without Rust (do these first):**
    - Reproduce or confirm a finding on the baseline by following its `TRIGGER` in the exact file listed below; report whether you see the described result.
    - Review the `IMPACT` wording for accuracy and add a real-world example where you have seen this happen.
    - Check the related tracked issue listed under each theme and report whether this finding is already covered there.
    - Improve the documentation or user-facing message for the locale and wording findings.
    Exact files for this unit:
    - `crates/tui/src/commands/config_main_host.rs`
    - `crates/tui/src/commands/groups/config/config.rs`
    - `crates/tui/src/commands/groups/project/init.rs`
    - `crates/tui/src/commands/groups/utility/update.rs`
    - `crates/tui/src/commands/session_export_host.rs`
    - `crates/tui/src/commands/user_commands.rs`
- **Ways to help with Rust:** add the regression test named in `REGRESSION CHECK`, make the minimal fix described in `FIX`, then run the focused test.
- **Local test command:** `scripts/dev-test.sh <path-from-LOCATION>`; the script maps a source path to the fastest crate test and refuses a green run when a filter matches nothing. Each finding also has its own `LOCAL TEST` line.
- **Done-when:** every finding here has a regression test that fails without the fix and passes with it; the focused area test is green; no compiler warning is silenced and no error is hidden to make a test pass; `scripts/preflight.sh --check` is green for the area you touched.
- **What maintainers already hold:** stage-D verification for every finding (quote opened at baseline, reachability traced, severity re-scored), the dedup decision, the private-advisory routing and this draft. Nothing has been fixed in code by this audit.
- **How to claim:** claim a finding by commenting on this issue with its finding ID; one finding per PR keeps the change reviewable. The maintainer resolves conflicts with `main` so contributors never rebase around our churn.


## Theme L4 — Error handling — swallowed cause, wrong fallback

Refs: none — new finding in this audit.

### R12-L4-01 — config load error returned as unknown setting

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| FINAL SEVERITY | minor |
| FINAL CONFIDENCE | 9 |
| VENUE | public |
| LOCATION | `crates/tui/src/commands/config_main_host.rs:441` |
| FINGERPRINT | `crates/tui/src/commands/config_main_host.rs:441:config-load-error-returned-as-unknown-setting` |
| DUPLICATES | none |
| UPSTREAM REFS | none |
| CONFIRMATION | static |
| VERIFIER | stage-d-verifier-R12-L4 |
| DATE | 2026-11-22 |

QUOTE — copied from the verified finding file (baseline `bc58781ba`; code lines are verbatim):

```text
448: "workspace_follow_symlinks" | "follow_symlinks" => Settings::load().ok().map(|settings| {
449:     format!(
450:         "{} (restart required for engine tools)",
451:         settings.workspace_follow_symlinks
452:     )
453: }),
454: "search" | "search.provider" | "search_provider" => load_command_config(app)
455:     .ok()
456:     .map(|config| search_provider_display(&config, app.ui_locale)),
457: "telemetry" => load_command_config(app).ok().map(|config| {
458:     codewhale_engine::telemetry_notice::saved_preference_enabled(&config).to_string()
459: }),
...
487: Some(v) => ConfigReply::message(format!("{key} = {v}")),
488: None => ConfigReply::error(unknown_setting_message(&key)),
```

**CALL PATH:** user enters `/set search` (also `/set workspace_follow_symlinks`, `/set telemetry`, `/set prompt_suggestion`, `/set auto_review.reviewer_model`) -> command dispatch -> config_main_host::show_single_setting -> the matched arm calls `.ok()` on `load_command_config(app)` or `Settings::load()` -> `None` -> match at line 487-488 maps `None` to `ConfigReply::error(unknown_setting_message(&key))`.

**TRIGGER:** the config file cannot be loaded at query time (corrupt TOML, unreadable file or profile), and the user asks for one of the settings whose query arm discards the `Err` with `.ok()`.

**MECHANISM:** `show_single_setting` returns `Option<String>`; the caller at lines 487-488 treats any `None` as "unknown setting" and produces `unknown_setting_message(&key)`. Five arms in the match (lines 448-459, 463-472) call `.ok()` on a fallible config load, so a real load failure is collapsed into the same `None` used by the `_ => None` arm at line 482 for genuinely unknown keys. The actual `Err` and its cause are discarded at the `.ok()` call; no log or notice records it. The same function's `base_url` and `provider_url` arms (lines 229-240 and 249-263) handle the identical failure by returning `ConfigReply::error(format!("Failed to load config: {err}"))`, which proves the silent path is an inconsistency rather than a deliberate contract.

**IMPACT:** A user whose config is unreadable or malformed asks `/set search` and is told the setting is unknown, rather than being told the config failed to load. They are misled into believing a supported setting was removed, and the underlying config corruption stays invisible. No data is lost, but the diagnostic is actively wrong and the failure leaves no durable trace.

**EVIDENCE:** `show_single_setting` signature at config_main_host.rs:172 confirms the `ConfigReply` return; the `Some`/`None` mapping at lines 487-488 is the single consumer of the `Option`. Contrasting correct handling for the same `load_config` failure exists at lines 230-237 and 250-260. Test files for config status exist (config_policy_status_tests.rs), but no test covers a failing config load reaching these query arms.

**FIX:** In each affected arm, replace `.ok()` with an explicit `match` that returns `ConfigReply::error(format!("Failed to load config: {err}"))` on `Err`, matching the `base_url`/`provider_url` arms; keep `None` reserved for genuinely unknown keys. Alternatively change the intermediate value to `Result<Option<String>, String>` so the error reaches the reply without being flattened.

**REGRESSION CHECK:** Add a test that makes `load_command_config`/`Settings::load` fail, invokes `show_single_setting` with `search`, and asserts the reply text contains "Failed to load config" rather than the unknown-setting message.

**CORRECTION:** none

**VERIFICATION (reviewer's own check):** Opened config_main_host.rs at baseline bc58781ba. Lines 448-472 match the quote exactly: `"workspace_follow_symlinks" ... => Settings::load().ok().map(...)` (448), `"search" ... => load_command_config(app).ok().map(...)` (454-456), `telemetry`, `prompt_suggestion`, `auto_review.reviewer_model` all call `.ok()` on fallible config loads, collapsing `Err` into `None`. The single consumer at 486-488 maps `None` to `ConfigReply::error(unknown_setting_message(&key))`, so a real load failure is reported as "unknown setting". The `_ => None` arm at 475-484 uses the same `None` for genuinely unknown keys — confirm the conflation. Contrasting correct handling for the identical load failure exists in the same function: base_url lines 230-237 `Err(err) => return ConfigReply::error(format!("Failed to load config: {err}"))` and provider_url lines 250-260 likewise. Reachability shown: contract/config_main.rs:103 `get_value(&mut self, key) -> ... show_single_setting(&app, key)` and :69 `search_provider_status` -> `show_single_setting(&app, "search.provider")` are command-contract entry points for `/set <key>` queries. No test or product run needed for confidence 9 per rubric §6; mechanism fully traced through code with quotes.

**LOCAL TEST:** `scripts/dev-test.sh crates/tui/src/commands/config_main_host.rs` — run after adding the regression test named above.


### R12-L4-02 — unreadable command file silently dropped

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| FINAL SEVERITY | minor |
| FINAL CONFIDENCE | 7 |
| VENUE | public |
| LOCATION | `crates/tui/src/commands/user_commands.rs:192` |
| FINGERPRINT | `crates/tui/src/commands/user_commands.rs:192:unreadable-command-file-silently-dropped` |
| DUPLICATES | none |
| UPSTREAM REFS | none |
| CONFIRMATION | static |
| VERIFIER | stage-d-verifier-R12-L4 |
| DATE | 2026-11-22 |

QUOTE — copied from the verified finding file (baseline `bc58781ba`; code lines are verbatim):

```text
179: /// Load one reviewed command component from an immutable plugin snapshot.
180: /// Components may name either one markdown file or a directory of markdown
181: /// files; every returned entry retains the exact staged path for diagnostics.
182: pub(crate) fn load_command_entries_from_component(
183:     component: &Path,
184: ) -> Vec<(String, String, PathBuf)> {
185:     if component.is_file() {
...
192:         return std::fs::read_to_string(component)
193:             .ok()
194:             .map(|content| vec![(stem.to_lowercase(), content, component.to_path_buf())])
195:             .unwrap_or_default();
...
218:         let content = match std::fs::read_to_string(&path) {
219:             Ok(c) => c,
220:             Err(_) => continue,
221:         };
```

**CALL PATH:** command discovery at startup/palette build -> user_registry.rs:185 and contract.rs:4009 -> user_commands::load_command_entries_from_component -> line 192 `std::fs::read_to_string(component).ok().map(...).unwrap_or_default()` (directory branch lines 204-221 uses `Err(_) => return Vec::new()` / `Err(_) => continue`) -> no entry is produced -> command missing from palette and `/help` with no log or notice.

**TRIGGER:** a custom or plugin `.md` command file exists in a scanned commands directory but cannot be read as UTF-8 (invalid bytes) or is unreadable due to permissions; the loader silently omits it.

**MECHANISM:** Both branches of `load_command_entries_from_component` discard the `io::Error` from `read_to_string` (`.ok()` plus `unwrap_or_default()` for a single file, `Err(_) => continue` for a directory). The function returns `Vec`, so there is no channel to report the failure; no `warn!`, log line or user notice is emitted anywhere in the loader. A command file that fails to decode therefore disappears from the command set exactly as if it did not exist.

**IMPACT:** A user with an invalid-UTF-8 or unreadable custom command file sees the plugin/directory as active but the command absent from `/help` and the palette, with no hint why. The doc comment at line 181 says entries retain their staged path "for diagnostics", yet the failure that most needs diagnostics produces no entry and no path. This is a silent false success with no durable trace, not a crash.

**EVIDENCE:** Production callers confirm reachability: user_registry.rs:185 and contract.rs:4009 call `load_command_entries_from_component`; user_registry.rs:206 calls `load_commands_from_dir`. The sibling loader `load_commands_from_dir` is documented at line 171 as "Errors are silently skipped". The same file does use `tracing::warn!(target: "commands", ...)` at lines 388 and 393 for lock contention, so the logging channel is available and used for comparable degraded paths; the two read-failure sites emit nothing. Tests exist for missing directories (user_commands.rs:447) but none for an unreadable/invalid file.

**FIX:** Have the loader return read errors (e.g. `Vec<Result<..., (PathBuf, io::Error)>>`) and have callers in user_registry.rs/contract.rs emit a `warn!` or surface a toast naming the skipped path; at minimum add a `tracing::warn!` at the two `Err` sites (lines 192-195 and 218-221) so the skip leaves a durable trace.

**REGRESSION CHECK:** Add a fixture with a commands directory containing one valid `.md` and one invalid-UTF-8 `.md`, call `load_command_entries_from_component`, and assert a warning/diagnostic is recorded for the skipped file (or that the error is returned), not just that the valid file loads.

**CORRECTION:** none

**VERIFICATION (reviewer's own check):** Opened user_commands.rs at baseline bc58781ba. Lines 182-221 match the quote: single-file branch 192-195 `std::fs::read_to_string(component).ok().map(...).unwrap_or_default()` and directory branch 218-221 `match std::fs::read_to_string(&path) { Ok(c) => c, Err(_) => continue }` both discard the io::Error; the fn returns Vec, so no error channel exists and no `warn!` is emitted at either site. The same file does use `tracing::warn!(target: "commands", ...)` for comparable degraded paths at 388 and 393 (verified), so a durable-trace channel exists but is unused here. Reachability confirmed in production callers: contract.rs:4009 `load_command_entries_from_component(path)` feeds `plugin_command_names` (palette/help names), and user_registry.rs:185 feeds `plugin_entries` into `registry.load_from_entries(...)`; user_registry.rs:206 calls `load_commands_from_dir` -> `load_command_entries_from_component` (line 173). Missing commands therefore vanish from the user-facing command set with no log. Confidence 7 (rubric §6: confident pattern match in read code with quote) — the triggering condition (invalid-UTF-8/unreadable .md) is a real but uncommon edge case and no product run was performed by design. Note: doc comment at 171 says "Errors are silently skipped" for the sibling loader, so the silence is partly by design; the durable-trace gap still stands, keeping this minor.

**LOCAL TEST:** `scripts/dev-test.sh crates/tui/src/commands/user_commands.rs` — run after adding the regression test named above.


## Theme L8 — Fail-closed, gates, receipts, contract drift

Refs: #6559, #7435, #7434, #7328 (fail-closed, receipts, contract drift).

### R12-L8-01 — import apply report write failure silent

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| FINAL SEVERITY | minor |
| FINAL CONFIDENCE | 7 |
| VENUE | public |
| LOCATION | `crates/tui/src/commands/groups/config/config.rs:1000` |
| FINGERPRINT | `crates/tui/src/commands/groups/config/config.rs:1000:import-apply-report-write-failure-silent` |
| DUPLICATES | none |
| UPSTREAM REFS | none |
| CONFIRMATION | static |
| VERIFIER | verifier-R12-L8 |
| DATE | 2026-11-22 |

QUOTE — copied from the verified finding file (baseline `bc58781ba`; code lines are verbatim):

```text
        }
        if outcome.wrote_report {
            message.push_str(&format!(
                "\nFull report: {}",
                facet.display_path(&outcome.report_path)
            ));
        }
        return ConfigCommandResult::message(message);
    }
    let mut message = super::import_claude::render_plan(&plan, &|path| facet.display_path(path));
```

**CALL PATH:** `/import-claude --apply` -> `groups/config/config.rs::import_claude` (955) -> `facet.write_artifacts` (977) -> `config_main_import_host.rs::write_artifacts` (48-71, `atomic_write(...).is_ok()` at 58/61) -> back at config.rs:978-1006 where the false bool is silently dropped -> `ConfigCommandResult::message` (1006).

**TRIGGER:** the report or portable-bundle destination `.codewhale/imports/` is not writable (read-only home, disk full, permissions) while the user runs `/import-claude --apply`; the apply of instructions may still succeed.

**MECHANISM:** `config_main_import_host.rs:57-61` collapses each `atomic_write` `Result` into a bare bool with no `tracing` event and no error value. In the `--apply` branch, `config.rs:1000` uses `wrote_report` only to decide whether to append the "Full report:" line; there is no `else`. `wrote_bundle` is never read anywhere in the apply branch (config.rs:978-1006). A failed artifact write therefore produces an ordinary success `ConfigCommandResult::message` with no indication that the promised report or bundle is missing.

**IMPACT:** A user who applies an import is told what was applied and what remains manual, but is never told that the durable report (the receipt of what was imported) or the portable bundle was not written. Because nothing is logged, the loss cannot be reconstructed after the fact. This is the #6559 false-success / missing-receipt class: a failed artifact write is presented as a normal completed command.

**EVIDENCE:** (1) `config_main_import_host.rs:57-61` — `atomic_write(&report_path, ...).is_ok()` and `atomic_write(&bundle_path, ...).is_ok()`, both error values discarded. (2) The non-apply branch at `config.rs:1014-1021` has the explicit `else` message "(the report could not be written; the plan above is complete)", proving the apply branch's omission is a gap, not a deliberate global policy. (3) `config.rs:978-1006` contains no reference to `artifacts.wrote_bundle`. (4) The only tests (`config_main_import_host.rs:252-311`, `config.rs` import tests) cover writable happy paths; no test forces a write failure and checks the message.

**FIX:** In the apply branch mirror the non-apply branch: when `!outcome.wrote_report`, append an explicit warning line, and when a bundle was requested but `!artifacts.wrote_bundle`, append one as well; or return an error-flagged `ConfigCommandResult` and emit a `tracing::warn!` carrying the `atomic_write` error. Preserve the underlying error from `write_artifacts` instead of reducing it to a bool so the durable trace names the cause.

**REGRESSION CHECK:** a test that points `CODEWHALE_HOME` at a read-only imports directory, runs `/import-claude --apply`, and asserts the resulting message contains the report/bundle write-failure notice (and/or `is_error` is set); current tests only assert success.

**CORRECTION:** none

**VERIFICATION (reviewer's own check):** Opened at bc58781ba. config.rs:978-1006: the apply branch reads `outcome.wrote_report` only to append the "Full report:" line (1000-1005), with no else, and never references `wrote_bundle` in that branch (grep hits in this file: 979, 1000, 1014, 1022 — 1022 is the non-apply branch). config_main_import_host.rs:57-61 collapses both `atomic_write(...)` Results into bare bools with no tracing event; apply_plan (78-83, 194-199) passes wrote_report through unchanged, so no failure surfaces elsewhere. The sibling non-apply branch at config.rs:1014-1021 does have an explicit else: "(the report could not be written; the plan above is complete)", so the omission is local to apply. Reachability: `/import-claude --apply` is a real user command (config.rs:951-958) and a failed report/bundle write returns an ordinary success `ConfigCommandResult::message` — the TRIGGER is a real path. §6 minor row (narrow edge case with a workaround, no data loss); confidence 7 stands on the quoted line plus traced two-file call path.

**LOCAL TEST:** `scripts/dev-test.sh crates/tui/src/commands/groups/config/config.rs` — run after adding the regression test named above.


## Theme L9 — Resource limits, bounded buffers

Refs: #6554, #6560 (unbounded reads and missing limits).

### R12-L9-01 — read to string uncapped command file load

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| FINAL SEVERITY | minor |
| FINAL CONFIDENCE | 7 |
| VENUE | public |
| LOCATION | `crates/tui/src/commands/user_commands.rs:140` |

Candidate re-verification: plan §4.3 assigns the L12 ids #7048 to R8/R17, #6953 to R19/R20 and #7071 to R7, with theme zones U01/U04/U07 — none maps to R12/C01, and no checked-in per-ID L12 candidate list exists under docs/audit. This is CLASS new, not a re-report.

**FIX:** Add a `MessageId` with named placeholders for `{enabled}`, `{suffix}` and the chord (e.g. `CmdConfigAllowShellOn`/`CmdConfigAllowShellOff`), add its translations to every shipped locale, resolve it in `contract/config_messages.rs`, and replace lines 2214-2219 with `ConfigReply::message(ConfigMessage::keyed_with("cmd_config_allow_shell_on", &[("suffix", &suffix)]))`. Render the `Shift+Tab` hint through `shell_key_routing::display_chord(binding(ShellBindingId::Catalog).catalog_chord)` (or a placeholder substituted with that value) instead of the literal.

**REGRESSION CHECK:** A locale-aware test calling `commands::set_config_value` with `app.ui_locale = Locale::ZhHans` and `Locale::En` for key `allow_shell` that asserts the reply text differs across locales and is not the hardcoded English literal. None exists today.

**CORRECTION:** none

**VERIFICATION (reviewer's own check):** Opened at baseline bc58781ba (git rev-parse HEAD = baseline; no tracked changes in tree). QUOTE verified verbatim: config_main_host.rs:2213-2219 `app.set_agent_shell_access(enabled); let mode_hint = if enabled { " Work mode will expose shell on the next turn with approval gating. Full Access (Shift+Tab) also enables shell and auto-approves." } else { " Shell tools will be hidden on the next turn. Re-enable with `/config allow_shell true`." }; return ConfigReply::message(format!("allow_shell = {enabled}{suffix}.{mode_hint}"));` — the entire reply is one `format!` literal wrapped in `ConfigReply::message`. Mechanism confirmed: `render_config_reply` receives `locale` (config_host.rs:466-469) but its inner `message_text` emits `ConfigMessage::Literal(text) => Ok(text)` verbatim (config_host.rs:479) while only `Keyed` resolves `codewhale_localization::tr(locale, id)` (config_host.rs:487-500), so the locale argument never touches this string. Reachability confirmed: `set_config_value` is `pub fn` (config_main_host.rs:1744); the host caller `commands::set_config_value` passes `app.ui_locale` into the renderer (mod.rs:529-534); `render_config_reply` places the text in `CommandResult.message` (config_host.rs:525-529) — the reply is user-visible. The localization channel exists at this same call site: sibling arms use `ConfigReply::error(ConfigMessage::keyed_with(...))` (config_main_host.rs:977-989, 1769-1776) and `ConfigReply::message(ConfigMessage::concat([literal, keyed(scope_key), literal]))` (config_main_host.rs:1818-1822). Key-hint contract break confirmed: `crates/tui/AGENTS.md:13` says "Key hints come from the `shell_key_routing` binding table, never from a string literal", and the canonical renderer `display_chord` exists (shell_key_routing.rs:593), yet line 2215 hardcodes `Shift+Tab`. Impact scoped correctly by child to English locale drift on a permission-relevant setting, no data loss or behavioural error.

**LOCAL TEST:** `scripts/dev-test.sh crates/tui/src/commands/config_main_host.rs` — run after adding the regression test named above.
