# engine/src/extension_host/: 4 verified defects from R11 (baseline bc58781ba)

## How to read this document (terms used below)

- **R<number>** — review unit, one area of the codebase; this document is about R11.
- **L<number>** — one of twelve review lenses (themes) applied to every unit; the table below names each lens.
- **P0 / P1 / P2** — priority rank: P0 highest, P2 lowest. It orders the work, not the severity of a finding.
- **Stage D** — the verification step: every cited line was opened at the baseline, the reachability was traced, and severity was re-scored. **Stage E** — the drafting step that produced this report.
- **Baseline `bc58781ba`** — the exact commit every quote refers to; re-check before acting if `main` has moved.
- **Confirmed** — a verifier opened the cited line, traced a reachable path and kept the finding; rejected and uncertain findings are not here.
- **Public** — this issue contains only findings cleared for a public report; security-class findings are handled through a separate private channel.
- **needs-test** — the written proof is static; a focused test named in the finding would settle the remaining question. No test was run in this audit.
- **Cell** — one audit cell: a review unit crossed with one lens; finding IDs keep the cell number, so a gap in numbering means a candidate was rejected, marked duplicate or routed to the private index.
- **NOT READ** — a scope marker in a cell: that region was not opened, so no claim is made about it.
- **not-applicable / sampled-rescan-passed** — negative-check outcomes: the lens did not apply to that cell, or a sampled rescan found no new signal.
- **Refs #N / UPSTREAM REFS** — existing tracked issues related to the theme or to the exact code site; they are cross-links, never a claim to close or fix those issues. A 500-issue open/closed sweep found no exact duplicate of these findings at the same file and line.
- **CALL PATH, TRIGGER, MECHANISM, IMPACT, EVIDENCE, FIX, REGRESSION CHECK** — copied verbatim from the verified finding file. CALL PATH = how a user reaches the code; TRIGGER = the condition that fires it; MECHANISM = what the code actually does; IMPACT = what the user sees; EVIDENCE = the supporting lines; FIX = recommended change; REGRESSION CHECK = the test that should be added.

Unit R11 (P1 — highest priority is P0, then P1, then P2), DSH attachments, grants, terminal. Confirmed unique findings: **4** — **4 public** in this draft and **0** withheld as private-advisory or held. Finding IDs keep their original cell numbers; a gap means the candidate was rejected, marked duplicate or routed to the private index.

No finding in this unit is withheld as a private security advisory or held item.

## Coverage

- Files scanned: all 30 paths in the unit manifest were covered by at least one of the twelve theme scans; per-cell detail was recorded during the audit.
- Files read: every signal-matched production region was opened and quoted by the capturing and verifying agents; the exact per-theme counts and regions are in those cell files.
- Files not read: full sequential line-by-line reads of all files were not performed. Each cell records its own `NOT READ` scope; no claim is made beyond the matched regions.
- Themes applied: all twelve, L1–L12 — bugs, logic, edge cases, error handling, security, ordering, process lifecycle, fail-closed behaviour, resource limits, durable writes, async blocking, platform and Unicode. Each theme section below names its lens and its related tracked issue.
- Baseline: `bc58781ba` for every quote and every verification.
- Negative checks: not-applicable 4/12 cells, sampled-rescan-passed 8/12 cells.
- needs-test items: none in this unit. No test or product run happened in this audit.

## Related upstream issues

These are cross-links found in a sweep of 500 open and closed issues; none is a duplicate at the same file and line.

| Issue | State | Title |
|---|---|---|
| #6555 | CLOSED | [audit] Durable writes not crash-atomic (tmp+rename without fsync) |

## Contents

| finding id | final severity | theme | one-line problem | confirmation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| R11-L10-01 | minor | L10 | materialize file rename without fsync | static |
| R11-L7-01 | minor | L7 | timeout drops reconcile joinhandle | static |
| R11-L9-01 | minor | L9 | deserialize then apply byte cap | static |
| R11-L9-02 | minor | L9 | verdict deserialize then size guard | static |

## Planned-work issue card

- **Status:** verified at baseline `bc58781ba`; not fixed in code by this audit.
- **Ways to help without Rust (do these first):**
    - Reproduce or confirm a finding on the baseline by following its `TRIGGER` in the exact file listed below; report whether you see the described result.
    - Review the `IMPACT` wording for accuracy and add a real-world example where you have seen this happen.
    - Check the related tracked issue listed under each theme and report whether this finding is already covered there.
    - Improve the documentation or user-facing message for the locale and wording findings.
    Exact files for this unit:
    - `crates/engine/src/extension_host/command.rs`
    - `crates/engine/src/extension_host/hooks.rs`
    - `crates/engine/src/extension_host/mod.rs`
- **Ways to help with Rust:** add the regression test named in `REGRESSION CHECK`, make the minimal fix described in `FIX`, then run the focused test.
- **Local test command:** `scripts/dev-test.sh <path-from-LOCATION>`; the script maps a source path to the fastest crate test and refuses a green run when a filter matches nothing. Each finding also has its own `LOCAL TEST` line.
- **Done-when:** every finding here has a regression test that fails without the fix and passes with it; the focused area test is green; no compiler warning is silenced and no error is hidden to make a test pass; `scripts/preflight.sh --check` is green for the area you touched.
- **What maintainers already hold:** stage-D verification for every finding (quote opened at baseline, reachability traced, severity re-scored), the dedup decision, the private-advisory routing and this draft. Nothing has been fixed in code by this audit.
- **How to claim:** claim a finding by commenting on this issue with its finding ID; one finding per PR keeps the change reviewable. The maintainer resolves conflicts with `main` so contributors never rebase around our churn.


## Theme L7 — Process lifecycle, cancellation, cleanup

Refs: #6558 (worker and child-process lifecycle).

### R11-L7-01 — timeout drops reconcile joinhandle

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| FINAL SEVERITY | minor |
| FINAL CONFIDENCE | 7 |
| VENUE | public |
| LOCATION | `crates/engine/src/extension_host/mod.rs:4735` |
| FINGERPRINT | `crates/engine/src/extension_host/mod.rs:4735:timeout-drops-reconcile-joinhandle` |
| DUPLICATES | none |
| UPSTREAM REFS | none |
| CONFIRMATION | static |
| VERIFIER | verifier-R11-L7-D |
| DATE | 2026-11-22 |

QUOTE — copied from the verified finding file (baseline `bc58781ba`; code lines are verbatim):

```text
4727:            return;
4728:        }
4729:        let manager = Arc::clone(&self.manager);
4730:        let task = tokio::spawn(async move {
4731:            if let Err(error) = manager.reconcile_with_policy(false).await {
4732:                manager.shared.diagnostic(error);
4733:            }
4734:        });
4735:        let _ = tokio::time::timeout(limit, task).await;
4736:    }
```

**CALL PATH:** crates/engine/src/core/engine/host_profile.rs:75 (also crates/engine/src/core/engine.rs:6866) -> HostAttachment::sync_creator_within (mod.rs:4725) -> tokio::spawn of reconcile_with_policy (mod.rs:4730) -> tokio::time::timeout(limit, task) (mod.rs:4735)

**TRIGGER:** A creator-eligible session start where reconcile_with_policy(false) takes longer than EXTENSION_FIRST_SYNC_WAIT; the timeout expires while the reconcile task is still running.

**MECHANISM:** `sync_creator_within` moves the `JoinHandle` for a spawned `reconcile_with_policy` task into `tokio::time::timeout`. When the deadline elapses the timeout future returns `Err(Elapsed)` and drops the `JoinHandle`; dropping a Tokio `JoinHandle` detaches the task, it does not abort it. The function returns `()` with no signal that the sync did not finish, so the caller proceeds while the reconcile task may still be spawning, tearing down, or activating extension hosts — a completion/late-effect race with subsequent setup.

**IMPACT:** On a slow extension host launch at session start, the first-turn profile/tool view can be assembled before the detached reconcile finishes; a late host completion or teardown then lands after the caller has moved on. The effect is a transient first-turn inconsistency (missing creator tools or a host change arriving late) rather than data loss.

**EVIDENCE:** Nearby guards checked: `reconcile_with_policy` takes `shared.sync_lock` (mod.rs:2651), so two reconciles cannot interleave destructively; this limits but does not remove the late- effect window. No `task.abort()` exists on the timeout path (mod.rs:4735). Production callers confirmed at host_profile.rs:75 and engine.rs:6866. `creator_tests.rs` exercises this helper only with generous 5–10 s limits where the reconcile completes, so no test covers the timeout path.

**FIX:** Make the timeout explicit rather than silently detaching: return a status from `sync_creator_within` so callers know sync did not settle, and drive the spawned reconcile with a `CancellationToken` that is cancelled on deadline expiry so the task winds down at its await points. Do not simply call `JoinHandle::abort()` mid-reconcile without first making the reconcile cancellation-safe — aborting while it holds `sync_lock` could leave partially applied host state.

**REGRESSION CHECK:** A test that sets a very small `limit`, blocks `reconcile_with_policy`, and asserts that the deadline produces an observable status/cancellation instead of an untracked detached task. None exists today.

**CORRECTION:** Child's "late teardown" framing is imprecise — in creator mode policy=false still spawns/activates host:creator through reconcile_builtin(false); the demonstrable effect is a late host activation, not teardown. Impact is bounded to a transient first-turn inconsistency (the next turn re-reads registry state and picks up the completed host), not data loss — consistent with minor severity. The identical detach-on-timeout pattern appears in sync_within (mod.rs:4839-4851), indicating a deliberate best-effort "wait up to limit, then let reconcile finish in background" design rather than an isolated oversight.

**VERIFICATION (reviewer's own check):** Opened mod.rs:4725-4736 at baseline (HEAD == bc58781ba, file clean at baseline). Verbatim: "let task = tokio::spawn(async move { if let Err(error) = manager.reconcile_with_policy(false).await { manager.shared.diagnostic(error); } }); let _ = tokio::time::timeout(limit, task).await;" — on Elapsed the timeout future drops the JoinHandle, which detaches the task (Tokio semantics), it does not abort; the fn returns () with no completion status. Both callers reachable: host_profile.rs:70-76 and engine.rs:6864-6867, guard `ext_enabled == false && creator_eligible && is_creator && !creator_ready()`, limit = EXTENSION_FIRST_SYNC_WAIT = 10s (engine.rs:107). The detached task demonstrably mutates state: reconcile_with_policy(false) reaches reconcile_builtin(false) at mod.rs:3190 (creator_users>0 / has_creator_owner), which calls ensure_host(&HostCohort::Builtin, false) at 3412 and activate_owner registering "host:creator" Active (3422+) — so a late completion can land after the caller returns. Callers proceed to install_creator_tools (engine.rs:6873), which reads registry owner "host:creator" (mod.rs:4738-4750) and yields no creator tools if reconcile has not finished. Guards narrow but do not remove the window: sync_lock serializes reconciles (mod.rs:2651); a reconcile_settled Notify exists (mod.rs:2650/1412/2159) but these two callers do not await it; creator_tests.rs exercises sync_creator_within only at 5-10s where reconcile completes and asserts creator_ready (lines 106/122/151/174), so no timeout-path test exists.

**LOCAL TEST:** `scripts/dev-test.sh crates/engine/src/extension_host/mod.rs` — run after adding the regression test named above.


## Theme L9 — Resource limits, bounded buffers

Refs: #6554, #6560 (unbounded reads and missing limits).

### R11-L9-01 — deserialize then apply byte cap

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| FINAL SEVERITY | minor |
| FINAL CONFIDENCE | 8 |
| VENUE | public |
| LOCATION | `crates/engine/src/extension_host/command.rs:302` |
| FINGERPRINT | `crates/engine/src/extension_host/command.rs:302:deserialize-then-apply-byte-cap` |
| DUPLICATES | none |
| UPSTREAM REFS | none |
| CONFIRMATION | static |
| VERIFIER | stage-d-verifier |
| DATE | 2026-11-22 |

QUOTE — copied from the verified finding file (baseline `bc58781ba`; code lines are verbatim):

```text
302: let wire: CommandResultWire = serde_json::from_value(value)
303:     .map_err(|error| format!("returned a malformed result: {error}"))?;
304: match wire {
305:     CommandResultWire::Success { text } => Ok(CommandOutcome::Show {
306:         text: text.as_deref().map(display_text).unwrap_or_default(),
307:     }),
205: fn strip_escapes(text: &str) -> String {
206:     let mut clean = String::with_capacity(text.len());
207:     codewhale_sanitize::sanitize::strip_ansi_into(text, &mut clean);
208:     clean
209: }
213: fn display_text(text: &str) -> String {
214:     let mut clean = strip_escapes(text);
215:     if clean.len() > MAX_TEXT_BYTES {
```

**CALL PATH:** /command invocation -> command::run (command.rs:277) -> host.call (283) -> serde_json::from_value::<CommandResultWire> (302) -> display_text (306/308) -> strip_escapes (214) -> String::with_capacity(text.len()) (206) -> MAX_TEXT_BYTES check (215)

**TRIGGER:** an extension command result carries a `text` (or `prompt`) field sized close to the 32 MiB protocol frame cap; the 64 KiB / 128 KiB caps are only enforced after the whole value has been deserialized and copied.

**MECHANISM:** `serde_json::from_value(value)` at line 302 fully materializes the plugin-controlled result, including a `String` of arbitrary size up to the protocol frame cap, before any byte cap is consulted. `display_text` then calls `strip_escapes`, whose `String::with_capacity(text.len())` at line 206 allocates a second full-size copy before line 215 finally enforces `MAX_TEXT_BYTES` (64 KiB) and truncates. The `Submit` branch repeats this: `strip_escapes(&prompt)` at line 310 allocates a full-size copy before the `MAX_PROMPT_BYTES` check at line 314. The caps are therefore applied strictly after the allocation cost they are meant to bound.

**IMPACT:** a single command result near the 32 MiB frame cap forces roughly 64-96 MiB of transient allocation (serde Value + deserialized String + with_capacity copy) before truncation to 64 KiB. Because core_call allows 256 in-flight calls, repeated large results multiply this transient memory; a buggy or hostile extension can inflate host RSS well beyond what the displayed 64 KiB limit suggests. Cost is bounded by the protocol cap, so this is a wasteful-allocation/minor issue rather than an unbounded one.

**EVIDENCE:** no `len()` check on `text`/`prompt` exists before line 302 or before the `with_capacity` at line 206/310. protocol.rs:56 sets `MAX_FRAME = 32*1024*1024`; read_frame checks `length > MAX_FRAME` before allocating the payload (protocol.rs:334-337), which bounds but does not prevent the pre-cap allocation. Tests exist for the cap itself (command.rs display tests) but none assert that no oversized copy is allocated before truncation.

**FIX:** before `serde_json::from_value`, inspect the raw `Value` result fields and reject `text`/`prompt` longer than the applicable cap; alternatively change `strip_escapes` to stream into a `String` with a bounded capacity (e.g. `String::new()` plus an early `return` once `MAX_TEXT_BYTES` is exceeded) so no full-size copy is allocated before the cap.

**REGRESSION CHECK:** a unit test that passes a command result with a `text` field larger than the protocol cap would be rejected would be bounded upstream; a focused test asserting `strip_escapes`/`display_text` never allocate more than `MAX_TEXT_BYTES + ANSI-overhead` for a multi-megabyte input would catch reintroduction. None present.

**CORRECTION:** none

**VERIFICATION (reviewer's own check):** Opened command.rs directly. Line 302 `let wire: CommandResultWire = serde_json::from_value(value)` fully materializes the plugin-controlled Value before any byte cap is consulted; lines 205-206 `fn strip_escapes(text: &str) -> String { let mut clean = String::with_capacity(text.len());` allocate a second full-size copy, and only line 215 `if clean.len() > MAX_TEXT_BYTES` (64 KiB, const at line 63) truncates afterward. The Submit branch repeats this at line 310 `let prompt = strip_escapes(&prompt);` before line 314 `if prompt.len() > MAX_PROMPT_BYTES` (128 KiB, const at 65). CALL PATH is reachable: command::run (246) -> host.call (283) -> serde_json::from_value (302) -> display_text (306/308) -> strip_escapes (214) -> with_capacity (206) -> cap (215). The 32 MiB bound is real and verified from code: protocol.rs:56 `pub const MAX_FRAME: usize = 32 * 1024 * 1024`; read_frame (317-339) rejects `if length > MAX_FRAME` at 334 before `let mut payload = vec![0u8; length]` at 337; supervisor.rs:1995 routes every inbound response through read_frame, and call() (2331-2379) returns that framed Value over a channel. Cost is therefore bounded per frame and no data is lost (truncation/refusal still correct; tests.rs:4350-4398 exercises a 128 KiB text result and asserts truncation). Minor stands: not major (no broken user scenario, no unbounded wait) and not critical (bounded, not cost runaway).

**LOCAL TEST:** `scripts/dev-test.sh crates/engine/src/extension_host/command.rs` — run after adding the regression test named above.


### R11-L9-02 — verdict deserialize then size guard

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| FINAL SEVERITY | minor |
| FINAL CONFIDENCE | 7 |
| VENUE | public |
| LOCATION | `crates/engine/src/extension_host/hooks.rs:91` |
| FINGERPRINT | `crates/engine/src/extension_host/hooks.rs:91:verdict-deserialize-then-size-guard` |
| DUPLICATES | none |
| UPSTREAM REFS | none |
| CONFIRMATION | static |
| VERIFIER | stage-d-verifier |
| DATE | 2026-11-22 |

QUOTE — copied from the verified finding file (baseline `bc58781ba`; code lines are verbatim):

```text
91: let verdict: HookVerdictWire = serde_json::from_value(value)
92:     .map_err(|_| "extension hook returned a malformed verdict".to_string())?;
93: let stdout = verdict_stdout(verdict.clone())?;
210: fn verdict_stdout(verdict: HookVerdictWire) -> Result<String, String> {
219:     let stdout = serde_json::to_string(&value)
220:         .map_err(|_| "extension hook verdict is not JSON".to_string())?;
223:     if revises
224:         && crate::hooks::parse_tool_call_before_stdout(&stdout)
230:     Ok(stdout)
```

**CALL PATH:** extension pre-execute hook -> hooks.rs:76 host.call -> serde_json::from_value::<HookVerdictWire> (91) -> verdict_stdout (93/210) -> serde_json::to_string (219) -> revises-only size guard (223-229) -> Ok(stdout) (230) -> HookResult.stdout (111)

**TRIGGER:** an extension hook verdict carries a very large `reason` (Deny/Ask) or `text` (Annotate) field, up to the 32 MiB protocol frame cap.

**MECHANISM:** line 91 fully deserializes the plugin-controlled verdict before any size validation, allocating String fields up to the protocol frame cap. `verdict_stdout` re-serializes the verdict into `stdout` at line 219; the only size guard (line 223-229) is gated on `revises` (the `Revise` variant). For `Deny`/`Ask`/`Annotate`, a huge `reason`/`text` is serialized and returned at line 230 with no explicit byte cap before being stored in `HookResult.stdout` (line 111). The truncation that `parse_tool_call_before_stdout` performs on parsed `reason`/`additionalContext` (hooks/executor.rs:1048-1071, `sanitized_hook_field`, `HOOK_TEXT_FIELD_MAX_CHARS = 2000`) applies to the parsed struct, not to the raw `stdout` string retained here.

**IMPACT:** a hostile or buggy extension can make a hook verdict return a multi-megabyte stdout that is held and propagated as hook output, despite the project's 2,000-character hook-text field limit. Transient allocation occurs before any cap, so memory use scales with the protocol frame cap (32 MiB) rather than the intended field limit; repeated hooks multiply this. Bounded by the protocol cap, so minor.

**EVIDENCE:** `HOOK_TEXT_FIELD_MAX_CHARS = 2000` is defined in hooks/executor.rs:579 and applied in `sanitized_hook_field`, but hooks.rs:223 only invokes that validation for `revises`. No pre-deserialization size check exists on `value` at line 91. protocol.rs:56 caps frames at 32 MiB, bounding but not preventing the pre-guard cost. Hooks tests cover valid verdicts but not oversized non-revise fields.

**FIX:** apply the existing `parse_tool_call_before_stdout` size validation to every verdict variant, not just `Revise`, and cap `reason`/`text` before `serde_json::from_value` (inspect raw `Value` field lengths) so no oversized copy is allocated before the guard.

**REGRESSION CHECK:** a test where a `Deny`/`Annotate` verdict carries a field above `HOOK_TEXT_FIELD_MAX_CHARS` and asserts the stored stdout is bounded would catch reintroduction. None present.

**CORRECTION:** Impact narrowed — the 2,000-char hook field limit is applied downstream (parse_tool_call_before_stdout / sanitized_hook_field) before model/UI; the real effect is transient, frame-bounded memory, not an unbounded blob propagated as hook output. The deserialization-before-cap / revises-only-guard mechanism itself is confirmed.

**VERIFICATION (reviewer's own check):** Opened hooks.rs directly. Line 91 `let verdict: HookVerdictWire = serde_json::from_value(value)` deserializes the plugin verdict before any validation; verdict_stdout (210-230) re-serializes at 219 `let stdout = serde_json::to_string(&value)` and the only size guard at 223-226 is gated on `revises` (`if revises && crate::hooks::parse_tool_call_before_stdout(&stdout).updated_input.is_none()`), so Deny/Ask/Annotate reason/text reach line 230 `Ok(stdout)` with no explicit byte cap and are stored at line 111 `stdout: answer.unwrap_or_default()`. CALL PATH is reachable: tool_before_hooks (18) -> host.call (76) -> from_value (91) -> verdict_stdout (93) -> HookResult.stdout (111). The 32 MiB bound is real (protocol.rs:56 MAX_FRAME; read_frame 334-337 checks length before allocating; supervisor.rs:1995 routes responses through read_frame; call() 2331-2379 returns that framed Value), so cost is bounded and there is no data loss -> minor, not major. CORRECTION applies to the child's IMPACT wording: `HOOK_TEXT_FIELD_MAX_CHARS = 2000` (hooks/executor.rs:579) IS enforced on reason/additionalContext before they reach model/UI — turn_loop.rs:7672/7698/7716 funnel stdout through parse_tool_call_before_stdout, whose sanitized_hook_field (executor.rs:975-982; applied at 1048-1051 and 1068-1071) bounds them. The residual effect is transient, frame-bounded allocation of the raw stdout string, not propagation of a multi-megabyte field into hook output/decisions.

**LOCAL TEST:** `scripts/dev-test.sh crates/engine/src/extension_host/hooks.rs` — run after adding the regression test named above.


## Theme L10 — Crash-atomic durability, idempotent replay

Refs: #6555, #6556 (crash-atomic writes and replay).

### R11-L10-01 — materialize file rename without fsync

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| FINAL SEVERITY | minor |
| FINAL CONFIDENCE | 8 |
| VENUE | public |
| LOCATION | `crates/engine/src/extension_host/mod.rs:277` |
| FINGERPRINT | `crates/engine/src/extension_host/mod.rs:277:materialize-file-rename-without-fsync` |
| DUPLICATES | none |
| UPSTREAM REFS | none |
| CONFIRMATION | static |
| VERIFIER | stage-d-verifier-R11-L10 |
| DATE | 2026-11-22 |

QUOTE — copied from the verified finding file (baseline `bc58781ba`; code lines are verbatim):

```text
        std::fs::write(&staging, bytes)
            .map_err(|error| format!("cannot write {}: {error}", staging.display()))?;
        #[cfg(unix)]
        {
            use std::os::unix::fs::PermissionsExt;
            let _ = std::fs::set_permissions(&staging, std::fs::Permissions::from_mode(0o400));
        }
        if let Err(error) = std::fs::rename(&staging, &path) {
            let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&staging);
            if !matches(&path) {
```

**CALL PATH:** ExtensionHostManager host ensure -> plan_launch (mod.rs:711) -> materialize_bundle (mod.rs:710, 243) -> materialize_file (mod.rs:277) -> std::fs::write(staging) (284) -> std::fs::rename(staging, path) (291) -> read-back matches (299) -> Ok(path)

**TRIGGER:** crash or power loss after the rename at mod.rs:291 but before the OS flushes the staging file's bytes and its directory entry to durable storage.

**MECHANISM:** materialize_file writes the embedded bytes to a private UUID staging file, marks it read-only, renames it over the final path, then treats a successful read-back (`matches`, defined at line 279 and re-checked at line 299) as its receipt and returns Ok(path). There is no sync_all/sync_data on the staging file before the rename and no fsync of the parent directory after it; a grep of mod.rs for sync_all/sync_data/OpenOptions returns no matches at all. The read-back observes the page cache, so Ok(path) is returned before the bytes are proven durable — the effect's receipt precedes its durability.

**IMPACT:** A power loss after line 291 can leave the content-addressed bundle file zero-length or partial on disk even though materialize_bundle already reported success; a native host could be launched against a non-durable bundle. Blast radius is limited and self-healing: the target directory is keyed by the bundle's sha256 (mod.rs:244, 266) and every host ensure re-runs materialize_bundle (mod.rs:710, 3257, 3343), whose matches check (279/299) rewrites any missing or mismatched file on the next start. No user data is lost; the durability contract is nonetheless violated, so severity is minor.

**EVIDENCE:** A grep of crates/engine/src/extension_host for sync_all/sync_data/persist finds exactly one fsync site in the whole unit — windows.rs:499, where a copied runtime.exe is synced before its own receipt — so the omission in mod.rs is a deliberate asymmetry, not a shared durable-write helper. materialize_bundle is invoked at mod.rs:710, 3257 and 3343, confirming verify-on-load runs on every host ensure. No crash-injection or fsync regression test exists in mod.rs's test module.

**FIX:** After std::fs::write(&staging, bytes) (line 284) and before std::fs::rename (line 291), open the staging file and call sync_all() exactly as windows.rs:499 does; after a successful rename, open the parent directory and call sync_all() so the new directory entry is durable. Return Ok(path) only after both syncs succeed.

**REGRESSION CHECK:** smallest check is a static guard that asserts every std::fs::rename in mod.rs has a preceding sync_all on the staged file and a following sync_all on the parent directory; a dynamic crash-injection test that powers down between rename and flush would be stronger but none exists in scope.

**CORRECTION:** Minor call-path label fix — materialize_bundle (710) and plan_launch (711) are sibling calls inside prepare_launch (675), not `plan_launch -> materialize_bundle` as the CALL PATH line reads; reachability and mechanism are unchanged. Severity and confidence unchanged.

**VERIFICATION (reviewer's own check):** Opened mod.rs:277-303 at baseline bc58781ba. The quoted mechanism is accurate: line 284 `std::fs::write(&staging, bytes)` writes embedded bytes to a UUID staging file, line 289 sets 0o400, line 291 `std::fs::rename(&staging, &path)` publishes it, and line 299 re-checks `matches` (closure at 279: `std::fs::read(path).is_ok_and(|on_disk| on_disk == bytes)`) before `Ok(path)` at 303. `git grep -E 'sync_all|sync_data|persist|OpenOptions' bc58781ba -- crates/engine/src/extension_host/mod.rs` returns no matches, confirming no file fsync before rename and no parent-directory fsync after; the unit's only fsync is windows.rs:499 (`target.sync_all()?` after copying runtime.exe), confirming the asymmetry rather than a shared durable-write helper. Both child-cited mitigations confirmed from code: (1) content addressing — `bundle_sha256()` (mod.rs:234) feeds `supervisor::bundle_dir(root, sha256)` (supervisor.rs:2650: `root.join("extension-host").join(sha256)`), so a torn file cannot poison another build's directory; (2) verify-on-load repair — materialize_file's `if !matches(&path)` guard (mod.rs:279-282) rewrites any missing or mismatched file on each call. Call sites confirmed at 710 (prepare_launch, the normal host-ensure path), 3257 (tier-0 restart), 3343 (materialize default builtins via spawn_blocking), so repair re-runs on every ensure. Reachability holds: prepare_launch -> materialize_bundle(710) -> materialize_file(277) is a real path; the TRIGGER (power loss after rename at 291 before the OS flushes bytes/dir entry) is a genuine OS-level window. Impact correctly bounded: bytes are embedded, content-addressed and self-healing; no user data loss, only a transient non-durable bundle repaired on next start — a narrow edge case with a workaround, so minor (rubric §6 minor row) and confidence 8 (quote present, mechanism traced; power-loss consequence remains inference) are retained.

**LOCAL TEST:** `scripts/dev-test.sh crates/engine/src/extension_host/mod.rs` — run after adding the regression test named above.

issues.body:
# engine/src/fleet/, work_graph, hooks: 8 verified defects from R10 (baseline bc58781ba)

## How to read this document (terms used below)

- **R<number>** — review unit, one area of the codebase; this document is about R10.
- **L<number>** — one of twelve review lenses (themes) applied to every unit; the table below names each lens.
- **P0 / P1 / P2** — priority rank: P0 highest, P2 lowest. It orders the work, not the severity of a finding.
- **Stage D** — the verification step: every cited line was opened at the baseline, the reachability was traced, and severity was re-scored. **Stage E** — the drafting step that produced this report.
- **Baseline `bc58781ba`** — the exact commit every quote refers to; re-check before acting if `main` has moved.
- **Confirmed** — a verifier opened the cited line, traced a reachable path and kept the finding; rejected and uncertain findings are not here.
- **Public** — this issue contains only findings cleared for a public report; security-class findings are handled through a separate private channel.
- **needs-test** — the written proof is static; a focused test named in the finding would settle the remaining question. No test was run in this audit.
- **Cell** — one audit cell: a review unit crossed with one lens; finding IDs keep the cell number, so a gap in numbering means a candidate was rejected, marked duplicate or routed to the private index.
- **NOT READ** — a scope marker in a cell: that region was not opened, so no claim is made about it.
- **not-applicable / sampled-rescan-passed** — negative-check outcomes: the lens did not apply to that cell, or a sampled rescan found no new signal.
- **Refs #N / UPSTREAM REFS** — existing tracked issues related to the theme or to the exact code site; they are cross-links, never a claim to close or fix those issues. A 500-issue open/closed sweep found no exact duplicate of these findings at the same file and line.
- **CALL PATH, TRIGGER, MECHANISM, IMPACT, EVIDENCE, FIX, REGRESSION CHECK** — copied verbatim from the verified finding file. CALL PATH = how a user reaches the code; TRIGGER = the condition that fires it; MECHANISM = what the code actually does; IMPACT = what the user sees; EVIDENCE = the supporting lines; FIX = recommended change; REGRESSION CHECK = the test that should be added.

Unit R10 (P1 — highest priority is P0, then P1, then P2), fleet lifecycle, work graph, hook dispatch. Confirmed unique findings: **10** — **8 public** in this draft and **2** withheld as private-advisory or held. Finding IDs keep their original cell numbers; a gap means the candidate was rejected, marked duplicate or routed to the private index.

## Coverage

- Files scanned: all 42 paths in the unit manifest were covered by at least one of the twelve theme scans; per-cell detail was recorded during the audit.
- Files read: every signal-matched production region was opened and quoted by the capturing and verifying agents; the exact per-theme counts and regions are in those cell files.
- Files not read: full sequential line-by-line reads of all files were not performed. Each cell records its own `NOT READ` scope; no claim is made beyond the matched regions.
- Themes applied: all twelve, L1–L12 — bugs, logic, edge cases, error handling, security, ordering, process lifecycle, fail-closed behaviour, resource limits, durable writes, async blocking, platform and Unicode. Each theme section below names its lens and its related tracked issue.
- Baseline: `bc58781ba` for every quote and every verification.
- Negative checks: not-applicable 7/12 cells, sampled-rescan-passed 5/12 cells.
- needs-test items: R10-L6-01. No test or product run happened in this audit.

## Related upstream issues

These are cross-links found in a sweep of 500 open and closed issues; none is a duplicate at the same file and line.

| Issue | State | Title |
|---|---|---|
| #6555 | CLOSED | [audit] Durable writes not crash-atomic (tmp+rename without fsync) |
| #6559 | OPEN | [audit] Fail-open paths, swallowed errors, and false-PASS gates |
| #7071 | CLOSED | zh-Hans and other locales: common TUI strings hardcoded English |
| #7328 | OPEN | Provider failures: diagnostic log has no cause, typed code dropped |

## Contents

| finding id | final severity | theme | one-line problem | confirmation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| R10-L10-01 | major | L10 | append flush without fsync | static |
| R10-L10-02 | minor | L10 | webhook retry without idempotency key | static |
| R10-L12-01 | minor | L12 | store error bypasses locale translation | static |
| R10-L4-01 | minor | L4 | home error empty path fallback misclassifies fleet scope | static |
| R10-L6-01 | minor | L6 | cached seq recovery two process duplicate | needs-test <static proof shows recovery is cached once and a second process is acknowledged by the code; demonstrating duplicate seq end-to-end needs an interleaved two-writer test, which is not run here> |
| R10-L8-01 | minor | L8 | flush acks after failed durable append | static |
| R10-L8-02 | minor | L8 | lane load error collapsed to owner missing | static |
| R10-L9-01 | minor | L9 | oversized batch error fan out | static |

## Planned-work issue card

- **Status:** verified at baseline `bc58781ba`; not fixed in code by this audit.
- **Ways to help without Rust (do these first):**
    - Reproduce or confirm a finding on the baseline by following its `TRIGGER` in the exact file listed below; report whether you see the described result.
    - Review the `IMPACT` wording for accuracy and add a real-world example where you have seen this happen.
    - Check the related tracked issue listed under each theme and report whether this finding is already covered there.
    - Improve the documentation or user-facing message for the locale and wording findings.
    Exact files for this unit:
    - `crates/engine/src/fleet/members.rs`
    - `crates/engine/src/fleet/store.rs`
    - `crates/engine/src/rlm/bridge.rs`
    - `crates/engine/src/work_graph/runtime.rs`
    - `crates/hooks/src/lib.rs`
    - `crates/hooks/src/lifecycle_outbox.rs`
- **Ways to help with Rust:** add the regression test named in `REGRESSION CHECK`, make the minimal fix described in `FIX`, then run the focused test.
- **Local test command:** `scripts/dev-test.sh <path-from-LOCATION>`; the script maps a source path to the fastest crate test and refuses a green run when a filter matches nothing. Each finding also has its own `LOCAL TEST` line.
- **Done-when:** every finding here has a regression test that fails without the fix and passes with it; the focused area test is green; no compiler warning is silenced and no error is hidden to make a test pass; `scripts/preflight.sh --check` is green for the area you touched.
- **What maintainers already hold:** stage-D verification for every finding (quote opened at baseline, reachability traced, severity re-scored), the dedup decision, the private-advisory routing and this draft. Nothing has been fixed in code by this audit.
- **How to claim:** claim a finding by commenting on this issue with its finding ID; one finding per PR keeps the change reviewable. The maintainer resolves conflicts with `main` so contributors never rebase around our churn.


## Theme L4 — Error handling — swallowed cause, wrong fallback

Refs: none — new finding in this audit.

### R10-L4-01 — home error empty path fallback misclassifies fleet scope

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| FINAL SEVERITY | minor |
| FINAL CONFIDENCE | 8 |
| VENUE | public |
| LOCATION | `crates/engine/src/fleet/store.rs:881` |
| FINGERPRINT | `crates/engine/src/fleet/store.rs:881:home-error-empty-path-fallback-misclassifies-fleet-scope` |
| DUPLICATES | none |
| UPSTREAM REFS | none |
| CONFIRMATION | static |
| VERIFIER | stage-d-verifier-R10-L4 |
| DATE | 2026-11-22 |

QUOTE — copied from the verified finding file (baseline `bc58781ba`; code lines are verbatim):

```text
877:     let fleet = FleetFile::parse(&text).map_err(|e| FleetStoreError::Parse {
878:         path: path.display().to_string(),
879:         message: e.to_string(),
880:     })?;
881:     let scope = if path.starts_with(personal_fleets_dir().unwrap_or_default()) {
882:         FleetScope::Personal
883:     } else {
884:         FleetScope::Workspace
885:     };
886:     Ok((fleet, scope))
```

**CALL PATH:** codewhale_config::codewhale_home() -> Err -> personal_fleets_dir() (store.rs:592-603) -> Err -> load_fleet_at() (store.rs:881) -> unwrap_or_default() = empty PathBuf -> path.starts_with(empty) = true -> FleetScope::Personal -> callers: exact.rs:155-156 freeze_saved_fleet -> QualifiedFleetId.origin (exact.rs:355) -> cost_status::record_runtime_usage_async(origin.scope()) (exact.rs:797); members.rs:334/379 save_fleet; tui/src/lib.rs:8275 scope.label()

**TRIGGER:** HOME is unset/invalid (or CODEWHALE_HOME cannot be resolved) so codewhale_config::codewhale_home() returns Err, while load_fleet_at() is asked to classify a workspace-scoped fleet file.

**MECHANISM:** personal_fleets_dir() (store.rs:592-603) returns Err(FleetStoreError::Io) when codewhale_config::codewhale_home() fails to resolve a home. At line 881 the error is swallowed by unwrap_or_default(), which for PathBuf yields an empty path. Path::starts_with returns true when the base has no components, so an empty PathBuf is a prefix of every path; any fleet file, including one under the workspace store, is classified FleetScope::Personal. No log or error reaches the caller — load_fleet_at returns Ok with a wrong scope.

**IMPACT:** In a headless/container session where HOME is unset, a workspace Fleet is silently classified Personal. That value flows into freeze_saved_fleet (exact.rs:155-156) and becomes QualifiedFleetId.origin = scope.label() (exact.rs:355), which drives cost attribution via record_runtime_usage_async(origin.scope()) (exact.rs:797) — runtime spend is recorded under the wrong scope. TUI fleet pickers display the wrong "personal" label (tui/src/lib.rs:8275), and save_fleet/member-edit callers receive the wrong scope (members.rs:334/379). The underlying home-resolution error is lost with no durable trace.

**EVIDENCE:** personal_fleets_dir() signature and error path at store.rs:592-603. Every other call site in this file handles the Result rather than defaulting it: line 630 uses the Result directly, 652/837/947/1248 use `?`, 689/984/999 use `if let Ok(dir)`, 764/1066/1088 use `.ok()`. Line 881 is the sole unwrap_or_default() in the file. exact.rs:355 sets origin from scope.label(); exact.rs:797 uses origin.scope() for cost. Existing test store.rs:1797-1805 asserts Workspace scope only while home resolves; no test covers codewhale_home() failure. RISK NOTE: save_fleet re-calls personal_fleets_dir()? (store.rs:947) and will fail cleanly in the same broken-home condition, so no misdirected write occurs; the silent damage is the wrong scope label/receipt origin and its cost attribution.

**FIX:** Propagate the resolution error instead of substituting an empty path: `let scope = match personal_fleets_dir() { Ok(dir) if path.starts_with(&dir) => FleetScope::Personal, Ok(_) => FleetScope::Workspace, Err(e) => return Err(e) };` This makes load_fleet_at fail loudly when scope cannot be determined, matching every other call site in store.rs.

**REGRESSION CHECK:** Unit test that unsets HOME/CODEWHALE_HOME, saves a Fleet at FleetScope::Workspace in a temp workspace, then calls load_fleet_at on that path and asserts it returns Err (not Ok with FleetScope::Personal). The existing store.rs:1797-1805 test does not cover the failure path.

**CORRECTION:** EVIDENCE overstatement corrected — line 881 is not the file's only `unwrap_or_default()` (store.rs:722 file_stem and 1201 provider also use it); it is the only one on the home-resolution path, so the mechanism is unaffected. IMPACT narrowed — the cost-attribution leg (`cost_status.rs:797 origin.scope()`) is not fully traced: `accounting_origin` is a separate parameter built from a saved-operation lease (tui/src/lib.rs:15769-15770 `usage_origin(scope_token())`), not directly from QualifiedFleetId.origin; confirmed downstream effects are the label at exact.rs:355 and tui/src/lib.rs:8278. Severity kept out of major for these reasons.

**VERIFICATION (reviewer's own check):** Opened at baseline bc58781ba. store.rs:881 reads exactly `let scope = if path.starts_with(personal_fleets_dir().unwrap_or_default()) {` followed by `FleetScope::Personal` / `FleetScope::Workspace`; store.rs:597-602 shows personal_fleets_dir() maps a failed `codewhale_config::codewhale_home()` to `FleetStoreError::Io`. The error premise is real: crates/paths/src/lib.rs:144-149 returns Err for a relative HOME and crates/config/src/state_dirs.rs:17-21 turns Ok(None) into Err via `.context(...)`. The `starts_with(empty)==true` premise is confirmed from the toolchain stdlib: path.rs:2816 `iter_after(self.components(), base.components()).is_some()` and path.rs:315-316 return Some on `(Some(_), None)` / `(None, None)`, so an empty base prefixes every path. Reachable: load_fleet_at has production callers (exact.rs:155, members.rs:334/379/497, identity.rs:51, tui/src/lib.rs:8275/11213, config_policy.rs:255) and home-resolution failure is tolerated at startup (tui/src/lib.rs:4672 `unwrap_or_else(|_| PathBuf::from("~/.codewhale"))`), so execution reaches the site. Impact is genuine but bounded: members.rs:358/386 pass the wrong Personal scope into save_fleet, which calls ensure_fleets_dir -> personal_fleets_dir()? (store.rs:652/897) and fails cleanly in the same broken-home state, so no misdirected write; no data loss, crash or cost runaway. The confirmed silent harm is the wrong scope label in QualifiedFleetId.origin (exact.rs:355, "user" vs "folder" per store.rs:91-95) and in the diagnostic owner string (tui/src/lib.rs:8278). Trigger is a broken-home misconfiguration with a direct workaround (fix HOME/CODEWHALE_HOME), matching the minor row. Existing test store.rs:1792-1805 exercises load_fleet (by name) with a resolved home only; no test covers load_fleet_at under home failure.

**LOCAL TEST:** `scripts/dev-test.sh crates/engine/src/fleet/store.rs` — run after adding the regression test named above.


## Theme L6 — Ordering, generation, TOCTOU

Refs: #6557 (ordering and generation fences).

### R10-L6-01 — cached seq recovery two process duplicate

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| FINAL SEVERITY | minor |
| FINAL CONFIDENCE | 7 |
| VENUE | public |
| LOCATION | `crates/hooks/src/lifecycle_outbox.rs:356` |
| FINGERPRINT | `crates/hooks/src/lifecycle_outbox.rs:356:cached-seq-recovery-two-process-duplicate` |
| DUPLICATES | none |
| UPSTREAM REFS | none |
| CONFIRMATION | needs-test <static proof shows recovery is cached once and a second process is acknowledged by the code; demonstrating duplicate seq end-to-end needs an interleaved two-writer test, which is not run here> |
| VERIFIER | stage-D-verifier-R10-L6 |
| DATE | 2026-11-22 |

QUOTE — copied from the verified finding file (baseline `bc58781ba`; code lines are verbatim):

```text
356:         if !self.recovered {
357:             self.next_seq = recover_last_seq(&self.path).await?;
358:             self.recovered = true;
359:         }
360:
361:         let mut lines = Vec::with_capacity(events.len());
362:         let mut webhook_posts = Vec::new();
363:         for event in events {
364:             let seq = self.next_seq;
365:             self.next_seq = self.next_seq.saturating_add(1);
```

**CALL PATH:** LifecycleOutbox::emit (hooks/src/lifecycle_outbox.rs:179) -> OutboxInner::enqueue -> WriterState::run (312) -> WriterState::deliver_batch (348) -> recover_last_seq once (357) -> cached next_seq (364) -> append_lines (419)

**TRIGGER:** Two live Codewhale processes configured with the same outbox file path emit lifecycle events concurrently. Each process's writer task lazily recovers next_seq once from the same on-disk last line (both see the same value), then caches it; both assign identical seq values to distinct events.

**MECHANISM:** `next_seq` is recovered exactly once per writer (`self.recovered` latch at 356-359) and thereafter advanced only in local memory (364-365). `append_lines` uses `crate::open_private_append` (O_APPEND) with no lock spanning recover+append (419-420). The module doc at lines 20-23 promises "seq is monotonic per outbox file", and the append comment at 421-424 explicitly acknowledges "a second process appending to the same file can interleave lines" — so the two-writer case is a designed scenario, not hypothetical. Two concurrent writers recover the same last-line seq and emit duplicate seq values, breaking the documented per-file monotonicity and collapsing distinct events onto the same ordering key.

**IMPACT:** An operator running two Codewhale processes that share an outbox path (e.g. same workspace/config) gets a JSONL audit log in which two different lifecycle events carry the same `seq`. Any downstream consumer that uses `seq` as the ordering/idempotency key for `RuntimeEventEnvelope` (the exact `(binding, seq)` idempotency pattern used in work_graph/runtime.rs:837-840) will treat the second event as a duplicate no-op and silently drop it, or mis-order events from the two writers. The failure is silent: both appends succeed and the file looks well-formed.

**EVIDENCE:** `recover_last_seq` (448-491) reads the last complete line once and returns `seq+1`; no exclusive file lock is taken across recovery and append. Tests `seq_is_monotonic_and_recovers_across_reopen` (840-875) and `missing_and_empty_files_start_at_seq_1` (877-884) cover only sequential reopen of a single writer — no test exercises two live writers on one file. The `[fact]` claim of a second-process appending scenario is from the code's own comment at 421-424.

**FIX:** Either (a) document and enforce a single-writer-per-file contract (per-process outbox path, e.g. include PID in the path) so `next_seq` caching is valid, or (b) drop the `recovered` latch and re-read the last committed seq under an exclusive advisory file lock immediately before each batch append, assigning seqs while the lock is held so two processes cannot recover the same value.

**REGRESSION CHECK:** Add a test that spawns two `WriterState` instances pointed at one temp path, interleaves emits between them, and asserts the resulting seq column is globally unique and strictly increasing (1..N). This fails on the current code because both writers start from the same recovered value.

Call path is reachable: `emit` -> `deliver_batch` spawns `sink.post_payload(payload)` (lifecycle_outbox.rs:399-400), and the sink is built from config `webhook_url`/`webhook_token` at `crates/app-server/src/exec_agent.rs:887-891`. The trigger (endpoint commits the side effect but its response is lost, then the identical body is resent) is a real at-least-once delivery with no dedup handle offered; `event.seq` is only a non-contractual correlation field, not a documented receiver dedup key. Impact stays minor: observability-only, delivery failures are logged and dropped, retries capped at 2, so at most one duplicate notification.

**LOCAL TEST:** `scripts/dev-test.sh crates/hooks/src/lib.rs` — run after adding the regression test named above.


## Theme L12 — Platform, Unicode, display width, locale

Refs: #7048, #6953, #7093, #7071 (platform and Unicode).

### R10-L12-01 — store error bypasses locale translation

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| FINAL SEVERITY | minor |
| FINAL CONFIDENCE | 8 |
| VENUE | public |
| LOCATION | `crates/engine/src/fleet/members.rs:131` |
| FINGERPRINT | `crates/engine/src/fleet/members.rs:131:store-error-bypasses-locale-translation` |
| DUPLICATES | none |
| UPSTREAM REFS | none |
| CONFIRMATION | static |
| VERIFIER | stage-d-verifier-R10-L12 |
| DATE | 2026-11-22 |

QUOTE — copied from the verified finding file (baseline `bc58781ba`; code lines are verbatim):

```text
128             Self::NotInFleet { route, fleet } => tr(locale, MessageId::FleetModelErrorNotInFleet)
129                 .replace("{route}", route)
130                 .replace("{fleet}", fleet),
131             Self::Store(error) => error.to_string(),
132         }
133     }
```

**CALL PATH:** TUI fleet-model toggle (crates/tui/src/tui/ui/handlers.rs:130) -> toggle_fleet_model (crates/engine/src/fleet/members.rs:227/328/373) -> Err(FleetModelError::Store(FleetStoreError::...)) -> FleetModelError::message(locale) (members.rs:119, 131) -> error.to_string() -> handlers.rs:144 -> set_sticky_status (status toast)

**TRIGGER:** app.ui_locale is a non-English locale (e.g. ZhHans) and the fleet load/save fails during `/fleet add|remove` or the roster picker's ⇧F toggle — missing, invalid, ambiguous, parse-failed, name-taken, or unwritable fleet file — producing FleetModelError::Store.

**MECHANISM:** `FleetModelError::message(locale)` is documented at members.rs:117 as "The person-facing explanation in `locale`" and every sibling variant calls `tr(locale, MessageId::...)`. The `Store` variant at line 131 instead calls `error.to_string()` on `FleetStoreError`, whose `thiserror` `#[error("...")]` formats (store.rs:267-280: "invalid fleet: {0}", "fleet file not found: {0}", "failed to parse {path}: {message}", etc.) are hardcoded English literals with no locale parameter. The `locale` argument is ignored on this branch, so the English text reaches the status toast unchanged.

**IMPACT:** A user whose UI locale is not English sees an English error string embedded in an otherwise localized `FleetToggleFailed` toast (handlers.rs:143-145) whenever the fleet file cannot be loaded or saved — for example a non-English user on a machine with a malformed `.codewhale/fleet/*.json` gets "fleet file not found: ..." while every other message in the surface is in their language. This is wording/locale drift only: no data loss, no data-integrity or security effect, and the operation still fails closed.

**EVIDENCE:** Nearby guards checked — members.rs:94-95 explicitly states the type exists so the surface picks the person's locale, and `Display` (line 136-139) is the deliberate English-for-logs form, so the `Store` branch is inconsistent with `message`'s own contract rather than intentional. The person-facing call sites are `crates/tui/src/tui/ui/handlers.rs:144` and `crates/tui/src/tui/ui/apply.rs:3030, 3049`, both passing `app.ui_locale`/`locale` into `error.message(locale)`. `crates/tui/AGENTS.md` requires "User-visible prose uses `tr(locale, MessageId::...)`". `FleetStoreError` (crates/engine/src/fleet/store.rs:266-281) has six hardcoded-English `#[error(...)]` formats and no locale-aware message method. Tests at members.rs:1047 and :1138 exercise `message(Locale::En)` only, so a non-English assertion would have caught this; none exists. No L12 candidate ID maps to unit R10 (plan §4.3 assigns #7048 to R8/R17 and #6953 to R19/R20; zone F02 has no candidate set), so this is CLASS new, not a known:#N re-report.

**FIX:** Either (a) add `MessageId` variants + translations for the six `FleetStoreError` kinds and map them in `FleetModelError::message`, passing the structured path/message fields as `{path}`/`{message}` placeholders; or (b) at minimum, wrap the raw error as a `{error}` placeholder inside an already-localized generic `FleetModelErrorStore` message when `locale != Locale::En`. Keep `Display` (logs) on the raw English `error.to_string()`.

**REGRESSION CHECK:** Add a test alongside members.rs:1047 building `FleetModelError::Store(FleetStoreError::NotFound(...))` and asserting `err.message(Locale::ZhHans)` differs from `err.message(Locale::En)` and contains no English literal from store.rs:267-280. (No test is run in this pipeline.)

**CORRECTION:** Two minor evidence imprecisions, mechanism unchanged: (1) the EVIDENCE cites a second `message(Locale::En)` test at members.rs:1138, but that line asserts on `change_receipt(Locale::En, ...)`; only members.rs:1047 calls `message(Locale::En)`; (2) `Display` (members.rs:136-139) calls `self.message(Locale::En)` rather than directly `error.to_string()` — still the English log form, so the Store branch's locale-ignoring behavior is unchanged.

**VERIFICATION (reviewer's own check):** Opened at baseline bc58781ba. members.rs:117 documents message(locale) as "The person-facing explanation in `locale`" and the doc on the enum states the surface "picks the person's locale; `Display` is the English form for logs". Every sibling branch uses tr(locale, MessageId::...); line 131 reads `Self::Store(error) => error.to_string(),` ignoring locale. store.rs:266-281 confirms all six FleetStoreError `#[error("...")]` formats are hardcoded English with no locale parameter (e.g. "fleet file not found: {0}", "failed to parse {path}: {message}"). Reachability confirmed: toggle_fleet_model (members.rs:369) propagates FleetStoreError via `?` from resolve_selected_fleet/load_fleet_at/save_fleet through From<FleetStoreError> to FleetModelError::Store, and handlers.rs:130/143-145 wraps `error.message(locale)` inside tr(locale, MessageId::FleetToggleFailed) -> set_sticky_status. Locale files confirm FleetToggleFailed is genuinely translated (zh-Hans.json:1844 "无法更新 Fleet：{error}"), so only the injected {error} stays English — the drift is real. apply.rs:3030/3049 pass ui_locale the same way. crates/tui/AGENTS.md:25 requires "User-visible prose uses `tr(locale, MessageId::...)`". No security/data-integrity effect; operation fails closed.

**LOCAL TEST:** `scripts/dev-test.sh crates/engine/src/fleet/members.rs` — run after adding the regression test named above.

# engine/src/core/authority/, protocol, commands: 3 verified defects from R9 (baseline bc58781ba)

## How to read this document (terms used below)

- **R<number>** — review unit, one area of the codebase; this document is about R9.
- **L<number>** — one of twelve review lenses (themes) applied to every unit; the table below names each lens.
- **P0 / P1 / P2** — priority rank: P0 highest, P2 lowest. It orders the work, not the severity of a finding.
- **Stage D** — the verification step: every cited line was opened at the baseline, the reachability was traced, and severity was re-scored. **Stage E** — the drafting step that produced this report.
- **Baseline `bc58781ba`** — the exact commit every quote refers to; re-check before acting if `main` has moved.
- **Confirmed** — a verifier opened the cited line, traced a reachable path and kept the finding; rejected and uncertain findings are not here.
- **Public** — this issue contains only findings cleared for a public report; security-class findings are handled through a separate private channel.
- **needs-test** — the written proof is static; a focused test named in the finding would settle the remaining question. No test was run in this audit.
- **Cell** — one audit cell: a review unit crossed with one lens; finding IDs keep the cell number, so a gap in numbering means a candidate was rejected, marked duplicate or routed to the private index.
- **NOT READ** — a scope marker in a cell: that region was not opened, so no claim is made about it.
- **not-applicable / sampled-rescan-passed** — negative-check outcomes: the lens did not apply to that cell, or a sampled rescan found no new signal.
- **Refs #N / UPSTREAM REFS** — existing tracked issues related to the theme or to the exact code site; they are cross-links, never a claim to close or fix those issues. A 500-issue open/closed sweep found no exact duplicate of these findings at the same file and line.
- **CALL PATH, TRIGGER, MECHANISM, IMPACT, EVIDENCE, FIX, REGRESSION CHECK** — copied verbatim from the verified finding file. CALL PATH = how a user reaches the code; TRIGGER = the condition that fires it; MECHANISM = what the code actually does; IMPACT = what the user sees; EVIDENCE = the supporting lines; FIX = recommended change; REGRESSION CHECK = the test that should be added.

Unit R9 (P1 — highest priority is P0, then P1, then P2), authority order, command surface, wire schema. Confirmed unique findings: **4** — **3 public** in this draft and **1** withheld as private-advisory or held. Finding IDs keep their original cell numbers; a gap means the candidate was rejected, marked duplicate or routed to the private index.

## Coverage

- Files scanned: all 66 paths in the unit manifest were covered by at least one of the twelve theme scans; per-cell detail was recorded during the audit.
- Files read: every signal-matched production region was opened and quoted by the capturing and verifying agents; the exact per-theme counts and regions are in those cell files.
- Files not read: full sequential line-by-line reads of all files were not performed. Each cell records its own `NOT READ` scope; no claim is made beyond the matched regions.
- Themes applied: all twelve, L1–L12 — bugs, logic, edge cases, error handling, security, ordering, process lifecycle, fail-closed behaviour, resource limits, durable writes, async blocking, platform and Unicode. Each theme section below names its lens and its related tracked issue.
- Baseline: `bc58781ba` for every quote and every verification.
- Negative checks: not-applicable 4/12 cells, sampled-rescan-passed 8/12 cells.
- needs-test items: none in this unit. No test or product run happened in this audit.

## Related upstream issues

These are cross-links found in a sweep of 500 open and closed issues; none is a duplicate at the same file and line.

| Issue | State | Title |
|---|---|---|
| #7071 | CLOSED | zh-Hans and other locales: common TUI strings hardcoded English |

## Contents

| finding id | final severity | theme | one-line problem | confirmation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| R9-L12-01 | minor | L12 | chars total label reports byte length | static <the label/value mismatch is visible in the quoted call and needs no runtime to establish; the exact displayed number depends on the prompt contents> |
| R9-L12-02 | minor | L12 | char budget uses byte length for threshold and omitted count | static <the unit mismatch between the charset-based truncation and the byte-based guard/count is established by the quoted code; no test is run here> |
| R9-L2-01 | major | L2 | approval required precedes typed error category | static |

## Planned-work issue card

- **Status:** verified at baseline `bc58781ba`; not fixed in code by this audit.
- **Ways to help without Rust (do these first):**
    - Reproduce or confirm a finding on the baseline by following its `TRIGGER` in the exact file listed below; report whether you see the described result.
    - Review the `IMPACT` wording for accuracy and add a real-world example where you have seen this happen.
    - Check the related tracked issue listed under each theme and report whether this finding is already covered there.
    - Improve the documentation or user-facing message for the locale and wording findings.
    Exact files for this unit:
    - `crates/commands/src/debug/change.rs`
    - `crates/commands/src/debug/tokens.rs`
    - `crates/engine/src/core/runtime_contract/termination.rs`
- **Ways to help with Rust:** add the regression test named in `REGRESSION CHECK`, make the minimal fix described in `FIX`, then run the focused test.
- **Local test command:** `scripts/dev-test.sh <path-from-LOCATION>`; the script maps a source path to the fastest crate test and refuses a green run when a filter matches nothing. Each finding also has its own `LOCAL TEST` line.
- **Done-when:** every finding here has a regression test that fails without the fix and passes with it; the focused area test is green; no compiler warning is silenced and no error is hidden to make a test pass; `scripts/preflight.sh --check` is green for the area you touched.
- **What maintainers already hold:** stage-D verification for every finding (quote opened at baseline, reachability traced, severity re-scored), the dedup decision, the private-advisory routing and this draft. Nothing has been fixed in code by this audit.
- **How to claim:** claim a finding by commenting on this issue with its finding ID; one finding per PR keeps the change reviewable. The maintainer resolves conflicts with `main` so contributors never rebase around our churn.


## Theme L2 — Logic — conditions, off-by-one, intent drift, cost and pricing

Refs: #7179, #7096, #7067 (cost and pricing correctness).

### R9-L2-01 — approval required precedes typed error category

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| FINAL SEVERITY | major |
| FINAL CONFIDENCE | 7 |
| VENUE | public |
| LOCATION | `crates/engine/src/core/runtime_contract/termination.rs:89` |
| FINGERPRINT | `crates/engine/src/core/runtime_contract/termination.rs:89:approval-required-precedes-typed-error-category` |
| DUPLICATES | none |
| UPSTREAM REFS | none |
| CONFIRMATION | static |
| VERIFIER | verifier-R9-L2 |
| DATE | 2026-11-22 |

QUOTE — copied from the verified finding file (baseline `bc58781ba`; code lines are verbatim):

```text
        TurnOutcomeStatus::Failed
            if matches!(error_category, Some(ErrorCategory::InvalidInput)) =>
        {
            RunTerminationReason::ModelError
        }
        TurnOutcomeStatus::Failed if approval_required => RunTerminationReason::ApprovalRequired,
        TurnOutcomeStatus::Failed => match error_category {
            Some(ErrorCategory::Budget) => RunTerminationReason::BudgetExhausted,
            Some(ErrorCategory::Timeout) => RunTerminationReason::Timeout,
```

**CALL PATH:** app-server exec_agent run loop (crates/app-server/src/exec_agent.rs:1610, 1845) -> engine::core::termination::classify_turn_termination(Failed, Some(Budget/Timeout/Network/Tool/State/Internal), ..., approval_required=true) -> line 89 returns ApprovalRequired

**TRIGGER:** A headless `exec` run where a tool call is denied for approval (sets approval_required=true at exec_agent.rs:1252/1278) and the same run later emits a fatal typed error such as Budget or Network (sets last_error_category=Some(...) at exec_agent.rs:1319), ending in TurnOutcomeStatus::Failed.

**MECHANISM:** For a Failed turn the match arms are ordered InvalidInput -> approval_required -> typed error_category. Only InvalidInput is special-cased to override approval; every other typed cause (Budget, Timeout, Network, Tool, State, Internal) is matched in the final arm, which is unreachable when approval_required is true. The function's own doc comment (lines 62-67) states "the terminal error category wins over historical tool failures ... approval/tool evidence is the fallback when the terminal event has no typed cause" — so approval must be consulted only when error_category is None. The arm order inverts that contract.

**IMPACT:** An automated `exec` run that needed approval at one step and then hit a real terminal failure (budget, timeout, network) is reported with termination_reason `approval_required` and process exit code 3 instead of the true cause (e.g. `budget_exhausted`, exit 1). Machine consumers of the exec receipt/JSONL see a misleading failure class. The existing tests cover InvalidInput+approval and None+tool_error but never a typed cause other than InvalidInput combined with approval, so the gap is unguarded.

**EVIDENCE:** Doc contract at termination.rs:62-67; arm order at lines 84-107; approval_required set independently of last_error_category at exec_agent.rs:1252, 1278 vs 1319; both passed together to classifier at exec_agent.rs:1611-1616 and 1845-1850. Tests at termination.rs:200-256 exercise InvalidInput+approval (assert ModelError) but no Budget/Timeout/Network+approval case. The InvalidInput duplication at lines 84-100 (present in both the special guard and the final match arm) is harmless because the guard wins; approval precedence is the real defect.

**FIX:** Move the `TurnOutcomeStatus::Failed if approval_required` arm to after the typed-error match so it applies only when error_category is None (and tool_error_seen is false). Concretely: fold approval into the final `None => if approval_required { ApprovalRequired } else { Unresolved }` branch, keeping the InvalidInput guard first. Add a regression case classify_turn_termination(Failed, Some(Budget), false, true) == BudgetExhausted.

**REGRESSION CHECK:** Unit test in crates/engine/src/core/runtime_contract/termination.rs asserting classify_turn_termination(Failed, Some(ErrorCategory::Budget), false, true) returns RunTerminationReason::BudgetExhausted (currently returns ApprovalRequired).

**CORRECTION:** none

**VERIFICATION (reviewer's own check):** Opened termination.rs:84-90 at bc58781ba — the `TurnOutcomeStatus::Failed if approval_required` arm at line 89 precedes the typed `match error_category` at line 90-107, so every non-InvalidInput typed cause (Budget/Timeout/Network/Tool/State/Internal) is shadowed when approval_required is true; this matches the child's QUOTE verbatim. Doc contract at lines 62-67 says "the terminal error category wins over historical tool failures ... approval/tool evidence is the fallback when the terminal event has no typed cause", confirming intent drift. Reachability traced: exec_agent.rs:1252 (denial) and :1278 (sandbox denial) set approval_required=true; :1319 sets last_error_category on a fatal non-recoverable Error envelope (exec_events.rs:212-214), and :1487-1491 derives it otherwise; both reach classify_turn_termination at :1611-1616 and :1845-1850 with terminal_status=Failed. Static only — not reproduced in a product/test run (CONFIRMATION: static), which caps confidence at 7. Machine-facing mislabel of termination_reason and exit class, not a security class.

**LOCAL TEST:** `scripts/dev-test.sh crates/engine/src/core/runtime_contract/termination.rs` — run after adding the regression test named above.


## Theme L12 — Platform, Unicode, display width, locale

Refs: #7048, #6953, #7093, #7071 (platform and Unicode).

### R9-L12-01 — chars total label reports byte length

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| FINAL SEVERITY | minor |
| FINAL CONFIDENCE | 8 |
| VENUE | public |
| LOCATION | `crates/commands/src/debug/tokens.rs:466` |
| FINGERPRINT | `crates/commands/src/debug/tokens.rs:466:chars-total-label-reports-byte-length` |
| DUPLICATES | none |
| UPSTREAM REFS | none |
| CONFIRMATION | static <the label/value mismatch is visible in the quoted call and needs no runtime to establish; the exact displayed number depends on the prompt contents> |
| VERIFIER | stage-d-verifier-R9-L12 |
| DATE | 2026-11-22 |

QUOTE — copied from the verified finding file (baseline `bc58781ba`; code lines are verbatim):

```text
    let display = if prompt_text.len() > 500 {
        let truncate_at = prompt_text
            .char_indices()
            .take_while(|(i, _)| *i <= 500)
            .last()
            .map_or(0, |(i, _)| i);
        format!(
            "{}...\n\n(truncated, {} chars total)",
            &prompt_text[..truncate_at],
            prompt_text.len()
        )
    } else {
```

**CALL PATH:** `SYSTEM_INFO` (/system, tokens.rs:35-40) -> `SystemCmd` handler dispatch -> `system_prompt` (tokens.rs:448) -> `diagnostics.system_projection()` and prompt assembly (tokens.rs:453-458) -> truncation/display (tokens.rs:459-469) -> `CommandResult::message` (tokens.rs:473)

**TRIGGER:** A user with non-ASCII text in the effective system prompt (for example Cyrillic or CJK project instructions folded into the projection) runs `/system`; the prompt exceeds 500 bytes, so the truncated branch prints the UTF-8 byte length under a label that says "chars".

**MECHANISM:** The truncation boundary itself is correct: `char_indices()` plus `last()` yields the byte offset of a valid char boundary, so `&prompt_text[..truncate_at]` cannot panic on multibyte input. The defect is the reported total: the format argument at line 468 is `prompt_text.len()`, which is the number of UTF-8 bytes (`str::len`), but the literal at line 466 labels it "chars total". For text with multibyte scalar values the printed number is larger than the real character count by up to 4x (2x Cyrillic, 3x CJK), while no byte figure is requested. The byte threshold at line 459 is also a byte budget, but the message never says "bytes".

**IMPACT:** A user reading `/system` output gets a wrong count of the system prompt length whenever that prompt contains non-ASCII text, and may mis-estimate context size (a Chinese prompt of 300 characters is reported as roughly 900 "chars"). This is a Unicode accounting / display drift with no data loss, so minor per rubric row "wording/locale drift without data loss".

**EVIDENCE:** `crates/commands/src/debug/cache.rs:235` deliberately prints `chars={}, bytes={}` from distinct `layer.char_len` and `layer.byte_len` fields, showing the codebase distinguishes the two; `crates/commands/src/diagnostics_reports/receipts.rs:6-12` uses `text.chars().count()` when a `max` is expressed in characters. No test asserts the `/system` length label (grep for "chars total" and "MAX_INLINE_CHANGELOG" found only the two production sites). Nearby guard `char_indices()` was checked and rules out a panic; no test or product run was performed.

**FIX:** Replace the second argument with `prompt_text.chars().count()` so the value matches the "chars" label. If a byte count is genuinely wanted for context budgeting, print both explicitly, as `cache.rs:235` does (for example `{} chars, {} bytes total`), and make the 500 threshold a named byte budget.

**REGRESSION CHECK:** Add a unit test around `system_prompt` that supplies a projection whose prompt is more than 500 bytes of multibyte text (e.g. 300 CJK characters) and asserts the message contains the character count (300) and not the byte count (~900). It fails with the current `len()` argument and passes after switching to `chars().count()`.

**CORRECTION:** none

**VERIFICATION (reviewer's own check):** Opened crates/commands/src/debug/tokens.rs at baseline bc58781ba (HEAD equals baseline). Line 459 gates on `prompt_text.len() > 500` (bytes); line 462 uses `char_indices().take_while(|(i, _)| *i <= 500).last()`, so the truncation boundary is a valid char boundary and cannot panic. Line 466 prints "(truncated, {} chars total)" while line 468 supplies `prompt_text.len()` — a byte count under a "chars" label. Reachability traced: `SYSTEM_INFO` (tokens.rs:35-40, name "system", alias "xitong") -> SystemCmd impl (tokens.rs:72-79, handler `|contexts, _| system_prompt(contexts)`) -> `system_prompt` (448). A multibyte system prompt over 500 bytes therefore prints an inflated "chars total" (up to 3-4x for CJK). No data loss; minor per rubric row "wording/locale drift without data loss".

**LOCAL TEST:** `scripts/dev-test.sh crates/commands/src/debug/tokens.rs` — run after adding the regression test named above.


### R9-L12-02 — char budget uses byte length for threshold and omitted count

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| FINAL SEVERITY | minor |
| FINAL CONFIDENCE | 8 |
| VENUE | public |
| LOCATION | `crates/commands/src/debug/change.rs:161` |
| FINGERPRINT | `crates/commands/src/debug/change.rs:161:char-budget-uses-byte-length-for-threshold-and-omitted-count` |
| DUPLICATES | none |
| UPSTREAM REFS | none |
| CONFIRMATION | static <the unit mismatch between the charset-based truncation and the byte-based guard/count is established by the quoted code; no test is run here> |
| VERIFIER | stage-d-verifier-R9-L12 |
| DATE | 2026-11-22 |

QUOTE — copied from the verified finding file (baseline `bc58781ba`; code lines are verbatim):

```text
pub fn inline_changelog_section(section: &str) -> String {
    if section.len() <= MAX_INLINE_CHANGELOG_CHARS {
        return section.to_string();
    }

    let truncated: String = section.chars().take(MAX_INLINE_CHANGELOG_CHARS).collect();
    format!(
        "{truncated}\n\
\n\
[... {} characters omitted from the bundled Codewhale changelog]",
        section.len() - MAX_INLINE_CHANGELOG_CHARS
    )
```

**CALL PATH:** `ChangeCmd::handler()` (change.rs:36-41) -> `change()` (change.rs:44) -> `change_report()` (change.rs:62) -> `inline_changelog_section(&latest_section)` (change.rs:109) -> threshold/omitted-count at change.rs:152 and :161

**TRIGGER:** The selected bundled changelog section contains non-ASCII characters (for example contributor names in CJK/Cyrillic) such that its UTF-8 byte length exceeds 4096 while its character count is at or below 4096; `/change` then appends a "characters omitted" notice that overstates or invents omitted content.

**MECHANISM:** `MAX_INLINE_CHANGELOG_CHARS` is declared at line 25 with the doc "Maximum length ... (characters)". The truncation at line 156 honours that unit by using `chars().take(4096)`, but the early-return guard at line 152 and the omitted-count arithmetic at line 161 both call `str::len()`, which counts UTF-8 bytes. When bytes exceed 4096 but characters do not, the guard falls through, `truncated` still contains every character, and the message reports `bytes - 4096` as "characters omitted" even though zero characters were omitted. When both exceed 4096, the reported number still overstates the true omitted character count by the number of extra bytes in multibyte scalars.

**IMPACT:** `/change` can claim that content was hidden when the whole section was displayed, or report an inflated omission count, misleading users reading release notes in a locale whose text enters the changelog. No data loss; minor per rubric row "wording/locale drift without data loss".

**EVIDENCE:** Unit mismatch is visible between the constant doc at change.rs:22-25, the byte-based guard at :152, the char-based truncation at :156 and the byte-based count at :161. `crates/commands/src/diagnostics_reports/receipts.rs:6-12` shows the repository's char-budget convention (`text.chars().count() <= max`). No test covers `inline_changelog_section` (grep across `crates/commands/src` found only the definition and its one caller at change.rs:109). No test or product run was performed.

**FIX:** Compute `let total_chars = section.chars().count();` once and use it for both the line 152 guard and the line 161 subtraction, keeping `chars().take(MAX_INLINE_CHANGELOG_CHARS)` for the truncation. Rename nothing else; the constant name and doc then become truthful.

**REGRESSION CHECK:** Add a unit test for `inline_changelog_section` with a 4090-character string containing 10 three-byte CJK characters (≈4110 bytes): assert the output has no "characters omitted" notice. A second case with 4200 CJK characters must report `4200 - 4096 = 104` omitted characters, not a byte-derived number; both fail with the current `len()` arithmetic.

**CORRECTION:** none

**VERIFICATION (reviewer's own check):** Opened crates/commands/src/debug/change.rs at baseline bc58781ba (HEAD equals baseline). Line 25 declares `MAX_INLINE_CHANGELOG_CHARS: usize = 4096` with doc "(characters)"; line 152 guards `section.len() <= MAX_INLINE_CHANGELOG_CHARS` (bytes); line 156 truncates with `section.chars().take(MAX_INLINE_CHANGELOG_CHARS)` (characters); line 160 labels the notice "{} characters omitted" while line 161 computes `section.len() - MAX_INLINE_CHANGELOG_CHARS` (bytes). When bytes exceed 4096 but characters do not, the full section is displayed yet a nonzero "characters omitted" count is reported; when both exceed it, the count is inflated by the extra multibyte bytes. Reachability traced: ChangeCmd::handler (36-41) -> change (44) -> change_report (62) -> inline_changelog_section (109). No data loss; minor per rubric row "wording/locale drift without data loss".

**LOCAL TEST:** `scripts/dev-test.sh crates/commands/src/debug/change.rs` — run after adding the regression test named above.
