## Theme L11 — Async blocking and budget discipline

Refs: #6553 and the #6149 blocking-call rule.

### R2-L11-01 — artifact mutex held across blocking transcript io

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| FINAL SEVERITY | minor |
| FINAL CONFIDENCE | 8 |
| VENUE | public |
| LOCATION | `crates/engine/src/tools/subagent/engine.rs:1360` |
| FINGERPRINT | `engine.rs:1360:artifact-mutex-held-across-blocking-transcript-io` |
| DUPLICATES | none |
| UPSTREAM REFS | none |
| CONFIRMATION | static |
| VERIFIER | verifier-R2-L11-2026-11-22 |
| DATE | 2026-11-22 |

QUOTE — copied from the verified finding file (baseline `bc58781ba`; code lines are verbatim):

```text
        let output = {
            let mut artifact = self.artifact.lock().await;
            let writer = artifact
                .as_mut()
                .ok_or_else(|| anyhow!("child transcript writer is unavailable"))?;
            writer.append_messages(&[], true)?;
            let messages = super::load_subagent_transcript_artifact(
                &writer.state_root,
                &self.authority.owner_agent_id,
            )?;
```

**CALL PATH:** drive_child_actor (engine.rs:2002) -> job.capture_activation_output (engine.rs:2286) -> self.artifact.lock().await (engine.rs:1360) -> writer.append_messages (engine.rs:1364) -> load_subagent_transcript_artifact (engine.rs:1365) -> fs::OpenOptions::open + read_to_string (mod.rs:13400-13403, 13383-13386)

**TRIGGER:** A child turn completes while other sub-agents are active; capture_activation_output runs on a Tokio worker thread for every child that produced streamed text.

**MECHANISM:** capture_activation_output is an async fn invoked directly from drive_child_actor, which runs on the Tokio runtime (engine.rs:2286 has a plain `.await`, not spawn_blocking). It holds the tokio Mutex guard `artifact` across several synchronous `std::fs` operations: writer.append_messages (lines 1364 and 1393) and load_subagent_transcript_artifact (line 1365), the latter opening a state file with fs::OpenOptions::new().open() (mod.rs:13400-13403) and reading up to MAX_SUBAGENT_STATE_BYTES (16 MiB) with read_to_string (mod.rs:13383-13386). These blocking calls execute inline on the Tokio worker while the mutex is held.

**IMPACT:** When several children finish turns concurrently, multiple Tokio worker threads block on disk I/O instead of polling other tasks. The engine's async runtime is starved for the duration of each transcript open/read (up to 16 MiB) and append, delaying tool-result delivery, UI events and cancellation across the whole session. This is the "sync work inline on Tokio" class tracked by #6553; no data is lost, so severity is minor.

**EVIDENCE:** No spawn_blocking wraps this call path — grep for spawn_blocking in engine.rs returns no hits. The sibling callers of the same blocking helpers DO use spawn_blocking (mod.rs:16254 DeliveryEvidence::capture_for_handle; mod.rs:17312 changed_paths/checkpoint_uncommitted; mod.rs:17395 compute_delivery_verification; mod.rs:16361 spawn_prep_blocking), which shows the codebase treats this I/O as blocking elsewhere. load_subagent_transcript_artifact is a plain sync `fn` (mod.rs:13396-13409), confirmed blocking. No test covers the threading of this path; existing tests only assert the resulting output value.

**FIX:** Move the synchronous transcript work off the Tokio runtime: capture the needed inputs (writer state_root, owner_agent_id, streamed_text, admission index, stop reason), run the append + load + selection inside tokio::task::spawn_blocking, and return only the derived ChildActivationOutput to record_child_output. Do not hold `artifact` across the spawn_blocking await; serialize the writer mutation inside the blocking closure or use a blocking mutex confined to that closure.

**REGRESSION CHECK:** A test that spawns a task holding a deliberately slow/blocking transcript read and asserts that an unrelated tokio task makes progress would catch reintroduction; none exists. Static check: grep that capture_activation_output body contains no `.append_messages`/`load_subagent_transcript_artifact` outside a spawn_blocking closure.

**CORRECTION:** Child EVIDENCE line "grep for spawn_blocking in engine.rs returns no hits" is inaccurate — engine.rs:1196, 1746, 2311 do contain spawn_blocking. Correct statement: none of those sites wraps capture_activation_output or its two blocking helpers; the substantive mechanism is unaffected.

**VERIFICATION (reviewer's own check):** Opened engine.rs:1348-1424 at baseline bc58781ba (HEAD == baseline). At 1360 `let mut artifact = self.artifact.lock().await;` acquires the tokio Mutex; within the same block `writer.append_messages(&[], true)?;` (1364) and `super::load_subagent_transcript_artifact(&writer.state_root, &self.authority.owner_agent_id)?;` (1365) run while the guard is live (held until the block ends at 1412). append_messages (mod.rs:12827-12841) calls append_private_subagent_transcript (mod.rs:13436-13451): fs::OpenOptions::open (13465) and `file.sync_all()` (13448) — synchronous fs. load_subagent_transcript_artifact (mod.rs:12902-12907) -> load_subagent_transcript_projection (12921-12928) -> read_subagent_state_file (13371-13393): open_subagent_state_file (fs::OpenOptions::open, 13400-13403) and `file.take(MAX_SUBAGENT_STATE_BYTES + 1).read_to_string(&mut raw)?` (13385-13386, 16 MiB cap at 13369). Both are plain sync `fn`s, so blocking disk I/O runs inline on the Tokio worker under the artifact mutex. capture_activation_output is `async fn` (1348) reached with a plain `.await` at engine.rs:2286 in drive_child_actor's settle path (drive_child_actor defined 2002), with no spawn_blocking around this call path. Fact (blocking fs under a held tokio Mutex) and impact (worker starvation/contention, no data loss) confirmed independently. Severity minor and confidence 8 unchanged per §6.

**LOCAL TEST:** `scripts/dev-test.sh crates/engine/src/tools/subagent/engine.rs` — run after adding the regression test named above.


### R2-L11-02 — artifact mutex held across await

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| FINAL SEVERITY | minor |
| FINAL CONFIDENCE | 8 |
| VENUE | public |
| LOCATION | `crates/engine/src/tools/subagent/engine.rs:1446` |
| FINGERPRINT | `engine.rs:1446:artifact-mutex-held-across-await` |
| DUPLICATES | none |
| UPSTREAM REFS | none |
| CONFIRMATION | static |
| VERIFIER | verifier-R2-L11-2026-11-22 |
| DATE | 2026-11-22 |

QUOTE — copied from the verified finding file (baseline `bc58781ba`; code lines are verbatim):

```text
        let mut artifact = self.artifact.lock().await;
        if self.authority.runtime.cancel_token.is_cancelled() {
            // `project` has durably synced this exact Core Session and updated
            // the captured worker. Return that checkpoint rather than discarding
            // it while projecting the cancellation result.
            let checkpoint = self
                .authority
                .runtime
                .manager
                .read()
                .await
                .get_result(&self.authority.owner_agent_id)?
```

**CALL PATH:** drive_child_actor (engine.rs:2002) -> job.finish (engine.rs:1437) -> self.artifact.lock().await (engine.rs:1446) -> insert_subagent_full_transcript_handle(...).await (engine.rs:1484-1498) -> budget_work_preservation_note(...).await (engine.rs:1538-1543) -> write_digest_artifact(...).await (engine.rs:1548-1553)

**TRIGGER:** A child reaches a terminal state (done, interrupted or budget-exhausted) and finish() finalizes it.

**MECHANISM:** ChildJob::finish acquires the tokio Mutex `artifact` at line 1446 and holds that guard across at least seven subsequent `.await` points: manager.read().await (1455, 1503, 1527), insert_subagent_full_transcript_handle(...).await (1498), budget_work_preservation_note(...).await (1543), and write_digest_artifact(...).await (1553). The guard is not dropped until finish returns at line 1568. budget_work_preservation_note internally runs spawn_blocking and write_digest_artifact performs a spawn_blocking file write (budget_handback.rs:72), so a Tokio mutex is held while the runtime dispatches blocking work and waits.

**IMPACT:** Holding a tokio Mutex across await serializes all access to the same child's transcript artifact for the whole finalization window. Any concurrent task needing that artifact (for example capture_activation_output on the same job, F-01) blocks until finish completes, including the duration of the budget-handback blocking I/O. Under many finishing children and a saturated runtime this extends cancellation and delivery latency. This is the "lock across .await" anti-pattern named in the L11 card and tracked by #6553; it is a contention/scalability defect, not data loss, so severity is minor.

**EVIDENCE:** The lock acquisition (1446) and all cited awaits are in the same function body as read from the file; no explicit `drop(artifact)` occurs before the return at 1568. Awaited helpers that receive `artifact` take `&mut` (lines 1469, 1492) and do not re-lock it, so this is contention rather than a proven self-deadlock. No test asserts lock scope; existing finish tests assert result/status values only.

**FIX:** Scope the artifact guard to the synchronous mutations only: perform insert_subagent_full_transcript_handle's artifact write under a short-lived lock, drop it, then run the manager reads and budget-handback awaits without the guard. If artifact must be passed to a helper that awaits, clone the minimal owned state out under the lock and drop before awaiting.

**REGRESSION CHECK:** A test with a task waiting on `artifact.lock()` that must acquire within a bounded time while finish() is suspended on a slow awaited helper would catch reintroduction; none exists. Static check: assert no `.await` appears between the line 1446 lock and an explicit drop.

**CORRECTION:** Child CALL PATH names drive_child_actor (engine.rs:2002) as the direct caller of job.finish, but finish() is never invoked in engine.rs; the actual callers are core/engine/child_host.rs:238/322/368. The finding's site and mechanism are unaffected by this corrected hop.

**VERIFICATION (reviewer's own check):** Opened engine.rs:1437-1569 at baseline bc58781ba (HEAD == baseline). At 1446 `let mut artifact = self.artifact.lock().await;` acquires the tokio Mutex; the guard is held across awaits at 1455-1456 (manager.read()), 1474 (cancelled_subagent_result(...).await), 1498 (insert_subagent_full_transcript_handle(...).await), 1503-1504 and 1527-1528 (manager.read().await), 1543 (budget_work_preservation_note(...).await) and 1553 (write_digest_artifact(...).await). The guard is passed as `&mut artifact` (1469) and `artifact.as_mut()` (1492); no explicit `drop(artifact)` occurs before the function returns at 1568. write_digest_artifact itself does `tokio::task::spawn_blocking(...).await` while this mutex is held (budget_handback.rs:65-78, specifically 72 and 78) — the documented "lock across .await" anti-pattern (L11/#6553). Reachability shown through the three terminal finalizers in core/engine/child_host.rs:238 (cancelled), 322 (budget exhausted) and 368 (normal completion), each calling `job.finish(...).await`; ChildJob::finish is defined at engine.rs:1437. Contention rather than proven self-deadlock: awaited helpers take `&mut artifact` and do not re-lock it; no data loss, so severity minor. Confidence 8 unchanged per §6.

**CALL PATH:** create_isolated_worktree (worktree.rs:104) -> resolve_worktree_path (worktree.rs:389) -> branch_worktree_slug (worktree.rs:501) -> sanitize_worktree_slug_within (worktree.rs:526)

**TRIGGER:** two workers spawned with distinct caller-supplied non-ASCII branch names that sanitize to the same short ASCII slug and no explicit worktree_path, e.g. branch "功能A" and "功能B" both become "a"; branch "功能" alone becomes "task".

**MECHANISM:** `sanitize_worktree_slug_within` maps every non-ASCII character to `-`, and the consecutive-dash suppression at 536-538 collapses a whole CJK or Cyrillic branch name into a single dash; `trim_matches` at 544 removes it and line 546 substitutes the literal `task`. The hash disambiguation added for long branches (`branch_worktree_slug`, lines 501-516) only runs when the sanitized slug differs from the `usize::MAX` cut, which never happens for a short all-non-ASCII name, so distinct Unicode branch names map to the same worktree directory.

**IMPACT:** A user working in a non-Latin script who delegates two workers on branches such as `功能A` and `功能B` gets the same default worktree path; the second `ensure_worktree_path_unlinked` / `provision_worktree` call fails on the existing checkout or reuses the first worker's directory. The user sees a spawn failure with no explanation that the branch name was the cause, and has no way to express the branch in their own script.

**EVIDENCE:** `resolve_worktree_path` (worktree.rs:420) uses `branch_worktree_slug(branch)` when no path is supplied; `create_isolated_worktree` (worktree.rs:111-115) takes `request.branch` from the caller and only validates git branch syntax, which permits UTF-8 names. The collision test at worktree.rs:626-645 covers two long ASCII branches sharing a prefix and explicitly asserts a short branch keeps its plain slug; no test covers non-ASCII input. Byte slicing in this file (`worktree.rs:470`, `:475`, `:514`) is guarded by `str::get`/ASCII sanitization and is not the mechanism here.

**FIX:** When the sanitized slug has no ASCII alphanumeric content, still append the short hash of the full branch name (the same suffix path used for long slugs at lines 506-516), e.g. detect `slug == "task"` with a non-ASCII original and feed the hash suffix; alternatively derive the slug from the branch's Unicode characters with a reversible ASCII encoding so distinct scripts cannot collapse.

**REGRESSION CHECK:** Extend `long_explicit_branches_sharing_a_prefix_get_distinct_paths` (or add a sibling test) asserting `branch_worktree_slug("功能A") != branch_worktree_slug("功能B")` and that `feature/短名` keeps a stable non-colliding path.

Core mechanism and impact stand; only the illustrative example is corrected.

**VERIFICATION (reviewer's own check):** Opened worktree.rs:501-548 at bc58781ba. `sanitize_worktree_slug_within` maps every non-ASCII char to '-' (`else { '-' }` at :534), collapses consecutive dashes (:536-538), trims (:544), and substitutes `"task"` when the result is empty (:545-546). `branch_worktree_slug` appends a hash suffix only when `slug != sanitize_worktree_slug_within(branch, usize::MAX)` (:503-505); an all-non-ASCII name yields `"task"` under both caps, so no hash is added and distinct Unicode names collide. Reachability shown: `branch` is caller-supplied via `worktree_branch`/`branch` (mod.rs:22030-22040), `validate_git_branch_name` uses `git check-ref-format --branch` (worktree.rs:346-360) which accepts UTF-8, and with no explicit `path` `resolve_worktree_path` returns `default_root.join(branch_worktree_slug(branch))` (:420). Mechanism + impact independently confirmed.

Planned usability and observability release: clipboard-image retention/cleanup, running-command detail, pet qualification, Fleet save-in-role/model presentation, usage/tool diagnostics, per-call cache views and clickable file previews.

Undated planning target approved November 5, 2026. Scope and data-loss semantics must be resolved before implementation; preserve accessibility, explicit cleanup controls and authoritative accounting. This milestone does not create a published release.

issues.body:
# engine/src/core/engine/: 3 verified defects from R1 (baseline bc58781ba)

## How to read this document (terms used below)

- **R<number>** — review unit, one area of the codebase; this document is about R1.
- **L<number>** — one of twelve review lenses (themes) applied to every unit; the table below names each lens.
- **P0 / P1 / P2** — priority rank: P0 highest, P2 lowest. It orders the work, not the severity of a finding.
- **Stage D** — the verification step: every cited line was opened at the baseline, the reachability was traced, and severity was re-scored. **Stage E** — the drafting step that produced this report.
- **Baseline `bc58781ba`** — the exact commit every quote refers to; re-check before acting if `main` has moved.
- **Confirmed** — a verifier opened the cited line, traced a reachable path and kept the finding; rejected and uncertain findings are not here.
- **Public** — this issue contains only findings cleared for a public report; security-class findings are handled through a separate private channel.
- **needs-test** — the written proof is static; a focused test named in the finding would settle the remaining question. No test was run in this audit.
- **Cell** — one audit cell: a review unit crossed with one lens; finding IDs keep the cell number, so a gap in numbering means a candidate was rejected, marked duplicate or routed to the private index.
- **NOT READ** — a scope marker in a cell: that region was not opened, so no claim is made about it.
- **not-applicable / sampled-rescan-passed** — negative-check outcomes: the lens did not apply to that cell, or a sampled rescan found no new signal.
- **Refs #N / UPSTREAM REFS** — existing tracked issues related to the theme or to the exact code site; they are cross-links, never a claim to close or fix those issues. A 500-issue open/closed sweep found no exact duplicate of these findings at the same file and line.
- **CALL PATH, TRIGGER, MECHANISM, IMPACT, EVIDENCE, FIX, REGRESSION CHECK** — copied verbatim from the verified finding file. CALL PATH = how a user reaches the code; TRIGGER = the condition that fires it; MECHANISM = what the code actually does; IMPACT = what the user sees; EVIDENCE = the supporting lines; FIX = recommended change; REGRESSION CHECK = the test that should be added.

Unit R1 (P0 — highest priority is P0, then P1, then P2), turn loop, tool catalog, approval. Confirmed unique findings: **5** — **3 public** in this draft and **2** withheld as private-advisory or held. Finding IDs keep their original cell numbers; a gap means the candidate was rejected, marked duplicate or routed to the private index.

## Coverage

- Files scanned: all 28 paths in the unit manifest were covered by at least one of the twelve theme scans; per-cell detail was recorded during the audit.
- Files read: every signal-matched production region was opened and quoted by the capturing and verifying agents; the exact per-theme counts and regions are in those cell files.
- Files not read: full sequential line-by-line reads of all files were not performed. Each cell records its own `NOT READ` scope; no claim is made beyond the matched regions.
- Themes applied: all twelve, L1–L12 — bugs, logic, edge cases, error handling, security, ordering, process lifecycle, fail-closed behaviour, resource limits, durable writes, async blocking, platform and Unicode. Each theme section below names its lens and its related tracked issue.
- Baseline: `bc58781ba` for every quote and every verification.
- Negative checks: child-attested 1/12 cells, not-applicable 5/12 cells, sampled-rescan-passed 6/12 cells.
- needs-test items: none in this unit. No test or product run happened in this audit.

## Contents

| finding id | final severity | theme | one-line problem | confirmation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| R1-L4-01 | major | L4 | accounting error hardcoded none | static |
| R1-L4-02 | minor | L4 | approval decision error cause discarded | static |
| R1-L9-01 | major | L9 | server tool deltas exempt from content cap | static |

## Planned-work issue card

- **Status:** verified at baseline `bc58781ba`; not fixed in code by this audit.
- **Ways to help without Rust (do these first):**
    - Reproduce or confirm a finding on the baseline by following its `TRIGGER` in the exact file listed below; report whether you see the described result.
    - Review the `IMPACT` wording for accuracy and add a real-world example where you have seen this happen.
    - Check the related tracked issue listed under each theme and report whether this finding is already covered there.
    - Improve the documentation or user-facing message for the locale and wording findings.
    Exact files for this unit:
    - `crates/engine/src/core/engine/child_host.rs`
    - `crates/engine/src/core/engine/turn_loop.rs`
- **Ways to help with Rust:** add the regression test named in `REGRESSION CHECK`, make the minimal fix described in `FIX`, then run the focused test.
- **Local test command:** `scripts/dev-test.sh <path-from-LOCATION>`; the script maps a source path to the fastest crate test and refuses a green run when a filter matches nothing. Each finding also has its own `LOCAL TEST` line.
- **Done-when:** every finding here has a regression test that fails without the fix and passes with it; the focused area test is green; no compiler warning is silenced and no error is hidden to make a test pass; `scripts/preflight.sh --check` is green for the area you touched.
- **What maintainers already hold:** stage-D verification for every finding (quote opened at baseline, reachability traced, severity re-scored), the dedup decision, the private-advisory routing and this draft. Nothing has been fixed in code by this audit.
- **How to claim:** claim a finding by commenting on this issue with its finding ID; one finding per PR keeps the change reviewable. The maintainer resolves conflicts with `main` so contributors never rebase around our churn.


## Theme L4 — Error handling — swallowed cause, wrong fallback

Refs: none — new finding in this audit.

### R1-L4-01 — accounting error hardcoded none

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| FINAL SEVERITY | major |
| FINAL CONFIDENCE | 7 |
| VENUE | public |
| LOCATION | `crates/engine/src/core/engine/turn_loop.rs:6009` |
| FINGERPRINT | `turn_loop.rs:6009:accounting-error-hardcoded-none` |
| DUPLICATES | none |
| UPSTREAM REFS | none |
| CONFIRMATION | static |
| VERIFIER | verifier-R1-L4 |
| DATE | 2026-11-22 |

QUOTE — copied from the verified finding file (baseline `bc58781ba`; code lines are verbatim):

```text
        let accounting_error: Option<String> = None;
        let accounting_record = if pending.primary && !pending.accounting_owned_elsewhere {
            ...
            crate::cost_status::record_runtime_usage_async(
                pending.accounting_scope,
                pending.accounting_origin.as_ref(),
                &record,
            )
            .await;
            Some(record)
        } else {
            None
        };
        let _ = self.send_event(Event::ProviderRequestReceipt {
            receipt: json!({
                "accounting_error": accounting_error,
                ...
        }).await;
        Ok(accounting_record)
```

**CALL PATH:** provider response completes -> Engine::settle_provider_request_receipt (turn_loop.rs:5960) -> record_runtime_usage_async (cost_status.rs:2263, discards owner_work error via `let _ =`) -> Event::ProviderRequestReceipt emitted with accounting_error: null -> TUI event_loop.rs:5086 / engine manager.rs:19777 gate on `receipt["accounting_error"].as_str()` and never fire.

**TRIGGER:** any provider request where usage settlement fails (owner_work returns Err in record_runtime_usage_async); the receipt still reports accounting_error: null, so no warning or uncertain-usage state is raised.

**MECHANISM:** `settle_provider_request_receipt` initializes `accounting_error` to `None` and never assigns it again; the function's `Result<_, String>` error type is likewise never used (only `Ok(accounting_record)` is returned at line 6060). Usage recording is fire-and-forget: `record_runtime_usage_async` discards the `anyhow::Result` from `owner_work` with `let _ = ...` (cost_status.rs:2272-2278), so a settlement failure cannot reach this receipt. The `accounting_error` key is therefore structurally always null.

**IMPACT:** Two consumers treat a non-null `accounting_error` as the signal that usage settlement is uncertain — the TUI calls `app.mark_usage_uncertain("usage_settlement_unacknowledged")` and shows a status warning (event_loop.rs:5086-5091), and the engine logs `"provider usage settlement failed; the turn continues"` (manager.rs:19777-1979). Because the field is never set, a real settlement failure produces no warning, no uncertain-usage mark and no log line: cost/usage accounting can be silently wrong while the diagnostic receipt looks clean (false success).

**EVIDENCE:** Assignment searched crate-wide: only `turn_loop.rs:6009` defines the variable; `crates/tui/src/tui/ui/event_loop.rs:5086` and `crates/engine/src/runtime_threads/manager.rs:19777` consume the field. `cost_status.rs:2263-2279` swallows `owner_work`'s Result. No test asserts a non-null `accounting_error` on a failed settlement.

**FIX:** Make `record_runtime_usage_async` return the `owner_work` Result (or an `Option<String>` error) and have `settle_provider_request_receipt` capture it into `accounting_error` instead of the hardcoded `None`; propagate the same cause through the function's `Err` path and the `ProviderRequestReceipt` field so both consumers fire.

**REGRESSION CHECK:** smallest test — force `owner_work` to return Err during a provider request and assert `Event::ProviderRequestReceipt.receipt["accounting_error"]` is a non-null string and that `mark_usage_uncertain` is reached.

**CORRECTION:** none

**VERIFICATION (reviewer's own check):** Opened baseline turn_loop.rs:6009 — `let accounting_error: Option<String> = None;` with no later assignment; `git grep accounting_error` shows only line 6009 (definition) and 6036 (serialize into receipt). Both consumers gate on `receipt["accounting_error"].as_str()` — manager.rs:19777 emits `tracing::warn!("provider usage settlement failed; the turn continues")` and event_loop.rs:5086 calls `app.mark_usage_uncertain("usage_settlement_unacknowledged")` — so both branches are dead while the field is null. cost_status.rs:2263-2279 `record_runtime_usage_async` returns `()` and discards `owner_work`'s Result via `let _ = ...await`, so no settlement Err can reach the receipt. `owner_work` (runtime_control.rs:13-40) can return Err on the 60s permit timeout, which is silently dropped: a real settlement failure produces no warning, no uncertain-usage mark, and no log — silent false success, major under the L4 "log/receipt" rubric row.

**LOCAL TEST:** `scripts/dev-test.sh crates/engine/src/core/engine/turn_loop.rs` — run after adding the regression test named above.


### R1-L4-02 — approval decision error cause discarded

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| FINAL SEVERITY | minor |
| FINAL CONFIDENCE | 7 |
| VENUE | public |
| LOCATION | `crates/engine/src/core/engine/child_host.rs:614` |
| FINGERPRINT | `child_host.rs:614:approval-decision-error-cause-discarded` |
| DUPLICATES | none |
| UPSTREAM REFS | none |
| CONFIRMATION | static |
| VERIFIER | verifier-R1-L4 |
| DATE | 2026-11-22 |

QUOTE — copied from the verified finding file (baseline `bc58781ba`; code lines are verbatim):

```text
                    Some((id, decision)) = approvals.next(), if !approvals.is_empty() => {
                        if runtime.cancel_token.is_cancelled() || handle.is_cancelled() {
                            handle.cancel();
                        } else {
                            let handle = handle.clone();
                            approval_deliveries.push(Box::pin(async move {
                                match decision {
                                    Ok(reply) => handle.accept_child_approval(id, reply).await,
                                    Err(_) => handle.deny_tool_call_unavailable(id).await,
                                }
                            }));
                        }
                    }
```

**CALL PATH:** probe_child_tool_batch loop (child_host.rs:601) -> approvals.next() yields (id, decision) at line 606 -> approval_deliveries future matches `Err(_)` at line 614 -> handle.deny_tool_call_unavailable(id) sends ApprovalDecision::Unavailable (handle.rs:1138).

**TRIGGER:** a child approval's decision receiver resolves Err (e.g. the host drops the approval request before a decision is returned); the code maps it to an Unavailable approval with no log of the underlying error.

**MECHANISM:** The `decision` value is a `Result` returned by the approval receiver (registered at child_host.rs:628, awaited at 629). On `Err`, the binding `Err(_)` discards the error without logging it and maps the outcome to `deny_tool_call_unavailable`, which merely sends `ApprovalDecision::Unavailable` (handle.rs:1138-1141). The surrounding `approval_deliveries` branch at lines 619-622 does log errors from the *delivery* future, but that future resolves to the `Result<()>` of the send — it never sees the discarded decision cause.

**IMPACT:** An operator or the user sees the tool reported as "unavailable" with no record of why the approval decision failed. Because the fallback is fail-closed (the tool is denied), this is a diagnostic gap, not a permission bypass: the lost cause makes post-mortem of a dropped or failed approval decision impossible from logs, and presents a misleading reason to the user.

**EVIDENCE:** `handle.rs:1138-1141` shows `deny_tool_call_unavailable` only sends `ApprovalDecision::Unavailable`; no tracing call on the Err branch at child_host.rs:614. The sibling `Err` handling at child_host.rs:620-621 logs a different error (the delivery Result), confirming the decision cause is not logged elsewhere in this loop.

**FIX:** Change `Err(_)` to `Err(error)` and add `tracing::warn!(%error, %id, "child approval decision failed; denying as unavailable")` before calling `deny_tool_call_unavailable`, so the cause is durably traced while keeping the fail-closed denial.

**REGRESSION CHECK:** smallest test — drive a child approval whose receiver yields Err and assert a warning event containing the error is emitted (or a log-capture assertion that the cause string appears).

**CORRECTION:** none

**VERIFICATION (reviewer's own check):** Opened baseline child_host.rs:614 — `Err(_) => handle.deny_tool_call_unavailable(id).await,` discards the decision cause. The receiver is a `tokio::sync::oneshot::Receiver<ChildApprovalReply>` (subagent/mod.rs:4394-4428), whose `.await` yields Err when the sender drops without a reply — reachable when an approval is cancelled or the host drops the request before deciding. The sibling branch at child_host.rs:619-622 logs only the delivery future's `Result<()>`, not the decision cause, and handle.rs:1138-1141 confirms `deny_tool_call_unavailable` merely sends `ApprovalDecision::Unavailable` with no tracing. Denial is fail-closed (no permission bypass); the defect is a missing durable cause in logs, minor under the L4 "log/receipt" rubric row.

**LOCAL TEST:** `scripts/dev-test.sh crates/engine/src/core/engine/child_host.rs` — run after adding the regression test named above.


## Theme L9 — Resource limits, bounded buffers

Refs: #6554, #6560 (unbounded reads and missing limits).

### R1-L9-01 — server tool deltas exempt from content cap

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| FINAL SEVERITY | major |
| FINAL CONFIDENCE | 7 |
| VENUE | public |
| LOCATION | `crates/engine/src/core/engine/turn_loop.rs:8057` |
| FINGERPRINT | `turn_loop.rs:8057:server-tool-deltas-exempt-from-content-cap` |
| DUPLICATES | none |
| UPSTREAM REFS | none |
| CONFIRMATION | static |
| VERIFIER | stage-d-verifier-R1-L9 |
| DATE | 2026-11-22 |

QUOTE — copied from the verified finding file (baseline `bc58781ba`; code lines are verbatim):

```text
8052:             Delta::ThoughtSignatureDelta { thought_signature } => thought_signature.len(),
8053:             Delta::RefusalDelta { refusal } => refusal.len(),
8054:             Delta::ReasoningStateDelta { .. }
8055:             | Delta::CitationsDelta { .. }
8056:             | Delta::WebSearchCallDelta { .. }
8057:             | Delta::ServerToolCallsDelta { .. } => 0,
8058:         },
8059:         _ => 0,
8060:     }
8061: }
```

**CALL PATH:** Engine stream loop (`turn_loop.rs:6140`) -> `stream_event_content_bytes` (`turn_loop.rs:8003`) -> `server_blocks` update (`turn_loop.rs:6634`/`6681`) -> `StreamOutcome.server_blocks` (`turn_loop.rs:6851`) -> assistant message `content_blocks` (`model_step.rs:919`) -> persisted in session history and replayed on later turns

**TRIGGER:** A provider stream emits `WebSearchCallDelta` (with large `sources`/`action`/`page`/`error` JSON) or `ServerToolCallsDelta` (with a large `steps` vector), or a large `CitationsDelta`. Each such delta is counted as 0 bytes toward `stream_max_content_bytes`, so the configured content cap never fires no matter how large the payload.

**MECHANISM:** The stream guard at turn_loop.rs:6256-6258 adds `stream_event_content_bytes(&event)` to `stream_content_bytes` and breaks when it exceeds `max_content_bytes`. But `stream_event_content_bytes` returns 0 for `CitationsDelta`, `WebSearchCallDelta` and `ServerToolCallsDelta` even though the `Delta` variants carry arbitrary-size `serde_json::Value` / `Vec<serde_json::Value>` payloads (models/src/lib.rs:684-705). The handlers at turn_loop.rs:6634-6679 and 6681-6688 write those payloads into `server_blocks` (replacing, not appending, so a single large delta or progressively larger replacements are stored whole), which is returned in `StreamOutcome.server_blocks` at turn_loop.rs:6851 and appended into the assistant message at model_step.rs:919. Thus content that would breach the cap if delivered as `TextDelta`/`InputJsonDelta` is admitted uncounted and persisted.

**IMPACT:** A buggy or hostile provider (or a compromised upstream tool-result source) can inject arbitrarily large server-tool-result payloads into the conversation without tripping the operator-configured `stream_max_content_bytes` cap. Once persisted, the oversized blocks are replayed to the model on every later turn — unbounded memory growth in the session and runaway input-token cost, exactly the failure mode the cap is meant to prevent. No other bound on `server_blocks` size was found in this unit.

**EVIDENCE:** Cap invocation at turn_loop.rs:6256-6258; zero-byte mapping at turn_loop.rs:8054-8057; `WebSearchCallDelta` field replacement at turn_loop.rs:6634-6679; `ServerToolCallsDelta` replacement at turn_loop.rs:6681-6688; initial-block accounting at turn_loop.rs:8031-8044 counts only `id/status/kind/action` for `WebSearchCall` (omits `sources/page/error`) and counts `steps` only at block start, not on deltas; commit to history at turn_loop.rs:6851 and model_step.rs:919. Guard tests `stream_event_content_bytes` coverage (turn_loop.rs:9050+) exercise only `RedactedThinking` block-start counting, not these zero-byte deltas. No test in this unit asserts a cap on server-tool-result deltas.

**FIX:** In `stream_event_content_bytes`, account for the serialized size of the payloads these variants carry, mirroring the `WebSearchToolResult`/`ServerToolCalls` block-start arms: for `WebSearchCallDelta` sum `action`, `sources`, `page`, `error` (`to_string().len()`) plus `status`/`kind`/`signature`; for `ServerToolCallsDelta` sum `steps[].to_string().len()`; for `CitationsDelta` use `citation.to_string().len()`. Alternatively, cap the accumulated `server_blocks` byte size explicitly before accepting each delta.

**REGRESSION CHECK:** Add a unit test for `stream_event_content_bytes` asserting that a `WebSearchCallDelta` with a multi-kilobyte `sources` value and a `ServerToolCallsDelta` with large `steps` return a byte count greater than zero and proportional to the payload; extend the stream-loop guard test so such a delta at the cap boundary triggers `StreamError::Overflow`.

**CORRECTION:** Two narrowings to the child's TRIGGER/IMPACT. (1) `Delta::CitationsDelta` is not an impact: the turn_loop handler at 6630 discards it entirely (`Delta::CitationsDelta { .. } => {}`), as recorded in this cell's rejected.md; no payload is accumulated or persisted for that variant. The finding stands on `WebSearchCallDelta` (and the Deserialize-tagged `ServerToolCallsDelta`). (2) `ServerToolCallsDelta` has no in-tree client emitter (only the enum, the turn_loop handler, the TUI conformance serializer and the responses.rs non-streaming accumulator); it is reachable only through a stream decoder that deserializes the serde-tagged `Delta` from JSON. The delta handlers require a matching `ContentBlockStart` to already exist in `server_blocks` (6634-6688 use `iter_mut().rev().find`), which is satisfied by the `WebSearchCall`/`ServerToolCalls` starts at 6519-6543. Path reference `model_step.rs:919` resolves to `crates/engine/src/core/engine/turn_loop/model_step.rs:919`. No change to severity or confidence: major/7 is consistent with rubric §6 (a real resource-limit failure, not the direct cost-runaway/exploit threshold for critical).

**VERIFICATION (reviewer's own check):** Opened the cited lines at baseline bc58781ba (HEAD == baseline; turn_loop.rs clean). turn_loop.rs:8054-8057 matches the QUOTE verbatim: `Delta::ReasoningStateDelta { .. } | Delta::CitationsDelta { .. } | Delta::WebSearchCallDelta { .. } | Delta::ServerToolCallsDelta { .. } => 0,`. The guard at 6256-6258 adds `stream_event_content_bytes(&event)` and breaks on `> max_content_bytes`, so these events are admitted with zero cost. The payloads are arbitrary-size: models/src/lib.rs:688-703 defines `WebSearchCallDelta` with `action/sources/page/error: Option<serde_json::Value>` and 705 defines `ServerToolCallsDelta { steps: Vec<serde_json::Value> }`. Reachability is shown in-tree: crates/engine/src/client/responses.rs:731-745 emits `Delta::WebSearchCallDelta { sources: event.get("sources").cloned(), action: event.get("action").cloned(), page, error }` for real `response.web_search_call.in_progress|searching|completed` SSE events, and :756-779 emits it again on `response.output_item.done` with an `action/sources` fallback — all provider-controlled JSON. The handler at turn_loop.rs:6634-6679 writes those fields into `server_blocks` by whole replacement (`if sources.is_some() { *existing_sources = sources; }` at 6667-6669; `*existing = steps;` at 6687), so a delta can enlarge a stored block arbitrarily while the guard charges 0. The block-start arms at 8031-8044 count `id/status/kind/action` and `steps` only at start, omitting `sources/page/error` and later delta replacements. Commit path verified: `StreamOutcome.server_blocks` (6851) -> `content_blocks.extend(server_blocks)` (turn_loop/model_step.rs:919, correction to the cited path `model_step.rs:919`) -> persisted assistant message. Test gap confirmed: the only guard test at 9049-9062 (`redacted_block_start_counts_its_payload_as_content_bytes`) exercises a block-start, not these zero-byte deltas. Reachable scenario: an OpenAI Responses stream carrying a web-search result with large `sources` inflates session history with no cap, contradicting the operator-configured `stream_max_content_bytes`.

**LOCAL TEST:** `scripts/dev-test.sh crates/engine/src/core/engine/turn_loop.rs` — run after adding the regression test named above.

issues.body:
- [x] I searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate. (Checked open and closed for "subagent budget", "subagent resume", "subagent truncation", "continuable", "BudgetExhausted": #7044 is the closed predecessor this continues; #6316 and #6315 are closed neighbours on stale sub-agent docs and missing metrics.)

**Where:** TUI (terminal interface), CLI command (`codewhale exec`), Docs.

> Continues #7044 ("Sub-agent max_steps is model-guessed and can only narrow"), fixed in `574dc76e26`. That removed the model's step cap. What remains is the stop itself: when a budget is exhausted, the child cannot be resumed, its partial work is clipped without notice, and the documentation says the opposite of what the code does.

## Problem

Four defects, all in the delegation path, all discovered while investigating #7432. The first three are one story: a budget stop is presented as an ordinary failure, and the work behind it is partly thrown away without a signal.

### 1. A budget stop is final — the child cannot be resumed

`SubAgentStatus` has a dedicated variant for this case (`crates/engine/src/tools/subagent/mod.rs:613`):

```rust
/// Worker stopped at an own/shared token, step, or wall-time budget.
/// Partial output retains usage and deliverable receipts without claiming
/// successful completion.
BudgetExhausted,
```

Where that status is set (`:17220-17228`):

```rust
result.status = SubAgentStatus::BudgetExhausted;
…
let checkpoint = result.checkpoint.get_or_insert_with(|| {
    build_subagent_checkpoint(&result.agent_id, cause, &[], result.steps_taken, false)
});
checkpoint.reason = cause.to_string();
checkpoint.continuable = false;
```

And resumption requires the *other* status — `subagent_checkpoint_is_continuable` (`:12475`):

```rust
matches!(snapshot.status, SubAgentStatus::Interrupted(_))
    && snapshot.checkpoint.as_ref().is_some_and(|c| c.continuable && !c.messages.is_empty())
```

`followup` accepts only `["running", "interrupted_continuable"]`. So a budget-stopped child, whose checkpoint exists and whose messages exist, is not continuable — by a flag set to `false` in the same function that builds it.

**Why this matters:** a budget stop is the *most expected* way for a child to stop. #7044 removed the model's ability to invent a step cap; it did not make the remaining stop recoverable. The operator's options are: re-run the whole task and pay for it again, or accept a partial result. This is the "tokens down the drain" outcome #7044 was opened to fix, surviving in a different form.

The code does not say why `continuable` is `false` here. `Interrupted` produces a continuable checkpoint with the same builder; `BudgetExhausted` passes `false` explicitly.

### 2. The partial result is clipped to 4 000 characters, silently

`:17205`:

```rust
let partial = match text {
    Some(text) => text.chars().take(4_000).collect::<String>(),
    …
```

The parent receives `"... Partial output:\n{partial}"` — with no marker saying it was cut, no original length, and no pointer to the checkpoint where the rest lives. Combined with defect 1, the remainder is not reachable at all.

**This is a silent half-failure, and it violates the repository's own rules.** Compare with the sibling path that does it correctly: `clip_evidence_block` (`:18156-18163`) uses the same 4 000-char budget but returns a `bool`, which becomes `summary_truncated` and reaches the notice. Two limits, one signalled, one not.

Against `AGENTS.md`:
- `:98-101` — "**Model-visible means logged.** Anything that reaches a model request must be reconstructable from the session log". The cut text reaches a model (the parent) and the fact of the cut does not.
- `:102-104` — "**Misconfiguration fails loud**… Never silently skip a missing referent." A 4 000-char cut with no marker is the same class: content goes missing and nothing says so.
- `:105-107` — "**Write down what a design does not do**, beside the behaviour it owns". The clip is not documented anywhere.

Against `docs/SUBAGENTS.md`:
- `:27` — "At the limit the host **preserves** a partial-result receipt without an extra model reporting request." It preserves a *slice* of it.
- `:30-31` — "An exhausted budget **or interrupted request preserves the recorded checkpoint and a continuation handle**." For a budget stop there is no usable continuation handle — `continuable = false`. The docs describe the `Interrupted` path and apply it to both.

Self-report risk: a parent that reads `Partial output:` has no way to know whether the child finished and stopped, or wrote a tenth of its report. Both look the same.

### 3. What survives a budget stop, and what does not

To be precise about the loss, because the code does more right than the clip suggests. On a budget stop the host runs `budget_work_preservation_note` (`crates/engine/src/tools/subagent/mod.rs:17030-17090`): it inventories the workspace changes against the spawn-time delivery baseline, names up to 12 paths plus "and N more", and checkpoint-commits the dirty tree, reporting `Committed { sha }` / `Clean` / `Failed { reason }`.

So **file work is preserved and named**. What is lost is the child's *written report* — the part that says what it concluded, which path failed, why it stopped — clipped to 4 000 characters at `:17205`. For a review or investigation child, that report *is* the work product; the files it touched are incidental.

This distinction matters for the fix: the machinery for "do not lose the work" already exists and is good. What is missing is the same care for the text, and a way to resume.

### 4. The 4 000-character clip is not configurable

`SUBAGENT_EVIDENCE_CHAR_BUDGET` (`:18156`) and the inline `4_000` at `:17205` are compile-time constants. There is no `[subagents]` key for either, and no key for the partial-result body. An operator whose children produce long evidence sections has no lever except raising every other budget so the child never stops — which is precisely the trade #7044 rejected.

### 5. `write_authority` is documented as narrower than it is, and the model still chooses it

`apply_spawn_write_authority` (`:16313`) narrows the child's shell as well as its write permission:

```rust
runtime.worker_profile.permissions.write = false;
if matches!(request.agent_type, FleetRole::Worker | FleetRole::Builder | FleetRole::Custom) {
    runtime.worker_profile.shell = runtime.worker_profile.shell.min_with(ShellPolicy::ReadOnly);
}
```

The schema description of the field says only: "Optional typed narrowing of the child's write permissions. `read_only` admits no write scope…" (search `fn input_schema`, the `write_authority` property). It does not say that the shell is clamped to the read-only classifier, and therefore that with any `permissions.toml` deny rule present, dynamic shell forms are refused outright:

```rust
// crates/execpolicy/src/lib.rs
if expansion.dynamic && deny_rules_configured { … Forbidden }
```

Consequence for a real operator: a parent that passes `write_authority: read_only` — the reasonable-looking choice for an investigator — loses `for` loops, `$(…)`, globs and piped scripts, and the child reports permission denials instead of doing the work. This is reachable by the model on every spawn.

Unlike `max_steps` and `wall_time_secs`, which `ignored_limits` (`:15108`) now discards when the model sends them, `write_authority` is honoured. #7044's principle — the owner sets budgets, not the model — was not extended to the authority field.

### 6. Two terminal statuses travel as "done" sentinels

The completion sentinel is built from a three-arm match (`crates/engine/src/tools/subagent/mod.rs:18114-18125`):

```rust
let sentinel = match &result.status {
    SubAgentStatus::Failed(error) => subagent_failed_sentinel(result, error),
    SubAgentStatus::BudgetExhausted => subagent_failed_sentinel(result, …),
    _ => subagent_done_sentinel(&result.agent_id, result, summary_truncated),
};
```

`Interrupted(_)` and `Cancelled` fall into `_`. So:

- An **interrupted** child emits `<codewhale:subagent.done>`. The payload's `status` string is truthful (`subagent_status_name` at `:22626` renders `Interrupted: …`), but the envelope carries no `event: subagent.failed` and no `failure_class`. The runtime-event preamble the parent reads (`:18775-18782`) tells the model that only `event=subagent.failed` is high priority and must be re-planned — so an interrupted child is steered to look like an ordinary completion.
- A **cancelled** child emits the same done sentinel, and `subagent_done_sentinel` stamps `"summary_kind": if truncated { "truncated" } else { "complete" }` (`:18238`). For a cancellation there is no report at all; the "previous line" is the single word `Cancelled` (`:22608`). A parent branching on `summary_kind == "complete"` reads a cancellation as the child's finished work.

This is the same class as the silent clip: the record is technically accurate, and the shape of it says something else. A fan-out of eight children reports eight "done" lines; two of them may have done nothing.

### 7. Two more, found on the second pass

- **`repair_stopped_tool_calls` is `#[cfg(test)]`** (`crates/engine/src/tools/subagent/budget_handback.rs:14-15`), and its only caller is `budget_handback_tests.rs:1010`. The function rewrites a truncated final `ToolResult` into "Tool call not executed: task execution stopped at its budget boundary…" — but it never runs in production. So a budget-killed child's last turn can keep an unrepaired tool pair, and the specific message written for that case is test-only.
- **`BudgetExhausted` collapses into `Failed` in the mailbox** (`mod.rs:2692-2696`), and `MailboxMessage` (`mailbox.rs:55-64`) has no variant for it — only `Completed`, `Failed`, `Interrupted`, `Cancelled`. A consumer keyed on the message type cannot tell a genuine failure from a budget stop, even though the sentinel's `status` string does distinguish them.

### 8. Six more, verified but lower severity

Found in the same audit and confirmed by reading `main`. Listed so a maintainer can triage in one pass:

- **The operator's child budgets are unreachable from the tool schema.** `[subagents] default_max_steps` and `default_wall_time_secs` are resolved (`crates/runtime/src/config.rs:6951-6968`) and rendered to the *child* (`child_runtime_budget_context`, `mod.rs:330-363`), but the model-facing `agent` schema has no field naming them. A parent that re-dispatches after a wall-clock stop knows neither the limit nor that one exists.
- **`deliverables` verdicts are capped at four and can be sorted away.** `compact_row` (`crates/engine/src/tools/subagent/lifecycle.rs:187-215`) sorts verdicts, records `deliverables_omitted`, then truncates the array to 4; `compact_roster` (`:383-401`) replaces the whole verification object with a preview, dropping a missing file's identity entirely.
- **Child tool results are clipped at 1 MiB inside the child, and the parent never learns.** `hard_cap_tool_result` (`mod.rs:421-452`) appends `[truncated: true]` for the child's own model; `cap_child_tool_output` (`crates/engine/src/core/engine/turn_loop.rs:403-426`) records `output_persistence_failed` when a spill file cannot be written. Neither fact reaches the parent's completion payload, which carries only `evidence` (≤4 000 chars) and `usage`.
- **`until: "all"` reports a vanished child as settled.** `coord.rs:845-878` pushes `{"status": "gone"}` for a child whose record was evicted, and `all_settled` (`:931-953`) counts an empty `still_running` as settled. `"gone"` is not in the documented status vocabulary (`docs/SUBAGENTS.md`), and retention (`COMPLETED_AGENT_RETENTION = 1h`, `mod.rs:475`) can evict a child mid-join.
- **Config clamps beat the operator with no notice.** `max_admitted` is `.clamp(max_concurrent, MAX_SUBAGENT_ADMISSION)` (`crates/runtime/src/config.rs:6928-6946`), so writing `max_admitted = 4` next to `max_concurrent = 64` yields 64. `max_subagents()` (`:6802-6813`) lets `[subagents] max_concurrent` beat the top-level `max_subagents`. No clamp emits a note.
- **`write_roots` says "paths outside the parent workspace are refused", but a sibling worktree is admitted** (`mod.rs:14775-14778` vs `worktree.rs:68-78`, `is_sibling_worktree_path`). Narrow, but the schema text and the admission rule disagree.

### 9. Nesting depth has no default limit

`DEFAULT_SPAWN_DEPTH = u32::MAX` (`crates/protocol/src/fleet.rs:1898`), documented as "Runtime delegation has no default product depth limit". With no `[subagents] max_depth` set, a child may spawn children which spawn children, indefinitely. Each level holds its own context and its own budget, and nothing sums them.

The owner key exists (`crates/runtime/src/config.rs:1223-1226`), so this is not a missing mechanism — it is a default that favours the risky direction, with the operator given no notice.

## What the audit found sound

So a maintainer does not re-check these: terminal-event delivery cannot lose an event (`send_terminal_event` awaits capacity on `Full`, only `Closed` drops, `mod.rs:2612-2663`); `hard_cap_tool_result` always appends its marker and truncates on a char boundary; `stamp_subagent_summary_with_ref` (`:22528-22562`) reports `head+tail of total` and names a retrievable artifact or says the middle cannot be retrieved; `clip_evidence_block` does set `evidence_truncated` into `summary_kind`; the parent-message queue cap fails closed with a named limit (`MOD_MAX_QUEUED_PARENT_MESSAGES = 64`, `:478`, `:8481-8485`); `followup_child` returns an explicit error rather than accepting undeliverable mail (`:8540-8551`); `verify_changes` and `default_agent_run_verification` default to `self_report_only`; worktree containment and path-unlink refusals are implemented; `narrow_optional_limit`/`narrow_model_steps` never widen an inherited cap.

## Proposed solution

Eight parts. Parts 1–4 replace one broken behaviour with a resumable one; 5–8 make existing choices visible, settable, and honestly reported.

**1. `BudgetExhausted` produces a continuable checkpoint.**

Set `continuable = true` in `budget_partial_result_with_note` and accept `BudgetExhausted` in `subagent_checkpoint_is_continuable`. `followup` then works for the most common stop, and the affordance the docs already promise matches the code.

Stated limit: this makes resumption *possible*, not automatic. The parent still decides. A budget stop that a restart cannot fix (a provider that never returns) is unaffected.

**2. Remove the silent clip — show the whole partial result, or say it was cut.**

Two changes, in order of preference:

- (a) Do not clip at all: the parent's own context budget and compaction already bound the transcript. If a bound is genuinely needed, reuse `clip_evidence_block`'s contract so the notice carries `summary_truncated` alongside `Partial output (N of M characters)`.
- (b) If a bound must stay, make it visible: the current `…[truncated]` convention `docs/HOOKS.md` uses for hook output, plus the original length and the checkpoint id.

Either way, the parent must be able to tell "the child finished" from "the child was cut". Right now it cannot.

**3. Say what was lost, in the receipt the parent already reads.** Independent of the clip size: when a budget stop happens, the parent's notice should name (a) that the child's text was cut and by how much, and (b) the preservation receipt — how many files changed and the checkpoint sha. Item (b) is already computed; it is appended to the child's result but never surfaced in the parent-facing sentinel. This is the cheapest part and the one that answers "I could not have imagined this was possible".

**4. Make the clip an opt-in setting, not a default.**

```toml
[subagents]
# 0 = no clipping (default). Positive values cap the partial-result body and the
# evidence block together, and both carry a truncation marker when they bite.
partial_result_max_chars = 0
```

`0` as the default answers the reporter's point directly: nobody expects their child's output to be silently shortened, so the default must not do it. An operator who wants a bound sets one and gets a marker.

**5. Correct the `write_authority` description, and let the owner suppress it.**

Two independent changes:

- The schema text must state the shell clamp and the dynamic-command consequence. That is a documentation fix in the tool description and in `docs/SUBAGENTS.md`.
- `[subagents] honor_model_write_authority = false` would make the model's `write_authority` ignored, exactly as `ignored_limits` already ignores `max_steps` and `wall_time_secs`. Default `true` keeps current behaviour; `false` gives the owner the same guarantee #7044 gave for steps.

**6. A terminal status must pick the right envelope.** Interrupted and Cancelled should build a failure-shaped sentinel carrying a failure_class, not subagent.done. If the wire format must not change, the minimum is a summary_kind that is not "complete" when there is no report, plus a status the parent's preamble already treats as needing attention.

**7. Fix the six lower-severity items in one pass.** They share a cause: a value or a verdict that is dropped, capped or clamped without a receipt. Naming the resolved child budgets in the schema or the spawn receipt; showing omitted deliverables by identity and count; propagating truncated and output_persistence_failed into the parent's completion payload; making status "gone" a distinct, documented state that all_settled does not treat as success; emitting a note when a config clamp changes the operator's number; aligning the write_roots text with is_sibling_worktree_path.

**8. Make the depth default safe, or make it loud.**

Either default `max_depth` to `2`, or keep `u32::MAX` and print the resolved value with a one-line notice the first time a child spawns a grandchild. The reporter's requirement is not "limit it" — it is "do not let it happen without my knowing".

## Use case

The reporter runs long review passes with delegated children on a 1M-context route. Their loss mode, in their words: a child stops at a budget, the work is gone, and the tokens are spent. #7044 removed the model's step cap and they thought the problem was closed. It was closed for *one* stop cause; the other causes still terminate the child, and the partial work behind that stop is clipped to 4 000 characters without a word.

The same operator passes `write_authority: read_only` to delegate an investigation, and gets children that refuse `for` loops because a deny rule is configured — a consequence the schema neither states nor lets them turn off.

## The rules this breaks

Not invented for this report — these are the repository's own stated principles, and the clip violates three of them at once.

**`AGENTS.md:98-101` — "Model-visible means logged."**
> Anything that reaches a model request must be reconstructable from the session log, and a new model-visible input needs a session event. Live presentation and the persisted record must agree; when they disagree the record is right.

A 4 000-character cut reaches the parent model. The fact of the cut, and the 90% that was dropped, do not. The record and the presentation disagree, and the presentation is the one the model acts on.

**`AGENTS.md:102-104` — "Misconfiguration fails loud."**
> at load when it is self-contained, otherwise at the earliest point it can be resolved. Never silently skip a missing referent.

The clip is not a misconfiguration, but it is the same rule applied to data: content goes missing and nothing says so. The report's author did not know truncation existed at all — that is the failure the rule is written against.

**`AGENTS.md:105-107` — "Write down what a design does not do."**
> beside the behaviour it owns — a short known-limitations note in the owning module. A stated limit stops the next reader from assuming a capability that was never built.

`docs/SUBAGENTS.md:27` says "At the limit the host **preserves** a partial-result receipt", and `:30-31` says "An exhausted budget **or interrupted request** preserves the recorded checkpoint and a continuation handle". Both statements describe something the budget path does not do: it preserves a slice, and it sets `continuable = false`, so there is no handle.

**`docs/AGENT_ETHOS.md:36-38` — sub-agent output is evidence, and the parent owns the decision.**
> Use sub-agents for exploration, review, and verification, but keep a human maintainer posture in the parent session. Sub-agent output is evidence; the parent is responsible for the final decision.

A parent cannot weigh evidence it was not given, and cannot tell that it was not given it. The silent clip moves the parent's decision onto material the parent believes is complete — which is the one thing this posture cannot survive.

**`docs/RECEIPTS.md:87-89` — truncation removes outcomes.**
> Truncating the conversation removes outcomes beyond the retained history, so later turns cannot inherit their failures.

The doc already knows that truncation destroys the record of failure. The sub-agent path does it to a single result, with no retained history at all.

## Alternatives considered

- **Raise every budget so children never stop.** This is what an operator does today, and it is exactly the trade #7044 rejected: real token cost to avoid a stop that could be resumable instead.
- **Treat `BudgetExhausted` like `Failed` and document it as final.** Honest, and cheaper than part 1. Rejected because the checkpoint already exists with its messages — the only thing preventing resumption is a boolean.
- **Keep the clip and only add a marker.** Fixes the silence but not the loss; worth doing as an interim step if part 3 is declined.
- **Force `write_authority` off entirely.** Then no child can be narrowed, which removes a real safety affordance. The proposal keeps narrowing available and makes the consequence documented and suppressible.

## Impact

- Runtime: one boolean in the checkpoint builder, one match arm in `subagent_checkpoint_is_continuable`. Small, testable, and it makes `docs/SUBAGENTS.md:30-31` true.
- Notice format: the partial-result body becomes either whole or explicitly marked. Any consumer that parses "Partial output:" keeps working; a new marker is additive.
- Config: two optional `[subagents]` keys (`partial_result_max_chars`, `honor_model_write_authority`), both defaulting to current behaviour except the clip, which defaults to *off* as the reporter requests.
- Docs: `docs/SUBAGENTS.md:27,30-31` need to describe the budget-stop path accurately; the `write_authority` description needs the shell consequence.
- No prompt or KV-cache effect. No new label, workflow or bot.

## Open questions

1. Is `continuable = false` on `BudgetExhausted` deliberate? If a checkpoint whose only difference is that flag is unsafe to resume, what makes it unsafe — a partially written file, an uncommitted claim, worktree state? Naming that reason would let the fix be precise instead of flipping a flag.
2. Should the partial result reach the parent whole by default, or is there a hard reason for a bound (context accounting, transcript size)? If a bound is required, what is the number, and why 4 000?
3. Should `honor_model_write_authority = false` also drop `write_roots` and `exact_files`, or only `write_authority`? Narrowing a scope is different from narrowing a *posture*, and only the latter has the undocumented shell side effect.
4. For part 5, is a first-grandchild notice enough, or should the resolved depth appear in the spawn receipt every time?

## References

- #7044 — the predecessor: model-chosen step caps removed in `574dc76e26`. This issue is the stop causes that fix did not cover.
- #7432 — the skills-index regression, where the same "silent half-failure" pattern surfaced and started this line of investigation.
- #7433 — the proposed behaviour-change protocol; part 2b there (`Behaviour:` line) would have made the `continuable = false` change visible.
- `crates/engine/src/tools/subagent/mod.rs:613` — `BudgetExhausted` variant; `:17205` — the 4 000-char clip; `:17220-17228` — `continuable = false`; `:12475` — the resumption predicate; `:15108` — `ignored_limits`; `:16313` — `apply_spawn_write_authority`; `:18156-18163` — `clip_evidence_block`, the signalled sibling.
- `crates/protocol/src/fleet.rs:1898` — `DEFAULT_SPAWN_DEPTH = u32::MAX`.
- `crates/execpolicy/src/lib.rs` — the dynamic-command refusal when deny rules are configured.
- `crates/runtime/src/config.rs:1189-1263` — `SubagentsConfig`, including `max_depth`, `default_max_steps`, `default_wall_time_secs`.
- `docs/SUBAGENTS.md:27,30-31` — "preserves a partial-result receipt" and "preserves the recorded checkpoint and a continuation handle".
- `AGENTS.md:98-107` — "Model-visible means logged", "Misconfiguration fails loud", "Write down what a design does not do".

<details>
<summary>Verification performed for this report</summary>

- `budget_partial_result_with_note` body read on `main`; `checkpoint.continuable = false` at `:17228`; `text.chars().take(4_000)` at `:17205`.
- `subagent_checkpoint_is_continuable` at `:12475` matches only `Interrupted`; `followup` accepted statuses `["running", "interrupted_continuable"]`.
- `clip_evidence_block` returns `(String, bool)` and the bool becomes `summary_truncated` at `:18113` — the contrast with the unsignalled clip at `:17205` is the core of finding 2.
- `apply_spawn_write_authority` at `:16313`, with the shell clamp under the role match.
- `DEFAULT_SPAWN_DEPTH = u32::MAX` at `crates/protocol/src/fleet.rs:1898`; no `[subagents] max_depth` in the reporter's config.
- `docs/SUBAGENTS.md:27,30-31` quoted verbatim from `main`.
- `ignored_limits` at `:15108` includes `max_steps`, `max_depth`, `wall_time_secs`, `max_output_tokens` and their camelCase forms; `write_authority` is not in it.
- Live: a child spawned with `workspace_write` ran three probe commands successfully; a child with `read_only` reported permission denials. The reporter's config has 51 deny rules, which is what makes the dynamic-command refusal bite.

Not verified: whether `continuable = false` on `BudgetExhausted` protects against a specific hazard (no comment states one); the exact behaviour of `followup` on a `BudgetExhausted` child at runtime (not exercised — it would spend real tokens); whether any consumer parses the "Partial output:" body beyond the parent's own reading.
</details>
