milestone.title: v0.10.5
milestone.description:
Planned usability and observability release: clipboard-image retention/cleanup, running-command detail, pet qualification, Fleet save-in-role/model presentation, usage/tool diagnostics, per-call cache views and clickable file previews.

Undated planning target approved November 5, 2026. Scope and data-loss semantics must be resolved before implementation; preserve accessibility, explicit cleanup controls and authoritative accounting. This milestone does not create a published release.

issues.body:
When a provider request dies after dispatch, the cause survives as English prose in two places (the session record and `codewhale receipts`) and **never reaches the diagnostic log**. The prose is also the only machine-readable form there is: no receipt field, no log field, no structured tag.

1. **The session record keeps prose, not a cause.** `turn_outcomes[].error` holds a sentence; the `Provider request receipt` carries `outcome: "open_failed" | "incomplete"` and `coverage: "missing"` but **no cause field**, so a consumer must regex English to tell a header stall from a mid-stream read drop from a proxy reset. `codewhale receipts` re-renders that same sentence, so it inherits the same limitation.
2. **The diagnostic log holds neither.** `~/.codewhale/logs/tui-*.log` records `engine turn completion settled status=Failed` and nothing about the reason: a grep for every provider failure family returns **zero** hits across 62 log files, while the settlement line appears 463 times.
3. **The rendered card drops the typed code.** The card is prose composed from the raw provider string; the typed `code` the envelope already carries (`llm_network_error`, `llm_timeout`, `llm_server_<status>`, …) never reaches the reader, and neither does `RequestTransmission` (`NotDispatched` / `Rejected` / `OutcomeUnknown`) — the one field that answers "did the provider see it".

None of this is a retry-policy complaint, and none of it says the cause is lost — `receipts` proves it is not. It is a "the evidence is not where a support reader looks, and is not structured where a tool could use it" complaint, and it is cheap to fix.

**Stated up front so nobody has to discover it:** `codewhale receipts <id> --format json` already returns the cause (verified live, quoted in § Defect 1). This issue argues the log and the card should carry it too, not that it is unavailable.

---

## What is measured, and how

Two corpora, both from one operator's machine:

- **Session records** — `~/.codewhale/sessions/*.json`, 610 files, 2026-09-15 → 2026-11-12. Each carries a `journal` (`message` + `system` entries) and `turn_outcomes[]`.
- **Diagnostic logs** — `~/.codewhale/logs/tui-*.log`, 62 files, 2026-11-05 → 2026-11-12, 8.4 MB. These files are appended to while a session runs, so the counts below are a snapshot; `Completed` drifts upward between reads while `Failed` stays at 15.

### Where the failures actually are

`turn_outcomes[]` with `status: "failed"` across the whole corpus: **180 records, every one carrying an `error` string**. Grouped by cause:

| Cause (verbatim leading text) | Count | First seen | Last seen |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Provider returned an empty response` | 44 | 2026-10-05 | 2026-10-26 |
| `Upstream idle timeout exceeded` | 26 | 2026-10-06 | 2026-11-02 |
| rate-limit / 429 family | 25 | 2026-10-18 | 2026-11-06 |
| `Provider stream connection dropped…` (transport read) | 12 | 2026-10-10 | 2026-11-12 |
| auth family | 10 | 2026-10-xx | 2026-11-09 |
| `Chat Completions stream closed before [DONE] or finish_reason` | 5 | 2026-10-23 | 2026-11-06 |
| `Network error: Request failed: error sending request` | 2 | 2026-11-12 | 2026-11-12 |
| `Provider usage settlement failed…` | 2 | 2026-11-11 | 2026-11-11 |
| `Request timed out after 0ns` | 1 | 2026-11-12 | 2026-11-12 |
| other (tool, policy, quota, malformed provider text) | remainder | | |

### What survives into the log

Zero. Across all 62 files:

```
$ grep -c "Provider stream connection dropped" ~/.codewhale/logs/*.log   → 0 in every file
$ grep -c "error decoding response body"        ~/.codewhale/logs/*.log   → 0
$ grep -c "error sending request"               ~/.codewhale/logs/*.log   → 0
$ grep -c "did not receive response headers"    ~/.codewhale/logs/*.log   → 0
$ grep -c "Upstream idle timeout"               ~/.codewhale/logs/*.log   → 0
```

What the log *does* contain is the bare settlement line — `engine turn completion settled status=Failed` — 15 times in the same window:

```
394  engine turn completion settled status=Completed
 54  engine turn completion settled status=Interrupted
 15  engine turn completion settled status=Failed
463  total
```

Attributing each `Failed` to the nearest preceding log line gives: 4 × usage-receipt retention, 3 × snapshot prune, 4 × tool failures, 1 × proxy refusal, 1 × turn stall, 1 × session retention, 1 × nothing. The provider failures above are not among them — they did not write a line at all.

### What survives into the session record

Free text only. For a `Provider request receipt` with `outcome: "open_failed"` or `"incomplete"`, the full key set is:

```
source_accounting, accounting_error, session_id, turn_id, request_index, request_id,
source_id, route, primary, transmission, coverage, physical_requests,
physical_requests_dropped, prefix_check, reused_preparation, wire_observations,
wire_observations_dropped, usage, usage_reported, outcome, transport_retries,
elapsed_ms, cache_attribution
```

There is no `error`, `cause` or `failure_class` field. `accounting_error` exists but is `null` for these. So the only machine-readable statement about a failed request is `outcome` (3 values) and `coverage` (`missing`); the cause lives exclusively in `turn_outcomes[].error` as English prose — and that prose differs by code path, so a consumer has to string-match on sentences that are periodically reworded (see § "Why the prose is not a stable key").

---

## Defect 1 — the diagnostic log has no cause for a failed turn

**Claim, verified against `28b755f6e`:** the failure branches that build the user-visible card have no `tracing` call at `warn`/`error` level, and the one line that does settle a turn carries the status but not the cause.

Where the two cards are actually built:

- **Stream-open failures** — `crates/engine/src/core/engine/turn_loop/model_step.rs:424` calls `initial_stream_error_user_message(...)`, then the `Err` arm runs to `model_step.rs:~486-536` and returns `TurnOutcomeStatus::Failed`. That file has exactly two `tracing` calls: `:577` `tracing::debug!` (target `provider_response_diagnostics`) and `:637` `tracing::warn!` (child usage settlement). Neither carries the error.
- **Transport-read failures** (`Provider stream connection dropped…`) — built at `crates/engine/src/core/engine/turn_loop.rs:5073` via `stream_read_error_user_message(&message, any_content_received)`, in the same shape, also with no `tracing` call.

The umbrella settlement line does exist — `crates/engine/src/core/engine.rs:7961-7968`:

```rust
tracing::info!(
    target: "engine.turn",
    status = ?status,
    event_sent = turn_complete_event_sent,
    "engine turn completion settled"
);
```

(Quoted verbatim from `engine.rs:7961-7968`. The `error` value exists in scope two lines above and is **not** included.)

`info` with `status` — and **no error**, **no route**, **no provider**, **no transmission state**. So the log says a turn failed and cannot say why, which is exactly the question asked after a crash.

**The `debug` line does not rescue this, and that is measured, not assumed.** `crates/runtime/src/runtime_log.rs:137-139` builds the file-subscriber filter as `EnvFilter::try_from_default_env().unwrap_or("info")` — so `debug` is dropped by default. In 62 log files / 8.4 MB:

```
grep -c "parent model response settled"  → 0
 grep -c "provider_response_diagnostics"  → 0
 grep -c "engine turn completion settled" → 463
```

That is: the `info` settlement line reaches the file; every `debug` diagnostic does not. Raising `CODEWHALE_LOG_LEVEL`/`RUST_LOG` to `debug` would surface `provider_response_diagnostics` — but it still would not carry the error text, and the default install never sees it.

**What already works, and must be stated or this issue is wrong.** `codewhale receipts <id> --format json` **does** return the cause, because `session_receipt` reads `turn_outcomes[].error` and renders it as a `TurnFailed` action (`crates/engine/src/receipts.rs:142-172`, `:1887-1902`, with `bounded(&redact(...))` for secret hygiene). Verified live against a real session:

```
$ codewhale receipts <session> --format json | jq '.actions[] | select(.tool=="turn" and .status=="failed") | .error'
"Network error: Request failed: error sending request"
"Provider stream connection dropped while reading the response body. …"
```

So the gap is narrower than "the cause is lost", and the honest statement is: **the cause survives in the session record and (truncated) in `receipts`, and never reaches `tui-*.log`.** A reader who knows to run `receipts` gets the prose; a reader tailing the log — or reading a log shipped by someone else, which is the usual support case — gets `status=Failed` and nothing else.

`receipts` also bounds the sentence: `MAX_ERROR_CHARS = 160` (`crates/engine/src/receipts.rs:50`), and the live output shows the cut — 52 chars for the short one, exactly 160 plus an ellipsis for the long one:

```
52   Network error: Request failed: error sending request
160  Provider stream connection dropped while reading the response body. Some output had already
     streamed, so Codewhale is surfacing the warning instead of replayin…
```

The truncated tail is where the distinguishing detail lives (`Details: Stream read error: error decoding response body`). So `receipts` gives a *recognisable* cause, not a complete or structured one — a third reason the structured field belongs in the envelope and the log.

**Why the log gap still matters.** `receipts` prints the same free-text `turn_outcomes[].error` sentence, so it inherits the instability described in § "Why the prose is not a stable key" — it can say what the sentence says and nothing structured. It also cannot be grepped across a fleet of sessions without re-implementing the sentence matching. And `not_recorded` / `omitted_actions` mean `receipts` may itself be bounded away from the failure.

**Why there is still no cheap workaround inside the log.** `codewhale_runtime::logging::warn` is stderr-only and gated on `CODEWHALE_LOG_LEVEL` (`crates/runtime/src/logging.rs:106-113`); it never reaches `tui-*.log`. Only `tracing::*` at `info`+ does. Several sibling diagnostics in the same file use `logging::warn` (`turn_loop.rs:5018, 5045, 5097`), so setting `CODEWHALE_LOG_LEVEL=debug` still leaves nothing durable.

**Suggested direction.** One `tracing::warn!` (or `error!` when the turn ends) at each failure-card site, carrying the fields the envelope and receipt already have: `code`, `category`, `transmission`, `provider`, `model`, and `http_status` when present. No new event, no new persistence, no behaviour change — the neighbouring `tracing::error!(%error, "provider usage has no durable acknowledgement")` at `turn_loop.rs:4858` is the shape to copy.

---

## Defect 2 — the card drops the typed cause and the transmission state

`crates/engine/src/llm_error_envelope.rs:21-24` sets `envelope.message = display_message`, overwriting whatever the typed mapping produced. The typed `code` survives on the event (`ErrorEnvelope::code`), and `apply_engine_error_to_app` stores only `message` and `severity` into the transcript cell (`crates/tui/src/tui/ui/apply.rs:232`). So the reader sees prose and the machinery keeps the code — the two never meet.

Six distinct failures, as the operator sees them:

| Layer | What the operator reads | Says the layer? | Says "provider saw it"? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Pre-dispatch (DNS/TCP/TLS/proxy) | `Connection failed before request dispatch: …` | yes | yes, implicitly |
| Post-dispatch, transport read | `Provider stream connection dropped while reading the response body. … Details: Stream read error: error decoding response body` | no | no |
| Post-dispatch, request send | `Network error: Request failed: error sending request` | no | no |
| Header stall | `SSE stream request did not receive response headers after Ns; request outcome unknown` | partially | says "unknown" |
| Local idle/timeout ceiling | `SSE stream idle timeout after Ns — no data received (bytes_received=…)` | yes, it's ours | n/a |
| Upstream status | `Server error (503): <provider text>` | yes | yes |

The vocabulary to fix this already exists and is 15 codes wide:

```
llm_quota_window, llm_rate_limited, llm_quota_exhausted, llm_server_<status>,
llm_network_error, llm_connect_before_dispatch, llm_timeout, llm_auth_error,
llm_authorization_error, llm_invalid_request, llm_model_error, llm_content_policy,
llm_context_length, llm_parse_error, llm_other
```

and `RequestTransmission { NotDispatched, Rejected, OutcomeUnknown }` at `crates/engine/src/llm_client/mod.rs:370-374`.

**Suggested direction (composition only):** render a short tag from `code` and the transmission state beside the message — e.g. `provider stream read failed · outcome unknown · resend to continue`. Keep `message` as the detail line. No new types.

---

## Why the prose is not a stable key

The failure sentences are reworded often enough that no consumer can depend on them, which is the concrete argument for Defect 1's structured field:

| Phrase | Present at `28b755f6e`? | Note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Provider returned an empty response` | **no** (only in a test fixture) | 44 historical failures carried it |
| `Upstream idle timeout exceeded` | **no** (only in a taxonomy test) | 26 historical failures carried it |
| `SSE stream request failed after HTTP/1.1 fallback` | **no** | the fallback error now goes through `h1_fallback_error` (`stream_entry.rs:215-238`) |
| `Request timed out after 0ns` | replaced | now `… (provider request exceeded its transport budget; exact duration not recorded)` — `da201bac8` |
| `Provider stream connection dropped` | yes | `streaming.rs:390-411` |
| `Chat Completions stream closed before [DONE] or finish_reason` | yes | `chat.rs:1732` |

Both rewordings are good on their own — `da201bac8` stopped fabricating `0ns`, and `21c8f86c4` named determinate rejections instead of calling them `internal`. Together they mean the sentence text is not an API, while nothing else carries the same fact.

---

## Corrections to my own earlier counts (so a reader can reproduce)

My first pass over `sessions/*.json` counted **substrings**, which over-counted badly: agent transcripts quoting the failure text, earlier analysis sessions quoting source code, and one conversation describing the same error three times all inflated the numbers. Recounting only `turn_outcomes[].error` — a field the engine writes, never a transcript — gives the 180-record table above. Raw substring counts (e.g. 480 × `error sending request`) are **not** occurrence counts of the fault and should not be read as such.

The distinction matters for one claim I am *not* making: I cannot show that every one of these 180 was recoverable by a single follow-up message. I can show the weaker, verifiable thing: every failure class above except rate-limit and auth was followed in the same session by further successful turns, so the session's work continued.

---

## How to reproduce the counts

A maintainer cannot run my classifier, so here is the exact method. It reads fields the engine writes, never transcript text.

```sh
# Count of failed turns across every saved session.
# -s (slurp) is required: without it jq drops files mid-stream on this corpus.
jq -rs '[.[] | .turn_outcomes[]? | select(.status=="failed")] | length' \
  ~/.codewhale/sessions/*.json          # → 180

# The same records, one cause sentence per line, grouped by leading text:
jq -rs '.[] | .turn_outcomes[]? | select(.status=="failed") | .error' \
  ~/.codewhale/sessions/*.json \
| sed -E 's/^(.{0,40}).*/\1/' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn
```

Two things a reader must know to reproduce these numbers honestly:

- **`-s` matters.** Without slurp, the same one-liner printed 42, 192 and 180 on three consecutive runs over an unchanged directory. The corpus contains multi-megabyte session files, and non-slurped `jq` appears to stop early on this input set. Use `-s`, and expect the total to drift upward while the session doing the counting is itself being saved into the same directory.
- **No deduplication.** A turn that failed twice counts twice. That is intentional: the claim is about how often a reader is left without a cause, not how many distinct faults exist.

Field path: `turn_outcomes[].error` on the session document root, written by `SavedTurnOutcome` (`crates/engine/src/session_manager.rs:2092`).

**The "other 53" bucket is not a junk drawer, and deliberately not expanded.** It decomposes into tool failures, provider plan-quota exhaustion, malformed provider text (`ERROR` alone), a wall-clock ceiling, and a handful of one-off rejections. None of those are transport failures, and none would change the two defects above; expanding them would pad the table without adding an argument.

**What the numbers do not prove.** They are one operator's sessions, from one provider, on one machine, over 59 days. They do **not** establish a rate, a frequency per turn, or that a typical user sees this. They establish only that the failures are common enough in one real corpus to justify a diagnostic line — which is the whole claim.

---

## What this issue does not ask for

- No change to retry policy, defaults, or `[retry]`/`[stream]` semantics.
- No replay of anything after dispatch. The unknown-outcome stop (`92b4900d1`) stays as is.
- No new persistence format — the fields proposed for the log already exist on the envelope and the receipt.

---

## Deferred: the replay knob

The obvious next ask — "give me an opt-in knob that replays these" — was pulled from this draft because its central premise does not survive review:

> **The premise, and why it is wrong.** A header stall or a post-dispatch `NetworkError` means *the client saw no bytes*. It does **not** mean the provider produced no completion. The provider may have generated and billed the entire answer while the client was gone. That is precisely the case `92b4900d1` exists for (`docs/CONFIGURATION.md:2914-2917`).

Two smaller blockers found while checking it, worth recording here so they are not rediscovered:

- `ErrorEnvelope::recoverable` is not a "resend hint". It drives offline-mode / turn-liveness (`crates/tui/src/tui/ui/apply.rs:177-198`) and headless exit status (`exec_error_event_is_fatal` = `!recoverable`, `crates/engine/src/exec_events.rs:206-214`). Repurposing it would change `exec` exit codes and CI behaviour.
- `[retry]` merges **whole-table** per profile (`crates/runtime/src/config.rs:10181`: `retry: override_cfg.retry.or(base.retry)`), unlike `[stream]`'s per-key merge (`:10187`). Any new `[profiles.x.retry]` opt-in would silently discard the base `max_retries`. Also, `crates/config/src/settings_schema.rs` defines **no** `retry.*` keys at all, so `/config` and `config set` cannot reach a new key without schema work.

If it is ever proposed, the honest framing is "replay when the client received no bytes, accepting that the provider may already have billed a completion", with per-attempt cost accounting — not "replay when the provider cannot have answered", which is not knowable.

---

## Related

- `92b4900d1` (2026-11-02) — "stop replaying inference with unknown outcomes". The policy this issue leaves alone.
- #6184 (**open**) — "Engine silently freezes mid-run: user messages are persisted but never answered; no error, no log line, no crash entry". Closest open neighbour; Defect 1 may belong with it.
- #6796 (closed) — "Retry attempts are invisible". Addressed the *retry* banner; the *failure* record is still missing.
- #6843 (closed 2026-10-08) — determinate rejections labelled `internal`. Why prose can be a poor key, and proof the wording moves.
- #6699 (closed) — no retry when the SSE request never received headers.
- #7045 (closed) — SSE retries capped by the stream-open window; HTTP/1.1 fallback returned raw HTTP errors.
- #5769 (closed) — network errors stopping the engine; closed as working-as-intended, which is why this issue is scoped to diagnostics rather than recovery.

## Environment notes (anonymised)

- The local proxy refuses connections on a six-hour cadence (01:54, 07:54, 13:54, 19:54 local), self-heals within ~2 s, 17 times in the 7-day log window: `net: local proxy refused connections; requests go direct until it returns`.
- That window is the environment this issue is written from: a flaky edge, a third-party OpenAI-compatible provider, a model that streams reasoning. Nothing in the report depends on the provider's identity.
- One `Provider plan quota exhausted` cluster (2026-11-09) is the provider's own weekly limit and is not a defect.

milestone.title: v0.10.3
milestone.description:
Corrective release and exact-candidate qualification. Release scope approved November 5, 2026.

Keep history/undo and compaction continuity, login/model selection, worker durability and safe retries, bounded input/output, runtime responsiveness, and supported installation/client qualification here. Use release-blocker for the unresolved repair/qualification gates. Use status:awaiting-release for source fixes that are landed but still need final verification and shipment; do not close them merely because main contains the fix.

Broad refactors, optional features, full historical audit sweeps and unqualified optimization claims move to the later planning milestones. This replaces the previous all-refactors-for-0.10.3 umbrella scope; unfinished requirements are deferred, not completed or discarded. Confirmed release-critical defects must not be hidden by a future umbrella target.

Freeze the final source and binaries, finish the required platform/client evidence, then run final validation. Provider spend, signing and publication retain their separate approvals. No due date or published release is created by this milestone.

issues.body:
What 0.10.3 is still working on, and where you can help. The current source candidate is described in the [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) under `[0.10.3]`. It is not a published release until the tag, packages and checksums exist.

## Start here

Every work item below lists **ways to help** (with the files, the command to test locally and what "done" means), and also what maintainers are already building, so you don't duplicate it. Comment on the issue to claim a piece.

| If you… | Try |
| --- | --- |
| don't write Rust but use DSH plugins | qualify one plugin row in #7278 |
| have Claude Code, Codex, Kimi or another agent CLI installed | try it inside Codewhale and report (#7279, way 1) |
| use Zed or another ACP editor | drive Codewhale from it and report (#7280, way 1) |
| are on Windows (especially ARM64 or a non-English locale) | run the checklist in #7281 |
| want a first Rust PR | add an ACP agent such as Qwen Code to the registry (#7279, way 2) |
| write docs, in English or Chinese | the editor setup page (#7280), the other-agents page (#7279), or the dial docs (#7283) |

New to the repo? [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) covers setup, the fast local test loop, and how your PR lands with you as its author.

## Work items
- #7278: all surveyed DSH plugins pass unmodified on the 0.2.2-rc.1 host
- #7279: run installed agents (Claude Code, Codex, Kimi and others) as Codewhale sessions over ACP
- #7280: drive Codewhale from an editor over ACP (ACP server)
- #7281: Windows test suite green on the release candidate
- #7282: terminals and background jobs belong to their conversation
- #7283: one permission dial with Accept Edits as the default

## Reported bugs in this release
Everything else in the [v0.10.3 milestone](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/milestone/73). Issues labelled `status:awaiting-release` are fixed in source and wait for the tag. Open bugs without a linked PR are open to take, the same way.

## Moved out of 0.10.3
- **Codex App Server v2 compatibility.** Finishing it is paused so this release can focus on ACP and the DSH plugins. The HTTP/SSE Runtime API stays the supported way for the desktop, mobile and other clients to reach the Engine.

- **Complete and verifiable uninstall** moves to 0.10.4 (#7091).

prs.title: fix(fleet,work_graph,rlm,hooks): resolve 8 R10 audit defects
prs.body:
## What and why

Fixes all 8 verified defects from audit unit R10 across `fleet`, `work_graph`, `rlm`, and `hooks`:

- **R10-L4-01** (`crates/engine/src/fleet/store.rs`): Propagate `personal_fleets_dir()?` errors in `load_fleet_at` instead of falling back to an empty `PathBuf` (which made `path.starts_with("")` return `true` and silently misclassified workspace fleets as `FleetScope::Personal`).
- **R10-L6-01** (`crates/hooks/src/lifecycle_outbox.rs`): Remove the process-local `next_seq`/`recovered` cache in `WriterState` and serialize tail seq recovery + batch append under an exclusive advisory file lock (`File::lock` inside `spawn_blocking`) so concurrent writers sharing one outbox path produce strictly monotonic, unique `seq` values.
- **R10-L8-01** (`crates/hooks/src/lifecycle_outbox.rs`): Carry `Result<(), String>` through `OutboxCommand::Flush` and track pending append/webhook failures across batches so `LifecycleOutbox::flush` surfaces failures instead of acknowledging `Ok(())` after a failed durable write.
- **R10-L8-02** (`crates/engine/src/work_graph/{events,reducer,runtime}.rs`): Distinguish lane load failures (e.g. corrupt JSON or I/O errors) from `NotFound` absences in `reconcile_workspace_snapshot` by logging a structured `tracing::warn!`, emitting `OperationObservation::OwnerUnreadable`, and recording a distinct `reconcile_operation_owner_unreadable` receipt while remaining fail-closed (`NodeState::Stale`).
- **R10-L9-01** (`crates/engine/src/rlm/bridge.rs`): Return a single bounded `SingleResp` error from `batch_guard` for oversized batches and invalid `dependency_mode` instead of fanning out `O(prompt_count)` allocations.
- **R10-L10-01** (`crates/hooks/src/lifecycle_outbox.rs`): Call `file.sync_all()` after `file.flush()` in `append_lines` before spawning webhook posts or acknowledging flush barriers.
- **R10-L10-02** (`crates/hooks/src/lib.rs`, `crates/hooks/src/lifecycle_outbox.rs`): Attach a stable `Idempotency-Key` header reused across retries in `WebhookHookSink` (derived from outbox sink identity + `event.seq` for outbox deliveries) and document the deduplication contract.
- **R10-L12-01** (`crates/engine/src/fleet/{store,members}.rs`, `crates/localization/`): Add localized `MessageId` entries for all six `FleetStoreError` variants across all 15 shipped locale packs and route `FleetModelError::Store` through `FleetStoreError::message(locale)`.

## Where this came from

Closes #7466

## How I tested it

- `cargo test -p codewhale-engine --lib rlm` (`RUST_MIN_STACK=16777216`): `test result: ok. 107 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 7773 filtered out; finished in 15.33s`

prs.title: fix(tui): let a session switch adopt a populated Runtime store
prs.body:
## What this changes

A session switch can now open a conversation whose Runtime store already holds history.

Before, `apply_loaded_session_with_goal` refused any target store with a non-empty `threads/` directory. The check was aimed at the wrong store. A switch never abandons the target — that store stays on disk for whichever process opens it next — and the host keeps holding the one it already has until the switch explicitly releases it. What a switch must not do is release a store that still needs *this* process, which is a property of the store being **left**.

So the check moves:

- `HasDurableWork` stops being a refusal. Only conditions that make the target unusable from here still refuse: a live process holding its lock, an unconfined or non-directory path, or a scope-pinned automation.
- `current_store_is_disposable` (async) asks whether the store being left has work in flight: a loaded engine with an active turn, or a request waiting on a decision that lives only in memory (`has_unsettled_requests`). Finished history is not work.
- A binding whose recorded scope no longer matches its own owner file is stale, not adoptable — that stays on the recover-onto-this-host path.
- `LoadedSessionOutcome` reports the store to adopt; `adopt_runtime_store` settles the old engines, releases the process-owner lock, and starts a new manager with the saved binding.
- The abandoned store goes through `retire_unbound_store_in_background`, which moves an unbound store to `.set-aside/` and refuses one any document still names.

### Why the first version of this was wrong

The initial patch reused `adoption_refusal` to judge the *current* store. That predicate answers "may a host take this store over?", and opening a store writes `owner.json`, `state.json` and the work directories — so a store that has never run a turn already reports `HasDurableWork`. Every switch out of a freshly started host would have been refused. Three existing tests caught it; `ee28d088f` is the correction.

## Verification

```
runtime_store_binding   15 passed, 0 failed   (default 2 MiB test stack)
tui::ui::tests::       941 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored
```

`main` (05a9a62e0) at the same point: 939 passed, and `picker_adoption_keeps_a_store_another_document_binds` overflows at the default stack — that group only passes with `RUST_MIN_STACK=32MiB`. This branch runs all 15 at the default stack.

`52fb7e9d4` fixes that: `adopt_runtime_store` returns a boxed future (it contains `TaskManager::start`, whose state machine inlined into the session-load path), and the exit test boxes each of its two `TaskManager::start` calls separately.

Two new tests:

- `switch_adopts_a_store_holding_finished_history` — a populated target is adopted, and the returned binding names it.
- `switch_allows_leaving_a_store_with_finished_history` — history in the store being left does not block a switch.

`cargo fmt --all -- --check` passes. Clippy reports pre-existing findings in `client.rs`, `compaction.rs`, `config.rs` and `runtime_threads.rs:13523` — none in the files this PR touches.

## Known limitations

- A turn active on *another thread* in the store being left is not visible to `session_transition_blocked` (it reads the current conversation's panel). `shutdown_and_wait` interrupts it, and the record is marked `Interrupted by process restart`. Naming the switch as the cause would need `interrupt_turn` to take a reason.
- The failure path in `adopt_runtime_store` (manager set to `None`, user told to run `codewhale resume`) has no test coverage.

Refs #6207, #6225, #6418

prs.title: perf(engine): cache the item index across processes
prs.body:
## What and why

The first thread a process opens pays a pass over the whole items directory: an item's filename carries only its item id, never its turn, so the only way to learn which items a turn owns is to open the item records. The in-memory index made that a one-time cost per process, and the server already warms it at startup — but nothing about the answer outlived the process, so a restarted engine (or any other client process) paid it again. Against a 55,572-item store that is the entire open time of the first conversation.

The index is now cached beside the directories it describes (`item-index.json` at the store root) and rebuilt from a directory listing plus only the entries the cache does not hold. The listing decides membership, so the cache cannot make an answer wrong: an entry that names a deleted item is simply not consulted, and a missing, unreadable or out-of-date file costs one full read — exactly what every process used to pay.

Measured on the same 55,572-item store, first index build in a process:

| | |
| --- | --- |
| before | 3.9s |
| after | 93ms |

Three deliberate choices:

- **Reading never writes.** Caching is `RuntimeThreadStore::cache_item_index`, called only by the startup warm-up. A `GET` that created a file would break what those routes promise, and the existing tests that snapshot a store to prove a route is read-only cover it.
- **The cache is not fsynced.** Losing it to a crash costs the next process one full read, which is the state every process was in before it existed. The write is a rename over a per-process temporary, so a reader never sees a partial file.
- **The cold pass no longer materializes records.** Deserializing into a one-field reference instead of `TurnItemRecord` avoids allocating a tool result's `detail` and `metadata` to learn an id.

## Where this came from

A bug fix with no issue: reopening a long conversation after a restart sat on the previous conversation for seconds, with the delay growing with the store. Diagnosis and measurements are in the commit message.

## How I tested it

```
cargo fmt --all --check                                   # clean
cargo clippy -p codewhale-engine --lib                    # no new warnings
cargo test -p codewhale-engine --lib -- runtime_threads::tests
                                                          # 346 passed
cargo test -p codewhale-app-server --lib -- \
  thread_summary_search_does_not_scan_the_whole_store_per_thread \
  thread_summary_listing_never_walks_the_items_directory \
  turn_operation_lookup_is_authenticated_read_only_and_survives_restart
                                                          # 3 passed
```

New tests cover the cache surviving a process, learning items written while it was closed, forgetting a deleted item, falling back from a damaged or foreign-version file, a read-only handle never writing, and — the invariant above — a read leaving the store byte-identical.

One pre-existing failure, unrelated: `runtime_threads::tests::engine_withdrawal_retires_approval_and_unblocks_queued_events` is flaky on `main` (it fails 2 of 3 runs there and 1 of 3 here; it passes when run alone). The same module needs `RUST_MIN_STACK` raised in a debug build for two other cases to fit, also on `main`.

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change, started from current `main`
- [x] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior
- [x] No user-facing docs or `docs/features.toml` row: this changes how fast a thread opens, not what it does

prs.title: feat(ci): add the maintainer gate and regression stage (#7433)
prs.body:
## What and why

Implements the protocol in #7433: a maintainer gate before agent work, and a regression stage after it.

- **Part 1 — startability is a grant.** The Agent task form no longer self-applies `agent-ready`. The metadata contract test now rejects the default instead of pinning it. CONTRIBUTING, ISSUE_TRIAGE, AGENT_ETHOS (en/zh), FLEET (en/zh), the fleet-manager skill and the remote-smoke runbook say that absence means not startable.
- **Part 2a — behavioural guards.** `crates/engine/tests/behavioural_guards.rs` holds one positive assertion per promise, each citing its issue: the agent-ready gate (#7433) and the tool-call fallback id rule (#7423). A rename can no longer invert it silently.
- **Part 2b — behaviour statements.** `scripts/check-behaviour-line.py` requires `Behaviour: <old> -> <new>` or `No-behaviour-change: <why>` on fix/feat/perf/refactor commits in the push range; it is wired into `scripts/preflight.sh` and the helper-contract CI step.
- **Part 3 — regression stage.** `docs/RELEASE_CHECKLIST.md` names the per-slice review receipt (`review --base <sha> --path <path> --write-receipt`, then `--check-receipt`) as the regression pass. A receipt with unresolved risk blocks the candidate until a maintainer reads the findings.
- **Part 4/5 — triage standards.** ISSUE_TRIAGE gains Startability, the regression threshold, the severity mapping (`p1` minimum, `release-blocker` by maintainer decision, `p0` only for data loss/security/release path), the closing standard, and the #7432 disposition.
- **Part 5b — docs drift.** `scripts/check-docs-drift.py` requires a touched feature row to update its summary and to name its flag or id on the docs page it points at.

## Where this came from

Refs #7433. The protocol is forward-looking; #7432 is left open for the maintainer to resolve by restoring the parent index or correcting the docs.

## How I tested it

- `cargo test -p codewhale-engine --test behavioural_guards` — 2 passed
- `cargo test -p codewhale-skills --lib` — 194 passed
- `bash .github/scripts/agent-task-metadata.test.sh` — passed
- `PYTHON=python bash scripts/check-behaviour-line.test.sh` — passed
- `python scripts/check-docs-drift.test.py` — 4 passed
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` — passed
- `python scripts/check-behaviour-line.py main HEAD` and `python scripts/check-docs-drift.py main HEAD` — passed on the four commits in this branch

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change, started from current `main` (no need to rebase when `main` moves)
- [x] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior
- [ ] If this adds or changes a user-facing feature, I updated its docs and its row in `docs/features.toml` (`cargo test -p codewhale-tui --test feature_registry` checks it)

prs.title: feat(acp): file tool calls carry their absolute location and the requested diff
prs.body:
## Summary Refs #7280 (ACP server lane for 0.10.3). I checked #7280's four gaps against the code. One code gap was still open: - **Session load/resume:** already on this branch (`session/list`, `session/load` with prefix match, durable replay, checkpoint after each turn). - **Permission dial:** already on this branch. The editor gets `session/request_permission` tied to the Runtime approval, with responder `ApprovalResponder::Acp`. The posture is server-owned and read-only, and remembered grants are never given. That is the documented contract. - **Plugins in ACP sessions:** already on this branch (CW-7941 and CW-8050: extension host plus configured MCP servers, and nested approvals). - **File/terminal tool updates:** this was the gap, and this PR fixes it. A tool call carried only a title and `rawInput`, so an editor could not follow the agent to the file or show the change. `tool_call_start(call, workspace)` now: ``` kind ∈ {Read, Edit} && input.path → locations: [{ path: workspace.join(path) }] kind == Edit → content: [diff { path, newText: content }] // write [diff { path, oldText: search, newText: replace }] // edit (+ old_string/new_string… aliases) ``` - The live projection gets the workspace from `ThreadRecord.workspace`. - `session/load` replay gets it from `SessionMetadata.workspace`. - `apply_patch` gets no diff. - Shell output is still text content: editor-owned ACP `terminal` content is not used. `docs/RUNTIME_API.md` now says so. - CHANGELOG has a new 0.10.3 line, and `scripts/sync-changelog.sh` was run. ## Tests (Linux, bubblewrap installed) - `cargo test -p codewhale-app-server --lib acp_server`: **44 passed; 0 failed**. This includes the new `file_tool_start_names_absolute_location_and_requested_diff`. - `cargo test -p codewhale-app-server --test integration acp`: **4 passed; 0 failed**. These are `acp_conformance::every_frame_the_acp_server_writes_is_an_official_v1_shape` and the 3 `acp_journey` tests. - `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean. Not run: a real-editor (Zed) journey. ---

provider = "trustedrouter"

prs.title: feat(workflow): verify sealed candidates with an isolated host oracle
prs.body:
Refs #7250
Extracted from #7262

This is the maintainer-requested, opt-in verified evaluator slice. The evolutionary Draft PR remains separate and unchanged.

## Evaluator

- Freeze a versioned host spec, clean Git baseline, authorized write/protected scope, trusted public and held-out cases, executable identities, and a Linux bubblewrap capability probe.
- Accept completed Workflow worktrees; seal added/modified/deleted/binary/mode changes and replay from the sealed artifact after the writer worktree is gone.
- Run candidate commands in isolated processes and compare actual JSON output with the host oracle. Receipts bind spec, baseline, oracle, artifact/tree, sandbox and native binary identities. Public PASS requires public-plus-held-out replay.
- Wire the evaluator into the existing `operate_best_of_n` search Workflow only when `args.evaluator` is supplied. Results are `proposal_only`; there is no candidate apply, push, merge, policy genome, or mutation operator.

## Maintainer review fixes

- **Normal-user namespace creation:** the evaluator-specific `RLIMIT_NPROC` is 4096, and the probe reports that effective value. The old 32 limit counted all tasks owned by the Linux user. PID namespace isolation, `--die-with-parent`, cancellation, CPU/time bounds, filesystem/network restrictions and process cleanup remain in place.
- **Published-crate source identity:** the evaluator hashes the actual loaded Workflow source and compares it with a checked-in SHA-256 constant. The repository script path is referenced only by excluded test source. Exact checked-in content is accepted; a modified script fails closed. The update procedure is documented.
- **Evaluation deadline:** the aggregate budget counts active candidate evaluation and replay time, starting after generation. Receipts record effective start, elapsed time, deadline and stop reason; the delayed-generation regression passes.
- **Artifact capture:** a frozen policy records and excludes untracked root `target/` and `__pycache__/` outputs. Tracked and protected files remain checked, legitimate new source remains captured, and out-of-scope writes still fail. Exclusions appear in artifact and receipt provenance.
- **Descendant test and macOS:** the lifecycle test uses a writable in-sandbox marker, a surviving negative control, and timeout/cancellation cleanup checks. The non-Linux `UNSUPPORTED_ISOLATION` branch no longer has the unnecessary-return warning.

## Final validation at `61b889cf6ec10df5c048ef15715dbb272ccacf77`

- [Upstream PR CI](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/actions/runs/43344788042): 10 successful jobs, 12 path-skipped, 0 failed. Workspace format, strict Clippy and Windows all-targets check passed. The PR view also counts the successful triage check.
- [Hosted final-head build](https://github.com/axobase001/DeepSeek-TUI/actions/runs/43345093377): Rocky Linux 8 full CLI build, 9 focused Rust tests, evaluator crate checks and package file listing passed; Windows focused check and 5 tests passed; macOS focused check and strict Clippy passed. The hosted Linux runner lacked bubblewrap, so real isolation was validated separately.
- **Real non-root Linux isolation:** on the 47 VPS, `nobody` (uid 65534) owned 40 preflight tasks. A 32-limit bubblewrap control reproduced the namespace error; 4096 succeeded. All 9 evaluator tests then executed under bubblewrap and passed (113.64 s), including cancellation and descendant cleanup.
- **Native Workflow E2E:** the exact final-head CLI ran a local scripted provider. A false PASS claim failed 2 public cases; the isolated candidate passed 2 public and 3 public-plus-held-out replay cases, ending `proposal_only`. No-evaluator and modified-source rejection controls passed. An independent verifier recomputed 7 case outcomes and 2 sealed tree hashes.
- **Package file set:** [independent run](https://github.com/axobase001/DeepSeek-TUI/actions/runs/43345093627) compiled the exact listed engine files with the repository Workflow script removed, using local sibling 0.10.3 crates. The artifact records this final SHA.

## Evidence and release gate

The [final-head validation report](https://github.com/axobase001/DeepSeek-TUI/blob/experiment/7250-native-evidence/evidence/7250/PR7294_final_61b889c_validation_2026-11-13.md) and [100 KB evidence bundle](https://github.com/axobase001/DeepSeek-TUI/blob/experiment/7250-native-evidence/evidence/7250/CodeWhale_PR7294_Final_61b889c_Evidence_2026-11-13.zip) contain raw non-root/native receipts, the independent verifier, package file-set proof, and the standard package failure log. Historical failures remain in the [earlier evidence bundle](https://github.com/axobase001/DeepSeek-TUI/blob/experiment/7250-native-evidence/evidence/7250/CodeWhale_PR7294_Review_Fixes_Evidence_Lite_2026-11-13.zip). The [final Linux binary artifact](https://github.com/axobase001/DeepSeek-TUI/actions/runs/43345093377/artifacts/14001504445) binds the CLI and Rust test executable used on the VPS.

`cargo package --locked -p codewhale-engine` still exits 101 during dependency resolution: crates.io offers `codewhale-agent` up to 0.10.2, while this workspace requires 0.10.3. The [raw failure artifact](https://github.com/axobase001/DeepSeek-TUI/actions/runs/43345093377/artifacts/14002692655) is preserved. Standard package verification awaits the sibling crate release; the independently compiled package file set validates the removed out-of-crate source reference.

prs.title: experiment(workflow): evidence-gated evolutionary coding search
prs.body:
## Scope and state

Addresses #7250 with an opt-in, review-only evolutionary coding experiment using the existing Workflow/Fleet/Runtime infrastructure. This PR remains **Draft**. The initial host evaluator is its own commit (`c544521`); subsequent host hardening and orchestration changes are separate reviewable commits.

## R3 response to the independent R2 audit

- Derive admission reservations from the effective genome, reserve two final Reviewer turns, and include planner, writer and extra DEV Reviewer usage in selection, including failed calls.
- Bind Rust evaluator, Workflow and Reviewer to the sealed artifact ID, candidate tree hash and complete review-material SHA256/length. An unknown verdict records `INCOMPLETE` and `unreviewed_scope: ["whole_artifact"]`.
- Keep the Reviewer independent and read-only; a bounded second request handles an observed tool-only first response. A repeated tool-only response remains `NONE`.
- Checkpoint complete generation boundaries, verify binary/baseline/oracle/policy/artifacts and request events on resume, restore population and budget, and reject unknown post-checkpoint work. Cross-process replay uses verified sealed artifacts; fresh evaluation still requires a completed current-process worker.
- Add native CLI E2Es for sandbox denial, inherited host descriptor/provider environment, CAS replay/tamper, unavailable backend, descendant cancellation and G2→G3 restart. The host closes inherited Linux descriptors before launching the isolated evaluator.
- Add a frozen two-policy × two-DEV-task receipt selector with full reported costs, then validate one frozen policy on a new held-out task.

## Earlier real-provider diagnostic (preserved)

Plan SHA256 `e81facde236ad81f1c8b6a04e31bff4a99a1ab1e73f0fefbdce3dc7269784274`; real-run CLI SHA256 `8b62f3f528a77f883a827db59e9cf10584bba0a902aa22ae088165f2f87a2a8a9`. One candidate per cell, at most 11 host-reserved model turns, shared baseline/oracle per DEV task. `replicate_0` is a label; the provider did not offer seed control.

| DEV task | Base policy | Inherited evolved policy |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CSV | public 20/20, replay 30/30, final Reviewer PASS, completed `proposal_only`; 9,720 microUSD | public 20/20, replay 30/30, final Reviewer PASS after one failed DEV review; workflow degraded/CLI exit 1, `proposal_only`; 17,121 microUSD |
| JSONPath | public FAIL at case 22/41, winner NONE; 25,785 microUSD | public 41/41, two DEV Reviewer calls tool-only, no replay/final review, winner NONE; 58,281 microUSD |

Both policies complete 1/2 DEV tasks. Full reported panel cost: base 35,505 microUSD; evolved 75,402 microUSD. The selector chooses base (`selection_id` `6a4d9a73fa76de69f43556c9fd702ddb4d899d92fb9fa7c17ac15e2be01c0051d`). Recomputing from raw task receipts produced the same ID and ranking.

On a fresh Accept-Language holdout, the selected base policy achieved public 24/24, sealed replay 30/30, final Reviewer PASS and `proposal_only`, at 45,897 microUSD. Promotion was **NOT_QUALIFIED**: the selected genome was unchanged base and it passed only one of two DEV tasks. An earlier holdout run carried an incorrectly transcribed source evaluation ID; that provenance failure and raw run are retained.

## Latest-upstream real-provider result

The exact `3cd684d` CLI was fully built in Rocky Linux 8 and verified on the VPS (SHA256 `88f1004542e62f5c09be378c09028b5795a228d970e5c261c5737d390cbbb0a0`, GLIBC_2.28 required, host 2.32). Frozen panel SHA256 `72f068b437c57aa3a5a135fbde11bd38c85f78a55900b437c4e2dcc59b2a2f17`; two genomes × two shared DEV tasks, one candidate and 11 reserved model turns per cell. `replicate_0` is a label, not a provider-controlled seed.

| DEV task | Base | Inherited evolved |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CSV | public 20/20, replay 30/30, final COMPLETE/PASS; 9,862 microUSD | public 20/20, replay 30/30, final COMPLETE/PASS; 24,662 microUSD |
| JSONPath | public 41/41, replay 54/54, final COMPLETE/FAIL, winner NONE; 82,525 microUSD | public 41/41, replay 54/54, final COMPLETE/PASS; 162,462 microUSD |

The base JSONPath Reviewer found an unhandled `NaN`/`Infinity` JSON-contract failure despite the functional gates passing. The policy selector therefore counted evolved 2/2 tasks and base 1/2, with full reported panel costs 187,124 and 92,387 microUSD. It selected evolved (`selection_id` `ed72ed9fbff5f7fa06981b934ffa6e0002a38cdd9edc8686e1b421b0397cfb4a`). The selected genome alone transferred to fresh Accept-Language: public 24/24, sealed replay 30/30, final COMPLETE/PASS, completed Workflow, 94,185 microUSD. The independent proposal is **`QUALIFIED_FOR_REVIEW`**, `proposal_only`, ID `bfe2f343036445c1a293d220f4e3def7211bf910d3e7bd29eefb725b38ae9e7b`. It changes no production policy.

## Native verification

The reviewer prompt is now genuinely read-only: an outbound provider probe
captured nine schema-bound DEV/final review requests and verified that they
offered no tools, explicitly prohibited tool use, and omitted the former
`read`/`bash` guidance. The same native E2E reached public PASS, sealed replay
PASS and final COMPLETE/PASS. Its intentionally failed first DEV reviews leave
the Workflow degraded, as recorded in the raw receipt.

On the compiled `823e697` CLI (SHA256 `b0d6362bc3578e6e9f687dac8677c04e7c4bde398c07c8205bb22ddc4aac84969`), seven native E2Es exited 0: generation-boundary resume, inherited descriptor/provider environment denial, sealed CAS replay/tamper, missing backend refusal, descendant cancellation, admission preflight and bounded Reviewer retry. The upstream `1f9ad30` preflight passed on `5c2e615`. The exact ninth path canonicalization in `experimental_search.rs` is counted in the blocking-call ratchet; its Workflow call sites run in `spawn_blocking`.

Upstream `main` advanced to `8ddd9025`, merged in `5acf8452` without conflict. The 3.5 GiB VPS hit global OOM in `codewhale-engine` on three full-build attempts; all failed logs are preserved, and temporary swap/settings were restored. A hosted Ubuntu build of `0bcd0685` completed but requires GLIBC_2.39; its incompatible loader receipt is retained. The Rocky Linux 8 build of Draft head `3cd684d` succeeded in run `42984213312`; artifact ZIP SHA256 `3bca58f5f08e6d92b900a6508e8e24e3eab0dd7d65e6a035e936731d00491ad0` matches GitHub, and the extracted CLI ran on the VPS. All seven native E2Es exited 0 on that exact binary, including G2→G3 restart, isolation, CAS tamper, backend refusal, cancellation, preflight and Reviewer retry. Final PR CI Lint (including Clippy) and Windows full-workspace compile passed in run `42980847436`. The failed checkout and `safe.directory` receipt attempts are preserved alongside the successful full build log.

## Open acceptance items

- Earlier JSONPath tool-only Reviewer failures remain in the raw evidence. The latest frozen panel and holdout all produced structured real DeepSeek Reviewer verdicts; wider provider reliability is unmeasured.
- Resume is qualified only at a completed generation boundary; unknown mid-request work refuses automatic replay. Settlement of duplicate/out-of-order provider completions remains open.
- Candidate/process limits and host model-turn reservations are enforced. A global hard token/currency cap and aggregate scratch/memory quota remain open.
- The test VPS uses Alibaba Cloud Linux 3 `bubblewrap-0.4.0-2.2.al8` with 2024 backports. Requalify on a patched backend before wider trust claims.
- The final-binary four-arm real-provider comparison is still open. After the panel and holdout, the authorized account balance was CNY 6.80; a real second-generation four-arm run could exceed it, so no extra paid calls were made. Prior R2 four-arm data remains in its original handoff, with no generalized improvement claim.

No merge or production setting change is requested.

prs.title: feat: source navigation echoes and guarded fork-prefix inheritance
prs.body:
Native `read` windows retain their revision guard through the final model-request projection. `grep_files` adds bounded Rust navigation hints, and forked agents retain eligible parent prefixes.

<details>
<summary>GPT 6.1 Sol 900k High</summary>

## Source and scope

Current head: [`db1390a64`](https://github.com/AdityaVG13/CodeWhale/commit/db1390a64445533dcc0285bd3f8499ca05695e76), incorporating the approved upstream snapshot [`1f9ad30c1`](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/commit/1f9ad30c1f8ab5c94652d77e6bed512eb97a4cc2). Earlier integration commits, including `f46d406da`, remain ancestors. Original contributor commits and credit are preserved; this is a non-rewriting update of the existing PR branch.

There is no replacement turn loop, persistent source index or indexing daemon.

- Revision-qualified Rust references carry a path, source window and revision. Changed source is refused; guarded continuations require forward progress and retain snapshot identity.
- Focused Rust searches can supply bounded declaration windows and small complete bodies. Syntax-derived identifier and one-hop call-candidate hints are bounded evidence, not macro expansion, name resolution, type resolution or a complete impact graph. Broad/truncated searches retain their ordinary output.
- Native `grep_files` is eager beside file-name search. Child/scout/workflow fixtures retain current catalog, cache-budget and root-goal authority boundaries.
- Echoes are append-only tool/history evidence, not volatile additions to the pinned system/tool prefix. Host observations, current authority and evidence actually delivered to a model remain separate.
- Fork-prefix inheritance requires matching route/model/opaque receipt and a supported dialect. Unsupported or changed identities take the cold path; no live-provider cache saving is claimed.
- The skill index keeps eligible names enumerable without exposing mutable native skill paths. Workflow events retain task/workspace ownership.
- Execution-matched canonical reads retain their native envelope through final Chat Completions projection. Legacy, missing/mismatched execution identities and over-budget results retain the ordinary backstop. A source-looking footer is not authority.
- Finite headless turns receive a logged working-deadline notice while tools remain usable. Exhausted ordinary turns can deliver a final text report without falsely becoming successful; cancellation and the distinct goal-pause contract remain intact.
- Configuration help and its generated website copy now match the native reader: 50 KiB by default, at most 2,000 lines, 2,000-character line truncation and an operator-only byte override up to 2 MiB. The model has no `max_bytes` parameter. Raising the read budget does not disable ordinary spillover.

## Verification of the integrated engine

The selected engine library suite compiled through a remote RCH job on Linux/aarch64. Its initial run had **318 passing tests and one failing Rust-format normalization assertion**. With no source changes, rerunning the same compiled selection produced **319 passed, 0 failed, 0 ignored**. Both outcomes are retained; the first failure is not relabeled as a pass and its cause is not established.

The selection covers echolocation, native reads and dispatch, guarded search, wire projection, deadline/admission/report-only fences, catalog deferral, fork-prefix and warmed-tool behavior, schema-cache admission limits, goal pause and the shared base-prompt previews. The committed tree is `0d0c9bb7c3296ef443f74fe3c0623a8f95722cc7`, identical to the staged tree used for the declared input manifest.

The RCH job executed this one-package Cargo command:

```sh
cargo test --locked -p codewhale-engine --lib -- \
  tools::echolocation:: \
  tools::file::tests:: \
  tools::file_tool::tests:: \
  tools::search::tests:: \
  client::chat::stream_decoder_tests:: \
  admission_gates:: \
  small_surface_ \
  model_tool_catalog_applies_native_and_mcp_deferral \
  capability_compact_surface_defers_nonessential_core_tools \
  capability_full_surface_preserves_small_default_head \
  goal_turn_uses_goal_step_allowance_and_pauses_budget_limit_after_final_report \
  eager_agent_and_workflow_stay_offered_without_search_rejection \
  forked_subagent_messages_preserve_parent_prefix_then_append_task \
  session_projection_exposes_forked_prefix_cache_contract \
  warmed_surfaces_rebuild_byte_identical_wire_tools \
  best_match_survives_byte_overflow_eviction \
  oversized_schema_is_never_admitted \
  prompts::base_preview::tests:: \
  --test-threads=1
```

DSR reported that `codewhale` is not configured when queried with `dsr quality --tool codewhale --dry-run`; RCH was the fallback. This is bounded declared-input verification, **not an exhaustive compiler-input or source-content receipt**. There was no local heavy compilation or full workspace test run.

Additional checks passed:

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and integration-relative whitespace validation.
- Four selected existing website test files: **37 passed**.
- Website TypeScript and generated-facts validation. The published v0.10.2 tag is absent locally, so its committed baseline was retained rather than claiming it was recomputed.
- UBS on the edited prompt file: **0 critical, 0 warnings**, five informational findings. This is not a security-audit claim.

The integration retains upstream's version-aware tool rows, fetch deadlines, scheduled-handler checks and regenerated public facts alongside the PR's guarded-read and cache contracts. Upstream-only changes outside these selected areas were not exhaustively retested. No packaged release or native macOS/Windows acceptance is claimed.

## Native CLI admission of this head

A fresh Linux/aarch64 development CLI for the integrated candidate passed the unchanged standalone v3 scripted native probe on both cold and pre-seeded startup paths. It reports `codewhale 0.10.3 (dev)`; binary SHA-256: `d91f36e98227210c71cde32c4a91da2ac804cc90a948eb1a27c917b0fd2536f1`.

The RCH job built only `codewhale-cli` and exited 0. The declared **2,358 source and embedded inputs** matched before and after the build. The build began from the merge worktree before its commit was created: the original identity retains the pre-commit `f46d406da` metadata, while the manifest records the verified merge tree `0d0c9bb7c3296ef443f74fe3c0623a8f95722cc7` subsequently committed as `db1390a64`. This is a bounded input manifest, not an exhaustive compiler-input receipt.

- A **101,904-byte** native read reached the final provider request byte-for-byte in both cases.
- All **five negative guards** rejected source/test mutations, a nonempty writer lease, an extra runtime file and an unlocked foreign descriptor.
- Both cases preserved the complete post-startup workspace snapshot and retained `failed / budget_exhausted` for intentionally exhausted turns.
- Four scripted loopback requests were used, with **zero live-provider requests**. The loopback listener is closed and both native processes have exited.

The probe sets an explicit 128,000-byte operator read budget and requests a 1,940-line window of an existing frozen file. It retains the greater-than-100,000-byte assertion and stays below the unchanged classic 100 KiB spillover threshold. Earlier failed default-budget and spillover attempts remain failures, not passing receipts. This developer-build proof does not establish live task quality, packaged-release acceptance or native macOS/Windows acceptance.

## Still draft: task-quality gates

This merge integrates the fixed, approved `1f9ad30c1` snapshot, including its website removals. It does not automatically track subsequent upstream changes or claim mergeability against a moving base. The shared base prompt now explicitly restricts tool recommendations to tools offered in the current request. That is a new source condition, not evidence that earlier prompt wording caused a particular model choice.

This remains draft in accordance with [the contributor's scope decision](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/pull/6393#issuecomment-6207193232). Earlier failed and incomplete comparisons remain in [the maintained progress record](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/pull/6393#issuecomment-6185897898) and [the previous findings](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/pull/6393#issuecomment-6524708140).

Earlier live controls remain unqualified. An unchanged earlier answer later passed the behavior oracle offline using retained grading dependencies; that diagnosis does not retroactively qualify its stopped paid block. Grading dependencies are now hash-pinned outside mutable worker build pools.

A fresh fixed-order screen on this exact executable qualified both controls, then stopped on its first treatment. All three submitted repairs passed the unchanged behavior oracle, preserved existing tests and source-write boundaries, used only allowed tools, and reconciled usage without new uncertain requests.

| Slot | Native outcome | Behavioral oracle | Elapsed seconds | Cost upper bound, USD |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| `none_execute_8` | Completed; qualified | Pass | 103.628877 | 0.047872212 |
| `none_fileops_8` | Completed; qualified | Pass | 37.960547 | 0.017406456 |
| `full_execute_8` | Failed: 16 working model steps exhausted; unqualified | Pass | 139.475011 | 0.081516144 |

The treatment delivered a final report but correctly retained `failed / budget_exhausted`; a correct repair is not equivalent to completing within the frozen runtime allowance. The remaining three slots did not run. There were no paid retries or substitutions. Two earlier launcher failures forwarded zero provider requests and remain recorded separately.

The three executed slots made 41 provider requests with an aggregate cost upper bound of **$0.146794812**. The cumulative campaign upper bound is **$3.079885524 of $5**, including the retained historical unresolved reservation. These are ledger upper bounds, not invoices. The prior ledger prefix is unchanged; the gateway and all three native processes exited, and its forwarding port was independently checked closed.

This is not a positive efficiency result: on the execute task, the full treatment took longer, cost more, and failed the completion gate while its control qualified. It is one observation per executed slot, not a general causal result. None of the three attempts used a revision-qualified read. Provider/model, prompt bytes for the matched task, tool-schema hash and executable identity matched; request-prefix checks were stable. These observations neither establish guarded-reference adoption nor measure live fork-cache economics.

No general task-quality improvement, speedup, cost reduction, guarded-reference adoption, live-provider cache saving, independent quality review or merge readiness is claimed. Fresh controls must qualify before any fixed-order treatment; earlier answers are not retried or substituted for successful trials. There are no live fork-cache trials in this six-slot block; selected local prefix tests do not establish provider cache economics.

Refs #6393, CW-6439

</details>

prs.body:
## What and why

Fixes all six verified defects reported in audit R15 for `crates/config`:

- **R15-L4-01 (`legacy_root.rs`, `config_document.rs`)**: Pair each planned migration op with its receipt note and propagate `set_config_document_value` / `unset_config_document_value` errors (naming the conflicting path) from `apply_op_to_document`. Only emit receipt notes for ops that actually landed, keep `preview_document` consistent with `apply_to_document`, and have `migrate_legacy_root_config` use `try_apply_to_document` so a non-table destination parent fails loudly without writing a backup or false notice.
- **R15-L6-01 (`config_migration.rs`, `persistence.rs`)**: Add `persistence::atomic_write_if_absent` backed by `NamedTempFile::persist_noclobber` (mapping `AlreadyExists` to `Ok(false)`) and use it in `migrate_config_if_needed`, closing the `exists()`-then-replacing-rename TOCTOU race.
- **R15-L9-01 (`redaction.rs`, `path_io.rs`)**: Add shared `path_io::read_bounded_file_to_string` (checking `metadata().len()` up front and bounding reads via `.take(max_bytes + 1)`) and reuse it in both `read_string_no_follow` and `redaction::config_binding` with the 1 MiB ceiling before TOML parsing.
- **R15-L9-02 (`user_constitution.rs`)**: Enforce a 1 MiB file-byte ceiling (`MAX_USER_CONSTITUTION_FILE_BYTES`) before reading or deserializing in `load_from`, `migrate_file`, `rollback_file`, and `migrate_raw`, and pass `value` directly to `serde_json::from_value(value)` instead of cloning the full JSON graph.
- **R15-L10-01 (`persistence.rs`, `permissions.rs`)**: Sync the parent directory on Unix (`sync_parent_dir`, no-op on non-Unix) after `tmp.persist`, `tmp.persist_noclobber`, `rewrite_in_place`, and `write_permissions_atomic`, propagating sync failures instead of returning false success.
- **R15-L10-02 (`user_constitution.rs`)**: Write the migration rollback backup and rollback restore via `persistence::atomic_write` (file + parent directory fsync) before `save_to` runs, and log cleanup errors with `tracing::warn!` instead of dropping them with `.ok()`.

prs.title: fix(audit): resolve 8 verified R20 defects across net, notify, telemetry, ingest, and web gates
prs.body:
## What and why

Fixes all 8 verified R20 audit defects across `crates/net`, `crates/notify`, `crates/telemetry`, `telemetry-ingest`, and `web/scripts`:

- **R20-L4-01 (`crates/net/src/import_claude.rs`, `crates/command-contract/src/config.rs`, `crates/tui/src/commands/groups/config/import_claude.rs`)**: Preserve the `serde_json::Error` detail (including line/column) in `CommandSourceStatus::InvalidJson(String)` and include it in `CommandSourceStatus::describe` instead of discarding it.
- **R20-L7-01 (`crates/notify/src/audio.rs`)**: Bound external audio player execution (`afplay` / `aplay`) with a 15-second timeout via `spawn` + `try_wait` polling, killing and reaping a hung child so `Reset::drop` always releases the `PLAYING` busy latch.
- **R20-L8-01 (`web/scripts/check-release-docs.mjs`, `web/scripts/release-docs-lib.mjs`, `web/lib/agent-docs.test.ts`)**: Fail closed when the published release tag is unavailable and `derived` is `null` instead of printing OK, unless explicitly opted in via `--allow-shallow` or `CODEWHALE_ALLOW_SHALLOW_CHECKOUT=1`.
- **R20-L8-02 (`web/scripts/check-facts.mjs`, `web/scripts/release-baseline-lib.mjs`, `web/scripts/release-gates.test.mjs`)**: Extract `checkReleaseBaseline` and fail closed when the published release tag is unavailable instead of warning and exiting 0, unless explicitly opted in via `--allow-shallow` or `CODEWHALE_ALLOW_SHALLOW_CHECKOUT=1`.
- **R20-L9-01 (`telemetry-ingest/src/index.ts`, `telemetry-ingest/wrangler.jsonc`, `telemetry-ingest/test/ingest.test.ts`, `telemetry-ingest/test/support.ts`)**: Add a server-keyed `INGEST_RATE_LIMITER` binding keyed on `INGEST_PATH` before body reads, JSON parsing, and downstream delivery so rotating `install_id` cannot bypass Worker rate limiting, while preserving the zero-IP red line (`test/no-ip.test.ts`).
- **R20-L9-02 (`crates/telemetry/src/envelope.rs`)**: Bound `install_id.json` and `state.json` reads to 4 KiB (`MAX_METADATA_BYTES`) via metadata length pre-check and `File::take(MAX_METADATA_BYTES + 1)` before deserialization.
- **R20-L10-01 & R20-L10-02 (`crates/telemetry/src/buffer.rs`)**: Route both `rewrite` and `write_tombstone` through a shared `persist_atomic` helper that fsyncs the staged temp file (`sync_all`) before `persist` and fsyncs the parent directory after rename.

## Where this came from

Closes #7476

## How I tested it

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` — passed (0 diffs)
- `cargo test -p codewhale-command-contract -p codewhale-net -p codewhale-notify -p codewhale-telemetry --locked`:
  - `codewhale-command-contract`: `test result: ok. 79 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored`
  - `codewhale-net`: `test result: ok. 88 passed; 0 failed; 1 ignored`
  - `codewhale-notify`: `test result: ok. 33 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored`
  - `codewhale-telemetry`: `test result: ok. 79 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored`
- `cargo clippy -p codewhale-command-contract -p codewhale-net -p codewhale-notify -p codewhale-telemetry --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` — passed (0 warnings)
- `cargo clippy -p codewhale-notify --features test-thread-scoped-state --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` — passed (0 warnings)
- `telemetry-ingest`:
  - `npm test`: `Test Files 8 passed (8)`, `Tests 226 passed (226)` (including `no-ip.test.ts`, `schema-doc.test.ts`, and new rotating `install_id` rate-limit regression test)
  - `npm run typecheck`: passed (`tsc --noEmit`)
  - `npm run check`: passed (`wrangler deploy --dry-run` resolved `TELEMETRY`, `RATE_LIMITER`, and `INGEST_RATE_LIMITER`)
- `web/scripts`:
  - `node --test web/scripts/docs-sources.test.mjs web/scripts/release-gates.test.mjs`: `tests 3, pass 3, fail 0`
  - `node web/scripts/check-release-docs.mjs`: `[check-release-docs] OK — snapshot is for v0.10.3, the published release`
  - `node web/scripts/check-facts.mjs`: `[check-facts] OK — committed facts.generated.ts matches workspace`
  - `node web/scripts/check-cloud-facts.mjs` & `node web/scripts/check-media-honesty.mjs`: passed

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change, started from current `main` (no need to rebase when `main` moves)
- [x] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior
- [x] If this adds or changes a user-facing feature, I updated its docs and its row in `docs/features.toml` (`cargo test -p codewhale-tui --test feature_registry` checks it)

prs.title: fix(bridges): keep code fences intact when a reply is split by bytes
prs.body:
## What and why

`splitMessage(text, maxChars, maxBytes)` applies the UTF-8 byte cap (added in #7209 for WeCom, `WECOM_MAX_REPLY_BYTES`, default 3800) as a second pass. That pass cuts each fence-aware chunk at the last code point that fits, and it does not look at newlines or code fences. A 3500-character CJK chunk is about 10 KB, so almost every long Chinese reply on WeCom goes through this pass. When the reply contains a code block:

- the first chunk ends mid-line (here, mid-word) and leaves its ```` ```js ```` fence open;
- the second chunk starts with no opening fence, so its closing ```` ``` ```` opens a new block, and the rest of that message renders as code.

**Repro** (current `main`, a reply with a heading line, a 120-line commented JS block and a closing line, 4014 chars / 6680 bytes, `splitMessage(reply, 3500, 3800)`):

```
chunk 0: bytes=3798 fenceLines=1 ends="这是第68行的中文注释说"
chunk 1: bytes=2002 fenceLines=1 ends="行的中文注释说明\n```"
chunk 2: bytes=889 fenceLines=2 ends="注释说明\n```\n完成。"
```

With this change:

```
chunk 0: bytes=3750 fenceLines=2 ends="行的中文注释说明\n```"
chunk 1: bytes=2939 fenceLines=2 ends="注释说明\n```\n完成。"
```

**Change.** The byte cap now goes through the same chunker as the character cap. `takeRenderedSplitMessageChunk` already shrinks its payload when a chunk is over the character limit. It now also shrinks the payload when the chunk is over the byte limit, by at least the overflow divided by 4 bytes per code point. The split still prefers newlines and still closes and reopens the fence. The single-chunk shortcut now also requires the text to fit the byte cap. The existing code-point pass (`splitChunkByBytes`) stays as the fallback for caps too small to hold the fence markup.

The change only affects callers that pass a byte cap, which today is WeCom alone. With `maxBytes = 0` (Telegram, Feishu, Weixin, DingTalk) the output is the same as before.

## Where this came from

Bug fix, no issue. It follows up #7209. It is not in the integrations audit #7477.

## How I tested it

On Node 22.23.5, the version the `Integrations` job uses, I ran the same bridge loop that job runs:

- `npm test` in `bridge-core`: 78 tests, 77 pass, 1 skipped (that skip is already on `main`). `feishu-bridge` 19/19, `telegram-bridge` 39/39, `wecom-bridge` 22/22, `weixin-bridge` 59/59. `npm run check` in `bridge-core` passes.
- The new test "splitMessage byte cap keeps code fences balanced and splits on lines" passes. On the previous `src/lib.mjs` it fails, with a chunk containing one fence line.
- Old against new, outside the repo:
  - 9,021 random inputs with no byte cap: identical output.
  - 2,000 generated markdown replies (CJK and ASCII prose plus fenced blocks) at caps of 3500/3800, 1000/1200, 300/400 and 120/160 (chars/bytes). Every new chunk was within both caps, every chunk had balanced fences, and no text was lost. The old code left fences unbalanced in 687 to 1,746 of the 2,000 replies, depending on the cap, and it also produced more chunks.
  - At an unrealistic 16-byte cap, a fence prefix plus one character can exceed the cap, and the code-point fallback still applies, as before.

No Rust was touched, so I did not run `cargo fmt` or clippy.

## Checklist

- [ ] One focused change, started from current `main` (no need to rebase when `main` moves)
- [ ] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior
- [ ] If this adds or changes a user-facing feature, I updated its docs and its row in `docs/features.toml` (`cargo test -p codewhale-tui --test feature_registry` checks it)

prs.body:
Bumps [parking_lot](https://github.com/Amanieu/parking_lot) from 0.12.5 to 0.13.0.
Release notes

Sourced from parking_lot's releases.

parking_lot-v0.13.0

  • Signficantly improved Mutex and RwLock performance under contention by deferring waking up parked threads until after the lock is released. (#545)
  • Added per-acquisition state to lock_api raw locks. RawMutex::Guard replaces GuardMarker; rwlocks have separate SharedGuard, ExclusiveGuard, and UpgradableGuard types. Unlock operations consume this state, while upgrade and downgrade operations return replacement state. Bump and raw condition-variable waits borrow and update the state. Consuming operations must release their acquisition on unwind; borrowing operations must restore ownership and valid state, or abort if restoration fails. (#544)
  • Raised the MSRV to Rust 1.95 and upgraded all crates to edition 2024. (#533)
  • Removed the hardware-lock-elision feature. (#533)
  • Removed automatic eventual fairness. Fair unlocking remains available through the explicit fair-unlock APIs. This removes UnparkResult::be_fair. (#533)
  • Removed the no-op lock_api/nightly feature. (#533)
  • Removed the legacy lock_api const_new methods and the redundant parking_lot const_* constructor functions; the corresponding new methods can be called in constant contexts. (#533)
  • Replaced the recursive read methods on RwLock with a dedicated reader-biased RecursiveRwLock type. The RawRwLockRecursive and RawRwLockRecursiveTimed extension traits have been removed from lock_api. (#533)
  • Added Once::new_completed for constructing a Once in the completed state. (#520)
  • Added Once::{is_completed, wait, wait_force} and the corresponding OnceState query methods. (#533)
  • Made additional lock, timeout, parking, and spin-wait accessors usable in constant contexts. (#533)
  • Added into_inner_with_raw to lock_api's Mutex, RwLock, and ReentrantMutex. (#524)
  • Added RawCondvar, RawCondvarTimed, and the generic Condvar wrapper to lock_api, and implemented parking_lot::Condvar using them. Custom raw condition variables may allow spurious wakeups; their notification methods must then return false or 0. parking_lot::Condvar still guarantees no spurious wakeups and exact notification counts. (#523) (#533)
  • Corrected the Send and Sync bounds of lock guards in lock_api. (#533)
  • Made RawMutex::is_locked and RawRwLock::{is_locked, is_locked_exclusive} required methods. (#533)
  • Renamed MappedRwLockReadGuard::try_map_or_else to try_map_or_err. (#533)
  • Clarified the safety requirements of raw lock implementations, including acquire/release synchronization, moving or dropping a locked raw lock, preserving the original lock mode on a failed upgrade, and stable thread IDs. Acquisitions may unwind without leaving a new acquisition held; consuming guard operations release their acquisition on unwind, while bump and wait operations must restore ownership or abort. (#533) (#544)
  • Clarified the aliasing requirements of unsafe raw-access, force-unlock, and guard-construction APIs in lock_api. (#533)
  • Guard unlocked and unlocked_fair operations now abort if re-locking panics. Default raw-lock bump implementations also abort if re-locking panics. (#533)
  • Guard with_upgraded operations abort if raw upgrading or downgrading panics, preserving continuous lock ownership. (#544)
  • Parking-lot operations in parking_lot_core are now guaranteed to never unwind. (#533)
  • Documented that parking-lot-based synchronization primitives must not be used
