prs.title: fix(telegram): stop one refused reply from wedging the poll loop
prs.body:
## What and why

When handling a Telegram update throws, `pollTelegram` leaves the batch without advancing the offset and calls `getUpdates` again right away. Telegram has an update pending, so it answers at once with the same update. When the failure repeats on every delivery, the bridge goes into a busy loop. Every later update, including the owner's, waits behind the failing one until Telegram drops it about a day later.

Errors that fail this way every time include 403 `Forbidden: bot was blocked by the user`, 403 kicked from a group, 400 `not enough rights to send text messages`, and 400 `chat not found`. `telegramApi` only retries 429, so these are thrown straight back to the poll loop. The replies sent before an update is deduplicated include the pairing refusal to an unlisted user, the "only text messages" reply and the "group control disabled" reply. So a stranger who messages the bot and blocks it before the refusal arrives, or a group where the bot has no send rights, is enough to stop the bridge from serving its owner.

**Repro.** I ran the bridge (`src/index.mjs`) against a local mock Bot API (`TELEGRAM_API_BASE=http://127.0.0.1:<port>`). Update 500 is "hi" from unlisted chat 999, whose `sendMessage` returns 403 "bot was blocked by the user". Update 501 is `/help` from allowlisted chat 111. On current `main`, after 15 s the mock had counted 27,520 `getUpdates` calls and 27,520 refused `sendMessage` calls to 999. `/help` was never answered, and the offset never moved.

**Change.**
- A Telegram 4xx other than 429 now marks the update handled and continues with the rest of the batch. Redelivering it cannot succeed. The check is `isPermanentTelegramError` in `lib.mjs`, next to `telegramSendRetryDelayMs`. Only Telegram API errors carry `errorCode`, so Runtime failures never match it.
- Any other failure (5xx, network, Runtime down) still breaks without advancing, so the same update is redelivered as #3658 intended. The re-poll now waits `telegramRetryDelayMs(error)` (the `retry_after`, or 3 s) instead of starting immediately.

| failure while handling an update | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| 403 blocked / kicked, 400 no rights / chat not found | busy loop, later updates never handled | logged once, offset advances, next update handled |
| 429 after `telegramApi`'s own retries | immediate re-poll loop | waits `retry_after`, then redelivers |
| 5xx / network / Runtime down | immediate re-poll loop | waits 3 s, then redelivers the same update |
| no error | unchanged | unchanged |

## Where this came from

Bug fix, no issue. It is not in the integrations audit #7477. Related history: #2967 (item 5, offset safety and backoff) and #3658 (redeliver on handler error), whose redelivery this keeps.

## How I tested it

On Node 22.23.5, the version the `Integrations` job uses:

- `cd integrations/telegram-bridge && npm run check && npm test`: 40 tests, 40 pass.
- New `test/poll-loop.test.mjs` runs the bridge against the mock Bot API described above. It passes with this change. On the previous `src/` it fails after 15 s with `{"getUpdates":27520,"sendTo999":27520,"sendTo111":0}`.
- The `pollTelegram` regex in `test/dispatch-concurrency.test.mjs` pinned the old catch block, so I updated it to the new one. It still asserts that the transient path breaks without marking the update handled.
- Transient path, checked by hand: with `sendMessage` returning 500, the same update came back 3.27 s later instead of immediately.

No Rust was touched, so I did not run `cargo fmt` or clippy.

## Checklist

- [ ] One focused change, started from current `main` (no need to rebase when `main` moves)
- [ ] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior
- [ ] If this adds or changes a user-facing feature, I updated its docs and its row in `docs/features.toml` (`cargo test -p codewhale-tui --test feature_registry` checks it)

prs.body:
Bumps [rio-vt](https://github.com/raphamorim/rio) from 0.5.30 to 0.5.32.
Release notes

Sourced from rio-vt's releases.

v0.5.32

Full Changelog: https://rioterm.com/changelog

v0.5.31

Full Changelog: https://rioterm.com/changelog

Changelog

Sourced from rio-vt's changelog.

0.5.32 (2026-11-15)

  • Windows ships a modern ConPTY. The installer and the new portable .zip put conpty.dll and OpenConsole.exe from the Windows Terminal project (1.25, MIT) next to rio.exe, so Rio drives a current pseudoconsole instead of the one built into Windows: sixel, iTerm2 and kitty images render, the screen is restored when a TUI exits, and the IME candidate window follows the caret, with no manual sideload. The portable .exe remains for this release. Rio loads conpty.dll from its own directory only, so a copy on PATH is never picked up, and a pseudoconsole that fails to open or resize is reported instead of aborting Rio (#1767, #1764, closes #1759, #2031).

  • A long command can ring the bell or send a desktop notification when it finishes. The new [notify-on-command-finish] section is off by default (#2043). when is never, unfocused (the command's pane is not the one you are looking at: another window has focus, or another tab or split is active) or always. bell (default true) rings the bell through the [bell] settings, so the audio bell and the tab indicator follow them; notify (default false) sends a notification such as "Command Failed: Command took 2m 3s and exited with code 1."; after (default 5000) skips commands that ran that many milliseconds or less. It needs a shell that marks commands with OSC 133 C and D. Rio's zsh integration now sends those marks itself, so prompt navigation (ScrollToPrevPrompt, ScrollToNextPrompt) and this notification work in zsh with no setup: A and B around the prompt, carried inside PS1 so a redraw repeats them, P;k=s on continuation lines and PS2, C when a command line runs and D with its exit status when it ends. Hooks installed by your own rc files never see the marks, and a theme's PS1 is marked after the theme sets it. fish 4 already sends the marks; the PowerShell script still only reports the directory. librio hosts get Action::CommandFinished (RIO_ACTION_COMMAND_FINISHED, with the exit status in data_a and the duration in milliseconds in data_b).

  • librio: Sixel and iTerm2 images reach embedders, in one placement list with kitty. rio_render_state_image_count, rio_render_state_image_placement, rio_render_state_image_info and rio_render_state_image_rgba give every image placement on screen in draw order, each with its protocol, layer, z-index, viewport geometry, a change stamp to cache textures by, and RGBA pixels on request; rio_render_state_image_placements_generation says when the list changed so a host keeps its draw list otherwise. Sixel and iTerm2 pixels, which the terminal hands over once, were dropped by librio before; the rio_render_state_kitty_* calls stay as the kitty subset (#2045, closes #2034).

  • Rio no longer claims OSC 7501 support it does not act on. The program status query is answered only in librio hosts that set program_status_cb, and the reply lists the accepted states and kinds so a program can fall back (#2040).

  • More input bounds. An XTGETTCAP request over 1 MiB gets no reply and the next one is served normally; an OSC 8 hyperlink whose params and URI exceed 2047 bytes is ignored rather than opening or closing a link, and when id= repeats the last non-empty value wins; OSC 1337 SetUserVar is recognized and ignored instead of stored for the session, as other terminals do (#2042).

0.5.31 (2026-11-13)

  • OSC 8 hyperlinks keep their whole URI. Everything after the second ; is now the URI, taken verbatim, so a link like https://x.dev/a;b; no longer opens as https://x.dev/a, however many ; it contains (#1983). Clicking or hint-opening an OSC 8 link opens exactly what the program sent: post-processing (trailing punctuation, unmatched brackets) now only applies to regex matches. A URI with invalid UTF-8 starts a new link instead of being dropped, and an empty URI always closes the link, even when an id is given. The same parser change covers every OSC whose payload is free text, which used to be split on ; and cut at 16 parts: a window title (OSC 0/2) is kept exactly as sent, and one with invalid UTF-8 or over 255 bytes is dropped rather than shown as a guess; an OSC 7 or 9;9 working directory survives any number of ;, and an empty one clears the stored directory instead of leaving it stale; an OSC 9 or 777 notification shows its whole body, 9;4 progress splits as before, a bare 9;4 or 9;9 is a one-character notification, and the ConEmu sub-commands Rio does not implement are dropped instead of popping a notification with a junk body.

  • Pathological output can no longer exhaust memory or stall the parser. A long run of combining marks on one cell (e U+0301 repeated 65535 times with REP) took 8.6 s and 3.3 GB because every mark re-interned the cell's extras; a cell now keeps at most 64 marks and the same input takes 7 ms and 3 MB. An unterminated APC or OSC grew its buffer until the process died; sequences over 64 MiB are discarded whole and both buffers release capacity above 1 MiB between sequences, so one large image or paste no longer pins that memory. Kitty graphics chunked uploads follow kitty: one transmission in flight at a time, the declared S= size is no longer reserved up front (a bogus size tried to allocate gigabytes before any data arrived), and on Linux a FIFO under /dev/shm is rejected instead of blocking the parser (#2041).

  • librio: OSC 7501 program status reports reach the host. Programs report their state (idle, working, done, blocked, error, with a kind, a progress and a message) in one escape sequence, so a host can show which tab needs attention without per-tool hooks (#2039). Reports are validated against the spec (rev 0.4) with its size limits, and the host gets Action::ProgramStatus with the report, a prompt start on OSC 133 A/N and a reset on RIS; the C ABI adds program_status_cb. Rio's own windows do not display it yet.

v6.3.0

Behavior change: Java problem matcher is now opt-in

Starting with v6.3.0, setup-java no longer registers the Java problem matcher by default (#1326, fixes #1322). Java compiler warnings, compiler errors, and uncaught exceptions are no longer turned into annotations on pull request diffs unless you opt in.

To keep annotations, set problem-matcher: true:

Compiler output still appears in the build logs, and compilation errors still fail the build. Only annotations are affected.

Why: inline annotations cluttered pull request reviews, and GitHub Actions caps annotations at 10 errors, 10 warnings, and 10 notices per step, and 50 per job. prs.title: fix(tui): open a new reasoning card below a tool that already followed it
prs.body:
fix(tui): open a new reasoning card below a tool that already followed it

## What and why

`ActiveCell` renders its entries in insertion order and nothing sorts them.
`ensure_active_entry` returned the stored index unconditionally, so once a
tool card was appended below a live reasoning card, the next reasoning delta
was written into the card **above** it. New reasoning then renders on top of a
command the reader has already seen.

The reachable path needs the pointer to survive a tool card. The engine emits
`ToolCallStarted` only after the whole response stream is consumed, so the
tool cannot appear between two `thinking_delta` batches of one response.
What does survive: a provider that opens a thinking block but never sends its
`content_block_stop` (the engine only emits `ThinkingComplete` on that stop,
`turn_loop.rs:6706`), leaving `streaming_thinking_active_entry` set while the
tool card lands; a later response that sends `thinking_delta` without a new
`content_block_start(thinking)` then appends to the card above it.

## Issue

Refs #7454

## How I tested it

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` — clean.
- `cargo check -p codewhale-tui --tests --lib` — clean.
- Five new `codewhale-tui` tests in `streaming_thinking::tests`, each driving
  `ensure_active_entry` in the handler's order:
  - `issue_7454_reasoning_after_a_tool_opens_a_card_below_it`
  - `issue_7454_unrevealed_bytes_stay_in_the_card_above_the_tool`
  - `issue_7454_a_stream_with_no_sibling_keeps_one_card`
  - `issue_7454_a_stale_pointer_opens_a_new_card`
  - `issue_7454_a_split_card_shows_its_text_instead_of_a_placeholder`
- **They were not run locally.** rustc cannot link the `codewhale-tui` lib test
  target on this machine: `memory allocation of 169869328 bytes failed` on a
  24 GB box with `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=1` and incremental off, the same limit #7137
  reported. CI owns the run.
- **No live gateway was exercised.** The defect was reported from use and the
  sequence above is read from source, not observed against a provider. That is
  why this says `Refs` rather than `Closes`.

## Known limits

- One reveal slice can land on the far side of the split: the beat commits
  before it resolves the entry, so the slice that triggers the split goes to the
  new card. It is pre-tool backlog bounded by one beat's budget (38 B at 16 ms),
  so at most one short slice of pre-tool reasoning renders below the tool. It is
  not the reported defect (no post-tool reasoning above a tool), but it is a
  seam.
- Under translation the settled card shows its original text and is never a
  translation target; the new card gets the translation. That is the trade
  against a placeholder that spins forever, and it is visible to a user with
  translation on.
- Pre-existing and untouched: the other finalize paths (`MessageStarted`,
  `ThinkingComplete`, session restore) discard a translation-mode tail and can
  strand a placeholder the same way.
- No test drives `EngineEvent::ThinkingDelta` through `run_event_loop`.

## Checklist

- [x] Tests for the behavior change
- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- [x] No CHANGELOG or contributor-credit edits
- [x] Scoped to one defect

## Attribution

prs.title: fix(tui): keep a streamed delta in the cell its own kind owns
prs.body:
fix(tui): keep a streamed delta in the cell its own kind owns

## What and why

A block's kind is decided by its start event alone. When a gateway opens a
text block in the middle of a thinking stream and then keeps sending
thinking deltas, block 0 stays marked text: `commit_streaming_display_tick`
reads `block_is_thinking(0)`, gets false, and writes the reasoning into the
assistant body. One reasoning sentence is then split across the thinking
card and the prose that follows it.

This is the same visible defect as #7123, with the two block kinds swapped:
the PR that fixed #7123 taught the display beat to route by the block's own
kind, but the kind itself is only ever set by a start event, so a gateway
that starts a block of the other kind mid-stream poisons it.

`StreamingState::set_block_kind` relabels one live block in place. Unlike
`reset` it leaves every other block and both accumulated counters alone.
`streaming_thinking::resync_block_kind` delivers the pending tail to the
cell the old kind owned first, then relabels; a relabel away from thinking
also finalizes the reasoning card and stashes its text, so the spinner stops
and replay still has the words. Both delta handlers call it before pushing,
so the normal Anthropic ordering returns after one comparison.

## Issue

Refs #7123

## How I tested it

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` — clean.
- `cargo check -p codewhale-tui --tests --lib -p codewhale-tui-kit` — clean.
- `cargo test -p codewhale-tui-kit --lib` — `test result: ok. 221 passed; 0 failed; 1 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out`, including the new
  `streaming::tests::set_block_kind_reroutes_the_next_delta`.
- Four new `codewhale-tui` regression tests in `crates/tui/src/tui/ui/tests.rs`
  (`reasoning_after_an_interposed_text_block_returns_to_a_thinking_card`,
  `a_relabel_to_text_finishes_the_reasoning_card`,
  `a_relabel_to_text_keeps_the_card_alive_under_translation`,
  `prose_after_an_interposed_thinking_block_returns_to_the_assistant_cell`):
  **type-checked but not run.** rustc cannot build that lib test target on this
  machine — `memory allocation of 169869328 bytes failed` on a 24 GB box, with
  `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=1`, `CARGO_PROFILE_TEST_DEBUG=0` and incremental off. This
  is the same limit #7137 reported. CI owns the run.
- No live gateway was exercised. The defect was diagnosed from the code path
  and reproduced in the tests above, not observed against a real provider.

## Known limits

- The provider's own content-block index is still ignored: the TUI keeps one
  active block, and a gateway that interleaves two live blocks can still
  misattribute. This fixes the kind, not the indexing.
- A gateway that flips kinds twice renders one passage as two cards, the second
  without a duration stamp.
- Not addressed, both pre-existing and reachable on the same gateways: a second
  `MessageStarted` still drops a text block's uncommitted tail, and it still
  leaves the previous assistant cell marked streaming. The same handler also
  freezes a translation placeholder, because the `MessageDelta` arm calls
  `flush_active_cell` and that takes the reasoning entry before
  `ThinkingComplete` can supply a cell index. The resync is guarded under
  translation so it does not clear the buffer or the entry earlier than that
  flush already does; it does not fix the freeze.
- The two `event_loop.rs` call sites are covered only by review until CI adds a
  handler-level test; the new tests drive `resync_block_kind` and the display
  beat directly.

## Checklist

- [x] Tests for the behavior change
- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- [x] No CHANGELOG or contributor-credit edits
- [x] Scoped to one defect

releases.name: Codewhale v0.10.3
releases.body:
## What's in v0.10.3


Codewhale v0.10.3 brings a unified Plugins surface with Creator mode (`[features] plugin_creator`) and unmodified DeepSeek Harness (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-*`) plugin compatibility, an upgraded Auto-Review guardian with workspace boundaries, soft rules, sub-agent return review, and one-use retry approvals, and a single `Shift+Tab` permission dial defaulting to Accept Edits (`Ask → Accept Edits → Plan → Auto-Review → Full Access`). It moves the ACP server and external-agent sessions (including Qwen Code and GitHub Copilot CLI) onto the official Agent Client Protocol SDK, publishes native signed HarmonyOS ARM64 release assets, adds a verified signed model-and-provider registry channel alongside unified model-ID resolution and managed `/v1/models` pricing, updates design tokens to `5.4.0` with a docked single-line approval strip, folded turn activity, live working-row light sweeps and 13 hex-lattice dot-whale forms, adds `claude-org` billing auth, `show_data` transcript charts, `codewhale sessions migrate`, DeepSeek Chatbot web search and speech tools, receipted self-updates and `codewhale uninstall`, and lands reliability, CJK/Unicode, Windows, and sandbox security fixes.

## Install

### Recommended — official GitHub release

New macOS/Linux install (checksummed binaries from this release):

```bash
curl -fsSL https://codewhale.net/install.sh | CODEWHALE_VERSION="v0.10.3" sh
"$HOME/.local/bin/codewhale" --version
```

For Windows, use the matching installer or archive below. For an existing
direct install, run `codewhale update`; it prints the executable path and
keeps newer builds. If the install directory is occupied by a different build,
use the fresh-directory migration in [the installation guide](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/CodeWhale/blob/main/docs/INSTALL.md).

### Secondary packaging — npm and Cargo

```bash
npm install -g codewhale
# or build from source
cargo install codewhale-cli --locked
```

The wrapper downloads the matched `codewhale` and `codew` command assets
from this Release. Both contain the same compiled runtime.

### Docker / GHCR

```bash
docker run --rm -it \
  -e DEEPSEEK_API_KEY="$DEEPSEEK_API_KEY" \
  -v codewhale-home:/home/codewhale/.codewhale \
  ghcr.io/codewhale-hq/codewhale:v0.10.3
```

The image exposes the same runtime as both `codewhale` and `codew`. The
`latest` tag is also updated on release.

### Cargo (Linux / macOS)

```bash
cargo install codewhale-cli --locked
```

The Cargo package installs `codewhale`. Cargo cannot create a second command
alias from one binary target; users who want the shorter spelling can add a
`codew` symlink to that installed executable. The npm, Homebrew, archive,
shell-installer, and container channels install both command names directly.

### Manual download — platform archives (recommended)

Each archive below contains the same runtime under the `codewhale` and
`codew` command names, plus an install script:

| Platform | Archive | Install script |
|---|---|---|
| Linux x64 | `codewhale-linux-x64.tar.gz` | `install.sh` |
| Linux ARM64 | `codewhale-linux-arm64.tar.gz` | `install.sh` |

**Unix (Linux / macOS):**
```bash
tar xzf codewhale-<platform>.tar.gz
cd codewhale-<platform>
./install.sh
```

**Windows:**
- For the installer path, run `CodeWhaleSetup.exe`; it installs
  `codewhale.exe`, `codew.exe`, and `codewhale.bat` under
  `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\CodeWhale\bin`, adds that directory to the
  current-user PATH, and creates a Start Menu shortcut that prefers
  Windows Terminal (`wt.exe`) when it is installed.
- Extract the archive for your machine: `codewhale-windows-x64.zip` or
  `codewhale-windows-arm64.zip`
- Double-click `codewhale.bat` (not the raw `.exe`) to launch
- Run `install.bat` to copy the binaries and launcher to `%USERPROFILE%\bin`
- Add `%USERPROFILE%\bin` to your PATH

The **portable** Windows archive skips the install script — extract and run `codewhale.bat` from any directory. The NSIS installer is currently unsigned and may trigger Windows SmartScreen until a signing certificate is wired into the release pipeline.

Each platform also has **bare, unarchived** `codewhale-<platform>` and
`codew-<platform>` assets. The seven `codewhale-tui-<platform>` filenames
attached to v0.9.5 are byte-identical compatibility copies used only to let
already-installed v0.9.4 clients discover and cross this single-binary
transition; current installers do not expose a third runtime. The legacy npm
package `deepseek-tui` is deprecated and is not republished. For migration
from v0.8.x legacy binary names, see `docs/REBRAND.md`.

### Verify (recommended)

Download the checksum manifests from this Release and verify:

```bash
# Linux — archive bundles
sha256sum -c codewhale-bundles-sha256.txt --ignore-missing

# Linux — individual binaries
sha256sum -c codewhale-artifacts-sha256.txt --ignore-missing

# macOS
shasum -a 256 -c codewhale-bundles-sha256.txt --ignore-missing
shasum -a 256 -c codewhale-artifacts-sha256.txt --ignore-missing
```

issues.body:
### Summary

On 2026.11.6, the session observer disables itself ("returned invalid JSON twice") when the
utility model is `anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5` (via claude-cli). The rejected outputs are
syntactically valid JSON: the model copies a `revision` field from the `previousDigest` in
the user payload into its answer, and `ModelDigestSchema` is a `strictObject`, so the extra
key rejects the whole digest.

Same family as #175646 (`planProgress: null` leaking from the payload), but a different
leaked field that nobody has reported yet.

### Root cause (source inspection, 2026.11.6 dist)

- `buildSessionObserverPrompt` strips only `sessionId` and `lifecycleRevision` from
  `previousDigest`; `revision` (and other internal fields) are sent to the model.
- The system prompt's example contains only headline/assessment/health/planProgress, but
  small models mimic the shape of `previousDigest`.
- `normalizeSessionObserverModelOutput` -> `safeParseJsonWithSchema(ModelDigestSchema)`
  with `strictObject` -> unknown key `revision` -> null -> retry -> null -> run disabled.
- The logged "last rejected output" is capped at 160 chars, so the extra key is never
  visible in the log (it appears after `assessment`).

### Reproduction

`SESSION_OBSERVER_SYSTEM_PROMPT` verbatim, a user payload shaped like
`buildSessionObserverPrompt` output (previousDigest with `revision`, 4 notes,
`planProgress: null`), validated with the shipped `normalizeSessionObserverModelOutput`.
6 calls per model:

| Model | Pass | Rejected keys |
|---|---|---|
| claude-haiku-5-5 | 4/6 | `headline,assessment,health,revision` (x2) |
| claude-sonnet-5-5 | 6/6 | - |

Real log line:

```
session observer disabled after consecutive failures
{consecutiveFailures: 2, error: "session observer returned invalid JSON twice; last rejected output: {\"headline\":\"Wrapping up workspace onboarding\",\"assessment\":\"The main agent finished ..."}
```

### Related

- `utilityModel.fallbacks` does not help on this build: fallback triggers only on call
  errors, and an invalid-but-successful Haiku answer is accepted by the chain before the
  observer rejects it (#196345 addresses this; not observed in 2026.11.6 behavior).

### Suggested fixes (any one would resolve it)

1. Send only model-facing fields in `previousDigest` (headline, assessment, health,
   planProgress), dropping `revision`, `runId`, `updatedAt`, etc.
2. Strip unknown keys (`.strip()` / pick known fields) instead of rejecting the digest.
3. Log the full rejected key set (not just a 160-char prefix) so this is diagnosable.

### Environment

OpenClaw 2026.11.6 (app-managed), macOS 27.2.1 arm64, utility model
anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5 via claude-cli runtime, no utility fallbacks.

issues.title: [Bug]: Telegram DM auto topic label renames the topic, but the session keeps its placeholder title

labels.name: clawsweeper:intake:bug
labels.description: Preliminary submission classification; full source review pending.

issues.body:
When `autoTopicLabel` renames a Telegram private (DM) topic, the topic gets the generated name but the OpenClaw session keeps the client's placeholder title ("Garden irrigati...") until the user sends another message there. Session lists, the Control UI sidebar and anything reading `sessions.list` show the wrong name in the meantime.

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

The bot's own `editForumTopic` returns only `true` and Telegram sends no `forum_topic_edited` service message for it, so the title-update path added in #166011 never runs for an auto label. `scheduleDmTopicLabel` updates only the topic-name cache after the rename ([bot-message-dispatch.ts:502-510](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/b419318b217/extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-dispatch.ts#L502-L510)); the session's `topicName`, which `displayName` reads ([session-utils-display.ts:55](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/b419318b217/src/gateway/session-utils-display.ts#L55)), changes only when the next inbound message is recorded.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Telegram bot with BotFather threaded mode (`getMe.has_topics_enabled`), `autoTopicLabel` on (default).
2. In the bot's DM, open a new topic; the client names it from the first words ("Garden irrigati...") and sends `forum_topic_created`.
3. Send one message in the topic and wait for the reply and the auto label (`editForumTopic` with the generated name).
4. `openclaw gateway call sessions.list` (or look at the Control UI sidebar).
5. Send a second message in the topic and check again.

### Expected behavior

After step 3 the session's name is the generated label, as the docs describe for renames ([threads-and-sessions.md:60](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/b419318b217/docs/channels/telegram/threads-and-sessions.md?plain=1#L60): "Observed private-topic creation and rename events update the existing session's name"). A manual session label still wins.

### Actual behavior

| Moment | Telegram topic | Session `displayName` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| After the first reply and the auto label | `Status labels` | `Garden irrigati...` |
| After a second user message | `Status labels` | `Status labels` |

Released 2026.11.10-beta.1, disposable gateway with a Bot API stub and a stubbed model. A session whose user sends one message and then waits (a long-running task) keeps the placeholder indefinitely.

### OpenClaw version

2026.11.10-beta.1; code unchanged on main b419318b217. On 2026.11.6 the cache is not updated either, so the session keeps the placeholder after later messages too.

### Operating system

Linux x64, Node 26.13.1

### Install method

npm global

### Model

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO (not model-related; stubbed OpenAI-compatible model)

### Provider / routing chain

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO (not provider-related)

### Additional provider/model setup details

none

### Logs

```
Bot API calls (stub):  sendMessage "Status labels" -> editForumTopic name="Status labels"
sessions.list:         agent:main:main:thread:1001:823 | displayName: 'Garden irrigati...' | label: None
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Repro details below. Seen in production as session lists (and a status board built on `sessions.list`) showing truncated first-message placeholders for topics Telegram already shows with their generated names.

### Impact and severity

Low to medium: wrong session names in every client that lists sessions, for every auto-labelled DM topic until its next message.

### Additional information

Suggested fix: after the rename, record the label through `recordInboundSession` with `createIfMissing: false`, as the `forum_topic_edited` path in [bot-message.ts:194-213](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/b419318b217/extensions/telegram/src/bot-message.ts#L194-L213) does. PR to follow. Related: #166011 (observed renames), #184821 (labels from the first real message), #183368 (refine labels once; would hit the same gap).

<details><summary>Claude Opus 5.5</summary>

**Repro.** Disposable gateway on 2026.11.10-beta.1 with `channels.telegram.apiRoot` pointed at a local Bot API stub that reports `has_topics_enabled` and injects DM-topic updates, and an OpenAI-compatible stub model (`models.providers.labelstub`, `api: openai-completions`) that answers every request with "Status labels", used as the agent's primary model, so the reply and the label need no key. The script injects `forum_topic_created {name: "Garden irrigati..."}` in thread 823, then a user message in that thread, waits for `editForumTopic`, reads `sessions.list`, then injects a second message and reads it again.

**Why the next message fixes it.** `resolveTelegramForumTopicMetadata` reads the topic-name cache that `scheduleDmTopicLabel` updated, so the next inbound context carries `ThreadLabel = "Status labels"` and the session metadata patch writes it as `topicName`.

**Why there is no echo.** The Bot API returns `true` for `editForumTopic`, and Telegram does not deliver a `forum_topic_edited` service message for the bot's own edit, which is also why `scheduleDmTopicLabel` updates the cache itself.

</details>

labels.name: P2

labels.description: ClawSweeper found a high-confidence source-level issue reproduction.

labels.name: issue-rating: 🦞 diamond lobster
labels.description: Very strong issue quality with high-confidence source-level or clear reproduction.

labels.name: impact:ux-friction
labels.description: User-facing flow adds avoidable confusion or support burden without fully blocking progress.

issues.body:
## Summary

On every gateway start, `post-ready.startup-maintenance` materializes plugin sources and emits a burst of Node warnings:

```
(node:19976) Warning: File descriptor 17 closed but not opened in unmanaged mode
(node:19976) Warning: File descriptor 18 closed but not opened in unmanaged mode
... 32 warnings total
```

All 32 share the same stack and originate from `withPluginSourceFile()` closing a descriptor that was opened through the fs-safe boundary layer.

## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| OpenClaw | 2026.11.1 (4ffdd20), npm global install |
| Node | v26.13.0 |
| OS | Windows 10.0.22000 x64 |
| @openclaw/fs-safe | 0.26.5 (native win32-x64 addon present) |
| Plugins | 43/70 enabled |
| Gateway mode | `local`, front-running `openclaw gateway run` (no service) |

## Steps to reproduce

1. Install OpenClaw 2026.11.1 on Windows with Node 26.x and any plugin set that needs source materialization.
2. Start the gateway **with Node warn-tracking enabled so worker warnings carry stacks**:

```powershell
$env:NODE_OPTIONS='--trace-warnings'
node <npm>/node_modules/openclaw/openclaw.mjs gateway run
```

3. Watch startup. Right after:

```
startup phase: startup.maintenance.plugin-registry
startup phase: post-ready.startup-maintenance
```

the warnings burst.

Note: `node --trace-warnings ...` does **not** work — worker threads clear `execArgv`, so `NODE_OPTIONS` is required.

## Expected

No process warnings during plugin source materialization.

## Actual

32 warnings, one per copied plugin source file.

Distribution of descriptor numbers (identical number is reused across copies):

```
fd 17 : 30 times
fd 18 : 2 times
```

## Stack trace (first warning, paths trimmed)

```
at Object.closeSync (node:fs:727:11)
at withPluginSourceFile (dist/plugin-generation-source-lookup-DVOeXzNC.mjs:42:6)
at copyPluginSourceFile (dist/plugin-generation-source-lookup-DVOeXzNC.mjs:106:9)
at copy (dist/plugin-generation-artifact-D-V41Nc0.mjs:175:38)
at copy (dist/plugin-generation-artifact-D-V41Nc0.mjs:160:233)
at file:///.../dist/plugin-generation-artifact-D-V41Nc0.mjs:200:11
at Object.materialize (dist/plugin-generation-artifact-D-V41Nc0.mjs:1036:11)
at copyPackage (dist/plugin-generation-artifact-D-V41Nc0.mjs:1275:16)
at createPluginGenerationArtifact (dist/plugin-generation-artifact-D-V41Nc0.mjs:1287:16)
at file:///.../dist/plugin-generation-source-lookup-DVOeXzNC.mjs:941:24
```

(Hashed file names are from this build.)

## Relevant source

`src/plugins/plugin-source-file.ts` (compiled above):

```js
function withPluginSourceFile(source, boundary, read, openFile = openRootFileSync) {
  const opened = openFile({ absolutePath: source, rootPath: boundary, boundaryLabel: "plugin build source", rejectHardlinks: false });
  if (!opened.ok) throw new Error(`Cannot capture plugin source ${source}`, { cause: opened.error });
  try {
    return read(opened.fd);
  } finally {
    fs.closeSync(opened.fd);   // line 42
  }
}
```

## Analysis

* Node emits this message from `Environment::RemoveUnmanagedFd()` (`src/env.cc`), and `tracks_unmanaged_fds()` is only true for **Worker** environments. So the close happens inside a worker thread, while the descriptor was opened outside that worker's bookkeeping.
* `openRootFileSync()` comes from `@openclaw/fs-safe` and is the boundary-checked open (path-escape / hardlink checks). The matching close is done with plain `node:fs`.
* Because the open is not registered in the closing environment, Node warns. The OS-level close succeeds and the copy completes correctly, so this is currently cosmetic — but it means a worker thread is closing a descriptor it does not own, which is exactly the situation Node's bookkeeping exists to catch.

## Impact

* No functional failure observed: the 32 source files are copied, plugin registry loads, sessions/models/tools all work.
* Cosmetic log noise, but it hides real descriptor bookkeeping problems and looks alarming to operators.

## Suggested directions

1. Close the descriptor through the same layer that opened it (fs-safe should expose a matching close, or return a handle with `close()`), instead of `node:fs` `closeSync` in the copy path.
2. Or perform plugin source materialization on the main thread instead of a worker.
3. Or make `withPluginSourceFile` ownership explicit, so a worker never closes a descriptor opened outside its environment.

Happy to test a patch on Windows/Node 26.13.0.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

I've been running 2026.7.1 with ~/.openclaw bind-mounted from a Windows drive (Docker Desktop, WSL2) for months. Every version I've tried since 2026.9.3 exits on startup on the same mount: right after writing a file, OpenClaw can't read it back (ENOENT), treats the write as failed, rolls it back and exits.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create an empty folder on a Windows drive, e.g. `D:\oc-test`
2. `docker run --rm -v "D:\oc-test:/home/node/.openclaw" ghcr.io/openclaw/openclaw:2026.11.5-beta.1 node openclaw.mjs gateway --allow-unconfigured`
3. Container exits with code 1 after ~17s.

### Expected behavior

Gateway starts and `/health` returns 200, like 2026.7.1 does on the same mount.

### Actual behavior

Exit code 1 before the gateway serves anything.

What happens: OpenClaw writes the file and renames it into place. That works; the file is on disk with the right content and shows up in the directory listing. Then it checks the file it just wrote, while still holding it open. On this mount that check gets ENOENT, so the write is treated as failed and rolled back.

Not an ownership issue: same result after `chown 1000:1000` on the folder.

### OpenClaw version

2026.11.5-beta.1

### Operating system

Windows 11 Enterprise 26300, Docker Desktop 4.95.0 (WSL2 backend), WSL 2.6.3.0

### Install method

docker (ghcr.io/openclaw/openclaw image)

### Model

N/A — exits before any model loads

### Provider / routing chain

N/A — exits before any model loads

### Additional provider/model setup details

_No response_

### Logs

```shell
# OpenClaw startup
Doctor could not complete maintenance. Check the reported service state and resolve the failure.
Config was written to /home/node/.openclaw/openclaw.json, but post-write processing failed: ENOENT: no such file or directory, fstat
The config write was rolled back.

# Same mount, plain Node, no OpenClaw: write tmp file, rename it while the fd is still open
fstat before rename -> dev=69 ino=1125899908462790
renameSync(tmp,dst) -> ok
fstatSync(fd) -> ENOENT
statSync(dst) -> ENOENT
lstatSync(dst) -> ENOENT
openSync(dst,'r') -> ENOENT
readdirSync(dir) -> ok ["dst.json"]
closeSync(fd) -> ok
statSync(dst) after close -> ok ino=1125899908462790 sameInoAsBefore=true
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Mount inside the container:
`9p D:\ rw,aname=drvfs;path=D:\;uid=0;gid=0;metadata;symlinkroot=/mnt/host/,cache=5,access=client,msize=65536,trans=fd`

Calling fs-safe 0.26.13 directly on the same mount (native addon loaded), every atomic write fails the same way. The file ends up on disk with the expected content:

```
ENOENT: no such file or directory, fstat (errno -2)
  at fstatSync
  at AtomicFile.statExact (atomic-io.js)
  at inspectFileIdentity (strict-file-identity.js)
  at AtomicTempOwner.assertCurrent (replace-file-temp-owner.js)
  at AtomicTempOwner.assertPublished (replace-file-temp-owner.js)
```

`replaceFileAtomic`, `writeTextAtomic`, `replaceFileAtomicSync`: all fail. Native `root().write`: `helper-failed`, cause `inspect staged child: No such file or directory (os error 2)`. Same calls on a named volume: all pass.

Root cause is the plain-Node case in Logs. Looks like microsoft/WSL#8443.

### Impact and severity

- Affected: Docker Desktop on Windows, state dir bind-mounted from a Windows drive.
- Severity: gateway won't start.
- Frequency: every run (2026.9.3, 9.6, 9.7, 11.5-beta.1 all fail).
- Consequence: stuck on 2026.7.x unless the state dir moves to a named volume.
- Why not just use a volume: a named volume works, but then I can't edit openclaw.json, skills and workspace files directly from Windows, which is the whole point of the bind mount.

### Additional information

- Last good: 2026.7.1 (fs-safe 0.4.1). First seen bad: 2026.9.3 (fs-safe 0.8.5). 7.35 and 8.x not tested.
- Workaround: put the state dir on a named volume (healthy in ~97s on 11.5-beta.1).
- Possibly the same root cause as the `lstat` ENOENT in #142653 (that one is the read side, not confirmed).
- I can share the repro scripts or test a patched build.

### Summary

Measure and ship further lean-only reductions that pay for themselves.

### Problem to solve

Even the lean prototype idles at about 528 MiB after a fresh start and about 680 MiB after work, against 419 MiB on v2026.7.1. Its remaining always-on workers and native costs haven't been tuned.

### Proposed solution

Measure each candidate separately on top of lean, and ship only those with a clear RSS saving and an acceptable trade-off:

- the stall flight recorder off in lean (~106 MiB native measured on a large deployment);
- the session-archive worker started on demand and retired when idle (~48 MiB heap);
- the small always-on helpers (watch I/O, native lifecycle, heartbeats) consolidated where safe (~46 MiB heap total);
- lower V8 heap limits for lean and its workers;
- deferring code that compiles over time after startup (~45 MiB of main-isolate code growth by 35 minutes idle).

### Alternatives considered

None yet. Results go here.

### Impact

Could bring lean idle close to the 7.1 level. That's an estimate, pending measurement.

### Evidence/examples

Lean prototype per-worker heaps: session-archive 48 MiB, state heartbeat 19, watch I/O 9, native lifecycle 9, stall observer 8, gateway heartbeat 9. Main-isolate retained heap grew about 77 MiB between a fresh start and 35 minutes idle, mostly compiled code.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Yes, for the candidates that measure well.

### Additional information

Part of #202373.

labels.name: P1

issues.body:
### Environment

- OpenClaw **2026.11.5-beta.1** (official npm package); Node.js **26.12.1**
- Android DSHBox/PRoot, Linux arm64
- `/proc/self/ns` exists, but `/proc/self/ns/pid` is absent.
- Both `fs.statSync('/proc/self/ns/pid')` and `fs.readlinkSync('/proc/self/ns/pid')` return `ENOENT`.
- npm tarball SHA-1: `cc6d3b105b938acaf9301f17daa3985acd29fce0`; SHA-512 verified against registry `dist.integrity`.

Tests used **credential-free disposable SQLite and synthetic state**. No production state, Gateway startup, or plugin lifecycle commands were used.

This is distinct from #171385 / #174974, where `readlink()` succeeds but `stat()` fails.

### Observed behavior

| Owner sidecar | Beta's real state-lease heartbeat worker |
| --- | --- |
| No owner sidecar (control) | Ready; lease renewed |
| Synthetic self-owned `gateway` sidecar, `processNamespace: null` | Ready; lease renewed |
| Synthetic self-owned `sqlite-maintenance` / `schema` sidecar, `processNamespace: null` | Rejected; no renewal |
| Sidecar created by beta's own `acquireGatewayStateOwner({ databasePath })`, no payload override | Acquisition succeeds; heartbeat refuses its own maintenance record |

The last sidecar was created by the same test process and contained its own PID, `role: sqlite-maintenance`, `processNamespace: null`, and no `stateOwnerKind`.

**Exact observed error** (disposable path redacted):

```text
OpenClaw state at <disposable>/state/state/openclaw.sqlite is undergoing offline maintenance by sqlite-maintenance process 10485; retry when it finishes. For update progress, run `openclaw update status --json`.
```

PID `10485` belonged to the test process itself. Both `onLost` and `ready` rejection surfaced hydrated `name: Error`. The real-acquisition branch throws `StateDatabaseOfflineMaintenanceError`; the synthetic schema-kind case selects `StateDatabaseAdmissionPendingError`.

### Relevant source

In the published beta's `dist/state/openclaw-state-lease-heartbeat.worker.js`:

- Lines **18635–18654**: unknown-namespace maintenance refusal; the same-PID worker allowance requires namespace classification `same`, while Gateway/agent-embedded roles are allowed.
- Near line **74730**: lease renewal calls `assertStateDatabaseAccessAllowed(params.path)`.

Related functions include `readGatewayLockProcessNamespace`, `classifyGatewayLockProcessNamespace` / `classifyGatewayOwnerProcessNamespace`, `defaultPayload`, `acquireGatewayStateOwner`, and `assertPersistedStateDatabaseAccessAllowed`.

### Minimal credential-free reproduction

1. Use a dependency-complete copy of `openclaw@2026.11.5-beta.1` and a machine where both namespace probes return `ENOENT`.
2. Run Node with sanitized environment; redirect `HOME`, config, cache, temp, and `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` to a fresh disposable workspace.
3. Open a synthetic state DB with `openOpenClawStateDatabase`; call `acquireGatewayStateOwner({ databasePath })` **without overriding its payload**.
4. Seed one synthetic `state_leases` row with a 30-second expiry.
5. Start the beta's real `startOpenClawStateLeaseHeartbeat` for that row with a one-second interval; observe `ready`, `onLost`, and the persisted heartbeat timestamp for eight seconds.
6. Repeat independently in fresh state without the owner sidecar. In the control case, renewal succeeds.

This is an **internal-API reproduction**: Gateway-role heartbeat success does not establish full Gateway startup, and the test does not prove every supported maintenance CLI path fails.

### Expected behavior / maintainer question

Is maintenance intentionally unsupported when the PID namespace link is absent, or is a particular delegated host-maintenance context required?

If maintenance is meant to work in such environments, which supported entrypoint preserves verifiable custody across the worker? Otherwise, could unsupported admission be rejected **before** the maintenance sidecar/acquisition and expensive work begin?

### Security considerations

Matching numeric PIDs alone is **not** sufficient: PID reuse, namespaces with identical PIDs, shared storage across hosts, and replaced/spoofed sidecars must be considered. Missing namespace identity should remain `unknown`, not silently become `same`.

No request is made to bypass namespace checks, trust matching PIDs alone, relabel maintenance as Gateway, delete locks, or weaken cross-process custody protections.

### Related

- #171385 — Termux/PRoot namespace-probe regression
- #174974 — `readlink()` fix for `stat()` failure
- #188424 — hardened-systemd missing/unreadable namespace identity
- #180209 — null-namespace test fixture

issues.body:
### Summary

Upgrading with `npm i -g openclaw@latest` **while the Gateway is running** makes the Gateway detect `installation_replaced` and restart *before npm has finished writing the package tree*. The restart lands on a half-written tree, so the old process's lazy imports fail with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`, the restart handoff row cannot be written, and every plugin is force-retired after a 5 s grace.

Recovery works (the Gateway comes back and serves on the new build), so this is not a "Gateway stays down" report. The defect is the premature restart and the loss of the restart record.

### Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.11.6 → 2026.11.7, npm global install (`C:\Users\hbgan\AppData\Roaming\npm\node_modules\openclaw`)
- Windows 11 (10.0.26300), x64
- Node v24.22.1, npm 11.19.1
- Gateway managed by Scheduled Task `OpenClaw Gateway` (logon trigger, `RestartCount=3`, `RestartInterval=PT1M`)
- `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_STARTUP_TRACE=1` in `~/.openclaw/.env`

### Steps to reproduce

1. Have the Gateway running on 2026.11.6.
2. In another shell: `npm i -g openclaw@latest`.
3. Do not stop the Gateway first.

Observed twice: 2026-11-19 (11.5 → 11.6) and 2026-11-23 (11.6 → 11.7).

### What happens — run of 2026-11-23 02:17Z (verbatim)

```
02:17:40 Installation replaced: running 2026.11.6 build 2026.11.6-release-06afb10d3272-...; on-disk 2026.11.7 build 2026.11.7-release-e31b...
02:17:40 admission closed: restart (SIGUSR2: gateway.installation_replaced ...)
02:17:40 received SIGUSR2; restarting
02:17:40 Restart marker persistence failed: Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find module '...\dist\session-restart-resume-BzRgzT_h.mjs'
02:17:40 plugin service degraded (plugin=memory-core ...): Cannot find module '...\dist\session-restart-resume-BGxPJyTB.mjs'
02:17:47 shutdown failed in 6969ms: plugin-services
02:17:47 shutdown step failed (gateway close): Gateway resource cleanup failed | Plugin runtime still owns resources
02:17:47 Plugin tavily forced retirement after 5000ms: 1 still-running call(s), 0 retained consumer(s); resource cleanup remains pending.
02:17:47 Plugin memory-core forced retirement after 5000ms: ...
02:17:47 Plugin acpx forced retirement after 5000ms: ...
02:17:47 Plugin openclaw-weixin forced retirement after 5000ms: ...
02:17:47 Plugin opencode forced retirement after 5000ms: ...
02:17:58 failed to write gateway restart handoff: SqliteWorkerError: SQLite worker stopped before its result was received: Cannot find module '...'
02:19:01 loading configuration…
02:21:10 starting HTTP server...
```

Five `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` in this run, all in 02:17–02:18. The missing files are build-specific hashed chunks plus one worker:

```
dist/session-restart-resume-BGxPJyTB.mjs      (previous build's chunk)
dist/session-restart-resume-BzRgzT_h.mjs      (new build's chunk)
dist/config/sessions/session-transcript.worker.js
```

### The restart really did precede the end of the write

File timestamps from the installed tree, same run (UTC):

| Path | mtime |
| --- | --- |
| `.../openclaw/package.json` | 02:23:23.096 |
| `.../openclaw/openclaw.mjs` | 02:23:31.176 |
| `.../openclaw/dist/` (dir) | 02:23:40.153 |
| `.../dist/abort-BSsSO6Oz.mjs` (sample) | 02:23:26 |

`installation_replaced` fired at **02:17:40**, i.e. **6 minutes before the last write landed**. Whatever the detector compares (a version/build manifest) is written early in npm's in-place reify, so the trigger is available long before the tree is consistent.

### The same shape on the previous upgrade (2026-11-19, 11.5 → 11.6)

```
17:54:40 Installation replaced: running 2026.11.5 ...; on-disk 2026.11.6 ...
17:54:47 shutdown failed in 7507ms: plugin-services
17:54:47 forced retirement ×7 (memory-core, acpx, openclaw-weixin, opencode, tavily, acpx)
17:55:46 loading configuration…
17:56:43 starting HTTP server...
```

Five `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` again, at 17:54–17:55. So the pattern is repeatable across two consecutive upgrades, not a one-off.

### Source locations

- `src/infra/gateway-boot-lifecycle.ts` — emits `installation_replaced` (dist `gateway-boot-lifecycle-91eVy9es.mjs:74`)
- `src/infra/restart-handoff.ts` — `failed to write gateway restart handoff` (dist `restart-handoff-DeU7GhfT.mjs:184`)
- `src/daemon/schtasks-control.ts` — the scheduled-task lifecycle mutations (dist `service-CWOs2fKM.mjs:492`)
- `src/cli/gateway-cli/host-lifecycle.ts` — `Gateway host is not serving this iteration` (dist `run-CQugf48S.mjs:436`)

I did not read the detector's comparison rule, only the emitted message, so I cannot say which file it watches.

### What this is not

- **Not a "Gateway stays down" bug.** Both runs recovered on their own: run of 11-23 was serving at 02:21:10, run of 11-19 at 17:56:43. No manual start was needed for either restart.
- **Not a crash.** No uncaught exception and no stability bundle for this restart path; the only bundle written was `gateway.restart_close_failed` at 02:17:47.
- On the 11-23 run the operator issued `openclaw gateway stop` after the Gateway was already serving (IPC refused at 02:22:05 with `UNAVAILABLE: Gateway host is not serving this iteration`, then falling back to `schtasks-stop` at 02:22:07). The downtime after that is an operator action and is explicitly out of scope here.

### Why it matters anyway

- Between `installation_replaced` and the end of the write, a running tree is a mix of old and new modules; any lazy import in that window can hit a hashed chunk that no longer exists. The five failures above are that, not a broken install.
- The restart handoff row is not written, so this restart has no recorded reason afterwards.
- Every plugin is force-retired after 5 s with `resource cleanup remains pending`, and the shutdown reports `shutdown failed in ~7s: plugin-services` on every such upgrade.

### Possible direction (proposal, not tested here)

- Defer `installation_replaced` until the tree settles (for example require the manifest plus a quiet-period check on the install directory) so the restart happens once, against a complete tree.
- Make the handoff write survive the swap: retry once the tree is stable instead of dropping the record when a module is momentarily missing.
- Consider deferring lazy chunk imports while a restart is pending, so a missing mid-swap module cannot fail a service.

### Scope and limits

- Windows 11 x64 only, npm global install, Scheduled Task. Not verified for pnpm, `openclaw update`, or Git checkout installs.
- Two observations, same host. Run of 11-19 has no npm log left (log rotation), so the "detection precedes completion" interval is quantified only for 11-23 (6 minutes).
- I did not measure how long the tree is inconsistent; the 02:17:40 → 02:23:40 window is the bound from log time to last mtime, not a proof of continuous inconsistency.

issues.body:
Deferred advisory Doctor inspections never run after an update, on either update path, although the update tells the user they will.

**First hop (shipped in-place updater drives, candidate from `main`):** observed 2026-11-23 on Linux systemd, Control UI click from published v2026.11.7 to a `main` (2e8c1ad0aa97) candidate, run `85491ff5` succeeded in 186.9 s. A read-only watcher captured the candidate's live Doctor receipt with 13 `deferredInspectionCheckIds`, then the post-core receipt with `[]`. The final run row has no `post-activation doctor inspections` step. The same happened with the #203924 candidate (run `4cfae77d`), so that change did not cause it. The shipped updater runs post-activation inspections when it receives selectors (`v2026.11.7:src/cli/update-cli/post-update.ts:672-687`), so the selectors appear to be dropped before it reads them; post-core runs in the candidate (`OPENCLAW_UPDATE_POST_CORE=1`), which makes this candidate-side and fixable on `main` [INFERENCE from the receipts].

**Release path (`src/update/`):** no advisory Doctor runs after the trial commits; `src/update/gateway-trial.ts:63-76` records boot verification and success only. `end-state.md` §4 promised "Doctor advisory in the background; findings in the run record".

**What the user sees:** "N warnings need attention", 11 of them "Advisory inspection deferred until after update activation … Run `openclaw doctor --lint --only <check>` after activation", and `src/flows/doctor-health-contributions.ts:674-676` says the updater runs them. It does not, so the security, OAuth-TLS, model-reference and runtime-tool-schema inspections are skipped after every update.

Evidence: maintainer handoff `update-rewrite/beta-gate/deferral-not-warning/` (`base-control/` and the #203924 run). Supersedes the noise-only framing of #203743; #203924 is closed because hiding the notices would hide this.

issues.body:
## Summary

Two Discord DMs to the main session started failing with `GatewayDrainingError` at 04:45:17 UTC while the Gateway's global admission was open (no `[admission] closed` line between the process start at 03:44:57 and 06:36:40). The channel ingress drain released each claim with `recordAttempt: false` and no delay, and the pump re-claimed it about every 45 ms. Every attempt ran the Discord preflight, which downloads and saves the message's attachments, so one 1.4 MB screenshot was written to `~/.openclaw/media/inbound` 154,374 times (205 GB). The loop survived a Gateway restart and stopped only when the two `channel_ingress_events` rows were marked failed by hand.

## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.11.3 (847611d), `@openclaw/discord` 2026.10.10, Node 24.22.1
- Linux x64, systemd user service `openclaw-gateway.service`, `--max-old-space-size=3872`
- Channels at the time: Discord, WhatsApp, Telegram. Most turns use the `claude-cli` runtime.

## What happened (2026-11-20, UTC)

| Time | Event |
|---|---|
| 03:44:57 | Gateway process starts (after a normal restart). |
| 04:45:17 | A Discord DM arrives with a phone screenshot (`rn_image_picker_lib_temp_<uuid>.jpg`, 1,428,680 bytes); a second text-only DM follows. Both fail at once: `message run failed: GatewayDrainingError: Gateway is temporarily unavailable. Please try again shortly.` `duration=2ms`. |
| 04:45:17–06:36:40 | Both events re-claimed and re-dispatched every ~45 ms each, alternating. The Gateway sits at about 90% of a core. Global admission stays open; other channels and the Control UI work. |
| 06:36:40 | `openclaw gateway restart`. Admission closes for the restart as expected. |
| 06:37:18 | 18 s after the new process starts, the loop resumes: the rows were still `claimed`/`pending` in `state/openclaw.sqlite`. 146,814 `GatewayDrainingError` lines in the next 30 min. |
| 07:07:07 | Gateway stopped, the two `channel_ingress_events` rows set to failed by hand, Gateway started. No `GatewayDrainingError` since. |

Totals from the journal, 04:45–07:08: **615,815** `GatewayDrainingError` lines and **307,906** `message processed: channel=discord ... outcome=error` lines, about 2,170 failed dispatches a minute.

On disk: **154,374** files in `~/.openclaw/media/inbound/` named `rn_image_picker_lib_temp_<uuid>---<new uuid>.jpg`, every one 1,428,680 bytes with the same md5, written 04:45:17 to 07:07:07 at about 1,000 a minute (1.4 GB a minute). That is one copy per dispatch attempt of the message that had the attachment (307,906 attempts across the two messages). Nothing referenced any copy; only the original event row pointed at the CDN URL.

## Why it loops

`dist/ingress-drain-*.mjs` (2026.11.3), `applyFailureDisposition`:

```js
if (err instanceof GatewayDrainingError) {
    await releaseClaim(claim, { recordAttempt: false });
    return;
}
```

The claim goes back with no attempt recorded and no delay, so `retry.failure(...)` (attempt count, backoff, `retry-limit-exceeded` dead-letter) never applies. #142013's fix keeps the row unclaimed while *global* admission is closed. Here the `GatewayDrainingError` came from a narrower admission (the target session's root work, as in #152999 / #199412) while the global gate was open, so the pump kept claiming.

## Why it fills the disk

`@openclaw/discord` `dist/.setup/message-handler.preflight-*.mjs` resolves media in preflight, before dispatch:

```js
const preparedMedia = await resolveMediaList(message, params.mediaMaxBytes, mediaResolveOptions);
```

Each re-dispatch runs preflight again, fetches the attachment from the CDN and saves it under a fresh UUID (`<sanitized>---<baseId><ext>` in `dist/store-*.mjs`). Nothing ties the saved file to the ingress event, so a retry cannot reuse it.

## Expected

1. A `GatewayDrainingError` that is not a global drain should count as an attempt and back off (for example the normal retry policy, or a fixed hold until admission for that lane reopens), and dead-letter after the usual limit. A storm should not be possible even when the cause is a per-session admission state.
2. Ingress media should be fetched once per event: keyed by event id and attachment id, reused on retry, or fetched only after admission succeeds.
3. Optional but useful: content-hash dedupe in the inbound media store, and a disk budget check before saving.
4. A row stuck in `claimed`/`pending` should not resume the same storm after a restart without a backoff.

## Workaround used

Stop the Gateway, back up `state/openclaw.sqlite`, set the stuck `channel_ingress_events` rows to failed, start the Gateway; then delete the duplicate files, keeping one. The local watcher now raises a notice when the inbound folder gains 100 files or 1 GB in 10 minutes.

## Logs (first and last cycle, ids masked)

```
2026-11-20T04:45:17.413Z [diagnostic] message processed: channel=discord chatId=user:<id> messageId=<msg A> sessionKey=agent:main:main outcome=error duration=3ms error="GatewayDrainingError: Gateway is temporarily unavailable. Please try again shortly."
2026-11-20T04:45:17.415Z [discord] message run failed: GatewayDrainingError: Gateway is temporarily unavailable. Please try again shortly.
2026-11-20T04:45:17.460Z [diagnostic] message processed: channel=discord chatId=user:<id> messageId=<msg A> ... outcome=error duration=3ms
...
2026-11-20T06:37:18.778Z [diagnostic] message processed: channel=discord ... outcome=error   (18 s after the restart)
```

issues.body:
After a successful Control UI update, the Updates settings can stay disabled with "Checking for updates…", and Update/Retry shows "Admin access required", across reloads and a Gateway restart.

**Observed** 2026-11-23 on Linux (systemd user service from `openclaw gateway install`, npm global install, Gateway head 1e34a8f1ba from #203925, isolated profile; evidence in the maintainer's `update-rewrite/beta-gate/dead-owner-at-start/side-findings.md`):

1. Control UI click → Gateway SIGKILLed during `prepare:install` → restart settles the run `interrupted` → Retry enabled.
2. Click Retry, then Update and restart → run `59183b5d` succeeds (05:07:30 UTC) → close the success dialog.
3. Settings switches and the Update Gateway button stay disabled with "Checking for updates…"; a 60 s wait, two reloads and a later Gateway restart do not clear it. The page still shows Connected. Retry later says "Admin access required."

Meanwhile `openclaw gateway call update.status --json` succeeds and returns the succeeded last run, `updateAvailable: null`, `effectiveChannel: stable`. The browser console shows no JavaScript exceptions; only aborted avatar requests and failed `healthz` requests around the reconnect.

**Not known yet:** whether this needs the interrupted-then-retried sequence or happens after any successful update, and whether the "Admin access required" means the reconnected browser session lost operator scope. `updateAvailable: null` from a successful status read may be the state the UI never leaves [INFERENCE].

Impact: a user can be left with no way to update or change update settings from the UI after an update that succeeded.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Crash (process/app exits or hangs)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On main [`58b6e27781be`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/58b6e27781beb72f05294955ddf089375d4ea6e8), paired-node `readDirectory` keeps requesting `dir.list` pages for as long as the node returns `truncated: true` and a strictly larger `nextPageToken`. There is no page count.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Read `readDirectory` in `extensions/file-transfer/src/workspace-bridge.ts` on [`58b6e27781be`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/58b6e27781beb72f05294955ddf089375d4ea6e8) (lines 348-411).
2. The function starts `offset` at 0 and loops with `while (true)`. Each pass calls `dir.list` with `maxEntries` 4096, or 120 when that node has `boundedReplies`. It returns only when `payload.truncated === false`. A truncated page is accepted when `nextPageToken` parses as an integer greater than `offset`.
3. Each `dir.list` invoke passes `timeoutMs` 60000. The next page starts a new invoke. The default path does not add a timeout around the whole loop. `boundedReplies` adds one 60 second signal around the loop and still has no page count.

The closed pull request built a real directory of 131073 empty names (one past 32 pages of 4096) and listed it through production `createNodeWorkspaceBridge` and `handleDirList` in one process. That run was on the patched head, so it stopped after 32 pages. This report did not repeat that directory on `58b6e27781be`. A second OS process enrolled as a node was not part of that run.

### Expected behavior

`file.fetch` on the same bridge clamps a read at 16 MiB (`MAX_BYTES` at line 20, applied around lines 110-116). Directory listing has no matching total budget.

The closed pull request stopped after 32 pages. A directory that finishes on page 32 still returned every name. [steipete's comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/165805#issuecomment-6103892158) agreed the unbounded loop is present, and left the 32-page size as an open policy choice because it also rejects a valid directory above 131072 entries.

### Actual behavior

On `58b6e27781be` the loop has no page budget. A node that answers quickly and keeps advancing `nextPageToken` causes another `dir.list`. The names already collected stay in the `entries` array for that call.

Bootstrap discovery calls that function with only `filePath` (`src/agents/workspace.ts` lines 882-884). It does not pass a signal. When workspace access is set, a listing error is rethrown (lines 901-903) instead of being recorded and skipped.

### OpenClaw version

main [`58b6e27781be`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/58b6e27781beb72f05294955ddf089375d4ea6e8) (package.json 2026.11.7). Source read of that commit. The 131073-name listing is from the closed pull request, not a new run of this commit.

### Operating system

Source read of GitHub main. The closed pull request's listing ran on macOS Darwin arm64, Node v26.12.1.

### Install method

The closed pull request used a local checkout. This report's current check is the main tree on GitHub.

### Model

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Provider / routing chain

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Logs

Closed pull request, patched bridge, in-process handlers, directory of 131073 names:

```console
OK: files=kept instructions diagnostics=[{"dir":"fat","reason":"io","detail":"Directory listing exceeded 32 pages"}] dirList=34 stat=0 fetch=1
```

`dir.list` ran 34 times: one page for the root, 32 pages for the oversized directory, and one page for the sibling. That diagnostic is from the patch. It is not what `58b6e27781be` prints.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Closed pull request: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/165805

Stale notice: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/165805#issuecomment-6906544368

Close comment: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/165805#issuecomment-7091010760

Maintainer note that the loop is real and the size limit was left open: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/165805#issuecomment-6103892158

Current loop: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/58b6e27781beb72f05294955ddf089375d4ea6e8/extensions/file-transfer/src/workspace-bridge.ts#L348-L411

Bootstrap call: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/58b6e27781beb72f05294955ddf089375d4ea6e8/src/agents/workspace.ts#L882-L884

The pull request was closed unmerged on 2026-11-23 by openclaw-barnacle for inactivity. Head [`b06896ea3a7`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/b06896ea3a713ac2eb66170f8ab83e625ee81533). No open issue mentioned that pull request before this report.

### Impact and severity

Affected: a gateway using the file-transfer workspace bridge to list a paired-node directory, including bootstrap discovery of that workspace.

Severity: the accumulated `entries` array grows by one page per reply for as long as the node advances the token. This report did not observe a process exit on `58b6e27781be`.

Frequency: any directory whose listing stays truncated with a larger `nextPageToken`. One page is at most 4096 names, or 120 when `boundedReplies` is set for that node.

Consequence: one directory read has no total page stop. `file.fetch` on the same bridge already stops at 16 MiB.

### Additional information

The closed pull request kept the 32-page cap. `readDirectory` threw `Directory listing exceeded 32 pages` after 32 pages, and a finished page 32 returned every name. Bootstrap glob discovery treated that page-budget error like a local unreadable directory: it recorded one `io` diagnostic and still loaded the rest of the pattern. Other remote listing errors still failed the pattern.

This issue does not reopen that pull request. It is the tracker for the unbounded listing still on main. The 32-page number was the pull request's proposed contract, and the maintainer comment left that number open.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

Running `gateway install` through npx installs the Gateway service but does not create the terminal command: it prints `Terminal default unchanged: keeping ~/.npm/_npx/<hash>/node_modules/.bin/openclaw`, and fresh login and interactive shells have no `openclaw`.

### Steps to reproduce

1. On Linux, use a fresh account that has its own systemd user manager, Node and npm, no `openclaw` command and no `~/.openclaw*` directories.
2. Pack main at `3c8c7bf` into a tarball with the repository's `scripts/package-openclaw-for-docker.mjs`. The released 2026.11.6, 2026.11.7 and 2026.11.10-beta.1 do not have the terminal command step yet.
3. Set `CUSTOM_UNIT_NAME` to a custom systemd unit name and `MAIN_TARBALL` to the path of the tarball from step 2, then run:
   ```bash
   OPENCLAW_SYSTEMD_UNIT="$CUSTOM_UNIT_NAME" OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PORT=21789 \
     npx --yes --package "$MAIN_TARBALL" openclaw gateway install --port 21789
   ```
4. Read the `Terminal default …` line in the output.
5. Start a fresh login shell and a fresh interactive shell under `env -i` (`bash -lc`, `bash -ic`) and run `command -v openclaw`.

Observed on 2026-11-22; see the evidence section.

### Expected behavior

`docs/cli/gateway/service.md` says that on macOS and Linux, "When no existing command or configured profile already owns the terminal default, the first installation makes it discoverable as `openclaw` in new Bash, zsh, fish, and POSIX sh shells." The same page says that when `gateway install` runs from `npx`, the temporary copy can be deleted, so the service runs the copy in `~/.openclaw/npm` instead. On a fresh account, the first install from npx should therefore create the managed terminal command, and new shells should find `openclaw`.

### Actual behavior

- `gateway install` exited 0. The user service was installed and `enabled`, with `ExecStart` pointing to the copy at `~/.openclaw/npm/lib/node_modules/openclaw/dist/index.js` (npm `openclaw@2026.11.6`).
- The output had exactly one line about the terminal command (home shown as `~`, the Node binary as `<node>`, the npx cache key as `<hash>`):

  ```text
  Terminal default unchanged: keeping ~/.npm/_npx/<hash>/node_modules/.bin/openclaw; this Gateway: <node> --max-old-space-size=8192 ~/.openclaw/npm/lib/node_modules/openclaw/dist/index.js --profile default
  ```

- The kept path is npx's own copy (it resolves to `~/.npm/_npx/<hash>/node_modules/openclaw/openclaw.mjs`), not a command the account had before the run.
- `~/.openclaw/bin/openclaw` was not created. `~/.bashrc` and `~/.profile` were unchanged (same SHA-256 before and after).
- In a fresh `bash -lc` and a fresh `bash -ic`, both started under `env -i`, `command -v openclaw` found nothing.

### OpenClaw version

main at `3c8c7bf` (package version 2026.11.6), run through npx; the service is set to run npm `openclaw@2026.11.6`

### Operating system

Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS (x86_64)

### Install method

Not installed: `npx --yes --package <tarball packed from main>`, Node v24.22.1 from nodejs.org, npm 11.19.1

### Model

None (no model involved)

### Provider / routing chain

None

### Additional provider/model setup details

_No response_

### Logs

```shell
Terminal default unchanged: keeping ~/.npm/_npx/<hash>/node_modules/.bin/openclaw; this Gateway: <node> --max-old-space-size=8192 ~/.openclaw/npm/lib/node_modules/openclaw/dist/index.js --profile default
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Terminal output and file checks only. Home is shown as `~`, the Node binary as `<node>`, the npx cache key as `<hash>`.

- **Environment**: a fresh, disposable Linux account with its own systemd user manager; Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS (x86_64); Node v24.22.1 from nodejs.org and npm 11.19.1. Before the run the account had no `openclaw` command and no `~/.openclaw*` directories. The package was packed from main at `3c8c7bf` (version 2026.11.6) with `scripts/package-openclaw-for-docker.mjs`, because the released 2026.11.6, 2026.11.7 and 2026.11.10-beta.1 do not include `src/daemon/terminal-cli.ts`. The run set `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PORT=21789` and a custom systemd unit name.
- **Service**: `systemctl --user is-enabled` printed `enabled`; the unit's `ExecStart` points to `~/.openclaw/npm/lib/node_modules/openclaw/dist/index.js gateway --port 21789`.
- **Terminal command**: `~/.openclaw/bin` did not exist after the run. `~/.bashrc` and `~/.profile` had the same SHA-256 before and after, and neither mentions `openclaw`.
- **New shells**: `bash -lc` and `bash -ic`, both under `env -i` with PATH set to the system directories, found no `openclaw` (`command -v openclaw` printed nothing).

### Impact and severity

- Affected (observed setup): a fresh Linux account running `gateway install` through npx, from a package built from main. Only builds that include the terminal command step are affected; the released 2026.11.6, 2026.11.7 and 2026.11.10-beta.1 do not have this step yet.
- Severity: the `openclaw` command is not available in new shells, and the message points at npx's temporary copy.
- Frequency: 1/1 observed run.
- Consequence: after `gateway install` exits 0, fresh login and interactive shells find no `openclaw`.

### Additional information

- main at `3c8c7bf`, `src/daemon/terminal-cli.ts:150-180`: the terminal step looks up `openclaw` on the install process's PATH. Under npx that PATH has `<npm cache>/_npx/<hash>/node_modules/.bin` ahead of the account's own PATH directories (only the Node and system directories can come before it), so the first match is npx's copy. Because it is not the managed launcher, a first default-profile install prints "Terminal default unchanged: keeping …" and returns before creating the launcher or adding the PATH line.
- #192331 already treats one-off runner copies as disposable (`isDisposableInstallPath` in `src/daemon/durable-service-entrypoint.ts`, with the comment that a service "must never point into one or keep one on its PATH") and leaves those directories out of the service PATH (`src/commands/daemon-install-plan.shared.ts`). The terminal command choice does not apply the same check.
- Onboarding's foreground summary prints "To keep the Gateway running in the background later: {command}" with the npx form of `gateway install` for npx runs (`src/commands/onboard-quickstart-host.ts:89-94`, text in `src/wizard/i18n/locales/en.ts:344`).
- This report is about running `gateway install` directly. Only npx was run; pnpm dlx and bunx were not tried.
- Related, but different:
  - #200425 added the terminal command step; this report is about which command it treats as already installed when run from npx.
  - #192331 added the durable copy for npx installs and the runner-path rule above.
  - #202822 (fixed by #202824) is about the next-step commands that onboarding prints under npx, not about the terminal command step.
  - #202309 (fixed by #202312) is about `install-cli.sh`'s finish output, a different installer.
- Searched existing issues and PRs (open and closed) for "Terminal default unchanged", `installGatewayTerminalCli`, `isDisposableInstallPath`, and npx with terminal, `gateway install`, `.openclaw/bin` and "command not found"; none covers this.

issues.body:
A containerized Gateway that is hard-killed (SIGKILL, OOM kill) does not come back when Docker restarts the container: the restarted Gateway waits about 95 s and exits 1 at `cli.bootstrap.gateway-lock`:

```
cannot verify Gateway ownership … holder 1 at <host>/pid-ns 4026533702 … Run this command inside the Gateway container or with a shared PID namespace; if the holder has stopped, run `openclaw gateway recover-lock` …
```

**Observed** (2026-11-23, isolated Docker container, self-installed npm package, Gateway as PID 1, state on a volume; receipts in the maintainer's `update-rewrite/beta-gate/dead-owner-at-start/`): SIGKILL PID 1, then `docker start` (same as a restart policy). The new container has a new PID namespace; the lock records holder PID 1 in the old namespace, which this process cannot classify as dead, so startup refuses (`src/infra/gateway-lock-payload.ts` `GatewayLockNamespaceError`, `classifyGatewayLockProcessNamespace`). The same code is in v2026.11.7.

**Impact:** with `restart: unless-stopped`, an OOM-killed or force-killed Gateway container stays down until someone runs `openclaw gateway recover-lock` by hand. The refusal protects against two containers sharing one state volume, but a restarted container of the same deployment hits it too.

**Related:** #196846, #202040 (other PID-namespace refusals in containers). Found while proving the update fix in #203925, which cannot prove its container case because the Gateway never starts.

A graceful `openclaw gateway restart` while a Gateway-run update is installing the candidate fails the run as `package-install-failed` with "Spawn broker exited; command outcome is unavailable | IPC channel disconnected", which blames the package install instead of the restart.

**Observed** 2026-11-23, Linux systemd, run `cb5f841b` (trigger `api`): restart requested at 05:11:40.788 UTC during `prepare:install`; SIGTERM at 05:11:41.965; the old Gateway recorded the terminal failure at 05:11:42.703; the new Gateway was ready at 05:11:49.470. Source: `src/update/prepare-package.ts:147-159` maps a terminated install to `package-install-failed`; `src/update/run.ts:305-309` records it. Evidence in the maintainer's `update-rewrite/beta-gate/dead-owner-at-start/side-findings.md`.

The outcome is visible and terminal (not stuck), so this is the reason text only: a run cancelled by the Gateway's own shutdown should say the update was interrupted by a restart and can be retried. The update prepares inside the Gateway process (`src/gateway/server-methods/update-run.ts` `runUpdateInBackground`), so any Gateway restart during preparation cancels it.

issues.body:
Follow-up from #203497 (review on head 344ac77ca8).

`openclaw update --full-integrity-check` is documented, but on the release update path (Git installs since #203194, package installs since #203497) it is accepted and does nothing: `ReleaseUpdateOptions` has no field for it, and neither in-process release preparation nor `update.run` delegation carries it to a verification owner. Before, the package path and the post-core Doctor honored it.

Fix: carry the request to the release path's verification owner (the target's `openclaw update check-release` running from the staged release, or the boot-time state check), and cover it with a test of the shipped invocation. Until then the flag should not be silently ignored: either run the full check or tell the user it is not available on this path.
