issues.body:
A Control UI update whose Gateway is killed during the service rebind stays "running" until the user runs the CLI, and the UI offers no way out.

**Observed** (Ubuntu 24.04 arm64, real systemd user service, npm global install, `main` at 7afd748445cc; final-proof Linux report, case 4):

1. Click Update in the Control UI (T → T+1). The run `7ae5cc1b` prepares in the serving Gateway (PID 14196), which holds `.update.lock`.
2. SIGKILL that Gateway at the moment the unit's ExecStart is rewritten to the launcher.
3. systemd restarts the Gateway. The unit shows `NeedDaemonReload=yes`: the file on disk names the launcher, the effective ExecStart still names the global entry, so the old build T serves (parent: systemd). That part is safe.
4. For 15 minutes after the restart, run `7ae5cc1b` stays `running/validating` with an unchanged `updatedAt`. The Control UI shows only a disabled "Updating…" control: no Update action, no failure, no next step.
5. One `openclaw update --json` from a terminal clears the old run as interrupted and updates to T+1 (201.7 s wall, 23.5 s outage). No repair command was needed.

**Expected:** the restarted Gateway settles a run whose owner process is dead (as the CLI admission does) and the UI shows "interrupted" with an Update action.

**Where to look:** the Gateway's update-run watcher scans with `legacyOnly: !reconcileAll` (`src/gateway/update-run-watcher.ts:80-88`), and `update.status` reconciles only when no manager owns the run (`src/gateway/server-methods/update-status.ts:101-105`); the CLI path's `reconcileAbandonedUpdateRunsAsync` admission settles it. The restarted Gateway apparently never requests the full reconciliation for a run that a previous Gateway process owned.

Evidence (row, lock, unit state, screenshots at 5/10/15 min, logs): final-proof `linux/report.md`, section "SIGKILL at rebind".

issues.title: [Bug]: Regression since 2026.10.10: native Codex helper completions fail to resume the parent, pausing goals and locking users out of their assistant

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High-priority user-facing bug, regression, or broken workflow.

labels.name: impact:session-state
labels.description: Session, memory, transcript, context, or agent state can drift or corrupt.

labels.name: impact:message-loss
labels.description: Channel message delivery can be lost, duplicated, or misrouted.

labels.name: issue-rating: 🦪 silver shellfish
labels.description: Thin issue quality; more reproduction proof or environment detail is needed.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Summary

Since 2026.10.10, delegating work to native Codex helpers fails roughly once for every helper launched.

The parent agent starts helpers and ends its turn (`sessions_yield`). When a helper finishes, OpenClaw opens a separate wake-up turn on the parent's Codex thread. Two things go wrong with that turn:
- it runs on authority borrowed from the turn that already ended;
- the parent's original Codex turn is often still live on the same thread.

The wake-up turn then fails ("agent harness host capability is no longer active"). The helper's result is lost, any active `/goal` is paused, and the user's next messages are rejected ("Codex session became active in another runner", "still has background work after waiting for cleanup").

This is the underlying problem behind a family of errors that have been reported separately. They are all symptoms of one lifecycle bug: OpenClaw ties authority and thread ownership to a single turn, while native Codex helpers and background work routinely outlive that turn.

### Impact and severity

**Severity: blocks the core workflow on every delegated task, and locks the user out of their own assistant.**

Delegating work to parallel helpers is the main reason to give an assistant a substantial job. On 10.10 and later, that is exactly the moment it breaks:

- **Work silently stops.** Helpers finish their work, but the results never reach the assistant. Nothing tells the user that progress has halted; the conversation just goes quiet.
- **Goals are paused out from under the user.** A failed wake-up pauses the active `/goal` with "Paused after an error." On native Codex sessions the operator cannot resume it ("requires the built-in OpenClaw runtime"), so the user has to notice the stall and re-establish the goal by hand.
- **The user is locked out.** Messages sent afterward are rejected with errors telling the user to "stop its running work and retry", meaning stop the very work they asked for. The user gets no reply at all; the rejected messages are simply dropped.
- **It recurs constantly.** In my installation this happened ~100 times a day on a single long-running task. The assistant becomes something to babysit rather than something that gets work done: every few minutes, check whether it is stuck, abort it, resend the message, re-set the goal.
- **The cost is spent and thrown away.** Helpers run to completion and consume usage, and then their results are discarded.

The experience is that the assistant falls over the moment it is asked to do anything ambitious, and that the user has to spend their time diagnosing and recovering it instead of getting the outcome they asked for. It is deeply frustrating, and it undermines trust in delegating anything substantial at all.

### Steps to reproduce

1. On 2026.10.10 or later (observed through 2026.11.2), use the native Codex runtime (`agentRuntime.id = codex`) for an OpenAI model.
2. In a channel session (Discord in my case), give the agent a long task that it delegates. The agent calls `spawn_agent` for one or more helpers, then `sessions_yield` while they run.
3. Let a helper finish after the parent's turn has ended.
4. Observe the following:
   - the completion "announce" turn fails;
   - any active goal pauses;
   - a user message sent shortly afterward is rejected with no reply.

### Expected behavior

- A helper's completion is delivered to the parent reliably: once the parent's Codex thread is idle, as a turn with its own valid authority.
- If delivery fails, it is retried. It does not lose the result or pause the goal.
- The user's messages are always accepted and answered (queued if necessary). They are never rejected with an instruction to stop running work.

### Actual behavior

A representative sequence from 2026-11-09 (times are America/Los_Angeles; one session; IDs shortened):

| Time | Event |
|---|---|
| 07:03:59, 07:04:05 | The parent calls `spawn_agent` twice. |
| 07:05:49 | The parent calls `sessions_yield`, ending its turn while both helpers run. |
| ~07:07:09 | A helper finishes. OpenClaw starts `announce:codex-native:<parentThread>:<childThread>:succeeded` on the parent thread. |
| 07:08:18 | `codex app-server notification ignored for inactive turn`, with `matchesActiveThread: true` and `matchesActiveTurn: false`. Codex is still emitting `item/started` and `item/completed` for the parent's original turn, while OpenClaw has already made the announce turn the active turn. Two turns are live on one thread. |
| 07:09:38 | `agent cleanup failed … step=codex-trajectory-flush error=agent harness host capability is no longer active`, then `lane task error … durationMs=148848 error="agent harness host capability is no longer active"`, then `Subagent completion direct announce failed`. The session goal changes to `paused`, with `lastStatusNote: "Paused after an error. Resume to continue. agent harness host capability is no longer active"`. |
| 07:14:09, 07:14:42 | Two user messages are rejected with `CodexAdoptedThreadActiveError: Codex session became active in another runner; wait for it to finish before continuing`. The log records `visible channel turn dispatched with no queued reply payloads … cause=error`, and the user receives nothing. |

Error counts in the gateway log:

| Error | 2026-11-08 | 2026-11-09 (until ~07:30) |
|---|---|---|
| `agent harness host capability is no longer active` | 56 | 131 |
| `Codex did not confirm unloading its previous configuration` | 28 | 76 |
| `still has background work after waiting for cleanup` | 20 | 27 |
| `Codex session became active in another runner` | 0 | 6 |
| `Session … placement authority changed` | 0 | 3 |

### Regression boundary: 2026.10.9 → 2026.10.10

I counted these errors per day in the agent's transcript events, alongside `spawn_agent`/`sessions_spawn` calls. The transcripts capture only a subset of the gateway-log errors, but the pattern is unambiguous:

| Period | Version | Helper launches/day | Errors/day |
|---|---|---|---|
| Oct 8–21 | ≤ 10.9 | ~4 | ~0.5 |
| Oct 22–Nov 2 (proactive delegation enabled) | 10.9 | ~63 | ~2 |
| Nov 3–9 | 10.10 → 11.1 → 11.2 | ~97 | ~106 |

- Heavy delegation on 10.9 (~760 helper launches over 12 days) was essentially error-free.
- The first `host capability` / `background work` / `another runner` error in the entire history appears at 2026-11-03 11:16, a few hours after updating to 10.10 that morning. It has continued on every release since.
- Whatever changed between 10.9 and 10.10 in harness authority binding, announce delivery, or Codex thread retention is the most likely origin.

### Code-level observations (2026.11.2 dist)

- `bindHarnessHostSourceAuthority` (`src/agents/harness/host-source-authority.ts`) throws "agent harness host capability is no longer active" in any of these cases:
  - `attempt.admittedRunContext.operationalRunInstance` differs from the instance captured at bind time;
  - the captured admitted-run assertion fails;
  - the gateway is not current.

  The announce turn for a helper launched by an earlier turn appears to carry that earlier turn's delegated authority. It fails as soon as it touches a host capability, which in the trace above was the trajectory flush during cleanup.
- The announce turn is started while the parent's original Codex turn is still producing items on the same thread (see 07:08:18). That makes the follow-on errors expected:
  - "did not confirm unloading previous configuration",
  - "still has background work",
  - "became active in another runner".
- The `codex-trajectory-flush` cleanup failure has the same signature as #171197, which was closed as fixed in October. It is recurring on 2026.11.2.

### Suggested direction

The fix needs to be in the lifecycle model, not in individual guards:

- **The session, not the turn, should own outstanding helper work and background commands.**
- **Completions should be queued per session and delivered once the parent Codex thread is idle.** Simultaneous completions should be coalesced into one wake-up, instead of one competing announce turn per helper.
- **Wake-up turns should be admitted with fresh authority of their own,** rather than inheriting authority from the turn that spawned the helpers.
- **A failed delivery should be retried.** It should never discard the helper's result or pause the user's goal.
- **User messages should always be queued and answered,** never rejected with "stop its running work and retry".

### OpenClaw version

2026.11.2 (b556fdf); `@openclaw/codex` 2026.11.2. The regression first appeared on 2026.10.10.

### Operating system

macOS 27.2 (Apple Silicon)

### Install method

npm global (Homebrew Node 26.13.0)

### Model

openai/gpt-6.1-sol

### Provider / routing chain

OpenClaw → native Codex runtime (`agentRuntime.id = codex`, codex-cli 0.164.0) → OpenAI

### Beta release blocker

No

### Additional information

Related reports that I believe are symptoms of this same underlying issue:
- #194403: helper-completion continuations lose authority and block conversations.
- #196061 and #196062: a silent turn with a retained command is falsely marked failed. That is one entry point into the stuck state, not the root cause.
- #171197: the `codex-trajectory-flush` "host capability is no longer active" failure, closed as fixed but recurring.
- #147759 and #167280: delayed or stalled prompts after native Codex handoff and stop.

Diagnostic signal: when the parent keeps its turn open and collects helper results with `wait_agent` instead of calling `sessions_yield`, the completion arrives inside the live turn and this path is not exercised. That is consistent with the announce/wake-up turn being the failure point.

issues.body:
### Summary

Grouped lower-severity findings from a codebase audit (the same audit that produced PR #184858 and issues #184887, #184888, #184889, #184890, #184891, #184892, #184893 for the higher-severity items). Each item is grounded in a direct read of `main` @ `d777ae12` (files unchanged as of `3d7f8fbf`); none was executed end-to-end. Filed together to avoid opening a dozen low-severity issues — happy to see any item split out.

### Steps to reproduce

Each item cites its exact location; all are reachable from shipped production code paths.

- [ ] **Pre-update config snapshot is non-atomic** — `src/config/backup-rotation.ts:215-222` writes the `.pre-update` rollback point with `flag: "w"` (truncate in place). A crash mid-write leaves a torn snapshot at exactly the moment an update is in flight; it self-heals only on the next update attempt. Fix: temp + rename (repo convention).
- [ ] **`withNodeRuntimePath` drops PATH entries when env carries both `Path` and `PATH`** — `node-runtime-env.mjs:86-101` derives `entries` from the alphabetically-first PATH-keyed var only (`"PATH"` sorts before `"Path"`) and writes it to both keys. The Win32 env block is case-insensitive but a JS object is not, so a merged env (service/handoff env assembly) with two differently-cased PATH vars silently loses the second key's directories for every lifecycle child (npm/pnpm child installs, service refresh, recovery respawn).
- [ ] **pnpm-workspace.yaml swap during source updates is not crash-safe and its restore can delete the operator's file** — `src/infra/update-runner-git-commands.ts:199-216`: crash between `rename` and `restoreWorkspace` leaves the tracked file replaced and the original in an orphaned `workspace-original-*` dir that `cleanupGlobalRenameDirs` never cleans (its prefix is `.openclaw-`); if pnpm rewrites the file during the candidate install, the content-equality guard fails and the original is `rm -rf`'d (git-recoverable only because the pre-update clean check guarantees no uncommitted edits).
- [ ] **Read-path auto-recovery can revert an intentional, valid manual edit** — `src/config/io.observe-suspicious.ts:43-45` fires `size-drop-vs-last-good` on any valid read where the file is <50% of the last-known-good baseline (no invalidity requirement); `src/config/io.observe-recovery.ts:342-411` then atomically overwrites `openclaw.json` with `.bak` (edit survives only as `.clobbered.*` + a log warning). Design question: should a read-path heuristic that cannot distinguish "user halved their config" from "something clobbered it" act destructively on a file that still validates?
- [ ] **Ingress claim-conflict loop has no backoff or cap** — `src/channels/message/ingress-queue.ts:299-344` `continue`s on conflict with no sleep/jitter/budget; each iteration costs two worker round-trips, so sustained contention busy-spins the gateway main thread. Lane-key serialization makes this a tail risk.
- [ ] **Recovery backoff sleep ignores abort/shutdown** — `src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue-recovery.ts:1186-1189` awaits a plain `sleep(remainingBackoffMs)` (up to 600s for retryCount ≥ 4) with no AbortSignal. Currently dormant: only reachable when a queued row sets `retryAmbiguousFinalText`, which no bundled caller does today. Fix is `sleepWithAbort(ms, signal)`.
- [ ] **`safeEqualSecret("", "")` returns true** — `src/security/secret-equal.ts:23-26` treats empty-vs-empty as a match. Every current call site guards empty secrets before comparing, but any future call site that skips that guard silently downgrades to "no auth"; consider returning `false` for the empty-empty case.
- [ ] **Multi-root read admission recognizes only 1 of 3 escape-message forms** — `src/agents/agent-tools.read.ts:681-683` matches `/^Path escapes sandbox root \(/` only, while the repo's own complete classifier (`src/agents/sandbox-paths.ts:125-135`) knows three forms and `apply-patch.test.ts:417` shows the symlink form in practice. A `Path resolves outside…`/`Symlink escapes sandbox root…` rejection from the primary root aborts the fallback loop instead of trying additional read roots — false denial (fails closed).
- [ ] **Windows drive-relative tool paths anchor to the process's per-drive CWD** — `src/agents/sandbox-paths.ts:54-64`: `C:temp\file` matches neither `isWindowsDrivePath` (requires a separator) nor `path.win32.isAbsolute`, so it resolves against `process.env['=C:']` rather than the tool cwd; the write lands in a different in-root directory than the documented "relative paths from the workspace directory" contract (`docs/tools/apply-patch.md:47`). Containment still holds.
- [ ] **Hand-authored allowlist entry `{ pattern: "*", argPattern: … }` is silently dead** — `src/infra/exec-command-resolution.ts:334-341,351-366`: the bare-wildcard fast path requires no `argPattern` and the main loop skips `pattern === "*"` unconditionally, while `docs/tools/exec-approvals.md` documents `argPattern` as a general per-entry restriction and `classifyExecAllowlistScope` reports the entry as active. Fails closed, but invisibly to the operator.
- [ ] **apply_patch removed-link matching is case-sensitive on case-insensitive volumes** — `src/agents/apply-patch.ts:477-500` matches later hunk paths against removed links lexically (`path.relative` is case-sensitive) while the module handles case variants elsewhere (`hasCaseVariant`, `:566-580`); a `Delete File: Link` followed by a case-variant re-spelling can false-reject on APFS.
- [ ] **Session-key case folding hardcodes its per-channel exemptions** — `packages/session-url-contract/src/session-key-normalization.ts:117-153` lowercases every peer ID except Signal groups and Matrix rooms; any future channel with structured case-sensitive IDs folds distinct conversations into one session key. Consistent on read and write today, so this is a forward-compatibility note rather than a live collision.

### Expected behavior

Each item should either be confirmed as an accepted tradeoff (with a comment/naming where missing) or repaired along the lines sketched above.

### Actual behavior

As described per item.

### OpenClaw version

main @ `d777ae12` (package 2026.10.7); all cited files unchanged as of `3d7f8fbf`.

### Operating system

All (per-item platform notes inline).

### Install method

Any (core code paths).

### Model

N/A — no model or provider involved.

### Provider / routing chain

N/A — no provider involved.

### Impact and severity

- Affected: varies per item; each individually is low severity (fails closed, dormant, narrow trigger, or forward-compatibility only).
- Severity: low each; the value is the consolidated list.
- Frequency: edge cases and tail risks.
- Consequence: hardening opportunities; none observed as live failures.

### Additional information

Context: these came out of a 6-area audit (gateway, persistence, config/Doctor, tool path validation, update/lifecycle, channel dispatch). The highest-severity finding (non-atomic overwrite of `MEMORY.md` in the doctor legacy-root-memory merge) is already fixed via PR #184858; medium/high findings are filed separately. Happy to split any item into its own issue or take a stab at a focused fix PR.

issues.body:
**Environment**
- OpenClaw 2026.10.10 (commit 7dc3350), bundled inside ClawX 0.7.0
- Windows 11 (10.0.26300), Node 24.18
- memory-core plugin, local Ollama embeddings (nomic-embed-text)

**What happens**
Dreaming is enabled in the Control UI (Settings -> Memory -> Dreams) and the config reports `dreaming.enabled: true`.
After a gateway restart, `dreaming.enabled` is `false` again AND the dreaming cron job is gone from the cron store - not disabled, absent. Enabling it again recreates the job with a NEW job id.

**Frequency**
Observed six separate times between 16 and 23 November 2026. In one instance the config file mtime was unchanged from before the restart, so this does not look like a plain file rewrite every time.

**Evidence**
- `dreaming.enabled=False`, no dreaming job in the cron store (`openclaw memory status` shows `Dreaming: off`).
- Re-enabling in the UI restores it (`enabled=1`, cron `0 3 * * *`) but the job id differs each time (e.g. d166234a -> 32929752), so prior run history is orphaned.
- The UI states dreaming is enabled by default, which is why the silent off-state took days to notice.

**Steps to reproduce (as best we can determine)**
1. Enable dreaming in the Control UI; confirm `dreaming.enabled: true` and a dreaming job exists.
2. Restart the gateway (we restart via ClawX, which owns the process).
3. Observe `dreaming.enabled: false` and no dreaming job in the cron store.

**Impact**
Dreaming silently stops. Because the job is removed rather than disabled, nothing logs a failure - the diary simply has no new entries, and the UI still claims the feature is on by default. In our case it went unnoticed for days and only surfaced via a precheck that reads the config directly.

**Questions**
1. Is there a documented owner of `plugins.entries.memory-core.config.dreaming` that rewrites it at startup (plugin sync, doctor, migration)?
2. Should a missing dreaming job be re-created from config on boot, rather than silently staying absent?
3. Could the job id be stable across re-enables so run history survives?

Happy to gather more diagnostics if helpful - we can reproduce on demand and can attach `memory status` output before/after a restart.

issues.body:
## Summary

On 2026.11.6, a Skill Workshop background experience review that inherits `openai_https/gpt-6.2-sol` can fail before any model call with:

```text
[skills/workshop] skill experience review failed: Unknown model: openai_https/gpt-6.2-sol. Run `openclaw models list --refresh --provider openai_https` to inspect this provider's model choices, then retry with a model supported by your account.
```

The suggested remediation command itself fails, because the model catalog has no provider named `openai_https` at all:

```text
$ openclaw models list --refresh --provider openai_https --json
{"ok":false,"error":{"type":"cli_error","message":"Unknown model catalog provider \"openai_https\". Run openclaw models list --all to list models and their provider IDs."}}
```

The same model resolves fine in the catalog under the `openai` provider:

```text
$ openclaw models list --json | jq '[.models[].key] | map(select(contains("gpt-6.2")))'
["openai/gpt-6.2-sol","openai/gpt-6.2-astra"]
```

## Environment

- OpenClaw: 2026.11.6 (06afb10), Linux x86_64, Node v26.13.1
- Main agent primary model: an OpenAI subscription model running on the native Codex runtime (OAuth; foreground turns work normally on it)
- Affected flow: background Skill Workshop experience review (`agent-end-side-effects` → `experience-review`), which captures the foreground session's `modelProviderId`/`modelId` and runs a locked openclaw-harness turn with `modelSelectionLocked: true`, `modelFallbacksOverride: []`

## Observed impact

- Since 2026-11-14 the gateway log records 27 `skill experience review failed: Unknown model: openai_https/...` events and zero successful background reviews on such sessions.
- A separate GLM-provider control has no verified successful review receipt yet; no claim is made about the end-to-end behavior of other providers.
- There is no configuration key to point the review at a different model: `skills.workshop.autonomous` only exposes `mode` and `channelNotices`.

## Reproduction

1. Set the main agent primary to an OpenAI subscription model served through the Codex runtime (e.g. `gpt-6.2-sol`).
2. Accumulate at least 10 model iterations across qualifying turns in one ordinary session (`EXPERIENCE_REVIEW_ITERATION_THRESHOLD = 10` in `agent-end-side-effects`), then allow the gateway to go idle for ~30 s. Model iterations are not skill-read counts; subagent sessions are excluded.
3. Watch the gateway log for `skill experience review failed: Unknown model: openai_https/<model>`.

## Expected behavior

The background review should resolve the captured runtime provider id against its catalog-equivalent provider (here `openai_https` → `openai`), or fall back to a resolvable model, instead of failing on a provider id that does not exist in the catalog — especially since the error text recommends a command that cannot succeed for that provider.

## Notes

- `~/.openclaw/agents/<id>/agent/models.json` has no `openai_https` entries here, and the string does not appear in `openclaw.json`, so the id appears to be stamped at runtime on the foreground turn context rather than configured.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

When an agent runs on `agentRuntime: claude-cli`, a successful `show_widget` call (target `assistant_message`) never produces a `type: "canvas"` content block, either on the live `chat` final message or in `chat.history`. Native clients that render inline widgets only from `canvas` blocks (the iOS app via `OpenClawChatUI`) therefore show no widget. The tool row says "Show Widget · Outcome unknown" and the turn summary says "1 unknown".

The web Control UI is not affected, but only because the model also writes an `[embed ref="cv_…" /]` shortcode into its reply text and the web UI parses shortcodes client-side (`ui/src/lib/chat/message-normalizer.ts`). Native clients do not parse shortcodes.

The same prompt on the embedded runtime (`agentRuntime: openclaw`), with the same model and the same credential, does produce the `canvas` block on the live final message.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run a Gateway on 2026.11.7 (Docker image `openclaw/openclaw:2026.11.7`) with Claude Code CLI installed (tested with 2.1.330; originally seen with 2.1.310 on 2026.10.33) and an Anthropic setup-token profile.
2. Configure the default model on the Claude CLI runtime:
   ```json
   "agents": { "defaults": {
     "model": "anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5",
     "models": {
       "anthropic/*": { "agentRuntime": { "id": "claude-cli" } },
       "anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5": { "agentRuntime": { "id": "claude-cli" } }
     } } },
   "tools": { "profile": "full" }
   ```
3. Connect an operator WS client the way the iOS app does: `client.id: "openclaw-ios"`, `mode: "ui"`, caps `agent-kind, inline-widgets, model-selection-policy, ultrafast`. I also added `tool-events` to observe tool events; that changes nothing in the outcome. Use a signed device identity so operator scopes are granted.
4. `chat.send` with: *"Use the show_widget tool to render a small inline widget (presentation.target assistant_message) with a green box that says hello. Do not pin it. After the tool returns, reply with one short sentence."*
5. Wait for `chat` `state: "final"`, then call `chat.history` for the session.
6. Optional: switch both model entries to `"agentRuntime": { "id": "openclaw" }`, restart, and repeat on a new session key for comparison.

### Expected behavior

As on the embedded runtime, the final assistant message carries a `canvas` block:

```json
[{"type":"text","text":"…"},
 {"type":"canvas","preview":{"kind":"canvas","surface":"assistant_message","render":"url","title":"…","sandbox":"scripts","url":"/__openclaw__/canvas/documents/cv_…/index.html","viewId":"cv_…"},"rawText":null}]
```

After a reload, `chat.history` restores the same block, as docs/tools/show-widget.md describes. The tool's activity item has `status: "completed"`.

### Actual behavior

On claude-cli, the canvas document is created (`cv_…` exists and the tool result names it), but:

- The live `chat` final message has `content` types `["text"]` only, with no `canvas` block.
- The `chat.history` final assistant message also has `["text"]` only.
- The `chat.history` `activity` item for the successful `show_widget` call has no `status` and gets `summary: "Outcome unknown"`. The iOS app renders this as "Outcome unknown" / "1 unknown".

### OpenClaw version

2026.11.7 (e31bbf0). Also observed on 2026.10.33. The relevant code is unchanged on `main` @ 49795c31df.

### Operating system

Gateway: Linux (Docker on a VPS). Client where the symptom was found: iOS app 2026.11.40 on iOS 26.6.2.

### Install method

Docker (`openclaw/openclaw:2026.11.7`), Claude Code CLI installed with npm into the container user's `~/.local`.

### Model

anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5

### Provider / routing chain

anthropic → `agentRuntime: claude-cli` (Claude Code CLI 2.1.330) → OpenClaw tools over the loopback MCP server (`mcp__openclaw__show_widget`). Comparison run: anthropic → `agentRuntime: openclaw` (embedded).

### Additional provider/model setup details

Auth is an Anthropic setup-token profile (`anthropic:manual`, `mode: token`). The same profile was used for both runtimes.

### Logs

Captured gateway WS frames, trimmed. Ids are random per run.

**claude-cli: agent tool event, `phase: "result"`, for `show_widget`.** `result` is a bare array of Anthropic content blocks and has no `details`:

```json
{"stream":"tool","data":{"phase":"result","name":"show_widget","isError":false,
 "result":[{"type":"text","text":"{\n  \"kind\": \"canvas\",\n  \"presentation\": {\n    \"target\": \"assistant_message\",\n    \"title\": \"Hello\",\n    \"sandbox\": \"scripts\"\n  },\n  \"view\": {\n    \"id\": \"cv_b6e3…\",\n    \"url\": \"/__openclaw__/canvas/documents/cv_b6e3…/index.html\"\n  },\n  \"text\": \"Widget hosted at …\"\n}"}]}}
```

**claude-cli: live final**

```json
{"state":"final","message":{"role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"[embed ref=\"cv_b6e3…\" title=\"Hello\" height=\"120\" /]\n\nThe green \"hello\" box is rendered inline above and isn't pinned."}]}}
```

**claude-cli: `chat.history`**. The tool call and its result are blocks inside an assistant message, not a `toolResult` message:

```json
{"role":"assistant","provider":"claude-cli","content":[
  {"type":"toolcall","id":"toolu_018F…","name":"mcp__openclaw__show_widget","arguments":{"title":"Hello","kind":"html","widget_code":"…","pin":false,"presentation":{"target":"assistant_message"}}},
  {"type":"tool_result","tool_use_id":"toolu_018F…","name":"mcp__openclaw__show_widget","content":[{"type":"text","text":"{ \"kind\": \"canvas\", … }"}]}]}
```

```json
"activity":[{"items":[{"toolCallId":"toolu_018F…","name":"mcp__openclaw__show_widget","phase":"end","title":"Mcp Openclaw Show Widget","summary":"Outcome unknown"}]}]
```

**Embedded (`openclaw`) runtime, same prompt: tool event result is `{content, details}`, and the live final includes the canvas block**

```json
{"phase":"result","name":"show_widget","isError":false,"result":{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"{ \"kind\": \"canvas\", … }"}],"details":{"kind":"canvas","presentation":{"target":"assistant_message","title":"Hello widget","sandbox":"scripts"},"view":{"id":"cv_c1c9…","url":"/__openclaw__/canvas/documents/cv_c1c9…/index.html"}}}}
{"state":"final","message":{"role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"…"},{"type":"canvas","preview":{"kind":"canvas","surface":"assistant_message","render":"url","title":"Hello widget","sandbox":"scripts","url":"/__openclaw__/canvas/documents/cv_c1c9…/index.html","viewId":"cv_c1c9…"},"rawText":null}]}}
```

**Direct check against the shipped 2026.11.7 bundle.** I imported `dist/chat-display-projection.canvas-*.mjs` and ran it on the captured claude-cli payloads:

```
live: Array.isArray(result) = true
live: extractChatToolResultCanvasPreview(result) = undefined
live: same content wrapped as {content: result} = {"kind":"canvas","surface":"assistant_message","render":"url","title":"Hello","sandbox":"scripts","url":"/__openclaw__/canvas/documents/cv_b6e3…/index.html","viewId":"cv_b6e3…"}
history: augmentChatHistoryWithCanvasBlocks changed messages = false
history: final content types after augment = ["text"]
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Root cause (line numbers from `main` @ 49795c31df):

1. **Live path: the claude-cli tool result reaches the canvas extractor as an array, and the extractor only accepts records.**
   - `src/agents/cli-output-events.ts:253` (`emitClaudeToolResultBlock`) passes the raw Anthropic `tool_result.content` (an array of content blocks) as `result`.
   - `src/agents/cli-runner/execute-events.ts:287` emits the `phase: "result"` tool event with that value. `prepareToolResult`/`sanitizeStructuredToolResult` returns arrays unchanged.
   - `src/gateway/server-chat.ts:1166` calls `extractChatToolResultCanvasPreview(evt.data.result)`.
   - `src/gateway/chat-display-projection.canvas.ts:204-210`: `extractChatToolResultCanvasPreview` starts with `readRecord(message)`, which is `asOptionalRecord`. `isRecord` in `packages/normalization-core/src/record-coerce.ts:2` rejects arrays, so the function returns `undefined` before the text fallback (`extractChatHistoryBlockText` → `extractCanvasFromText`) can parse the canvas JSON. `run.canvasBlocks` stays empty and `appendChatCanvasBlocksToMessage` attaches nothing.
   - Also, `details` never reaches the CLI at all: the loopback MCP `tools/call` handler returns only `content` and `isError` (`src/gateway/mcp-http.handlers.ts:249`). So on this runtime the text fallback is the only route that could work.

2. **History path: claude-cli transcripts keep tool results inside assistant messages.**
   - `augmentChatHistoryWithCanvasBlocks` (`src/gateway/chat-display-projection.canvas.ts:273`, the `role === "assistant"` branch at `:288`) never extracts previews from assistant messages. It only harvests standalone tool-result messages. The claude-cli history shape is `role: "assistant"` with `toolcall` + `tool_result` blocks, so no preview is ever collected.

3. **"Outcome unknown": a Claude `tool_result` without `is_error` is treated as unknown.**
   - Anthropic only sets `is_error` on a `tool_result` when it is `true`. `readToolErrorFlag` (`src/chat/tool-content.ts`) returns `undefined` when the field is absent. The activity projection in `src/infra/agent-activity-events.ts` (around lines 111-133) then has no status and emits `summary: "Outcome unknown"`. Only the failed call in the same turn (which has `is_error: true`) gets `status: "failed"`. On the embedded runtime the same call is `status: "completed"`.

4. **Native client:** `apps/shared/OpenClawKit/Sources/OpenClawChatUI/ChatMessageViews.swift:698` (`inlineWidgets`) renders only assistant `content` blocks with `type == "canvas"` and a `preview.inlineWidgetPath`. It has no `[embed …]` shortcode handling, so the text-only reply renders no widget.

Suggested fix direction (any one of 1a/1b fixes live delivery; 2 and 3 are needed for reloads and the status row):

- **1a.** Normalize CLI tool results before emitting the tool event. In `execute-events.ts` (or `emitClaudeToolResultBlock`), wrap an array or string `content` as `{ content: [...] }`, the same shape the embedded runtime emits.
- **1b.** Alternatively, make `extractChatToolResultCanvasPreview` accept an array of content blocks (treat it as `{ content: value }`).
- **1c.** Better still for MCP App previews: since the Gateway executes the loopback tool itself (`mcp-http.handlers.ts`, `onToolCallResult` already receives the full result with `details`), bind that result's canvas details to the run. The `details.mcpAppPreview` path would then work on claude-cli too, not only the JSON-text fallback.
- **2.** In `augmentChatHistoryWithCanvasBlocks`, also harvest previews from `tool_result` / `toolResult` blocks inside assistant messages. Attach them to the next renderable assistant message, as is already done for standalone tool messages.
- **3.** For Claude-native `tool_result` blocks, treat a missing `is_error` as `false` (completed) when projecting history activity.
- **Optional.** For connections that advertise `inline-widgets`, the Gateway could convert owned `[embed ref=…]` shortcodes in assistant text into `canvas` blocks, so native clients match the web UI even when no tool-result preview is available.

Related, not a duplicate: #168625 (embedded runtime, `show_widget` through Tool Search loses its widget in `chat.history`; closed, and its PR #168785 was closed unmerged). In my embedded-runtime run `show_widget` was also called through the Tool Search `exec` wrapper. The live final had the canvas block, but `chat.history` again returned the final message without it, so that history gap still seems to reproduce on 2026.11.7.

### Impact and severity

Affected: native clients that render from `canvas` blocks (confirmed on iOS; the Apple apps share `OpenClawChatUI`) for any agent on the claude-cli runtime, which `openclaw onboard` writes for Anthropic Claude CLI sign-in.
Severity: medium. The feature silently does nothing on native clients, and the tool row shows a misleading "Outcome unknown" for a successful call.
Frequency: 100% reproducible.
Consequence: users on Claude CLI cannot see inline widgets on mobile. The web Control UI works only through the model-written shortcode.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Summary

With the Docker sandbox backend pointed at Podman's Docker-compatible API, every existing sandbox breaks after any `podman.service` restart, and `openclaw sandbox recreate` cannot recover it.

### Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.11.6 (06afb10), Gateway in a container, `agents.defaults.sandbox.backend: docker`
- `DOCKER_HOST=unix:///run/podman/podman.sock` (rootful `podman.socket`, socket-activated `podman.service`, which by default exits after 5 s idle)

### Actual behavior

After a `podman.service` restart (idle exit, or a reboot), agent runs fail with:

```
The Docker sandbox belongs to a different daemon; restore its recorded target or explicitly recreate it.
```

`openclaw sandbox list` fails, and `openclaw sandbox recreate --all --force` (offline, with exclusive state ownership) fails with:

```
Original Docker daemon changed; persistent process cleanup is uncertain.
```

### Cause

Each persistent docker target records `daemonId` = `docker info --format {{.ID}}` (`docker-persistent-target-*.mjs`). Podman's compat `/info` returns a fresh random `ID` for every podman process, so the recorded ID goes stale on every restart:

```
$ curl -s --unix-socket /run/podman/podman.sock http://d/info | jq -r .ID   # call 1
$ sleep 10
$ curl -s --unix-socket /run/podman/podman.sock http://d/info | jq -r .ID   # different value
```

`assertDockerPersistentTargetCurrent` runs before `recreate` can clean up, so there is no supported way to recover short of making the daemon report the old ID.

### Expected behavior

Sandboxes survive a Podman service restart, or `recreate --force` can drop records whose daemon changed.

### Suggestions

- Treat Podman's compat `ID` as unstable (detect Podman via `/version` `Components`), or derive daemon identity from something stable.
- Or let `sandbox recreate --force` (or a `--forget-daemon` flag) drop records whose daemon changed, with a warning that cleanup on the old daemon is uncertain.

Related but distinct: #180311 (daemon selection order). The native Podman backend may not have this pin; we have not verified that in a containerized Gateway.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Bug (not a beta release blocker)

### Summary

`openclaw backup create --to local-archive` can never complete on an instance with a large session directory. After ~10 minutes of work it fails with:

```
Backup archive write failed: Backup manifest exceeds 1048576 byte limit. (after 1 attempt)
```

The manifest is capped at 1 MiB, but a long-running install has tens of thousands of files under `agents/main/sessions` (`*.jsonl` + `*.trajectory.jsonl` per session), so the manifest alone exceeds the cap and the whole backup is discarded. There is no include/exclude flag and no way to raise the manifest limit.

### Environment

- OpenClaw: 2026.11.5 (e13cf15)
- Node: v24.22.1
- OS: Linux 5.14 (RHEL 9)
- Storage location: `local-archive`
- `agents/main/sessions`: 19,152 files / 2.7 GB
- `~/.openclaw` total: 17 GB
- Command: `openclaw backup create --to local-archive --namespace ai-agent --keep-daily 7`

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run an OpenClaw instance long enough that `agents/main/sessions` holds ~19k files.
2. Run `openclaw backup create --to local-archive --namespace ai-agent --keep-daily 7`.
3. Wait ~10 minutes.
4. Observe `Backup archive write failed: Backup manifest exceeds 1048576 byte limit. (after 1 attempt)`, exit code 1.

### Expected behavior

- The backup completes and produces a restorable archive, and/or
- the manifest limit scales with payload size (or is configurable), and/or
- `backup create` accepts include/exclude globs so large transcript trees can be handled separately.

### Actual behavior

- Scratch dir left behind (e.g. `/tmp/openclaw-backup-owned-IEJa6f`, 333 MB) containing `state-snapshot-attempt-1/.sqlite-snapshot-*/` with a leftover `database.sqlite.partial`.
- Archive never written; the storage location only contains `openclaw-storage.json` and `backups/<namespace>/owner.json`.
- As a scheduled automation the job reports `lastRunStatus: error`, `lastRunError: "command timed out"`; the manifest error only surfaces on a manual run with a longer timeout.

### Impact

Scheduled backups silently produce nothing, and retention has nothing to prune. Users believe they have backups but have none.

### Workaround

Self-managed pipeline: `sqlite3 .backup` for the three SQLite stores + `tar --zstd` of `~/.openclaw` with the transcript/backup/cache dirs excluded. Happy to test a fix against the 19k-file case.

issues.body:
## Summary

On OpenClaw 2026.11.6 (build `06afb10d`), a large locally loaded TypeScript plugin intermittently fails to load at Gateway startup or during `plugins.reload` with:

```
[plugins] memory-lancedb-pro failed during load from <state-dir>/plugins/memory-lancedb-pro/index.ts: Error: Plugin preparation callback timed out
```

The message comes from a hard-coded 15,000 ms deadline in the preparation worker's host-callback loop (`performance.now() + 15e3` in `dist/plugins/plugin-generation-preparation.worker.js`). While the plugin is being prepared, the Gateway main thread is blocked for just over 15 s in the synchronous module-load / `require` path. The worker's callback deadline expires, the load is aborted, and the plugin never reaches `register()`. Loading the same unmodified plugin again — via a later reload or a Gateway restart — usually succeeds.

There is no automatic retry, no failure event, and no `readyz` degradation signal. Once an initial load fails, the plugin remains unregistered until an operator intervenes.

Reproduced on two independent macOS arm64 hosts in different locations, with the same OpenClaw version and plugin. All counts and tables below are from one host.

## Environment

- OpenClaw **2026.11.6**, build `06afb10d3272cc9deaf38ca6a3b7b839d5935638`
- Gateway runtime: Node **26.12.1** (macOS arm64, Darwin 27.2.0)
- The same error also occurs in separate non-Gateway processes on Node **26.5.0**
- Plugin: `memory-lancedb-pro@1.1.0-beta.10`, loaded through `plugins.load.paths`
  - TypeScript entry `index.ts` (~4,100 lines); top-level imports include `@lancedb/lancedb` (native addon), `apache-arrow`, `openai`
  - Local LanceDB directory ~155 MB; embeddings from local Ollama `qwen3-embedding:4b`
- Intermittent: the same plugin and config sometimes load normally and sometimes time out, with no changes in between.

## What happens

A failing `plugins.reload` takes 47.3–47.8 s and contains **exactly two 15 s prepare attempts**:

| Reload start (+08) | Total | Preload segments | Prepare attempt 1 | Timeout #1 at | Prepare attempt 2 | Timeout #2 at |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 11-22 09:55:55.705 | 47.664 s | 1.050 s + 4.859 s | 15.123 s | +28.181 s | 15.133 s | +46.082 s |
| 11-22 09:56:54.326 | 47.430 s | 4.847 s | 15.138 s | +28.029 s | 15.112 s | +45.938 s |
| 11-22 09:57:46.694 | 47.330 s | 1.941 s + 4.833 s | 15.109 s | +27.971 s | 15.119 s | +45.849 s |
| 11-22 10:02:59.340 | 47.791 s | 4.872 s + 4.892 s | 15.167 s | +28.238 s | 15.127 s | +46.210 s |
| 11-22 10:05:12.496 | 47.812 s | 4.901 s + 4.842 s | 15.208 s | +28.184 s | 15.126 s | +46.308 s |
| 11-23 07:07:29.501 | 47.703 s | 4.918 s + 4.818 s | 15.217 s | +28.214 s | 15.123 s | +46.118 s |

In every row, each 15.x s block is a **main-thread stall** reported by the Gateway's own stall profiler, ending 0.3–0.5 s before the corresponding timeout log line. Thirteen such stalls were measured in total: **15.109–15.218 s**.

Representative inclusive stacks (leaf → caller):

| Segment | Frames |
|---|---|
| preload / artifact | `createPluginGenerationArtifact → capturePluginGenerationArtifact → bindPluginInstanceModuleLoader` |
| prepare attempt 1 | `enterAsyncStore → runWithAsyncStore → runFrame → withPluginRuntimePluginScope → enter@plugin-setup-module` |
| prepare attempt 2 | `nextStep@node:internal/modules/customization_hooks → cjs loader → wrapModuleLoad → require@node:internal/modules/helpers → plugin-setup-module` |
| other failures | `join@plugin-generation-worker → requestSync → GenerationCodec.exportRoot → result → sourceForOutput` |

## Where the 15 s goes

`dist/plugins/plugin-generation-preparation.worker.js` in 2026.11.6:

```js
function requestHost(t) {
  ...
  const a = performance.now() + 15e3;
  for (;;) {
    const e = receiveMessageOnPort(u)?.message;
    if (e?.kind === `callback-result` && e.id === n) { ... return e; }
    if (performance.now() > a) throw Error(`Plugin preparation callback timed out`);
    Atomics.wait(r, 0, 0, 2);
  }
}
```

The host services this port by polling (`receiveMessageOnPort(h)` in `plugin-generation-worker-*.mjs`, via `service()`), which runs on the Gateway main thread. While that thread is inside a synchronous `require()` chain it cannot answer the worker, and the worker gives up at exactly 15 s. The same synchronous worker proxy is the subject of the open regression #174681 (`requestSync` blocking the main thread).

The host's own startup trace for the failing load agrees:

```
startup trace: plugins.gateway-load.plugin.memory-lancedb-pro
  configValidationMs=0.3 artifactPreparationMs=0.3
  loadMs=17475.6 modulePreparationMs=2184.2
  loadFailedCount=1.0 workersStarted=1
  workerScripts=plugin-generation-preparation.worker.js:1
```

`modulePreparationMs` accounts for 2.18 s; the load aborts at 17.5 s, with the remainder dominated by the 15 s callback deadline.

**This is not LanceDB open, embedding initialization, disk I/O, or a plugin error.** All stall samples are inside the host's module loader / `require` frames; no `lancedb`, `ollama`, or embedding frames appear. The plugin opens its database and embedding path successfully on the next attempt with no changes. Operator-side checks also excluded page cache (data directory fully warm), embedding latency (0.06 s), lock holders (none), and the patched vs stock plugin version (both fail).

## Evidence: retry succeeds unchanged, but nothing retries automatically

- 11-22 09:56:23.886 → timeout #1; 09:56:41.787 → timeout #2 → `plugins.reload` fails after 47.664 s.
- 11-22 10:17:19.806 / 10:17:54.168 / 10:18:26.189 → three more timeouts during startup/retry.
- 11-22 10:18:37.937 → `memory-lancedb-pro@1.1.0-beta.10: plugin registered (db: <state-dir>/memory/lancedb-pro, model: qwen3-embedding:4b, smartExtraction: ON)` — same binary, config, and data.
- 11-22 12:30:02.952 → `plugin registered` again without touching the plugin.
- After the 04:16:59 failure there is no successful registration line until 10:18 (about 6 hours). On the second host the operator reports the plugin was unloaded for two days until a Gateway restart.
- During the failed startup, `http server listening (14 plugins: ...)` lists the other plugins but not this one; the failed plugin is simply absent.
- No log line shows a retry after the failure; every recovery corresponds to an operator-triggered reload or restart.

## Frequency (one host, 2026-11-22 00:00 → 2026-11-23 12:00, +08)

- 26 Gateway-side prepare timeouts; 12 of them belong to the six failed reloads above (two per reload). The rest are startup or reload attempts outside those sessions.
- 28 timeouts logged by separate Node 26.5.0 processes, in six bursts (one burst of eight, the others of four), 31–38 s apart.
- The second host reproduces the same error; the hosts share no code, data, or configuration.

## Related

- #174681 — open regression: plugin preparation blocks the Gateway main thread (sync worker proxy). This is likely the underlying defect; the symptom here is the hard-coded 15 s callback deadline firing on top of it.
- #202210 — closed as "not a host timeout"; in that report the plugin had a bad internal import and the timeout message was a misleading side effect. Here the identical plugin loads successfully seconds later, so this is not an import or packaging error. The hard-coded 15 s cap is still present in 2026.11.6 and has no plugin-facing config override.

## Requests

1. **Automatic retry on preparation timeout.** Retry the failed plugin with exponential backoff (for example 30 s / 2 min / 5 min, three attempts), so a transient main-thread stall does not leave the plugin unregistered for hours.
2. **Make the preparation callback deadline configurable.** For example `plugins.preparationTimeoutMs` or `OPENCLAW_PLUGIN_PREPARATION_TIMEOUT_MS`, with an optional per-plugin override, and log the actual wait duration and the callback phase on timeout.
3. **Surface the failure.** Emit a subscribable event and reflect degraded plugin state in `readyz` / status, so supervisors can alert or self-heal instead of waiting for a human to notice a missing plugin.

## Raw log lines (paths abbreviated)

```
2026-11-22T09:56:23.886+08:00 ERROR [plugins] memory-lancedb-pro failed during load from <state-dir>/plugins/memory-lancedb-pro/index.ts: Error: Plugin preparation callback timed out
2026-11-22T09:56:23.896+08:00 WARN  main-thread stall: elapsedMs=15123 task=unattributed stallStartMs=1795312568374 stallEndMs=1795312583497
2026-11-22T09:56:41.787+08:00 ERROR [plugins] memory-lancedb-pro failed during load from <state-dir>/plugins/memory-lancedb-pro/index.ts: Error: Plugin preparation callback timed out
2026-11-22T09:56:41.794+08:00 WARN  main-thread stall: elapsedMs=15133 task=unattributed stallStartMs=1795312586262 stallEndMs=1795312601395
2026-11-22T10:18:37.937+08:00 INFO  memory-lancedb-pro@1.1.0-beta.10: plugin registered (db: <state-dir>/memory/lancedb-pro, model: qwen3-embedding:4b, smartExtraction: ON)
```

issues.body:
## Environment

- openclaw: **2026.11.1** (installed via npm, `dist/index.js`)
- node: v24.22.1
- OS: Ubuntu 24.04, kernel 7.0.0-29-generic
- Runtime: systemd user unit `openclaw-gateway.service` (persistent gateway)
- Load profile: 1 Feishu channel (WebSocket), 13 cron jobs, skills watcher
- Machine: 7.6 GB RAM total (shared with two other gateways)

## Symptoms

The main gateway process (`node .../openclaw/dist/index.js`) grows steadily after startup:

| Metric | Value | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Uptime at sampling | **17h 23m** | single process lifetime, no restart |
| VmRSS | **1,910 MB** | |
| cgroup `anon` | **1,854 MB** | true heap (file cache only 597 MB) |
| cgroup `MemoryPeak` | **3,063 MB** | reached within the window |
| VmSwap | **848 MB** | kernel started swapping it out under pressure |
| cgroup `MemoryCurrent` | 5,921 MB | anon + file + kernel of the whole unit |
| 60s RSS delta | **+0.89 MB** | flat at plateau (swap-throttled) |

Growth pattern: ~**110 MB/h** from startup until plateau around ~1.9–3.0 GB, then flat
(the process has been pushed into swap by the 7.6 GB host, so RSS understates true heap).
The pattern **reproduces across restarts**: a previous incarnation (v2026.11.1, restarted
2026-11-05) peaked at **3.2 GB** before being recycled — so it is a deterministic
accumulate-to-plateau behavior, not a one-off.

## What was ruled out

- **SQLite state DB is small**: `~/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite` = **33 MB**
  (plus migration .bak files) — DB page cache cannot explain 1.85 GB anon.
- **Log files**: `~/.openclaw/logs` = 2.6 MB.
- Steady-state idle growth is not visible in short windows (60 s ≈ +0.9 MB);
  the growth happens over hours, suggesting long-lived accumulated structures
  (sessions / timers / listeners / WebSocket state) rather than a hot loop.

## Correlated observations

- 61 "slow SQLite query" warnings in logs over the same period (host is CPU/RAM
  constrained, but queries taking seconds point at growing in-process state).
- Feishu WebSocket reconnects cleanly after restart; memory resets to ~150 MB
  at startup (restart is the only mitigation found).

## Reproduction

1. Start `openclaw-gateway.service` on a small host (7.6 GB) with a Feishu channel
   and ~13 cron jobs.
2. Sample `ps -o rss= -p <main PID>` / `cat /sys/fs/cgroup/<unit>/memory.stat`
   every hour.
3. Observe `anon` climbing ~100 MB/h until ~1.9–3 GB, `MemoryPeak` ≈ 3 GB,
   swap usage appearing, then plateau.

## Expected behavior

Gateway anon memory should stabilize (a few hundred MB for this workload) instead
of accumulating ~3 GB per day-cycle. If growth is expected (e.g., session cache),
please document a tuning knob (cap/TTL) — currently there is none visible.

## Suggested investigation areas

- Session/conversation objects retained after sessions close (LRU/TTL missing?)
- WebSocket reconnect state from the Lark/Feishu channel accumulating
- Timers/listeners registered per cron tick (13 jobs) never released
- `v8.getHeapStatistics()` snapshot after N hours to identify the retaining set
  (heap snapshot on demand would help: `kill -USR2 <pid>` if supported)

---
Environment note: submitted by an assistant operator; `gh` CLI token expired at
filing time, so this may be pasted manually.

issues.body:
## Repeated plugin capability resolution during WebSocket reconnects

Filed by Nexus, an AI assistant, on behalf of the operator. Evidence reference: Inspector's November 22 diagnostic reports; this filing does not claim an independent profiler reproduction.

### Reported observations

Inspector reports an approximately 44% gateway idle CPU floor, repeated capability-resolution bursts spanning roughly 39 plugins, and a roughly 10-second WebSocket reconnect loop. The suspected mechanism is repeated uncached capability-provider resolution. The CPU attribution needs profiling/ablation; these observations alone do not establish that the resolver accounts for the entire CPU floor.

A related trigger is a native macOS client rejecting an oversized `agents.list` response: gateway logs reviewed by Inspector showed responses of 18,314,039–18,317,549 bytes; a separate source review reported a 16 MiB native receive limit. This can perpetuate reconnects. Payload composition is not established by those byte counts.

### Request

Please audit whether repeated capability queries on unchanged plugin/config state reuse a generation-scoped registry/cache, including negative lookups and concurrent-request coalescing. Invalidate on relevant plugin/config/permission changes; retain account and capability scope boundaries rather than sharing results across incompatible contexts.

Suggested regression coverage: repeated reconnect/catalog requests should not rerun plugin discovery/registration for every unchanged capability query; config/plugin changes should invalidate; cached failures should not persist indefinitely; distinct account/permission contexts should remain isolated. Compare resolver invocations and CPU with and without reconnect churn.

### Related upstream work

Closed issue [#73793](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/73793) describes an older explicit-plugin-config cache bypass. This report may be a recurrence or another path; the older source location is not asserted to be current. Open issue [#192736](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/192736) covers native roster inflation through inline avatars, a plausible related payload mechanism rather than a proven explanation of this deployment's frame.

issues.body:
### Summary

On OpenClaw 2026.11.6 (06afb10) on macOS 12.7.6 (x64, Node 24.22.2), dashboard / MCP Apps widgets never finish loading. The sandbox iframe completes the *proxy* handshake but never receives the resource-loaded signal, so the client times out and reloads the iframe in a loop. From the user's side this looks like the agent panel is "frozen".

### Environment

- OpenClaw: `2026.11.6 (06afb10)` (CLI and Gateway report the same build)
- Gateway: LaunchAgent `ai.openclaw.gateway`, `--port 18789`, bind loopback
- Sandbox listener observed on `127.0.0.1:18790`
- OS: macOS 12.7.6 (x64), Node v24.22.2
- Control UI opened at `http://127.0.0.1:18789/`

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open the Control UI dashboard.
2. Render any widget/app in the dashboard panel (a plain-text widget reproduces it just as well as a complex one).
3. Watch the widget iframe in DevTools (Console + Network).

### Observed

1. `GET /mcp-app-sandbox?csp=default` returns **400** `invalid MCP App sandbox policy` — a request without the client-generated CSP payload is rejected.
2. The same route with the full client-generated `csp` parameter (base64url JSON containing `resourceDomains`, `mediaDomains`, `blockDescendantFrames`) returns **200** with correct CSP response headers and the expected `<!doctype html>` proxy document (~20 KB, ~24 ms). So routing, CSP decoding and proxy document generation all work.
3. Inside the iframe, `ui/notifications/sandbox-proxy-ready` **does** reach the parent (origin and `sandboxUrlMatch` verified true).
4. `sandbox-resource-loaded` **never arrives** — observed for 60+ seconds.
5. The client then resets the iframe; Network shows `net::ERR_ABORTED` for the sandbox document, and the cycle repeats.

### Ruled out

- **Network / CDN reachability:** `cdn.jsdelivr.net` 200, `esm.sh/react` 200, `unpkg.com` 302, `fonts.googleapis.com` 200 from the same host.
- **Widget content:** a trivial plain-text widget fails identically, so this is not a user widget bug.
- **Server-side sandbox document:** step 2 above returns a valid document quickly.

### Hypothesis

The parent-side handshake stops after `sandbox-proxy-ready`: either the resource load is never requested from the sandbox origin, or its completion notification is dropped. The client then treats the missing `sandbox-resource-loaded` as a timeout and reloads the iframe, producing the `ERR_ABORTED` loop.

### Impact

Every MCP Apps widget / dashboard app is unusable. Because the failure is silent in the UI (only a console `ERR_ABORTED`), a user who asked an agent to "show a dashboard" experiences it as the agent hanging, and may interrupt a run that was otherwise healthy.

### Asks

- Emit a user-visible error when the resource-load handshake times out, instead of reloading silently.
- Add a bounded retry (or surface the failing stage) so the failure is diagnosable from the UI.

issues.body:
## Summary

On slow or high-latency connections, the iOS **New Thread** agent picker can take a very long time to load, or never load at all. The roster request carries every configured agent avatar as an inline base64 data URL. Browser clients avoid this because they get authenticated `/avatar/<agent>` resource URLs instead.

## Current behavior

- `agents.list` (`src/gateway/server-methods/agents.ts`) passes `httpAvatarBasePath` only when the client is `CONTROL_UI`. For every other client, `listAgentsForGateway` resolves local avatar files through `resolveAgentAvatarUrlFromSource` (`src/agents/identity-avatar-file.ts`), which returns `data:<mime>;base64,<file>` in `identity.avatarUrl`.
- `agent.identity.get` (`src/gateway/server-methods/agent-identity.ts`) follows the same rule. `resolveGatewayAssistantAvatar` documents it: "Browser clients use authenticated images; native/CLI RPC retains inline avatars."
- The shared native catalog loader (`OpenClawChatAgentsListResponse.load` in `apps/shared/OpenClawKit/Sources/OpenClawChatUI/ChatAgentCatalog.swift`) shows nothing until the full `agents.list` response decodes. It then sends one `agent.identity.get` per agent, and each of those inlines the same avatar again.
- The catalog refreshes every time the picker opens.

Local avatars can be up to 2 MiB each (`AVATAR_MAX_BYTES`), before roughly 33% base64 overhead. With several agents using full-resolution portraits, the roster becomes a multi-megabyte frame that blocks the picker, and the same bytes are downloaded a second time through the identity requests.

## Expected behavior

The roster should load in a few kilobytes, whatever the avatar sizes. Portraits should load separately and be cacheable.

## Proposed fix

The native apps can already load authenticated same-origin avatar routes: `OpenClawSidebarAgentAvatarSource.resourceURL` accepts canonical `/avatar/<agent>` paths. Suggested changes:

1. Return the revisioned `/avatar/<agent>?v=<revision>` resource path to native operator clients that support it (capability-gated if needed), in `agents.list` and `agent.identity.get`, rather than limiting that to `CONTROL_UI`.
2. Keep inline data URLs for clients that can't load HTTP resources, such as CLI or older apps.
3. Let native clients cache avatars by revision, so reopening the picker doesn't download them again.

## Related

- #186812 adds an opt-in `includeAvatars: false` to `agents.list`. It removes the bulk from the roster, but clients then lose portraits unless something else fetches them, and the iOS app would need a matching change to send the flag. Resource URLs would keep portraits and shrink the payload for every native client by default.

### Summary

A managed npm upgrade from 2026.11.1 to 2026.11.3 activated the new core, then post-install Doctor failed with `SQLite WAL commit publication could not be verified`. The updater refused rollback as `state-migrated-no-rollback`, recovered a serving 11.3 Gateway, but left external plugin convergence unfinished. Offline `update repair` subsequently completed.

### Environment

- Debian GNU/Linux 13 (trixie), Linux/x64
- Managed Node 24.22.1
- npm package installation, systemd user Gateway, existing operator service overrides preserved
- Target/serving version: 2026.11.3, commit `847611d`
- Source 2026.11.1 had a local header-probe deadline workaround for the already-fixed large-tree timeout. The target retained that override for recovery but replayed **zero** local overrides. Target dist inspection during repair reported no content mismatches or extra paths.

### Observed sequence

1. Candidate snapshot, Doctor/lint/config/plugin/startup checks passed.
2. The old Gateway was stopped and 11.3 was installed.
3. Post-install Doctor failed. Bounded diagnostic:

```text
SQLite read-only worker SQLite WAL commit publication could not be verified:
$OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR/state/openclaw.sqlite
```

   Immediately preceding diagnostics reported two slow `update.run` transactions in the Doctor process: about 1650 ms on the main thread, then about 1653 ms on worker thread 4.
4. Run outcome: `state-migrated-no-rollback`. The protected rollback refusal preserved changed state; the native recovery started the 11.3 Gateway and verified readiness.
5. External official plugins remained on 11.1 until repair.

This is one observed production occurrence, **not a deterministic reproduction**. Read-only diagnostic observers had been used during the original update. A connection/SHM or write-publication interaction is a hypothesis, not an established cause; the second logged transaction could also be failure bookkeeping.

### Recovery evidence

After stopping the Gateway through its existing service owner, with no concurrent OpenClaw CLI/direct SQLite observers:

```sh
OPENCLAW_SERVICE_REPAIR_POLICY=external openclaw update repair --yes --json
```

Exit 0, final status `warning`; all finalization phases completed:
- Doctor ~229 s
- plugin convergence ~94 s
- final configuration/Doctor convergence ~290 s
- seven official external plugins updated from 11.1 to 11.3
- post-plugin error-level Doctor lint: exit 0, no findings

The same user service was started afterward: authenticated read RPC reports 11.3, `readyz` reports `ready:true`, `coreReady:true`, no failing components; plugin version drift is empty. Existing recovery artifacts were retained. No database restore, manual state edits, lease deletion, or guard bypass was used.

### Expected behavior / investigation request

The updater should finish its own post-install Doctor without losing its stable WAL-publication witness, or safely converge/recover with actionable diagnostics. Please distinguish which witness predicate failed (generation changed, WAL-index header copies differed, or nonempty WAL had no initialized index) without exposing private state.

The installed implementation checks this in `update-doctor-migration-attribution` / `update-physical-database-generations`. The current message does not identify the predicate, so this report does **not** establish database corruption or justify relaxing the consistency guard.

### Scope

This failure occurred after header probing passed. It is separate from the configurable header deadline proposal #197079 and the previously fixed all-path 10-second timeout. No current-main acceptance test or targeted code fix for this WAL failure has been produced.

Private paths, database contents, credentials, recording contents, and internal session identifiers are omitted.

issues.body:
## Summary

A built-in Goal with an explicit token budget should stop scheduling ordinary work while it can still deliver one useful partial-result status.

## Problem to solve

Correcting the Goal's usage counter does not decide what to do near a cap. The current continuation check admits another ordinary turn while the accounted Goal is active; once it becomes budget_limited, there is no dedicated reserve in that check. A user can get a terminal budget state without a clear account of what finished and what remains. This is separate from the accounting defect in #203350.

## Proposed solution

After #203350 is resolved, use the existing Goal continuation owner to reserve modest headroom for an explicit per-Goal budget. On the transition into reserve, stop admitting normal Goal work and deliver one short, visible handoff: completed output or references, what remains if known, token usage, and stop reason. A deterministic message from existing state is sufficient; no extra model call is required. Preserve Stop, ordinary chats, and explicit resume behavior. No global spend contract or child propagation.

**Acceptance:** In an isolated built-in Goal with a 100,000-token cap and a 15,000-token fixture reserve, settled usage of 45,000 allows the next ordinary turn. At 90,000, no third ordinary turn starts, and the user sees exactly one partial handoff. Duplicate settlement or restart does not publish it again. Unbudgeted Goals are unchanged.

## Alternatives considered

Stop only at the cap: no planned handoff. Prompt the model to remember to wrap up: it cannot enforce scheduler admission. Add a global budget hook: broader than this user-facing Goal transition.

## Impact

People running long, explicitly budgeted Goals retain useful partial work and know whether to extend the budget. Reserving room can stop marginally earlier even if another small task might have fit. This is an opt-in Goal behavior, not a new universal default.

## Evidence/examples

At [3f3a4b0c03b330d61b9b17d489dc2909ac572370](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/3f3a4b0c03b330d61b9b17d489dc2909ac572370), injecting accounted threshold values into OpenClaw's [Goal accounting](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/3f3a4b0c03b330d61b9b17d489dc2909ac572370/src/config/sessions/goals-transitions.ts#L26-L64) and [continuation check](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/3f3a4b0c03b330d61b9b17d489dc2909ac572370/src/auto-reply/reply/goal-continuation.ts#L78-L94) gave next-turn eligibility **yes / yes / no** at **79,999 / 80,000 / 100,000**. Under the same threshold fixture, ARTEX's [ledger](https://github.com/BaaRai/ARTEX/blob/5bed53b6ae9bf3b29e29988f43e42d5ce3870587/agent/budget.go#L130-L171) gave **yes / no / no** and signaled wrap-up exactly once. Fixture outputs are below. This demonstrates control behavior, not delivery of a real handoff. The two OpenClaw files matched upstream main at [3fd1657e7d72](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/3fd1657e7d7249a2d0701f84d4eba63f9c4b00be). Rechecked 2026-11-21: the named source files are unchanged on main at e201b64f8d7.

## Do you plan to open a PR for this?

No, proposing the idea only.

## Additional information

File as an enhancement contingent on correct settled accounting, not as a repeat of the undercount bug. Related: [#179292](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/179292) is a broader per-surface cost policy. [#202270](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/202270) is an uncapped Discord continuation loop; this request applies only to explicitly budgeted Goals.

issues.body:
## Summary

`openclaw gateway restart` reports a hard failure on restarts that actually succeed, and **exits 0 while doing so**. The readiness budget it enforces is hardcoded to 60 s, which is shorter than a real cold start of this gateway, so the CLI times out on a service that comes up healthy a minute later.

There is no flag to raise the budget: `--wait` controls the delay *before* restarting, not the post-restart readiness timeout.

## Version / platform

- OpenClaw 2026.9.6 (eb377ac, npm latest)
- macOS 26 / arm64, Node 26.8.1
- LaunchAgent-managed gateway (`gui/501/ai.openclaw.gateway`), `--max-old-space-size=6144`
- Config `/Users/jiang/.openclaw/openclaw.json`, bind loopback, port 18789

## The budget

`gateway-shutdown-budget.mjs`:

```js
// Shared stop policy; v2026.9.5 restart-health.constants.ts fixes the replacement window.
export const GATEWAY_RESTART_REPLACEMENT_TIMEOUT_MS = 60_000;
export const GATEWAY_SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_MS = 315_000;
```

and `dist/restart-health.constants-*.mjs` derives the probe budget directly from it:

```js
const DEFAULT_RESTART_HEALTH_TIMEOUT_MS = GATEWAY_RESTART_REPLACEMENT_TIMEOUT_MS;   // 60_000
const DEFAULT_RESTART_HEALTH_ATTEMPTS = Math.ceil(DEFAULT_RESTART_HEALTH_TIMEOUT_MS / 500);
```

So the health budget is the shutdown budget constant, reused verbatim. 60 s is not configurable from the CLI — `gateway restart --help` exposes only `--force`, `--json`, `--preserve-definition`, `--safe`, `--skip-deferral`, `--wait`, and none of them adjust the readiness timeout.

## Reproduction

Observed cold starts of this gateway (measured by polling `/healthz` + `/readyz` every 5 s from a separate shell):

| Run | Elapsed to `healthz=200` **and** `readyz=200` |
|---|---|
| 1 | 70 s |
| 2 | 75 s |
| 3 | 75 s |
| 4 | 200 s |

Every one of these is a successful start. The 200 s run is presumably a slow catalog/plugin warm-up, but the point is that the spread is wide and unbounded from below the user's perspective — a fixed 60 s budget will miss part of the distribution.

Actual `openclaw gateway restart` output from the run above:

```
Restarted LaunchAgent: gui/501/ai.openclaw.gateway
Timed out after 98s waiting for gateway port 18789 to become healthy.
Readiness budget exhausted after 98s. Last observed startup phase: waiting for Gateway health and identity.
Service runtime: status=running, state=active, pid=65913
Port 18789 is already in use.
- pid 65913 jiang: /opt/homebrew/opt/node/bin/node --max-old-space-size=6144 ... (127.0.0.1:18789)
Gateway probe failed: gateway timeout after 3000ms
Gateway target: ws://127.0.0.1:18789
Gateway restart timed out after 98s waiting for health checks.
Tip: openclaw gateway status --deep
Tip: openclaw doctor
```

Total wall time: 121 s. The service came up and served requests normally immediately afterwards (`healthz=200`, `readyz=200`, and the log shows successful `ws` traffic on the same pid 65913).

Two separate problems are visible in that output:

**1. The false failure.** The service was `status=running, state=active, pid=65913` and the port was bound by *the new process*, yet the CLI still concluded "timed out". The health probe that failed was a 3 s `ws` connect attempt, which is a much stricter criterion than the service being up.

**2. `exit 0` on failure.** The command printed a timeout error and a stack of "Tip:" lines, then **exited 0**. Any wrapper script or automation that checks the exit status will treat a failed restart as a success. This is the more dangerous half of the bug — it is what let a nightly restart silently do nothing for 8 hours on my host before I noticed.

## Suggested fixes

- Exit non-zero when the readiness budget is exhausted, regardless of the underlying service state
- Either raise `GATEWAY_RESTART_REPLACEMENT_TIMEOUT_MS`, or derive it from `GATEWAY_SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_MS` (315 s) the way the drain budget already is, or expose a `--health-timeout <ms>` flag
- Distinguish "service is not running" from "service is running but slow to become ready" — the latter should not be reported as a restart failure, and the `Port 18789 is already in use` line is misleading here, since the process holding the port *is* the replacement

## Workaround

Drive `launchd` directly (`launchctl bootout gui/501/ai.openclaw.gateway` + `launchctl bootstrap gui/501 <plist>`) and poll readiness yourself with a larger budget. Note that `bootout` is asynchronous — bootstrapping immediately afterwards fails with `Bootstrap failed: 5: Input/output error`, so the replacement needs a wait-and-retry loop. That part works reliably and is what I use for a scheduled daily restart.
