issues.body: ### Bug type Behavior bug ### Summary When the Gateway runs inside WSL2 and an attach-only browser profile points at Chrome running on the Windows host (CDP over `127.0.0.1`), every download is canceled and the browser tool returns `download.saveAs: canceled`. Chrome receives the whole file, then cancels it, because the `downloadPath` it is given is a Linux path. ### Cause `connectOverCdpTransport` calls `chromium.connectOverCDP(transport, { timeout })` with no `artifactsDir`. Playwright then creates `os.tmpdir()/playwright-artifacts-XXXXXX` (a Linux path such as `/tmp/playwright-artifacts-abc123`) and sends the browser `Browser.setDownloadBehavior({ behavior: "allowAndName", downloadPath: "/tmp/playwright-artifacts-abc123", eventsEnabled: true })`. Windows Chrome cannot write to a POSIX path, so the download ends in state `canceled`. `/json/version` on that Chrome reports `"File-Path-Style": "windows"`. No config key changes this path today (`downloadDir` only applies to browsers OpenClaw launches itself). ### Steps to reproduce 1. WSL2 (Ubuntu), Gateway running in WSL. Chrome on the Windows host started with `--remote-debugging-port=9222`. 2. Profile: `{ "cdpUrl": "http://127.0.0.1:9222", "attachOnly": true }`. 3. `openclaw browser --browser-profile navigate 'https://httpbin.org/response-headers?Content-Disposition=attachment%3B%20filename%3Dtest.txt'` (or `download` / `waitfordownload` on a link to that URL). 4. Result: `Error: download.saveAs: canceled` after a few seconds. Nothing is saved. Minimal Playwright-only repro (no OpenClaw), run in WSL against the Windows Chrome: ```js // repro.mjs import { chromium } from "playwright-core"; const browser = await chromium.connectOverCDP("http://127.0.0.1:9222"); const page = await browser.contexts()[0].newPage(); await page.setContent('dl'); const [dl] = await Promise.all([page.waitForEvent("download"), page.click("#a")]); await dl.saveAs("/tmp/test.txt"); // throws: canceled ``` ### What Chrome accepts (same file, only `downloadPath` changed) | `downloadPath` sent | result | |---|---| | `/tmp/playwright-artifacts-test` (what Playwright sends) | file received, then `canceled` | | `/mnt/c/...` (WSL mount form) | `canceled` | | `C:/...` (forward slashes) | `canceled` | | `C:\...` | `completed` | | `\\wsl.localhost\\tmp\...` (`wslpath -w` of a Linux folder) | `completed`, the file lands in the Linux folder | The last row is the fix: Chrome writes to the Windows (UNC) form of a folder and Playwright reads the same folder through its Linux form. ### Fix that works locally In `connectOverCdpTransport`, pass a fixed `artifactsDir` (for example `/pw-artifacts`) to `connectOverCDP`, and when the Gateway runs in WSL (`os.release()` contains `microsoft`; note `WSL_DISTRO_NAME` is usually absent under systemd) and `Browser.getVersion().userAgent` contains `Windows`, re-send `Browser.setDownloadBehavior({ behavior: "allowAndName", downloadPath: , eventsEnabled: true })` from a browser CDP session that stays attached (Chrome resets a session's download behavior when that session detaches). With that, the httpbin download above completes in about 200 ms and `saveAs` copies a correct file. Related, different cause: #157547 (attach-only download path is overridden), #185713 (artifacts dir for a browser under another Unix user). A configurable or translated `artifactsDir` would cover all three. ### Second, smaller symptom in the same setup `screenshot` through the Playwright path times out (`Screenshot via Playwright timed out after 20000ms`) when the target tab is a background tab: Chrome does not paint a hidden tab, so the capture waits for a frame. The raw-CDP screenshot path already calls `Page.bringToFront` first; `runScreenshotOperation` does not. Calling `page.bringToFront()` before the capture fixed it locally (about 4 s instead of a timeout). ### OpenClaw version 2026.11.3 (bundled playwright-core 1.63.0), Chrome 157 on Windows 11, WSL2 kernel 6.x. ### Operating system Windows 11 host, Gateway in WSL2 Ubuntu.

issues.body:
### Summary

An authenticated Slack command owner replying in a bot-created task thread is admitted as a normal sender, but a privileged OpenClaw delegation rejects the turn as not owner-started. This blocks supported plugin/bootstrap operations even though the exact Slack sender is present in `commands.ownerAllowFrom`.

### Reproduction

1. Configure the Slack sender in `commands.ownerAllowFrom`.
2. Have the agent create a top-level Slack task/approval message.
3. The configured owner replies in that thread with an explicit approval/request.
4. From that exact turn, invoke an owner-gated OpenClaw setup/delegation action.
5. The action rejects with: `openclaw needs the owner's authority, and this turn was not started by the owner.`

Read-back confirms the sender is in `commands.ownerAllowFrom`. Repeating from the owner's reply does not help because authority appears tied to the session/thread opener rather than the current authenticated inbound sender.

### Expected

Owner authority should be derived and rechecked from the current authenticated inbound message (or a scoped one-use owner grant), not from who authored the thread root. A configured owner reply in a bot-created task thread should be able to perform the same owner-only action as an owner-created root, with scope and liveness rechecked at commit.

### Actual impact

- Bot-created approval threads cannot complete privileged operations.
- Teams using "title in root, body/approval in replies" are forced to create a new owner-authored root.
- This conflicts with the documented per-message `senderIsOwner` model and encourages unsafe shell/inter-session workarounds.
- Bootstrap can deadlock when `commands.plugins` and `commands.config` are both disabled: the agent cannot enable the supported chat path, while the configured owner reply is not accepted by the delegated setup surface.

### Suggested implementation

1. Resolve `senderIsOwner` from the current authenticated Slack inbound sender for every turn, including replies in bot-created threads.
2. Pass a one-use, run-bound owner grant to privileged delegation/setup tools.
3. Recheck `commands.ownerAllowFrom`, sender identity, account, channel, active run, and revocation immediately before mutation.
4. Do not infer authority from thread-root authorship or inter-session provenance.
5. Add integration tests for:
   - owner-created root → owner follow-up
   - bot-created root → configured owner reply
   - non-owner reply
   - revoked owner between approval and commit
   - inter-session handoff remains non-owner

### Environment

Observed on OpenClaw 2026.11.x, Slack channel thread, configured explicit command owner. No credentials or private identifiers included.

## Bug type

Regression / incomplete fix (warning only — the command succeeds)

## Summary

Changing a **per-agent** model with `openclaw config set agents.entries.<id>.model ...` makes the CLI load provider plugins for model validation without a published runtime config snapshot. The bundled Codex plugin then fails to register:

```
[plugins] codex failed during register from ~/.openclaw/npm/projects/openclaw-codex-<hash>/node_modules/@openclaw/codex/dist/index.js: Error: Runtime config is not prepared. Await captureRuntimeConfigAsyncReader()() first.
```

The same change on `agents.defaults.model.primary` no longer logs the error, so it looks like #177680 ("pin runtime config before plugin load in config set model validation") covers the defaults path but not `agents.entries.<id>.model`.

The write itself validates and persists correctly, and the running Gateway serves Codex normally (`plugins.list` / agent turns work). The impact is a misleading red error on every per-agent model change.

## Steps to reproduce

With the Codex plugin enabled and an agent `main` defined under `agents.entries`:

```bash
# 1. Defaults path — no register error (fixed by #177680)
openclaw config set agents.defaults.model.primary '"anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5"' --strict-json --dry-run

# 2. Per-agent path, string form — register error
openclaw config set agents.entries.main.model '"anthropic/claude-opus-5-5"' --strict-json --dry-run

# 3. Per-agent path, object form — register error
openclaw config set agents.entries.main.model '{"primary":"openai/gpt-5.6-sol","fallbacks":["github-copilot/claude-opus-5"]}' --strict-json --dry-run
```

Notes:

- The error only appears when the value actually changes the model references. Re-setting the current value does not trigger it.
- It happens both with `--dry-run` and on a real write.

## Expected behavior

`config set` publishes the prepared runtime config before loading provider plugins for any model-reference validation, including `agents.entries.<id>.model`, as it now does for `agents.defaults.model.primary`.

## Actual behavior

Case 1 prints only `Dry run successful`. Cases 2 and 3 print the Codex `failed during register ... Runtime config is not prepared` line, then `Dry run successful`.

## Environment

- OpenClaw: 2026.11.1 (4ffdd20), npm install, stable channel
- @openclaw/codex: 2026.11.1
- OS: macOS 27.2 (arm64)
- Node: 24.22.1

## Related

- #177680 — same fix for `agents.defaults.model.primary` (merged 2026-10-23)
- #170445 / #172428 / #172876 — same error class in Doctor and `openclaw codex` commands
- #169714 — strict prepared-only runtime config reads

issues.body:
## Summary

Codename ClippyClaw turns OpenClaw's built-in agent into the guide that sets a person up. Every new agent is born in a conversation, and OpenClaw can explain and repair itself. On the Mac, a desktop companion shows what the agents are doing.

I pitched this at the Focus Week kick-off. This issue is the reasoning, the plan, and the tracker for the pull requests that deliver it.

## Why

I believe OpenClaw is for everyone, not only for people who write code.

I believe an agent should be yours from its first minute. You name it, you tell it who you are, and it becomes yours in a conversation, not in a settings page.

I believe the first hour is a story, and OpenClaw should be the one telling it.

I believe software this capable should set itself up and repair itself. Asking another assistant to make OpenClaw work should never be the answer.

I believe OpenClaw should keep setting the tone for what an agent harness and an agent should be. We took a detour for a while, because we had to grow OpenClaw exponentially while building OpenClaw with OpenClaw. Now it is time to return to that DNA and to the main road, and to set the pace and the tone for every agent harness. The anniversary is the right moment to set that theme.

**OpenClaw is for everyone, and an agent should be yours from its first minute.** Nobody should need a programmer, a terminal, or another assistant to make OpenClaw work.

**We had this.** OpenClaw started as a terminal app, and its setup was a conversation. It asked a question, said what it was doing, linked your account, and then hatched your agent. The hatching was the special part. A new agent woke up, asked what to call it, asked who you were and what it was for, and the conversation went on from there. Within minutes you had an agent that was yours. Other assistants had one name and one personality. OpenClaw let you make your own.

**We lost some of it on the way to something better.** The Control UI and the apps made OpenClaw far more capable. They also moved setup out of the conversation and into screens and settings. A new person now accepts a few steps, lands in a dashboard with many windows, and has to work out alone who to talk to. The first hour reads like a tool for programmers.

**It costs people their first day.** I sat with a first-time user while they installed OpenClaw. It took three and a half hours. Their phone was not paired at the end, and we opened a different coding agent to get unstuck. Using another agent to set up or fix OpenClaw is the habit this work ends.

## How

**Give the job to the one part of OpenClaw built to survive.** OpenClaw has an agent that is always there: the built-in OpenClaw agent, once called Crestodian. It was made to keep working when everything else is broken. Updates are reliable now, so it rarely has anything to rescue, and most people never meet it. It is already on every install. That makes it the right narrator for the first hour and the right first responder afterwards. A person who is not a programmer will never run `openclaw doctor` in a terminal. Someone has to do that for them and say what it found.

These rules shape every pull request:

- **Setup is a conversation.** Today it is a list of steps to accept. OpenClaw speaks first and says what is happening. Choices are buttons. Nobody is shown a command.
- **One character.** The guide narrates. It does not compete with the person's agent, and it hands over where the person can see it.
- **Scripted until a model works.** The first minutes cannot depend on inference, so they cannot be wrong.
- **Every agent is born.** It wakes up and meets its person, where today it is created from a form. The birth template already puts it this way: "This file is a ritual, not a gate." The person's own request always comes first.
- **It sees the installation and leaves conversations alone.** OpenClaw reads the state of the install and the machine. It reads a conversation only when the person opens it there.
- **It remembers only its own interactions**, and the person can read that memory and erase it.
- **It says what it found, in plain words, and asks before it changes anything.**
- **It always works.** Its wiring has to survive mistakes that break the person's agent or the Gateway.
- **Reuse what exists.** Each piece extends an existing owner: the system agent's typed operations, Doctor, the approval card, the birth template, the bundled skills.

## What

A guided first run, one birth for every agent, an OpenClaw that knows and repairs itself, and a companion on the Mac. First what a person meets, then the problem it answers, then the work.

### The experience, step by step

1. **Install.** The person opens the app. OpenClaw speaks first and says what is happening. Until a model works, what it says is scripted, so it cannot be wrong. Choices are buttons. Nobody is shown a command.
2. **Meet the guide.** OpenClaw says who it is and that the person's own agent comes next. It is the only guide, and the person's agent stays the only assistant they manage.
3. **Take the tour, or skip it.** A short tour points at the parts of the Control UI. Then it asks: learn more, or wake your agent?
4. **Choose what the agent may do.** On the guided first run, OpenClaw explains the permission modes before the first wake-up. The person can keep the current mode or approve a change. Whether **+ New agent** and **Template Add** should ask again is a separate decision below.
5. **The hand-off.** OpenClaw says "Wake up, my friend!" in the agent's chat, where the person can see it, and steps aside.
6. **The birth.** The agent wakes up. It says it was just born, asks its name, asks who it should be and offers a few roles, and asks who the person is. It offers avatars. When the birth ends, OpenClaw says so once. The person's own request always comes first, and the birth waits for it.
7. **Every agent after that.** A second agent, or one installed from a Template, is born the same way. An agent that arrives prepared by a Template sets itself up, wakes up, says who it is and what it came with, and offers three choices: keep it, give it a new name, or change something about the recipe.
8. **Later.** OpenClaw notices things a person would not look for, such as API keys saved as plain text, and offers to fix them. It can answer questions about OpenClaw from the docs. On the Mac, the desktop lobster shows which agent is working, who is speaking, and when an agent needs the person.
9. **When something breaks.** OpenClaw looks, says what is wrong in plain words, and proposes a repair plan the person approves. It works in the terminal when the Gateway is down.

### The problem it solves

A new person cannot finish setting up OpenClaw alone. In the session I watched, seven things failed. Each belongs to a different owner, and nothing connects them:

- Setup ended with no conversation started. We had to find **Talk to my agent** in Settings.
- Two agents were on screen and nothing said which one to talk to.
- The new agent asked for a name and an avatar. It never asked who the person is or what they need.
- An agent made with **+ New agent** skips the birth and asks a role question. A Template agent gets a third kind of opening.
- The phone could not connect, and the first sign was an error.
- Asked to fix it, the built-in OpenClaw agent could not look at a log, could not run a Doctor repair, and told us to use a terminal.
- A broken plugin said only "Needs attention".

### The work

Six workstreams. Each pull request is useful alone and says "Part of" this issue. Inside a workstream the pull requests sit in one line, bottom first.

| Workstream | What it delivers | Steps of the experience | Remaining boundary |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A. The guide in the Control UI** (6 PRs) | The guide wakes the agent, introduces itself, offers the permission choice, the tour, and the plaintext keys fix, keeps its own notes, and receives what the person is looking at on Home. | 2, 3, 4, 5, 8 | The guide tells where a wake-up came from by its key. C1 moves the wake-up to the Gateway. |
| **B. The desktop lobster on macOS** (9 PRs) | The companion, who is speaking, status moods, agent activity, the 52 Blobster looks, and narration of Mac onboarding. | 1, 8 | macOS only. Narration follows #202613 and #202598. |
| **C. The birth, and setup without dead ends** (5 PRs) | One birth for every new agent. A way back from channel setup. Phone access offered by the guide. A broken plugin says why. Doctor names two problems it could not name. | 6, 7, 9 | Phone pairing itself stays with #103271, #120762, and #120764. |
| **D. OpenClaw knows OpenClaw** (2 PRs) | A handbook skill and a docs map for every agent, with a rule to check before answering "OpenClaw can't do that". A Doctor reference for the built-in OpenClaw agent. | 8, 9 | The built-in OpenClaw agent cannot read skills. It reads the reference through its docs reading. |
| **E. OpenClaw repairs itself** (draft PRs) | The built-in OpenClaw agent may investigate freely, run its own commands with one approval per change, and run anything else as an approved repair plan of typed steps checked against a table of allowed tools. Doctor's diagnosis sets the access level. | 9 | Changes what the most privileged agent may do. Needs a maintainer decision. |
| **F. P0 issues on the first-run path** | Each open P0 about install, onboarding, first use, providers, and connectors is verified against `main`. Unowned ones provable on macOS get one PR each. | all | Fixes on Windows, Linux desktop, Android, and a real iPhone need an owner with that platform. |

Each workstream has its own issue with the pull request checklist, its order, and its current state:

- A. The guide in the Control UI: #203781
- B. The desktop lobster on macOS: #203775
- C. The birth, and setup without dead ends: #203782
- D. OpenClaw knows OpenClaw: #203783
- E. OpenClaw repairs itself: #203784
- F. P0 issues on the first-run path: #203785

### How the built-in OpenClaw agent repairs (Workstream E)

People reach for another coding agent because OpenClaw's own commands are often not enough. The cause is in the service manager, the network, a permission, a dependency, or a file. So the proposal is:

1. **Look, freely.** Read-only investigation without a prompt.
2. **Its own commands.** Commands that only read run freely. A command that changes something asks once, as every change by this agent does today.
3. **Anything else runs as an approved repair plan** of typed steps, limited to what the installation owns plus a named list of tools it depends on. OpenClaw has no OS-level confinement on the host, so the limit is the table of allowed steps. One approval covers the whole plan, and it covers exactly the listed steps.
4. **Outside that boundary, it hands the person the step** and checks the result.
5. **Access follows the diagnosis.** Doctor names the problem, and a table in code says what that unlocks. The agent cannot raise its own level.
6. **Every request can be said plainly**, with three facts worked out by code beside the model's words: what the step touches, whether it can be undone, and whether it leaves the machine.
7. **Commands that destroy data or act outside the machine always ask.**

## Alternatives considered

- **An editable wake-up draft the person sends** (#202108). A new person should not have to press send to meet their agent. An editable wake-up fits later as an option for advanced users.
- **Retire the Ask OpenClaw conversation and do setup inside the person's own agent** (#202148). The person's agent runs on the Gateway it would be repairing. When OpenClaw is broken, that agent is broken too, so the guide has to be the part that survives.
- **Hand repairs to the person's agent.** Rejected for the same reason.
- **Only add more typed actions to the built-in OpenClaw agent.** That covers the problems someone predicted. People leave for another tool because of the ones nobody predicted. The typed setup actions in #202164 fit with Workstream E as its fast path.
- **Give the built-in OpenClaw agent a general shell.** Rejected. A non-technical person cannot judge a raw command, so the approval would protect nobody. What protects a person is the boundary and a plan they can read.

## Impact

- **A new person** finishes setup with a guide, meets an agent that asks who they are, and never opens a terminal.
- **Someone adding a second agent or a Template** gets the same birth, adapted to what the agent already knows.
- **Someone with a broken install** gets a diagnosis and a repair plan from OpenClaw itself.
- **Maintainers** get first-run failures named by Doctor, and fewer support requests that start with "I asked another agent to fix it".
- **Existing installs** are not changed. The guide appears on first run and when asked for.

## Evidence/examples

- **The clean install of 18 November 2026**, row by row, is below.
- **What the models establish:** In [Workstream A](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/203781#checked-statechart), the at-most-once rule holds, but a guide-created agent can skip the permission question. [C1’s model](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/203782#rules) covers that guide-created path. Its permission rule is explicitly **guide-only**; it does not prove that **+ New agent**, **Template Add**, or a terminal birth asks the question.
- **What the real-app run establishes:** #203781 reports two faults: waking a just-created agent before the Gateway knows it, and retrying a cancelled wake after Gateway restart. A1 and A2 contain fixes. Replies in the reported Control UI run came from the QA mock provider. See the workstream evidence below for the subsequent A1 check; it is not a real-model, final-stack acceptance run.
- **Workstreams A and B** pass the tests, type checks, and lint for everything they touch. Real-app recordings are attached to each pull request when it opens.
- **A4** has a test that the open P0 #126470 does not affect it.

<details>
<summary>The clean install of 18 November 2026, row by row</summary>


A person who had never set up OpenClaw installed the macOS app from the website and tried to reach three things: a first conversation with their own agent, a paired iPhone, and a working set of plugins. An experienced user guided them on a call. It took about three and a half hours, and the iPhone was still not confirmed as paired at the end.

This is one session on one Mac. The app build was the public download of that day. The exact version was not recorded. The rows below are what was seen on screen and read aloud, not reproduced bugs. Causes are unknown unless a row says otherwise.

**Already addressed**

| What happened | Where it is addressed |
|---|---|
| **Connect a device** could not create a setup code ("Gateway is only bound to loopback") and offered no way forward. | #202071, merged 21 Nov, adds **Set up secure access** with three routes. |
| Onboarding ended in channel setup and no conversation with the new agent ever started. It was reached by hand through Settings, then Ask OpenClaw, then Talk to my agent. | A1 and A2: automatic first wake-up and a **Talk to my agent** button. |
| The user asked what the difference is between OpenClaw and their own agent. | A2 and A3: the guide introduces itself and offers a product tour. |

**Still open**

Where each row goes: row 1 is C1. Rows 2 and 9 belong with #103271, #120762 and #120764, and C4 opens a door to them. Rows 3 and 7 are Workstream E, and C3 names the problems in row 7. Row 5 is C2. Row 8 is C6 for plugins. The skill half of row 8, and rows 4 and 6, are the three issues in the plan.

| # | What happened | What the person needed |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | The new agent asked for a name, a vibe and an avatar, then considered itself done. It never asked who the user is, what they do, or what they want help with. The birth template on `main` has four beats: name, vibe, avatar, plugin recommendations. | One short question about the person and their goals before the avatar, saved where the agent reads it. |
| 2 | Onboarding never mentioned reaching the Gateway from a phone. The first sign was the loopback error listed under "Already addressed", after the phone app was installed. | A way to turn on phone access during setup or when the phone app is linked, so the error is not the introduction. |
| 3 | Asked to turn on Tailscale Serve, the agent reported that its config tool failed to save the Gateway address, asked the user for the tailnet name, and tried to open iPhone Mirroring to look at the phone. | The agent completes or cleanly refuses this one task, and says which step failed. |
| 4 | In the iPhone app, **Connect Manually** with a host, port 443 and TLS showed nothing after the tap. Going back, the app showed the Gateway as offline. | A visible result for the attempt, with the reason when it fails. |
| 5 | In channel setup the user picked a channel they could not finish and found no way back to the previous step. | A back or skip action in that step. |
| 6 | The macOS app quit unexpectedly while the location permission was being granted. It reopened normally. | No crash. This one was not investigated. |
| 7 | `openclaw doctor --fix` repeated the same yes/no prompts, then reported "Gateway service inspection is unavailable; automatic service restart was skipped". `openclaw update repair` printed that the Gateway is managed by OpenClaw update and did nothing. `openclaw gateway stop` reported the service as not loaded. The user could not tell whether the Gateway was running. | One command that says whether the Gateway is running and what to do next. |
| 8 | Plugins switched on in Settings showed as loaded, but the agent later reported that memory was not working and needed configuration. A bundled skill showed "missing requirements" with no action. | Switching a plugin on either works or says what is still missing. |
| 9 | After Serve was on, the phone still could not reach the Gateway. The cause was the access rules of the tailnet used for the call: another phone on the same tailnet opened the address, this one could not. Nothing in OpenClaw pointed there. The agent confirmed Serve was running, HTTPS answered 200 on the Mac and the phone was online in the tailnet, and concluded only that no connection attempt had arrived. Finding the cause took close to an hour. Doctor already checks that Tailscale is signed in and that Serve routes match (`doctor-tailscale.ts`). It does not check whether a given device can reach the Gateway. | When everything on the Gateway side is healthy and no attempt arrives from the phone, say so in those words and name tailnet access rules as the likely cause. The phone app is the side that can see the failed connection, so its error should name it too. The Gateway cannot read the tailnet's rules, so it can only point at the likely cause. |

**Seen in the session but not counted**

- A third-party design hook did not appear under Hooks. That screen belonged to another tool.
- A Labs toggle that would not stay on, and a profile field that showed "unavailable". Seen once, not looked into.

**What this adds**

These rows are why this umbrella has workstreams C to F. Workstreams A and B alone would have left this person with an agent that does not know who it works for, a phone that is not part of setup, and no way to recover without outside help.

</details>

## What we can reproduce on main

Tested 23 November 2026 on [d5c8befeec1f](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/d5c8befeec1f17c437969e3ec983144e4edf847c), the head of `main` at verification time. Debian 12 x64, Node 24.20.0, pnpm 12.15.0. These are new observations, not a reconstruction of the 18 November Mac session.

**1. Before a model is configured, asking the built-in guide for read-only diagnosis stops before Doctor runs.** From the pinned checkout with dependencies installed, use an empty disposable profile and an unused local Gateway port (43179 in this run):

```sh
mkdir -p .openclaw/tmp
case_dir=$(mktemp -d "$PWD/.openclaw/tmp/clippyclaw-repro-XXXXXX")
(
  export OPENCLAW_HOME="$case_dir" OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR="$case_dir/state"
  export OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH="$case_dir/state/openclaw.json" OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PORT=43179
  pnpm openclaw setup --baseline --workspace "$case_dir/agent"
  grep -E '^## [1-4][.]' "$case_dir/agent/BOOTSTRAP.md"
  pnpm openclaw setup --message 'doctor'  # expected exit 1 in this no-model profile
  pnpm openclaw doctor --json             # standalone read-only control; expected exit 0
)
```

Baseline setup exited 0. The request through the guide exited 1: “OpenClaw requires working inference: No agent model is configured. Run `openclaw onboard` first.” No Doctor findings were returned; the config file was unchanged. The [one-shot setup entry point](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/d5c8befeec1f17c437969e3ec983144e4edf847c/src/commands/system-agent-with-inference.ts#L62-L103) checks inference before invoking the system agent. On the same fresh profile and pinned revision, the standalone [read-only advisory command](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/d5c8befeec1f17c437969e3ec983144e4edf847c/docs/cli/doctor/running.md#L67-L78) exited 0 and returned a structured report with four findings. The config file’s SHA-256 was unchanged after each command. The number and IDs of findings may vary by machine; the reproducible distinction is **no report via the guide, valid report via standalone Doctor**, on the same installation without a model. Proposed acceptance: with no model configured, the guide explains that condition and offers the next step where the person is, without a terminal or new repair permissions.

**2. The new workspace tells the agent how to establish its own identity, but not how to learn the person’s goal.** Baseline setup produced the same four numbered steps in two fresh workspaces: “Ask What to Call You,” “Choose Your Vibe,” “Choose Your Avatar,” and “Finish With Recommendations.” There is no required beat asking what the person wants help with. This is the [seeded birth contract](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/d5c8befeec1f17c437969e3ec983144e4edf847c/docs/reference/templates/BOOTSTRAP.md#L14-L31), not a claim that a real model can never ask on its own. Proposed acceptance: if the person has not stated a goal, ask one optional question about it; if they have requested work, do that first.

**3. On the guide-created agent path, the Control UI hands off a draft.** The existing [component test](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/d5c8befeec1f17c437969e3ec983144e4edf847c/ui/src/pages/custodian/custodian-page-agent-create.test.ts#L80-L99) passed on this revision. With a simulated successful Gateway response, the mounted page selects the created agent and navigates to its chat with “Wake up, my friend!” as a draft. This verifies the handoff URI, not a delivered wake-up, native rendering, or a real model reply. Repeat with `pnpm --dir ui test src/pages/custodian/custodian-page-agent-create.test.ts -t 'refreshes the roster' --maxWorkers=1`.

Two supporting suites also passed (6 tests): `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node pnpm test src/system-agent/new-agent-welcome.test.ts src/system-agent/operations.tui.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`. They confirm the role/team/custom-work welcome and the intentional refusal of Doctor repairs before a write or audit. These are owner tests, not a native onboarding run.

### What each reproduction means for the workstreams

| Reproduced on `main` | Covered by | State |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Before a model is configured, the built-in guide cannot run even a read-only Doctor request. | Not covered yet. A keeps the existing "needs a model" notice, and E's repair paths, including `openclaw setup`, still require working inference. | Open gap. A follow-up for E: let read-only diagnosis run before a model is configured. |
| 2. The seeded birth has no beat that asks what the person wants help with. | C1 adds "And who are you?": what they do and what they want help with, asked only when it is not already known, and skipped when the person has already asked for work. | Built and checked. Real-app proof running. |
| 3. The Control UI hands the new agent a draft; the component test does not show a sent turn. | A1 initiates the guided wake. C1 proposes the Gateway as sender for the four Control UI birth paths; CLI and TUI retain separate wake paths. | Built. A1 re-proven in the real app with a scripted mock; no real-model acceptance claimed. |

## Decisions and remaining proof

- **Guide and handoff:** [#202148](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202148) keeps backend recovery but retires the separate frontend; [#203781](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/203781) keeps a visible guide and hands off to the personal agent. Independent recovery does not, by itself, decide which conversation the person should see. **Decision requested:** which conversation owns first-run guidance, and who sends the first wake-up after the permission choice?
- **Repair authority:** The umbrella rejects a general shell; [#203784](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/203784) still proposes an opt-in unconfined command running with full user rights. Recommendation: keep it out of first-run acceptance. A Doctor finding is not a permission grant. Any new host-changing action, its policy owner, and its enforcement need a separate maintainer/security decision.
- **Native proof already available:** [#203786, Evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/203786) reports a fresh-profile run on macOS 26.5.2 at standalone app commit `dcdd4270961` with the stack’s Gateway package: welcome, connection choice, Gateway startup and AI discovery. The native suites passed 99 tests in nine suites. This covers those screens, not a real provider’s first reply or the original 18 November build.
- **Missing acceptance:** On an identified app build and matching candidate Gateway revision, use a fresh test profile and a real provider. Record the provider/model (no credentials), which conversation opened, whether the permission choice appeared before the wake, whether the person had to find Settings, open a terminal or press Send, and how many first assistant replies appeared. Record success as well as failure. Check immediate-after-create and restart-during-wake separately on the candidate head. This is a new run; the original Mac build remains unknown.

## Completion criteria

- [ ] A person with no OpenClaw state installs the macOS app and reaches a first conversation with their own agent without opening Settings or a terminal.
- [ ] In both guide paths (**Talk to my agent** and **create an agent through the guide**), show the permission choice before the automatic wake. Keeping the mode leaves it unchanged; changing it requires approval. Verify one delivered wake on success and no duplicate after reload/retry. If the person writes first, serve that request without inserting another wake.
- [ ] For **+ New agent** and **Template Add**, verify the maintainer-selected policy: show the permission choice, or retain the configured mode without silently changing it. C1 currently describes the latter. If the decision is to ask on every path, these two paths remain open work; the guide’s passing model is not proof.
- [ ] Record and verify one sender for the four Control UI paths. C1 proposes the Gateway; CLI/TUI have their own paths and require separate proof before claiming one sender across all clients.
- [ ] An agent created by the guide, by **+ New agent**, and from a Template is born the same way, adapted to what it already knows.
- [ ] The birth asks who the person is, and OpenClaw says once when the birth has ended.
- [ ] A broken plugin and a stopped Gateway service are named where the person is looking, with a next step.
- [ ] Any agent answers "can OpenClaw do X" from the handbook and the docs map, and checks before saying no.
- [ ] The built-in OpenClaw agent diagnoses the first-run failures above and proposes a repair plan a non-technical person can read. This criterion depends on the Workstream E decision.
- [ ] Each open P0 on the first-run path is verified as still present, fixed, or in flight, and the unowned ones provable on macOS have a pull request.
- [ ] Each clean install finding has a merged fix, its own issue, or a named owner.

## Maintainer decisions

**First-run decisions to record with the product contacts for this issue and #202148:** (1) Does the person meet a separate visible guide or stay in their personal agent’s Home? (2) Is the Gateway the sole sender for the four Control UI birth paths? (3) Do **+ New agent** and **Template Add** reuse the configured mode or ask again? Choosing the visible conversation does not grant host repair authority.

1. Should **+ New agent** run the birth in place of the role question? C1 removes the saved greeting "Hi, I'm {name}. Happy to help." for those agents. It exists in 16 languages.
2. Should the birth ask who the person is?
3. May the built-in OpenClaw agent investigate and repair as Workstream E describes, and how is the installation boundary enforced on each operating system?
4. Two lobster settings: keep, change, or drop.

## Related work, rechecked 22 November 2026

- #202108, #202148, #202164: a parked draft stack that takes the other route. See "Alternatives considered".
- #202613, #202598: drafts that shorten Mac setup. B9 follows them.
- #202071, #202042: merged. C4 reuses the first.
- #103271, #120762, #120764: phone access and Tailscale during setup. C4 is a door into them, and the clean install is evidence for them.
- #197465: an earlier request for a guided first run.
- #168372, #191593: open P0 issues on the surfaces the guide uses. Workstream F verifies them.

## Follow-ups, not claims made by these pull requests

- The guide narrating the installer on Windows and Linux. B9 covers Mac onboarding only.
- A small local model, so the guide can talk before any provider is connected.
- The desktop companion on Windows at the same level as the Mac.
- Signature sounds for the lobster.
- An editable wake-up for advanced users.
- The built-in OpenClaw agent as a built-in agent template, with its purpose written down in files of its own.

## Known boundaries

- The clean install is one session on one Mac. The app version was not recorded.
- The full Swift suites do not complete on the development Mac. Workstream B is green on the suites it touches, and PR CI is the first full run.
- Nothing here proves a repair boundary as a security sandbox. Workstream E has to show what each operating system can enforce.

## Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Yes. Workstreams A and B are written. Workstreams C and D are being built. All four open against this issue. Workstream E opens as drafts once its design is reviewed. Workstream F opens one pull request per verified issue.

작성: 2026-11-23, 코비 (OpenClaw 2026.11.6 / 06afb10)
상태: 초안 — Teo 검토 후 GitHub issue로 제출 예정

## 요청 배경 (실측 재현 3회)
승인 대상 exec 호출에 ask 필드로 구조화 설명을 전달해도 Gateway 승인카드 UI에는 명령 원문만 표시된다:
- 09:16 ask 없이 호출 → 카드 명령만 표시(호출자 위반)
- 09:23 ask 4줄 전달 → 카드 미표시(렌더링 부재)
- 09:28 ask 4줄 전달 → 카드 미표시(재현)
config schema 전수 확인 결과: 승인 대상 exec의 ask 비어있음을 조건부 검증하는 설정 기능 없음(security=allowlist/ask=always/askFallback=deny 조합은 승인 발생 여부만 제어).

## 요청 1 — 승인카드 ask 렌더링 (UI)
- 승인 이벤트 payload의 ask 문자열을 카드에 명령과 함께 표시 (명령 원문 보존, escaping 필수).
- 접기/잘림 처리, Control UI·모바일 대응.

## 요청 2 — 설명 없는 승인 요청 차단 (런타임 게이트, fail-closed)
- approvalRequired(exec) AND ask 미제공/공백 → 승인카드 생성 거부 + 호출 거부 + 누락 필드 반환.
- 최소 검증: 공백·무의미 1줄 우회 방지(구조화 필드 또는 최소 길이).

## 요청 3 — 웹채팅 어시스턴트 중간 메시지 유실 수정 (전달 계층)
- 현상 [실측 재현 다수, 2026-11-23]: 턴 처리 중 어시스턴트가 작성한 중간 메시지(진행 설명·승인카드 직전 4줄 설명)가 웹채팅(webchat surface)에 표시되지 않고 최종 답변 위주만 도착.
- 영향: 승인자가 카드 직전 설명을 볼 수 없어 요청 1·2의 효과가 반감됨. 승인 전 설명 확인 절차가 전달 계층에서 무력화됨.
- 요청: 중간 어시스턴트 메시지도 최종 답변과 동일한 전달 신뢰성 보장. 유실 시 재전송 또는 명시적 오류 표시.

## 검증 시나리오
1. ask 없음/공백 → 카드 미생성, 실행 거부
2. 정상 ask → 카드에 전체 표시
3. 거절 → 미실행
4. escaping·긴 텍스트·multiline 안전성
5. rollback: 기능 flag 비활성화 시 기존 동작 복구
6. 요청 3: 턴 중간 어시스턴트 메시지 3개 이상 + 도구 호출 사이 → 웹채팅에 전부 표시됨

## 기대 효과
승인자가 카드만 보고 승인/거부를 판단 가능. 초보자도 위험을 이해한 승인 가능. 호출자 절차 의존 제거(회상 실패 원천 차단). 중간 메시지 신뢰성 확보로 카드 직전 설명 절차가 실제로 작동함.

issues.body:
### Bug type
Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker
No

### Summary
A Slack reply from the Gateway owner does not carry owner authority when it is posted in a thread whose root message was created by the agent, so owner-only tools are refused even after explicit approval.

### Steps to reproduce
1. In a Slack channel connected to OpenClaw, have the agent create a top-level message for an approval-gated task.
2. Have the configured Gateway owner reply in that message's thread with explicit approval.
3. In the resulting turn, call an owner-only tool such as `openclaw`.
4. Observe that the runtime records the actual Slack sender but resolves `senderIsOwner` as false and gates the tool.
5. Repeating the approval in another agent-created task thread produces the same refusal.

### Expected behavior
Owner authority should be derived from the authenticated sender of the current inbound approval message. The owner-only tool should be callable within that approved turn, regardless of whether the thread root was authored by the agent.

### Actual behavior
The owner-only tool is unavailable and returns: `openclaw needs the owner's authority, and this turn was not started by the owner. Do not retry openclaw.` The approved operation does not run.

### OpenClaw version
2026.11.3 (965be9c)

### Operating system
macOS 26.6.2 (arm64)

### Install method
npm global; Gateway runs as a macOS LaunchAgent

### Model
openai/gpt-5.6-sol

### Provider / routing chain
OpenClaw Default -> OpenAI

### Additional provider/model setup details
The failure occurs in the host's pre-execution owner-only tool gate; no model-provider error is involved.

### Logs
```shell
openclaw needs the owner's authority, and this turn was not started by the owner. Do not retry openclaw.
```

Installed bundle location of the refusal:
`dist/agent-tools-*.mjs`, in `resolveTurnToolSurface`, where tools in `ownerOnlyDenied` are replaced by an unavailable execution gate.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence
The inbound turn retained the authenticated Slack sender identifier, but its runtime projection set `senderIsOwner: false`. The parent/root message was agent-authored and the current reply was human-authored.

### Impact and severity
- Affected: Slack workflows that use agent-created task roots and thread replies for approvals.
- Severity: High for owner-gated operations because the approved action is completely blocked.
- Frequency: Reproduced on the observed approval attempts, including after moving the task to a separate channel/thread.
- Consequence: Operations such as plugin installation or Gateway configuration cannot proceed through the documented conversational approval flow.

### Additional information
This is adjacent to, but not the same as, #124556. That issue exposes causal owner metadata to pre-model plugin hooks and explicitly says the observation does not grant live action authority. This report concerns the core per-turn owner-only tool authorization gate.

A safe fix should bind authority to the authenticated current inbound event (sender identity, account/channel scope, and exact turn), or issue a one-time approval receipt bound to the owner reply and requested action. It should not infer authority from message text or from the thread root author.

Filed with AI assistance and reviewed against a live reproduction and the installed 2026.11.3 bundle.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On 2026.11.6, reading a compressed session archive (`*.jsonl.zst`) fails with `ERR_BUFFER_TOO_LARGE` whenever the plain transcript is bigger than the compressed file plus 1 MiB; #192743 already fixes this on main, but no stable release carries it.

### Steps to reproduce

1. On 2026.11.6, archive a session whose transcript is about 3,000 records (several MB of plain JSONL).
2. Read its history.
3. Result: `ERR_BUFFER_TOO_LARGE`.

### Expected behavior

The archive reads, as the same fixture does on 2026.11.4.

### Actual behavior

The read fails with `ERR_BUFFER_TOO_LARGE` ("Session archive … exceeds N decompressed bytes; the archive is unchanged. Export it as uncompressed JSONL to read it."). That covers archived history, CLI history, transcript and usage reads, and the memory session indexer.

### OpenClaw version

2026.11.6

### Operating system

Ubuntu 24.04 (Linux x86_64)

### Install method

npm (pinned dependency)

### Model

Not model-specific (archive read, no inference)

### Provider / routing chain

None (local archive read)

### Additional provider/model setup details

_No response_

### Logs

```shell
Session archive … exceeds N decompressed bytes; the archive is unchanged. Export it as uncompressed JSONL to read it.
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

2026.11.6, `src/config/sessions/archive-compression.ts`, `readSessionArchiveContentSync`:

```ts
const maxOutputLength = expectedBytes ?? stored.length + 1024 * 1024;
```

Writers pass `expectedBytes`. Readers don't, so they get the fixed +1 MiB budget. The cap came in with #190690 (Nov 1).

#192743 ("read compressed archives as streams instead of refusing expansion", merged Nov 4) replaces the cap with a streaming decode and a 4 GiB ceiling. Its description measures the impact: on team-metal, 9,461 of 16,806 archives (56%) were refused. #193548 (Nov 5) follows it up. Both are in v2026.11.10-beta.1 and missing from v2026.11.6, which is the current npm `latest`.

garrytan/alphaclaw#470 had to cut its live test fixture (`tests/live/openclaw-archive-read-cache.e2e.test.js`) from 3,000 to 1,000 records to pass on 2026.11.6.

### Impact and severity

A stable user who upgrades from 2026.11.4 loses read access to long archived sessions until the next stable release. That was 56% of archives on team-metal, per #192743.

### Additional information

Ask: a 2026.11.6.x patch with #192743 and #193548, or the next stable release that carries them.

Last known good: 2026.11.4. #200232 hit the same error on 2026.11.5-beta.3 and was closed as already fixed on main, which is true; this issue asks only for a stable release that carries the fix.

issues.body:
### Environment

- OpenClaw **2026.10.3 (59cb447)**, npm global install (`%APPDATA%\npm\openclaw.ps1`)
- Windows 11 Pro, build **26200**, x64, **16 GB RAM / 16 logical cores**
- Node **v24.18.0** (`node:sqlite`)
- Gateway managed by Windows Scheduled Task `OpenClaw Gateway`
- Agent DB `~/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite`: **595 MB** (freelist = 0)
- Shared state DB `~/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite`: **51 MB**
- Plugins enabled (8): admin-http-rpc, feishu, memory-core, ollama, openai, openclaw-weixin, searxng, deepseek

### Summary

During normal interactive use (webchat), a turn blocks the Gateway event loop for 76–163 seconds. The embedded agent worker then hits its timeout and the client receives an error instead of a reply:

```
Embedded agent failed before reply: worker task timed out | timeout
message dispatch completed: channel=webchat ... outcome=error duration=140664ms
```

While blocked, even lightweight requests fail — `models.list` returned `UNAVAILABLE` after **138 079 ms**:

```
⇄ res ✗ models.list 138079ms errorCode=UNAVAILABLE
  errorMessage=Error: Gateway requester profile changed
```

### Evidence

Event-loop diagnostics, same process, over ~2 hours:

```
liveness warning: reasons=event_loop_delay,event_loop_utilization interval=138s
  eventLoopDelayP99Ms=137573.2
liveness warning: reasons=event_loop_delay,event_loop_utilization interval=129s
  eventLoopDelayP99Ms=128379.3
liveness warning: reasons=event_loop_delay,event_loop_utilization interval=164s
  eventLoopDelayP99Ms=162940.3
liveness warning: reasons=event_loop_delay,event_loop_utilization,cpu interval=88s
  degradedFor=321s
```

Reclamation and interactive writes contending:

```
slow SQLite transaction hold
slow SQLite session write {"agentId":"main","pid":21068,"threadId":0,
  "isMainThread":true,"operation":"session.transcript.report","elapsedMs":2860}
slow SQLite session write {"agentId":"main","pid":21068,"threadId":0,
  "isMainThread":true,"operation":"session.reclamation.worker-commit"}
slow SQLite session write {"agentId":"main","pid":21068,"threadId":0,
  "isMainThread":true,"operation":"session.entry-replacements","elapsedMs":1159}

SQLite automatic session maintenance paused after repeated input changes
  {"error":{"name":"SqliteReclamationInputsChangedError"}}

transcript cold storage failed: Error: database is locked
```

WAL growth while the Gateway was mostly idle (checkpoint blocked by a long-lived reader):

```
WAL:  0.3 MB -> 44.3 MB -> 146.1 MB over ~5 h
checkpoint failure: "openclaw-state WAL checkpoint PASSIVE blocked by a reader"
consecutiveBlocked=165, blocking connection operation=plugins.metadata.sourceAdmission.publish,
  ownerKind=worker, ageMs=1800048
```

Cold start is slow and gets misread by the supervisor:

```
startup phase: process.bootstrap          166 123.8 ms
startup phase: startup.maintenance         24 445.7 ms
startup phase: ready                       total 325 490.2 ms   (5.4 min)
(observed range across restarts: 195 s – 304 s – 325 s)
```

When the health monitor runs while health is not yet 200, it issues `/End` + restart, and the new instance re-enters the same slow path (several concurrent boot trees observed, each holding the same SQLite file).

### What was tried (results)

1. **`openclaw doctor --session-sqlite compact --session-sqlite-all-agents`**
   - `main`: `compact reclaimed=2137624 bytes, db=623857664->622333952`
   - i.e. **2.1 MB reclaimed out of 595 MB**; `freelist = 0`, data is live.
2. **`openclaw doctor --state-sqlite compact --json`**
   - `reclaimedBytes: 9203176`, state DB 51.5 → 43.3 MB, `integrityCheck: ok`.
3. **Disabling the `codex` plugin** (it was emitting `forced retirement after 5000ms` every ~2.5 min in an idle Gateway)
   - The 2.5-minute retirement cycle disappeared, but stalls **remained** at ~76 s during turns, so codex is an amplifier, not the sole cause.
4. **`openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive`** (recommended by the acpx warning)
   - Could not complete: `Doctor stopped because a state migration refused to continue. Failing check session-entry-state (step-refused): database is locked`. A second attempt ran >8 min with no output and was aborted.

### Agent DB composition (for context)

```
memory_index_chunks_vec_vector_chunks00     82 rows   246.0 MB
memory_embedding_cache                  14 428 rows    86.6 MB
memory_index_chunks                      8 281 rows    55.1 MB
memory_index_chunks_fts_data             9 704 rows    37.2 MB
transcript_events                       15 488 rows    50.5 MB
trajectory_runtime_events               10 833 rows    20.9 MB
```

~425 MB of the 595 MB is the memory-core vector/FTS index (embeddings from local `ollama / nomic-embed-text`); conversation history is only ~50 MB.

### Hypothesis (not proven)

- The blocking work happens on the **main thread** (`isMainThread:true`) in the session write/reclamation path, so it is not an I/O-wait story: the loop is busy or synchronously waiting while holding the writer.
- `SqliteReclamationInputsChangedError` suggests reclamation repeatedly restarts because interactive writes keep changing the same session, which would explain why the stall correlates with *sending a message* rather than with idle time.

### Related existing reports

- #162211 — startup blocks the event loop 40–200 s; health monitor misreads the stall and escalates into a restart loop (another Windows reporter is on **2026.10.3 59cb447**, same as this host; a macOS reporter says it persists at 2026.10.4)
- #148307 — `database is locked` when session reclamation exceeds the 5 s busy timeout (464 MB DB, zero freelist); a later comment on 2026.10.2 reports a 426 MB compact only partially mitigates it and points at reclamation-vs-interactive-write contention rather than DB size
- #112423 — large SQLite transcript cleanup blocks the gateway event loop
- #112758 — missing `mmap_size` / `cache_size` pragmas contributing to event-loop stalls
- #175003 — 2026.10.3 upgrade: RSS and worst event-loop overdue stepped up

### Question

Is there a supported way to bound or yield the session-write path so interactive requests stay responsive during reclamation (as #158073 attempted for commits)? If the intended mitigation is `busy_timeout` / `mmap_size` tuning, which knobs are safe to set for `node:sqlite` in 2026.10.3?

**Reported repro** — On OpenClaw 2026.11.1 (`4ffdd20`), use a disposable copy of a `main` store with an active `agent:main:main` transcript of roughly 70,920 events (261 MB). Run `openclaw sessions compact agent:main:main --max-lines 200`, then exercise Telegram turns and subagent spawning. The incident is intermittent. A deterministic trigger has yet to be identified.

**Expected** — After owner retirement, subsequent work can acquire a current owner. If a mutation may have committed, preserve its settlement status and retry only when safe.

**Actual** — Compaction returns `UNAVAILABLE` with `Agent database execution admission is closed` after about 3–4 seconds while the request signal remains active. Telegram turns and subagent spawning also fail. One stack reaches the guard through an already retained durable session actor.

**Code** — `src/state/openclaw-agent-execution-owner.ts`, `assertCurrent()` (installed bundle line 709). Log the failing guard operand and the owner’s close or revoke reason to distinguish native worker loss, explicit drain, and a scope change.

Environment: OpenClaw 2026.11.1 (4ffdd20), Linux x64, Node v26, single gateway. Affected only agent main (agent DB ~1.5 GB); reclamation worker repeatedly reports clean-close receipt `active-leases` for that DB. A gateway restart clears it temporarily.

issues.body:
# [Bug]: memory index `scopeHash` uses `localeCompare` on extraPaths, so reindexing from a terminal with a non-default locale permanently disables memory_search ("index scope changed")

**Version:** OpenClaw 2026.11.5 (e13cf15) (code present since at least 2026.11.3)
**Related:** #91902 (canonical tracker: CLI rebuild metadata rejected by runtime — providerKey/workspace drift family) and its satellite #91592 (`index scope changed` after force-rebuild, Linux/WSL, provider+workspace-resolution causes). **This report is a distinct, third mechanism for the same failure code:** none of those involve locale-dependent `localeCompare` collation of `extraPaths`; all reported cases there had empty or ASCII-only `extraPaths`, so collation ambiguity could not surface. Please consider adding `scopeHash` collation stability to the #91902 identity policy scope.
**Platform:** macOS gateway running as launchd service; reindex performed from interactive Terminal (zh_CN.UTF-8)
**Severity:** high — silent, permanent retrieval disablement after a documented, supported reindex action; deterministic for CJK-locale users.

## Symptom
After `memory index --force --agent <id>` completes successfully (log shows `Memory index updated: N files indexed`), `memory_search` for that agent returns `disabled: true / error: index scope changed` forever. Repeating the reindex from the same terminal keeps it broken; the index content itself is correct.

## Root cause (verified against dist source and by byte-exact recomputation)
`resolveConfiguredScopeHash` (extensions/memory-core manager-runtime, ~L1277-1293) normalizes `extraPaths` entries and sorts them with:

```js
.toSorted((a, b) => JSON.stringify(a).localeCompare(JSON.stringify(b)))
```

before `sha256(JSON.stringify({extraPaths, multimodal}))`. `localeCompare` is **locale-sensitive**:
- The Gateway service (launchd, no `LANG`/`LC_*` set → ICU default ~en-US) computes `configuredScopeHash` with en-US collation.
- An interactive Terminal on a Chinese macOS (LANG=zh_CN.UTF-8) running `memory index --force` writes `meta.scopeHash` with zh_CN collation (paths containing CJK names and mixed ASCII sort differently).
- The two hashes can never match → `resolveContentScopeIdentityState` fails on `t.scopeHash !== e.configuredScopeHash` → `configuredIndexMismatch("scope", "index scope changed")` → search permanently disabled.

Empirical proof on one real config (13 extraPath entries, several with CJK directory names), recomputing with the shipped `normalizeExtraMemoryPathEntries`/`hashText`:

| Environment | scopeHash | matches stored meta? |
|---|---|---|
| LANG=zh_CN.UTF-8 (user terminal) | `6886dda2…` | equals the value written by terminal reindex |
| LANG unset / en_US (gateway) | `0a31f10b…` | the value the gateway expects |

Same agent, same config file, same OpenClaw build — only the collation differs. A second agent's index showed the identical pattern (`dadb5f2f…` zh vs `7b527337…` en). Before the config change, when `extraPaths` was empty/single-entry, the ambiguity did not surface, which explains why the first-ever terminal reindex "suddenly" broke retrieval.

## Why it matters
Every user on a CJK (or any non-ICU-default) locale who follows the documented "reindex after extraPaths changes" workflow from their terminal will silently permanently disable that agent's semantic retrieval, with no error pointing at locale. `TICKET`, `docs/reference/memory-config.md`, and the CLI give no warning.

## Expected
Index identity hashes are stable across processes on the same machine and same config — retrieval collation must not leak into a persisted identity hash.

## Actual
Persisted `meta.scopeHash` depends on the collation of whichever process happened to run the reindex.

## Suggested fix
Sort with a deterministic codepoint comparator, e.g.

```js
.toSorted((a, b) => (JSON.stringify(a) < JSON.stringify(b) ? -1 : JSON.stringify(a) > JSON.stringify(b) ? 1 : 0))
```

(or `new Intl.Collator('en-US', { usage: 'sort' })` with a frozen locale, or better: a locale-independent byte comparator). Note existing indexes written under another collation would need a one-time migration/explicit reindex check.

## Workaround (unblocks affected users today)
Reindex from the terminal with an explicit en-US locale so it matches the gateway's collation:

```bash
openclaw gateway stop
LANG=en_US.UTF-8 openclaw memory index --force --agent <id>
openclaw gateway start
```

(Equivalently `env -u LANG -u LC_ALL -u LC_COLLATE …`. Running the reindex via a session-side exec/agent that inherits the gateway environment is naturally consistent.) Verified to restore `memory_search` immediately on both affected agents.

## Repro (minimal, synthetic)
1. Config: one agent with `memory.search.extraPaths` containing ≥2 directory entries whose names sort differently under zh vs en collation (e.g. names starting with CJK characters plus ASCII names, such as `A…`/`资…`/`工…`).
2. Start the gateway as a launchd/systemd service **without** `LANG` (default).
3. From an interactive zh_CN.UTF-8 terminal: `openclaw memory index --force --agent <id>` → completes and logs files indexed.
4. `memory_search` on that agent → `disabled: true`, `index scope changed`. Repeat: still broken.
5. `LANG=en_US.UTF-8` reindex → search works again.

issues.body:
Part of #203737. This is one section of my Focus Week 5 work on the first run.

## Why

I believe trust in a first run is lost on the first unexplained failure. A guide, a birth, and a lobster do little for a person whose setup hangs on "Testing your AI connection", or whose app fails on first launch with "Permission denied".

Those failures are already filed. When I checked the open P0 issues on the first-run path, about a fifth were fixed on `main` and still open, and others had no owner. I believe part of making the first run work is plain housekeeping: check each one against current code, fix what can be proven, and give maintainers what they need to close the rest.

## How

Verify first: every open P0 issue about install, onboarding, first use, connecting providers, and connecting connectors is checked against `main`. Fix only what has no owner and can be proven on macOS. Each fix is its own pull request with a test that fails on `main` and passes with the fix, and can be merged alone.

For issues that are already fixed, offer the evidence on the issue so a maintainer can close it.

## What

- A verification of 68 open P0 issues against `main`. The result on 22 November 2026: 20 are still present, 15 have a fix in flight, 15 are fixed on `main` but still open, and 18 cannot be settled by reading the code.
- One pull request per fix, each with a test that fails on `main` and passes with the fix.
- Closing evidence for the 15 issues that are already fixed: for each one, the commit that fixed it and how to confirm it, offered on that issue.

## Out of scope

- Fixes that can only be proven on Windows, Linux desktop, Android, or a real iPhone. They are verified by reading and need an owner with that platform.
- Issues that already have a fix in flight. Their pull requests keep their owners.
- Running the macOS native tests on a developer machine. The repository allows them only in the `macos-swift` CI job.

## Pull requests, in opening order

Each sits on `main` and depends on no other.

- [ ] **#167636 Onboarding writes a default model the subscription lacks when the model list cannot be read.** The fix leaves the model unset and tells the person to choose one. Written. Three tests fail on `main` and pass with the fix. Also proven with the real CLI on isolated state. "Part of #167636": it covers one of the two ways the bug happens.
- [ ] **#185817 Model setup hangs on "Testing your AI connection" after the config write.** The wait gets a limit of 150 seconds. Setup keeps the saved connection and says it is saved and still being applied, with the next step. Written. Two tests fail on `main` and pass with the fix, and type checks, format, and lint pass. "Part of #185817": a real Gateway on macOS applied the setup in about a second and never stalled, so what makes it stall on the reporter's Windows machine is still unknown.
- [ ] **#198902 The macOS app fails on first launch with "Permission denied" and does not say which step failed.** The error names the stage and the path. Written. It compiles. Its Swift test has not run. This fixes the message only. The cause of the failure is unknown.
- [ ] **#141413 and #166707 The macOS app sends no token when the Gateway token is a stored secret.** This pull request makes the failure visible and names the next step. It does not fix the bug. It asks for the real fix, local pairing for the bundled app without the secret, which needs a security review. Written. It compiles. Its Swift test has not run.
- [ ] **#202258 Connecting with a setup code fails with "duplicate column name: setup_id".** Reproduced on unmodified `main` with an isolated Gateway: `openclaw qr` adds the column from its own process while the Gateway runs, and the Gateway keeps its old view of the schema, so every phone connect fails, also after a restart. The fix checks the table before adding the column and refreshes the Gateway's view of the schema the same way an in-process change does. The new test fails on `main` and passes with the fix, and the same real `openclaw qr` scenario connects on the fix. Routing `openclaw qr` through the running Gateway is the proposed follow-up, not built.
- [ ] **#168372 and #173204 Ask OpenClaw says an agent was created when nothing was written.** Reproduced on unmodified `main` with an isolated Gateway and a scripted model: when the step that reads the person's approval fails closed, nothing is created and the host adds nothing, so the person sees only the model's own text. The fix keeps fail-closed and adds a host line saying nothing has changed yet and how to apply or skip the change. The new test fails on `main` and passes with the fix. Written, and its tests, type check, format, and lint pass. The scripted model proves the host gap, not what a real model says.

## State, 22 November 2026

- Four of the six are proven. The two macOS app fixes compile, and their Swift tests have not run yet.
- The verification table and the closing evidence are local files. Nothing has been posted on any issue.

## This issue closes when

Each pull request in the checklist is merged, declined, or dropped with a recorded reason, and the closing evidence has been offered on the issues that are already fixed.

issues.body:
Observed on installed OpenClaw 2026.9.8. A bounded isolated cron test used a collector-mode profile spawn, explicitly collected its result, and continued in the parent to commit a verification marker through native automation scratch CAS. The requested terminal outcome was silent (`NO_REPLY`), with no child announcement.

Actual: child completion and parent continuation were verified, but the cron run ended after approximately 68 seconds with `Agent couldn't generate a response` and a warning that tool actions may already have occurred. Parent Gateway diagnostics reported `stopReason=stop`, `hasLastAssistant=yes`, `hasCurrentAttemptAssistant=yes`, `payloads=0`, `tools=6`, `replaySafe=no`. This was not a timeout. We have not rerun potentially side-effectful work.

Evidence limit: native history did not expose the parent final message, so we cannot independently assert that its authored final text was exactly `NO_REPLY`; zero terminal payloads and the completed parent marker are observed.

Installed-source candidate: `shouldTreatEmptyAssistantReplyAsSilent` delegates to `shouldSkipNonVisibleTurnRetry`, which rejects any retained `acceptedSessionSpawns`. `hasAcceptedSessionSpawn` checks nonempty length, regardless of collection/settlement; the incomplete-turn exemption instead checks `hasCompletionMessageSessionSpawn`, false for a collector (`expectsCompletionMessage:false`). Could a settled collector therefore block optional silence without owning a future completion message?

Expected regression coverage: completed collector + parent consumes result + permitted silence finishes successfully without announcement; outstanding collector/failed child/required-visible final retain their correct non-success or visible-response behavior. Do not blindly exempt every accepted spawn.

Related: #141556 / #141957 and #130675 concern silent terminal classification, but their documented causes differ. Please confirm whether this accepted-spawn variant is already tracked or fixed. This source analysis is based on installed shipped code, not a claim of reproduction on current upstream main.

Private prompts, tokens, channel IDs, session/job IDs and task data are deliberately omitted.

issues.body:
**Version:** 2026.11.6 (06afb10)

**Description:**
In multi-agent setups using inter-session messaging (`sessions_send` between agent sessions), two related transport defects appear intermittently:

1. **Echo-leak:** the final reply to an inter-session message gets enqueued back into the *source* session queue (echo), instead of being delivered only to the target session.
2. **Announce envelopes arrive empty:** delivery envelopes for announce-style inter-session messages sometimes reach the destination without payload.

**Expected:**
Replies are delivered exactly once to the target session; the sender queue is not modified. Envelopes always carry their payload; stale replies deduplicated.

**Actual:**
Replies mirrored into sender queue; empty envelopes; ordering races enable duplicate sends.

**Evidence (production instance, 2026-09-22 → 2026-11-22, condensed RCA):**
- Gateway = stock 2026.11.6 (06afb10); local plugins do not touch inbound Telegram nor inter-session delivery.
- Upstream issues with matching symptoms: #10377 and #61758 (inbound message duplicated ingestion ×2), #71761 (injected messages ×2 after 2026.4.23→.24 upgrade), #83404 (followup queue duplicate transcript writes via failover cascade).
- Operational lesson already adopted in production: checking `sessions_history` before any re-send avoids duplicates.

**Mitigations in production (reduce impact, do NOT fix the root cause — runtime queue):**
- Verify `sessions_history` before re-sending.
- Use `mode:"followup"` for fire-and-forget acks.
- Minimal replies to echoes (do not feed the loop).
- Treat empty envelopes as no-op (never re-deliver verdicts unverified).

**Notes:**
May be related to #10377/#61758/#71761 (duplicate ingestion) and #83404 (followup queue duplicate transcript writes). Workaround used in production: verify `sessions_history` before any re-send, prefer `mode:"followup"` for acks.

If I clear a failed job from my Inbox, I'd like it to stay cleared when I open the same gateway somewhere else. I can see the same failure again just by changing the address on one laptop.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open a local gateway at `http://127.0.0.1:<port>`. Sign in and open **Inbox → System**. Pick an enabled automation whose last run failed.
2. Dismiss the failed job and reload. The job stays hidden.
3. In the same browser, open `http://localhost:<port>` and sign in with the same gateway token. Open **Inbox → System** again.

I had the same Inbox open in two tabs. I dismissed **Archive check** in one and **Index check** in the other. Archive check disappeared from the first tab, then came straight back in both. Both jobs still had the same last-run timestamps.

## Steps to reproduce

1. In a fresh Chromium profile, open the same gateway URL in two tabs. Open **Inbox → System** in each. Start with two failed automations visible in both tabs.
2. Dismiss different rows in the two tabs at the same time. To make the timing repeatable, I scheduled the two X buttons to be clicked at the same timestamp. To try that in DevTools, pick a time roughly 30 seconds ahead with `Date.now() + 30000`. Copy that number into both tabs. Replace the sample name with the exact name of one visible job in the first tab and the other job in the second.

   ```js
   const at = /* paste the same timestamp in both tabs */ 0;
   const job = "Archive check"; // Use "Index check" in the other tab.
   setTimeout(() => {
     document.querySelector(`button[aria-label="Dismiss ${job}"]`).click();
   }, Math.max(0, at - Date.now()));
   ```

3. Compare the two Inboxes, then reload them. The timing matters. If both dismissals stick, open a fresh browser profile and repeat. I used a fresh session for each attempt and saw the loss on the second simultaneous attempt. Leaving a short gap between clicks saved both dismissals.

**Expected.** Both rows disappear from both tabs and stay dismissed after reload.

**Actual.** Only the Index check dismissal survived in the run pictured below. Archive check disappeared and returned in the first tab. It was still visible in both tabs after reload.

Both local-storage writes succeeded. The first value contained just the Archive check ID. The next contained just the Index check ID. Each tab reads, adds its own ID, and writes back the whole list. Two tabs can read the same starting list and overwrite one another. [Dismissal write](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/22255926f9cf4fd7a297d5a6dc3f6abe58c52d97/ui/src/components/sidebar-attention-dismissals.ts#L89-L108) · [Cross-tab refresh](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/22255926f9cf4fd7a297d5a6dc3f6abe58c52d97/ui/src/components/sidebar-attention-store.ts#L693-L705)

I paused a job after dismissing its failed run. When I enabled the job again, that same failure came back. The job wasn't due to run, and its history still had exactly one entry.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Create an enabled automation with its next run well in the future. Run it once and have it fail. I used a yearly job named **Archive check**.
2. In the Control UI, open **Usage**, select **All agents** in the agent picker, and open **Inbox → System**. Dismiss **Archive check**.
3. Leave that Inbox open. Run `openclaw cron edit <job-id> --disable`. Use `openclaw cron list --all --json` to check that the job has `enabled: false`. Give the open Inbox a moment to receive that change, then run `openclaw cron edit <job-id> --enable`.

**Expected.** Pausing the schedule shouldn't make me dismiss the same run twice. I'd expect a new failure to show up if the job runs again.

**Actual.** The row returns as soon as I enable the job. I checked `openclaw cron runs <job-id>` before and after. The run ID and timestamp were identical. Switching between individual agents and **All agents** on its own kept the row hidden.

While the job is paused, it drops out of the list of active failures. When the Inbox receives that list for **All agents**, it removes the job ID from its saved dismissals. Enabling it makes the previous failed status visible again. [Active failure check](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/22255926f9cf4fd7a297d5a6dc3f6abe58c52d97/ui/src/lib/cron-status.ts#L23-L34) · [Dismissal cleanup](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/22255926f9cf4fd7a297d5a6dc3f6abe58c52d97/ui/src/components/sidebar-attention-dismissals.ts#L179-L213)

## Summary

Move the shared iOS session presentation contract out of the Overview view into one app-internal owner.

## Problem to solve

Chat, Sidebar, and Sessions depend on `CommandCenterTab` for the session work-item type and title, detail, and relative-time formatting. These are shared presentation rules, but their owner is a separate screen.

## Proposed solution

Move the existing `WorkItem`, factory, and formatting implementation into an iOS-internal `SessionPresentation` owner. Migrate every production and test caller together and remove the old members without forwarding aliases. Keep the existing fields, defaults, colors, title priority, copied-key rejection, redaction, snooze behavior, and time formatting unchanged.

The cutover excludes routing, grouping, filtering, layout, refresh, mutations, and connection/permission policy. Regenerate the native string inventory for the five moved localized call sites.

## Alternatives considered

The shared chat formatter has different title fallback and redaction behavior. Substituting it would change the product contract. Keeping forwarding aliases on the Overview view would retain the dependency this change is intended to remove.

## Impact

No intended user-visible change. This reduces coupling for developers maintaining the shared session presentation rules. The small import/type-wrapper growth is justified by one explicit owner used by all four surfaces.

## Evidence and validation plan

The current source has the shared implementation in `apps/ios/Sources/Design/CommandCenterTab.swift` and consumers in `ChatProTab`, `RootSidebarSessionButton`, `CommandSessionsScreen`, and `CommandSessionRow`.

The owner of the overlapping Sessions PR approved a separate cleanup and will update its one factory call if this lands first: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192521#issuecomment-7085734637.

Validation will compare the moved bodies and fields, confirm no old member references remain, run native i18n generation/verification, and exercise the existing presentation/filter tests through the iOS app-hosted target. Existing Gateway connection test code will change only its helper receiver. No passing implementation result is claimed yet.

## Implementation intent

Yes, implementation and a focused PR are planned under the maintainer-requested iOS cleanup campaign.
