prs.title: feat: invite someone to help in one session without giving them Gateway-wide write access
prs.body:
Related: #201526

## What Problem This Solves

A session owner can't let one teammate type in one session without giving them write access to the whole Gateway. That access also lets them start their own Full-access sessions, send through channels, control nodes, loosen the owner's permission mode and approve the owner's commands. The only alternative is `operator.sessions.write`, which covers only a member's own sessions, so an invited member can watch but not type.

## User Impact

User impact: an admin can give a role an invite ceiling. A session's creator or an admin can then invite a person with that role into **one** session at **Can read**, **Can suggest** or **Can send**, without giving them any Gateway-wide write access. Gateways and roles that don't set the new field behave exactly as before.

- **Opt-in config:** `gateway.roles.definitions.<role>.sessions: { others: "invited", maxInvitedAccess: "read" | "suggest" | "send", invitedTools?: [...] }`. The invited person's role only needs `operator.sessions.read`. Example: `collaborator: { sessions: { others: "invited", maxInvitedAccess: "send" }, scopes: ["operator.sessions.read"], agents: ["main"] }`.
- **Choosing a level:** the creator picks the level when @mentioning someone (default **Can read**), and can change it later in the sharing panel. A new `session.members.setAccess` method backs this; `session.members.add` accepts an optional `access`.
- **What a Can send member can do:** `chat.send`, `chat.abort` for their own runs only, `session.typing`, and a `sessions.patch` that can only make the permission mode stricter, all in that session only. They can't create sessions or use channels, nodes or config. They also can't approve commands or change sharing.
- **How their turns run:**
  - Never looser than **Ask me**, worked out from the session's real effective policy, including Agent default.
  - Only the tools in a core-tool allowlist. The default list is `read, write, edit, apply_patch, ls, exec, process, web_search, web_fetch, tool_search, tool_describe, dispatch_action`, and `sessions.invitedTools` changes it per role.
  - Always queued as their own turn, never merged into another person's turn, and slash commands are ignored.
  - Only the OpenClaw runtime running locally on the Gateway; CLI, ACP, native harnesses and worker placements are refused.
  - `process` only sees commands from that session, and file tools stay inside that session's own workspace.
- **Approvals:** the session's creator approves commands from these turns, even without admin. The approval card says whose turn asked. The participant sees only a "waiting for approval" status.
- **Lowering or removing access** immediately cancels that member's queued and running turns. Re-inviting them does not bring those turns back.
- **⚠️ Database migration:** the agent database moves to **schema 44** (a nullable `session_members.access` column), which older builds cannot open. To downgrade, restore a pre-upgrade backup, as with any schema bump. This happens on every Gateway, opted in or not.
- **⚠️ Budget exception:** the Control UI **Chat** JS gzip budget goes from **1,332,637 to 1,336,683 bytes** (+0.3%), after making the invite bar and notices load only when needed (37.6% smaller than the first version). The SDK declaration budget is unchanged; the declarations are now 10.5 KB *smaller* than on the base.

## Why This Change Was Made

`sessions.others` was the only per-person control, and it doesn't separate seeing a session from acting in it. A stored per-member level, capped by the role, adds "this person in this session" without a new Gateway-wide scope. Admission to the fixed method list is checked against the exact existing session after membership is known, so nothing else is widened. Because a guest's turn uses the owner's agent, the limits on what that turn can do are attached to the input itself and travel with it through queuing, recovery, retries and model fallback. Changing the session's mode alone would not have been enough.

Design walkthrough and the decisions behind it: Josh's Participate design session. Builds on the role model in #201610 (OpenClaw ID members use the profile role). #201615's goals for invited members are covered here.

## Evidence

Real Gateway, real authenticated browser members (non-admin creator *Morgan*, collaborator *Alice*, viewer, admin) and a live model, in Crabbox containers on a Mac Studio. **Before:** `da816e2` (merge base). **After:** `9f459e5`. 1440×1000, dark theme, the same named test data. The images are wide, so each pair is stacked: before, then after.

### Clean comparison: invited member in the creator's session

**Before**: locked composer
![Before: invited collaborator sees "You need permission to send messages in this session" and a locked composer](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3f8f6fa9-2716-4da5-80c7-4ecb9cebd594)

**After**: Can send; composer unlocked, turns limited to Ask me
![After: collaborator's composer is unlocked and the permission chip reads "Ask me · set by Morgan Creator"](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/045aaa55-1d7d-4fb2-8487-8ff27831d8ca)

### Clean comparison: creator @mentions an invite-only person

**Before**: no way to choose access
![Before: creator's composer with an @mention of Alice Collaborator and no access choice](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/28d533f9-b010-4e84-852a-a3dd30a729bf)

**After**: invite level bar, default Can read
![After: a bar above the composer reads "Invite Alice Collaborator to this session as" with a "Can read" picker](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/aab616dc-a059-4ee1-9699-e6e4630fc7f2)

### Annotated comparison

![Before, annotated: the "need permission" notice is highlighted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/60636bf2-b73c-4990-984e-07488383c65e)
![After, annotated: the "Ask me · set by Morgan Creator" chip is highlighted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/76367767-fbdf-4935-8be6-c3fbf372cf5d)
![Before, annotated: the composer with no access choice is highlighted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1e02d306-0cb4-4521-b4a9-ce77aba3017c)

### After only: approvals and notices

![Creator's approval card: "Requested during Alice Collaborator's turn" with Deny / Always allow / Allow once](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3a2875d0-0fb5-49a0-9e06-14c9b0046845)
![Participant view: waiting-for-approval status and no approval buttons](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/130a7de0-7fc6-495b-97a7-1b2513e6cbfd)
![Transcript notices: "Morgan Creator invited Alice Collaborator with read access" and "changed Alice Collaborator's access to send"](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/32d38655-d1a6-4098-bee1-dd5b1d6bec58)

### Behavior checked on the real Gateway (all passed)

1. **No opt-in:** without `maxInvitedAccess`, the invited member's composer stays locked and `chat.send` is refused, as on main.
2. **Can read:** a real @mention invite creates the membership; the participant and the viewer are both refused when sending.
3. **Can suggest:** Alice's suggestion reaches Morgan, who accepts it, and the live model answers it.
4. **Can send:**
   - In a Full-access session Alice's turn shows **Ask me**, with only Read only and Ask me offered.
   - The model was given exactly the allowed tools (no `sessions_spawn`, `message` or `skills_read`).
   - An `exec` was approved by the **non-admin** creator, and the command really ran (`PARTICIPATE_EXEC_OK`).
   - Alice saw only "waiting", and her attempt to approve was refused.
5. **No escalation:**
   - Alice can't create sessions, switch to Full or pick ACP.
   - A tighten-only patch succeeds.
   - Alice's message sent during Morgan's running turn ran as its own turn and also needed approval.
6. **Revocation:** lowering Alice to Can read stopped her turn that was waiting on approval and cancelled her queued input, which never reached the model.
7. **`invitedTools`:** `["read","ls"]` gave the model exactly those two tools.
8. **Migration:** a real schema 43 database was migrated to 44 on first boot.

**Tests (updated at `d0f030c`):** removed the 582-line Participate mock-Gateway Playwright suite and consolidated redundant cases after a test-value audit. Cleanup is net **−581 test/support lines and 45 fewer registered cases**, including five cheap replacement unit rows for unique mention/composer behavior. Retained authorization, containment, revocation and migration boundaries; six guard-mutation experiments supported the audit. **574 selected cases passed** (including existing sibling cases, not 574 new tests), along with core/UI/test typechecks, generation guards, formatting and typed lint. Two independent Astra reviews of the cleanup/integration found no verified P0–P2 issues. The missing frozen-wrapper dependency inventory was reproduced and repaired.

**Current readiness (`d0f030c`):** rebased onto `bd67a3f9a184`; main advanced again and GitHub reports conflicts. The paired clean build measures Chat startup JS at **1,337,099 bytes**, **416 bytes above** the existing 1,336,683-byte cap. New and largest-JS budgets pass; CSS and request-count limits already fail on the paired base. The unchanged test-line allocation is still **2,179 lines short**; no further audited security-test deletion is justified. No additional budget or allocation increases were made.

**Gaps:**
- The screenshots and live-Gateway observations above are historical proof for `9f459e5`, not final-head live-Gateway proof for `d0f030c`.
- A previous combined participation-test timeout did not reproduce in the final combined run; no timing workaround was added.
- Revocation was shown on a turn waiting for approval, not on a shell command that is already running.
- Downgrading to an older binary is untested; it needs a backup restore, as described above.
- Hosted CI hasn't run yet.
- This PR isn't rebased onto #201610 yet. I'll do that once #201610 lands.

## Shared publication update (`f54cc17cd69e`)

Invited participants can publish through the Gateway's shared GitHub publisher without linking a personal account. The participant path does not select personal credentials, create personal publication sidecars, or fall back to a personal account. Ordinary human personal publication is unchanged.

The original participant, active invitation, tool ceiling and source remain attached to queued, child and task publication. Existing PR updates require linked authorship or the original participant's shared publication; contributor credit is not ownership. Original ownership survives a maintainer's later update. Both publication backends check reuse before external writes, including when new work has a different head. Workflow edits remain unavailable to participants even when their original connection had write scope. Attribution and publication handoff/cancellation behavior are preserved.

**Validation:** the final participant suite passed all 10 cases; both full publication-backend suites passed 67 cases after the last ordering repair. Earlier affected-owner suites passed 197 cases plus 3 native Gateway cases, with 10 handoff, 18 runtime and 16 prefix-stability cases also passing. Core and five affected test type graphs, scoped lint/format, generated config/validator checks and line caps passed. Independent full-delta review and follow-up correction reviews found and resolved the ownership defects; the final correction has no remaining verified P0–P2 findings. Regressions were observed failing before each repair, including extra local push and repository object/ref writes, then passing with zero unauthorized writes and a successful original-owner update.

**Test accounting:** removal of the rejected personal-publication scope and reuse of existing fixtures/tables reduced the candidate from 55 paths / 3,140 added lines to 41 paths / 1,938 added lines. The justified new allocation is 861 lines: full-PR test growth 8,863 minus the unchanged 400-line allowance and 7,602 existing allocation lines. No existing allocation, file cap or global threshold was raised.

**Current scope and gaps:** this remains a draft and GitHub reports conflicts with main. This update does not include a rebase, deployment, or live GitHub publication/model end-to-end proof; transport effects were verified at the registered Gateway and executor boundaries. The screenshots/live observations and broader readiness notes above are historical. Hosted checks for this head are not claimed complete.

🦞 Made with [OpenClaw](https://openclaw.ai)


### Rebase validation — November 21

Rebased onto `af7c2407dc41866b6b523019d16b8fcbe7cbf5ef`, retaining upstream worktree restoration and issue creation without widening participant authority. Published head: `a4dc3c2710d0ee55091528024832eaaa1282bbd3`. Agent schema remains 44 (unreleased), state schema 41; no collision with the pinned main’s agent 43.

- Full type graph and build passed; SDK declarations 5,297,055 bytes, below the unchanged limit. Generated protocol/config/database checks, changed-source formatting, import-cycle check, line caps and test-line budget passed. A one-line allocation covers restoring the historical migration fixture’s old column shape; no existing allocation, assertion or threshold changed.
- Owning Gateway tests: 223 passed; recursive spawn boundary: 144; affected agent support: 30; migration fixtures: 16; tool ceilings: 24; sharing UI: 13; descriptor/scope consumers: 85. Native admission/approval cases passed; isolated retained-child authority and upstream workspace restoration passed all 6 cases.
- Final paired UI: chat boot 1,334,367 gzip bytes against the unchanged 1,336,683 cap (+2,292 versus pinned main). Both use 21 requests against the 20-request cap. CSS ceiling warnings also occur on pinned main. The 23 remaining core-lint errors match pinned main exactly (25 there); no candidate-only lint error. Whole-worktree formatting flags only an excluded, pre-existing untracked proof artifact; all changed source and tracked docs are clean.
- The native child/grandchild completion proof still times out at its unchanged 120-second limit. A historical pre-rebase control at `82281c7` also reproduced the timeout with `source_owner_changed`; this is not an exact-head proof or a fresh full-native pass. No assertion or timer was weakened.

Review caught a static protocol-guard incompatibility in an intermediate extraction; the final version keeps method rows inline and passes the protocol guard.

The PR remains draft. No merge, ready transition, deployment or Gateway restart was performed; hosted checks remain separate from this local evidence.

Separate normal push: `fb87f37b81aacae72ea26214e6f8a2523c59b250`. Added `sessions_yield` to the default participant tools. It claims only the current participant turn’s own native children—not another turn’s children, background/runtime wakes, scheduler authority, or incoming message waits. prs.title: fix(plugin-sdk): honor declared DeepSeek reasoning efforts in OpenAI-compatible wrapper
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A `custom-compatible` DeepSeek Flash route that declares `low` as a supported reasoning effort still sent `reasoning_effort: "high"` when the user selected `low`, because the shared OpenAI-compatible wrapper ignored `compat.supportedReasoningEfforts`. This change resolves the effort from the model's declared capabilities, while keeping an explicit provider resolver authoritative and preserving the legacy fallback for undeclared models.

### Summary

The DeepSeek V4 OpenAI-compatible wrapper overwrites a declared Flash `low` effort with `high`. Resolve the effort from the model's declared capabilities instead.

- Use the existing model-aware helpers when `compat.supportedReasoningEfforts` is nonempty.
- Keep an explicit provider resolver authoritative and preserve the legacy fallback for undeclared capabilities.
- Preserve Pro behavior: unsupported `low` clamps to `high`, while `high` and `max` remain unchanged.
- Preserve disabled thinking, nonmatching models, and assistant reasoning replay.

### Validation

Validated against upstream `35b84dab3891fb9213a64300e968a59bbf78c8a8` with Node 24.22.1 and pnpm 12.15.0.

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
  --config test/vitest/vitest.plugin-sdk.config.ts \
  src/plugin-sdk/provider-stream-shared.test.ts
```

- Unmodified baseline: 28 passed.
- New regression tests against baseline production code: 39 passed, 2 failed with `expected 'high' to be 'low'`.
- Patched production code: 41 passed.

Both official typecheck lanes passed:

```sh
pnpm tsgo:core
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs \
  -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.plugin-sdk.json --incremental
```

Formatting and patch checks passed:

```sh
node scripts/run-format.mts --check \
  src/plugin-sdk/provider-stream-shared.ts \
  src/plugin-sdk/provider-stream-shared.test.ts
git diff --check
git apply --check upstream.patch
```

### Limitations

The full upstream test suite and PR CI were not run. Dependencies were installed with `--ignore-scripts`. The tests capture serializer payloads with stubs; they do not prove a remote provider's interpretation of effort or establish a latency improvement.

## Evidence

Environment: OpenClaw `2026.11.10-beta.1` (build `995f905`), CLI embedded run
(`openclaw agent exec`), provider `custom-compatible` (`api: openai-completions`),
model `deepseek-flash` with:

```json
"compat": {
  "supportsReasoningEffort": true,
  "supportedReasoningEfforts": ["none", "low", "high", "max"],
  "reasoningEffortMap": { "off": "none", "low": "low", "high": "high", "max": "max" },
  "thinkingFormat": "deepseek"
}
```

Command (endpoint and key redacted):

```bash
openclaw agent exec "Reply with exactly: OK" \
  --isolated \
  --model custom-compatible/deepseek-flash \
  --thinking low \
  --json
```

Requests were captured by a local logging reverse proxy in front of the real provider.
Before = unpatched bundle; after = same bundle with only the PR's changed statement applied.

### Before (unpatched)

```
2026-11-23T02:49:16.166+08:00  POST /v1/chat/completions
{"model":"deepseek-flash","thinking":{"type":"enabled"},"reasoning_effort":"high","max_tokens":4096,"stream":true}
2026-11-23T02:49:23.472+08:00  HTTP 200
CLI exit code: 0
```

### After (this PR)

```
2026-11-23T02:47:25.569+08:00  POST /v1/chat/completions
{"model":"deepseek-flash","thinking":{"type":"enabled"},"reasoning_effort":"low","max_tokens":4096,"stream":true}
2026-11-23T02:47:27.115+08:00  HTTP 200
CLI exit code: 0
CLI envelope: {"ok":true,"status":"ok","final":"OK","model":"deepseek-flash",
               "provider":"custom-compatible","usage":{"input":8761,"output":3,"total":8764}}
```

Notes:
- Both runs made real provider calls; no stubbed stream was used.
- The host has 8 GB RAM and cannot complete a full `pnpm build` (the build guard reports
  ~4.7 GB peak), so the runtime capture used the installed `2026.11.10-beta.1` bundle with
  exactly the changed wrapper statement applied. The before/after pair is otherwise identical.
- Endpoint, IPs, and API key are redacted.

prs.title: fix: open older session links without reloading chat
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Clicking an older session link in a chat message opens the right session, but first the whole Control UI disappears behind “Connecting to OpenClaw.” The browser treats the click as a new page load instead of a change of conversation.

## User Impact

Links for this Gateway with a full session key now look like other session links and open in place. Back returns to the original conversation without reloading it. Links to other Gateways still use normal browser navigation.

## Why This Change Was Made

Chat now uses the same legacy URL conversion as startup before handing the destination to the existing session router. It preserves the mounted path, dashboard or chat destination, other query parameters, and fragment. When an old link does not identify its agent, startup remains responsible for resolving it. No changes to native authentication or Gateway reconnect behavior.

## Evidence

In the actual Control UI in Chromium, a fixture message links to a second synthetic conversation. The same click replaced the document on `fb629723a4f3`; on `2dd499a2bc58` the destination rendered and Back restored the source with the same document time origin. The Gateway was simulated for this browser test; it does not diagnose a macOS authentication failure. Related: #203918 fixes a separate Knowledge link.

prs.title: fix(control-ui): show saved replies and skip an extra wait when opening active chats
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

If an assistant finished while you were reading another chat, returning to the original conversation could show its tool activity but not the saved reply. Separately, opening an active chat that the sidebar was already following made the UI wait for two consecutive Gateway responses before it could show any saved messages.

## User Impact

Reopening a conversation shows the saved reply beneath the tool activity without a refresh or follow-up message. When the sidebar is already following an active chat, opening it can now show its messages on the first Gateway response after the click.

## Why This Change Was Made

The sidebar can learn that a run finished before the retained chat receives its last message. On return, the chat compares the sidebar's last run with the one in its most recently loaded history. It catches up in the background without clearing the transcript. An unchanged, idle chat still reopens without fetching history again.

For an active chat, the sidebar already has a lightweight subscription. The client used to upgrade it to a full chat subscription without requesting history, then send a separate `chat.startup` request. The existing upgrade now carries the opening viewer's history request. Other viewers can share the observer, but not that one-time history response.

## Evidence

[Before and after: reopening the same synthetic conversation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/203938#issuecomment-7092264395)

In Chromium, returning to a conversation that finished in the background used to show only the tool call. With the fix, the saved reply appeared; a second return sent no extra history request. A separate isolated real Gateway run confirmed the saved reply appeared on return.

For the active-chat case, one browser kept a synthetic turn running and a fresh browser opened it from the sidebar. With each opening response delayed by 1.4 seconds, two matched baseline openings needed two round trips and took 3.42–3.43 seconds from click to visible saved message. All five openings with the fix needed one round trip and took 1.916–1.935 seconds (median 1.933). The Gateway returned the saved message on the existing subscription; the browser made no subsequent `chat.startup` request. These are controlled measurements, not production timings or evidence of a specific host bottleneck.

The design review covered placement of the recovered reply. Local autoreview found no actionable P0/P1 issues in the final diff against `e42e2404dc33`. No production conversations or recordings were used in the captures.

prs.title: fix: recognize Portuguese requests to search earlier conversations
prs.body:
Closes #195855

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Active Memory misses explicit Portuguese requests to search or review earlier conversations, and questions using the past-tense spelling `combinámos`.

## User Impact

People using these phrasings can pass the existing recall-intent gate. Future instructions, greetings, generic fix requests, and searches of current documentation retain their negative classification. This does not force deep recall on every message or change contextual follow-up handling.

## Why This Change Was Made

Extend two patterns in the existing Portuguese matcher. Conversation-search commands need an explicit match; `combinámos` distinguishes an unambiguous past agreement from the unaccented future-ambiguous form. The existing test tables gain seven positive controls and seven negative controls, with a separate allocation for their 14 lines.

This follows the Portuguese support in #135137; it does not replace that work or alter memory storage, authority, configuration, or diagnostic-prefix rendering.

## Evidence

[Current-head running-Gateway evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/195859#issuecomment-6822774006) now supplements the unit regressions. Exact clean head `bd4b96093bcc70718b186e8f01b4459ba8b57df1` was built through the supported source CLI and exercised via persistent `chat.send`, `agent.wait` and stored history with default escalation. Both `Pesquisa nas nossas conversas o que ficou decidido` and `O que combinámos para amanhã?` produced the actual recall-model HTTP request before the terminal answer. A future reminder, current-documentation search and greeting produced only the answer request with the no-recall-intent outcome. All five reached terminal replies.

External inference was synthetic and returned `NONE` for recall. This proves routing through the running Gateway and production prompt hook, not retrieval quality, a memory-tool result or live-provider reasoning. Empty memory used keyword/FTS fallback because the embedding provider was not loaded. No daily runtime, credentials or production source was changed; task processes stopped and ports closed. No before-fix Gateway run is claimed; the RED evidence below is unit-level.

Tested against public `main` at `7ebc4f3e67137c34b0850dfa8cab2b8d68e6576d`, with the same final regression cases on both sides:

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Base matcher with regression cases | Five intended false negatives fail; 175 tests pass |
| Patched escalation, prompt, and query owners | 180 tests pass across three files |

The native `run-vitest.mjs` owner command used `--maxWorkers=1`. The final baseline run took 40.74 seconds wall time; the cached passing run took 9.56 seconds. This is not a performance comparison. The tests make no live provider calls and do not establish model-driven deep-recall behavior.

Targeted type-aware lint, formatting, the test-line allocation ratchet, and the file-line cap passed. Independent review approved the production change; one redundant negative case was removed, retaining the explicit generic-request and greeting controls. The test allocation is exactly the 14 added lines.

4.9.9 - 2026-11-15

prs.title: fix: preserve completed Claude tool calls in chat history
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Reopening a Claude CLI conversation could show “Commands · Outcome unknown” for commands that had already returned successfully. The same command appeared complete while the conversation was live.

## User Impact

Successful calls stay complete after reload. Explicit errors still show as failures, and calls with no recorded result are not marked successful. No command is rerun.

## Why This Change Was Made

Claude CLI can omit `is_error` on a successful tool result. The history importer now interprets that omission the same way as live activity. Other providers and the shared activity renderer are unchanged.

## Evidence

Replaying the affected history changed seven recorded calls from unknown to completed. The browser showed “Ran commands” instead of “Commands · Outcome unknown.”

The [public, synthetic `chat.history` example](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/974e3e0d31c5d08d0dde7118f6d07cc4ac8c6dfb/src/gateway/server-methods/chat-history-handler.cli-import.test.ts#L212-L247) exercises three calls in the same response: `ok` → `completed`, `error` → `failed`, and `missing` → `unpairedCall: true`. [The case passed in the PR run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45097062119/job/137439675911). No private transcript is included.

The [only failing test in the PR run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45097062119/job/137439675747) checks cross-agent model inheritance during session creation, before chat history is read. [A scheduled run on unmodified `main`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45094583749/job/137431941353) reported the same case and assertion: expected `undefined`, received `"default"`.

prs.title: fix: reject hidden shell startup assignments in env commands
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Commands run through `env -S` can hide shell startup environment assignments from the command execution checks. A shell could then load a startup file before running the requested command.

## User Impact

Shell startup assignments such as `BASH_ENV` and `ENV` are rejected consistently, including inline and nested `env --split-string` forms. Ordinary environment assignments and commands keep their existing behavior. No configuration changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing `env` parser now retains assignment keys from split-string payloads. Both command environment validation and shell startup-file approval binding consume that information. The patch adds no new policy owner or configuration surface; its five-file delta is 65 additions and 8 deletions, including focused regression coverage.

## Evidence

At `d404f4c7d16df6a66e68dac8bf10bb5573015e0e`, a compiled CLI launched a real isolated loopback Gateway and node host on local Linux. The Gateway relayed `system.run` requests to the running node. Inline `BASH_ENV`, inline `ENV`, and nested split-string payloads were rejected with `SYSTEM_RUN_DENIED: command env assignment rejected`; the startup-file marker remained absent. A benign `env -S` assignment executed a real Node subprocess, exited 0, and wrote the expected control marker.

The focused node-host regression was also red on the base and green on this head. Parser and approval-binding tests cover the affected consumers. No agent/model turn, external channel, remote host, or other OS was exercised.
Focused validation passed: wrapper resolution (154 tests), approval binding (42), node-host environment (3), node-host invocation (58), command risks (31), and system-run command parsing (14). Focused lint, formatting, core typecheck, import-cycle check, and `git diff --check` passed. Environment: local Linux checkout, with separate temporary Gateway/node state and plugins disabled. The live proof used this head’s successfully built CLI.

<details>
<summary>Focused commands</summary>

```sh
pnpm test src/infra/exec-wrapper-resolution.test.ts src/infra/system-run-approval-binding.test.ts src/node-host/invoke-system-run.environment.test.ts src/node-host/invoke-system-run.test.ts src/infra/command-analysis/risks.test.ts src/infra/system-run-command.test.ts
pnpm tsgo:core
pnpm check:import-cycles
git diff --check
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>Running Gateway/node proof</summary>

The following CLI commands used separate private temporary state/config paths and a free loopback port. The node advertised only `system.run`, `system.run.prepare`, and `system.which`.

```sh
pnpm openclaw gateway run --port "$port" --auth none --bind loopback --allow-unconfigured
pnpm openclaw node run --host 127.0.0.1 --port "$port" --commands system.run,system.run.prepare,system.which --display-name isolated-command-proof
pnpm openclaw gateway call node.invoke --params "$params" --json --timeout 25000
```

Each `$params` contained the paired node ID, `command: "system.run"`, `params.command` set to one argv below, a unique idempotency key, and `timeoutMs: 15000`. `$payload` was a synthetic shell file that would write a marker if sourced.

| Command argv | Observed result | Startup marker |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `["env", "-SBASH_ENV=$payload", "bash", "-c", "echo main"]` | command environment assignment rejected; CLI exit 1 | absent |
| `["env", "--split-string=ENV=$payload sh", "-c", "echo main"]` | command environment assignment rejected; CLI exit 1 | absent |
| `["env", "-S", "env -SBASH_ENV=$payload bash", "-c", "echo main"]` | command environment assignment rejected; CLI exit 1 | absent |
| `["env", "-SPROOF_VALUE=okay", "node", "-e", "<write PROOF_VALUE to control marker; print benign-control>"]` | CLI exit 0; stdout `benign-control`; control marker contains `okay` | absent |

This exercises the real Gateway relay, node admission, and subprocess execution path without a model or external service. Regression risk is concentrated in shared `env` parsing and shell startup approval binding; ordinary subprocess controls and the related focused suites passed.

</details>

prs.title: fix: match macOS browser favicons to the app theme
prs.body:
## What problem this solves

When OpenClaw uses Light on a Mac set to Dark, a reading tab can ask a website for its dark-mode icon. A white icon then nearly disappears against the light tab and address bar. A second issue affects System mode: if macOS changes appearance while the Dashboard is hidden, reopening it can show the old icon even though the reading tab already has the new one.

## What changes

Reading tabs now receive the Dashboard’s resolved light or dark preference. Sites that follow that preference can update their content as well as their favicon. Sites that choose their own theme still can; OpenClaw does not recolor single-variant icons. When the Dashboard reopens, it presents the current native tab state without reloading the article or the Dashboard.

## Evidence

These are matching crops of the real macOS app in a disposable macOS VM. The article is a local fixture with separate light- and dark-mode icons and a fixed cream background. The explicit-Light comparison uses native main at `92e92d76b921` before and the PR’s native appearance change at `6f21272df04c` after; only the icons differ below the tab in this comparison. In a separate WebKit check on the reported GitHub page, GitHub’s own light- and dark-mode icons also changed. No provider-specific rule is involved.

| Before: white icon on Light | After: dark icon on Light |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: the white icon blends into the tab and address bar](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/818fbfa9-8eb2-4e87-b0f9-6aa4c1f37b20) | ![After: the dark icon is visible in both places](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ef53d4c9-d9fd-4fd7-926b-15e776b7b378) |

| Before, annotated | After, annotated |
| --- | --- |
| ![The arrow identifies the nearly invisible tab icon](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d5d12599-f988-425e-92f4-5c45b531f9bd) | ![The arrow identifies the dark icon in the same place](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e61411da-8638-44a6-a8b4-9488536d8e15) |

**System mode, retained window.** On the integrated candidate, we opened the article from Chat, hid the Dashboard, changed Light to Dark in macOS System Settings, and reopened the same window. The tab and address bar painted the new icon. The same article and Dashboard documents survived. The guest was returned to Light afterward.

![The same tab reopened on Dark, with a white icon in both locations](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6e3910c1-4a7b-4c85-9a6b-e2864b11cdd6)

Reported by and co-authored with @vyctorbrzezowski.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/ea87ebcf-4296-4703-a793-9a77b14d6627)

## Worked on by

- @vyctorbrzezowski

prs.title: fix: make openclaw available in new terminals when gateway install runs from npx
prs.body:
Closes #203942
Related: #200425, #192331

## What Problem This Solves

People who try OpenClaw only through `npx` have no `openclaw` command installed. When they then run `npx openclaw@<version> gateway install`, the command onboarding suggests for keeping the Gateway running in the background later, the Gateway service is installed, but new terminals still have no `openclaw`. The install prints `Terminal default unchanged: keeping ~/.npm/_npx/<hash>/node_modules/.bin/openclaw`: it treats npx's temporary copy as a command the user already chose, so it does not set up the terminal command.

## User Impact

User impact: when an install has no existing terminal command or configured profile, running `gateway install` from npx, or from another one-off runner such as pnpm dlx or bunx, now sets up the managed terminal command the way `docs/cli/gateway/service.md` describes. It creates `~/.openclaw/bin/openclaw`, which runs the service's copy in `~/.openclaw/npm`, and appends to shell startup files the same guarded PATH line that other first installs add, so new shells find `openclaw`. An `openclaw` the user already has on PATH is still kept, including one listed after the runner's directory. Runs whose PATH contains no one-off runner directory are unchanged. Only builds that include the terminal command step (#200425, on main) are affected; the released 2026.11.6, 2026.11.7 and 2026.11.10-beta.1 do not have it yet. No new config, flags, or defaults.

## Why This Change Was Made

The terminal command step (`installGatewayTerminalCli` in `src/daemon/terminal-cli.ts`) looks up `openclaw` on the install process's PATH and keeps any match that is not its own launcher (`:150-180` on `3c8c7bf`; line numbers below are on that commit). Under npx, that PATH has npx's `.bin` directory ahead of the account's own directories, so the first match is npx's copy. #192331 already treats these copies as disposable (`isDisposableInstallPath` in `src/daemon/durable-service-entrypoint.ts`, whose comment says a service "must never point into one or keep one on its PATH") and leaves their directories out of the service PATH (`src/commands/daemon-install-plan.shared.ts`). This change applies the same check to the terminal command lookup: PATH entries whose real path is a one-off runner directory are skipped before the lookup, and every other entry is passed on as written. The rest of the step is unchanged.

Skipping the runner's directories, rather than treating a runner match as "no selection", keeps the existing rule for every other directory: if the user's own `openclaw` comes later on PATH, it is still found and kept, with the existing message.

Unchanged on purpose: the desktop app's `setup --terminal-path` path, which has the same lookup but runs only from the desktop app's own CLI; the PATH setup at CLI startup; how the launcher and the startup-file line are written; `isDisposableInstallPath` itself. This change is limited to the terminal command step; install paths that do not run that step are unchanged.

Known limits: the lookup still follows the existing rule for every other directory on PATH. An `openclaw` in a directory that the CLI adds to PATH at startup but that is not on the user's interactive shell PATH is still kept, as on main and as for runs outside npx. Only directories that `isDisposableInstallPath` classifies as runner caches are skipped; an `openclaw` link that points into a runner cache from another directory is still kept, as on main. That check matches path segment names, so it also skips a PATH entry whose real path contains a segment equal to `_npx` or `dlx`, matching `dlx-<digits>`, or starting with `bunx-` or `.bunx-`, even when it is the user's own directory; the guarded startup-file line still leaves an `openclaw` that the shell already finds in place.

<details>
<summary>Implementation notes</summary>

- Each PATH entry is classified by `fs.realpath`, falling back to `path.resolve` when the entry cannot be resolved, as #192331 does for the service PATH. Unlike that loop, entries are not trimmed, and empty and relative entries are kept, because the terminal lookup (`resolveExecutablePathAsync`) still searches relative entries and drops empty ones itself.
- The kept entries are joined back as written, not as real paths, so the "keeping" message is built from the user's PATH entry, not from its real path.
- If every entry is skipped, the lookup gets an empty PATH and finds nothing; it does not fall back to the process PATH.
- The first-install check (`:172-180`) and the later branch used by reinstalls and named profiles (`:187-195`) read the same lookup result.
- Against `3c8c7bf`: `src/daemon/terminal-cli.ts` +10/−1 (one import), `src/daemon/terminal-cli.test.ts` +38.

</details>

## Evidence

"Before" results were taken on main `3c8c7bf`. "After" results were taken on `3c8c7bf` with this PR's change applied: the focused tests ran with this PR's full diff applied (the same tree as commit `bd8df34f48b4`), and the after run used a package built from `3c8c7bf` plus this PR's production change.

Real runs through npx, before and after:

- **Setup**:
  - Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS (x86_64). Each run used a fresh, disposable Linux account with its own systemd user manager, Node v24.22.1 from nodejs.org and npm 11.19.1. Before each run, the account had no `openclaw` command and no `~/.openclaw*` directories.
  - The package was built with `scripts/package-openclaw-for-docker.mjs` (version 2026.11.6), because the released 2026.11.6, 2026.11.7 and 2026.11.10-beta.1 do not include the terminal command step.
  - Both runs used `npx --yes --package <package> openclaw gateway install --port 21789`, with `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PORT=21789` and a custom systemd unit name; the terminal command step reads neither.
  - The service is set up to run npm's `openclaw@2026.11.6` copy in `~/.openclaw/npm`.
  - "New shells" are a fresh `bash -lc` and a fresh `bash -ic`, both under `env -i` with PATH set to the system directories.
- **Before** (`3c8c7bf`, 2026-11-22):
  - `gateway install` exited 0; the user service was installed and `enabled`, with `ExecStart` pointing to `~/.openclaw/npm/lib/node_modules/openclaw/dist/index.js`.
  - The only line about the terminal command was `Terminal default unchanged: keeping ~/.npm/_npx/<hash>/node_modules/.bin/openclaw; this Gateway: …`.
  - `~/.openclaw/bin/openclaw` was not created, `~/.bashrc` and `~/.profile` were unchanged, and in both new shells `command -v openclaw` found nothing.
- **After** (`3c8c7bf` plus this change, 2026-11-23, another fresh account):
  - After the install, running the same package with `npx --yes --package <package> -c 'command -v openclaw'` printed `~/.npm/_npx/<hash>/node_modules/.bin/openclaw`, the same `<hash>` as the copy the install ran from, so npx's copy was still the `openclaw` found on npx's PATH, as in the before run.
  - `gateway install` exited 0; the user service was installed and `enabled`, with the same unit file and `ExecStart` as before.
  - The install printed no `Terminal default unchanged` line and no other message about the terminal command.
  - `~/.openclaw/bin/openclaw` was created (a regular file owned by the account, mode 755); it runs `<node> --max-old-space-size=8192 ~/.openclaw/npm/lib/node_modules/openclaw/dist/index.js` and does not point into `_npx`.
  - `~/.bashrc` and `~/.profile` each gained one line at the end, `if ! command -v openclaw >/dev/null 2>&1; then export PATH="$PATH":~/.openclaw/bin; fi` (home shown as `~`), and were otherwise unchanged.
  - In both new shells, `command -v openclaw` printed `~/.openclaw/bin/openclaw`, and `openclaw --version` in a new login shell exited 0 with `OpenClaw 2026.11.6 (06afb10)`.
- The change is in the terminal command step of `gateway install`: no agent or model is involved, and it does not change update, Doctor, config, or state, so no agent run or upgrade run is attached. The latest stable release does not have this step, so an upgrade from it takes the first-install path.

<details>
<summary>Redacted terminal output (before and after)</summary>

The account's home is shown as `~`, the Node binary as `<node>`, and the npx cache key as `<hash>`. The new-shell checks are shown as the command and its result.

Before:

```text
Terminal default unchanged: keeping ~/.npm/_npx/<hash>/node_modules/.bin/openclaw; this Gateway: <node> --max-old-space-size=8192 ~/.openclaw/npm/lib/node_modules/openclaw/dist/index.js --profile default
bash -lc: command -v openclaw   -> no output
bash -ic: command -v openclaw   -> no output
```

After:

```text
(no line about the terminal command)
~/.openclaw/bin/openclaw:
  #!/bin/sh
  # OpenClaw managed terminal CLI
  export OPENCLAW_PROFILE="${OPENCLAW_PROFILE:-default}"
  exec <node> --max-old-space-size=8192 ~/.openclaw/npm/lib/node_modules/openclaw/dist/index.js "$@"
~/.bashrc, last line:  if ! command -v openclaw >/dev/null 2>&1; then export PATH="$PATH":~/.openclaw/bin; fi
~/.profile, last line: if ! command -v openclaw >/dev/null 2>&1; then export PATH="$PATH":~/.openclaw/bin; fi
bash -lc: command -v openclaw   -> ~/.openclaw/bin/openclaw
bash -ic: command -v openclaw   -> ~/.openclaw/bin/openclaw
bash -lc: openclaw --version    -> OpenClaw 2026.11.6 (06afb10)
```

</details>

Focused tests (`src/daemon/terminal-cli.test.ts`):

- A new table runs the terminal command step with a one-off runner's `.bin` first on PATH, laid out like npm (`.npm/_npx/<hash>/node_modules/.bin/openclaw` linking to the package's `openclaw.mjs`), pnpm 9+ dlx (a `dlx` segment) and bunx (a `.bunx-` segment). Each row expects no warnings, and that a new `bash -ic` with only `/usr/bin:/bin` on PATH runs the installed launcher.
- A new case puts the user's own `~/.local/bin/openclaw` after an npx `.bin` on PATH, and expects it to be kept, with the existing message and no launcher.
- The existing cases keep their assertions: a user's command first on PATH, normal first installs in each shell, an operator-owned file at the launcher path, and another configured profile.
- On `3c8c7bf` with only the test change, the 4 new cases fail at their own assertions: the three table rows at `expect(f.warnings).toEqual([])`, each receiving `Terminal default unchanged: keeping <runner dir>/.bin/openclaw; this Gateway: …`, and the after-runner case because the message keeps the runner's copy. The other 32 pass, and 7 are skipped (the zsh rows run only on macOS, and fish is not installed on that host). With this change, 36 pass and 7 are skipped.
- `pnpm test src/daemon/terminal-cli.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 39 s wall time with this change (41 s before); Vitest reports 34.6 s, about 96% of it module transform (about 1 s of test time), and the new cases take 5–33 ms each.
- Consumer: `src/cli/daemon-cli/install.integration.test.ts`, which runs `gateway install` through to this step, passes (18 tests).
- Targeted checks: oxfmt and oxlint (0 warnings, 0 errors) on the two changed files, `pnpm tsgo:core`, and `git apply --check --whitespace=error` on the diff pass.
- `pnpm check:changed --base 3c8c7bf` for the two changed files passes locally, including `check:import-cycles` and `check:max-lines-ratchet`.
- Local review: autoreview (P0–P2) on the full diff against `3c8c7bf` reported no findings.
- CI: pending at the time of opening

Not covered:

- Only npx was run live; the pnpm dlx and bunx rows cover the same path check that #192331 uses for the service PATH.
- "New shells" are fresh `bash -lc` and `bash -ic` processes with a clean environment, not new SSH sessions.
- macOS was not run, live or in tests: the focused tests ran on Linux, and macOS CI runs a fixed list of tests that does not include `src/daemon/terminal-cli.test.ts`.
- zsh and fish were not run: their existing rows are the 7 skipped tests above. This change does not touch how startup files are written.

prs.title: fix: remove the updater runtime a shipped update leaves behind on the next update
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a shipped updater (for example npm 2026.11.6) updates an install to the current release, it keeps its own running code in an `openclaw-update-runtime-*` directory, about 640 MiB, and prints `Runtime retained at …: worker generation settled; cleanup deferred to the next eligible update or openclaw doctor --fix`. Every later update now runs on the prepared-release path (`src/update/`), and that path never ran this cleanup. The directory stayed forever, and the message was untrue.

## User Impact

User impact: the next `openclaw update` after a shipped in-place update removes the leftover updater runtime and says so (`Removed abandoned updater runtime: …`). This covers updates with or without a running Gateway, the Gateway's `update.run` and its automatic updates. A runtime that another process may still use is kept, the update reports why, and the update never fails because of it.

## Why This Change Was Made

Only the legacy in-place executor (`src/infra/update-retained-runtime.ts`) and Doctor called the cleanup owner, `maintainRetainedUpdateRuntimes`. Release updates did not call it.

- `prepareUpdate` (`src/update/run.ts`), which every release update goes through, now runs that owner after admission and before staging. It uses Doctor's discovery of where runtimes can be (temp directories, state `tmp`, package parents, plus the running root, which recognizes a runtime a shipped updater projected for the package it replaced). It records what it removed or kept as a `retained-runtimes` run step. A thrown error becomes a recorded line, and the update keeps its outcome.
- `openclaw update` also runs it in its own process before it asks the Gateway. Shipped updaters wrote no `owner.json`. For such a runtime the census has to treat any live `openclaw update` process as a possible holder, because an old updater loads code from its runtime while its argv names the installed package. So the Gateway cannot remove it while the requesting CLI waits, but the CLI, as the inspector, can.
- Doctor's helper is split into `prepareRetainedUpdateRuntimeMaintenance`, which returns lines, and the existing Doctor wrapper, which notes them. There is still one cleanup implementation and one custody decision.
- The retained message now says what happens: `the next update or openclaw doctor --fix removes it once no OpenClaw process uses it`. This text is in main's legacy executor, which still serves the routes that have not moved (`--tag main`, channel switches between Git and package, `--dry-run`). Shipped updaters keep their old text, which becomes true with this change.

Update behavior for published updaters: no change is needed in a shipped updater. Its first update still retains its runtime as before. The next release update, run by the new code, reclaims it. No config key, stored field, schema, protocol or dependency changes.

Automation: nothing is left to a person in the covered case. A runtime is kept only when custody cannot be shown (another possible holder, or processes that cannot be listed), and every later update retries it. Inside a Linux container the census refuses because host processes are not visible (existing behavior from #154324), so container installs keep the runtime and the line says to run Doctor on the host.

## Evidence

**End to end, same installed-package cell on base and head.** The cell is a real systemd user Gateway (systemd as PID 1, lingering user manager, real user bus) with a busy database writer (256 MiB, 1 MiB/s). It installs published `openclaw@2026.11.6` with npm and runs `openclaw update --yes` three times: to T (main plus a version bump to 2026.11.11, served as registry.npmjs.org inside the container), to T1 (bump to 2026.11.12), and a no-op repeat. It then runs `openclaw doctor --fix`. The cell hides Docker's container markers (no `/.dockerenv`, private cgroup namespace) so the census behaves as on a host; otherwise both base and head keep the runtime with the container message.

| After step | Base `82848e3103d` (red) | Head `42f0c9b4c1f` (green) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| u1: 2026.11.6 → T (shipped updater, in place) | runtime kept: 655444 KiB (640 MiB) in `$TMPDIR`, no `owner.json` | same: 655444 KiB, no `owner.json` (the shipped updater's own step) |
| u2: T → T1 (`openclaw update --yes`, Gateway route, trigger `api`) | still there, 655444 KiB | **`Removed abandoned updater runtime: ~/um/tmp/openclaw-update-runtime-9hgkGW`**; cell `$TMPDIR` 696 MiB → 82 MiB after the update |
| u3: no-op repeat | still there | none |
| u4: T1 → T2 (head only, T → T+1 → T+2) | not run | none, update succeeded, serving 2026.11.13 |
| `openclaw doctor --fix` with the Gateway running | refused (`Gateway process changed during maintenance drain`); still there | refused the same way; nothing left to remove |

The red run was captured twice with the same result (runtimes `B0Hz4W` and `LKCYWe`). Per-directory figures come from the cell's own sampler: cell `$TMPDIR` baseline, peak extra, extra after the update, in MiB; red u2 `696 / +472 / +27`, green u2 `696 / +0 / −614`. Route facts for each update: the run trigger (`cli` for the shipped updater, `api` for release updates); the Gateway journal shows `[gateway] update.run <runId> actor=gateway-client`; the service runs `~/.openclaw/git-install/openclaw-launcher.mjs` from a unit that `openclaw gateway install` wrote. The cell sets no `OPENCLAW_UPDATE_PACKAGE_SPEC`, `--tag`, `--no-restart` or shortened `--timeout`. The served dist-tags were `latest` = each candidate, `beta` = `2026.11.10-beta.1`. T, T1 and T2 are version-bump-only builds of the tested commit; they prove the switch and the cleanup, not a migration.

Recordings (asciinema, rendered to MP4):

RED, base `82848e3103d` (asciinema of the live cell, then the raw evidence):

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6029a92d-7ca9-4c55-9fce-bf5a7850add1

GREEN, head `42f0c9b4c1f`:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f9c355d8-d77b-4301-b6da-02a0306bf238

SHA-256: red `a18d672f…65003`, green `427ac74b…0768f`. The full raw cell logs are not attached because the Crabbox artifact store rejected the upload (`http 401`); the decisive lines are below.

<details><summary>Raw lines from the cells (paths shortened to ~)</summary>

Red, u1 (shipped 2026.11.6 updater):
```
[infra:temp-artifacts] Runtime retained at ~/um/tmp/openclaw-update-runtime-LKCYWe: other OpenClaw processes are still running (PIDs: 2312, 3076, 5186); let these holders finish, then rerun openclaw doctor --fix
[infra:temp-artifacts] Runtime retained at ~/um/tmp/openclaw-update-runtime-LKCYWe: worker generation settled; cleanup deferred to the next eligible update or openclaw doctor --fix
```
Red, u2 / u3 output: `Updated to 2026.11.12.` / `Already up to date.`; layout after each: `RUNTIME 655444 KiB ~/um/tmp/openclaw-update-runtime-LKCYWe owner.json=no; runtime-count=1`.

Green, u2:
```
Removed abandoned updater runtime: ~/um/tmp/openclaw-update-runtime-9hgkGW
staging: staging
staging: prepare:pack
staging: prepare:install
validating: validating
validating: service-definition
restarting: restarting
finished: restarting
Updated to 2026.11.12.
```
Green layout: `after-u1-T RUNTIME 655444 KiB … owner.json=no; runtime-count=1`, then `runtime-count=0` after u2, u3, u4 and Doctor.

Doctor, both cells:
```
Doctor could not enter maintenance. Error: Gateway process changed during maintenance drain Stop the Gateway service and other OpenClaw processes using this state, then run openclaw doctor --fix from an independent shell
```
</details>

**Focused tests** (fail on base, pass on head):

- `src/update/prepare.test.ts` › `retained updater runtimes`: a real `openclaw update --no-restart` on a dev checkout that is already current, with three ownerless projections in the fixture temp directory. One is abandoned, one is held by another process, and for one the census fails. Result: the abandoned one is removed, the other two stay, all three lines are recorded and printed, and the run still ends `already-current`. On base, the abandoned runtime is still there.
- `src/update/cli.test.ts`: the CLI reclaims before it sends `update.run`, prints the lines, and in `--json` mode sends them to stderr so stdout stays the record. When it falls back to updating in its own process, it prints a kept runtime once, not twice.

<details><summary>Test and check commands (head 42f0c9b4c1f)</summary>

Red (production files from base, tests from head):
```
× src/update/prepare.test.ts > retained updater runtimes > reclaims an earlier updater's runtime and keeps uncertain ones without failing
  → promise resolved "undefined" instead of rejecting
× src/update/cli.test.ts > reclaims earlier updaters' runtimes itself before the Gateway updates (json=false|json=true)
  → expected "vi.fn()" to be called with arguments: [ ObjectContaining{…} ]
× src/update/cli.test.ts > prints a kept runtime once when the update falls back to this process
  → expected [ 'Already up to date.' ] to deeply equal [ …(2) ]
```
Green on head:
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` across `src/update/*.test.ts`, `src/infra/update-retained-runtime*.test.ts`, `src/flows/doctor-retained-runtime*.test.ts`, `src/infra/temp-artifact-cleanup.test.ts`, `src/commands/doctor-maintenance.requester-authority.test.ts`, `test/scripts/eager-import-closure.test.ts` and `test/scripts/update-restart-module-outcome.test.ts`: all passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:core:test`: passed.
- oxlint on the touched files: clean. `pnpm check:docs`: passed. `git diff --check`: clean.
- `pnpm check:baseline-ratchets --base 2e8c1ad0aa9 --no-merge-base`: all ok, including test-lines and session-identity.

</details>

**Test file audit.** `src/update/prepare.test.ts` and `src/update/cli.test.ts` were read whole.
- prepare.test.ts: every case now runs real retained-runtime maintenance through `prepareUpdate`, so `beforeEach` keeps `TMPDIR`, `TMP`, `TEMP`, `OPENCLAW_HOME` and the package-root discovery inside the fixture. No case can touch the host's temp directories.
- cli.test.ts mocks reclamation (prepare.test.ts covers the real thing). `afterEach` now restores spies: `defaultRuntime` spies previously leaked between cases.
- cli.test.ts's package target followed a hard-coded `2026.11.6`, so after main moved to 2026.11.7 three cases took the downgrade-confirmation branch and failed on base `096214ac84d`. They now use the running `VERSION`, and the downgrade cases still set their own older target.
- `src/infra/update-retained-runtime.test.ts` and `src/infra/update-retained-runtime-exit.test.ts` only change the expected message text (`worker generation settled; the next update`); their positive and negative assertions keep the same meaning. I reviewed both files' structure (cases, mocks, the single platform `skipIf`, teardown) and found nothing dead or redundant to prune.
- Nothing was removed.

**Independent review.** A fresh read-only reviewer (`autoreview` does not run on this machine) found nothing blocking. I fixed its findings:
- the no-Gateway fallback printed kept lines twice (fixed, with a failing-first test);
- a failure-path test was missing (added: the census failure case);
- an assertion that mirrored the implementation (removed);
- a comment on why Doctor's same-process worker fence does not apply (added).

Its remaining notes are accepted tradeoffs, listed under Not proven.

CI: `checks-node-changed-5/6` failed on the first head because two legacy tests asserted the old message text; fixed in `d5a65e784d6`.

## Not proven

- Real hosts outside Docker: the cell imitates a host by hiding the container markers, and the census itself ran for real.
- pnpm: one earlier pnpm acceptance cell printed `no recognized runtime marker` for a 2026.11.6 runtime. That is pnpm projection recognition inside the existing owner, not this path, and is not changed here.
- On a release-path install with a running Gateway, `openclaw doctor --fix` stopped with `Doctor could not enter maintenance. Error: Gateway process changed during maintenance drain` in the base cell, so the "or openclaw doctor --fix" half of the message did not hold there. This PR makes the update half true. The Doctor maintenance issue is separate and is reported as a follow-up.
- Inside the Gateway, the census for a candidate runtime is synchronous, with a budget of about one second. It blocks the event loop briefly, once per leftover runtime.
- For a CLI-requested update, the Gateway's own pass can record the requesting CLI's PID as a holder for an ownerless runtime that the CLI kept. The line is true but noisy.
- The update proof rules in `docs/install/updating.md` (#203915) ask for runs on four platforms. Only the Linux systemd user service ran here. The Linux container (no user bus), macOS LaunchAgent and Windows Scheduled Task runs are unproven; in a container the census refuses by design, so the runtime stays and the line says why. The T builds are version bumps, so no migration or rollback ran (not affected by this change).
- `src/update/AGENTS.md` came from main unformatted, which failed `check-docs`' format step; this PR includes the formatter's output for it.

prs.title: l10n(sv): translate native status labels
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Swedish native-app catalogue still exposed one hundred and twenty-one ordinary interface labels in English across Android, Apple and macOS. This translates user-facing labels for skills, session search and history, web search, Git incheckning, pull-begäran, support, connection state, the offline Gateway state, the automatic system-icon choice, and common session-tool actions. It also completes everyday tool names such as pin, import, set groups, roles, notify, tool call, get goal, conversation send, screenshot, computer, attach and events, as well as task, media and conversation actions. The latest batch covers memory and media actions including get memory, image generation, upload, role management, view image, screen recording, screen snapshot and timeout, while retaining identifiers, commands and product names unchanged.

## Evidence

- `apps/.i18n/native/sv.json` parses as JSON.
- Hunspell-sv recognizes every newly introduced Swedish word.
- svlang finds no issue in the reviewed individual labels; its combined-input warning is a false V2 result caused by concatenated UI fragments.
- A focused Gitleaks scan of the new values found no secrets.
- The existing Swedish catalogue already uses `Ansluten`, `Frånkopplad`, `Färdigheter`, `incheckning` and `pull-begäran` for the relevant concepts.
- The current PR revision passed `native:i18n:verify` in an isolated checkout: 4,873 native entries, 21 Android app keys, 4 third-party Android keys, 131 Wear keys and 1,784 macOS source keys.

`native:i18n:sync` also passed without contradictions, generating Android, Apple and 84 InfoPlist resources. The reviewed Swedish values are present in the generated Android, iOS and macOS catalogues. Rebuilt-app screenshots are still not attached, so this PR remains open for runtime verification.

## Follow-up review

Nine additional native labels now use established Swedish UI terminology: `Kodkörning`, `Tillägg`, `incheckning`, `Ansluten`, `Frånkopplad` and `Stöd`. Their source contexts were checked in the Android, Apple and macOS code paths. JSON parsing, Hunspell-sv, svlang and a focused Gitleaks scan pass for this follow-up. `l10n-lint` does not support this versioned native JSON catalogue.

Two further tool labels are included in the latest revision: camera list is now Kameralista and camera PTZ is now PTZ-kamera. PTZ is retained as the established technical abbreviation; Hunspell-sv does not contain it.

The latest follow-up also replaces Presence and Sub-agent with the established terms Närvaro and Underagent, consistent with the Swedish Control UI translation memory.

A further reviewed batch translates twelve user-visible tool actions: channel, edit, emoji list, event create, poll, present, reactions, sticker, stop, tabs, thread create and wake. The Swedish values retain only established technical abbreviations and no command identifiers.

The current revision also replaces the remaining visible native connection labels and counters with Ansluten, Frånkopplad and anslutna. Placeholder syntax is unchanged.

The newest follow-up replaces five visible uses of patch in the Android session-diff view and tool display with Swedish terms for an edit or change comparison. The remaining svlang hits are code placeholders only.

prs.title: fix(issue-203912): automated resolution by Harness
prs.body:
Resolves #203912

### Autonomous fix summary
Fixed the GatewayDrainingError re-claim storm in `src/channels/message/ingress-drain.ts`.

**Root cause:** When a `GatewayDrainingError` occurred, `applyFailureDisposition` released the claim with `recordAttempt: false` and immediately returned, so the retry policy never applied. The pump re-claimed the event every ~45 ms, and each re-dispatch ran the Discord preflight which downloaded and saved the attachment again, causing 154,374 duplicate files (205 GB).

**Fix:** Removed the early return that short-circuited the retry policy for `GatewayDrainingError`. Now the error falls through to `retry.failure()` which:
- Records the attempt and applies backoff instead of immediate re-claim
- After the retry limit is exceeded, fails the claim (dead-letters the event)
- Prevents the storm even when global admission is open but a per-session admission is closed

The comment explains that the original intent of preserving the row for successor dispatches after a gateway restart is handled by the retry policy itself - when the limit is exceeded the claim is properly settled, and on restart the row will be unclaimed and can be re-admitted when the lane opens.

### Verification and diagnostics
- **Model:** `auto`
- **Step Budget:** 45 max steps
- **Quality Score:** 0/100
- **Changes:** 30 modified lines
- **Sandbox:** `docker`
- **Job ID:** `25dbcfd4-2916-49db-99f9-480f9327be5c`

## What Problem This Solves

`src/update/cli.test.ts` fails on `main` (3 cases: "preserves a one-off package tag" ×2, "restarts the local Gateway after preparing an explicit package tag"). Its fixture, added in #203497, pins the selected release at `2026.11.6`. Since `main` moved to `2026.11.7` (#203880, release close-out), those cases see a downgrade, wait for downgrade consent (unanswered in the test) and prepare nothing. It turns `checks-node-changed-1` red on PRs that touch the update CLI (seen on #203925).

## Change

The default selected release is the build's own `VERSION`, set before each test; the downgrade case uses `2000.1.1`, which stays older than any build. Explicit `--tag` inputs are unchanged.

## Evidence

- `ocx test src/update/cli.test.ts`: 17/17 (main at 2e8c1ad0aa97: 3 failed, 14 passed).

prs.title: fix: let background reviews keep the session's hosted web search
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A background session fork that runs its own tools dropped the provider-hosted `web_search` tool from its request, even when the parent session listed it. The skill-workshop review is one example. Its tool list then differed from the session's, so on a provider with hosted search every review request missed the session's prompt cache from the first token. The review paid for the whole prompt each time.

## User Impact

A background review now lists exactly the session's tools, including hosted web search, and reads the session's cached prefix.

**Owner decision (security trade-off):** this was approved explicitly as a product choice. A review fork can now run a hosted web search when its session allows hosted search. Hosted search runs at the provider, before any local tool gate, and the native endpoint has no provider-side way to list a tool but block it (`tool_choice: allowed_tools` returns `400 invalid_value`). So listing the tool and allowing it are the same decision. Review forks stay read-only otherwise: no new write or exec tools are granted, exec stays owner-gated as before, and a tool-free fork still sends `tool_choice: none`.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Removed the special case.** `attempt-stream-settle.ts` no longer applies the fork's execution cap to hosted search. `sessionForkGatesHostedTools` (the "tool-free forks only" rule) is deleted.
- **Byte replay of a live parent:** `applySessionForkRequest` no longer falls back to the rebuilt request when the parent lists a hosted tool. A fork with tools now replays the parent's bytes in that case too.
- **Kept:** the execution cap still governs hosted search for non-fork runs that set one (for example the system agent's `toolExecutionAllow: ["openclaw"]`). Deleting the whole clause would widen those runs, which is outside this decision.

**Production LOC:** +10 / −25, net **−15**.

## Evidence

**Prefix journey (#201723): new step "fork of a parent that lists hosted web_search".** A parent chat runs on a hosted-search route: the router plugin's hosted route, with the real `nativeWebSearchAllowedByToolPolicy` policy input. It lists `{type: "web_search"}`. A fork with a granted client tool (like the skill review) must send tools byte-equal to the parent's, including `web_search`. Only Responses carries provider-hosted search, so the step runs on that lane. The other four lanes run the rest of the journey unchanged, with tool-free forks.

| | Responses lane |
|---|---|
| base 096214ac | **red**: `A fork with a granted client tool must preserve the parent's hosted web_search tool bytes` (the fork omits `web_search`) |
| head | green (anthropic, bedrock, google and completions lanes also green) |
| mutation: restore the execution cap for forks (`attempt.sessionForkRequest !== undefined ||` removed) | **red**, same assertion |

**Transport contract** (`test/embedded-agent-attempt-stream-transport.test.ts`):

- A fork granted only client tools (`skill_workshop`) now lists hosted `web_search`.
- A capped non-fork run still does not.
- Client tool schemas are unchanged, and only a tool-free fork sends `tool_choice: none`.

`session-fork-request.test.ts`: a fork with tools replays a parent request that lists a hosted tool.

**Scratch Gateway E2E.** Native `https://api.openai.com/v1`, `openai/gpt-6.2-astra`, SSE, code mode, with the bundled skill-workshop background review firing after a subagent settles. A scratch-only patch captured every request body and its `response.completed` usage. The driver is the same on both sides.

| request | base 096214ac: tools / tool hash / input / cached | head: tools / tool hash / input / cached |
|---|---|---|
| parent, last request before the review | 8 / `3d88f97d` / 19,830 / 18,659 | 8 / `3d88f97d` / 19,839 / 18,669 |
| skill-review fork | 7 / `2dc7c3ea` / 15,169 / **0** | **8 / `3d88f97d`** / 19,615 / **18,669 (95%)** |

On base the fork's tool hash differs from the parent's and the fork reads nothing from cache. On head the fork's tool list is byte-equal to the parent's, and the fork reads the parent's whole cached prefix.

prs.title: fix: keep browser error details beside the message
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a Browser tab reported an error, **Show details** always occupied a second row, even if the message and control fit side by side. The strip took space away from the page underneath.

## User Impact

The message and **Show details** now share a compact row when they fit. On narrower panels the control moves below without clipping the message. Opening it still shows the full diagnostic beneath the row.

## Why This Change Was Made

Only the Browser panel’s inline error strip needed a different layout. The existing disclosure, keyboard controls, text size, and browser error handling are unchanged.

## Evidence

I clicked Reload on a mounted Browser tab with a simulated Mac host returning an error. At 390, 820, 1180, and 1440 CSS pixels wide, the collapsed strip went from 66 px to 41 px. At 320 px the control wrapped without clipping. Enter opened the full-width diagnostic and Space closed it without moving the control or losing focus. These screenshots are Chromium captures with synthetic tab data, not a native Mac capture. Baseline: `e42e2404dc338`. Fix: `7ec12a1566696`.

### Clean comparison

**Before**

![The error and Show details occupy two rows](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8d090774-f857-4965-b131-7b22090944b0)

**After**

![Show details sits beside the error on one row](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/19bc4ad0-056f-4d57-aae4-1bd17fead25d)

### Annotated comparison

**Before**

![The disclosure is below the message in a 66 px strip](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/85e54d36-03dc-457f-9845-73f64d586a5a)

**After**

![The disclosure is beside the message in a 41 px strip](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9125a0aa-57df-4691-9b98-5b6ff83d3e74)

Contributor: @vyctorbrzezowski.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/0bfa560b-6bf6-4ea6-aea6-4b52c7042325)

prs.title: feat(workboard): preserve common work objectives
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A shared Work could lose or replace its admitted objective as lifecycle and dispatcher operations crossed the runtime boundary. Discovered side objectives could consume resources without explicit approval, and ordinary helpers or specialists could interject into the user flow despite the admitted single reporting lead.

## Summary

- preserve admitted Work objective, scope, acceptance criteria, and reporting lead across lifecycle transitions
- classify discovered side objectives without allowing them to replace or consume resources from the admitted objective
- enforce one reporting lead while retaining normal reporting for directly requested specialists
- expose the complete strict contract through the Workboard Gateway runtime boundary

## Evidence

- focused Vitest: 36/36 passed across common-work, objective-boundary, and Gateway schema suites
- strict focused TypeScript: passed
- Oxfmt: passed
- test-line ratchet: passed with +533 net test lines and 133 allocation credit
- source-boundary line-cap and max-lines ratchets: passed
- git diff --check: passed
- native security review: no sensitive product changes

Queue #499. Clean origin/main lineage; excludes Queue #491.
