prs.title: perf(update): reuse verified database digests within one update run
prs.body:
Related: #182616

## What Problem This Solves

Within one update run, Doctor hashes the same unchanged SQLite files in full again and again while the Gateway is stopped. Each Doctor generation read starts a fresh worker, so no verified digest survives to the next read, and a database without a journal or WAL is hashed twice per read (provisional and final). On a 10.8 GB test state, 23 processes hashed and SHA-256 took 93.5 s of CPU in a 304.7 s stopped window (profiled run), hashing files nothing was writing.

Goal of this PR: inside a Doctor database write capture, an unchanged database file is hashed in full on its first read only. Later reads in the same capture reuse the digest that capture verified, under the exact fingerprint and age rule from the maintainer answer on #182616 (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/182616#issuecomment-6930916800).

Result against that goal:

- An unchanged family with no journal or WAL hashes 0 bytes on its second read in a run (4,218,880 bytes with the production change reverted).
- On the 10.8 GB state, processes that hashed fell from 23 to 4, and SHA-256 CPU in the stopped window from 93.5 s to 35.9 s: Doctor 42.3 s to 15.9 s, post-update verification 39.5 s to 8.0 s.
- The hashing left is each Doctor process's first read of each database and the activation snapshot, which this PR does not change.

Out of scope: the rest of #182616 is not addressed here. Already merged: #182632 (digest reuse within one check) and #187921 (candidate state inventory without a database copy). Open in separate PRs: #200916 (agent file scanning during update preparation), #201093 (plugin downloads before the Gateway stops) and #200908 (cold-history navigation after readiness). Still open on #182616 itself, per the maintainer updates there: the native SHA-256 speed gap in `@openclaw/fs-safe` (a dependency change) and Doctor's other whole-database reads.

## User Impact

Shorter Gateway downtime during updates on installs with large SQLite state, as a result of the hashing removed above. On a 10.8 GB test state the Gateway was down for a median of 233 s instead of 293 s (3 runs per side). Updating from the latest stable release (v2026.11.5) on a 10.7 GB state, it was down for 415 s instead of 481 s (one run per side). Nothing changes for small installs, and there is no new setting.

## Why This Change Was Made

Following the maintainer answer on #182616 (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/182616#issuecomment-6930916800, "don't redo verified work within a run"):

- The Doctor database write capture owns a digest map for its run, in memory only. Its generation reads, and the migration attribution reads inside it, pass the map to the existing generation worker and take back the digests the worker verified. Nothing is written to disk and nothing outlives the capture.
- A digest is reused only while the file matches the recorded fingerprint exactly (`dev`, `ino`, `size`, nanosecond birth, m and c times) and passes the existing `canRetainDigest` age rule. A new, recent or imprecise-timestamp file hashes fresh. Every family with a journal or WAL hashes fresh.
- Only a worker from the same runtime exchanges digests. Seeds leave the map before the worker runs; only a successful worker writes digests back.
- The activation snapshot, restore verification and refusal paths are unchanged.

Final-check reuse: this extends reuse to the final check of a read, not only the provisional read. The maintainer answer on #182616 covers that step: "yes, carry verified digests across generation observations within one update run", with the fingerprint, age rule, in-memory scope and unchanged snapshot and restore paths listed above. Before this change a read of a database without a journal or WAL always proved fresh bytes at its final check, and `readUnchangedUpdateDatabaseGeneration` said "Never carry a digest reader across observations". That comment now states the new rule. A first read in a run still hashes fresh bytes twice; a later read of an unchanged file hashes none. Reuse at the provisional read only was measured first on an earlier version of this branch: hashing CPU in the stopped window fell from 92.7 s to 64.2 s, and the stopped window did not change beyond run-to-run noise. That is why reuse reaches the final check.

Accepted edge case: a write that leaves size and all nanosecond timestamps identical to a digest older than 2 s (for example a clock stepped back and a same-size write in the same timestamp quantum) would be read as unchanged for the rest of that update run. Per the boundary in the maintainer answer, no code is added for it.

## Evidence

Before and after on one machine, state and driver (macOS arm64, 32 cores, NVMe; Git install updated by driver 2516bca9fdb through `update.run`; synthetic state built through Doctor's legacy import, all SQLite). Base is 53278c30303; the fix is b9d1882fab5 (this branch). Runs alternate base and fix.

Since those runs the branch merged main at 95449145a82 and added a test fixture field (`rebuiltIndexAlternates`, required on main since #201330), the digest reuse paragraph in `docs/install/updating.md`, and a replacement for the write capture test. The production change is the same as b9d1882fab5 apart from the merge resolution: the generation worker keeps main's unmarked-read path and `inspectEngine` parameter, and paired reads pass the run's digests as a trailing argument.

Large state (4 agents, 16k sessions, 2.54M transcript events, 240k memory chunks, 10.8 GB agent SQLite, 42k state files), 3 unprofiled runs per side:

| Step (median, range) | base | fix |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| activating (Gateway stopped) | 283.2 s (278.9 to 287.9) | 224.3 s (217.5 to 249.9) |
| . database snapshot | 56.7 s (55.3 to 56.7) | 57.7 s (56.3 to 59.6) |
| . openclaw doctor | 109.3 s (107.0 to 110.3) | 84.0 s (79.9 to 101.7) |
| . post-update verification | 96.1 s (95.0 to 98.8) | 61.3 s (59.1 to 65.8) |
| Gateway down (`/readyz`, 250 ms poll) | 292.6 s (288.1 to 296.4) | 233.3 s (226.5 to 259.2) |

Runs in order (activating / Gateway down): base 278.9 / 288.1, fix 217.5 / 226.5, base 287.9 / 296.4, fix 224.3 / 233.3, base 283.2 / 292.6, fix 249.9 / 259.2. Other jobs shared the host during these runs.

SHA-256 CPU inside the stopped window, from `--cpu-prof` on every process (one profiled run per side; profiling adds time):

| | base | fix |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| processes that hashed | 23 | 4 |
| database snapshot (activation snapshot, unchanged) | 11.7 s | 12.1 s |
| openclaw doctor | 42.3 s | 15.9 s |
| post-update verification | 39.5 s | 8.0 s |
| total SHA-256 CPU | 93.5 s | 35.9 s |
| activating (profiled) | 304.7 s | 237.4 s |
| Gateway down (profiled) | 315.4 s | 249.5 s |

The hashing left in Doctor is each Doctor process's first read of each database; the post-core Doctor runs in its own process and starts with an empty map.

Small state (57 MB SQLite), one run per side:

| | base | fix |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| activating | 98.3 s | 91.6 s |
| Gateway down | 107.3 s | 100.4 s |

Latest-stable upgrade, v2026.11.5 to this head, with settings and data checked before and after:

- Driver: a Git install at v2026.11.5 (e13cf15ece9), detached at the tag, built with `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && pnpm ui:build && pnpm build`. Its own `openclaw doctor --non-interactive --fix` imported the legacy state, then a v2026.11.5 Gateway ran on it before the template was saved, so every database was last written by the stable release.
- Settings: loopback Gateway with token auth, 4 agents with their own workspaces, `update.channel: dev` (the route from a stable Git install to an untagged commit).
- Update: `openclaw gateway call update.run` on the running v2026.11.5 Gateway, so the v2026.11.5 updater runs preflight, candidate Doctor, activation, Doctor and post-update verification. Targets are this head b9d1882fab5 and its base 53278c30303. Both report version 2026.11.4 because main's package version has not moved past the release.
- Settings and data check: settings above, row counts of `session_windows`, `transcript_events` and `memory_index_chunks` in every agent database, and `PRAGMA quick_check` on every SQLite database, read from the template before and from the updated state after.

| v2026.11.5 to | small (61 MB): head | large (10.7 GB): base | large (10.7 GB): head |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| result | succeeded | succeeded | succeeded |
| activating (Gateway stopped) | 125.5 s | 471.4 s | 406.1 s |
| . database snapshot | 2.7 s | 78.1 s | 57.6 s |
| . openclaw doctor | 47.3 s | 314.1 s | 278.0 s |
| . post-update verification | 43.8 s | 35.3 s | 29.5 s |
| Gateway down (`/readyz`, 250 ms poll) | 134.6 s | 481.2 s | 415.2 s |
| settings, row counts, quick_check after | identical, 6 of 6 ok | identical, 8 of 8 ok | identical, 8 of 8 ok |

Doctor takes longer here than in the main-to-main runs above because it migrates state last written by v2026.11.5 (the state database goes from 103 to 104 tables). Other builds and tests shared the host during these runs, which also slowed the unchanged snapshot step (78.1 s and 57.6 s); one run per side is not enough to size the gain from stable.

<details>
<summary>Runtime output: v2026.11.5 to b9d1882fab5 on the large state (selected lines from the harness log, host redacted)</summary>


Tests:

- `update-database-generations.test.ts`: an unchanged family with no journal or WAL hashes 0 bytes on its second read in a run (2 x size on the first); a new inode with the same bytes, changed timestamps with the same bytes, and a content write are all hashed fresh at both checks; a journal that appears after the digest is hashed fresh.
- `update-doctor-result.test.ts`: a write capture runs the real isolated generation worker. After its first read, the test replaces the recorded digest with a wrong one that keeps the file's fingerprint. The capture's next read then reports the database as changed, which only happens if the worker reused the recorded digest instead of hashing. A second capture over the same file starts with its own map and reads the file as unchanged. The worker's clock runs 3 s ahead so the file passes the age rule without the test waiting.
- That test fails when the capture stops passing its map to the worker, when the worker is sent no earlier digests (`expected true to be false` on the changed-database check), and on 95449145a82 with the production change reverted.
- On the merged head, against 95449145a82: the focused update tests pass apart from the two named below; with the production change reverted and the tests kept, the unchanged-file test fails (4,218,880 bytes read, expected 0).
- `update-doctor-migration-attribution.test.ts`: two "completes retirement after Doctor migrations" tests fail with `JSON Parse error: Unexpected identifier "state"`, the same on 95449145a82 without this change.
- `pnpm check:changed` against 95449145a82: every step passes except the dead export scan, which lists unused exports in `src/cli`, `src/config`, `src/cron`, `src/gateway` and `src/update` files outside this diff, the same on the base.

Gaps: three runs per side on one machine, with other jobs on the host; one stable-to-base and one stable-to-head run on the large state; synthetic state built by the product's legacy import, not a copy of a real install; one attempted large pair failed on both sides at the driver's git checkout ("Unable to create" a file in the install, before any database step) and was rerun; no external plugins; a Git install with a foreground Gateway rather than npm with launchd or systemd. The driver's recovery capture (activation snapshot) is not changed.

prs.title: fix(update): report deferred update inspections as progress, not warnings
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A first update from a published OpenClaw release can finish with warnings for inspections that the updater deliberately scheduled after restart. Those notices make a successful update look like it needs manual repair.

## User Impact

Planned inspection deferrals no longer add attention warnings. Real findings, incomplete inspections, and required validation errors remain visible.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove the candidate lint's synthetic scope-warning findings. Doctor already reports planned deferrals as progress, and the installed updater runs the deferred checks after the restarted Gateway is ready and saves their results in `post-activation doctor inspections`.

Both v2026.11.6 and v2026.11.7 have that post-ready owner. Prepared-release updates call `update check-release`, not candidate Doctor lint, and do not emit these scope warnings. Adding advisory Doctor execution to that separate release path is not part of this change.

No state, flags, hooks, or timers were added. Genuine budget-exhaustion deferral diagnostics are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Regression fails against the unchanged `origin/main` producer: two synthetic scope warnings instead of no planned-deferral findings. The same test preserves explicit selection and required-error behavior.
- Five focused test files, the full package build, and focused lint/format pass. Exact-head local review is complete with no findings.
- `check:changed` stops in the existing SQLite worker ratchet with a 4 GiB Node heap exhaustion; it does not reach the remaining stages.
- CI's unrelated `src/update/AGENTS.md` formatting failure is tracked in #203921 and reproduced on the exact main base; see the override comment.
- The required Linux systemd Control UI first hop from published v2026.11.7 is pending the shared registry-fixture recipe. The macOS click was a setup failure (`already-current`), not update proof. Required live proof remains a landing gate.

Related: #203743

prs.title: fix: honor Azure Sandbox memory limits and worker sizes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Azure Sandbox worker commands inherit the Gateway's host memory reserve and can be stopped below the Sandbox's own limit. Worker sizing also exposes generic machine classes instead of Azure's native CPU, memory, and disk tiers.

## User Impact

Dedicated Azure Sandbox workers on updated node hosts use the provider's outer memory boundary. Operators can select native tiers from XS through 3XL in the machine picker or configure `settings.type`; generic classes keep their existing 2 CPU / 4 GiB mapping. Gateway commands and workers on shared hosts retain host memory protection.

Older node-host supervisors retain the previous safeguard until the node host is updated. Refreshing only the worker bundle does not enable the new behavior or require replacing the retained workspace.

## Why This Change Was Made

Ports `feaa5332d4b`, including the prerequisite launch-descriptor and exec plumbing. Only a deployed worker with authenticated provider launch authority uses the Sandbox memory boundary. Tool arguments and environment variables cannot grant it. Older supervisors receive a compatible descriptor without forcing reprovisioning or replaying started work.

The refreshed baseline preserves Gateway cgroup discovery and reuse, idle cache reclaim, and cleanup after process extinction alongside the dedicated-worker change.

## Evidence

- At `a9cd529291` (main parent `b151c83071`), 11 focused Linux test files passed, including cgroup and supervisor tests, real process cleanup, worker launch negotiation, inventory, and Azure sizing. Core and full extension test types, targeted type-aware lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed; there were zero static import cycles.
- Independent source review of the refreshed integration found no P0–P2 issues. The added and removed product lines match the previously reviewed range, where full committed-range autoreview (`35a75a4a73`, Codex `gpt-6.1-sol`, P0–P2) found no actionable findings. The local ClawSweeper and autoreview attempts for the refreshed range produced no verdict.
- At `81953704f8` (main parent `577af7ba2a`), the full updated subagent-completion restart fixture passed with pinned Bun, and five focused worker, supervisor, cgroup, and profile files passed. The update incorporates the upstream restart/custody repair (#203839). Independent integration review found no new P0–P2 issues; all 34 PR paths have identical before/after blobs and modes compared with the previous candidate.
- [Hosted CI for `81953704f8`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45114660929) **failed**. Each of its six failed jobs reproduced independently on the exact tested main parent `e42e2404dc`, with the same pinned Bun version for the test fixtures. The failures were formatting in unchanged `src/update/AGENTS.md` and tests for worker destination preparation, Gateway update CLI, device-folder creation, imported PR actions, and PR workspace preparation. The relevant failing inputs are identical in the CI merge. `security-fast` passed. The aggregate CI gate remains red; this evidence supports only the repository’s inherited-failure route, not a passing CI result.

**Proof gaps:** Live Azure provisioning and a full latest-stable upgrade with retained leases and workspaces were not run. The tests exercise the profile and negotiated launch boundaries.

<details>
<summary>Previous CI and implementation proof</summary>

[Run 44784820554, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44784820554) was red on the prior head `35a75a4a73`. The hook concurrency, delegated effects, and Telegram final restart failures matched on its exact main parent `09bef75c4f` with the pinned Bun runtime. The Steer FIFO database rollback did not reproduce locally on that parent or on the tested PR merge; it remained unclassified. The refreshed baseline includes the upstream delegated-effects test repair (#202655) and changes in the state read path. Fresh CI is needed to assess the effect of those changes.

[Secretless AWS implementation proof](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_6192d89f8cd2d1ac6e00a1f06097c1e0) verified source tree `8813aed38ec381d40090f2bbbe09d744afeb8003` before execution: 251 focused tests passed and the CI artifact build verified all 163 public Plugin SDK subpaths. Its Control UI size-budget overruns were advisory; no budget was changed.

[The base-supervisor negative control](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_ba61dd0f5ccfa8df2da666edadbdb37a) stopped the command under the host reserve; the corrected worker completed it. The base launch adapter also failed by sending an unsupported field; the corrected old/new-host cases passed while preserving workspace and launch identity.

</details>

Original PR by @galiniliev.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/bbdbf84b-add1-4a3a-bdf0-1abb08f8aebc) — review corrections and verification.

prs.title: fix(ui): keep plugin links in chat from reloading the dashboard
prs.body:
Related: #168743

## What Problem This Solves

Opening a Knowledge record link from chat reloads the Control UI and forces a new Gateway sign-in. If macOS native sign-in fails during that reconnect, the dashboard can become inaccessible even while the Gateway is reachable.

## User Impact

Knowledge links in chat open the requested record within the current dashboard. Back returns to the original chat without reloading it.

## Why This Change Was Made

Route same-origin plugin links in the chat transcript through the existing app navigator. This preserves the plugin URL and normal behavior for modified clicks, downloads, and links targeting other windows. Native authentication and its retry policy are unchanged.

## Risk and coverage

- The existing Knowledge browser scenario reproduced the full document reload on `main`. With the fix, it checks that the correct record opens, the document and record parameters are preserved, and Back restores the chat. Both Knowledge browser scenarios passed.
- Scoped lint, UI typecheck, formatting, and independent review passed.
- The browser test runs the Control UI against an isolated Gateway fixture. It covers removal of the reload trigger; it does not reproduce or fix the underlying macOS sign-in refusal.

prs.title: fix: explain why oversized videos cannot be sent
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Drop a large video into the command palette and try to send it. The attachment offers **Compress to fit**, but the composer says **Reading attachment**. Waiting does not help: the video needs a decision, not more time to load.

## User Impact

The composer tells you why the video cannot be sent and offers two choices: compress a copy or remove it. It says **Compressing video…** only after you choose to compress. The original is unchanged, and the message still waits for you to send it.

## Why This Change Was Made

A video waiting for consent and a file being read both count as pending attachments. The palette, New Session and Chat now use the video's existing preparation state to explain the difference, including to screen readers. The attachment limits and send rules are unchanged. With multiple attachments, the notice prioritizes the video that needs a choice rather than listing every pending file.

## Evidence

In the built Control UI in Chromium, the same drop and send shortcut produced the misleading notice before the fix and the actionable notice after it. Choosing compression prepared a smaller copy; only a separate Send submitted it. A mobile Chat run also checked that the encoder did not load while waiting for consent. The recordings and Gateway responses were synthetic.

Local autoreview examined the committed diff from e42e2404 to 1b46caa1 and reported no actionable P0–P2 findings. This was a diff review, not a live Gateway run.

**Before**

![The video offers compression while the composer says Reading attachment.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/019e56aa-7969-4aec-9a9f-eac72049abf5)

**After**

![The same composer explains that the video is too large and can be compressed or removed.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b43f34a1-1e80-4eb1-82e4-89b207eb8931)

**Annotated comparison**

![Before: the read notice persists while waiting for a choice.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5c36ff68-78ab-4fad-a511-3469ea418dfe)

![After: the notice explains why sending is blocked and what to do next.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/78cd2cc3-fcf3-4665-8d86-d86381638704)

prs.title: fix(update): refuse --full-integrity-check on the release update path
prs.body:
Closes #203629

## What Problem This Solves

Git and npm, pnpm, or Bun release updates accept `--full-integrity-check` but do not run the requested checks. This can make an operator believe a safety check ran when it did not.

## User Impact

The command now refuses this flag before it creates an update run or delegates to the Gateway. The error names `openclaw doctor --fix --full-integrity-check` for separate migration checks and explains that it is not a scan of an already-current database. Update without the flag afterward.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing release-admission refusal for unsupported local-override replay. No new option, update state, verification path, or protocol. Help and the two update guides no longer promise unsupported checks. The existing refusal regression is extended rather than adding a second fixture.

## Evidence

The new regression fails on origin/main: the integrity request resolves instead of refusing. The real packaged base CLI also silently accepts the flag, exits 0, and creates an `already-current` run. On the fix, the focused package/CLI suites and all 47 direct-importer tests pass. The full build passes.

On an isolated converted npm install on macOS, `openclaw update --full-integrity-check --json` exits 1 with the intended reason and Doctor command. The four pre-existing update run IDs, statuses and reasons stay identical; no row is added. The complete release-store layout and file hashes are identical before/after. The isolated foreground Gateway keeps the same listening PID and socket descriptors and stays ready throughout. Conversion setup uses a disposable local-registry candidate; the refusal invocation has no package-spec override, tag, restart flag, registry override, or timeout.

`check:changed` passes its first four guards, then the SQLite-worker ratchet runs out of the local 4 GiB Node heap. This is a known local limit; hosted CI owns that remaining check. Targeted lint passes. Canonical packed-tarball integrity and import-graph checks pass. Local ClawSweeper review of `0815be6d5416` is complete: correct, zero findings.

CI `check-docs` reports only unchanged `src/update/AGENTS.md` formatting from the base. [Base reproduction and inherited-failure note](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/203926#issuecomment-7092074652). This PR leaves that file unchanged.

This change is CLI admission only; it does not change the launcher or installed release preparation. Cross-platform managed-service update execution is unproven and blocks stable claims; no such execution claim is made here.

prs.title: refactor(github): migrate repository integration to a plugin
prs.body:
## Summary

Depends on #192349. Review and merge the SDK foundation first.

GitHub repository integration spans account connections, repository discovery, execution identity, publication, and browser presentation. This PR moves the vendor implementation into the bundled `github-repositories` plugin using [the Plugin SDK foundation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192349).

The plugin supplies the existing GitHub workflows. OpenClaw retains sessions, approvals, local Git custody, durable account/publication records, and recovery. Generic SDK additions belong to the foundation; this consumer supplies GitHub registration, lifecycle, configuration migration, and presentation.

**Upgrade:** run `openclaw doctor --fix` to move legacy native GitHub settings into `plugins.entries.github-repositories.config`. Explicit plugin allowlists and deny rules remain authoritative; include `github-repositories` to use this integration.

The independent `github` plugin continues to own `github_read`, `github_search`, public link previews, and reader views. GitHub Copilot, Gateway sign-in, and verified profile identity remain separate owners.

## Ownership

| Capability | `github-repositories` supplies | OpenClaw retains |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Accounts and OAuth | Credential selection, GitHub transport, refresh policy, and connection presentation. | Canonical managed/personal account records, profile authority, config writing, and refresh settlement. |
| Repository sources | Discovery, URL admission, authenticated clone/fetch, repository/object identity, and worker adapters. | Picker/session admission, checkout storage and leases, worktree placement, accepted checkpoints, and recovery. |
| Execution identity | Identity facts, credential scrubbing, private child-launch adapters, and supported sandbox preparation. | Command policy, approvals, final launch, and sandbox provisioning/permission. |
| Publication | GitHub targets/content, remote operations, and author/coauthor policy. | Local Git/index custody, verified participant/consent facts, exact receipts, accepted-operation settlement, and live effect authority. |
| Agent tools | `github_identity_status`, `github_publish`, and their policy descriptions. | Caller-bound dispatch, workspace access, tool/child-policy ceilings, handoff, and cleanup. |
| PR/check presentation | Reads, subscriptions, plugin read store, badges, actions, Settings, and session accessories. | Session/audience admission, layout, navigation, captured requests, and retained operations. |
| Board and Doctor | GitHub Actions binding, secret/config metadata, migration, and health checks. | Grant preparation, config persistence/migration orchestration, managed service scheduling, and cleanup. |

The plugin entry registers repository and execution contributions, tools, Board data, Gateway methods, and a V2 managed account service. The manifest declares startup activation, Settings views, secret exclusions, and Doctor participation. Heavy handlers load when invoked. The host keeps its existing stores and lifecycle owners. The released `GatewayRequestContext.githubOAuthService` lookup remains a guarded projection of the canonical plugin-owned service through the documented December 31, 2026 compatibility window; it does not create a second account service.

### Repository and execution

The qualified source `github-repositories/repositories` feeds the repository picker and follows `sessions.create` into session, checkout, and worker preparation. Default worktree preparation uses source-owned `resolveBase()` to observe authenticated remote HEAD, hydrate the selected commit, and follow a renamed default branch. Explicit selectors preserve their Git namespace and literal branch names; missing refs remain actionable. The host verifies the commit locally without ambient-origin fetches, retains safe local branch updates under checkout custody, and pins ref/commit before setup. Retries retain that accepted pin. The isolated Fake Forge plugin uses the same contract with a local transport and an HTTPS canonical origin. GitHub callbacks perform authenticated transport; the host retains destinations, cancellation, pinned commits, and recovery.

Worker preparation returns immutable repository/object identities and a nonsecret cache partition. The host revalidates the lease around Git-pack preparation; the plugin asserts caller and credential authority at effects. Cache identity is not access authority. Admitted credential readers retain the original dispatch actor and request; issued credentials register cleanup with the host.

Execution uses the SDK environment provider. Local wrappers enclose the reviewed command after policy/approval. Sandbox preparation explicitly selects backend and scope rather than copying local identity. Declared exclusions keep bearer credentials out of nonsecret environment facts and prepared repository snapshots.

### Publication and lifecycle

The plugin consumes `native-github-account-host`, `native-github-publication-host`, and `native-github-session-read` to work with the existing native records and receipts.

- `github_publish` uses caller-bound Gateway operations and the existing publication/handoff owner. Session and approval checks remain in force. PR preparation retains the selected requester through the existing host continuation; publication keeps its existing accepted-operation settlement.
- The plugin supplies typed provenance and Git author facts. Core records and compares existing receipt fields for replay and uses the author for source-integration commits. Live request/account assertions authorize effects; verified participant/consent facts stay host-owned.
- PR automation reads the session’s own publication without an import-authorship preflight. A different captured target retains its existing authenticated read workflow. The recipe retains jobs after authentication, inspection, network, and checkout blockers and after successful remediation; cleanup is reserved for a verified merged/closed result.
- Plugin-owned `session-pr:v1` declarations retain their SHA256 identity bytes. Wire/storage DTOs and accepted publication records retain their contracts.
- Refresh, publication-provider installation, and session presentation use managed scheduler, Gateway, and plugin-instance lifetimes. The legacy service projection shares its existing exact-Gateway lookup across native and compiled module graphs. Native source loading and compiled SDK consumers use the same canonical owner and installed publication-host lookup. Accepted publication and checkout transfers remain one-use operations under that owner; cleanup, replacement, and revocation end stale capabilities.

### Browser presentation and reader independence

Control UI V2 contributions provide Profile connections, Agent tools Settings, session PR/check accessories, actions, and retained publication operations. They reuse host controls, responsive layout, serialized config mutations, and captured requests. Plain host-owner subscriptions feed plugin-local reactive state across the separately bundled Solid runtimes. The plugin read store owns PR presentation. Hovercards preserve the compact ten-PR limit and remaining count; branch/diff metadata occupies an adjacent row in the existing accessory layout. Branch and publication controls stay in the native Environment section through the generic `session-environment` slot; published PRs use the separate context section.

Explicit shorthand such as `owner/repo#123` names `reader: { pluginId: "github", id: "github" }`. Both contributions must be admitted and active; the reader owns URL filtering and remote reads. Checkout names, project aliases, and adjacent links never infer a destination, so formatting needs no background project-catalog read.

Public `github.preview` and `github.detail` use the reader's data path directly, so disabling `github-repositories` leaves public reading operational. Enabled managed identity retains its current-selection checks; disabled integration skips that managed selection and uses the existing service/environment/anonymous public path. GitHub App installations verify identity with a temporary installation token and support public reads/search scoped to the requested repository. Temporary tokens are revoked before delivery; App access does not broaden the public-only reader or enable shell execution/publication. Request authority is checked during reads and before delivery. Session/Enterprise readers retain their admitted session-specific path.

Disabling repository integration removes its operations, managed service, tools, and browser contributions. Disabling `github` removes public reading without changing repository ownership. Neither operation broadens allow/deny policy.

Session rows render passive plugin badge facts through the native row renderer. The same bounded, data-only facts join the existing scoped sidebar snapshot, so PR indicators survive a reload before plugin reconnect. Pending results retain facts only for the same complete session target and current registration; ready-empty results and retirement clear them. No plugin code, catalog, new storage manager, or capture timer is persisted.

## Configuration and upgrade

Canonical settings live under `plugins.entries.github-repositories.config`:

| Setting | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `system` | Shared managed GitHub execution identity. |
| `agents.<id>` | Complete per-agent identity override and optional sandbox permission. |
| `host`, `apiBaseUrl` | Matching GitHub or Enterprise endpoint pair. |
| `service.host`, `service.token` | Gateway-side discovery and reader service credential. |
| `repositorySearch.useNativeCredentials` | Explicit opt-in for native-credential repository search. |

`openclaw doctor --fix` invokes the plugin-owned transform for `tools.github`, per-agent `tools.github`, `gateway.github`, `gateway.controlUi.github`, and `gateway.projects.nativeGitHubSearch`. Explicit canonical values win, identities remain atomic, and unknown legacy fields remain available for explicit repair. Normalization is idempotent; conflict warnings omit credential values.

Managed OAuth records, personal connections, and accepted publication state retain their existing storage owners. Runtime reads canonical configuration; migration does not add a legacy runtime reader or rewrite receipts. Explicit allowlists, deny rules, disabled entries, and independent-reader policy are preserved.

See `docs/plugins/github.md` and `extensions/github-repositories/config-migration.test.ts` for configuration and migration details.

## Test scope

Native contracts remain with their host owners. GitHub unit and integration suites live with the plugin; native UI fixtures activate its declared public browser entry and consume protocol events. Coverage includes canonical configuration migration, serialized writes, account selection and retirement, publication handoff, worker credentials, execution approvals, browser freshness and independent reader admission. A standalone fixture allocation covers real provider setup, typed public adapters, lifecycle cleanup and passive-badge reload proof; the shared scalar is unchanged. A separate exact allocation covers App status/read lifetime, automation target/blocker guidance, and App capability presentation regressions.

## Validation

- Full local `pnpm build` passes, including SDK declarations, all 102 bundled plugins, all 167 public SDK subpaths and Control UI. Core, Gateway, agent-execution, extension and UI typechecks pass for the affected scopes. The supported local package passes tarball inventory and import-graph integrity checks.
- The intervening handoff and worker-recovery owners pass 98 targeted cases. Publisher installation rollback passes eight host/loader cases; native-menu error isolation and plugin-owned live/persisted badge parity pass 31 UI cases, with affected production/test typechecks and scoped lint.
- A supported local CLI turn with both GitHub plugins disabled executes successfully with the independent Fake Forge identity and no GitHub token in its child environment.
- Published 2026.10.9 state survives Doctor migration, a second idempotent Doctor run and restart, preserving its project, managed worktree, session and published request. Explicit deny remains authoritative when both GitHub plugins are also allowlisted: two Doctor runs and a restart leave both plugins unloaded and absent from UI/repository catalogs while OpenAI remains active. A separate real Gateway interruption during an accepted publication resumes the same request/account/destination through idempotent replay and produces exactly one PR with the expected commit. A crash after a remote effect with its response lost remains synthetic-fault coverage.
- Focused native checkout/publication, RPC, execution identity/approval, sandbox, App/OAuth/Git transport and browser suites pass. Cached badge reload and cross-tab deletion proof includes actual persisted badge facts; capture cadence is unchanged.
- Real isolated Gateway checks verify App identity, public PR reading/search, and refusal to disclose a private PR despite installation access. Native identity also publishes to disposable public/private repositories, resumes an advanced private head, refreshes the base, and uploads/associates sandbox evidence.
- A real scheduled auto-fix occurrence reads the selected PR's feedback, verifies the requested edit, and publishes to the same PR while retaining its job. The 14 recipe contract cases pass; repeated fresh-observation behavior remains unqualified as described below.
- Focused repair suites pass: 63 App/reader/RPC cases, 15 connections cases, 14 automation cases, and the SDK readiness regression.
- Targeted account lifecycle proof verifies unavailable selection and exact-config recovery with real reads; seven credential/profile retirement and cleanup cases pass. Nineteen publication response-loss, duplicate replay, authority, and restart-recovery cases pass through the real host/plugin adapter with synthetic GitHub faults.
- Fresh isolated Fake Forge proof passes: plugin transport supplies the advanced remote commit, the host owns the managed worktree, and one real successful agent `exec` receives `FAKE_FORGE_IDENTITY=sdk-trial`. The Gateway remains available locally; the model is a synthetic loopback fixture.
- Production and test compiler-boundary guards pass without exemptions. English catalogs load through the declared public artifact and retain Vite dependency watching and fresh reloads; source localization verification passes.
- Startup JavaScript gzip passes its unchanged cap: 90,661 bytes against 90,687 bytes. Startup/auth behavior, native Agents settings, browser subscription cleanup and reconnect have focused passing proof.

Interactive OAuth issuance, distinct-account isolation, native Codex-harness execution, Enterprise endpoints, real cloud provisioning, factory-native proof issuance/redemption, and migration from the newer 2026.11.1 release remain unqualified. Reliable full recurring auto-fix monitoring also remains unqualified: the complete recipe can return quietly without reading fresh feedback, and that failure mode is reproduced on untouched upstream as well. Live feedback-to-publication execution is verified separately.

## Browser evidence

Existing sanitized synthetic captures illustrate shorthand and desktop/mobile Settings presentation; they are not live OAuth or current-head runtime qualification.

| Shorthand before | Shorthand after |
| --- | --- |
| ![Shorthand before the reader-owner fix](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9596a8ed-17fd-4809-9c45-f0bc359d40af) | ![Shorthand after the reader-owner fix](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dd794946-ed7c-4567-a1bf-4862d23afb6d) |

| Native desktop | Plugin desktop |
| --- | --- |
| ![Native GitHub connections](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/333e056f-5322-429d-a30e-f3d785d89120) | ![Plugin GitHub connections](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ef691381-28d5-4da0-9261-6b99f58de6b5) |

| Native mobile | Plugin mobile |
| --- | --- |
| ![Native mobile GitHub connections](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6434b428-a4cb-459b-a1ba-fae5794d1c02) | ![Plugin mobile GitHub connections](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0d36dcdc-6584-48e5-9ba9-4258b70a85c3) |

The Environment row uses the host control wrappers and explicit plugin icon/diff styling. The following synthetic browser captures show the repaired layout.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |

prs.title: feat(gateway): admit sessions_send wake starts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`sessions_send` can fan out wake-starting work through the gateway `agent` RPC. Before this change, concurrent senders could bypass sender-local batching and rate limits. This adds an optional gateway-owned admission boundary for typed `sessions_send` wake traffic. It intentionally does not affect `mode:notify`, which does not create recipient work.

## Summary

- add a disabled-by-default `gateway.sessionsSendWakeAdmission` policy (six starts per 15 minutes by default)
- enforce it at the common gateway `agent` admission boundary only for typed `inputProvenance.kind=inter_session` / `sourceTool=sessions_send`
- persist one idempotent per-recipient decision in a separate SQLite database, atomically, and fail closed if state is unavailable

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway.config.ts src/gateway/sessions-send-wake-admission.test.ts`: 4/4 passed (default-disabled, seven-recipient load, restart/idempotency, fail-closed state error)
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm format:check`, and `git diff --check` passed locally
- implementation is based on released OpenClaw `v2026.10.9` / `8b18b557`, matching the runtime that exposed the issue

## Rollout

Feature remains off by default. This PR contains no config enablement, runtime rollout, or gateway restart. Rollback is retaining the disabled flag or reverting this commit; the receipt database remains as audit evidence.

Tracking: cbire880/the-roost#2473, OP#1548

prs.title: fix: send once while the command palette restores session settings
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Pressing Send in Cmd+K while the palette was restoring session settings discarded the send attempt. The prompt and image remained on screen with “Restoring your last session setup…”, but nothing happened when the settings arrived.

## User Impact

Send once, by button or keyboard. The palette waits for the saved agent and settings, then starts one background session with the original text and attachments. Closing the palette cancels a waiting send.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the pending send the palette already carries through first-open preparation. Only preference restoration is treated as a wait rather than a rejected send; actual creation still goes through the existing admission checks. The full New Session page is unchanged.

## Evidence

Reproduced on the base in Chromium: held the preference response, pasted an image, submitted, then released the response. No session was created. On the fix, the same flow sent the original image and text to the remembered agent exactly once. The regression also covers dismissal, reopening the attachment draft, and repeated keyboard submission.

The three focused browser suites and the palette draft suite passed. Browser proof used a controlled Gateway response, not live credentials. Local UI typechecking could not run against the shared dependency installation; local autoreview of the code change against 461b02a48f587 stopped at authentication without a report.

## What Problem This Solves

When a new chat resumes the opening request under a different run ID, the Control UI can briefly show “Ran a script” above the user's message. It looks as though the assistant acted before anyone asked. The saved transcript has the request first.

If the current request is the first native user message (transcript sequence 1), there is no earlier turn to attach an unmatched run to. prs.title: fix(update): finish an update whose Gateway died while preparing
prs.body:
Closes #203757

## What Problem This Solves

If a Gateway dies while preparing an update from the Control UI, its restarted Gateway leaves the update marked as running. The page stays on a disabled “Updating…” action until a terminal update clears it.

## User Impact

The restarted Gateway records the interrupted update as failed and releases its preparation lock. The Control UI can show the failure and let the user update again. A live CLI preparation in another process keeps its run and lock.

## Why This Change Was Made

Gateway readiness already owns trial outcome settlement. It now also reads the existing preparation lock and applies the existing interrupted outcome when the owner is dead or the new Gateway has reused its PID, including PID 1 in a container.

No new state, timers, flags, or recovery owner. The necessary growth is 13 net production lines, 66 net test lines, and a four-line contract note; no behavior was removed.

## Evidence

- Regression on `origin/main` (`2e8c1ad0aa97`): both a dead owner and a reused Gateway PID stay `running` instead of `failed`/`interrupted`; the live-owner case passes.
- Fixed tree: all 51 tests pass across `gateway-trial`, `store`, `prepare`, and `stale-install` (193.46 s including worker preparation; changed test file's test bodies total about 32 s). These tests use the real lock and run ledger and a real child process.
- Exact-head full build with declarations completed; packed tarball integrity and a fresh npm-installed CLI smoke pass (`OpenClaw 2026.11.7 (1e34a8f)`). Initial acceptance packages serve through a product-installed systemd user service and served as container PID 1 before the fault.
- Focused formatting and lint pass. `check:changed` passes conflict, line-cap, suppression, and assertion guards, then its SQLite worker ratchet aborts at its 4 GB heap limit; this PR does not alter that tool.
- Linux systemd, genuine Control UI: SIGKILL during `prepare:install` → `failed` / `interrupted`, lock released in 41.634 s from the kill; the UI shows the reason and enabled Retry. A second click succeeds to the registry-selected `.1` target. [Screenshot and receipt summary](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/203925#issuecomment-7092120853).
- Product `gateway restart` during prepare, through `update.run` API: the old owner itself records terminal `failed` / `package-install-failed` (spawn broker disconnected), before the new Gateway starts. Startup correctly does not overwrite that terminal result. Observed terminal in 9.165 s from the restart request.
- PID 1 container: **not provable: the Gateway cannot start after a container kill (#203932)**. The real attempt reached `prepare:install` with lock PID 1; general Gateway-lock admission blocks restart before this hook. No manual lock recovery was used. The same-PID regression test passes.
- Live CLI prepare: Gateway starts while CLI PID 7402 holds the install lock; the run stays running/staging and that same lock stays intact. The CLI exits 0 with its candidate prepared; the next product restart activates it and the run succeeds. This preservation case intentionally has trigger `cli`.
- Local review of `1e34a8f1ba4d`: complete, patch correct, no findings. Red CI formatting and three unchanged CLI-test failures reproduce on main without this patch; [exact failure evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/203925#issuecomment-7092133859). They are not repaired here.
- macOS LaunchAgent and Windows Scheduled Task: **unproven, blocks stable**.

The settlement fixture candidates are healthy re-stamps of the same built source, with the same build ID and schema. They test settlement, not migration or rollback. Initial acceptance packages include the final production change built before commit (parent commit in build-info, retained source patch); an additional clean frozen package has this PR head in its build-info. Target selection uses the normal public-npm channel lookup through the isolated TLS registry fixture, with its hosts entry and `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` captured; no package-spec override, `--tag`, or `--no-restart`.

prs.title: fix: node directory listing pages until the gateway stops
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Node directory listing stops after 32 pages so one oversized directory cannot pin the gateway. Bootstrap discovery used that stop to skip the directory, then still loaded a sibling, but it recorded no diagnostic. A configured `*/AGENTS.md` file inside the oversized directory disappeared with `diagnostics: []`.

## Evidence

Head `b06896ea3a7` on macOS Darwin arm64, Node v26.12.1. The production trace below was run on `055d09e2943`. `b06896ea3a7` merges current main and adds the 112-line test grant. It does not change the listing or the diagnostic. A real directory held 131073 empty names, which is one past 32 pages of 4096. Its sibling `keep/AGENTS.md` contained `kept instructions`. Production `createNodeWorkspaceBridge` listed that tree. Each `dir.list` call went to production `handleDirList` on that directory, not a scripted page payload. `loadExtraBootstrapFilesWithDiagnostics` then loaded `*/AGENTS.md`.

```console
OK: files=kept instructions diagnostics=[{"dir":"fat","reason":"io","detail":"Directory listing exceeded 32 pages"}] dirList=34 stat=0 fetch=1
```

`dir.list` ran 34 times: one page for the root, 32 pages for the oversized directory, and one page for the sibling. `file.fetch` read the sibling once. The oversized directory is named in the diagnostic and its instructions were not loaded.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Bootstrap discovery skips one directory after the real 32-page listing cap, records that skip, and still loads a sibling `AGENTS.md`.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS Darwin arm64, Node v26.12.1, head `055d09e2943` in `/tmp/oc-165805`, then merged forward as `b06896ea3a7` without changing the listing or the diagnostic. The directory was a local folder with 131073 names. The node command handler and the gateway bridge ran in one process.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Created the oversized directory and `keep/AGENTS.md`. Called `createNodeWorkspaceBridge` with `invoke` dispatching to `handleDirList`, `handleFileStat`, and `handleFileFetch`. Called `loadExtraBootstrapFilesWithDiagnostics` for `*/AGENTS.md`.
- **Evidence after fix:** terminal output from that production path:

```console
OK: files=kept instructions diagnostics=[{"dir":"fat","reason":"io","detail":"Directory listing exceeded 32 pages"}] dirList=34 fetch=1
```

- **Observed result after fix:** The sibling file was loaded. The oversized directory produced one `io` diagnostic, `Directory listing exceeded 32 pages`, after 32 real listing pages.
- **What was not tested:** A second OS process enrolled as a node over the gateway websocket. The same handlers ran in-process.

## Summary

A directory past the listing page budget is still skipped, and its sibling still loads. The skip is now a diagnostic instead of a silent omission.

prs.title: fix(gateway): project Claude CLI show_widget results into canvas blocks
prs.body:
Root cause: src/gateway/chat-display-projection.canvas.ts:207 `extractChatToolResultCanvasPreview` reads the tool result with `readRecord`, which rejects the bare MCP content-block array that the Claude CLI runtime reports as a tool result, and `augmentChatHistoryWithCanvasBlocks` (:288) skips assistant rows, where Claude CLI history coalesces its `tool_result` blocks; so a successful `show_widget` on `agentRuntime: claude-cli` never yields the `type: "canvas"` block live or in `chat.history`.

Fixes #203893

Thanks @fonchaves for the detailed report, the captured frames and the root-cause trace.

## Problem

On `agentRuntime: claude-cli`, `show_widget` creates the canvas document, but native clients (iOS `OpenClawChatUI`) show no widget: they render inline widgets only from the `canvas` content block, and the Gateway never adds it to the live `chat` final or to `chat.history`. The embedded runtime with the same widget does get the block.

- Live: the Claude CLI tool event carries `result: [{type:"text", text:"{...canvas JSON...}"}]` (raw `tool_result.content`). The canvas extractor accepts only a record, so it returns nothing before its text fallback runs.
- History: Claude CLI history merges the `tool_result` blocks into the assistant tool-call row (`toolcall` + `tool_result`). The history projection only harvests previews from standalone tool-result rows and passes over assistant rows.

## Fix

Both changes are in the existing canvas projection owner; no new block type, extractor, protocol or schema change:

- `extractChatToolResultCanvasPreview` treats a bare content-block array as `{ content }`, so it takes the same details/text projection the embedded result shape already uses.
- `augmentChatHistoryWithCanvasBlocks` also harvests previews from tool-result blocks inside assistant tool rows and attaches them to the next renderable assistant message, exactly as it already does for standalone tool-result rows.

The "Outcome unknown" tool-row status is a separate owner (Claude history `is_error` normalization / activity projection, #203877) and is unchanged here.

## Evidence

Built Gateway (`pnpm build` in a secretless `node:24.22.1` container) with `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5` on `agentRuntime: claude-cli`, and a stand-in `claude` that emits Claude Code 2.1.330 stream-json (`tool_use` `mcp__openclaw__show_widget`, `tool_result` with the raw MCP content array, text reply) after calling the Gateway's real loopback MCP `tools/call show_widget`, and writes the matching Claude project JSONL. Operator WS client shaped like iOS (`openclaw-ios`, mode `ui`, caps incl. `inline-widgets`, signed device), `chat.send`, live final, `chat.history`. Two runs per side:

| case | base 7d0cc1ec8157 live / history | fix live / history |
|---|---|---|
| claude-cli show_widget | `["text"]` / `["text"]` | `["text","canvas"]` / `["text","canvas"]` (same `cv_` id as the tool result) |
| claude-cli, no widget | `["text"]` / `["text"]` | `["text"]` / `["text"]` |
| embedded runtime show_widget | `["text","canvas"]` / `["text"]` | identical bytes (ids normalized) |
| Control UI (web) on claude-cli | 1 rendered widget (from `[embed]` shortcode) | 1 rendered widget (shortcode deduped against the block) |

Full receipt: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/203922#issuecomment-7091779268

Regression tests: one coalesced Claude CLI history case in `chat-display-projection.test.ts`, and the existing live widget snapshot test now feeds one result as the bare Claude CLI array. Both fail on base and pass with the fix.

Deltas vs merge base: production +14/-2 (one file), tests +15/-1.

## Merge danger

Two-way door: display projection only, no stored state or contract change; a revert fully undoes it. Blast radius: canvas blocks on `chat` finals and `chat.history`/`chat.message.get` for tool results delivered as bare arrays or nested in assistant rows (Claude CLI). The Control UI already dedupes shortcodes against canvas blocks by view id.

prs.title: refactor(agents): delete captureAdmittedRunActiveAssertion and the Stop-only tool-caller captures
prs.body:
## Problem

R3+R4 of the one-admission receipt cluster: delete the last two names in `LIFETIME_CHECK_CALLS`, `captureAdmittedRunActiveAssertion` and `captureGatewayToolCallerAssertion`. After R1, R1b, R1c and R2 (#203664, #203788, #203760, #203892) neither body reads authority. What is left is Stop and session data fences.

## Change

**Cut less (Fable 5.2 consult, option C).** This PR deletes `captureAdmittedRunActiveAssertion` and the 2 Stop-only sites of `captureGatewayToolCallerAssertion`. The ratchet keeps one name.

- `captureAdmittedRunActiveAssertion` is deleted. Its body (Stop on the run signal, run occurrence, `foregroundClosed`, registry claim and the run's registry session source) moves into `resolveAdmittedRunActiveAssertion`, which already wrapped it and already has ~50 callers. The 4 other callers (`runWithPreparedRunSourceScope`, `prepareAgentRunAdmission`, `bindHarnessHostSourceAuthority`, `createAdmittedGatewayToolCallerIdentity`) call `resolveAdmittedRunActiveAssertion(context)`. Each passed the lease's own root authority, so the result is the same. `bindHarnessHostSourceAuthority` loses its now-unused `delegatedAuthority` parameter.
- `captureGatewayToolCallerAssertion`, the 2 Stop-only sites: the plugin tool `assertInvocationCurrent` (`openclaw-plugin-tools.ts`) and `prepareGatewayToolCallerAssertion` now call `throwIfAborted()` on the caller's own `approvalSignals`. Both used only the synchronous call, which was Stop-only. The plugin factory context wraps the check in a closure, so the receipt's prepared properties never reached a write.
- `LIFETIME_CHECK_CALLS` now holds only `captureGatewayToolCallerAssertion`.

Production: 6 files, +24/−44. No new export, `capture*` name, hook, flag, guard, timer or state. Behavior is unchanged.

## What is left, and why it was not cut here

I removed `captureAdmittedRunActiveAssertion` and 2 of the 9 tool-caller calls. The other 7 calls (6 files) still need the "prepared-only receipt" shape. I did not patch them.

These sites compose the capture as a session source: the in-process Gateway dispatch and commit guard (`in-process-gateway.ts` ×2), media launch admission (`media-generate-background-shared.ts`), `agent-step.ts`, `operator-invocation-authority.ts`, `server-plugin-in-process-authority.ts` and the message tool (`message-tool-execution.ts`). The capture's synchronous call is Stop-only, and its prepared session-source properties carry the receipt's data fences. Detached work calls the synchronous check after the run closed. For example, media background `run` calls `assertAdmissionCurrent()` before the provider call.

- Passing `caller.receiptAuthority` directly would also run the receipt's fences (including `foregroundClosed`) on those synchronous calls. Background media and other detached work would then be refused after the run closes, which is lost work. It would also reverse the edge case accepted in #203487.
- Copying the "sync no-op, prepared = receipt" idiom into 7 producers removes the name, not the concept.

**Proposed follow-up:** move "prepared-only source" into the `composeSessionSourceAssertion` owner as a relocation of the existing shape, then delete the last name and empty the list. If that needs a new flag or parameter on the composer, that cut is wrong too.

## What users see

Nothing changes. Stop still cancels, and stale-writer, generation and run-occurrence refusals are unchanged.

## Evidence

- **Stop proof on both changed tool-caller paths (new tests):** `openclaw-plugin-tools.stop.test.ts`: a plugin tool's `assertInvocationCurrent` passes, then throws the Stop reason after the run signal aborts. `gateway-caller-context.test.ts` "lets Stop on the caller refuse a prepared watch admission": same for `prepareGatewayToolCallerAssertion`. The admitted-run path keeps `signal?.aborted` → refuse unchanged.
- **Tests (pre-push):** the importer set is 554 files, over the 150 cap, so CI runs it. Locally, one `ocx test` call with `OPENCLAW_NODE_TEST_PLAN_CONTINUE_ON_FAILURE=1` on 67 files: every test that names `resolveAdmittedRunActiveAssertion`, `runWithPreparedRunSourceScope`, `bindHarnessHostSourceAuthority` or the refusal string, plus the admitted-run, harness host, plugin-tools, gateway-caller-context, sessions-send-followup and ratchet tests. All green, including stale-writer, generation and occurrence tests (unedited).
- **Typecheck / lint / ratchet:** `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:test` clean; oxfmt and oxlint clean on changed files; lifetime-check ratchet OK.
- **One-admission E2E** on exact head `1b9812f6114c`: `pass: true`, R/Q/S all pass (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/203920#issuecomment-7091909560).
- **Local ClawSweeper review** on `1b9812f6114c`: complete, patch is correct, 0 findings.

prs.title: fix(slack): normalize typed command owner IDs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Configured Slack owners expressed as typed targets such as `slack:user:U123` were normalized to `user:U123` globally but compared against the authenticated bare sender ID `U123` by the Slack adapter. As a result, a legitimate owner reply in a bot-created task thread reached privileged delegation with `senderIsOwner: false`. This patch normalizes only typed human-user targets to the bare Slack sender ID while preserving workspace-qualified, channel, bot, and invalid targets.

## Problem

A typed Slack command owner such as `slack:user:U123` is stripped to `user:U123` by the global owner resolver. Slack's allowlist formatter previously only lowercased that value, so it remained `user:u123` while the authenticated inbound sender normalized to `u123`. The owner-only OpenClaw tool gate then saw `senderIsOwner: false`.

This is a normalization defect, not thread-root authority: current source already derives Slack authority from the current inbound sender. The bot-created-thread regression protects that behavior explicitly.

Addresses #203884. Related normalization evidence: #203870.

## Solution

- normalize unscoped typed Slack human-user targets to the bare sender ID using the existing Slack target parser
- preserve workspace-qualified, channel, bot, and invalid entries instead of widening them
- cover a bot-created root followed by a typed configured-owner reply, non-owner denial, bot-message rejection, and runtime-config owner revocation
- register the Slack plugin in the test runtime so the production authorization resolver sees the channel formatter; this repairs the harness without bypassing authorization

## Evidence

- baseline proof: the formatter regression fails on `origin/main` because `user:u123owner` and `slack:user:w456owner` retain their prefixes
- `./node_modules/.bin/vitest run extensions/slack/src/config-adapter.test.ts extensions/slack/src/shared.test.ts extensions/slack/src/monitor/message-handler/prepare.bot-threads.test.ts` — 2 discovered files, 12 tests passed
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/extensions-test.tsbuildinfo` — passed
- focused oxlint passed for all 3 changed files
- oxfmt check and `git diff --check` passed for all 3 changed files
- the corrected integration fixture uses `slack:user:U123OWNER`, asserts canonical `u123owner`, and verifies the owner tool path plus non-owner refusal
- local autoreview was unavailable because the canonical shared autoreview installation is absent on this host
- no live Gateway/Slack transport proof was performed; the behavior proof is the in-process registered-ingress integration test with mocked Slack I/O

prs.title: fix(googlechat,msteams): approval card clicks skip the approver check when no approvers are configured
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Google Chat and Microsoft Teams approval cards resolve a decision from whoever clicks when the account has no explicit approvers at the moment of the click.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both card handlers call the channel's `authorizeActorAction` and only check `.authorized`. With an empty approver list, that hook returns the implicit same-chat result. The result exists for typed `/approve`, where core also requires the sender to be command-authorized (`src/auto-reply/reply/commands-approve.ts`). Card clicks go through neither message admission nor command authorization, so that fallback shouldn't decide them.

The SDK approval guide asks channel-owned native callbacks to check `isImplicitSameChatApprovalAuthorization(...)` before resolving (`docs/plugins/sdk-channel-plugins/approvals.md`). Every other native approval control already requires an approver:
- Discord, Telegram and Matrix match the sender against the approver list.
- Slack does the same, except when the operator has written `allowFrom: ["*"]`.
- iMessage polls and the shared reaction helper used by Signal, WhatsApp and iMessage reject an empty list.

Google Chat and Teams were the two exceptions. This change rejects the implicit result in both handlers rather than routing it elsewhere: neither channel sends a card when no approvers resolve, so there is no legitimate implicit card click to keep. The capability-level `authorizeActorAction` is unchanged, so typed `/approve` in chats without approvers still works (`extensions/msteams/src/approval-native.test.ts` pins this).

A separate, older docs error sat in the same place, so it's fixed here too. `docs/tools/exec-approvals-advanced.md` told operators to put Google Chat approvers in `channels.googlechat.dm.allowFrom`. The schema rejects a nested `dm.allowFrom` (the `dm` object is strict and only takes `enabled`), and the approver resolver reads `channels.googlechat.allowFrom`, which is what the Google Chat channel page and the setup hint already say.

## User Impact

Approval card decisions on Google Chat and Teams now come only from configured approvers. That's what the docs describe; the Teams page already says "OpenClaw checks the clicking user's AAD object ID before resolving the request". Setups with approvers see no change: cards are only sent while approvers resolve, and those approvers keep deciding them. A click on a card while no approver resolves is ignored, and the log names the reason. The approval stays pending, so it can still be resolved with `/approve` or the Web UI, or left to expire.

Operators following the exec approvals page now get a Google Chat approver key the config accepts.

## Evidence

Real Gateway run, built from this branch (head `61317915791`). Two isolated local Gateways with the Google Chat and Teams plugins enabled and no Google or Teams credentials: `:18797` has an approver configured on each channel, `:18798` has none. The harness is throwaway and not part of this change. For each case it:

1. Opens a real two-phase `exec.approval.request` whose turn source is the Google Chat space or Teams conversation, then waits on `exec.approval.waitDecision` the way the exec runtime does.
2. Hands a card action to the exported `maybeHandleGoogleChatApprovalCardClick` or `maybeHandleMSTeamsApprovalCardSubmit`, with no module mocks. Inside a Gateway, a channel account task resolves through its scoped approval runtime. Here that runtime forwards to a real operator connection to the same Gateway, so the Gateway's approval owner, channel custody and account binding decide the outcome.
3. Prints the decision the Gateway recorded.

The before run swaps in the two handler files from the base commit `464f199984d`. The Gateways and everything else stay the same.

Before, on the Gateway with no approvers, both channels' approvals are allowed by a click from someone who is not an approver. The Gateway accepts it, so the card handler is the only place that rule is enforced:

```
[gateway :18798] [googlechat] approvers=[] clicker=users/999: Gateway recorded decision allow-once after 0.0s
    note: terminal card update failed after resolve (Could not load the default credentials)
[gateway :18798] [msteams] approvers=[] clicker=aaaaaaaa-bbbb-4ccc-8ddd-eeeeeeeeeeee: Gateway recorded decision allow-once after 0.0s
    log: msteams approval resolved {"approvalId":"…","approvalKind":"exec","applied":true,"status":"allowed","senderId":"aaaaaaaa-bbbb-4ccc-8ddd-eeeeeeeeeeee"}
```

After, those two clicks are ignored and the approvals stay undecided until they time out. On the Gateway with approvers, a non-approver is still ignored and the approver still decides, same as before:

```
[gateway :18797] [googlechat] approvers=["users/123"] clicker=users/999: Gateway recorded no decision (timeout after 8.0s)
    log: [default] googlechat approval ignored: unauthorized actor users/999
[gateway :18797] [googlechat] approvers=["users/123"] clicker=users/123: Gateway recorded decision allow-once after 0.1s
    note: terminal card update failed after resolve (Could not load the default credentials)
[gateway :18797] [msteams] approvers=["11111111-2222-4333-8444-555555555555"] clicker=aaaaaaaa-bbbb-4ccc-8ddd-eeeeeeeeeeee: Gateway recorded no decision (timeout after 8.0s)
    log: msteams approval ignored {"reason":"unauthorized actor aaaaaaaa-bbbb-4ccc-8ddd-eeeeeeeeeeee"}
[gateway :18797] [msteams] approvers=["11111111-2222-4333-8444-555555555555"] clicker=11111111-2222-4333-8444-555555555555: Gateway recorded decision allow-once after 0.0s
    log: msteams approval resolved {"approvalId":"…","approvalKind":"exec","applied":true,"status":"allowed","senderId":"11111111-2222-4333-8444-555555555555"}
[gateway :18798] [googlechat] approvers=[] clicker=users/999: Gateway recorded no decision (timeout after 8.0s)
    log: [default] googlechat approval ignored: card clicks require explicit approvers
[gateway :18798] [msteams] approvers=[] clicker=aaaaaaaa-bbbb-4ccc-8ddd-eeeeeeeeeeee: Gateway recorded no decision (timeout after 8.0s)
    log: msteams approval ignored {"reason":"card submits require explicit approvers"}
```

(Google Chat rows that resolve also report a failed terminal card update, because the harness has no Google service account. The update runs after the Gateway has recorded the decision.)

What stands in for the real channel:
- `requireDeliveryRoute: false` on the approval request stands in for a delivered card. No card is posted.
- The channel runtime's Gateway connection is a device-authenticated operator with `operator.approvals`, not the Gateway's in-process runtime.
- The Chat and Teams card events are constructed.

<details>
<summary>Handler-only transcript from the first revision (resolver requests recorded, no Gateway)</summary>

Throwaway harness, not part of this change. It calls the exported `maybeHandleGoogleChatApprovalCardClick` and `maybeHandleMSTeamsApprovalCardSubmit` directly, with no module mocks. The Gateway approval runtime is supplied through the production seam `withGatewayNativeApprovalRuntime`, and the harness records each `approval.resolve` a handler sends. The before run swaps in the two handler files from the base commit `464f199984d`; nothing else differs.

Before, with an empty approver list, a non-approver click is sent to the Gateway on both channels:

```
[googlechat] no-approvers-member-clicks: approvers=[] clicker=users/999 -> RESOLVE SENT
    approval.resolve {"id":"approval-gc-no-approvers-member-clicks","kind":"exec","decision":"allow-once","reviewer":{"channel":"googlechat","accountId":"default","senderId":"users/999"}}
[msteams] no-approvers-member-clicks: approvers=[] clicker=aaaaaaaa-bbbb-4ccc-8ddd-eeeeeeeeeeee -> RESOLVE SENT
    approval.resolve {"id":"approval-teams-no-approvers-member-clicks","kind":"exec","decision":"allow-once","reviewer":{"channel":"msteams","accountId":"default","senderId":"aaaaaaaa-bbbb-4ccc-8ddd-eeeeeeeeeeee"}}
```

After, the same clicks are not sent. With approvers listed, results match the base commit: a non-approver is ignored and the approver resolves.

```
[googlechat] approver-listed-member-clicks: approvers=["users/123"] clicker=users/999 -> NOT SENT
    log: [default] googlechat approval ignored: unauthorized actor users/999
[googlechat] approver-listed-approver-clicks: approvers=["users/123"] clicker=users/123 -> RESOLVE SENT
    approval.resolve {"id":"approval-gc-approver-listed-approver-clicks","kind":"exec","decision":"allow-once","reviewer":{"channel":"googlechat","accountId":"default","senderId":"users/123"}}
[googlechat] no-approvers-member-clicks: approvers=[] clicker=users/999 -> NOT SENT
    log: [default] googlechat approval ignored: card clicks require explicit approvers
[msteams] approver-listed-member-clicks: approvers=["11111111-2222-4333-8444-555555555555"] clicker=aaaaaaaa-bbbb-4ccc-8ddd-eeeeeeeeeeee -> NOT SENT
    log: msteams approval ignored {"reason":"unauthorized actor aaaaaaaa-bbbb-4ccc-8ddd-eeeeeeeeeeee"}
[msteams] approver-listed-approver-clicks: approvers=["11111111-2222-4333-8444-555555555555"] clicker=11111111-2222-4333-8444-555555555555 -> RESOLVE SENT
    approval.resolve {"id":"approval-teams-approver-listed-approver-clicks","kind":"exec","decision":"allow-once","reviewer":{"channel":"msteams","accountId":"default","senderId":"11111111-2222-4333-8444-555555555555"}}
[msteams] no-approvers-member-clicks: approvers=[] clicker=aaaaaaaa-bbbb-4ccc-8ddd-eeeeeeeeeeee -> NOT SENT
    log: msteams approval ignored {"reason":"card submits require explicit approvers"}
```

(The Google Chat resolve rows are followed by a terminal card update error, because the harness has no Google service account. It happens after the request above is recorded.)

</details>

Tests:
- One new test per handler. Each fails on the base commit because the Gateway resolver is called, and passes here. Deleting either new guard turns exactly its test red.
- `approval-card-click.test.ts` 12/12, `approval-card-submit.test.ts` 14/14.
- All Google Chat approval tests 36/36; all Teams approval tests 46/46.

Checks: both extension `tsgo` lanes (source and test), `lint:extensions`, `oxfmt --check`, `check:assertion-safety`, `check:max-lines-ratchet`, `format:docs:check`, `lint:docs`.

What was not tested: no live Google Chat or Teams workspace, so no real-user reproduction. In normal operation the handler never sees an empty approver list while a card is live. Cards are only sent while approvers resolve, and changing approvers restarts the channel, which retires pending card tokens. The only window I can point to is that restart, where the old approval handler stops asynchronously, and I haven't measured it. This change enforces the approver rule in the handlers, which the run above shows is the only place it's checked for these cards, instead of relying on that lifecycle.
