prs.title: fix(state): preserve maintenance contention across state worker replies
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A state read refused during maintenance loses its error class when the worker sends the failure back to the caller. Callers can no longer recognize retryable maintenance contention, so a temporary refusal can become a terminal failure.

The failure was observed while qualifying #203860 in [CI run 45094548300, job 137431843852](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45094548300/job/137431843852): `StateDatabaseAccessError: OpenClaw state at …/state/openclaw.sqlite is undergoing offline maintenance by sqlite-maintenance process 20681 … retry when it finishes.` The stack enters the generic `new Error(node.message)` branch during read-reply hydration. This PR independently reproduces the transport defect on main with fs-safe 0.27.1; it does not claim to identify the historical reader PID.

## User Impact

Callers retain the existing retry classification and database path for admission-pending and offline-maintenance failures. Access and maintenance-scope failures remain non-retryable. The placement-authorization test also reports an unexpected early rejection promptly instead of hanging until its 120-second timeout.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared state-worker error graph now preserves all four state-access classes, and the base class uses the same global identity mechanism as its subclasses. The read worker, SQLite broker, and other existing consumers continue using that one codec. No admission, lock, or retry policy changes.

The placement test attaches its rejection assertion before awaiting startup and races the assertion against startup. No exact sibling rejection-after-startup pattern was found.

## Evidence

Two real read-worker cases hold an actual schema/offline owner in a separate process: both fail the class assertion before this fix and pass with it. The four codec cases fail before the fix; the passing cases preserve messages, paths, aggregate classification and non-retryable outcomes. A module-reload check covers canonical base-class identity.

Focused local tests: 102 passed across `openclaw-state-read-maintenance.test.ts`, `openclaw-state-worker-error.test.ts`, `sqlite-worker-broker-reply.test.ts`, `gateway-state-owner.test.ts`, and `sessions-placement-authorization.test.ts`. Individual test time for the changed files was under two seconds; the wrapper also compiles native worker entries on a cold cache.

The optional automatic wait-and-success test is omitted: deterministic coordination of the read worker's admission loop would require additional instrumentation. The real worker refusal and receiving-side retry classification are exercised directly.

Core typecheck, affected state/gateway test typechecks, targeted lint, formatting and diff checks pass. Independent Codex autoreview of committed head `b2bfede816c6ac3fea770c13441fd32178092894` against main `096214ac84d` is clean at P0–P2. The native-worker build registry also includes the subprocess fixture; its real-worker replay, tooling typecheck and independent P0–P2 delta review pass. The full-tree file scan now reports only the two pre-existing manual-release files. Final-head normal PR CI (attempt 2, completed with the inherited failures below): [45108560486](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45108560486). Five test jobs have independently qualified baseline failures, listed below. The original baseline-ratchet runner shut down; its exact-head local replay passed all checks, and the targeted hosted retry passed as job 137486756452. Attempt 2 carries the other completed jobs forward; all five failed test logs are byte-identical to attempt 1. The superseded first run was cancelled after this push and also recorded a ratchet-runner shutdown.

Simplification review: the existing graph remains the single transport owner; the only production growth is canonical error identity and four codec cases. The real-process fixture is needed to exercise the foreign-owner branch without mocked admission or synthetic lock records.

Related: #203860


### CI baseline evidence

The normal CI run is red; landing uses the native inherited-failure route after the interrupted infrastructure check was recovered. This does not treat failed checks as passing.

| Candidate job | Observed failure | Baseline proof |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [137486759505](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45108560486/job/137486759505) | Three destination-authority cases: `No model is configured` | All three reproduce on original base `096214ac84d`, fs-safe 0.27.1, after building the actual e2e runtime. |
| [137486759167](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45108560486/job/137486759167) | Cross-agent inherited selection and four exec-approval requester assertions | Same cases and signatures in scheduled main [45100561778](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45100561778), jobs 137450773456 and 137450773394. |
| [137486758437](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45108560486/job/137486758437) | Three session-group creation revocation assertions | Same cases and signatures in scheduled main 45100561778, job 137450773526. |
| [137486758660](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45108560486/job/137486758660) | Pending-input dismissal accepts a revoked write | Same case and signature in scheduled main 45100561778, job 137450773397. |
| [137486758348](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45108560486/job/137486758348) | Session-create permission-revocation timeout, three following hook timeouts and retained resource cleanup | Same sequence and cleanup failure in scheduled main 45100561778, job 137450773430. |

These failing test and runtime source files are unchanged by this PR. The scheduled-main Windows log that returned 404 is not used as proof for any of these attributions.

prs.title: fix: reuse release evidence after orchestration-only repairs
prs.body:
Related: #203854

## What Problem This Solves

Release operators cannot reuse authenticated child validation after combining a parent-orchestration repair with a waiver-policy update, even when the candidate and child execution are unchanged. The waiver-only exception rejects that combined change and unnecessarily repeats qualification.

## User Impact

No runtime or package changes. Release qualification can retain eligible evidence across explicitly recognized orchestration-only repairs. Changed upgrade baselines, child inputs, actual workloads, expired artifacts, or invalid provenance still prevent reuse. No budgets, tests, or release gates are waived by this repair.

## Why This Change Was Made

Extend the existing same-workload decision with a small explicit set of parent orchestration, reuse-owner, associated test/documentation, and waiver-policy paths. Only a complete forward comparison consisting of modified recognized paths qualifies; all other changes retain the existing workflow/tree comparison. Discovery and final validation use the same owner. Current policy, exact candidate/inputs, authenticated receipts, and live attempt checks remain intact.

## Evidence

- Four-role regression fails before the repair and passes after it; all 73 child-reuse tests pass. Changed harnesses, child workflows, dependency/source inputs, divergent history, and capped inventories remain covered.
- Targeted tooling TypeScript check, type-aware lint (zero warnings/errors), formatting, and git diff check pass.
- Live read-only selection against current qualification policy accepts prior performance run 45077371530 and CI run 45077354288 when their original execution inputs match.
- The same CI receipt is correctly rejected for the newer 11.7 upgrade baseline versus its original 11.6 inputs. This repair does not remove that separate qualification requirement.
- Canonical local review: scoped-clean, no actionable P0-P2 findings. Self-simplification retained one decision owner and no new helper or persistent state.

Live selection proves eligibility only; it is not a new release seal or a claim that historically waived jobs passed.

prs.title: fix(ui): finish provider sign-in after reconnecting
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Returning from browser sign-in after the Gateway connection drops can leave the provider dialog showing a request error even though authorization succeeded. Reconnect notifications could recursively schedule hundreds of resumes before the first resume started.

## User Impact

Provider sign-in can finish after a connection drop or page reload. Existing identity, agent, and permission checks remain in place; no configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The sign-in owner now claims one pending resume before admission publishes updates, then releases that claim when the wizard runner takes over. A later disconnect can still resume normally.

The existing real-Gateway tests now enter providers through the inline catalog. Their completion and editable-error checks are unchanged. The guard stays in the existing sign-in owner; the shared mutation controller and its authority checks are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Four real-Gateway browser scenarios passed: reconnect, reload, rejected-key correction, and editable rejected-key entry.
- The new regression covers repeated notifications while admission is pending and a second disconnect before sign-in completes. The same regression fails on the original owner with two admissions instead of one, then passes after restoring the fix.
- The 23 existing focused runner, refresh, and external-login tests passed. UI typechecking, touched-file lint and formatting, and whitespace checks passed.
- Measured startup, chat boot, and CSS asset sizes match the test-only baseline; its existing CSS and chat-budget warnings remain.
- Local ClawSweeper completed at high reasoning on `80b4433af79d4cdf5dabf961f3b409d0d87643c9` against `ee9fb85d09602803e30039abfa4573c4a9453ad0`: no actionable findings; security cleared.
- Follow-up `98c707194321e0266f24f4206961599e4b6007d3` removes a redundant default `void` type argument reported by CI. It changes no runtime behavior; the review and behavior proof above remain applicable. [CI passed on the corrected head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45109219640), including type-aware lint and all three UI shards. The first attempt hit a lint timeout and a terminated UI process; its failed-job retry passed without further changes.

prs.title: improve: make common Chat controls quicker to open
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The first time someone opens a common Chat control, the browser may still need to load its menu code. The composer’s `+` menu also waits for capability setup even when the person only wants to attach a file.

## User Impact

Chat prepares the effort picker, composer `+`, Layout, and the side-panel launcher once the transcript and composer are ready. Attachment actions are available while skills and integrations initialize. The session and sidebar account/action menus get a small hint on interaction, rather than being warmed for everyone.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing idle scheduler and fetch only assets, without opening panels or making Gateway requests. Intent hints request just the menu entry script (9.3 KiB gzip for the Chat session menu, 13.9 KiB for the sidebar renderer); opening the menu still owns its dependencies and data. Keep existing ⌘K and model-picker behavior unchanged.

## Evidence

- 47 focused tests passed, including selecting an attachment while capabilities are still pending and checking that speculative assets exclude nested menu code. Formatting and scoped lint passed.
- A focused Chromium regression on the production bundle with a fixture Gateway verified idle effort-picker warming, entry-only session-menu warming on hover, and the controls opening and reopening with usable actions.
- The production build succeeded. Against unchanged base `3d2e3a27fde25`, normalized Chat boot JS was identical (21 requests, 1,333,132 bytes gzip), as was the largest CSS asset (58,587 bytes gzip). Both builds reported the same two existing budget warnings (20-request Chat cap and 58,315-byte CSS cap). No macOS speedup was measured.

Co-authored with @vyctorbrzezowski.

### Attachment actions while capabilities load

When the extra items arrive during a click, Camera, Media, and File now stay beside the composer. The other items appear above them; keyboard traversal follows that order. Both images show the actual built UI with a fixture Gateway.

| Before | After |

Related: #203661 (separate Command Palette backdrop fix)

## What Problem This Solves

In the macOS Dashboard, an open Browser tab can cover the bottom of both toast lanes. That can hide part of the notification and prevent the user from clicking **Open session**.

## User Impact

The fix keeps both toast lanes readable and actionable without hiding, resizing, or reloading the open Browser tab. When the toast leaves, the page receives clicks in that area again.

## Why This Change Was Made

The native browser view sits above the Dashboard’s web rendering, so CSS stacking alone cannot resolve the overlap. The toast host reports the visible toast shapes; the native presentation uses those same shapes for clipping and click routing. Older app builds do not receive the new bridge message.

Reported and co-authored by @vyctorbrzezowski.

prs.title: feat(update): keep the Gateway running while package updates prepare
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Global npm, pnpm, and Bun updates replace the package underneath the running Gateway. A broken candidate or a failed restart can leave it stopped, and the running updater must keep recovering code that has already been replaced.

## User Impact

Owned global package installs now prepare the next release beside the serving one, as Git installs do since #203194. The resident launcher commits the trial when the new Gateway becomes ready, or starts the previous release again when the candidate cannot start.

`--no-restart` leaves the serving Gateway alone and activates the same rollback-protected trial at its next start. Plugin maintenance uses the new release's code; plugin problems are reported without failing the core update.

## Why This Change Was Made

The CLI, Gateway `update.run`, and automatic updates share the release owner. Packages are packed and extracted outside `node_modules`, then production dependencies are installed there. Staged manifests omit development dependencies and checkout-only preparation hooks while retaining runtime dependencies, peer checks, and install hooks. Existing global entry points forward to the launcher; owned user-service definitions are staged through the existing definition-backup owner, without stopping the serving Gateway. System-owned definitions retain forwarding entries. Native restarts verify the listener's launchd job membership when the resident launcher, rather than its Gateway child, is the supervised PID.

Unowned installs and unfinished legacy recovery retain their existing admission owners. Explicit package artifacts, package-spec overrides, downgrade consent, campaign targets, local-only delegation, and timeout budgets are preserved.

Package dev-channel selections still use the existing Git conversion owner. Schema compatibility is checked against pinned Git/package metadata before staging, so an older release cannot strand the Gateway on newer state.

Accepted compatibility boundaries: `update.run` cannot yet carry package target specs, `--accept-capabilities`, or the invoking checkout identity. Explicit package specs stay local; the optional protocol fields and their caller migration follow separately. This PR does not change that protocol. Deletions follow in PR 3; the explicit local-override owner and shipped-updater bridge remain until their compatibility readers can be retired.

Accepted edge cases:
- Targets lacking the release-update/check-readiness contract are refused without publication, forwarding, service changes or a trial; the error gives the exact manual install/build command. Shipped older versions also support older state schemas and were already refused by the existing updater's schema guard. The remaining affected same-schema targets are developer-pinned commits between the schema bump and the release-path introduction; supporting them automatically would require permanent compatibility readiness/finalization machinery. A briefly explored direct-switch route was removed after real qualification demonstrated a dead Gateway and false success.
- Explicit `--reapply-local-overrides` is temporarily refused instead of silently losing edits or reintroducing another activation owner. Save edits, update without the flag, then [reapply them manually](https://docs.openclaw.ai/install/updating#local-packaged-code-overrides). Staged replay restoration with real update/rollback proof is tracked in #203498.
- Through a running Gateway, `update.run` cannot yet carry `--channel` or `--accept-capabilities`. The CLI saves the channel first, but a Gateway with `gateway.reload.mode=off` (or inside the reload debounce) can prepare the previous channel, and plugin maintenance runs without the consent. Both arrive as optional `update.run` fields in #203504; the same channel gap exists for Git installs since #203194. Today `--no-restart` (in-process preparation) carries both.
- When an update settles an interrupted earlier update before preparing its release, the settlement note ("kept, because its Gateway was verified on the version it installed…") is recorded on the interrupted run's history (`openclaw update status`), but the new run's CLI report does not repeat it, as the in-place executor's report did.
- A CLI run from one installation while the managed Gateway serves another, with an explicit `--tag`, prepares the release in the invoking installation instead of the served one; the served Gateway restarts on its current version. Carrying the admitted service target is part of #203504.
- Local release preparation validates the target with the invoking runtime, not the service's pinned runtime; a target the service runtime cannot run fails its launcher trial and rolls back. Tracked in #203628.
- `--full-integrity-check` is not yet carried to the release path's verification. Tracked in #203629.

The shipped updater requires more than a schema-only finalizer: executor delegation, retained-owner binding, and Gateway restart completion remain necessary. The bridge and its dependency closure are retained unweakened; their deletion follows in PR 3, after the supported upgrade floor passes the release containing this change. No schema, protocol-version, or runtime dependency version/range changes.

Using the same production update-surface selection as #203194: **114,944 → 115,339 lines (+395); 107,033 → 107,418 code lines (+385)**. Outside that selection, the native launchd listener-ownership fix and launcher-child restart routing preserve native restarts. The complete diff removes **8,474 net test/support lines** that asserted retired normal-entry swap, rehearsal, handoff, and lifecycle execution; standalone repair, shipped post-core continuation, and helper-owner contracts remain. Overall: **2,212 additions / 10,255 deletions (−8,043 lines)** across 82 files.

## Evidence

- Real macOS npm first hop: shipped `2026.11.6` updater → final source `e72deb6d3625b81e915bd8f4b87461d5eb75859f`, terminal succeeded; 19,774 installed files, `/readyz` 200, and Gateway RPC verified after the recorded manual restart. Automatic first-hop restart is not claimed.
- The same final artifact passed real package A→B with one restart and a committed trial (136.6 s total; sampled outage 5.0–7.0 s); a genuinely crashing candidate rolled back after two attempts (141.3 s total). `--no-restart` retained the serving PID with 102 ready samples until the next start committed C. Real plugin maintenance updated lossless-claw 1.1.1→1.2.0, and a refused downgrade wrote no update run.
- Final source `e72deb6d3625b81e915bd8f4b87461d5eb75859f` passed physical-home macOS LaunchAgent conversion through managed `update.run`, two subsequent ordinary native restarts, and B→C `--no-restart` followed by a committing native restart. The frozen service definition and resident parent→Gateway relationship were preserved. An actual updater SIGKILL immediately after definition-backup creation also preserved the old serving Gateway; retry staged successfully and one restart committed the candidate.
- Repair batch: changed-file formatting/Oxlint and `pnpm -s tsgo:core` passed. The touched/direct-and-support-importer set runs together in one `ocx test` call.
- The e72 source above passed a full build (including declarations) and self-contained package integrity/import-graph checks on macOS arm64, Node 24.21.0. The frozen launcher and service conversion are unchanged since e72, so those receipts are reused. Package preparation changed after e72 (below), so the npm case was rerun on the final head `c3d8f62d9b` (Node 24.21.0): A→B through the release path, one succeeded run, the trial committed after one restart (123.0 s), B verified by RPC build id and `/readyz` 200, the staged manifest without development metadata and with all 76 runtime dependencies and `postinstall` kept.
- Final head `b40cfee13e` (after the CI-round fixes to refusal order, launcher-marker cleanup and restart ownership), same method on macOS arm64, Node 24.21.0: A→B through the release path, CLI exit 0, one succeeded run, trial committed after one restart (update wall 111.8 s), B serving with `/readyz` 200 and RPC build id `2026.11.6-b40cfee13e04-…`; all 76 runtime dependencies and `postinstall` kept.
- Bun-run package installs: preflight checks Bun's own capability contract (Bun 1.4.4+ with WAL-reset-safe `node:sqlite`, through the existing `isBunRuntime`/`resolveBunRuntimeInfo` owner) instead of comparing Bun's version with `engines.node`; packing uses the existing `resolveNpmCommand` (npm bundled with Bun, so a Bun-only host needs no system npm or Node) with `--quiet`, taking the tarball from the pack destination instead of parsing the multi-megabyte `--json` listing; the staged install runs `bun install --trust`; the staged manifest also drops checkout-only `workspaces`. Node installs keep the sibling npm. Real proof on macOS arm64 with Bun 1.4.5 (`c06f48cf9f`): A→B through the release path, a `--no-restart` pending trial committed on the next start, `ready`/`coreReady`, a succeeded row, Bun as both launcher and Gateway runtime.
- A large piped stdout from an exit-0 child arrived half-read under Bun in the shared command runner (1,376,256 of 2,854,736 bytes, no truncation flag); preparation no longer depends on that output. Filed separately as #203519.
- Downgrade and older-target qualification on a real macOS LaunchAgent profile: A→B committed with B serving over RPC; the shipped v2026.11.6 target refused before any change (state schema 41 > 36); a pre-release-path target refused before staging with the manual command; an ordinary native restart afterwards kept the launcher as parent; three requests left exactly three rows. The removed direct-switch route's dead-Gateway run and its manual recovery are kept in that report as the reason for the refusal.
- Combined local changed-test/importer runs hit timeouts in unchanged Git→package wrapper rollback and retained legacy pin-migration compensation; the former also produced a subsequent late-output assertion. The same CLI file and the isolated pin case passed unchanged with one worker; the pin case also passed on the merged baseline. The repair batch's combined call also timed out in retained cancellation/repair cases and the existing Git beta→package switch. All new release-support cases passed. No timeout or assertion was relaxed; hosted CI is the gate for these retained suites.
- The local `check:changed` SQLite-worker ratchet exhausted its fixed 4-GiB heap, as on #203194; that ratchet is left to hosted CI.

## Merge Danger

**One-way install conversion:** reverting source alone does not remove the release store, forwarding marker, or staged service definition. Previous releases and definition backups remain available. Writes during a failed trial can be lost; PostgreSQL migrations do not have data rollback. Blast radius: owned global package updates through the CLI, Gateway, and scheduler; shared read-only admission guards; and launchd restart ownership checks for resident-launcher Gateways.

prs.title: fix(clawrouter): preserve provider paths for Messages models
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

ClawRouter Messages models can advertise a provider-specific URL prefix, such as Cloudflare AI Gateway's `/anthropic/v1/messages`. OpenClaw discarded that prefix and sent requests to a different endpoint. Rejected or ambiguous catalog entries could also regain a configured model fallback.

Related: https://github.com/openclaw/clawrouter/pull/468

## User Impact

Eligible native Messages models use the catalog-selected route and Router credential. Rejected, withdrawn or ambiguous Messages offers fail before inference. Genuinely absent legacy offer metadata remains supported, and existing Vercel, Chat and Responses selection precedence is preserved.

## Why This Change Was Made

The client validates the provider, model, upstream identity, POST method and both Messages formats, then removes only the terminal `/v1/messages` suffix before handing the base URL to the Anthropic transport. Provider/model uniqueness uses the same normalized identity as catalog projection, so whitespace-equivalent duplicates cannot select another row's route or metadata.

This is a client correction. It does not activate or deploy Cloudflare support, close the related ClawRouter work, or establish shipping Worker/SQLite, physical upstream retirement or internal SDK reader/releaseLock behavior.

## Evidence

- The original registered HTTP regression reproduced the lost `/anthropic` prefix through both stream hooks. Additional red cases demonstrated rejected-offer fallback and ambiguous selection. On c6, all five normalized provider/model identity controls failed before the production correction.

- Corrected source passes **87/87 cases on Node 24.22.1 and 87/87 on pinned Bun**: the affected native-model-facts file plus the prior 78 cases in native-messages, provider-catalog, index and capability-offers. prs.title: docs(update): point update changes at src/update and mark the in-place updater as a bridge
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Owned installs (Git checkouts and npm, pnpm and Bun global installs) now update through prepared releases in `src/update/` (#200578, #203194, #203497). The instructions still send every update change to the in-place updater:

- Root `AGENTS.md` sends update changes to the update implementation contract in `docs/install/updating.md`. That section is about 1,000 lines of notes, most of them about the in-place flow ("the installed updater must contain this fix"). Nothing in it describes the release path or says where new update behavior goes.
- On 2026-11-22 and 2026-11-23, while the release path landed, five update fixes changed only the legacy code and no file in `src/update/` (#203529, #203555, #203486, #203578, #203849). For example, #203578 refuses an update while a node service holds the state database, but only on the legacy path.
- A fix to a shipped updater's own steps reaches users on that version only through a backport to their stable line, as v2026.11.7 carried #203097 and #202370. A fix on `main` alone changes only the routes that still use the legacy code.

## Changes

- `docs/install/updating.md`: the contract now starts with **Release updates**: the six-step path, the rules for update changes, and what the "installed updater must contain" notes mean now (they apply only to a shipped updater's first update). The existing notes stay, under **Recorded contract notes**, with one rule for adding new ones.
- New `src/update/AGENTS.md`: a file-by-step map of the owner, and a rule that a legacy fix for a behavior release updates also have lands in `src/update/` in the same PR.
- New `src/cli/update-cli/AGENTS.md`: marks the in-place updater as a bridge. It lists what still runs there: shipped updaters' first update and its contracts (migrated-finalize worker, post-core entry, `daemon-cli` exports, compat inventory), the routes not moved yet (`--dry-run`, Git↔package channel switches, `--tag main` packages, immutable installs, `update repair`, `update status`, legacy recovery admission), and Gateway `update.*` methods other than `update.run`. It also gives the rules for changing that code and the removal order.
- Root `AGENTS.md`: one sentence that points to both files.

## User Impact

None directly. Maintainers and agents now put update behavior in `src/update/`, and know when a legacy fix needs a stable-line backport to reach users.

## Evidence

- I checked the routes listed as still using legacy code against `updateCommandWithRuntime` in `src/cli/update-cli/update-command.ts` (release routing condition and fallthrough) and `routedUpdateHandlers` in `src/gateway/server-methods/update-run.ts`.
- I checked the launcher facts ("two failed starts", trial budget, Node built-ins only) against `src/update/launcher.ts`.
- `pnpm check:agents-md-size` (27 files within 20,000 chars), `pnpm format:docs:check` and `pnpm docs:check-mdx` pass. The `lint:docs` and `docs:check-links:anchors` failures are in files this PR does not touch (`docs/releases/*`, `tools/code-mode/troubleshooting.md`, and an untracked local `docs/internal` file). `git diff --check` is clean.

## Merge danger

Two-way door: docs and instruction files only. A revert fully undoes it. No code, config, state or published contract changes.

prs.title: test(macos): prove staged voice rpath normalization
prs.body:
## Purpose
Proof-only recovery for `macos-voice-rpath-45095807853`. Do not merge this one-off workflow into main or the release branch.

The macOS x64 preflight rejected a missing Codex voice-host Bazel runfiles LC_RPATH. The candidate extends existing staged-only normalization to that exact path form while leaving the portability audit unchanged.

## Native proof

prs.title: fix: preserve restarted child results and gateway test ownership
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Restarting the Gateway while a child result is being prepared can send that internal result through human-chat recovery and rebuild different input under its original idempotency key. The result can be cancelled or conflict with its accepted receipt.

Gateway test fixtures also duplicated Windows process ownership and contained outdated lifecycle assumptions, creating failed cleanup and misleading CI failures.

## User Impact

Child completion recovery keeps its original input and current owner across a restart. Human queued messages retain their existing principal, device and scope checks.

The raw-payload field already shipped for private completions now also retains public attempts, with an explicit non-private marker. Upgrades preserve old private semantics. Older binaries do not understand that marker: downgrading with outstanding public completion attempts is not covered by this change.

## Why This Change Was Made

- The freshly recovered, exact completion cohort owns its queued input; human replay neither dispatches nor cancels it. Unmatched, refused, browser-bound and explicitly ended inputs retain their existing handling.
- The completion owner retains pre-hook raw bytes for every attempt. Recovery reuses them only for the same run identity; a new retry still builds a fresh prompt. Strict full-message idempotency and authority checks remain.
- All platforms use the canonical Gateway process owner, preserving the absolute startup deadline and first cancellation error. Failed cleanup retains ownership.
- Lifecycle fixtures now follow the existing hook budget, Telegram replay, model admission, direct-chat restart, Gateway acquisition, retention maintenance, role enforcement and ready-child partition contracts.

Production +63 lines adds the missing completion ownership and raw-input preservation. Shared test infrastructure -104; tests +353; retired mock baseline -3; total +309. The duplicate Windows stopper and obsolete implementation-specific test are removed. No SQLite schema version or table changes. The two unmarked/stale-requester fixtures use the existing preparation hold to preserve the intended unconsumed result before marker edits; zero-input, pending-delivery and exactly-once assertions remain unchanged.

## Evidence

- Targeted formatting, Node syntax checks and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent owner review and scoped P0–P2 autoreview found no actionable issue. [Runtime validation of final head `7b35f40cb7745e24483ce739a5853a1e5777b496`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45106405982) passed: **58 jobs succeeded, 29 skipped, zero failed**, including the aggregate gate. The final static delta reviews were P0–P2 scoped-clean (0.88 and 0.85).
- [Raw-input unit proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45106405982/job/137469170477): 30/30 passed, including public/private/yielded retry payloads. [Custody and released-payload proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45106405982/job/137469170546): 16/16 passed, including both literal v2026.11.7 queued-private cases. Both executed under Bun on the final-head test merge `f8b08432f846e5a72c4c363a15c58bb23b7c1450`.
- [Completion restart proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45106405982/job/137469170401): **13/13 passed** under Bun, including preparing-announcing (40.445s), unmarked-requester (42.612s), and stale-settle-requester (42.595s). Those last two fixtures failed before restart on the prior head and now preserve their intended pending state. The original preparing-announcing failure is recorded in [CI45102016431](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45102016431); its strict idempotency assertion remains intact.
- Added regressions cover public/private/yielded completion bytes after a sibling changes, actual queued input ownership, explicit cancellation, replaced-session/run/agent/source rejection, and public/private failure-notice visibility. The custody test loads literal v2026.11.7 private registry/pending-row payloads, closes and reopens SQLite, then preserves the flagless private input and exact queued bytes/hash under recovered ownership. This proves payload compatibility, not execution of the old binary or a full historical schema migration.
- [Native Windows proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45088093522): 72 passed, 5 skipped at `4442d2af622d2866394f325e5bf674d9429befd2`; later changes preserve that execution path.
- [Published `2e01cd9` CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45104140507) finished with 46 passed, 28 skipped and 13 failed. The original preparing-announcing case passed (27.678s); eleven of thirteen completion cases passed, and all six restart-resume cases passed. Unmarked/stale-requester cases failed because graceful shutdown had already delivered the supposedly pending result; the final fixture holds preparation before consumption. Custody/wake unit tests were selected, but their exact execution result was not verified in that run.
- The same CI exposed an Iterable/array type mismatch and redundant session identity pin. Both are fixed in the final delta; the queue reader owns replaced-transcript exclusion.
- Local runtime testing remains unqualified because the shared dependency installation has a broken workspace link. Earlier task-owned Testbox allocations did not execute; the exact-head hosted run above supplied runtime proof.

## Limits and Follow-up

The original November 21 empty-attempt Windows failure did not reproduce; this PR does not claim to repair that historical incident. The native runner retained one temporary namespace without aggregate descendant-settlement proof.

Follow-up: preserve the specific missing-model refusal in session-event acceptance errors; that production path currently emits a generic admission failure.

prs.title: fix: refresh catalog scroll edges and show the installed skills count
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Skills and Plugins category strips could keep stale scroll-edge flags when their contents changed without a resize. On Skills, retrying a failed category request could leave newly overflowing categories without the correct edge controls. The collapsed Installed shelf also did not show how many skills were installed.

## User Impact

Category strips update their edge controls after content arrives, including a Skills category retry. The Installed shelf shows its count with an accessible heading. No migration, new setting, request-limit increase, or timeout change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Use the existing scroll-state revision contract to invalidate edges when category content changes, while preserving the strip element, current search/pagination behavior, and chip references.
- Show the installed count and keep the truncated name preview out of the accessible name.
- Share the existing Skills readiness/interaction steps between browser and benchmark consumers. Populate the shared transition fixture so direct visits and transitions both meet the same 20-result readiness contract.
- Keep the current Plugins discovery expectations: installed providers appear in search, rather than ordinary browsing or later discovery pages.

The earlier three-file upload-limit extraction is already on `main` through [#202756](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202756), so it is no longer part of this diff. This retains Patrick-Erichsen's contributor work and adds the bounded transition-fixture and Skills retry corrections.

## Evidence

The integrated candidate `33d2ccd7225f30d905088e6991388deea418a4fc`, compared with `6eb70d4ece4de1744cb88bdb7a2bfcf1f2351448`:

- The original-order Skills retry regression failed at the intended edge-state assertion before the owner fix, then passed with it. It checks the same strip element and geometry, zero scroll offset, exact category request count, and unchanged skill-search count.
- Node and Bun each passed 80 selected cases: 14 fixture cases, 45 scroll/discovery sibling cases, and 21 browser cases. No selected failures, skips, todo cases, or unhandled errors.
- Three desktop Chromium scenarios passed, including two route transitions. This is selected Chromium coverage, not whole-browser-suite or Firefox/WebKit coverage.
- Formatting, four type checks, typed lint, and the build passed. One existing lint warning remains in `catalog-results.tsx`.
- The unchanged enforcing performance comparison passed. Chat grew 389 gzip bytes to 1,334,126 (cap 1,334,480); New Session grew 389 bytes to 819,561 (cap 822,243). Request counts stayed 21 and 17, startup JavaScript was unchanged, and CSS decreased. This is a measured cost within the existing caps, not zero growth or a new exception.

The remote workload completed successfully. Its outer wrapper exited 7 during the first workspace-release attempt; the later native stop and independent verification confirmed resource/process settlement. Earlier failed attempts remain failed and are not counted as passing whole runs.

[Representative clean and annotated category-strip screenshots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202715#issuecomment-7090701544) compare the earlier `6eb70d4` and `efc8e461` plus transition-fixture correction, using the same synthetic inventory, Chromium, 390×844 viewport, English, and LTR layout. The clean images are byte-identical: they demonstrate preserved appearance, not reproduction of the Skills retry defect or screenshots of the final integrated commit. [The original installed-count screenshots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202715#issuecomment-7050055796) remain historical evidence.

Final native source review completed all five whole-file assignments with zero findings. Required hosted CI and ClawSweeper review of this exact published head remain pending.

<details>
<summary>Review scope</summary>

Eleven changed files, 636 gross lines: application source +18/−5, tooling +176/−95, and tests +259/−83. The application growth supplies content-change invalidation and the installed-count presentation through the existing owners; no parallel observer or fallback path is introduced.

</details>

prs.title: fix(slack): keep thread typing across queued follow-up turns
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Slack thread status is per thread, but each inbound dispatch owned its own typing lifecycle. A mid-turn mention that cannot be steered (claude-cli) is parked and later runs as a queued follow-up. That follow-up reused the predecessor dispatch's typing controller. Core cleanup seals that controller, and the channel callbacks close with it, so the queued turn never publishes `processing`. A stop from the parked or finished dispatch can also publish `active` while another turn on the same thread is still the one that should look busy.

## Why This Change Was Made

Admitted follow-ups now get a successor typing controller. The predecessor stays sealed. The successor reopens channel typing as a new generation, so a late stop from the sealed lifecycle cannot clear the new indicator. Slack session status uses the same generation: a parked pipeline that never published `processing` does not publish `active`, and a queued turn can publish `processing` again before its own visible output, then return to `active` when it finishes. Status writes are serialized, so a predecessor `active` request cannot take effect after the successor's `processing` request. A finished successor is not started again when that older request resolves. The existing visible-output gate still suppresses status once this turn itself has output.

## User Impact

In a Slack thread, a message sent while the agent is already working no longer drops the native working indicator just because that message was parked. When that message later runs as its own turn, Slack shows the working status again until the turn finishes.

## Evidence

Head: `d4ba62ab06df9b544c5eacf7bd8d1d5a2cac75c1`

Previous CI on `0573de80c75bfb19616c2d8ddc1c7bb13333262c` failed in two jobs:

- `check-lint-core-3`: `src/channels/typing.ts:103:7: error: Function 'stopIfCurrent' expected no return value. (typescript(consistent-return))`
- `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets`: `First-party mock factories must preserve real exports or explain isolation` for the new follow-up lifecycle test. The same job also warned `1073 -> 1074 counted lines (cap 700)` on `src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply.ts`.

Those are fixed without new suppressions. `stopIfCurrent` now always returns a promise. The lifecycle test spreads `importOriginal`. `get-reply.ts` no longer passes the silent-token default explicitly, so its counted lines move `1076 -> 1075` against current main. Local `check:test-mock-exports` and `check:line-cap-ratchet` against `upstream/main` passed. oxlint on the touched files is clean, including the extension tsconfig rule that rejected unbound test helpers.

Local publisher stub, no Slack Socket Mode and no user token. `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/followup-runner.typing-lifecycle.test.ts extensions/slack/src/monitor/message-handler/thread-status.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed. The follow-up runner drove the stub and printed:

`FOLLOWUP_EVENTS ["processing#0","active#0","processing#1","followup-started","active#1"]`

A later stop and start on that sealed predecessor did not append another event. With the predecessor `active` write held until after the successor had started, settlement was `["processing","active","processing"]`. When the successor also finished before that write resolved, settlement was `["processing","active","processing","active"]`, and a further stop published nothing.

The ordering regression fails on the previous cycle: while the delayed `active` write is still pending, the successor `processing` write is already in flight (`expected 2 to be 1`).

Maintainer decision still open: whether `beginNextLifecycle` should become a supported optional `TypingCallbacks` contract. Issue #158350 does not pin that public-API choice.

Fixes openclaw/openclaw#158350

prs.title: fix(telegram): exclude inactive transcript identities from channel context
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

After a Control UI rewind, cached Telegram chat-window rows from the cut branch can still reach the next turn. Projection-marker dedupe already on main only stops an active transcript turn from being added twice. It does not drop a cached row whose transcript identity is no longer on the active path.

## Why This Change Was Made

Two of the four leftovers named when #148525 closed are already on main. This PR lands the other two. Exclusion stays identity-based. It does not match rendered text, and it does not rebuild #148500 or #148525.

Landed:

1. Projected Telegram chat-window messages now carry `session_transcript_id` from their prompt-context projection marker.
4. Inactive-identity probes do indexed point reads against the active-path projection. Those reads resolve the session through the existing session-entry worker and run the membership query on the existing session history worker. The channel-window merge drops a cached row only when its transcript id, or its exact transport source-turn id (`channel-user:v1` hash of provider, account, conversation, and message id), is recorded and off the active path. Unknown identities, ambient rows, a cold or rebuilding projection, and `session:` ids are kept. The cache itself is not modified.

Already on main, not changed:

2. Persisted ambient rows are already excluded from the group-history channel window. `buildPromptContextForMessage` and `selectTelegramGroupPromptContext` both apply the ambient watermark before the window is kept. "omits transcript-owned ambient rows" covers that path.
3. Richer media and reply-target fields are already preserved. The chat window is built from cache nodes and clipped in place. The old thin `groupHistories` overwrite merge is gone, so there is no second copy that can drop those fields.

## User Impact

Rewinding a session keeps discarded cached turns out of the next channel context when those turns have a transcript id or the same transport identity the ingress writer stored. Retained history, new messages, and ambient rows without a proven identity still flow through. Control UI rewind semantics are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Rebased onto `upstream/main` `992724e0fd1ffae88578089c10550a003394d0eb`. Head `a6598d878491b48fc3e91aa3b69fb905c443105c`.

- `pnpm check:assertion-safety --base HEAD`, `pnpm check:database-worker-ratchet --base HEAD` (T1 455 -> 455), `pnpm check:line-cap-ratchet --base HEAD`, and `pnpm check:max-lines-ratchet --base HEAD` passed.

## What Problem This Solves

Bounded Codex app-server turns, including Codex Hosted Search, keep one automatically selected OpenAI auth profile. A structured usage-limit or rate-limit failure ends the turn even when `auth.order.openai` still has another eligible profile.

Automatic bounded turns now walk the canonical same-provider profile order after `usageLimitExceeded` or `rateLimitExceeded`. Retries share the original deadline and the existing app-server startup recovery. Planning resolves the effective agent directory once, loads ordered profiles through the async prepared store, and reuses that directory and store for startup and cooldown bookkeeping. When Codex reports a reset time, the failed profile is recorded with `markAuthProfileBlockedUntil` (`source: codex_rate_limits`). Pinned profiles, prepared auth, native user homes, and auth or credential failures stay fail-closed. There is no new config surface.

Closed PR #102402 proved the same rotation contract, then closed unmerged after the bounded-turn lifecycle gained a shared deadline, interruption, and startup recovery. This change rebuilds the retry around that current owner instead of transplanting the old loop. The agent-directory and async-store behavior follows clawSean's contributor-preserving replacement (https://github.com/clawSean/openclaw/commit/28a14a0b50ae01ff9139733b3871200e641b9f79) without rotating pinned or credential failures.

## User Impact

Operators with more than one eligible OpenAI profile can keep hosted search and other automatic bounded turns working after the first profile hits a usage or rate limit. An explicitly pinned profile still fails immediately. Native homes, prepared auth, and credential or authentication failures still fail closed and do not move to the next profile.

## Evidence

Local stub on head `916fa15c51cee00dcd3347345d40a258c4848833`. No live OAuth and no user API key. A fake app-server client returned a structured usage-limit error:

```text
PROOF usage-limit-rotation {"text":"The message was sent successfully.","profilesTried":["openai:primary","openai:backup"],"agentDirs":["/agent","/agent"],"storeForwardedToBothAttempts":true,"quotaBlock":{"profileId":"openai:primary","source":"codex_rate_limits","agentDir":"/agent","blockedUntil":1791945594000}}
PROOF pinned-fail-closed {"profilesTried":["openai:primary"],"attempts":1,"quotaBlocksAdded":0}
PROOF credential-fail-closed {"profilesTried":["openai:primary"],"attempts":1,"quotaBlocksAdded":0}
```

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/bounded-turn.auth-rotation.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 10 passed.
- Sibling `bounded-turn.test.ts` and `bounded-turn.clock.test.ts` passed.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` on the changed files — 0 warnings, 0 errors.
- Extension production and extension test `tsgo` passed.
- Assertion, line-cap, and max-lines ratchets passed. `OPENCLAW_*` count stayed 455/455.

Prior CI on `fafb78647d5` failed for real patch issues, now fixed without raising budgets: `only-throw-error` on `throw lastError`, test mock parameter types (`TS2322` / `TS2493`), and one uncommented type assertion in `bounded-turn-auth-rotation.ts`.

Fixes openclaw/openclaw#168231

prs.title: fix(signal): inline external-native outbound attachments
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Outbound Signal attachments are handed to signal-cli as a filesystem path under the gateway-owned `0700` outbound media directory. An external-native signal-cli daemon running as a different uid cannot traverse that path, so image and video sends fail at the last hop with `AttachmentInvalidException (Permission denied)` after the attachment was already validated.

## Why This Change Was Made

Native signal-cli already accepts an RFC 2397 data URI in place of a path, and the Signal plugin already has a bounded file-to-data-URI encoder for the container transport. External-native sends now reuse that encoder, so the already-authorized bytes travel over the open JSON-RPC connection. Managed-native still passes the staged path because that daemon shares the gateway uid. Container still receives the path and performs its own conversion. Directory permissions stay private, and this does not add a config switch or a new attachment channel.

## User Impact

Hardened deployments that run signal-cli as its own service user can send outbound media again. Same-uid managed-native sends and container REST sends keep their existing behavior. External-native payloads grow by about a third because the bytes are base64, and they remain bounded by the existing media size cap.

## Evidence

Head `5ef2734b8945cabaf2fd36f3f09c2dc46fd868aa`, rebased onto `upstream/main` `0e6eb6908bd5743aab9c1190998c3e89ce88974d`.

`check-test-types` on the previous head failed with a real type error:

```text
extensions/signal/src/send.test.ts(41,44): error TS2556: A spread argument must either have a tuple type or be passed to a rest parameter.
```

The hoisted attachment mock had dropped its rest parameter, so the `unknown[]` spread was illegal. Restoring `(..._args: unknown[])` matches the resolver mock on main. Local `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` then exited 0.

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-signal.config.ts \
  extensions/signal/src/send.test.ts \
  extensions/signal/src/media-access.test.ts \
  extensions/signal/src/outbound.media-limit.test.ts \
  extensions/signal/src/client-container.test.ts
```

```text
Test Files  4 passed (4)
     Tests  62 passed (62)
```

oxlint on the five changed files: 0 warnings, 0 errors.

Live JSON-RPC stub, no Signal account: `sendMessageSignal` staged a real 68-byte PNG under the private outbound media directory and posted to a local `POST /api/v1/rpc` stub. External-native carried a `data:` URI whose decoded bytes matched the file. Managed-native carried the staged path. The outbound directory mode was `700`. The JSON-RPC `id` is redacted. No phone number was used.

External-native body:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"send","params":{"message":"proof","account":"proof-account","attachments":["data:image/png;filename=chart.png;base64,iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAAAAEAAAABCAQAAAC1HAwCAAAAC0lEQVR42mP8/x8AAwMCAO+ip1sAAAAASUVORK5CYII="],"groupId":"proof-group"},"id":"<redacted>"}
```

Managed-native body:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"send","params":{"message":"proof","account":"proof-account","attachments":["/home/synth/.hermes/cache/scratch/oc-vt-Tihmj7/openclaw-signal-rpc-proof-6vc4G2/state/media/outbound/chart---1492f4c2-3cbe-43f7-8259-7ae195778ee2.png"],"groupId":"proof-group"},"id":"<redacted>"}
```

Fixes openclaw/openclaw#123815

prs.title: feat: let deployments manage Gateway skill changes and sources
prs.body:
Closes #203875

## What Problem This Solves

Operators who manage a Gateway from a deployment system cannot keep its selected skill set aligned with that deployment. Read-only configuration does not stop skill installs or publication, and normal file-backed precedence lets a same-named workspace skill replace an extra-directory skill.

## User Impact

Deployments can reject Gateway, plugin, and personal Library skill mutations while keeping reads available, and can pin each deployed skill name to an exact Gateway-hosted `SKILL.md`. Fresh authenticated sessions no longer seed retained Library entries while mutations are disabled; existing selections and delegated spawn inheritance are unchanged. Protect selected source directories with deployment-managed filesystem permissions. Unmanaged behavior remains unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Two process-owned controls provide the policy without a mutable Gateway config option: `OPENCLAW_DISABLE_SKILL_INSTALLS` and `OPENCLAW_PINNED_SKILL_FILES`. Gateway dispatch uses existing method scopes; direct authoring and Library services enforce the same restriction. Selection and resource delivery preserve the exact Gateway source across workspace collisions and compact session snapshots. Configuration cannot override either control. The environment-name ratchet budget increases by two for these owner-approved controls.

## Evidence

A disposable running Gateway rejected a managed skill install, retained skill reads, selected the approved source over a workspace collision, and kept that selection after restart. Focused production-path regressions and review cover direct Library and Workshop mutation paths. Verification below records the exact head, version, RPC outcomes, and limits.

## Verification

Tested head `86ccfacce0d4c09e534fe174ee251d802733b459`; the launched source CLI reported `OpenClaw 2026.11.6 (86ccfac)` on Node `v24.22.1`. The running Linux Gateway used disposable state, loopback token authentication with a generated test token, a clean environment, disabled bundled plugins, and synthetic skill files. Both the workspace and a Gateway extra directory contained a skill named `guide`.

- PASS: authenticated `skills.status` selected `guide` from `openclaw-extra`, description `Approved Gateway source`, path `<approved>/guide/SKILL.md`, rather than the workspace collision.
- PASS: read-scoped `skills.files.get` returned `# Approved instructions` from that selected file.
- PASS, expected refusal: `skills.install` returned `{"ok":false,"error":{"type":"gateway_request_error","code":"UNAVAILABLE","message":"Skill mutations are disabled on this managed Gateway.","retryable":false}}`.
- PASS: after stopping and restarting the same disposable Gateway, `skills.status` selected the same approved file again.

Focused production-path checks also passed for direct admitted model-tool Library refusal with retained reads, fresh-session seed suppression, Workshop refusal, compact-session resource preparation, forged provenance refusal, and config override denial. The personal Library regression first reproduced publication under the restriction, then passed after the fix. Targeted typechecks, lint, formatting, and independent focused review passed; ClawSweeper reviewed the live evidence on this exact head, found no code issue, and retained a compatibility-proof hold for a real model turn and a v2026.11.7 upgrade preserving existing session and Library state.

Limits: the running-Gateway proof did not execute a model turn, deliver a supporting file to a model/runtime, or upgrade from a stable installation. The public ClawHub SDK usage query was unavailable (`fetch failed`), and local autoreview could not start inside its required read-only sandbox.

Current CI has an unrelated failed shard: its cross-agent model-override failure matches the [scheduled-main job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45094583749/job/137431941353), and its Talk recovery failure is tracked in [#203507](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/203507).

prs.title: fix(test): recognize successful no-op release updates
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The published-upgrade survivor check fails when its second update is already current: the release updater now returns a lifecycle record, but the harness still expects the older command receipt. The observed failure is in [the legacy-operator-state main CI job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45090792955/job/137420023740).

## User Impact

No user-visible runtime changes. The upgrade check can recognize a successful no-op update without weakening its checks for package mutations, repairs, or incomplete plugin maintenance.

## Why This Change Was Made

Recognize the current lifecycle record in the existing no-op assertion. Require a finished, already-current update with skipped package staging, completed plugin maintenance, no extra steps, and no repair or repair request.

Retain the existing strict command-receipt checks because the harness also supports historical candidate tarballs. This changes only the harness and its existing regression table; no new helpers or runtime compatibility paths.

## Evidence

- The base assertion rejects a valid current lifecycle record; the changed assertion accepts it. This replay exercises the assertion payload itself, not a complete installed update.
- All 41 existing and added harness tests pass on isolated Linux (Node 24.22.1, 8 CPUs, 15.6 GiB RAM). The script-test TypeScript project, targeted lint/format, Bash syntax, and whitespace checks pass.
- The fresh full Docker attempt passed package build, integrity, registry preparation, installed update/migration, and Gateway/legacy-operator probes. It then failed at unchanged native-assignment recovery: a retained completion never reached its parent (0 requests, expected 1). This phase runs before the modified no-op assertion, which was not reached. The failure is unresolved; no full end-to-end pass is claimed.
- Normal PR [CI run 45107393770](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45107393770) passed for this head, including the applicable security and aggregate gates. Its preflight executed the two-parent test merge. This supersedes the earlier manual run that reported baseline unused-code errors.
- Local ClawSweeper review is complete at high reasoning for `ae1e9ee0fe765e1fcbeda2468f39761537f79f04` → `636cbcf8d646089f1cbb5b5c7390cd80a4169ac2`: no findings; security cleared. Its source/assertion review is separate from the execution results above.

<details>
<summary>Focused validation</summary>

```sh
CI=1 OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/test-projects.mts test/scripts/upgrade-survivor-update-noop.test.ts -- --maxWorkers=1
CI=1 node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.root.scripts.json --incremental
pnpm exec oxlint test/scripts/upgrade-survivor-update-noop.test.ts
pnpm exec oxfmt --check test/scripts/upgrade-survivor-update-noop.test.ts
bash -n scripts/e2e/lib/upgrade-survivor/run.sh
git diff --check
```

</details>

The two-file diff is +86/−34 lines, primarily indentation of the preserved legacy assertions and table cases for invalid current-record outcomes. No runtime files change.

prs.title: feat: rename saved model accounts in Models
prs.body:
Related: #202695

## What Problem This Solves

People can connect two model-provider workspaces that use the same email. In Settings → Models, those accounts can look identical, making it hard to tell which workspace or subscription you’re looking at.

## User Impact

User impact: Gateway administrators can rename a saved account without signing in again or restarting the Gateway. Leave the name blank to restore its default. Known subscription plans appear beside the account name; names controlled by configuration and accounts owned elsewhere remain read-only.

## Why This Change Was Made

The admin-only Gateway operation updates only the selected saved profile’s display label. It leaves credentials, authorization, profile IDs, and routing priority unchanged and publishes the new label to the running Gateway. A plan badge uses a known stored tier, not a new usage request. Reconnect name preservation moved here from #202667, which can shrink to the optional sign-in naming prompt after this lands. No sign-in prompt is included here. For xAI, reconnect preserves a custom name only when the previous and new OAuth credentials carry the same nonempty issuer and subject. An email match alone never carries the name to a replacement or unverified account. Token refresh rotates the grant without overwriting a saved label or restoring a label the user cleared.

## Evidence

- Real Control UI and isolated Gateway: two synthetic same-email accounts could be named independently; Enter saved, Escape sent no write, and clearing restored the default. Names and plan badges rendered correctly, and browser reload read back the result without restarting the Gateway.
- The isolated Gateway, real CLI, and synthetic HTTPS provider verified token rotation, ordinary reconnect, and reconnect with `--force`: the name survived all three. A different account replacing the same slot did not inherit the name. That flow adds no sign-in prompt or config write.
- Gateway tests covered non-admin denial, inherited and config-managed profiles, exact-row and priority preservation, and authorization-grant continuity. The protocol generation and compatibility checks passed without a protocol version change. All 72 focused tests passed, along with targeted lint, UI typecheck, and protocol checks.

- The follow-up reuses the existing form and chip styles. The Control UI budget check passed against the same base with zero added raw CSS (previously +359 B). All 64 focused UI tests passed; real Chromium verified rename, clear, and the editor at 390 px. The [Spanish settings-search CI failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44938469909/job/136950817376) also reproduces on clean `main` at `91566908` ([clean-main reproduction run, Team sign-in required](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/8c4423af-5bfd-4b09-965a-558474623e67)). The `modelo` search returns the extra `Modo de código` result. This PR does not fix it; see #203201 for the separate change.

- **xAI reconnect (`a36e1e37`):** Both the `oauth` request and the legacy `device-code` request (now routed to OAuth) lost the saved name before this fix. The same tests now pass for ordinary reconnect and `--force`, including same-email replacement and missing subject without name inheritance. The matcher separately rejects a different or missing issuer and blank identity, and does not load the OAuth runtime just to compare accounts. All 127 focused tests in eight files passed; the reconnect suite took about 12 seconds including setup (about 89 seconds across all focused suites). Targeted lint, format, xAI typecheck, and `git diff --check` passed.
- **xAI token refresh (`fbb0c87b`):** At the real refresh-provider boundary with synthetic OAuth responses, a provider-supplied name replaced both a saved label and a cleared label before the fix. Both regressions passed after the fix while the access and refresh tokens rotated and the account subject stayed intact. All 132 focused tests in nine files passed in about 78 seconds (including the reconnect cases); targeted lint, formatting, xAI typecheck, and whitespace checks also passed. This is focused provider/CLI-flow coverage, not a new packaged Gateway upgrade run.
- **Stable-upgrade proof at `fbb0c87b`:** A stock `v2026.11.6` Gateway seeded two synthetic xAI accounts. On a copy, the candidate preserved the saved names, credentials, profile IDs, routing order, and configured override before the first edit. Real CLI reconnect kept the saved label; actual Gateway token rotation kept a renamed label and did not restore a cleared label. Only synthetic credentials and a loopback provider were used.

**Chutes reconnect:** The real CLI and an isolated Gateway reproduced saved-name loss on `935ceb59` and passed on [the Chutes fix `45473eef`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/45473eef4ae1368cff1789f96acfee2718f035b4). With synthetic OAuth, the same authenticated UserInfo subject under the same OAuth client retained its saved label on ordinary reconnect and `--force`. A different subject or an absent subject did not inherit it, even with the same username. The persisted credentials were checked separately, and stock v2026.11.6 already stores the necessary identity fields. No live credentials were used. 35 focused tests, lint, formatting, typecheck, and runtime build passed on the Chutes fix.

**Current CI (`15931569`):** Sharing the xAI device-code test fixture brought the [hosted test-line ratchet to **394/400**](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45105249790/job/137465498873) with no dropped scenarios or production changes. All UI and UI E2E shards, Android Wear, and dependency review passed. The [required gate is still red](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45105249790/job/137472047671): all six Node assertions (three updater, one delayed session catalog, two requester revocation) reproduced with matching failures on both [the exact clean CI base `b151c830`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/b151c830713020fe0de9e37c3d21b76671fe0add) and the CI merge snapshot `4d24e6fb`. No changes for those inherited failures are included here.

**Validator conflict resolution (`3055bc2c`):** Regenerated protocol validators after integrating `main`. 69 focused tests, protocol registry and version checks, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. The Chutes and xAI implementations and their reconnect matcher are unchanged from `45473eef`. Full end-to-end proof was not repeated on this merge commit.

**Upgrade and xAI lifecycle on `935ceb59`:** Real Gateway/CLI proof passed from stock OpenClaw v2026.11.6 against two synthetic xAI accounts. Reconnect retained the saved name; controlled token rotation retained a renamed label and did not restore a cleared one. No live provider or inference was tested.

prs.title: feat: let the memory slot owner report its own dreaming status
prs.body: Related: #138366 ## What Problem This Solves A memory plugin that owns the memory slot and does its own consolidation has no way to describe its dreaming on the Memory page. The page reports dreaming as disabled or unscheduled while it in fact runs every night. Two host assumptions cause this: - `resolveMemoryDreamingConfig` gives all three phases the same expression, so a plugin whose REM and deep passes run on separate schedules, or whose light pass is event-driven, cannot say so. - The promotion counters come from memory-core's own store, which stops advancing once another plugin takes over consolidation. The workaround is worse than the symptom. Setting `dreaming.enabled: true` on the slot owner makes memory-core create its managed promotion cron at the same frequency, so the same workspace gets two consolidation passes in the same minute. ## Why This Change Was Made `MemoryPluginCapability` already has this shape once. `publicArtifacts` lets a non-`memory-core` slot owner contribute data through an optional provider, while the host keeps ownership of semantics. This PR applies the same pattern to dreaming: ```ts export type MemoryPluginCapability = { publicArtifacts?: MemoryPluginPublicArtifactsProvider; dreaming?: MemoryPluginDreamingProvider; // added // … }; ``` The contract is reporting-only. Lifecycle, memory-core's managed sweep cron and the dream actions stay with memory-core. The full rules are in `docs/plugins/sdk-overview/memory-and-context.md`: - **Overlay.** `doctor.memory.status` overlays the report field by field on the host resolution. Without a provider the response is unchanged. - **Every status path.** The provider is consulted with a search runtime, without one, and when the plugin answers through its own `providerRuntime` (new in this revision, see below). - **Owner lock.** Any report arrives as `reportedByProvider: true`. That locks the page's switch against turning the host sweep on, since both would dream at once. A running host sweep can still be turned off. The Off confirmation then says that the orphan-cron cleanup from #156667 (now on main, at plugin reload and at startup) removes the promotion job memory-core already scheduled. - **Switch and scene.** Reported `enabled` arrives as `reportedEnabled`. The switch keeps showing the memory-core configuration it writes. The Dreams scene lights while the owner reports running, or while a phase is enabled and scheduled. - **Counters.** Reported counters arrive as `reportedStats` next to memory-core's figures, not in their place. The Dreaming status line and Settings > Memory › Activity show the owner's counters, with n/a for any it omits. The Review lists keep memory-core's figures, entries and actions, together with a note that says so. - **Schedule rows.** Settings > Memory › Sleep schedule takes each phase's state from its own `enabled` and `scheduled` flags while an owner reports. ## Revision on current `main` This revision merges current main and resolves the two P2 findings of the last review: - **Provider-runtime slot owners.** A plugin that registers both `providerRuntime` and `dreaming.getStatus` took the provider-runtime branch, which returned before the dreaming lookup. That reply now carries the same composed dreaming section. `respondProviderMemoryStatus` keeps its authority checks, health and close. Test: `doctor.dreaming-provider.test.ts` › "composes the slot owner's report into a provider-runtime health reply". - **Admitted-plugin value contract (#163818).** The report now crosses by reference. The validator and copier helpers, their tests and the matching docs are gone. A throw or a `null` report still keeps memory-core's resolution. - **Ported onto main's new owners.** The payload fields now live on the `gateway-protocol` `DoctorMemoryDreamingPayload` type. The Dreams controls, review and confirmation dialog are now Solid. Settings > Memory › Overview is memory-core's packaged browser view (`extensions/memory-core/browser/overview.tsx`). Main's phase chips no longer show times, so the earlier "last run" chip helper was dropped. `lastRunAtMs` still appears in the Overview schedule rows. ## Evidence **Before / after on current main** (`pnpm dev:ui:mock`). Both runs use the same `doctor.memory.status` fixture: slot owner `acme-memory` reports REM/deep schedules, an event-driven light phase and `promotedToday: 4`, while memory-core's own count is 2 and the host switch is off. | | Before (main) | After (this PR) | |---|---|---| | Overview: phases and counters | | | | Dreams: scene and switch | | | **Live.** The previous revision of this change, on a 2026.10.10 build, has been running in a production installation since 2026-11-05 with a third-party memory slot owner that dreams on its own schedule. The Memory page shows the owner's schedule and counters, and memory-core's sweep stays off. **Patched Gateway (sandbox, 2026-11-09).** A Gateway built from this PR head (`5c7facacab3`, `pnpm build:runtime` plus the Control UI) ran isolated on loopback with no channels. The memory slot is held by a small **fixture** plugin, `acme-memory-fixture`, which registers `dreaming.getStatus` per this PR's contract and reports clearly fake data: REM 01:15, deep 04:00, an event-driven light phase, 4 promoted today / 139 total / 9 waiting. memory-core's own store was seeded with 1 waiting and 2 promoted today, so the two sets of figures stay visibly apart. Fixture source, seed script and the redacted config are in [`fixture/`](https://github.com/Cyb3rb1ade/openclaw/tree/085a88f5ac5116d948f162af22ac95905a0e5453/proof-2026-11-09/fixture); the [README](https://github.com/Cyb3rb1ade/openclaw/blob/085a88f5ac5116d948f162af22ac95905a0e5453/proof-2026-11-09/README.md) maps every file to a scenario. | Owner reports, host sweep off | Host sweep on: Off confirmation | |---|---| | | | - `reportedStats` separation and the Review comparison: [RPC](https://github.com/Cyb3rb1ade/openclaw/blob/085a88f5ac5116d948f162af22ac95905a0e5453/proof-2026-11-09/01-owner-reports-host-off.rpc.txt), [Review](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Cyb3rb1ade/openclaw/085a88f5ac5116d948f162af22ac95905a0e5453/proof-2026-11-09/01-owner-reports-host-off.dreams-review.png) and [Overview](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Cyb3rb1ade/openclaw/085a88f5ac5116d948f162af22ac95905a0e5453/proof-2026-11-09/01-owner-reports-host-off.overview.png) screenshots. The status line shows the owner's figures; memory-core's 1 waiting / 2 promoted stay in its own fields and Review lists. - Host sweep on (owner lock released, revised Off text): [RPC](https://github.com/Cyb3rb1ade/openclaw/blob/085a88f5ac5116d948f162af22ac95905a0e5453/proof-2026-11-09/02-owner-reports-host-on.rpc.txt), [cron list](https://github.com/Cyb3rb1ade/openclaw/blob/085a88f5ac5116d948f162af22ac95905a0e5453/proof-2026-11-09/02-owner-reports-host-on.cron-list.txt), [Dreams](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Cyb3rb1ade/openclaw/085a88f5ac5116d948f162af22ac95905a0e5453/proof-2026-11-09/02-owner-reports-host-on.dreams.png). - Provider-runtime branch: [RPC](https://github.com/Cyb3rb1ade/openclaw/blob/085a88f5ac5116d948f162af22ac95905a0e5453/proof-2026-11-09/03-provider-runtime.rpc.txt) with the composed dreaming section and `reportedStats`, [Dreams](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Cyb3rb1ade/openclaw/085a88f5ac5116d948f162af22ac95905a0e5453/proof-2026-11-09/03-provider-runtime.dreams.png); the [cron list after a restart with the host sweep off](https://github.com/Cyb3rb1ade/openclaw/blob/085a88f5ac5116d948f162af22ac95905a0e5453/proof-2026-11-09/03-provider-runtime.cron-list-after-host-off-restart.txt) is empty (no log line for the removal was captured). - Fallback with no report and with a throwing provider, on both paths: [04a](https://github.com/Cyb3rb1ade/openclaw/blob/085a88f5ac5116d948f162af22ac95905a0e5453/proof-2026-11-09/04a-fallback-provider-runtime-no-report.rpc.txt), [04b](https://github.com/Cyb3rb1ade/openclaw/blob/085a88f5ac5116d948f162af22ac95905a0e5453/proof-2026-11-09/04b-fallback-provider-runtime-provider-throws.rpc.txt), [04c](https://github.com/Cyb3rb1ade/openclaw/blob/085a88f5ac5116d948f162af22ac95905a0e5453/proof-2026-11-09/04c-fallback-search-runtime-no-report.rpc.txt), [04d](https://github.com/Cyb3rb1ade/openclaw/blob/085a88f5ac5116d948f162af22ac95905a0e5453/proof-2026-11-09/04d-fallback-search-runtime-provider-throws.rpc.txt), [log excerpt](https://github.com/Cyb3rb1ade/openclaw/blob/085a88f5ac5116d948f162af22ac95905a0e5453/proof-2026-11-09/04-fallback.gateway-log-excerpt.txt). Without a report the provider-runtime reply carries no dreaming section, and the other path keeps memory-core's figures. **Tests** (`pnpm test --maxWorkers=1`). The gateway, plugins and Overview tests and `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:extensions` and `tsgo:test:src` ran on the merge commit `a4f6587ad0b` (`main` at `f541dccb796`); the UI tests, `tsgo:ui`, `tsgo:test:ui`, lint and the ratchets ran again on `4e25af3ac82` after the line-cap refactor: - `src/gateway/server-methods/doctor.dreaming-provider.test.ts`, `src/plugins/registry.dual-kind-memory-gate.test.ts`: passed - `src/plugins/memory-state.test.ts`: 28 passed - `ui/src/pages/agents/memory/memory-panel.slot-owner.test.ts`: 10 passed. These are the owner-lock and counter tests, moved out of `memory-panel.test.ts` unchanged so both files stay under their line caps; the `wiki.get` reply normalization moved to `wiki-page-preview.ts` for the same reason. - `ui/src/pages/agents/memory/memory-panel.test.ts`: 35 passed, 1 skipped (pre-existing); `memory-panel.enablement.test.ts` (main's unavailable-config fix, kept in the merge): 9 passed; `toggle-confirmation.test.ts`: 5 passed; `view.test.ts`: 20 passed; `dreaming.test.ts`: 26 passed - `extensions/memory-core/browser/overview.test.tsx`: 28 passed - `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:ui`, `tsgo:extensions`, `tsgo:test:ui`, `tsgo:test:src`: clean. `oxfmt` and `oxlint` on all changed files (one existing `solid(reactivity)` warning from `main` in `view.tsx:406`, no errors), `check:line-cap-ratchet`, `check:max-lines-ratchet`, `check:test-lines-ratchet`: clean. Net test growth is +517; the allocation record now covers only the 117 above the 400-line per-PR allowance from #197602. No real timers, sleeps or Gateway boots in the new tests. **Plugin SDK surface.** The budget comment adds +3 type-only exports (`MemoryPluginDreaming{Provider,Status,PhaseStatus}`), on top of main's 3867. On this head `plugin-sdk:surface:check` reports public entrypoints 163 > 162, public exports 3891 > 3870, callable exports 2243 > 2236 and wildcard reexports 1 > 0. With this PR's three exports reverted it reports the same four overages (exports 3888 > 3870), so they come from `main`; this PR adds no entrypoint, callable export or wildcard.
