prs.title: feat: let operators select Codex MCP startup readiness
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A Codex user can choose whether an MCP server needs a live connection or can use a valid tool catalog to satisfy startup readiness. An operator configuring that same server in OpenClaw currently has no way to pass this choice to the app-server thread.

Related: #202199

## User Impact

Set `mcp.servers.<name>.codex.startupReadiness` to `"catalog"` or `"connection"` for an individual server. Omitting it preserves Codex's default. The option also works with the server's regular tool filter and approval settings.

## Why This Change Was Made

Codex already owns these two modes. Forwarding its setting keeps authentication, tool execution and approvals on the native path. OpenClaw still checks the current conversation's tool policy before thread startup. True first-use HTTP discovery remains open in #202199 and [openai/codex#2335](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/2335).

## Evidence

The projection regression failed before the change and passed afterward. It covers both explicit modes, omission, and a server with an exact tool filter. The config tests cover both valid values and an invalid one.

I also exercised Codex 0.160.0 on macOS arm64 with a loopback Streamable HTTP server, a fixed model response and a 250 ms delay in tool listing. For each mode I started one cold and two warm threads. All six greetings still initiated one HTTP handshake and one list request. Each follow-up read ran once and its result reached the model and final reply. The two modes had the same cold time to the first model request (319 ms), with overlapping warm timings.

### Isolated runtime evidence at `8963ae8715ca`

An isolated run loaded saved OpenClaw settings through this head's configuration schema and production per-run MCP projection, then passed its output to a real Codex 0.169.0 app-server thread. The model endpoint and HTTP MCP echo server were local fixtures. The stable 2026.11.6 CLI validated the existing configuration with the new field omitted. The candidate read those same bytes unchanged. Two further threads read explicit catalog and connection settings respectively.

| Saved option | Native thread/start config produced by OpenClaw | Successful echo in that thread | Tool-list calls before first use |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| omitted | key omitted | 1 | 2 |
| catalog | catalog | 1 | 2 |
| connection | connection | 1 | 2 |

All three threads completed the first turn and the permitted echo call on the second turn. Each preparation listed tools once and each native startup listed them once more. This shows the optional field round-tripping and old settings continuing to work. The test exercised the per-run configuration function and a real native thread with synthetic inputs. It establishes no HTTP-discovery or latency improvement and leaves the public option to the maintainers.

### Current upstream integration

Merged upstream main `8d1e59c2fddc`. At `2978e5b08390`, the official generator reconciled the configuration baseline and its check passed. All 42 focused MCP configuration and schema tests passed locally. A Gateway run with an authorized live provider remains outstanding. [Hosted CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45033550659) awaits maintainer approval (0 jobs).

### Remaining Gateway proof

The isolated capture above verifies the saved setting, native thread projection and successful echo. The full Gateway-to-model turn requested in the latest review is still outstanding. It needs a reviewed runner with a test-scoped provider identity. The direct preparation capture uses a synthetic model. It establishes neither the full Gateway result nor a reduction in discovery work.

prs.title: improve(ci): start long upgrade checks before the final validation wave
prs.body:
## Performance hold — November 23, 2026

**Not currently RFR.** New fully drained workload evidence models a small wall-time regression on one trace. This supersedes the November 21 readiness assessment; do not land under the task's no-wall-time-regression requirement without resolving or explicitly accepting this tradeoff. No code or validation coverage was changed during this reassessment.

## What Problem This Solves

Long ACPX tool-bridge upgrade checks can wait behind the matrix cap and finish last. Add `acpx-openclaw-tools-bridge` to the existing stable priority list, after `plugin-update` and before `legacy-operator-state`. Preserve complete row objects, baseline/scenario identities, timeouts, independent failures/retries, fresh-container isolation, concurrency caps and stable remainder order. No new planner, cache, setting, jobs or runner capacity.

This extends #198925 (`8656c447df05`) and #199911 (`f947bdc94981`), preserving their deliberate recovery-first policy. #202688 separately raises the qualifying hosted cap from 48 to 64. Do not add standalone savings together. Simplified implementation: production +2/-0, existing test +3/-1, docs +5/-0.

## Original four-trace evidence

All four matrices have 92 successful rows and drained parents, not passing release qualification. Full job durations include setup, downloads, execution and cleanup. Earliest-free-slot replay uses frozen source-planner order and retains the observed 0–3s residual plus sibling/collector barriers.

| Parent / candidate child | Observed matrix | Base48 → proposed48 | Total FRV gain at48 | Incremental total gain after64 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|[44773914831](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44773914831) / [44777975959](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44777975959)|3150s|3148→2812s|336s|287s|
|[44790287992](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44790287992) / [44794544663](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44794544663)|3032s|3029→2697s|332s|329s|
|[44635836314](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44635836314) / [44639105831](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44639105831)|2912s|2910→2902s|0s; CI barrier|0s|
|[44832835993](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44832835993) / [44835864437](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44835864437)|2704s|2704→2704s|0s; first-hop barrier|0s|

The first two final ACPX rows are [136440786047](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44777975959/job/136440786047) and [136497002115](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44794544663/job/136497002115), with 1441s/1414s admission delay and 1709s/1618s execution envelopes. The November 21 93-row current-source comparison preserved identical complete row objects. Historical inventories were replayed separately, not padded with invented timings.

## New adverse evidence

Both new matrices have **90/90 successful targeted rows**, terminal children, no requested cancellation and matching execution-plan/drain digest fields. They target C `bbcf2a4a90962e6988191124847c244588fee57c` (2026.11.10-beta.2), using the 2026.11.6 upgrade baseline. They are not successful qualification: parent45087316190 is `blocked_complete` with four reused independent children; parent45076850560 is `orchestration_error`. Reused child timestamps remain their actual earlier timestamps.

Replay reconstructs all 90 rows from the exact planner and dependencies at Q `9b6d7844abc46e483efacc19d9f787cad57c3473`, with the logged baseline/scenario inputs and frozen compatibility inventory. Exact label-set equality is asserted. Do not use observed timestamp order as a substitute for source order when jobs start together.

| Parent / candidate child | Observed matrix | Base48 → proposed48 | Total FRV change at48 | Base64 → proposed64 | Incremental total change at64 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|[45087316190](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45087316190) / [45089693610](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45089693610)|3018s|3015→2787s|228s faster|2724→2452s|272s faster|
|[45076850560](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45076850560) / [45078959662](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45078959662)|2777s|2774→2780s|**6s slower**|2413→2432s|0s; 19s matrix regression hidden by CI|

Both retain their +3s replay residual. On45076850560, normal CI ends23:37:17 UTC; the observed candidate seals23:39:01. At64, either candidate ordering finishes before that CI floor, so cap64 alone and the combined changes each model only104s total gain. At48 the six-second ordering regression is exposed. Retained32-cap sensitivity also regresses26s/9s on these new duration sets. These are deterministic model results, not measured production regressions, and small relative to real runtime variability; they still invalidate a blanket nonregression claim.

I evaluated all eight simple insertion positions. None removes the new48-cap regression; moving the same priority entry is not a demonstrated repair. I did not add release/version-specific exceptions, retune the planner to memorize these traces, weaken tests or dispatch another campaign.

## Residual critical path

After both changes, latest candidate45089693610 is limited by [update-restart-auth137420388190](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45089693610/job/137420388190): 00:49:45–01:30:37 UTC,2452s. The next replay chain is2451s, so optimizing that row alone initially exposes only1s of matrix benefit. Its required workload includes a723s baseline→candidate update,267s standalone Doctor and872s candidate→future managed-restart update. The latter verifies replacement of the serving supervisor and authenticated serving afterward; these are not independent tests that can simply be split without changing coverage.

## Validation and remaining decision

Head remains `93897401daea0182b165e9138a9942deaa1541b7`. November23 refresh:49 successful checks,73 skipped,1 neutral; no failed or pending checks. GitHub reports OPEN, MERGEABLE, CLEAN. [ClawSweeper completed this head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202894#issuecomment-7056571971) without findings on November21, **before this new adverse performance evidence**.

Original proof remains valid: existing real-CLI regression red on base/green on this entry; complete row and ordering assertions;740 affected tests passing; targeted typecheck, type-aware lint, format, MDX and diff checks passing. Local independent-review waiver retained. No new tests, code, FRV dispatch or native campaign were added today.

**Recommendation:** hold this PR rather than claim it meets the no-regression task acceptance. Resolving the conditional scheduling tradeoff requires owner judgment or a genuinely general improvement with new proof. Deeper candidate-owned update/Doctor profiling is separately blocked in this environment: no Docker socket, no paired node, and configured Crabbox provider authentication unavailable. No new service, credential change or paid allocation was attempted.

## Reproduction

Use `scripts/plan-targeted-docker-lane-groups.mjs` and its dependencies at the Q above. Logged inputs from [planner job137419365496](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45089693610/job/137419365496):

prs.title: fix: stop Gateway memory growing on every plugin reload
prs.body:
Refs: #198802

## What Problem This Solves

A Gateway that reloads plugins — cron, hooks, or a plugin path repointed on each release — grows its heap until it hits the cap and needs a restart. Each rebuild leaves another full copy of every plugin's native member map reachable for the life of the process, so a long-running Gateway keeps growing even after the plugin that owned those bytes is gone.

## User Impact

Reloading plugins no longer accumulates native namespace maps in the process admission cache. Operators who hot-reload plugins see the retainer from #198802 stop growing per rebuild instead of reaching `--max-old-space-size` after several days.

This does not replay the full Gateway workload reported in #198802, so that issue stays open; it closes the one retention path named below.

## Why This Change Was Made

`createNativeRecovery(...).retain(cache)` copies every namespace of a generation into the shared process admission state (`state.namespaces.set(key, namespace)`). Disposing that recovery dropped its capture pins and its roots, but never touched `state.namespaces` — so each rebuild left another complete member map on the process cache, including maps for plugins that are now disabled.

Two generations can adopt the same capture root (a fork and its parent, or a newer admission that reuses a namespace), so a plain `delete` on dispose would strip namespace resolution from a sibling that is still live. The fix counts adoption per owning recovery in `plugin-native-admission-state.ts` and releases it on dispose, keeping any entry that a live receipt, file fact, or sibling generation still names.

`#199042` fixed a different path — a same-key receipt replacement pruning a namespace map on rename. It does not release maps when a generation is disposed, which is the path here.

## Evidence

New tests in `src/plugins/plugin-native-admission-recovery.test.ts` cover the three states that matter:

- a disposed recovery's namespaces leave the shared map;
- disposing one of two generations sharing a capture root leaves the sibling's namespaces resolvable;
- five repeated capture/retain/dispose rounds keep the shared map bounded and empty after each dispose.

<details>
<summary>Red on base, green with the fix</summary>

On the base commit (`907e17b9ff`, which contains #199042 and #200320) the three new tests fail because the shared map still holds a namespace after the generation is disposed:

```
✓ puts a published namespace back in the shared map after a prune
✓ keeps a recovered namespace resolvable after a newer receipt prunes the shared map
× drops a disposed recovery's namespaces from the shared map
× keeps a sibling generation's namespaces when one recovery is disposed
× does not grow the shared map across repeated generation rebuilds
```

With the fix:

```
✓ drops a disposed recovery's namespaces from the shared map 72ms
✓ keeps a sibling generation's namespaces when one recovery is disposed 133ms
✓ does not grow the shared map across repeated generation rebuilds 62ms
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  5 passed (5)
```

The sibling test is load-bearing: degrading the release to an unconditional `state.namespaces.delete(id)` turns it red (`expected +0 to be 1`), because a live fork then loses the map its parent still needs.

</details>

Consumers of the changed state module still pass — 52 tests across `plugin-generation-artifact.admission.test.ts`, `plugin-generation-artifact.native-reference.test.ts`, `plugin-module-generation.disposal.test.ts`, and `plugin-native-namespace.test.ts`:

```
Test Files  4 passed (4)
     Tests  52 passed (52)
```

`oxlint` (including the 700-line limit on `plugin-native-admission.ts`) and `oxfmt --check` pass on the changed files.

## Merge Danger

Low. The change is additive: a new counter map in `plugin-native-admission-state.ts` and one line in `retain()`. The release path only deletes a namespace when no live receipt, file fact, or sibling generation names it, so a live admission keeps resolving exactly as before. Nothing changes about capture, admission validation, or publication.

The counter lives in module-level `WeakMap`s keyed by `AdmissionState`, so it disappears with the state and needs no separate cleanup on cache retirement.

prs.title: fix(message): keep accepted message ids when a send fails partway
prs.body:
Closes #195066

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a message send that delivers one message and then fails on a later part hides the delivered message id, so the caller cannot tell partial delivery from total failure.

## User Impact

Callers (agent tool calls and MCP clients) now see which messages already landed and that the rest is unconfirmed, while the send still reports failure. This prevents resending content that was already delivered.

## Why This Change Was Made

Ordinary sends throw `ChannelPartialDeliveryError` when a later part fails. The typed error carries the provider-accepted message ids, but both error surfaces - the native tool error result and the MCP `tools/call` response - project only the error text, so the ids were lost.

The fix projects the partial delivery at the message-tool boundary (`projectMessageActionPartialFailureResult`) and returns a result with `ok: false`, `deliveryStatus: "partial_failed"`, `sentBeforeError: true`, the accepted message ids, and `remainderUnconfirmed: true`. The native harness and the MCP handler both classify a returned result through its details, so each caller keeps failure semantics and gains the delivery facts. Scheduled authority keeps its existing projection, and queued delivery is unchanged.

Some transports (X) attach accepted ids only to the receipt, not to `messageIds`; the projection now falls back to the receipt's platform message ids. The production transport run below is what exposed that case.

## Evidence

### Production transport proof (after fix, head `64348875802`)

Harness: the real `createMessageTool` and the real MCP `tools/call` handler, routed through the real X channel action, the real `sendXDelivery`, and the real `createXApiClient` transport client, issuing real HTTP requests. Only the HTTP responses were controlled: `POST /2/tweets` accepted the first post with id `100000000000000021`, then rejected the second post with HTTP 403. Credentials, ids, and content are synthetic; no live endpoint, real account, or user data was involved, so nothing needs redaction.

Observed caller-visible result on both surfaces (identical text payload; MCP sets `result.isError: true`):

```json
{
  "ok": false,
  "action": "send",
  "deliveryStatus": "partial_failed",
  "sentBeforeError": true,
  "error": "X reply chain failed after one or more posts were sent | X API /2/tweets failed (HTTP 403) | OPENCLAW_PLATFORM_MESSAGE_NOT_DISPATCHED | OPENCLAW_PLATFORM_MESSAGE_NOT_DISPATCHED",
  "acceptedMessageIds": ["100000000000000021"],
  "remainderUnconfirmed": true,
  "message": "Delivered 1 message(s) before the send failed; the remaining content is unconfirmed. Do not resend the accepted message(s)."
}
```

Transport requests observed in the run: one `POST /oauth2/token`, one `GET /2/tweets?ids=90` recipient lookup, and two `POST /2/tweets` posts per surface (accepted, then rejected).

### Caller-boundary regressions

- `pnpm test src/agents/tools/message-tool-execution.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` - 71/71 pass; the partial-delivery cases fail on base (`8a6761d8690`), where both tool calls throw and lose the ids.
- `pnpm test src/gateway/mcp-http.partial-delivery.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` - red on base with `"second attachment failed"` alone, green with the accepted id and `isError: true`.
- New receipt-only case: red on base, green with `64348875802`.

The MCP case drives the real message tool and the JSON-RPC handler instead of feeding a fabricated projection result into a mock tool, so it fails if the production catch integration is removed.

### Checks

- `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:test:src` pass.
- oxlint on the changed files: 0 findings; repo format check passes.
- Suites re-run green: `message-tool.test.ts`, `message-tool-execution.test.ts`, `message-tool.scheduled-lifetime.test.ts`, `message-tool.scheduled-writes.test.ts`, `mcp-http.test.ts`, `agent-loop.async-tools.test.ts`, `agent-tools.prefix-stability.test.ts`, `message-action-execution{,.accepted-results,.source-reply}.test.ts`, `outbound-payload.contract.test.ts`.
- Test-line budget: this change adds 117 net test lines and `config/test-lines-allocations/195224-partial-delivery-ids.txt` grants exactly that growth. The ratchet is still 28 lines over from the shared comparison base, unchanged by this PR (another open PR run on the same base reports the same 28-line overage).
- `pnpm check:changed`: typecheck core, lint, format, line-cap, and assertion-SAFETY ratchets pass. `changelog attributions` (repo-wide) fails on the base commit for unrelated reasons.

Gap: the transport proof is a controlled-response production path, not a live channel post; the reproduction matches the reported failure and never contacts the real provider.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The CI failure reporter executes shell Node without first selecting the workflow's declared supported version. The checkout-free CI gate also relies on whatever shell Node happens to be installed to render its failure summary. This is runtime-contract hardening, not a demonstrated runner outage.

Dallin requested this separate, narrow CI fix.

## User Impact

No product behavior changes. CI explicitly selects its supported Node runtime for failure classification, while the gate retains its checkout-free contract and the same summary and machine-readable failure output. No new package dependencies, permission changes, or user actions.

## Why This Change Was Made

The sparse reporter checkout now includes the existing `ensure-node.sh` helper and calls it with `NODE_VERSION` before running the reporter. This avoids installing pnpm, Bun, or workspace dependencies just to select Node. The gate uses Python's standard-library JSON decoder instead of shell Node; its lane decisions and failure-classification rules are unchanged.

Author self-review and simplification kept the original runtime fix to two files; no new runtime owner or helper. Local autoreview and independent prepublication review were skipped as explicitly requested. ClawSweeper completed the initial review and the repair-head re-review with no actionable findings. One repair-head re-review request was posted after verifying no matching review was pending.

prs.title: feat: filter shared sessions by owner or involvement
prs.body:
Replaces #191138, which is far behind `main`. This is a focused port of request-scoped relationship filters onto the current Session Share owners, and it consolidates the plugin's optional node commands into one pair.

## What Problem This Solves

The sidebar's **Owned by** / **Involving me** filters run on rows already downloaded from a shared source, so matching sessions on later source pages never appear. Selection has to happen on the source before pagination, and survive opening, paging and importing the selected session.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **One optional catalog pair.** Session Share keeps `openclaw.sessions.list.v1` / `read.v1` unchanged (with their desktop default) and adds one optional node pair, `openclaw.sessions.catalog.list.v1` / `.read.v1`. List takes an optional `profileRelation` and `includeOriginalPath`; read takes an optional `profileRelation`. It replaces every optional variant, including the unreleased `list-with-links.v1` from #203044, so "Open original" now uses the catalog list with `includeOriginalPath: true`. Outbound Gateway sources get the matching `session-share.catalog.list` / `.read` methods, advertised in `features.methods`; they never carry original links.
- **One receiver path.** A node that advertises the pair gets every list and read through it; other nodes use the legacy pair.
- **Selection narrows, never widens.** The source intersects the relation with its own publication boundary (groups, `share.involvingProfileId`, device grants, read rechecks) before pagination. Cursors are bound to their relation.
- **Visible fallbacks.** When the receiver viewer has no verified GitHub link, the source cannot resolve the target, or the source is older or unapproved, the receiver keeps the authorized rows, filters them client-side, and marks the host `FILTER_PARTIAL` with guidance. The source reports an unresolved target as a typed `relationUnresolved` page (from a closed `PROFILE_RELATION_UNRESOLVED` code), not as error text.
- **Capability-gated UI.** The Control UI sends `profileRelation` only when a catalog advertises `capabilities.profileRelation`, in one aggregate `sessions.catalog.list`; the Gateway forwards it only to providers that support it.
- **Freshness unchanged.** Every explicit catalog request starts a fresh source read, as on `main`; snapshots are keyed by node and relation, and eviction protects only the snapshots a request needs.

## User Impact

Nothing is enabled by default. Setup is in `docs/plugins/session-share.md` ("Open original on a paired node", then "Relationship filtering"): allow the catalog pair in `gateway.nodes.commands.allow` on the receiver, reinstall the source node with all four session commands in `--commands`, and approve the widened surface with `openclaw nodes pending` / `openclaw nodes approve`. Until then the receiver uses the legacy pair: shared sessions stay readable and filters fall back to client-side matching with guidance.

Disclosure, documented under Security boundary: an approved reader can name any numeric GitHub account as the target, and the results can show whether it resolves on the source and its owner, participant or mention membership within sessions already published to that reader. Source profile-ID targets are not accepted.

Config surface: no new config keys (help text only). If you type a prompt in the Cmd+K composer and then switch models, Send can stay disabled after the new model is selected. Editing the prompt makes Send come back.

prs.title: infra: add generic circuit breaker
prs.body:
## Summary

- Add a reusable circuit breaker primitive to `src/infra/circuit-breaker.ts`.
- The project currently has ad-hoc circuit breaker implementations scattered across Nostr relays, Telegram sendChatAction, Feishu typing, and tool-loop detection. This adds a generic, tested utility that can be used by any subsystem (providers, channels, extensions) to protect against cascading failures.

## Design

Standard three-state circuit breaker (closed → open → half-open):

- **Closed**: requests flow through; consecutive failures are counted.
- **Open**: requests are rejected immediately with `CircuitBreakerOpenError`; after `resetMs` elapses, transitions to half-open.
- **Half-open**: a single probe request is allowed; success closes the circuit, failure re-opens it.

Options:
- `failureThreshold` (default 5): consecutive failures before opening
- `resetMs` (default 30s): cooldown before half-open probe
- `shouldTrip`: optional predicate to filter which errors count
- `now`: clock override for deterministic testing

## Test plan

- [x] 9 unit tests covering all state transitions, threshold enforcement, shouldTrip predicate, manual reset, and edge cases
- [x] All tests pass: `pnpm vitest run src/infra/circuit-breaker.test.ts`

prs.title: CI: re-enable dead-code report and add CodeQL security analysis
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Re-enable dead-code detection job** in CI: the `deadcode` job was fully implemented (knip, ts-prune, ts-unused-exports with artifact uploads) but disabled with `if: false` while initial findings were triaged. It is report-only (not a hard gate), so re-enabling it won't break CI — it simply makes dead code visible again.
- **Add CodeQL security analysis workflow**: the project has secret scanning, dependency audit, and workflow audit, but no code-level SAST. This adds GitHub CodeQL for TypeScript/JavaScript with `security-extended` queries, catching vulnerabilities like prototype pollution, path traversal, and ReDoS.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `.github/workflows/ci.yml` | Restore original `if` condition on `deadcode` job (remove `if: false`) |
| `.github/workflows/codeql.yml` | New workflow: CodeQL analysis for `javascript` (covers TS) |

## Test plan

- [ ] CI `deadcode` job runs on next PR that touches code (produces artifact, does not gate)
- [ ] CodeQL `analyze` job runs on next PR that touches code (results appear in Security tab)
- [ ] Docs-only PRs skip both jobs (via `paths-ignore`)

prs.title: fix: show app update guidance instead of a failing Update button on app-managed Macs
prs.body:
Closes #198506 Prior work: #198562 tried this and was closed without merging because the update handlers it edited have since moved. This PR is written against current main. ## What Problem This Solves On a Mac where OpenClaw.app owns the Gateway, Settings > Updates still shows an enabled "Update Gateway..." button and an "Update status unavailable" row. Clicking the button gets a refusal from the Gateway ("Managed by OpenClaw.app. Update OpenClaw.app to update this Gateway."). The page then keeps that refusal as an update error with a "Retry update" button, and the error stays until the page is reloaded. A healthy install looks like it failed an update, and Retry cannot succeed because the Gateway marks the refusal as not retryable. ## User Impact User impact: on an app-managed install, Settings > Updates now says "Managed by OpenClaw.app" in the status row and shows the app's own guidance ("Update OpenClaw.app to update this Gateway.") where the update button used to be. There is no button to click, so no error appears and nothing is left to retry. Other installs (package, Git checkout, separately managed Gateways) look and behave as before. ## Why This Change Was Made The Gateway already knew the install was app-owned, but `update.status` dropped that fact, so the page had no way to tell this install from any other and offered the normal action. The Gateway now sends the owner under `schedule.install.host`, and the Settings page uses it. Ownership comes from the same install marker the Gateway's refusal already uses, so a Mac connected to a separately managed Gateway still gets the normal update flow. The protocol schema gains an optional `install.host` object and a `host` install kind, and the generated validators are regenerated from it. The Control UI adds four English strings. The updating doc notes where the owner is reported. Update behavior: this only changes what `update.status` reports and what Settings shows. Config, the state schema, migrations and the way updates run are untouched. An app-owned Gateway still refuses Gateway update requests with the app's hint, and package and Git installs keep their current update flow. ## Evidence ClawSweeper's last review left two pieces of end-to-end proof open: the built Settings flow, and an upgrade from v2026.11.6 that keeps settings and data. The Settings flow is covered below. The upgrade is not (see Not verified). The current head, `8a511b6`, is `1b71766` rebased onto main `15e5f75`. Apart from the generated `predicates.js`, which was regenerated from the schema, its diff is identical to `1b71766`'s, so the browser run on `1b71766` recorded in [this comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200910#issuecomment-7066419264) applies to this head. That run built fresh Gateways with `pnpm build:ci-artifacts` from the base (`dc6e31a`) and from `1b71766`, both with the Mac packaging ownership marker, and ran the same Settings > Updates steps in Chromium on each. The changed Updating guide was built with `docs:build:preview` on both sides. Before, Settings offered "Update Gateway…", confirming it left the ownership refusal as an update error, and the guide did not mention the Settings display. After, Settings shows "Managed by OpenClaw.app" with the app's guidance and no Gateway update button, and the guide describes that behavior. The screenshots below come from an earlier run of the same steps against Gateways built from `d119c6b` and `0f678cb`, using the exact ownership marker written by the Mac packaging script, with fresh Gateway state and no model or credentials. `0f678cb` has the same hand-written changes as the current head. Before: Settings shows "Update status unavailable" and offers "Update Gateway…". Confirming it leaves "Couldn’t update OpenClaw. Managed by OpenClaw.app. Update OpenClaw.app to update this Gateway." in the status row. `update.status` returned `schedule.install: null`. After: Settings shows "Managed by OpenClaw.app" and the guidance "Managed by OpenClaw.app. Update OpenClaw.app to update this Gateway." There is no Gateway update button. `update.status` returned `schedule.install: {"kind":"host","host":{"owner":"macos-app","displayName":"OpenClaw.app","updateHint":"Update OpenClaw.app to update this Gateway."}}`. With main's sources at `dc6e31a` and this PR's tests, the new Settings test fails the way the issue describes: the status row reads "Update status unavailable" where it should say "Managed by OpenClaw.app". The 9 Gateway and schema cases that expect the owner fail the same way. On the current head, all of them pass.
Tests and checks on the current head (Node 26.8, macOS arm64) - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` over the five changed test files: 93 tests pass. That is 43 in `ui/src/pages/config/updates.test.ts`, 28 in `src/gateway/server-methods/update-status-schedule.test.ts`, 12 in `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/config.test.ts`, and 10 across `src/infra/update-install-status.test.ts` and `src/infra/update-startup-host-owned.test.ts`. The three new cases took 21 ms (Settings), 283 ms (update status schedule) and 2 ms (schema). - `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:ui` pass. Type-aware `oxlint` on the 11 changed TypeScript files reports no diagnostics. - `pnpm gateway:validators:check` reports no drift, and `git diff --check` is clean. - `oxfmt --check`, the line-cap ratchet, docs markdown lint, `protocol:check`, `ui:validators:check` and `ui:i18n:verify` passed on these same file contents before the final rebase onto `15e5f75`, which left all 13 files unchanged.
Not verified: - No run inside OpenClaw.app itself. The browser runs above used Gateways built from source with the Mac packaging marker. The issue's reporter offered to check a fix on their Mac. - No upgrade from a released version with settings and data kept. I tried one with the published v2026.11.6 in an isolated home, but my test environment blocks the process listing that release uses to verify SQLite ownership, so it could not read its own config there. - A separately managed Gateway was not run in a browser; the existing `updates.test.ts` cases for the "Update Gateway…" action still pass. - The full `pnpm check:changed` was not run.

prs.title: fix(models): preserve unknown prices and limits across 12 discovery providers
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Missing model prices and token limits were converted into free pricing or invented capacities, while ClawRouter discovery used static cards instead of the selected account's advertised inventory.

## User Impact

Unknown prices and limits remain unknown. Selected endpoint pricing takes precedence by presence: absent inherits global pricing, explicit null stays unknown, and zero/partial rates remain intact. Explicit zero prices and authoritative billed totals, including zero, are preserved. Models stay listed when limits are absent; Anthropic requests require an explicit or qualified output bound before dispatch. Chat shows unknown cost separately from a recorded zero.

When ClawRouter advertises a supported discovery offer, the selected proxy credential retrieves its complete catalog. A successful empty catalog suppresses static seeds. Supported families are Cerebras, NVIDIA, Chutes, Venice, Baseten, Arcee, Novita, Featherless, DeepInfra, Bifrost, LiteLLM and Requesty.

## Why This Change Was Made

The runtime types now permit partial prices and absent output limits. Resolution, persistence, usage aggregation and reporting preserve that absence instead of filling it with zeros or default capacities. Discovery uses exact provider contracts through the existing guarded reader/cache, with credential and endpoint isolation, cancellation, bounded refresh and no anonymous or upstream-key fallback.

Worker transcript projection also omits unavailable cost properties before launch hashing. Partial/unknown costs now retain the same identity across JSON transport; recorded zero and provider-billed totals remain intact. Receipt validation and timeout policy are unchanged.

This combines the dependent pricing, limits and acquisition slices: acquisition needs the optional runtime types to materialize truthful executable rows. It removes the catalog cost-completion helper and the reached fabricated defaults, without adding a separate discovery framework.

**SDK compatibility:** consumers must handle optional model cost/rates and maxTokens, and possibly incomplete estimated usage cost. Known complete values retain their behavior. A local execution budget is not advertised provider capacity. No deployment, live provider request or new server capability activation is included.

## Evidence

Current signed candidate: `397e0b4d53b1b077cfb3dbe9b957b9c7e660e583`, tree `9c4bf470b40d9d3696e0eef8ee32b7a11f2fc2a6`. This remains a **draft, NEEDS WORK**, published for exact-candidate proof. No current-head CI, security, platform, or SDK result is claimed.

The latest correction lets ordinary canonical manual CI reach its existing GitHub-hosted profile when the repository is configured for Boat. Admission still requires default runner and shape, no qualification dispatch, and the target's hosted-runner contract. Push, pull request, other repository, missing-contract, override and qualification cases keep their refusals; explicit Boat qualification and retry behavior remain unchanged. This is not the full Boat backend implementation or a global runner-setting change.

The actual extracted workflow step failed the two new positive cases before the fix. Qualified local Node24 proof covers 18 focused cases by composition: 16 successful unchanged sibling/negative cases plus the final two changed cases. The actual manifest fixture produces the same scope outputs as configured-GitHub manual CI; runner-expression comparisons use the normalized profile context. Targeted types/lint/format, actionlint, zizmor, Git-owner checks, normal signed hooks and privacy checks pass. One scoped P0-P2 review found no actionable findings; the subsequent mechanical test-iteration typing adjustment passed fresh types and affected-case proof. The new allocation is exactly 102 net test lines, separate from the unchanged 417 earlier credits, preserving 19 lines of slack.

One candidate-level manual CI is [run 43611575729](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43611575729), attempt 1, dispatched from this exact branch/head with `target_ref=397e0b4d53b1b077cfb3dbe9b957b9c7e660e583` and `release_gate=false`; all other defaults are unchanged. Completed preflight proves controller and selected checkout both equal this candidate, with configured `boat` normalized to `runner_profile=github` and `node_runner_backend=github`, qualification false and default CI shape. The baseline-ratchet, dependency-inventory and security-fast jobs passed; security-fast is not independent security approval or full release qualification. Observation stopped at the first failure: [iOS release E2E / qualify, job 132497897426](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43611575729/job/132497897426). Its exact candidate checkout passed native generation and the native build, then failed inside `native-build-reuse` before test trials; the console log does not expose the underlying exception. The uploaded sanitized proof artifact 14120403917 is the next diagnostic surface and has not been inspected. At the 15:51:27 UTC observation, 59 jobs had passed, 1 failed, 6 were skipped, 137 were running and 53 queued. This is an in-progress snapshot, not a terminal-run result; no rerun or cancellation was requested. Android was unselected. This does not establish generated-merge integration, complete Node/Bun or platform coverage, clear the five holds, or qualify executable SDK/full declarations. No newer MLX controller or other backend implementation was copied.

Prior b4 incremental proof below retains its original input identities. The original unknown-price/optional-limit and 12-provider discovery scope remains:


- Correct accounting fixtures to distinguish genuine empty usage from recorded zero. Preserve explicit-zero, partial-count, priced/unpriced aggregation, exactly-once settlement and failure coverage. The four affected files passed 132 cases on the qualified local Node24 runtime at their signed correction inputs.
- Preserve historical delivery-mirror idempotency through a narrow one-way comparison of the shipped zero-filled mirror format against current empty-cost mirrors. Accepted rows, IDs, stored usage and writer/session authorization are unchanged; ordinary/provider usage remains strict. Core, SDK and actor-memory coverage passed 34 focused and 67 full cases at that correction.
- Join the isolated profile-attempt fixture's actual owned completion and runtime lease. Its instrumented 18-case observation and final uninstrumented changed-case pass are distinct evidence; the original 1000ms timeout cause remains unknown.
- Apply scoped existing Workshop/QA declaration-export repairs and model the Tokenjuice benchmark's real workspace dependency ownership in the existing Knip policy. The production 15000ms Workshop deadline is unchanged. Local dependency inventory passed at its signed correction; final helper unused-file and export scans passed with zero findings. This does not prove controller-augmented inventory or runtime Tokenjuice availability.
- Make deferred OpenResponses fixtures release their producer on every exit and join actual fetch, SDK, wire and agent work before the next shared-mock reset. Keep all 61 registrations and existing deadlines. A deterministic early-assertion regression verifies retirement followed by a distinct HTTP request. Cleanup recognizes the genuine SDK user-abort class only for its owned SDK promise; primary and unexpected errors remain failures.

**OpenResponses proof limit:** the normal extracted full-file run recorded **59 passes and two zero-dispatch failures at the unchanged 1000ms wait**. One later passive instrumented run passed **61/61**, with 449 events and zero overflow; it did not reproduce the zero boundary. Temporary observers were removed. This is **not** a fresh uninstrumented final-tree full-suite pass, proof of the original failure's cause, or runtime coverage of cleanup-triggered aborts. Persistent HTTP connection closure is separate from joining actual per-request work.

Final scoped types, lint, formatting, privacy checks, signed commit hooks and independent P0-P2 review pass. The coherent test helper meets native line caps; the exact allocation is 417 (39 accounting +225 mirror +153 response tests), with 19 lines of remaining ratchet slack. No global baseline, deadline or capacity guard was increased. These are composed scoped receipts with their original source identities, not a new all-suite execution.

The usage-refresh independence correction in `1536faab19f2adf524b7ef1acef5c24501b35652` remains unchanged: the partial overview returns while its original owned refresh stays pending and unaborted, followed by existing cleanup. Its selected and 24-case local proofs establish the test contract, not improved pricing or cold-read latency.

**Historical manual CI:** [run 43576909441](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43576909441) selected exact `1536faab19f2adf524b7ef1acef5c24501b35652`, not this candidate. Its terminal result was 208 passed, 48 failed, one cancelled and 11 skipped jobs. It supplies no new-head success. Build artifacts omit full declarations; an SDK API-diff report is not executable SDK or actual client-to-Worker composition proof.

**Five qualification holds remain:**

1. Exact controller-augmented dependency/export inventory. Local scans used committed configuration; the hosted controller's release-evidence entry was not included.
2. Complete current UI unit/browser proof and remaining SQLite, post-ready, sidebar, Doctor and capped-unknown failure accounting. Scoped Workshop results are not full UI closure.
3. Actual current-candidate paired Node/Bun qualification admitted under real capacity and unchanged native reserve/ownership guards.
4. Android, iOS and macOS default-profile proof. Historical controller/candidate missing-executable failures, including MLX before tests, are not waived; controller-target compatibility must be reviewed before another product run.
5. Fresh exact-candidate CI/security/required SDK report and truthful aggregate, with every remaining incoming finding resolved through supported evidence. The investigated zero-dispatch and profile-timeout causes remain unknown.

No inherited-failure exemption, READY status, deployment, live provider request or provider activation is claimed. Actual client-to-Worker qualification remains separate. Historical source equality and passing replays do not establish failure cause.

Candidate: `8f65e2bc007f17cfdae0d0636858b88c2e5c9e2b`. Supported native preparation integrated exact `aedae9dc410202f22504c6183823fd411699f723` to consume known UI and unused-export corrections. The only additional correction changes the synthetic Crabbox fixture version from 0.80 to the actual supported 0.81 minimum; no production credential path, assertion or allocation changes.

- **Retained local build proof (`0a9322a8`):** full build passes in 3m27s, including package/plugin/SDK declarations and the Control UI build. prs.title: fix(macos): find text in the focused browser tab
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Opening a source file or a long article in a Mac browser tab left no way to find text on the page. Neither ⌘F nor Ctrl+F opened a search field, even with the page focused.

## User Impact

Click in a Mac tab and press **⌘F** or **Ctrl+F** to search that page. Return and Shift+Return move through the matches; Escape closes the bar and puts the keyboard back on the page. The chat keeps its own shortcut when it has focus. Streamed Agent browser tabs are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The tab already owns the WebKit document. It now gives that document to AppKit’s text finder and reserves space above it for the system find bar, so a match on the first line stays visible. Search terms and page contents do not go through the Gateway.

## Evidence

In an isolated macOS 26.6.2 VM, the same two shortcuts left the original plain-text page unchanged. On the fix, the native bar reported two hits, Return and Shift+Return selected matches on different lines, and Escape restored focus to WebKit. Captures show the production reading-tab view in a test window with synthetic source text, not the surrounding dashboard or an operator desktop. Base: `b31ea65546f`; fix: `2e7f7e399ec`.

**Before and after**

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: the focused source page has no search field after Ctrl+F](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/11778944-fe62-4548-aa05-b645b50e20fe) | ![After: the search bar shows two results and highlights the first occurrence](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/89c4dacb-78ed-41e9-ac08-191798d0b734) |

**Annotated comparison**

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![No search bar above the first line](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1e64a494-a8d6-4c5c-bcdf-245bb9131e26) | ![Find count in the active tab, with the first line still visible](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1dfcb201-f460-41dc-aedf-09b445b9c89e) |

The Mac app and its native test bundle built at `d533c1c979f`. On the base, both keyboard cases failed because the page never gave focus to a find field. All 11 browser-host tests passed on the fix, including field placement and focus restoration for both shortcuts. Local autoreview found no actionable P0–P2 issues in the implementation against `b31ea65546f` or in the test-only follow-up against `2e7f7e399ec`.

prs.title: fix: let a half-switched Git checkout finish updating from its new release
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A Git checkout that tracked `main` between #199706 (2026-11-17) and #200578 can be left half-switched by its own updater, and nothing after #203194 gets it out. That updater builds a release, links it at `git-install/lib/node_modules/openclaw` and arms a trial without the `v` field. It never starts the release, leaves the service on the checkout's build and exits 1 with `openclaw doctor`. From then on:

- Plain `openclaw update`, `openclaw doctor --fix` and the Gateway's automatic updates all run that old build (unpatchable). Repeats report `already-current` while the Gateway serves 2026.11.4 on schema 40/42. When `main` moves, each one builds another 4.6 GiB release and fails the same way.
- The only current code a user can reach is the release that updater built, run by its full path: `node ~/.openclaw/git-install/lib/node_modules/openclaw/openclaw.mjs update`. On `main` that CLI sends `update.run` to the running old Gateway. The old Gateway answers with its own handler (`managed-service update handoff`, `driver:adopted`), builds another release and fails the same way.
- With `--no-restart`, `update repair` or `doctor --fix`, the new CLI cannot write the state database. The old Gateway owns it, and the database needs a forward migration that the new code may only do at the release's boot. `gateway install --force` pins the service to that release's `dist/index.js`, outside the launcher, with no trial and no rollback.

This is a real install shape: any checkout that tracked `main` in that window, including a live instance we run.

## User Impact

From that state, one command converges: `node ~/.openclaw/git-install/lib/node_modules/openclaw/openclaw.mjs update`.
1. It builds the target release beside the serving checkout and checks it with `check-release`. Neither step touches the state database.
2. It points the service definition at the release launcher through the definition-backup owner, and restarts the service.
3. The launcher starts the release on trial. The release migrates state at boot and keeps the `.pre-*` originals that a rollback restores.
4. The trial commits when the release is ready. The run is then recorded and settled by the Gateway that serves the release, and `openclaw update` follows it to `succeeded`.

Every later update takes the normal release path. Plugin maintenance waits for the next update (an already-current update maintains plugins too), because it needs the state database that the old build owned during the conversion.

Every other install is unaffected. The new route runs only in three states:
- `releases/.trial` lacks the format field (only #199706's updater writes that), and the effective service still starts the checkout rather than the launcher. An install that #200578's machinery finished, with a deferred format-1 trial, already starts the launcher and keeps the normal route.
- The launcher has rolled such a conversion back onto a checkout build without the release forwarder.
- A conversion pointed the service at the launcher but its restart never happened. The next `openclaw update` only restarts into the prepared release and records the run.

The conversion refuses before changing anything in these cases, and each message says so:
- The service starts another checkout.
- The service selects another state directory or config. The comparison uses the service's own environment, not the CLI's overrides.
- `--timeout` is already spent before the restart.

A resume starts only the trial that was prepared for this checkout and config. `--sha` prepares afresh instead of resuming. Installs whose trial cannot need conversion keep the normal route without a native service read.

## Why This Change Was Made

**Which entry points can run the fix.** Everything on the user's path runs the old build: `openclaw` on PATH (a link to the checkout), the service (`<checkout>/dist/index.js`, which has no forwarder), the Gateway's `update.run` and automatic updates. The release that build's updater left behind is the only one that runs code from this change, and only by its full path. So that CLI owns the conversion.

**Owner and invariant.** The release path's preparation (`prepareUpdate`) records every step in the state database. Here the database belongs to a build that cannot be migrated while it runs. `prepareUpdate` now takes the run ledger as a parameter; the default is the state database, so no other caller changes. The conversion collects the run's progress in memory and records it once the release owns state. It also passes the checkout's serving commit, because the CLI's own build is not what serves.

**Service definition.** `src/update/convert-service.ts` is the same module, with the same interface, as #203497's `stageReleaseService`. It stages the launcher through the existing definition-backup owner, without stopping the Gateway. Whichever PR lands second drops its copy. After staging, the conversion reads back the effective command, drop-in overrides included. If that command does not start the launcher (for example a system-owned unit or an override), the conversion stops before any restart, puts back the earlier updater's trial, and says that the current version is still running. The next `openclaw update` then tries the conversion again. Once the restart has been attempted, the trial stays with the launcher, which may already be booting the release and needs the trial to roll back. Waiting for the trial gets its own budget, which starts at the restart: the launcher's 20-minute trial plus one minute, within what remains of `--timeout`. When that budget runs out, the message names `node ~/.openclaw/git-install/openclaw/openclaw.mjs update status`. The conversion runs only when the CLI targets the configured local Gateway.

**Rollback.** The trial's fallback is the checkout's own build, which is what serves. If the release does not become ready, the launcher restores the boot-migration originals and starts the checkout's build. The next `openclaw update` converts again: the route also matches a rolled-back trial whose serving tree has no forwarder.

**What stays manual.** `openclaw` on PATH still starts the checkout's 2026.11.4 build. That build now refuses with its own true message ("uses newer schema version 41; this build supports 40") and changes nothing. The run records a `warning:checkout-cli` step, which `openclaw update` prints. It names `node ~/.openclaw/git-install/openclaw/openclaw.mjs`, which follows every release. Fixing PATH automatically would mean rewriting the user's pnpm global link or rebuilding their checkout. This change does neither.

**Prior decision.** #203194 rejected settling #199706's format-1 trials and the `lib/node_modules` link, because "main-only code is not a shipped contract". This PR asks maintainers to revisit that for one reason: the state is observed on a production instance, and no entry point recovers it without hand edits. It does not settle format-1 trials or follow the legacy link. It replaces the trial with the current format through the normal preparation, and leaves the legacy link and releases to the normal 24-hour release collection.

**Update behavior.** This runs from new code only. The old updater and Gateway are unchanged and cannot be patched. The user runs the release CLI once, by full path. That release must contain this change, which holds after the old Gateway's own automatic update builds a newer `main`. No schema, config key, protocol, dependency or retention change.

## Evidence

Real Linux container with systemd as PID 1, a lingering user manager and a real user bus. A user systemd Gateway service, a Gateway-gated writer on a 512 MiB agent database, and 1,000 marker rows checked by count, SHA-256 and `PRAGMA quick_check` after every step. Synthetic state only. Setup: a checkout at `8f80fe08cad` (#199706 era) with the service installed, and `origin/main` pointed at the code under test. The checkout's own `openclaw update` (the 8f80 updater) then leaves it half-switched: exit 1 `openclaw doctor`, the release linked at `lib/node_modules`, a format-1 trial, the service on the checkout, schema 40/42. `origin/main` then moves one commit.

RED: base `a1aa1276017`, whose release the 8f80 updater built.

| Step (who runs it) | Result | Wall | Gateway | State after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `node …/lib/node_modules/openclaw/openclaw.mjs update --yes --json` (release CLI → `update.run` → the old Gateway's own handler) | exit 1, `trigger: api`, `openclaw doctor`; a third release built; a new format-1 trial | 154 s | 2026.11.4, untouched | schema 40/42; 3 releases |
| plain `openclaw update` (8f80 on PATH) | exit 0, `skipped` / `already-current` (false) | 118 s | 2026.11.4 | unchanged |
| release CLI `doctor --fix` | exit 1: "Refusing a forward database schema migration … the Gateway service runs 2026.11.4" | 1 s | 2026.11.4 | unchanged |
| release CLI `update repair` | exit 1: "refused shared state schema mutation … another Gateway owns that state directory" | 13 s | 2026.11.4 | unchanged |
| release CLI `update --no-restart` | exit 1: "state database is busy … schema migration pending" | 2 s | 2026.11.4 | unchanged |
| release CLI `gateway install --force` | exit 0; unit pinned to that release's `dist/index.js` (no launcher, no trial, no rollback) | 3 s | restarts on the pinned release | migrated 41/43 |

GREEN: PR head `beaa7d2c706`, with the 8f80 updater building that head as the half-switched release.

| Step | Result | Wall | Gateway outage | State after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `node …/lib/node_modules/openclaw/openclaw.mjs update --yes --json` | exit 0, run `succeeded` (`trigger: cli`, before 2026.11.4, after 2026.11.6 at the target build). The unit now names `git-install/openclaw-launcher.mjs`. Trial v2 `committed` after 1 attempt, with the checkout as fallback. The run records the deferred plugin note and the `warning:checkout-cli` note. | 406.1 s | one outage of 30.0 s (stop, boot migration, ready) | schema 41/43; marker rows and hash unchanged; `quick_check` ok; `/readyz` 200 |
| `openclaw` on PATH (8f80) | exit 1, with its own true refusal: "uses newer schema version 41; this build supports 40". Nothing changed. | 1.5 s | 0 | unchanged |
| Next update, upstream moved again: `node ~/.openclaw/git-install/openclaw/openclaw.mjs update --yes --json` | exit 0, `succeeded` through the new Gateway's `update.run`. Trial committed, fallback the previous release. | 372.8 s | 8.8 s | marker unchanged |

The same green rows passed at two earlier heads: `5ba368f4ebc` (428 s, 31.5 s outage) and `3f1e3eb7dbc` (408 s, 33.7 s outage).

Raw red output, unedited: [release CLI attempts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/203608#issuecomment-7084602254), [plain update on PATH](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/203608#issuecomment-7084602493), and the 8f80 updater's half-switch ([part 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/203608#issuecomment-7084602699), [part 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/203608#issuecomment-7084602910)). Red recording: [base](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/203608#issuecomment-7085239066). Green recording and raw output at the head: [head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/203608#issuecomment-7085798829). Full logs are not attached because the artifact store rejects uploads from this machine.

Tests:
- `src/update/half-switched.test.ts` (new):
  - Detection: format-1 trial; v2 trial; rollback onto a build without a forwarder; and with one.
  - Preparation with a collected ledger publishes a v2 pending trial whose fallback is the checkout, and opens no state database.
  - The serving commit, not the CLI's own build, decides `current`.
  - A full conversion: the definition is pointed at the launcher, one restart, and the run is recorded with the deferred plugin note and the checkout-CLI warning.
  - A definition that cannot be pointed at the launcher: no restart, the earlier trial restored, and the next update converts again.
  - A restart that throws: the published trial stays for the launcher, and the next update resumes it and records the run.
  - A service that starts another checkout, or uses another state directory: nothing changes.
  - Red on the base for every case except the detection helper, which does not exist there.
- `src/update/cli.test.ts`:
  - New: a half-switched install routes to the conversion and sends no `update.run`. Red on the base: it sent `update.run`.
  - Every case now runs in its own temporary state directory, so none can read the developer's real `releases/.trial`.
  - Removed the per-case `try/finally` env restore, which the shared `afterEach` now covers.
- `test/vitest/vitest.database-worker-core-paths.mjs`: the new file runs with the state database broker, as `prepare.test.ts` does.

Checks: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/update/ src/gateway/server-methods/update-run.test.ts`, `update-restart-module-outcome` and `eager-import-closure`, `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, oxlint and oxfmt on the touched files, `pnpm check:baseline-ratchets` (all ok, session-identity included), `git diff --check`.

Review:
- ClawSweeper's local review, round 3 (the last round): overall F, proof D, patch F. Fixed after it, with tests where noted:
  - Verify the service starts this checkout before publishing (tested).
  - Compare the service's own config, not the CLI's overrides.
  - Check checkout and config again on resume.
  - Skip the service read for trials that cannot need conversion.
  - Do not resume a different commit under `--sha`.
  - Stop before the restart when `--timeout` is spent.

  Not fixed: it asks to identify a rolled-back checkout's running build by its capabilities rather than by the forwarder file at its root. A checkout pulled to current `main` without a rebuild would have the file but still run the old build. Listed under "Not proven".
- ClawSweeper's local review, round 2: overall F, proof D, patch F. Its findings, all handled:
  - Convert only a checkout the service still starts: done.
  - Require the same state and config: done, with a test.
  - Keep a conversion whose restart never ran retryable: the `resume` route, tested.
  - Follow the run within one `--timeout` budget: done.
- ClawSweeper's local review, round 1: overall F, proof D, patch F. Its findings, and what I did:
  - Verify the effective command: done.
  - Do not restore the earlier trial after the restart was attempted: done, with a new test.
  - Give the boot wait its own budget: done.
  - Do not convert under a Gateway URL override: done.
  - Isolate the tests from main's own Docker-marker probe: done.
  - It also raised a maintainer decision: carry a temporary converter, or give operators a one-time recovery. That is the question in "Prior decision" above.
- A fresh independent reviewer found three P1 issues, all fixed:
  - A skipped rebind stranded the install.
  - A dead earlier lock's outcome aborted the replay.
  - The conversion had no tests.
- Its P2 findings, handled:
  - An unknown serving commit fell back to the CLI's build. Fixed: null now means unknown.
  - Plugin maintenance failed on every conversion. Now deferred.
  - A rollback ended the retry path. The route now covers it.
  - Kept as accepted: a narrow race between creating the run and the Gateway settling it.
- `autoreview` cannot run here. The worktree sits under a shared temp directory, and its Codex preflight refuses that.

Not proven:
- A system-owned or foreign service definition end to end. The refusal path is unit-tested only.
- A conversion whose release fails to start, so the launcher rolls back. Re-detection is unit-tested; the launcher rollback itself is #203194's.
- A rolled-back checkout that was pulled to current `main` but not rebuilt. Detection reads the forwarder file at the checkout root, so this case is not converted again.
- No service manager at all (a foreground Gateway). The conversion restarts through the service and would fail to restart. Not run.
- A CLI killed between the restart and recording the run. The release serves, but the run is never recorded, and the Gateway's settlement retries on every maintenance tick.
- macOS launchd and Windows.
- The cells remove `/.dockerenv`, because #203586 (the container refusal) is not merged.

Adds an optional “What should we call you?” step to the existing Control UI onboarding for an unnamed writable profile. “Maybe later” skips it for the current visit. Names remain editable in Settings → Profile; an already named profile is not overwritten. This does not create an external sign-in flow or change profile permissions. If another client names the profile first, onboarding returns that existing profile without another write. Explicit Profile edits retain their existing behavior. During review, a newer name/clear observation exposed a UI reconciliation defect: a display fallback could be mistaken for the editable saved name. The correction reloads the raw profile through the existing owner-guarded loader and preserves busy-state settlement across that reload. The existing regression cases cover the owner, generated-label and linked-login variants, plus connection replacement during both write and refresh. Capture-only test plumbing was removed; the feature's measured test allocation drops from 642 to 612 lines. ## Verified behavior Recorded through normal UI actions with fresh isolated real Gateways, Chrome for Testing 156 and Safari in an iOS 27.2 Simulator: - Save with Enter; reject a whitespace-only name; skip, continue and revisit. - Edit the saved name in Profile, reload it and return without another onboarding name prompt. - Let Safari save first while Chrome holds an older draft: Chrome preserves Safari's name and the existing record timestamp. - Interrupt the task proxy during save, reconnect and retry successfully. Existing write-scope and self-profile permission distinctions remain intact. The exact name → clear → late-response interleaving is **synthetic regression coverage**, not a claim made by the live videos. Both faithful non-owner variants fail before the repair and pass afterward. ## Validation and limits The final repair passed 12 onboarding lifecycle tests, 29 adjacent page tests, 67 storage/handler tests, 4 focused authorization cases and 3 browser tests. Runtime/UI builds, protocol generation, UI type checking, targeted lint/format and the required English-source locale baseline pass. Independent full-feature inspection and the shared P0–P2 review of the exact repair found no remaining actionable issue. Two checks are not green: the foreign catalog awaits the documented locale-refresh workflow for seven new keys; the test-line ratchet retains the merge base's 32-line overage. No ceiling or fallback baseline was relaxed. Hosted CI remains separate; this is not an all-green claim. Physical iPhone, VoiceOver and external identity-provider sign-in were not tested. ## Before and after Main is `87c57b41c5906fc25205aaf18363d37750f07b2a`; candidate source is the tree `a6c3938987d7bb4d4bf7afce069b4aadf5f3a7c3` published as `83accfbc70ae9aac26689d03d60f1a7bb8753a1e`. The candidate uses the unchanged original PR backend and the repaired production UI. Final main check `6914b5a` has no further change in these owners. The local build's original revision marker is recorded-source metadata, not an indication that the repair was absent. Desktop before: onboarding without a name prompt. Desktop after: optional name prompt, with the AI connection ready in both comparisons. Safari before: no name step. Safari after: the optional name field and both actions fit the narrow viewport. Subsequent Profile edit remains saved after a fresh page read. Chrome preserves the name saved first by Safari. ## Complete recordings All clips run at original speed, without cuts or pixel redactions. Only container metadata was removed. prs.title: fix(agents): warn when a protected store entry overrides an inherited exec value
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A protected secret-store entry that shares a name with an inherited environment value can replace that value with a restart-dependent sentinel during exec. The precedence is intentional, but the replacement was silent. Operators using a stable local value, such as a file-backed keyring password, could not see why it changed (#196120).

## User Impact

Exec now explains a same-name protected-store override only when the sentinel actually wins. Explicit or plugin-provided overrides continue to work without this warning.

## Why This Change Was Made

The warning is decided after final exec environment composition, not from an earlier intermediate environment. The docs describe the override and sentinel lifetime. This is the diagnostic slice; confirming whether the reported installation has a same-name store entry is still needed to establish that it resolves that specific keyring failure.

## Evidence

A real isolated Gateway, local OpenAI Responses-compatible fake model, actual agent turn and Gateway-hosted `exec` were exercised on head `9c7ec1d771e36d180fb0a712fffedcecdfe1872a`. No external credentials or paid model were used. Terminal output from the local proof driver (`pnpm exec tsx .artifacts/196698-exec-warning-proof.mts`), selecting the returned warning line and subprocess outcome from the fake model request:

```json
{"winner":"sentinel","status":"ok","warningLine":"Warning: secret store entry \"GOG_KEYRING_PASSWORD\" overrides the inherited \"GOG_KEYRING_PASSWORD\" value with a protected sentinel. The sentinel is regenerated on every Gateway restart and substitutes only for its bound hosts; remove the same-name store entry or rename one side if the command needs a stable local value.","execOutcome":"EXEC_DONE"}
{"winner":"plugin","status":"ok","warningLine":null,"execOutcome":"PLUGIN_WON"}
```

The committed E2E test `test/pr196698-exec-warning-proof.e2e.test.ts` independently asserts the actual tool result in both cases; it passed 2/2 on this head. Focused siblings passed: `bash-tools.exec.store-env.test.ts` 21/21; `bash-tools.exec.resolve-env-hook.test.ts` and `bash-tools.exec-github-credential.test.ts` 32/32. Core typecheck exit 0 and targeted format/lint clean. The test-lines allocation `config/test-lines-allocations/196120-exec-store-override-warning.txt` covers the new regression.

No config migration or user action is required.

prs.title: fix(ui): keep Skills first-visit requests within budget
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Skills can exceed its first-visit request limit when background sidebar assets finish before the page is ready. [Main CI recorded 30 completed requests against the limit of 28](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44913885381/job/136875600229).

The Skills library imports upload-size constants through the protocol barrel, which also brings runtime schema code into the browser.

## User Impact

Skills reads its existing upload limits without fetching two unnecessary schema chunks. Upload limits, wire schemas, and existing exports stay unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Move the four constants into a dependency-free module owned by the protocol package. The schema re-exports them for existing callers; the UI imports the constants directly and imports its schema types with `import type`.

## Evidence

The same production-bundle browser scenario on the failing CI commit and the candidate showed:

| Skills first visit, 100 ms request latency | Base | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Requests completed by ready | 28 | 26 |
| Schema chunks requested | 2 | 0 |
| Bytes completed by ready | 468,803 | 406,256 |

The local base passed because two sidebar requests finished after readiness; CI counted those same assets before readiness. The candidate removes the two schema requests without raising the existing limit.

All four existing route scenarios passed, including deferred skill-reader loading. Candidate ready-window counts were 26/28 for Skills, 29/31 for Skill Settings, 53/56 for Plugins, and 54/61 for Plugin Settings. The 23 library tests, targeted format/lint, UI typecheck, and protocol registry check passed.

The local ClawSweeper committed-range review found no code or security defects. Runtime results were collected separately from that source review. Temporary diagnostic logging was restored after execution, and the three candidate source files were verified by hash.

The [exact-head canonical performance check](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44922622564/job/136902172794) passed. Its dispatch base is newer than this fix's parent, so the parent comparison below uses the [parent's existing canonical CI measurement](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44913885381/job/136875599061). Both runs used Node 24.22.1, Vite 8.3.5, Pako 3.0.3, and the same lockfile and performance/build code. These are separate CI runs, not interleaved timing samples; the values are normalized asset sizes.

| Cold boot JS, gzip bytes | Parent `6577f41` | Candidate `817f310` | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Startup | 90,879 | 90,879 | 0 |
| Chat | 1,333,702 | 1,333,796 | +94 |
| New Session | 820,757 | 820,851 | +94 |

No thresholds were changed. Acceptance of the two 94-byte increases is pending.

An earlier absolute-budget diagnostic against the E2E bundle failed. That fixture deliberately omits compression sidecars and uses synthetic build metadata, so its CSS totals are not release measurements. An additional exact-parent remote probe stopped before measurement because its preflight expected the source SHA as HEAD instead of the wrapper's transport carrier; no result from that attempt is counted.

The canonical build and both selected UI E2E shards passed. [Real-Gateway CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44922622564/job/136902172446) reported a 120-second timeout in `required-human-action.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts` (`manual-in-panel`, last phase `manual-page-closed`). This matches the [prior main failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44369795594/job/135034001765) at `fd5471bc2d57192072bc8fcec7f7980846dcfb31`: same test/case and 120-second timeout. The test's actions, assertions, and timeout are unchanged from that failure; only failure telemetry was added in [#201386](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201386). This is retained as an inherited CI failure, not claimed fixed here. Its exact stalled click still needs separate diagnosis.

<details>
<summary>Focused validation</summary>

Base: `6577f41b9aba3b2e01f073b68a76aa419ade0ae1`.
Candidate: `817f3107c608c9ba0331d03855be3a675f6070c9`.
Linux, Node 24.22.1, 8 CPUs, 16 GiB RAM, one test worker.

- `pnpm test ui/src/pages/skills/library-uploads.test.tsx ui/src/pages/skills/library-detail.test.tsx --maxWorkers=1`

prs.title: fix: show each steered attachment once to the model
prs.body:
Closes #203657

## What Problem This Solves

When you send a document into an already-running chat, the model receives two notes describing the same attachment. The second description costs context and can make one document look like two.

## User Impact

The model sees one attachment note while retaining the document's rendered text and a readable attachment reference. The fallback still provides that note if document rendering fails.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the structured media projection for the steering prompt. Remove a portable marker only when it was generated for this input and the same reference appears in the structured projection. Normal sends continue to use their existing attachment handling.

## Evidence

- On the upstream base, a Gateway regression steered a synthetic `notes.txt` and captured two attachment notes both when rendering succeeded and when rendering failed. The patched fixture captures one typed note with the same managed reference and verifies that successful rendering still sends the document text.
- The isolated Gateway replay journeys use real steering and document staging through the Gateway and capture requests at loopback Anthropic Messages and OpenAI Responses endpoints. Both asserted one attachment note, retained the document text, and checked that subsequent requests preserved the message in the prompt prefix.
- 255 focused tests and both Gateway replay journeys passed at `790beadc0978`. Formatting, targeted lint, core typecheck, and the runtime build passed. The runtime build reported an advisory Control UI request-budget warning.


### Live model proof

I ran the built `openclaw.mjs` Gateway at `790beadc0978` with an isolated state directory and a real GPT-6 Luna through OpenAI Responses. A local relay forwarded the request bytes without modification and recorded only the fields needed for these assertions. A synthetic hold tool kept the turn open while the second `chat.send` uploaded `notes.txt`. The user prompt asked for the project color, and the attached file supplied the value. The Gateway staged the file before the tool was released, and the live model request placed the steered user row after that active tool result.

The first live run at `da38c828f663` exposed a staging case the fixture providers missed. Workspace staging can replace the managed URL, leaving both the staged-file note and the portable marker. The added regression reproduces two notes at that revision. The fix matches the rendered note to the original attachment slot and keeps the staged-file reference.

```text
model: gpt-6-luna
upstream HTTP responses: 200, 200, 200, 200, 200
document: notes.txt
steered request: one attachment note, rendered document text present
workspace-staged file: verified against the original bytes
real model replies: STEER-OK COBALT / REPLAY-OK
steered user text SHA-256: ee007d0103459d595e47dbd503e68a1ebfc108bf30cba8c059771eec0fe6b4dc
replayed user text SHA-256: ee007d0103459d595e47dbd503e68a1ebfc108bf30cba8c059771eec0fe6b4dc
```

The isolated run used synthetic content, full Responses replay for both requests, and a single configured model.

## What Problem This Solves
Sending documents to a Claude CLI chat could show the caption and file cards, then a second user bubble containing staging paths, attachment markers, and extracted document text. The second bubble was an imported native prompt, not another send.

New document uploads keep their original caption and attachment cards. Claude still receives the expanded input. Existing unmarked native rows are not removed retroactively, and standalone native messages remain visible.

## Why This Change Was Made
Use the same persisted-turn identity that already associates Claude image prompts with their chat messages, including when an attachment has no image path. Both history indexes prefer that exact match; the UI does not filter text that merely resembles a prompt.

## Evidence
