prs.title: fix: retry the primary model when a recovery check never started
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When the primary model is in cooldown, OpenClaw periodically checks whether it has recovered. If a worker goes offline before sending that check, the next turn can skip the primary for 30 seconds and use a fallback or suspend the session.

Closes #127649

## User Impact

As soon as the worker is available, the next turn can retry the primary. The 30-second limit still applies when a request reached the provider or a worker disconnected after accepting it.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fallback runner reserves the check before it yields to observers. Local admission and worker launch can release that reservation when they can establish that execution never started, including an explicit capacity refusal from the worker supervisor. Each release belongs to one reservation, so a late failure cannot clear a newer check.

A transcript write can fail after the model has already replied. The execution boundary lets OpenClaw preserve throttling in that case and when result processing discovers missing tool output. Related work includes #128616 and #203469.

## Evidence

### Captured Gateway and model output

Two `agent` RPCs ran in separate sessions of one isolated Gateway with the same cooled-down auth profile and no fallback. `probe-model` was local Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct served by llama.cpp. A forwarding HTTP proxy counted completion POSTs in `modelCalls`. The placement fixture counted entries in `admissions`.

**Worker offline before dispatch.** The placement fixture raised `WorkerRunnerUnavailableError` before running the first turn. The next RPC followed immediately. The following lines are from the terminal capture.

Base `7a570c41bc2`

```text
ISSUE_PROBE first {"offline":true,"admissions":1,"modelCalls":0}
ISSUE_PROBE retry {"status":"error","admissions":1,"modelCalls":0}
ISSUE_PROBE baseline: primary skipped before admission
```

Fixed runtime `f7dcf12e72b`

```text
ISSUE_PROBE first {"offline":true,"admissions":1,"modelCalls":0}
ISSUE_PROBE retry {"status":"ok","model":"probe-model","hasReply":true,"admissions":2,"modelCalls":1}
```

**Transcript failure after the model replied.** The fixture awaited a nonempty model reply and then raised `SessionTranscriptWriterClaimReboundError`. Success had cleared the synthetic profile’s cooldown (`profileStillCooling` was `false`), so the fixture reapplied it before the retry. The retry began 21,298 ms after the first turn began. The request count stayed at one.

```text
ISSUE_PROBE post-provider {"modelAnswered":true,"writerFailure":true,"profileStillCooling":false,"retryAfterMs":21298,"skipped":true,"admissions":1,"modelCalls":1}
```

**Late completion of an older probe.** The fixture advanced the clock past the probe interval and admitted a newer probe. The older pre-dispatch failure arrived after the newer model call. A third attempt observed the newer reservation.

```text
ISSUE_PROBE overlap {"olderFailedAfterNewer":true,"newerModelCalls":1,"third":"MODEL_FALLBACK_SKIPPED","clockAdvancedMs":30001}
```

### Committed regression on base and head

I copied only the [committed worker test](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/9c0da2ee43b585bd5ab9f62b64f85f2cc88c22bb/src/gateway/worker-environments/worker-turn-launcher-failure-recovery.test.ts#L519-L576) into a clean worktree at `7a570c41bc2`. The test holds the clock across both attempts so a slow worker cannot outlast the 30-second interval. Without that clock control a cold baseline run took 54 seconds and the pre-dispatch case passed.

To select the two disconnect cases in either checkout, run

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/worker-environments/worker-turn-launcher-failure-recovery.test.ts \
  --maxWorkers=1 -t 'retries a cooled-down primary only if'
```

Base output, with the common file prefix omitted and the fixture model name redacted

```text
× retries a cooled-down primary only if the worker disconnects before dispatch (disconnect: before) 50570ms
✓ retries a cooled-down primary only if the worker disconnects before dispatch (disconnect: after) 3875ms
Caused by: FailoverError: All models failed (1): [fixture model]: Provider openai is in cooldown (overloaded)
Tests  1 failed | 1 passed | 16 skipped (18)
```

PR head `9c0da2ee43b`, including all 18 tests in the worker file

```text
✓ retries a cooled-down primary only if the worker disconnects before dispatch (disconnect: before) 5981ms
✓ retries a cooled-down primary only if the worker disconnects before dispatch (disconnect: after) 4316ms
Tests  18 passed (18)
```

The 289 focused tests across 16 files, build, production and affected test typechecks, lint, formatting, and docs link checks passed on the runtime change. The follow-up changes only the test clock. The full worker test file, its typecheck, lint, and formatting passed on that change. The [upstream CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45022306861) for `9c0da2ee43b` is awaiting GitHub Actions approval.

<details>
<summary>Review, test timings, and change size</summary>

- Local Codex autoreview covered the runtime change in `f7dcf12e72b` against `7a570c41bc2`. A second pass covered the test-clock change in `9c0da2ee43b`. Both reported no actionable findings through P2.
- Vitest recorded 149.2 s for the final worker launch recovery file, 37.9 s for runtime refresh integration, and 2.8 s for personal cooldowns. The integration files exercise worker handoff and runtime admission.
- Relative to the merge base, production code adds 125 lines and removes 64, tests add 106 and remove 5, and documentation changes one line. The existing cooldown owner holds the reservation. The runtime wiring carries its release callback to the code that observes dispatch.
- Maintainer edits, including workflow edits on this fork branch, are enabled.

</details>

prs.title: test(ui): expect no rail search in the compact chat drawer
prs.body:
Fixes #203492

## What Problem This Solves

`main`'s `checks-ui-e2e` is red on `native-nav-responsive-layout.e2e.test.ts`. The case `keeps compact chat search reachable` opens the mobile drawer, waits for `.shell-nav .sidebar-brand__search` to become visible, clicks it, and asserts the command palette opens. After #203440 removed the desktop-only search control from the mobile sidebar rail, that element is hidden, so `expect.poll(() => drawerSearch.isVisible()).toBe(true)` fails at line 102 for both parameter rows.

## User Impact

No runtime change. The test now asserts the behavior #203440 shipped instead of the behavior it replaced, so the UI e2e lane goes green again.

## Why This Change Was Made

#203440 changed the mobile layout rule from "hide the rail control except search under merged chat chrome" to "hide the desktop-only rail control on every mobile page":

```css
/* before */
.shell--mobile-nav .sidebar-brand__desktop-control:not(.sidebar-brand__search),
.shell--mobile-nav:not(.shell--merged-chat-chrome) .sidebar-brand__search { display: none; }
/* after */
.shell--mobile-nav .sidebar-rail .sidebar-brand__desktop-control { display: none; }
```

The stale test still expected the drawer to carry search under merged chat chrome. Both parameter rows are compact widths — the non-phone row is 900 px, which `isMobileNavLayout()` also treats as mobile (`max-width: 900px`) — so the rail search is hidden in both.

Fix classification: `behavior-completing` for the test — it follows the shipped design rather than reverting it.

## What The Case Now Proves

The first version only asserted the control was invisible, which also passes on a page that failed to render. The case now checks:

1. **The control is still mounted**: `expect.poll(() => drawerSearch.count()).toBe(1)`. The drawer still renders its rail; only the layout hides the button, so this cannot pass on a page that never rendered.
2. **It is not visible**: `isVisible() === false`, the observable result.
3. **The palette is still reachable**: after closing the drawer, `mod+k` (Meta on macOS, Control elsewhere) opens `.cmd-palette__input`. The old case proved palette access by clicking the rail control; that path is gone, so this keeps the palette-coverage intent alive and fails if the rail change also took the palette away.

The hiding mechanism itself is not pinned here: `form-controls.browser.test.ts` already renders the rail fixture directly and asserts the search control is hidden, so re-asserting `display: none` in this file would duplicate that coverage and couple this case to how the control is hidden. (An earlier revision did assert it; removed after review.)

The palette chord is deliberately **not** pressed while the drawer is open: `handleNavDrawerKeydown` (`ui/src/app/navigation-surface.ts`) calls `preventDefault()` + `stopImmediatePropagation()` for the palette chord while the drawer traps focus, so the case closes the drawer with `Escape` first.

## Evidence

`ui/src/e2e/native-nav-responsive-layout.e2e.test.ts` with the repository's bundled Control UI e2e harness (real Chromium, real built Control UI, mock Gateway):

```sh
npx vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts \
  ui/src/e2e/native-nav-responsive-layout.e2e.test.ts
```

- **BASE** (`cc7b482f887`, unchanged test): **2 failed | 5 passed (7)**. Both failures are `keeps compact chat search reachable (phone: false/true)`, `AssertionError: expected false to be true` at `native-nav-responsive-layout.e2e.test.ts:102` — the exact failure the issue reports.
- **HEAD**: **7 passed (7)**, including both rows of the rewritten case.
- **Discriminating check**: mutating the mobile rule back to `.sidebar-brand__desktop-control:not(.sidebar-brand__search)` (i.e. showing rail search again) makes both rows fail with `expected true to be false`, so the case catches the regression rather than passing vacuously. Re-ran this after removing the computed-style assertion: still 2 failed, so coverage did not weaken.

`oxlint`, `oxfmt --check`, and `git diff --check` are clean on the changed file.

## Not tested

- The other three files the issue lists (`openclaw-id-menu.e2e.test.ts` — a 30 s `waitForEvent("page")` timeout; `chat-composer-redesign.e2e.test.ts`; `config-controls-visual.e2e.test.ts`) are not covered here. Their failures have a different cause from the stale rail-search assertion, so this PR does not touch them.
- No live browser verification beyond the bundled Chromium harness above.

prs.title: fix(sessions): allow reset of a session paused as a precaution
prs.body:
Related: #178441
Related: #195598

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a session paused by a provider review can never be reset, so when the provider re-flags every continuation the session is permanently dead. For `agent:main:main` there is no way out at all.

## User Impact

User impact: an operator can now run `sessions.reset` (CLI, gateway call) or send `/new` or `/reset` from a channel to reset a paused session. Reset keeps the session id and its history and starts a fresh context. The reviewed findings are not continued. Continuing the flagged run still requires acknowledging the findings, as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reset keeps the session id and starts a new lifecycle generation (a new `lifecycleRevision`). The session write policy already drops `providerReview` when the lifecycle revision changes. But reset ran the same work-start check as ordinary new work, so the pause refused the replacement before it could happen.

Real case: an OpenAI provider review paused our owner's `agent:main:main` on 2026.9.33 and again after upgrading to 2026.11.3. Each acknowledgment resent the same transcript and was re-flagged. `/reset`, `sessions.reset`, `sessions archive`, `sessions delete` and `session.mainKey` were all refused or ignored. The only way out was stopping the gateway and removing `$.providerReview` from `session_nodes.entry_json` by hand.

This adds a narrow `allowProviderReviewReplacement` work-start option. Only the gateway reset service and the reply path's `/new`/`/reset` trigger pass it. Ordinary sends, agent commands, restart resume and Talk still hit the pause unchanged.

Not included: the Control UI composer and its outbox still hold `/reset` locally for a paused session. That's a follow-up. Until then, operators can reset from the CLI or a channel.

## Stuck on a release without this fix?

Symptoms:

- `Gateway call failed: Session "agent:main:main" is paused as a precaution. Review the provider findings in chat before continuing.`
- **Chat paused as a precaution** / **Session paused as a precaution**. Clicking **Acknowledge findings and continue** gets paused again.
- `/reset`, `sessions.reset`, `sessions archive` and `sessions delete` all refuse the session.
- Provider side: OpenAI `misalignment_policy_violation` / "Potentially unintended activity".

Manual recovery. Back up first, and run this as the account that owns the OpenClaw state:

```bash
# 1. Stop the gateway through whatever supervises it (launchd, systemd, terminal).
# 2. Back up the agent database.
cp ~/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite ~/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite.bak
# 3. See which sessions are paused.
sqlite3 ~/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite "SELECT session_key FROM session_nodes WHERE json_type(entry_json,'\$.providerReview') IS NOT NULL;"
# 4. Clear the pause on the one you need (example: main).
sqlite3 ~/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite "UPDATE session_nodes SET entry_json = json_remove(entry_json,'\$.providerReview') WHERE session_key='agent:main:main'; SELECT changes();"
# 5. Start the gateway, then send /reset in that session FIRST.
```

Send `/reset` before anything else. If you send anything else first, the flagged transcript goes back to the provider, which usually pauses the session again.

## Evidence

- `src/config/sessions/sessions.test.ts`: the pause still blocks ordinary work and `allowPendingWorkspace`. The new option passes the pause only, and an archived session stays blocked.
- `src/gateway/server.sessions.reset-cleanup.test.ts`: `sessions.reset` on a paused `agent:main:main` and on a peer session succeeds. It starts a new lifecycle generation with no `providerReview`, and a second reset also succeeds. Both cases fail on `main` without the fix and pass with it.
- Docs: `docs/web/control-ui/chat.md` now explains how to recover when acknowledgment keeps pausing the session, and quotes the exact error text.
- `pnpm test src/config/sessions/sessions.test.ts src/gateway/server.sessions.reset-cleanup.test.ts src/config/sessions/provider-review-store.test.ts src/gateway/session-lifecycle-provider-review.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 71 passed, 0 failed.
- `pnpm check:changed`: passed (typecheck, lint, format, line-cap ratchet and guards). It ran with `OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_SKIP_DEADCODE=1` because the dead-export scan fails on current `main` in `extensions/knowledge/**`, which this PR doesn't touch.
- The commit was made with `--no-verify` because the pre-commit hook's Node version didn't match the local shell. `oxfmt` was run on every changed file by hand first, and `pnpm check:changed` covers the same format and lint checks.
- Not run: a real provider refusal. The live run below pauses the session by writing the same `providerReview` record a refusal writes. The production session that hit this was recovered with the manual steps above.

## Live Gateway proof

Built this branch (`pnpm build`, head merged with current `main`) and ran the shipped CLI against an isolated `--dev` profile (throwaway `HOME`, port 19001, channels skipped). I created `agent:main:main` with `sessions.reset`, stopped the Gateway, wrote a `providerReview` into its `session_nodes` row exactly as a refusal stores it, and restarted the Gateway. The scoped calls use `callGatewayCli` with an explicit `scopes` list.

```text
== 1. paused
state: sessionId=6d97b123-0f9b-42f3-9a7b-094664124516 lifecycleRevision=4d8f5ae3-2d31-411e-a1fd-1151af8ee268 providerReview=review-proof-1
== 2. ordinary send is still refused
Gateway call failed: Session "agent:main:main" is paused as a precaution. Review the provider findings in chat before continuing.
== 3. write-scoped reset
scopes=operator.write sessions.reset: refused: missing scope: operator.admin
state: sessionId=6d97b123-0f9b-42f3-9a7b-094664124516 lifecycleRevision=4d8f5ae3-2d31-411e-a1fd-1151af8ee268 providerReview=review-proof-1
== 4. admin reset
scopes=operator.admin sessions.reset: ok sessionId=6d97b123-0f9b-42f3-9a7b-094664124516 lifecycleRevision=b73a0074-ce38-4f94-8e38-6572464f168e
state: sessionId=6d97b123-0f9b-42f3-9a7b-094664124516 lifecycleRevision=b73a0074-ce38-4f94-8e38-6572464f168e providerReview=none
== 5. second admin reset
scopes=operator.admin sessions.reset: ok sessionId=6d97b123-0f9b-42f3-9a7b-094664124516 lifecycleRevision=205cd255-3f9e-493b-98d4-9ba6edc83507
== 6. send after reset
  "runId": "proof-send-2",
  "status": "started",
```

What this shows:

- The pause still blocks ordinary work (step 2).
- A caller without `operator.admin` cannot reset, and the pause stays in place (step 3). This PR doesn't change who may reset; `sessions.reset` already requires `operator.admin`.
- An admin reset clears the pause, keeps the session id, and starts a new lifecycle generation (step 4). A later reset still works (step 5).
- Nothing is replayed. The message refused in step 2 is stored nowhere in the agent or state database afterward. Only the new step 6 message is stored.

Stored-data compatibility: this PR adds no stored field and changes no schema. The live run starts from the same `providerReview` row shape that real paused sessions already have.

prs.title: refactor(gateway): check runtime and HTTP authority once at request start
prs.body:
## Problem

After a request was admitted, some paths still re-read permission and refused or aborted part-way through:

- Model selection from plugin/SDK code (`captureOperatorToolGatewayAuthority`) re-checked the caller's live Gateway authority at commit. Revoking access mid-request turned an accepted selection into "Gateway caller authority is no longer active".
- Session requests from a personal-tool turn (`resolveSessionRuntimeAuthority`) re-checked the turn at every response, every commit guard and every shared-read delivery.
- `GET /sessions/{key}/history` re-authenticated the bearer, re-read scopes and re-read session membership before every streamed SSE update. A revoked token or a removed member closed a stream that was already open.
- `POST /tools/invoke` aborted the running tool when the operator-access revocation signal fired.

The rule in `AGENTS.md` ("Choose good compromises") is to check authority once, when the work starts. Revocation applies to the next request.

## Fix

- `operator-invocation-authority.ts`: delete `captureOperatorToolGatewayAuthority`. `captureAmbientGatewayOperatorAuthority` reads the admitted grant once. Its invocation check keeps only Stop (direct and scope signals) and the tool caller's session fences. A direct operator source with no Gateway binding gets the existing missing-binding error at the start.
- `apply-session-model-selection.ts`: read the admitted grant once and refuse at the start when an operator source has no grant (same message as before). The commit guard keeps the model-policy check. The session store fences the write itself (`initialEntry`, model-selection lock).
- `session-runtime-authority.ts`: the personal-tool turn check runs once in `handleGatewayRequest`, before dispatch. In-process dispatch also goes through that path. Every `runtimeAuthority.assertCurrent` re-check is deleted from `server-methods.ts` and `server-plugin-in-process-authority.ts`.
- `sessions-history-http.ts`: each SSE publish keeps the data fences (captured storage owner, session id, lifecycle revision, start time). It no longer re-authenticates, re-reads scopes or re-reads membership.
- `tools-invoke-http.ts`: the tool signal ends only on client disconnect and request end.
- `LIFETIME_CHECK_CALLS` loses `captureOperatorToolGatewayAuthority`, `resolveSessionRuntimeAuthority` and `captureMediaGenerationAdmission`.

Kept on purpose (cut less):

- `captureMediaGenerationAdmission`: code unchanged, name removed from the ratchet. Its own checks are data fences: the run-registry lifecycle generation and the transcript storage location, which guard the task launch and the image review action's queue writes. Its remaining authority piece is `captureGatewayToolCallerAssertion`, and the tool-caller PRs remove that. Same call as #203572 made for the capability lease.
- `plugin-node-host.ts` `prepareExecAuthorization`: the plugin calls it when it launches the command, and its `assertCurrent` runs before the spawn of that same launch. This is launch-time admission, not a mid-run check.
- Stop and every session data fence.

Accepted edge cases:

- A request that started before a revoke finishes.
- An SSE history stream opened before a revoke keeps streaming until the client reconnects; the reconnect is refused.

## Tests

- New: `tools-invoke-http.abort.test.ts` "finishes an admitted tool when operator access is revoked mid-run" (red on base `40d8a3953663`, green on head).
- New: `sessions-history-http.revocation.test.ts` "keeps streaming an admitted stream after profile revocation" (red on base, green on head).

prs.title: feat(macos): let the guide explain each step of Mac setup in plain words
prs.body:
Part of #203737 and #203775

Part of the desktop lobster workstream, but independent of the role-template changes. This draft is based directly on `main`.

Related: #202613 and #202598 are open drafts on the same first-run path. "Why This Change Was Made" describes how each one relates to this PR.

## What Problem This Solves

When you set up OpenClaw on a Mac for the first time, you see progress steps, cards and buttons. Nothing tells you what a step means, what it needs from you, or what comes next. The hardest moments are a failed "Getting things ready", an AI page that found nothing or rejected a key, and long waits. The mascot reacts to each step but never speaks. On the "find OpenClaw on another computer" page, it does not react when you click **Check connection**.

## User Impact

User impact: every setup page shows a short line from OpenClaw beside the mascot. The line says what is happening, what to do and which button to click, also after a failure.

- **Setup itself does not change.** There are no new steps, settings, permissions or installs. The lines are written in advance and work with no model and no network. They add 34 strings to the translation inventory.
- **Accessibility.** VoiceOver announces each new line without moving focus. **Next** stays on screen in the smallest window.
- **Known limits.** On the AI page, quick line changes interrupt the previous VoiceOver announcement. A stale "That key didn't work" can outrank a newer test failure, though both cards stay visible.
- **Docs.** `docs/start/onboarding.md` no longer describes the first-run screen removed in #196759. It now describes the setup window and the guide.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **One source for the face and the words.** The line comes from the same setup state that picks the mascot's mood, so the two cannot disagree.
- **Failure lines name the existing button that fixes the problem.** No line contains a command, path or port.
- **The find page now reacts.** Mood selection treated it as the welcome page, so it ignored the connection check.

Neither open draft replaces this PR, and this PR replaces neither:

- **#202613 ("set up this Mac in fewer steps on first launch") overlaps in code, but its goal is separate.** It removes steps, and this PR narrates the steps that exist. It edits the same onboarding files and docs section. If it lands first, two of this PR's lines move: the "where should it run" line to the welcome page, and "Click Finish and I'll open the Dashboard" to the moment the AI test passes.
- **#202598 ("let people choose their AI during first-run setup") is in an adjacent lane, with no code overlap.** It changes the Dashboard's first-run AI card, and this PR narrates only the native Mac window. Whichever lands second needs a small merge in `docs/start/onboarding.md`.

## Evidence

- **Published standalone draft (`dcdd4270961`):** Vitor built the native app and test bundle on macOS, then ran the built tests on a disposable macOS 26.5.2 VM: **99 passed in 9 suites**. He also exercised the welcome, connection choice, Gateway startup and AI discovery pages in the real app with a fresh profile. The draft app used the Gateway package from the stack. See the supplied proof note `9-published-203786.md` and log `tests/PR-macos.log`.
- **Regenerated stacked B9 (`8cb5013fe65`):** The separate VM run also passed **99 tests in 9 suites**. The four captured pages show the same guide lines and placement. The desktop companion and shaded mascot are from earlier stack changes, not from this standalone PR. See `9.md` and `tests/B9-macos.log`.
- **Not covered by the VM runs:** The proposed standalone refresh with the ClawSweeper fix for a rejected AI-account test was verified by source replay and whitespace checks only. It still needs the exact-head native build and focused tests, plus real-app checks for the rejected-account path, VoiceOver and minimum-window behavior.

Regenerated source range: `5d621dede8fcccfa812439ddee64cdec2dde6cfa` → `8cb5013fe65907991874e0182fb5bead03a030de` (four B9 commits; B1–B8 excluded from the standalone replay).

Contributor: [@TheAngryPit](https://github.com/TheAngryPit).

prs.title: fix(control-ui): retain dismissed failures across cron pause
prs.body:
Closes #202652

## What Problem This Solves

Dismissing a failed automation in the Inbox, then pausing and enabling its schedule, brings the same failure back even though no new run occurred. This happens when the All agents inventory refresh treats the paused job's hidden row as a resolved failure.

## User Impact

A dismissed failure stays hidden across pause, enable, and page reload. A later failed run or automatic-disable incident still appears. Existing saved dismissals are retained; recovered or removed jobs stop retaining them.

## Why This Change Was Made

Dismissal retention now follows the underlying failure instead of whether its row is currently visible. Failures are identified by their recorded run or automatic-disable time, and existing job-only dismissals are bound to the currently known failures. A row may represent both a failed run and an automatic-disable incident; dismissing it acknowledges both, so clearing one cause does not revive the other. Paused-job visibility and other Inbox categories are unchanged.

## Evidence

The actual built Control UI was exercised in Chromium through the repository's E2E harness with synthetic Gateway WebSocket responses. On the base revision, dismiss → pause → enable returned the old row and failed the assertion. With the fix, the old row stayed absent and a distinct later failure appeared. This verifies the UI boundary, not a live scheduler or provider.

Before: the same dismissed failure returns after enabling.

![Before: Archive check returns in the Inbox after pause and enable](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2b3fe9cd-d7f3-434d-9c77-e6185894ca21)

After: the same failure stays dismissed.

![After: the Inbox remains empty after enabling the same failed job](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c9d1d592-cfc3-44e0-8a4f-8245a5268544)

Both captures use the same 1440×900 viewport, light theme, synthetic job and All agents scope. Before is `dc73ec0bac`; after is this patch. No layout or styling change.

The permanent store regression covers persistence across a paused reload, a later failure, recovery, removal, and legacy job-only dismissals. Additional regressions reproduced automatic-disable transitions, failed and successful manual runs, and legacy history without a run timestamp. The repair retains each present failure independently so enabling or manual recovery does not revive an acknowledged incident.

<details>
<summary>Validation details</summary>

- Base regression: two expected failures because pausing removed the saved dismissal.
- Final related suites: 4 files, 61 tests passed.
- Changed store suite: 41 tests passed, 2.40 s Vitest duration / 5.52 s command wall time with one worker. Net test growth: 124 lines. CI seconds are not available yet.
- Browser base: `Same failed run after pause/enable: 1`, expected 0; exit 1.
- Browser fix: `Same failed run after pause/enable: 0`, `Distinct failed run after pause/enable: 1`; exit 0. [New failure screenshot](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/179b166c-a974-41f4-84b2-904f52002d17).
- Changed checks, UI production/component test types, lint, format, controller guard, test-line budget and diff checks passed. The three dead-export scans passed with zero entries and were reused on the final changed-check rerun. Earlier line-cap and test-table typing failures were corrected without dropping coverage.
- Independent local review was completed after correcting its automatic-disable findings.

Focused suite command:

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config ui/vitest.config.ts \
  ui/src/components/sidebar-attention-store.test.ts \
  ui/src/components/sidebar-attention-items.test.ts \
  ui/src/components/sidebar-attention-dismissals.test.ts \
  ui/src/components/sidebar-attention-cron-events.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

</details>

## Upgrade from v2026.11.6

The published `openclaw@2026.11.6` Control UI and the bundle built from `c53c398db97f` ran at the same origin in the same Chromium context. The release tarball matched the registry SHA-1 `1399d4ec476c2bb47ceb5e1c70d8aa6c89f22cfc`. Both used synthetic Gateway responses for the same account and job.

In the release UI, dismissing **Archive check** from the Automations tab wrote the original browser record. Reloading with the PR bundle migrated that record. Pausing the job and reloading the page retained the dismissal. Enabling it kept the old failure hidden, and advancing the failed-run time by one minute produced one visible row. The browser test also compared the saved theme, theme mode, sidebar agent mode, and current Gateway selection before and after the upgrade.

```text
old release browser dismissal [ 'archive-check' ]
upgraded dismissal [ 'archive-check@1795197600000' ]
paused reload retained dismissal
Same failed run after pause/enable: 0
preserved named settings: [ 'theme', 'themeMode', 'sidebarAgentsMode' ]
Distinct failed run after pause/enable: 1
Tests  1 passed (1)
```

prs.title: fix(tlon): require approval before responding in group DMs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Tlon group DM messages carry author claims that the Tlon transport does not authenticate. OpenClaw could treat a claimed ship in a group DM as if it matched the verified 1:1 DM allowlist, admitting unapproved input to the agent.

## User Impact

User impact: the owner enables a group DM once per club by default, then the agent can respond automatically in that club. Operators can require approval for each message, disable clubs, or allow and deny specific club IDs. Existing clubs need one-time enablement after upgrade; claimed authors and legacy approvals do not grant standing access.

## Why This Change Was Made

Club admission now depends on the club's own policy and recorded decision. Claimed participants never provide owner or command authority. Approved club messages use a club-specific group session, and replies return to the club. The change also decodes Tlon's wrapped settings events so saved decisions work across restarts.

Enabling a club accepts unverified input delivered under that club ID with the agent's ordinary permitted tools. It does not authenticate the author or membership; the owner prompt and Tlon docs explain that tradeoff.

This is a replacement for #196109. Thanks to @mmaps for identifying the group DM author-claim boundary and preparing the first fix. This version keeps approval friction to once per club by default and adds explicit stricter modes and club reply routing.

## Evidence

- The two regression cases failed on the base and pass with this change: an allowlisted claimed author cannot admit an unknown club, and a club turn uses a group route rather than the claimed author's direct route.
- In an isolated Gateway with a real model, a bot-side Tlon club event claiming allowlisted `~nec` produced one owner prompt and no agent turn. A verified `~bus` DM approved the club; the saved message ran through the model, which read a proof file and replied inside the club. A later message claiming the owner received an automatic club reply without another prompt. After Gateway restart, the saved club rule still allowed an automatic reply.
- Upgrade check: the published `@openclaw/tlon@2026.11.5` plugin created a legacy pending club request in isolated ship state. The replacement plugin loaded it; owner approval replayed the saved message without adding the claimed ship to the DM allowlist or enabling the club. The next message prompted for a new club decision.
- Startup persistence check: with no saved club rules, an explicit file-config allow rule migrated into the real Urbit settings store as a JSON string. A regression test failed before this serialization repair and passes after it.
- All 322 Tlon tests in 35 files passed on merged current `main`. After the final test-file split and direct-settings compatibility repair, the affected tests (47 sender/monitor cases and 5 settings cases), Tlon production and test typechecks, lint, format, the assertion-safety ratchet, and diff whitespace checks pass. Docs MDX/config examples/internal links also pass.
- The generated config baseline records six intentional Tlon schema paths for club policy and rules at the channel and account levels. Relative to current `main`, core and plugin counts are unchanged; `pnpm config:docs:check` passes. The merged current-main tree also passes all 322 Tlon tests and the Tlon production typecheck.
- CI on current head `7f3e790c331` passes `openclaw/ci-gate`, the assertion-safety and config baselines, docs, Tlon changed-code checks, security checks, and Control UI e2e. No required check failed. An earlier assertion-safety failure on `33be0deafbc` was repaired by using the existing record parser and shrinking the per-file allowance from 7 to 5.
- Local autoreview of the complete staged source change against base `053fb62c` reported `scoped-clean` for P0–P2 with no actionable finding at `b293ba33`. The later commits add generated baseline files and merge current `main`; the Tlon source patch is unchanged. Its assessment covered the supplied patch, not a live Tlon round trip.
- Local ClawSweeper reviewed the final committed range `461b02a48f5..7f3e790c331`: `review_status: complete`, patch correct, no code findings, security cleared. Its initial compatibility finding led to retaining the prior direct settings event shape alongside Tlon's wrapped events, with a focused regression test. The local-range reviewer did not receive the PR's live and upgrade evidence, which is recorded here; the default policy was approved for this work by the requesting maintainer.
- Authenticated remote ingress proof: a test-only Gall agent on isolated fake `~ten` sent a native remote `%chat-club-action` poke over Ames to fake `~zod`, claiming author `~nec`. The remote poke was acknowledged and `~zod` stored the club message. The isolated Gateway emitted one approval prompt to verified `~ten` DM and no agent turn before approval. After that DM approved the club, the real model read a proof file and replied `papaya` into `~zod`'s club. A second remotely delivered message claiming owner `~ten` received an automatic club reply without another approval prompt; saved `clubRules` contains the allow rule and no pending approval.
- Tlon transport diagnosis: fresh non-fake comets on the same released `%groups` desk hash (`a6eta`) exchanged Ames `|hi` and a direct DM invitation, but stock club creates remained local. Verbose Gall tracing showed no outgoing peer poke. A temporary `%chat` trace confirmed that club gossip selected the peer but its final card list omitted the remote poke. In the disposable VM only, changing `=. cor (emil (gossip:cu-pass diff))` to `=. cor.nu-core (emil:cor.nu-core (gossip:cu-pass:nu-core diff))` retained the gossip cards. Before the local Tlon correction, the peer's club list stayed empty; afterward, a new invite reached it and a peer message reached the creator. The test desks retain only that one-line correction, with trace prints removed. Neither Git repository was changed by this investigation.
- Full remote round trip on the locally repaired Tlon desks: an isolated Gateway running this PR on the peer comet received a real club message from the other comet claiming allowlisted author `~nec`. It saved one club approval request and sent one prompt to the verified owner's DM, without starting an agent turn. The owner approved by verified DM. The real `openai/gpt-4.1-mini` agent used its `read` tool on `proof-input.txt` and replied `quince`; both ships' club histories contained the reply. A second club message claiming to be the owner received an automatic `second-turn-ok` reply on both ships, without another owner DM. The persisted Tlon settings have `clubRules` allowing only that club and no pending approval; OpenClaw stored one `tlon:group:club:0vp.abcde` session. Stock Tlon club gossip remains broken on the tested desk, so this proof depends on the isolated one-line Tlon repair.

prs.title: feat: let agents answer questions about OpenClaw itself
prs.body:
Part of #203737.

## What Problem This Solves

People ask their OpenClaw agent about OpenClaw itself: "can it do X", "how do I connect Telegram", "why won't my Gateway start". The agent knows only where the docs folder is. It has to guess which of about 1,200 pages answers the question, which bundled skill already covers it, and which commands are safe to run. When it guesses wrong, people turn to another coding agent to set up or fix OpenClaw.

## User Impact

Every agent gets two bundled skills, on by default:

- `openclaw-handbook` routes each question about OpenClaw to a bundled skill, a docs page, or a read-only command. It also has a troubleshooting reference for common first-run failures.
- `openclaw-docs` finds the docs page for any other topic from a map of every page. If the local copy is unavailable, it tries the published page.

Before the agent says OpenClaw cannot do something, the handbook makes it check `openclaw help`, the docs map, and the published `llms.txt` as needed. Each skill adds one short line to the skill list in the prompt. Nothing else in the prompt changes.

The Ask OpenClaw guide (the system agent) does not get these skills. Its turns allow only the `openclaw` tool, so it cannot read skill files.

## Why This Change Was Made

The handbook follows the hub shape of Hermes' `hermes-agent` skill. It has a short identity, key paths, a routing list, and a rule against answering "it can't do that" from memory. It routes config, Doctor, secrets, access, and skill refresh questions to the existing guidance. For pairing, it sends agents to the live route checks in `node-connect` before proposing configuration changes. Troubleshooting preserves authorization the user has already given and still honors runtime approvals.

The docs map is generated from `docs/docs.json` by `pnpm docs:skill-map:gen`. `pnpm docs:skill-map:check` runs in the docs CI lane and fails when the map is stale. The map uses navigation only, so it changes when a page is added, moved, or removed. That includes each release-notes page. The heading mirror removed in #117398 changed on every heading edit.

The skill is named `openclaw-handbook`, not `openclaw`. A skill named `openclaw` would claim the `/openclaw` slash command, which is the system agent's rescue command.

## Evidence

The contributor’s `PROOF-90673223005.md` records these checks on [`a799df4c89a`](https://github.com/TheAngryPit/openclaw/commit/a799df4c89a54410327057fb06f9e1124f775bf1):

- The skill snapshot included both skills and ranked `openclaw-handbook` in the top three for Telegram, permission-mode, and Gateway questions. The docs map matched the generator, and stale-map detection worked (16/16 focused tests).
- Prompt stability passed (16/16), along with four type checks, docs validation, skill validation, formatting, and targeted lint. The full repo lint wrapper did not run because the local install lacked the Solid lint dependency.

The four-file follow-up at `f7a5edd0c4` passed `git diff --check`. The affected documentation routes, anchor, and skill references were checked against source. The focused docs-map and bundled skill snapshot suites passed (16/16), and the generated docs map check passed.

prs.title: fix(ui): move automation notices out of the Inbox
prs.body:
Closes #202913

## What Problem This Solves

Failed and overdue automations add to the Inbox count. Their run details live on the Automations page.

## User Impact

Automation notices leave the Inbox. The Automations clock shows a single red dot while any automation in the current agent view is failed. The settings guide points readers to Automations for the run details.

## Why This Change Was Made

Vyctor asked for the failure indicator on the clock. The rail shares the Automations sidebar’s failure styling and uses the same definition of a current failure. During startup, a model auth status read receives a retryable error. The Inbox keeps saved dismissals when the Gateway reports auth status as temporarily unavailable.

## Evidence

A real Gateway ran a failing backup in each fresh browser profile. The regression failed on main and passed on the branch. With two failed jobs, the dot stayed through the first successful rerun and cleared after the last. Clicking the clock opened Automations.

### Main vs PR head

| --- | --- |

Fresh profiles on main `0abe03d1008` and head `002ecce1981`. The head capture shows Daily backup in Automations, the clock dot and an empty Inbox.

### Clock placement on the PR head

### Existing-profile upgrades to the PR head

I tested upgrades to `002ecce1981` from three published releases: `v2026.9.37` extended-stable, `v2026.10.10`, and `v2026.11.6`.

In each release, I dismissed the Anthropic and OpenAI account warnings, saved Light mode and the blue accent, and ran Daily backup to produce a real failure. I kept the browser tab open while restarting the same Gateway with the PR build, then reloaded the same browser profile.

In all three upgrades, both settings survived and both account warnings stayed dismissed. The Gateway still reported the warnings. The same failed backup remained in Automations, the clock showed a red dot, and Inbox was empty.

prs.title: fix(cli): preserve explicitly allowed message tools in MCP
prs.body:
Related: #167085. Reported by @jaimeehenry.

## What Problem This Solves

CLI MCP preparation drops an explicitly requested `message` tool under a restrictive profile. Its final cap cannot restore a tool already removed during catalog construction.

## User Impact

Explicit message requests survive restrictive profiles consistently with embedded assembly. Configured denials, channel/account policy, final exact/policy caps and invocation authority remain enforced. Delivery mode and configuration are unchanged. Maintainer security approval remains required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both current assembly and MCP preparation use the existing shared policy owner for a message-only profile allowance. The MCP hint derives from captured `context.toolsAllow`; it does not promote the complete cap into `alsoAllow` or force `message_tool_only`.

The current normal integration preserves main's 31-line compatibility wrapper and shared assembly module. The original patch's small policy reuse is moved into that live assembly owner; the old generator is not restored. Global-deny construction, ring-zero tools, loopback-config checks, Automations ownership and current Tool Search controls stay with main's owners.

Run-bound MCP context is cloned from the host-minted grant. The server-session and caller-token/header branches do not supply `toolsAllow`, so client headers cannot introduce this profile hint. Final catalog filtering and live invocation checks remain separate.

## November 23 main integration

Integrated official main 4b94c6d136f6 into this PR at 969e58ae9f6cccfaeb81dba37cd40792cf9b43c6. The embedded assembly file uses the exact current main blob, including main's fixed-listing behavior. The remaining proposed behavior is in MCP catalog preparation. The catalog table uses the in-memory direct-route fixture already used by upstream channel-availability tests. This follows main's rule that catalog entries require a supported message route.

10 isolated catalog cases passed, covering the explicit message request, restrictive profiles, and existing policy and exact denials. Core and relevant Gateway test types, typed lint, formatting, test-line budget, and independent source review passed. Earlier proof below retains its recorded revision. This PR still awaits the shipped runtime evidence and maintainer security review recorded below.

## Evidence

Pre-integration head `e77122f8e3015af9f4078a47c90f650076827535`, tree `cc867bb203ddcf3381b1b1fe51ce8c9d8875bb33`, normally merges author `c7f5a78f96d910abaffe83394fb16ff413da22a1` and official main `49018bf5f67e36a721be5ea3c28c93d2779b3961`. The final commit tree matches the fully reviewed and locally tested candidate.

- **Real current-main before → after:** with production source exactly at `49018bf5f67e36a721be5ea3c28c93d2779b3961` and only the existing regression table overlaid, the actual MCP policy/exact resolvers produce **4 intended missing-message failures / 3 passing denial or read-only controls**. Each failure returns `read` without requested `message`; 25 other cases are unselected. Wrapper cost is **372.014 seconds**. The candidate retains every input/expectation in the original seven rows.
- **121 cases across 6 complete files pass**, covering both catalog/runtime owners, CLI cap policy, embedded assembly, definition/prompt-prefix stability and the simulated native observer. Wrapper cost is **929.044 seconds**, including native compilation, execution auditing and routed project startup. Counts are distinct routed cases, not summed duplicate summaries. The natural CI result below is separate from this local wrapper cost.
- Production types pass in **53.662 seconds**. The canonical changed-test selector passes the three affected core test graphs in 530.125 seconds. The observer test consumer also passes with canonical extension settings and ambient declarations (467.894 seconds). These durations include checkout-artifact ownership waiting. Typed lint passes on all three production paths (400.259 seconds), the Gateway test (53.328 seconds) and observer fixture (48.916 seconds).
- Format, native mock-export, line-cap and whitespace guards pass. The absolute local native test-line gate passes at **6,654,837 / 6,654,837**, with **0 LF slack**. This is an absolute pass, without a zero-growth over-budget exemption.
- The existing seven-row catalog regression contributes exactly **97 net LF**. A separate record grants exactly 97, with the shared scalar and every other record unchanged. These rows exercise the real catalog owner, which can lose a requested tool before the final cap; a helper-only assertion misses the defect. The denial/read-only rows independently protect narrowing.
- A known integration prerequisite aligns one strict observer-result expectation with the shared compact JSON contract adopted in [#196756](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/196756). It carries the previously verified correction from our `304d4d5e` revision: **0 LF growth**, with payload values, details, arguments, context, identities, call count and all other assertions preserved. Production serialization and native protocols are untouched. Its seven serializer/startup inputs match the previously audited source, and its full 12-case mock file passes in this collection.
- `execve` auditing observes **zero Codex CLI executions** in both the failing control and complete passing collection. Protocol clients are fake/in-memory; the private OpenClaw test scheduler is not an operator Gateway. No native Codex login, status, version, app-server or review command was run on ECS.

Natural [CI run 42998313249](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42998313249) succeeds for this head: **73 terminal jobs, 44 successful and 29 skipped**. The maintainer security-sensitive review remains pending; its separate classic CI-gate status requires approval. The behavior gaps below remain separate merge requirements.

prs.title: fix(cron): re-prepare script runtimes when the plugin inventory changes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An existing script automation kept reporting `ReferenceError` for a plugin tool after online enablement, although a new automation could call it in the same Gateway. Restarting the Gateway restored the old job (#199478).

## User Impact

Existing automations can use newly enabled plugin tools on their next invocation without a Gateway restart.

## Why This Change Was Made

Cron preparation now includes the existing active plugin registry version in its cache identity. Registry publication invalidates an unchanged job even when its previous registry was retained. Gateway-owned cron runs read the current Gateway config, not the startup config, before preparing plugin tools; standalone cron retains its existing config fallback. The duplicate registry-version export and its mocked call-count test were removed in favor of a real plugin-loading regression.

## Evidence

An isolated Gateway with a synthetic plugin was started once; the same disabled script job was run before and after `plugins.setEnabled`. The following is terminal output from `pnpm exec tsx .artifacts/199492-gateway-proof.mts`, selecting only the status, error, and returned marker fields from its CLI/RPC JSON records (identifiers and local paths omitted):

```json
{"step":"BEFORE","status":"error","error":"cron script payload failed (internal_error): ReferenceError: inventory_probe is not defined"}
{"step":"INVOKE","ok":true,"details":{"marker":"plugin-online-ok"}}
{"step":"AFTER","status":"ok","completionStatus":"succeeded"}
{"step":"NEW JOB","status":"ok","completionStatus":"succeeded"}
{"step":"JOB","lastRunStatus":"ok","triggerState":{"marker":"plugin-online-ok"}}
```

`BEFORE` and `AFTER` are the same pre-existing job. `JOB` is the stored state of that job; its `triggerState` contains the actual plugin tool return marker, beyond the completion status. `NEW JOB` is a separate job created after enablement. This proof uses no live account or external model.

The committed real plugin-loading regression also checks a registry-only publication with an unchanged config object, followed by live config publication with the updated plugin generation. Focused cron suites: 37/37 passed. Core TypeScript, changed-file oxlint and oxfmt, line-cap ratchet, test-line budget, and `git diff --check` passed. Fresh review identified and resolved a registry-only invalidation proof gap before this push.

No config migration or user action is required.

prs.title: fix: keep Gateway follow-up work authorized after earlier requests end
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Gateway follow-up work can lose its usable authority after the original request ends. A descendant may try to retain an already retired recovery claim, or be refused because an earlier invocation's failure was mistaken for revocation of the original source. Tokenless recovery must also preserve the original device's next-start revocation checks.

## User Impact

Authorized descendants can continue after the originating request ends. Source revocation still refuses the next start, without retroactively cancelling already-admitted work. No configuration, public API, or stored-data format changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Continuation capture shares its already-acquired original/restored holds using idempotent reference-counted release, instead of reacquiring a retired ancestor claim. Each new start still checks both policy owners. Original Gateway reauthorization checks source-policy owners and signals independently of invocation-specific failure state, retaining device, committed-source, identity, role, profile, and model restrictions.

The current-main integration preserves the explicit tokenless device-revocation guard from #202318, along with current membership and trusted-proxy policy changes. The allowed/revoked tokenless regression moves into the focused invocation test file and now also exercises descendant capture and release of the preceding hold; existing coverage is retained without exceeding the test-file line cap. The scripted product fixture is unchanged from current main.

The simplification pass keeps the existing authority owners; no new manager, store, configuration, retry, or timeout was introduced.

## Evidence

- The two original regressions reproduced before repair: retaining a descendant after the recovery claim retired, and starting a descendant after the original invocation failed. The earlier stable-source proof passed 111 tests across seven files and two shards.
- Prior published head `d97af15f6a71819b280ef1179290d20c4151662a`: CI run `44532032648`, attempt 2, passed; hosted review completed with no findings. These are prior-head results, not evidence for the integration commit.
- Integration base: `7d1d7d035ce611b0d99f52f218ccd7b80297dac5`. Published commit: `b76eea52d58e9b35b2750d995c53c2ecca136f3b`. The focused final suite passed 47 tests across three files, including the relocated regressions and scripted Gateway product flow. An earlier post-integration four-file recovery/authority/device suite passed 83 tests before the test-only relocation.
- Scripted Gateway scenarios: allowed work produced one effect and one wake; device-revoked work produced no effect or wake and one refusal. The owned process tree was joined. These use scripted model responses, not a real provider.
- Production core and Gateway-root typechecks, targeted lint/format, and the scoped diff check passed. Gateway-root types and targeted lint were checked again after the test relocation.
- Fresh full-context independent review of the final four-file diff found no concrete P0–P3 defects. Canonical autoreview of the committed range from the integration base through `b76eea52d58e9b35b2750d995c53c2ecca136f3b` completed P0–P3 scoped-clean with no findings and exit 0 (OpenClaw engine, effective model `openai/gpt-6.1-sol`). Canonical review was supplied-diff only, without unchanged implementation context or test execution; it supplements the full-context review and focused tests.
- The integrated PR diff is four files (+207/-88); SHA-256 of `git diff --binary 7d1d7d035ce611b0d99f52f218ccd7b80297dac5 b76eea52d58e9b35b2750d995c53c2ecca136f3b` is `a49365fa7679f0fa843907dc5780ce6c5c6bc1eef2f234d01342c8424c650da7`.

- November 21 live proof: rebuilt the runtime from published head `b76eea52d58e9b35b2750d995c53c2ecca136f3b`, then used the supported isolated live-test launcher, an empty fixture HOME/config/state, a real agent, and OpenAI `gpt-5.4` inference. The selected descendant case passed (one test, 11 provider requests); no other live cases were selected. Native `sessions_spawn` calls preserved the hidden-subagent restriction against `sessions_send`, with completion handoffs disabled.
- The live sequence observed the original and continuation terminal results before allowing the descendant to proceed, accepted its next child, removed the original device through the real Gateway owner, and rejected its following child with the owner refusal “Operator access was revoked; start a new user turn.” The already-admitted descendant finished; the refused child made zero provider requests. The owned Gateway stopped and fixture state was removed. No production authorization changes were required.
- Exact published-head CI run `44735418115`, attempt 1, completed successfully. The live harness changes remain private/unpublished; the PR source diff and head are unchanged.

### Remaining proof limits

The real-agent/model sequence now passes on the published integration head using an isolated Gateway and actual OpenAI inference. It establishes parent terminal results before descendant admission, not a deterministic observation that every ancestor authority hold has already been released: `agent.wait` is a terminal-result barrier, and native registry custody can outlive the model turn. Exact release/closed-connection ordering remains covered by the deterministic production-owner regression in `operator-run-recovery.invocation.test.ts`. The live sequence is complementary end-to-end evidence, not a replacement for that regression or a real-provider restart/recovery test. Prior hosted review does not cover this integration commit. Unpublished quiet-steering live-test work remains excluded.

prs.title: fix(cron): optional-silent cron run fails after the agent collects its collector child's result
prs.body:
Root cause: `src/agents/accepted-session-spawn.ts:102` (`hasOwedSessionSpawn`) counts every `collector: true` receipt as owed work for the whole run, and nothing retires that obligation when `agents_wait` returns the child as done. So `finalizeCronRun` (`src/cron/isolated-agent/run-finalize.ts:395-399`) treats a run that already collected all its children and ended with `NO_REPLY` as a spawn-only handoff and adopts the children's raw results.

Fixes #164887
Fixes #203821

## What Problem This Solves

An isolated cron job spawns collector children (`sessions_spawn` with `collect: true`), collects them all with `agents_wait`, and ends with exactly `NO_REPLY`.

- `delivery.mode: "announce"` (#203821): the scheduler posts the children's internal JSON results to the channel and records the run as `delivered`, with the first child's JSON as the summary.
- `delivery.mode: "none"` (#164887): the run waits on the children again and records their internal results as its summary. Older releases reported this variant as an incomplete-turn error. Main no longer fails that way since #170534, but the same false handoff is still there.

## Fix

`agents_wait` already runs under the admitted run's caller identity in every harness. When it returns a child as `done`, it now clears `collector` from that run's spawn receipt, the same way `retireAcceptedSessionSpawnCompletionForRun` ends an owed completion after a confirmed cancellation. Acceptance stays recorded. `hasOwedSessionSpawn` and cron finalize are main's, unchanged. A child that is still pending, or that `agents_wait` reports as failed, keeps its collector obligation. A child that owns a completion message (`expectsCompletionMessage`) is not affected. One change covers both variants because both read the same receipt check.

The receipt lives only in memory for the run (`acceptedSpawnsByRun`). Nothing is persisted, and no schema, config or tool text changes.

## Evidence

Built Gateway (`pnpm build`) in a secretless `node:24.22.1` container, real isolated cron jobs (`cron.add` + `cron.run`), a scripted OpenAI Responses fixture that replays the reporter's sequence (3 collector children, `agents_wait` until `pending` is empty, final `NO_REPLY`), and the QA stand-in channel for announce delivery. Base `50ff9d46337` (merge base) twice and this head twice. Observed results: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/164949#issuecomment-7088122259

| Case | Base | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| announce + 3 collected + `NO_REPLY` | `delivered`, 1 channel post with the 3 children's raw JSON, summary = child JSON (2/2) | `ok`, `deliverySuppressionReason: silent`, 0 posts (2/2) |
| `delivery.mode: none` + 3 collected + `NO_REPLY` | `ok` but summary = the children's raw JSON (false handoff adopted) (2/2) | `ok`, no summary, 0 posts (2/2) |
| control: collector never collected | child result posted (2/2) | unchanged (2/2) |
| control: child owns a completion message | child result posted after ~125 s (2/2) | unchanged (2/2) |
| control: collected + visible final reply | parent digest posted (2/2) | unchanged (2/2) |

Tests: `agents-wait-tool.native.test.ts` runs the real `agents_wait` tool under an admitted run with persisted done, failed and cancelled collectors, then merges a Copilot-style projection. It fails with main's production files (1 failed, 3 passed) and passes on this head. The touched tests and their importers pass (`agents-wait-tool`, `sessions-spawn-tool`, `swarm-tools.integration`, `code-mode-swarm`, `requester-run-settlement`, `subagent-registry-restart-collector`, cron `run.meta-error-status`). oxfmt, oxlint, `tsgo` core and core tests are clean. `check:changed`'s full-tree dead-export scan fails only on unused exports in files this PR does not touch (`src/cli/id-cli-unlink.ts`, `src/update/*`, others), which is the same on the base.

## Credit

Thanks to @jayzhou2309 for the original fix and the `agents_wait` receipt test, @Hensarj for #164887, @ArthurBook for the announce-mode report and analysis in #203821, @alexph-dev for the repeated production reproductions, and @jlapenna for the real-model runs. The maintainer commit on top replaces the added `collected` field with retiring the existing `collector` obligation and drops the cron field-copy test, which became a duplicate of main's existing fire-and-forget case.

## Merge danger

Two-way door: a revert restores the previous behavior fully, and nothing is written to disk. Blast radius: runs that spawn `collect: true` children and collect them with `agents_wait`; their cron finalize no longer waits for or adopts those children.

prs.title: fix: show native notification settings in the iOS app
prs.body:
Closes #164557

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Settings → Notifications shows Safari Home Screen installation instructions when opened inside the native iOS app.

## User Impact

User impact: iPhone and iPad app users can see their native notification delivery and permission settings and open the existing device settings pages. Browser/PWA and macOS notification flows remain separate and unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The page already observes the native device-settings capability but did not pass its snapshot into the notification view. This repair uses that existing owner, shows a loading state while its snapshot is pending, and keeps missing status values unknown. Device links use application navigation so the native Back history is retained; modified clicks keep normal link behavior.

Upstream migrated the settings UI from Lit to Solid. This update keeps the current Solid renderer and ports the native-notification regression with it. Native notification presentation and capability-to-view props live in focused siblings to respect the existing file-size guards. No notification transport, native permission operation, configuration key, dependency, or generated translation memory changes.

## Evidence

Current tested head: `c326ed5fc8fc63d243f337ff928a9cca42304f5b` (tree `f7d308969f6204e5309accb9137dfac74b82069c`). This is a normal two-parent merge preserving the original PR head `d7bdb5a3c123b1db96eeb9322a42efeb0075df71` and upstream `5584b16af9109db5235f776cb1302093f6bf2f59`.

- The real Notifications route, ConfigPage, capability adapters, and rendered DOM are exercised together. The migrated test fails eight native cases against untouched upstream production; the Safari/PWA/Mac controls pass.
- Final focused run: **140 tests passed in six files, 8.12 seconds wall time**, covering iPhone/iPad, base paths, delayed and changed native snapshots, missing fields, ordinary/modified clicks, absent callbacks, and browser/Mac controls.
- Production Control UI build completed successfully in **18.94 seconds**.
- i18n verification, focused style checks, documentation MDX/link checks, formatting, line-cap/max-lines/assertion-safety guards, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent source review identified missing route-loader result narrowing in the migrated test fixture. Explicit route and result guards address it; the final focused rerun and fresh canonical P0–P2 autoreview passed without remaining actionable findings.

**Outstanding verification:** Physical iPhone QA and inspected before/after screenshots remain unavailable. The DOM tests provide synthetic bridge-contract evidence and do not establish native-device or visual behavior. Production UI typechecking, a reduced focused typecheck, and typed lint were terminated with exit 137/SIGKILL without source diagnostics; those gates are not claimed green. Full repository tests have not run, and current-head hosted CI is not yet verified. This remains a draft pending those checks and the required native/visual evidence.

Checks ran on Node 24.19.0 through the repository wrappers. Dependencies were installed with the frozen lockfile using the environment's pnpm 11.25.0. The pinned pnpm 12.9.0 install was attempted but could not open its store operation lock on this host's read-only filesystem; this tooling limitation remains explicit.

Codex generated the change and performed the code review and automated checks described above; no human review is claimed.

Focused command:

node ../scripts/run-node-package-bin.mts vitest run --config vitest.config.ts src/pages/config/config-page.notifications.test.tsx src/pages/config/config-page.test.ts src/pages/config/notifications-section.test.tsx src/app/native-notifications.test.ts src/app/native-device-settings.test.ts src/app/web-push.test.ts --project unit --maxWorkers=1

prs.title: fix: reduce catalog and database read memory overhead
prs.body:
> **Do not merge — performance acceptance fails.** Head `a30b415ce3ac443a53c2156993bd57e998c214ae` passes CI and functional checks, but the five-pair comparison shows **sessions.list p99 +32.35%** and event-loop delay tail telemetry **+20.04%**. Both cross the unchanged 20% stop threshold. No merge is requested.

## What Problem This Solves

Catalog lookup loads standalone configuration schemas and system-event execution machinery when it only needs prepared inventory. Database reads also repeatedly scan SELECT bodies for mutation keywords, creating temporary allocations and falsely treating ignored SQL tails as writes.

## User Impact

Across five compiled baseline/candidate pairs, retained catalog-worker heap falls **96.205 → 79.593 MiB (−17.27%)**. Under eight-agent Gateway load, median peak process RSS falls only **3796.992 → 3702.832 MiB (−2.48%)**, while process CPU falls **2.68%**. The remaining approximately **3.62 GiB** peak is still substantial.

This branch is **not accepted for landing**: session-list p99 rises **105.351 → 139.432 ms (+32.35%)**, history median rises **14.86%**, and several other latency metrics worsen. These measurements compare the **whole branch** with the frozen baseline; they do not isolate the incremental RSS effect of the SELECT change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Prepared catalogs consume captured facts through shared AuthStorage/ModelRegistry implementations; standalone facades retain public identity and acquire config/source/environment readers before yielding. Narrow schema and runtime-snapshot imports avoid broad validation graphs. Model suppression reuses captured plugin metadata.

The plugin loader supplies its lazy system getter through a synchronous factory using the existing native resolver and captured cache owner. A stable compiled system entry preserves source/packaged loading and host-facade identity.

Native-prepared SELECT statements now skip mutation and transaction-control scans. Native execution observation stays in place, so callback writes still invalidate receipts. Batches, CTEs, PRAGMAs and writes retain their existing classification. This follows the [SQLite first-statement prepare contract](https://www.sqlite.org/c3ref/prepare.html), without a result cache or parser replacement.

Production/build net **+208 lines**, tests/support **+229**, metadata **0**, against the frozen baseline. The SELECT increment is **+3 production / +12 test lines**: it enforces the prepared-statement boundary while removing repeated scanning. Earlier growth establishes prepared/standalone and synchronous runtime ownership boundaries. No new cache, configuration/environment option, schema, protocol, or feature removal. Test-line allocations total **195 LF lines**; the additional 12 cover receipts, ignored SQL tails, callback writes and batch mutation.

## Evidence

### Current compiled comparison

[Completed five-pair run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_6980540522120a5d74e4d94c889687ff), direct AWS m7i.xlarge, observed 4 CPUs / 15.33 GiB RAM, Node 24.22.1, pnpm 12.15.0. Both arms were independently built and run serially in B1,C1,…,B5,C5 order.

- Baseline: `f1c93577085244aa96aa87b53a2df9b59d293bd7`.
- Candidate carrier: `7ff30cd57a93ffb8423f0abc3585c4657fd5a22c`.
- Candidate tree: `ec8a6f7a7d09f6726057000dabe0ffae95b37ff3`, exactly matching published head `a30b415ce3a`.
- All 20 catalog/team processes completed 100 requests each. Ordered response hashes and counts match: catalog/configured/runtime rows **501/1/501**, or **2001/1/2001** for four providers.
- All ten Gateways launched, completed and verified **24 turns** each. Per run: **256 history, 100 updates, 64 each readiness/UI/session-list/load-subscription probes, 128 cron calls, four initial subscriptions and one fresh connection**. No failed requests, budget violations, early exits or unclean exits. Plugin metadata scans during load: **zero**.
- All **640 readiness responses were HTTP 200 but reported eventLoop.degraded=true**. Successful transport is not healthy event-loop qualification.
- Compiled catalog static closure: **1340 files / 15,168,434 bytes → 1055 / 11,310,978**. Checked broad config/protocol/system-execution boundaries are absent from the candidate closure.
- Catalog heap is measured after forced GC outside request timing. Whole-harness RSS includes the source controller. Gateway RSS covers all isolates and instrumentation. Main-heap endpoints vary with GC phase and are **not retained-memory savings**.
- This is isolated synthetic Linux proof, not deployment, ARM or constrained-device qualification.

An independent archive audit reproduced the numbers and functional counts. Session-list p99 equals the maximum of each run's 64 raw samples:

| Pair | Baseline p99 ms | Candidate p99 ms |

Activity-recap inference counts vary **12/12/12/9/6 → 6/6/6/12/6**; benchmark turns remain 24 and session-observer inference zero. Embeddings remain eight requests / 9776 bytes. Candidate benchmark-turn request bytes are consistently 468 bytes higher; the effect is not attributed.

- Restoring the old classifier produces exactly **one failure / one pass / 46 skipped** in the selected regression. The ignored-tail SELECT increments the write receipt to 2 instead of preserving 1 at `src/infra/sqlite-schema-facts.test.ts:78`. Candidate bytes were restored and the source diff verified clean before measurement.
- Independent P0–P2 review of the SELECT increment found no actionable defect. A separate dependency/sibling audit confirms callback observation and unchanged batch/CTE/PRAGMA/control paths. This is source/contract review, not performance acceptance.

The earlier benchmark's focused-proof shell masked a stale call-count failure and invalid smoke/negative-control assertions. That aggregate-success claim is **retracted**; corrected runs above replace it. The earlier five-pair numerical observations were separate valid measurements, not correctness proof for this head.

The separate completed CPU/heap captures in the packaged-owner run motivated the SELECT repair. Sampling includes collected objects: these are **allocations, not retained heap or a leak measurement**.

Three classifier stacks across transcript-worker profiles account for approximately **165 + 155 + 175 MiB**: unquoted-character scanning, whitespace normalization and mutation-keyword scanning under prepared snapshot reads. SQLite workers repeat that work. The SELECT fast path removes those scans at their owner. Its incremental allocation/RSS saving has not been isolated in a separate profile.

A few short-lived worker captures are incomplete, and main-thread heap polling misses some nested isolates. Worker heap sums are partial; process RSS is the aggregate measure. Traced timings do not replace untraced acceptance samples.

### Unchanged acceptance rule

Same isolated host/runtime, separately built arms, five serial alternating pairs, fresh state, recorded host load, cold/warm observations separated; report median, p95 and spread.

1. Compiled catalog: committed `scripts/perf/catalog-worker-retention-measure.ts`, `--built-worker`, five workspaces, 5000 remote rows, runtime plugin, 20 rounds; separate four-provider team case. Compare post-GC heap, first-request and warm latency.
2. Real isolated Gateway: committed `scripts/bench-gateway-concurrency.ts`, mock provider over real transport, 250 sessions, eight concurrent agents, three turns each, 20 history messages of 1024 characters, 64 probe rounds, 100 updates, two update clients, two history clients, four subscribers and control-plane probes; fresh process, zero warmups.
3. Profile separately, never substitute traced timings.

Acceptance requires measurable retained catalog-heap reduction and stable/improved user-facing metrics. Every worsening metric requires explicit owner acceptance; **a 20% move is a stop, never “within spread.”** Current session-list p99 and event-loop tail results fail that rule.

### Review follow-through and named follow-ups

The old ClawSweeper config-capture finding is repaired: standalone facades acquire their reader before the first await. That old review does not cover this head. Request one exact-head re-review once the performance hold is resolved; no prepare/merge request has been submitted.

- Catalog loader imports still reach the install-record writer/install barrel instead of the existing reader. Source-only counterfactual removes 44 modules with zero production LOC growth; unimplemented and unmeasured.
- Resident-worker limits are mostly per-pool and CPU-based. Transcript lanes can total 12 slots on four CPUs and nine on one/two CPUs; demand creation and idle retirement exist. No lifecycle leak or safe pool merger was established. Preserve writer/FIFO and native-settlement boundaries.
- History workers reach shared-state writer code through cron-store selection. A read-only selection kernel removes 19 modules in source-only analysis; unimplemented, no RSS claim.
- Non-SELECT prepared statements retain conservative full-input mutation classification. Evaluate their native compiled-statement boundary separately; this patch does not broaden their behavior.

Eager-system provenance: [runtime split](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/132716), followed by [session-event handoff](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/180079), both authored/merged by @steipete. Source edges are verified; historical RSS impact is not quantified.

prs.title: fix: keep SQLite read receipts stable
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/189111

## What Problem This Solves

SQLite prepares only the first statement in an input string, but OpenClaw classified the entire string when recording writes and schema changes. A read followed by ignored `INSERT` or `CREATE` text could therefore advance write/schema receipts even though SQLite executed no mutation.

## User Impact

Read-only prepared queries keep their write and schema receipts stable. Real writes, schema changes, callback writes, and multi-statement `exec` batches retain their existing behavior. No configuration or database migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Classify the native statement's `sourceSQL`, which reflects what SQLite actually prepared. Resolve and cache that classification at execution so empty-statement preparation keeps its native error timing and iterator binding stays with its existing owner.

Production changes are +7/-3 lines; the additional four lines preserve this compiled-statement boundary and lazy error ordering. Tests are +117/-1 lines. This is a correctness fix; it makes no performance claim.

The original-input classification was introduced in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/156643, extended for write receipts in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/164490, and carried into the observer in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/168029 (all authored by @steipete). It is present in [v2026.11.6](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.11.6/src/infra/sqlite-native-observer.ts#L248-L250).

## Evidence

- Baseline with the regression tests: all four prepared APIs (`get`, `all`, `run`, `iterate`) reproduce the false write receipt on Node 24.22.1 and pinned Bun `191755ec`. The Bun fork-worker executable was verified against the pinned SHA-256.
- Final head `d89c333e4137e4784b940b7a4aacf17bdba83c7b`: observer and schema-facts suites pass, 70/70 tests on Node 24.22.1 and 70/70 on pinned Bun. File-backed controls verify both unchanged receipts for ignored tails and advancing receipts for real mutations.
- The unchanged write-scope, transaction, and post-commit suites pass, 49/49 tests per runtime on `5f0404f91cd78a848e9e4a313a3eb43caa75fe46`; its production observer blob is identical to the final head.
- Final SQLite test typecheck, targeted lint, and oxfmt/Bun formatting parity pass. [Native qualification run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45088550943).
- Independent source review and fresh full-context P0–P2 autoreview found no actionable issue.
- Before/after closed-handle matrices preserve `ERR_INVALID_STATE`, with no SQL callbacks or pending execution custody. A cold closed statement can now report “statement has been finalized” before the observer's “database is not open”; exact error wording is not promised.

The tests cover SELECT/CTE/read-PRAGMA inputs with ignored mutation tails, actual first-statement DML/DDL, complete trigger bodies, repeated statement use, native error tuples, callbacks, iterator custody, and transaction siblings.
