prs.title: fix: keep exec launches working after a stale state read
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When an exec request prepares its approval policy, a state read can be invalidated after its context is captured. The request then returns an unavailable-state error before launch, so users can see a failed exec even though the state database is healthy.

## Why This Change Was Made

The retry applies only to the explicit admission-invalidation error during preparation. It captures the same database path and environment, then runs the normal approval-policy read again. Other errors still surface unchanged.

## User Impact

A stale state-read admission is retried once with current state, avoiding a false failed launch while preserving fail-closed behavior for other errors.

## Evidence

The focused regression failed on validation base 6986a307262daa71ad0b5dbe294f82bf1edde12c with STATE_DATABASE_READ_ADMISSION_INVALIDATED. On head 95cb79376de7e3cbfa9fcb3f7591bafa01a0f3b7, both the regression and the existing admitted-policy stability control passed using the SQLite-backed state worker (2 passed).

Reproduce with `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/exec-approvals-store.read-worker.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --testNamePattern "recaptures a stale state admission|keeps a prepared policy read on its admitted policy after a later policy write"`.

```text
Validation base: 1 failed, 1 passed, 23 skipped; the new regression raised STATE_DATABASE_READ_ADMISSION_INVALIDATED.
Exact head: 2 passed, 23 skipped; the stale-admission regression passed. Negative-control: the admitted-policy stability control also passed.
```

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
```

prs.title: fix(pr): report exact proof rejection identities
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199006 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192263

## What Problem This Solves

Native PR proof publication can reject a review because the selected workflow differs from the reviewed workflow, but the current error does not identify the revisions it compared. Once temporary selection state has retired, maintainers cannot reconstruct that decision from the generic error alone.

## User Impact

Internal maintainer tooling only; no provider or end-user behavior changes. A rejected proof now reports the exact selected and reviewed identities without granting admission or exposing review contents.

## Why This Change Was Made

Append one versioned `PR_PROOF_REJECTION` JSON record to the existing error message. The six identity fields contain only exact lowercase 40-character Git OIDs or `null`. The fixed schema has a maximum encoded record size of 424 bytes, below its 512-byte bound. Existing admission predicates, workflow selection, bindings, transitions, and the original error text are unchanged; successful admission emits no diagnostic.

This makes a rejection observable. It does not fix either related provider PR or the workflow-selection race, and it does not activate or patch any installed launcher.

## Evidence

- Signed candidate: `6ebc2947b2623d9ef730052d975eafe85e0e8e71`, based on `6986a307262daa71ad0b5dbe294f82bf1edde12c`.
- Red baseline: four rejection cases reached the original guard and failed because the diagnostic was absent; the valid-admission control passed.
- Corrected native helper-to-shell run: **10 passed, 26 unselected**, 155.116 seconds wall time (153.65 seconds Vitest). It covers the wrong workflow, missing/malformed/uppercase/trailing-newline identities, one stderr record and none on stdout, no raw-review leakage, silent success, and existing binding/tree/review/lease rejection controls.
- The selected cases take over 30 seconds because they exercise real signed Git fixtures and native shell admission, including unchanged source, binding, transition, and remote-mutation boundaries. A message-only unit test cannot establish those contracts. The timing above is from the retained local run; no hosted timing is claimed for that selected test set.
- Owning tooling test types, focused policy/test lint, formatting, and diff checks passed. Test growth is +84 lines within the 400-line allowance, with no allocation credit.
- Qualified private physical install: Node 26.13.0, pnpm 12.15.0, macOS arm64; frozen dependency inputs remained unchanged.
- Independent source review of the exact committed two-file range reported no P1/P2 findings. The test addition is disjoint from the related workflow-equivalence change in #199006.

Native review validation and preparation admitted the unchanged head under workflow `4a75d53968967449576105649f05d0adc701ffb4`, binding `e12e9580091c1bd1b42b4a6c91711ae264157ece`. Preparation used `github_pending`; this was not a hosted pass or final READY. The native review now records `tests.result=fail` and exact-head/run/attempt baseline attribution while preserving the local 10-pass proof and scope review.

- **Hosted failure:** supported draft [CI45090430568](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45090430568), attempt 1, completed with 32 successful jobs, 32 conditional skips and 2 failures. [Knip job137419141653](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45090430568/job/137419141653) failed all three reports; [CI gate137421483184](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45090430568/job/137421483184) failed consequently. Executed checkout and producer workflow source were exact `6ebc2947b2623d9ef730052d975eafe85e0e8e71`; the generated merge was only a diff/planning input.
- **Baseline reproduction:** one unmodified `6986a307262daa71ad0b5dbe294f82bf1edde12c` run of `pnpm deadcode:report` exited 1 in 91.619 seconds, without timeout or capture fault. Every scan/path/symbol signature matched: 7 script export/type findings, 19 production findings, and 52 full-tree findings plus the same 2 unused files; zero differences. Frozen install, scan/config and workflow inputs matched. Node 24.22.1, pnpm 12.15.0 and Knip 6.40.0 matched. S1 independently verified the comparison.
- **Evidence limits:** baseline execution used a private physical install on macOS arm64; hosted execution used Ubuntu 24.04.4 x64 / Blacksmith 4vCPU. This local reproduction is not a hosted baseline pass or CI exception. Baseline raw output SHA256: `f4b44a3d0919f4ef3b3d4788f3bf4b325ac17aca0cf0c64b0548d70df702c548`; complete comparison receipt SHA256: `b5b7d471151b488c86f36ba16e438ba4e34cb9d5a5c92bdc3e85d25a896639cc`.

The PR remains draft and is not final READY. Required hosted gates remain red; final native qualification and the standing no-deletion constraint remain unresolved. No hosted rerun, source or binding change, admission waiver, activation, deployment, merge, checkout deletion, installed-launcher patch, or retry of the original provider task is included.

prs.title: fix(update): show migration warnings from the configured database
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On PostgreSQL installations, `openclaw update status` reads migration warnings outside the database selection used for update history. Pending plugin migrations can disappear, while session migration warnings can remain visible after the underlying problem has been fixed.

## User Impact

Update status reports pending migrations from the configured database and suppresses resolved session warnings. If a warning source fails or stalls, the command still reports the other completed results. No configuration change or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Start all database-backed status readers inside the existing update database scope. Keep their results independent so a slow warning reader cannot discard completed history, recovery details, or another warning source. Warning formatting still uses the observed active-update state.

## Evidence

A real PostgreSQL regression failed on the original code: the pending plugin warning was absent and the resolved session warning remained. With this change, the same test passes, including read-only artifact checks and malformed-configuration handling.

Final commit `cb96c24a230e02606c77adbe049b97bb4eb20d8f`: 53 tests passed (7 real PostgreSQL updater conformance tests and 46 status, deadline, snapshot, and read-only tests). Core and affected test type checks, targeted lint, formatting with Bun parity, and `pnpm build` passed. Independent local autoreview found no actionable P0–P2 issue.

Proof ran on Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01m82vz3yptnk3zh0mqpn18g1w` ([run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45087436254)); the wrapper verified the source tree and completed with exit 0. The build reports UI asset-budget warnings; UI source and budget inputs are unchanged by this PR. No live installation was updated.

Coverage limit: the regression invokes the production status command in-process against PostgreSQL, not the shipped binary's argument parser. A latest-stable upgrade drill is outside this read-only diagnostic repair: installer, update execution, schema, and migration behavior are unchanged.

- PostgreSQL 17: `node scripts/test-database-conformance.mjs --engine postgres --connection <isolated-local-dsn> -- src/infra/database-engine/update-command.conformance.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`

## What Problem This Solves

In the macOS Dashboard, pressing ⌘K blanks the active Browser page even when most of it is still visible outside the palette. The tab itself stays open, but the user loses the page they were referring to.

## User Impact

The palette keeps a dimmed still of the Mac tab in place without letting the page take clicks or keyboard focus. Esc restores the same live tab without reopening or reloading it. The still is not a live preview; video and other hardware-rendered content may not appear in the WebKit snapshot.

## Why This Change Was Made

The native page sits above the web Dashboard, so leaving it live could cover the palette. Both the loading and loaded palette reuse the existing Mac-tab snapshot bridge and modal lifecycle, and the Browser pane discards the temporary still when the live view returns. Other overlays keep their existing behavior.

Reported and co-authored by @vyctorbrzezowski.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/314473bc-a104-4b4c-9328-3571091a7727)

## Evidence

- The production Control UI regression failed on the base at the missing backdrop, then passed with simulated Mac chrome and a fixture native bridge. It opens a tab from chat, presses ⌘K, checks palette focus and the inert still, and verifies that Esc restores the live presentation without opening another tab.
- All 73 focused unit tests and all 3 native-link browser tests passed. UI typecheck, targeted lint and formatting, and Solid ownership checks passed. The WebKit test runner timed out before executing its tests.
- Manual diff review covered the palette lifecycle, snapshot lifetime, and existing modal/menu behavior; no independent review result is claimed. Reusing the snapshot bridge avoids changes to the native app API.
- Native macOS verification is still pending. Chromium uses a simulated native bridge and does not verify real `WKWebView` capture or timing.

### Studio Chromium comparison

Same Dashboard session, viewport, and report fixture with the command palette open. The simulated native bridge returns the same report frame; the patch keeps it visible as an inert backdrop. Baseline `3d2e3a27fde2`; reviewed patch `7f4226894f9d`.

| ![The Browser pane is blank behind the command palette](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/60aef502-582c-4eb3-96a6-758ad4caba84) | ![The report is visible behind the command palette](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b3bde3bf-8ad0-405a-afa5-0ba315b9610c) |

Three bundled Chromium cases passed, including reopening the palette before the native presenter acknowledged the previous show request. The focused overlay tests also cover a plain modal taking precedence over the palette backdrop.

prs.title: fix: keep filesystem fixtures valid across fs-safe upgrades
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The fs-safe upgrade exposed filesystem fixtures that assumed synchronous reads and direct exclusive creation at the final lock name. These fixtures missed their intended fault or contention boundary after asynchronous admission and crash-safe staged publication, contributing to the full scheduled CI failure behind #194589.

Related: #194560, #194589.

## User Impact

Prepares the regression suite for the coordinator's fs-safe patch upgrade. This draft contains fixture changes only; dependency pins, lockfile, and runtime behavior are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep fault injection attached to the actual operation: recognize exclusive sibling stages, observe an existing lock for contention, model both metadata paths consistently, and inject read/cache conditions at the owning boundary. Synthetic volume statistics now preserve real bigint identities. Existing confinement, ownership, cleanup, FIFO, and error assertions remain intact.

The investigation also found two upstream regressions, fixed in openclaw/fs-safe#1079 and openclaw/fs-safe#1081. The non-9p preparation optimization is openclaw/fs-safe#1080. Those corrections are tested together here without landing the dependency bump.

## Evidence

- Reproduced the relevant failures with published fs-safe 0.27.1, 0.27.2, and 0.28.0. Async-read fixture differences begin at 0.27.2; staged-publication differences begin at 0.28.0. Adapted read cases also pass on 0.27.1.
- A local packed library containing all three upstream fixes, plus its matching native addon, passes all 16 originally failing test files: 280 tests passed, one Windows-only test skipped. This includes full lifecycle, migration, state-owner, build-ownership, capacity, workspace, sandbox, memory-read, prewarm, and affected tooling files.
- The real async FIFO swap still rejects. The explicit nonblocking flag contract is additionally covered upstream by `test/path-stress-regression.test.ts` and `test/pinned-open.test.ts`; both async and sync opens consume the shared flags in `src/pinned-open.ts`.
- Formatting, targeted typechecks/lint, test-line budget, and `git diff --check` pass. Net test growth is 40 lines, with an exact allocation; no new test cases were added.
- Independent isolated Codex P0–P2 review of the complete candidate against `f6a8ce9a6f2207121b7ffd5c6d65365fe1875d84` is clean. Review covers the supplied diff; runtime proof is the separate test execution above.
- Exact Windows execution remains a gap: the available remote provider rejected that target before provisioning. The Windows-only contender case must be covered by the full matrix before the actual re-bump lands.

Release-note context: test-only upgrade compatibility preparation; user-facing fs-safe fixes belong to the linked upstream changes.

### Full matrix required for the actual re-bump

Changed-scope PR CI is insufficient. The real manifest generator produces the same main matrices for a same-revision manual main-tier run and the schedule: 75 Node jobs, five Windows jobs, two macOS Node jobs, four Android jobs, plus the same UI/contracts/QA matrices, using the repository's configured hybrid backend.

On the canonical re-bump branch, after verifying its head:

```sh
branch='<canonical-rebump-branch>'
head=$(gh pr view <rebump-pr> -R openclaw/openclaw --json headRefOid --jq .headRefOid)
actual=$(gh api "repos/openclaw/openclaw/git/ref/heads/$branch" --jq .object.sha)
test "$actual" = "$head"
gh workflow run ci.yml -R openclaw/openclaw --ref "$branch" \
  -f target_ref="$head" -f validation_tier=main \
  -f test_runtime_policy=bun-all -f include_android=true
```

Use that branch as `--ref`; dispatching from `main` with a different target fails the same-revision guard. Bind results to the selected checkout SHA. No full-matrix workflow was dispatched as part of this fixture-only draft.

prs.title: improve(ui): Cmd+K lists named settings first and improves session search
prs.body:
Requested by @vyctorbrzezowski.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/1a5cfb8d-a446-47ff-bd14-38afb5b63bf2)

## What Problem This Solves

Searching for a setting in Cmd+K buries it below any session that mentions the same word, and archived sessions never show up at all.

## User Impact

User impact: typing a setting or command name in Cmd+K shows it first, sessions follow newest first, and archived sessions whose title matches appear in their own muted "Archived" group (at most three) instead of being missing.

## Why This Change Was Made

Results now follow intent instead of a single match score:

1. Settings and commands whose name matches the query.
2. Sessions: an exact match first, then newest first. Where a word falls inside a sentence-like session title no longer changes the order.
3. Archived: up to three archived sessions whose title matches, newest first, muted. A separate best-effort `sessions.list` call with `archived: true` and `searchTitlesOnly: true` supplies them. Live results appear without waiting for that lookup; a failed archive lookup only omits archived rows until the next search.
4. More results: commands, settings, plugins, skills and models that match only by description or keywords, in their own group so they cannot crowd the top.
5. In messages: transcript hits, unchanged.

Archived message text is still not searched; the existing palette note about that remains. The Sessions filter tab counts active and archived sessions together.

## Evidence

Scenario: query `appearance` with three active and two archived matching sessions. Control UI E2E harness with a mocked Gateway and fixture sessions, 1280×900, light theme. Before: `main` at 48cd549. After: this branch at 9ea31d4. Dark theme was also checked.

### Clean comparison

![Before: three sessions listed above the Appearance setting; no archived sessions](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9f1fa358-4627-468f-90ab-3a0fb754fe68)

![After: Appearance setting first, then three sessions, then two muted archived sessions](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7b5a5f1e-34b1-4bea-be7e-6c63547c0217)

### Annotated comparison

![Before, annotated: sessions listed first, Appearance setting after sessions](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d58bb8a9-97f9-4d4e-80ca-07311f83730e)

![After, annotated: named setting first; archived sessions in their own muted group](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d70d5675-01a1-4472-a732-399fb567690d)

Checks:

- Command palette unit suites: 146 tests passed, including new ordering and archived-group cases.
- `pnpm tsgo:ui`, oxlint on changed files and `pnpm lint:ui:styles` passed.
- Opening an archived result navigates to the session's existing archived view with its Unarchive action (verified in the same harness).
- Local autoreview (Codex, gpt-6.1-sol) on branch range 48cd549..9ea31d4 at P1: scoped-clean, no findings.

## Worked on by

- @vyctorbrzezowski

<!-- openclaw-publication:23ab8be0-c4c2-4026-8eae-5a05aa62cd83 -->

## Maintainer repair and verification

The repair in `8f1d76d648b` preserves this design and fixes three result-handling defects:

- A setting-name match stays ahead of description matches before the catalog's ten-result cap. The name-match flag is computed once per item.
- Available live results appear while archived search is pending. Later archived results preserve the item already selected with the keyboard.
- Archived title matching happens in the existing Gateway filter before pagination, so ten newer model/provider matches cannot hide an older matching title. The optional `sessions.list.searchTitlesOnly` parameter defaults to the existing search behavior. Query identity and the generated runtime validator include it. No database migration or saved-preference change is involved.

The two client regressions and the Gateway filtering regression failed before the repair. Validation covered 131 palette tests, 10 query-ownership tests and 7 Gateway filter tests; the four affected catalog cases and lint passed again after the final catalog cleanup. Core, UI and selected test typechecks passed, as did the official validator-generation check and an independent P0–P2 review.

A real isolated Gateway, built from the repaired sources, returned:

| Query | Page size | Total matches |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Existing broad search | 10 | 13 |
| Title-only search | 1 | 1 |
| Explicit `searchTitlesOnly: false` | 10 | 13 |

The title-only result was the intended older conversation. The first RPC attempt exposed the missing compiled validator in the repair; regenerating it with the official owner and rebuilding fixed that rejection. No provider or model execution was needed. Private-row exclusion was checked at the existing filter owner, not with a separate live private-identity RPC.

The captures below compare the original PR with the repair while the archive lookup is held, then show the completed results. They use the real Control UI with a scripted Gateway; the real RPC check above is separate. All data is synthetic.

![Original PR: live results wait for the archived lookup](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1630fa75-a482-4e41-bc2e-f42742185f97)

![Repaired: live results are available while archived search waits](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/46cfe305-cd68-46c5-8cb3-294d93b029b2)

![Repaired: archived results join without replacing the live results](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2a176ab0-a4fd-4b2a-9a14-fe3e103835ea)

prs.title: fix: stop PR CI watchers blocking on superseded security checks
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

PR CI watchers can reject an otherwise successful replacement run because a cancelled CodeQL matrix placeholder has a different name from its expanded jobs. This blocked #203197 on the stale Security High matrix placeholder.

## User Impact

Maintainers can wait for CI without treating a proven superseded cancellation as a current failure. Current failing or unfinished checks and incomplete evidence still block completion. No product configuration or runtime behavior changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Extend the existing run/suite replacement proof to cancelled checks outside the attached CI workflow. Require a newer completed, successful run, matching workflow and event, and exact PR/head/suite evidence for both runs. Reobserve the rollup after metadata reads and retain the existing bounded evidence budget. Old-run identities reuse the attachment cache across polls, while successor success is re-read each poll because reruns retain their run IDs. This preserves the existing 32-read bounded-progress contract. There is no check-name allowlist or blanket cancellation ignore.

## Evidence

- The production CLI replay failed on the base with exit 15 and the cancelled Security High matrix placeholder, then passed with the fix.
- All 16 focused CodeQL cases pass, including current failures, unresolved checks, incomplete rollups, running/failed replacements, and wrong PR/head/workflow/event/suite evidence.
- Remote review follow-up: 32/33 cancelled-run backlogs reproduced TIMEOUT on the first revision, then passed with persistent old-run identities. Negative regressions reject a successor that fails between polls and a deferred foreign-PR association; each poll remains bounded to 32 metadata reads.
- Script typecheck and focused test typecheck pass.
- All 251 tests in the three watcher suites pass (109.55s test duration; 110.34s wrapper wall time). The main suite contains subprocess/API-boundary, deadline, ownership, pagination and failure guards.
- Targeted script/test lint, formatting and git diff checks pass.
- Author simplification pass: reuse the existing replacement owner and bounded read budget; no name matching, new API, or alternate classifier. Production delta: +81/-16 lines; test delta: +128/-7 lines.

<details>
<summary>Validation commands</summary>

- node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run test/scripts/watch-pr-ci.test.ts test/scripts/watch-pr-ci-conditional.test.ts test/scripts/watch-pr-ci-dependencies.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
- node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.scripts.json --incremental
- Focused test typecheck extending test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.root.json with the touched test and normal declaration includes.
- node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.scripts.json scripts/watch-pr-ci.mts
- node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.root.scripts.json test/scripts/watch-pr-ci.test.ts
- node scripts/run-format.mts --check scripts/watch-pr-ci.mts test/scripts/watch-pr-ci.test.ts
- git diff --check

</details>

The historical PR is already merged; live run metadata confirms the old cancelled and newer successful CodeQL runs share the same workflow/head, but now omits PR associations. The regression uses synthetic exact-PR associations, and missing associations intentionally remain fail-closed.

prs.title: fix: seal release evidence with the admitted evaluator
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Full release validation can reject previously collected test evidence after an operator-approved waiver change. The immutable-plan step still evaluates child reuse with the qualification branch’s older policy code, even though the admitted publisher evaluator is already checked out and used for the final summary. This blocked the beta.2 reseal on the explicitly accepted Mac test cancellation.

## User Impact

Release operators can seal eligible retained evidence using the admitted policy evaluator. This is release-tooling only: it does not change the release candidate, waive additional failures, rewrite raw outcomes, or relax evidence/closure checks.

## Why This Change Was Made

Select the plan script from the same admitted publisher checkout and admission condition as the existing summary validator. Preserve the qualification checkout as the waiver-data owner and preserve the existing fallback when target resolution/admission is absent. No new policy owner or compatibility path is introduced.

## Evidence

- Recorded production incident: parent 45087316190/1, plan job 137416285104 rejects normal-CI reuse with “Full release child evidence workload does not pass recovery release policy.” Evaluating the same recorded Mac job and Q ledger rejects under old Q code and matches the exact cancellation grant under admitted P.
- Routing regression: 2 assertions fail on the base; all 14 workflow tests pass with the fix, covering successful admission and failed-resolution fallback.
- Focused sibling tests: 169/169 passed across continuation workflow, release no-push workflow, and child reuse.
- Targeted type-aware lint, formatting, and git diff checks passed. Initial shared-dependency setup was rejected; a frozen offline install inside the task-owned checkout resolved it without changing dependency versions.
- Independent read-only review of the entire two-file diff and direct owners: no P0–P2 findings; independently ran 14/14 routing tests. Canonical autoreview (OpenClaw, openai/gpt-6.1-sol, P0–P2) reviewed the local diff against 41b8e9f42614980cffd0282b9918201d9639b0da and returned scoped-clean; its context was limited to supplied diff excerpts, supplemented by the full-owner independent review.

The hosted reseal itself has not succeeded yet. This patch does not promise that a changed workflow preserves every child’s workload closure; normal evidence compatibility checks remain authoritative.

prs.title: fix: show earlier attachments in Session files
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Opening Files in a long chat could show only the recent uploads. A file shared at the beginning could be missing until someone scrolled back through the conversation.

## User Impact

Session files now includes older attachments without loading earlier chat pages. New uploads also appear while Files stays open, without waiting for the active run to finish. Files keep their native previews, and “Show in chat” goes to the source message. A partial-list notice remains when the Gateway really cannot supply the whole list.

## Why This Change Was Made

Files already requests the session’s artifacts. The Gateway collects attachment references in that same transcript pass and reuses its revision-aware cache. There is no new table, migration, history preload, or extra catalog request. A 4 MiB ceiling bounds the extra metadata; if it is reached, the panel retains both the collected references and attachments from the loaded chat. Older Gateways retain their existing fallback.

## Evidence

- Parity of the two SQLite artifact reads: the same admitted attachment IDs and sequence numbers survive both cached metadata and include-download queries. The fixture fails with the old visitor and passes with the repair; 22 Gateway tests and nine focused UI checks passed. Both import-cycle guards report zero cycles.
- The production asset check passes on the repaired candidate 33712df50015. In the paired build, Chat used the same 21 requests and stayed below the JavaScript gzip cap. Six Files browser checks also passed with the shared deduplication rule.

- In Chromium, with the same paginated chat fixture, the original project brief was missing on `abd8b92cfa` and present on `b63c38fb27`. Both versions made one catalog request. This verifies the Control UI, not a native macOS run.
- 58 focused UI tests, the real Gateway integration test, core and UI type checks, and the UI production build passed. The build reported advisory bundle-budget overages; no budgets were raised.
- In a local synthetic session with 1,204 messages and 27 messages carrying attachments, the catalog RPC took 13.9 ms on the first request after appending history, then 3.7 and 2.6 ms. The response was 6,469 bytes. These are local observations, not a production latency guarantee.

### Live upload while Files stays open

Both captures show the same Chromium fixture after a PDF arrived in chat during an active run. On the previous PR head the panel stays stale; on the repaired head it shows the new upload once, keeps the earlier files, and still makes only one catalog request.

| Previous PR head | Live update |

| ![The new upload is already in chat but Files still lists two files](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/48c0be91-1319-4973-9043-766407c077d2) | ![Revised diagrams.pdf appears alongside the two older files](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/65f38e2e-5bfa-4074-8cc3-eae34ae1a2b6) |

- Both complete and capped catalog regressions failed before the repair. The repaired code passes 53 focused UI tests, 33 Gateway artifact tests, UI type checking, and changed-file lint.
- Chromium also opened a catalog-only image in the native lightbox through the mocked artifact download, then fetched the older chat page on “Show in chat” and displayed the source. The grid action stayed inside its tile. These are Control UI interactions against a fixture Gateway, not a native macOS run.
- The local UI bundle comparison passes with no additional raw or gzipped CSS versus the PR base. No budget changed. The local independent review helper did not start with the worktree-scoped temporary directory; this follow-up does not claim a fresh automated review.

prs.title: fix: name the agent when a followed-up child finishes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a parent chat sends a follow-up message to one of its child sessions, the "finished" notice for that follow-up run says "An agent finished" instead of the child's name. The child session already has a name (for example "Cross-thread message summaries and video proof"), so readers can't tell which agent finished.

## User Impact

User impact: completion notices for follow-up runs now show the child session's name, the same way the first run's notice does.

## Why This Change Was Made

The completion notice takes its name from the run record. The first run gets the spawn label, but a follow-up run sent with `sessions_send` was registered without one, so the UI fell back to its generic "An agent" text. The follow-up registration now copies the child session's current label onto the new run. Steered follow-ups already reuse the existing run and its label, so they are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Regression test: the existing watched-child follow-up test now gives the child session a label and asserts that the follow-up run record carries it. It fails without the fix (`label: undefined`) and passes with it.
- Focused sibling tests pass: the raw-entry registry suite (15 tests), plus the `sessions_send` follow-up and owner-continuation suites (14 tests).
- Live symptom: a Team session showed "An agent finished" for a follow-up run of a labeled child session. Its completion receipt had the child's session key but no label.

Requested by @vyctorbrzezowski.

prs.title: fix(pr): retain equivalent reviewed workflows for baseline proof
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Initial baseline-proof preparation rejects a retained reviewed workflow whenever main advances, even when the complete workflow, dependency and policy inputs remain equivalent. This change admits that case without relaxing later publication or merge gates.

## User Impact

Maintainers can reuse an equivalent reviewed workflow for initial baseline proof while preserving authenticated ancestry, source identity, signed evidence and custody. This is maintainer tooling; it does not change the runtime product. No measured speedup or resolution of the macOS test deadlines is claimed.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Authenticate current main and compare complete workflow inventories, file types/modes, dependency/install inputs and runtime policy. Carry provenance through native context and signed baseline bindings. Reuse same-commit facts only within each check; preserve fresh admission boundaries.
- Validate custody and preparation inputs before retiring active evidence. Preserve pending-proof acceptance retirement and qualified-baseline rejection. Keep the selected workflow's dependency revision independent of bootstrap, including creator reentry and unbound commands.
- Integrate frozen main `181656c5749804e8584af726d67eebdecaf017a7`, preserving verified-bootstrap completion and expansion order alongside workflow proof verification. Retain main's native Git captured-byte stdin hashing, `--no-filters`, conditional object writes and no-spill ownership. The proposed descriptor batching was removed. Replay, signatures and FD7/8/9 custody retain their existing owners.
- Keep the private fixture adapter's fresh ordered ref reads and remove both the standalone adapter-only suite and lifecycle query-count instrumentation. The final cleanup removes 73 test lines while preserving all 27 native calls, publication/replay outcomes, signed OIDs, receipt bytes and transport-authority refusals.
- Exercise historical six-field signed-proof records through current native consumers, with the optional field absent before signing. Preserve binding/signature identity, retained bytes and tamper refusals. This qualifies a historical format through current code, not an old released binary. Correct operation-scoped archive assertions, custody injection and the creator-reentry FD9 oracle without weakening assertions or deadlines.

The authored difference from frozen main is **21 files**: production **+740/-329 (net +411)**, tests **+1201/-237**, docs **+28/-5**, inventory **+17**, and a three-line allocation record. Production growth owns workflow equivalence, sealed provenance, validation before retirement and consolidated dependency/materialization accounting. The native staged test-line ratchet passed: **945 eligible net lines = 400 allowance + 545 allocation**, with no extra credit. The separate `.mjs` fixture explains the difference from test numstat. Allocation does not waive proof or review.

## Evidence

Current commit: `fdd9ab4aee15fbbfe307be55940311784edfc4a4`; tree `853ccaef3f39e4c4c57b6d7f97ac207186352a7f`; parent `6dd41479d11142b3f213fd4cc1c4e26c7cf56c12`. The signed one-line backport matches merged [PR #202401](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202401): remove only `export` from the internal Gateway token issuer. Its body, public preparation/completion, tests and dependency inputs are unchanged. Independent scoped review accepted the exact patch; normal hooks and signature verification passed.

[Dual-runtime CI 44924189700](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44924189700) completed **SUCCESS on 2026-11-21 at 16:59:36 UTC: 41 successful jobs, zero failed, 31 skipped**. Comparison base `a81218e17a0bed096972ea4b47de9eba62fb72fd` and synthetic merge ref `4cfe58c7117ff31bc39923906973f89bace832db` are CI comparison inputs, not new source integration. Preflight verified maintainer qualification, release validation and `dual-all`. Logs show **Linux x64, Node 24.22.1, Bun 1.4.4-canary.1+191755ec1 and Vitest 5.0.5**. Preflight log SHA-256: `0cb6da373dacd1539116f5fcf23036279bea6f162dc1994244ef6b2d1c7367b1`.

| Current-head selected file | Node | Bun |
| --- | ---: | ---: |

The six failures were signing **152.394s**, successor **191.389s**, incoming-source **215.894s**, ordinary replay **206.336s**, historical replay **185.716s**, and workflow publication **134.859s**, all against 120s. Selections overlap and are not added together. Linux/Bun passes do not establish the macOS cause or a cross-host speedup. Instrumented, interrupted and timed-out runs are not clean proof.

A later diagnostic at the current `fdd9ab4a` source measured the same baseline-successor publication scenario at **144.579s**, still failing the unchanged **120s** test deadline. prs.title: refactor(agents): delete the scheduled owner-only receipt re-check
prs.body:
## Problem

R1c of the one-admission receipt cluster. #203664 (R1) found that the receipt boolean (`receiptAuthority: () => boolean | void`, the `composeReceiptAuthority` loop, `assertAllowed` in `captureGatewayToolReceiptAssertion`) could not be deleted yet. Some receipt producers return `false` for run checks. One receipt re-checks a permission in the middle of a call.

## Change

- **Scheduled owner-only tools (`scheduled-owner-tool-guard.ts`):** the receipt was `assertOwnerCurrent`, which re-checks the requester's owner status at every dispatch and commit inside a call. That is a permission-only re-check in the middle of a call, so the receipt is **deleted**. The owner check before each call stays. A started call finishes, and Stop still cancels it.

Production: 1 file, +2/−22. No new export, name, hook, flag, guard, timer or state.

## Producer classification

Test: can the answer change when only a permission, approval or config changes, with no change to session data? Yes → authority (delete). No → data fence or Stop.

| Producer | Check | Class | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| `scheduled-owner-tool-guard.ts` `assertOwnerCurrent` | owner status | Authority | **Receipt deleted** |
| `mcp-http.ts` `isGrantAndLineageCurrent` | grant row identity and completion lineage | Run instance | Still returns a boolean. See "Blocked" |
| `agent-tools.caller.ts` `settleBatch.isCurrent` | settle batch occurrence | Run occurrence | Still returns a boolean. See "Blocked" |
| `createAdmittedGatewayToolCallerIdentity` with no delegated authority | `() => false` | Missing run | Still returns a boolean. Internal constant |
| cron automation invocation (`createAutomationRunGuard`) | invocation close, run context, claims | Run occurrence | Already throws. Not changed |
| node skill runtime `assertCurrent` | claim loss, disconnect, placement, session | Data and run occurrence | Already throws, and the claim and disconnect handlers abort its signal. Not changed |
| `host-capability.ts`, `trigger-script.ts`, worker-environment sources, `plugin-command-scheduled-run.ts` | run instance, Gateway binding, worker claim | Data and run occurrence | Already throw. Not changed |
| `tool-authority.runtime.ts` `assertReplyActive`, `plugin-native-subagent.ts` `assertCurrent` | run checks plus `operatorAuthority.assertCurrent()` | Mixed | Already throw. The operator re-check belongs to the operator source work (R1b and later) |

## Blocked: converting the boolean producers (cut less)

The first head of this PR (`7d6d7bae0873`) changed the MCP and settle-batch producers to throw ("agent tool caller authority is no longer active"). CI turned two ratchets red on exactly those lines:
- `check-session-identity-ratchet`: `agent-tools.caller.ts 1 > 0`, `mcp-http.ts 1 > 0` (do not refuse with a "no longer active" message);
- `check-lifetime-check-ratchet`: `+1` in each file (do not add a re-check in the middle of a request).

The ratchets are right. A throwing producer is a new re-check in the middle of a request; the boolean producers were the same re-check, but hidden from the ratchet. So these producers must be **deleted**, not converted. Deleting them conflicts with tests that this task said must stay green and unedited:
- `mcp-http.test.ts` "fences caller authority when the grant is replaced during tool execution" requires `receiptAuthority()` to stop returning `true` after the grant row is replaced in the middle of a call.
- `settleBatch.isCurrent` reaches the tools' commit only through the receipt.

I reverted both conversions and kept the clean deletion. **Next PR (R2):** delete the MCP and settle-batch receipts, delete or rewrite the MCP "grant replaced" test as obsolete (it asserts a re-check in the middle of a call), then delete the boolean. A draft of the boolean removal (17 production files, +61/−183, plus about 45 test fixtures that return `false`) is kept with the task proof.

## What users see

An owner-only tool call that was already running when owner status was revoked now finishes. Before, it was refused at its commit. The next call is still refused before it starts.

## Evidence

Exact head `e219a4ca880c` (production diff against the merge base: `scheduled-owner-tool-guard.ts` only):

- **Local ClawSweeper review:** `review_status: complete`, "patch is correct", 0 findings (report `e219a4ca880c.md`).
- **One-admission E2E** (isolated Gateway, real model, exact head): `pass: true`. `results.jsonl` is kept with the task proof. `verdict.json`:
  ```json
  {"pass":true,"checks":[{"id":"R.running-turn-finishes","pass":true,"detail":{"state":"final","toolEnds":3,"toolEndsAfterRevoke":3}},{"id":"Q.queued-input-refused-visibly","pass":true,"detail":{"accepted":true,"providerRequestsWithQueuedMarker":0,"visibleRefusalInTranscript":true}},{"id":"S.stop-cancels","pass":true,"detail":{"abort":{"ok":true,"aborted":true},"state":"aborted","requestsWithStopMarker":1}}]}
  ```
- **Typecheck / lint / ratchets:** `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:test` clean. oxfmt and oxlint clean. Session-identity and lifetime-check ratchets OK locally on this head.
- **Tests:** one `ocx test` call on 114 files (importers of every file the first head changed, plus owner-tool, settle-batch and node skill-runtime tests). Only the known main red `mcp-http.async-scope.test.ts` failed. After the revert, a second call on the 15 importers of the two reverted files, the owner-tool tests and the two named tests (`mcp-http.test.ts`, `node-claude-skill-runtime.test.ts`) was green.

prs.title: fix(agents): release deleted agents’ catalog contexts
prs.body:
## Current State

The published PR remains the regression-only, expected-red baseline at `8306012fc822d15da843a843ef7602099e4b46c9`. Its expected failure has **not yet been observed**.

The implementation is complete in the signed local candidate `faa393eaaec0226eaaab47d84a32da861de5d29f` (tree `e01f9e0cf15f796fba4756a8f47ceb4d9f35a7d2`). That candidate is **unpublished and has not run runtime validation**. Independent committed-range review completed with no P0–P2 findings; this is source review, not execution proof. The candidate covers exact agent/directory retirement, shared contexts, active cleanup, credential receipts, and compact-input dispatch ordering.

Native exact-head CI dispatch is blocked by contention on the shared PR dependency-cache metadata lock. Dispatch stopped before creating a GitHub run. No lock or competing process was changed, and no retry is scheduled. The pending sequence is baseline reproduction, then candidate publication and affected runtime, lint, type, build, and CI proof.

## What Problem This Solves

This draft establishes a regression for catalog contexts retained after an agent is deleted. The shared catalog worker can keep a workspace context after the parent runtime owner and database readers have retired.

## User Impact

The intended repair releases a deleted agent's unused catalog context while keeping another agent's shared workspace and worker usable. This initial commit contains only regression coverage; it does not implement that repair or claim RSS savings.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing integration fixture exercises real runtime retirement, database-reader closure, and survivor access. It now covers shared and distinct workspaces and observes the worker's owned `catalog-index` context count.

The expected baseline failure is specific: two distinct workspace contexts are loaded, deletion completes, and the count remains two instead of falling to one. The shared-workspace control must retain its one context and the same worker. Missing sampler data, catalog setup failures, or database-lock failures would be fixture failures, not confirmation of the retention defect.

## Evidence

- Frozen source baseline: `1692cb83f791512bb33ac6d7273689f0a3355989`.
- Regression-only head: `8306012fc822d15da843a843ef7602099e4b46c9`.
- Baseline source review: independently reviewed the real deletion path and both fixture cases; its production code is unchanged. The unpublished candidate also completed independent source review, with execution evidence still pending.
- Local validation: `git diff --check` and the repository commit-hook formatter passed. Focused runtime tests, lint, types, and build have not run.
- Proof route: local task dependencies are unqualified. The documented draft-PR exact-head CI route remains pending the native metadata contention described above; no runtime test result is claimed.
- Published baseline delta: net +17 test lines; production delta: 0. The unpublished candidate has net +244 production lines for cross-thread context ownership and cleanup, and +419 test/fixture lines. Its required 19-line test allocation covers the additional shared-worker dispatch and lifecycle regressions. No GC, RSS, latency, or performance acceptance result yet.

This one draft will carry the owner-level repair after the baseline failure is captured. It is not ready to merge.

Candidate acceptance is fixed before execution: distinct owned contexts must fall from two to one after deletion; a shared workspace must retain one context; the survivor must keep working on the same worker. Existing alternating-workspace coverage must still show one worker, two retained registrations/callbacks, and exactly one initial metadata transfer per workspace. Active retirement must join targeted cleanup, preserve committed credential receipts, and prevent late publication without waiting for an unrelated workspace's active task. These are ownership and direct-work checks, not RSS or latency claims.

prs.title: fix(browser): report crashed tabs as tab-scoped failures
prs.body:
Closes #194667

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the browser tool reports a crashed tab as a generic 20 s timeout and tells the agent the whole browser is unavailable, even though the browser and its other tabs keep working. `navigate` on a crashed target waits the full request budget, and the tab list gives no hint that the target is dead.

## User Impact

User impact: a crashed tab now fails fast with tab-scoped guidance to open the page in a new tab (or retry once a busy page settles), instead of steering the agent into browser-wide troubleshooting. `snapshot`, `screenshot`, and `navigate` all take that path; `tabs` marks targets observed as crashed in both the JSON payload and the CLI text output, and implicit tab selection prefers a healthy tab. Existing-session and extension-relay drivers keep their current behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

A crashed renderer leaves its Chrome target listed while every page-level CDP command stalls. Snapshots waited out the full action budget and then attached the browser-wide unavailability hint, and `navigate` timed out the same way. The fix adds one bounded `Page.getFrameTree` liveness probe before snapshot and navigate work, maps Playwright `Target crashed` errors to a 409 with tab-scoped recovery text, and keeps the observed crash on the tab record for listing, the CLI handle list, and implicit selection. A dead renderer and a long-blocked main thread look the same to that probe, so the wording names both and suggests a retry once the page settles. Snapshot media helpers moved to a sibling module to stay under the file line cap.

## Evidence

- Targeted suite: `pnpm test extensions/browser/src/browser/cdp-liveness.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/target-crash.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/tabs.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/agent.snapshot.local-managed.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/client-fetch.loopback-auth.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/server-context.selection.crash.test.ts` — 6 files, 93 tests passed.
- Real renderer crash (gated Chromium test, system Chrome): `OPENCLAW_BROWSER_CRASH_E2E=1 PLAYWRIGHT_CHROMIUM_EXECUTABLE_PATH=... pnpm test extensions/browser/src/browser/cdp-liveness.chromium.test.ts` — `Page.crash` then probe rejects with `BrowserTargetCrashedError` inside the bounded probe window.
- Real crash-frame shape on `79e875aabfa`: the same gated test crashes a renderer and asserts the message Playwright itself produces for a screenshot on the dead tab. Measured locally, the first line is `page.screenshot: Target crashed ` (trailing space) followed by a `Call log:` block; the matcher accepts the headline, the typed error is returned, and reverting only `target-crash.ts` makes 2/7 `target-crash.test.ts` cases and 1/23 `client-fetch.loopback-auth.test.ts` cases fail.
- Shipped Gateway + CLI proof on `4b9f8291e0d` (isolated state dir, local loopback only, no real credentials; headless system Chrome 157; local HTTP fixture; the target was crashed with CDP `Page.crash`, then observed through the normal CLI entry point):
  - `openclaw browser navigate http://127.0.0.1:18080/crashme.html --target-id crashme` — fails fast (~2 s) with `The tab crashed or stopped responding. The browser and other tabs are still available: open the page again in a new tab, or retry this target once the page settles.` instead of waiting out the request budget.
  - `openclaw browser tabs` — `2. crashme [crashed use: crashme tab: t1 label:crashme]`; the healthy tab stays listed unchanged (`1. healthy [use: healthy tab: t2 label:healthy]`).
  - `openclaw browser screenshot crashme` — same tab-scoped crash error before Playwright reports its own `Target crashed` frame; `openclaw browser screenshot healthy` still writes `$OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR/state/media/browser/<uuid>.png`.
  - Recovery: `openclaw browser open http://127.0.0.1:18080/crashme.html --label recovered` then `openclaw browser snapshot --target-id recovered` returns the page's AX tree (`RootWebArea "crashme"` / `heading "crash target"`).
- Independent live check by @wr-web (`Page.crash` + CLI on Windows) confirmed snapshot/screenshot on `906d205`; their navigate and tab-list findings are wired in `76b7e18520f` and `905b07cae7b`.
- Base behavior reproduced locally: after `Page.crash`, the listed page's WebSocket accepts connections but `Page.getFrameTree`, `Runtime.evaluate`, and `Accessibility.getFullAXTree` never answer; a healthy page answers in milliseconds.
- Ratchet and suite on the merged tree (`52c81a6a2b1`, merges `origin/main` `bd9166435e9`): the only conflict was the import block in `agent.snapshot.ts`, where upstream added `resolveProfileHeadless` while this branch moved the media helpers to `agent.snapshot-media.ts`; the resolution keeps upstream's `headless` wiring and this branch's helper extraction. `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet` reports `Test lines OK. Net test lines: +395; allowance: 400; allocation credit: 350`. Full browser project suite (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-browser.config.ts`) passes 257 files / 3091 tests with 127 skipped; `pnpm tsgo:extensions` and `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` pass, oxlint reports 0 problems on the 21 changed files, and `pnpm format:check` is clean.
- Gap: the live check drives the shipped CLI routes but not a full agent model turn; request-boundary behavior stays covered by the route tests.

prs.title: fix: keep approval history in place while revoking a standing grant
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

In Approvals, clicking Revoke changed the button label to “Revoking…”. On a phone, the wider button could force the command onto another line and push the approval history down while the request was still pending.

## User Impact

The grant and history stay in place while a revocation is pending or becomes available to retry. The button still tells you what it is doing.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reserve enough space for the wider of the two translated button labels. This changes only the layout; the request, permissions and retry behavior are unchanged.

## Evidence

Before the fix, the button widened by 19 px and the phone history moved down by 17 px. After the fix, the command wraps in the idle state and the history stays put during the request. A simulated rejection and retry also preserved the expanded history entry. The layout was checked on phone, portrait tablet, landscape tablet and desktop; no real grants were revoked or commands run.

The first comparison row shows **Revoke**; the second shows **Revoking…** for the same synthetic grant. Mounted Control UI, 390 × 844 emulated phone. Comparison: stock main `da13d2a9c3023` and local repair `321ebebc04ac7`.

### Clean comparison

|---|---|

prs.title: fix: keep app domains compact in the Logbook day summary
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

In Logbook’s day summary, a long app domain broke in the middle of a word and made its chip twice as tall as a short domain. Two similar domains took four lines in the narrow summary column.

## User Impact

Each domain now takes one line. When space is tight, an ellipsis replaces the beginning, so endings such as **museum.example** and **gallery.example** still distinguish the entries. The complete domain remains in the text for assistive technology and in the hover title. Short domains keep their previous appearance.

## Why This Change Was Made

The day summary is for scanning, not a list of destinations. The chips remain plain labels; no new action or domain lookup is needed.

## Evidence

The screenshots show the same populated **Day at a glance** card in a simulated 1180 × 820 viewport, comparing the previous PR head `0256179781632` with `5dfc0c93aca8d`. Both long chips went from 38 px to 21 px, matching the short chip. The same change was verified at 1440 × 900. At 390 × 844 and 820 × 1180 both full domains already fit and remained on one line. At all four sizes, opening a timeline card, navigating to an empty day, and returning restored the correct summary. The focused bundled Chromium regression also passed. Synthetic Logbook data only; no device capture or analysis was started.

The original [overflow comparison](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b36a0eee-d351-44cd-af58-639f55fca3e0) and [previous wrapping version](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e86ce07a-ed79-4431-80ad-9aeacd12bc08) are preserved for reference.

prs.title: fix: show the New agent role choices when Custodian’s reply arrives
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Choosing **New agent** from Agents could leave Custodian showing an earlier conversation instead of the list of roles it had just offered. Custodian scrolled to the new reply while it was still empty, before the list had a height.

## User Impact

When the welcome reply arrives, you can read the role choices above the composer without scrolling past old messages. If you scroll back to read an earlier message and type a draft, the view stays where you put it.

## Why This Change Was Made

Custodian waits until the next layout frame to bring the latest message into view. A new message triggers the scroll; editing the draft or updating status does not. This changes where the conversation scrolls, not how agents are proposed or created.

## Evidence

With the same conversation on a 390 px phone, three of six roles were fully visible at default text size and none at 140%. After the fix, all six were visible at both sizes. The existing phone screenshots show the completed reply at 140%. Across four viewports, two text sizes, and three history lengths, all six roles fit on arrival in 24 of 24 cases, up from 11 of 24.

The focused browser regression failed on the baseline and passed with the fix. It also checked that typing an unsent draft did not move someone who had scrolled back. The plugin-help and agent-create component tests and phone and compact-panel browser tests passed. All replies were synthetic; no agent was created. Stock main: `450441b904031`. Atlas repair: `ba53bef861ebb`.

### Clean comparison

| Before | After |
|---|---|

prs.title: ci: inventory retained native worker lifecycles
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The runtime lifecycle inventory omits the native worker supervisor and two worker entrypoints that hold resources through it. Maintainers need to see which owner starts those workers and when it releases them.

## User Impact

CI's lifecycle registry now records the four existing launch modes and their cleanup owners.

## Why This Change Was Made

The native worker supervisor starts on first use. Its default source joins at runtime cleanup, and a retained generation joins its supervisor before releasing the captured runtime. The same registry now tracks cleanup for plugin preparation and SQLite snapshot staging.

The lean admission ledger has executable-level heap estimates for the supervisor and plugin preparation. Per-mode heap expectations are still unmeasured, so the registry uses its supported unknown value.

## Evidence

A focused source check verified four modes on three unchanged manifest entrypoints, all owner paths, and preservation of the existing declarations. Scoped autoreview with the owning implementations found no actionable P0–P2 issues. The patch adds 30 registry lines. Hosted CI passed the runtime-process lifecycle ratchet and the full PR gate. CodeQL passed on the same head.

prs.title: fix: tell the agent to answer in plain text when Telegram refuses a widget
prs.body:
Closes #200761

## What Problem This Solves

With Telegram widgets turned on, the agent builds an interactive card and calls `show_widget`. The production Telegram Bot API can refuse that send with `INPUT_MEDIA_WIDGET_NOT_ALLOWED`, even in a private chat. OpenClaw passed the raw error back as a generic `presentation_error`, the same code it uses for card problems the agent can fix. The agent then had to guess whether editing the card or retrying would help, and the user got no card and no answer.

## User Impact

User impact: when Telegram refuses a widget, the agent is told that retrying or editing the card will not help and to answer the current request in plain text, so the user gets a reply instead of a dead end. The `widgets` setting is not changed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Telegram widget presenter now recognizes `INPUT_MEDIA_WIDGET_NOT_ALLOWED` in the delivery error. It keeps the Telegram error text in the tool result and adds one sentence with the plain-text instruction. Every other delivery failure returns the same message as before. The Telegram rich messages doc has a new "Refused delivery" note.

## Evidence

I added two tests in `extensions/telegram/src/widgets/widget-presenter.test.ts`. One checks that a refused send keeps `INPUT_MEDIA_WIDGET_NOT_ALLOWED` and tells the agent to answer in plain text. The other checks that an unrelated delivery error gets no plain-text advice.

Not run here: the tests, typecheck and lint. The sandbox this change was written in could not install dependencies, so CI is the first run of them. I also did not exercise the refusal against the live Telegram Bot API.

<details>
<summary>Commands for the reviewer</summary>

```
pnpm test extensions/telegram/src/widgets/widget-presenter.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/widgets/widget-send.test.ts src/canvas/widget-tool.test.ts
pnpm tsgo:extensions
pnpm lint:extensions
```

</details>

prs.title: fix: show why a chat’s desktop is unavailable next to Retry
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a chat’s assigned desktop was unavailable, the Desktop panel put **Retry** far from the explanation. If checking for that desktop failed, the panel said **Desktop disconnected** and showed connection controls even though it had not found a device.

## User Impact

The reason and **Retry** now appear together. Retry checks whether the assigned desktop is available before showing connection controls. You can cancel a pending check with **Disconnect**; a late reply won’t reconnect you without an explicit **Reconnect**.

## Why This Change Was Made

Checking for a desktop is different from connecting to one. The panel now shows the status and action for the step it is actually performing. The same button retains keyboard focus while the check runs or fails.

## Evidence

The existing phone screenshots show an unavailable desktop and a failed retry. Across the phone, both tablets, and desktop, the gap between the reason and Retry went from 132–416 px to 16 px. Touch targets were at least 44 px tall. All 40 focused Desktop tests passed on the isolated patch, including failure, cancellation, and explicit reconnection. prs.title: feat(ios): prototype device-local native chat text sizing
prs.body:
Related: #170428

## What Problem This Solves

Native iOS chat has no in-app text-size control. The embedded Dashboard's Appearance picker controls a separate web surface.

## User Impact

**Draft design prototype.** Chat Actions gains a native **Chat text size** sheet with Smaller, Default, and Larger choices. The implementation stores the choice with the existing appearance owner; reload was verified in the simulator. The chat transcript and UIKit composer follow a relative normal Dynamic Type step; Default retains today's sizing, and system accessibility sizes take priority.

These are relative system type steps, not Android's percentage presets. The preference applies to native chat rather than the app's navigation toolbar.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing AppAppearanceModel owns the persisted selection. Native chat receives the resulting Dynamic Type size, and the existing UIKit composer follows that size without replacing the focused editor. No Gateway setting, shared bridge schema, or dependency is added.

**iOS design decision requested:** Is a native Chat Actions text-size sheet an acceptable first increment, or should this wait for the existing Appearance picker to bridge into native typography? Coordinate with #191524's local-device-settings work. This prototype does not fix the embedded web picker's persistence or claim to complete #170428.

## Evidence

- Updated draft head `680981e11a57` integrates `main` at `80e233cdf6e6`. The merge preserves main’s Chat Actions changes and regenerates the native localization inventory.
- **23 focused iOS simulator tests passed** on iOS 27.0, covering persistence in a fresh appearance owner, system accessibility size precedence, native typography, and Smaller/Larger resizing without replacing the focused editor or losing its cursor and draft.
- Removed the explicit UIKit font refresh after repeating the focused-editor test with the original text-view implementation. The full focused suite passed again after removal.
- A separate app UI test opened Chat Actions → Chat text size, verified Default on a fresh simulator, selected Larger, and confirmed it stayed selected after relaunch. Synthetic captures show the transcript resizing and the persisted selection.
- Changed-file SwiftFormat, strict SwiftLint, native localization verification, and `git diff --check` passed.

- **Stable-source upgrade passed on an iOS 27.0 simulator.** Installed a Debug build of published stable [v2026.11.6](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/releases/tag/v2026.11.6) (`06afb10d3272`) and seeded Dark through its appearance launch option with the simulator set to Light. Installed the exact draft head over the stable build using the same bundle ID. The Dark preference was present before the first candidate launch, native chat rendered in Dark after launch, and the new text-size preference remained unset. Only the stable generated Xcode project's lint phase was disabled for this run because the stable demo transport hit an existing function-length lint error. The stable source was used as published.

- **Physical iPhone Duo persistence passed.** Selected Larger in the native Chat text size sheet on the development-signed build of this head. Confirmed the stored value was `larger` before and after terminating and relaunching the app into the synthetic native chat.

- **Physical iPhone Duo VoiceOver check passed with Larger selected.** With system VoiceOver enabled in the signed test app, focusing a synthetic chat reply read the reply aloud and focusing the composer announced “message field.”

The draft still needs the iOS design decision.

The change reuses the appearance and Chat Actions owners; no parallel settings bridge or browser-storage policy is introduced.

prs.title: fix(update): convert package installs on hosts without a systemd user bus
prs.body:
Related: #203735

## What Problem This Solves

The first update of an npm, pnpm, or Bun global install can fail on Linux when no Gateway service is installed and the systemd user bus is unavailable. Containers, WSL without systemd, and Gateways started by hand or by another supervisor should not need a systemd session to prepare an update.

## User Impact

These installs can prepare their next release without a service manager. A detected installed unit still requires effective inspection and retains the existing session-repair instructions when the bus is unavailable. No flags, retries, states, or service-reader behavior change.

## Why This Change Was Made

`src/update/convert-service.ts:23` requested `readCommand(..., { requireEffective: true })` before checking whether there was a definition to rebind. The systemd reader deliberately queries the manager even without a local base file because global and loaded fragments can exist (`src/daemon/systemd-service-files.ts:578-590,657-675`; introduced by #129170). Changing that reader would break valid inspection.

Conversion now consumes the existing `hasInstalledDefinition` operation before requesting the effective command. Only this conversion caller changes; status, install/uninstall, Doctor, lifecycle, node-service inspection, and update admission retain their existing discovery and refusal behavior. Production delta: +3 lines. Tests: +53/-2 lines.

Accepted edge case: the existing Linux definition probe scans `~/.config/systemd/user` (current/legacy profile or explicit unit identity), `/etc/systemd/system`, `/usr/lib/systemd/system`, `/lib/systemd/system`, and marker-owned system units in those system directories. The manager reader can also load global user fragments such as `/etc/systemd/user` and alternate XDG/runtime/custom load paths. This PR does not expand shared discovery. An undetected unit is not rewritten: its standard old package entry still reaches the launcher after `markForwarding` writes `.openclaw-launcher` (`src/update/run.ts:365,416-426`). Both `openclaw.mjs` and `src/index.ts:35-40` use `release-launcher-forward.mjs:13-41`, which reads that marker and imports the resident launcher. This is the same retained-entry route used by system-owned definitions and the documented next-start contract (`docs/install/updating.md:31-41`).

## Evidence

- Base `42f8c5bcb9f51973338a3d26c0e75fe7c6be65d7`: focused regression fails with `systemd-user-bus-unavailable` for no unit/no bus; the installed-unit refusal passes. This used the real Linux service adapter and native-command failure fixture, not a mocked presence answer.
- Green (vitest-source): one `ocx test` call passed all 261 tests in 10 files, including conversion, package preparation, and the existing systemd reader/transport/mutation suites (165.95s runner time). Conversion file: 4 tests, 8.47s wall; absent-unit case 23ms, installed-unit refusal 14ms. CI time is not yet available.
- `pnpm check:changed`: core/test typechecks, touched-file lint/format, and the other guards passed. The command exits 1 on its repository-wide Knip dead-export scan in untouched CLI/cron/gateway/update files (including `LAUNCHER_FORMAT`, `InstallKind`, and old update-CLI test helpers). This PR changes none of those exports.
- Full candidate build (`ocx build --dts`) passed: build phase 389s, followed by canonical packing and tarball integrity/import-graph checks (48s checker). Build emitted unrelated Control UI asset-budget warnings.
- Linux proof candidate is local merge `121bbb9a73aca806edfc8dc0f0efd1ff336ef39a`, containing PR head `e6ef2df3aa04ec10d4bfb274ac4d6ca71b2964ef` plus `main` at `58a3c7e9a8f2bd47369edd7a3af68df122ecf5c3` (#203735); the proof merge is not pushed. Tarball SHA-256: `65884047f686abcc53b22c52adfecaf9fc716d525386de618426c697aacf01f9`.
- **Linux next-start proof PASS** on OrbStack Docker 29.8.2, Linux arm64, Node 24.22.1, uid 1001. A clean npm global install had no Gateway unit, no `busctl`/`systemctl`, no systemd boot, and no user bus. `update --tag file:<same-survivor-fixture.tgz> --yes --no-restart --json` exited 0 in 74.997s. Starting the **old package's direct `dist/index.js`** entry once reached `/readyz` in 5.513s (`ready:true`, `coreReady:true`, no failing checks; CPU advisory reported). RPC verified serving `2026.11.7-first-hop.0` / build `121bbb9`. Read-only SQLite inspection recorded exactly one `update_runs` row: `fb46f568-899d-4b76-bfbe-c1919ba2c7f4`, `finished/succeeded`, reason null, `verification.booted=true`, candidate running version/build verified. No live providers were used.
- Persisted successful-run timings (overlapping spans, not additive): requested 15.715s; staging 54.372s; prepare:pack 82.932s; prepare:install 34.103s; validating 2.544s; plugins 1.811s; activating 26.654s. Row lifetime 99.285s; isolated install/config 43.160s; proof core wall 144.681s (outer Docker command 149.17s). No pre-existing serving Gateway, so no update outage is claimed.
- **Requested `package-installed-recovery` scenario FAIL: harness asserts the retired legacy displacement hook** (`scripts/e2e/lib/upgrade-survivor/installed-recovery.mjs:128`). Its update now exits **0** in 74.453s, then the harness rejects that success because no legacy displacement interruption occurs. Returned ledger row `1a75c2e7-7841-449a-9b83-638e1c19f414` is `activating/running`, reason null, candidate recorded: the expected pending state for `--no-restart` (`src/update/cli.ts:273-275`). Completed phases: requested 14.754s, staging 54.164s, validating 3.006s, plugins 2.161s; prepare/activation spans were still open in that snapshot. Outer scenario wall 145.86s. No recovery cuts passed; the harness is unchanged. The separate next-start proof above closes the real activation/serving contract.
- Local ClawSweeper review on pushed head `e6ef2df3aa04ec10d4bfb274ac4d6ca71b2964ef`: complete, **patch is correct**, zero code findings, security cleared. Its synthetic local-range context did not include this PR's execution evidence and therefore marked real-behavior proof missing; the red/green receipts and successful Linux next-start/SQLite/RPC proof above supply that evidence.
