prs.title: fix(web-fetch): keep Gateway responsive during cold provider discovery
prs.body:
Fixes #166641

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Gateway stalls caused by synchronous plugin source capture when `web_fetch` first discovers fallback providers, including providers that do not declare `webFetchProviders` in their manifest.

## User Impact

During cold fallback discovery, a worker prepares external plugin sources while the Gateway continues serving requests. Undeclared-provider discovery, configured selection, sandbox restrictions, and synchronous listing callers retain their existing behavior.

Plugin evaluation and `register()` still run in their original owner; this change does not make arbitrary plugin initialization nonblocking.

## Why This Change Was Made

The synchronous and asynchronous resolvers now share one decision sequence. Fetch execution awaits the existing asynchronous loader, which already owns source preparation, cache identity, and pending-load sharing. Registration reentry still avoids waiting on itself, and an inspection released during supplemental loading cannot publish providers.

No new cache, configuration, schema, or plugin-manifest requirement.

## Evidence

### Validation on the current branch

Validated PR head `a88fa90242512ac5ec29eb4d8fbba530a6c4d1cd` against upstream `b7bf937423f65c313c8fe98b81b112537286ecaf`. Synchronous and asynchronous setup discovery both forward the caller’s plugin install records and pending state migrations. The bundled-artifact test now runs the same asynchronous fetch resolver as production and checks that repeated lookups reuse each caller’s own artifact.

The same Gateway regression sent two concurrent requests for distinct URLs on each revision. On upstream it observed one synchronous plugin source capture and zero asynchronous preparations. On the PR it observed zero synchronous captures and one shared asynchronous preparation. Both requests returned the expected fallback content. A third, warm URL reused the same provider. The regression passed on Node 24.22.1 and the repository-pinned Bun runtime.

An independent Node process running `openclaw.mjs gateway run` exercised an undeclared fallback provider with 1,200 source files. All three fetches returned the expected content. During the cold requests, 169 health probes returned HTTP 200. Of those, 89 started and finished within a plugin preparation worker interval. The cold requests together added one registration and the warm request added none.

- 256 tests passed across 12 focused files. The Gateway regression above passed separately on both runtimes.
- Core and all four affected test TypeScript configurations passed. The change-scoped checks passed, including formatting, lint and unused-export scans. The test-line and mock-export checks also passed.
- The full build stopped at the public plugin SDK declaration budget on the PR and on a clean checkout of `b7bf937`. Both produced 5,406,356 bytes against the 5,385,536-byte limit.

### GitHub Actions

[Checks for the current PR](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194612/checks)

### Focused reproduction commands

```sh
pnpm test src/plugins/public-artifact-environment.test.ts src/plugins/web-provider-runtime-shared.test.ts src/plugins/web-fetch-providers.runtime.test.ts src/plugins/web-search-providers.runtime.test.ts src/plugins/tools.inspection.test.ts src/plugins/loader-load-context.test.ts src/plugins/contracts/web-fetch-provider.contract.test.ts src/web-fetch/runtime.test.ts src/agents/tools/web-tools.fetch.test.ts src/agents/tools/web-fetch.provider-fallback.test.ts src/cli/capability-cli.test.ts src/gateway/server.auth.guest-dictation.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
pnpm build
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node OPENCLAW_E2E_USE_PREBUILT_DIST=1 pnpm test src/gateway/web-fetch-discovery.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=bun OPENCLAW_E2E_USE_PREBUILT_DIST=1 pnpm test src/gateway/web-fetch-discovery.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
pnpm check:changed --base b7bf937423f65c313c8fe98b81b112537286ecaf --head a88fa90242512ac5ec29eb4d8fbba530a6c4d1cd --delegate-compilers
```

### Initial reproduction on 2026-11-07

Base: `openclaw/openclaw` main `020ec24568b12416bf4315732532bae8762101aa`, fetched on 2026-11-07. Local Node 24.22.1, pnpm 12.15.0, repository-pinned Bun, macOS arm64.

The initial regression ran a real isolated Gateway and `POST /tools/invoke` against a local HTTP 503 fixture, with provider selection unset and a synthetic external plugin lacking the web-fetch manifest declaration. Startup, discovery, registration, and loading were not mocked; spies observed the real source preparation. Acceptance was correct fallback content with no plugin source traversal on the Gateway thread.

| Observation | Base: one fallback request | Fixed: two concurrent URLs, then a warm URL |
| --- | --- | --- |
| HTTP/content result | 200, expected provider text | All three 200, expected provider text |
| Main-thread source traversal | 1 | 0 |
| Asynchronous source preparation | 0 | 1 total |
| Request-time registrations | 1 additional | 1 additional; warm call adds none |

The base failed the main-thread traversal assertion. Startup had already registered the fixture once, so this demonstrates request-time recapture, not a never-loaded plugin. The final test extends that regression to concurrent and warm calls with distinct URLs to avoid response-cache sharing.

Validation:

- Across focused runs, 227 unique tests across nine files passed: 226 focused tests covering provider resolution, web-fetch runtime/fallback, web-search compatibility, CLI, and inspection lifetime, plus the dedicated real Gateway concurrent/warm E2E regression.
- Core and four owning test TypeScript configurations passed, including the final dedicated Gateway file.
- Targeted lint and formatting, diff whitespace checks, the test-line allocation check, and the mock-export ratchet passed.
- Full `pnpm build` passed (exit 0), including plugin SDK declarations and Control UI.
- Independent Codex source review: no actionable P0–P2 findings in the local change.

### Shipped Gateway trace at `3bea597`

Executed at `3bea597ec8db7a4cca22ec803108673ba336acc4`, Node 24.22.1 on macOS arm64, against the rebuilt runtime. A separate process launched the package entry point with `node openclaw.mjs gateway run --port "$GATEWAY_PORT" --bind loopback`. An external driver waited for `/readyz`, sent two concurrent `POST /tools/invoke` requests for `web_fetch` with distinct URLs, then a third warm URL, while polling `/healthz` every 20 ms. All three requests returned the fixture provider's expected text after direct HTTP 503 responses.

The isolated configuration used a synthetic external plugin with no `webFetchProviders` manifest declaration, no configured provider selection, and 1,200 referenced source files. Bundled discovery was disabled (`OPENCLAW_DISABLE_BUNDLED_PLUGINS=1` and `OPENCLAW_BUNDLED_PLUGINS_DIR` pointing to an empty directory) to exercise the external-only, undeclared-provider inventory path. No Gateway, loader, discovery, or registration functions were mocked. This proof uses a synthetic HTTP fixture and does not require a model or external service.

A read-only `diagnostics_channel` subscriber, loaded with Node's `--import`, recorded the existing `openclaw.worker.task` completion events for `plugin-generation-preparation.worker.js`. Worker intervals are derived from completion timestamps minus reported `runMs`; 61 complete external health requests fell within those intervals. During the complete cold-request window, 66 health requests returned 200 (median 3 ms, maximum 110 ms). Startup registered the fixture once; both concurrent cold requests together added one registration, and the warm request added none. This measures request-time source recapture after startup, not a never-loaded plugin.

<details>
<summary>Redacted terminal trace (milliseconds relative to driver start)</summary>

Paths, addresses, credentials, and local endpoints are omitted. Selected events from the external driver and the existing worker diagnostics:

```json

prs.title: feat: let Talk and Discord request GPT-Live-1.1 with ChatGPT sign-in
prs.body:
Closes #202806.

## What Problem This Solves

ChatGPT subscribers can select `gpt-live-1-codex` for voice. OpenClaw currently treats `gpt-live-1.1-codex` as an unlisted model, so the explicit 1.1 selector is missing from the picker and skips the subscription route.

## User Impact

User impact: Subscribers can select `gpt-live-1.1-codex` in Talk or set `channels.discord.voice.realtime.model` for Discord.

## Why This Change Was Made

Register `gpt-live-1.1-codex` in the existing Codex model classifier. The classifier supplies the catalog entry, Codex voices, and eligibility for the existing ChatGPT WebRTC path. Both selectors use the same authentication behavior and credential order. Talk and the Discord gateway relay forward the selected model in the offer. Existing defaults stay in place. Changes to credential fallback and startup error reporting are follow-up work.

## Evidence

- 60 focused tests passed on the revised commit. They cover catalog and OAuth readiness, and confirm that native Talk and the Discord gateway relay each send the exact selector in the ChatGPT WebRTC offer. With the original classifier in place, the new routing test fails because the catalog omits the selector. Formatting, lint, and the docs MDX check passed.
- On the earlier PR revision, an isolated Control UI call and a separate gateway relay call exchanged audio and returned transcripts after submitting the explicit 1.1 selector over ChatGPT OAuth. The server did not identify the model that served either call. [Redacted browser results](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202807#issuecomment-7054806575)
- The [Codex CLI 0.171.0 source](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.171.0/codex-rs/core/src/realtime_conversation.rs#L118) uses `gpt-live-1.1-codex` as its frameless realtime default.

A long address could turn the Browser’s **Go to** button into three lines on a phone. It also made the suggestion taller in a narrow Chat panel on a landscape tablet. The address field already holds the whole editable destination.

prs.title: fix: keep dismissed automation failures out of the Inbox
prs.body:
Closes #202650
Closes #202652
Closes #202653
Closes #202661

## What Problem This Solves

A failed automation can come back after you dismiss it if browser storage is full, two tabs dismiss different failures at once, or you pause and re-enable the automation. Opening the same Gateway from a different browser or address also brings the failure back.

## User Impact

A dismissed run stays hidden for your account on that Gateway, including when you switch browsers, addresses, or devices. A dismissed auto-disable stays hidden after a successful manual run. A later failed run still appears. A dismissal that the Gateway refuses because a restart is in progress is saved for the same browser profile to submit when the Gateway returns. Update notices can reappear after a Gateway restart.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway saves the latest dismissed failure for each automation in the signed-in operator’s existing profile preferences. The profile writer merges acknowledgements in one transaction, and the existing preference event refreshes open tabs. A structured restart refusal uses the existing per-profile reconnect queue with the exact failure timestamp. Pausing an automation leaves its last-run identity intact. For an auto-disabled job, dismissal covers the failed run and the automatic disable shown in the same row.

The Inbox imports existing account-scoped browser dismissals. Those records contain job IDs, so the first import uses the failure timestamp the Gateway knows for that job. Later imports preserve the first receipt. Import requires a browser record tied to the signed-in profile.

## Evidence

The current comparison uses main `3c8c7bf781fb` and this PR at `83ba861a5079`. The targeted Plugins readiness check passed on both builds.

On the PR head, 208 focused tests passed, including Inbox, profile preferences, and Gateway method order. Both Inbox opening latency cases and the Gateway protocol and generated validator checks passed.

I created Inbox dismissals and saved a theme on the published `2026.9.37`, `2026.10.33`, and `2026.11.6` builds, then started PR build `7f66802e9ad` on each isolated copy of the saved Gateway and browser state. All three imported the dismissal, preserved the theme, kept the original failure hidden after re-enable, reload, and a fresh browser, and displayed a later failure.

### Product captures

The paired captures compare main `e6d441549fe2` with the Inbox persistence implementation at `2720891948c5`, each against a copy of the same isolated Gateway state. The stable-upgrade captures use `2eda19b546a`. The isolated Gateway comparison below also covers that upgrade at `18b3695e8ad`. The receipt regressions compare main `5fe76f0073b4` with PR head `2dfaed67aaab`.

| Scenario | Main | PR head |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Browser storage full after two dismissals | ![Main shows Archive check again](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/7179f138305120510649db4679c182f08c9e746c/images/2026/11/ae8c7e84-96fc-4c48-a11d-b035dfa86004.png) | ![Both failures stay hidden](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/7179f138305120510649db4679c182f08c9e746c/images/2026/11/e57fbd94-8c5e-4178-9f0f-32a72cc2874f.png) |
| Automation paused and re-enabled after dismissal | ![Main shows Archive check with Index check](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/7179f138305120510649db4679c182f08c9e746c/images/2026/11/acd96639-1811-4223-99ff-a6f924fc3fcb.png) | ![Only Index check remains](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/7179f138305120510649db4679c182f08c9e746c/images/2026/11/aa7d9fbd-47aa-4bde-ac9f-030104e74e03.png) |
| Same Gateway opened at another address in a separate profile | ![Main shows both failures in the other browser](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/7179f138305120510649db4679c182f08c9e746c/images/2026/11/b90930a5-0eae-4bd7-a4c5-8e285976d63d.png) | ![The other browser shows only Index check](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/7179f138305120510649db4679c182f08c9e746c/images/2026/11/4e67960e-177d-4273-8b25-ca05c0f31de6.png) |

- **Two tabs.** Main lost one dismissal when both tabs clicked at the same timestamp. The PR build hid both rows in both tabs, and the Gateway held both run timestamps.
- **Browser migration.** A dismissal carried over from the old browser while the job was paused. It stayed hidden in a fresh profile after re-enable. A genuine later failure appeared even when another browser still held an old dismissal.

| Imported dismissal in a fresh browser | A later failed run |
| --- | --- |
| ![Only Index check after importing the Archive check dismissal](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/7179f138305120510649db4679c182f08c9e746c/images/2026/11/a0fe65c8-c529-4cb5-ba12-18860a11450d.png) | ![A new Archive check failure appears](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/7179f138305120510649db4679c182f08c9e746c/images/2026/11/ff223519-afd7-49df-a707-ddd3e830c4a3.png) |

### Control UI behavior against isolated Gateways

I built main `3ac8d23a2cb6` and PR head `18b3695e8ad` and exercised both in Chromium against isolated Gateways.

| Scenario | Main | PR head |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Dismiss a failed automation, reload, and restart the Gateway | Stays hidden in the original browser | Stays hidden in the original browser and in a fresh browser after restart |
| Dismiss with browser storage full | Returns on reload | Stays hidden on reload |
| Two tabs dismiss separate failures | Both stayed hidden in this run | Both stayed hidden and the Gateway stored both receipts |
| Upgrade from v2026.11.6 with a browser dismissal and a profile setting | The setting and original browser dismissal survive, and the failed run appears in a new browser | Imports the dismissal, preserves the setting, and hides the original failure in a new browser. A later failed run appears |
| Update notice and execution approval | The snoozed notice returns after restart. Pending approval requires a decision | Same behavior |
| Dismiss a seeded mention | Stays gone after reload and restart in a fresh browser | Same behavior |

A real Gateway refused the dismissal as shutdown began at `3106387303e`, and the original request never stored a receipt. At `18b3695e8ad`, I reproduced the same structured refusal during a real shutdown. After restart the dismissal was submitted, the Gateway saved it, and a fresh browser showed the failure hidden. The focused regression was red on `3106387303e` and green on the exact head. The runtime build, 108 focused tests, and targeted lint and format passed.

Overdue automation dismissal stayed browser-local on both builds. Built-browser fixtures covered model-auth dismissal, read-only scope guidance, and OpenClaw ID recovery notices and the other OpenClaw ID rows that require action. The browser outbox suite passed on both builds with simulated delivery rejection. The update test seeded a release check result. The mention test seeded an already-received mention and used the real Gateway for dismissal and persistence.

### Auto-disable followed by a manual run

In a built Control UI with an isolated Gateway and a scripted model response, a real one-shot automation failed and was automatically disabled. I dismissed its Inbox row, ran the job successfully without re-enabling it, and reloaded the page. At `05a4906c5d4`, the row came back. At `3106387303e`, it stayed dismissed and appeared again only after a later failed run.

The new regression failed on `05a4906c5d4` and passed on `3106387303e`. The 107 focused Inbox and Gateway preference tests passed on `3106387303e`, along with the runtime build and targeted lint and format checks.

### Upgrade from v2026.11.6

I dismissed Archive check in the published v2026.11.6 Control UI, saved a profile theme preference, and paused the job. I replaced the stable Gateway with a build of `2eda19b546a` using the same test state and browser profile. The Gateway imported the dismissal for the paused run and preserved the theme preference. Re-enabling the job kept the original run ID and timestamp, and a fresh browser profile on `localhost` kept the row dismissed after reload. Running the job again produced a new failed run and a visible Inbox row.

| Dismissal on v2026.11.6 | Relaunched browser on the PR build | Later failed run |
| --- | --- | --- |

## What Problem This Solves

When a focused dashboard link matches several sessions, ten long names can push the exit off a phone screen. On the earlier PR revision the first name took three lines; **Close dashboard** was another 307 px below the viewport.

## User Impact

Each choice shows one line for its name and a quieter second line for its agent and session ID. Long names shorten with an ellipsis. ## Why This Change Was Made

Only the ambiguous-link chooser needs these compact rows. The short error and missing-session views keep their existing layout. The chooser can still scroll if its surroundings leave less vertical space.

## Evidence

On an emulated 390 × 844 phone, the first long title went from 61 px to 22 px tall. The center of **Close dashboard** moved from y = 1,151 outside the screen to y = 737 inside it. On the phone, both tablets and desktop, all ten titles fit on one line with distinct IDs; selecting the eighth opened the exact synthetic dashboard, and Close returned to Dashboards. Repeating with a long agent ID preserved the full distinguishing session ID at all four sizes. Three focused bundled Chromium regressions passed, including the missing-session state.

prs.title: feat(release): release fast-track system
prs.body:
## Problem

Prepare exact fast-track requests without a separate Google Chat/Firebase approval system. The maintainer has explicitly chosen the normal release-managers group and existing release approval process, accepting the shared-token procedural trust model.

**This PR still does not enable a validation bypass or authorize publication.** Existing parent, npm/plugin, Docker and closeout gates and the historical `authorized-beta-focused-v1` contract remain unchanged.

## Simplified design

- `pnpm release:publish-preflight approval request --request request.json` prepares a local canonical payload/digest and explicit human-review instructions. No network, credentials, decision store, custom status API or machine approval operation. Output explicitly reports `publicationAuthorized: false`.
- Another human release manager must explicitly approve the exact request/action/digest, candidate, artifacts, scope, run/attempt and expiry in the normal release-managers group. Preserve the decision permalink, identity and timestamp with release evidence. Generic release authority, silence and previous approvals are insufficient. Changes/expiry require fresh approval.
- Both release-maintainer and release-CI skills emphatically prohibit agents approving requests or using human tokens to impersonate approval. This is a procedural safeguard, not proof of independent human action. No new email allowlist or domain-wide access.
- Keep the existing `npm-release` environment approval and `scripts/release-approval-receipt.mjs` publication record. No replacement approval receipt.
- Remove the Google service transport/verifier, ID-token/origin configuration, custom request/status exchange, delivery/error protocol and obsolete service-client tests. The separate source/deployment proposal [releases#56](https://github.com/openclaw/releases/pull/56) is superseded. No Firebase/Cloud Run deployment dependency remains in this PR.

## Retained policies

- `approved-fast-track-v1`: inclusive **10 commits AND 10,000 total added/deleted lines** from a published fully validated ancestor. Exclude exact `package.json`, `package-lock.json`, `npm-shrinkwrap.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `yarn.lock`, `bun.lock` and `bun.lockb` basenames at any directory depth from LOC only. All commits still count; other generated files count. Binary/submodule/unmeasurable changes and shallow history still reject, including in excluded files. Fast-tracks cannot reset the baseline. Git counts are recomputed, not trusted from the request.
- `approved-partial-frv-v1`: separate explicit incomplete-validation action, no delta ceiling, original FRV run/attempt/candidate and snapshot URL/digest, result counts and all outstanding jobs retained. A failed FRV never becomes a passing FRV. Small-delta eligibility still rejects this policy until authenticated evidence integration exists.

Canonical request serialization and the separate partial-FRV contract are unchanged. The small-delta policy now uses the requested 10k LOC cap and package-file exclusions. A request packet/hash is not authenticated validation evidence or publication authorization.

## Validation

- 21 manual approval/contract checks pass, including exact local packet output, rejected approve/reject/status operations, expiry, Git thresholds, full generated delta, binaries/submodules and partial-FRV retention contracts.
- 61 existing preflight/approval-receipt checks and 6 existing interface checks pass. The interface suite is classified outside the tooling lane, so it was explicitly run with an external scoped local config; initial tooling/isolated discovery did not execute it and is not counted as proof.
- Real local CLI synthetic request verified canonical SHA-256 and `publicationAuthorized: false`, without service credentials or a human decision.
- Production scripts, tooling-leaf and explicit manual-suite TypeScript checks pass; targeted lint, formatting and whitespace checks pass.
- Test ratchet: net counted test lines **0**, allocation credit **0**. New feature checks stay manual-only and refuse `CI`; no CI lane or test-budget allocation added.
- Fresh independent incremental P0-P2 review: scoped-clean. Reviewer assessed the supplied diff, not unchanged dependencies or live behavior; tests were executed separately.
- Simplification against prior head: **457 net lines removed**, including 192 production lines and 223 obsolete test lines. One existing publication approval record remains, with no new durable state or service owner.

## Remaining work / operational limits

Publisher enforcement and authenticated reference/original-FRV evidence acquisition remain unfinished. Before enabling skips, bind independently derived candidate/artifact/scope/run identities, preserve integrity/signing/publication authorization, migrate all existing consumers together and test normal/exception paths. Record “validation skipped by approved fast-track,” never fabricated successful validation.

Removing the dependency and superseding the source PR does **not** delete previously provisioned cloud resources, Firestore records or setup credentials. No live cloud cleanup/deployment, current human/mobile approval, merge or release is claimed. Historical Google mobile proof is not proof of this new procedural model.


### CI preflight repair

The initial `.spec.ts` manual-suite filename was still selected by CI's changed-owner/import-consumer graph, despite not belonging to a canonical Vitest shard. CI preflight failed before executing tests with “test targets lack canonical shard metadata.” Renamed it to `.checks.ts` and updated only the explicit local config; no discovery policy, CI lane or budget was weakened/added. The existing suite contents are byte-identical.

Local proof: all 21 manual checks pass; actual changed-owner target selection and shard construction over the complete PR diff succeed with no fallback and no manual-suite target; explicit `CI=true` invocation still refuses; manual-suite types, targeted lint/format/whitespace and zero-allocation test ratchet pass. Hosted CI run [45081973562](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45081973562) completed successfully at `a082f0e97224783d859b92697bc5133ecd957fc4`, including preflight and downstream CI jobs. The separate Darwin tooling check and aggregate status were still pending at this observation; no merge-readiness claim.



### Updated small-delta policy

Inclusive 10 commits AND 10,000 added/deleted lines, excluding the enumerated package manifest/lockfile basenames from LOC only. Delta `added`/`deleted` values use those filtered counts; commit counts and integrity checks still cover the whole delta. Local regressions prove 10,000 accepted/10,001 rejected, dependency-only commits retained, nested lockfile exclusion, similarly named source files counted and binary excluded files still rejected. 22 manual checks pass, including red/green threshold/exclusion regressions. No CI lane or budget added.

Targeted scripts/tooling/manual-suite typechecks, lint/format/whitespace and fresh incremental P0-P2 review passed for the policy repair (review was diff-only; a subsequent mechanical optional-access adjustment satisfied TypeScript). The new suite remains manual-only.

prs.title: fix: let Escape cancel an address edit without closing the Browser panel

## What Problem This Solves

When editing the Browser address in Chat on a phone or portrait tablet, pressing Escape to discard the edit also closed the Browser sheet. You had to reopen it to try another address, even if you had only cleared the field.

## User Impact

The first Escape now cancels the edit and selects the current address so you can immediately type a replacement. If there is no edit to discard, Escape still dismisses the sheet. Canceling does not navigate the browser.

## Why This Change Was Made

The address field handles Escape only when it has an edited or invalid address. Otherwise it leaves the key available to the surrounding panel. This changes neither the shared panel nor the layout of address suggestions.

## Evidence

The existing phone screenshots show the same Chat panel immediately after the first Escape: the baseline returned to Chat, while the fix kept the Browser open with its current address selected. The original sheet dismissal also reproduced on the portrait tablet, but not in the landscape tablet or desktop layout.

The regression passed in Chromium on the independent patch. It checked a typed address, an empty field, and an invalid address: Escape restored and selected the current address without sending a navigation request. Another Escape closed the sheet. The tab and page were synthetic; no remote browser was used. Stock main: `450441b904031`. Atlas source: `c67fc9db1a121`. Independent repair: `0847f615c3e6b`.

prs.title: fix(auth): preserve refresh token on provably undispatched OAuth refresh failures
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes #201933

OpenAI `chatgpt-token-sharing` and xAI `device-code` refresh transports wrapped
every transport failure as an unknown-outcome error, even when the failure
proved the refresh grant was never dispatched, such as a refused connection
to a local proxy, a resolver failure, or a local SSRF block. The OAuth
manager then wrote a terminal failed refresh fence, invalidating a still-valid
rotating refresh token and forcing manual re-login after a brief local outage.

This change classifies provably undispatched refresh failures as
`phase: "before-dispatch" / outcome: "not-attempted"` so the manager rolls the
claim back instead of fencing the credential:

- New shared helper `createNotAttemptedOAuthRefreshError` in
  `openclaw/plugin-sdk/provider-oauth-runtime` (used by both adapters, so the
  policy lives in one place). It uses the existing delivery-proof helper to
  check every transport attempt, including nested Undici errors. DNS and
  socket errors need evidence from the relevant syscall. A typed
  `SsrFBlockedError` also qualifies when the adapter has seen no response.
  A mixed error containing any ambiguous attempt stays unknown.
- Both adapters track `responseSeen` via `onResponse` and classify only when
  no response was received. Any response — including a redirect — means the
  provider may have consumed the rotating grant, so the failure stays unknown.
  The OpenAI classification applies only to `grant_type=refresh_token`;
  login/JWKS transport failures are untouched.
- Ambiguous failures (`ECONNRESET`, timeouts after dispatch, aborts, unknown
  errors) keep their existing behavior: the OpenAI adapter rethrows them
  unchanged, the xAI adapter keeps its `token-response / unknown` error, and
  the manager still fences them.

No manager change was needed: `oauth-manager` already rolls back the claim
when `isTransientOAuthRefreshFailure` is true, and the new outcome satisfies
that check. The issue's suggested manager retry was omitted deliberately —
rollback already preserves the credential for the next attempt.

## Contributor test report

New regression tests, red on the base and green with the fix:

- `src/plugin-sdk/provider-oauth-runtime.test.ts` — the classifier returns a
  `before-dispatch / not-attempted` error (recoverable per
  `isRecoverableOAuthRefreshFailure`) for `ECONNREFUSED` (direct and nested
  under undici's `fetch failed`), `ENOTFOUND`, `EAI_AGAIN`, and
  `SsrFBlockedError`; returns `undefined` for `ECONNRESET`,
  `UND_ERR_SOCKET`, unknown errors, and aborts.
- `extensions/xai/xai-oauth.test.ts` — `refreshXaiOAuthCredential` against a
  stubbed fetch throwing `ECONNREFUSED`/`ENOTFOUND`/`EAI_AGAIN` rejects with
  the `not-attempted` outcome; a 302 response followed by `ECONNREFUSED`
  stays `token-response / unknown` (response seen).
- `extensions/openai/token-sharing-oauth.runtime.test.ts` — same
  `not-attempted` classification for refresh attempts; ambiguous failures
  (`ECONNRESET`, unknown) keep their existing shape and stay unrecoverable.

Suites run (`--maxWorkers=2`):

- `pnpm vitest run src/plugin-sdk/provider-oauth-runtime.test.ts` — 14 passed.
- `pnpm vitest run extensions/openai/token-sharing-oauth.runtime.test.ts` — 40 passed.
- `pnpm vitest run extensions/xai/xai-oauth.test.ts extensions/xai/xai-oauth-refresh-bytes.test.ts` — 54 passed, 2 failed.
- `pnpm vitest run src/agents/auth-profiles/oauth-manager.test.ts` — 19 passed.
- `pnpm vitest run src/agents/auth-profiles/oauth-refresh-failure.test.ts src/agents/auth-profiles/oauth-refresh-fence.test.ts src/agents/auth-profiles/oauth.unknown-outcome.test.ts` — 3 files, 52 passed.

The 2 xAI failures are pre-existing device-code polling flakes in this
environment, not regressions: `stops authorization with stalled=false
cancel=false` and `preserves authorization_pending and slow_down pacing
before valid tokens` fail identically on the unmodified base (verified with
`git stash`).

`oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` are clean on all touched files; `tsgo:core`
exits 0.

## Maintainer follow-up

- The mixed-error regression failed on contributor head `24b560165446` with
  the new test applied. The classifier incorrectly returned `not-attempted`
  for a refused connection grouped with an ambiguous socket failure.
- All three focused suites passed on `82d339bff0b4` (tree
  `effb88ac3f9da6de274282c82a6b8705a5f542a4`) in an isolated Linux runner
  with Node 24.22.1 and a frozen dependency install. This covers the shared
  classifier and both provider adapters, including the redirect case.
- Independent autoreview through P2 found no actionable issues in the
  maintainer correction. Real transport proof through both adapters and
  the durable credential store remains pending.
- Merged current main `1692cb83f791` into the contributor branch at `85ec951e77a4baf53ae41a1cda6e640357d3fe1f` to resolve the SDK import conflict. The refresh classifier body and all five other file patches match the already-reviewed correction. [CI for this head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45086575221).

Filtering Dashboards by an author with a long name could push the remove button off the screen. On a phone, the filtered directory stayed visible but you could not clear the filter directly.

## User Impact

You can clear a long author filter with one tap. When space runs out, only the displayed author name shortens; the avatar, “Author is” label, and remove button stay on one line. Short names and the multiple-author count keep their existing presentation.

## Why This Change Was Made

The applied filter previously grew to fit the entire name. It now stays within the directory width and leaves the button its original space. Filtering itself is unchanged.

## Evidence

In the existing 390 px phone comparison, the right edge of the remove button was at 611 px before the fix. It now sits at 376 px and is tappable. The 256-character case also kept the button reachable on both tablet orientations and desktop. The short-name filter looked identical at all four widths. The grouped heading below the filter is a separate change, not part of this PR.

On the publication checkout, the mounted regression applied the filter, verified the button’s center was reachable, tapped it, and confirmed that both synthetic dashboard cards returned. Original comparison baseline: `c55eea9b74a1e`. Isolated repair: `e3cb42860f1be`.

prs.title: fix: make agent tool access easier to read on phones and remove dead preview links
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On a phone, an agent’s Tool Access summary stacked each value below its label, pushing the tool names out of view. When a session discovered a tool that was not in the catalog, its name still looked and behaved like a link, even though there was nowhere to go.

## User Impact

You can read the tool profile, source, enabled count, and preview count side by side with their labels. In the preview, selecting a cataloged tool opens its group and focuses the tool’s details. Other discovered tools are still listed by name, without a dead link.

## Why This Change Was Made

The four short facts fit in two columns on a phone. The preview also checks whether the catalog contains the tool before offering a link. Neither change alters which tools the agent may use.

## Evidence

On a 390 px phone, the four-row summary shrank from 237 px to 122 px at default text size and from 296 px to 152 px at 140%. Both tool names in the existing phone comparison are now visible without scrolling at default size. The summary matched the baseline pixel for pixel on the two tablets and desktop at both text sizes.

With synthetic tool data, checks confirmed that two discovered tools without catalog entries were not links, and that selecting a cataloged plugin tool opened its group and moved focus to the correct row. Checks also covered an unavailable preview, a catalog failure, and recovery on retry. No live tool was called or setting changed. Stock main: `450441b904031`. Atlas repair: `cef0d04b44eeb`.

prs.title: fix(ui): show archived session state on first paint
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Reloading a cached archived conversation can restore its transcript before the archived-session banner arrives, leaving the composer area empty for an initial frame. The scheduled [main CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44913885381) catches this in both archived and deleted-parent sessions.

Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/185788

## User Impact

Archived conversations show their existing status and Unarchive control with the first composer paint. Cached controls retain their existing pending-authority behavior until reconnect.

## Why This Change Was Made

The banner is required session presentation. Render it synchronously with the composer instead of behind an empty lazy-loading fallback. The existing fixture now requires immediate rendering while retaining its focus, callback, disabled-action, and progress assertions.

**Draft: the measured Chat boot budget overrun is unresolved.** No budget has been changed.

## Evidence

- Unmodified base `3a20a7bcffff7bee97d774980c4ab3ee0507ec2d`: archived and deleted-parent fail the existing first-paint assertion; active and read-only pass.
- Candidate: all four unchanged bundled Chromium scenarios pass, including live-state replacement after reconnect.
- Strengthened fixture: four expected failures on the old renderer; four passes with the fix.
- Scoped format (oxfmt/Bun parity), lint, and UI typecheck pass.
- Local ClawSweeper reviewed `3a20a7bcffff..bf6f6fd9c153`: complete, no actionable correctness/security findings. It did not rerun tests; the budget overrun remains a landing blocker.
- Proof used the real production bundle with synthetic Gateway data on a task-owned Boat Linux lease. The before capture holds the actual banner bundle request open; no DOM replacement or production test hook.

| Same-host bundle comparison | Base | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Initial startup JS gzip | 90,879 B | 90,879 B |
| New Session boot JS gzip | 820,757 B | 820,757 B |
| Chat boot JS gzip | 1,333,702 B | 1,334,099 B |
| Chat boot JS requests | 21 | 21 |

The current Chat cap is **1,333,899 B**: the candidate adds **397 B** and exceeds the cap by **200 B**. This failure is introduced by the patch. Existing CSS warnings are unchanged or improve by 3 B; they do not explain the Chat failure.

The change removes four production lines net and two test lines net. Before/after images: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/203136#issuecomment-7064713198

Updates `actions/setup-java` from 6.1.0 to 6.3.0
Release notes

Sourced from actions/setup-java's releases.

v6.3.0

Behavior change: Java problem matcher is now opt-in

Starting with v6.3.0, setup-java no longer registers the Java problem matcher by default (#1326, fixes #1322). Java compiler warnings, compiler errors, and uncaught exceptions are no longer turned into annotations on pull request diffs unless you opt in.

To keep annotations, set problem-matcher: true:

- uses: actions/setup-java@v6
  with:
    distribution: temurin
    java-version: '25'
    problem-matcher: true

Compiler output still appears in the build logs, and compilation errors still fail the build. Only annotations are affected.

Why: inline annotations cluttered pull request reviews, and GitHub Actions caps annotations at 10 errors, 10 warnings, and 10 notices per step, and 50 per job. Larger Java builds therefore showed only a truncated subset of their diagnostics as annotations. See Java problem matcher (compiler annotations).

Updates `github/codeql-action/init` from 4.38.3 to 4.39.3
Release notes

Sourced from github/codeql-action/init's releases.

v4.39.3

  • Fixed diff-informed alert filtering incorrectly removing alerts in changed files whose paths contain spaces, special characters, or non-ASCII characters. #4283

v4.39.2

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.4. #4284
  • Upcoming breaking change: CodeQL version 2.22.3 and earlier were discontinued on 16 October 2026 alongside GitHub Enterprise Server 3.18, and will be unsupported by the next minor release of the CodeQL Action. Added a deprecation warning for customers using these versions of CodeQL. #4266
  • Starting with macOS 27 and Xcode 27, traced analyses are unsupported. See this blog post for more information. The CodeQL Action will now try to identify if a workflow is about to perform a traced analysis on version 27 or above of macOS or Xcode. If so, the CodeQL Action will emit a corresponding warning that will also be visible on the Tool Status Page. This check will be rolled out following this release of the CodeQL Action. #4221
  • The undocumented TRAP cache cleanup feature that could be enabled using the CODEQL_ACTION_CLEANUP_TRAP_CACHES environment variable has been removed, as announced in the release notes for CodeQL Action 4.35.2. The analyze Action now warns if this environment variable is set. If you used TRAP cache cleanup to limit Actions cache usage, we recommend disabling TRAP caching by passing the trap-caching: false input to the init Action. #4243

v4.39.1

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.3. #4256

v4.39.0

  • Breaking change: Bump the minimum required CodeQL bundle version to 2.20.7. #4205
  • The codeql-action/analyze step now validates that a correct argument for the checkout_path input has been provided. The checkout_path input must be set to the path where the repository that is being analyzed is checked out at on the runner, if that path is something other than the workspace root. If the path does not point to a repository checkout or is different from the path that was used by codeql-action/init, then the CodeQL Action now produces a warning. #4148
  • Resolved an issue with third-party caching implementations that prevented caches from being restored correctly. #4206
  • The codeql-action/start-proxy step that is used in Code Scanning Default Setup now finds CodeQL releases using the same logic as codeql-action/init. This primarily benefits customers who are using GitHub instances other than github.com where the codeql-action/start-proxy step may previously have been unable to locate recent releases and ended up using outdated versions of the private registry authentication proxy as a result. #4198

prs.title: fix(gateway): recover guest tasks after concurrent managed-workspace edits (#187911)
prs.body:
Closes #187911

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a managed sandbox conversation stays stuck when an administrator and the guest edit the same file at once. Both versions are preserved, but Files and every later turn of the original task keep returning "Local sandbox edits conflict with the managed workspace" instead of letting the authorized user merge the contributions and continue.

## User Impact

The affected conversation can recover without discarding either side. A normal authorized Files save is the acknowledgement: when the operator's expected hash matches the guest copy they read, the save is recorded against that guest version, the resolved file is copied into the private sandbox checkout, and the original task can continue. Files that are still conflicted stay pending. A guest version written after the capture is still rejected, and a save on a worktree without a pending conflict no longer writes a synthetic checkpoint.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Conflict acknowledgement goes through the projection state's own update operation, so the next synchronization sees the current binding rather than a changed one.
- A Files save binds the selected candidate path through the actual write, so nested `fileRoot` sessions cannot resolve the same relative path twice.
- Acknowledgement is only recorded for a retained conflict or a pending receipt, so ordinary saves leave the checkpoint empty.
- A save whose own file is accepted while other conflicts remain is reported as an accepted save, while real write and authority failures still propagate.
- Reconciliation commits resolved canonical files onto the complete accepted baseline, preserving unconflicted guest additions, edits, and deletions.
- Canonical imports hold the existing guest pause through acceptance for either direction, so a background guest process cannot race verified bytes.
- A guest directory that may contain unreviewed descendants is refused, never recursively deleted; a legacy checkpoint without the new fields still settles.
- Resolved copies keep the existing authority revalidation, realpath/symlink containment, recursive replacement of a conflicting type, and a recorded guest version so a later guest edit of the same path conflicts again instead of being overwritten.

## Evidence

- `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192 pnpm tsgo:core` — clean, no diagnostics.
- `pnpm test src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-files.worktree.test.ts src/gateway/worker-environments/local-workspace-projection.conflict.test.ts --maxWorkers=4` — 2 files, 32/32 tests passed. Key cases:
  - `acknowledges and saves a reconciled version via sessions.files.set during conflict` (then prepares the next guest workspace successfully)
  - `resolves conflict hash correctly when session has a nested fileRoot`
  - `preserves compare-and-swap protection for unseen canonical edits outside retained conflicts`
  - `accepts a newer guest version that the operator actually reviewed in projection`
  - `treats a resolved path as a new conflict after the guest edits it again`
  - `does not synthesize a checkpoint for an ordinary managed save`
  - `resolves canonical workspace-relative path when saving absolute path candidates`
  - `overlays resolved paths onto complete accepted baseline preserving unmutated baseline entries`
  - `preserves newer guest divergence in projection if edited while conflict is pending`
  - `rejects unreviewed newer guest version written after administrator review`
  - `refuses to replace a guest directory that gained unreviewed descendants`
  - `settles a legacy checkpoint that predates the conflict fields`
- Broader focused batch (projection, manifest scan, store, checkout, CAS, fingerprints, diagnostics, reconcile/publication, workspace-local reconciliation): 205 passed, 1 skipped.
- `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192 pnpm test:unit:fast --maxWorkers=4` — 13,740 passed, 49 skipped; failures only in untouched suites: `completion-fish` spawnSync result shape, `bench-session-history` node spawnSync ETIMEDOUT under load, and one provider-header test that passes alone and only failed in the full shard.
- The suite runs the production `sessions.files.*` handlers against prepared git worktrees, the projection custody owner, and the SQLite worker boundary; it is not a mocked handler harness.
- Supporting Docker-backed regression (`pnpm test test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/managed-workspace-conflict-recovery.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`, 1/1 passed) uses a mock provider: `pnpm test test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/managed-workspace-conflict-recovery.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 1/1 passed (28 s). It starts a real Gateway child with a Docker sandbox, creates a managed worktree session, provisions the private projection, preserves a real conflict, recovers it through `sessions.files.set`, and completes the next guest turn with both trees holding the merged bytes.
- Real-model product trace (isolated Gateway, Docker sandbox, Codex CLI ChatGPT login; model and paths redacted): three turns through the running Gateway. Turn 1 replied `READY` and provisioned the managed worktree projection (Docker container started, sandbox backend timings recorded). Diverging guest/admin edits produced the preserved `LocalWorkspaceConflictError` on turn 2. `sessions.files.set` returned the updated `preview.html`; turn 3 replied `CONTINUED`, and canonical and projection both held `merged by administrator and guest`.
- The branch is merged with current `main` (`910f6b9427d`).
- Latest-stable upgrade proof (`openclaw@2026.11.5`): created a real managed-worktree conflict with a pending canonical result through the stable release, then opened the same state with this branch. Before upgrade the checkpoint contained only `baseManifestRaw`, `baseManifestRef`, `currentManifestRaw`, `currentManifestRef`, `fingerprints`, `records`, `removed`, roots, tree roots, and `version` — none of the new fields. The upgraded run migrated the state database, preserved an unrelated settings file byte-for-byte, kept the pending ref and both file contributions, and after acknowledgement settled to `pending_ref: null` with canonical and projection both holding `merged after stable upgrade`. All paths and identifiers are redacted here.
- Accepted limits: guest-version probing is bounded at 8 MiB, so a larger guest file records no reviewed version and the retained conflict capture stays authoritative; automatic file-to-directory conflict resolution is refused instead of partially applied.

prs.title: fix: keep dashboard author headings on one line
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When Dashboards is grouped by author, a long name can run past the edge of the phone. Wrapping the full name instead makes that author’s group heading twice as tall as its neighbors.

## User Impact

Each author stays on one line beside their avatar. Names that fit are unchanged; longer names end in an ellipsis. The full name remains in the accessible heading and is available on hover.

## Why This Change Was Made

Only the author label needs to shrink. The group keeps the same alignment as a short author, without changing the cards, their order, or the separate author filter.

## Evidence

On a 390 × 844 phone, the earlier wrapped heading measured 40 px. The revised heading measured 20 px, matching the neighboring author. The same long name fit in full at 820, 1180 and 1440 px. Switching grouping off restored the same two dashboard cards at every width. Bundled browser regressions covered directories of two and 64 dashboards and opening a gallery card.

The screenshots show the same synthetic, unfiltered gallery on a phone. Before: original upstream baseline `c55eea9b74a1e`. After: revised PR `7f8693fe6206e`.

prs.title: fix: keep Save in place when filtering Workboard labels
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a Workboard card’s label picker opened above the labels on a phone, typing a search could make the menu shrink away from the card. The **Save** and **Cancel** buttons moved as the results changed. With the full list, **Save** could fall outside the visible menu.

## User Impact

You can narrow the list, select a label and reach **Save** in the same place. When space is tight, the choices scroll between the search field and the buttons.

## Why This Change Was Made

A picker that opens above the label field now keeps its opening height while you filter. Closing it releases that space. Pickers that open below the field keep their existing layout.

## Evidence

The phone screenshots show the same synthetic Workboard card after filtering twelve choices to one. Before, the gap between the picker and the label field grew from 6 px to 85 px. After, it stayed at 6 px. The Chromium regression checked that the search field, first result and **Save** stayed in place when the query was entered and cleared, and that **Save** remained reachable.

The regression passed on the publication checkout. Across 28 matched states at four screen sizes, 23 unaffected menu or control crops were pixel-identical. No real card was updated. Screenshot baseline: `8621a7c6647f4`. Original repair: `386a57fd02162`.

|---|---|

prs.title: fix: show the full file path when reading or editing a skill on phones
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On a phone, selecting a supporting file with a long path could stretch the skill dialog beyond the screen. The end of the filename and the right edge of its text area disappeared, both when editing a personal skill and when reading a shared one.

## User Impact

You can read the full selected file path above its contents without scrolling the dialog sideways. The editor keeps the same margins as the other fields. Shared skills remain read-only.

## Why This Change Was Made

The selected-file field now fits the dialog and lets long paths wrap. File selection, contents, and save behavior are unchanged.

## Evidence

In the 390 px phone viewport, the dialog had 366 px of available width, but the selected file expanded its contents to 582 px. After the fix, the contents fit in 366 px in both the personal editor and shared reader. Checks covered switching between text and binary files, owner search and no matches, and closing the dialog with the keyboard and returning focus. Across phone, both tablets, and desktop, 28 comparisons of the original library rows and wider filename labels were pixel-identical.

The screenshots show the same synthetic personal skill and selected file on an emulated 390 × 844 phone. No skill was saved, installed, attached, or removed. Stock main: `450441b904031`. Atlas repair: `844bc8d87bbd0`.

prs.title: fix: keep file-question buttons on screen on phones
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On a phone, selecting a file with a long name could push the question’s Submit and Skip buttons off-screen. Wrapping the name brought the buttons back but pushed Remove onto the next line.

## User Impact

The selected file and Remove stay on one line. When the name does not fit, it ends in an ellipsis; its full text remains available to assistive technology. Submit and Skip remain visible below.

## Why This Change Was Made

The file chooser can shrink, and the selected-file row reserves space for Remove instead of letting the filename push it aside. File selection, removal, and answer handling are unchanged.

## Evidence

On an emulated 390 × 844 phone, the selected-file row went from 54 px on the earlier PR revision to 33 px, the height of Remove. Skip stayed inside the card at x=365. At all four campaign widths, selecting a synthetic file enabled Submit; removing it disabled Submit again and left Skip reachable. The focused phone and long-question browser tests passed. No file reached an external service and no answer was submitted.

The screenshots show the same file on the standalone question page. Before: saved upstream baseline `0058b08e8f1a3`. After: `e0f1b0baac9ed`.

### Clean comparison

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| ![Before: Submit extends beyond the phone and Skip is out of view.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4ebb9a57-0615-40a9-9919-158945e7262e) | ![After: the name and Remove share one line, with Submit and Skip visible below.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/499d3361-8212-4880-be45-52f1e55610db) |

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: app-resource results remain selectable after their source server disappears, allowing an attachment to be labeled with the newly selected server.

## User Impact

Removed-server results disappear without losing the query or closing the picker. Users can search the remaining server, and attachments keep their supplying server’s identity.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the supplying server and scope on the existing search receipt, retire that receipt when its server disappears, and use its identity for attachment delivery. Ordinary discovery reorder, real errors and explicit retry remain unchanged. No new capability, permission or iframe policy.

## Evidence

- Production/narrow-test types, scoped lint/format, controller guard and diff checks pass. Existing strict-read diagnostic signatures also occur on base and were not suppressed.
- Fresh coordinator review inspected the complete result/catalog owners, attachment event/consumer, original Solid implementation, regressions, receipts and actual screenshots; no unresolved actionable findings. Automated review and remote CI not claimed complete.

An unusually long file extension could take all the space in a Chat Files row. The filename before the dot disappeared. Wrapping the extension instead made that row taller than neighboring files.

## User Impact

Files stay on one line. When space is tight, the long extension ends in an ellipsis so the filename and the arrow remain visible. Short extensions such as `.ts` stay readable. Selecting the row still opens the exact file.

## Why This Change Was Made

The mobile and desktop Files lists give both parts of the name room instead of letting the extension grow without limit. No file paths, text sizes, or Sessions sidebar styles change.

All 10 focused browser tests passed. At all four campaign widths, opening the exact file and returning preserved the chat draft and issued no file write. prs.title: fix(ci): remove unused Mantis pnpm cache restore
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Mantis Slack desktop smoke workflow restores a candidate pnpm cache into home-directory paths that its installs do not use. Shared `setup-node-env` already exports a workspace-local store and metadata cache, and the candidate install inherits that environment. The separate `mantis-slack-pnpm-*` namespace also has no writer in the repository.

This is the separate, narrow cache cleanup requested by Dallin following the audit.

## User Impact

No user-visible runtime change. Mantis stops attempting the ineffective extra restore and continues using the shared setup cache. This does **not** claim to fix or measure the reported runtime slowdown. No new cache publisher, dependency change, or migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove the redundant restore instead of adding another cache owner. Add one focused workflow contract test that protects shared restore ownership, setup ordering, and candidate inheritance of pnpm store/cache configuration. Production diff: 10 deleted lines; regression: 24 added lines. Author self-review and simplification complete; local autoreview and independent prepublication review intentionally omitted under the task policy. Hosted ClawSweeper review will be tracked separately.

## Evidence

- The new regression failed against the unchanged workflow on the extra cache restore, then passed with this fix (1 test, 9 ms test time; latest direct-run duration 119 ms, command wall time under 1 second).
- Direct focused validation used the installed Vitest with an isolated temporary Node/forks config and only this test; it did not run the normal repository setup. CI test time is not yet available.
- `git diff --check` and targeted `oxfmt --check` pass.
- `env -u GH_TOKEN -u GITHUB_TOKEN pnpm check:workflows` passes: actionlint, zizmor, generated Git-owner checks, composite-input checks and conflict-marker checks. The first attempt stopped because an ambient empty token was rejected; removing only those empty environment overrides let the unchanged checker complete.

Validation limits: the normal test wrapper cannot load the missing `@solidjs/vite-plugin`; targeted lint cannot load `eslint-plugin-solid`; the typecheck wrapper rejects the borrowed dependency installation because declaration inputs escape this checkout. Those checks are **not passing** locally. No dependencies were added or reinstalled to work around these limits. Standard-wrapper proof, type-aware lint/typecheck and broad CI remain remote validation work. The paid/live Mantis desktop workflow was not dispatched.

## What Problem This Solves

In Appearance, two themes with names that start the same could look identical in the picker. Both “Northern Lights Midnight” and “Northern Lights Moonrise” appeared as “Northern Lights …”.

## User Impact

You can tell the two themes apart before choosing one. Short built-in theme names and their preview tiles stay the same size.

## Why This Change Was Made

Let long names wrap beneath their own preview. This keeps the previews and the first line of each name aligned without changing the number of columns. Unlike the [earlier, unmerged tooltip proposal](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/185872), this makes names readable without hovering or focusing a tile.

## Evidence

The full Midnight and Moonrise names fit on the phone, both tablets and desktop. Selection was checked by touch at all three touch widths and by keyboard on desktop. Keyboard focus remained visible at all four widths. The original built-in tiles kept their dimensions and column counts. No live preferences were changed or themes imported.

Mounted Control UI, synthetic theme family, 390 × 844 emulated phone. Comparison: stock main `da13d2a9c3023` versus local repair `a902c2eb0d4d8`.

prs.title: fix(cron): add remedy hints to scheduled read and message target errors
prs.body:
Closes #193196
Related: #154801, #126634, #150166

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: legacy cron jobs that predate scheduled tool policy fail every delegated channel read with an error that names no remedy, when their stored job has no `toolsAllow`.

## User Impact

Operators hit by this now see the recovery command in the error itself (`openclaw automations edit <jobId> --tools message`), and the automation troubleshooting page gains an entry for the exact failure signature alongside the existing inference-account ladders. The message tool's target error now names a concrete target shape (`channel:<id>` / `user:<id>`) instead of restating the requirement.

## Why This Change Was Made

The recovery is already documented in prose (`payloads.md`) and a same-style embedded-command precedent exists in `resolveCronToolsAllowExecTargetRecoveryError`; the errors were the only place the remedy was missing. Hints follow the existing `Hint:` convention in `target-errors.ts`. No gate behavior, policy, or authority decision is changed — fail-closed stays fail-closed.

## Evidence

- Both touched error strings keep their asserted prefixes; existing assertions were extended to pin the new hint text (`message-action-dispatch.registry.test.ts`, `message-tool.test.ts`).
- Targeted Vitest runs on the touched files pass locally (registry gate suite + message-tool suite); full gate CI runs on the branch.
- Production verification of the remedy (not this diff): two jobs on v2026.10.10 failed with the exact signature, recovered after `automations edit --tools message`, verified `ok` by forced runs — recorded in #193196.


## Behavior proof (patched shipped entry point, head `eef09c1e846`)

Gateway built from this branch ran as the live gateway on an Ubuntu 24.04 host with the official Discord plugin loaded; a test cron job in the legacy shape (no stored `toolsAllow`) ran isolated scheduled turns through it. Raw gateway log captures (verbatim, channel id redacted):

```
2026-11-08T18:08:18.276+00:00 [tools] message failed: GatewayClientRequestError: Error: Delegated discord:read requires current provider and account context. Hint: if this read runs from a scheduled job, reauthorize its complete tool cap, including message, from a trusted operator shell: "openclaw automations edit <jobId> --tools <tool,...>". | UNAVAILABLE
2026-11-08T18:24:44.888+00:00 [tools] message failed: BeforeToolCallFailureError: Explicit message target required for this run. Provide target/targets (and channel when needed). Hint: use a target such as "channel:<id>" or "user:<id>".

prs.title: test(e2e): retire package-installed-recovery cuts that target the retired in-place package path
prs.body:
## Problem

Since #203497, owned global package installs use prepared releases, not the in-place package executor. The existing upgrade-survivor cuts still expect the retired path.

Observed candidate evidence supplied with this task: run `1a75c2e7` selected the candidate and remained `activating` with `--no-restart`; the displacement update exited **0** after about **74 seconds**. `scripts/e2e/lib/upgrade-survivor/installed-recovery.mjs:128` then asserted that it must exit nonzero. This is an obsolete assertion, not a failed update. I did not rerun that reported failure.

## Cut classification

Citations refer to base `bdb444f3e940`. No replacement hooks were added, and no `src/` files changed.

| Cut | Hook / interrupted path | Production file:line | Decision |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `displaced` (shared prerequisite) | `fsp.rename(live, anchor/previous)` with exchange tools disabled | `src/infra/package-update-publication-owner.ts:403` | Retired for package installs |
| `partial-previous` | Unlink inside recursive retirement of retained `previous` | `src/infra/package-update-publication-owner.ts:570-581` | Retired |
| `anchor-before` | Before `fsp.rmdir(anchor)` | `src/infra/package-update-publication-owner.ts:598` | Retired |
| `anchor-after` | After `fsp.rmdir(anchor)` | `src/infra/package-update-publication-owner.ts:598` | Retired |
| `anchor-sync` | Directory fsync after anchor removal | `src/infra/package-update-publication-owner.ts:603` | Retired |
| `helper-before` | Before `fsp.unlink(helper())` | `src/infra/package-update-publication-owner.ts:626` | Retired |
| `helper-after` | After `fsp.unlink(helper())` | `src/infra/package-update-publication-owner.ts:626` | Retired |
| `helper-sync` | Directory fsync after helper removal | `src/infra/package-update-publication-owner.ts:628-630` | Retired |
| `live-gateway` | Fixture Doctor kills its updater after activation and service stop | `src/cli/update-cli/update-command-finalize.ts:449`; `src/cli/update-cli/update-command-fresh-doctor.ts:327` | Retired |
| `owed-plugin-retry` | Same post-activation Doctor kill prerequisite before exercising owed plugin retry | `src/cli/update-cli/update-command-finalize.ts:449`; `src/cli/update-cli/update-command-fresh-doctor.ts:327` | Retired |
| `data-at-risk` | Same post-activation Doctor kill prerequisite before exercising recorded data risk | `src/cli/update-cli/update-command-finalize.ts:449`; `src/cli/update-cli/update-command-fresh-doctor.ts:327` | Retired |
| `older-runtime` | `OPENCLAW_SURVIVOR_PACKAGE_FAULT=verification-rollback`: observe the published 2026.10.9 updater's `package_activation` publication receipt, then fail its post-publication Doctor | **v2026.10.9:** `src/infra/package-update-publication-owner.ts:474`; `src/cli/update-cli/update-command-finalize.ts:361` | **Kept unchanged:** the scenario starts that published updater, not current main's package executor |

Ten registered current-writer cuts target (a); the historical `older-runtime` cut targets (b) and remains. Its driver passes the published `root/openclaw.mjs` to the candidate handoff helper (`scripts/e2e/lib/upgrade-survivor/older-runtime-recovery.mjs:198-216`); the observer sees that published updater spawn at `older-runtime-recovery-observer.mjs:58-67`. For current writers, package routing returns through `runReleaseUpdateCli` at `src/cli/update-cli/update-command.ts:133-171`, before the legacy executor/finalization path. The replacement owner prepares a package at `src/update/run.ts:279`, checks it at `:313`, publishes a release at `:321`, and records a pending launcher trial at `:376`. It does not run the retired cuts.

## Scope

Removed the ten current-writer lanes, their family alias and package script; their scenario branches, private-evidence scheduler finalization, obsolete driver/fault/helper modules, recovery-only diagnostics, fixtures, test assertions and frozen-target dependency references. Readers of every removed exported symbol were listed with `rg` before source removal; LSP cannot index this worktree (it reports that it indexes the primary checkout only).

Kept `package-installed-recovery-older-runtime` unchanged, with only the shell/setup/evidence helpers it needs. All remaining `rg -n 'package-installed-recovery'` hits serve this one retained historical lane or its tests. Kept the generic file identity, package-tree, hashing and private evidence helpers because installed-terminal observers still import them, and kept their contract tests. Kept published-baseline package-activation recovery lanes and their fault helper: they test shipped older updaters. Searched documentation, release/workflow files and `scripts/AGENTS.md`; no stale lane/script references remain there.

Diff: **+129 / -4,002 lines (net -3,873)** across 36 files; runtime `src/` delta is zero.

| Deleted or reduced machinery | Added / removed lines |
| --- | --- |
| Ten obsolete harness files (`installed-recovery{,-access,-cases,-command,-fault,-gateway,-package}` and declarations) | +0 / -1,657 |
| Killed-updater Doctor package fixture | +0 / -25 |
| Diagnostics implementation/declaration/CLI | +10 / -431 |
| Recovery observation helpers/declarations | +3 / -133 |
| Remaining harness, scheduler, planners and package script | +41 / -267 |
| Tests and test fixtures | +75 / -1,489 |

## Proof

- `vitest-source`: one combined `ocx test` call covers 32 files: the touched tests, Docker E2E plan tests and direct helper consumers (result recorded below).
- Touched-file Oxfmt: clean.
- Script and tooling-test Oxlint: zero warnings or errors.
- Tooling-test typecheck: clean (`node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.root.tooling.json --incremental`).
- `git diff --check` and both touched Bash entrypoint syntax checks: clean.
- `rg -n 'package-installed-recovery'`: only the retained historical lane, its setup branch and its plan/workflow tests.

**Readiness is held; the all-green acceptance gate is not met.** The combined 32-file call found 83 failures across four files. The two fixture defects attributable to this cut were corrected (the shared config-recipe fixture directory and obsolete scheduler shared-mode assertions). One combined follow-up `ocx test` call passed all **7 affected consumer files / 173 tests**. The Docker E2E plan tests and other unchanged-input consumers passed in the original combined call.

The remaining 18 package-acceptance failures share an unchanged macOS Bash 3.2 workflow-shell failure: `0: ambiguous redirect`, followed by `SyntaxError: missing ) after argument list`. Exact-base proof at `bdb444f3e940` reproduces the representative `allows Package Acceptance Telegram deferral only for beta validation` case with exit 127 using `ocx test test/scripts/package-acceptance-workflow.test.ts -t 'allows Package Acceptance Telegram deferral only for beta validation' --maxWorkers=1`. That untouched workflow/test-runtime defect is outside this deletion's scope and remains unchanged. No tests were skipped to hide it.

Local ClawSweeper review on pushed head `18527af8df49f2fa02d712cd8360839c63dcaadc`: **complete; patch is correct; zero correctness/security findings; security cleared**. Execution proof/readiness remains separate from that source-review verdict.

No Docker replay is needed for a removed scenario, and the supplied failed run remains the base-side evidence. This changes test coverage only; users see no runtime change.

prs.title: fix: keep meeting summary progress and retry aligned with the notes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When Meetings was generating a summary, its progress message started 44 px to the right of the notes. At larger text sizes on a phone, that indent pushed the message onto two lines. If generation failed, the Retry label stayed small.

## User Impact

The progress message now starts where the notes will appear, and Retry follows the reader’s text size. Saved notes keep their existing layout.

## Why This Change Was Made

Summary feedback now uses the notes column instead of the general loading layout, with the spinner after the message. This changes presentation, not when the app generates a summary.

## Evidence

The existing before/after phone screenshots use the same 140% text setting. The message now fits on one line. In the mounted phone regression, generation failed, Retry grew to 18.2 px, and pressing Enter retried once and displayed the recovered notes. That regression failed before the repair and passed again on the publication checkout.

The earlier comparisons also covered both tablet orientations and desktop. Six saved-note crops were pixel-identical before and after. The tests used disposable meeting records and simulated generation; no live model ran. Switching tabs after a failed generation can still request the summary again without pressing Retry; that is a separate behavior, not fixed here. Original verified repair: `7ebee2c7ccdc4`.

|---|---|

prs.title: fix: use your selected text size for meeting downloads
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Increasing the text size in Appearance left the meeting download buttons and their feedback small. On a phone, even the meeting title stayed at its default size.

## User Impact

The meeting title on a phone, the Markdown and JSONL download buttons, and the download status or error now follow your selected text size. When the buttons need more room, they move onto separate rows. The export formats and permissions do not change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The meeting reader used fixed sizes for these labels. Using its existing text-size setting lets the buttons and feedback grow within the same header without changing how a download starts.

## Evidence

The existing before/after comparison shows the same phone and meeting at 140% text size. The title grew from 22 to 30.8 px, the button labels from 13 to 18.2 px, and the status from 14 to 19.6 px. Both buttons fit on their own rows, and the download confirmation remains readable.

All seven Meetings browser tests on the publication checkout passed, including preparing a download, displaying a size-limit error, and re-enabling the button. The earlier mounted comparisons covered phone, both tablet orientations, and desktop; 56 browser downloads matched the expected Markdown or JSONL bytes from disposable meetings. This PR does not fix a separate case where switching tabs during preparation discards a pending download. Original verified repair: `b3361c15b6e59`.
