prs.title: fix(channels): unblock ingress after a transient shutdown release failure
prs.body:
Closes #193019

## Main compatibility refresh — 2026-11-06

Published merge head `3e7a10e467cf355f5a02d71b899efa3eb4068832`, integrating main `b11b610d173cc6ff87eb026b6506c20fc7e5fd62` without rewriting PR history. The single `ingress-drain.ts` conflict is resolved preserving upstream failure callback extraction, queue-cap drops, selective custody retirement and test consolidation.

**Updated scope:** main #193423 already mitigates the old indefinite hold by retiring failed drains and permitting recovery of known never-adopted claims after disposal. This PR retains the bounded, token-fenced native cancellation-release retry before disposal; it does not claim current main remains indefinitely blocked. Pinned-main production overlay fails the focused retry regression (one release instead of two). Exhaustion coverage now follows upstream recovery after joined disposal; uncertain outcomes remain fenced.

**New-head verification:** 180 tests across 13 affected files passed; final worker handoff rerun 12 passed, coordinator independent rerun 12 passed. Targeted production/test typechecking, lint, format, source-line ratchet and scoped whitespace passed. Independent exact-head semantic review found no actionable P0–P2 findings. Frozen pnpm 12.15.0 install used target-identical manifests/lockfile. Test-line ratchet retains main's 25-line debt: pinned main is 25 over, candidate is 25 over, and the PR adds exactly its existing 182-line grant. No shared ceiling was changed. New-head CI is not claimed green.

**Proof provenance:** all Telegram/Claude live evidence below remains historical at `934ca4166ec58d9dc24deaf248051da44392a0a2`. Writer bytes are equivalent, but upstream custody/disposal, dependencies and test contracts changed; no live-proof equivalence or new-head live run is claimed. No production restart or new Telegram traffic occurred.

Later observed main `c63b3a2e58c45e82ea4d4955c1ac3bbb6a275d2e` also merge-probes cleanly; intervening changes are iOS tooling, so no additional merge was introduced.


## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: queued channel messages remain blocked when a pre-adoption cancellation release fails once during shutdown and the retained old drain continues holding its claim.

## User Impact

A transient known release failure can recover automatically so a replacement monitor can deliver the queued conversation. Cancellation preserves delivery retry history. No configuration or database migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Retained cancellation after abort now joins at most three token-fenced release attempts, with 1s and 2s backoffs. The existing settlement owner holds custody throughout. Explicit disposal prevents another attempt; failed completion, ordinary abandonment, standalone drains, and uncertain write outcomes keep their existing safety behavior. Exhaustion or an uncertain cancellation write remains observable and retains custody. The bounded retry can add up to three seconds of backoff to shutdown, plus storage I/O.

## Evidence

- A real production ingress monitor stop/restart with an actual isolated SQLite-backed queue fails on the unchanged base and passes with the repair. One known failure is injected before the native release write; the lifecycle callback is invoked only once. The replacement processes same-lane events in order, rejects stale-token writes, and does not replay already-adopted unrelated work.
- Focused drain, monitor, handoff and claim-owner suites: 73 tests passed. Added checks cover exhausted retries, nested uncertain outcomes, explicit disposal during backoff, takeover during retry, standalone cancellation and ordinary abandonment. Existing failed-completion and retry-history controls pass.
- Targeted production/test typechecking, lint, format, line-cap/test-line ratchets and whitespace checks are recorded in the local handoff.
- Independent shared autoreview: Codex GPT-6.1 Sol, medium reasoning, P0–P2, one pass over the complete uncommitted candidate against `06d4059a3d06` and supplied unchanged owner context; no actionable findings. This is evidence-based review, without a repository mount or test execution in the reviewer sandbox. Subsequent test edits only added required braces and an explicit already-completed return and removed a redundant default type argument. The coordinating parent independently inspected the final source and clean commit and reran all 10 boundary cases successfully.

**Initial test scope (historical; supplemented by the real Telegram/model run below):** proof here is the owning monitor/SQLite boundary with a synthetic pre-write failure. Actual SQLite locking, a complete Gateway process, a real agent/model, and Telegram transport were not exercised; no live outage reproduction is claimed. Exact live Gateway channel stop/restart under an actual storage lock remains a broader integration gap. No external API or transport contract changes here.

The dedicated allocation grants exactly 182 added test lines for this recovery regression and its distinct custody bounds; the shared baseline is unchanged. The change reuses existing owners and removes redundant release wrappers; production code grows by 12 lines. The four-suite run took 41.92s including worker preparation; the final boundary file took 4.63s in Vitest (50.61s wrapper including compiler preparation), and the parent independently measured 4.92s (53.90s wrapper). CI timing is unmeasured before publication.


## Additional shipped-entry-point evidence — 2026-11-05

The earlier Evidence section describes the initial monitor tests. This additional run used the real built CLI/Gateway, its plugin loader, and the public `channels.stop` / `channels.start` RPCs. It was **not another in-process monitor test**. The channel was a task-only local diagnostic plugin (`ingress-proof/default`), not Telegram. Its delivery callback deliberately calls synthetic `onDeferred` / `onAdopted`; **no real agent/model response or external transport was exercised, so this does not claim the root real-agent/model E2E gate is fully satisfied**.

**Isolation and provenance.** Separate task HOME, config, SQLite state, workspace and loopback ports; only the diagnostic plugin enabled; no provider credentials copied, no production Gateway restart/config/state change, no real-channel messages. The same fixture and one-shot fault wrapper ran against head `934ca4166ec58d9dc24deaf248051da44392a0a2` and runtime inputs from base `06d4059a3d06e1a34a3cacfd3f635b93fe803a38`. For the base run, only the two owner files were temporarily restored byte-for-byte from the base and rebuilt through the CLI; all other runtime inputs matched base (only the new test/allocation differed). This was a documented base-runtime overlay in the head checkout, not a Git checkout whose HEAD changed. Original source was restored afterward.

The external plugin uses public SDK `createChannelIngressMonitor` and `api.runtime.state.openChannelIngressQueue`. It throws exactly once **before** calling the native release operation, logs refresh only after the real queue returns `true`, and reads the committed queue via the public API. There is no SQLite method mock, SQL reset, forced owner retirement, manual second cancellation callback, or claimed actual `SQLITE_BUSY`. The fixture SHA-256 is `d1d039654e952e53eff1e39baa8680360637a26f3e8cf0bad372773df0b7fcb3`.

**Base observation.** Real Gateway PID `95449`: the channel stop RPC reported `stopped: true`, but the internal joined monitor stop rejected the injected error. Starting the replacement channel did not drain its lane. Only `unrelated` was synthetically adopted; `task` remained claimed and `waiting` pending. Committed `claimedAt` values advanced at `2026-11-05T11:03:19.612+09:00`, `2026-11-05T11:03:21.614+09:00`, and `2026-11-05T11:03:58.706+09:00`; heartbeat commit counts were `[4, 6, 43]`. This is a bounded observation of continued old-owner renewal, not an empirical claim that it can never recover.

```text
11:03:18 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"cancel-callback","generation":1,"pid":95449,"id":"task","ownerGeneration":1}
11:03:18 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"channel-abort","generation":1,"pid":95449,"ownerGeneration":1}
11:03:18 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"release-attempt","generation":1,"pid":95449,"attempt":1,"ownerGeneration":1}
11:03:18 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"injected-known-prewrite-failure","generation":1,"pid":95449,"ownerGeneration":1}
11:03:18 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"channel-stop-rejected","generation":1,"pid":95449,"message":"Error: Synthetic known cancellation release failure before native write","ownerGeneration":1}
11:03:18 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"cancel-callback-returned","generation":1,"pid":95449,"ownerGeneration":1}
11:03:18 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"heartbeat-committed","generation":1,"pid":95449,"ownerGeneration":1}
11:03:21 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"channel-started","generation":2,"pid":95449,"ownerGeneration":2}
11:03:21 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"heartbeat-committed","generation":2,"pid":95449,"ownerGeneration":1}
11:03:58 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"heartbeat-committed","generation":2,"pid":95449,"ownerGeneration":1}
```

**Head observation.** Real Gateway PID `93148` remained the same across channel generation 1→2. One cancellation callback caused one known pre-write failure, then release attempt 2 committed about one second later and joined stop succeeded. The replacement synthetically adopted `task`, then `waiting`; the already-adopted `unrelated` was not replayed. The old token's release/complete/refresh all returned `false`, the successor token differed, and re-enqueue of `unrelated` returned `completed`. Final pending and claimed sets were empty.

```text
10:58:29 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"channel-started","generation":1,"pid":93148,"ownerGeneration":1}
10:58:59 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"adopted","generation":1,"pid":93148,"id":"unrelated","ownerGeneration":1}
10:59:55 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"cancel-callback","generation":1,"pid":93148,"id":"task","ownerGeneration":1}
10:59:55 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"release-attempt","generation":1,"pid":93148,"attempt":1,"ownerGeneration":1}
10:59:55 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"injected-known-prewrite-failure","generation":1,"pid":93148,"ownerGeneration":1}
10:59:56 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"release-attempt","generation":1,"pid":93148,"attempt":2,"ownerGeneration":1}
10:59:56 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"release-result","generation":1,"pid":93148,"id":"task","committed":true,"ownerGeneration":1}
10:59:56 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"channel-stop-joined","generation":1,"pid":93148,"ownerGeneration":1}
11:00:11 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"channel-started","generation":2,"pid":93148,"ownerGeneration":2}
11:00:11 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"stale-token-check","generation":2,"pid":93148,"release":false,"complete":false,"refresh":false,"changed":true}
11:00:11 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"adopted","generation":2,"pid":93148,"id":"task","ownerGeneration":2}
11:00:11 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"adopted","generation":2,"pid":93148,"id":"waiting","ownerGeneration":2}
11:00:14 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"dedupe-check","generation":2,"pid":93148,"kind":"completed"}
11:00:37 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"channel-stop-joined","generation":2,"pid":93148,"ownerGeneration":2}
```

**Shipped command path.** Under each task-only environment: `corepack pnpm openclaw gateway run --bind loopback --auth none --verbose`; then `corepack pnpm openclaw gateway call` with `--expect-url` pinned to that task's configured loopback Gateway, using `ingressProof.seed`, `ingressProof.arm`, `channels.stop`, `ingressProof.snapshot`, `channels.start`, `ingressProof.snapshot`, and `ingressProof.dedupe` (head). Public lifecycle params were `{"channel":"ingress-proof","accountId":"default"}`. All these RPC commands exited 0; the base's reported stop success is distinguished above from its monitor failure. Both task Gateways later handled SIGTERM and exited 0 with clean shutdown. No commit/push was required for this instrumentation.

**Interpretation and limits.** A generally slow model cannot explain this comparison because no model runs; identical fixture, queue, lane and fault behavior plus the advancing native timestamps distinguish a retained old-owner claim from a delayed initial read. However, the fixture deliberately supplies deferred/cancelled work and observes its own callback receipts. Its synthetic adoption is not evidence of agent execution, outbound send, Telegram acceptance, or user-visible response. It does not prove an actual database lock, indefinite blockage beyond the observed interval, every channel adapter, or a whole-Gateway process restart. It proves a real Gateway-hosted local channel stop/replacement through shipped entry points with actual SQLite persistence. Whether this layer satisfies the requested real-behavior gate remains for review; the broader real agent/model/transport gap is explicit.


## Real Telegram and real model recovery evidence — 2026-11-05

**Observed result:** recovery eventually succeeded through the production Telegram adapter, real Claude CLI agent/model, and Telegram Bot API. It did **not** succeed on the first replacement: the task relay refused two overlapping local polls and the adapter automatically restarted twice before both replies completed. The human operator confirmed in the Telegram client that the replies arrived in A → B order. Per-event counts below are backed by the queue, transcript and Bot API receipts; the human confirmation specifically establishes client-visible order.

Pinned PR head: `934ca4166ec58d9dc24deaf248051da44392a0a2`. The requesting user confirmed their dedicated bot was unused elsewhere, then sent a fresh exact handshake and prescribed A/B prompts manually in the verified private DM. No automated user account or team QA pool was used. The isolated Gateway had task-owned config/state/workspace/ports. A parent-owned, destination-bound protected HTTPS relay consumed the stored token sentinel; no credential value was extracted or copied into the Gateway. The operator Gateway was untouched.

Temporary instrumentation held only A before real admission and injected one known error before the original claim's native cancellation release write. It never invoked synthetic adoption. Native cancellation, the PR's existing bounded writer retry, real Telegram replay, real agent/model execution and outbound delivery remained production paths. Setup `deleteWebhook` was a recorded local no-op after verified empty webhook; no upstream webhook deletion or queue flush occurred. Command-menu deletion attempts were refused locally.

Measured timeline, KST:

```text
13:31:16.764  A held before native adoption
13:31:58.907  bound B observed by real Telegram poller
13:32:36.938  read-only task SQLite: A claimed, B pending; same lane; attempts=0
13:32:38.283  one known pre-write release failure for original A token
13:32:39.285  second release attempt for that same token (+1002ms)
13:32:40      manual channel replacement starts
13:32:41      local concurrent-poll refusal; automatic restart scheduled
13:32:47–48   first automatic restart also hits local poll guard
13:32:58      second automatic restart starts
13:32:59.308  real A adoption/completion write commits with new claim token
13:33:03.954  Telegram accepts final A response
13:33:04.053  real B adoption/completion write commits
13:33:06.414  Telegram accepts final B response
```

The old long-poll request remained in the relay until its bounded upstream request returned after the downstream client was cancelled. The relay's single-poll guard refused the two successor attempts rather than starting another upstream poller. This was task relay lifecycle behavior, not a second bot consumer or a newly fixed PR behavior. No queue reset, forced retirement, manual second cancellation callback or failed-send retry was used to recover.

Final read-only SQLite inspection found exactly A and B, both `completed`, both attempts=0, with no pending/claimed work. The real agent transcript contains exactly two assistant records matching the prescribed A and B responses in order, both `provider=claude-cli`, `api=cli`, with actual usage: A input10/output181/cache-write11936; B input10/output81/cache-read11936/cache-write710. Telegram returned two distinct accepted message receipts, A then B; no duplicate-send refusal or uncertain-send event occurred. Native launch/probe/maintenance subprocess counts are not misrepresented as exactly two model requests. The separate one-shot provider setup qualification is excluded from this recovery proof.

The native Claude child used its existing login without copying credentials, with global home file writes denied by an OS policy, tools/customizations and native session persistence disabled. Gateway/OpenClaw state stayed task-owned. This was a real provider, not mock-openai or synthetic `onAdopted`. Source instrumentation was restored byte-for-byte, Git was clean at the pinned head, and the uninstrumented head build completed successfully. The Gateway logged a clean shutdown in82ms; its launcher group received SIGTERM and reported-15, so that wrapper is not reported as exit0. Parent verified the protected relay ended code0 and both task ports closed. No live task processes remain; persistent review Remote is retained.

**Client observation:** on 2026-11-05 at 13:43 KST the human operator confirmed the replies arrived in order. This is a human client observation, not an inference from Bot API acceptance.

**Limits:** Actual SQLite locking, every transport/provider, and whole-Gateway restart were not tested or required for this known pre-write failure. The earlier base/head Gateway comparison and existing safety regressions are separate supporting evidence. This run establishes eventual real-channel/model/outbound recovery with the explicit transient relay failures above; it is not presented as a clean first-restart run or proof of all client-rendering behavior.


## Current-head real Telegram / Claude recovery proof — 2026-11-18

This section supersedes the earlier statement that live proof exists only for the old head. The earlier runs and their limitations remain historical evidence, not evidence combined with this run.

**Pinned head:** `3e7a10e467cf355f5a02d71b899efa3eb4068832`. The same retained source/build/dependency manifests were verified, including 21,484 compiled files and the temporary scoped instrumentation. The supported Node 24.22.1 shipped CLI/Gateway path was used, with the production Telegram adapter, actual SQLite-backed ingress, public native `channels.stop` / `channels.start`, and real `claude-cli / claude-haiku-4-5` responses. A separate successful provider qualification preceded this live run and is not counted as recovery proof.

**Observed live sequence (KST):** A was held before native adoption at 18:04:45.753; B was durably pending in the same lane at 18:05:18.331. Exactly one known error was injected before the original token's native cancellation-release write. The same token's second release attempt occurred 1,001 ms after the first. It committed before the channel stop joined at 18:05:21.207, with payload and attempt/error history unchanged. The outstanding old long poll was joined before the native replacement start returned at 18:05:45.663. The replacement acquired a distinct token; stale release, complete and refresh all returned false. Native adoption committed A then B, and both completed-event duplicate probes returned duplicate. The machine lifecycle and relay observations matched at 18:05:55.890.

**Real provider and delivery correlation:** two successful intended Claude CLI output records matched the exact expected A/B reply hashes in order (4,207 ms and 1,470 ms, 23 output bytes each). The protected Bot API journal contains exactly two message send intents and two accepted sends, A at 18:05:52.705 then B at 18:05:55.725. At 18:12 KST the human requester confirmed receipt in the Telegram client in response to the A/B receipt check. This is not inferred solely from API acceptance.

**Isolation and retained failures:** the user confirmed the dedicated bot was idle elsewhere. Gateway HOME/config/state/workspace and loopback ports were task-local. The parent retained protected credential custody; native Claude used its existing login with the unchanged home-write-denying policy. No credential copying, global config change, production Gateway restart, memory-guard change or provider substitution occurred. The first Node fresh-A attempt timed out before native receipt; a single scoped non-advancing read identified that exact pending A. The successful run consumed that real pending update through native polling, without resend, synthetic enqueue, queue flush, offset rewind or replay. B was a new human input. Earlier harness, Bun-memory, OAuth-refresh and missed-cue failures are retained and do not count as passes. Node host admission and real provider qualification passed before this successful run.

**Cleanup:** the task Gateway wrapper received SIGTERM and exited -15; its listener closed. The parent stopped and joined the protected relay with exit 0 and independently confirmed both task ports closed. A shutdown-time BrokenPipe and an uncertain `getUpdates` result (`send:false`) are retained: the downstream Gateway had already ended while an outstanding read was being closed. There was no uncertain outbound send or additional accepted message. The retained Remote review session is not an active Gateway or bot consumer.

**Limits / remaining status:** the fault was a known synthetic pre-write failure around the real native write, not an actual `SQLITE_BUSY` reproduction. This proves the current-head scoped native channel stop/replacement with real model and Telegram delivery, not every adapter, a whole-Gateway restart or Bun parity. CI remains red on `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` and aggregate `openclaw/ci-gate`; this live proof neither resolves nor hides those failures and does not claim maintainer approval or merge readiness. No source push was needed for this evidence update.

prs.title: fix: keep Lobsterdex cards in place when the visit count reaches ten
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On a phone, the Lobsterdex visit count jumped from the right side of the description to a new line on the left when the collection went from 9 to 10 visits. The first row of cards moved down with it.

## User Impact

The count stays beside the description as new palettes visit, and the cards stay in place. At enlarged text sizes the description can wrap without sending the count to another row.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reserve space for the visit count in the phone header. The collection cards, visit tracking and wider layouts do not need to change.

## Evidence

On the 390 px phone at default text size, the tenth visit used to push the first card row down 35.39 px. After the fix it moved 0 px. At 140% text the cards start 48.59 px higher than before. The tablet and desktop headers were pixel-identical to main at both text sizes. Both new browser regressions failed on main and passed with the fix, including a visit recorded in another tab.

Mounted Control UI with a synthetic browser-local collection, 390 × 844 emulated phone. The first pair shows 9 visits and the second shows 10. Comparison: stock main `da13d2a9c3023` versus local repair `ab8c6ad0fd6c3`.

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| ![Nine visits: the badge fits on the right above the first row of cards](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a1d9f5ed-6c75-426f-9a65-96bdfa4c2b21) | ![Nine visits: the count and description share the same row](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8fa22d6a-27c5-4401-875f-3d955d76cbb8) |
| ![Ten visits: the badge drops below the description and pushes the cards down](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fe5bc0e2-2fb3-454b-8e2e-bb8673e7baa4) | ![Ten visits: the badge stays on the right and the first card row stays still](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e655a267-35bc-4ebb-b5e8-d809dd4b3c16) |

Contributor: @vyctorbrzezowski.

prs.title: refactor(agents): bind only the caller's session source into the run registry
prs.body:
## Problem

R1b of the one-admission receipt cluster (follows #203664). `prepareAgentRunAdmission` binds one run source into the agent run registry. On `main` that source is `compose([callerSource, operatorAuthority.assertCurrent])`. Every reader of the registry source (`captureAgentRunDelegatedSourceAssertion`, `validateAgentRunDelegatedAuthority`, `getActiveAgentRunDelegatedAuthority`, the native pre-tool recovery lease and `prepared.assertSourceCurrent`) therefore re-checks operator permission mid-run. Admission already checks it once.

## Change

- `prepareAgentRunAdmission` composes only the caller's session source (`params.assertSourceCurrent`: transcript write token, entry lifecycle and other data fences) into the registry. `operatorAuthority.assertCurrent` is no longer part of that composition.
- `captureAgentRunDelegatedSourceAssertion` and `validateAgentRunDelegatedAuthority` are unchanged: they keep the session checks, run occurrence, `readActiveAgentRunDelegatedAuthority` and `approvalLeases`. They lose only the operator re-check, because it is no longer in the source they read.
- Not changed: `readOperatorAuthority` and the operator lease retain/release (R5/R6 scope), receipt-boolean producers (R1c).

Production: 1 file, +2/−3. No new name, flag, hook or guard.

Tests (all deleted cases assert a refusal after an operator permission change while the run, its tools or its catalog were already started; this PR removes that re-check):
- `admitted-run-context.test.ts` "fences native recovery": dropped the 5 lines that expected the recovery lease and `prepared.assertSourceCurrent` to refuse after the operator source threw.
- `operator-access-policy.invalidation.test.ts`: deleted "checks each person's original grant once through deep lineage and again before the next effect" (the operator re-check through the parent run's registry source).
- `mcp-http.runtime.test.ts` "does not let a source-less cached list hide a later admitted writer": dropped the tail that expected a refusal after the operator signal aborted.
- `mcp-http.runtime.portal-readiness.test.ts`: dropped the `cached authority` case.
- `harness/host-capability.source-lifetime.test.ts`: deleted "records completed turn bookkeeping while revocation blocks the next tool effect".
- `harness/tool-authority.runtime.admission.test.ts`: dropped the mid-publish "Plugin grant revoked" step.

Kept unchanged and green: the stale-generation, writer, occurrence and source-failure tests ("revokes after replacement/rotation/abort/claim-loss", "retains the first source failure after revocation", the `session-sharing-preparation` rollback fence, the retained-source lifetime cases).

## What users see

A run that has started is not refused when the operator's permission changes during the run. A queued run still goes through admission and is refused visibly. Stop still cancels. Stale transcript writes are still refused.

## Evidence

Head `c0dff1b00ad3`:

- **Importer run:** one `ocx test` call on all 414 test files that import `admitted-run-context.ts` or its test support, `OPENCLAW_NODE_TEST_PLAN_CONTINUE_ON_FAILURE=1` (~71 min at load 20-48). Reds:
  - 6 files fixed above (obsolete mid-run revocation cases); rerun green.
  - `clawrouter-failover.integration`, `agent-runner-required-maintenance.pending-input` (60 s timeout under load): green in a standalone rerun on this head; neither passes an operator authority.
  - Red on the merge base `0bc6bd400ebd` too (separate run): `mcp-http.async-scope`, `cron.scheduled-policy-adoption.integration` (3 cases), `question.communication`, `question.recovery`, `settled-turn-finalization.incomplete`.
- **Typecheck / lint:** `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:test` clean; oxfmt and oxlint clean on the 7 files. `pnpm check:changed` not run locally (its SQLite worker ratchet aborts on the local heap, #203466); CI covers it.
- **One-admission E2E** (isolated Gateway, real model, exact head `c0dff1b00ad3`): `pass: true`. `results.jsonl` (50 KB transcript) is kept with the task proof. `verdict.json`:
  ```json
  {"pass":true,"checks":[{"id":"R.running-turn-finishes","pass":true,"detail":{"state":"final","toolEnds":3,"toolEndsAfterRevoke":3}},{"id":"Q.queued-input-refused-visibly","pass":true,"detail":{"accepted":true,"providerRequestsWithQueuedMarker":0,"visibleRefusalInTranscript":true}},{"id":"S.stop-cancels","pass":true,"detail":{"abort":{"ok":true,"aborted":true},"state":"aborted","requestsWithStopMarker":1}}]}
  ```
- **Local ClawSweeper review** (exact head): `review_status: complete`, "patch is correct", 0 findings.

prs.title: fix: keep command palette text as typed
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Control UI command palette can show a native correction for text such as `test`, even when the lowercase text is intentional. The same field is used for search terms and short prompts, so automatic changes can rewrite either one.

## User Impact

## Why This Change Was Made

Both the loading and loaded palette use the same field and pass it the active mode. The shared field sets the browser’s writing preferences directly, without rewriting input or changing keyboard handling. It also owns the existing per-mode line limits, removing the separate mappings in the two views.

## Evidence

- The focused Chromium regression failed on the base because the palette allowed native writing assistance. It passes on the fix, including the first-open handoff, lowercase text retention on `Tab`, and both mode policies.

- No app styling changed. The native macOS popup and passive spelling underlines have not been visually verified on a real Mac; Linux Chromium cannot capture that system UI. Draft for review; broad CI was not run.

prs.title: feat(update): capture PostgreSQL stores while the Gateway serves
prs.body:
## Summary

### High Level TLDR

On updates that take a pre-migration image, OpenClaw starts capturing PostgreSQL stores while the Gateway serves. It reuses unchanged captures after taking exclusive ownership and captures changed stores again. For a custom service or foreground Gateway, `openclaw update --wait-for-gateway-stop <seconds>` prepares the update first, then asks the operator to stop the Gateway before activation. https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/196154

SQLite stores still get their capture after the stop. The default managed-service flow owns its stop and restart. The installed updater must contain this change. The landing scope retains both the stop handoff and default PostgreSQL capture; this is not approval to merge before verification.

### What Problem This Solves

The previous updater required exclusive state ownership to capture PostgreSQL, even though each store can be copied from a repeatable-read snapshot while the Gateway serves. A Gateway with an external owner could therefore require the operator to stop it before staging and validation, extending downtime.

### Root Cause

The updater now records the generation and reuse digest from the same snapshot as each capture. Under exclusive ownership, it compares the current digest and captures any changed or unreadable store again. This usually includes shared state because the updater records its run there. Restore still checks the existing generation fingerprint. The reuse digest has a theoretical collision risk when two row sets have the same count and sum of 64-bit hashes.

The low-space skip runs before the final capture copies any data. An earlier online capture can already have a server schema and manifest, so the skip retires the schema through the existing capture owner before removing files. A failed drop preserves the manifest. Online server copies use the existing PostgreSQL prune marker, keyed to the online capture directory. A later online server capture can reap a marked copy after its directory is gone. Retained captures and restored live schemas stay in place. https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201579

## Verification

### Evidence

- **Pushed head `edca9115`:** [all four PostgreSQL conformance shards, `pg16-smoke`, and the required CI gate passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44860715131). The published-driver job was skipped. Static checks passed. Earlier CI on `466ab69d` covered [low-space cleanup and manifest retention](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44853257676/job/136691538342) and [orphaned PostgreSQL schema cleanup](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44853257676/job/136691537808).
- **Pushed head regression:** the mixed-store test failed on `edca9115`. The online pass privately copied the shared SQLite file before deciding whether the PostgreSQL export fit. On a nearly full Gateway volume, a temporary copy is enough to exhaust space.
- **Signed, unpublished correction `2c2f8fd234e639593bddf3e890f2f5c85ad7d063`:** read-only discovery preserves existing PostgreSQL registrations without staging SQLite. The mixed-store regression passed. With an 85,880,832-byte SQLite file and 48,336,896 bytes free, the optional PostgreSQL export was deferred, free space fell by just 4,096 bytes, and SQLite accepted another write. The existing registered agent row survived. Focused PostgreSQL 17 compatibility, retention, and recovery checks passed.

### Real behavior proof

- **Package:** built `2c2f8fd2` with the repository's published-driver CI recipe. The tarball checker passed; the embedded commit matched the signed SHA. Tarball SHA-256: `5ea5bded0703937e3b2568d89d25697aad5f535b79966df8d5ac10df086b609a`.
- **Latest stable → signed candidate:** on a disposable Linux VM, the published `2026.11.6` build (`06afb10d`) used a real systemd user service and PostgreSQL 17.11 for shared state and agent history. Its installed `openclaw update --tag <candidate.tgz> --yes --json` restarted the service onto `2c2f8fd2`. The serving build was checked by authenticated RPC, not by version alone. A pre-existing shared row and durable chat message survived.
- **Signed updater → forced rollback:** the repository's failing-Doctor successor activated, then Doctor exited 1. Database and package rollback both exited 0. systemd served `2c2f8fd2` again; both PostgreSQL store IDs, the shared row, and both acknowledged messages survived in restored namespaces. A separate successful update by that same installed signed updater preserved all three acknowledged messages. On both candidate-driven runs, `/readyz` responded while the original service PID and an online capture directory were present; the stopped-state receipt explicitly recorded reuse of the agent's online capture.
- **Retention:** both retained capture directories had manifests matching the PostgreSQL state and agent store IDs. Rollback retained the replaced namespaces for manual recovery. On the successful hop, Doctor reported an unknown writer after the snapshot; the updater retained the recovery image rather than risking those later writes.
- **Earlier contributor evidence:** the [foreground macOS Git test](https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/commit/7da4339c06f71c3ae52f30f67a16168c16cf7e91) reported survival of a write between capture and stop and about 287 seconds of downtime versus 941 seconds on its stopped-first baseline. Those timings were not remeasured on the signed correction.

### What was not tested or remains blocked

The separate full source build still fails `check-plugin-sdk-exports`: **5,396,987 bytes vs. a 5,385,536-byte limit** on the untouched base, the pushed head, and the corrected production code. The published-driver tarball passed a distinct CI recipe; it does not make the full build green. Independent whole-diff review stopped before producing a verdict. The correction is not pushed, so hosted CI and [ClawSweeper's P1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200294#issuecomment-6932530027) are still tied to `edca9115`, not the tested correction.

prs.title: fix(build): Git install updates fail with "Declaration input escapes checkout" since #198661
prs.body:
Closes #200357

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw update` on a Git install fails at `preflight-build` with `Declaration input escapes checkout`, and the install stays on its old commit. This affects updates started by v2026.11.5 and earlier, which do not have #189463, when the target contains #198661 and the install's dependency versions differ from the target's for a package the SDK declarations reach. Today's trigger is the `undici` 8.12.3 to 8.12.4 bump in #200006. The CLI and `update.run` fail the same way, because `update.run` hands off to `openclaw update --yes`.

## User Impact

User impact: Git installs can update to main again. Normal builds keep the fast command-line declaration pass. A dependency that exists only outside the checkout still fails the build and names the escaped file.

## Why This Change Was Made

On POSIX the updater builds each candidate in a worktree inside the install it replaces (`<install>/.artifacts/.openclaw-update-preflight-*/worktree`). The Anthropic and OpenAI SDK declarations type `RequestInit` with relative `node_modules/undici` imports up to 10 parent directories up, so the compiler also reads the install's own `node_modules/undici`. The command-line pass from #198661 cannot deny that read, so it fails the build. When both sides have the same `undici` version the compiler does not read the parent copy separately, so updates between matching versions pass; any dependency bump between the installed release and the target brings the failure back. Updaters built from main set `OPENCLAW_RUN_NODE_SKIP_DTS_BUILD=1` (#189463) and skip this step, but no release tag contains that change yet.

This keeps #198661's intent: declarations still depend only on files inside the checkout, and normal checkouts keep the fast pass. #198661 accepted "parent-install shadowing now fails loudly" because the command line cannot hide those reads. The updater's own preflight worktree is such a parent install, and already shipped updaters choose that path, so moving the worktree cannot fix updates from them.

When the command-line pass lists a file that is outside the checkout by path and by real path, the build discards that pass and emits through the bounded API filesystem from before #198661, which treats outside candidates as absent (the contract from #158674). Links that leave the checkout still fail as before. If the bounded compile fails, the error shows the compiler's diagnostic first, then the escaped read.

Maintainer decision: this undoes #198661 behavior change 1 for parent installs (fall back to the bounded compile instead of failing).

## Evidence

### Runtime output

Fresh Git install at `v2026.11.4` (d843d6af39a4), built with `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && pnpm build && pnpm ui:build`, macOS arm64, home directory not a symlink, internal disk. Gateway stopped, isolated state and config. Command:

```
OPENCLAW_UPDATE_DEV_TARGET_REF=<target sha> node <install>/openclaw.mjs update --channel dev --yes --no-restart
```

Base, target f947bdc94981:

```
install at d843d6af39a4 (2026.11.4), target f947bdc94981
update exit 1
install now at d843d6af39a4
[... 8 lines cut ...]
  ✓ preflight-checkout (229ms)
  ✓ preflight-deps-install (15.85s)
  ✗ preflight-build (23.11s)
    Failing check preflight-build (command-failed): Error: Declaration input escapes checkout: [redacted-path]
  ✓ preflight-cleanup (13.21s)
Failed: validating
[... 1 line cut ...]
```

`preflight-build` fails on the escape and the install stays at d843d6af39a4. The updater redacts the path. Building f947bdc94981 by hand in the same nested layout shows it:

```
Error: Declaration input escapes checkout: <install>/node_modules/undici/types/utility.d.ts -> <install>/node_modules/.pnpm/undici@8.12.2/node_modules/undici/types/utility.d.ts.
```

Head, target 133cfd5d3f76 (this PR), same built install:

```
install at d843d6af39a4 (2026.11.4), target 133cfd5d3f76
update exit 0
install now at 133cfd5d3f76
[... 8 lines cut ...]
  ✓ preflight-checkout (366ms)
  ✓ preflight-deps-install (27.42s)
  ✓ preflight-build (330.54s)
  ✓ candidate-state-snapshot (2.04s)
  ✓ candidate-doctor (14.96s)
  [... 18 lines cut ...]
  ✓ git-checkout (18.96s)
  ✓ git-runtime-activation (111ms)
  ✓ database snapshot (3.65s)
  ✓ database migration writes (0ms)
  ✓ git-verify-head (14ms)
  ✓ preflight-cleanup (15.4s)
```

`preflight-build` passes, the candidate checks run, and the install moves to 133cfd5d3f76.

Bisect from the same install: target 1c1814a0bf78 (parent of #198661) exit 0, target 5a7d1718aa5 (#198661) exit 1 with the same escape.

Scope check against main 54d85be92e92 (undici 8.12.4 since #200006), same harness:

| From | Entry point | Target | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| v2026.11.5 (e13cf15ece9b, undici 8.12.3) | CLI | 54d85be92e92 | exit 1, `preflight-build` escape, install unchanged |
| v2026.11.4 (d843d6af39a4) | `gateway call update.run` | 54d85be92e92 | handoff `openclaw update --yes` fails at `preflight-build` with the escape, install unchanged |
| v2026.11.5 | CLI | b9d1882fab51 (main-based, undici 8.12.3) | exit 0, install moved |
| install at b9d1882fab51 (has #189463) | CLI | 54d85be92e92 | exit 0, install moved |

Nested build of 54d85be92e92 inside the v2026.11.5 install:

```
Declaration input escapes checkout: <install>/node_modules/undici/types/utility.d.ts -> <install>/node_modules/.pnpm/undici@8.12.3/node_modules/undici/types/utility.d.ts.
```

### Tests

- `test/scripts/native-declaration-boundary.test.ts`, `bounds optional SDK relative imports to a checkout nested in a parent install`: on base f947bdc94981 it fails with `Declaration input escapes checkout`. On head it passes. With the fix reverted by `git apply -R` it fails again. It also checks that changing the parent install changes neither the declarations nor the inputs.
- Declaration consumers on head: `native-declaration-boundary`, `tsdown-declaration-resolution` (the escaped ancestor module, ambient types, package symlink, source symlink and source reference cases still refuse), `native-declaration-subprocess`, `write-plugin-sdk-entry-dts`, `run-tsgo-worktree`, `prepare-extension-package-boundary-artifacts.native`: 6 files, 77 passed, 7 skipped.
- `pnpm check:changed --base f947bdc94981` on head: passed. The dead export scan was skipped: on this base it reports unused exports only in files this change does not touch.

### Local review

Local ClawSweeper (`review --local-range`, Claude runner) on base f947bdc94981, head 133cfd5d3f76, complete review: patch is correct, security cleared, no maintainer decision required, patch rating B. Remaining: one P3 suggesting the escape note be added only when the bounded compile fails on module resolution. The compiler's diagnostic now comes first; matching diagnostic codes was left out to keep the error path simple.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Long question titles, answers, or rejection details in an inline answer summary can extend past the chat transcript edge. People lose part of the question or the reason their answer was not sent, even on desktop.

## User Impact

Inline answer summaries wrap their complete text instead of clipping it. Short summaries stay compact, and sending, retrying, and confirming an answer work as before. Standalone question pages and attachment cards are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Apply wrapping only at the inline async-summary owner instead of changing global transcript overflow, clamping diagnostics, or adding controls. Both existing Retry placements continue to use the same failed outbox item and operation.

## Evidence

- A fresh real-Chromium regression fails on the base at all three reported column widths and passes with the fix. Existing live-region and inline Retry placement checks remain green. Six browser cases pass; the direct async-question consumer suite passes 38 tests.
- UI typecheck, targeted formatting, Stylelint, oxlint, and diff sanity passed. Browser regression wrapper wall time: 1.79 s; direct consumer wrapper: 3.78 s. CI timing is pending.
- Matched source-UI checks cover 320/390 px phones and desktop, light/dark, valid unbroken titles/answers, long benign diagnostics, and an ordinary short summary. Short-summary dimensions and measured summary pixels are unchanged; nearby normal message and document-card geometry is unchanged.
- The production UI was also built and exercised at 390 × 900. The same valid long title, answer, and diagnostic clip before the fix and fully wrap afterward. Served entry-asset bytes were checked against the retained production output; the two runtime source files were hash-bound to their baseline/candidate revisions.
- Normal UI controls verified Retry answer → awaiting delivery confirmation → canonical Answer sent, unchanged queue identity and answer payload, preserved independent draft/focus, and scrolling back to the earlier document.
- Local ClawSweeper completed a full read-only committed-range review, exit 0/status complete, for base 42f8c5bcb9f51973338a3d26c0e75fe7c6be65d7 through head 411f999a3fbad5d7de6355ca368937eaf33a7a19: keep_open/high, no review findings or identified correctness/security defect. It did not receive external screenshots. Its requested built-client proof was subsequently captured and inspected without changing the reviewed commit.

**Proof scope:** these are real source/production-built Control UI clients using supported synthetic Gateway responses, not an actual Gateway/backend or external-provider integration test. No live external message or provider call was made. The production bundle used the supported local preview harness. Broad CI has not run; this PR is intentionally a draft for human review, not a merge request.

prs.title: fix: tell similarly named subagents apart in the panel
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Two subagents with names that start the same could look identical in the Subagents panel. Opening one did not help: the transcript header hid the same ending. In the phone example, neither row showed whether it was the North or South district run.

## User Impact

You can tell similar runs apart before opening one and confirm which transcript you are reading afterward. Ordinary names wrap. Very long names keep both ends visible in the list; you can scroll the full title in the transcript without moving Back or Stop.

## Why This Change Was Made

The list and transcript header each clipped names to a single line. The list now gives names room while keeping exceptionally long rows bounded. The header lets the title scroll only when it needs to, leaving the transcript and its controls accessible.

## Evidence

The existing phone comparisons show the two district rows and the South district transcript. The first name previously extended 456 px beyond its column and now fits. The short **Reading receipts** title still fits on one line. Opening a child and returning restored focus to its row and preserved the parent draft.

The atlas checked the list and transcript on a phone, both tablet orientations, and desktop at two text sizes. Both phone and desktop regressions failed before the fix and passed again on the publication checkout, including keyboard access to the end of a 512-character title. Only synthetic sessions were used. No real subagent was started, contacted, or stopped. Original verified repair: `c1fd7fdb7b25b`.

prs.title: fix: keep a steered document's text in later runs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A message steered into a running turn can carry a document attachment. The model sees the message with its media note and the rendered document text. The transcript stored only the typed text. The next run replayed the shorter message, so its bytes changed in the middle of history. That broke the provider's prompt-cache prefix from that point on, and later runs lost the document text. Normal sent turns did not have this problem.

## User Impact

After you steer a message with a document into a running turn, later runs replay the same message the model first saw. They keep the document text, and the cached prefix stays intact. Nothing changes in config, and no new storage field is added: the existing `__openclaw.modelPromptProjection` field holds the text.

## Why This Change Was Made

One owner already freezes what the model saw for a sent turn: `installModelPromptProjection` (`attempt-llm-boundary.ts`). It captures the text into the turn recorder's `modelPromptProjection` before the request leaves. It only ever looked at the recorder that started the attempt. A steered message has its own recorder, so its row kept plain text.

The change makes the same owner capture steers too:

- The attempt's transcript-context registry now keeps each queued user message's recorder (`attempt-user-transcript-context-registry.ts`, `attempt-session-prepare.ts`).
- `installModelPromptProjection` walks those contexts. It captures each steered message's expanded text through that message's own recorder, with the same `captureModelPromptProjection` contract a sent turn uses.
- Send and steer now share one projection path. No steer-only builder was added.
- **Second cause, found once continuation was on (#203568):** on OpenAI Responses, the steered message carries a runtime-context carrier that is marked `retained`. A later prompt update moved that carrier ahead of the cached assistant tool call, so the next continued request failed the prefix check (`history_changed`) and sent full history. Retained carriers now keep their position. The carrier-anchoring logic moved into its own module (`openai-responses-carrier-anchoring.ts`) so the replay file stays under its line cap.

Out of scope, recorded as a follow-up: the live steer request describes each attachment twice. `chat-attachments.ts:457` appends a portable marker, and `chat-send-message-injection.ts:305` prepends a staged note. Replay now equals the live bytes, so this PR does not change that.

**Production LOC:** +112 / −43, net **+69**, measured against main after #203568. This is the real number. It covers the registry field, the projection loop over queued recorders, and the retained-carrier fix. About 40 of the added lines are the anchoring logic moved into its own module.

## Evidence

**Prefix journey (#201723).** The existing steer step now steers with a `text/plain` document (`STEER-DOC-BODY`). The journey checks that the steered request contains the document text, and that every later request extends earlier ones byte for byte.

| Journey | base 8d1e59c2fddc | head |
|---|---|---|
| anthropic-messages | **red**: break at step `cron`, message 38 (the steered message). Live: media note + text + document; replay: typed text only. | green |
| openai-responses | not run on base | green (continuation stays on across the steer) |
| openai-completions, google, bedrock | not run separately; CI runs all five | — |

**Responses replay regression:** `openai-responses-async-replay.test.ts` adds a test where a prompt update follows a retained steering carrier.

**Focused regression:** `agent-session-steering-context.test.ts`, test "replays a steered document attachment with the bytes the model first saw". It steers expanded text whose stored turn is the plain text, reopens the session from durable storage, and asserts the replay keeps the first request's bytes. Red on base (replay holds only the plain text), green on head.

**Mutation:** the projection loop skips queued recorders (only the attempt's own recorder is captured, as on base). Both the focused regression and the anthropic journey turn red. Run in a scratch copy of head.

**Scratch Gateway E2E.** Native `https://api.openai.com/v1`, `openai/gpt-6.2-astra`, SSE. The driver runs a turn, starts a turn with an 8-second exec, steers a message with a `text/plain` document into it, and then sends one more turn. A scratch-only capture saved every request body and its `response.completed` usage. Base is main after #203568.

| request | base: `previous_response_id` / items / input / cached | head: `previous_response_id` / items / input / cached |
|---|---|---|
| #4 first request after the steer | no / 12 / 17,601 / 15,815 | **yes / 3** / 17,610 / 15,812 |
| #6 next run | no / 17 / **17,546** / 15,815 | **yes / 2** / **18,454** / 17,796 |

- On base the next run sends full history, and its input is smaller than the turn before it (17,546 < 17,787): the document text is gone.
- On head every request continues. The next run keeps the document (18,454 input) and reads 17,796 of those tokens from cache.

prs.title: fix(agents): move active node presence to current-turn context
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #192364. `active_node` and `active_node_identity` are on the Runtime line, and `openai-completions` routes relocate that line into the first user message. When a Mac app quits or comes back, the value changes, message 1 is rewritten, and everything after the system prompt falls out of an exact-prefix cache. The report measured 67-85 s replies instead of about 1 s on a ~90k-token session.

## User Impact

A node going away or returning no longer rewrites earlier messages, so the conversation stays cached. The model still sees the current active computer every turn, now in the newest message's runtime context.

Two visible changes:

- CLI backends now always get the fact in the turn context. It used to be skipped when the system prompt was sent, because the Runtime line carried it.
- **Known gap:** `settled-tool-finalization` and raw model runs carry no runtime facts by design, so those runs no longer see `active_node`. They previously saw it through the system prompt. The report also flags this. I kept their exact-prompt rule rather than adding text; a maintainer may want to weigh in if finalization needs it.

## Why This Change Was Made

The direction comes from @dertbv's diagnosis and local test in the issue. The CLI and harness paths already deliver this as a per-turn fact, so this moves the embedded path onto the same model:

- Removes the two fields from `buildRuntimeLine`, the runtime info types, `buildSystemPromptParams` and the prompt-cache field labels.
- `prepareEmbeddedAttemptPromptContext` runs `prepareActiveNodeContext` for the admitted run's operator profile and then adds `buildActiveNodeContextText` as a `conversation-data` fragment. The hint is read synchronously, so the keyed refresh has to come first or a revoked pairing could still show the retired node.
- `buildCliTurnAppendContext` appends it unconditionally, before media progress, which stays last.

## Evidence

![Prefix A/B](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wr-web/openclaw/proof-assets/192364/proof-192364.png)

Real Gateway on Windows with real agent turns in one session. A stub `openai-completions` provider diffs each request's messages against the previous request. Presence is on for requests 1-2, gone for 3-4, and back for 5.

| Request | Presence | Before: earlier messages | After: earlier messages |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | `mac-node-1` | identical | identical |
| 3 | gone | **`msg[1]` rewritten** | identical |
| 4 | gone | identical | identical |
| 5 | back | **`msg[1]` rewritten** | identical |

Before, the value lives in `msg[1]` and changes there. After, each turn's value is in that turn's own message (`msg[2]`, `msg[5]`, `msg[8]`, ...) and later requests leave those bytes alone. In the before run, the rewritten requests kept 54162 of 56011 and 54162 of 57600 characters as an unchanged prefix; the small size is the stub session's, not a real session's.

**CLI backend.** I registered a stub executable with `api.registerCliBackend` (`systemPromptArg`, `systemPromptWhen: "first"`, `resumeArgs`), so the real CLI runner builds the arguments. The stub logs what it received:

| Turn | Before: value in system prompt / prompt | After: value in system prompt / prompt |
|---|---|---|
| First (new session) | `mac-node-1` / none | none / `mac-node-1` |
| Resumed, node gone | not passed / `unknown` | not passed / `unknown` |
| Resumed, node back | not passed / `mac-node-1` | not passed / `mac-node-1` |

`system-prompt.active-node-prefix.test.ts` serializes the real system prompt plus a three-message history through `openai-completions` for the same session twice — once with `mac-123` connected and once with no node — and asserts that every message except the newest is byte-identical, that the relocated `Runtime: ` region really lands in `msg[1]` (so the test cannot pass vacuously), and that the newest message carries `active_node=mac-123` / `active_node=unknown`. With this PR's non-test sources reverted to main's behaviour it fails on the first byte-compare at `msg[1]`; with the change it passes. Suggested by @dertbv in the review thread.

Tests, with regressions in `attempt-prompt-context.test.ts` that fail without the embedded fact and without the refresh before reading it:

| File | Result |
|---|---|
| `system-prompt.active-node-prefix.test.ts` | 1 passed on `24ecacb` and on the merged head `157112b`; fails at `msg[1]` with this PR's non-test sources reverted |
| `attempt-prompt-context.test.ts` | 21 passed |
| `system-prompt-params.test.ts` | 23 passed |
| `runtime-facts-prompt.test.ts` | 10 passed |
| `runtime-prompt.test.ts` | 8 passed |
| `gateway/node-registry-pairing.test.ts` | 12 passed |
| `worker-turn-launcher-remote-handoff.test.ts` | 2 passed on `42b8f41` |
| `tool-result-truncation.test.ts` | 1 failed, 55 passed: a Windows path error (ENOENT on a drive-letter path joined under the temp dir) in a spill-pointer test this PR does not touch; I did not rerun it on base |
| `attempt-prompt-build.*`, `attempt-prompt-submit`, `attempt-context-advancement`, phase and media-hint tests | passed |
| `cli-runner/prepare.durable-context.test.ts` | 13 failed, 7 passed, same as base |
| `cli-runner/prepare.test.ts` | 13 failed, 100 passed, same as base |

Those two CLI files already fail on this Windows machine (for example `/bin/echo` not resolvable and `EBUSY`). I compared failing test names with and without the change and none are new, but this means CLI path coverage is weak locally, so please check them in CI.

Passed locally: oxfmt, oxlint, `check:line-cap-ratchet`, `check:test-lines-ratchet` (credited exactly by `config/test-lines-allocations/192423-active-node-prefix.txt`), `agents-root` and `agents-other` test types (the project CI failed on before).

**Merge of `upstream/main` @ `ae8155cf` (head `157112b`).** The branch had become `CONFLICTING`. One file conflicted, `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-prompt-build.ts`, and only in its import block: upstream added `import type { McpToolCatalogDiagnostic }`, this branch adds `readAdmittedRunOperatorAuthority` (still exported by `src/agents/admitted-run-context.ts:356`, still used at line 545). Both imports are kept; no behaviour changed by the merge. Re-ran on the merged tree in a git worktree with the main tree's `node_modules` junctioned in:

| Suite | Result on `157112b` |
|---|---|
| `system-prompt.active-node-prefix.test.ts` | 1 passed |
| `attempt-prompt-context.test.ts` | 23 passed |
| `oxfmt --check attempt-prompt-build.ts` | clean |

Typecheck stays CI-only in this worktree (`run-tsgo` refuses a checkout whose declarations resolve through junctioned `node_modules`).

## What was not tested

- Presence was changed with a preload calling `setActiveNodeContexts`, because this box has no paired Mac. The node connect and disconnect path was not exercised; the report did exercise it on a similar patch.
- The stub compares bytes. I did not measure real cache hits or latency on a caching server; the report's numbers are from its own patched build.
- The CLI proof uses a stub executable through the real runner, not Claude Code or another real CLI.
- Requester-scoped refresh is covered by unit tests and the default-profile live path; I did not run a non-owner profile with a revoked pairing end to end.


## Related defect deliberately left out of this PR

The remote macOS skills note has the same effect on the cached prefix: `getRemoteSkillEligibility` builds `Remote macOS node available (…). Run macOS-only skills via exec host=node on that node.` in `src/skills/runtime/remote.ts`, `prepareSkillsForPrompt` appends it to the skills text, and that text becomes the `## Skills` section of the frozen system prompt. A Mac node going online or away therefore rewrites the same bytes this PR just moved out of the Runtime line.

@ensignwesley reproduced that on main with serialized-request evidence (two identical online requests, first differing byte at offset 6444; [run](https://github.com/ensignwesley/openclaw/actions/runs/43812563271)) and is preparing a separate embedded-only change that sends the note through the current-turn carrier introduced here, leaving CLI and Codex output byte-identical. It is not folded in because the note lives in the snapshot/projection path shared by the CLI and Codex skill-prompt builders, so including it would widen this PR's proof scope from presence placement to skills-snapshot behavior. It will be linked here once opened.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A named macOS app profile in Local mode can refuse an independently started foreground Gateway even when both were started with the same profile name. The error only suggests changing ports, which does not help someone who wants to keep using that Gateway.

## User Impact

The error points to Remote mode for an independently managed Gateway and still explains how to choose a free port when the app should start a local one.

## Why This Change Was Made

The app keeps its existing listener ownership check. The developer guide documents a separate app-only Direct connection to the explicitly chosen Gateway; the foreground Gateway keeps its Local configuration. This changes guidance, not attachment, authentication, or the supported macOS floor.

## Evidence

- On a separately built Intel macOS 15.8.3 test candidate, the Local refusal was reproduced. A separate Remote/Direct app config connected to the same isolated foreground Gateway and a new native-chat prompt completed. This validates the documented route, not this patched build or the embedded Dashboard.
- Seven recovery-helper tests passed on Linux and macOS arm64; the pinned CLI accepted the generated config without warnings. The three-file patch passed a no-fuzz apply check against the producer source and upstream main at `8e248ca7317c`; README formatting and diff checks passed.
- **Draft: the patched native build and Swift regression were not run.** The Team sandbox does not provide a qualified macOS/AppKit runner. Run the existing named-profile `AppStateIsolationTests` lane in a disposable macOS environment before marking ready. Independent Auto Review timed out without a verdict.

prs.title: fix(update): explain missing macOS developer tools when Git is unavailable
prs.body:
Related to #202701.

## What Problem This Solves

On `main`, switching a macOS npm install to the dev channel can fail during cloning when the updater selects Apple's Git stub and no developer directory is active. An existing source checkout can be reported as an unmanaged install for the same reason.

## User Impact

This PR reports that `/usr/bin/git` needs the macOS developer tools and stops before invoking the stub. The message tells users to run `xcode-select --install` or select an installed Xcode, then retry.

## Why This Change Was Made

The updater checks the active developer directory when its existing executable search selects `/usr/bin/git`. The existing search order still gives `/usr/bin` precedence over inherited PATH entries. Whether the updater should trust a standalone Git is a separate decision for maintainers.

## Evidence

### Native macOS CLI

Built an npm package directly from PR head `04f1650` and ran its CLI on macOS arm64. For the refusal paths, an OS sandbox hid the Command Line Tools directory from the process. Apple's real selector returned exit `2` while `/usr/bin/git` remained executable. The pinned main comparison at `b4a41aa` denied Git execution in its isolated process.

| CLI path | Pinned main | PR head |
| --- | --- | --- |
| npm install switching to dev | Attempted cloning, then exited `1` with `update-failed`. | Exit `1`, `git-version-unsupported`. No clone step or new checkout. |
| Update from an existing source checkout | Exit `0`, skipped as `unmanaged-package-install`. | Exit `1`, `git-version-unsupported`. Checkout HEAD stayed at `04f1650`. |

The head trial ran these commands.

~~~sh
openclaw update --channel dev --yes --json --no-restart
node ./openclaw.mjs update --yes --json --no-restart
~~~

Both refusals printed this message to stderr.

~~~text
Update refused: /usr/bin/git requires the macOS developer tools. Install the Command Line Tools with xcode-select --install or select an installed Xcode, then retry openclaw update.
~~~

With the installed developer tools visible, `git version 2.54.0 (Apple Git-157)` completed the npm-to-source switch using an existing checkout that tracked a private Git mirror pinned to the PR head. The updater returned `status: "ok"` with exit `0` and the checkout resolved to `04f16506ea34fa8bf28b38711300c0f1fc0d04b5` after the switch. The head check, package swap, and runtime verification each exited `0`.

### Released npm updaters

Each published updater installed the package built from `04f1650` with `openclaw update --tag head.tgz --yes --json --no-restart`. The 9.x extended-stable updater also needed `--channel stable` to select the local artifact. Each run used an isolated, loopback Gateway and stopped it for the update.

| Starting release | Exit and installed commit | Before/after checks |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `2026.9.37` (extended-stable) | `0`, `ok`, `04f16506ea34` | Workboard card `0eee1704-d0dc-4434-85fa-89bea492f31b` and its title preserved. Workspace SHA-256 `0a6b4676c814…` matched. `/readyz` returned `200` both times. |
| `2026.10.10` (10.x) | `0`, `ok`, `04f16506ea34` | Workboard card `8cdf8ef3-dd70-415e-8038-295cefe92ea7` and its title preserved. Workspace SHA-256 `56a57ab3d0b8…` matched. `/readyz` returned `200` both times. |
| `2026.11.6` (latest stable) | `0`, `ok`, `04f16506ea34` | Workboard card `8ed50274-09e7-4323-94d4-dbe4cdf4a074` and its title preserved. Workspace SHA-256 `64147b95291c…` matched. `/readyz` returned `200` both times. |

The cards were read through the Gateway RPC. The CLI returned the same `messages.ackReaction` value (`🧪`) and configured workspace path. The 10.x and latest-stable runs retained their stable channel. The 9.x run saved stable as explicitly requested.

### Regression tests

The same two test files ran on macOS arm64 with Node 24.22.1. The base was pinned main at `b4a41aa` with only the two test-file changes applied. The passing run used `2bb9c2ac0`, whose Git tree matches signed PR head `04f1650`.

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/update-cli/update-command-install-layout.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --reporter=verbose
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/update-runner-git-commands.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --reporter=verbose
```

| Regression | Pinned main with the new tests | Candidate with the same tests |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Source update with no confirmed package owner and missing developer tools | 1 failed, 8 passed. The CLI exited `0`; the assertion expected `{ code: 1 }`. The test command exited `1`. | 9/9 passed. The test command exited `0`. |
| macOS system Git with no selected developer directory (`selected: false`) | 1 failed, 6 passed. Git was invoked (`true`); the assertion expected `false`. The test command exited `1`. | 7/7 passed. The test command exited `0`. |

Full core lint stripe 5 passed locally on macOS arm64 at `04f1650` in 36.44 seconds. Exit `0`, 0 errors, and 7 warnings in files outside the PR diff.

prs.title: fix(gateway): clarify reused pull request publication messages
prs.body:
Related: [original PR #192940](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192940). This is the bot-published replacement of that message-only change; the original PR remains open separately.

## What Problem This Solves

A worktree publication that reused an existing pull request told the user “Published,” even though that request did not push a commit or trigger CI.

## User Impact

When the Gateway confirms reuse, the conversation links to the existing PR and explicitly says this request pushed no new commit and triggered no CI run. Other successful results still link to the PR. There are no public receipt or protocol changes, migrations, or required user actions.

## Why This Change Was Made

The conversation notice uses the recorded source head, published head, and GitHub effect evidence from the worktree receipt. A recovered publication that pushed a commit still receives the ordinary PR notice. Publication execution and storage are unchanged.

## Evidence

This replacement reuses the patch-identical operator proof recorded in [#192940](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192940); the tests and independent review below were not rerun in this publication session.

- Three real-Git transcript regressions fail on the pinned base at the old “Published” notice and pass with the fix. Reuse keeps the existing commit and write count; both lost-response cases show the ordinary PR link.
- 156 focused tests passed across worktree, repository, personal publication, transcript reporting, readiness, and source/compiled protocol validation. The three regressions passed again after the final test-helper cleanup.
- Core typecheck, typed lint, and format passed. Independent review found no actionable P0–P2 issue. The test-line ratchet is +48 against the +400 allowance, with no allocation change.
- This publication session verified the exact transferred patch hash, full tree, eight-file scope (90 insertions, 24 deletions), whitespace, and index/worktree consistency. Protocol packages, protocol documentation, and workflows are identical to the pinned base.
- Hosted CI for this replacement has not yet been observed. No workflow approval, rerun, or dispatch is part of this publication.

<details>
<summary>Exact source and transfer identity</summary>

- Original source head: `e771907fef94831f1ac738fa8450e250b7d81584`.
- Pinned base: `eedb353df007419105cd4d2b11fd73b84bc1a509`.
- Full source and replacement tree: `2782b4ba17b8c133db92411f800023c1404b5bfa`.
- Decoded patch: 14,638 bytes; SHA-256 `7dc979d357863ded63595f800a9fb7a0e6cba12452a9cf15c29c28f4740560f1`.
- The managed publisher may create an attribution/marker commit with a different commit SHA; the full tree must remain identical.

</details>

## Live Gateway evidence

Built [`b7b6d499`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/b7b6d4992d16f0b00151af0dfb673699481d402c) and ran a real agent turn in an isolated local Gateway. Submitted two distinct `sessions.github.publish` requests from the same worktree with identical source contents.

- The first request created [the fixture PR](https://github.com/MertBasar0/openclaw-gateway-publication-proof-202078/pull/1) at `bf08a60bd974` and triggered [a successful GitHub Actions run](https://github.com/MertBasar0/openclaw-gateway-publication-proof-202078/actions/runs/45076781769) (run `45076781769`, attempt `1`).
- The second request returned the same PR and commit. The Gateway wrote this notice into the conversation:

  > Reused the existing pull request for MertBasar0/openclaw-gateway-publication-proof-202078 branch openclaw/202078-live-proof: https://github.com/MertBasar0/openclaw-gateway-publication-proof-202078/pull/1. No new commit was pushed or CI run triggered by this request. Using @MertBasar0 (Shared agent account).

- GitHub snapshots at `2026-11-22T22:16:39Z` and `2026-11-22T22:18:34Z` showed the same PR and branch head `bf08a60bd9742bbcb3236f7af09c7c5209669ce0`, the same single branch creation event (`51424699560`), and the same run and attempt. There were **0 new push events, 0 new Actions runs, and 0 reruns**. The final snapshot was 84 seconds after the second request was submitted.

prs.title: fix: keep project picker errors readable
prs.body:
Related: #187062

## What Problem This Solves

When project discovery, repository search, or project registration returns a diagnostic with a long unbroken name, the New Session project picker clips it at the edge. The project-list Retry button also runs directly into the diagnostic text.

## User Impact

The full diagnostic stays readable, and Retry and Browse folders remain usable without losing the composer draft or selected project. This is presentation-only: no retry semantics, permissions, or session-creation behavior change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Wrap diagnostics at the existing picker styles and place the catalog Retry button on its own row. Folder-browser wrapping is scoped to this project picker; the shared session-group folder browser is unchanged. No text is clamped or hidden, and no state owner or helper is added.

## Evidence

The containment regression failed on main for list/search diagnostics, and independently failed for registration diagnostics before that sibling repair. The Places browser suite passed all seven tests. The exact final scoped candidate passed its focused regression, UI production build, UI typecheck, targeted lint/stylelint/format, and diff checks. The browser regression uses a **390×844** viewport.

The actual production UI was exercised through visible controls with synthetic responses from the repository's supported mock Gateway. Capture coverage uses **390×900** in dark/light and **1280×900** in dark, plus **390×660** for tall-error scrolling, pending Retry, and registration failures. It includes simultaneous list/search failures, local results alongside remote failure, missing credentials, folder access explanations, disabled Browse with its tooltip, and a failed background catalog refresh after choosing a loaded project. Retry restores the selected row; Browse and Escape/back work; the draft survives. No live failure was triggered, real provider credentials used, or external model request made.

Local ClawSweeper completed read-only review of base `8e248ca7317c0cd4a294ce034c552ad6e691d84e` through head `f012cd52c1e4291697c1bf58277850131cd6d9e5` using canonical runner `a76b6b0`, with no code-blocking findings. Its P3 suggestion to trim draft/selection assertions was declined: those assertions protect the compound list/search-error and registration-failure flow, which the existing list-only retry regression does not cover. The matched clean and annotated comparison below supplies the visual proof requested by the reviewer. Independent parent code/visual review also found no blocking defect on the identical two-file patch. No hosted re-review is required for this local-review route.

Production builds exited successfully; inherited advisory CSS-gzip and chat-boot-request budget warnings remain. Mock proof validates the appearance and UI recovery paths, not real-provider failure behavior. The optional real-Gateway navigation smoke was not run.

### Clean comparison

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: the unbroken project diagnostic is clipped at the picker edge](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d8f0ed22-6e69-4d4f-a0b4-d3cb0eedffca) | ![After: the complete diagnostic wraps and Retry occupies its own row](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/daccba69-27ac-4b9f-a697-bdaa0495251b) |

### Annotated comparison

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![The clipped diagnostic edge is outlined](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7927ba26-1fbf-48fb-8ab5-e4a53d5fb975) | ![The wrapped diagnostic and separate Retry are outlined](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/56023f58-3c96-437e-80d0-e58a57a6378b) |

Matched **390×900**, dark theme, identical synthetic fixture, draft and picker interaction. Before: main at `8e248ca7317c0cd4a294ce034c552ad6e691d84e`. After: reviewed implementation `f012cd52c1e4291697c1bf58277850131cd6d9e5`; published head `edbb6e2aa085a9714c79cafd5bd3fe98586ad78d` is its metadata-only child with an identical full Git tree, verified after publication. These are screenshots of the production components with mock Gateway responses, not live-provider failure captures.
