prs.title: feat: move a conversation that has no project into one
prs.body:
Closes #202268

## What changes

On main, moving work from the default workspace into an existing project requires another conversation and a manual transfer of local edits.

Say **“let’s work on OpenClaw”** in the default workspace. The model moves this conversation into the registered project with `session_project`. The model can carry out the rest of that message in the project’s managed checkout. For a move-only request, the reply confirms the destination. The conversation keeps its messages. The tool is available by default for eligible sessions, subject to tool policy. The Gateway refuses a second move.

Choose **Move to project…** in the conversation menu to do the same move yourself. When a matching checkout has file changes, the dialog previews how many will be copied. The project checkout restores those changes before repository setup. The original checkout stays in place, and earlier links still open its files.

Project moves share the checks for active runs, background processes, terminals, and child sessions with PR workspace preparation.

Sandboxed conversations can move with Docker or Podman. For other sandbox backends, the picker explains why the move is unavailable and the Gateway refuses before saving a project or creating a checkout.

## Control UI comparison

Captured in the built Control UI with a synthetic project and two file changes. Main screenshot at `e309df612e`.

| Conversation menu on main | Project move dialog in this PR |
| --- | --- |
| ![Main conversation menu without a project move action](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/e12ca5c06db1fb176425bb65d8fd35c03cf65dde/images/2026/11/8ea3ec35-58db-4f9b-8e2a-0143e9ef7810.png) | ![Move to a project dialog showing Changes to 2 files will be copied](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/e12ca5c06db1fb176425bb65d8fd35c03cf65dde/images/2026/11/ac26f04c-e00c-4972-b493-62ce632fe8eb.png) |

## Evidence

### Live model handoff

The live Qwen3-8B capture at `4b990ab` shows the same conversation in Juniper and the release code from its README. The model called `session_project` and finished the read in the project checkout.

![Control UI showing the same conversation in Juniper and the release code returned from its README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/b31285503734f99cc587a206f8819c0fb4cd455b/images/2026/11/51b055c2-4807-4c96-ab56-c24d904eb87e.png)

### Sandbox admission

On `9546f55`, an isolated Gateway with a real loopback SSH sandbox showed the Docker or Podman requirement in the picker and refused the direct move request. The session kept its original workspace and ID, had no project worktree, and replied to the next message.

The carry fixture exercises the Docker move handoff after the initiating turn ends. Live Docker and Podman carry remain pending.

### Upgrade compatibility on `9546f55`

Each published binary created a conversation, saved a user message and reply, and registered Juniper in its own profile. On startup, the Gateway built at `9546f55` loaded that profile. The same conversation then moved into Juniper through the built Control UI and got a new reply. These checks used synthetic repositories and a scripted local model.

| Starting release | Result |
| --- | --- |
| [2026.9.37](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/releases/tag/v2026.9.37) (extended stable) | Passed |
| [2026.10.33](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/releases/tag/v2026.10.33) | Passed |
| [2026.11.6](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/releases/tag/v2026.11.6) | Passed |

Each run preserved the session ID, both original messages, the project record, and the source commit. Repository setup saw the copied edit. The untracked file survived and the original files stayed in the source checkout.

The Control UI capture shows the same upgrade scenario at `4b990ab`.

![Control UI after the upgrade showing the released version’s reply, the successful move to Juniper, and the new reply](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/b31285503734f99cc587a206f8819c0fb4cd455b/images/2026/11/e49925c6-e928-43c6-bc47-120f555523b5.png)

### Build and tests

- Full build and Plugin SDK declaration budget passed. The declaration graph was **5,284,258 / 5,385,536 bytes**.
- 139 focused tests passed across Gateway moves, worktree carry, sandbox preparation, handoff, tool and prompt behavior, and the Control UI. Core typecheck, scoped lint, and formatting passed.
- The test-line allocation includes 47 lines for the regression that checks the session and worktree after an SSH move is refused.
- A paired Qwen3-8B measurement found that the compact project tool description and guidance save 95 input tokens.
- Shared tool-display metadata keeps direct JSON imports out of startup. A paired build with that change removed put chat boot 136 B over main.

prs.title: fix(templates): allow re-adding a deleted template agent
prs.body:
Closes #198475

## What Problem This Solves

Template Add fails with “deletion is in progress” when the same agent ID was previously deleted successfully.

## User Impact

Users can add the template again and receive a fresh agent and chat after deleting its previous agent.

## Why This Change Was Made

Chat preparation runs before config publication consumes the completed deletion record. Carry the existing creation claim through session admission and the history reader, so only the current creator can prepare that agent. Keep reader custody and cleanup with their existing owners, including rejection of an ordinary request trying to reuse the creator's warm reader.

The main integration preserves the current session-store source-custody argument and its source-current guard separately from the creation witness. It also retains upstream's reviewed-setup retry controls.

Reported and reproduced by @DonnieFi in the linked issue.

## November 23 upstream verification

[#200628](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200628) fixed the linked issue and entered official main as [b609d22c129](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/b609d22c129f2944c1abaec1d2895eb659493a36). After resolving the two test-fixture conflicts against current main bdb444f3e94, the resulting tree is byte-identical to main. The selected same-ID Add → Delete → Add case passed on that official main revision using the isolated service/SQLite fixture.

The original implementation and earlier results remain recorded below with their respective revisions.

## Evidence

Current validation covers merge commit `9f298accc9129ad2874cbcd40e0ef813e1ea2998` against main `60c112a1bfa94ea4a5d43e4302e18375429d879f` (Node 24.22.1, pnpm 12.15.0).

- **Before:** with the same recreation fixture and all eight production files restored to that fixed main, actual Add → production deletion → same-ID Add fails with `Agent fixture-first deletion is in progress; new work is unavailable.` The command exits 1 (253.900 seconds, including cold worker compilation); this is the intended service-boundary failure.
- **After: 13 selected cases passed across five files.** They cover recreation with a fresh session, creator warm-read success and outside-claim refusal, fresh creation, post-commit revocation, pre-commit compensation, reviewed-setup retry, reader cleanup/revocation, source-custody revocation and retargeting in ordinary and inspection modes, and session preemption. Canonical production SQLite workers were compiled by the test wrapper.
- Production core, Template test and session test types passed. Typed lint passed on the eight production files and the Template test. Formatting, whitespace, the nine-file line-cap check and the test-growth check passed; net test growth is 76 lines.
- Fresh independent desktop review through read-only SSH covers the complete nine-file patch and its owning contracts, with no unresolved P0–P2 findings. The merge commit preserves the reviewed tree `4301538ac2bd3f99f3d4253a039cec934f6a8e0f`.

Live Gateway RPC, browser/provider and broad CI validation are not included. The existing real-Gateway evidence gap and maintainer-owned CI/review gates remain pending.

<details>
<summary>Focused commands, cost and limits</summary>

```bash
OPENCLAW_VITEST_NO_OUTPUT_TIMEOUT_MS=300000 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.infra.config.ts src/templates/gateway-add-pending.test.ts src/infra/agent-database-readers.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --pool=forks -t 'admitted-recreated$|admitted-reviewed-chat-retry$|admitted-applied$|: revoked$|abort-before-commit$|runs every registered closer and keeps deleted databases closed until revived'
OPENCLAW_VITEST_NO_OUTPUT_TIMEOUT_MS=300000 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.runtime-config.config.ts src/config/sessions/session-store-reader-preparation.test.ts src/config/sessions/session-transcript-worker-lanes.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --pool=forks -t 'reuses a live prepared source and rejects revoked custody|rejects a locator retargeted after qualification|revokes readers and joins cleanup.*pending=true, capable=true|retains reads dispatched after cleanup.*capable=true'
OPENCLAW_VITEST_NO_OUTPUT_TIMEOUT_MS=300000 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.unit.config.ts src/sessions/session-controller.lifecycle.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --pool=forks -t '^preempt interrupts a captured subordinate effect before running the mutation$'
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --noEmit
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.templates.json --noEmit
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.agents-sessions.json --noEmit
```

The three test commands completed in 424.190, 85.776 and 89.509 seconds. These are whole wrapper times, including compilation and transforms, not isolated assertion time. The real recreation/cleanup lifecycle needs the production SQLite service boundary; cheaper helper-only assertions would miss the original failure and retained-reader leak. Other cases in these files were intentionally unselected. The finite 300-second wrapper no-output budget was retained; behavioral test timeouts were not increased.

The compiler commands used separate incremental build-info files. Core typed lint's existing root-config route also prepared plugin SDK declarations; no additional check was rerun just to remove that preparation cost. Normal merge hooks retain the content guard and canonically skip formatting/freshness under MERGE_HEAD; the affected-file checks above ran explicitly before committing.

This is isolated production-service/SQLite proof. Live Gateway RPC, browser, vendor/provider acceptance and broad package/CI validation remain outside this local evidence. The existing real-Gateway evidence gap and maintainer-owned CI/review gates remain pending.

</details>

prs.title: feat(ui): render LaTeX in Control UI markdown
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Control UI Markdown displayed supported LaTeX literally. This renders bounded math while preserving code, escaped input, currency, URLs and sanitized output.

## User Impact

Math is lazy-loaded; ordinary messages request no KaTeX engine, styles or fonts. Equations stay readable as source until ready, and failures keep that fallback. Wide equations scroll inside the message and now show a fade where content continues. Math stays findable in transcript search and readable in paste excerpts and web source previews.

Original contribution by @jjjhenriksen; repair work requested by @RomneyDa. Contributor authorship and coauthor credit are preserved; Allow edits from maintainers remains enabled.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @RomneyDa](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/clawtributor-review-pr-144324)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/41d889a9-23c8-4603-889b-a35ad86acfb6)

- [Rebase discussion and verification with @vyctorbrzezowski](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/ac39fc44-8e46-4656-ba81-f57ba2533d4c)

## Why This Change Was Made

Preserve the existing parser, generation-fenced leaf, shared lazy runtime, MathML and separate sanitizer. One 200-expression allowance covers stable streamed additions and the mutable tail. KaTeX **0.18.2** addresses GHSA-238p-pmpm-9mq7 while retaining `trust: false`. Plain-text consumers of the shared parser (search, paste excerpts, source previews) read math tokens as their TeX source, so math stays searchable and readable outside the rendered view. Wide equations reuse the table fade convention rather than adding a new affordance.

This remains built-in math, not a plugin. Product decision (2026-11-08, @vyctorbrzezowski): use built-in math rendering with KaTeX and prepare this selected PR for merge; merging remains a separate decision. #175507 contains the earlier equivalent implementation, not this latest rebase. KaTeX is the one new dependency (MIT, pinned 0.18.2, loaded only when a message contains math); dense math retains real CPU cost, bounded by the 200-expression message budget.

## Evidence

- **Rebased November 22, 2026:** signed head `d9d99865410de426d0827e34e7e0f935b79b8b46` on main `f066f9cba3135d28a6ff7df1e1e1ba95684dda74`; tree `3b29185c5bcf51f74f56cf2a4104a62903c792ff`. Frozen install, **147 tests in 9 files** (including table coverage), UI typecheck, formatting, lint and test-line ratchet passed. Boot-manifest generation succeeded; its generated upstream graph changes were retained verbatim after verifying that it was the only changed tracked file and comparing the imported bytes. The production build below ran with that generated manifest. The lease has been released.

Existing absolute-baseline debt remains; no budget was raised. No new visual behavior was introduced, so the earlier screenshots below are reused, not recaptured.
- **Hosted checks:** [new-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45073662292) still needs to complete, and dependency review is pending. Historical failures below remain unresolved evidence, not current-head results.

- **Previous rebase November 18, 2026:** signed head `9a657d163052cd39f9f9ac5504d6d673994ed942` on main `fe83a7e0afa56fb311f3c43f459abaffd7c5e248`; tree `faf8f8330cfb569109fb505f6f3f87debe08dd18`. prs.title: fix: let Git checkouts inside containers update again
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Since #203194, `openclaw update` refuses every Git checkout on a host that has `/.dockerenv` (or `container`, `DOCKER_CONTAINER` or `OPENCLAW_CONTAINER` set). It fails with `container-install`, "This installation belongs to a container image. Update the image instead." A checkout that someone cloned and built inside a container or devbox is not part of any image, and the updater before #203194 updated it. Today it cannot update at all, and the next action it names is wrong for it.

## User Impact

A Git checkout inside a container updates through `openclaw update`, `update.run` and automatic updates like any other checkout. The run records a `warning:preflight` step, and `openclaw update` prints it: whatever is not on a mounted volume is reset when the container is recreated from its image, so keep the checkout and the state directory on volumes or build the new version into the image. If only the state directory is on a volume, the warning also says that the image's original build may refuse the upgraded state after a recreate. Nothing else changes. OpenClaw's own image is a package install and is still skipped with `container-image-install`. Nix and Homebrew refusals are unchanged.

A Gateway with `OPENCLAW_SUPERVISOR_MODE=external` now refuses `update.run` on a Git install with `external-supervisor-update-required`, as the package route, `openclaw update` and automatic updates already do. #203194's Git route had dropped that check, and container deployments are where external supervisors are common.

A Gateway that is a container's main process, with no service manager or launcher above it, cannot start a new release without stopping the container: the update restart hands off to a detached successor and exits, which ends the container. `update.run` and automatic Git updates now refuse that case with `restart-unavailable` before anything is prepared, and the message names the step that works: `openclaw update --no-restart` in the container, then restart the container. "Main process" means PID 1 or a direct child of the container's init shim or shell, since that exit ends the container. A Gateway started with `docker exec` has no parent inside the container and hands off as it does on a host. A Gateway under systemd, launchd or the release launcher inside a container is also unaffected; the green cell below is that case.

## Why This Change Was Made

**Why the refusal existed.** It came in with #203194 as one preflight line ("container installs refused before any change"). I found no other reasoning for it in the PR description, the review thread or the docs. The case where it is right is an install that lives in the image layer, where an in-place change is lost when the container is recreated.

**Evidence that the line cannot see that case.**
- `src/update/preflight.ts` runs only for Git installs on main. Every caller of `prepareUpdate` routes `installKind === "git"`: `update-command.ts`, `update-run.ts` and `update-startup-auto-run.ts`.
- OpenClaw's own image (`Dockerfile`) ships a package at `/app` with no `.git`. The existing update-command admission already skips it as `container-image-install` (`resolveUnmanagedUpdateInstallReason`), before `src/update` is reached.
- So on main the check refused only checkouts that someone cloned into a container. It also treated `OPENCLAW_CONTAINER` as evidence of a container. That variable is the host-side `--container <name>` target (`src/cli/container-target.ts`), and inside the container the CLI clears it.

**Rule.** A container signal alone never refuses. Preflight uses the existing detector, `isContainerEnvironment()` (`/.dockerenv`, `/run/.containerenv`, container cgroups, Fly). Inside a container it continues and returns a warning, which the run records. Every refusal that follows (Nix, Homebrew, writable prefix, tools, dirty checkout, Node engine, disk space) still applies, in the same order.

**What stays refused.** An image-owned install: the official image, and any package root without a package-manager owner. Those are skipped by the existing admission owner with "Pull or build the target Docker/container image, then redeploy it with the same state/config mounts". The green cell below checks this.

**Alternatives rejected.**
- Keep refusing unless the checkout is on a volume, by reading mountinfo. Mount layouts vary (bind mounts of a subdirectory, Kubernetes, Podman), so the rule would be brittle. A recreated container loses an unmounted checkout's changes, but no state is at risk. The updater before #203194 updated these checkouts too.
- Refuse only on an image marker. The official image sets no marker that the Git path could ever see, because the official image is not a Git checkout.

**Update behavior.** This changes the updater inside the release path, so it applies once the installed CLI or Gateway has this code. An installed build from #203194 (merged 2026-11-22, main only) up to this change still refuses its next update inside a container, because the refusal runs in the installed code. That one hop cannot be patched from here. Remove `/.dockerenv` as root for that update (Docker recreates it with the container), which is the control row below, or pull and build the checkout by hand once. Every later update uses this rule. No schema, config, protocol, dependency or retention change.

## Evidence

Real Linux container with systemd as PID 1, a lingering user manager and a real user bus. A user systemd Gateway service, a Gateway-gated writer on a 256–512 MiB agent database, and 1,000 marker rows checked by count, SHA-256 and `PRAGMA quick_check` after every step. Synthetic state only. The checkout was cloned and built inside the container, and its home is a volume.

| Run | Commit | `/.dockerenv` | Result | Wall | Gateway outage | Data |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| RED: update to the next commit | base `a1aa1276017` | present | exit 1, `container-install`, "Update the image instead"; Gateway untouched | 2.2 s | 0 | intact |
| RED: repeat | base | present | same refusal | 2.2 s | 0 | intact |
| Control: same cell, marker removed only | base | removed | exit 0, `succeeded`, serving the target build | 384 s | 12.3 s | intact |
| GREEN: update to the next commit | head `a631d9991b9` | present | exit 0, `succeeded`, serving the target build, `warning:preflight` recorded | 369.8 s | 11.9 s | intact |
| GREEN: no-op repeat | head | present | exit 0, `already-current` | 6.5 s | 0 | intact |
| GREEN: package root in the container (image shape) | head | present | exit 0, `skipped`, `container-image-install`, "Pull or build the target Docker/container image..." | 4.3 s | 0 | n/a |

"Data intact" means the 1,000 marker rows kept the same count and SHA-256 (`69cb2f12…`), and `quick_check` returned `ok` before and after every step. The same green rows also passed at two earlier heads: `039ac631f2d` (369 s, 11.8 s outage) and `91087630aff` (380 s, 11.8 s outage).

Red and green terminal recordings, and the raw head output: [recordings and green raw logs at the head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/203586#issuecomment-7085471241). Raw red and control output: [red and control](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/203586#issuecomment-7083377133). Full logs are not attached because the artifact store rejects uploads from this machine.

Tests (`src/update/prepare.test.ts`):
- New: a checkout inside a container goes through `runReleaseUpdateCli` with a real Git fixture and state database. It ends with a pending trial and exit 0, records the warning, and prints it. The fixture presents both container signals, the shared detector and the `/.dockerenv` marker the base preflight reads, so on the base it fails with `status: failed` (`container-install`).
- New (`update-run.test.ts`): a Gateway that is a container's main process refuses `update.run` with `restart-unavailable` and the `--no-restart` next step, and prepares nothing (red on the base handler, which accepted the run). Negative controls: the same container under a supervisor (the release launcher) prepares the release, and so does a Gateway started with `docker exec`.
- New (`update-run.test.ts`): an externally supervised Gateway answers `update.run` with `external-supervisor-update-required` and prepares nothing. Red on the base handler, which accepted the run.
- New: a Nix install is still refused inside a container. This guards the order: the warning must not skip the refusals that follow it.
- Added a negative control to the existing build-failure case: outside a container, no warning is recorded.
- Removed: the `/.dockerenv` `fs.access` spy and the `container`/`DOCKER_CONTAINER`/`OPENCLAW_CONTAINER` stubs. Production no longer reads them. The module mock of `isContainerEnvironment` replaces them, so no case depends on the host's container status. Also removed: the old "refuses a Docker marker" case, whose behavior is retired on purpose.

Checks: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/update/ src/gateway/server-methods/update-run.test.ts` (44 passed), `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, oxlint and oxfmt on the touched files, `pnpm check:baseline-ratchets` (all ok, including session-identity, mock-exports and test-lines +42), `pnpm check:docs`, `git diff --check`.

Review: ClawSweeper's local review round 3 rated overall F, proof C, patch F. Its findings, and what I did:
- (P2) A devbox whose PID 1 is `sleep infinity` would be refused. Fixed: the refusal now needs PID 1 or a direct child of PID 1.
- (P1) A container signalled only by `container=systemd-nspawn` goes undetected, where main used to refuse it. Not changed: the shared detector does not read that variable, and adding it would change every caller of the detector. Listed under "Not proven".
- (P2) The Control UI maps `restart-unavailable` to package wording. Not changed: that is a UI change, and it needs its own screenshots.
- (P2) Automatic updates count a `skipped` refusal outside the failure backoff. Not changed: the refusal happens before anything is prepared and costs one check.

Round 2 raised the container main-process restart (fixed above) and asked that `openclaw update` print the warning even when it stops following a run at its `--timeout` (done, covered in `cli.test.ts`). Round 1 raised the supervisor gap (fixed above), asked that the warning cover a recreated image refusing upgraded state (added), and asked that the regression test exercise the base's own signal (done). `autoreview` cannot run here. The worktree sits under a shared temp directory, and its Codex preflight refuses that. A fresh independent reviewer found no P0 or P1 issues. Its two P2 findings are fixed: the step is now a `warning:` step, so reports, the Control UI and the warning headline show it, and the negative control above is new.

Not proven:
- Recreating a container and watching the checkout fall back to the image's build. The warning text describes that case.
- An externally supervised Git Gateway, and a container whose main process is the Gateway, end to end: both refusals are covered by handler tests only. The `--no-restart`, then restart-the-container path is not run.
- Automatic updates share the same refusal helper (`describeUpdateRestartUnavailable`); that caller has no test of its own.
- An upgrade from the latest stable release: 2026.11.6 still runs the older in-place updater, which never reaches this preflight.
- CI: `checks-node-changed-compact-large-9-1` fails on `src/flows/doctor-health.legacy-update.test.ts`, three cases. They fail the same way on `main` without this change, and open PRs #203560 and #203569 fix them. Main will be merged in once they land.
- Kubernetes on cgroup v2 and systemd-nspawn: the existing detector may not report a container there. No warning is printed, and the main-process refusal does not apply. A Gateway that is PID 1 of such a container would hand off to a detached successor, as on main before #203194.
- macOS and Windows containers (not applicable). A uid-mismatched checkout on a volume ("dubious ownership").

## What Problem This Solves

Installed plugin settings list tools but give administrators no way to block one without leaving the page.

## User Impact

In Settings → Plugins, turn off `discord_moderate` for all agents without disabling Discord or changing `discord_actions`. Turning a tool back on removes only its individual block. A broader global block stays visible and cannot be lifted from that row. Viewers without config-write access keep the read-only list.

## Why This Change Was Made

The switches edit the existing global tool deny list, not the plugin’s enabled state or an agent’s own settings. They preserve unrelated entries and do not change individual actions inside a tool or the plugin’s background behavior.

## Evidence

Built Control UI on the Studio: the tool switch is absent on main and works on the integrated branch. All 12 Chromium scenarios and 42 configuration-owner tests passed. On the same saved configuration, disabling one tool preserved its sibling and unrelated deny patterns; enabling removed only the exact tool entry. Reload, wildcard restrictions, rejected writes and read-only access were checked. These tests use synthetic Gateway data.

The controller guard, UI typecheck and scoped lint passed. Paired production builds showed no increase in startup JS or CSS. This uses the existing deny list and adds no schema or migration.

prs.title: fix: keep GitHub Checks compact in Link Reader on WebKit
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When GitHub Checks cannot load, WebKit 26 can render the fallback icon at the width of the Link Reader panel. The oversized icon pushes the PR summary, changed files, and comments out of view.

## User Impact

The unavailable Checks state stays in one compact row. You can expand it with the keyboard or mouse, open the full Checks page on GitHub, and keep reading the PR without scrolling past a giant icon.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Link Reader now uses the same host-selector styling as the other docked panels instead of relying on `@scope` inside a native disclosure. It also reuses the shared dock and tab styles. No data migration or configuration change is needed.

## Evidence

- Matched Dashboard captures in Playwright WebKit 26 with synthetic GitHub data: the Checks icon went from 624 × 624 to 17 × 17 CSS pixels. The compact-size assertion failed on the base and passed on the patch. These are browser captures, not a native macOS app run.
- Verified keyboard expansion, mouse collapse, the GitHub Checks link, Files, and Discussion in builds tested with WebKit 26, WebKit 27, and Chromium. The final GitHub panel browser suite passed all three tests; 76 focused tests passed across seven files. The committed regression runs in the existing Chromium harness; the WebKit-specific reproduction was exercised separately.
- Targeted source lint and formatting passed. Independent local review did not complete: the available review route requires temporary storage outside the task checkout. No independent review verdict is claimed.

prs.body:
Related: #198316

## What Problem This Solves

Cmd+K Compose hid the selected project inside Settings. Users had to open it to check where a new session would run.

## User Impact

A project field beside Settings shows the current workspace. Open it to choose a project by machine or toggle **New worktree**. When enabled, a branch icon replaces the folder. Agent selection and **Remember settings for Cmd/Ctrl+K** stay in Settings; the model, Send, and the footer are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Project and worktree describe the same destination. They now share a picker, without adding a separate worktree button or changing saved preferences, permissions, or placement rules.

## Evidence

Real Cmd+K Compose with synthetic Gateway data at a 1280 px viewport. Before: main at `42f8c5bc`. After: the project-field change, rebased onto `ab2da2bf` (intervening change touched an unrelated test). The same flow was exercised at an emulated 390 px width.

## What Problem This Solves

Chat shows a separate “Preparing a tool call” label while the model writes its next tool request. The label adds a transient status before any tool has actually started.

## User Impact

Chat keeps its normal working indicator, output-token count, and elapsed time. Tool activity still appears when the tool starts.

## Why This Change Was Made

The model’s preparation signal now returns chat to its existing working state. This retires the dedicated label without leaving stale waiting text or creating a tool entry early.

prs.title: docs: explain where the Control UI creates agent workspaces
prs.body:
Related: #186847

## What Problem This Solves

The Control UI explains how to create another agent, but not where the Gateway puts its workspace. If a configured workspace root makes the new path look unexpected, the creation guide does not tell you how to check it.

## User Impact

Readers can tell which setting controls the default directory and find the actual workspace with `openclaw agents list`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The agent creation dialog leaves workspace selection to the Gateway. The new paragraph explains its two defaults for additional agents and links to the workspace reference. This is documentation only; it does not diagnose the reported 2026.10.8 installation or change workspace placement.

## Evidence

- Traced the current Control UI creation request through `agents.create` and the Gateway workspace resolver. A separate source review confirmed both defaults, the CLI output, and the reference link.
- OpenClaw's MDX validator passed on the changed file. A focused documentation check failed before the edit and passed afterward, including the workspace-reference anchor. `git diff --check` passed.
- Windows Qwen assisted with the first draft. No live agent creation or Gateway behavior change was tested.

prs.title: fix(ui): allow retrying failed Worktrees refreshes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a failed Worktrees inventory refresh leaves stale rows without a read-only retry after restoring a worktree.

## User Impact

Retry the failed read in place without repeating restoration or starting cleanup. Accepted rows, creation drafts and destructive confirmations remain intact.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing list owner distinguishes failed reads from mutation errors, allowing its existing alert to offer the appropriate Retry. Replacing the error also replaces its origin, so a later confirmation or operation error cannot inherit a misleading read retry.

## Evidence

- Compiled Control UI regression fails on unmodified base 802573f8fb68e9a5a4211c316434d8069565194a and passes fixed with a valid snapshot-backed restoration fixture. Held Retry retains rows; success reconciles inventory with exactly one restore request.
- Independent coordinator review caught stale error attribution after a later confirmation failure. The added mounted regression failed on the first proposal and passes after the same owner clears that attribution when replacing the error.
- All 27 page tests and both compiled-browser scenarios pass, retaining rejected creation drafts, cancel/force-delete confirmation, exact mutation targets and queued-to-partial cleanup outcomes. UI/narrow test types, scoped lint/format and diff checks pass.
- Coordinator re-reviewed the final owner, renderer, regressions, original history and actual captures; no unresolved actionable findings. Existing strict-read fixture warnings are also present in baseline. Automated review and remote CI are not claimed complete.
- Actual compiled UI with synthetic Gateway responses, light theme, 1280×900 captures. No live worktree/Git maintenance, physical-device or WebKit proof.

prs.title: fix(webchat): keep GitHub publication receipts out of assistant replies
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When an agent publishes a PR, the Gateway can add its receipt to the conversation as if the agent said it. The extra message can repeat the agent’s real answer, and a PR from a separate publication task may not appear in the conversation’s Details panel.

## User Impact

Successful publishes appear under Details → Pull requests without an automatic assistant message. Failures and requests for confirmation still appear in chat as system notices.

## Why This Change Was Made

Chat distinguishes Gateway publication receipts from actual assistant replies. Details uses the existing recorded PR list, including task PRs, without treating them as publications of the current checkout. If GitHub metadata is unavailable, the verified publication link remains available without guessing its status.

## Evidence

The focused Chromium test reproduced the old receipt and missing Details link on the base, then verified the published PR in Details without an automatic chat message on the fix. It ran the bundled Control UI with synthetic Gateway data, not a live GitHub push. Focused transcript, Details, mobile, and Gateway tests passed, along with core/UI type checks and targeted lint. Draft for review; broad CI and independent review were not run.

[Clean and annotated before/after screenshots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/203689#issuecomment-7085572477)

prs.title: fix(ios): nest child sessions and fold subagent runs in the sidebar
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

#190403 landed the nesting half on iOS: `ChatSessionSidebarModel.tree(from:)` nests children from `childSessions`, and `RootSidebar.displayRows` renders them with a chevron, depth indentation, collapse and search expansion. What was still missing is the folding layer: subagent runs are listed as rows, even though they have no transcript of their own, so the conversation that started them never shows what they are doing.

This revision rebases on current `main` and reduces the PR to exactly that layer, on top of #190403's renderer. No second tree renderer, no changes to nesting, and it no longer touches `RootTabsSidebarRegressionTests.swift`, which `main` has removed.

A run's persistent children take the run's place. The run's status and unread state move to the conversation that owns it, including **Home** for runs started from Home.

## User Impact

- Subagent runs no longer appear as chats in the iPhone drawer. Whatever conversation a run started appears in its place, nested under the same parent.
- The owning conversation shows the run's state: a spinner while one runs, a warning triangle and the error line when one failed, an unread dot, and "Waiting for a concurrency slot" while one is queued.
- This holds whether the parent lists the run in `childSessions` or only the run names its parent through `spawnedBy` / `parentSessionKey`.
- Runs started from Home show on the Home row: running, failed (with the error line) or unread.
- The recent-chats cap counts top-level chats only, so one busy parent cannot push other chats out of the list.
- A row's subtitle prefers a failed child, then queued work, then the row's own work line.
- Mark as Read on a conversation also clears the unread runs folded into it.
- A parent's unread dot also covers unread runs folded anywhere below it, so collapsing the parent never hides them.
- Home has a Mark as Read menu when Home or a run folded into Home is unread. It clears them together.
- Sidebar search still lists a matching run as its own row, as macOS does.

No configuration, migration or data change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The rules come from the Control UI session tree (`ui/src/components/app-sidebar-session-tree.ts`) and from the macOS sidebar, not from this PR: runs are never rows, their persistent children take the run's place, and the owner keeps their badges and attention.

- **Run classification is shared with macOS.** `isSidebarRun` and `Node.previewSessions` moved out of the macOS-only files (`ChatSessionSidebar+Tree.swift`, `ChatSessionSidebar.swift`) into `ChatSessionSidebarModel`, so macOS and iOS use one copy. macOS behaviour is unchanged.
- **Folding happens after placement.** `ChatSessionSidebarModel.foldingSubagentRuns(sections)` folds runs inside each section once placement is known, because a pinned or grouped parent can sit in a different section than its run. A run that ends up at the top of a section is resolved through `owningConversationKey`, which prefers the roster's `childSessions` link, then falls back to `spawnedBy` / `parentSessionKey`, walking up through intermediate runs to the first ordinary conversation. A run with no owner at all hands over only its conversations.
- **Home reuses that walk.** `foldedRuns(in:under:)` resolves Home's runs with the same ownership rule, so backref-only runs reach Home too.
- **iOS stays thin.** `RootSidebarModel` wraps `sections()` with the folding call, `RootSidebar` renders the result through #190403's `displayRows`, and `RootSidebarSessionButton` reads its subtitle and unread state from the folded node.

The two open review points in the folding code are fixed here, each with a focused shared-model test:

- **(a) Badges reach every surviving ancestor.** Badges a folded run adds to its owner now propagate through every ancestor of that owner, as nesting would — `a folded run's badges reach every ancestor that survives the fold`. Before, they stopped at the immediate owner.
- **(b) Mark as Read for an unread folded run.** `Node.unreadSessionKeys` carries the row plus the runs folded into it, and the row menu offers Mark as Read when any of them is unread, clearing them together — `mark as read covers an unread run folded into its parent`. Before, the menu only saw the parent and offered Mark as Unread.

The ClawSweeper review of `d53ea12` found two more gaps. Both are fixed in a separate commit on top (`3053676`), each with a focused shared-model test:

- **(c) Unread reaches a collapsed ancestor.** A row's unread dot and its "Unread" accessibility value now read `Node.showsUnread`, which is the aggregated `badges.hasUnread`. The macOS row reads that badge too. Before, the dot read only the row and its directly folded runs, so collapsing a grandparent hid a completed unread run: a completed run brings no spinner or failure line. Mark as Read stays scoped to the row and its own folded runs (`unreadSessionKeys`) — `a collapsed ancestor shows a folded run's unread while mark as read stays on its row`.
- **(d) A read action for runs folded into Home.** Home now has a context menu with Mark as Read whenever Home or one of its folded runs is unread. It clears `ChatSessionSidebarModel.unreadSessionKeys(in:)` over the main session plus `foldedRuns(in:under:)`, through `RootSidebar.performSessionMutation`, the same transport and refresh that session rows use. The mutation is `CommandSessionActionsModifier.markingRead(_:)`, shared with the row menu, so Home and session rows clear unread the same way. I chose an explicit menu over marking runs read whenever Home opens. Opening a session row clears only that session, so an implicit Home clear would quietly acknowledge runs the user never opened — `mark as read on Home covers the runs folded into Home`.

A fifth test covers the basic fold plus Home (`subagent runs fold into their owner and hand over the chats they start`). `displayRows` and `collapsedParents` are untouched, so no production-renderer tests change.

## Evidence

Fixture data only: the app's screenshot transport with a temporary fork-only fixture flag (not part of this PR), on a GitHub-hosted `xcode-27` runner (iPhone 18 Pro simulator, iOS 27; `macos-26` runners were unavailable). The chain is a real parent → subagent run → child: "Release plan" lists the run "Competitor research" in `childSessions`, the run lists "Findings summary" in `childSessions`, and "Findings summary" points back with `parentSessionKey`. Two runs name their owner only through `spawnedBy`: "Inbox triage" (running, started from Home) and "Morning digest" (failed, unread, started from Home). "Hotel booking" (failed, unread) is under "Trip planning".

| `main` at `6d1726a` | This PR at `d53ea12` |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: Inbox triage, Morning digest and Competitor research are chats of their own; Home shows no failed run; Trip planning looks idle](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/05adccff-376c-4466-9468-b5a3a9edc4d6) | ![After: runs are gone, Findings summary sits where Competitor research was, Home shows "Child session Morning digest failed: Digest…" with an unread dot, and Trip planning shows its failed unread run](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/05a82650-42dd-49d8-89f2-b9f18dd96567) |

On `main`, "Inbox triage", "Morning digest" and "Competitor research" are rows of their own, Home shows no sign of its failed run, and "Trip planning" looks idle. On this head the runs are gone, "Findings summary" appears in the place of "Competitor research", Home carries the failed run's error line and unread dot, and "Trip planning" shows its failed unread run.

The row menu on "Release plan", whose folded run "Competitor research" is unread, now offers **Mark as Read**:

![Row menu on Release plan showing Mark as Read because a folded run is unread](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d5a6fb86-ae20-4981-8511-ebb39897e949)

The drawer re-captured on `3053676` matches the screenshot above apart from the clock.

The same fixture now also builds a grandparent → parent → unread run chain, with the run named only through `spawnedBy`: **Launch prep** → **Launch copy** → **Copy review** (completed, unread). Only "Copy review" is unread, and it is never listed in `childSessions`, so any unread state on "Launch prep" comes from aggregation. With "Launch prep" expanded, "Copy review" is folded into "Launch copy" and no run row exists. Collapsing "Launch prep" removes "Launch copy" and leaves the unread dot on the collapsed row (c):

![Collapsed Launch prep with no child rows still shows the unread dot from its folded run](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6a4bb856-7ef3-4882-acc2-1572641397bc)

Home in the same run is unread because of "Morning digest". Long-pressing it offers the new **Mark as Read** (d):

![Home long-press menu showing Mark as Read for the run folded into Home](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4e175bac-e14c-49b0-8878-7c07632fe165)

After tapping it, Home's dot and its "Child session Morning digest failed" line are gone, and the run stays folded:

![Home after Mark as Read: no unread dot and no failure line](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/824a560a-edc9-4ccd-a061-38b3b3cc8b5e)

The UI test asserts the same behavior, not just the pixels: the collapsed row's accessibility value contains "Unread", Home's value is "Unread" before the menu and empty after, and its label no longer mentions the failure.

Checks on this head `3053676` ([run](https://github.com/jorge-monalee/openclaw/actions/runs/45071044541)):

- `swift test --filter 'ChatSessionSidebar|ChatCommandPalette'` in `apps/shared/OpenClawKit`: 312 tests in 24 suites pass, including the five above ([shared job](https://github.com/jorge-monalee/openclaw/actions/runs/45071044541/job/137357824767)).
- SwiftFormat and SwiftLint (iOS and macOS scopes), `pnpm native:i18n:verify`, and the changed-file format check pass in the same job.
- Focused iOS unit tests (`RootTabsPresentationTests`, `RootSidebar*`, `CommandCenterTabSessionFilterTests`, `OpenClawTypographyTests`): 110 tests in 11 suites pass ([iOS head job](https://github.com/jorge-monalee/openclaw/actions/runs/45071044541/job/137357824453)).
- The sidebar UI tests pass on the head, including the read-evidence test above. On `main` the fold test fails at `XCTAssertEqual(runRows, [])` with `["Competitor research", "Hotel booking", "Inbox triage"]` (the before state above) and the read-evidence test fails because "Copy review" is still a row of its own ([iOS base job](https://github.com/jorge-monalee/openclaw/actions/runs/45071044541/job/137357824846)).

Not covered: a physical iPhone. Search intentionally still lists a matching run, as on macOS.

Prepared by Jorge's AI assistant on his behalf.

## What Problem This Solves

When choosing a Desktop source on a phone, the picker showed a shortened device ID instead of the device name. Several machines with the same ID prefix could look identical, even though each **Connect** button opened a different one.

## User Impact

You can identify the machine before connecting. A uniquely named device shows just its name. Devices that share a name also show their full IDs, and an unnamed device shows its full ID without cutting off the ending.

The picker already knows each device’s name and ID. It now shows the extra ID only where it helps distinguish machines, and associates each Connect button with the description in its own row. The connection target and desktop controls are unchanged.

## Evidence

The existing phone comparisons show a single named machine and the list after a refresh with duplicate and missing names. The picker regression failed on the screenshot baseline. It passed in Chromium on the isolated fix: both duplicate IDs were readable, and pressing Enter on the second Connect button requested that machine, not the first. prs.title: fix: show channel contributors by name in session People
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Opening People in a channel session can show a sender’s numeric ID instead of their name. A linked sender can appear twice: once as that ID and once as their OpenClaw profile.

## User Impact

People shows unlinked contributors by their channel names when available. A contributor whose recorded channel activity consistently belongs to a verified profile appears once under that profile. The list and count agree. Access, co-author credit, and original contribution records do not change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Participant recording used to discard the sender’s name and verified profile link. This change saves both when the message arrives and uses them to build the roster. Equal names or IDs across channels or accounts are not enough to group two rows. A later account link does not reassign earlier activity.

For older sessions, People can recover a missing name from an already-loaded message when its full sender identity matches. Ambiguous rows remain separate. There is no bulk transcript scan or migration.

## Evidence

With the same synthetic Discord input, the actual Control UI showed a linked profile and two numeric IDs before; afterward it showed the linked profile once and the unlinked contributor’s channel name. Focused tests covered persistence across restart, renames, out-of-order input, changed account links, equal IDs from different sources, and historical labels. All 27 SQLite participant tests passed on the committed head. The UI comparison used synthetic Gateway responses, not a live Discord installation or customer session.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Opening an old chat could show “Couldn’t save the previous draft” before the user typed anything. When browser storage was unavailable, this appeared on top of the notice that saved messages couldn’t be accessed.

## User Impact

Browsing with an empty composer now shows only the storage-access notice in that situation. If you type a draft or add a Side chat comment that can’t be saved, you still get a warning and the edit stays in the tab. No migration or user action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The composer and Side chat both check for saved input when a chat opens. Neither check is a failed edit. The shared recovery check leaves its notice to the recovery panel; a failure reading an individual chat draft reports an access error without consuming the warning for a later failed save.

## Evidence

prs.title: fix(update): let container installs update and official images start again
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Since #203194 (Git) and #203497 (packages), update preflight refuses every install whose process sees `/.dockerenv` or a `container`, `DOCKER_CONTAINER` or `OPENCLAW_CONTAINER` environment value: "This installation belongs to a container image. Update the image instead." v2026.11.6 had no such rule. npm, pnpm, Bun and Git installs that users set up themselves in a devcontainer, a Podman/LXC host (both set `container=…`) or a self-built image can no longer update. The upgrade-survivor `package-installed-recovery` scenario fails on `main` at this refusal (run `14fe677f`), and the Docker update lanes that install npm packages into test containers are refused the same way.

The official image built from `main` also cannot run any `openclaw` command: #203194 made `openclaw.mjs` import `./release-launcher-forward.mjs`, and the Dockerfile copies root modules one by one without it (`ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`). The existing `test/scripts/docker-launcher-closure.test.ts` catches exactly this but is not selected when only `openclaw.mjs` changes.

## User Impact

- Installs inside containers update again, as in v2026.11.6.
- Images built from `main` start again.
- The official image still never replaces its code from inside the container. It now says so through the existing owner marker: `/app/openclaw-install-owner.json` declares `owner: "container-image"`, so `openclaw update`, `update repair` and Gateway update requests return "Managed by the OpenClaw container image. Pull the new image and recreate the container to update this Gateway." without changing anything, and background checks skip registry updates, as for the macOS and desktop apps.

## Changes

- `src/update/preflight.ts`: remove the container environment guess.
- `src/infra/install-owner.ts`: accept `container-image` as a marker owner.
- `Dockerfile`: write the marker in the runtime image; copy `release-launcher-forward.mjs` next to `openclaw.mjs` in both stages.
- Docs: `install/updating.md`, `install/docker.md`.

## Evidence

- `src/update/prepare.test.ts` "prepares an install that runs inside a container": fails on `main` (container refusal), passes with the fix; `prepare.test.ts` and `install-owner.test.ts` 34/34.
- `test/scripts/docker-launcher-closure.test.ts`: fails on `main`'s Dockerfile (`Cannot find module …/release-launcher-forward.mjs` in both stages), 3/3 with the fix.
- Official image built from `82bd1cff35` (Linux arm64, OrbStack, image user uid 1000): `openclaw --version` works; the default CMD serves `/readyz` 200; `openclaw update --json` and `openclaw update --dry-run --json` both return `status: "host-managed"` with the `container-image` owner and the pull-and-recreate hint; `/app/package.json` and `/app/dist/index.js` hashes are unchanged and no update run succeeded. The same build from `8c16706688` (before the Dockerfile copy) failed every command with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`.
- Upgrade survivor `package-installed-recovery` with a candidate from `8c16706688`: passes the container refusal it stopped at on `main`, then stops at the next existing failure (service inspection on a host without a systemd user bus, run `4c326c22`), fixed separately in its own PR.

prs.title: feat: prepare worker placements for recovery after restart
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

After a worker is confirmed lost, Codex recovery needs to know which placement it is replacing, even if the Gateway restarted. The shared database has no field for that fact yet. Upstream v41 is reserved for approval requester metadata; this independent migration uses v42.

## User Impact

This prerequisite adds storage only; it does not enable recovery or change existing placements. Shared state advances from v41 to v42 (the agent schema is unchanged). Older builds require restoration of the verified pre-upgrade backup before downgrade.

Related: #201026, #201032. The existing shared branch and both PRs are untouched.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing placement row and migration owner: one nullable field on SQLite and PostgreSQL, no backfill, no automatic loss inference, and no reader or writer for the new field in this PR. The placement owner can later record the predecessor with its existing placement update; a separate store would add another write and rollback boundary. No repository reset, permission change, or new retention policy is included. [Maintainer design acceptance](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/2d5e4b6d-a60b-4a09-a054-d919b7a422c0).

## Evidence

- SQLite fixtures from published stable v36, beta v40, and current-main v41 all preserved their original rows and markers on commit refusal, then upgraded to v42. The existing v41 approval requester was preserved and the new placement field remained NULL. This was a migration-owner replay, not a packaged updater run.
- Isolated PostgreSQL 18.6 passed 17 focused migration and owner cases plus two existing first-use regression cases. Historical catalogs and optional repository fragments were preserved. The CI artifact build, focused typechecks, lint, formatting, generated checks, and test-line budget (+302 before the compatibility follow-up; 400 allowed) passed. The build reported two nonfatal UI budget notices; no UI code changed. Local independent review tooling could not start inside its required sandbox.
- The published npm 2026.11.6 updater activated an explicit tarball built from the tested v42 source tree in isolated, offline Podman. The candidate Gateway startup check passed; the update ledger recorded `succeeded` / `finished` and the activation journal reached `anchor-retired`. SQLite advanced v36 → v42; `quick_check` passed, and all original placement and worker fields matched. The synthetic approval survived with its transport reference normalized by existing Doctor behavior; the new nullable fields remained NULL. No managed service restart was requested.
- The follow-up at `d650a99b8c6f` registers the migration in the extracted PR wrapper and keeps v8 and v21 placement repairs on their historical layouts. The v42 migration alone adds the new field to those stores. The local repair run passed 66 selected storage and provisioning cases, including rollback, live-claim refusal, and cold extracted provisioning. The wrapper source-closure check passed; one additional extracted-package assertion was blocked locally by a mismatched installed `undici` version. [CI for the repaired head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45066136506).
- The fixture-only follow-up at `9291b3c580d0` makes the copied registry, first-use, preflight, and Doctor databases genuinely pre-v42. All four selected suites passed, including the packaged CLI Doctor repair followed by fresh Gateway readiness for the copied v2 state. Local database dialect and worker ratchets passed before this test-only delta; the previous hosted ratchet job was interrupted by its runner. [CI for the fixture follow-up](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45067587314).
- The `prepare-state` PostgreSQL command suite now checks the canonical current schema for both `prepared` and `ready`. Its stale v41 assertion reproduced on the prior v42 head (1 failed, 2 passed); isolated PostgreSQL 18.6 passed all 3 cases with the test-only follow-up at `7ac3e3df12e2`. [Current-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45070683884).
- In the prior run, [models-auth](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45067587314/job/137347873950) matched the [scheduled-main failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45060721787/job/137326224598). On its exact base `128d31793346`, isolated replay reproduced both the [packaged worker revocation timeout](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45067587314/job/137347870205) and the [Codex native-config rejection mismatch](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45067587314/job/137347874035) without this PR. This is baseline attribution, not a passing CI gate.
- [Hosted CI on `7ac3e3df12e2`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45070683884) passed all four PostgreSQL conformance shards and PG16 smoke. The worker revocation, models-auth and Codex native-config failures matched the baseline evidence above. [The CI planner mismatch](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45070683884/job/137358763804) reproduced on the exact main checkout base `948c233eaedf`: both report the same six deleted update test paths retained in the inventory after #203497. [The separate lint job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45070683884/job/137359697455) hit its 15-minute limit. The required CI gate did not pass.
- **Upgrade cost:** one nullable ALTER on `worker_session_placements`, no backfill or row rewrite; SQLite retains existing idempotent index checks and quick/placement integrity checks. The scoped SQLite backup copies placement rows and publication metadata; the package updater retains its existing full rollback capture. PostgreSQL takes its normal DDL lock and publishes the version. Largest-deployment row counts and backup/lock timings were not available; managed-service restart and a Swift build are still unverified.

Original implementation: @galiniliev, selectively ported from `a1b9b73924b6`.

prs.title: fix: keep GitHub project chats waiting for a busy clone
prs.body:
Related: #184272 addressed a similar wait for a registered checkout, not the shared clone lock.

## What Problem This Solves

When someone starts a local chat from a GitHub project whose shared clone is busy, workspace preparation can fail after 30 seconds. The first message never reaches the agent, even if the other operation releases the lock shortly afterward.

## User Impact

The first message stays pending while the clone is busy and runs once in the same chat when the lock is released. The user can stop the turn while it waits. Only this workspace-preparation path uses the longer, bounded wait; other callers keep the existing default.

## Why This Change Was Made

The admitted turn already owns cancellation and workspace preparation. It now uses the same 30-minute limit as worktree contention for acquiring the clone lock, without retrying the chat or starting a second clone. No configuration or migration is needed.

## Evidence

- Before: `sessions.create` failed with a held project-clone lease while a real SQLite holder was still active. The test advances the waiter’s clock past 30 seconds without sleeping for 30 seconds.
- After: both regressions passed (7.3 seconds of test execution). Release dispatches the original message exactly once and completes its original run. Stop settles the original run while the lock is still held, without dispatching or creating a worktree. Formatting, lint, and the scoped TypeScript check also passed.
- Adjacent checks: the project environment suite passed. The initialized repository-child test failed with the same label collision on the unchanged base. Two project registry cases could not run past fixture setup because the host blocks shallow fetches in linked worktrees; 39 registry cases passed. The independent reviewer could not start in the local isolated scratch environment.

Reported and co-authored by @vyctorbrzezowski.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

prs.title: fix: surface favorites and recommended models in picker search
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Searching for a version such as `5.5` lists one provider’s entire block before another provider’s equally good matches. A starred model can land below a dated snapshot even when the snapshot’s rolling alias is already visible.

## User Impact

In Chat and New Session, exact names and model IDs beat partial matches. Among equally close matches, selectable favorites and catalog recommendations rise across providers. A dated build stays directly searchable; browsing without a query is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing catalog recommendation and the user's saved favorites rather than guessing capability from a version number, provider name, or context size. Only defer a dated ID when its own provider also offers the undated ID. Other ties keep their existing order. Search rendering and keyboard selection consume the same ranking.

## Evidence

In the real Control UI with a synthetic six-model catalog, the same `5.5` search moved the starred Opus from fourth to first and recommended Sonnet from fifth to second. Enter selected the starred result; typing the full snapshot reference selected that exact row. The regression failed on `abd8b92cfa49` and passed with the fix. The picker unit suites (28 tests), bundled desktop/mobile Chromium suite (4 tests), UI typecheck, scoped lint and formatting passed. No live provider inference was used.

Related: #200217, #186714, #197587

## What Problem This Solves

With Group by → None, browsing older conversations in the sidebar stops at the first page and requires repeated clicks on Show more.

## User Impact

- With **Group by → None**, scrolling to the end of the native **Other** list reveals the next 15 loaded sessions. It still opens at 30 and keeps Show more for keyboard users and for lists too short to scroll.
- Grouped modes and catalog sections continue to use Show more. Opening the drawer or fitting the first page on screen does not reveal extra sessions without scrolling.
- This reveals sessions already loaded. Fetching older pages from the Gateway is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The sidebar projection identifies the native Other list in the ungrouped layout. That section alone observes its end while the list is scrolled. Show more and Collapse still load only where they are needed.

## Evidence

Group by none, 100 sessions, after scrolling to the end of the list twice:

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: the list stops at Conversation 30 with Show more](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/cad2e20862be439f5f5755439937cdc8e656430a/images/2026/11/1a2df424-1b27-4cdd-a775-6fdb6450154a.png) | ![After: the list continues past Conversation 30](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/cad2e20862be439f5f5755439937cdc8e656430a/images/2026/11/b3af6ea3-531a-444c-9a0e-d570a87d96c9.png) |

- E2Es that page the flat list with Show more press it without Playwright's scroll into view, since that scroll would reach the list's end and show a page by itself.
- Author’s prior validation of the shared paging path in headless Chromium: 8 sidebar unit/browser files (`app-sidebar*` projection, visibility, freshness, memo, feedback, stress, sessions, people), 18 sidebar, session-management and chat E2E files, UI typecheck and UI test typecheck, lint, and formatting.

prs.title: fix(release): keep platform optional deps out of bundled dependencies
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The published `@openclaw/memory-lancedb` 2026.11.5/2026.11.6 ship a single `@lancedb/lancedb-*` native binding — the release host's variant. On macOS arm64 (and every platform that is not the build host) the plugin then fails with `Cannot find native binding`, so `openclaw doctor --fix` refuses to converge after an update. Fixes #203211.

## User Impact

A published plugin package declares all seven platform bindings as `optionalDependencies` and no longer bundles whichever one the release machine happened to install, so `npm` resolves the matching binding at install time on macOS, Linux (gnu/musl) and Windows. Regular runtime dependencies keep bundling as before, and a dependency with an approved workspace patch keeps its patched bytes in the package in every bundling mode.

## Why This Change Was Made

The packaged manifest computed `bundledDependencies` from `listPackageRuntimeDependencyNames`, which merges `dependencies` **and** `optionalDependencies`. When the release pipeline enables bundling, the build host's installed optional dependency therefore entered the bundled closure — exactly the "10 bundled packages: the seven @lancedb/lancedb-* packages, apache-arrow, openai, typebox" shape reported in the issue.

Optional dependencies are now excluded from the auto-collected bundle list (the explicit `bundleDependencies` config is untouched). Any plugin that opts a native package in explicitly can still do so.

That exclusion must not drop the neighbouring contract at the same owner: the producer has preserved approved workspace patch bytes in published artifacts since #133616, so a patched dependency must never fall back to the unpatched registry package. The published list therefore unions the verified patched names in **both** modes — automatic bundling skips an optional dependency, but never skips a patched one.

## Evidence

**Destination installation, using the real published artifact as "before".** `npm pack @openclaw/memory-lancedb@2026.11.6` gives the shipped package: its manifest lists all seven `@lancedb/lancedb-*` packages under `bundledDependencies`. Installing it with the destination platform forced (`npm install <tarball> --os=darwin --cpu=arm64`, npm platform overrides on this Windows x64 host) yields:

| Run | Artifact | `lancedb.darwin-arm64.node` after install | Bindings present |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Before | published `@openclaw/memory-lancedb@2026.11.6` | **not found anywhere** | only the bundled `@lancedb/lancedb-linux-x64-gnu` |
| After | this branch packed with `plugin-npm-build-and-pack.mts` + `OPENCLAW_PLUGIN_NPM_BUNDLE_DEPENDENCIES=1` | `node_modules/@lancedb/lancedb-darwin-arm64/lancedb.darwin-arm64.node` | destination platform resolved |

That is the reported failure (`Cannot find native binding` on a platform other than the release host) and its recovery, without needing the macOS host itself: the published package suppresses the optional install because it claims the binding is bundled, and the fixed package leaves it to npm.

**Packaging manifest A/B** through the shipped pack entrypoint on this Windows host (build-host variant `@lancedb/lancedb-win32-x64-msvc`):

| Run | Source | Packaged `bundledDependencies` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Before | `upstream/main` | `["openai","apache-arrow","typebox","@lancedb/lancedb-win32-x64-msvc"]` |
| After | this branch `fb29ef4e` | `["apache-arrow","openai","typebox"]` |

![Destination install + packaging before/after for platform optional dependencies](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wr-web/openclaw/proof-assets/203211/platform-bundle-proof.png)

**Regression tests in the existing packaging boundary** (`test/plugin-npm-package-manifest.test.ts`). These run the real `npm pack` and a real consumer `npm install` against a loopback registry, so the runtime value read back is the dependency bytes a destination install would actually load:

| Fixture | What it declares | Reviewed head `95d0f0a7` | This head `fb29ef4e` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `optional-auto` (new) | `local-runtime-dep` optional **and** workspace-patched, `unpatched-sibling` optional (unpatched), `OPENCLAW_PLUGIN_NPM_BUNDLE_DEPENDENCIES=1` | ❌ consumer install loads registry value **1** (patch silently dropped) | ✅ consumer install loads patched value **2**; `bundledDependencies: ["local-runtime-dep"]`; `node_modules/unpatched-sibling/` absent from the tarball |
| `optional-direct` | `local-runtime-dep` optional + workspace-patched, automatic bundling off | ❌ `[]` expectation contradicts the patch contract | ✅ `bundledDependencies: ["local-runtime-dep"]` (restored) |
| `skipped-optional` | patched optional dependency npm cannot install on this platform | expected packaging rejection | expected packaging rejection (unchanged) |
| explicit / nested / partial bundles | explicit `bundleDependencies` | `["local-runtime-dep","unpatched-sibling"]` | `["local-runtime-dep","unpatched-sibling"]` (unchanged) |

Red/green, `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run test/plugin-npm-package-manifest.test.ts -t "optional-auto"`:

- Reviewed head (source-only revert of `listPackagedBundledDependencyNames`): `AssertionError: expected [ 1, null ] to deeply equal [ 2, null ]`
- This head: `✓ preserves patched dependency packaging contracts (optional-auto)` — 1 passed
- Whole file on this head: **58 passed**

**Patch preservation contract** (the two provenance items):

- `Verified workspace patch preservation` (`c093e859`): every verified patched dependency is in the published bundle in both modes again; the earlier revision dropped optional ones under automatic bundling.
- `Patched optional-dependency fixture` (`76c22742`): the `optional-direct` expectation is restored, and the new `optional-auto` case covers the automatic-bundling variant instead of weakening it.

Gates: `check:line-cap-ratchet` OK; `check:test-lines-ratchet` net +28, allowance 400; `oxfmt --check` and `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` clean on the changed files; `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.root.tooling.json --incremental` exit 0; `git diff --check` clean.

## Compatibility

The change only affects the *automatic* bundle closure: `bundledDependencies` in a published plugin no longer contains that plugin's unpatched `optionalDependencies`, while patched ones stay. Explicit `bundleDependencies` entries keep bundling, so a package that intentionally pins a native dependency can still do so; and regular `dependencies` keep bundling exactly as before. Installers see the platform packages as ordinary optional dependencies of the published package, which is the contract `@openclaw/memory-lancedb` already declared in its manifest.

## What was not tested

- No install on a real macOS arm64 or Linux host: the destination leg uses npm's `--os/--cpu` platform overrides on Windows x64 and asserts which binding npm installs, which is the same decision npm makes on the real host.
- The fixture suite needs GNU tar to read Windows paths as local (`TAR_OPTIONS=--force-local`) on this checkout; that only affects the local extraction step, not what `npm pack` puts in the tarball. CI on Linux runs the same file without it.
- Core typecheck (`tsconfig.core.json`) remains CI-only: `run-tsgo` cannot resolve the workspace `@openclaw/proc-safe` on this machine (it fails the same way on clean `upstream/main`). The tooling project that covers these files exits 0 locally.

prs.title: fix: keep scheduled runs from starting a second Goal turn
prs.body:
Related: #203029, #187126

## What Problem This Solves

When a scheduled automation completes in a conversation with an active Goal, the Goal queue can try to start another turn with the automation’s expired permissions. The scheduled reply may have been saved successfully even though the chat then shows a failed follow-up.

## User Impact

A scheduled run can still advance the Goal and save its result. The scheduler owns later scheduled runs, including an explicit rearm; the original run does not also start an unscheduled Goal turn. An authenticated Resume can continue the same Goal through normal chat admission.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep scheduled occurrence authority attached to the occurrence, even when a background completion carries its requester. The Goal queue does not turn that authority into a new Goal start. This does not change scheduler retirement or take the chat owner’s permissions.

**Draft scope:** This patch does not add automatic continuation based on a previously settled Start or Resume. A separate authorized request must still start the next chat turn. The background-completion boundary is covered in focused tests, not by a detached-command Gateway scenario.

## Evidence

- The Gateway test with a local scripted model verified that a scheduled run saved its checkpoint without starting a Goal turn; an explicit Resume then started and completed the same Goal with one automatic chat follow-up.
- The timer-driven Gateway test verified that `next_check` fired one new scheduled occurrence, did not start an additional Goal turn, and let the one-shot job retire after success.
- 111 focused Goal-queue and requester-admission tests passed, including Stop, revocation, and scheduled-origin cases. Targeted runtime lint, core typecheck, and format checks passed. CI and independent review were not run.

Reported and co-authored by @vyctorbrzezowski.

prs.title: chore(test): align latent-red tests with one-time admission and no-auto-disable cron
prs.body:
Related: #203488, #203106, #203516

## What Problem This Solves

Twenty test cases fail on `main`, but main's push CI never selects them, so `main` looks green. They only show up on PRs whose changed-test selection reaches them through a shared hub such as the state-db cache, so unrelated PRs go red (for example #203530 and #203539). This PR repairs fourteen of them, plus one update.run handoff fixture. Each of these asserts behavior that a reviewed, landed change removed on purpose.

## User Impact

None for users. This is a test-only change. PR CI stops reporting these failures on unrelated PRs.

## Why This Change Was Made

**One-time admission (#203488 `6ff7a062e54`, #203516 `cc7b482f887`).** A Gateway request now checks the caller's authority once, when it is admitted. If the requester is revoked while the request is running, the request is allowed to finish, and the revocation applies to the next request (root `AGENTS.md`: "Check authority one time, when work starts"). Ten cases still expected the old mid-request "Gateway requester authority changed" refusal. Each test keeps whatever it still proves:

- `exec-approvals.test.ts`: the native commit keeps its write by an admitted requester. The legacy get/set cases now prove that a mutation already started finishes after the requester is revoked. The revoke-before-save case is deleted, because the set case covers it.
- `sessions-diff.test.ts`: still proves that polls share preparation and that metadata stays per session.
- `system-changes.test.ts`: keeps the delayed rejected-read case.
- `sessions-create-device-folder.test.ts`: keeps the device data fence, where the node connection goes away.
- `server.sessions.create.lifecycle.test.ts`: keeps the membership-revocation data fence.
- `server.sessions.create.projects.test.ts`: keeps the data fence where the parent repository is reassigned mid-copy.
- `auth-api-key.test.ts`: the revoked-requester save case is deleted.

**No auto-disable on run failures (#203106 `8bdaed5c352`).** `doctor-health.legacy-update.test.ts` had three heartbeat-owner "notification" variants. They expected the tenth failure to auto-disable the job and queue a "10 consecutive run failures" safety notice, and #203106 removed both. Update Doctor now settles the interrupted run from its recorded failure: `consecutiveErrors` goes to 10, `runningAtMs` is cleared, and the job keeps its schedule with no auto-disable. History is unchanged. The variants now assert that.

**Git installs left the handoff (#203194 `be5f7fad9df`).** In `server.roles-allowlist-update.test.ts`, "update.run persists the accepted handoff before parking and restarting its foreground owner" used a Git install fixture. #203194 moved Git installs onto prepared releases and the resident launcher, so update.run no longer reached the managed-service handoff this test asserts. The fixture now uses an npm package install, which still takes that path; the assertions are unchanged apart from the sentinel `mode` (`npm`).

Rejected alternatives: reverting #203488 or #203106, which were deliberate and reviewed. I also chose not to pin the native commit's current "Gateway state owner or requester changed" refusal, because that is an older re-check the one-admission cuts are still removing.

## Not covered here (named gaps)

- `test/cli-message-authority.integration.test.ts` and `test/cron-message-read.integration.test.ts`: #203551 (open, tracking #203512) is already repairing these, so I left them out.
- `test/gateway-restart-resume.e2e.test.ts` > "records a visible outcome when a marked run loses requester authority before restart": I didn't change this test. Replayed and restarted work is supposed to check authority again when it starts, so the missing "could not resume" notice may be a real silent-outcome regression, not a stale assertion. It fails on `cc7b482f887` (#203516) in our runs. It needs the owner's call.
- `src/gateway/worker-environments/destination-authority.e2e.test.ts` (3 cases): this fails with "No model is configured" in `placement-session-runtime.ts`. That's a different cause from the one-admission and auto-disable changes, so I left it out.

## Evidence

- Bisect: the five gateway files pass at `6ff7a062e54~1` and fail at `6ff7a062e54`. `doctor-health.legacy-update` passes at `8bdaed5c352~1` and fails at `8bdaed5c352`. `auth-api-key` passes at `6ff7a062e54` and fails at `cc7b482f887`. Every failure reproduces on `2754763da23`.
- On head (base `afa93a83e4e`), `node scripts/test-projects.mts` passes: the five gateway files 103/103, and `auth-api-key` 46, `doctor-health.legacy-update` 14 and `server.sessions.create.projects` 18 all pass.
- `server.roles-allowlist-update.test.ts`: fails on `afa93a83e4e` (no `handoff`/`sentinel` in the payload), 17/17 with the package fixture.
- `run-oxlint` on the changed files is clean, and so is `git diff --check`.
- $autoreview P2 on the first commit came back scoped-clean. An independent read-only Codex review of the first commit found no findings. Both reviews were rerun on `56bd31fde7f` and were clean again. The last commit changes only the two fixture lines.
- Tests: +232 / -453. No production change.
