## What Problem This Solves

The tool-usage CLI accepted hexadecimal and exponent notation as bounded integers, so inputs such as `0x10` and `1e1` could silently select a range even though these options are documented as integer day/count values.

## User Impact

Decimal integer values within the existing bounds continue to work, while non-decimal, fractional, zero, and out-of-range values are rejected before any Gateway request is made.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both `tools usage import --since` and `tools usage status --limit` now use the shared strict positive-integer parser. The parser stays private to the CLI owner, the help text keeps plain ASCII ranges, and the two tracked CLI files are stored as LF again so the diff only contains the behavior change.

## Evidence

At head `a6927a4ffc072bb42c151e41e9b4d0904a551df8` (rebased onto `main` `1a0a24dcd2c`), both flags reject non-decimal and fractional input before any Gateway call, while in-range decimal values still parse.

Checks: `run-format.mts --check` passes on both files, and `git -c core.whitespace=cr-at-eol diff --check upstream/main...HEAD` passes.

prs.title: fix(openai): embed system prompt in input on ChatGPT Responses when uncached (#202372)
prs.body:
Closes #202372

## What Problem This Solves

On `openai/gpt-6.2-sol` and other models using the ChatGPT Responses backend (`openai-chatgpt-responses`), top-level `instructions` are not cached by the provider, but the request builder always placed the system prompt in `instructions` and disabled input prompt conversion. This resulted in the entire system prompt being reprocessed uncached on every turn, causing excessive subscription quota usage and avoidable prefill latency.

## User Impact

User impact: Restores prompt caching for system prompts on GPT-6.2 models accessed via ChatGPT OAuth subscriptions by embedding the prompt in leading developer input as indicated by `cachesInstructions: false`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The model catalog already configures `cachesInstructions: false` for GPT-6.2, but the ChatGPT Responses adapter hardcoded `includeSystemPrompt: false` and always populated `instructions`. Consulting `cachesInstructions` enables system-prompt input conversion and omits the uncached `instructions` field when `cachesInstructions` is `false`, while preserving existing `instructions` behavior for models that support and cache it.

## Evidence

### Wire Comparison (`openai-chatgpt-responses`)

| Field | Base (before fix) | Head (with fix, `cachesInstructions: false`) |
|---|---|---|
| `instructions` | `"You are an autonomous agent."` (uncached on 6.2) | `undefined` (omitted from payload) |
| `input[0]` | `{ type: "message", role: "user", ... }` | `{ type: "message", role: "developer", content: [{ type: "input_text", text: "You are an autonomous agent." }] }` |
| `input[1]` | Next user turn message | `{ type: "message", role: "user", ... }` |

### Multi-turn WebSocket Continuation & Cache Reuse Trace

Verified over unmocked `WebSocketServer` via `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-chatgpt-responses.test.ts`:

1. **Turn 1 (Cold request, initial developer prompt)**:
   ```json
   {
     "model": "gpt-6.2-sol",
     "stream": true,
     "input": [
       { "type": "message", "role": "developer", "content": [{ "type": "input_text", "text": "System Prompt 1" }] },
       { "type": "message", "role": "user", "content": [{ "type": "input_text", "text": "turn 1" }] }
     ]
   }
   ```
   *Outcome*: `instructions` omitted; system prompt placed in leading developer input for prefix caching.

2. **Turn 2 (Continuation with unchanged prompt)**:
   ```json
   {
     "model": "gpt-6.2-sol",
     "stream": true,
     "previous_response_id": "resp_1",
     "input": [
       { "type": "message", "role": "user", "content": [{ "type": "input_text", "text": "turn 2" }] }
     ]
   }
   ```
   *Outcome*: `previous_response_id` continues the stored chain. The delta input carries only the new user turn without duplicating the developer prompt or breaking prefix caching.

3. **Turn 3 (System prompt changed to `System Prompt 2 (Changed)`)**:
   ```json
   {
     "model": "gpt-6.2-sol",
     "stream": true,
     "input": [
       { "type": "message", "role": "developer", "content": [{ "type": "input_text", "text": "System Prompt 2 (Changed)" }] },
       { "type": "message", "role": "user", "content": [{ "type": "input_text", "text": "turn 1" }] },
       ...
     ]
   }
   ```
   *Outcome*: Continuation is safely invalidated (`previous_response_id` omitted) and a full replay is dispatched with the new developer prompt.

### Automated Test Suite Execution

- **Reproduction**: Unit test proved red failure on base (`AssertionError: expected { model: 'gpt-6.2-sol', ... } to not have property "instructions" (received "You are an autonomous agent.")`) and passes green with the fix.
- **Suite Results**:
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-chatgpt-responses.test.ts`: **35 passed** (including uncached prompt placement, cached prompt retention, and multi-turn WebSocket continuation).
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-chatgpt-responses.replay.test.ts`: **4 passed**
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-chatgpt-responses-streaming.test.ts`: **9 passed**
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-chatgpt-responses-protocol.test.ts`: **5 passed**
  - `packages/ai/src/transports/openai-responses-uncached-instructions.integration.test.ts`: **4 passed**
  - `packages/ai/src/transports/openai-responses-payload-policy.test.ts`: **28 passed**
- **Standards & Code Quality**:
  - `oxlint`: 0 warnings, 0 errors.
  - `run-format.mts` & `git diff --check`: Clean.

prs.title: fix: show sender phone number for quoted WhatsApp messages (#202554)
prs.body:
Closes #202554

## What Problem This Solves

When replying to a quoted message in a WhatsApp group where the quoted sender is identified by an internal `@lid` (such as `1234567890@lid`), the agent's inbound reply context displays the opaque `@lid` JID rather than the contact's phone number or display name, even though the receiving account already has the contact's reverse mapping stored in its local credentials folder (`authDir`).

## User Impact

User impact: When someone quotes another user in a WhatsApp group, the AI agent correctly sees the sender's phone number (e.g. `+15555550123`) in the quote context instead of an unreadable `@lid` identifier.

## Why This Change Was Made

Inbound quote extraction (`describeReplyContext`) was not provided with the receiving account's `authDir`, so the participant lookup fell back to the unmapped identifier. Additionally, `resolveComparableIdentity` retained the raw identifier in the `label` property even after resolving the phone number, causing the downstream reply envelope formatter to render the stale raw `@lid`.

This patch:
1. Passes `authDir` from delivery intake and message enrichment into `describeReplyContext`.
2. Updates `resolveComparableIdentity` to update `label` to the resolved `e164` when the existing label is a raw identifier (`@lid` / `@s.whatsapp.net`).
3. Explicitly normalizes and asserts `sender.lid` (and `sender.label = e164`) in expectations, preserving the existing identity normalization contract.

## Evidence

### Behavior comparison

- **Before:**
  Quoted group message with sender `1234567890@lid` mapped to `+15555550123`:
  Agent sees: `[Replying to 1234567890@lid]\noriginal message\n[/Replying]`
- **After:**
  Agent sees: `[Replying to +15555550123]\noriginal message\n[/Replying]`
  Identity data cleanly retains `lid: "1234567890@lid"`, `e164: "+15555550123"`, and `label: "+15555550123"`.

### Automated Tests Verified

All tests pass cleanly across unit, visibility, and monitor integration suites:
1. `extensions/whatsapp/src/inbound/extract.test.ts`: Added unit test `resolves quoted LID sender to phone number via authDir mapping` asserting `sender.lid`, `sender.e164`, and `sender.label`.
2. `extensions/whatsapp/src/auto-reply/monitor/inbound-helpers.test.ts`: Added visibility context test `resolves quoted LID sender to mapped phone label via authDir` asserting `resolveVisibleWhatsAppReplyContext` yields mapped phone label.
3. `extensions/whatsapp/src/monitor-inbox.reply-context.test.ts`: Added monitor inbox test `resolves quoted LID sender to phone number using account authDir` verifying full delivery through Baileys event emission.

<details>
<summary>Test execution logs (Vitest)</summary>

## What Problem This Solves

The plugin catalog cut off long package names and publisher handles beside Install. On a phone, OpenClaw DeepSeek Provider lost the end of its name and the publisher appeared as “@…”. Two search results with the same prefix could look identical even though they were different packages from different publishers.

## User Impact

You can read the package name and publisher before choosing Install or opening the detail page. Short names and handles still share a line when they fit.

## Why This Change Was Made

Let long names and publisher handles wrap in plugin catalog rows. Keep the official badge with the name, and let a wide action move below the text rather than squeeze it into a column of letters. The change is scoped to plugin results, not the shared Skills or Templates cards.

## Evidence

The saved 390 px phone comparisons show the full DeepSeek name and publisher in the catalog, then distinct Cobalt and Amber names and publishers in search. Across 96 matched states on the phone, both tablets, and desktop at default and 140% text, keyboard navigation kept the publisher and Install as separate targets. Enter opened Matrix; tapping Amber opened that exact package. Back restored the previous tab or search query. The Matrix detail title and README crops were unchanged at every width and text size. Two compact layout cases failed on main; all 15 catalog browser tests passed after the fix.

The catalog used synthetic entries. No plugin was installed and no external publisher link was opened. Stock main: `da13d2a9c3023`. Atlas repair: `69278aefc109c`.

prs.title: feat(ios): filter sessions by attention and work
prs.body:
Related: #162814

## What Problem This Solves

On iPhone, finding conversations waiting for an answer or approval requires checking individual session rows.

## User Impact

Sessions gains All, Needs you, and Working filters with conversation counts for the selected Gateway, agent, and existing status scope. One conversation counts once even when it has multiple requests. Working includes active or queued runs and active child work; it can overlap Needs you. Request badges reuse the existing native preview and approval flow.

All preserves offline browsing. Live activity filters are disabled while disconnected, and incomplete rosters retain a + count qualifier.

This is a draft for the initial iOS design review. Physical Duo and VoiceOver checks remain before readiness. Android parity is a separate follow-up using the same filter meanings.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Sessions screen consumes the existing live roster instead of keeping a second nonarchived snapshot. The existing owners retain question/approval matching, expiry, navigation, grouping, mutations, and Gateway policy. No server, protocol, schema, permission, or persistent setting is added.

Android's native SessionsScreen already has the needed roster and attention/run-state contracts. This PR does not modify or claim validation of Android.

## Native Sessions proof with a real Gateway

Captured on the Mac Studio with an iPhone 18 Pro Max simulator running iOS 27.0. The comparison uses upstream `ed3230dd29d1` and published draft head `5c8b666d53e5`. Both apps used the same three fictional conversations from an isolated OpenClaw `2026.11.4` Gateway. The agent ran Qwen3 4B locally through llama.cpp. A test operator created and answered the ordinary question through the Gateway API, and the model generated the separate work turn.

### Clean comparison

| Upstream Sessions | Draft Sessions |
| --- | --- |
| ![Upstream Sessions shows three rows with no activity filter](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2e28e8bf-83a1-4663-b9a6-20923b75021e) | ![Draft Sessions shows the same three rows, with All 3, Needs you 1, and Working 0](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ee20cc17-e197-439d-a1c0-984f26e77384) |

### Annotated comparison

| Upstream | Draft |
| --- | --- |
| ![The rows start immediately below the status scopes](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f2e07899-2d29-4309-b46e-9541c2e72b3c) | ![Activity controls and counts appear between the status scopes and the rows](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ad6e8492-764d-4e94-866c-2401e19d519e) |

### Live updates

| Needs you selected | Working selected | After both settle |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ![Needs you shows only Color review with a pending question](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e9f2873e-da2d-4a86-8442-6b27f3315369) | ![Working shows only Launch checklist during a real model run](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dd7b47fe-cea3-49e2-9fe2-3a98893e1d4e) | ![After the question and run settle, All stays at 3 and both activity counts are 0](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ad309f62-7f9f-45ce-af63-cf17e4183e86) |

The native Sessions screen stayed open during the transition. This trace records the visible filter values and the corresponding Gateway state.

```text
Pending question in Color review     All 3   Needs you 1   Working 0
Needs you selected                  Color review is the only row
Qwen starts on Launch checklist     All 3   Needs you 1   Working 1
Separate capture with Working open  Launch checklist is the only row while the model runs
Gateway accepts Fern                Question status: answered
Model finishes                      All 3   Needs you 0   Working 0
Gateway final state                 Launch checklist: done, no active run
```

The captured proof covers this simulator and the published Sessions screen. The broader design previews below are from separate work.

## November 17 draft update

Merged upstream `ed3230dd29d1` into the existing activity-filter branch. Resolved the four conflicts while retaining upstream session grouping, collapsed sections, and the partial-load retry. The Sessions clock now refreshes when the roster changes and continues to refresh when request or snooze deadlines expire.

Verified on the iOS 27.0 iPhone 18 Pro Max simulator at `5c8b666d53e5`:

- 19 focused Swift tests passed (3 activity logic and 16 typography).
- Both native Sessions flows passed against an isolated synthetic Gateway. The activity flow verified filter counts and live request/run updates. The recency regression verified that a planning row aged past “just now” when a different row changed, with no pending requests or snoozes.
- Native localization verification, SwiftFormat, app-target SwiftLint, and diff checks passed.

The layout images below are from the earlier design prototype. This draft is still asking for an iOS design decision on the focused activity filters.

## Layout prototype for design feedback

The latest local prototype puts a compact filter dropdown beside **Sessions** in the sidebar, with compact icon-and-count cards on the full Sessions screen. Both locations offer **All**, **Needs you**, and **Working**.

On the full Sessions screen, attention rows have one tappable hand or shield on the left. The hand means **Waiting for answer**; the shield means **Waiting for approval**. Both use amber status text and a subtle warning tint because both need a user response. Working rows and the Working card use informational blue. Text and distinct symbols convey the state as well as color. Status labels consistently use sentence case, including Recent, Working, Waiting for answer, and Waiting for approval. The existing native request previews remain available. The sidebar keeps its native attention badges and work indicators.

These images show eight fictional conversations: two waiting for an answer or approval, three working, and three idle. Each image compares **All / Needs you / Working**, with no before/after panels. They are native standard-iPhone simulator captures with synthetic Gateway state. No personal conversations, private Gateway addresses, or real agent tasks appear.

Feedback requested: does keeping the sidebar control beside Sessions make its scope clear? Do the compact cards and the attention-row styling feel clear without adding clutter? Feedback on wording, spacing, colors, and selection styling is welcome. Android parity remains a separate follow-up using the same filter meanings.

**Sessions screen: All / Needs you / Working**

![Latest local Sessions prototype with amber question and approval rows, blue Working states, and compact filter cards](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/04f3b1a7-059a-4c8e-80d0-7aa24a343e14)

**Sidebar: All / Needs you / Working**

![Latest local sidebar prototype with filtering beside the Sessions heading and fictional conversations](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/49b52069-9ba1-41c3-b259-5b3b8bf28392)

These are design previews from uncommitted local refinements atop local prototype `4650e6cf067c249871fa7ee7871c466a450b6d01`. The sidebar placement, card styling, status-row cleanup, and adaptive scope control shown here have not been pushed to this draft's published head, `cbb83f9eff100aa5437f15c19c9c3383ee4657d4`. They are not exact-head merge proof. The PR remains a draft for design feedback.

Local refinement checks: 24 typography tests and four activity-owner logic tests pass, as do the native filter flows at standard and largest accessibility text sizes. The sole leading hand and shield were each tapped to verify that the correct native preview opens without leaving Sessions. Light and dark appearances were inspected. The latest local prototype, including sentence-case status labels, was installed and launched on the physical Duo as the separate OpenClaw Sessions build 10. The installed version was read back from the device. A fresh physical visual/interaction check of this revision and a full VoiceOver audit are still pending. The Evidence section below describes the earlier published implementation separately.

## Evidence

- Base: 42aab1ce38cdde59eaa3f2babc3eef488ea9db2c. The native baseline reaches All Sessions and fails because the activity filter is absent.
- Three focused native logic tests pass: distinct conversation counts, overlapping work/attention, terminal and explicit run-state precedence, resolution/expiry/agent matching, and offline/partial data. Test execution: 0.016 seconds; runner setup/execution: 20.805 seconds.
- Native iPhone UI flow passes with synthesized screen taps at rendered targets, selected-state and membership assertions, 44-point targets, and live count changes after run completion and question/approval resolution. Standard-size run: 53.400 seconds; largest system accessibility text: 47.326 seconds. The filters stack vertically at the largest size. Existing session-row text still elides at that size; this is not a full accessibility audit.
- XCTest AX hit-point lookup reports no hit point for the activity filters and existing status picker on this simulator. The test explicitly synthesizes screen touches rather than relying on AX activation, then checks the resulting state. VoiceOver is not covered by this result.
- 23 focused typography tests pass. Targeted SwiftLint/SwiftFormat, Node syntax, native i18n verification, docs formatting/MDX, link audit, and diff whitespace checks pass.
- Fresh independent source review has no actionable P0-P2 findings. It caught an offline-cache cold-open regression and incomplete archive counts, both repaired before the final run.
- Full-app local qualification: unchanged base strict SwiftLint fails in the Apple review demo fixture, also tracked by #191296. Both UI comparison builds use an independently written, local-only extraction of two unchanged fixture branches, preserving guards, payloads, and timestamps. The synthetic Gateway path never enters those branches. No guard or lint configuration is weakened. That qualification and unrelated generated Info.plist changes are excluded from this PR. These results are not exact-tree full-app CI.
- Evidence uses the native app and an isolated synthetic Gateway. No live agent, provider, command, or account is used. Physical Duo, VoiceOver, exact-head CI, ClawSweeper, and maintainer approval are not claimed.

prs.title: refactor(agents): drop authority reads from the admitted-run receipt body
prs.body:
## Problem

R1 of the one-admission receipt cluster: remove the authority reads from the receipt bodies (`captureGatewayToolReceiptAssertion`, `composeReceiptAuthority`, `captureAdmittedRunActiveAssertion`, `captureAgentRunDelegatedSourceAssertion`). Admission already checks authority once.

This PR lands the part of R1 that holds up. Step 0 below shows why the rest cannot be cut inside these bodies yet.

## Change

- `captureAdmittedRunActiveAssertion`: removed `scopeOperatorAccessDecisions` (operator access-decision sharing) and the authority-lease identity compares (`lease.authority !== authority`, `delegatedAuthorityLeases.get(context) !== lease`). Each production caller passes the lease's root authority, and the run instance plus the registry claim already cover replacement. Kept: Stop (`signal.aborted`), run occurrence, `foregroundClosed` (run close does not abort the caller's optional `signal`) and the registry source.
- Removed the reader-less `cronAuthorityCheck` field from the Gateway tool caller identity and its one producer. #203487 removed its only reader.

Production: 3 files, +4/−16. No test changes. No new export, name, hook, flag or guard.

## Step 0: leaf reads and how each is classified

Test: can the answer change when only a permission, approval or config changes and no session data changes? Yes → authority. No → data fence or Stop.

| Body | Leaf read | Classification | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| `captureAdmittedRunActiveAssertion` | `scopeOperatorAccessDecisions` | Authority (shares operator access decisions) | **Removed** |
| same | `lease.authority !== authority`, `delegatedAuthorityLeases.get(context) !== lease` | Authority-lease identity, not a writer lease | **Removed** |
| same | `signal?.aborted` | Stop | Kept |
| same | `context.operationalRunInstance !== operationalRunInstance` | Run occurrence | Kept |
| same | `lease.foregroundClosed` | Lifecycle. Run close does not abort the caller's optional `signal` | Kept |
| same | `readAgentRunDelegatedAuthorityFailure` | Diagnostic `cause` only | Kept |
| `captureAgentRunDelegatedSourceAssertion` | `context.assertSourceCurrent` (registry run source) | **Mixed:** the caller's run source (data fences, for example `session-fork-run.ts` transcript write token and entry lifecycle) composed with `operatorAuthority.assertCurrent` | Kept. Removing it turned `admitted-run-context.test.ts` red (stale transcript writes) |
| same | `current !== context`, `current.assertSourceCurrent !== source`, `readActiveAgentRunDelegatedAuthority` claim/instance/generation | Run occurrence and generation | Kept |
| same | `isCurrentAgentRunApprovalAuthority` (approval leases) | Run occurrence plus approval-lease abort signals (Stop for one tool call) | Kept |
| `composeReceiptAuthority` | `check()` loop over predicate booleans | **Mixed:** bare predicate booleans carry authority *and* occurrence fences (MCP grant lineage `isGrantAndLineageCurrent`, node claim loss and disconnect, cron invocation close, caller-turn retirement) | Kept. Removing the boolean turned `mcp-http.test.ts` "fences caller authority when the grant is replaced during tool execution" and `node-claude-skill-runtime.test.ts` "rejects publication after awaited file work when claim-loss / disconnect wins" red |
| `captureGatewayToolReceiptAssertion` | `receipt()` boolean + `assertAllowed` on the callable and prepared `assertCurrent` | Same mix; the prepared path is the one that refuses a bare-boolean fence at commit | Kept (same evidence) |
| same | `nativeSource`, `opaqueCommitGuard`, `prepareSessionSource*`, `release`, `assertScopeCurrent` | Session data and writer custody | Kept |
| `prepareAgentRunAdmission` | `prepared.assertCurrent()` | Preparation lifecycle, Stop, run occurrence and generation | Kept |

## What remains (proposed split)

The receipt boolean and the registry run source cannot be cut inside their bodies, because each mixes authority with real data fences.
1. **Registry run source:** `prepareAgentRunAdmission` binds `compose([callerSource, operatorAuthority.assertCurrent])` into the registry. Bind only the caller's source. Then `captureAgentRunDelegatedSourceAssertion` (and `validateAgentRunDelegatedAuthority`) keep the data fences and lose the operator re-check.
2. **Receipt boolean:** convert the boolean receipt leaves that carry occurrence fences into throwing fences or signals at their producers: `mcp-http.ts` `isGrantAndLineageCurrent`, the cron automation invocation receipt, `settleBatch.isCurrent`, the node skill-runtime claim. Then `composeReceiptAuthority` can become `composeSessionSourceAssertion` and `captureGatewayToolReceiptAssertion` a pass-through (R2).

## What users see

Nothing changes. Refusals, Stop and fences behave as on `main`.

## Evidence

Exact head `aaec361a54e1`:

- **Local ClawSweeper review:** `review_status: complete`, "patch is correct", 0 findings (report `aaec361a54e1.md`).
- **One-admission E2E** (isolated Gateway, real model, exact head): `pass: true`. `results.jsonl` (50 KB transcript) is kept with the task proof. `verdict.json`:
  ```json
  {"pass":true,"checks":[{"id":"R.running-turn-finishes","pass":true,"detail":{"state":"final","toolEnds":3,"toolEndsAfterRevoke":3}},{"id":"Q.queued-input-refused-visibly","pass":true,"detail":{"accepted":true,"providerRequestsWithQueuedMarker":0,"visibleRefusalInTranscript":true}},{"id":"S.stop-cancels","pass":true,"detail":{"abort":{"ok":true,"aborted":true},"state":"aborted","requestsWithStopMarker":1}}]}
  ```
- **Typecheck / lint / ratchets:** `pnpm tsgo:core` clean. `pnpm tsgo:test` clean on the first revision; re-run on this head pending CI. oxfmt and oxlint clean on the 3 files. The session-identity, lifetime-check, SQLite dialect, test-timeout-race and mock-export ratchets are OK. Locally, `pnpm check:changed` crashed in the SQLite worker ratchet with an abort, exit 134 (known local heap limit, see #203466). CI covers it.
- **Importer run:** one `ocx test` call on 441 test files (each one imports `gateway-caller-context.ts`, `admitted-run-context.ts` or `attempt-gateway-tools.ts`, plus the files that name the receipt symbols or messages), with `OPENCLAW_NODE_TEST_PLAN_CONTINUE_ON_FAILURE=1`. 11 files went red:
  - Also red on the merge base `8866e18656c5` (separate run): `mcp-http.async-scope`, `github-publication-imported-actions` (3 "requester" cases), `question.communication`, `question.recovery` ("current client") and `settled-turn-finalization.incomplete`. `cron.scheduled-policy-adoption` ("No model is configured", MAIN-ALSO in earlier program PRs) was not re-run on base here.

One standalone run of `subagent-registry-lifecycle` failed 4 *different* cases, and the next run passed. I read this as load flakiness; I have not proven the cause.
- **Earlier revisions (cut too deep, reverted):** removing the registry run source turned `admitted-run-context.test.ts` red. Removing the receipt boolean turned `mcp-http.test.ts` (grant replaced) and `node-claude-skill-runtime.test.ts` (claim-loss and disconnect) red. That evidence is behind the split above.

prs.title: fix: show HEIC photos in Control UI chat previews
prs.body:
Root cause: src/gateway/managed-image-thumbnail-cache.ts:25 (main 45b96ba60b1d). `encodeImageThumbnail` admitted only still PNG, JPEG and WebP and always encoded WebP (line 36). A still HEIC/HEIF upload was refused before encoding, so the preview route returned 404 and chat showed "Unavailable". Admitting HEIF alone would not fix a sips-only macOS Gateway, because `sips` cannot write WebP.

Fixes #203518

Thanks @RaphazZze for the detailed report and @brianmcguire for the fix.

## What Problem This Solves

On a Mac where the Gateway only has the built-in `sips` converter, still HEIC and HEIF uploads can show “Unavailable” in chat previews even though the original upload is intact.

## User Impact

HEIC photos can be previewed without installing an extra WebP encoder. Downloading the original still returns the exact uploaded bytes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use JPEG for still HEIC and HEIF thumbnails and carry the encoded type through the thumbnail cache and response paths. Existing WebP renditions and preview size limits stay in place. HEIF sequences stay outside the still-thumbnail path. The lightbox downloads still HEIC and HEIF originals as attachments with their original extension, while the rules for opening image blobs in a new tab stay in place.

## Evidence

I uploaded the same synthetic HEIC through the real Control UI into two isolated Gateways on Apple Silicon macOS. The Gateway PATH contained only system tools, with `sips` handling HEIC conversion. Chrome used a narrow 420 × 850 viewport. The test used a local fixture model.

| Before · `45b96ba60b1d` | After · `c561f4e93176` |
| --- | --- |
| ![The Control UI shows an Unavailable card where the HEIC preview should appear](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/283d3545-1d17-4b66-bb87-d88a16677b10) | ![The Control UI renders the same synthetic HEIC as a colorful thumbnail](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/02fb7df3-3333-4730-8231-77c35d62a38f) |

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Original Gateway | Thumbnail request returned HTTP 404 and chat showed Unavailable |
| Patched Gateway | Thumbnail request returned HTTP 200 `image/jpeg` and Chrome decoded 160 × 96 pixels |
| Lightbox download | Original returned HTTP 200 `image/heic`. The browser saved the `.heic` file and all 782 bytes matched the upload. |
| Focused regression suites | 22 Gateway tests and 6 image-download tests passed. The duplicate helper test was removed and the HEIF sequence checks remain. |

Original fixture SHA-256: `4eb0eb9ec93816d0878d734116ca8648648dc7a4b66de64e743402a01444c92a`. The byte-for-byte browser download proof was captured in Chrome on macOS. A follow-up on a physical iPhone Duo in Safari used the Files picker. The isolated Gateway received the same 782-byte HEIC. The tester confirmed the thumbnail rendered and Safari saved a `.heic` file. The tester reported that the fixture model’s reply was not visible on the Duo. That reply is outside the preview and download checks.

This addresses the [ClawSweeper proof request](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/203585#issuecomment-7083500720).


Maintainer follow-up (e1b135d89735): the encoder now maps its requested format straight to the returned type, because Rastermill emits exactly the requested format. `scripts/bench-control-ui-media.ts` now uses the new thumbnail record, so the scripts typecheck passes.

Runtime proof on an isolated macOS guest with only `sips` on the Gateway PATH covers main twice, this PR twice, JPEG and PNG controls, and an ImageMagick control. It includes before/after screenshots and a byte-identical original download: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/203585#issuecomment-7085270553

Merge danger: two-way door. The thumbnail cache is in memory only, keyed exactly as before. Nothing is stored or migrated, and no config, dependency or protocol changes. Blast radius: still HEIC/HEIF previews now render as JPEG. PNG, JPEG and WebP previews keep the same WebP bytes. HEIF sequences are still refused.

prs.title: fix: keep chat replies going when a GitHub confirmation arrives
prs.body:
Related: #201477

## What Problem This Solves

A follow-up in chat can fail before the assistant answers if the previous turn’s GitHub publication confirmation arrives while the follow-up is starting. The confirmation is saved, but the user has to resend their message.

## User Impact

The publication confirmation stays visible, and the follow-up gets one reply without a resend.

## Why This Change Was Made

A pending background result can sit after the new user message in stored history without being the answer to that message. Replay now looks past host-marked pending results, as it does for operational notices. Real replies still close the turn. The existing replay identity and retry checks are unchanged; no new retry or storage change is needed.

## Evidence

The regression drives native `chat.send` through a real, isolated Gateway and agent with a local model fixture. It saves a synthetic GitHub result through the real publication reporter just before follow-up admission. On main (`50ff9d4633719`), the receipt appeared and the reply failed with `Persisted user turn changed before replay admission`. With the fix, the receipt stays visible once, the provider gets one follow-up request with the receipt in its normal position after the user message, and chat gets one answer. Both Gateway tests and all 22 replay-cohort tests passed, including refusals for replaced or already-answered turns. Core/test type checks, targeted lint, format and diff checks passed. Broad CI and independent review have not been run; this is a draft.

## Worked on by

- Reported and scoped by @vyctorbrzezowski.

## What Problem This Solves

## User Impact

Three browser cases passed on the repaired build using synthetic responses; no files were imported or replaced.

prs.title: fix(history): one message over the 8 MiB page limit no longer makes a session unreadable
prs.body:
Refs #203439. This fixes the SQLite history readers; the in-memory actor-history reader is the other half of that issue (see *Not in this PR*), so it should not close it.

## What Problem This Solves
One transcript row over the 8 MiB source page limit — in practice a `view_image` result holding several full-size PNGs inline — makes every `chat.history` page that contains it throw `Transcript history message exceeds the 8388608-byte page limit`. The Control UI then shows "Failed to load history" and the whole session can no longer be opened, although docs/web/webchat.md promises a `[chat.history omitted: message too large]` stand-in for exactly this case.

## Fix
- A display-history read serves a row whose recorded bytes exceed the page bound as the documented stand-in (`__openclaw: { truncated: true, reason: "oversized" }`) and charges the page only the stand-in's bound, so the rows around it still load. Covers recent, offset, anchored (`messageId`) and closed-reset-interval reads.
- **The oversized payload is never selected.** A message range read for a display page selects the payload column only for rows within the bound (`CASE WHEN bytes + 1 > bound THEN NULL`); an oversized row's stand-in is built from its `transcript_event_identities` id and parent plus its `message_role`. Closed-reset history fetches payloads only for rows within the bound and builds the rest from identities. Oversized boundary rows (compaction, reset, `custom_message`) are built from the identity the reader already holds. The schema caps compressed and cold rows at 4 MiB, so every row past the 8 MiB bound is stored inline and the cold-payload fallback is never reached for one.
- Admission and projection compare the same quantity, recorded row bytes plus the one JSONL separator, so a row of exactly the limit cannot be billed as a stand-in and then decoded whole.
- Anchored windows keep expanding past an oversized neighbour instead of truncating and dropping the rows behind it with nothing disclosed to the client.
- The stand-in carries the record's own id (its identity row; the JSONL parser no longer promotes an `id` nested in the payload), so its exact read and its pagination anchor point at a row that exists.
- Model-context source pages and exact reads still decode a row whole or refuse it (unchanged).

Third revision (review 2's P1): `e1f639512fb` stops selecting oversized message payloads in the live and closed-reset readers, +231/-58 over 6 files, 67 of them the new test. Second revision: 547 changed lines over 11 files down to 288 over 8. The in-memory actor-history reader is no longer touched (see *Not in this PR*), the duplicated stand-in builders and the payload-scanning id recovery are gone, and the tests cover the same four read paths in half the lines.

## Evidence

**Live, this revision (`e1f639512fb`).** Same throwaway lab container and isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` as the run below, gateway on loopback only (127.0.0.1), token auth, no model provider. The two fixture rows that run inserted straight into `transcript_events` had no `transcript_event_identities` entries, which is why its anchored reads could not resolve. Step 2 gives them the identity rows a real write records, then this branch reads the session. Step 4 overwrites the 10 MiB row's stored body with unparseable JSON and keeps its recorded size, the same technique the existing `bounds unbounded anchor windows and caps payloads before decoding` test uses. A page that selected that body would fail to parse it.

```
$ node openclaw.mjs gateway run --port 18791 --bind loopback --allow-unconfigured
$ node openclaw.mjs gateway call chat.history --params '<params below>' --json --port 18791 --token <redacted>

[14:47:39Z] === 1. state: copy of the earlier proof's state dir; rows of the session ===
  seq 0  bytes 182  role null  identity 5b5e8af4-6969-4bc6-8894-df566b4cb9a1
  seq 1  bytes 755  role user  identity bd195f05-853b-47a7-92a2-2a6039959aa8
  seq 2  bytes 460  role null  identity 1176cd2d-d603-441e-9b52-515f40a21b8e
  seq 3  bytes 844  role user  identity d65679b5-39d6-4fe0-ae57-4c7fb65680af
  seq 4  bytes 460  role null  identity 2dfc4426-cc44-43dd-8093-603a65b1dc26
  seq 5  bytes 10486393  role user  identity (none)
  seq 6  bytes 175  role assistant  identity (none)
[14:47:39Z] === 2. give the two inserted rows the identity rows a real write records (the gap that blocked anchored reads before) ===
  indexed seq 5 as huge-view-image
  indexed seq 6 as after-huge
[14:47:39Z] === 3. this branch: recent page and anchored pages ===
[14:47:52Z] gateway [a] up on 127.0.0.1:18791  version=OpenClaw 2026.11.6 (e1f6395)  http=200
[14:47:53Z] chat.history recent  params={"sessionKey":"agent:main:lab-oversized","limit":10}
  3 messages, 1231 bytes on the wire
  - bd195f05-853b-47a7-92a2-2a6039959aa8 [user]: take a screenshot of each tab (1)
  - huge-view-image [user] TRUNCATED reason=oversized: [{"type":"text","text":"[chat.history omitted: message too large]"}]
  - after-huge [assistant]: all five tabs look the same
[14:47:53Z] chat.history anchored-on-huge  params={"sessionKey":"agent:main:lab-oversized","limit":10,"messageId":"huge-view-image","sessionId":"<transcript id>"}
  3 messages, 1231 bytes on the wire
  - bd195f05-853b-47a7-92a2-2a6039959aa8 [user]: take a screenshot of each tab (1)
  - huge-view-image [user] TRUNCATED reason=oversized: [{"type":"text","text":"[chat.history omitted: message too large]"}]
  - after-huge [assistant]: all five tabs look the same
[14:47:54Z] chat.history anchored-on-neighbour  params={"sessionKey":"agent:main:lab-oversized","limit":10,"messageId":"after-huge","sessionId":"<transcript id>"}
  3 messages, 1231 bytes on the wire
  - bd195f05-853b-47a7-92a2-2a6039959aa8 [user]: take a screenshot of each tab (1)
  - huge-view-image [user] TRUNCATED reason=oversized: [{"type":"text","text":"[chat.history omitted: message too large]"}]
  - after-huge [assistant]: all five tabs look the same
[14:47:55Z] === 4. poison the 10 MiB body in the store, keep its recorded size: a page that selected it would fail to parse ===
  poisoned rows: 1 (recorded size kept, body is now unparseable JSON)
[14:48:06Z] gateway [b] up on 127.0.0.1:18791  version=OpenClaw 2026.11.6 (e1f6395)  http=200
[14:48:06Z] chat.history poisoned-recent  params={"sessionKey":"agent:main:lab-oversized","limit":10}
  3 messages, 1231 bytes on the wire
  - bd195f05-853b-47a7-92a2-2a6039959aa8 [user]: take a screenshot of each tab (1)
  - huge-view-image [user] TRUNCATED reason=oversized: [{"type":"text","text":"[chat.history omitted: message too large]"}]
  - after-huge [assistant]: all five tabs look the same
[14:48:07Z] chat.history poisoned-anchored-on-huge  params={"sessionKey":"agent:main:lab-oversized","limit":10,"messageId":"huge-view-image","sessionId":"<transcript id>"}
  3 messages, 1231 bytes on the wire
  - bd195f05-853b-47a7-92a2-2a6039959aa8 [user]: take a screenshot of each tab (1)
  - huge-view-image [user] TRUNCATED reason=oversized: [{"type":"text","text":"[chat.history omitted: message too large]"}]
  - after-huge [assistant]: all five tabs look the same
[14:48:08Z] done
```

The recent page and both anchored pages (on the oversized row and on its neighbour) resolve, and the stand-in keeps the row's id. With its body unparseable in the store, the recent and anchored pages still load, so neither reads that body.

**Red on base for the new regression case** (`serves an oversized row from its identity without selecting its payload`, same file, run in the lab):

| code under test | historical=false | historical=true |
|---|---|---|
| this revision `e1f639512fb` | pass | pass |
| previous head `f00515b7a` | `SyntaxError: Expected property name or '}' in JSON` (the poisoned body was selected and parsed) | same |
| `origin/main` `3ad2cce` | `Transcript history page exceeds the 8388608-byte limit` | `Chat history message exceeds the 8388608-byte page limit` |

**Earlier live before/after (second revision).**

**Live before/after on a real Gateway.** Throwaway lab container, isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, gateway on loopback only (127.0.0.1), token auth, no model provider. Base: released `openclaw@2026.11.6` (`06afb10`) from npm. Head: this branch at `f00515b7a76`, rebased onto `origin/main` `3ad2cce4cd85826d52b2f8f4d56456170ff31a84` and built with `pnpm build`.

The session is built by the gateway itself: two real `chat.send` calls create it and its first four rows. One oversized display row is then added to that session's `transcript_events` — a `view_image`-shaped tool result with five inline base64 PNGs, 10,486,394 recorded bytes against the 8,388,608-byte limit — followed by one ordinary assistant row, so the oversized row has a neighbour on each side. Both builds then read the same state dir, BEFORE first.

```
$ .proof/stable/bin/openclaw gateway run --port 18791 --bind loopback --allow-unconfigured
$ .proof/stable/bin/openclaw gateway call chat.history \
    --params '{"sessionKey":"agent:main:lab-oversized","limit":10}' --json --port 18791 --token <redacted>

[09:02:43Z] === 3. BEFORE: released openclaw 2026.11.6 reads that session ===
[09:02:55Z] gateway [before] up on 127.0.0.1:18791  version=OpenClaw 2026.11.6 (06afb10)  http=200
[09:02:56Z] chat.history before  params={sessionKey:agent:main:lab-oversized,limit:10}
  REFUSED -> "Error: Transcript history message exceeds the 8388608-byte page limit",
```

```
$ node openclaw.mjs gateway run --port 18791 --bind loopback --allow-unconfigured
$ node openclaw.mjs gateway call chat.history \
    --params '{"sessionKey":"agent:main:lab-oversized","limit":10}' --json --port 18791 --token <redacted>

[09:02:58Z] === 4. AFTER: this branch, same state dir, same session ===
[09:03:39Z] gateway [after] up on 127.0.0.1:18791  version=OpenClaw 2026.11.6 (79a4ca3)  http=200
[09:03:40Z] chat.history after  params={sessionKey:agent:main:lab-oversized,limit:10}
  3 messages, 1265 bytes on the wire
  - bd195f05-853b-47a7-92a2-2a6039959aa8 [user]: take a screenshot of each tab (1)
  - huge-view-image [user] TRUNCATED reason=oversized: [{"type":"text","text":"[chat.history omitted: message too large]"}]
  - after-huge [assistant]: all five tabs look the same
```

The page that was refused now returns 1,265 bytes: the oversized row as the documented stand-in, its neighbours intact, and the 10 MiB payload never selected.

That run could not show anchored reads (its fixture rows had no identity rows); the run at the top does.

**Tests.** `vitest run src/gateway/session-transcript-readers.test.ts src/gateway/session-transcript-record-parser.test.ts src/config/sessions/session-actor-memory-history.test.ts src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-history-events.test.ts src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-history-cache.test.ts src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-history-query-plan.test.ts` → **68 passed, 2 failed**. The two failures are `reads production-like / repeated-byte bomb archives during discovery and exact reads`; re-run in this revision, they fail the same way with unmodified `origin/main` sources in my container and are unrelated to this change. New or changed cases:

- `serves an oversized row from its identity without selecting its payload` (live and closed-reset interval): poisons the stored body and keeps its recorded size, then reads offset, recent and anchored pages and the `chat.history` kernel. Red on base as shown above.
- `keeps history readable across an inline-image row larger than one page` — the reported shape, across the offset page, the recent read, an anchor on the row, an anchor on its neighbour, and the `chat.history` kernel the Control UI calls.
- `stands in for an oversized non-message display row` — an oversized `custom_message` display row.
- `bounds source pages by bytes and stands in for a message larger than one page` — converted from asserting the throw; still asserts that model-context source pages refuse the row and that the exact read stays whole.

`node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json` exits 0, `pnpm lint:kysely` reports "Kysely guardrails OK", `oxfmt --check` is clean on the touched files.

## Owner decision: why this replaces the refusal kept in #170898 and #188483

Those PRs refused oversized rows so the history worker would not decode and copy huge payloads. This PR keeps that guarantee and changes only what the reader shows:
- The oversized body is never selected. The query returns NULL for any row whose recorded bytes exceed the page bound, and the stand-in is built from the indexed id, parent and role. The new test poisons the stored body and still passes; on the previous head it failed parsing that body.
- The raw admission ceiling is unchanged. Model-context source pages and exact reads still refuse an oversized row.
- Display-history pages swap that row for the bounded stand-in that https://docs.openclaw.ai/web/webchat already documents, so one large message no longer makes the whole session unreadable.
- Actor-memory parity is a separate follow-up (see *Not in this PR*).

## Not in this PR
- **The in-memory actor-history reader.** `session-actor-memory-history-navigation.ts` / `-projection.ts` still refuse an oversized row, so a session whose transcript is held in actor memory (rather than read from the store) is not fixed here. That is a self-contained follow-up — "stand in for oversized rows in the actor-memory history reader" — on top of this one; it was 79 lines of the first revision and I dropped it to keep this change reviewable.
- `session-actor-memory-history-facts.ts` throw site.
- A by-id `historyContext` neighbour can still be decoded whole.
- The stand-in is message-shaped, so an oversized compaction or `custom_message` row renders as a generic placeholder rather than keeping its kind.

prs.title: l10n(sv): translate shared UI labels
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Swedish Control UI translation memory still contained 115 user-facing English or unnecessarily anglicized strings. This updates shared labels for support, skills, automatic mode, online presence and the popular plugin category, improves wording for patches and heartbeat monitoring, distinguishes reading in UI resources from downloading files, normalizes Git terminology to the established Swedish words *incheckning* and *pull-begäran*, and standardizes visible plugin terminology as *tillägg*. The latest batches replace visible uses of “Skills” with *färdigheter* in the library, agent overview, search, navigation, filter, catalog, learning and configuration views; use *tillägg* in visible labels, help and messages without changing technical paths or commands; replace remaining visible Git uses of “commit” with *incheckning*; and use Swedish macOS names for System Settings, Screen Sharing and Remote Management. Technical paths such as `skills.*` remain unchanged. The shared labels are used by multiple views, so the change also keeps terminology consistent with the native-app catalogue.

## Evidence

- Updated JSONL records parse successfully.
- Hunspell-sv recognizes the ordinary new Swedish words; the latest batch reports only the product name `OpenClaw`. svlang finds no anglicisms; its combined-input V2 warnings are false positives caused by concatenated UI fragments.
- A focused Gitleaks scan of the introduced values found no secrets. The full generated catalog contains opaque record hashes that make a raw standalone Gitleaks scan unsuitable.
- `l10n-lint` does not currently support this translation-memory JSONL schema, so it was not presented as a passing check.
- Existing catalog wording supports `Färdigheter`, `Stöd`, `automatiskt`, `Anslutna`, `Frånkopplad`, `incheckning` and `pull-begäran`.

The requested rebuilt-app screenshots are not attached yet. This PR remains open for that runtime verification.

The latest follow-up translates five visible Control UI status and support labels: Get support, offline duration, device-offline status, and the active/idle presence states. It uses the established terms Stöd, Ansluten and Frånkopplad. JSONL parsing, Hunspell-sv, svlang and a focused Gitleaks scan of the delta pass. l10n-lint does not support this translation-memory JSONL format.

Four more visible offline messages now use Frånkopplad or the natural phrase utan anslutning. Session interpolation and count placeholders are unchanged. JSONL parsing, Hunspell-sv, svlang and focused Gitleaks pass for this delta.

One additional visible configuration-help entry now uses Tilläggs-ID and ägartillägg. Configuration keys and commands remain literal. JSONL parsing, Hunspell-sv, svlang and focused Gitleaks pass.

Update: normalized the remaining short, user-facing plugin labels to Swedish “Tillägg” across the tab, tool source, plugin panel, and plugin-app catalog. This adds five shared records (eight visible placements) without changing configuration keys, command names, or identifiers. Focused JSONL parsing, Hunspell-sv, svlang, and Gitleaks checks pass. The archive is updated: https://github.com/yeager/translations/blob/main/openclaw/2026-11-15/ui.md . Runtime screenshots remain unavailable locally, so I have not requested another ClawSweeper review.

Follow-up: standardized eight more short, user-visible labels in navigation, search, category and settings contexts: “Hantera tillägg”, “Utforska tillägg”, “Sök efter tillägg”, “Tilläggskategorier”, and “Inställningarna för tillägg”. Configuration keys, commands, and identifiers remain unchanged. Focused JSONL parsing, Hunspell-sv, svlang, and Gitleaks checks pass. prs.title: feat: add opt-in Agent Profiles for small local models
prs.body:
Related: openclaw/rfcs#18 (Agent Profiles RFC)

## What Problem This Solves

A local model with a small context window gets the same system prompt as a hosted model. On a 32K window that prompt already fills about 40% of the window before the user says anything. The only switch today, lean mode (`experimental.localModelLean`), trims little, removes the scheduling tool, and cannot follow the model: one agent that uses a hosted model and a local model has no way to slim the prompt for the local model only.

## User Impact

User impact: an OpenClaw agent can pick a smaller prompt per model. `agentProfileId` sets a profile by hand. One switch, `agents.defaults.agentProfileId: "auto"`, lets models that report their total parameter count (Ollama, LM Studio, llama-server, catalog entries) get the right profile automatically. The switch is off by default.

- With no `agentProfileId` set, every agent uses `openclaw/base`. A model of any size gets the same prompt and tool list as on `main`.
- `openclaw/small` caps `AGENTS.md`, `SOUL.md`, `IDENTITY.md` and `USER.md` at 11,500 characters together, uses compact context serialization, and removes seven heavy tools (`browser`, `message`, `image_generate`, `music_generate`, `video_generate`, `tts`, `pdf`) behind bounded Tool Search. It keeps `automations` and `exec`. Memory and other injected files keep the operator limits. It is selected by `agentProfileId: "openclaw/small"`, or by `auto` for models up to 20B total parameters.
- Only two profiles ship: `openclaw/base` and `openclaw/small`. Medium and large models use `openclaw/base`.
- With no profile selected, the prompt and tool list are byte-identical to `main` for the same workspace files, for every model size.
- Lean mode is retired. Run `openclaw doctor --fix`: `experimental.localModelLean: true` becomes `agentProfileId: "openclaw/small"` at the same scope. See the migration table below.
- `openclaw agent exec --local-model-lean` is removed and fails with `--local-model-lean was removed. Use --agent-profile openclaw/small.` `--agent-profile auto` turns on size selection for one run.
- A new workspace is seeded with a shorter `IDENTITY.md` template (see Risks).

### Upgrade behavior

Nothing changes for an existing install until the operator sets `agentProfileId`, either `auto` or an explicit profile. A model that reports 20B or fewer total parameters stays on `openclaw/base` with the full tool list. An operator who set `experimental.localModelLean: true` keeps the small profile: `openclaw doctor --fix` writes `agentProfileId: "openclaw/small"` at the same scope, so the migration needs no switch. `openclaw/small` also applies the 11,500-character workspace budget and compact context serialization, which the old lean flag did not, so a migrated user sees those too. `agentProfileId: "openclaw/base"` at the same scope restores the full prompt. A script that passes `--local-model-lean` to `agent exec` must switch to `--agent-profile openclaw/small`; the flag never lived in saved config, so Doctor has nothing to rewrite.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is the first code slice of the Agent Profiles RFC. It starts from Onur Solmaz's implementation (7 commits, kept under his authorship, with Mitchell Etzel credited as co-author on each) and adds:

- Selection by total parameter count, as the RFC defines it, behind the `agentProfileId: "auto"` switch. Mixture-of-experts models count total parameters, never active ones. A model name or a GGUF `size_label` is never read. An unknown size falls back to `openclaw/base`.
- The retirement of Lean. The old flag's runtime is removed, and its behavior is `openclaw/small`. The `agent exec` flag is removed with an error that names the replacement.
- Profile budgets on every route that builds context: embedded, CLI, Codex, agentsapi, Copilot, worker turns, Side chat, memory flush and compaction.
- Fixes found while measuring on a real 8B model (the AGENTS.md budget, an IDENTITY.md overflow, two serialization bugs).

Size classes:

| Class | Total parameters | Profile |
|---|---|---|
| tiny | up to 1B | `openclaw/small` |
| small | over 1B, up to 20B | `openclaw/small` |
| medium | over 20B, up to 50B | `openclaw/base` |
| large | over 50B | `openclaw/base` |

Used only when `agentProfileId` is `auto`. Trusted size sources, in order: `models.providers.<id>.models[].modelSizeClass` set by the operator, then the route-matched total `parameterCount` that a provider or catalog reports (Ollama reports it from `/api/show`, LM Studio and the remote catalog report it too, and llama-server reports it as `meta.n_params` in `/v1/models`). Nothing else selects a size. A model with no trusted size uses `openclaw/base`. With `agentProfileId` unset, size is not consulted.

Config surface: `agentProfileId` is added (defaults and per agent; `auto`, or a profile id), `models.providers.<id>.models[].modelSizeClass` is added, and `experimental.localModelLean` is retired. `auto` is the only way to turn on size selection, so no other key is added for it. The selected profile owns context serialization (`default` or `compact`) and the tool profile (`compact`); there is no separate `contextSerialization` key and no numeric parameter-count key in user config.

Compact serialization keeps the behavior of #151099 for Telegram: the standalone current-message carrier supplies the current body, and only the inline composition keeps the bare header.

## Evidence

Behavior checked on a real local model, Qwen3-8B Q8_0 served by llama.cpp, with the shared 10-task suite (3 runs each, 32,768-token window). Prompt tokens are the server's own `prompt_tokens` for the first model call. Every one of the 30 runs per row returned model id `qwen3-8b-q8_0`. Builds: `main` is `d72d2bac495`, the before row is Onur's series `89c33c3cc70`, the branch rows with an explicit profile are `2fd304383f3`, and the last row is the branch with the opt-in switch. These task runs were measured at earlier commits of this branch and before the rebase; the profile behavior they exercise is unchanged by the later commits. The snapshots, the gates and the runtime output below were rerun at head `c3f9edd5f54` on `main` `afa93a83e4e`.

| Build | Tasks passed | T9 (reads a 7,203-char AGENTS.md) | T10 (schedules a reminder) | Median first-call prompt tokens |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `main` (d72d2bac495), no profile | 29/30 | 3/3 | 2/3 | 13,144 |
| Onur's 7 commits, `openclaw/small` (before) | 24/30 | 0/3 | 0/3 | 11,247 |
| this branch, no profile | 27/30 | 3/3 | 0/3 | 12,974 |
| this branch, `openclaw/small` | 30/30 | 3/3 | 3/3 | 11,997 (-8.7% vs main) |
| this branch, `agentProfileId: "auto"`, model entry reports `small` | 28/30 | 3/3 | 1/3 | 12,006 (-8.7% vs main) |

The last row sets `agents.defaults.agentProfileId: "auto"` and no explicit profile: the model entry reports `modelSizeClass: "small"`, and the size class selects `openclaw/small`. Every model call in it returned `qwen3-8b-q8_0` (104 of 104). Both misses are T10: in one run the model said the system requires authentication to create reminders, in the other it ended after 15 calls without a scheduled action. Six more T10 runs on the same build passed 5 of 6, and an earlier run of the same configuration on an earlier commit of this branch passed 30/30, so this is the same variance shown below for `main`. The "before" row failed T9 because the 4,000-character AGENTS.md cap cut the sentinel line, and T10 because the profile removed the scheduler. Both are fixed here. The no-profile T10 result is variance, shown next.

AGENTS.md budget, T9 on the same model, 3 runs each:

| AGENTS.md / total cap (chars) | T9 | Prompt tokens |
|---|---|---|
| 4,000 / 8,000 | 0/3 | 11,247 |
| 6,000 / 10,000 | 0/3 | 11,807 |
| 7,500 / 11,500 (chosen) | 3/3 | 12,028 |

T10 variance with no profile, alternating runs, one at a time:

| Run | this branch | `main` |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | pass, 494 s | fail, 131 s |
| 2 | pass, 320 s | pass, 512 s |
| 3 | pass, 162 s | pass, 822 s |
| Total | 3/3 | 2/3 |

An earlier set gave 0/3 for this branch without a profile and 2/3 for `main`. Across both sets this branch is 3/6 and `main` is 4/6, and one `main` run used 25 tool calls. The 8B model is noisy on this task. In one of the six runs a short two-turn probe looped for 26 model calls until the 900 s timeout (this branch, run 2); it did not recur.

No profile, same workspace files: the first request is byte-identical to `main` (system text, tool JSON, tool hash `cfa55d541417`). A model entry that reports `modelSizeClass: "small"` with `agentProfileId` unset gives the same request, byte for byte. The live request of a freshly seeded workspace is about 150 tokens shorter, only because of the new `IDENTITY.md` template (see Risks).

Snapshots of the first request (fake model server, stock seeded workspace; tokens by a fixed tokenizer, system plus tools). "Size small" is a model entry that reports `modelSizeClass: "small"`; "on" sets `agentProfileId: "auto"` and "off" leaves it unset. The no-profile, size small off, `auto` with size small and `small` scenarios were run at head `c3f9edd5f54`; the no-profile first request equals `main` `afa93a83e4e` built the same way, byte for byte (system text and tool JSON):

| Scenario | System chars | Tools | Tokens | Tool hash |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| no profile, `base`, any size class off, size medium on, size large on | 37,356 | 13 | 13,116 | `cfa55d541417` |
| `small`, size tiny on, size small on | 36,462 | 12 | 12,001 | `94a218caf648` |

A second set with a short `IDENTITY.md` seed shows the same split: 28,081 chars and 10,948 tokens without a profile, 27,383 chars and 9,893 tokens with `small`. The profile validator (`agentprofiles` schema, Ajv 2020) passes for both built-ins, `openclaw/base` and `openclaw/small`, with 0 failures (2 profiles run).

### Runtime output

Shipped entry points against a real Qwen3-8B on llama.cpp. Head `c3f9edd5f54`, base `main` `afa93a83e4e`. Hostnames, paths, ports and session ids are redacted.
Build SHA: `c3f9edd5f54b9b58215f1ee18ee34b5955f5de83` (branch head; base `main` `afa93a83e4e`). Built with `pnpm build` on the build host from this exact tree.
Model server: Qwen3-8B Q8_0 on llama.cpp (`qwen3-8b-q8_0`), one request at a time. Every server response below reports model id `qwen3-8b-q8_0`.

Setup, identical for the three turns except `agentProfileId`: a throwaway `OPENCLAW_HOME`, no Gateway, one `models.providers.llama-cpp` entry that has only a `baseUrl` and `api` (no model row, no `modelSizeClass`, no `parameterCount`), agent model `llama-cpp/qwen3-8b-q8_0`. A capture proxy sits between OpenClaw and the model server and records every request body and every server `usage` block.

- (a) `agentProfileId: "openclaw/small"`
- (b) `agentProfileId: "auto"`: the size comes only from llama-server discovery
- (c) no `agentProfileId` (control)

Discovery on the same server, run through `discoverLlamaServer` at the build SHA:

```text
{"kind":"success","models":[{"id":"qwen3-8b-q8_0","parameterCount":8190735360,"contextWindow":32768}]}
```

Two paths per turn, both on the same home, config and capture proxy:

- Path A, inbound with history: `getReplyFromConfig` (`get-reply-run-context`), the entry every channel plugin reaches, with a Telegram-style group message that carries four history entries. `openclaw agent --local` has no way to carry inbound history, so this path is used for the compact inbound block. The Gateway lifecycle owner is replaced by one `GatewayScheduler` bound to the session MCP runtime; nothing else is stubbed.
- Path B, shipped CLI: `openclaw agent --local --agent main --session-key <key> --message "Reply with one word: pong (<nonce>)" --json --timeout 300`, run from the built `openclaw.mjs`. It selects the profile the same way but sends no history.

### Runtime output: v0.9 task runs and upgrade path

Command (branch build `fefbef212d1`, base `main` at `d72d2bac495`; local llama.cpp server on a loopback address; paths redacted):


Upgrade path. The latest stable release (`openclaw 2026.11.6`, installed from npm into a scratch folder) validated each legacy config. Each case used its own state directory and an environment without the gateway variables, so no real install was touched. Command, once per case:

Case 1 keeps the user on the small profile they asked for. Case 2 matches main: onboarding-owned lean is removed and nothing is pinned. Case 3 keeps the agent's opt-out as `openclaw/base`. Case 4 repairs a config that was valid on stable and would be rejected without the migration. The models in these configs were not served, so these runs show the config result, not a model turn.

What an existing small-model user sees after upgrade: with `agentProfileId` unset, nothing changes. A model that reports 8.19B total parameters stays on `openclaw/base`, and the first request equals the no-profile request. With `agentProfileId: "auto"` it selects `openclaw/small`: 13 tools become 12 (`message` is removed behind Tool Search), the system prompt is 894 characters shorter, and the first request is 1,115 tokens smaller on the fake-server snapshot (13,116 to 12,001). `agentProfileId: "openclaw/base"` on an agent opts it out of an `auto` default.

### Tests and gates

Each fix below has a red run, a green run and a mutation (revert only the fix, the test fails again, restore). All commits are signed.

### Lean retired: doctor migration

| Legacy input | Result |
|---|---|
| `true` at any scope | `openclaw/small` at the same scope |
| `false` at defaults | key removed |
| `false` on an agent under a `true` default | `openclaw/base` on that agent |
| `false` on an agent otherwise | key removed |
| explicit `agentProfileId` already set | profile kept, flag dropped |
| before doctor runs | config validation reports the key and points to `openclaw doctor --fix` |

The migration writes an explicit profile, so it does not depend on `auto`. Each row has a test. `wizard.localModelLeanAutoModel` is still handled by main's own retired-key rule. Main's test keeps its first assertion unchanged. The last assertion now lists the exact paths that the Agent Profile migration still reports, instead of expecting no issues, because that migration owns the remaining flags.

### Credit

Onur Solmaz authors his 7 commits (`4f1d08e4b48` to `12f3d8d3726`). The commits after them are by Mitchell Etzel and are split by topic.

### Risks

- Fresh workspaces are seeded with a shorter `IDENTITY.md` (Onur's template edit, about 600 fewer characters). This changes the prompt of a new workspace for every profile, including none. An existing workspace keeps its file. Under `openclaw/small` an `IDENTITY.md` over 1,024 characters is truncated with a visible marker, so a workspace from the old template still runs.
- The `toolSearchDirectoryLean` field of the worker gateway protocol keeps its wire name, so gateways and workers on different versions keep working. A rename needs a dual read first.
- Size selection is opt-in. An operator who sets `agentProfileId: "auto"` changes the tool list, workspace budget and context serialization for every model that reports 20B or fewer total parameters (an Ollama or LM Studio model, for example). Main retired automatic lean in #138850 so local models keep full capabilities through Tool Search. To keep the full surface for one agent under `auto`, set `agentProfileId: "openclaw/base"` on that agent.
- With `auto`, a model whose provider reports no parameter count stays on `openclaw/base` until the operator sets `modelSizeClass`. A llama-server row that is listed explicitly under `models.providers.llama-cpp.models` does not trigger discovery in a local `agent --local` turn (the capture shows no `/v1/models` request and `auto` stays on `openclaw/base`), so set `modelSizeClass` on such a row. A model that is not listed is discovered at run time and carries its count.

### Suggested review order

87 commits. Read them in these groups; each group builds on the one before.

1. Foundation, Onur Solmaz's 7 commits: Agent Profiles, resolver, config schema, workspace budget, serialization, tool surface, diagnostics, Doctor migration. `4f1d08e4b48..12f3d8d3726`
2. Lint, typing and mock-export fixes for the foundation. `7728a214196..f1091ea35bb`
3. Size classification from total parameter count on the CLI, embedded and harness routes. `cd6e0128a8d..f3a2a0dfd6c`
4. Lean retirement and profiles on workspace, worker, Codex and utility routes. `627d8162c9b..214bd0761d3`
5. Refactors and test moves that keep files within budget. `e2bae932a85..1233d22201b`
6. Workspace budget, IDENTITY and AGENTS limits, no model-name binding, Doctor order. `aa767c78b7c..2d4139c4f0c`
7. Cleanup and hardening of size selection and compact context. `143a9e011f7..2388fa03058`
8. Opt-in selection and its docs. `0c0e37f07cc..b2b24db1902`
9. Compact inbound context: carrier, markers, instructions. `8aea38bd13a..e995f9fad03`
10. Review findings: catalog size class, Codex size metadata, history window, Telegram carrier, benchmark, published anchors. `1be41df109f..f7c030779b4`
11. Decisions as built: serialization ownership, two built-ins, flag removal, wire-name note, llama-server count, baseline, formatting. `18cb558f992..c3f9edd5f54`

Each decision was settled by the evidence shown. The last column says how to undo it.

| # | Choice | Evidence | How to reverse |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Size selection stays opt-in: `agentProfileId: "auto"` turns it on, unset means `openclaw/base`. | Main retired automatic lean in #138850. The control turn (c) with an 8.19B model stays on `openclaw/base`. | Treat an unset value as `auto` in the resolver. |
| 2 | Keep `agentProfileId` and `models[].modelSizeClass`. Drop the standalone `agents.defaults.contextSerialization` and per-agent `contextSerialization` keys: the profile owns serialization. Keep the deprecated SDK member `localModelLeanApplied` next to `agentProfile`. | The two keys exist on no release and not on `main`; they came only from Onur's branch, and removing them touched 13 files (schema, help, labels, scope config, resolver, 2 callers, 3 tests, 2 docs). `localModelLeanApplied` is on `main` and in releases since v2026.9.6, and the Plugin SDK rules require a shipped replacement, an announced window and maintainer approval before removing a shipped member. It already warns as deprecated. | Re-add the two schema keys and the two resolver branches. Drop the alias after the announced window. |
| 3 | The small budget covers only `AGENTS.md`, `SOUL.md`, `IDENTITY.md` and `USER.md`. Memory and other injected files keep the operator limits. | The code already did this. A new test keeps a 5,000-char `MEMORY.md` whole while `AGENTS.md` is cut to the profile total; bounding passthrough files fails it. | Apply the profile total to passthrough files in `workspace-context.ts`. |
| 4 | `toolProfile` stays `compact`. | No change. | Rename the value in the OpenClaw extension schema. |
| 5 | Ship only `openclaw/base` and `openclaw/small`. Medium and large size classes bind to `openclaw/base`; the classes stay tiny, small, medium, large. No Doctor rule. | Medium and large were byte-identical to base (tool hash `cfa55d541417`). The ids never shipped in a release and are not on `main`, so no saved config can name them. The validator accepts both built-ins (2 profiles). | Re-add the two definitions and the two bindings. |
| 6 | Remove `--local-model-lean` from `agent exec`. It fails with `--local-model-lean was removed. Use --agent-profile openclaw/small.` No Doctor note. | The flag has been in releases since v2026.8.1 as a CLI option only and never in saved config. The error text is captured from the built CLI. | Re-register the flag as an alias for `--agent-profile openclaw/small`. |
| 7 | Keep the wire name `toolSearchDirectoryLean`, with a code comment and a doc line. | Gateways and workers on different versions exchange this field. | Read both names, then rename. |
| 8 | Keep the compact deny list: `browser`, `message`, `image_generate`, `music_generate`, `video_generate`, `tts`, `pdf`. | 30 of 30 task runs passed on the 8B model with `openclaw/small`; T10 needs `automations`, which stays. | Edit `COMPACT_TOOL_DENY_NAMES`. |
| 9 | No numeric `parameterCount` in user config. `modelSizeClass` is the operator lever. | The field is typed internal only and absent from the config schema. | Add the field to the model schema. |
| 10 | The `qwen3.6-35b-a3b` name binding stays removed. | 34.7B total parameters is `medium`, which uses `openclaw/base`. No model-name binding exists in `src`. | Re-add a binding by name. |

Turn (b) selects `openclaw/small` with `selectionSource: model-size` and no size in config. Unit tests use a recorded response. | Revert the llama-cpp commit; `modelSizeClass` still works. |
| 12 | Opt-in may become the default later. | Covered by 1. | See 1. |

- Sign-off on the new `agentprofiles` 0.1.0 dependency (MIT, exact pin, published by the RFC author). Production code imports only its types, and the built-in profile tests run its validator.
