prs.title: feat(whatsapp): edit the bot's own messages
prs.body:
Related: #189815

## What Problem This Solves

WhatsApp is missing the `edit` message action that Telegram and Discord have, so an agent cannot correct a message it already sent.

## User Impact

User impact: agents can edit their own WhatsApp messages. Turn it off with `channels.whatsapp.actions.editMessage: false`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds `edit` the same way `react` works, behind the host's exact-current chat gate. Editing another user's message is refused when the cache knows the sender. On a cache miss the edit goes out under the bot's own key (`fromMe: true`); WhatsApp applies an edit only when it comes from the original sender, so such an edit has no effect on the other phone. That is provider behaviour, not something this PR enforces. Baileys resolves on the socket write, so the result says `submitted: true, confirmed: false`.

The edit key's chat is pinned to the chat the caller named. The message-cache lookup that quoting uses also matches a message through its sender. Only an entry whose stored peer number is the target's own number counts as this one-to-one chat under its other JID (phone number or LID) and may supply the key's `remoteJid`; anything else (a status update keyed by its poster, a broadcast list, a match through a bare participant JID) is another chat, and the edit is rejected with `message belongs to another chat`.

Caller authority: `edit` is declared in `writeAuthorityActions`, and the host's `assertDirectAdapterHandoff` is passed down the edit chain as a plain parameter. It is checked at the action handler and again inside the queued socket task, right after the socket-identity check and right before the native `sendMessage`. An edit whose originating run lost authority while it waited in the per-socket queue is dropped before any I/O. A revocation is never retried: the caller guard runs at the start of every send attempt, also while the socket is away, so a revoked caller never waits for a reconnect backoff, and the retry path re-checks the caller before classifying an error as a disconnect, so the caller gets the original guard error. Edits now use the ordinary send path, so the separate single-attempt path is gone.

Provider ownership (`fromMe`, the message cache) only scopes which messages are eligible; it does not stand in for caller authority. Both are required.

Scheduled edits stay out on purpose: `edit` is not in `providerOwnedReadGates`, so the host keeps its exact-current chat check and rejects a scheduled edit. A contract test locks that.

Known limitation: for an external install the host compares targets literally (it applies `normalizeTarget` only to bundled plugins), so a delegated edit must name a DM as `+E164`, the spelling the agent's prompt shows, or omit the target; a `...@s.whatsapp.net` spelling is rejected, fail-closed. Changing that is host policy and out of scope here.

## Evidence

### Live proof on 2026.11.1 (latest stable)

**Upgrade.** A real linked WhatsApp install was upgraded from 2026.10.10 to 2026.11.1 with the normal npm install, `plugins update` and `doctor --fix`. Before and after the upgrade, the full config (sorted JSON), the WhatsApp auth creds and the number of files in the WhatsApp auth dir hashed identically, and the cron list count was unchanged. The channel came back `linked, connected, health:healthy` and the agent answered on its primary model. The config has no `actions.editMessage` key.

**Edit.** Then this PR's commit was cherry-picked onto `v2026.11.1`, `extensions/whatsapp` was packed with `scripts/plugin-npm-publish.sh --pack`, and only the plugin's `dist` + manifest were swapped in (same dependency versions; all 94 `plugin-sdk/*` imports exist in the installed 11.1 core). Afterwards the stock 2026.11.1 plugin was put back. The cherry-pick differs from this branch only where 11.1's file layout differs from main (the action list lives in `channel-actions.ts` there, plus import lines); the edit, authority and socket code is the same as the pushed head, including the final same-chat guard and the no-socket caller check.

Phone number redacted; the message id is a random WhatsApp id.

```text
$ openclaw --version
OpenClaw 2026.11.1 (4ffdd20)

$ openclaw message send --channel whatsapp --target +<owner> --json \
    --message "Proof test for the WhatsApp edit action: meet at 3"
"action": "send", "handledBy": "core", "messageId": "3EB0C0887D06069C093CA8"
[exit 0]

$ openclaw message edit --channel whatsapp --target +<owner> --message-id 3EB0C0887D06069C093CA8 --json \
    --message "Proof test for the WhatsApp edit action: meet at 4"
"action": "edit", "handledBy": "plugin",
"payload": { "ok": true, "submitted": true, "confirmed": false, "messageId": "3EB0C0887D06069C093CA8" }
[exit 0]

$ openclaw message edit --channel whatsapp --target +15555550100 --message-id 3EB0C0887D06069C093CA8 --json \
    --message "must not arrive"
ToolAuthorizationError: WhatsApp edit blocked: chatJid "+15555550100" is not in the
configured allowFrom list for account "default".
[exit 1]

$ openclaw message edit --channel whatsapp --target +<owner> --message-id 3EB0C0887D06069C093CA8 --json \
    --message ""
Error: WhatsApp edit rejected: text is empty.
[exit 1]

# a message the other phone sent earlier; after the restart the cache does not know it
$ openclaw message edit --channel whatsapp --target +<owner> --message-id 3A7E5B8528B197B3CF6A --json \
    --message "must not arrive (not this account's message)"
"payload": { "ok": true, "submitted": true, "confirmed": false, "messageId": "3A7E5B8528B197B3CF6A" }
[exit 0]
```

**Receiving side.** On the receiving account's WhatsApp Web (read-only IndexedDB lookup by message id), the received message `3EB0C0887D06069C093CA8` carries `latestEditMsgKey`, with the edit's sender timestamp 4.4 s after the original. So the edit reached the other phone; it is not only a socket write. The last command above targets a message the other phone itself sent: the socket accepted the write (`submitted: true`), but on the receiving side that message has no `latestEditMsgKey`. WhatsApp dropped the edit because it did not come from the message's sender, which is the provider behaviour the Why section relies on for a cache miss.


### Delegated edit from a real inbound turn (2026.11.1)

Same install and plugin port, plugin installed under `~/.openclaw/extensions` (origin `global`, so the host treats it as an external plugin, the same trust class as the integration test below). The owner's phone sent the bot a WhatsApp DM asking it to call the `message` tool twice. The group is configured and allowed (`groups` + `groupAllowFrom`, the bot is a member), so the plugin itself would accept it. Gateway log plus the session trajectory from `openclaw sessions export-trajectory`; numbers redacted, times UTC:

```text
14:19:11  CLI (direct operator)  message send -> +<owner>  messageId 3EB0982B3059BFDD8B7B19  "...: meet at 3"
14:19:43  web-inbound            Inbound message +<owner> -> <bot> (direct, 494 chars)
14:19:49.724  tool.call  message  {"action":"edit","channel":"whatsapp","target":"+<owner>",
                                   "messageId":"3EB0982B3059BFDD8B7B19","message":"...: meet at 4"}
14:19:49.724  tool.call  message  {"action":"edit","channel":"whatsapp","target":"<allowed-group>@g.us",
                                   "messageId":"3EB0982B3059BFDD8B7B19","message":"must not arrive"}
14:19:49.762  tool.result (group)  error: Delegated whatsapp:edit requires the exact current conversation and account for this plugin.
14:19:49.789  tool.result (DM)     {"ok":true,"submitted":true,"confirmed":false,"messageId":"3EB0982B3059BFDD8B7B19"}
14:19:52      web-outbound         the bot's text reply with both raw tool results
```

Receiving side (read-only WhatsApp Web IndexedDB lookup by message id): before the turn the received message had no `latestEditMsgKey`; after it, `latestEditMsgKey` is set with edit sender timestamp 14:19:49.783, the moment of the DM tool result. The group call was stopped in `message-action-dispatch` before the plugin ran (gateway log: `[tools] message failed: Error: Delegated whatsapp:edit requires the exact current conversation and account for this plugin.`); the only outbound socket traffic in that window is the edit and the bot's text reply.

The earlier `openclaw agent --to ...` attempts were rejected for a different reason: a CLI-started run has no host-minted turn capability, so the gateway receives no tool context or requester account and fails closed before comparing targets. That is the host's design, not this PR.

Not covered live: a second linked account and revocation while queued (one linked account; revocation cannot be timed from outside). Both are covered by the host-issued-guard integration test below.

### Tests on this branch, rebased on current main

- Host-issued caller guard, end to end (`test/whatsapp-message-edit.integration.test.ts`, on the shared `createMessageReadAuthority` harness, reaching the plugin only through `api.js` and a new `extensions/whatsapp/test-api.ts`, the same public test surface the Discord and Slack suites use): a really minted turn capability and run claim, the message tool under the gateway caller identity, the in-process `message.action` handler (which builds `assertDirectAdapterHandoff` itself), the plugin registered as an external install, the real WhatsApp handler and the real socket session; only Baileys' `sendMessage` is a mock. The test never supplies a guard. The config allows both the other chat and the other account, so only the host can refuse them. Cases:
  1. the current chat's edit reaches the socket with the edit key and returns `submitted: true, confirmed: false`;
  2. the same run naming another allowed chat is rejected before the socket;
  3. the same run's identity sent straight to the gateway's `message.action` with another allowed account is rejected by the host before the socket;
  4. `revokeMessageActionTurnCapability` (what the reply run calls when it ends), called after the edit's preflight while it waits behind a busy send, drops it with `agent runtime authority is no longer active`; the socket only ever sees the busy send.

  Red checks: with the in-queue re-check removed, case 4 fails (the edit reaches the socket); with the host's account comparison disabled, case 3 fails. The old vertical test with a hand-written guard in `channel-actions.test.ts` is removed; this test replaces it.
- Socket session (unit level, with a test guard): the queued caller check runs after the socket-identity check and before native I/O; a revoked caller is not retried and gets the guard's own error, also when the error text looks like a disconnect; a revoked caller with no current socket is rejected at once, without a backoff wait; a guard rejection leaves no send-ready proof behind for the next send.
- Message cache: ids containing `:` are never cached or found, so the colon-joined cache key cannot collide.
- Contract: a scheduled `whatsapp:edit` is rejected with "requires provider-owned target authorization".
- Through the plugin handler: a target outside `allowFrom`, another account's `allowFrom`, a message cached as foreign, a message cached in another chat (a status update, or another person's chat matched only through a participant JID), and `actions.editMessage: false` all stop before the socket; a message cached under the other spelling of the same chat, with the target's number as its stored peer, keeps its cached `remoteJid` in the edit key.
- Through the host dispatcher: a direct operator's edit reaches the listener, a delegated caller naming another chat stops at the gate, and a chat removed from `allowFrom` stops the next edit.
- Upgrade compatibility: a config without `actions.editMessage` parses and enables edit; the message cache is in memory and its shape is unchanged.

Rebased on `main` at 694224f4432 (18 Nov); the only conflicts were the generated `docs/.generated/config-baseline.counts.json` and `config-baseline.sha256`, regenerated with `pnpm config:docs:gen` (one new channel field, `actions.editMessage`). No code changes. On that head, `pnpm check:changed --base origin/main` passes every lane (typecheck, lint, format, config/metadata checks and the dead-export scan). The WhatsApp extension (101 files), the edit-gate contract, the WhatsApp schema tests and the three integration suites on the shared read-authority harness (WhatsApp edit 4/4, Matrix, Slack) pass.

Before that rebase: WhatsApp extension: 101 files, 1107 tests passing; the new integration file 4/4; the extension test-boundary suite 13/13. Contract, dispatcher (`message-action-dispatch.registry`) and schema tests pass; `tsgo` (core, extensions, extension tests, root tests), oxlint, format, `config:docs:check` and `check:baseline-ratchets --base origin/main` are clean.

### Test-line allocation

Duplicated cases were removed (the vertical queued-revocation test with a hand-written guard in `channel-actions.test.ts` and its helpers, now replaced by the host-issued-guard test; the duplicate queued-revocation case in `monitor-inbox.socket-lifecycle.test.ts`; the per-dispatch allowFrom case in `channel-actions.test.ts`; the successful-edit case in `channel-actions.test.ts`, which the host-issued-guard test proves end to end; the cached-foreign case in `send.test.ts`); each contract is still proven at an equal or stronger boundary. The attached-listener setup that `channel-actions.test.ts` and the new test both need lives once in `extensions/whatsapp/src/inbound/attached-listener.test-support.ts`, and the shared harness only gained an optional gateway-context resolver. The remaining net growth of 1152 lines is recorded in `config/test-lines-allocations/whatsapp-edit-own-messages.txt`, shared scalar unchanged. It is needed because this adds a new write action whose authority has to hold across the host gate, the plugin's account/`allowFrom` checks and the queued socket write, and each of those boundaries has its own test.

Related: #203284

## What Problem This Solves

The macOS dashboard's Details panel can show a horizontal scrollbar. Details is a narrow reading panel, and sideways gestures should not move its rows.

## User Impact

Details scrolls vertically when content is tall without panning sideways. Long branch and pull request names keep their existing truncation, and row actions stay in place.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared desktop Details scroll container allowed both axes. Restricting it to vertical scrolling fixes the behavior for the macOS dashboard and the same floating or docked web panel, without changing the mobile Details layout.

## Evidence

- The focused Chromium regression sent a real diagonal wheel gesture with oversized content. On the base (`d813b208b1f49`), Details moved 64 px sideways. With the fix (`bd7525a3403c6`), vertical scrolling still worked and horizontal movement stayed at zero. All three tests in the Details body suite passed.
- In Linux WebKit with simulated macOS dashboard chrome and synthetic Gateway data, the Worktree, pull request and Outputs rows kept the same layout. Expanded Outputs still scrolled vertically in a short window. The reported native scrollbar did not reproduce in this WebKit harness, and the native macOS app was not run.
- UI typecheck, focused stylesheet lint, formatting, and diff checks passed. Broad CI was not run for this draft.

![After: a short Details panel scrolls vertically, without a horizontal scrollbar](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7ae17f00-8af2-4e3a-a6f2-4201594e1e49)

This fixture verifies that tall Details content still scrolls vertically. It does not reproduce the native macOS scrollbar; the matched Linux WebKit before and after layout captures were identical.

prs.title: feat(acpx): let operators narrow plugin tools loaded for ACP sessions
prs.body:
Related: #203436

## What Problem This Solves

The ACPX plugin-tools bridge can load plugins an ACP session never uses, adding startup time and memory cost. Disabling those plugins globally also removes them from sessions that need them.

## User Impact

Operators can set `pluginToolsMcpBridgeAllow` and `pluginToolsMcpBridgeDeny` just for the ACPX bridge. These optional filters only narrow existing tool access; unconfigured sessions keep their current behavior. Older external hosts reject configured filters rather than silently ignoring them.

## Why This Change Was Made

Apply bridge filters to the tools already permitted by OpenClaw and skip importing plugins with no eligible tools where their manifest provides enough information. This reduces startup work without changing the per-session process model.

## Evidence

109 focused tests passed, including real-registry checks that filtering does not grant optional tools and skips importing excluded plugins. Core type checking, config-doc checks, targeted lint, formatting, and the local `pnpm build:ci-artifacts` build also passed.

In an isolated cold-start probe (one run per scenario, seven bundled plugins), the unfiltered bridge took 71.7 s and 2,240 MiB RSS. Denying three plugins took 51.7 s and 1,581 MiB; allowing only Browser and GitHub took 3.4 s and 940 MiB. These are measurements of that test setup, not general startup guarantees.

prs.title: fix: show background results to the model as labelled input, not its own replies
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When an automation or subagent posts results into a chat, OpenClaw records each result as an assistant message so the next reply has context. The model then saw those results as its own turns that nothing had asked for. After an hourly automation's results piled up in one chat, the next reply continued the pattern on its own: it emitted about two dozen invented "future" hourly reports, with PR numbers, commits and nudges that did not exist, all as one long message.

## User Impact

Background results now reach the model as clearly labelled input, not as messages the model wrote. The chat still shows them exactly as before, and nothing stored changes. Sessions that already hold background results get one prompt-cache miss on the first request after upgrade, because those rows now render differently in the request.

## Why This Change Was Made

The model-facing projection that already labels content from other sessions (`sessions_send` arrives as labelled user input) now also covers background results. Each stored result row maps 1:1 to a user message that starts with a constant label:

> [OpenClaw background result] You sent the message below to the user in this chat from a separate background run. It is a record of what they saw, not a new request.

followed by the original text. The label has no time, job id or run id, so the request prefix stays stable per row. The same function runs before history assembly, at provider dispatch and in exact-replay facts, and it runs before turn merging, so a result can never merge into an assistant turn on any route (append-only Anthropic or strict merging routes). The model still knows it sent the message and that the user saw it.

`annotateInterSessionUserMessages` is renamed to `annotateCrossSessionMessages`; all three callers move to it. The row predicate `isOpenClawAutomationResultMessage` sits next to `AUTOMATION_RESULT_MODEL`. The duplicate-mirror exclusion for automation results stays: the dispatch boundary normalizes assistant rows before it projects them, so a result placed mid-run still arrives there as an assistant row and must not be dropped as a mirror.

Out of scope, left as follow-ups: the Codex harness history seed, compaction summarization input, the existing mid-run placement case where a placed result is the last request message, and `NO_REPLY` followed by trailing text (not the cause here).

## Evidence

**Real Gateway, real model (isolated scratch Gateway, `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6`, Anthropic request payload log).** A dashboard chat got one user turn and one reply. An isolated 30-second automation then delivered status reports into that chat (natural schedule, no forced runs). After disabling it, one more user message was sent and the outgoing Anthropic request was captured.

Before (merge base): the results are consecutive assistant turns after the real reply.

```json
{"role": "assistant", "content": ["Got it — I'll keep an eye out for the status reports and won't clutter the chat."]},
{"role": "assistant", "content": ["PR flow 01:00:00: all green, no open PRs."]},
{"role": "assistant", "content": ["PR flow 01:01:00: all green, no open PRs."]},
{"role": "assistant", "content": ["PR flow 01:01:00: all green, no open PRs."]},
{"role": "user", "content": ["<redacted by payload log: the new user message>"]}
```

After (this branch): only the model's own reply is an assistant turn; each result is labelled user input (`↵↵` marks the blank line between label and text).

```json
{"role": "assistant", "content": ["Got it — I'll keep an eye out for the status reports."]},
{"role": "user", "content": "[<message timestamp>] [OpenClaw background result] You sent the message below to the user in this chat from a separate background run. It is a record of what they saw, not a new request. ↵↵ PR flow 01:15:00: all green, no open PRs."},
{"role": "user", "content": "[<message timestamp>] [OpenClaw background result] You sent the message below to the user in this chat from a separate background run. It is a record of what they saw, not a new request. ↵↵ PR flow 01:16:00: all green, no open PRs."},
... (5 more results, same shape)
{"role": "user", "content": ["<redacted by payload log: the new user message>"]}
```

The reply to "What is the latest status?" was "As of 01:18, all green with no open PRs." `chat.history` still returns the results as assistant rows, so the chat view is unchanged.

**Tests (red on the merge base, green here):**
- `sanitizeSessionHistory` + `validateReplayTurns` with [user, real reply, 3 results, user] on append-only Anthropic and on a merging route: no assistant turn for any result, each result labelled with its original text.
- Dispatch boundary: a placed result that repeats the previous reply word for word dispatches as labelled user input and is not dropped as a duplicate mirror.
- Updated `background-session-result.test.ts` to dispatch through the production boundary; the live-placement prefix check (mid-run request vs. next turn after reopen) stays byte-identical.

Merge danger: two-way door. Only the model-facing projection changes; stored rows, UI and protocol are unchanged, and a revert restores the old projection (one more cache miss). Blast radius: every embedded-runner request from a chat that holds automation or subagent results.

<details><summary>Local checks</summary>

- Touched tests plus every test importing a changed file (65 files, 13 Vitest shards): pass.
- `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:core:test`, oxlint, oxfmt on changed files: pass.
- The E2E head build predates two edits that do not change runtime behavior: one code comment and one return-type annotation in `replay-provenance.ts`.
- `pnpm check:changed`: the SQLite worker ratchet ran out of heap at its 4 GB limit in the whole-repo semantic scan on this host, two runs out of two. This change touches no database code. Hosted CI runs that lane.
</details>

prs.title: fix: queued messages show no typing indicator while they wait behind a live run
prs.body:
Closes #162547

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a direct message that queues behind a live run shows no typing indicator for the whole wait, even though `docs/concepts/queue.md` says typing still fires on enqueue.

## User Impact

User impact: on Telegram and other channels whose turns carry an adoption lifecycle, a message queued behind a busy session keeps showing "typing…" until its own run starts and replies. Typing stops when the queued item finishes, is cancelled, or is dropped from the queue. Messages that do not queue are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The enqueue path already signals typing when a follow-up queues behind a live run, and the follow-up runner keeps the same typing controller. But the buffered dispatcher that handled the inbound message then returns. Its dispatcher idle callback and its `finally` (`markRunComplete` and `markDispatchIdle` in `src/auto-reply/dispatch.ts`) seal that controller and call the channel's `onIdle`, which closes the channel typing loop for good. So typing starts and stops within the same ~360 ms dispatch the issue's log shows (`message dispatch completed ... duration=363ms`).

Related: #92287 starts typing when a queued turn begins to execute (#92267). This change covers the wait before that, and keeps the controller that run would use from being sealed when the inbound dispatch returns.

This follows the direction in the ClawSweeper review: the queued item owns typing from enqueue to settlement.

- `createReplyDispatcherWithTyping` returns a new internal `onTypingHandoff` reply option. It lives in `InternalReplySessionOptions` next to `onReplyOperationOwned`, not in the public `GetReplyOptions`, and `publicReplyOptions` strips it from plugin-supplied options. Core builds these reply options itself in `dispatchReplyWithBufferedBlockDispatcher`, so Telegram still gets the handoff. After it is called, the dispatcher no longer completes the typing controller. When typing comes only from `typingCallbacks`, their `onIdle` (typing teardown) is deferred, and the queued item's typing cleanup runs `onCleanup` and then that `onIdle` once. The handoff state lives in `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-dispatcher-typing-handoff.ts`.
- A channel that passes its own `onIdle` gets no `onTypingHandoff`, so its whole typing lifecycle is unchanged. That `onIdle` can do more than stop typing: Feishu's (`extensions/feishu/src/reply-dispatcher.ts:1232`, `queueIdleSideEffects`) finalizes streaming delivery and closes the card preview. Deferring it made finalization wait on itself (ClawSweeper revision 3). Running it while the handed-off controller kept ticking let the next tick's `onReplyStart` reopen the closed preview (revision 5). So Feishu does not get typing through the queued wait. Channels that pass only `typingCallbacks`, such as Telegram, do.
- `runReplyAgent`, on the enqueue-behind-a-live-run path, closes typing from the queued item's `turnAdoptionLifecycle.onSettled`. Queue completion calls that for a run that finished, a cancelled item, a cleared queue, and the sources of a collected batch.
- The handoff happens only when the follow-up has an adoption lifecycle and queued typing actually started (`typing.isActive()` after `signalToolStart`). Without a lifecycle nothing would settle the typing. In `message` typing mode typing does not start before text, so the controller's `cleanup` never calls `onCleanup` and a deferred `onIdle` would never run. Both cases keep today's behavior. That keeps a dropped item from leaving a typing loop running forever.
- The dispatcher exposes `onTypingHandoff` only when the channel supplied a cleanup callback, because the deferred `onIdle` runs from that callback.
- Each queued `FollowupRun` now carries the typing controller of the dispatch that queued it (`typing`), and the follow-up runner completes that one (`queued.typing ?? defaults.typing`). The queue keeps only the latest runner per key, so before this an earlier queued message, when it finished, completed the later message's controller and sealed it before that message's own turn (ClawSweeper revision 6).

`waitForReplyDispatcherIdle` moved to `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-dispatcher-idle.ts` with main's current body (including its `abortSignal` handling), the queued item's `onSettled` wrap lives in `bindQueuedFollowupTyping` in `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-run-typing.ts`, and the two queued-typing cases moved to `agent-runner.runreplyagent.queued-typing.cases.ts`, so the line-cap ratchet holds for `reply-dispatcher.ts`, `agent-runner-run.ts`, and the runner e2e file.

## Evidence

- New `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-utils.test.ts` case drives a real `createReplyDispatcherWithTyping`, `createTypingController`, and `createTypingCallbacks` (channel TTL off, as on Telegram) through handoff, dispatcher idle, `markRunComplete`, and `markDispatchIdle`. On the test commit the channel `start` runs 0 times in the next 60 s. On the fix it runs 30 times, `stop` is not called during the wait, and `stop` runs once after the queued run settles.
- New `agent-runner.runreplyagent.queued-typing.cases.ts` case: a follow-up with a lifecycle queued behind a live run calls `onTypingHandoff` once and keeps typing open, and `completeFollowupRunLifecycle` on the queued item cleans typing up once. On the test commit `onTypingHandoff` is called 0 times.
- Channel with its own idle (ClawSweeper revisions 3 and 5, fixed in 0f720c428ae). The `reply-utils.test.ts` case with distinct `onReplyStart`, `onIdle`, and `onCleanup` callbacks uses fake timers: it calls the handoff option if offered, completes the run and the dispatcher, then advances 5 s. On 4f0fc716970 it fails: the controller never cleans up (`["idle"]` instead of `["cleanup", "idle"]`) and keeps calling `onReplyStart`, which is the call that reopens a Feishu preview. On 0f720c428ae it passes: cleanup and `onIdle` run once at dispatcher idle, and `onReplyStart` is not called again. It replaces the case that raced finalization against a real 50 ms timer.
- Message typing mode. New `queued-typing.cases.ts` case: a follow-up queued behind a live run in `message` mode never starts typing, so it must not take over idle. On 10d05599818 `onTypingHandoff` is called once. On a0ebdb83961 it is called 0 times. The existing handoff case now marks the mock controller active when its typing loop starts, as the real controller does.
- Two messages queued behind one live run (ClawSweeper revision 6, fixed in 2c7c47c9acd). New `followup-runner.test.ts` case runs a queued item that carries its own controller through a runner whose default controller belongs to a later message. On 0f720c428ae it fails: the item's own `markRunComplete` runs 0 times and the later message's controller is completed instead. On 2c7c47c9acd it passes: the item's own controller is completed once and the later one is untouched. The queued-typing handoff case now also checks that the enqueued run carries the dispatch's controller.
- On 2c7c47c9acd: `followup-runner` 30/30, `src/auto-reply/reply/queue` 75/75, `agent-runner.runreplyagent.e2e.test.ts` 226/226 with the e2e config, `dispatch-from-config.delivery.test.ts` 294/294, `extensions/feishu/src/reply-dispatcher.test.ts` 79/79, `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:core:test` pass.
- On 0f720c428ae: `reply-utils` and `reply-flow` 74/74, `extensions/feishu/src/reply-dispatcher.test.ts` 79/79, `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:core:test` exit 0, `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` on the changed files clean. `agent-runner.runreplyagent.e2e.test.ts` (226/226 on 4f0fc716970) was not rerun: this commit does not touch the runner, and its queued-typing cases pass a mock `onTypingHandoff`.
- CI on 0f720c428ae: `checks-node-changed-1` failed in `src/agents/model-fallback.reply-entry.e2e.test.ts` and `checks-node-changed-5` in `dispatch-from-config.delivery.test.ts` ("delivers deferred Telegram text when generation fails after a block"). Both assert the old error copy ("API rate limit reached", "Authentication failed", "Something went wrong") that main changed in d0b48d63efb (#163381) after this branch's base. CI's merge ref picked up the new copy. Main updated the delivery test in 08eb496e2c6. The model-fallback e2e on main still expects the old strings. On this branch's base the delivery file passes locally (294/294) and the model-fallback e2e passed 10/10 in an earlier pass. This PR does not touch the error copy.

On 8afd852ac2d: `followup-runner`, `reply-flow`, and `reply-utils` 103/103, `agent-runner.runreplyagent.e2e.test.ts` 226/226 with the e2e config, `pnpm tsgo:core` exit 0. Commit ids in the bullets above name the head they were measured on; the 2026-10-09 line below gives the current ones. prs.title: chore(deps): refresh dependencies through the November 13 cutoff
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw’s runtime, native apps, and build tooling are pinned to older dependency releases. This sweep picks up compatible updates while keeping the seven-day supply-chain cooldown in place.

## User Impact

The Gateway and bundled WebSocket consumers move to the [ws 8.23.0 security release](https://github.com/websockets/ws/releases/tag/8.23.0). Other changes refresh install, native, release, and CI dependencies without introducing new settings, migrations, or user actions.

## Why This Change Was Made

The inclusive cutoff is **2026-11-13 22:51:20 UTC**. This updates 74 distinct npm pins or existing overrides, 22 Fastlane transitive gems, five Cargo locks, and qualified scanner and container pins. No cooldown exclusions or patches were added. TypeBox 1.4.5 preserves OpenClaw’s namespace contract. The CI repair retains the existing npm-bundled tar and brace-expansion pins, AWS/Smithy, Teams SDK, and Oxlint releases, and uses Matrix music-metadata 12.3.5 after newer versions failed to load a runtime export. parse5 8.1.x and fs-safe 0.27.2 are deferred because their actual consumers regressed.

## Evidence

- The fixed-cutoff audit verified 162 new pnpm package identities relative to `8ab246473799`, 46 in the Vercel/Sandbox lock, 154 in the Cargo locks, and all 22 updated gems. No newly resolved version missed the cutoff; no retained pnpm edge downgraded. Frozen installs and locked Cargo metadata passed.
- The repaired tree passed the CI artifact build, clean paired Control UI budget comparison, extension test types, targeted lint and formatting, and all 114 selected npm lock validations. 108 focused tests passed, including Bedrock transport, Teams cancellation, Matrix media, Muse, Codex, Tlon, scheduled discovery, MCP custody, and the scanner assertions. The original Vercel/Sandbox materialization also passed; no deployment ran.
- The exact-source review covered all 107 changed paths and found no confirmed P0–P2 defects. Local Codex autoreview and ClawSweeper did not complete; those attempts are not counted as evidence. The integrated tree preserves main’s tokenjuice and Vitest changes and fixes the stale scanner, Codex, and OpenTelemetry pin assertions without weakening them.
- Rust workspace, Watch RTC, and both iroh binding suites passed. One local Linux desktop failure reproduced on the exact base; opt-in logind cases exceeded the host socket path limit. Fastlane Supply and Deliver loaded against frozen locks. OpenGrep scan and SARIF conversion, zizmor validation, PostgreSQL/Node container smoke, and local Litestream restore/rollback passed. Hosted CI on the published head is still required.

Co-authored by [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete).

prs.title: fix: honor OpenClaw tool ownership in custom CLI backends
prs.body:
Closes #197423

## What Problem This Solves

Custom CLI backends can declare that OpenClaw owns certain tools, but ordinary turns did not consistently honor that declaration outside Claude CLI. A backend could miss OpenClaw-mediated bootstrap file access or expose its native version of a tool alongside OpenClaw's.

## User Impact

Custom CLI backend authors can opt into OpenClaw-managed tools through their existing ownership declaration. Bundled Claude CLI behavior is unchanged. Backends that prepare their own execution must explicitly confirm that they enforce partial ownership.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the declared capabilities and the projected tool catalog to decide when to mediate tools and bootstrap files. Pass partial ownership to the backend and reject startup if it is not explicitly enforced.

## Evidence

61 focused tests passed, covering custom backend opt-in, bootstrap file access, and rejection when a backend acknowledges only the broader tool-availability contract. Core type checking, targeted lint, and formatting also passed. The local `pnpm build` completed; it reported non-fatal Control UI CSS and request-budget warnings.

prs.title: fix: let background reviews reuse their session's cached prompt
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A background session fork sends the session's request plus its own instruction at the end, so it should read the session's cached prompt prefix. When the session listed the provider-hosted `web_search` tool, a tool-free fork left it out. The fork's tool list then differed from the session's, and the request missed the cache from the first token. A tool-free fork already sends `tool_choice: none`, which stops hosted tools, so listing the tool is safe.

## User Impact

A tool-free background fork now lists exactly the session's tools, including hosted search, and reads the session's cached prefix. Behavior and permissions are unchanged: hosted search still honors the fork's execution cap, and tool-free forks still block hosted tools with `tool_choice: none`. Forks that run their own tools (for example, the skill-workshop review) still omit hosted search unless they are granted it, so they keep missing the cache when the session uses hosted search (see Limitation).

## Why This Change Was Made

- **One decision owner.** `sessionForkGatesHostedTools(api, allowedTools)` in `session-fork-request.ts` answers one question: can the provider stop hosted tools for this fork? The answer is yes only for a tool-free fork on an API with `tool_choice: none`. `attempt-stream-settle.ts` now lists hosted search when the execution cap allows it or when that owner says the provider gates it.
- **Byte replay kept (gate failed).** The plan was to delete the fork's byte replay of a live parent's last request (about 200 lines). A new journey step forks a live turn held inside a tool call, and it passed on all five transports without the replay. But local review found a case the step does not reach: a fork during the session's first live turn, before the first response, is anchored ahead of the session's system-prompt checkpoint. There the transcript pin is missing, and only the live replay keeps the session's system prompt. So the replay stays, and the new journey step stays as a guard.
- **Limitation, decided under standing authority:** a fork that has granted tools cannot list hosted search without being able to run it. The native endpoint rejects `tool_choice: allowed_tools` (`400 invalid_value`), so no provider-side gate exists, and hosted search runs before any local tool gate. The first push of this PR listed hosted search for every fork. Local review flagged that as an execution-scope regression, and it was reverted. Granting read-only `web_search` to review forks would let them hit the cache. That is a product choice and is not made here.

**Production LOC:** +33 / −19, net **+14**, measured against main after #203568. The replay deletion (−200) was reverted, for the reason above. The provider prompt state now builds the fork context it owns; this keeps `attempt-stream-prepare.ts` under its line cap.

## Evidence

**Prefix journey (#201723): new step "mid-turn fork".** It waits until the target run is inside a tool call, then forks through the latest persisted entry with `tools: []`. It asserts that the fork's system prompt and tools are byte-equal to the parent's, and that the fork's message list starts with the parent's last sent request.

| Transport | with replay | replay deleted (reverted) |
|---|---|---|
| anthropic-messages | pass | pass |
| bedrock-converse-stream | pass | pass |
| google-generative-ai | pass | pass |
| openai-completions | pass | pass |
| openai-responses | pass | pass |

**Transport contract** (`test/embedded-agent-attempt-stream-transport.test.ts`):

- The parent lists hosted `web_search`.
- A fork granted `web_search` lists it.
- A tool-free fork lists it and sends `tool_choice: none`.
- A fork granted only client tools does not list it.
- Client tool schemas are unchanged in every case.

**Mutation:** making hosted search ignore the execution cap turns the transport contract red (run in a scratch copy).

**Scratch Gateway E2E** (native OpenAI, skill-workshop review): that review grants its own tools, so it still lists 6 tools where the session lists 7 and reads 0 cached tokens, as before. An earlier ungated version reached 18,532 of 19,478 cached tokens on the same request, but that version was reverted for the reason above. A tool-free fork's listing is covered by the transport contract; the journey's fake providers have no hosted search.

prs.title: fix: fork large conversations without exhausting the database worker
prs.body:
Closes #203591

## What Problem This Solves

Forking a large local conversation can kill its database worker before the fork finishes, even when the conversation passes the existing token limit. The caller then gets a missing native completion/commit receipt error instead of a child conversation.

## User Impact

User impact: eligible same-store parent-entry forks (including native subagent context=fork spawns) can copy large historical message bodies without retaining all those bodies in the worker heap. No migration, configuration change, higher heap limit, or weaker commit acknowledgement is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Plan branch selection using per-row navigation, classification and tool-pairing facts, then hydrate selected events individually for the existing exact token estimate and streamed child append. The existing transaction, source resolver, append owner and native receipt contract still own correctness. This trades extra per-row reads/parses for lower peak heap use.

The bound is planning metadata plus the largest event, not constant memory for arbitrarily many rows or oversized malformed metadata. Cross-store/incognito preparation, main-thread fallbacks and other history readers are unchanged. The existing model-context navigation projection cannot be reused as-is: it introduces own `parentId`/`timestamp` keys and normalizes message bodies in ways that change legacy parentless navigation and malformed-row classification; the fork plan must preserve those raw distinctions.

## Evidence

- **Real red/green reproduction:** 8,192 synthetic assistant messages × 64 KiB body = **512 MiB** of history. The unmodified upstream worker fails with `ERR_WORKER_OUT_OF_MEMORY` and `outcome-unknown` before confirmed native settlement; the repaired worker completes under the unchanged 512/16 MiB production heap limits. It verifies child row count, first/last full body readback, inherited ancestry, the exact 20-token decision, and an unchanged parent entry. No live or private data. The stress case is in the existing release-only inventory; cheap body-non-retention and semantic checks remain in the ordinary tier.
- **79 focused tests passed on the final head:** 15 compact-plan differential/rollback tests, 1 real-worker stress regression, 61 existing parent-fork/context/branch consumers, and 2 release-tier inventory tests. Differential fixtures compare full and last-completed modes, indexed classification, exact estimates and hydrated source parity, including background placements, provider filtering, operators, compaction/reset, opaque/duplicate/malformed rows and labels.
- **Static/build proof:** repository-supported production, sessions-test and root-tooling-test typechecks, session-accessor/SQLite-transaction boundary guards, scoped core/tooling lint, six-file formatting, and `git diff --check` pass. Production worker bundles were built by the real test launcher; this is **not** a full release/package build.
- **Review:** independent native Claude CLI read-only review of the complete local candidate against `5b684035a11` found no P0/P1 defects and no submission blocker. Its actionable test-cost finding was addressed by the release-only inventory and a cheap non-retention assertion. Optional extra fixtures and per-row query optimization remain follow-ups, not correctness claims. The reviewed six-file patch is byte-identical after rebasing onto `34ce936db81`; final head is `22f846d82fa100fa8b7d9e6390eaebc15cecfe4c`. Review was code inspection, not reviewer-executed tests.
- **Measured local wall times:** latest-base red reproduction 62.23 s (18.044 s case, cold worker compile included); repaired stress measured alone 47.87 s (37.143 s case); existing consumers measured alone 47.61 s; cheap differential rerun 7.88 s (15/15). Final-head rerun: 77 sessions tests in 93.45 s wall plus 2 inventory tests in 1.65 s launcher time. Final production/sessions/tooling typechecks took 2.84/3.06/2.93 s wall. The expensive test proves survival at the unchanged production heap cap; a small fixture would miss the original failure. CI seconds are not available yet: the initial [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45056806919) is `action_required` with zero jobs, so CI has not executed. The aggregate CI gate is red pending successful CI admission/completion; `pnpm test:ci-failed 203595` reports no selected Vitest failures to rerun. Dependency and security-sensitive review statuses passed.

The earlier worker-test red reproduction is against `5b684035a11ecb3d65c26a483d83ab8b494e61be`; the final contribution is based on `34ce936db81eb0073025c05c920ea0a1506f5f7d`, whose intervening changes do not affect the relevant owners. Related rewind fix #198786 does not repair this parent-entry fork path. No full-suite, live deployment or exhaustive malformed-shape fuzzing claim.

## Captured public-entry behavior (2026-11-22)

Correction: **512 MiB old / 16 MiB young**, not 512/32, at both pinned builds. The original text was wrong. Both sqlite-worker-broker-lifecycle.ts and shared-worker-host.ts specify 512/16; native Worker.resourceLimits observations below confirm the effective values. No heap flag was increased.

Node runtime: v24.22.2. This runs the shipped openclaw.mjs CLI in separate processes against task-only loopback Gateways, not an in-process fork harness. Build metadata: before **34ce936db81eb0073025c05c920ea0a1506f5f7d**; after exact PR head **22f846d82fa100fa8b7d9e6390eaebc15cecfe4c**. The repository subprocess compiler (full preset) built the production CLI/Gateway and native-worker graphs, launched from isolated output directories. This is **scoped compiled-runtime behavior proof, not a packaged release build**. No source edits, mock receipts, transaction replacements, private transcripts, deployment, or live-state changes.

Fixture: 8,192 generator-seeded assistant messages, each 65,536 ASCII x bytes and usage {input:10,output:10}: 536,870,912 historical body bytes. Separate HOME, config, SQLite, cache/temp, and ports; all bulk data on a mounted data volume. A loopback synthetic OpenAI-compatible endpoint was configured for spawn admission; no real provider credentials or inference were used. Completion announcements were disabled on the final capture to preserve the parent.

**Surface:** CLI → WebSocket tools.invoke → core sessions_spawn(context=fork) → the repaired parent-entry worker. The broader sessions.create(fork=true) API uses a different full-history preparation path and still failed this workload in an exploratory capture; it is **not fixed or claimed by this PR**. Cross-store/incognito and unrelated whole-history readers remain outside scope.

<details>
<summary>Redacted terminal capture and persisted integrity checks</summary>

Only installation/state locations and the task-only credential are represented by shell variables. Flags, JSON arguments, SHA values, errors, result fields and verification below are captured. RUNTIME selects the corresponding isolated compiled CLI. Both Gateways ran with a whole-process-tree cgroup ceiling of 4 GiB and CPUQuota=200%; these are not per-worker V8 heap limits.

~~~sh
# Server, in its own isolated HOME/state/config environment:
node --require "$PROOF/worker-limits.cjs" "$RUNTIME/openclaw.mjs" gateway run \
  --bind loopback --port "$PORT" --auth token --allow-unconfigured
# Before PORT=29643; after PORT=29641. Observer only logs native
# Worker.resourceLimits; the cause capture additionally observes error events.
# Client, in the same isolated environment:
node "$RUNTIME/openclaw.mjs" gateway call tools.invoke \
  --url "ws://127.0.0.1:$PORT" --token "$TOKEN" \
  --params '{"name":"sessions_spawn","sessionKey":"agent:main:proof-parent","args":{"task":"Synthetic fork proof: return OK without using tools.","taskName":"pr203595-integrity-proof","context":"fork","mode":"run","model":"proof/proof","expectsCompletionMessage":false,"runTimeoutSeconds":30}}' \
  --timeout 180000 --json
# Additional before native-cause capture: taskName=pr203595-cause-proof.
~~~

**Before**, 20:05:04–20:05:08 UTC; Gateway request 3,185 ms:
~~~json
{
  "entry": "sqlite-store.worker.js",
  "resourceLimits": {
    "maxYoungGenerationSizeMb": 16,
    "maxOldGenerationSizeMb": 512,
    "codeRangeSizeMb": -1,
    "stackSizeMb": 4
  }
}
{
  "entry": "sqlite-store.worker.js",
  "error": {
    "name": "Error",
    "code": "ERR_WORKER_OUT_OF_MEMORY",
    "message": "Worker terminated due to reaching memory limit: JS heap out of memory"
  }
}
{
  "status": "error",
  "error": "Session patch has no confirmed native completion and commit receipt",
  "childSessionKey": "agent:main:subagent:34242834-0fb8-41af-b6c0-4624d95c1e70"
}
~~~
CLI exit 0: RPC success containing a **domain failure**, not fork success. The earlier public invocation returned the same domain failure. Whole-Gateway cgroup peak: 2,585,722,880 bytes; cumulative CPU 35.460872 s, including startup.

**After**, 20:02:19–20:02:50 UTC; Gateway request 29,299 ms:
~~~json
{
  "entry": "sqlite-store.worker.js",
  "resourceLimits": {
    "maxYoungGenerationSizeMb": 16,
    "maxOldGenerationSizeMb": 512,
    "codeRangeSizeMb": -1,
    "stackSizeMb": 4
  }
}
{
  "status": "accepted",
  "childSessionKey": "agent:main:subagent:0be21c99-c0ab-4040-b1e6-70017972d45c",
  "context": "fork",
  "expectsCompletionMessage": false
}
~~~
CLI exit 0, domain status accepted. Whole-Gateway cgroup peak: 3,847,110,656 bytes; cumulative CPU 67.874168 s, including startup/child lifecycle. These are not a claimed worker-memory benchmark.

Acceptance alone is insufficient: after stopping only the task-owned Gateway, a separate verifier read actual persisted parent/child payloads through the canonical per-row decoder. Assertions: every byte of all 8,192 bodies; endpoint IDs/usage; every copied non-header parent event; exact inheritedThrough against the actual parent leaf; parent entry deep-equal to its pre-request baseline. SHA-256 covers the ordered original 512 MiB body stream. The extra parent row is synthetic lifecycle metadata from exploratory setup; the extra child row is its task message, not missing/duplicated large payloads.

~~~json
{
  "parentEntryUnchanged": true,
  "parentLargePayloadMessages": 8192,
  "childLargePayloadMessages": 8192,
  "parentRows": 8194,
  "childRows": 8195,
  "entireParentNonHeaderPrefixCopied": true,
  "firstId": "event-0",
  "lastId": "event-8191",
  "everyBodyFullyEqual": true,
  "bodyBytes": 536870912,
  "parentBodiesSha256": "ddbb49d537146f639c1861504180e70f03249caca9fe7631d54e7c01429d85b5",
  "childBodiesSha256": "ddbb49d537146f639c1861504180e70f03249caca9fe7631d54e7c01429d85b5",
  "inheritedThrough": [
    "e5cc49f0-e369-4539-92d0-4dd3892ea450"
  ],
  "sqliteQuickCheck": {
    "quick_check": "ok"
  }
}
~~~
Verifier exit 0; wall time 13.01 s; maximum RSS 896,344 KiB; SQLite quick_check ok. This supplements—not relabels—the 79 previously reported focused tests. No model-inference, notification-delivery, optional context-engine cleanup, full-packaging, or all-fork-API success claim. The scoped compiled runtime logged a post-child optional context-engine cleanup module-resolution error; persisted fork and full readback above succeeded independently.

</details>

**Maintainer-only gate remains:** https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45056806919 is completed / action_required, zero jobs. No approval bypass, upstream workflow approval, merge, deployment, or live runtime replacement.

prs.title: fix(agents): long provider error messages stall the Gateway
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: one failed model request whose error message carries a long run of id-like text (letters or digits joined by `-`, `.`, `:` or `/`) freezes the whole Gateway for about 20 seconds and makes that failed turn take 11 to 29 seconds longer.

## User Impact

User impact: a provider, proxy or local model server that answers with a large error body no longer blocks other sessions, channels, the Control UI or `/healthz` while OpenClaw classifies and logs that error.

## Why This Change Was Made

Three checks on the provider failure path start with an id-like pattern and then look for a fixed part after it. On a long id-like run without that fixed part, the engine walks to the end of the run from every position in it, so the cost grows with the square of the run length:

- the Ollama retirement check in `isModelNotFoundErrorMessage` (`<id> was retired at <date> ... (ref:`), used by failover classification, error observation and the auth-key rate-limit check
- the same retirement wording in the run failover policy
- the `x-api-key: ...` style header pattern in the diagnostic credential redaction that projects every provider error

The streaming transport reads up to 64 KB of an error body, and one failure classifies and projects the message several times. In the run below the redaction runs on the Gateway main thread, and the retirement checks add their time to the failed turn.

Each check now finds its fixed part first (` was retired at ...`, or the credential header name and its colon) and then looks back over the id or header prefix with the same pattern. They accept exactly the same inputs as before, the redacted text is byte-identical, and each character is scanned a bounded number of times. In the failover policy the retirement wording moves out of the shared alternation into its own check with the same word boundaries.

## Evidence

### Conflict repair (2026-11-22)

Merged `main` at `c00e1854a50` in `0bc89ec2d6b` to resolve an append-at-end conflict in `credential-redaction.test.ts`. Both the PR's long-header regression and main's new unbounded diagnostic-JSON tests are retained. The PR's production delta is unchanged.

On the merged tree, `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run packages/ai/src/utils/credential-redaction.test.ts src/agents/live-model-errors.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/failover-policy.test.ts` passed all 41 tests across the three files. `oxfmt --check` and `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig tsconfig.json` passed on the six changed TypeScript files. `pnpm tsgo:core` and `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` passed. Node 24.21.0 and the frozen lockfile were used in an isolated worktree.

These are current-head local checks. The existing production-path timings below were not rerun for this test-only conflict resolution. GitHub CI and security-sensitive approval are still required for the new head.


Gateway from source (`node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts gateway run`), loopback, `/v1/chat/completions` enabled, with a mock OpenAI-compatible provider on loopback that answers HTTP 400 with the named error message. A separate process requests `/healthz` every 100 ms during the turn.

| Checkout | Provider error message | Turn | Longest `/healthz` wait | Gateway stall report |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| main `cb8c849` | prose control, 64,000 chars | 2.7 s | 77 ms | none |
| main `cb8c849` | `-a` repeated, 64,000 chars | 31.2 s | 20,369 ms | `main-thread stall: elapsedMs=17715 task="gateway:http"`, profile in `redactCredentialText` |
| main `cb8c849` | `a:` repeated, 64,000 chars | 13.8 s | 511 ms | none |
| this branch | prose control | 1.7 s | 109 ms | none |
| this branch | `-a` repeated | 1.8 s | 315 ms | one 324 ms report |
| this branch | `a:` repeated | 1.6 s | 67 ms | none |

The `a:` run leaves the credential header pattern fast (`:` ends its run), so its 11 extra seconds on main come from the retirement checks alone. Each turn made exactly one provider request on both checkouts. The branch rows come from two Gateway runs of the same commit `4175774`.

Rebased on main `fe3df80d15` (2026-11-17) after #200073 and #199234 added tests at the same place in `live-model-errors.test.ts` and `credential-redaction.test.ts`. Both sets of tests are kept, and the source changes are unchanged. The three test files pass (40 tests) on the rebased head.

With only the two retirement checks fixed, the same `-a` turn still blocked `/healthz` for 18.7 s, and the Gateway stall profile pointed at `redactCredentialText` under `projectProviderError`. That is why the credential header pattern is part of this change.

Single calls on a 64,000-character `-a` run:

| Helper | main | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `isModelNotFoundErrorMessage` | 3,915 ms | 2.8 ms |
| `classifyFailoverReason` | 4,151 ms | 43 ms |
| `isApiKeyRateLimitError` | 3,885 ms | 13 ms |
| `buildApiErrorObservationFields` | 7,485 ms | 91 ms |
| `redactDiagnosticText` | 3,737 ms | 45 ms |
| `projectProviderError` | 14,009 ms | 210 ms |

Differential fuzzers compared old and new results on 600,000 random strings per check. The strings mix id characters, spaces, newlines, quotes, partial and complete retirement suffixes, the other model-not-found phrases, and credential header names with and without `x-` style prefixes. They found 0 differences in `.test()` results for both retirement checks and 0 differences in `replace()` output for the header pattern (about 15,000 of those strings were redacted).

Commands run on this branch:

- `pnpm test src/agents/live-model-errors.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/failover-policy.test.ts packages/ai/src/utils/credential-redaction.test.ts packages/ai/src/utils/provider-error.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: all passed. The three new tests fail on main (2,228 ms, 2,375 ms and 17,917 ms against their 500 ms bound) and take a few ms here.
- `pnpm test src/agents/failover-error.test.ts src/agents/failover/failover-classification.corpus.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/assistant-failure.test.ts packages/ai/src/transports/transport-stream-shared.test.ts src/agents/payload-redaction.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 297 passed. These include the existing Ollama retirement fixtures and the provider error redaction consumers.
- `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` on the touched files, `git diff --check`: clean.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:core:test`: passed.
- `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-test-lines-ratchet.mts`: OK with the 33-line allocation in `config/test-lines-allocations/provider-error-retired-model-scan.txt`.

prs.title: fix: progress refresh stalls while a background command runs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Progress refresh can stall while the assistant polls a background command, leaving the active run waiting until its timeout instead of refreshing promptly. This ports the release repair from #203571 to main.

## User Impact

Progress can refresh while a background command is still running, without restarting that command or losing its eventual result. No configuration changes or migrations are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Extend the existing steering-aware wait owner to canonical native process polling, alongside native exec. Other process actions do not gain this behavior. Preserve main's wait-registration plumbing and native exec trailing-newline contract.

The smallest fix reuses the current owner and state; it adds no alternate execution path. The existing regression is parameterized to cover both wait modes and verify one command launch plus the original continuation.

## Evidence

- Main port: 82 tests pass across the AgentSession regression, Code Mode wait, and prompt-prefix stability suites. The process-poll regression verifies steering delivery and exact continuation without relaunch.
- Core typecheck, focused lint, formatting, and diff checks pass.
- Canonical local autoreview on the final staged main-port snapshot: P0–P2 scoped-clean, no actionable findings. Its coverage is the supplied diff; unchanged owner context was not independently loaded by that reviewer.
- The release implementation also passed an isolated Gateway/live-model progress-refresh test and exact-head CI before #203571 merged. That live test proves active-parent completion and idle-refresh behavior; it does not assert which nested poll cell is active at the instant of refresh. Main-specific live qualification has not been rerun.
- This is not final release qualification; the reserved full FRV remains unused.

prs.title: fix: prioritize recommended models in picker search
prs.body:
Related: #201450 (broader search changes)

## What Problem This Solves

A broad model search such as `5.5` can show GPT‑5.5 before Claude Opus 5.5 in the session and command-palette composers. Search used catalog order for equally good matches, and ClawRouter's live inventory did not carry the original provider's recommendation.

## User Impact

Available recommended models now win ties across providers. A `5.5` search puts Claude Opus 5.5 ahead of GPT‑5.5, while a specific `gpt-5.5` search still finds GPT‑5.5 first. This does not change selected or default models, or remove any choices.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing hosted recommendations as a tiebreaker, not an extra ranking list. When ClawRouter has no shortlist, match its qualified model IDs against the original provider's recommendations. No provider calls are added to search.

## Evidence

Both composer paths showed the wrong order on the baseline and passed on the fix in Chromium with a synthetic catalog. A hosted-catalog regression verifies that the recommendation reaches the ClawRouter row. Focused picker and catalog suites (66 tests), the four-test Chromium suite, UI typecheck, scoped lint, and formatting passed. No live model call was needed. Local Codex autoreview could not start in its isolated sandbox; no clean review is claimed.

Crops from matched 1280×900 Chromium captures of the command-palette composer; the same regression was exercised in the session composer.

prs.title: fix: let a Git install switch back to the npm package
prs.body:
Related: #200578

## What Problem This Solves

When a Git install that started from npm runs `openclaw update --channel stable` (or `beta`) to go back to the npm package, the update always fails. The error is `Occupied slot does not resolve to its original installation.` and nothing changes. Since #200578, the npm package an npm-to-Git switch leaves behind is a directory whose `openclaw.mjs` forwards to the Git release launcher. The update executor was still keyed by the Git install and refused to reserve that directory. Switching the executor's key alone was not enough: package activation, and then the installed target's post-core continuation, also refused the publication.

## User Impact

**Draft, NEEDS-MAINTAINER-DECISION.** With this change the switch back to npm completes: `openclaw` on PATH runs the npm package, and later npm updates work. The Gateway service is still left running the Git release. The update prints the existing warning `Gateway service management skipped: the service starts the Git release launcher … run openclaw triage`, and `openclaw gateway install --force` from the npm package rebinds the service.

## Why This Change Was Made

A switch from Git updates the npm package destination, so that destination now owns the update: the executor lease, package publication recovery and the recorded publication authority. The executor is admitted at the package destination after destination inspection, which already recognizes this install's forwarding entry. The pre-mutation executor entry moves into `admitUpdatePackageRoot` (package-activation module), because `update-command-target.ts` is at its line cap.

Rejected along the way, each proven on Crabbox:

- **Admit the forwarding package as an occupied slot and publish with the slot's authority.** The package swap and Doctor succeeded. The post-core continuation then refused (`Package publication recovery is pending`). That continuation runs in the installed target, meaning every published release, and its delegated executor authority is the parent's install lease. So the lease itself has to be the npm package.
- **Retain the Git install as the managed service root so the existing "rebind A to B after verification" path moves the service.** Preflight refused with `service-definition-not-writable`: the Git release launcher service has no owned, refreshable definition verdict.

Decision needed (owner of the Git release service and #203194/#203497): should a switch from a Git release to its package rebind the Git launcher service? If so, by what authority, given that the updater today "cannot yet confirm that the release it runs is its own"? The alternative is to keep the service untouched with the warning, which is what this draft does. Production LOC: +35/−20 across two files.

The same owner covers the Windows symptom from the update matrix, `ENOENT: realpath C:\Program Files\nodejs\node_modules\openclaw`, seen on a Git install that never had an npm copy. An executor keyed by the Git slot takes `realpathSync.native` of the missing package in its slot reservation. Keyed by the package destination, the reservation returns early. A Windows box lane was not run.

Regression test: `src/cli/update-cli/update-command-target.git-to-package.test.ts` runs target resolution with a real executor, then the package swap's destination reservation. On base it fails with `Occupied slot does not resolve to its original installation.` for the forwarding package and `ENOENT: realpath …/node_modules/openclaw` for the case with no npm copy. With this change both pass.

## Evidence

Crabbox AWS c7a.8xlarge. npm `2026.11.30` (main `feea72c1863`, relabelled), then `--channel dev` (Git release from the branch head), then `--channel stable --tag 2026.11.31`, then `--tag 2026.11.32`. Harness lane `g140-p2g.sh`; lastTouchedVersion re-stamped before hop 2 to undo a relabel artifact.

| Lane | hop1 npm→Git | hop2 Git→npm | hop3 npm→npm |
|---|---|---|---|
| base `feea72c1863` (×2) | rc 0, readyz 200 | rc 1 `Occupied slot does not resolve to its original installation.` | n/a (still Git) |
| slot + publication authority `8c5463ed30a` | rc 0 | rc 1 post-core `Package publication recovery is pending` (target dist) | rc 1 unfinished recovery |
| destination-keyed `12bdf100faa` | rc 0, readyz 200 | **rc 0**, npm 2026.11.31 on PATH, readyz 200; service left on Git release with skip warning | **rc 0**, 2026.11.32, readyz 200 |
| + service rebind `755fe4f0620` | rc 0 | rc 1 `service-definition-not-writable` (preflight, nothing changed) | n/a |
| this head's production code `86a7f73f2e3` (later commits are test-only) | rc 0, readyz 200 | **rc 0** (status ok), npm 2026.11.31 on PATH, readyz 200; Gateway still on the Git release with the skip warning | **rc 0** (status ok), 2026.11.32, readyz 200 |

Known cost of the split: hops 2 and 3 take about 800 s each, waiting on deferred Doctor inspections whose Gateway readiness is never verified. That is part of the decision above.

Local: `pnpm tsgo:core` clean, oxfmt/oxlint clean. Local `update-cli.test.ts` and `update-cli.target-schema.test.ts` failures (native-worker cleanup) were identical on base files in the same worktree, so PR CI is the gate.

prs.title: fix(gateway): reverting a deferred restart-required config edit still restarts the Gateway
prs.body:
Closes #119360

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Gateway still restarts after an operator reverts a restart-required config edit (for example `gateway.port`) to the exact running config while that restart waits for active work to drain.

## User Impact

User impact: probing a restart-class setting and putting `openclaw.json` back no longer drops Control UI and channel sessions for a full restart. A revert to any other config, a second restart-required edit, an explicit writer restart request, and plugin install changes still restart as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

When a restart is deferred, the reloader advances its diff baseline to the deferred candidate before the process actually restarts. The revert is then compared against that candidate, so it looks like a new `gateway.port` change and plans another restart. The reloader now remembers the config and plugin install records the process still runs while a restart is deferred. A candidate that matches them exactly takes the existing unchanged-config path and is accepted with `revertsDeferredRestart`. The managed reloader then drops its `acceptedRestart`, so the existing acceptance retires the paused restart with no rearm and no "still requires a restart" warning. `server-reload-restart.ts` is unchanged, so there is no second copy of restart-owned paths in the reloader (the open findings on #119576).

A revert never retires a restart whose plan carries a reason other than a changed config path, such as writer restart intent or hot-reload recovery, so a config revert cannot cancel those (the concern on #119577).

Install records are compared by path diff, as `pluginInstallRecordChangedPaths` already does, not with `isDeepStrictEqual`. The startup records are a plain object and the ledger reader returns null-prototype maps, so a strict compare never matches in a real Gateway. The live run below caught this. The tests now mock the reader with the production shape.

A revert does not retire the restart while a shared-auth requirement is pending (commit 077cca214c7). When the deferred candidate changed shared auth, for example a token to password switch, `runManagedRestart` has already marked the candidate's shared-auth generation as required, and only a restart clears it. Retiring the restart there would leave the Gateway rejecting the restored token with nothing scheduled to fix it. In that case the revert takes the normal restart path, as on main, where `runManagedRestart` sees an unchanged generation and clears the requirement. The guard is a `canRetireDeferredRestart` option on the reloader that the managed reloader answers from `sharedGatewaySessionGenerationState.required`.

Out of scope, and unchanged from main: a revert after a hot edit was applied during the deferral still restarts once, because the running snapshot then holds the hot-applied values. Batching distinct edits (#98436) is separate.

## Evidence

- New `deferred restart followed by a revert` tests in `src/gateway/server-reload-handlers.test.ts` drive the real managed reloader with its watcher and write listener (8 cases: revert by config write, revert by file edit, revert to a different config, writer restart intent, a second restart-required edit, a hot edit during the deferral, a new edit after a retired revert, and an auth mode change that reverts during the deferral). On the test commit 50c219cf955: 2 failed, 5 passed (both exact-revert cases still owe a restart). On the fix 84d63e3b783: 7 passed. The auth case was red on 6701e77d283 (the revert retired the restart and the restored token stayed rejected) and passes on 077cca214c7.
- Test time for `pnpm test src/gateway/server-reload-handlers.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`, vitest `Duration` over 3 local runs each (the first run of each set is a cold transform cache): base 0e17a464f0d, 119 tests, 26.71 s / 14.42 s / 14.30 s. Head 077cca214c7, 127 tests, 27.27 s / 14.63 s / 14.56 s. About 0.2 s added warm. In CI on 077cca214c7, `checks-node-changed` took 2m49s; there is no base-commit CI run of this file to compare.
- `pnpm test` on every `src/gateway/config-reload*.test.ts` and `src/gateway/server-reload*.test.ts` file: 24 files, 476/476 pass.
- `oxfmt --check` and `scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` are clean on the 3 changed files, `git diff --check` is clean, and `pnpm tsgo:core` plus `tsconfig.core.test.gateway-server.json` exit 0.
- The repo's `autoreview` skill (Codex, branch mode) reported no actionable findings.

### Real behavior proof (live Gateway, before and after)

The agent ran the Gateway from source (`node scripts/run-node.mjs gateway run --port 18960`) in a scratch HOME on Node 26.8.2 with `logging.level: "debug"` and no real credentials. A local OpenAI-compatible mock model answers any turn containing `SLOWTURN` after 40 s, which keeps work active. The script, the same on both commits:

1. Send `SLOWTURN` through `openclaw gateway call chat.send` on `agent:main:main`.
2. Copy `openclaw.json` byte for byte, then write it with `gateway.port` set to 18962. Wait for the deferral line.
3. After 2 s, copy the original back (`cmp` confirms it is byte-identical).
4. Wait for the slow turn to finish, then 15 s more.

Before (base 9fe692d3e29). The revert plans a second restart, which fires after the drain:

```
10:41:21.368 [reload] config change requires gateway restart (gateway.port) — deferring until 2 operation(s), 1 reply(ies), 1 embedded run(s), ...
10:41:24.486 [reload] config change detected; evaluating reload (gateway.port)
10:41:24.499 [reload] config change requires gateway restart (gateway.port) — deferring until ...
10:42:00.869 [gateway] received SIGUSR2; restarting
10:42:00.870 [reload] all operations and replies completed; restarting gateway now
10:42:03.763 [gateway] ready
```

After (fix 84d63e3b783). The revert retires the debt, and no restart follows:

```
11:05:57.786 [reload] config change requires gateway restart (gateway.port) — deferring until 2 operation(s), 1 reply(ies), 1 embedded run(s), ...
11:06:00.858 [reload] config matches the running Gateway; deferred config restart not required
(no SIGUSR2, no restart line, and no second ready line through 15 s after the slow turn finished)
chat.history tail: user: SLOWTURN proof final1 / assistant: chat turn finished normally
```

The base result held on 2 of 2 runs. The fix result held on 3 of 3 runs (two with the comparison applied to the working tree, one on the final head). In every run the Gateway kept listening on 18960, nothing listened on 18962, and the slow turn finished.

What this run did not cover: a supervised restart (launchd or systemd), a deferral timeout or forced restart, and a revert of auth-changing paths. The unit tests cover the remaining negative cases, including the auth-mode revert, which keeps the restart.

Rebased 2026-10-17 onto main 437db07c97f (head e1600f9). Main's #174112 inlined `prepareRestart` into a direct `opts.onRestart(...)` call, so the runtime baseline line now sits just before that call. The commit ids and counts above are from the old head. Commits now: c372247 tests, cc2d181 fix, 0f910c1 auth test, e1600f9 auth fix. An earlier rebase onto 4b791ee33e0 (head ff16e45) had 4 failing CI tests in `server.sessions.create.dispatch.test.ts` and `server-methods/agent.test.ts`. This PR does not touch those files. Main fixed them in 88d32ca6e63, so this rebase picks that fix up. On e1600f9, the config-reload and server-reload test files pass 229/229. `server-reload-handlers.test.ts`, `server.sessions.create.dispatch.test.ts` and `server-methods/agent.test.ts` pass 540/540. The live Gateway proof above ran on the old commits.

Rebased 2026-10-18 onto main 8afe5eff5d1 (head 072fc33). Main's #175911 removed the paused and conservative restart debt this fix used to hand the revert to, so the fix was ported to that design instead of rebased line by line. The two test commits applied unchanged, and on main without the fix the two exact-revert cases still fail (`expected false to be true` on `isConfigReloadSettled()`), so the bug is still there. The two fix commits are now one, `072fc33`. It adds `revertsDeferredRestart` to the reloader's acceptance and the `canRetireDeferredRestart` guard in the managed reloader. That guard covers both the pending shared-auth case and restart reasons that are not changed config paths. With either half of the guard removed, one of the 8 revert tests fails. On 072fc33, the 8 revert tests pass, the 23 `config-reload*` and `server-reload*` test files pass 489/489, `oxfmt --check` and oxlint are clean on the 4 changed files, and `tsconfig.core.json` plus `tsconfig.core.test.gateway-server.json` typecheck with exit 0. The live Gateway proof and timing runs above are from the pre-#175911 commits and were not rerun.

AI disclosure: an AI agent (Claude Code) reproduced the bug with the failing tests, wrote the fix, and ran the checks above: `pnpm test` on the new tests on the test commit and on the fix, `pnpm test` on the reload test files, `oxfmt --check`, `scripts/run-oxlint.mjs`, `git diff --check`, `pnpm tsgo:core`, `scripts/run-tsgo.mjs`, the timing runs above, and the repo's `autoreview`. It also ran the live Gateway proof above against a local mock model, on the base commit and on the fix.

prs.title: feat: make provider sign-in easy to find in plugin settings
prs.body:
Closes #203371

## What Problem This Solves

If I start on an installed provider plugin’s page, I have to go to Models separately to find its sign-in.

## User Impact

An enabled provider plugin with a guided sign-in has **Sign in** under **Settings → Accounts → Models**. It opens the existing Models dialog with that plugin’s methods.

The provider picker uses the plugin’s labels. The declared method label also supplies the default guided action text, and explicit action-label overrides keep their existing presentation. After guided sign-in, **Choose a model** lets me start a new chat with an available model and keep my current default.

## Why This Change Was Made

The plugin already declares its sign-in methods. OpenClaw can use that metadata for the entry point and the visible action text. Plugins without guided sign-in keep their existing Settings controls.

## Evidence

![GitHub Copilot plugin settings comparison](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/2cad13314f90dfc632e8548622fd445333712126/images/2026/11/82b2580b-f9c5-418a-8417-5b25204c0eb9.png)

- In the built Control UI, **Sign in** opened Gemini’s existing dialog with **Sign in with Google** and the action-label override omitted.
- 70 focused tests, UI typechecking, and Swift syntax passed. The tests cover guided label defaults, explicit overrides, and account connection through the OAuth callback. The live Model Setup probe hit a host Codex detection timeout.

The Mac groups the options the Gateway reports and shows the selected provider's steps on the page. The Gateway still owns detection, sign-in, and verification.
