prs.title: feat(microsoft-foundry): support typed System One decisions
prs.body:
Related: #155131

## What Problem This Solves

Operators with a Microsoft-Decision-1.1 Foundry deployment cannot select it for OpenClaw's typed Decision evaluations. Foundry chat and image support do not use the System One Decision endpoint.

## User Impact

Operators can select `microsoft-foundry-systemone/microsoft-decision-1.1` for Boolean, Choice, and Score evaluation with text or JSON evidence. They supply a Foundry resource hostname, a deployment alias, and a resource-scoped API-key SecretRef. Chat and image routes and automatic Decision assistance remain unchanged. The Decision route does not yet support images or Entra ID.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing Foundry plugin owns a separate Decision V2 provider identity and credential so the route cannot inherit chat or image credentials. This builds on the Decision infrastructure Vincent Koc helped land in #181574 and reuses the shared System One decoder from the TypeSafe work in #188251. The adapter binds the prepared route to the live credential owner's resource and deployment, then sends one guarded HTTPS POST without redirects, capture, or fallback.

## Evidence

- **Full local build passed on [`1066b77d6`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/1066b77d604449d8b11593ed61d5fe780bf0dc8b).** Rebased onto upstream `main` at [`19fcba182`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/19fcba1823d045d25ef912707ac1feb4e8e7efda); `git range-diff` matched all four PR patches without changes. With Node 24.22.2 and pnpm 12.15.0 on Linux x64, `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` and `pnpm build` both passed. The full build included Control UI, native loading of 56 built plugin control-plane modules and Doctor closure checks, and the public Plugin SDK artifact checks. The SDK declaration graph measured **5,317,085 bytes** against a **5,385,536-byte** limit; the earlier declaration-size blocker no longer reproduces on this base, which includes #203083.
- **151 focused tests passed on the same head** across eight files: 110 Foundry, 26 shared Decision HTTP, and 15 TypeSafe Decisions. The Foundry and shared executor regressions verify that an admitted request can finish with its captured resource binding and that the next request must pass a fresh admission check. `git diff --check` passed.
- **Fresh isolated runtime proof on `1066b77d6`.** The compiled Gateway served native `decision_evaluate` via `/tools/invoke`, using a synthetic host-scoped Store SecretRef and a local TLS endpoint through a trusted CONNECT proxy. Tagged V2 JSON returned Boolean `0.9`, Choice `billing`, and Score `0.27` (fixture usage 70/3). A second call using legacy untagged JSON returned Boolean `0.02` (31/1). A third fixture response returned HTTP 307; the tool returned `unavailable: transport` and made no redirected request. The fixture verified exactly three POSTs to the configured path, with the expected deployment and request JSON and only the plugin-owned API-key header (no `Authorization` header). The network namespace had only loopback; all responses and token counts here are synthetic.
- **Stable-chat configuration compatibility.** The same unchanged synthetic Foundry chat configuration validated and listed the same existing chat model on stable `2026.11.6` (`06afb10`) and the rebased build. This checks config loading and model discovery, not hosted chat inference.
- **Scope:** current-head proof covers the local build, focused tests, and an isolated compiled Gateway against a synthetic provider. No new Azure request or hosted CI run was performed. The live synthetic transcript below is from the earlier deployed revision, not the rebased head. The Foundry configuration and public SDK contract still need a maintainer decision.

- **Live Gateway, two turns on [`cb46332`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/203048/commits/cb46332e5c05345685fd4a7cdf3481763cc1b402).** In a fresh OpenClaw 2026.11.6 session, native `decision_evaluate` used the configured System One provider through a Store SecretRef. A synthetic duplicate-charge ticket returned all three V2 types: Boolean `P(true) = 0.9997561537008779`, Choice `billing`, and Score `0.0009255192282724577` on a 0–2 rubric (near the single-customer/no-outage level). A second call in the same session used legacy untagged JSON, the first turn’s `billing` choice, and a synthetic follow-up withdrawing the refund request. It returned `P(refund_still_requested) = 0.000015177557853765349`. Neither Boolean included an explicit `answer`. Both calls reported `microsoft-decision-1.1` and `ok`, with **345 input / 4 output** tokens total. No real ticket or refund action was involved.

<details>
<summary>Redacted two-turn session transcript (JSONL)</summary>

The excerpts retain the actual tool arguments, returned results, and assistant replies. They omit the deployment and resource hostname, credentials, private session and run identifiers, duplicate wrapper events, and internal provenance. The ticket is fictional.

```jsonl
{"turn":1,"role":"operator","excerpt":"Run the first half of a live Foundry System One acceptance test for draft openclaw/openclaw #203048. [Private operational context omitted.] Make exactly ONE call to this session's native `decision_evaluate` tool (not HTTP, CLI, subagent, or a simulated answer), contractVersion 2 and tagged JSON state. [The synthetic state and rubric are preserved in the actual tool call below.]"}
{"turn":1,"role":"tool_call","tool":"decision_evaluate","arguments":{"contractVersion":2,"state":{"type":"json","value":{"ticket":"DEMO-104","customerMessage":"I was charged twice for one subscription renewal and want the extra charge reversed.","serviceStatus":"operating normally","customerCountAffected":1}},"questions":{"duplicate_charge_reported":{"type":"boolean","instructions":"Does the customer explicitly report a duplicate charge?","criteria":{"true":"Duplicate charge explicitly reported","false":"Duplicate charge not explicitly reported"}},"destination":{"type":"choice","instructions":"Select the destination for this ticket.","criteria":{"billing":"payments, refunds and invoices","technical":"uptime/bugs","account":"sign-in and identity"}},"severity":{"type":"score","criteria":["single-customer payment problem with no outage","multiple people impacted or a workaround unavailable","service-wide critical outage"]}}}}
{"turn":1,"role":"tool_result","tool":"decision_evaluate","content":{"status":"ok","result":{"model":"microsoft-decision-1.1","answers":{"destination":{"type":"choice","choice":"billing","probabilities":{"account":0.0007503068031170933,"billing":0.9981381964915157,"technical":0.0011114967053672466},"confidence":0.9972072947372737},"duplicate_charge_reported":{"type":"boolean","probabilityTrue":0.9997561537008779},"severity":{"type":"score","score":0.0009255192282724577,"probabilities":[0.9992920367089196,0.0004904073538884592,0.00021755593719199922],"confidence":0.9989380550633795}},"usage":{"inputTokens":178,"outputTokens":3}},"provenance":{"providerId":"microsoft-foundry-systemone"}}}
{"turn":1,"role":"assistant","text":"`DEMO-104` — one native v2 call returned `ok` with all three typed results. Only synthetic data was sent.\n\n- **Boolean** `duplicate_charge_reported`: `probabilityTrue=0.9997561537008779`; no explicit Boolean answer returned.\n- **Choice** `destination`: explicit answer `billing`. Probabilities: `billing=0.9981381964915157`, `technical=0.0011114967053672466`, `account=0.0007503068031170933`.\n- **Score** `severity`: `0.0009255192282724577`. Probabilities for levels 0–2: `[0.9992920367089196, 0.0004904073538884592, 0.00021755593719199922]`.\n\nReported usage: **178 input tokens, 3 output tokens**. The second-turn test was not run."}
{"turn":2,"role":"operator","excerpt":"Second and final turn of the bounded live Foundry System One acceptance test for draft #203048. Using actual prior typed results in this same session, call native `decision_evaluate` exactly once with the legacy untagged JSON state format (omit `contractVersion`; no HTTP or CLI). [The synthetic state and rubric are preserved in the actual tool call below.]"}
{"turn":2,"role":"tool_call","tool":"decision_evaluate","arguments":{"state":{"ticket":"DEMO-104","previousDestination":"billing","originalCustomerMessage":"I was charged twice for one subscription renewal and want the extra charge reversed.","customerFollowup":"I checked again. The second line was only a pending hold, it dropped off, and there is exactly one completed charge. No refund is needed."},"questions":{"refund_still_requested":{"type":"boolean","instructions":"Does the latest customer follow-up still explicitly request a refund? Prioritize the latest follow-up over the original request.","criteria":{"true":"The latest follow-up still explicitly requests a refund.","false":"The customer withdrew the request or confirms no refund is needed in the latest follow-up."}}}}}
{"turn":2,"role":"tool_result","tool":"decision_evaluate","content":{"status":"ok","result":{"model":"microsoft-decision-1.1","answers":{"refund_still_requested":{"type":"boolean","probabilityTrue":0.000015177557853765349}},"usage":{"inputTokens":167,"outputTokens":1}},"provenance":{"providerId":"microsoft-foundry-systemone"}}}
{"turn":2,"role":"assistant","text":"`DEMO-104` — the single native call with legacy untagged JSON returned `ok`. The Boolean result for `refund_still_requested` contained `probabilityTrue=0.000015177557853765349` and no explicit `answer` field.\n\nReported usage: **167 input tokens, 1 output token**. Synthetic test complete; no refund was authorized or issued."}
```

</details>

prs.title: feat(memory): let workspaces exclude generated files from search
prs.body:
Related: #101422 Supersedes #177868 by @CheekyHobson (closed for inactivity on 2026-11-18): their reviewed head `a2008ab09`, ported onto current main with co-author credit on the commit, plus the proof ClawSweeper asked for. ## What Problem This Solves Generated dreaming reports under `memory/dreaming/` are indexed like curated notes and crowd them out of memory search, and there is no setting to exclude paths inside the default memory folders. ## User Impact User impact: operators can set `memory.search.excludePaths` (globally or per agent), for example `["memory/dreaming/**"]`, to keep matching workspace files out of memory search and file watching. - Unset or empty changes nothing. The index scope hash is identical to the one 2026.11.6 writes, so this setting adds no rebuild on upgrade. - Setting or changing the list is a scope change, like changing `extraPaths`: `openclaw memory status` reports it, vector search pauses, and `openclaw memory index` rebuilds and drops the excluded rows. - Search only: excluded files are not deleted, `memory_get` can still read them, `memory forget` still scrubs them, and short-term recall/promotion eligibility is unchanged. - Patterns are workspace-relative globs. A leading `./` or `/` and a trailing `/` are accepted (`memory/dreaming/` is the same as `memory/dreaming/**`), and per-agent lists add to the global list. ## Why This Change Was Made One workspace-relative glob check, using the same minimatch options as the `extraPaths` matcher beside it in the memory host SDK (so patterns behave the same on Node and Bun), is applied where search scope is decided: file discovery (local and remote workspace providers), watcher eligibility, and the index scope hash. Shared watchers include the exclusions in their selection keys, so agents with different exclusions on one workspace rebaseline when one joins or leaves (the P2 ClawSweeper found on #177868). **Portable glob matching (ClawSweeper's 2026-11-09 review on `05585b7`):** the exclusion matcher called `path.posix.matchesGlob`, which Bun implements with `Bun.Glob`: extglobs never match and wildcards match dotfiles, so `["memory/dreaming/**/!(*.keep).md"]` excluded a report on Node but not on Bun. Main's #194912 had just moved the `extraPaths` matcher to minimatch for the same reason. `1463f6e` moves those minimatch options into one shared constant and uses it for `excludePaths` too, with compiled matchers cached per configured list. Results on Node are unchanged; on Bun they now match Node. **Pattern spellings (`2b7dc7f`):** gitignore-style spellings such as `memory/dreaming/`, `./memory/dreaming/**` or `/memory/dreaming/**` excluded nothing. `resolveMemorySearchIndexConfig`, which every reader (scan, watcher, scope hash, remote file worker) gets its settings from, now normalizes each entry once: trim, drop empty entries, use `/` separators, strip one leading `./` or `/`, turn a trailing `/` into `/**`, and dedupe in order. The matcher is unchanged. The docs and help example drop `memory/.dreams/**`: that folder only holds `.txt` and `.json` dreaming state, which memory search never indexes. Changes compared with #177868 at `a2008ab09`: - Rebased onto main: the scope hash goes through the single `resolveConfiguredMemoryScopeHash()` owner, and the matcher is exported from `plugin-sdk/memory-core-host-engine-fs`, the subpath #181891 narrowed the file worker to, instead of `engine-storage`. Both are private local-only subpaths, so this adds no third-party SDK contract. - The matcher lives in `packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/internal.ts` beside `matchesExtraMemoryPathEntry` instead of core `src/memory/root-memory-files.ts`. - Added the config field label, corrected the docs about the rebuild step, and linked the setting from the dreaming docs. - Tests: replaced the 13 s CLI e2e case with a manager test of about 4 s that mirrors two unforced `openclaw memory index` runs (the real CLI run is below). Dropped a test that indexed an excluded file through a private method, a `selectionKeys` shape test covered by the join/leave behavior test, a worker integration test that still passed with the P2 fix reverted, and (after ClawSweeper's review) a test that only checked the worker request shape. Size against main `a2f7aa9`: production +102/-21 in 15 files (including moving main's glob options into the shared constant); tests +159/-3; docs +18/-4; generated baselines +3/-3. (#177868 was +439/-18 in 33 files.) ### Maintainer decision needed #101422 asks for both search exclusion and recall/promotion eligibility control. This PR is the narrow first stage: search discovery, watching, and index scope only, with defaults and promotion safeguards unchanged. ClawSweeper's review of #177868 recommended approving that narrow search stage and leaving recall inclusion and diagnostics to follow-up work; the alternative is one combined search+recall include/exclude design. An operator on #101422 said the search-only step covers their need. Config surface: `pnpm config:docs:gen` raises the core count by 4 (2668 -> 2672 on main `a2f7aa9`) for `memory.search.excludePaths` and `agents.entries.*.memory.search.excludePaths`, each with its `.*` item path. That is the new setting itself. ## Evidence Real runs on `78d4f9f` (on main `431392a`), starting from the latest stable release, `openclaw@2026.11.6` from npm (installed with `--ignore-scripts`; the CLI runs without the package's install scripts). The current head `fa31efc` adds only a merge of main `a2f7aa9`. Earlier runs from 2026.11.5 on `59298b8`, from 2026.11.4 on `ddb2348`, from 2026.11.3 on `c210875`, from 2026.11.2 on `1463f6e` and on `05585b7` (before the portable-matcher change), from 2026.11.1 on `6d9ace7` and from 2026.10.10 on `b607675` showed the same behavior. Synthetic workspace: 3 curated files (`MEMORY.md`, `memory/backups.md`, `memory/garden.md`) and 7 generated reports (5 light, 2 REM, one REM report containing only "No strong patterns surfaced."). Isolated `OPENCLAW_HOME` under `env -i`, Node 26.12.1, and a local OpenAI-compatible embeddings stub on 127.0.0.1 (deterministic vectors, no provider calls). **Upgrade from 2026.11.6 and existing data:** 2026.11.6 builds the index (10 files, 10 chunks). After this branch's `doctor --fix` (main's agent-database migrations since 2026.11.6, v38 -> v43), the existing index loads clean (`Dirty: no`) and returns the same results and scores as 2026.11.6, before any re-index. With `excludePaths` unset, `memory index` keeps the stored scope hash, the chunking version and every stored chunk row (same count and same fingerprint over `id`, `path`, `hash`). This PR adds no database schema or stored fields; the scope hash changes only when `excludePaths` is set. The branch build prints main's version string, 2026.11.5, because 2026.11.6 shipped from a release branch. **Opting in:** setting `excludePaths` marks the index dirty with a scope change and pauses vector search until a rebuild, both shown in `memory status`. `memory index` then drops the 7 reports and keeps the 3 curated files; the curated note ranks first, and an edit refreshes it.
Terminal output (paths redacted to $OPENCLAW_HOME) ```text $ openclaw --version # npm openclaw@2026.11.6 OpenClaw 2026.11.6 (06afb10) $ openclaw memory index --agent main Memory index updated (main): 10 files indexed. $ openclaw memory search "when does the nightly backup run" --agent main 0.449 memory/backups.md:1-5 0.223 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-28.md:1-5 0.218 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-27.md:1-5 0.213 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-26.md:1-5 0.208 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-25.md:1-5 0.204 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-24.md:1-5 # stored index identity (2026.11.6): {"scopeHash":"e861c1d291b583b9f4bf96233b72b9e6984cc92320671a0805e1063946e4b1a1","chunkingVersion":6} # stored rows (2026.11.6): {"chunks":10,"chunkIdsSha256":"e538aca49c37a70e"} $ openclaw --version # this branch OpenClaw 2026.11.5 (78d4f9f) $ openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive # main's state migrations since 2026.11.6 Upgraded agent database schema in $OPENCLAW_HOME/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite: v38 -> v43 $ openclaw memory status --agent main Indexed: 10/10 files · 10 chunks Dirty: no $ openclaw memory search "when does the nightly backup run" --agent main # existing 2026.11.6 index, before any re-index 0.449 memory/backups.md:1-5 0.223 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-28.md:1-5 0.218 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-27.md:1-5 0.213 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-26.md:1-5 0.208 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-25.md:1-5 0.204 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-24.md:1-5 $ openclaw memory index --agent main Memory index updated (main): 10 files indexed. # stored index identity (this branch, no excludePaths): {"scopeHash":"e861c1d291b583b9f4bf96233b72b9e6984cc92320671a0805e1063946e4b1a1","chunkingVersion":6} # stored rows (this branch, no excludePaths): {"chunks":10,"chunkIdsSha256":"e538aca49c37a70e"} $ openclaw config set memory.search.excludePaths '["memory/dreaming/**"]' --strict-json Updated memory.search.excludePaths. Restart the gateway to apply. $ openclaw memory status --agent main Indexed: 10/3 files · 10 chunks Dirty: yes Index identity: index scope changed (owner: configuration, code: scope) Vector search: paused until memory is rebuilt $ openclaw memory index --agent main Memory index updated (main): 3 files indexed. $ openclaw memory status --agent main Indexed: 3/3 files · 3 chunks Dirty: no # indexed rows by path: {"path":"MEMORY.md","chunks":1} {"path":"memory/backups.md","chunks":1} {"path":"memory/garden.md","chunks":1} $ openclaw memory search "when does the nightly backup run" --agent main 0.422 memory/backups.md:1-5 The nightly backup runs at 02:30 and copies the photo archive to the NAS. # edit memory/backups.md: 02:30 -> 03:15 $ openclaw memory index --agent main Memory index updated (main): 3 files indexed. $ openclaw memory search "when does the nightly backup run" --agent main 0.422 memory/backups.md:1-5 The nightly backup runs at 03:15 and copies the photo archive to the NAS. ```
**Pattern spelling on `2b7dc7f`:** the same synthetic workspace with a trailing-slash pattern, `["memory/dreaming/"]`, which matched nothing before `2b7dc7f`.
Terminal output ```text $ openclaw --version OpenClaw 2026.11.3 (2b7dc7f) $ openclaw memory index --agent main Memory index updated (main): 10 files indexed. $ openclaw memory search "when does the nightly backup run" --agent main 0.449 memory/backups.md:1-5 0.249 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-28.md:1-5 0.243 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-27.md:1-5 0.238 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-26.md:1-5 0.232 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-25.md:1-5 0.227 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-24.md:1-5 $ openclaw config set memory.search.excludePaths '["memory/dreaming/"]' --strict-json Updated memory.search.excludePaths. Restart the gateway to apply. $ openclaw config get memory.search.excludePaths [ "memory/dreaming/" ] $ openclaw memory status --agent main Indexed: 10/3 files · 10 chunks Dirty: yes Index identity: index scope changed (owner: configuration, code: scope) Vector search: paused until memory is rebuilt $ openclaw memory index --agent main Memory index updated (main): 3 files indexed. $ openclaw memory status --agent main Indexed: 3/3 files · 3 chunks Dirty: no $ openclaw memory search "when does the nightly backup run" --agent main 0.422 memory/backups.md:1-5 The nightly backup runs at 02:30 and copies the photo archive to the NAS. ```
**Gateway watcher:** a throwaway loopback Gateway with `excludePaths` set. One agent turn opens the Gateway's default memory manager and its watcher: a local chat-completions stub calls `memory_search` once, through `dispatch_action`, because current main keeps `memory_search` behind Tool Search for this model. Then, with no further CLI calls, a new dreaming report is written and the curated note edited: the watcher refreshes the note within about 2 s and never indexes the report.
Terminal output ```text $ openclaw memory index --agent main Memory index updated (main): 3 files indexed. $ openclaw gateway run --bind loopback ... # throwaway Gateway [gateway] ready $ openclaw agent --agent main --message "When does the nightly backup run?" # stub model calls memory_search once via dispatch_action Done. tool call: dispatch_action {"id":"memory_search","args":{"query":"nightly backup"}} # memory_search result paths (from the stub log): memory/backups.md # indexed memory/ rows before edits: {"path":"memory/backups.md","text":"# Backups The nightly backup runs at 02:30 and copies the p"} {"path":"memory/garden.md","text":"# Garden Water the tomatoes every second evening in summer."} # wrote memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-29.md and edited memory/backups.md (02:30 -> 04:45); no CLI calls from here # after the Gateway watcher sync (~2s), plus 5s more: {"path":"memory/backups.md","text":"# Backups The nightly backup runs at 04:45 and copies the p"} {"path":"memory/garden.md","text":"# Garden Water the tomatoes every second evening in summer."} # dreaming rows: {"dreamingRows":0} ```
**Regressions fail without the fix:** - `file-watcher.lifecycle.test.ts` "rebaselines shared exclusions when a differently scoped agent joins and leaves" fails with `excludePaths` removed from `selectionKeys` ("expected setScopes to be called once, but got 0 times"). - `manager-workspace-files.test.ts` "drops generated Dream reports once excluded and keeps curated edits fresh" fails when the config resolver drops `excludePaths` (the report is still found). - `internal.test.ts` "keeps generated dreaming reports out of default and overlapping extra paths" also lists files with `memory/dreaming/**/!(*.keep).md`. With the old `path.posix.matchesGlob` matcher, `listMemoryFiles` under Bun still returns the report: on stock Bun 1.3.14 it lists `memory/current.md, memory/dreaming/light/pinned.keep.md, memory/dreaming/light/report.md`, and with `1463f6e` only `memory/current.md, memory/dreaming/light/pinned.keep.md`. On Node both matchers agree, so the Node run passes either way; the CI shard that runs this test (`checks-node-changed-compact-large-6`) sets up the pinned Bun 1.4.4 test runtime. **Changed test files** (`pnpm test --maxWorkers=1` on `685db0c`, same test code as `8eb4b7b`): | File | Result | Wall | Vitest duration | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `file-watcher.lifecycle.test.ts` | 29 passed | 48s | 41.65s | | `manager-reindex-state.test.ts` | 49 passed | 40s | 36.19s | | `manager-workspace-files.test.ts` | 11 passed | 71s | 64.91s | | `watch-policy.test.ts` | 6 passed | 47s | 41.51s | | `internal.test.ts` | 43 passed | 4s | 749ms | | `memory-search.test.ts` | 39 passed | 46s | 42.06s | Vitest time is mostly cold transform; the new manager case takes about 4 s and the other new cases take 1-24 ms. **Checks:** `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base upstream/main` on `83eb31b` (main `200afde`, same code) passes typecheck (core, core tests, extensions, extension tests), lint, format, config docs baseline, Plugin SDK package exports, plugin boundaries and the other changed-file guards. Three lanes fail outside this PR: wrapper shadowing (`buildSkillWorkshopPromptSection`) and the public Plugin SDK surface budget (`agent-harness-runtime`) fail identically on clean main `200afde`, and the dead-export scan lists only auto-reply, gateway and UI exports this PR does not touch. The `pnpm check:docs` content checks pass. Test lines grow by a net +154, covered by `config/test-lines-allocations/memory-search-exclude-paths-188294.txt`: default scope-hash compatibility, the shared-watcher rebaseline, discovery and portable (Node/Bun) glob matching, and the exclusion rebuild. **PR CI:** CI has not run on the current head `fa31efc` (merging main `a2f7aa9`) or on the seven heads before it: GitHub holds this fork PR's workflows until a maintainer clicks "Approve and run" (`action_required`), so `openclaw/ci-gate` shows failure until CI completes. The last completed run, on `fc2ef72`, passed 72 checks; its three failing memory-core tests are in files this PR does not touch, failed the same way on main without this PR, and main fixed them in #197543. Earlier red runs also came from main and were fixed there. Merges of main conflicted only on the generated config baseline, which was regenerated each time. The full CI history is in this description's edit history. **Local review:** autoreview, Codex `gpt-6.1-sol`, branch mode against `upstream/main`, P0–P2: scoped-clean, "patch is correct" (0.87). It ran on `685db0c`, before the rebases onto `200afde` and `f980e01`, which changed only the base and the generated baseline files. For `2b7dc7f`: autoreview with the Claude engine, local mode, P0–P2: scoped-clean, "patch is correct" (0.8). On `2b7dc7f`, `memory-search.test.ts` (39/39; the updated case fails on `e768746`), `schema.help.quality.test.ts`, `internal.test.ts` and `workspace-memory-client.test.ts` pass, as do `tsgo:core`, oxlint, oxfmt, `check:docs`, `config:docs:check` and the test-line ratchet. On `fa31efc` (main `a2f7aa9`), `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:extensions`, `config:docs:check`, `prompt:snapshots:check`, oxfmt on this PR's files, `check:docs` and the test-line ratchet (net +154, covered by the allocation) pass, and so do the touched tests plus neighboring memory tests (18 files). Locally, one `cli.test.ts` test from main's #197543 (`fails index --force after full verification records orphaned provenance`) fails; it fails the same way on main `a2f7aa9` without this PR. Not covered: Windows paths (the matcher normalizes `path.sep`) and a live remote node workspace (the harness test checks that list and watch requests carry `excludePaths`).

prs.title: fix(cron): prevent late background turns after job timeouts
prs.body:
Related: #176511, #143355, #137274.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes additional model turns and repeated work when a scheduled job times out after launching background commands.

## User Impact

Timeout, cancellation, and restart revoke the originating occurrence's background work and completion events. Retained process output remains inspectable. **Already accepted exec follow-ups survive normal successful teardown**, preserving the contract from #176511 and ordinary interactive completion behavior.

**Maintainer decision still required:** scheduler and native-command deadlines do not automatically replay a job after execution starts or a dispatched command's outcome remains unknown. Recurring jobs keep normal cadence; one-shots follow existing terminal-failure handling. Known pre-execution failures and provider transient retry classification retain recovery. This intentionally differs from the policy discussed in #137274; this PR remains a draft.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing active-job marker to capture one occurrence's cancellation lifetime beyond its first model invocation. Successful retirement transfers accepted follow-ups to the session controller without cancelling them; timeout/cancellation/generation changes still revoke the captured lifetime. A superseded occurrence cannot regain authority when its older cleanup runs.

Originating-run liveness is still checked until event acceptance. Current destination and policy checks remain active afterward. Existing occurrence admission and completion source-run attribution are preserved. #143355 covers complementary child timeout propagation.

No public API, configuration, dependency, or schema changes. Upstream integration removes its retired conversation-origin field while preserving both notification-lifetime cleanup fields. The retry documentation now distinguishes scheduled execution deadlines from provider failures and forced manual runs.

## Evidence

- Review regression reproduced red against the original PR source: a real exec completion was accepted while its source turn was held, then successful marker teardown cancelled it before model execution.
- **95 affected tests pass on the integrated head** across active-job authority, real process/session-controller follow-ups, producer cancellation/recovery, and native child effects. Cases cover normal success, timeout, operator cancellation, restart, retirement before/during acceptance, and supersession. The supersession case was also reproduced red before its repair.
- Current-head core types, targeted lint, oxfmt/Bun parity, documentation MDX sanity, and whitespace checks pass. Independent review found no remaining P0-P2 issues in the upstream integration and retry documentation. The maintained runtime build passes. Previous-head focused test type graphs, line-cap guard, and full build also passed; broad GitHub CI subsequently passed on that head.
- **Shipped CLI trace:** a separate Gateway process ran synthetic cron jobs through public CLI/RPC and a loopback Responses provider that actually requested background exec. No production profile or paid provider was used.

```text
timeout: provider requests=2; child stopped=true;
         late child effects=0; late inference=0; cron outcome=error
success: provider requests=3 (2 source + 1 exec completion);
         child effects=1; queued follow-ups=1; cron outcome=ok
```

The success trace holds the source response until the child completes and notification admission has time to finish; the third provider request must contain both the exec-completion notice and the child's output. The real queue regression separately proves explicit successful marker teardown before follow-up execution. An initial delivery:none fixture intentionally disabled wakes; a second fixture released the source before asynchronous acceptance. Those failed fixtures were diagnosed and retained, not reported as passes.

**Fresh-install and latest-stable state compatibility:** Separate foreground Gateways exercised both a fresh candidate and published `2026.10.6` followed by the candidate's documented manual runtime replacement (`doctor --fix`, then restart with the same isolated state). Existing one-shot/recurring settings and full successful run history were preserved. Actual scheduled model-started timeouts disabled the one-shot and advanced the daily recurring job to its normal future occurrence. Restart preserved those terminal histories, enablement, and exact next scheduled time, with zero new provider requests. Each lane made four job requests (two successes, two timeouts) and one separately identified, expected main-session auto-disable notice. This is runtime/state compatibility proof, not a published updater-driver activation test or qualification of every historical schema.

The private compatibility fixture first used forced manual runs, which intentionally preserve future slots; it was corrected to use real scheduled firing. An extra request was traced to the exact synthetic auto-disable notice, not counted as a job replay. The final proof rejects unexpected requests and checks persisted next-run times so a delayed replay cannot pass unnoticed.

**CI:** The complete GitHub CI run passed on `a0b68f6` ([run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39814796168)); the review of that head reported no code findings. That is prior-head evidence. This integrated head must receive its own CI/review results; draft status is preserved, so some lanes may skip. A separate aggregate status was pending when inspected. Earlier inherited local planner/root-budget and UI-suppression failures remain recorded as historical gaps, not current-head passing claims; no baselines were weakened.

<details>
<summary>Local test cost</summary>

The current six-file affected run passed 95 tests in 100.76 seconds with one worker across three shards, including compiled-subprocess preparation, real child processes, controller custody, and scheduler/native-command deadline handling. The earlier four-file repair run passed 67 tests in 63.60 seconds.

</details>

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way. **Blast radius:** cron-owned child processes, completion admission, and deadline retry scheduling. Keep draft until maintainers accept the retry policy and required review/CI gates are satisfied.

prs.title: fix: keep the community invite out of the first Control UI visit
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Community card can appear in the sidebar when someone opens their first chat directly. It also appears if someone reloads the first chat after completing setup.

## User Impact

The card stays hidden during setup and throughout the first Control UI visit, including when navigating, reloading, or reconnecting to the Gateway. A new browsing session in the same browser can show the card on a later visit. The card keeps its position, design, and existing dismissal behavior. The Discord link under **Profile → Help** remains available.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Control UI uses browser preferences to recognize a returning visit and the current tab or web view's session storage to keep a protected visit quiet across reloads. If storage is unavailable, the card stays hidden. This changes only when the card can appear; setup, Home, and the Gateway keep their existing behavior.

## Evidence

- Bundled Control UI with Chromium and a mocked Gateway: 6 tests passed. The regressions reproduced on `34ce936db81e`: direct chat showed the card on first entry, and web and simulated macOS Web Chrome showed it on reload after setup. With the fix, the card stayed hidden in those cases and after reconnect. Opening a new tab allowed the card, and dismissal persisted after reload.
- 97 focused UI tests passed across navigation, sidebar interactions, and card dismissal. Control UI typecheck, lifecycle checks, changed-file lint, and formatting passed. No native macOS app launch or live Gateway run is claimed for this revision.
- Maintainer verification on the PR integrated into current main: 7 browser tests (one capture scenario and 6 product tests), 95 focused tests, UI types, formatting, typed lint and controller guard. Fresh review found no actionable findings.

### First chat after reload

Same production UI, 1280×760, with a mocked Gateway and fictional conversation.

prs.title: fix: keep failed scheduled commands from posting NO_REPLY
prs.body:
Closes #203596

## What Problem This Solves

A failed scheduled command that prints only the internal silence marker `NO_REPLY` currently sends that literal text to the configured chat.

## User Impact

The failed run stays visible in automation history with its exit code. The configured failure alert still reaches the channel. Completion delivery respects the command's silence marker.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing terminal-reply preparation to recognize silence even if the command fails. Preserve existing summaries for ordinary failed output.

## Evidence

On base `8ab246473799`, a real subprocess writing `NO_REPLY` and exiting 1 left the literal marker in the run summary and failed the new regression.

I used the built Gateway at `ddf289db8386`, an isolated state directory, and the unmodified IRC channel plugin connected to a loopback IRC fixture. Every case went through the cron RPC and real subprocess execution.

| Command output and exit | Saved history | Traffic received by the IRC fixture |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `NO_REPLY`, exit 1, failure alert configured | `error`, `command exited with code 1`, completion delivery `not-delivered` with reason `silent` | One failure alert with exit code 1 |
| `NO_REPLY`, exit 0 | `ok`, `not-delivered` | No message |
| Ordinary output, exit 3 | `error`, `delivered` | The ordinary output |

The focused cron and Gateway tests passed (130 passed, one skipped), including checks for both silent exit statuses. Targeted lint, formatting, core typecheck, and `pnpm build:runtime` passed. The build reported advisory UI CSS and request-budget warnings.

prs.title: fix(bedrock): scheduled automations are refused on AWS SDK credential-chain routes
prs.body:
# fix(bedrock): give the AWS SDK route an account scheduled runs can record

Fixes #192524.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: every scheduled automation on an Amazon Bedrock route that authenticates
through the AWS SDK default credential chain fails with "Automation has no
recorded inference account", and its advice cannot be followed.

`models.providers.amazon-bedrock.auth: "aws-sdk"` resolves credentials from the
host chain (instance role, container role, SSO profile, env), so nothing owned
the route in the auth store and the plugin registered no auth method — there was
no account id to name in `openclaw automations edit <jobId> --model
<model>@<profileId>`. Creating a new automation on that route was refused for the
same reason ("Automation requires a stored inference account or a key in the
environment or provider config"). The route worked interactively and was
unusable on a schedule, with no way out from the CLI.

## User Impact

User impact: Bedrock hosts that authenticate through the AWS SDK chain can run
scheduled automations again, and that authority is revocable like any other
account.

- Setup gains an "AWS credentials (SDK default chain)" choice for Amazon Bedrock.
  It stores no AWS credentials: it creates the account `amazon-bedrock:aws-sdk`
  holding OpenClaw's non-secret `aws-sdk-credentials` marker, sets the provider's
  `auth: "aws-sdk"`, and records the region when one is given. The choice is
  declared on the runtime provider registration too, which is where
  non-interactive setup reads a plugin's auth methods from
  (`openclaw onboard --auth-choice amazon-bedrock-aws-sdk`).
- `openclaw doctor --fix` creates that account on hosts already configured with
  `auth: "aws-sdk"` and adopts it for automations that have no recorded account,
  so existing installs are repaired without re-running setup.
- `openclaw models auth logout amazon-bedrock:aws-sdk` revokes it: bound
  automations are refused ("was removed or signed out"), and recreating the same
  id does not revive them ("was replaced") until the account is selected again
  explicitly — Doctor does not silently re-adopt a retired binding. Removing the
  record while a scheduled run is preparing its provider auth is refused too
  ("was removed or replaced during the run"), before the credential is installed
  for the request.
- Required action for existing installs: run `openclaw doctor --fix` once.
- If `amazon-bedrock:aws-sdk` is already taken by a different account, nothing is
  overwritten; Doctor reports the conflict and asks you to sign that account out
  or rename it.

## Why This Change Was Made

An OpenClaw authorization is the lifetime of an OpenClaw-owned auth-store
record, not a provider-side identity: `auth-profiles/authorization.ts` derives
`authorizationId` from opaque store incarnations. So the fix gives the AWS SDK
route a real store record instead of inventing a second notion of identity.

- The record is a credential-shaped marker (`api_key` /
  `key: "aws-sdk-credentials"`, already in the core non-secret marker list, same
  pattern as `gcp-vertex-credentials` and the Entra dynamic marker). Credentials
  are still resolved per request from the AWS chain; the record only says which
  account OpenClaw owns.
- Because the binding names a normal record, revocation, recreation and
  re-selection all go through the existing scheduler contract — `assertCurrent`
  and revalidate already fail closed on a removed or re-created incarnation.
  Nothing hashes config, and no new authorization path was added.
- `captureCronInferenceBinding` and Doctor's cron migration previously rejected
  the direct `aws-sdk` route as an ambient credential; they now record that
  stored account when the planner takes it. The runtime guard in
  `embedded-agent-runner/run/auth-plan.ts` is untouched: an AWS SDK route with no
  stored account still produces no binding and its scheduled runs are still
  refused.
- The binding deliberately does not pin an AWS principal. OpenClaw never
  observes one for this route (no `sts:GetCallerIdentity` is called, see #141983),
  and pinning one would make the scheduler depend on IAM state it cannot
  re-check.
- Two owner-side gaps on the way there are fixed with the existing checks. The
  post-preparation re-check in `embedded-agent-runner/run/auth-controller.ts`
  only ran for a captured OAuth authorization, so an api-key route could install
  a credential whose record had just been removed (the run's own pre-dispatch
  guard still refused the request); a scheduled run's binding owns every auth
  mode, so it is re-observed there too, and Cron names the automation and its
  account in the refusal. Doctor's account creation derived the store owner from
  the default agent, which refuses an explicit multi-agent fleet; the record is a
  shared credential, so it resolves the shared store's own owner.

Docs: `docs/providers/bedrock.md` gains a scheduled-run section; the
credential-semantics and gateway-auth pages describe the marker account and how
signing it out revokes bindings.

## Evidence

Unit and integration coverage: `extensions/amazon-bedrock/aws-sdk-auth.test.ts`,
`extensions/amazon-bedrock/lazy-import.test.ts`,
`src/agents/auth-profiles/order.test.ts`,
`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/auth-controller.binding.test.ts`,
`src/cron/inference-binding.aws-sdk-profile.test.ts`,
`src/cron/inference-binding-executor.test.ts`,
`src/cron/isolated-agent.auth-continuity.integration.test.ts`,
`src/commands/doctor/cron/inference-binding-migration.test.ts`,
`src/commands/doctor/shared/aws-sdk-auth-account.test.ts` — all green, plus
`pnpm tsgo:core`, `tsgo:extensions`, `tsgo:extensions:test`, `tsgo:test:src`,
oxlint and format on the touched paths.

Live validation on an EC2 host with only an instance role: isolated gateway in a
container, fresh state dir, port 28789, no messaging channels, live Bedrock
`global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5-5` in `us-west-2`. No IAM or STS call is made
by the change or by its validation.

| # | Scenario | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Legacy automation with no recorded account (refused on unpatched base: "Automation has no recorded inference account"), then `doctor --fix` on the patched tree | Account created ("Created auth profile amazon-bedrock:aws-sdk … it stores no AWS credentials"), job adopted ("retain amazon-bedrock:aws-sdk"), run `"status": "ok"`, reply `READY` |
| 2 | `models auth logout amazon-bedrock:aws-sdk --yes`, then trigger the bound job | Refused: "Automation inference account amazon-bedrock:aws-sdk … was removed or signed out. Explicitly select an authorized account again." |
| 3 | Recreate the same id, trigger again; `doctor --fix`; then `automations edit --model …@amazon-bedrock:aws-sdk` | Refused: "… was replaced"; `doctor --fix` leaves the retired binding untouched; after explicit re-selection the binding carries a new `authorizationId` and the run is `"status": "ok"`, `READY` |
| 4 | Restart the gateway in a new container, record and binding untouched | Credentials re-resolved from the chain, run `"status": "ok"`, `READY` |
| 5 | Interactive `openclaw agent -m …` on the same route | Replied `INTERACTIVE` |
| 6 | `amazon-bedrock:aws-sdk` pre-occupied by a different credential, then `doctor --fix` | Conflict reported, the occupying record left byte-identical, no account created |
| 7 | Upgrade from npm `openclaw@2026.10.10` on the same state dir: explicit ownership, two agents + systemAgent, one Bedrock automation per agent plus one on a non-Bedrock apiKey provider, then `doctor --fix` on this build | Both Bedrock jobs adopted with per-agent authorization ids, both live runs `"status": "ok"` / `READY`; config keeps every authored setting (Doctor adds only its own defaults and run metadata) |
| 8 | Fresh install: `openclaw onboard --non-interactive --auth-choice amazon-bedrock-aws-sdk` on clean state | Account saved (marker only), `auth: "aws-sdk"` written, a new automation runs `"status": "ok"` / `READY` |
| 9 | 24 raced attempts removing the record through `models.authLogout` at measured offsets into a scheduled run, Bedrock requests counted outside the product by a CONNECT-tunnel proxy | Every removal that landed before the run's last pre-dispatch check prevented the request: 13 attempts with zero Bedrock requests and a refusal naming the retired account |

The stored record is the marker only, read straight out of the state database:

```
amazon-bedrock:aws-sdk -> {"type":"api_key","provider":"amazon-bedrock","key":"aws-sdk-credentials"}
```

and the binding scenario 1 produces is

```
{"version":1,"provider":"amazon-bedrock","profileId":"amazon-bedrock:aws-sdk",
 "authorizationId":"ca9ddee0…","authRequirement":"api-key","source":"auto"}
```

(`authRequirement` is `"api-key"` because `CronInferenceBinding` admits only
`api-key | subscription`; it records the requirement class, not a stored key.)
Signing out rotates the account's authorization lifetime, which is what retires
the binding. A scan for `AKIA|ASIA|SecretAccessKey|SessionToken` across every
state directory and evidence log matches nothing, and no IAM or STS call is made
anywhere in the change or its validation.

## Known limits

- Per-account `awsProfile` / `roleArn` are out of scope; the region is carried by
  the plugin's `discovery.region`, otherwise the chain's own environment applies.
- One account per provider: if several marker records exist for one provider the
  lexicographically first is used. Choosing among multiple AWS accounts is
  #192009.
- A retired binding needs an explicit `automations edit --model <model>@<profileId>`
  (or a fresh unbound job); Doctor only adopts accounts for automations that have
  no binding at all.
- Revocation is observed at the owner checks a run makes, so a removal that
  commits in the last few tens of milliseconds before the request is written to
  the socket does not cancel that one in-flight request (measured live: 8 of 24
  raced attempts). Signing out stops every later run, and a whole-provider sign
  out aborts runs that have not dispatched yet.

prs.title: refactor(gateway): check HTTP request authority once at admission
prs.body:
## What problem this solves

HTTP routes checked the caller's authority when the request was admitted, then checked it again during the request. `captureHttpRequestAuthority` took a snapshot of auth policy, role policy, role revision, profile alias revision and shared auth generation. `bindHttpResponseAuthority` then made `assertCurrent()`, `revalidate()` and `hasCurrentClientAuthority()` compare against that snapshot, and against operator access and profile authority, at many points inside each route. Device-token routes re-verified the token in `revalidate()`. Plugin-cookie routes re-read the cookie grants and role policy. Because of this, an admitted request could stop halfway with 401/403 after an unrelated settings save or role edit.

The one-admission rule is: check authority once, when the request starts. A started request finishes. Revocation, removal and reload apply to the next request.

## What changed

- `src/gateway/http-request-authority.ts`: deleted `captureHttpRequestAuthority`, `bindHttpResponseAuthority`, `assertGatewayHttpRequestCurrent`, `GatewayHttpRequestAuthorityError` and the `GatewayHttp{Request,Response}Authority` types. `runGatewayHttpRequest` (request abort scope) and `finishGatewayHttpAuthorityError` stay.
- `http-auth-utils.ts`: HTTP auth results no longer carry `assertCurrent` or `revalidate`. The admission-time early refusals that compared against the snapshot are gone. The device-token `revalidate` overrides are gone.
- `http-auth-plugin-cookie.ts`: deleted `bindControlUiPluginCookieRequestAuthority` (the cookie/role re-check). `control-ui-plugin-assets.ts` authorizes the cookie one time.
- Route handlers no longer call those methods: Control UI bootstrap/avatar/session entry, channel/plugin/provider/workspace/project icons, managed media, user profile avatars and backgrounds, session kill, models, embeddings, OpenAI and OpenResponses, tools invoke, and plugin routes. `rememberResponseSession` lost its authority `assertCurrent` parameter (its only production caller passed the request guard).
- Removed both names from `LIFETIME_CHECK_CALLS`.

Kept:
- Request abort (Stop / client disconnect). The `runGatewayHttpRequest` scope signal and `finishGatewayHttpAuthorityError` still end the response. Response-ended checks (`res.writableEnded || res.destroyed`) stay where routes had them.
- Data fences: session lifecycle revision and avatar reference (channel avatars), session row generation (workspace icons), image replacement (`prepared.isCurrent()`), assistant media policy, managed-media grant and ingress-session reads, and session actor readability for session kill.

Production code: 29 files, +65 / −524.

## Decisions (recorded per the program rules)

- **Cut less at the WebSocket seam.** `AuthorizedGatewayHttpRequest.hasCurrentClientAuthority` stays as an optional field (profile + operator access only). The OpenAI, OpenResponses and tools-invoke routes pass it to the agent-turn and plugin-runtime scopes. There, *whether the field is present* changes behavior: `operator-run-authority` `isHttpOwner` needs `=== true`, and in-process approval dispatch checks presence. Removing it here would change owner attribution for OpenClaw ID HTTP callers. The session-mutation-guard and run-authority PRs remove it together with those readers. Plugin route scopes keep presence `requestAuth || operatorAccessAuthority || ingress`, so for gateway-auth routes the field is present whether the request came in by bearer or by cookie, as before.
- Not in scope, left for later PRs: `sessions-history-http` re-authenticates on each SSE publish through `checkGatewayHttpRequestAuth`. `tools-invoke-http` still adds `operatorAccessAuthority.signal` to the request signal. `operator-access-policy` aborts that signal on revocation (PR 7/8).

## Tests deleted (they assert a refusal after admission)

- `http-request-authority.test.ts` (role-policy fence on the snapshot)
- `http-auth-utils.openclaw-id-tunnel.test.ts` (device removed or role changed after admission → refusal)
- `channel-avatar-http`: "rejects revoked authority while channel avatar bytes are loading"
- `managed-image-attachments.authority`: revoked worker ownership read and revoked media authority after preparation
- `plugin-icon-http`: revoked authority during normalization or favicon fetch
- `workspace-icon-http`: changed authority during icon preparation (the workspace replacement case, a data fence, stays)
- `http-endpoint-helpers`: "does not admit a parsed body after its authority was revoked while reading"
- `http-utils.authorize-request`: trusted-proxy override revalidation
- `tools-invoke-http.abort`: "rejects a tool when policy authority changes during its awaited hook"
- `control-ui-assistant-media-metadata`: reader authority recheck variants
- `server-http.authority-outcomes`: nine client-expired / role / operator-revoked / unavailable variants. The disconnect and unexpected-error variants stay, and still prove Stop through the real HTTP router
- `openresponses-session-store` and the OpenResponses continuation support: revoked caller before commit / during the continuation lookup
- `control-ui-assistant-media-policy`, `control-ui-plugin-assets`, `control-ui-session-entry(.real-auth.e2e)`, `control-ui.response-authority`, `http-auth-utils.paired-device`, `http-session-control.incognito` (revoked=true rows), `server.plugin-http-role-scopes`, `server/plugins-http` (re-check before the next matched route), `session-kill-http` (policy-revocation and credential-rotation rows), `sessions-history-http.revocation` (ingress-policy row), `user-background-http.authority`, `user-profiles-http.auth` (credential rotation and device revocation during preparation), `team-reports-http.gateway` (expiry, generation and role change before delivery). Data-fence, admission-time and abort cases in those files stay.

## Evidence

- **Plugin HTTP route, through the real HTTP router (new test):** `server.plugin-http-auth.test.ts` › "finishes an admitted gateway-auth plugin request after its credential rotates". The plugin handler is blocked, the Gateway token rotates, then the handler calls the scope's `revalidate()`. The admitted request gets 200, and the next request with the old token gets 401. The same test copied onto base `3cd3a3118668` fails with `expected 401 to be 200`: base `revalidate()` re-checks the shared generation and refuses the admitted request. Stop through the real router: `server-http.authority-outcomes` › "cancels disconnected plugin reads without logging a handler failure". The one-admission E2E journey does not reach plugin HTTP routes, so this integration test is the plugin-route proof.
- **Pre-push tests (vitest-source):** one `ocx test` call over the 291 importer test files, with `OPENCLAW_NODE_TEST_PLAN_CONTINUE_ON_FAILURE=1`. It hit the 1 h tool deadline, so the 17 files it did not reach and every failed file ran again in two more calls. Everything passes except files that also fail on base `3cd3a3118668`: `cron/service.pr-automation` (13), `server-methods/question.own-run` (4), `server.config-security-policy` (3-4, timeouts), `server.sessions.create.projects` (1), and `operator-admission.table` › `token > principal > before-start`.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:test` are clean. oxfmt and oxlint are clean on the changed files. The lifetime-check ratchet passes.
- E2E (`one-admission-e2e/run.sh`): Q, R and S pass on `1d9bc6d06222` and on the final head `33a643a42c77`. The live Gateway pid did not change.

prs.title: feat(update): Git installs update through prepared releases and a resident launcher
prs.body:
## Problem

A Git install updates in place under the running Gateway, through a managed-service handoff helper. When the new build does not start, recovery depends on that helper and on the old updater that is already installed, so a failed update can leave the Gateway down or stuck in `update-recovery-pending`.

## Change

Git installs now update through prepared releases and a resident launcher:

1. `update.run`, `openclaw update` and automatic updates admit the run, resolve the target and run preflight (Node engine, required tools, disk space, container installs refused before any change).
2. The next release is built beside the running one (`git worktree add --detach`, then the target's install and build). The running checkout is not changed.
3. `openclaw update check-release` runs the new code offline against the current config and state and reports broken plugin or config surfaces. It does not migrate state.
4. `openclaw update plugins` runs from the published release: the existing plugin maintenance owner (`updatePluginsAfterCoreUpdate`), with the new core's code and version. A plugin problem, or a target too old to have the command, is recorded as a `plugins` step with a next action and never fails the update. An already-current install still runs it from the serving code and restarts a running Gateway when plugins changed (`docs/install/updating.md`).
5. The release is published as a pending trial, and the Gateway restarts with a process-replacing reason.
6. The launcher switches the release link at the next child start, counts attempts, commits the trial when the new Gateway is ready, and otherwise rolls back and starts the previous release.
7. The Gateway that starts after the switch (new on success, old after a rollback) finishes the run and sends the outcome to a requester that received the start notice.

Routing:
- `update.run` reads the install kind from the existing install-status owner (`resolveStartupInstallStatus`). `update-run.ts` wraps `update.run`; `update.ts` is unchanged and still serves package installs.
- `openclaw update` branches after `prepareUpdateCommand`, so every existing refusal (external supervisor, host-owned, immutable, system package owner, interrupted update) applies first. A requested non-dev channel on a Git checkout still switches it to a package through the existing flow, and `--dry-run` keeps the existing preview.
- Package installs move to this path in the next change, which also deletes the old Git machinery that this PR leaves unused.

Converting an existing install:
- The old entry points of a converted install (`openclaw.mjs`, `dist/index.js`) forward to the release launcher through a marker beside the tree. Existing service definitions and PATH shims keep working without a rewrite.
- A first update driven by an older installed updater still migrates state as it does today. Released updaters require migrated state: 23 stable and 6 extended-stable tags contain that check.

Fixes found by the real-install runs below, each a separate commit:
- `openclaw update --sha` now sends the tracked upstream that the protocol requires.
- The new path restarts with `update.run` / `update.auto`, so the process is replaced instead of restarted in place.
- A Gateway started by the launcher leaves its update successor to the launcher instead of spawning one outside it.
- Preflight skips dangling symlinks in agent homes, such as Codex `arg0` shims, when it sizes state databases.
- `check-release` writes its JSON result to stdout.
- Plain `openclaw update` keeps following the run while the restarting Gateway refuses connections with a retryable HTTP 503. Before, it exited 1 although the update succeeded.

Accepted edge cases:
- After `openclaw update` runs in a Git checkout, `openclaw.mjs` and `dist/index.js` in that checkout run the current release. A developer who edits the source of a checkout they also update from runs the release, not their edits.
- A stop request handled inside a launcher child exits with code 0, and the launcher starts the child again. A stop through the service manager stops the launcher and its child.
- On a Gateway with no service manager, the first update from a released version does not restart it. The released updater does this, and says so.
- Package updates now read the install status twice per request: once to route, once in the old handler.
- After a rollback, the previous release runs with plugins maintained for the new core. A plugin that cannot load stays off for that boot, as the plugin docs describe.
- `openclaw update --accept-capabilities` reaches plugin maintenance when the CLI prepares the release itself (`--no-restart`, or no Gateway answering). Through a running Gateway, `update.run` has no field for it, so a plugin that needs consent is reported with its `openclaw plugins update` next action. Carrying the flag through `update.run` is a protocol change and follows separately.
- `openclaw update` run from a different checkout than the one the configured local Gateway serves updates the Gateway's installation, not the invoking checkout. Binding the request to the checkout needs a protocol field and follows with `--accept-capabilities`.

## Evidence

Real install on macOS (Apple silicon). Isolated HOME, state, config and port, a foreground Gateway, no launchd service. Every candidate was built from `git archive` of its commit; the final candidate is this branch's head before review.

| Step | Run status | Trial | Served after | Health |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2026.11.6 → A (released updater) | succeeded | (old path) | A, after a recorded manual start | 200 / 200 |
| A → B′ (B′ fails at startup) | failed, `new build failed to start` | rolled-back, 2 attempts | A, as the launcher's child | 200 / 200 |
| A → B | succeeded | committed, 1 attempt | B, as the launcher's child | 200 / 200 |
| B → C | succeeded | committed, 1 attempt | C, as the launcher's child | 200 / 200 |

- The same launcher process stayed the parent through every replacement. The previous release was kept after each commit.
- Phase times (seconds), from the persisted run steps:

| Step | Staging (build) | Validating | Restarting | Total |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| A → B′ (rollback) | 192.5 | 0.8 | 29.2 | 222.7 |
| A → B | 195.7 | 1.1 | 32.9 | 229.8 |
| B → C | 201.6 | 0.9 | 36.9 | 239.5 |

- `check-release` on a copy of a real state directory (Linux, no network): exit 0 in 3.0 s, 187 surfaces checked, shared state schema 40 → 40, agent databases 43 → 43.

Plugin maintenance, real install on macOS (isolated, foreground Gateway, a real third-party npm plugin `@martian-engineering/lossless-claw` served through a scratch registry proxy that advertises 1.1.1, then the real latest 1.2.0):

| Case | Run | `plugins` step | Plugin | Gateway |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Core update through the new path | succeeded, trial committed (1 attempt) | completed | 1.1.1 → 1.2.0 | one restart into the new release |
| Already current, plugin outdated | skipped / already-current | completed | 1.1.1 → 1.2.0 | restarted |
| Already current, nothing to change | skipped / already-current | completed | unchanged | no restart |
| Already current, registry returns HTTP 503 | skipped / already-current | completed, detail names the plugin and its `openclaw plugins update` retry | kept 1.1.1 | no restart; CLI prints "Plugin notes: …" |
| Already current, `--no-restart` | skipped / already-current | completed | 1.1.1 → 1.2.0 | same process, no restart |

- An earlier head counted a `warning` result as a failed step with no message; the run above found it and the fix is in this PR.
- A run with `--timeout 1` showed the CLI calling a still-running update "Update failed: unknown reason". The fix ("The update did not finish in time. Run `openclaw update status` to see it.") is covered by `src/update/cli.test.ts`; it was not rerun on the real install.

Tests:
- New: `src/update/*.test.ts` (target, preflight, Git and package preparation, check-release, store, launcher, trial settlement and outcome notice, CLI request shape), plus a launcher-child case in `process-respawn.test.ts`.
- The gateway `update*` suites run against package installs. Tests that pinned the old Git handoff, Git preflight delegation, explicit Git targets and foreground parking are deleted. Tests of behavior that package installs still use (notice policy, owner checks, campaign adoption, platform admission) now run on a managed package install.

## Review

- `--no-restart` on a Git install now prepares the release in the CLI process instead of asking the Gateway, so the Gateway does not restart. The release starts at the Gateway's next start, and the CLI says so and exits 0, instead of reporting "Updated".
- The first conversion creates the `prefix/openclaw` link to the running tree before it writes the forwarding marker. Forwarded commands work between publish and the switch.
- The run row is written through the existing asynchronous update-run owner (`update-run-write.async.ts`). The synchronous second writer is deleted, so there is no SQLite work on the Gateway thread.
- Rejected: settling trials of the format-1 Git-release launcher (#199706). No released build contains it (not 2026.11.6 `latest`, 2026.10.33 `extended-stable` or 2026.11.10-beta.1 `beta`), and main-only code is not a shipped contract. Only a Git checkout that tracked `main` between 2026-11-17 and this change can have such a trial.
- The in-process path (`--no-restart`, or no Gateway answering) uses the requested channel, else the saved `update.channel` (`readUpdateChannelConfig`), else `dev`, as the existing CLI does. The Gateway path passes the checkout's tag and branch facts, as the existing handler does, so a configless checkout on a stable tag stays on stable.
- After publishing a Git release, `git worktree repair` records it at its final path, so `git worktree list` and a later `git worktree prune` see the serving release where it is.
- `prefix/openclaw` is repointed to the running tree when it does not already resolve there, so a link left from an earlier package install cannot become the rollback target.
- Rejected for this PR: carrying the package layout's `lib/node_modules/openclaw` link. That layout belongs to package-release installs, which this PR does not route; the next change moves package installs and owns it.
- A new build that exits 78 (it refuses the configuration) during a trial now rolls back like any other failed candidate. Outside a trial, 78 stays terminal.
- Rejected again, same reason as the format-1 trial: making `git-install/lib/node_modules/openclaw` follow `prefix/openclaw`. Only the main-only Git-release conversion (#199706) creates that link, and no release contains it.
- A Gateway with `OPENCLAW_NO_RESPAWN` set now refuses `update.run` with `restart-unavailable` before anything is recorded or prepared, as the existing handler does. The prepared release starts only in a new process, which that Gateway cannot start.
- `openclaw update --timeout <seconds>` on a Git install is the overall budget again: it bounds how long the CLI follows the run, reaches the Gateway as `update.run` `timeoutMs`, and target resolution, the release build and plugin maintenance get only what remains of it. Preflight and `check-release` keep their own short bounds.
- Rejected again, same reason as the format-1 trial: settling legacy `.trial` records in `stale-install.ts`. Only #199706 writes them; `settleGitReleaseTrial` is in no released build (2026.11.6 `latest`, 2026.10.33 `extended-stable`, 2026.11.10-beta.1 `beta`).
- Rejected: routing `--tag` on a Git install to the package flow. The existing Git flow ignores `--tag` ("--tag applies to npm installs only; git updates ignore it"), so the Git route keeps that behavior.
- After merging `main`: Control UI and desktop app requests on a Git install show the update in the app instead of the conversation (#203357), through the same `appUpdateNoticePublisher` owner as package installs.
- A manual `update.run` on a Git install during a scheduled campaign adopts the campaign through its existing owner: it applies the pinned commit, records `trigger: campaign` with the campaign ID, binds the run, and refuses a mismatched `--sha` or a campaign already applying, as package installs do.
- Rejected a third time: settling legacy `.trial` records (same reason as above).
- Rejected: restoring the plugin cohort across a trial rollback. Removing the cohort is the approved design (plugins are non-fatal). After a rollback the previous release runs with plugins maintained for the new core; a plugin that cannot load stays off for that boot. Listed under accepted edge cases.
- Updating without a Gateway (`--no-restart`, or none answering) reads the checkout's tag and branch facts, as the Gateway route does, so a stable-tag checkout with no saved `update.channel` stays on stable instead of preparing `dev`.
- `openclaw update --no-restart --json` no longer prints the human "is ready" line before the JSON result.
- Deferred: carrying `--accept-capabilities` through `update.run` (a protocol change); listed under accepted edge cases.
- `openclaw update` delegates to `update.run` only when the call targets the configured local Gateway (`isImplicitLocalGatewayTarget`). With `gateway.mode=remote` or a Gateway URL override it prepares this checkout in-process instead of updating the remote installation.
- `check-release` and `update plugins` run through the existing process owner (`runCommandWithTimeout` with process-tree termination), so a timeout ends npm and every descendant and waits for them before the step settles.
- A linked Git worktree gets the root-level `.openclaw-launcher` marker (its `.git` is a file); only a main working tree uses `.git/openclaw-launcher`. Before, the marker went to the main working tree, so the linked worktree never forwarded. Not covered by a new test: it needs a full release build through publish.
- Deferred with `--accept-capabilities`: binding `update.run` to the CLI's checkout. When the configured local Gateway runs another installation than the checkout the CLI runs from, the Gateway updates its own installation. Matching them needs the admitted root in `update.run` (a protocol change). The previous in-place Git updater had the same mismatch: it updated the invoking checkout and restarted the configured service.
- A Git install is already current only when the serving build's commit (`resolveLoadedCommitHash`) matches the target, not when the checkout's `HEAD` does. A checkout pulled to the target without a rebuild still runs the old build, so it now prepares the release. An unknown build commit prepares a release too.
- The Git route honors `update.run` `restartDelayMs` when it restarts into a prepared release or after changed plugins, as the package route does.

## Merge danger

- Two-way door for the code: a revert restores the old Git update path. The forwarder that reads the launcher marker ships in this change, so after a revert the checkout's `openclaw.mjs` runs the checkout again and the old updater updates it in place; the `git-install/` prefix is left unused. A revert was not exercised.
- One-way parts: a converted install has a `git-install/` prefix with releases, the launcher and a forwarding marker beside the checkout; a revert leaves them in place. No schema, stored-row or protocol version change.
- Blast radius: Git installs only (source checkouts updating with `openclaw update`, `update.run` and automatic updates). Package installs keep the existing path.

prs.title: fix: let Git installs without a global pnpm update again
prs.body:
Related: #203194

## What Problem This Solves

Git installs now update through prepared releases (#203194), but that new path only works when `pnpm` is installed globally. The OpenClaw installers bootstrap pnpm only for their own first build. So a Git install without a global pnpm (the normal Windows `install.ps1` result, and any Linux/macOS Git install without one) can't update anymore. Every `openclaw update`, chat `/update` or automatic update fails within seconds with `missing-tool` ("spawn pnpm ENOENT"), and the install is stuck on its current release.

On Windows, preparing a Git release also failed even when pnpm was present. Some test fixture paths exceed MAX_PATH under the release folder (`Filename too long`), so no Windows Git release could be prepared at all.

## User Impact

Git installs without a global pnpm update again on Linux and macOS. The update provides the pnpm version the target commit pins (through Corepack or a temporary pinned npm install, as the previous Git updater did). On Windows, Git updates now get past preflight, create the release worktree and install dependencies. One more Windows limit remains in the build step at the release folder's path depth (see Evidence); it is tracked separately and isn't changed here. If no pnpm can be provided, the update stops before any change and says to install pnpm or enable Corepack. The Gateway keeps running throughout.

## Why This Change Was Made

The new release preparation called a bare `pnpm` and a bare `git worktree add`, bypassing the owners the previous Git updater used:

- the build-manager resolver, which finds or provisions the pinned pnpm;
- the Windows rule that installs dependencies without lifecycle scripts;
- the Git command builder, which turns on long paths on Windows.

Preparation now uses those same owners, and preflight no longer requires pnpm on PATH, since preparation provides it. No new policy or config.

## Evidence

Base vs fix on real installs (Crabbox AWS), plus a regression test that fails on base and passes with the fix.

- **Windows Server 2025, `install.ps1` Git install, no global pnpm**
  - Base, main's updater: two updates both refused in 11 s with `missing-tool` / `spawn pnpm ENOENT`. The Gateway stayed up on the old release.
  - Base with a temporary global pnpm: preparation failed at the worktree step with `Filename too long` / `Could not reset index file`.
  - Fix: a clean `install.ps1` Git install at this head with no global pnpm. The update passed preflight, the release worktree (long paths) and `pnpm install` (pinned pnpm 12.15.0 via Corepack, `--ignore-scripts`). `pnpm build` then failed: the native TypeScript tooling timed out on its named pipe (`SyncRpcChannel: timed out connecting to named pipe`).
  - That last failure depends only on path depth. A manual build of the same commit, with the same pnpm and flags, fails at the release-depth path (`~\.openclaw\git-install\releases\.staging-<uuid>\openclaw`, 127 characters) and succeeds at `C:\r\openclaw`. It's a separate follow-up about where releases are built; the Gateway stays up on the current release.
- **Linux Git install already on a prepared release, all global pnpm removed from PATH**
  - Base: `openclaw update --channel dev` refused in 6 s with `missing-tool`.
  - Fix, with the fixed release serving: the same command updated to main `a1aa1276017` (run `succeeded`, 367 s, `/readyz` 200, service active).
- **Tests:** `src/update/prepare.test.ts` "builds with the target's pnpm when no pnpm is on PATH" fails on base (`spawn pnpm ENOENT`) and passes with the fix. The whole file passes (13/13).
- **Checks:** `pnpm run tsgo:core`, sharded oxlint (core) and oxfmt are clean.
- **Reviews:** `$autoreview` (Codex, P0–P1, with the resolver, runner and git-exec owners as context) is scoped-clean, and a separate read-only Codex review of the frozen head found no P0/P1 defects.

<details><summary>Details</summary>

- Production: `src/update/prepare-git.ts`, `src/update/preflight.ts` (about +48/−15); tests +27.
- Rejected: asking users to install a global pnpm (documents the regression instead of fixing it). Rejected: re-implementing the Corepack/npm bootstrap under `src/update` (a second owner for the same policy).
- Found by the daily update matrix (Windows Git lane, plus Linux lanes with pnpm hidden; the Crabbox Linux image ships a global pnpm, which masked this).

</details>

## Summary

Fixes the compaction gate outage blindness where the display shows 299% while the gate demands `totalTokensFresh+v1` and skips silently.

This patch makes the compaction gate trust stale `entry.totalTokens` at ×0.8 as a last-resort fallback when fresh token counts are unavailable.

## Changes

- Modified `resolveMaintenanceGateState` in `agent-runner-memory` to accept stale tokens with 0.8 decay factor
- Updated `freshPersistedTokens` to provide the decayed fallback

## Context

- Local dist patch: `compaction-gate-stale-trust-CB5m8f6C.js` (2026-09-04, Daz-approved Opt A)
- Applied via `workspace/scripts/patch_compaction_gate.py` (idempotent, backs up, node --check)
- Writeup: `memory/openclaw-compaction-investigation.md`
- Related upstream issues: openclaw/openclaw#203390, #203391

## Testing

- Patch verified via `node --check` on patched files
