prs.title: fix(goals): allow Goals on OpenClaw cloud workers
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Starting or resuming a Goal in an otherwise usable OpenClaw cloud-worker conversation is rejected before the worker can admit its input. Goal admission recognizes Codex workers but omits built-in OpenClaw workers in `worker-turn` mode.

## User Impact

Users can start and resume Goals on OpenClaw cloud workers. The Goal, input turn, and operation receipt commit together after runtime admission. Setup failure, a lost placement claim, or a blocking or throwing input-policy hook must not create or reactivate the Goal. Explicit runtime choices retain precedence, and policy rejection remains terminal for that input's operation ID. No new configuration, migration, or user action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing Goal admission, input staging, source guard, and acknowledgment path now also handles OpenClaw workers. A resumed Goal keeps its session access across worker writer handoffs, without treating a visibility or membership change as a writer-only change. The refreshed branch retains `main`'s missing-model guard and admitted-input checks, along with the existing transport-close and worker rejection assertions.

Original implementation by @galiniliev. The linked work session covers review and follow-up corrections.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/1982ca1f-7dc1-485c-9af9-265bbf8c3d61)

## Evidence

**Current head `0a9107c2308a225350bd3619c291a471f2ce8ff1`: published for proof, not ready to merge.** This signed commit resolves the Goal admission and worker test conflicts with `main` at `592b2aea2748d5697e547463cf19e5fc5cf62226`.

- [Isolated AWS proof](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_a574349d275c524788e71d806ce0d354) verified exact tree `749313a1f244144846a91a35d0510706768b4902`. All **20 focused cases passed**: eight committed sharing/authorization cases and 12 OpenClaw/Codex worker Goal cases. The two conflict files passed format checks and `git diff --check` passed. The AWS lease was released.
- Independent review of the signed candidate against pinned `main` supported proof-only publication. The Resume role recheck and local missing-model behavior are inherited and unchanged. The transport-close fixture simulates invalidation; these tests do not exercise a real provider or WebSocket disconnect.
- **Before merging:** the exact-head Azure Goal proof below passed. The [required CI run on this head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45053674968) reported a failing gate.

### Exact-head Azure Goal proof

**PASS** on signed head `0a9107c2308a225350bd3619c291a471f2ce8ff1`. The disposable Azure Gateway ran OpenClaw `2026.11.6` with the authorized Factory token helper. Package SHA-256 `de53ada6882d88366beb5269b93b9d54af39bfe676259838da7b1d0ad495e06e`. Worker bundle SHA-256 `5cb4b15916850a144e435c631784a911a04fe5aec01d6d1d1c50d6f9d3e0d24b`.

The session was idle on a real Azure Sandbox in OpenClaw `worker-turn` mode. Start wrote the Goal and its receipt. Before Resume, the same Goal was paused, the first turn had settled, and there was one human turn.

- `18:57:39.239Z` One Resume was accepted for Goal `acf82e99019d`, run `24545d011584`.
- `18:57:51.290Z` Distinct automatic successor `16241f463427` started on placement `e55bc910a776`, generation `5`.
- `18:58:04.764Z` Successful worker commit `29` persisted the final assistant row at SQLite sequence `32`.
- `18:58:04.877Z` The successor settled successfully.
- SQLite readback after reclaim confirmed the same Goal complete with one settled automatic continuation and exactly one Resume receipt. The session still had one human turn, and the final-stage marker was present in the reconciled disposable worktree.

The runner initially used the published message sequence as a SQLite row number. Direct readback verified the successor's final assistant row against the worker ledger. Azure reported zero Sandbox workers after reclaim. The disposable Gateway and allocator role were removed, and resource group deletion was submitted.

<details>
<summary>Historical Azure proof and regression timeline</summary>

- On `07610fc63480827693622e419b074237d1d41ea2`, live Start succeeded, worker setup rejection left no Goal or operation receipt, and a blocking input policy left Start absent and Resume paused. The worker marker was independently located on the Azure lease, not on the Gateway. Pause and Resume returned success, but the successor lost authority at transcript commit and the Goal returned to paused with zero settled continuations. The [required CI gate passed on that head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44789793338); that pass did not override the live failure. Package SHA-256 `a2f538a76b57afc596f51aa07195f8ea508d2cd3dbe905032670a0b6d472f861`; worker bundle `090e62ef54d1e3e0cc27c0dc54c7d818f6dc6199a44d490ec90d069ad327e452`.
- On `91d99b8a5474fefbc0f1521d50ca39757356a7ba`, live Azure proof with the Factory model route **passed**. Resume `196d908a2f2a` started distinct automatic successor `7fed8a0ca50d`; worker commit `28` persisted assistant transcript sequence `30`, and SQLite confirmed Goal `f22282d9b055` complete with one settled continuation and one human turn. A separate Azure lease read verified the worker marker. Native Codex with explicit Factory provider selection passed (`2d8e8b38a32b`); live implicit Codex placement was not run. Package SHA-256 `1e9f14732f36f166784cd00b1fa67874a4e5fa1559e4063b87dbf960c35bd030`; worker bundle `9738fbaa616f47c59b6f14fe7ce87ae420d40d51f6a9c8b3509653f648846715`. Azure reported zero workers after reclaim; the temporary identity bindings, allocator role, and Gateway were removed. The [old head's ratchet retry](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44930879191/job/136956274563) failed after its hosted runner lost contact; it did not establish a product assertion failure.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Earlier checks and known limits</summary>

- [AWS proof on `07610fc6348`](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_81ddacf6dccee860355778f6a757edaf) passed 30 active-steer and 12 worker Goal cases on tree `a526a6fb09d0f0bce1c85d2a3f2e38f0fe73de33`. Independent P0–P2 static review found no actionable findings in that scope. [Pre-refresh CI on `55f66bba1c6`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44268778221) passed the required gate, build artifacts, production types, and core lint. `55f66bba1c6` fixed three fixture lint failures on `e29da7a951c`.
- [Earlier AWS proof](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_41a4959c0545f270058daff7d98c3c01) passed seven worker Goal RPC and 71 recorder/runtime/prompt-stability cases. Both review defects were reproduced through public RPC before correction: rejected input leaving a Goal mutation, and implicit runtime selection ignoring the placed worker. Initial head `fba536ef71b` passed 66/66 Goal cases (`run_549134cf99b8dbe6e387ea3d7d6452f5`). One corrected-suite fixture initially failed synthetic auth (69/70); the seven worker cases passed after correction on tree `21807b430e96bd7e5560df007e0e202593d7332c`.
- [Retained declaration build reproduction](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_0e1590525e4d25f537239ce61cae0811) found the same six export diagnostics in unchanged files on both the incoming source and the correction. This is historical, separate from the passing build/type/lint CI on `55f66bba1c6`.
- The original author's first run passed 65 and failed `keeps pursuing after an owner's silent exec completion` (expected `Exec completed`, got an automatic nudge). Bounded replays passed on both base and candidate; this remains unclassified, not a claimed repair.

prs.title: refactor(agents): drop tool-caller re-checks from agent tool callers
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

#203487 made `captureGatewayToolCallerAssertion` stop re-checking permission in the middle of a started tool call. Its synchronous call now only checks Stop (`approvalSignals`); its prepared form carries the caller receipt's session fences. Agent-side callers still captured it just to call it synchronously, and some used "the capture returned a function" to mean "this is an admitted agent run".

## Why This Change Was Made

Admission checks permission one time, when work starts. This PR removes the capture where it was only a synchronous Stop check:

- `agent-tools.before-tool-call.approval.ts`, `bash-tools.exec-approval-request.ts`, `harness/gateway-question.ts`, `tools/agents-wait-tool.ts`: the capture only fed watchdog `isCurrent` callbacks. They keep their tool/request signal check where they had one. Exec approval has no signal in scope; its watchdog wait ends with the run's attempt, and the approval wait ends with `run-aborted`.
- `openclaw-plugin-tools.ts` (node MCP elicitation): the gate is `caller.operationalRunInstance`; Stop is the same signal the elicitation registers with (tool signal + caller `approvalSignals`).
- `tools/computer-tool-bindings.ts`: the gate is the existing `operationalRunInstance` check; Stop is `params.signal` / `request.signal`.
- `tools/personal-instructions-tool.ts`, `tools/presence-tool-authority.ts`: the gate reads `caller.operationalRunInstance`; personal instructions checks the tool signal.

**Kept on purpose (cut less):** where the capture is composed into a session source assertion or passed whole as one, it still carries the receipt's prepared session fence to the write. The brief says that fence must not be dropped, so these stay unchanged:

- `tools/in-process-gateway.ts`: composes it into `sessionMutationCommitGuard` for every in-process Gateway write (#203516).
- `tools/message-tool-execution.ts` / `message-tool-turn-authority.ts`, `tools/media-generate-background-shared.ts`, `tools/agent-step.ts`, and plugin tool `assertInvocationCurrent` in `openclaw-plugin-tools.ts`.

Replacing the capture with `captureGatewayToolReceiptAssertion` would bring back the "agent tool caller authority is no longer active" refusal on the synchronous path, and copying the 1a body would make a second implementation (Fable 5.2 consult: keep the carrier). PR 1e, when it deletes the declaration, must move the body to the remaining fence carriers as one implementation.

No new export, name, hook, flag or guard. Production: 8 files, +30 / −69.

Accepted edge case (no code for it): exec approval's watchdog `isCurrent` no longer checks Stop itself (no signal in scope); Stop still ends the run's watchdog attempt and the approval wait.

### Changed tests

None. No test asserted a mid-run refusal through the removed calls.

## User Impact

None visible. A started agent tool call runs to the end; Stop still cancels it; writes to a replaced or locked session still fail with the session conflict.

## Evidence

- Pre-push: one `ocx test` run, fail-fast off, over 146 files (direct importers of every changed source, importers of test-support files that import them, and every test that names `captureGatewayToolCallerAssertion`), then the repaired and re-touched set (37 files) again on the final tree. Green except:
  - `slack-download-read-authority.integration.test.ts` "rejects revoked output ... after result (revoke: claim)": also red on the merge base `cc7b482f887b` (run there with `ocx test`); not this PR.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:test`, oxfmt and oxlint on the changed files: clean. `check:lifetime-check-ratchet`: OK, no growth. `check:changed` SQLite worker ratchet OOMs locally on its 4 GB heap (known, whole-repo scan); CI covers it.

prs.title: fix: stop worker sessions from looping on a wait tool they can't use
prs.body:
Related: #203292 ## What Problem This Solves When a session runs on a worker (a paired node started with `openclaw connect --session-host`), the model is offered `sessions_yield`, the tool that pauses a turn until a child finishes. On a worker that tool can never work: every call returns `Yield not supported in this context`. Models keep calling it anyway. On current `main` with gpt-4.1, a plain "spawn a child session" request on a worker made 54 failing yield calls in a row before I stopped it, and it never reached the spawn. ## User Impact Worker sessions no longer get stuck repeating a tool that always fails. The model ends its turn normally, and child results still arrive by the usual completion delivery. Sessions that run on the Gateway host keep `sessions_yield` exactly as before. ## Why This Change Was Made Yield pauses the turn through an `onYield` owner. On the Gateway host the Gateway runs the model loop, so it can pause it. On a worker the loop runs on the node, and the Gateway only executes the tool. There is no loop for it to pause, so worker turns never get an `onYield`. The obvious fix is to special-case `sessions_yield` in the worker tool filter. That puts the knowledge in the wrong place. The yield tool is the one that knows it has no owner. So the tool now declares itself unavailable when it has no `onYield`, using the same `unavailableReason` mechanism `portal` already uses on workers. The worker tool surface already withholds unavailable tools. The worker prompt and delegation guidance are built from that surface, so they drop the yield instructions too and fall back to "completion is push-based, end the turn". Making yield actually work on workers would need a new worker protocol feature. Nothing needs it today, since children deliver their results without it. This fixes the loop, not the spawn. With yield gone, the model in my run went on to call `sessions_spawn` with `objective` and no `task`. It got the bare `Worker tool arguments are invalid` and asked me what to do. #203292 makes that error name the bad fields so the model can correct itself. Together, the two PRs make "spawn a child" on a worker recoverable end to end. ## Evidence Live, plain upstream gateway from source, gpt-4.1, same prompt, session placed on a worker node: | | `main` (1d9252c) | this PR | |---|---|---| | `sessions_yield` calls | 54, all `Yield not supported in this context` | 0 | | Gateway log | — | `Worker tool sessions_yield withheld` | | Outcome | looped until stopped by hand | tried to spawn, then ended the turn and asked the user | **Before (`main`):** the session runs on `r13-main-worker`. Every yield fails with `Yield not supported in this context`, and the model keeps calling it. **After (this PR):** same prompt, on `r13-fix-worker`. No yield calls, and the loop is gone. The "Couldn't launch subagent" error in this screenshot is a different bug, and this PR doesn't touch it. Now that the model can no longer get stuck on yield, it reaches `sessions_spawn`. It sends `objective` instead of the required `task`, and the worker answers only with the bare `Worker tool arguments are invalid`. With nothing telling it which field is wrong, the model gives up and asks the user. #203292 fixes that error: it names the invalid and missing fields, so the model can correct the call and retry. Tests (each fails on `main` and passes with this PR): - a real worker turn execution: `sessions_yield` is in neither the authorized worker tools nor the system prompt, and `sessions_spawn` still is; - full tool assembly keeps the unavailable marker without `onYield`, and adds none with it; - the worker tool filter withholds yield without an owner and keeps it with one.
Commands and scope - `pnpm exec vitest run` on the changed and related suites: tool registration, requester yield, worker turn execution, worker gateway tool runtime, MCP HTTP, restart-resume yield, worker runtime, and the vitest project config tests. All pass. - `oxlint` and `oxfmt` are clean on the changed files. - Only worker turns change behavior. The `unavailableReason` marker is read only by the worker tool filter. Non-worker runs without `onYield` still see the tool, as before. - Not covered: #180941, the same loop with `nothing_pending` on sessions where yield works but nothing is pending. That is a model-selection problem, and this PR doesn't change it.

prs.title: improve: offer a name for an added provider account
prs.body:
Related: #202626

## What Problem This Solves

When you connect another account for the same provider, the saved profiles can show identical emails. The account list leaves you to recognize an opaque ID or check usage to tell work from personal. Reconnecting a previously named account can also drop its name.

## User Impact

User impact: an interactive CLI sign-in or Models sign-in offers an optional name after saving another account. Press Enter to keep the prefilled label. Chat `/login` still signs in without prompting, and reconnecting a recognized account keeps its saved name, including `--force`. If a name cannot be saved, the sign-in stays connected and Models or the Gateway-backed CLI shows what happened.

## Why This Change Was Made

The prompt surfaces opt in to optional text; the chat adapter does not. Credential persistence completes before the question, so dismissing the name or failing to write it cannot undo the sign-in. A custom name uses the existing profile `displayName`: config-authored names keep precedence, and saving a label does not create an auth-order declaration. The suggestion uses an existing provider-supplied name or email when available. If neither exists, the provider label is suggested and is saved when accepted. Subscription tiers are not assumed to be workspace names.

## Evidence

**Main integration (`72a8d6a99174`):** After #202626 landed, this branch incorporated `main`, including the #202795 Plugins asset-budget fix. The merge keeps the shared-store reconnect matcher authoritative for saved names; a different API key or token or an unresolved secret reference does not inherit an existing name. The original visual flow is unchanged. All 130 focused shared login, auth naming, wizard, and Models runner tests passed on the integrated tree; targeted typed lint, formatting, line-cap ratchet, and `git diff --check` passed. Independent full-diff local Codex review through P2 found no actionable findings. Fresh hosted CI is still required on this head.

On unpatched main (`31ce94f0a`), seven new account-name cases failed at the absent prompt or lost name; the first-account and chat controls passed. With the change all ten pass against the real isolated auth store, including the additional review regression for a provider that supplies no name or email. The hosted CLI prompt-error case also fails before its fix and passes after. Shared auth, reconnect, chat-adapter, and WizardSession/Clack checks pass. Focused TypeScript, lint, format, diff check, and a bounded local runtime build pass.

The real CLI in a PTY and the real Models UI through an isolated Gateway use a synthetic local provider, not real OpenAI credentials. The CLI saved both profiles and one Enter kept the default. Models submitted **Work** with Enter and read back both saved profiles, with **Personal** unchanged. The screenshots show the same added-account interaction before and after. The production UI build completed, and the report-only budget check still flags limits that were already exceeded before the UI change. No budget was changed.

A real Models regression reproduced a stale name form after clicking **X**. With the fix, that click reaches the sign-in confirmation without another input, and both accounts remain saved with the new one unnamed. The narrow UI regression also fails before the fix; the runner, Models, and login-dialog suites pass afterward.

After repairing the draft ancestry onto `c1f70d3b7`, all 14 authored files matched the tested patch byte-for-byte. The affected core and UI suites were rerun on that base: 68 tests passed.

Independent excerpt review identified the missing fallback-label save and Models dismissal problems; both were fixed and reverified. The full diff was self-reviewed. The packaged Auto Review executable was unavailable in this worktree, so no completed Auto Review report is claimed.

[Follow-up review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202667#issuecomment-7048414949) found that replacing the account in an explicit `--profile-id` slot could inherit the old account’s name. Matching reconnects now keep the name; a replacement does not, and gets the optional offer when another account exists. The replacement case failed before that fix; all 55 tests in the three affected auth suites now pass, including explicit same-account reconnect. Focused typecheck, lint, format, and the CI mock-export ratchet also pass.

### OAuth accounts without a provider matcher

The [maintainer follow-up](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/f4153f88310ff6f004f34b2daa66531114c02760) keeps the provider matcher authoritative. Without a matcher, a reused OAuth slot keeps the saved name only when the provider-supplied account ID and OAuth registration match. A different or unknown account can be named without inheriting the old label. Credential writes, profile selection, config-authored labels, and API key/token behavior are unchanged.

Both regression cases failed against `66e6da85`: the naming prompt was skipped for a different account and when no account ID was available. After the fix, both cases and the same-account control passed; 61 tests passed across three focused auth suites. The naming suite took 33.34s locally; CI timing on the follow-up is pending. Targeted typecheck, typed lint, formatting, and diff checks passed. Local Auto Review found no P2-or-higher issues in the follow-up diff. Tests used synthetic credentials, not a live xAI sign-in.

### Failed name saves are visible and nonfatal

The [hosted review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202667#issuecomment-7048687460) found that a name-write failure only reached the Gateway log. The saved sign-in now sends an optional plain note through the existing wizard channel. Models displays it rather than silently acknowledging it; the Gateway-backed CLI prints it. The note says the account is connected, explains that the name was not saved, and shows where to set a display name in configuration. Dismissing it still retrieves the successful sign-in receipt. No Gateway protocol change.

Three real-store cases reproduced missed or rejected name writes with no client notice; one Models runner case reproduced the hidden notice and one reproduced the stale cancellation receipt. All are green with the repair. The seven affected test files pass 160 tests, including the Gateway CLI reader and wizard cancellation logic; core/UI typecheck, lint, format, mock-export ratchet and diff check pass. The real Models before/after below runs a loopback Gateway and Chromium with synthetic credentials and injects a null name-write result only. Before, Models went straight to confirmation. After, the warning is visible; clicking **X** still finishes sign-in, and read-back confirms both accounts remain saved and the new account has no custom name.

### Latest-stable existing-state upgrade

Built and ran latest stable `2026.11.6` from the exact source tag `v2026.11.6` (`06afb10d3272`) with frozen dependencies. Used an isolated profile and synthetic OAuth fixture only. Seeded and read the state using the stable CLI, then ran the candidate’s supported `doctor --fix --full-integrity-check` on the same isolated state (exit 0). Before any post-upgrade sign-in, all of these matched the stable readback:

| State | Stable and immediately after upgrade |
| --- | --- |
| Profile IDs | `example-upgrade-proof:personal`, `example-upgrade-proof:work` |
| Saved names and effective labels | Personal → Personal; Work → Office override (configured) |
| Saved auth order and first profile | Work → Personal; Work first |
| Resolved selected model | `example-upgrade-proof/example-v1` |

A real CLI sign-in then saved **Travel** as a third account without changing either existing profile or selected model. Reconnecting **Work** did not prompt for a name, refreshed that same profile ID, and kept both the saved **Work** label and the **Office override** config preference. Normal sign-in promotion changed first-profile order only after those new sign-ins. No live credentials, external provider endpoints, or inference were used; no naming migration was added.

### Required CI background

The reviewed-head [compaction job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44801338049/job/136514993232) failed `compact.queued-successor.test.ts:781` (during branch read: expected false to be true). A separate unmodified checkout of the published base `c1f70d3b7` reproduced that exact failure (18 pass, one fail). The [UI E2E job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44801338049/job/136514992833) failed the same plugin and skills readiness selectors and skill-settings request budget (33 > 31) that a local base replay reproduced without the PR’s UI change. These broader checks are not waived or fixed here.

### Models: failed account-name save

**Before**

![Models confirms sign-in without showing the unsaved name](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9f2a5099-38b1-49c4-b76b-5fb413167d64)

**After**

![Models explains the name was not saved while the account remains connected](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/88dc74bd-e151-4b37-8231-adba6c7d143d)

### CLI: adding a second account

**Before**

![CLI: sign-in saves the account without a name offer](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/da1ee446-cd8c-4422-8493-6e76abef1e69)

**After**

![CLI: the saved sign-in offers a prefilled optional name](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4a36c4cb-22fc-4df8-b779-de8d4d22f5b6)

### Models: adding a second account

#### Clean comparison

**Before**

![Models: the saved sign-in goes straight to confirmation](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/69ee5150-d068-4f26-a327-526f1cad6d46)

**After**

![Models: the saved sign-in offers a prefilled optional name](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f8d92a88-cef3-4f54-9ddc-c0851ce87c16)

#### Annotated comparison

**Before**

![Models before: highlighted sign-in confirmation](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fce90167-fda2-4555-86cd-9ff7c5fac3de)

**After**

![Models after: highlighted name field that accepts Enter](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5028fe10-f765-410c-945c-93468e2dcdfe)

Report, starting patch, and design requirements supplied by Vítor Cepeda Lopes (@TheAngryPit).

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @TheAngryPit](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/56f989b2-27a6-40b1-b1c0-7620a6f39e55)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/fed6a27b-739a-492c-82e8-f0ae748769d3)

prs.title: fix(cli): diagnose unreadable configuration in validation and setup
prs.body:
Closes #159029. Thanks to @masatohoshino for the report and prior closed, unmerged #159030.

## What Problem This Solves

Distinguishes unreadable configuration from settings that need correction. A missing include or failed file read should produce its underlying read error and retry guidance before setup offers changes or writes anything.

## User Impact

Validation, setup, configure, onboarding and bare startup retain the read-failure diagnosis. Malformed JSON and invalid schema keep their existing recovery paths. An unknown configuration does not authorize setup writes; include ownership, revision, path and writer checks stay intact.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing classifier and terminal-safe diagnostic owner supply the error. Bare startup keeps definitive engine-selection failures; validation uses the same failure kind for text and JSON. Shared `readSetupConfig` guards offline and Gateway-routed planning before writes. No new config option, runtime manager, permission, schema, protocol or dependency override is introduced.

## November 23 conflict resolution

Integrated official main 76aaafaa106a into this PR at fa24bffece4358660b29fbba14d0aa695e78859f. The guided quickstart fixture retains the unreadable-configuration regression and the upstream completion-message cases. The guest dictation fixture uses the exact current main blob. The earlier contributor patch there has the same patch ID as the already merged #195385.

44 focused configuration, guided onboarding, and setup tests passed. Core and affected test type checks, typed lint, formatting, and independent source review passed. The scoped local run used configuration and setup fixtures. The previous WebSocket fixture results, CI runs, and source snapshots below are tied to their recorded revisions.

## Evidence

Earlier author head: `ab705260b61e65e1db18583788aa2d7920b5908b` (tree `1a918b7f64a123f381fdd72ac0b898ba1d0d9ade`). The original CLI/configuration proposal is unchanged by this follow-up. Production, docs, manifests, lockfile and the original regression-test files are byte-identical to public head `e27aaf9612848c71e0ded4b6cdd83b1e858267d2`.

### November 9 CI repair

[CI42167756533](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42167756533), job127728885476, failed the guest-dictation WebSocket fixture at the old head. The first `talk.catalog` RPC did not produce an observed response within the fixture's5000ms polling window. The native classifier remains **unknown: no matching main job**; the exact tested merge/base and original failure remain retained.

The official [#195385](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/195385), commit [`a4e4638`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/a4e4638d6a94f6b205e730e9692130a49b31b52d), waits for the actual catalog-refresh root to settle before checking the published catalog. Its producer stores the snapshot before releasing that root. This branch carries that exact one-file repair as `02eb9ac888db10f3c1af21c88f867eea9e5655ad`, preserving the original author, date, message and existing trailers. The first warming response, final settled reason, exact catalog payload, guest/foreign-session permissions, relay ownership, late-event denial and revocation assertions all remain. The outer30000ms test limit is unchanged;the repair adds0 literal test LF.

prs.title: fix(codex): stop replaying nonportable compacted history
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

After Codex compacts a conversation, OpenClaw may have a receipt for the compaction but no summary the embedded runtime can use. Switching runtimes or falling back can then send conversation history that Codex had already compacted.

## User Impact

When the active transcript shows such a compaction with no portable cut, OpenClaw stops before the embedded provider receives that history. The user can keep using Codex or start a fresh session for the other runtime. A verified portable cut still works.

## Why This Change Was Made

Admission uses the active transcript's Codex terminal replies and compaction receipts, not the current model name or a stale native binding. An ordinary Codex reply after compaction no longer hides the receipt. The same check protects maintenance, automatic fallback and direct embedded replay without adding a database migration.

This is deliberately scoped to verifiable Codex evidence. It does not claim to detect ambiguous legacy manual receipts, export a native summary, or provide the separate model-picker warning.

## Evidence

- Before the fix, the synthetic replay made one embedded provider call containing the pre-compaction history. After the fix, the matched auto and manual cases made zero calls, including after later turns on the same Codex thread.
- The preflight regression stops before memory or compaction callbacks. The fallback regression confirms the refusal is local to embedded. A later eligible Codex candidate still runs and embedded receives zero requests.
- Control cases cover an existing portable cut, unrelated receipts, old native epochs and an existing embedded resume.
- 140 focused tests passed on the fallback correction. Four Codex receipt-producer tests passed on the preceding head. Core typecheck, changed-file lint and Git whitespace checks passed. Provider calls were simulated.
- The isolated full build completed. Its unchanged Control UI reported non-fatal CSS and chat boot budget warnings.

### Isolated Gateway and native Codex proof

Exact head `0c5afdedf`, built Gateway and real Codex 0.169.0 app-server. Only inference was simulated, using loopback.

1. A normal Codex turn completed. Gateway `sessions.compact` completed native compaction and retained its activity, but returned no portable summary or cut.
2. After selecting embedded on the same session, the next turn returned “This Codex conversation has no portable compaction summary.” The destination received **zero** requests.
3. A fresh embedded session reached the same destination once. Returning the original session to Codex continued the same native thread.

The later eligible Codex fallback, portable-cut replay, and unchanged legacy rows are covered by isolated regression tests, not by this Gateway trace.

### Published-release data compatibility

Published OpenClaw `2026.11.6` created a synthetic session and persisted an untagged manual compaction receipt using native Codex. After upgrading a copy to `0c5afdedf`, an ordinary embedded turn completed in the same session, made one loopback inference request containing the earlier history, and started no native thread. A read-only SQLite comparison confirmed all four original transcript records, including the old receipt, were byte-identical. This verifies that ambiguous legacy receipts do not enable the new refusal. Whether to refuse embedded continuation when a proven nonportable transcript would fit remains an upstream policy decision.

prs.title: fix: let a Windows reinstall replace the existing openclaw command
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Re-running the Windows installer (`install.ps1`) on a machine that already has the `openclaw` command fails at the very end. The build succeeds, then the installer exits with `Exception calling "Replace" with "3" argument(s): "The path is not of a legal form."` and leaves the previous `openclaw.cmd` wrapper in place. A reinstall or repair over an existing install therefore reports failure and can leave the command pointing at the old install.

## User Impact

Reinstalling or repairing OpenClaw with `install.ps1` over an existing install now updates the `openclaw` command and finishes successfully.

## Why This Change Was Made

`Publish-TextFileAtomically` swaps the wrapper with `[System.IO.File]::Replace($temporaryPath, $Path, $null)`. PowerShell passes `$null` to a .NET `string` parameter as an empty string, and `File.Replace` rejects an empty backup path. Passing `[NullString]::Value` sends a real null, meaning no backup, which is what the code intended.

## Evidence

- **Windows Server 2025, PowerShell 5.1.26100:** the exact call with `$null` fails with "The path is not of a legal form"; with `[NullString]::Value` it replaces the file.
- **Live:** `install.ps1 -InstallMethod git` over an existing wrapper exited 1 right after a successful build. Seen in the daily update matrix (Windows Git lane re-install).
- **Test:** `test/scripts/install-ps1.test.ts` "replaces an existing command wrapper when reinstalling" fails on base (`The value cannot be an empty string. (Parameter 'path')` under pwsh) and passes with the fix. The whole file passes (15 passed, 2 Windows-only skipped).

Introduced by #125992.

prs.title: fix(codex): reject over-budget input before fresh thread startup
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Codex budgets selected history on cold starts, but the remaining history allowance has a minimum of one token. An empty seed can pass selection even when the current rendered request exceeds the configured context budget. On the base, that request reached both native startup RPCs and persisted a binding.

## User Impact

The attempt now rejects oversized current input before starting a fresh native thread. It includes prompt-hook additions, instructions, dynamic tools, and current images in its estimate, preserving the generation reserve. A request that fits with no history still starts normally.

## Why This Change Was Made

Admit at the actual fresh-thread boundary, where startup has already decided it cannot reuse the thread. Checking the initial binding instead misses rotation and late replacement. The guard does not change how history is selected or how an already selected Gateway model preference is stored.

## Evidence

- A synthetic native attempt failed on the base after reaching `thread/start` and `turn/start` and writing a binding. On the patch none of those effects occurs for rejected fresh input.
- The same suite covers prompt-hook growth, token-fuse rotation, late replacement with predecessor binding preservation, and a fitting request with an empty seed.
- All 163 tests across the Codex attempt, context engine, and context budget suites passed locally in 89 seconds. Formatting and `git diff --check` passed.
- This proof uses a simulated native connection. It does not measure provider billing or change cross-runtime transcript handoff.

### Isolated Gateway and native Codex proof

Exact head `f4263a658`, built Gateway, real Codex app-server, and scripted loopback inference only. Sanitized trace:

| Fixture | Native thread starts | Native turn starts | Inference requests | Binding |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Fresh, oversized (234,000 bytes) | 0 | 0 | 0 | None |
| Fresh, fits | 1 | 1 | 1 | Saved after completion |
| Published stable `2026.11.6` → head, oversized replacement | 0 | 0 | 0 | Predecessor record unchanged byte for byte |
| Published stable `2026.11.6` → head, fitting replacement | 1 | 1 | 1 | New binding saved after completion |

The oversized fresh request initialized the app-server and returned the context-budget error before either native startup RPC. The stable seed was created by the published release and copied independently for each control. A fitting unchanged-settings turn also rotated after upgrade, so this demonstrates preservation on rejection, not same-thread continuity across versions.

prs.title: docs: guide small-host setup from saved keys to verified chat
prs.body:
Related: #200110, #200111, #200112

## What Problem This Solves

Someone setting up one Linux agent has to connect installation, a saved API key or existing local model, service startup, and their first working chat across several reference pages. The existing secure credential-import transport does not by itself make that journey discoverable for a beginner.

## User Impact

User impact: a guide linked from Getting Started and onboarding connects saved credentials or an existing Ollama server to first chat, with reusable non-secret configuration and precise resume actions. It now also supplies an assistant-facing workflow and acceptance scenarios aligned with the native macOS and model-management implementations below. Loading the dashboard is no longer described as proof that everything works.

This is a documentation-first contribution, not a new credential importer, profile format, installer, automatic receipt, or completed first-run UI. It should not close the broader workflow requests.

## Why This Change Was Made

The guides compose the existing onboarding, credential, config, service, Template, and plugin owners. They distinguish configured from exercised capabilities, explain that config dry-run is validation rather than a before/after diff, preserve separate plugin consent, and avoid replaying completed setup mutations.

Maintainer follow-up requested for #200110: its supported stdin/SecretRef transport is acknowledged. Please keep the basic-user access gap owned under #200112: a person with one API key in 1Password or a similar manager should be able to discover the supported connection path, authorize only the intended field, and reach verified chat without source inspection or assembling several internal workflows. A CLI pipeline is an optional route for people already using that CLI, not proof that password-manager selection is integrated into onboarding. No duplicate credential store/flag or reopening solely for the existing transport is requested.

## Coordination with implementation work

This PR supplies a shared assistant-facing workflow and acceptance scenarios for the work below; it is not a replacement implementation. States below were checked on 2026-11-18; the linked PR is authoritative. Cross-references are coordination context, not a claim that the authors have agreed to a dependency or handoff.

| Implementation work | Relationship to this documentation |
| --- | --- |
| #181011 (open) and #182075 (open, stacked on #181011) — custom endpoint editor and unified provider connection | Reuse Settings → Models, configuration/auth/discovery owners, and their preserved local-admin endpoint-definition boundary. Adding an endpoint or credential does not select or verify the primary model. Broader tracking: #177163 and #193323. |
| #200272 (experimental draft) — native macOS account/local-model onboarding | Apply the same detected → chosen → verified distinctions and first-chat acceptance, without treating the proposed picker as shipped or requiring a parallel CLI setup. |
| #200425 (merged) — native Gateway terminal-command installation | Preserve app/profile ownership and existing terminal defaults. For an app-managed Mac, use the bundled runtime and native setup; do not add a global runtime just because a CLI is not found. |
| #194841 (draft) — macOS existing-Gateway choice | The remote/attach acceptance scenario must not create or retain unwanted local hosting while approval is pending. Its native proof remains separate. |
| #200840 (draft) — compatible installed-browser dashboard handoff | Treat dashboard admission and an actual chat reply as separate evidence. The PR reports macOS dashboard validation but only partial onboarding proof. |
| #200329 (open) — Chat routes an unconfigured user to model setup | Preserve the unsent draft and use the existing setup entry point rather than making the user research model configuration. |
| #200858 and #200859 (open) — onboarding completion and diagnostic output | Keep phase completion and actionable diagnostics accurate; neither message formatting nor a success outro establishes working inference. |
| #200836 (open) — native macOS DMG captions; #200910 (open) — app-owned update guidance | Keep installation/maintenance instructions aligned with the native surfaces and installation owner. Installer presentation and update guidance are not first-chat acceptance. |

### Next implementation slice: let the setup agent use the framework

The documentation now defines **inspect → choose → propose through the existing owner → verify → resume → hand off** and four acceptance scenarios: a saved password-manager key, existing Ollama, native/remote macOS hosting, and interrupted setup. The assistant should do the routine inspection and present one next action, not assign these pages to the user.

**Current integration gap, verified in source:** the initial OpenClaw system agent receives docs/source locations, but its primary loop is restricted to the typed `openclaw` tool and its fallback planner explicitly has no file/network lookup. A pointer is not loaded documentation. Ordinary agents have separate docs-first guidance and may read/search only through their available tools. This PR does not claim to wire automatic documentation consumption into the initial bot.

Implementation should start at the existing `src/system-agent/assistant-prompts.ts` prompt builder and `src/system-agent/overview.ts` reference-discovery boundary, with the tool restriction in `src/system-agent/agent-turn.ts`. Reuse the release-matched canonical guide through bounded, deterministic setup context; do not create another installer, config owner, unrestricted reader, public receipt format, or growing copy of the whole docs tree in the prompt. A runtime implementation must preserve the normal/native app action owners, prompt-prefix stability, capability limits, consent, and source-of-truth rules.

Keep #200112 open for that integration and real entry-point acceptance. Validate through the actual initial setup agent and native/CLI entry points: no human documentation hunt, no raw key in model context, no duplicate installation on resume, and an observed chat result or one precise blocker. A documentation-only check or a prompt-string test cannot establish that outcome.

## Evidence

### Bot-consumption and adversarial review

Three sequential rounds used fresh `openai/gpt-6-astra` instruction-following consumers and independent `openai/gpt-6.1-sol` adversarial reviewers: six child runs and 16 synthetic scenario responses across successive drafts. No unsafe next action was observed in those responses; this is not a 16-case live regression suite or a separate verified “Astra-scale” mode.

The review-driven changes stop failed/partial secret reads before import, preserve the actual agent ID, scope the shortcut to OpenAI keys, separate terminal selection from native automatic trials, require an actual intended-agent Gateway chat result, avoid creating an agent or broadening permissions for an optional tool check, reconcile failed rescue work before retry, and gate service start on successful install. A contradictory incidental planning-tool claim in the existing reference was removed rather than treated as a new capability.

### Executed Bash failure/control tests

Actual documented snippets ran in real Bash with synthetic `op`/`openclaw` functions only. **All six final fixtures passed:** failed read; partial read then failure; importer failure; successful import under inherited tracing/autoexport; failed service installation; successful installation control. The captured key was not traced or exported to the importer environment. No real credential, password manager, or OpenClaw service operation ran.

The original snippets wrongly continued to onboarding after read/import failure and started a service after installation failure. The intermediate pipefail-only revision still started the importer after a partial failed read. The final snippet starts neither importer nor onboarding on a failed read, and starts no service after a failed installation. Success controls still proceed.

### Documentation checks and limits

- MDX syntax and targeted formatting pass for all seven changed/new pages; six Bash-fence syntax/continuation checks and `git diff --check` pass.
- The full configuration-example audit validates 1,408 examples with no findings; both new JSON5 examples are included. Internal route checks report no broken routes.
- The anchor audit still reports three unrelated findings in untouched pages/targets: ACP setup duplicate heading, release 2026.10.1 OpenAI runtime anchor, and Code Mode troubleshooting loop-detection anchor. No changed-link anchor finding was reported. ClawHub fragments remain unverified without their separate source checkout.
- Original source/draft review and this follow-up simplification keep the change documentation-only: no production code, state, new public command, receipt format, or competing config/installer owner.
- **Not verified:** a clean-host install, real password-manager import, actual initial setup-agent documentation loading, real model/provider/tool execution, native first-chat handoff, logout/reboot persistence, or outage failover. The synthetic reviews and shell stubs do not replace those implementation acceptance checks.

Requested by Richard O’Shaughnessy through the linked issues and discussion.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/d1f8b252-c950-4999-b9ef-66e08f64c9a6)

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A slow scan for local AI clients kept the provider sign-in and API key controls unavailable, even when the Gateway already knew those methods from plugin manifests.

## User Impact

In the Control UI and macOS onboarding, people can start those methods while the scan continues. Newly discovered candidates appear without replacing the active sign-in or API key field. The model must still pass the original verification before setup is complete.

## Why This Change Was Made

The clients ask the same Gateway for manifest/config choices alongside one full discovery request. No second Gateway, shorter timeout, or discovery cache. A pending first-run activation still reconciles before another attempt can start; local preparation continues to wait for the machine scan.

## Evidence

Compared base `cc849dd810e` with `4b1c5075852`: Chromium against isolated real Gateways, same synthetic Ollama service (4.5 s delay per response), fresh browser contexts. From page mount, the manual control became usable in **10.03 s before vs. 0.15 s after**. On the branch, we chose a provider and typed a synthetic key before discovery returned; after the late candidates rendered the same input retained its value and keyboard focus. In a separate run the custom endpoint wizard started once, remained open and kept its focused draft. No real credentials were submitted.

- 179 model-setup UI tests, 25 browser Gateway-fixture tests, and 113 macOS onboarding tests passed. The macOS suite used an unprofiled, isolated process. Its gated-socket regression starts sign-in before releasing the probe and observes exactly one start and no cancel.
- Focused discovery, Gateway method and onboarding command suites passed, as did protocol registry/vintage checks, native protocol contract, UI build and TypeScript lint. No full-repo typecheck or integration run. The native source formatter passed; SwiftLint flagged the size of the onboarding model file.
- Local independent review was **not completed**: no local ClawSweeper checkout was available and autoreview could not authenticate. This is a draft for human review.

**Control UI: API key section while the local probe is pending.** These are crops of the real form, captured about 1.5 seconds after navigation on both revisions.

prs.title: fix(codex): keep threads across skill authoring scope changes
prs.body:
Related: #148329

## What Problem This Solves

In a single-profile Codex session, turns that switch between workspace and personal skill authoring publish different tool definitions. Codex treats the catalog as incompatible and opens a new thread even though the conversation did not change.

## User Impact

Changing the current skill-authoring scope no longer forces a new Codex thread in this case. Personal turns do not gain Workshop access.

## Why This Change Was Made

The durable catalog keeps the workspace-authoring declaration in the supported single-profile case. Execution still uses the separate per-turn tool set and checks current workspace authority. This addresses Workshop registration, not Automations or other causes of cache misses.

## Evidence

- The synthetic Codex lifecycle regression failed on the base with thread sequence `1 → 2 → 3 → 3` and passed on the patch with `1 → 1 → 1 → 1`.
- Personal and revoked workspace calls did not reach the executor. Initial and re-granted workspace calls did.
- All 132 Codex attempt tests and 16 prompt-prefix stability tests passed. The Codex suite took 61 seconds locally. The new test took about three seconds and exercises the startup, resume, and tool-dispatch boundaries together.
- This uses a simulated Codex connection. It verifies thread reuse and authorization, not provider cache hits or billing.
- Targeted type-aware lint with SDK boundary declarations, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed locally. CI duration is not available yet.

### Isolated Gateway and native Codex proof

Tested head `a27d42ee7675` through a built OpenClaw Gateway, an authenticated fixture profile, real Codex 0.169.0 app-server, and the production Workshop executor. Only inference was simulated through a loopback-only Responses server. These sanitized trace rows came from the Workshop-only fixture, with Automations excluded to isolate the changed tool:

```text
stage       profile    target      native thread  Workshop
initial     profile-1  workspace   thread-1       executed
personal    profile-1  personal    thread-1       denied
regranted   profile-1  workspace   thread-1       executed
```

With Automations enabled, the control used threads `1 → 2 → 3`. Workshop remained registered throughout, and the only observed native catalog diff was the Automations input schema. This demonstrates continuity for Workshop, not full-catalog continuity, cache hits, or billing. Mid-turn grant revocation remains covered by the simulated-transport regression above.

The runtime build passed. The full build did not complete because declaration generation hit the host memory limit.

## Current correction and gates

Hosted candidate: `a48b5cd804603dbeb94b3488b5e79e0655a49371` (tree `c1305dd276e69bede2f5d3fae3fc08cc659ba2c3`). Native proof publication completed successfully. The PR remains open and **NEEDS WORK** with C1 unresolved. Publication is not merge approval.

Focused remote proof passed 24 residency tests, 9 native-scroll tests, both canonical UI Chat and packages type graphs, and syntax lint. The captured main revision is `69eb76e6347b37573f91b01240e6b1d6c12871d2`. Resolution inputs are prepared but not applied: preserve bounded packet admission and cancellation, preserve incoming automation rendering, remove duplicate thread types and the obsolete older-page helper, and carry the fixture's source sequence into its extracted owner.

The combined protocol validator was regenerated and its generation check passed on an isolated Testbox. This is generation proof only. The native refreshed candidate still needs focused cancellation/capacity/visibility tests, incoming UI coverage, types/lint/build, independent review, and exact-head CI/assets.

### Evidence for prior candidate N

[The previous integrated CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44570690892) tested merge `1f38271e94c1df6ebb264ac4f3d179796529b646`, whose parents are baseline `a38c7df01e968814be530663f931432e580e3be5` and candidate `97fb87fc939f8773a96f9bc9e6008611959d93e9`. It completed with 77 successful, 9 failed and 21 skipped jobs. Eight failures were substantive; the ninth was the aggregate gate. Build and all three UI unit shards passed.

- The two correction-owned type/lint failures are covered by the scoped O proof above.

Captured main now contains [the preparation fix](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202068), [automatic-name fixture fix](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201942), and [Cron ownership fixture fix](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201962). Their presence is source evidence; refreshed runtime results remain pending.
- The provider-removal case passed in the earlier baseline reproduction, so the cause of N's CI failure remains unknown. Captured main contains [a post-reload polling fixture change](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202009); that does not retrospectively prove N's cause.
- N exceeded the accepted Chat asset cap. Prior same-toolchain measurements follow; they do not measure O or the future refreshed candidate.

| Normalized gzip | Baseline a38c7df | Prior candidate N |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Startup JS | 90,540 B | 90,407 B |
| Chat boot JS | 1,332,622 B | 1,340,658 B |
| New Session boot JS | 820,950 B | 804,794 B |

The accepted Chat cap remains **1,339,362 B**. No cap increase is included. N exceeded it by 1,296 B. The earlier 1,341,357 B proposal remains unapproved and must be remeasured against the refreshed source. Existing CSS/request violations appeared on both sides of the prior comparison.

C1 stays open until refreshed integrated proof and the asset decision are resolved. No merge or deployment has been performed.

## What Problem This Solves

Long chat sessions retain more transcript bodies as readers page. This change bounds reloadable resident history, releases evicted bodies from presentation caches, and keeps older/newer navigation reversible.

## User Impact

Ordinary residency targets **400 entries / 3,145,728 serialized JSON code units / eight source segments**. Source atomicity, the current reader packet and live/pending/error custody have explicit exceptions; one bounded staged packet is separately charged. These are retained-body targets, not a whole-pane RAM ceiling.

Readers can move older/newer, return to Latest and restore semantic bookmarks. Search states its loaded-window scope; export loads complete history separately. Capacity/unavailable outcomes are visible. A local command after an authoritative empty-history read stays before the first later turn, including after resident-prefix retirement and older-page admission. Unloaded or unknown history never implies the beginning. Command replies retain transient custody and retire rather than entering persistent raw history.

**Tradeoff: bounded residency makes a full 900→1→900 traversal perform more pagination and rendering work. Historical matched comparisons remain rejected, with substantial wall-time and renderer-CPU regressions disclosed below. The owner accepts that product tradeoff after investigation; this is no numerical benchmark pass or speedup claim.**

## Why This Change Was Made

Canonical source/packet/cursor ownership controls trimming, reopening, continuity and retirement. SQLite and actor-memory reads certify same-snapshot Stop continuation; UI admission revalidates a fresh selected packet. Numeric adaptive budgets cross awaits, prepared bodies do not. One synchronous owner performs final prefix fit and accepted-prefix receipt adoption. Visible fitting reads commit without an unnecessary fallback/staged read, while sparse/raw progress, smaller-envelope retries and cancellation retain their existing contracts.

Accepted raw source facts and one canonical publication owner govern local-output placement; empty views, stale reads, pending inputs and unavailable outbox storage do not confer authority. Local occurrence placement preserves consecutive command order without inventing durable sequence zero. Edge-only history traversal advances navigation while preserving the original held packet bodies, certificate and opaque endpoints; actual cuts or body changes still revoke that custody.

One native offset producer supplies paging/follow facts before callback-induced rendering, preserving input/link ownership and anchor ordering. Its accepted reader-policy baseline is independent of geometric synchronization: measuring the current position before scroll capture cannot consume upward paging intent. Presentation-owned partial retirement releases dormant bodies while preserving safe survivor seeds. One shared weak derivation owner preserves exact digest bytes for fresh immutable stream/snapshot envelopes and per-source reactions. Reply-preview revisions follow final lookup facts; releasing nonempty quote bodies still invalidates their previews.

prs.title: fix(anthropic-vertex): scheduled automations refuse Claude on Vertex with gcloud ADC
prs.body:
## Problem

Since 2026.10.10, every scheduled `agentTurn` on `anthropic-vertex/*` with gcloud ADC fails with "Automation has no recorded inference account". Creating a new Claude-on-Vertex automation is refused too. Neither suggested fix works: ADC has no stored profile to record, and `doctor --fix` skips the job because it treats the credential as ambient. Gemini on Vertex, using the same ADC on the same install, keeps working.

The two Vertex providers end up with different evidence for the same credential:

- `google-vertex` declares its ADC file in manifest `setup.providers[].authEvidence`, so the planner classifies it as `environment` evidence. `isConfiguredKeyAuthSource` accepts that.
- `anthropic-vertex` has no manifest evidence. It falls through to the setup-provider fallback in `resolveProviderDirectAuthPlanningEvidence`, which `prepareAgentRuntimeAuth` turns into `runtime` evidence. The scheduled-run guard, automation creation and the Doctor migration all reject `runtime` evidence.

## Solution

The `anthropic-vertex` manifest now declares its ADC file as `local-file-with-env` auth evidence, using the paths the plugin itself reads in `region.ts`:

- `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` when set, with no fallback.
- Otherwise `${HOME}/.config/gcloud/application_default_credentials.json` or `${APPDATA}/gcloud/application_default_credentials.json`.

It returns the same `gcp-vertex-credentials` marker and `gcloud adc` source that the setup fallback already produced. Claude-on-Vertex ADC now gets the same classification as Gemini-on-Vertex ADC. The fix lives with the owning plugin, and the scheduled account guard in core is unchanged.

The planner, the scheduled guard, creation and Doctor all read the same source classification. So this one change fixes all three paths:

- Legacy jobs run.
- New jobs are created unbound, like any job using a configured key.
- Doctor leaves them alone.

Accepted edge case: a Gateway that uses only the metadata server (`ANTHROPIC_VERTEX_USE_GCP_METADATA=1`, no ADC file) still has no file to declare. It keeps today's behavior. `google-vertex` has the same limit.

## Impact

- Fixes refused scheduled runs and refused automation creation for Claude on Vertex with gcloud ADC (#203575).
- Interactive turns are unchanged. The planner already resolved the same marker through the setup fallback.
- The setup fallback, provider discovery (already driven by `syntheticAuthRefs`) and auth choices are unchanged. The new manifest entry declares no `authMethods` or `envVars`.

## Evidence

- **Reproduction through the real planner and real bundled manifests,** with a synthetic ADC file in a temp dir and no credentials or network:
  - Before: `anthropic-vertex` gives `{"kind":"direct","evidence":"runtime"}`, while `google-vertex` gives `{"evidence":"environment"}`.
  - After: both give `environment`.
- **New regression test** in `src/cron/inference-binding.test.ts`. It captures an automation binding for `anthropic-vertex/claude-sonnet-5-5`, with `apiKey: "gcp-vertex-credentials"` and an ADC file.
  - On `main` it fails with the reporter's exact creation error: "Automation requires a stored inference account or a key in the environment or provider config".
  - With the fix it passes.
- **Affected suites pass:** 46 of 47 files and 594 of 601 tests pass. The suites are `prepare-auth.setup-provider`, `model-auth.profiles`, implicit provider discovery, agent model discovery auth, workspace plugin auth, the cron inference-binding and executor suites, the cron auth-continuity integration test, the Doctor cron inference-binding migration, `extensions/anthropic-vertex`, and the plugin manifest and setup tests. The 7 failures are in `src/plugins/manifest-registry.test.ts` and fail identically on `main` without this change. They come from macOS temp-path differences in that suite's fixtures and are unrelated to this change.
- The `services-cron` test typecheck shard passes.
- `pnpm plugins:inventory:check`, `oxfmt` and `oxlint` are clean, and `git diff --check` is clean.

Not run: a live Vertex scheduled turn. That needs a Google Cloud project with Claude on Vertex enabled and real ADC credentials, which I don't have. The reporter verified that a guard bypass at this exact point makes their refused job return `ok`. It would help if someone with a Claude-on-Vertex ADC setup could confirm that `openclaw automations run <id> --force` succeeds on this branch.

Fixes #203575

prs.title: fix: let an updated Mac app move its Gateway to the new version instead of quitting
prs.body:
Closes #203065

## What Problem This Solves

After an in-place update, OpenClaw.app can stop its bundled Gateway and still be unable to replace it. Doctor sees the old service registration, refuses to prepare credentials, and the app quits. In the reported case, reopening the 2026.11.5 app kept bringing back the 2026.11.4 Gateway.

## User Impact

User impact: the old service registration no longer blocks an update when the Mac app has stopped that exact service. If credential preparation fails after changing the database, the app reports the original error and leaves the old Gateway stopped unless that build confirms it can still use the saved state. A separately installed CLI still refuses to migrate state needed by an older Gateway.

This does not fix configs that still contain `agents.defaults.heartbeat`. A config written by 2026.11.4 setup passed the service check but stopped at `Cannot prepare client credentials with invalid config`; its schema stayed at 22. Thanks to @skrubbb and @BObereder for reporting affected installs, and to @Speculorum9 for the update timeline, confirmation of the heartbeat key, and offer to test. There is no verified signed build of this change to recommend for a live installation.

## Why This Change Was Made

The app passes the stopped service’s entrypoint to its bundled Doctor child in `OPENCLAW_REPLACING_GATEWAY_SERVICE_ENTRYPOINT`. Doctor makes the exception only when that path resolves to the installed service’s entrypoint. It still needs the state lease. Normal startup drops any inherited value, and a plain `doctor --fix` keeps the protection from #186971.

Doctor can commit a schema migration before it discovers an invalid client identity. On that error, the app asks the previous build to check the service’s own config and database before restarting it. A refusal or an inconclusive answer leaves the service stopped; the check does not undo a migration.

<details>
<summary>Root cause</summary>

At merge base `08f45d611b7d`, `StaleGatewayServiceReplacement.run` (`apps/macos/Sources/OpenClaw/StaleGatewayServiceReplacement.swift:15`) stops the old service before preparing credentials. The CLI still reads the installed LaunchAgent (`src/cli/run-main.ts:844`, `src/cli/run-main-service-installation.ts:114`), so Doctor sees the older package and refuses the migration (`src/commands/doctor-update-schema-guard.ts:467`). The same-version check for #187000 did not exercise this case. The in-app Retry setup action still runs a plain `doctor --fix`; it is not reachable when the app quits during credential startup.

</details>

## Evidence

**Rollback regression, not a packaged-app upgrade.** A Swift harness exercised `StaleGatewayServiceReplacement.run` with the credential error `Invalid client identity requires explicit repair; startup preserved it.` The harness recorded service calls rather than starting a Gateway.

| Revision | What happened after the fixture advanced to schema 41 and credential preparation failed |
| --- | --- |
| `78fc7710` | `run` called `restore`, which would restart the old Gateway against state it cannot read. |
| `a5ff3209` | `run` preserved the original credential error and called neither `restore` nor `install`. The published 2026.11.5 CLI refused schema 41 (it supports 36). |

With compatible schema-36 state, the old CLI admitted the state and the harness recorded `restore`. A retry at schema 41 still did not restore; successful credential preparation called `install` instead.

**Packaged proof remains open.** No packaged app was verified completing a schema-changing upgrade, an upgrade from the latest stable release, or a fresh install on `a5ff3209`. The available local Mac has Command Line Tools only; they lack the SwiftUI macro plugins required to package the app. No isolated Mac with full Xcode was available for these checks. Gateway startup, a client connection, and preservation of credentials, settings, and data through a packaged upgrade remain unverified.

**Hosted CI:** [the CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45053349578) for `a5ff3209` requires workflow approval and has zero jobs. [Security Review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45053346740/job/137303182883) reports that the CI gate did not pass. There is no failing product test in that run.

<details>
<summary>Earlier CLI and release-state checks (not an app upgrade)</summary>

On Apple silicon with Node 26.8.1, the CLI ran against homes created by published 2026.11.4 and 2026.11.5 releases. The test supplied a stopped service registration and used `node --import tsx/esm src/entry.ts doctor --client-credentials --fix --non-interactive`. It did not start launchd, a Gateway, or a client connection.

- With the stopped 2026.11.5 service’s entrypoint, the merge base (`08f45d611b7d`) refused the schema migration. The PR’s CLI exited 0. Omitting the variable or passing another copy’s entrypoint still refused. With credentials already prepared, all six databases kept their versions, row counts, and integrity.
- After the fixture replaced the service registration, credential preparation exited 0 without the variable. `doctor --fix --non-interactive` moved the state schema from 36 to 41: all 26 rows remained, integrity checked out, and `agents list --json` still listed both agents. Doctor did not finish plugin maintenance or lease release in that environment; the agent databases stayed at 38.
- `pnpm test src/cli/run-main-service-installation.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 8 passed and the stopped-entrypoint case failed on the merge base; all 9 passed on the PR. Warm wall time was 40.4 s, cold 153.5 s. Adjacent service-installation suites passed 50/50; the credential and Doctor activation suites had 29 passed, 2 skipped.
- All four older-service protection cases passed. Ten backup and SIGINT cases in `src/commands/doctor-update-schema-guard.test.ts` failed with the same state-lock and backup errors on the merge base and the PR. Formatting, type-aware lint on the changed TypeScript, and `git diff --check` passed in that run. The full macOS app test suite was not run.

</details>

<details>
<summary>How the release-state runs were set up</summary>

- Releases: `npm install openclaw@2026.11.5` (e13cf15) and `openclaw@2026.11.4` (d843d6a), each in its own prefix. Branch and merge-base trees come from `git archive` with a production dependency install.
- Each 2026.11.5 case gets an empty HOME, and the published CLI creates the state in place:

  ```sh
  openclaw setup --baseline --workspace "$HOME/workspace"
  openclaw agents add proofagent --workspace "$HOME/proofagent-ws" --non-interactive
  openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive   # its Gateway discovery step cannot finish here
  # the 2026.11.5 app's startup credential step
  OPENCLAW_PROFILE=default OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR="$HOME/.openclaw" OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH="$HOME/.openclaw/openclaw.json" \
    openclaw doctor --client-credentials --fix --non-interactive
  openclaw agents list --json
  ```

  The 2026.11.4 home comes from 2026.11.4 `setup --baseline`. Its later seeding steps could not finish here because they wait on a state lease holder this environment cannot inspect.
- LaunchAgent: written with this branch's `buildLaunchAgentPlist` to `$HOME/Library/LaunchAgents/<label>.plist` under a custom `OPENCLAW_LAUNCHD_LABEL`, running `node <release package>/openclaw.mjs gateway --port <port>`.
- App Doctor run, from each source tree:

  ```sh
  OPENCLAW_PROFILE=default OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR="$HOME/.openclaw" OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH="$HOME/.openclaw/openclaw.json" \
  OPENCLAW_REPLACING_GATEWAY_SERVICE_ENTRYPOINT=<release package>/openclaw.mjs \
    node --import tsx/esm src/entry.ts doctor --client-credentials --fix --non-interactive
  ```

- Install step: the LaunchAgent is rewritten to run the branch's `openclaw.mjs`, then the app Doctor run repeats without the variable, followed by `doctor --fix --non-interactive` and `agents list --json` from the branch and from 2026.11.5.
- Databases are read with `node:sqlite`: `PRAGMA user_version`, `PRAGMA integrity_check` and `count(*)` per table, before and after each step.

</details>

Merge danger: the exception applies to the Mac app replacing its own Gateway. Reverting the code restores the CLI refusal; it does not reverse a database migration that has already happened. The migration exception still needs an owner decision.

prs.title: fix(telegram): send one notice for an unconfirmed reply
prs.body:
Closes #203562

## What Problem This Solves

When Telegram loses confirmation of a final reply and the queued retry also fails, the lifecycle sender and the Telegram turn can each send a failure notice about the same reply.

## User Impact

Telegram sends one failure notice if the lifecycle sender has already delivered it or the notice is in the retry queue. If the notice is refused and has no queue owner, the usual Telegram fallback is still available.

## Why This Change Was Made

Carry the terminal notice outcome from durable recovery back to Telegram. The exact notice’s delivery receipt or queue state establishes ownership. An owed flag in the session alone leaves the fallback available.

## Evidence

The loopback Bot API dropped both HTTP responses for the final answer. The real Gateway lifecycle sender then delivered the uncertainty notice. With the original Telegram dispatch restored as a negative control, the chat received two notices. With this branch it received exactly one.

| Fault after both final attempts lost their responses | Original dispatch | Fixed dispatch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Lifecycle notice accepted | Uncertainty notice and Telegram fallback | Uncertainty notice only |
| Lifecycle notice explicitly refused without retry custody | Telegram fallback only | Telegram fallback only |

Both runs used the real Telegram adapter, outbound queue, lifecycle sender and turn finalizer with synthetic chat data. They made two final-answer attempts and one lifecycle-notice attempt per case. The refusal control used an explicit Telegram error classified as terminal. Neither test left an outbound entry waiting to replay.

95 tests passed across the focused Telegram, durable delivery and queue recovery suites after adding both loopback cases. After removing the mocked field-copy assertion, the remaining 10 durable-delivery tests passed again. The negative control failed on the single-notice count as expected. No real Telegram account or external Bot API was used.

Reviewed changes address the [ClawSweeper proof request](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/203584#issuecomment-7083503704). ClawSweeper accepted the transport proof on `7a440879b58f`. The follow-up `a69bea901c15` removes only the mocked ownership table suggested in that review. Both Telegram suites passed again with 23 tests on the follow-up.

prs.title: fix(process): use glibc-compatible proc-safe bindings
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On supported Linux hosts with glibc 2.28 through 2.32, OpenClaw 2026.10.10 and later can refuse every supervised child-process launch because the published `@openclaw/proc-safe@0.4.2` GNU binding requires newer GLIBC symbols than the host provides. The affected user reports in #191841 cover Gateway `exec`, CLI backends, and scheduled scripts on RHEL 8 compatible systems.

## Root cause

OpenClaw selects the native child owner from the runtime entrypoint, then `proc-safe@0.4.2` fails to load when its GNU binding requests `GLIBC_2.33` or newer. The failure happens before the command launches. Falling back to process-group supervision would weaken the native descendant-cleanup guarantee.

`openclaw/proc-safe#37` was merged and released as `proc-safe@0.6.0`. Its GNU bindings are built against glibc 2.28, so the existing native ownership and cleanup semantics remain in place.

## Change

- Update the OpenClaw dependency from `@openclaw/proc-safe` 0.4.2 to 0.6.0.
- Refresh the lockfile for all platform optional bindings.
- Keep the existing native process-owner path unchanged.

This supersedes the fallback approach in #191914 and preserves the cleanup contract called out by the maintainer.

## Evidence

The verification host reports `glibc 2.28`.

- Before, loading the 0.4.2 GNU binding fails with `ERR_DLOPEN_FAILED: GLIBC_2.33 not found`.
- After, the 0.6.0 public API reports `loaded: true` for `linux-x64-gnu`.
- After, `readProcessAncestry` succeeds, `becomeChildSubreaper()` reports `isChildSubreaper() === true`, an orphaned child is observed through `inspectChildWaitState()`, and `reapChild()` returns exit code 0.

Targeted process-supervisor verification passed 6 tests across the Linux subreaper, relay startup, and native-owner suites.

## Packaged product behavior proof

Verified on the exact PR head `d2823b2ee5a8931826b2c9373a392d03ab8a532a` using the packaged runtime entry `openclaw.mjs` after the repository runtime build. The host reports `ldd (GNU libc) 2.28` and Node `v24.16.0`.

The real `openclaw agent exec --json` path launched a supervised command that created a delayed descendant, then the command was cancelled by the product timeout (`awaitResults=true`, `timeoutSeconds=2`, `yieldMs=1000`). A second real `exec` waited four seconds and checked the same marker path. Its captured output was:

```text
CLEAN
NORMAL_OK
```

The product command exited with `RC=0` and returned `ok: true`. The first tool call's timeout is the intentional cancellation step. No source or dependency files were changed during this proof, and no full test suite was run.

## References

- Fixes #191841
- Supersedes #191914
- Compatible native build in https://github.com/openclaw/proc-safe/pull/37
