prs.title: fix: connect AI without being asked about conversation history or memory
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Connecting your first AI used to come with history decisions. In the Control UI and the macOS app, the AI setup screen asked whether to show existing Claude Code and Codex conversations. Then, as soon as onboarding continued, a dialog offered to import memory from other coding agents. Someone who only wanted a working model had to decide what to do with their personal history first.

## User Impact

User impact: you can connect an AI without being asked about conversations, session copies or memory. Login records nothing beyond what it did before. Fresh installs keep native conversation discovery off, and a saved discovery preference stays as it is. When you want these features, they remain in Settings: **Appearance → Session sources** to browse native conversations in place, the sidebar catalog menu to copy a session into OpenClaw, and **Memory → Import memory** to migrate memory. Each one still shows its source and effect and can be cancelled.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Control UI (`ui/src/pages/model-setup`):** removes the "Find existing sessions" section. Activation and provider sign-in no longer send `nativeSessionCatalogsEnabled`.
- **macOS (`OnboardingAISetupView.swift` and its model):** removes the matching "Show existing native conversations" checkbox and stops sending that parameter.
- **Onboarding mode (`app-shell-view-state.ts`, `onboarding-memory-import-solid.tsx`):** removes the automatic memory import dialog, along with its strings, styles, test and retention scene. The voluntary `/memory-import` page stays unchanged.
- **Gateway behavior:** unchanged. When the Gateway still needs a first-time choice (`nativeSessionCatalogPreferenceRequired`) and no choice arrives, it already records "off" (`resolveSetupNativeSessionCatalogPreference`). When a preference is already saved, no consent is required and nothing is written. So a login never turns on discovery and never overwrites an existing choice.
- **Kept on purpose:** the Gateway protocol fields `nativeSessionCatalogs`, `nativeSessionCatalogPreferenceRequired` and `nativeSessionCatalogsEnabled` stay. Older macOS apps can connect to newer Gateways and may still send the parameter. Removing them would be a protocol change, which is outside this scope.
- **Scope:** Linux and Windows apps are not included. A repository search showed that neither app uses these fields.

## Evidence

**Behavior on the base:** on `main` at `cc849dd810e`, the new end-to-end test fails at the "Find existing sessions" assertion. The changed unit test fails because the native discovery section is still rendered. Both pass on this branch.

### Clean comparison

Fixture-backed real Control UI build (synthetic Gateway replies, 1180×900, light theme). Before is `cc849dd810e`; After is this branch.

**Connect AI (first run, Gateway reports that a native catalog choice is still needed)**

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: AI setup shows Find existing sessions with a checkbox for Claude Code and Codex](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ebe2908d-a938-4f5b-8259-7fca108cc647) | ![After: AI setup goes from the intro straight to installed agents and available models](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/08de8204-8f66-45d6-923f-817db2f73bdd) |

**Onboarding mode after connecting (`/new?onboarding=1`, Gateway has Codex memory available)**

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: Bring your agent memory with you dialog offers to import Codex memory](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d0a50cfe-a987-4488-9a98-c35dfd709597) | ![After: onboarding shows the new-session composer with no dialog](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/11328e85-09bf-48a8-b8fd-dcdc70078ca3) |

### Annotated comparison

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Sign-in asks about existing sessions highlighted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/944f68c6-fcaf-416b-9f3b-11bf6fdc58e9) | ![First section is now Use an installed agent](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/15125309-9ad2-4ce3-ae0e-71d234246c9d) |
| ![Memory import offer highlighted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c5fa30b5-1bda-496d-be7e-5febbad9b792) | ![Composer highlighted with no import dialog](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/018ce1c4-80f3-4855-a27e-4b604f05c586) |

### Voluntary access after connecting (unchanged surfaces, this branch)

| Import memory: source, effect, Cancel | Session sources: saved preference kept |
| --- | --- |
| ![Import from Codex? Copy 1 selected memory files into this agent workspace, with Cancel and Import memory](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cbd2a362-f793-462c-b0be-c056d2d5c49d) | ![Session sources with Codex on and Claude Code off, as saved in config](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/abd88708-4122-4d7d-8b8c-e80aa86c9dde) |

### Tests and checks

- New e2e `model-setup-history-opt-in`: first-run connect sends no catalog choice and shows no history question. Onboarding mode makes no `migrations.memory.plan` request and shows no dialog. Opening Import memory voluntarily shows the source (`/synthetic/codex`), the destination (`…/memory/imports/`) and the confirmation "Copy 1 selected memory files into this agent workspace". **Cancel** sends no `migrations.memory.apply`.
- Updated e2e: `model-setup-explicit`, `model-setup-headings`. Re-run e2e: `memory-import-readiness`, `session-sources`. 19/19 passed.
- Unit tests: model-setup (`discovery`, `refresh`, `view`, `first-run`, `wizard-runner`), memory-import page and view, and `src/system-agent/setup-native-session-catalogs.test.ts`. That last file covers the Gateway behavior: consent required with no request gives off, and a saved true or false preference needs no consent and is never written. 106/106 passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:ui`, `pnpm ui:i18n:baseline` and `pnpm ui:i18n:verify` (raw-copy baseline unchanged), `pnpm native:i18n:baseline` and `pnpm native:i18n:verify`, oxfmt, oxlint on changed files, `git diff --check`.
- macOS: `swift build --product OpenClaw` and `swift build --build-tests` succeed. `scripts/lint-swift.sh macos` and `scripts/format-swift.sh macos` are clean.
- Local autoreview (Codex helper, branch mode `cc849dd810e..HEAD`, priority up to P1): scoped-clean, no findings.

### Gaps

- The native before/after render below uses an isolated macOS SwiftUI fixture. The full native test suite and a signed app connected to an existing installation were not run in this fixture.
- Full `tsgo`, full lint and the rest of the repository checks are left to CI.

### macOS onboarding before and after

Real SwiftUI onboarding view rendered with identical synthetic Gateway responses in the repository's macOS sandbox. The prior form offers the existing conversation toggle; the updated form keeps the sign-in controls and removes that setup choice. Both images show the same scroll viewport.

| Before (main) | After (this PR) |

| ![macOS setup before: existing conversation toggle visible](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e87fc1f0-d40d-475a-99d5-7cc05de7a327) | ![macOS setup after: existing conversation toggle removed](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a1d3de3a-9988-4f10-8de1-7d22d2cb9f31) |

The localization inventory now stops expecting the retired string. The inventory and change-to-test mapping suites passed (121 tests).

prs.title: fix: stop asking for Local Network access when setting up OpenClaw on this Mac
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When someone opens the Mac app for the first time and picks **On this Mac**, macOS asks "Allow OpenClaw to find devices on local networks?" even though running and chatting on this Mac never uses the local network. The question appears on the "Where should your assistant run?" page, before the person has said anything about another computer. Opening the Connection window in local mode triggered the same network search.

## User Impact

Setting up a Gateway on this Mac no longer starts a search for other devices. The app searches when someone selects **Nearby** or opens Connection settings in Remote mode. macOS can still ask for Local Network access when the app connects directly to another computer on the local network.

## Why This Change Was Made

The dialog comes from the Bonjour gateway search (`GatewayDiscoveryModel.start()` → `NWBrowser`). Onboarding started it on both the hosting-choice page and the find page, together with the check for a Gateway already running on this Mac. The local check reads this Mac's Gateway port (`lsof`/`launchctl`), so it needs no network permission.

- Onboarding: the hosting-choice page now runs only the local port check. Network search starts when **Nearby** is opened on the find page and stops when it is closed or the person leaves the page.
- Connection window: network search runs only in Remote mode and follows mode changes.
- Camera, microphone, Accessibility and Screen Recording already follow the in-context path (`nodes.permission-missing` → chat permission card → Device Settings). This PR leaves that path unchanged.

Accepted limitation: the bundled Gateway (`bun`) still announces itself over Bonjour by default (`discovery.mdns.mode: minimal`), so macOS may still ask about **bun**. Changing that is a Gateway default and affects how other devices find this Mac, so it belongs in a separate decision.

## Evidence

- New mounted test `LocalNetworkDiscoveryTests`:
  - Local onboarding: on the hosting page and on the find page before **Nearby** is chosen, no search starts. Choosing **Nearby** starts it, and closing it stops it again.
  - Connection window: no search starts while the connection is not set up. Switching to Remote starts it, and switching back stops it.
- Red on base: the onboarding test fails on `origin/main` (search started on the hosting page and on the find page before **Nearby**). The Connection window test fails with only the mode check reverted.
- Updated `GatewayDiscoverySelectionFlowTests`, which had encoded the old behavior where search started on the hosting page.
- Sandboxed local run (`sandbox-exec` with `scripts/macos-health-render.sb` plus loopback and per-user temp access, default profile, private HOME): 209 tests in 11 suites passed: LocalNetworkDiscovery, GatewayDiscoverySelectionFlow, OnboardingAISetup, OnboardingViewSmoke, GatewayDiscoveryModel, OnboardingPage, OnboardingRemoteAuthPrompt, ConnectionWindow, HealthStoreState, OnboardingFirstRun and OnboardingDashboardHandoff.
- `swift build --build-tests`, `scripts/lint-swift.sh macos`, `scripts/format-swift.sh macos` and swiftformat on the touched tests: clean. `git diff --check`: clean.
- Existing in-context permission flow on main: `chat-permission-card.test.tsx` and `chat-thread-permissions.test.ts` passed (14 tests). They cover denial, retry after a grant, restart-required, and guidance when the request belongs to another device.
- No UI copy or layout changed. The mounted tests verify when the app starts discovery. They do not verify whether macOS presents a system dialog on a fresh installation. Full `macos-swift` CI and a clean-Mac run remain the integration proof.

prs.title: feat(memory): opt topic files into per-entry chunking with a marker
prs.body:
Closes #179954

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: curated memory kept in topic files under `memory/` is indexed with the size-based chunker, so unrelated one-fact bullets are merged into ~400-token chunks. A query pulls in neighboring facts and the mixed embedding ranks specific facts lower than the same bullets in `MEMORY.md`.

## User Impact

User impact: a topic file under `memory/` can opt into per-entry chunking by carrying one marker line. Files without the marker are indexed exactly as before; there is no new config key.

```markdown
<!-- chunking: entries -->
```

## Why This Change Was Made

Shape agreed with @steipete in the issue (option 1, chunking only):

- The marker uses the existing HTML-comment carrier style and is stripped before indexing like the other annotations. It must sit on its own line, so prose or code samples that mention it do not opt a file in. Only `memory/` files honor it.
- `prepareMemoryIndexChunks` gets one more input to the existing `perEntry` predicate; the chunker itself is unchanged.
- Recall metadata eligibility and path provenance are untouched (`memory-path-provenance.ts`, `curated-annotations.ts` extraction). The marker does not make a file a curated root, so trigger and importance annotations stay ignored in topic files. Project scope was already read for topic files and now applies per entry in marked files, which follows from the chunk boundaries.
- Adding or removing the marker changes the file content hash, so the normal per-file reindex handles it. `MEMORY_CHUNKING_VERSION` is not bumped because unmarked files chunk as before.
- Docs updated in `memory-builtin`, `memory`, and `memory-architecture`.

## Evidence

Tests (all pass; the three behavior tests fail on the base without the change):

- `manager-index-preparation.test.ts`: marked file chunks per entry with the marker stripped; unmarked file stays one size-based chunk; marker in prose, unknown mode, and non-`memory/` paths are ignored; trigger/importance stay null and project scope still applies as for an unmarked topic file.
- `manager-per-entry-marker.test.ts` (real manager, SQLite index): file indexed size-based, marker added then a normal sync gives per-entry chunks, marker removed then a normal sync returns the original size-based chunks.
- `curated-annotations.test.ts`: marker detection, stripping keeps line numbers, marker never reaches recall metadata.
- Full `extensions/memory-core`, `packages/memory-host-sdk`, `src/plugin-sdk` vitest run: 463 files pass, 9 skipped, 2 fail (see below). `pnpm check:changed` typecheck/format/guards and `pnpm lint:docs` pass.

Paired corpus: the same 24 synthetic one-line bullets (team facts), once in a topic file with the marker and once without. Chunks were produced by the real `prepareMemoryIndexChunks` (400 tokens, 80 overlap) and embedded with a local embedding model (Qwen3-Embedding-4B 4-bit served by a local OpenAI-compatible endpoint, plain queries, cosine similarity, vector ranking only). The unmarked file becomes 2 chunks (20 and 8 bullets); the marked file becomes 24 chunks.

| Query | marked: top score | marked: bullets returned | marked: target rank | unmarked: top score | unmarked: bullets returned | unmarked: target rank |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Which food should we avoid when booking a team dinner? | 0.602 | 1 | 1 | 0.395 | 20 | 1 |
| How many API calls per minute are allowed? | 0.892 | 1 | 1 | 0.529 | 8 | 1 |
| Who do I ask to change the analytics warehouse schema? | 0.779 | 1 | 1 | 0.501 | 20 | 1 |
| When is the database backup restore-tested? | 0.710 | 1 | 1 | 0.533 | 20 | 1 |
| What is the Friday deploy rule? | 0.731 | 1 | 1 | 0.584 | 20 | 1 |
| How long do we keep logs? | 0.823 | 1 | 1 | 0.492 | 20 | 1 |

With such a small corpus the right chunk is found either way. The difference is what comes back: one bullet at a clearly higher similarity versus 8-20 unrelated bullets in one chunk at a lower score. The gap grows with file size, since a larger unmarked file has more diluted chunks competing with each other.

Shipped-CLI proof (head `f81c3b246`; built `openclaw.mjs`, local oMLX embeddings `Qwen3-Embedding-4B-4bit-DWQ` through `memory.search.provider: "omlx"`, throwaway `HOME` and state dir, real index untouched). Corpus: `MEMORY.md` (3 bullets), `USER.md` (2), `memory/people-marked.md` (6 bullets + marker), `memory/people-unmarked.md` (6 bullets). `openclaw memory index --agent main`, then `openclaw memory search --json`:

| File | base `bec3ad81d` chunks | PR chunks |
|---|---|---|
| `MEMORY.md` | 3 | 3 |
| `USER.md` | 2 | 2 |
| `memory/people-marked.md` | 1 (lines 1-11) | 6 (1-5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10-11) |
| `memory/people-unmarked.md` | 1 (lines 1-9) | 1 (lines 1-9) |

| Query | base top hit | PR top hit |
|---|---|---|
| who is allergic to peanuts | 0.490 `marked:1-11` | 0.633 `marked:6` |
| who manages the Cluj warehouse | 0.577 `marked:1-11` | 0.794 `marked:7` |
| who is allergic to shellfish | 0.443 `unmarked:1-9` | 0.518 `marked:6` (then 0.445 `unmarked:1-9`) |
| vendor contract with the catering company | 0.503 `marked:1-11` | 0.730 `marked:9` |

Upgrade compatibility (same state dir: index with base `bec3ad81d`, switch to the PR build, run `openclaw memory index` again without `--force`): `MEMORY.md`, `USER.md` and the unmarked file keep identical chunk counts and chunk hashes (sha256 digests `6f2efb3f`, `f8bc8e7a`, `f9c76450`) through every step. The marked file is rewritten to 6 per-entry chunks when it is next touched or edited (7 after appending a bullet); adding the marker to the unmarked file gives 6 chunks and removing it restores the original single chunk with the original hash, with all other files untouched. A file that already carries the marker keeps its old chunks until it changes (or `--force`); the marker is new, so no existing corpus is affected. No index-identity warning and no rebuild were needed. Full tables are in the PR comment.

CI: type, lint and package-boundary checks pass on the earlier head. `test-lines` now passes locally (`slack: 237`, baseline untouched) after consolidating duplicated detector test rows; the add/remove-marker reindex test is unchanged.

Fence detection requires only spaces/tabs after a closing delimiter (as `packages/markdown-core/src/fences.ts` does). Upgrade from the latest stable (`v2026.10.8`) to this branch, with existing settings, files and index data preserved, is documented in [this comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186649#issuecomment-6468411633).

Known gaps, none caused by this change (each reproduces with the three source files reverted to `main`): `manager-search-knn-subprocess.test.ts` ("KNN child loaded unrelated runtime: kysely") and two `qa-runtime.test.ts` waitForHealth tests fail locally. `pnpm check:changed` reports two further failures. The Plugin SDK surface budget fails identically on a clean `main` (public entrypoints 160 > 158), and the SQLite worker ratchet could not run locally because `rg` is not installed. No Ollama was used; the embedding model above is the local provider.

prs.title: fix: stop an update before it starts while a node service holds the state database
prs.body:
Related: #203457

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw update` stops the Gateway before activation, but it never stops a node host service (`openclaw node install`; on macOS the `ai.openclaw.node` LaunchAgent) that shares the same state directory. The node host keeps `state/openclaw.sqlite` open the whole time. The new version's Doctor takes exclusive access to that database on every update, including patch updates without a schema change, so it fails with `database is locked`. Rollback is then refused ("the writer is unknown"), and the user has to run `openclaw update repair`.

## User Impact

User impact: with a node host service running on the same state directory, `openclaw update` now stops before it touches the Gateway or the package. The message names the database and the node service PID and gives the exact steps: `openclaw node stop`, rerun `openclaw update`, then `openclaw node start`. Node services on another state directory and stopped node services are unaffected, and so are hosts without a node service.

Users on older installed updaters still get the Doctor failure, because this check runs in the installed updater. Their recovery is `openclaw node stop`, `openclaw update repair`, `openclaw node start`, verified below and documented.

## Why This Change Was Made

Before the Gateway stop, the updater now reads the node service's definition and runtime. It refuses with the existing `database-migration-owner-live` refusal (#203170) when that service is:

- running;
- marked `OPENCLAW_SERVICE_KIND=node` (set on node service definitions since at least 2026.9.4); and
- resolved to this update's state directory.

The state directory is resolved through the existing service-environment merge, so this CLI's own `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`/`OPENCLAW_HOME` never leak into the node's. Directories are compared by filesystem identity, so symlinked spellings match. An unreadable service leaves today's behavior unchanged.

Stopping and restarting the node automatically was rejected here. A node can own running commands, terminal sessions and worker sessions, which is why its own updater waits for idle. Restarting it from every update exit path would also land in the activation sequence that #203497 is rewriting. Whether updates should quiesce node services is left as a maintainer decision.

Production change: +40/−0 (37 + 3) in `update-command-schema.ts` and `update-command-execution.ts`, plus docs.

Tests:
- `update-command-execution.test.ts`: the regression cases (+47).
- `update-command-execution.test-support.ts` (+17) and `update-cli-mocks.test-support.ts` (+13): mock the node service so fixtures never consult the host's real launchd/systemd.

## Evidence

All lanes ran live on Crabbox Linux (AWS), with a node service installed through `openclaw node install` beside the systemd Gateway, using the default state directory. This head (`9391f7403e3`) was built as 2026.11.28 and .29. Main `8d1e59c2fdd` was built as .30 and .31.

| Lane | Result |
| --- | --- |
| 2026.11.5 → 2026.11.6 (published) | The reporter's failure reproduced: rc=1 `post-update-failed`, Doctor `database is locked`. A file watcher showed the node host child holding `openclaw.sqlite`, `-wal` and `-shm` for the entire update. |
| 2026.11.6 → main | rc=1. Doctor `could not take exclusive access`, rollback refused, `state-migrated-no-rollback`, Gateway left stopped. |
| main → main (.30 → .31, no schema change) | rc=1 `post-update-failed`, the same Doctor exclusion failure. |
| fix → fix (.28 → .29, no schema change) | Refused with `database-migration-owner-live`, naming the node PID. The Gateway kept serving (`/readyz` 200) and the version stayed .28. |
| …then `node stop` → `update` → `node start` | `update` rc=0 in 218 s. Ended on .29 with `/readyz` 200, the node reconnected, and the run `succeeded`. |
| Old updater: 2026.11.5 → 2026.11.6 failure, then `node stop` → `update repair` → `node start` | `repair` rc=0, run `succeeded`, `/readyz` 200, node active. This is the documented recovery for current releases. |

Regression test: `refuses before the Gateway stops while a node service keeps the state open`, in `update-command-execution.test.ts`. Its cases are a same-directory node, a symlink alias, a different directory, a default node that omits the selector, and a stopped node. The same-directory case is red on `origin/main`. The alias and default cases are red on the first draft of this branch, which an independent review caught. The full `update-command-execution.test.ts` (70) and `update-command-original-service.test.ts` (49) pass. Type-aware oxlint (core shard), oxfmt, `tsgo:core` and `check:test-mock-exports` pass.

Reviews: autoreview is scoped-clean (P0–P2) on `9391f7403e3`. Independent Codex read-only reviews raised three findings:

- Fixed: caller state selectors leaked into the node's state directory, which caused false refusals.
- Fixed: path aliases bypassed the check.
- Declined (accepted edge case, no regression): a Windows node enrolled through OpenClaw ID has no `--port`, so schtasks runtime inspection reports `unknown`, and that node keeps today's Doctor failure. Fixing it means reworking Windows node process detection in the daemon owner.

Also accepted: PostgreSQL state (unshipped) with a local node service would be refused even though no SQLite exclusion is needed.

Not changed here:
- When rollback is refused, the "writer is unknown" message doesn't name the database (request 3 in the issue).
- Possible automatic node quiesce: NEEDS-MAINTAINER-DECISION.

prs.title: fix(cli): report host live-session refusals as host limits, not provider rate limits
prs.body:
## Problem

When a Claude CLI conversation cannot get a warm process because the host has no room for another one (16 busy live sessions, or less than 1 GiB free memory with only busy sessions to close), the live-session registry refused the turn as a `rate_limit` failure with a synthesized HTTP 429.

That one wrong fact had two visible effects:

- **Text.** For the session limit (no code), the chat reply and the WebUI failure card said `⚠️ The AI service needs a short break. Please try again in a few minutes.`: the provider was blamed for something the host did.
- **Retry policy.** CLI run settlement treats `rate_limit` as a provider fact, so both refusals put the conversation's saved Claude login into a rate-limit cooldown. A later message could then be refused for the cooldown (and a successful fallback could make the session prefer the fallback model) even after memory or a session slot was free again. The host-memory copy said "try again after active conversations finish", but the policy said "the provider is limiting you".

#192534 kept the `rate_limit` category on purpose and named it as a limit; this PR fixes it at the producer.

## Solution

- `cli-live-session-registry.ts`: both local refusals are now `FailoverError`s with reason `overloaded`, **no HTTP status**, and a code naming the cause: the existing `cli_live_session_host_memory` and a new `cli_live_session_limit` for the 16-session cap. `overloaded` keeps the original behavior that the turn can fail over to another model, and the existing policy never records it against a saved login (`resolveAuthProfileFailureReason`) and never makes a session prefer a fallback (sticky fallback is `rate_limit`-only). No provider request had been sent, so failing over does not replay work; this is unchanged from before.
- `failover/error.ts`: the two refusal codes keep their host-authored copy beside them (`CLI_LIVE_SESSION_REFUSAL_TEXT`, read by `renderFailoverCodeUserCopy`). New copy for the session limit: `⚠️ This host is already running as many sessions as it allows, so it could not start another one. Try again after active conversations finish.` The host-memory copy is unchanged.
- `agent-runner-failure-reply.ts`: for an `overloaded` failure, a host-authored failover code renders its own copy before generic "The AI service is temporarily overloaded" text (the cooldown code keeps its existing path), so the reply text and the policy describe the same cause.

A real provider 429 is unchanged: it stays `rate_limit`/429, cools the saved login down, and shows rate-limit copy.

## Impact

Gateways that use a warm CLI runtime (today Claude CLI). In the WebUI chat and in channel replies, a host refusal now explains the host and suggests waiting for active conversations; the saved login stays usable for the next message. One explanation reaches the reply and the run-failure card (the card's notice is the same reply text; the existing transcript projection already keeps the toast from repeating a failure shown by the card).

The macOS onboarding model test is not affected: its setup probe runs with an auth-binding callback, which never takes a warm live session.

No config, schema, protocol or stored-state change. `overloaded` is an existing failover reason; the codes are diagnostic strings on the existing error.

## Evidence

New `src/agents/cli-runner/cli-live-session-capacity.test.ts` drives the real producers (the registry's memory admission and its 16-session cap; a real CLI 429 through `createCliExitFailoverError`) into the real consumers: `settlePreparedCliRun` (saved-login cooldown) and `handleAgentExecutionError` (chat reply text and the run-failure card notice), for both the Control UI and channel routes. No provider calls.

| Case | Base (`2aca1a1c159`) | This branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Host memory refusal | `rate_limit`/429; saved login cooled with `rate_limit`; text: host-memory copy | `overloaded`, no status; no cooldown; same host-memory copy |
| 16-session limit | `rate_limit`/429; saved login cooled with `rate_limit`; text: "The AI service needs a short break…" (Control UI and channel) | `overloaded`, no status; no cooldown; host session-limit copy |
| Provider 429 | `rate_limit`/429; cooled; rate-limit copy | unchanged |

The new test fails on base for both local cases (reason/status and saved-login cooldown for each, plus the session-limit copy on both routes) and passes on this branch. Updated `execute-plugin.test.ts` host-memory expectation (`overloaded`).

Focused runs (green): `cli-live-session-capacity`, `execute-plugin`, `cli-live-session-registry`, `host-memory`, `agent-runner-failure-reply`, `failover/user-copy` tests; oxfmt on the changed files; line-cap ratchet; `git diff --check`.

Left to CI: full `tsgo`, type-aware oxlint (locally it starts by rebuilding the plugin-sdk package, so it was stopped), and the broad suites.

No UI component changed, so there are no screenshots; the WebUI card renders the reply text shown above.

prs.title: fix: let a pnpm install update again after an update died after activating
prs.body:
Related: #203458

## What Problem This Solves

A pnpm install can end up with a healthy Gateway on the new version and no supported way to update again. It happens when an update activates the new version, verifies it serving, and then its process exits before it settles the plugin recovery it reserved. #203458 fixes the main cause for future updates. An install already in this state stays stuck: every later `openclaw update` is refused within 2 s ("Update <id> has unfinished recovery … It belongs to the installation at <removed path> … Run openclaw update repair from that installation"). `openclaw update repair` is refused too ("Plugin cohort recovery belongs to a different installation."). The only way out was editing the state database.

## User Impact

User impact: `openclaw update repair` now settles that leftover recovery from the installation that replaced the old one, and the next `openclaw update` proceeds. When the dead update was killed and its lease is still in the lease store, the next `openclaw update` settles it by itself. Nothing changes for npm installs or for recovery whose recorded installation still exists.

**Update behavior.** The installed updater runs first and cannot be patched, so the first command that benefits is one run by a build that contains this change:

- **The stuck version contains this change** (for example, an update from an unfixed build B to a fixed build C failed): `openclaw update` refuses and names `openclaw update repair`. Run it once; the next `openclaw update` then proceeds.
- **The stuck version does not contain it:** install a build that does, then repair. `pnpm add -g --allow-build=openclaw openclaw@<version with this change>`, then `openclaw update repair`, then `openclaw update`. Verified in a real cell (below).

Without this change there is no working sequence. `pnpm add -g` of a newer build followed by `openclaw update repair` is refused the same way, `openclaw doctor --fix` does not touch the update recovery, and every `openclaw update` is refused (red cells below).

**What reaches this state.**

- An updater that was itself installed by an earlier OpenClaw pnpm update and lacks #203458, on pnpm 12 and 11.28. No published npm version has this pattern: `latest` 2026.11.6 and `beta` 2026.11.10-beta.1 predate it. So today the state comes only from main builds between #201735 and #203458.
- More generally, any pnpm update whose process dies after activation: killed, crashed, or the machine went down. pnpm gives every version its own package directory and activation moves the old one away, so the recovery always names a directory that is gone. Base refuses all of these the same way. With this change, a dead update that recorded its candidate serving is settled. One that died before that verification is still refused (see "What stays refused").

## Why This Change Was Made

**Cause.** A plugin-cohort recovery records its installation by the package's real path (`cohort.installKey`). On npm that path stays the same across updates. On pnpm each version has its own directory, and the global install path (`…/global/v11/<hash>/node_modules/openclaw`) is a link that activation re-points. Both owners compared that recorded real path with the current one:

- the next update's settlement of a dead update (`inspectInterruptedUpdateRecovery`);
- `openclaw update repair`.

After activation the two can never match. So neither command could act, and the refusal told the user to run repair "from that installation", which no longer exists.

**Rule.** `inspectPluginCohortInstallation`, in the settlement owner, decides whose recovery it is. A recovery whose recorded directory differs from the current installation is treated as this installation's only when all of these hold:

1. the recorded directory no longer exists. An `lstat` error counts as present.
2. the update's recorded install path (`from.root` and `to.root` of its reservation) now resolves to this installation.
3. the run is still recorded `running`, is not a managed handoff, recorded its driver processes, and every one of them is dead.
4. the run recorded its candidate serving: service running, version match, running version equal to the target, and the build ID when the target has one.

Then the existing settlement runs unchanged. It keeps the plugin and config changes, as for any verified candidate. A `warning:plugin-cohort:replaced-installation` step on the dead run names both directories and the evidence. That step name joins the retained-step list, so history compaction keeps it. History reconciliation then closes the run as `failed`/`abandoned`, and repair acknowledges it.

Claims:
- Both commands claim the recorded key, where the dead driver's lease lives, so `openclaw update` keeps its existing proof that the dead updater's children are gone. They also claim the current installation through the executor's existing `serviceRoot` lease.
- Under the claim they check the evidence again.
- The forward-settlement check for an unfinished package activation now looks at the current installation as well as the recorded one.
- A commit that the dead update had already selected is finished from a proven successor even when a later build is installed. Before, the exact-target check refused it. That check still refuses when no replacement is proven, or when the installed build does not show the original core gone. The proof is the forward rule's: a readable version or build ID that differs from the original. So the original version installed again refuses, even without the build ID it had, since committing would then keep the candidate's changes over the original core.
- `openclaw update`'s settlement note no longer says the Gateway was verified on the *installed* version when a later build replaced it.

Nothing is stored that was not stored before: no schema, config key, protocol or retention change.

**What stays refused.**
- While the recorded directory exists: today's refusals, word for word.
- With the directory gone but evidence missing: a refusal that names the missing fact. When the dead update's process may still be running (a live or unidentified driver, or a managed handoff), the message says to wait for it. Otherwise it names the `openclaw triage` agent route.
- `openclaw update`'s lease rule is unchanged. A driver that unwound on its own released its lease, so `openclaw update` still stops and names repair. That is the path the real stuck state takes; #201361 chose it deliberately.

**Designs rejected.**
- **Requiring the installed version to equal the run's target.** This would block the only way out for users stuck on an unfixed build, who must install a different, fixed build first. The existing forward rule already accepts any installed version other than the original.
- **Accepting an empty lease store as proof that the children are gone, when the store existed throughout.** That changes the children-gone rule of #201361 for every killed update, and nothing recorded today shows the store's age reliably. Left as a follow-up decision.
- **Recording success instead of `failed`/`abandoned`.** History reconciliation credits a dead driver's run with success only when a Gateway observer recorded `booted`. This run has no such fact, and inventing one would forge evidence.
- **Keying cohorts by the stable install path.** That changes stored data, so it is a separate decision.

Release lines:
- `release/2026.11.10`: the squashed change applies cleanly (`git apply --3way --check`), and the first commit's settle tests pass there. Nine refusal rows fail there, because that line's refusals do not yet name the `openclaw triage` route. A backport would adjust those expectations.
- `release/2026.11.7`: has no killed-update settlement module (`update-plugin-cohort-settlement.ts`), so only the repair half could apply.

## Evidence

**Real installed-package cells.** Docker, systemd as PID 1 with a lingering user manager, the Gateway as a real managed `systemctl --user` service, a busy 256 MiB agent database under constant writes, and 1,000 marker rows written before the first update. pnpm 12.21 unless noted. Every build has its own version; nothing was relabelled.

- A (`2026.11.20-beta.1`), B (`-beta.2`), C (`-beta.3`): main `e17201c964a` plus one version-bump commit each that changes only `package.json`: `795efe2` (A), `4f4f386` (B), `84269f3` (C). B lacks #203458, so B → anything fails after activation.
- Base B1/B2 (`-beta.10`/`-beta.11`): this PR's base `35b84dab389`.
- Head H1/H2 (`-beta.8`/`-beta.9`): built from `9d31439`, this PR's first commit before it was rebased over unrelated main commits (subagent and queue files only).
- H3/H4 (`-beta.12`/`-beta.13`): built from `8111057`, the second commit, which adds the round-1 review fixes below.
- H5/H6 (`-beta.14`/`-beta.15`): built from `8f11d78`, which adds the round-2 fixes and merges main.
- PR head H7/H8 (`-beta.16`/`-beta.17`): built from `9104b7a`, which adds the round-3 fix and merges main.

Each cell: install A; `openclaw update` A → B (passes); then B → X, which fails with `update-recovery-pending` and leaves the stuck state. That state is a `running`/`verifying` run with successful recorded verification, a plugin-cohort recovery keyed to a directory that no longer exists, and an empty update lease store.

| **Red**, base. X = B1 | `openclaw update` B1 → B2: refused, 1.8 s, "It belongs to the installation at <removed dir> … Run openclaw update repair from that installation". `openclaw update repair`: refused, 1.4 s, "Plugin cohort recovery belongs to a different installation." `openclaw update` again: refused. | stuck Raw log: [1/3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/203486#issuecomment-7080892141), [2/3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/203486#issuecomment-7080892411), [3/3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/203486#issuecomment-7080892651). |
| **Red**, base, manual way out. X = C, then `pnpm add -g` B1 | `openclaw update repair`: refused, same message. `openclaw update` B1 → B2: refused. | stuck Raw log: [1/3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/203486#issuecomment-7080892920), [2/3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/203486#issuecomment-7080893187), [3/3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/203486#issuecomment-7080893407). |

After `pnpm add -g` of #203458's own head build: repair refused, `openclaw doctor --fix` leaves the recovery untouched, update refused. After `pnpm add -g` of main `31c9a9a`: repair and update refused.

Recordings (cell log live, then each operator command's output):

- Red, base, stuck state then three refusals: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/270eb0bc-2efe-46df-accf-a8a585e7871e
- Red, base, manual install then refusals: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3dccabbe-1158-4404-b1d0-fa9c2b6fa47c
- Green, head, refusal naming repair, repair, update `ok`: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/81d155e3-be52-42dc-ab16-feb725af92fd
- Green, head, manual install then repair, update `ok`: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cdfe26e0-51d6-4023-8c78-77cefefa48e7
- Green, head, pnpm 11.28.13: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/eee991a0-5e45-4b1a-b295-f27245a1091e
- npm, head, unchanged: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f12a761a-94be-4ee6-8926-b78fcbfa2fd8
- Green, PR head `9104b7a`: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d0541d4f-79e7-4ca6-b74d-784ffdd472da
- Green, PR head, manual install then repair: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/27e4d1fb-4ed2-4f09-8e77-732debc6e151
- Green, `8f11d78`: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/358feb6a-a1b0-4ba8-9d2b-d73f6fb0b752
- Green, `8f11d78`, manual install then repair: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3dbd3e4c-0b55-4b01-9deb-99ef76e61382
- Green, `8111057`: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/edd5e877-95d6-4bdc-8534-088c9d12d283
- Green, `8111057`, manual install then repair: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9f233fec-d655-484b-95da-80118f8c80c5

Raw cell logs are posted as PR comments and linked from each table row above. Each log set opens with a header naming its builds, head, command lines and exit codes, then gives the harness log, every command's stdout and stderr, and the final `openclaw update status --json`, each in its own collapsed block. Nothing is cut. Host scratch paths, container hostnames and the container's machine ID are redacted. The rows for the intermediate heads `9d31439` (pnpm 12), `8111057` and `8f11d78` have no posted log; the PR-head rows repeat the same steps.

**Process tests at the owner** (`update-command-killed-run-replaced.process.test.ts`). A real child `openclaw update` process holds the installation lease, reserves its plugin recovery, writes config, records the outcome it reached and is SIGKILLed. The fixture then does what pnpm's activation does: the install path is re-pointed at a new package directory and the old one is removed. The real `updateCommand` and `updateRepairCommand` entries then run against real SQLite stores and the real lease store. Doctor's child process, plugin installs and the managed service are stand-ins.

- Settled by the next update while the dead driver's lease is still in the store. Changes are kept, the warning is recorded, the run is then closed.
- Settled by repair after the driver released its lease, which is the real cell's state. The next update first names repair, and proceeds after it.
- A commit the dead update had already selected is finished from a later fixed build, which is not the version that update verified. This is the manual way out after a crash mid-settlement.
- Refused, with the reserved recovery, run and config left byte-for-byte unchanged and no warning written, when exactly one fact is missing:
  - the updater is still alive (says wait);
  - the driver identity was not recorded (says wait);
  - the run is no longer `running`;
  - no verification was recorded;
  - the service was not running;
  - another version was serving;
  - the update recorded only its package directory;
  - another installation is asking.
- Today's exact refusals while the old directory still exists, and when its path cannot be read: real `lstat` errors from a file standing where the directory's parent was (`ENOTDIR`) and from a parent with mode `000` (`EACCES`). The `EACCES` case is skipped when tests run as root, because root reads through the mode. Treating an unreadable path as gone fails both cases (mutation check).

Red/green on the PR head `9104b7a`, same tests: with the three product files reset to base `35b84dab389`, 13 fail and 1 passes (the unchanged refusal while the directory exists); as committed, all 14 pass. Recordings: red https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/72b93149-ab17-4ab9-83ee-31097dab8211, green https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dcabe3fd-f152-416e-b644-75fab17f388e.

Mutation check: each evidence guard was removed in turn and only this suite was run. Every guard is caught by a named control:

- directory present → "keeps today's refusals";
- install path → "another installation";
- package-directory-only → its own row;
- `running` status → its own row;
- unrecorded driver → its own row;
- live driver → "still alive";
- service running → "without a running service";
- running version → "another version serving";
- the original-core-gone proof on a begun commit → "keeps a begun commit's refusal … without the build ID it had". The round-2 guard (`installed(from)`) fails this case.
- the begun-commit exception → "finishes a commit … after a later build";
- the replacement-specific settlement note → "settled by the next update".

Other checks on the head:
- The new suite plus the killed-run settlement, refusal, restart and checkout suites, the cohort-settlement tests and the repair package-activation tests: 129 passed on `9104b7a`'s files.
- `update-restart-module-outcome` and `eager-import-closure` pass.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `tsgo:core:test`, `pnpm check:docs`, `git diff --check` and `pnpm check:baseline-ratchets --base 35b84dab389 --no-merge-base` all pass, including session-identity and test-lines.

**Test files audited:**
- `update-command-killed-run-replaced.process.test.ts` (new).
- `update-command-killed-run.process.test-support.ts`: adds `linkedInstallation`, `replacePackageDirectory` and a `root` option. Nothing removed; every existing helper is still used.
- `update-run-kill.process.test-support.ts`: the child accepts an install path that differs from its installation key.
- The new suite is registered with the other killed-run suites in `vitest.database-worker-core-paths.mjs`, because it needs the host-owned SQLite broker.

**Independent review.** A read-only reviewer saw the diff and the behavior contract, not these conclusions, and found no blockers. Four of its findings were fixed here:
- the repair and update claims now also hold the current installation;
- "wait for that update" is now said only when its process may still run;
- the settlement warning is built from the checked evidence and passed in explicitly, and a failure to record it no longer reports the settlement as failed;
- the refusal names the root that failed the check, and says when an update recorded only its package directory.

The reviewer's test-gap list led to the extra control rows and the mutation check. Its remaining note, about pnpm keeping old directories, is under "Not proven"; the pnpm 11.28.13 cell removed the old directory as pnpm 12 does.

**ClawSweeper local review, round 1** (on `79bdfe4`): overall C, proof C, patch C. Both findings were real and are fixed in `8111057`:
- *A dead update that had already selected commit, followed by a manually installed different build, was still refused* by the exact-target check. With a proven successor, that recorded commit is now finished. A new test covers it.
- *The warning named the requested outcome* ("commit"), while the cohort owner may finish a rollback it had begun. The warning no longer names the outcome. The owner's own kept-changes warning still reports a rollback.

Its test note, that each refusal row ran the commands several times, is fixed: each command runs once and its refusal is checked for the reason, the next step and the unchanged state.

**ClawSweeper local review, round 2** (on `8111057`): overall C, proof C, patch C. All three findings were real and are fixed in `6c1525a`:
- *The begun-commit exception also admitted the original version reinstalled in a fresh directory.* It now still refuses then. A new control covers this, and it fails without the guard.
- *The update's settlement note said "verified on the installed version"* even when a later build had replaced it. It now names the version that update installed.
- *The docs promised the changes are kept.* They now say a rollback that had already restored something is finished instead.

**ClawSweeper local review, round 3** (on `8f11d78`, the last allowed round): overall C, proof C, patch C. One finding, real, fixed in `9104b7a`:
- *A reinstalled original version without the build ID it had did not count as "original core installed"*, so the begun-commit exception still applied. The exception now requires the forward rule's positive proof that the original core is gone, shared with the forward rule. A new row covers it and fails with the round-2 guard.

No fourth rating round was run. What held round 3 at C was this finding and its proof note: the held-lease and begun-commit routes have process tests but no shipped-CLI cell, and no cell starts from the latest stable release.

Round 2's test note is fixed too: the warning assertion now checks the facts (the old directory, the install path, the successor and the version) instead of the whole sentence. Its proof note is addressed in part: the exact-head cells are above. The killed-with-lease route and the begun-commit route still rest on process tests only (see "Not proven").

**CI.** Every failing job is inherited from main.

`checks-node-changed-compact-large-27`: `src/gateway/server.roles-allowlist-update.test.ts` › "update.run persists the accepted handoff before parking and restarting its foreground owner". The same test fails locally, with the same assertion, on main `31c9a9a90f5` (before #203458), `35b84dab389`, `b8a55ae9207` and `450441b9040`. This PR touches nothing it loads.

`checks-node-changed-compact-small-11`: all 20 cases of `src/cli/update-finalization-output.process.test.ts` fail with `SyntaxError: … dist/legacy-finalizer/src/config/config.js does not provide an export named 'getRuntimeConfig'`, imported from `legacy-finalizer/src/plugins/status-snapshot.js`. The same 20 fail locally with the same error on main `31c9a9a90f5` and `450441b9040`.

`checks-node-changed-compact-large-47` (since the latest merge of main): `src/gateway/server-methods/update.ocm.test.ts` › "refuses an invalid browser-authority before submitting to OCM" fails with `promise resolved "undefined" instead of rejecting`. Locally it passes on main `adb2f7c4d4b` and fails the same way on main `6ff7a062e54`. That range's only change under `src/gateway/server-methods` is #203488.

These suites are selected here because this PR changes `src/cli/update-cli`. Main's CI run on `450441b9040` passed; I did not check whether that run selects this test.


## Not proven

- `openclaw update` alone does not clear the real stuck state. Its dead driver released its lease, so the update names repair, and one `openclaw update repair` is needed. Automating that step needs a decision on the lease proof (see "Designs rejected"). Until then the refusal names the `openclaw triage` agent route first and repair second.
- A pnpm update killed after activation but before it recorded its candidate serving is still refused, with the `openclaw triage` route. Settling it would need a rollback-over-candidate decision for a directory that is gone.
- If an older updater recorded only the package directory and not the install path, it is refused. That happens when it ran from the package path rather than the pnpm link. The fixture test covers this case; no real cell does.
- The killed-and-lease-held route (`openclaw update` settles by itself) and the begun-commit-then-later-build route are proven by process tests only, not in a Docker cell.
- Upgrades from the latest stable release do not reach this state (no published updater has the pattern), so every cell starts from main builds.
- Not covered by any test: a build-ID mismatch (package builds carry none), a managed-handoff run, and a run with no recorded drivers.
- Old package directories that pnpm keeps on disk: check 1 then fails and today's refusal stays. No cell kept them.
- Bun, Windows, macOS.
- `autoreview` could not run on this machine. The Codex route was refused ("selected model_provider must match the operator config"), and the Claude engine's OAuth session had expired. An independent read-only reviewer took its place (below).

prs.title: fix: keep the Linux installer from hanging at the NodeSource step on Ubuntu 26.04
prs.body:
Refs #203460

## What Problem This Solves

On Ubuntu 26.04 (and other systems where `sudo` is sudo-rs with `Defaults use_pty`), downloading the installer and running it with `bash install.sh` hangs forever after `Downloading NodeSource setup script`. The NodeSource setup script's `apt install` is stopped by `SIGTTOU` inside sudo's pty and never resumes, while still holding the dpkg frontend lock.

## User Impact

- New Linux installs on Ubuntu 26.04 no longer appear frozen at the NodeSource step. The installer goes on to install Node.js and OpenClaw.
- `curl -fsSL https://openclaw.ai/install.sh | bash` was not affected, because quiet steps already gave commands `/dev/null` stdin when the installer's own stdin was not a terminal. Now the downloaded-file path behaves the same way.
- Password prompts are unchanged. sudo and sudo-rs read the password from `/dev/tty`; this was verified with `sudo -k` on 26.04.

## Why This Change Was Made

**Root cause.** `run_quiet_step` captures a command's output in a log file but still passed the user's terminal through as stdin. sudo-rs connects a terminal stdin to its own pty and runs the command there. With output redirected, the NodeSource script's `apt install` is stopped by `SIGTTOU` in that pty. Neither the spinner nor the Debian frontend is involved:

| Command, run from an interactive tty on Ubuntu 26.04 (sudo-rs 0.2.13) | Result |
|---|---|
| `bash -c 'sudo -E bash setup_24.x >log 2>&1'` | hangs (apt `T+`) |
| same, with `DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive` | hangs |
| same, with `</dev/null` | completes |

**Fix.** A quiet step hides or captures its output, so it can't be an interactive step. `run_quiet_step` now always runs the command with `/dev/null` stdin, on the plain, spinner and `--verbose` branches; the verbose branch matters because gum captures output there too. This drops the conditional `needs_stdin_isolation` branch. The spinner branch of the npm package install now matches its plain branch, which already used `/dev/null`.

The one quiet step that was actually interactive was the macOS Homebrew bootstrap, which asks for the admin password and RETURN. It now runs through `run_with_safe_stdin` with visible output, so it keeps the terminal. Under `curl | bash` with a tty, it now gets the controlling terminal instead of `/dev/null`. Without this, the stdin change would have pushed Homebrew into `NONINTERACTIVE` + `sudo -n` on Macs without cached sudo.

**Rejected alternatives.** Forcing `DEBIAN_FRONTEND` doesn't fix the hang. Bypassing the spinner for `sudo` commands would leave the plain path broken, since it hangs without gum too.

**Size.** Production: `scripts/install.sh` +8/−9 (net −1). Tests: +73.

## Evidence

- **Live, Crabbox AWS Ubuntu 26.04.1** (sudo-rs 0.2.13 with `use_pty`), interactive tmux tty, run as a password-sudo user in a fresh `ubuntu:26.04` container each time:
  - Published installer (sha256 `358d7625…`, the same file as the reporter's): hangs with `apt install -y apt-transport-https ca-certificates curl gnupg` in state `T+` on sudo's pty.
  - Standalone installer built from base `8d1e59c2fdd`: same hang.
  - Standalone installer built from this branch's final head `1b506e56861`: `INSTALLER-RC=0` in 80 s, and also `INSTALLER-RC=0` with `--verbose` in 105 s. Node v24.22.3 installed, `openclaw` bin published.
- **Regression tests:**
  - `quiet steps never hand terminal stdin to the command` (plain, gum, and gum with verbose): red on base, green on the fix.
  - `keeps the interactive Homebrew bootstrap on the terminal`: red on the first commit, green on the final head.
  - `test/scripts/install-sh.test.ts`: 239 of 239 pass.
- **$autoreview** (P0–P2) on the final branch: scoped-clean.
- **Independent read-only Codex review:** it found the Homebrew and verbose-path gaps, both fixed here, and reports no remaining P0–P2 issues on `1b506e56861`.

prs.title: fix: stop status commands and the update self-check from calling configs without agent entries invalid
prs.body:
Refs #203505

## What Problem This Solves

If you set up OpenClaw without `openclaw onboard` (for example with `openclaw models set` or the guided `openclaw config`), your config has `agents.defaults` but no `agents.entries`. That is a supported shape: loading adds the implicit `main` agent, and `openclaw config validate` says the file is valid. But `openclaw gateway status` and `openclaw update status` reported the same file as invalid ("agents.entries must contain at least one configured agent") and sent you to `doctor --fix`, which had nothing to fix. On current `main`, the new release self-check (`openclaw update check-release`, added for prepared-release Git updates) refused the same config as `config-invalid`, which would fail those updates.

## User Impact

User impact: `gateway status`, `update status` and the update release self-check now agree with `config validate` for configs without `agents.entries`, so a working config is no longer flagged as broken and the update self-check no longer refuses it.

## Why This Change Was Made

The raw config validator checked the roster rule against the file as written, while every loaded reader first adds the implicit `main` agent. The three affected commands are the only callers that hand the validator a config that has not been through that load. The raw validator now applies the same idempotent implicit-roster default itself, so every caller validates one view, and the duplicate application in `validateConfigObject` is removed. Explicit rosters (`ownership: "explicit"`) and configs that already have entries are unchanged. Nothing is written: the main writer still persists the authored candidate.

Rejected alternatives: patching the fast status path and `update status` to apply the default before calling the validator (what the issue suggests as the narrow fix) would leave the update release self-check and any future raw caller with the same trap.

## Evidence

Real CLI on an isolated profile whose only content is `{"agents":{"defaults":{"model":{"primary":"openai/gpt-5"},"models":{"openai/gpt-5":{}}}}}`:

| Command | Base `8d1e59c2fdd` | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `openclaw config validate` | valid | valid |
| `openclaw gateway status` | `(invalid)` for cli and service + `agents.entries` warnings | no config warning |
| `openclaw update status` | `Warning: agents.entries: ... at least one configured agent` | no config warning |
| `openclaw update check-release --json` | `{"ok":false,"reason":"config-invalid: agents.entries: ..."}` | `{"ok":true, ...}` |

Regression test `src/update/check-release.test.ts` ("accepts a config whose agents section has no entries"): red on base, green with the fix. The ACP-binding test in `validation.allowed-values.test.ts` now binds to the implicit `main` agent; with the fix, raw validation reports an unknown `agentId`, as the loaded validator already did. The consumer tests of the raw validator (config validation, doctor shared, update-cli, daemon status, setup runtime/credentials, model catalog) show no new failure versus base; the local update-cli process suites fail identically on base on this host (child TS module resolution) and are left to PR CI.

Production LOC: +3/−3 (`src/config/validation-core.ts`). Tests +10/−1.

prs.title: feat: let agents participate selectively in group conversations
prs.body:
## Problem and motivation

When mention gating is disabled in a group, the primary reply model receives admitted messages and decides whether to participate as part of an agent turn. Many of those messages are exchanges between other people, questions that have already been answered, or chatter where another reply would add little value. Starting the primary agent for every such message creates unnecessary work and conversation noise.

Requiring an explicit mention avoids some of that work but misses indirect invitations and useful opportunities to contribute. A configured Decision Model should make the participation choice using the existing group etiquette, while the primary model keeps generating replies in its usual voice.

## Solution

With the existing default-off Decision assistance setting enabled and a Decision Model configured, assess eligible unmentioned text messages in always-on groups and channels before primary generation.

The assessment receives the current message, reply reference, bounded recent model history, and bounded workspace identity text. Recent history uses the same reader as normal generation, preserving native message-tool calls and their actual delivery results. Identity context uses the existing workspace loader and context formatter, preserving heading/prose `IDENTITY.md` files and configured identity precedence.

History preparation runs inside the existing admitted Decision execution, after the selected model’s effective route limits are known. It reserves space for the current message, identity and question, then uses the existing history selector to keep a bounded suffix with complete tool-call/result pairs. In addition to the shared token-pressure estimate, aggregate state/question and request limits set a conservative UTF-8 byte envelope, checked against the complete serialized batch. Provider-specific encoded-input constraints keep their existing handling. It adds no second catalog preparation or provider hook call. If the required input cannot fit, or all prior context would be omitted, the existing ordinary-reply fallback applies. Diagnostics measure the prepared batch rather than its initial placeholder.

- **Reply:** continue through the ordinary agent generation and delivery path. The turn carries approval as the existing result-required completion policy, and turn context tells the primary model to generate its reply in its usual voice.
- **Silent:** record the incoming message through the existing transcript owner and finish the turn without primary generation.
- **Assessment unavailable:** use the ordinary reply path.

The existing admission, transcript, queue, cancellation, permissions, and delivery owners remain responsible for their normal work. A declined queued source is consumed after persistence, so the recorded input is not retried as an abandoned request. The completion owner uses confirmed current-source delivery evidence. `NO_REPLY` after message-tool delivery prevents duplicate output. An undelivered `NO_REPLY` remains an unfulfilled reply and follows existing bounded generation recovery and failure handling. Source-delivery retries retain that requirement; they do not make another participation choice. Exhausted or refused retries record failure through the existing runner, and system notices retain their existing permission.

## Scope and rollout

This uses the existing Decision assistance Labs flag and configured `decisionModel`; there is no separate participation setting. An already-saved enabled preference also enables this capability after upgrade.

Explicit mentions, commands, media inputs, ambient room events, internal events, and generic CLI backends keep their existing paths. When Decision assistance is disabled or unavailable, the primary model retains its ordinary participation behavior.

Assessments use the selected Decision provider and may incur its normal charges. The provider receives the identity and conversation evidence described above. Each assessment is bounded by the turn timeout and a maximum of 30 seconds.

## Validation

The existing approved-text case reproduced approval followed by primary `NO_REPLY` completing without an answer before the fix, then passed with normal generation recovery and delivery. The existing message-tool case still completes without a duplicate reply. A second revised existing case reproduced queued delivery retry being disabled by the stronger completion policy.

Focused validation covered 168 existing cases across five files. After the final source-receipt consolidation, all 73 affected immediate/queued consumer cases passed in 77.02 seconds. The unchanged terminal-resolution and stranded-recovery suites also passed. No test cases or fixture frameworks were added.

The final messaging type-check graph, formatting, syntax guards, whitespace checks, and source/test line ratchets pass. Independent source review is clean. It also traced private transcript receipts, exhausted retry settlement, and refused retry enqueue through the existing owners. The 180-line allocation covers the excess above the 400-line allowance: 580 net test lines retain participation, persistence, source settlement, delivery and prepared-input coverage. The budget repair extends existing cases without adding test cases or a fixture framework.

The history-input repair passes all 11 existing participation/queue cases, the messaging type-check graph, formatting, syntax guards, whitespace checks, and the runtime import-cycle check. An isolated synthetic SQLite transcript reproduces the prior omission and confirms that the shared model-history reader retains the reply text and matching settled source-delivery receipt in order. Independent review is clean; no tests were added for this repair.

A fresh live assessment reached TypeSafe and received HTTP 400 with token-limit wording; the earlier rejection traces remain unattributed. The budget repair passes 102 existing cases across seven focused files (109.38 seconds). After the final interruption correction, all 89 affected Decision host/native cases passed again (46.40 seconds). Messaging and agents-root type checks, formatting, syntax guards, runtime import-cycle and line ratchets pass. Independent source review is clean.

Live validation of that first budget repair still returned unsupported input. A controlled replay through the existing native Gateway Decision tool then compared reconstructed local history with all fields preserved: the approximate selection (85,580 submitted JSON bytes) was rejected; the byte-bounded selection (26,067 bytes, seven messages with complete paired turns) succeeded with 13,990 provider input tokens. A local protocol comparison confirmed HTTP 400 with token-limit wording for the former and HTTP 200 for the latter. These were reconstructed inputs, not captured copies of the original requests; no channel messages were sent.

The follow-up repair changes one production file (+12/-2) and adds no tests. All 13 existing participation/queue/history cases pass, along with the messaging type graph, formatting, focused guards, whitespace and source-line checks. Independent source review is clean. The byte envelope is conservative, not an exact tokenizer guarantee. Exact-commit package installation and live greeting, contextual follow-up and silent-branch validation remain pending.

prs.title: fix: keep a conversation's OpenAI Responses continuation across background runs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On OpenAI Responses, a background run on a conversation could reset that conversation's request chain. Examples are a skill review fork, memory flush, a `/btw` side question or a compaction summary. The background run reached the transport with the conversation's `sessionId`. It replaced the conversation's continuation baseline with its own request. The conversation's next request then failed the prefix check (`history_changed`). It sent the full history instead of a `previous_response_id` delta. On a busy production host this pattern cost about 14-19M uncached tokens per day (1.75-2.5% of input).

## User Impact

After a background run, the conversation's next request continues with `previous_response_id` and sends only the new input. Background runs keep the conversation's prompt-cache key, so they still read the cached prefix. Nothing changes in config or stored data.

## Why This Change Was Made

`options.sessionId` did two jobs at the transport:

- **Affinity:** the prompt-cache key, the `session_id` / `x-client-request-id` headers and the replay fence. A background run needs these.
- **Ownership:** the key of the HTTP continuation slot, the Responses WebSocket pool and its continuation, and the ChatGPT WebSocket pool, continuation and SSE fallback latch. A background run must not touch these.

The change separates the two jobs:

- `sessionId` now carries **affinity only**. Every caller still sends the same value.
- **Ownership** moves to a branded `ProviderStateScope`, passed as the symbol-keyed stream option `PROVIDER_STATE_SCOPE` (`packages/ai/src/session-resources.ts`). Every mutable store keys on the scope, and a store cannot take a plain string.
- **Without a scope there is no mutable state.** The request sends full input on its own connection. Forks, memory flush, `/btw` and compaction summaries get this with no code at their call sites.
- **Only lane admission mints a scope.** `claimRunProviderState` (`session-bootstrap.ts`) runs right after the writer claim in `lane-controller.ts`. It mints a scope for runs that write the conversation and none for detached runs. The scope reaches the attempt stream and the worker inference runtime (worker-placed turns).
- An oxlint `no-restricted-imports` rule allows `claimConversationProviderState` only in `session-bootstrap.ts`.

**Removed:** `cleanupProviderSessionResourcesOnDispose` and its two opt-outs. `AgentSession.dispose()` freed provider state by the transcript's session id. In a fork that id is the parent's id, so the embedded runner had to turn the cleanup off. Provider state no longer belongs to dispose.

**Kept on purpose:**

- **The prompt-cache tracker key stays as it is.** The tracker is fed the run's own `attempt.sessionId`. A fork's id is `internal-session-effects-<runId>`, so forks never shared the parent's tracker. The planned tracker re-key would change nothing, so it was dropped.
- **`cleanupSessionResources(forkSession.sessionId)` in `session-fork-run.ts` stays.** It frees the fork's own tracker entries.

**Production LOC:** +128 / −40 including the 28-line oxlint rule; TypeScript alone is +100 / −40 (net +60). The growth is the scope type, threading the scope to the attempt and worker paths, re-keying the stores, and the import guard that keeps minting in one place. This is the real number, not padded.

## Evidence

**Prefix journey (#201723): new step "background fork between two parent turns", run on all five transports.** A local test plugin starts a real fork through `api.runtime.subagent.runForkedTurn` between two target turns. The fork's requests are classified apart from the parent's. The step asserts two things:

1. The fork's system prompt and tool list are byte-equal to the parent's.
2. On openai-responses, where the fake provider opts into continuation, the parent's first request after the fork carries the parent's own last response id.

| Transport | base 8d1e59c2fddc | head |
|---|---|---|
| openai-responses | **red**: `expected undefined to be 'resp_2'` (the parent sent full input) | green |
| anthropic-messages, openai-completions, google-generative-ai, bedrock-converse-stream | not run on base. These lanes hold no continuation state, so the step checks fork system/tool bytes and that parent history only appends. | green |

**Transport guard:** the new test "preserves the writer continuation when a scope-less caller shares its session affinity" in `openai-responses-client.continuation.integration.test.ts`.

**Mutations.** Each mutation ran in a scratch copy of head against the guard test and the openai-responses journey:

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| (a) The HTTP continuation slot falls back to keying on `options.sessionId` when no scope is present | **red**: the guard test and the journey both fail |
| (b) Detached runs also get a scope | **survived**: the scope keys on the run's own `sessionId`. Every detached caller uses a private id (`internal-session-effects-<runId>`), so a fork's state stays isolated anyway. The detached rule only stops background runs from holding sockets and slots they never reuse. |
| (c) The attempt does not pass its scope to the stream | **red**: the journey fails (the parent loses continuation) |

**Scratch Gateway E2E.** Native `https://api.openai.com/v1`, `openai/gpt-6.2-astra`, SSE, code mode, the bundled skill-workshop background review. A scratch-only patch captured every request body and its `response.completed` usage. The driver and model are the same on base and head. Rows around the fork:

| request | base: previous_response_id / items / tools / input / cached | head d8c1b568: previous_response_id / items / tools / input / cached |
|---|---|---|
| #15 parent, last request before the fork | yes / 4 / 7 (2b9cd1ba) / 19701 / 18530 | yes / 4 / 7 (2b9cd1ba) / 19711 / 18537 |
| #16 skill-review fork | no / 29 / 6 (ccf4c23c) / 15040 / 0 | no / 29 / 6 (ccf4c23c) / 15047 / 0 |
| #19 parent, next request after the fork | no / 33 / 7 (2b9cd1ba) / 20800 / 18943 | yes / 2 / 7 (2b9cd1ba) / 20814 / 18950 |
| #20 parent | yes / 1 / 7 (2b9cd1ba) / 20972 / 19799 | yes / 1 / 7 (2b9cd1ba) / 20990 / 19810 |
| #22 parent (T3) | yes / 3 / 7 (2b9cd1ba) / 21809 / 20969 | yes / 3 / 7 (2b9cd1ba) / 21830 / 20987 |

- The parent's request after the fork changed from **full history (33 items, no `previous_response_id`) to a continuation (2 items)**. Request bytes for the whole run fell from 670,893 to 617,450.
- On this short conversation, both versions read about the same number of cached tokens (base 18,943, head 18,950). A full replay of the same conversation still hits OpenAI's cache. The token loss on the production host comes from long conversations, where the full replay misses beyond instructions and tools. That number is measured after landing.
- The fork itself still lists 6 tools instead of the parent's 7 (hosted `web_search` is missing), so it reads 0 cached tokens. A separate PR in this series fixes that.

<details><summary>Tests changed</summary>

- 15 packages/ai transport test files: the writer-contract tests now pass a scope. Each still asserts the same continuation, socket and SSE-latch behavior.
- `src/agents/sessions/*` and `attempt-session.test.ts`: fixtures no longer set the removed dispose flag.

</details>

prs.title: fix: let update repair finish after Homebrew cleanup removed retained launcher copies
prs.body:
Related: #197910

## What Problem This Solves

People who installed OpenClaw with Homebrew's Node can get stuck unable to update after a macOS update or reboot. `openclaw update` stops with `update-recovery-pending` ("device number changed only"). The `openclaw update repair` it recommends then fails with `ENOENT ... lstat '<anchor>/launchers'`, so the update can never be settled.

## User Impact

User impact: on Homebrew Node installs, `openclaw update repair` now settles a finished package update even after `brew cleanup` has pruned the update's retained launcher copies, so normal updates can continue. Nothing is republished or rolled back, and the installed package and launchers are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Homebrew's `brew cleanup` runs on its own every 30 days after `brew install` or `brew upgrade`. It walks `HOMEBREW_PREFIX/lib`, deletes every dangling symlink, and then removes the empty directories left behind. The update anchor lives in `lib/node_modules`, and it keeps copies of the npm launchers as relative symlinks (`../lib/node_modules/openclaw/openclaw.mjs`). Those links don't resolve from inside the anchor, so Homebrew deletes them and then the empty `launchers` and `previous-launchers` directories, leaving only `previous`. That is the layout both reporters on #197910 have.

Remount settlement only settles; it never republishes from those directories. It still bound each one's recorded identity, though, and that bind fails with ENOENT once the directory is gone. With this change, an absent launcher root is accepted. A launcher root that is still present must match its recorded identity. Every other check still applies: device-mapping consistency, the helper, the anchor, the journal, the full candidate tree fingerprint, and the live launchers. The fix doesn't accept anything based on its path alone.

Rejected alternative: recreating the launcher roots, or rewriting their recorded identities. That would forge evidence. The updating guide now explains the cause and the new behavior; it previously said no procedure covered this layout.

## Evidence

- Real Homebrew on macOS: `brew cleanup --prune-prefix --dry-run` against a synthetic `/opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules/.openclaw.package-activation-*` printed `Would remove (broken link) …/launchers/openclaw` and `Would remove (empty directory) …/launchers`. The probe directory was removed afterwards.
- A new regression test publishes a real candidate, remaps its devices the way the sibling remount tests do, and applies the same prune Homebrew performs. It fails on the base with the reported `ENOENT lstat <anchor>/launchers` and passes with the fix. It also checks that the live launcher is untouched and that admission is clear afterwards.
- The 17 package activation and publication test files pass (256 tests), as do the update-repair, recovery-command and legacy-recovery tests (88). oxlint, oxfmt and the `tsgo:core` typecheck are clean.
- Review: autoreview (P2) found no actionable findings, and an independent read-only Codex review returned NO FINDINGS.
- Gap: the real APFS device renumbering isn't reproduced. A real remount changes inode numbers too, so the device drift comes from the same synthetic journal remap the existing remount tests use. The test calls the exact public settlement entry point that `openclaw update repair` uses.

Production LOC: +11/−7 (`src/infra/package-update-activation-settlement.ts`). Tests: +33. Docs: +9/−5.

Affected users can apply this once a release contains it: run `openclaw update repair --yes` from that release. If the installed updater is older, use the separately installed settlement-only helper described in the updating guide.
