prs.title: fix: chat-requested updates no longer leave the Gateway stopped
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When someone updates OpenClaw from a chat channel (for example `/update` from a Telegram owner), the managed update could fail partway and leave the Gateway stopped. The update reported "Database rollback could not start … another SQLite connection is active", and the user's assistant stayed offline until someone repaired it by hand.

## User Impact

Chat-requested managed updates finish normally again. If a candidate does fail, database rollback can run and the previous Gateway comes back instead of staying stopped.

## Why This Change Was Made

The detached update helper checks that the chat requester is still a command owner while the Gateway is serving. Because a live Gateway owns the state database, that check reads shared state through a background read worker, and the worker keeps its idle reader open for up to 30 minutes. The helper then waits while the new version's Doctor takes exclusive database access for migration bookkeeping. The helper's idle WAL reader holds a shared lock, so Doctor refused ("another connection still has it open"), and the database rollback that followed refused for the same reason.

The helper's own requester-check entry points (the two `daemon-cli` exports only the handoff helper imports) now release worker-held state connections once the check settles, using the existing drain that exists for exactly this WAL shared-lock case. A failed check keeps its original error, and a failed release is reported with it. The shared requester capture is unchanged, so the updater's own concurrent progress reads are not cancelled.

Updates without a chat requester (Control UI, CLI) never ran this check in the helper and were not affected. The daemon exports the helper imports keep their names. The shared capture underneath is renamed internally (`prepareUpdateRequesterIdentity`), so the export-name check sees one behavior per name and the installed contract does not change.

Related: #203497 rewrites owned global package activation; it does not touch the helper's requester check or state readers, and installs that keep the managed handoff still need this.

## Evidence

A managed update was reproduced end to end and then run again on the fix, using real npm package builds of current `main` (relabelled versions on a local registry) on an AWS Linux box with a systemd user Gateway, started through Gateway `update.run` with a Telegram owner as requester.

On base `8d1e59c2fdd`, the chat-requested update failed with the reported rollback refusal, `/readyz` returned nothing, and the unit was inactive. The same update without a requester succeeded. The failing case was reproduced four times on `2c473901162` before that. `/proc/locks` showed the helper process holding READ locks on `openclaw.sqlite` and its `-shm` for the whole update, about 250 samples. A node:sqlite trace inside the helper tied the connection to its state-read worker, opened during the requester check.

On `fcb54159f8d`, three managed updates succeeded with the Gateway active on the target version:

- main to main with the Telegram owner requester: `/readyz` core-ready. The fake bot token keeps the channel itself unready, as in the harness baseline.
- the same requester with the channel disabled: `/readyz` 200.
- published `2026.11.6` to the fix: also succeeded.

The new test drives both helper entry points against a real state database and then takes native exclusive access. Without the release it fails with `database is locked`; with the fix it passes, 15/15 in the file. An independent Codex review of an earlier revision found two issues: draining in the shared capture could cancel the updater's in-flight progress reads, and a release failure could replace the deferred authority error. That review led to the helper-only placement. The final head has a clean autoreview and an independent review with no findings.


The later head `17bae7685b0` only renames the internal capture and keeps the helper runner untouched against base. The managed-handoff lifecycle suite, which covers profile and configured-owner requester rechecks, passes together with the requester tests (88/88), the export-name check passes, and autoreview is clean.

prs.title: fix: send WhatsApp videos and large media on slow connections
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On a slow upload connection, sending a WhatsApp video (or any media file of a few MB) fails with `Media upload failed on all hosts`, even though text and small images keep working. The agent then falls back to text only, so the user never gets the video they asked for.

## User Impact

User impact: WhatsApp videos, documents and other large media send normally on slow connections instead of failing after a few seconds.

## Why This Change Was Made

Baileys only puts a timeout on an upload socket when the message options carry `mediaUploadTimeoutMs`, and OpenClaw never set it. With no proxy, Baileys then uploads through Node's `https.globalAgent`, whose sockets time out after 5 seconds idle (Node 19+). The OS accepts a multi-MB body into the socket send buffer almost at once, so the socket looks idle while a slow uplink drains it. After 5 seconds Node fires `timeout`, Baileys aborts with `Upload timeout`, the remaining hosts fail to connect over the still-saturated uplink, and the send fails. Small images finish within 5 seconds, which is why only larger media broke.

This change passes a 60-second `mediaUploadTimeoutMs` on every media send, quoted ones included. That replaces the 5-second idle default on the upload socket. Text sends are unchanged. Stickers still go through the structured-send path without the option; they are small enough not to hit this.

## Evidence

**Live:** on a Gateway with about 340 KB/s upstream (OpenClaw 2026.9.7, Baileys 7.0.0-rc14, Node 26), a 4.4 MB H.264 video failed every time. Instrumenting Baileys' per-host upload loop showed the first host failing with `Upload timeout` and the next hosts with `ETIMEDOUT`. With an explicit upload timeout, the same video sent as a normal video in about 14 seconds.

**Repro test, red before the fix and green after:**
- `session.media-upload.test.ts` sends a document through `createWebSendApi`, Baileys' real `generateWAMessage` and its real uploader, using the same option merge as Baileys' socket `sendMessage`, to the existing local HTTPS upload origin. A slow origin answers only after the full body arrives, and `https.globalAgent`'s idle timeout is shortened to keep the test fast. The test first checks that an upload with no timeout fails with `Upload timeout`. The send then delivers with the media URL in the message.
- With the `mediaUploadTimeoutMs` forwarding removed from `send-api.ts`, the send fails with `Upload timeout`. With it, the send passes.

<details>
<summary>Commands</summary>

- `pnpm test extensions/whatsapp/src/session.media-upload.test.ts extensions/whatsapp/src/inbound/send-api.test.ts extensions/whatsapp/src/send.voice-delivery.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 47 passed (the slow-uplink send fails with the timeout forwarding removed)
- `pnpm test:extension whatsapp`: 1,059 passed
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig extensions/tsconfig.json extensions/whatsapp`: passed
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p extensions/whatsapp/tsconfig.json --noEmit` and `-p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json --noEmit`: passed
- oxfmt: clean

`pnpm check:changed` was killed for running out of memory on my machine, so the gates above were run individually; PR CI runs the full set.

</details>

prs.title: fix: let people finish Mac setup without an unsupported remote-access step
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

In macOS app builds that package the native OpenClaw ID transport (`OPENCLAW_IROH_NATIVE=1`), local setup ends with a **Reach it from anywhere?** step. Its only button, **Sign in with OpenClaw ID**, is enabled, but the action behind it is not implemented in the app, so every click ends in "Setup did not finish." The final summary then invites the person back to the same step with a **Reach it from anywhere · Learn more** row.

## User Impact

User impact: someone who sets up OpenClaw on this Mac goes straight from **Connect your AI** to **You’re all set!**, which says **Running on this Mac**. They no longer see a button that cannot work. Back from the summary returns to AI setup. Turning on remote access stays an explicit choice after setup, through the existing Dashboard account-menu action (**Turn on remote access**). That action already checks whether this claw can use it and explains when it cannot. The remote paths are unchanged: **On another computer**, OpenClaw ID sign-in, node invitations, and invite links.

## Why This Change Was Made

A packaged transport does not mean the app can make a Mac reachable. Both onboarding services answered the remote-reach request by throwing `featureUnsupported`, so the step only showed a failure. This change removes the local remote-reach page, its summary row, the **Not now** title, and the unused remote-reach request and result. Local setup now has the same steps whether or not the transport is packaged. Remote and invite page orders stay the same. The WebUI already offers remote access only as an explicit action after setup, so it needs no change.

## Evidence

**Base reproduction** (`main` cc849dd810e, built with `OPENCLAW_IROH_NATIVE=1` against a locally built arm64 `OpenClawIrohFFI` slice). A temporary test, not committed, drove the production `OnboardingOpenClawIDSignInService` through the real `OnboardingOpenClawIDModel`:

```
N01-BASE pageOrder(local)=[0, 1, 3, 5, 9] unavailable=nil account=nil error=Setup did not finish. Try again or continue without OpenClaw ID.
```

The reach page (5) was in the local path, its button was enabled because no unavailable reason applied, and clicking it always failed.

**After** (same packaged build mode): local order is `[0, 1, 2, 3, 9]` or `[0, 1, 3, 9]`. 76 tests passed in the focused onboarding suites: `OnboardingViewSmokeTests`, `OnboardingOpenClawIDTests`, `OnboardingOpenClawIDSignInTests`, `OnboardingOpenClawIDMemberJoinTests`, `OnboardingNodeInvitationServiceTests`, `OnboardingPageTests`, `OnboardingFirstRunTests`, and both render suites. Those suites cover the remote `[0, 1, 4, 3, 9]`, joined-claw, and Set up later orders. The new regression test `local setup goes from AI setup to the summary in every build` asserts the local orders; the packaged base produces `[0, 1, 3, 5, 9]` instead, so this test fails there.

### Clean comparison — final summary, local setup

| Before (main, packaged transport) | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: summary shows Reach it from anywhere with Learn more](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/62a61af5-0845-40f5-8c3e-34b4453f31e3) | ![After: summary shows Running on this Mac](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2fe18c4b-a2b0-42f2-8486-349ad46f14a2) |

### Annotated comparison

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Remote-reach row highlighted in the before summary](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d9e0d670-78bf-4109-b571-98e5dfec86ad) | ![Local-only summary row highlighted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8a69da73-6f38-4bfa-b264-720e60a60860) |

### Removed step (before only; it no longer exists)

| Reach page on main | Annotated | After clicking Sign in with OpenClaw ID |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ![Reach it from anywhere page with enabled Sign in button](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/55e955a7-8119-4c3f-9a6e-a6c73e08dea3) | ![Sign in button highlighted as enabled but always failing](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7490b7ec-038b-49d9-8cc1-b7a2d4ff1cf3) | ![Sheet shows Setup did not finish](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f3fb3624-8d9f-4b66-be04-6b13ab5f336a) |

These captures come from `OnboardingRenderTests` and a production-service sheet render: the real page views with fixture app state, the default 630×752 content rectangle, and navigation omitted. Before is cc849dd810e and after is this branch, both built with `OPENCLAW_IROH_NATIVE=1`. Rendering ran in the repository's native render sandbox (`scripts/macos-health-render.sb`), with no network, private HOME and state, and no preferences or Keychain access. "Launch at login · Unavailable under profile" appears because the sandbox uses a named profile.

<details><summary>Checks run and gaps</summary>

- `OPENCLAW_IROH_NATIVE=1 swift build --package-path apps/macos --build-system native --build-tests` built on both base and branch.
- Focused sandboxed run: the suites listed above, 76 passed and 0 failed.
- `scripts/format-swift.sh macos`: clean. `scripts/lint-swift.sh macos`: 0 violations.
- `pnpm native:i18n:baseline` regenerated the inventory, removing only the strings for the deleted step and row. `pnpm native:i18n:verify` passed.
- Not run locally: the default (unpackaged) app build and the full macOS native suite. CI's `macos-swift` job covers them. This change has no packaging-dependent code paths, but CI will confirm the default build.
- Not exercised: the Dashboard **Turn on remote access** flow against a live OpenClaw ID backend. It is unchanged here.
- Simplification: removed the local reach page, its view, the summary row, the `openClawIDEnabled` page-order switch, the `.makeReachable` intent, and the `.reachable` result. Diff: 24 insertions, 114 deletions.

</details>

prs.title: fix(gateway): scope the JSONL transcript usage estimate to the live window across boundaries
prs.body:
Refs #150579

## What Problem This Solves

A compacted session's transcript usage report (the JSONL artifact seam behind diagnostic reads) counted the whole append-only archive as live context. Content superseded by a compaction or reset stays in the file, and the chars-based estimate summed every user/assistant message ever written, so the reported total kept growing across clean compactions while the model's actual context stayed small.

A second gap sat next to it: once the estimate restarted at a boundary, eligibility was re-derived only from model-tagged assistant entries in the retained window. A summary-only window (the cut names an entry outside the message window) or a retained-user-only window (overflow compaction with a pending user message as its tail) lost the estimate until the next assistant reply, even though the summary and retained text were sitting in the model context.

## Root cause

`aggregateSessionTranscriptUsage` fills `totalTokens` from a chars estimate when no per-call usage snapshot provides one. `readLatestSessionUsageFromTranscriptFileAsync` feeds it the full JSONL transcript, and the estimate accumulated `estimatedTranscriptChars` over the whole scanned set with no notion of boundary markers or the retained window they name. The boundary restart also reset `sawEstimateModelIdentity` from the retained entries alone, while `finish()` requires that flag, so any window without a surviving model-tagged assistant reported no estimate at all.

## Fix

- The JSONL reader passes `compaction`/`reset` boundary records through with their `summary`/`firstKeptEntryId` fields, and forwards each entry's id, instead of skipping markers.
- The accumulator keeps per-entry char counts for the current window. At a boundary it keeps the retained tail named by `firstKeptEntryId` plus the compaction summary, matching the model-context contract (compactionSummary + retained entries + post-boundary messages) and the transcript tree selector's fallback (an unknown kept target drops the pre-boundary window). The previous revision restarted the estimate at zero, which undercounts a compacted session that retains a large summary or window.
- A boundary leaves the window estimate-eligible whenever it holds counted text. A compaction or reset marker is only written by a live model session, so requiring a model-tagged assistant to survive the cut only masked reads taken between the boundary and the next reply.
- Usage snapshots (input/output/cache/cost) still aggregate over the whole record, and a fresh per-call `totalTokens` snapshot still wins over any estimate, unchanged.

## Scope

This change lives entirely in the JSONL artifact seam: `readLatestSessionUsageFromTranscriptFileAsync` reads bounded transcript artifacts and its callers are diagnostic paths. The live budget-preflight path from #150579 reads the SQLite seam, which already scopes to the active context and is untouched here; that preflight symptom stays with #150579 and the PRs addressing it directly. This branch does not close the issue.

## Evidence

- New regressions in `session-usage-estimate.test.ts`: a compaction keeps its 500-char summary plus the 2000-char retained message named by `firstKeptEntryId` while dropping the 4000-char superseded prefix; a reset keeps its named retained tail; an unknown kept target drops the pre-boundary window but still counts the summary. Three further regressions end the transcript right at the boundary (summary-only window, compaction retaining only user messages, reset retaining only user text), covering the read between the boundary and the next assistant reply; earlier versions of these tests appended that reply, which masked the eligibility drop.
- Red/green: the boundary-terminal three fail on the previous head (no estimate reported). The consolidated table preserves all 10 independent scenarios, including snapshot precedence, reset boundaries, retained-user-only windows and the structural anchor.

prs.title: fix(telegram): sibling bot's deleted stream previews corrupt group history
prs.body:
Closes #164958

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: in a group running two OpenClaw bots, one bot's streamed reasoning preview (the 🧠 draft) is recorded into the other bot's persistent message cache as an ordinary message. Telegram never delivers message deletions to other bots, so when the streaming side deletes the superseded preview, every sibling cache keeps its copy. From then on, each group turn's history window carries that foreign reasoning text, and Anthropic rejects the whole turn with `reasoning_extraction`. The issue's live capture shows the orphaned preview surviving in cache long after it disappeared from Telegram.

## User Impact

User impact: multi-bot Telegram groups stop breaking on streamed reasoning previews. Once a preview is confirmed deleted, every account's history cache drops it, so later turns no longer inherit dead draft text from a sibling bot. No config change or migration is needed. The fix handles deletions observed after deployment and does not claim to clean up pre-existing orphans.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix tracks previews precisely instead of classifying by content, which is the direction the review discussion on the issue called for. The draft stream is the one component that knows the exact message id of a superseded preview, and it already waits for Telegram to confirm the delete. It now reports that id through a new `onPreviewRetired` callback, and the dispatch layer fans the retirement out to every configured account's message cache, including the sender's own (its cache recorded the preview too). Each cache drops the entry from the live map and the persisted store: retained group history through a compare-and-delete loop, bounded private-chat history through a map delete plus store delete. Nothing keys on message text, prefixes, or usernames, so ordinary bot messages are never misclassified. If Telegram rejects or never confirms the delete, nothing is retired, because the preview may still be visible and its history copies are then still honest.

## Evidence

- New `preview-retirement.test.ts`: two accounts each holding the same preview id in group (retained) and private (bounded) history, fan-out retires it from both and keeps neighboring messages; a single-account config with no `channels.telegram` section still covers the implicit default account.
- New cache tests: `retireMessage` evicts from the live map and the persisted store, a reopened bucket does not resurrect the entry, repeat retirement returns false, non-native ids are rejected, and other chats with the same message id are untouched.
- New draft-stream tests: `onPreviewRetired` fires exactly once after a confirmed supersede delete, and never fires when the delete is rejected or returns unconfirmed.
- Review round 4 follow-ups (head 8e35a3e79d5, rebased onto current main a134038ad7f): retirement fan-out now keys on the Bot API chat type carried from the inbound message instead of the `-100` id prefix, so a basic group whose id was recycled into the supergroup space stays account-local; `record()` and `retireMessage` serialize per cache key through a writer chain shared across all cache instances over the same bucket, so a record in flight while retirement lands from a separate fan-out handle can no longer write the preview back; the persisted tombstone settles before retirement reports done, keeping the fence across restarts. New regression tests cover the recycled-id basic group, channel fan-out, unknown chat type staying local, and both store paths racing retirement mid-write.
- `pnpm vitest run extensions/telegram/src/preview-retirement.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/message-cache.retained.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 24 passed. The same command over `message-cache.test.ts` and `draft-stream.test.ts`: 64 passed. oxfmt and oxlint passed on the five touched files.
- Earlier head `c3677719ea19cfb0f1c7461c70a535153adb4634` had green CI. Current head `3afe346625f` merges current main `e3e615b7115d2b1ee0744f1f40e6819cfe8a6005` without conflicts and allocates the PR's actual 592 added regression lines through the repository's test-lines mechanism. The first 14-line estimate from a sparse local tree was insufficient: authoritative CI still reported 543 lines over, so the allocation was corrected to the full 592 and pushed normally. Hosted CI on this new head is required; the live and upgrade gaps below remain open.

- New cross-instance regression in `message-cache.retained.test.ts`: two cache handles over the same bucket, one recording and one retiring the same key. The retire from the second handle completes its fence and delete before the first handle's compare commits; without the shared writer queue the stale observation resurrects the preview. This test fails on the previous per-instance chains and passes after moving `keyWriteChains` onto the shared bucket.
- New persisted-eviction regression: 3,000 rows are seeded with message 1 and preview 2. Reading message 1 makes it newest in memory, then row 3001 evicts preview 2 from the memory LRU while SQLite evicts message 1 by creation order. Retirement previously returned false and left preview 2 persisted; it now deletes the persisted key independently of memory membership and the reopened cache stays empty. Current verification across `message-cache.test.ts`, `message-cache.retained.test.ts`, `preview-retirement.test.ts`, and `draft-stream.test.ts`: 79 passed. oxfmt and type-aware oxlint pass on the changed files.

Gap I want to be explicit about: I could not stage the live two-bot Anthropic reproduction locally, so the end-to-end proof rides on the issue's live capture for the failure side and on the cache/draft-layer tests above for the fix side. The retirement path itself is covered at every layer it touches; a maintainer with two bots can confirm in one group turn by watching the sibling's cache stay empty after the preview is deleted. Latest-stable upgrade evidence with existing history and settings is also still open.

prs.title: fix(codex): record rejected dynamic-tool cleanup on ordinary runs
prs.body:
Fixes #177298

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: ordinary Codex runs silently discard a registered dynamic-tool cleanup rejection, so the existing cleanup diagnostics never report the failed cleanup. Only one-shot CLI runs currently report the same rejection.

## User Impact

Operators can diagnose rejected dynamic-tool cleanup during ordinary Codex runs through the existing `step=codex-dynamic-tool-cleanup` warning. The primary attempt result, final reply, once-only disposal, and subsequent MCP cleanup remain unchanged. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

`run-attempt-tool-setup.ts` forwarded collected cleanup rejections only when `params.oneShotCliRun` was true. The existing cleanup settlement owner already records and logs a rejection without rethrowing it, so the one-shot condition only hid ordinary-run failures. This change removes that condition and uses the same reporting path for both run kinds.

## Evidence

- The new ordinary-run regression drives a registered cleanup rejection without `oneShotCliRun`. The attempt resolves normally, cleanup runs once, and the warning contains `step=codex-dynamic-tool-cleanup error=Codex tool cleanup failed`. Restoring the old condition makes this regression fail because no warning is recorded.
- Exact-head focused validation: `npx vitest run extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.test.ts --project extension-database-workers` passed 127/127. `pnpm tsgo:extensions` and `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` both passed.
- [Independent corroboration](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177317#issuecomment-6267352626) against official base `dfc18caabc9f44d98e14d6250dd411d45096007a` plus the equivalent one-line correction passed 166 tests across four owner files, including primary-error preservation and subsequent MCP disposal. That run did not execute this PR's exact head.
- [Independent shipped-entry corroboration](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177317#issuecomment-6268783254) used an ordinary Gateway run, the pinned native Codex 0.162.1 executable, the shipped computer plugin, an isolated synthetic Unix-socket driver, and a loopback mock Responses endpoint. The successful-close control preserved the final reply with zero cleanup warnings; the rejected-close case preserved the final reply with one `codex-dynamic-tool-cleanup` warning. This also used the official base plus the equivalent correction, not this PR's exact head.
- Exact-head shipped-entry validation on `32336c4969205c8c75ceada92eb7c916d423fee9` used the normal QA runtime, ordinary `chat.send`/`agent.wait` Gateway runs, the pinned native Codex 0.162.1 executable, and the shipped computer plugin against isolated synthetic endpoints. The successful-close control completed with the final reply preserved and zero cleanup warnings; rejected close completed with the final reply preserved and one `codex-dynamic-tool-cleanup` warning matched to that run. The QA case passed in 103.66 seconds, and the owned Gateway was confirmed stopped.
- The reviewed head's changed-test, lint, and type-check CI lanes passed. The PR-context failure was a required-heading violation in this body, not a production-code failure.
- Merge head `cd7e2c0641791a711414d706d0870c15ec467af8` integrates current main `e3e615b7115d2b1ee0744f1f40e6819cfe8a6005` without conflicts. The net diff remains the same two owner files. Static test-line accounting on the merge result is 6,533,820 lines against a 6,534,366 ceiling, leaving 546 lines of slack; the previous 112-line overage is resolved by the current baseline. Hosted CI on this merge head is required and tracked separately.

The exact-head QA run used an allowlisted fresh environment with no management credentials, a synthetic Unix-socket computer driver, and a loopback mock Responses endpoint. It did not contact a live model provider or control a real desktop. The test-only QA fixture remains local and is not part of the PR diff.

prs.title: fix: keep the first setup and chat free of automatic side panels
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Someone who had the Home side panel open on an earlier visit (or in the macOS app's saved window state) and then sets OpenClaw up again gets that panel imposed on them: Home opens beside the model setup page and the onboarding conversation, and after **Exit setup** the first chat opens with an empty Ask OpenClaw panel docked on the right plus the community promotion card in the sidebar. The first conversation starts cramped and full of things that do not help connect or chat.

## User Impact

User impact: during first-run setup and the first chat it opens, the side panel stays closed until the person opens it from the menu, button, or Mod+Shift+H. The chat shows the agent, the composer with attachments, connection status, help, and the rest of the app; the community card waits for the next open. Saved panel preferences are not rewritten, so an established user who reopens the app gets their panel back.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shell records one fact when it shows a first-use setup route (`/settings/model-setup?firstRun=1|explicit` or `/custodian?onboarding=1`, the same markers the first-run redirect and onboarding already use). For the rest of that page:

- the assistant dock does not restore its saved open state and does not auto-minimize the onboarding conversation into the dock when setup ends (by a real reply that hands off, or by Exit setup); an automatic close request does not overwrite the saved choice;
- any explicit open or close (menu, sidebar Home button, shortcut, palette, plugin activation, update-failure triage) works as before and releases the hold;
- the sidebar does not show the community invitation.

Home availability still follows `chat.history` (`isHomePanelAvailable` is unchanged), and send errors, setup errors, and the channel nudge stay visible. The macOS app hosts this same UI; no native code changes.

Accepted edge: the quiet state lasts for that page (window) session. Reloading in the middle of the first chat restores the saved preference; on the default first chat (`/chat/main`) Home is already the page's own conversation, so it stays closed there anyway.

## Evidence

Scenario: a saved `open` Home dock preference, then first-run model setup → onboarding (one real turn) → Exit setup → first chat, against the mocked Gateway at 1280×800, dark theme. Before = `origin/main` @ cc849dd810e; after = this branch.

### Clean comparison

**Model setup**

| --- | --- |
| ![Before: Home panel open beside model setup](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5acf2a8b-e43e-44cc-a637-3efdf67c4565) | ![After: model setup without a side panel](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/04a9e7c4-95f4-4bc4-a25d-051dd67e8612) |

**Onboarding conversation**

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: Home panel open beside onboarding](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8f813ed2-454c-47e7-a0fb-1101de45956a) | ![After: onboarding without a side panel](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4bacee94-0333-4d36-b736-54088b62bc0b) |

**First chat after Exit setup**

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: empty Ask OpenClaw panel and community card in the first chat](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/63a76c07-8e33-4252-8e57-a19ca3fac314) | ![After: first chat with only the conversation and composer](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9e131730-81f1-4a63-8b49-c0d39427688d) |

### Annotated comparison

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Home panel opening on its own during setup highlighted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e5e0e7b0-6bc3-4701-b537-051b9e68b906) | ![Setup without a panel highlighted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8f7a1ab4-3779-4d97-9552-3ac436b22abe) |
| ![Automatic Ask OpenClaw dock and promotion in the first chat highlighted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6f5f58f8-a6ca-4a8a-b6cc-c0cebd2e3245) | ![First chat without panel or promotion highlighted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1f9dcdb1-33fa-48b6-b47b-f9c08345612c) |

Behavior checks (new `ui/src/e2e/first-use-home-panel.e2e.test.ts`, red on `origin/main`, green here), run for the web app and with the macOS web-chrome host flags:

- setup and onboarding: side panel closed despite the saved `open` preference;
- first chat: no side panel and no community card; composer and **Add attachment** present; `/help` shows the command list without sending; a rejected `chat.send` stays visible as **Not sent**; the saved preference is byte-for-byte unchanged;
- reopening on another session restores the open Home panel (established preference);
- Mod+Shift+H during setup opens Home.

<details><summary>Commands</summary>

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts --configLoader runner ui/src/e2e/first-use-home-panel.e2e.test.ts` — base: 3 failed; branch: 3 passed
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/components/assistant-panel.test.ts ui/src/app/app-shell-navigation.test.ts ui/src/app/invalid-deep-link.test.tsx ui/src/app/app-host.test.ts ui/src/app/app-host.panel-toggles.test.ts ui/src/app/app-host.dock-suppression.test.ts ui/src/app/app-shell-view.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 91 passed
- `pnpm tsgo:ui`, `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig tsconfig.ui.json <changed files>`, `node scripts/run-format.mts`, `pnpm check:control-ui-controllers` — clean
- Local autoreview (branch vs `origin/main`, P0–P2): scoped-clean

</details>

Not run locally (left for CI): full `tsgo` / test-file typecheck shards, the full UI E2E and unit suites. The macOS check emulates the app's web-chrome host flags in Chromium; the native app itself was not launched.

### Maintainer verification

The exact PR integrated with current main passed five production Chromium scenarios and 91 focused UI tests in Studio. This covered a 390 px automatic onboarding handoff and reopening after explicitly closing Home, in addition to the original web and simulated macOS host cases. UI types, the controller guard, and all 13 baseline ratchets passed. The [PR's three first-use cases also passed in hosted CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45048420402/job/137288468219). These checks use a mocked Gateway.

The [CI attempt](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45048420402) contains an unrelated ripgrep download HTTP 403 and browser assertions for compact search, sign-in and model auth that match scheduled main. The [Automations browser timeout](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45048420402/job/137288468069) occurred in a fresh browser context that opened Automations directly. The browser was connected on that route, and the test timed out waiting for the schedule picker before the MCP config read. This PR's new Home behavior only activates after a first-use setup route; the Automations editor, its route handling, and the fixture are unchanged. The two Automations cases passed on both the exact CI base and the tested merge; the hosted timing trigger was not reproduced. The findings here describe the scope of the CI failure, not a fix to Automations.

prs.title: fix(talk): voice-only sessions never get the daily session reset
prs.body:
Closes #185942

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: with `session.reset` set to `daily` (or `idle`), Talk voice consults never apply the reset. Typed messages evaluate session freshness and roll the session over; a voice consult reuses whatever session exists, so a voice-only user keeps sending previous days' history on every consult (the reporter saw about 110k prompt tokens per request) until they happen to type.

## User Impact

User impact: a voice consult on a session past its reset boundary now rolls the session over in place before it runs (same session id, a reset boundary in its transcript), so it no longer replays expired context. This applies to browser Talk, meetings, voice calls and FaceTime, which share the consult runtime.

- Automatic resets triggered by voice consults keep queued user requests; typed-chat resets, explicit `/new` / `/reset` and Stop keep their existing cancellation behavior.
- The reset runs in the session controller's lane (it waits for work on the old session instead of cancelling it). Cancellation, caller authority and the Access program are checked before native cleanup starts. Once admitted, the reset settles even if the call closes.
- When the session-memory hook is enabled, the ended day reaches session memory: the excerpt is captured before the reset and published with `session:auto-reset` after it (the bundled session-memory hook saves its usual excerpt, 15 messages by default, as for typed chat).
- Short session keys (`voice:consult`) reset the same stored row that consults read.
- Grants of the ended conversation do not carry over: `clearRotatedSessionMetadata`, the helper every in-place rollover uses (voice, Gateway agent turns, the CLI agent command), now also drops native-runtime consent, the elevated level, the active goal and pending worktree/project intents, as typed rollover's retained state already does. The Gateway and CLI automatic resets had the same gap; their reset suites pass unchanged.
- The consult's own surface picks the `resetByChannel` override, as a typed turn's ingress channel does: browser Talk `webchat`, phone and FaceTime `voice` (both send `voice`, so `resetByChannel.voice` covers both). A stored delivery route only routes replies.
- Native agent harnesses (ACP) restart their conversation just before the reset commits, as on a typed reset; once admitted, the reset finishes even if the call closes, so the two stay in step; coding-tool (CLI) session ids are cleared with the reset, as on a typed reset.

Limits:
- A voice reset ends the agent's context, not the live call's tools: unlike a typed reset it does not close the session's MCP servers or browser tabs, and it does not fire the plugin `session_end` / `session_start` hooks or shutdown tracking, which voice never fired on main.
- Session sharing is not re-checked per consult. On main, consults that arrive as Talk RPCs are refused at RPC ingress for a caller who lost participation, while Gateway-held consults (browser Talk tool calls run by the Gateway, relay-delegated consults) run the agent with the call's retained authority and no participation check (`client-agent-consult.ts` `assertConsultCurrent`, `client-run-authority.ts`, `prepareAgentRunAdmission`). The reset uses those same guards plus the Access program, so it adds no access the following run lacks; a per-consult participation check at the call owner is a separate follow-up.
- A spoken transcript saved before the consult counts as activity, so an idle window can be extended by the speech that ends it; tracked in #191870. The daily reset is unaffected.
- After a reset, only the agent stops receiving the old history. The realtime voice model keeps the history it was given when the call started, until the call ends; a call started after the boundary still gets the previous history at startup.
- If reloading the call's history fails right after a reset, the consult that triggered the reset fails and can be asked again; the next consult retries the reload.
- When typed chat or another Talk call rolls the session over, an open call keeps sending the agent the history it loaded at call start; only a reset this call applies reloads it.
- Each consult that reaches session preparation counts as activity for the idle reset, including one the model preflight then refuses (a caller allowed to use Talk but not the selected model).
- The native harness (ACP) restart is covered only by the storage test, which verifies the harness-reset call through a mock; it does not prove an external ACP conversation restarted. The live run uses an OpenAI agent model.
- Two consults that both read the stale session at once: the second can fail when the first has already reset it, and can be asked again.

## Why This Change Was Made

`consultRealtimeVoiceAgent` (`src/talk/agent-consult-runtime.ts`) prepared the session entry without any freshness evaluation. It now asks the freshness owner typed turns use (`resolveSessionEntryResetFreshnessAsync`, read-only) whether a reset is due, treating a reset owed by a deferred rollover as due, as typed setup does, and if so resets the entry on the call's own store with `resetSessionEntryLifecycle`, inside `runSessionMutation` (`kind: "reset"`, policy `wait`), re-checking freshness after the wait so a session that became active meanwhile is left alone. Cancellation, caller authority and the Access program are checked before native cleanup starts; once admitted, the reset settles even if the call closes, and the entry check at the write rejects a session changed meanwhile (the Access check is `assertOperatorAccessProgramAllowed` on the entry re-read after the wait); the new session's start time is taken when the replacement entry is built, after any wait for the old turn. Inside the lane it re-reads the entry and stops if the session changed, is model-locked or blocked. It captures the session-memory excerpt, then admits the reset once, before any effect: cancellation, caller authority and the Access program on the re-read entry. An admitted reset then settles even if the call closes, so the native conversation and the transcript stay in step: it restarts native harness conversations through the Gateway's harness cleanup (`resetSessionAgentHarnesses`, with the agent's retained registries; a harness-declared cleanup failure stops the reset so it stays due, other hook failures are logged by the registry, as for typed and Gateway resets), commits the reset (the entry check still rejects a changed or blocked session), then publishes the excerpt with `emitSessionAutoResetHook`. The reset targets the store's qualified key (`resolveSqliteSessionKey`, which reads use). `clearCommittedSessionResetRuntimeState` takes `preserveControllerInputs` so the reset keeps waiting inputs. Browser Talk then reloads the call's history (`client-agent-consult.ts`), and a failed reload is retried on the next consult. The plugin SDK keeps its consult contract; the internal callbacks, authority are not part of it.

Not changed: typed chat, the reset policy, explicit reset and Stop.

Upgrade: no stored-data format changes. Existing sessions need nothing new: the live proof creates the session with released OpenClaw 2026.11.6 and then runs this change on that state.

## Evidence

### Live run: full-product repro on `main` and the same run on this change

Built Gateway, a real browser Talk call (headless Chrome, WebRTC, OpenAI realtime with `brain: agent-consult`) and an OpenAI agent model, with the bundled session-memory hook on (`llmSlug: false`). Day one: released OpenClaw 2026.11.6 with `session.reset: { mode: "daily", atHour: 4 }`, one typed session asked to remember "PELICAN-DAY1". The Gateway clock then moves two days ahead and the call asks aloud: "Check with your agent: what code word did I ask you to remember earlier in this conversation? If you have none, answer none." Both runs use the same day-one state, on `main` `f02d9dc2725` and on `main` plus this change.

```
main:        agent request carried 20 messages including "PELICAN-DAY1"
             spoken answer: "PELICAN-DAY1"
             session memory: no file saved (no reset happened)
this change: agent request carried 7 messages (the exchanges the reset keeps and the question), no "PELICAN-DAY1"
             spoken answer: "none"
             session memory: memory/2026-11-24-0328.md saved for the ended conversation, containing
             'user: "Please remember this code word for later: PELICAN-DAY1. Reply only with OK."'
```

Proof artifice: the Gateway clock is shifted two days with a preload, and the spoken question is synthesized speech (OpenAI TTS) played into headless Chrome.

### Tests

- `src/talk/agent-consult-runtime.storage.test.ts` › "configured session reset": a stale daily session is reset on the call's own store and a same-day one is not; a reset owed by an earlier rollover (`updatedAt: 0`) is applied, also with automatic resets off; a blocked stale session is left for admission to reject; earlier queued input is kept; a caller that cancels or loses its authority during preparation, or whom the session's Access program refuses, leaves the session and its native harness untouched; a reset already in native cleanup finishes when the caller cancels or closes the call; each consult counts as activity; with the bundled session-memory hook registered, a daily reset saves a memory file holding the message the reset dropped from view, and the other rows save none; a short session key resets the qualified row; a phone consult (`voice`) with `resetByChannel.voice` off keeps its session; each reset restarts native harness conversations once. On `main` the reset, owed-reset, queue, authority and activity cases fail; the same-day, blocked and cancel cases pass, as they describe unchanged behavior.
- `src/gateway/talk/client-agent-consult.terminal-writes.test.ts` › "stops quoting call-start history once a consult rolls the session over": through the real browser runner and consult runtime, neither the resetting consult nor the next one quotes the call-start history. On `main` it fails (`expected [ true, true ] to deeply equal [ false, false ]`).
- With this change both suites pass, along with the Talk handler, consult-admission, mailbox, reset-cleanup and consult-runtime suites. Final-content bench checks found no PR-caused failures; two checks (Plugin SDK surface budget, dead-export scan) fail identically on the base. Test lines are net +276 against `main`: the reset is new runtime code with distinct guards, each a separate failure (owed reset, short key, channel policy, Access refusal, cancellation and lost authority before and during native cleanup, queue preservation, saved memory, native harness restart, activity), folded into the existing table-driven storage suite (its real per-store session fixture and consult runtime are reused, no new helper), plus one browser test in the existing terminal-writes suite for the history the agent receives; the earlier 169-line browser parity test was dropped because the storage suite covers its cases.

prs.title: fix(agents): keep bundle MCP access for turns woken by an exec completion
prs.body:
Closes #183589

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: when a backgrounded host exec exits and `tools.exec.notifyOnExit` (default `true`) wakes the originating session, the woken turn has no bundle MCP tools although the run that started the exec had them (Code Mode telemetry `sources: {openclaw: 51, mcp: 0}`, `tools.effective` notice `mcp-not-yet-connected`), and any child spawned from that woken turn inherits the restriction.

## User Impact

User impact: a turn woken by an exec completion keeps exactly the MCP access of the run that started the exec, and children it spawns do too: an unrestricted run keeps every configured server, a run capped to `fixture__*` wakes a turn that can reach only the `fixture` server, an exact-name policy such as `fixture__read` keeps only that tool. Runs with no `mcp.servers`, or whose cap excludes bundle MCP tools, behave exactly as before, so a woken turn never gains access the producer run did not have. No config, schema, or wire change; `notifyOnExit` no longer has to be disabled to keep MCP in long-lived sessions.

## Why This Change Was Made

`createOpenClawCodingTools` (assembled in `src/agents/agent-tools.assembly.ts`) builds each tool's Gateway caller with a default `sessionEventSourcePolicy` whose `toolsAllow` lists the finalized coding tools. Bundle MCP tools are materialized afterwards (`attempt-bundle-tools.ts`), so no `server__tool` name or `bundle-mcp` marker is ever in that list. The exec tool records the policy as the completion event's `producerPolicy`; `captureSessionEventTarget` intersects the woken turn's `toolsAllow` with it; `shouldCreateBundleMcpRuntimeForAttempt` then finds no bundle name and creates no MCP runtime for the woken turn or its children.

The fix captures the producer's final surface instead of predicting it (revision 5). `createOpenClawCodingTools` now fills a caller-owned array (`sessionEventToolsAllowRef`) with the coding tool names and hands that same array to every Gateway caller as `sessionEventSourcePolicy.toolsAllow`. The embedded attempt (`attempt-bundle-tools.ts`) appends the bundled MCP/LSP tools that survived the attempt's runtime allowlist, `applyFinalEffectiveToolPolicy`, and schema projection, by exact name, in the same place it already captures the cron creator cap and the spawn allowlist. The exec tool reads the policy when it records the completion, so the woken turn gets exactly the tools this run could call:

- sender-scoped denials (`tools.toolsBySender["id:alice"].deny: ["admin__*"]`) already removed `admin__reset` from the producer's final surface, so the senderless woken turn never sees it;
- intersected caps, partial globs (`fixture__read*` ∩ `fixture__*All`), and namespace-reaching globs (`fixture*`) are resolved by the existing runtime matcher on real tools, not approximated;
- a refresh replaces the previously appended bundled names, so a tool quarantined or filtered on refresh drops out;
- no marker or glob is ever added, so the continuation cannot widen past the producer.

The surface stays under the existing 512-name bound the target reader enforces (`SESSION_EVENT_TOOLS_ALLOW_LIMIT`, now exported from `session-event-target.ts`); past it, the attempt logs a warning and the woken turn keeps only the coding tools. Revision 5 deletes `agent-tools.session-event-policy.ts` and its tests (revisions 1–4 projected MCP access from allow patterns, which the review showed cannot preserve denials or every glob shape).

## Evidence

Regression in `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-bundle-tools.test.ts` (`session event tool surface`, 9 cases through `prepareEmbeddedAttemptBundleTools` with `fixture` and `admin` servers materializing `fixture__read`, `fixture__readAll`, `fixture__write`, `admin__reset`; each captured cap is then run through the woken turn's `intersectSessionEventToolsAllow` → `shouldCreateBundleMcpRuntimeForAttempt` → `applyEmbeddedAttemptToolsAllow`):

- unrestricted producer → all four MCP tools; `["exec", "fixture__*"]` and `["exec", "fixture*"]` → the three fixture tools; `["exec", "fixture__read"]` → `fixture__read`;
- intersected `[["exec", "fixture__read*"], ["exec", "fixture__*All"]]` → `fixture__readAll` (revision 4 returned nothing here);
- `["read", "exec"]` → no MCP tool and no bundle runtime in the woken turn;
- producer final policy drops `admin__reset` (the sender-scoped denial shape) → the woken turn never admits it;
- refresh after a projection drops `fixture__readAll` → the cap shrinks to `["exec", "fixture__read"]`;
- a coding surface at the bound → MCP names are not appended.

Red on `main`: the attempt never appends to the cap, so every case expecting an MCP tool fails, the reported loss.

Suites: `attempt-bundle-tools` 23/23; `bash-tools.exec-notify`, `tools/gateway-caller-context`, `agent-tools.prefix-stability`, `attempt-tool-prepare.web-search`, `session-event-handoff`, `session-event-context`, `session-event-permissions` 115/115. Oxlint clean; `git diff --check` clean.

### Live Gateway run (revision 5, head 18721460f1e, shipped entry point, scripted provider)

Built dist from this head (`build-all gatewayWatch` with `OPENCLAW_BUILD_PRIVATE_QA=1`), isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, non-interactive onboarding with `--custom-no-auth` against a loopback OpenAI-compatible provider written for the proof. The provider scripts each step from the conversation and logs every request's offered `tools[].function.name`.
Two loopback streamable-http MCP servers, `fixture` (`echo`) and `admin` (`reset`), each log every JSON-RPC request. Config: `mcp.servers` for both, `tools.profile: full`, `tools.codeMode: false`, `tools.toolSearch: false`, `tools.exec.security: full`, `tools.exec.ask: off`, `tools.exec.notifyOnExit: true`; Gateway `node openclaw.mjs gateway run --port 18399`.
Every scenario's producer turn runs `exec` with `background: true` and ends. Its woken turn then calls `fixture__echo`, `sessions_spawn` (child task: `fixture__echo`, then `admin__reset`) and `admin__reset`. The provider emits each call whether or not it was offered, so the Gateway has to refuse what the turn may not use.
Policy changes were applied with `node openclaw.mjs config patch --file …` while the Gateway was running (log: `config hot reload applied (…)`). Times are UTC; tool results come from the session transcript in the agent SQLite store.
No credentials, all loopback; the host was heavily loaded, which explains the minutes between exec exit and wake.

**S1: allowed completion-turn MCP call** (`tools.allow: ["read","exec","process","sessions_spawn","fixture__*"]`, session `agent:main:s3d`, dispatched with `node openclaw.mjs agent --agent main --session-key s3d --json`)

```text
18:40:53.533  provider  producer   offered=exec,fixture__echo,process,read,sessions_spawn,skills_read   -> exec {"command":"sleep 5; echo PROOF_EXEC_DONE","background":true}
18:40:53.686  provider  producer   -> "started" (turn ends, exec still running)
18:56:00.145  provider  woken      last user msg "[OpenClaw exec completion] Exec completed (… code 0) :: PROOF_EXEC_DONE"
                                   offered=exec,fixture__echo,process,read,sessions_spawn,skills_read   -> fixture__echo {"text":"from-woken-turn"}
18:56:00.155  fixture   tools/call echo {"text":"from-woken-turn"}
18:56:00.158  toolResult fixture__echo  "fixture.echo ok: {\"text\":\"from-woken-turn\"}"
18:56:00.279  toolResult admin__reset   isError "Tool admin__reset not found"
admin server: initialize / tools/list only, no tools/call
```

The turn woken by the exec exit got `fixture__echo` and its call reached the fixture server; `admin__reset`, outside the producer's cap, was not offered and was refused before any request left the Gateway.

**S2: sender-scoped admin denial preserved** (no `tools.allow`; `tools.toolsBySender: {"id:alice": {"deny": ["admin__*"]}}`). The producer message entered through the **qa-channel** plugin: the repo's qa-lab bus ran on loopback and `POST /v1/inbound/message` carried `{"conversation":{"id":"alice","kind":"direct"},"senderId":"alice"}`. The producer request shows `"sender":{"id":"alice","name":"Alice"}`.

```text
19:30:58.826  provider  producer (sender alice)  tools=70  fixture__echo=yes  admin__reset=no   -> exec background
19:31:06.503  provider  woken (senderless)       tools=70  fixture__echo=yes  admin__reset=no   -> fixture__echo
19:31:06.598  fixture   tools/call echo {"text":"from-woken-turn"}
19:31:06.995  toolResult sessions_spawn  accepted  childSessionKey=agent:main:subagent:61a17295-…
19:31:07.206  toolResult admin__reset   isError "Tool admin__reset not found"
admin server: no tools/call
control, same config, CLI sender (not alice), session agent:main:s2ctl:
19:38:41.052  provider  producer  tools=71  admin__reset=yes
19:38:48.506  admin     tools/call reset {"reason":"from-woken-turn"}
```

The denial applied only to alice's run, and the senderless woken turn inherited it: `admin__reset` was absent from the woken turn's tools and its call was refused. The same config still gave `admin__reset` to a non-alice sender, so the denial is sender-scoped and not global.

**S3: inherited restrictions in a spawned child** (children spawned from the S1 and S2 woken turns)

```text
S1 child agent:main:subagent:0e4cffe3-…
18:56:00.479  provider  child  offered=exec,fixture__echo,process,read,sessions_spawn,skills_read   -> fixture__echo
18:56:00.488  fixture   tools/call echo {"text":"from-child"}
18:56:00.505  toolResult admin__reset   isError "Tool admin__reset not found"
S2 child agent:main:subagent:61a17295-…
19:31:10.113  provider  child  tools=51  fixture__echo=yes  admin__reset=no   -> fixture__echo
19:31:10.254  fixture   tools/call echo {"text":"from-child"}
19:31:10.536  toolResult admin__reset   isError "Tool admin__reset not found"
admin server: no tools/call in either run
```

A child spawned from a woken turn keeps that turn's MCP access (`fixture__echo` works) and its restrictions: the S1 global cap and alice's denial still exclude `admin__reset`.

**S4: revocation after capture, before the woken turn** (S1 config; session `agent:main:s4`; exec `sleep 240`)

```text
19:10:29.444  provider  producer  offered=exec,fixture__echo,process,read,sessions_spawn,skills_read   -> exec {"command":"sleep 240; …","background":true}
19:10:30Z     producer turn returned (agent exit 0; exec still running, its completion target captured while fixture__echo was allowed)
19:11:52.750  gateway   config.patch write changedPaths=tools.deny            (tools.deny: ["fixture__echo"])
19:11:52.877  gateway   [reload] config hot reload applied (tools.deny)
19:29:59.180  transcript user "Exec completed (oceanic-, code 0) :: PROOF_EXEC_DONE"
19:30:02.327  provider  woken     offered=exec,process,read,sessions_spawn,skills_read   -> fixture__echo
19:30:02.575  toolResult fixture__echo  isError "Tool fixture__echo not found"
fixture server: last tools/call at 18:56:00.818 (S1), none after the revocation
```

The cap captured `fixture__echo`, but the woken turn applied its own current policy. After the hot-reloaded `tools.deny` the tool was not offered, and the call was rejected before any `tools/call` reached the fixture server.

Discovery (`initialize`/`tools/list`) still connects both configured servers during each run, as on `main`; policy filters tools, not discovery.

prs.title: fix: preserve assistant answers when media delivery reuses response indexes
prs.body:
Closes #166536

## What Problem This Solves

Distinct assistant responses can be suppressed when retries reuse content indexes or repeat text and images. Streamed media and recovered answers can also end up attached to the wrong response during finalization.

## User Impact

Each physical response keeps its own delivery and transcript identity. Streamed images survive finalization, source images remain visible alongside TTS audio, and canonical provider content and signatures remain intact. This prevents further corruption; it does not repair previously altered history.

## Why This Change Was Made

Upstream #177049 (`0d7df3fc2cf6bc9c53b04f7857b7cbca61b3c927`) now owns `AgentAssistantSourceReceipt` and exact transcript-anchor enrichment. This correction reuses that owner and removes the competing receipt pipeline. The remaining changes scope delivery dedupe, aggregate coverage, streamed-media finalization and timeout-recovery custody to each physical response.

Current head: `ceb73e236d370f3cd606c896203484b7840ef1f6`. Upstream main was merged into the branch with normal merges to resolve conflicts, most recently `118eb292b6b` on November 14. The diff against main is 22 files, including a test-line allocation for its +469 net test lines. No force-push, schema/configuration change, signing infrastructure or release publication is included. Maintainer edits remain enabled.

## Evidence

Current head `ceb73e236d3` (November 14):

- Core typecheck, the test-lines ratchet and the mock-export ratchet pass, and the two handler test files pass (62 tests).
- On the first November 14 merge, `53d55795b91`, Vitest passes on all 11 affected test files (472 tests), and `pnpm check:changed` passes core and core-test typecheck, lint and format. Its dead export scan flags 8 exports in compaction files this PR does not touch; that scan was not re-run on `ceb73e236d3`.
- CI has not run on `ceb73e236d3`. The fork workflow runs are waiting for maintainer approval ([CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43624427551)).
- ClawSweeper's last verdict, on `a751df45d01`, was "needs real behavior proof before merge" and is stale for this head. A re-review will be requested once CI has run.

Earlier heads, through `8716154f8d0`:

- Final complete affected Gateway suites: 149/149 passed, no skips, including committed/suppressed/indexed/unkeyed/owned source-media plus TTS cases.

- Main-production controls reproduced the occurrence and recovered-answer failures. Real transcript regressions reproduced TTS selection, append-key and owned-rewrite losses before their repairs.
- Type-aware lint on all 19 changed source files, production core typecheck, formatting and diff checks passed.
- The initial committed correction and the subsequent CI test repair each received fresh independent P2 review with no actionable findings.
- CI run [39902028749](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39902028749) exposed two test-type defects and a stale unkeyed fenced-stream lookup. All reproduced locally. The follow-up repairs only test callers: source-aware lookup with an unkeyed negative control, required assertion diagnostics, and the fixture return type tied to the real transcript writer.

prs.title: fix: retain safe causes when provider catalog discovery fails
prs.body:
Related: #165888

## What Problem This Solves

Provider catalog failures discard the safe cause needed to distinguish authentication, HTTP, timeout, and unexpected failures during model discovery.

## User Impact

Operators receive bounded diagnostic fields when discovery skips an unavailable catalog. Existing discovery outcomes, authentication handling, sibling discovery, and deadlines are preserved. This improves diagnosis; it does not claim to repair the underlying refresh failure or update the installed runtime.

## Why This Change Was Made

The inner catalog boundary and outer discovery deadline share a fixed warning containing a validated provider identifier, phase, closed failure reason, elapsed milliseconds, and optional numeric HTTP status. Exception messages, stacks, URLs, response bodies, and credentials stay out of the warning. Adversarial thrown values cannot replace the existing graceful failure.

Current head is `b01a3e78cab7f79b97f655e402033ae8b9ee4698`. It integrates upstream main's timeout handling, flattened test layout and per-provider failure isolation (request-wide rethrow, unavailable outcomes) while retaining the five-file diagnostic repair, plus a test-line allocation for its +198 test lines. No dependency, scanner, or runtime deployment change is included.

## Evidence

- Head `b01a3e78cab` adds one test-only commit to `0ad55a7ea34`. The leakage fixture's credential URL is now assembled at runtime, as `src/infra/update-candidate-admission.test.ts` does on main, because a literal credential URL trips the PR input-safety scanner. The thrown value and every leakage assertion are unchanged.
- Focused tests on `b01a3e78cab`: `src/plugin-sdk/provider-catalog-live-outcome.internal.test.ts` and `src/agents/models-config.providers.implicit.discovery-scope.test.ts` pass (32 tests), and the format check passes.
- CI on the previous head `0ad55a7ea34` ([run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42517944280)) had no failing checks, and both required `openclaw/ci-gate` checks passed. CI on `b01a3e78cab` is waiting for a maintainer to approve the fork workflow runs.
- ClawSweeper reviewed `b01a3e78cab` with no findings and asked for real behavior proof, which is below.
- Local review: not run. Neither autoreview nor a local ClawSweeper is set up in this checkout.

### Real behavior proof

Entry point: the CLI run from source with no Gateway, `node scripts/run-node.mjs models list --refresh --all --json`, in a throwaway `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_HOME`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`. Four `models.providers` entries (`bifrost`, `litellm`, `llama-cpp`, `lmstudio`) point at loopback fake servers: one healthy, one HTTP 404, one HTTP 401, one that never responds. Every API key, response body and URL query string carried a private marker.

After, on `b01a3e78cab`, stderr:

```
[agents/model-providers] Provider catalog discovery failed; skipping unavailable catalog provider=litellm phase=live-catalog reason=http elapsedMs=36 httpStatus=404
[agents/model-providers] Provider catalog discovery failed; skipping unavailable catalog provider=llama-cpp phase=live-catalog reason=http elapsedMs=12 httpStatus=401
[agents/model-providers] Provider catalog discovery failed; skipping unavailable catalog provider=lmstudio phase=live-catalog reason=timeout elapsedMs=5004
```

After, with `litellm` hanging past the 180 s discovery deadline:

```
[agents/model-providers] Provider catalog discovery failed; skipping unavailable catalog provider=litellm phase=provider-discovery reason=timeout elapsedMs=180001
[agents/model-providers] Provider catalog discovery failed; skipping unavailable catalog provider=litellm phase=live-catalog reason=timeout elapsedMs=180688
```

The file log carries the same events as JSONL, for example `{"provider":"litellm","phase":"live-catalog","reason":"http","elapsedMs":36,"httpStatus":404}`.

Before, on merge base `61120568f82`, the same runs log no cause for the 404, the 401 or the 5 s timeout. At the deadline the outer boundary logs exception text:

```
[models/provider-isolation] provider discovery failed for litellm: provider catalog timed out after 180000ms: litellm; skipping provider
```

- Healthy sibling: stdout lists both `bifrost` models in all four runs, and `providerOutcomes` are identical before and after (`ready`, `unavailable`, `auth-rejected`, `unavailable`).
- Leak check: the private marker appears 0 times in stdout, stderr and the log file in all four runs.
- Baseline red: with this PR's two test files copied onto the merge base, `provider-catalog-live-outcome.internal.test.ts` fails 9 of 10 and `models-config.providers.implicit.discovery-scope.test.ts` fails 1 of 22. On `b01a3e78cab` they pass 10/10 and 22/22.

Two things the proof showed that this PR does not change:

- A provider that hangs to the deadline produces two warnings about 0.7 s apart, one per boundary, because the inner fetch timeout equals the remaining outer budget.
- The existing `[fetch-timeout]` line still prints the provider base URL without its query string, on both the baseline and this head.

No approval, merge, or production rollout is claimed.

prs.title: feat(sessions): choose how many recent messages an automatic reset keeps
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An automatic idle or daily reset always carries the last six user/assistant messages into the new session, and there is no way to change that number. Some deployments want more continuity after a reset, others want a clean start.

## User Impact

User impact: operators can set `session.reset.tailMessages` (also in `resetByType` and `resetByChannel` entries) to choose how many recent messages an automatic reset keeps. The default stays 6, so nothing changes unless the key is set. `0` starts the new session empty. `/new` and `/reset` still always clear.

## Why This Change Was Made

The tail size was a constant inside the transcript selection. It is now resolved with the rest of the reset policy, so the per-type and per-channel overrides work the same way as `mode`, `atHour` and `idleMinutes`. The four places that write an automatic preserve-tail boundary pass the resolved value: the channel reply path, `openclaw agent`, the gateway agent turn and cron's stale-session rollover.

<details>
<summary>Changes</summary>

- `src/config/zod-schema.session-config.ts`: `tailMessages` (integer, at least 0) on the reset policy object, with label and help text.
- `src/config/sessions/reset-policy.ts`: `SessionResetPolicy.tailMessages`, type override first, then base, then `DEFAULT_RESET_TAIL_MESSAGES = 6`.

prs.title: refactor(infra): check exec approvals once at commit
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Exec approvals were checked twice for one command. The worker commit (`execApprovals.commitAuthorizations`) checks the command against the current policy row. After that, `retainExecApprovalsCurrentRead` kept a per-database policy view that the launch guard read again right before spawn. A policy write that landed between the commit and the spawn refused a command that was already admitted ("Exec approval changed before execution", "Exec approval policy is unavailable or changing before execution"). Under the one-admission rule, a policy change applies to the next command; a command that has started finishes.

## Fix

- `src/infra/exec-approvals-store.ts`: delete `retainExecApprovalsCurrentRead`, the `currentPolicies` map and its publication/lifecycle bookkeeping.
  - `prepareExecApprovalsCurrentRead` returns the policy it read at preparation, through the existing prepared-snapshot cache, which a publication still clears for the next reader.
  - The launch guard from `commitExecAuthorizations` keeps Stop (`signal.throwIfAborted()`) and the caller's own `assertCurrent`, and returns the committed file.
- `src/infra/exec-approvals-authorization.ts`: `commitExecAuthorizationLocked` no longer runs `assertCurrentUsageAuthorization` again on the file it just committed. The worker already ran that check inside the commit transaction.
- `scripts/check-lifetime-check-ratchet.mts`: remove `retainExecApprovalsCurrentRead` (it is gone) and `createPluginRuntimeCapabilityLease` from `LIFETIME_CHECK_CALLS`.

### Classification

| Name | Class | Action |
|---|---|---|
| `retainExecApprovalsCurrentRead` (#169584) | authority. It re-read the exec policy, which is the permission for the command, after the worker commit had admitted it. It refused while a policy write was pending or after one committed. | deleted |
| `createPluginRuntimeCapabilityLease` (#133297, "scope HTTP routes to account lifetimes") | resource lifetime fence. Its only `revoke()` callers are channel account stop (`server-channels.ts`), plugin service stop (`services.ts`), plugin CLI scheduler close (`cli-service-scheduler.ts`) and shutdown drain. It never reads role, scopes, profile or grants. It retires HTTP routes, listeners and schedulers that a stopped account or service still holds. | code kept; name removed from the ratchet list |

Kept: Stop on the launch guard, the worker commit check against the current row (it protects the usage/grant write), and the DB-lifecycle fences inside the shared-state reads.

Not in scope (accepted for now): `plugin-node-host.ts` still compares the node exec **config** (`resolveNodeExecConfigPolicy`) at launch. The ratchet does not list it; it can go in a later PR.

## User Impact

- If you tighten exec approvals while a command is between approval and spawn, that command now runs. The next command uses the new policy. Before this change, the command failed with "Exec approval changed before execution".
- Stop still cancels the launch.
- A policy change made before the worker commit still refuses the command.

## Tests

Deleted or flipped. Each one asserted a refusal after the commit had admitted the command, which this change removes:
- `bash-tools.exec-authorization.integration.test.ts`: "revalidates … after asynchronous shell preparation" ×3, "rechecks policy after deferred supervisor admission", the PTY fallback `revoked=true` case. Added "finishes an admitted launch when policy is revoked during supervisor admission" (real exec tool → supervisor).
- `invoke-system-run.test.ts`, `invoke-agent-cli-claude.test.ts`: the revoke cases now expect the admitted launch to finish (real node `system.run` / Claude CLI entry points).
- `plugin-exec-policy.test.ts`: approvals tightened after the invocation started → the launch is allowed. A config change is still refused.
- `agent-tools.browser-loopback-current.e2e.test.ts`: deleted the approvals-revocation case. The abort (Stop) and config cases stay.
- `exec-approvals-store*.test.ts`, `operator-approval-store.worker.test.ts`: the pending-write / committed-change refusals are replaced by "the prepared read keeps its admitted policy; a fresh preparation sees the write".

## Evidence

Pre-push: one `ocx test` run of the 78 importer/touched files (continue-on-failure); the remaining reds there (`server-methods/exec-approvals.test.ts` ×4, `agents-mutate.test.ts`, `bash-tools.exec-gateway-approval.e2e.test.ts` hook-token reload) fail the same way on the merge base `1a0a24dcd2cf`. Touched tests rerun green (202 cases). `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:test`, oxfmt, oxlint, lifetime ratchet pass. Head E2E and CI follow in comments.

prs.title: fix: progress refresh stalls while a background command runs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes progress refresh getting stuck while an active agent waits for a background command through repeated process polls.

## User Impact

Refresh can reach the running agent without stopping or restarting its command. The original result still completes normally. No configuration, migration, permission, or timeout change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The required Code Mode wait could yield to steering while awaiting exec, but not while awaiting process poll. Extend that same observer-only path to the native process tool's poll action; other actions and tools remain excluded. Reuse the existing AgentSession regression for both wait kinds.

This is a confirmed beta.2 release blocker repair against release/2026.11.10. It does not claim final release qualification or change any waiver. The corresponding main integration remains to be completed.

## Evidence

- Baseline: the real AgentSession/native-process regression fails after 10.7 seconds because steering arrives only after the held command finishes; the original exec case passes.
- Fixed: 77 focused tests pass across the AgentSession, wait, and prompt-prefix-stability suites. The regression verifies the original result and exactly one command launch.
- The unmodified isolated Gateway/live-model progress-refresh test passes (1/1, 31.6 seconds): active-parent continuation keeps its final result; idle-card refresh adds no chat or resumed work.
- Targeted agents-tools typecheck, lint, formatting, and diff checks pass.
- Fresh independent full-source review: no actionable findings.
- Canonical local autoreview, OpenClaw engine, P0–P2, one complete pass: scoped-clean. Reviewed the local snapshot based on 00f7ee6eb2b3843d4607036b348f852d31976d5b immediately before committing this patch. It did not independently rerun validation; the separate full-source review supplied unchanged-owner context.

Final full release validation remains outstanding. No test was skipped or weakened to produce the live pass. An initial live setup attempt encountered an unrelated older host-state schema; the successful run used a fresh isolated test-state source with the existing environment credential and left host state untouched.

prs.title: fix(agents): harness history moves only at compaction
prs.body:
Result: plugin harnesses (Codex app-server, Agents API, Muse) now read session history with the same guard as the embedded runner. Their history keeps everything since the latest compaction and only grows between compactions. Follow-up to #203536.

## What Problem This Solves

`resolveAgentHarnessHistoryLimits` (Plugin SDK) still computed its own byte cap: `contextTokenBudget × 8`. Each Codex hook/continuity read, Agents API prompt-hook read and Muse session transfer therefore cut the oldest turns once history passed 8 bytes per budget token. Reasoning, images and tool payloads reach that size far below the token budget. Each new attempt reread and cut the history again, so it was rewritten outside compaction. This is the same class #203536 fixed for the embedded runner.

## Why This Change Was Made

- `resolveAgentHarnessHistoryLimits` now returns `resolveEmbeddedSessionContextLimits({})` (16 MiB / 10,000 events) plus its existing `toolResultOverflow: "omit"`. There is one owner for the bound, and the duplicate budget-based computation is gone.
- The export keeps its name and signature. Its `contextTokenBudget` argument is still accepted, but it is **deprecated and ignored** (documented in the doc comment and in `docs/plugins/sdk-agent-harness/attempt-runtime.md`).
- Bundled callers stop passing it. Codex drops the `contextTokenBudget` argument from `readCodexMirroredSessionHistoryMessages` / `readMirroredSessionHistoryMessages`. Agents API drops the limits from its history-reuse scope key: the limits are now constant, so a budget change no longer forces a fresh read. Muse calls it with no argument.
- No schema, protocol or dependency change.

Tests that asserted the removed budget cut are deleted or rewritten:
- Codex `session-history.test.ts`: the budget-128 cut and budget-512 omission tests are replaced by the regression test below.
- `run-attempt.bounded-continuity.test.ts`: the "assistant-only bounded suffix" case is kept. Its user turn is now larger than the 16 MiB guard, so it still covers the fallback past the guard.
- Agents API: the "new budget" retry case is removed, and the pinned `maxBytes: 256_000` assertion is removed.

## Evidence

Regression test through the Codex harness history consumer (`readCodexMirroredSessionHistoryMessages`): 1.3 MB of history, which is past the old default-budget cut and far below compaction. Two consecutive reads with a new turn appended between them.
- Base `2754763da236`: red, `expected … to have a length of 43 but got 25` (the oldest turns were cut).
- Head: green. All 43 messages are returned, and the second read extends the first one exactly.
- Mutation: head with the harness cap set back to `128_000 × 8` is red again (the same 25-message cut).

Tests: the touched test files plus every test file that imports a changed source (25 files), oxfmt/oxlint on the changed files, and `pnpm check:changed`.

## What Changes for Users

Codex, Agents API and Muse sessions with reasoning, screenshots or large tool output keep their whole history (and the provider cache prefix) until compaction. Before, old turns dropped silently on each attempt.

## Merge danger

Two-way door. A revert restores the budget-based cut. Third-party plugins that pass a budget get the shared guard; their call still compiles.
