prs.title: fix(ui): retry dictation recordings when transcription returns no text
prs.body:
Related: #195982

## What Problem This Solves

A dictation recording that finishes without usable text cannot be recovered, so the user must record it again. Current main now preserves ordered pending transcripts and reports empty results, but still does not retain failed audio for explicit retry.

## User Impact

User impact: **Retry recording** resends the same captured audio without reopening the microphone. Recovered text stays in the editable draft until the user explicitly sends it. Successful retry clears only that recording’s obsolete error; unrelated errors remain.

Recovery is memory-only in the current tab and draft. Discard, Escape, draft replacement, or starting another capture releases failed recordings. Usable preview text keeps its existing recovery behavior. Pending successful recordings continue in recording order; an explicit retry joins the current pending-transcript tail rather than rearranging text already delivered.

## Why This Change Was Made

The November 22 integration preserves merged #200235: the existing lazy ordered-commit queue, preview placement, Gateway-first microphone admission, and typed capacity refusal remain in charge. Failed audio lives in the existing capture session, and its recovery stays with that queue—not the retired single-pending-session implementation. Discard targets the failed recording without cancelling another recording still transcribing.

Retry creates a fresh normally authorized Gateway transcription session. No persistent audio storage, new provider, permission/configuration change, automatic Send, or microphone fallback is introduced. Listening feedback/lazy loading from #198424 and #198643 remains. The separate PR #196063 is not imported or modified.

## Evidence

### Current candidate

Published head **ea31ea05bfa30f7ff0124a2a0c5f2f37bd58db84**; pinned integration/review base **f56171778657c9332e78eda92c4545143be07549**. The published tree exactly matches the tested tree **2aa7ea2a7aef808302a00690895ef641452aad8f**. [Substantive ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198845#issuecomment-6877437378) completed for this exact head: Findings None and Before merge None. The integrated real-Gateway transcription proof it separately requested is now recorded below. Required CI is not green; the two failed leaf jobs are classified below. Old 90165f97 results are not current integration proof.

- **Real Gateway + local Whisper, exact head: 1/1 passed (exit 0).** A disposable paired browser and the compiled Gateway reported build `2026.11.6-ea31ea05bfa3-2026-11-22T17-20-32.475Z` from `pnpm build:runtime`. After an intentional first CLI transcription failure, an explicit **Retry recording** replayed the same 16 chunks and produced the identical 131,116-byte WAV (SHA-256 `fe0c9cd3fc15934dfdf7ab7b2e8a3ba61625b3c08bf0ee276eb3136b92dfb15c`). Local Whisper recovered text in the unsent draft and cleared the stale error. The browser acquired the microphone once and issued zero `chat.send` calls. Scenario: 44.67 s; invocation: 90.20 s. Owned Gateway, provider, browser and ports were cleaned up. This test uses public test audio in a fake microphone, not a physical microphone or cloud STT.
- **Red before / green after through the actual bundled Control UI:** current-main capture reached a transcription error, an empty unsent draft, and no Retry control. The integrated main-chat and New Session flows now replay identical audio, acquire the microphone once, send no chat message, recover the draft, and remove the stale error. The New Session proof also checks a narrow 390 px viewport.
- **Five focused browser cases passed**, including the three existing narrow pending-transcript status cases. Normal repository Chromium/bundled-UI harness, maxWorkers=1; 16.63 s invocation. Fixtures supply microphone samples and typed Gateway replies; these are separate synthetic-Gateway UI/transport-boundary assertions.
- **121 focused unit/consumer tests passed** across dictation owner, direct dictation, main composer, New Session and split Talk. Added regressions cover retry/discard with a later pending recording, ordered replay delivery, busy retry admission without a second microphone, replacement/Escape/draft release, and Read aloud superseding replay. The moved fixture/placement assertions preserve coverage while honoring the existing test-file line limit.
- UI types, targeted lint/stylelint, formatting, i18n baseline/verification and diff checks pass.
- **Pinned-base production UI performance comparison passes** with the installed toolchain: startup JS unchanged at 90184 B gzip; chat boot 1332148→1332911 B (+763 B, below the 1334480 B limit); New Session 818842→819593 B (+751 B, below 822243 B). CSS gzip +6 B; inherited CSS/request-count warnings remain visible. No budgets/baselines were raised.
- Fresh local Auto Review was attempted against the pinned base with the complete repair and relevant owners at P0–P3. It timed out after 300 seconds without a report; this is **not a clean review**. Publication followed the current maintainer workflow’s explicit timeout continuation rule; the hosted exact-head review has since completed as described above.

### Exact-head CI classification

The [Control UI performance job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45044442956/job/137276410377) passed. The [required CI aggregate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45044442956/job/137279017277) remains failed; no gate is waived.

- [Baseline ratchets](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45044442956/job/137276410865): the runner received a shutdown signal at 16:37:24.023 UTC, followed by SQLite inventory exit 143 and cancellation. This is a terminal runner interruption, not evidence of a database/ratchet defect. No broad database rerun or guard change was performed.
- [UI E2E shard 3/10](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45044442956/job/137276410639): the auth-failed composer test still expects **Set up a model**, but merged [#203394](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/203394), commit [a30bdf3fd02a](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/a30bdf3fd02a44ec260addd9f940ec960cc03322), intentionally changed that recovery to **Open Models** and added an owning test for it without updating this E2E expectation. The owner, E2E fixture/test, banner renderer and English label have identical Git blobs at this PR’s integration base, the CI base, the published head and the tested merge. One bounded unchanged-candidate browser run reproduced the missing old-label control; its inspected screenshot shows the intended Open Models button and preserved typed draft. The existing owning Open Models test passes. This is an inherited stale expectation, not attributed merely because its file was untouched. No assertion, timeout or unrelated auth behavior was changed in this PR.

CI tested merge c1841cd11d5a3ee48550aa90de534b362bd6e57f (base feea72c186382804ceb75158a6c8fd41b7650e11 plus this head). The unrelated auth E2E expectation needs its owner’s correction, and the interrupted runner needs authorized infrastructure recovery; neither has been retried for green here.

### Clean comparison

Actual bundled Control UI, same synthetic failure and desktop viewport. Before: pinned current-main owners. After: the exact published candidate tree. Composer crops expand only to include the added recovery controls.

| Before: failed audio has no recovery control | After: same recording remains retryable |
| --- | --- |
| ![Current-main composer after transcription failure](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8c2a1558-208d-4c71-8fe5-800de024b21b) | ![Integrated composer with Retry recording and Discard recording](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bbde4150-711a-4a1c-ac59-00d372eebdec) |

### Annotated comparison

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Missing retry control identified on the same clean frame](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2745b171-cc28-4853-88cb-74bd80548a5b) | ![Same-recording retry identified on the same clean frame](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9d0f82d1-8ccd-47df-90de-c37a30aebf06) |

<details>
<summary>Historical November 14 evidence — not new-head proof</summary>

Head 90165f9792e5236f68571ef0c6c10c6e258503cb passed required CI and a substantive ClawSweeper review with no findings. Its isolated real Gateway/local Whisper scenario recovered identical retained audio with one microphone acquisition and no Send; a separate actual Read aloud scenario confirmed discard and no late insertion. Those runs preceded the upstream ordered-queue/admission changes and are retained only as historical evidence.

[Historical failed recording](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ec4d018c-285d-4677-bdb9-21144eb407a5), [historical recovered draft](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0eb55223-931d-4882-8860-05058fa8282c), [original before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/397e0f31-7dbd-4871-b837-59bcd090fbed), [original recovery controls](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9808f96f-6788-493c-9017-cb40bad01a08), [original synthetic replay](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9d5a4b98-40a9-4ec4-8bf3-e49d54819f89). No physical-microphone, cloud-STT or long-recording claims.

</details>

Reported and directed by @dankarization (Daniil Karpenko).

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @dankarization](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/352f46a3-5f77-4787-a96f-85944ce150b8)

releases.body:
## 2026.11.7

### Highlights

- **Conversation recovery:** Recover interrupted replies and child results across Gateway restarts without losing pending work. (#198905, #201544, #200924, #200967) Authored by @steipete. Thanks @RomneyDa, @galiniliev, and @vincentkoc.
- **Reliable automations:** Let an automation’s owner conversation repair failures, and distinguish recovered or intentionally skipped runs from genuine failures. (#161007, #201638, #152165, #194276) Related #194261 Thanks @RomneyDa, @vyctorbrzezowski, @vincentkoc, @obviyus, @pash-openai, @wr-web, and @slatem.
- **Smoother updates:** Finish Git and package updates through schema changes, busy databases, and retained recovery state instead of stopping before or after the new release starts. (#201600, #201463, #201545, #201330) Authored by @steipete. Thanks @RomneyDa, @vincentkoc, and @fuller-stack-dev.
- **Responsive Gateway:** Keep chats, readiness checks, and unrelated sessions responsive during slow filesystem operations, large recovery packs, and page extraction. (#191236, #201248, #200623, #200925) Authored by @steipete. Thanks @RomneyDa and @vincentkoc.
- **Browser pairing:** Pair another browser with a short code approved on the Gateway host, with clearer instructions while approval is pending. (#191513, #200905) Thanks @vincentkoc, @RomneyDa, @daniel-lxs, @jalehman, and @etzelm.
- **Current ChatGPT catalogs:** Discover newly available subscription models without waiting for another OpenClaw release and keep sign-in discovery independent of npm. (#201130, #201493) Related #201480 Thanks @RomneyDa, @obviyus, and @daniel-lxs.

### Changes

- **Knowledge search:** Find current records using superseded wording and match canonically equivalent Unicode keyword spellings. (#193742, #195092) Related #193054, #195031 Thanks @RomneyDa, @daniel-lxs, @Linux2010, @jalehman, and @saariuslystoned.
- **Talk transcription:** Use a saved Deepgram, ElevenLabs, or Mistral API key for live transcription. (#199858) Related #199684 Thanks @daniel-lxs.
- **Session control — breaking SDK change:** Move session-keyed setActiveEmbeddedRun(...) registrations into the host-provided runAttempt callback and retain their exact cleanup function; unadmitted registration now reports SESSION_CONTROLLER_ADMISSION_REQUIRED. (#175837) Authored by @steipete. Thanks @RomneyDa and @jalehman.
- **Gateway methods — breaking SDK change:** Replace mutable chatAbortControllers and chatQueuedTurns access with dispatchGatewayMethod from openclaw/plugin-sdk/gateway-method-runtime, declaring contracts.gatewayMethodDispatch: ["authenticated-request"] in the plugin manifest; existing caller permissions still apply. (#175837) Authored by @steipete. Thanks @RomneyDa, @vincentkoc, @johan-eilertsen, and @jalehman.
- **Start observation — breaking SDK change:** Update AgentTurnStartOwner.observe() consumers from expiresAtMs to startDeadlineAtMs; this is the execution-start deadline, not the execution timeout, and has no compatibility alias. See docs/plugins/sdk-migration.md for migration guidance. (#175837) Authored by @steipete. Thanks @jalehman.

### Fixes

- **Reply and command boundaries:** Keep slash commands in ordinary prose from executing and warn before retrying a tool action whose reply was lost. (#200458, #201523) Thanks @Patrick-Erichsen and @VACInc.
- **Stop and steering:** Answer messages sent after Stop, preserve steering through long-running tools, and let users steer while a Code Mode shell command runs. (#195612, #199878, #200998) Related #194303 Authored by @steipete. Thanks @RomneyDa, @amittell, @obviyus, and @VACInc.
- **Subagent results:** Keep results attached to their requesting turn and prevent one child’s delivery failure from dropping sibling results. (#200873, #201563, #195275) Authored by @steipete. Thanks @RomneyDa, @VACInc, and @jalehman.
- **Scheduled work:** Preserve automation ownership through account, sharing, and group changes, and keep scheduled global work in its existing conversation. (#201008, #201434, #188173) Thanks @RomneyDa, @obviyus, @vincentkoc, @jalehman, and @shakkernerd.
- **Claude CLI:** Retain final answers after progress messages, include long child results in completion turns, and show tool history with a custom Claude configuration directory. (#200470, #200226, #198337) Related #199633 Authored by @steipete. Thanks @RomneyDa, @gouyu-hou, @chaeyn, @obviyus, @etzelm, @VACInc, @mulderp82, @xiaoguomeiyitian, and @Szqub.
- **Codex:** Keep resumed conversations on the same native writer, distinguish API quota from subscription exhaustion, and preserve line breaks in streamed replies. (#201474, #192165, #201102) Thanks @RomneyDa, @jalehman, @vincentkoc, @TheRealUnknownSoldier, @VACInc, and @freeqaz.
- **Model and credential recovery:** Keep shared OAuth refresh with the running Gateway, use ambient AWS credentials for Bedrock Mantle, and report why a listed model rejects a request. (#198214, #190988, #200073) Related #163006 Thanks @RomneyDa, @obviyus, and @netcrazed.
- **Compaction:** Use configured fallbacks after quota errors, avoid false post-compaction stall aborts, and preserve selected skills in sandboxed sessions. (#194813, #194722, #198029) Related #194803, #194715 Authored by @steipete. Thanks @RomneyDa, @VACInc, @saariuslystoned, @vyctorbrzezowski, @jason-allen-oneal, and @obviyus.
- **Telegram:** Finish large media uploads, retain callback controls when replacement delivery fails, and answer messages even when their attachment cannot download. (#151923, #193948, #200682) Related #193947 Thanks @RomneyDa, @amittell, @obviyus, and @AmelioMansour.
- **Discord and Slack:** Reconnect all Discord accounts after outages, keep independent requests from replacing active tasks, and keep top-level Slack completions top-level. (#201415, #201518, #187065) Related #162189 Thanks @RomneyDa, @obviyus, @mattreyes0824, @vincentkoc, and @wr-web.
- **Matrix and Feishu:** Preserve image captions and reply placement, show Matrix polls and votes in Element X, and finish long Feishu replies in the same streaming card. (#188018, #191700, #161777) Related #188038, #191678, #139443 Thanks @seriouslysean, @thatsrue, @obviyus, @chelsealong, @geekforlife, @ArthurNie, and @Simon2256928.
- **Voice calls:** Avoid raw JSON and truncated long answers, ignore echoed caller transcripts, and answer when background noise prevents endpointing. (#151367, #191537, #191498) Thanks @Weiming-Hu, @weiming, @obviyus, and @mnowrot.
- **Mobile and macOS:** Start a new Android chat while a response is running, accept native Talk setups, and let the macOS app answer its first chat without a false low-memory refusal. (#191372, #191194, #200373) Related #191339, #200340 Thanks @RomneyDa, @gouyu-hou, @saariuslystoned, @vyctorbrzezowski, @obviyus, and @jalehman.
- **Browser tools:** Keep the user’s Chrome tab focused, read text from the correct page after navigation, and capture background tabs in headless mode. (#134400, #196659, #201626) Related #196658 Authored by @steipete. Thanks @RomneyDa, @scotthuang, @martins-oss, and @obviyus.
- **Control UI:** Preserve dictation while microphone permission is pending, show transcription progress, and recover connections promptly after returning to the app. (#199069, #200235, #199887) Related #199065, #199875 Authored by @steipete. Thanks @RomneyDa and @daniel-lxs.
- **Fast navigation:** Open Channels and Devices without waiting for unrelated Chat or configuration work, and open Knowledge Browse without scanning unrelated stores. (#194393, #194795, #194792) Authored by @steipete. Thanks @RomneyDa and @vyctorbrzezowski.
- **Configuration and Doctor:** Preserve guarded writes through symlinked state roots, restore reported truncated configuration, and avoid unrelated system Gateways blocking migrations. (#155538, #201501, #190194) Related #190177 Authored by @steipete. Thanks @RomneyDa, @mfurkanakinci, @vincentkoc, and @Satoshi-Kusumoto.
- **Backups and PostgreSQL:** Allow scheduled backups beyond ten minutes, protect verification from concurrent cleanup, restore through symlinked targets, and finish network database ports without hours of avoidable waiting. (#191346, #198659, #197795, #201374) Related #197779, #201249 Thanks @RomneyDa, @wangmiao0668000666, @vincentkoc, @chelsealong, @etzelm, @deepujain, and @evemorgen.
- **Update reporting and recovery:** Preserve warnings and accurate elapsed time, avoid asking owners to retry an update already running, and recover interrupted conversation state. (#194242, #194289, #188159) Related #188149 Authored by @steipete. Thanks @RomneyDa, @vincentkoc, and @shakkernerd.
- **Installation and plugins:** Install local file URLs on Windows, stage native dependencies when execution is denied, and keep Git installs working while Node is being provisioned. (#190734, #193801, #195382) Related #195366 Authored by @steipete. Thanks @RomneyDa, @AmelioMansour, @wr-web, and @okbilinmeyen7komut-alt.
- **Memory and knowledge:** Recover indexing after embedding timeouts, support configured local Ollama hostnames, and recover interrupted Knowledge writes without duplicating repair work. (#191556, #191479, #193116, #198146) Authored by @steipete. Thanks @RomneyDa, @galiniliev, @Finn763, @triciah73, @jalehman, and @vincentkoc.
- **Sandbox and templates:** Keep turns working after the default sandbox image changes, avoid unrelated workspace contention, and allow retries after partially written template creation. (#193986, #197561, #199447) Related #193964 Authored by @steipete. Thanks @RomneyDa, @karam2022, @zhangguiping-xydt, and @obviyus.
- **Files and paths:** Handle Markdown carriage-return line endings, dotfiles and consecutive dots, and multiline frontmatter without losing text. (#200783, #197398, #199739, #198439) Related #200757 Thanks @RomneyDa, @LinzeShi, and @obviyus.
- **Retained work:** Restore retained downloads after worker reclaim, keep recently used worktrees out of idle cleanup, and preserve reconciled files during fast-forward. (#198102, #201333, #137942) Authored by @steipete. Thanks @RomneyDa, @jalehman, @joshavant, and @zhangguiping-xydt.
- **Long text pastes:** retain long pasted text in the composer as user text rather than automatically converting it into an attachment. Thanks @RomneyDa.
- **Usage reporting:** distinguish historical usage from live inference cost rather than presenting missing historical cost as a measured zero. Thanks @RomneyDa and @vincentkoc.
- **Bundled Codex alignment:** align the ACP Codex override with the bundled 0.170.0 runtime while retaining ACP 2.2.2. Thanks @RomneyDa and @vincentkoc.
- **Provider hooks:** preserve installed agent and plugin transport hooks when the SDK loads later, instead of replacing them with inactive defaults. Thanks @RomneyDa and @vincentkoc.

### Complete contribution record

This audited record covers the complete v2026.11.6..3f05d1ac58c19a4bc5417e4685af2ffff56f7b22 history: 390 in-range PRs + 0 retained seed-only PRs = 390 unique PRs. The generation manifest also supplies direct commits as editorial input; the grouped notes above prioritize user impact.

prs.title: [security] fix(mcp): prevent enabledTools name collisions
prs.body:
## Summary
This PR hardens the MCP `enabledTools` capability boundary so lossy sanitized wrapped names cannot authorize a different raw MCP tool.

- Fixes a model-visible MCP tool identity confusion path where raw names such as `demo.read`, `demo/read`, `demo read`, and `demo__read` normalize to the same wrapped name.
- Keeps exact raw MCP tool names as the unambiguous allowlist identity for lossy names.
- Preserves wrapped-name compatibility for stable names that do not change during sanitization.
- Adds focused regression coverage and a Docker stdio-MCP proof that the previous colliding wrapped-name path now registers no tool.

## Security issues covered

| Issue | Impact | Severity |
|-------|--------|----------|
| MCP `enabledTools` wrapped-name collision | A mutable or malicious MCP server could cause an unapproved raw tool to inherit approval from a colliding model-visible wrapped name. In credential-bearing MCP deployments, this can bypass the operator's intended least-privilege tool boundary. | Medium; potentially higher in credential-bearing/action-bearing MCP deployments |

## Before this PR
- `enabledTools` accepted either raw MCP tool names or sanitized wrapped names such as `mcp_test_demo_read`.
- The wrapped names were generated through `_sanitize_name(...)`, which is lossy and many-to-one.
- A raw tool named `demo/read` could be registered when the operator allowlisted only `mcp_test_demo_read`, even though that wrapped name could have been produced by a different raw tool such as `demo.read`.
- Ambiguous wrapped names could also collide when all MCP tools were enabled, risking duplicate model-visible tool identities.

## After this PR
- Exact raw MCP names remain supported as the precise allowlist identity.
- Wrapped-name `enabledTools` entries only match when the wrapped name is stable and does not depend on lossy sanitization.
- Ambiguous wrapped-name groups are detected before registration.
- Ambiguous tools are skipped when all tools are enabled so duplicate model-visible MCP names do not silently overwrite each other.
- Regression tests lock in rejection for sanitized wrapped-name authorization and ambiguous wrapped-name groups.

## Why this matters
`enabledTools` is a least-privilege boundary for model-callable MCP tools. When that boundary uses lossy generated names as identities, a tool with a different raw MCP name can be registered under an approved model-visible name.

This matters most for MCP servers that carry credentials or side effects, such as repository, API, browser, database, or cloud integrations. A compromised, malicious, or mutable MCP endpoint should not be able to change raw tool names and inherit an operator's prior approval for a different capability.

## How this differs from related issue/PR
This is adjacent to the merged MCP `enabledTools` fix in [#4436](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/pull/4436), `fix(tools): gate MCP resource and prompt registration behind enabledTools`, which merged on 2026-06-25 and fixed [#4435](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/issues/4435).

| Merged PR | Boundary covered | What it fixed | Why this PR is still needed |
|-----------|------------------|---------------|-----------------------------|
| [#4436](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/pull/4436) | MCP resource/prompt registration under `enabledTools` | When a server used `enabledTools: []` or a specific tool list, ordinary tools were filtered but MCP resources and prompts were still registered and exposed. #4436 now registers resources/prompts only when the server is effectively allow-all (`["*"]`). | #4436 did not change the identity used for ordinary MCP tool allowlisting. A raw tool can still be authorized through a lossy sanitized wrapped name unless the tool-name boundary is hardened. |
| This PR | MCP ordinary tool identity under `enabledTools` | A wrapped/model-visible name such as `mcp_test_demo_read` could authorize a different raw MCP tool such as `demo/read` because `_sanitize_name(...)` is many-to-one. | It closes the sibling tool-identity path so `enabledTools` cannot be bypassed by raw-name collisions after resources/prompts are already gated. |

In short:
- [#4436](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/pull/4436) made `enabledTools` apply consistently across MCP capability *types* by blocking resources/prompts whenever the operator configured a restricted tool set.
- This PR makes `enabledTools` apply safely within the ordinary MCP *tool* type by ensuring an approved wrapped name cannot identify multiple or lossy raw MCP tool names.
- The vulnerable code path here is the tool registration allowlist check in `connect_mcp_servers(...)`, not the resource/prompt registration path fixed by #4436.
- Both fixes are needed because they protect adjacent layers of the same MCP least-privilege boundary: capability type coverage first, then capability identity correctness.

## Attack flow
```text
Operator allowlists a wrapped MCP tool name such as mcp_test_demo_read
    -> MCP server advertises a different raw tool such as demo/read
        -> Nanobot sanitizes the raw name to the same wrapped name
            -> enabledTools wrapped-name check treats it as approved
                -> the model-visible tool calls the unapproved raw MCP capability
```

## Affected code

| Issue | Files |
|-------|-------|
| MCP wrapped-name identity collision | `nanobot/agent/tools/mcp.py`, `tests/tools/test_mcp_tool.py` |

## Root cause
Issue 1: MCP `enabledTools` wrapped-name collision
- `_sanitize_name(...)` intentionally converts provider-incompatible characters to underscores and collapses runs.
- The result is not a stable authorization identity because multiple raw names can map to the same wrapped name.
- `connect_mcp_servers(...)` previously accepted the wrapped name directly in `enabledTools` without proving that it uniquely and reversibly identified the raw MCP tool.

## CVSS assessment

| Issue | CVSS v3.1 | Vector |
|-------|-----------|--------|
| MCP `enabledTools` wrapped-name collision | 4.2 Medium | `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:L/A:N` |

Rationale:
- The attacker condition is a malicious, compromised, or mutable configured MCP server, or an actor able to influence that server's advertised tool list.
- The direct bug is a capability-boundary bypass, not default unauthenticated code execution.
- Impact can be higher in deployments where the affected MCP server has credential-bearing or action-bearing tools, but this PR keeps the universal claim bounded to the authorization boundary failure.

## Safe reproduction steps
1. Configure an MCP server named `test` with `enabledTools: ["mcp_test_demo_read"]`.
2. Have that MCP server advertise only the raw tool name `demo/read`.
3. On vulnerable code, connect the MCP server and inspect the registered tool.
4. Observe that `mcp_test_demo_read` is registered even though the backing raw name is `demo/read`.
5. Execute `mcp_test_demo_read` and observe the raw MCP call goes to `demo/read`.

## Expected vulnerable behavior
On vulnerable code, the Docker stdio-MCP proof showed:

```text
enabledTools= ['mcp_test_demo_read']
registered_tool_names= ['mcp_test_demo_read']
registered_original_name= demo/read
execute_result= COLLIDING_TOOL_EXECUTED
expected_unapproved_raw_name= demo/read
```

After this PR, the same safe proof registers no tool:

```text
enabledTools= ['mcp_test_demo_read']
registered_tool_names= []
collision_blocked= true
```

## Changes in this PR
- Builds a wrapped-name to raw-name map before applying `enabledTools`.
- Detects ambiguous wrapped names generated by lossy sanitization.
- Allows wrapped-name matching only when the wrapped name is stable and unambiguous.
- Requires exact raw-name allowlisting for raw MCP names that need lossy sanitization.
- Skips ambiguous wrapped-name groups under wildcard allow-all to avoid duplicate model-visible registrations.
- Adds tests for sanitized wrapped-name rejection, ambiguous wrapped-name rejection, wildcard ambiguity handling, and exact raw-name compatibility.

## Files changed

| Category | Files | What changed |
|----------|-------|--------------|
| MCP registration hardening | `nanobot/agent/tools/mcp.py` | Tightens `enabledTools` matching around raw names, wrapped names, and ambiguous sanitized names. |
| Regression tests | `tests/tools/test_mcp_tool.py` | Adds focused tests for lossy wrapped-name rejection and collision handling. |

## Maintainer impact
- Existing exact raw-name `enabledTools` entries continue to work.
- Existing wrapped-name entries for stable tool names such as `demo` continue to work.
- Wrapped-name entries for raw MCP names that require sanitization now fail closed and should be changed to the exact raw MCP tool name.
- Ambiguous MCP tool name groups are skipped rather than silently producing duplicate model-visible identities.

## Fix rationale
The raw MCP tool name is the only precise identity available from the server. A sanitized model-visible wrapper is useful for provider compatibility, but it is not safe as an authorization identity when sanitization changes the name or when multiple raw names normalize to the same wrapper.

Failing closed in those cases preserves least privilege and makes unsafe configuration visible through warnings instead of silently registering the wrong capability.

## Type of change
- [x] Security hardening / bug fix
- [x] Regression tests
- [ ] Documentation-only change
- [ ] Refactor with no behavior change

## Test plan
The following commands were run successfully:

```bash
uv run --extra dev python -m pytest tests/tools/test_mcp_tool.py -q
# 68 passed
```

```bash
uv run --extra dev python -m ruff check nanobot/agent/tools/mcp.py tests/tools/test_mcp_tool.py
# All checks passed
```

```bash
git diff --check
# passed with no output
```

```bash

  -v /path/to/nanobot:/repo \
  -v /path/to/mcp_collision_server.py:/tmp/mcp_collision_server.py:ro \
  -v /path/to/repro_mcp_enabledtools_collision_fixed.py:/tmp/repro_mcp_enabledtools_collision_fixed.py:ro \

  uv run --extra dev python /tmp/repro_mcp_enabledtools_collision_fixed.py
# registered_tool_names= []
# collision_blocked= true
```

## Disclosure notes
This PR is intentionally bounded to MCP `enabledTools` identity handling. It does not claim default unauthenticated takeover, arbitrary host file read, secret theft, or RCE. The impact is an MCP capability-boundary bypass that becomes more serious when the configured MCP server has credential-bearing or action-bearing tools.

prs.title: Localize built-in slash command results across chat clients
prs.body:
**Review the split PRs instead of merging this aggregate.** This PR stays open as the original diff and discussion. The six split heads merge cleanly and produce the same Git tree as this PR on the same `main` snapshot.

| Part | PR | Base |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0. Independent JSON Schema typing fix | #6755 | `main` |
| 1. Command results, catalog and channel presentation | #6756 | `main` |
| 2. Deferred receipt ordering, retries and size limit | #6757 | #6756 |
| 3. Confirmed model switching and atomic first send | #6758 | #6756 |
| 4. WebUI and TUI localization | #6759 | #6756 |
| 5. Native IM localization | #6760 | #6756 |

---

Built-in slash commands report results in the language selected when the command is sent. WebUI and TUI use the `$` skill picker instead of `/skill`; text channels retain `/skill`. `/stop` ends work without a chat reply in WebUI and TUI; text channels receive a simple confirmation without a task count. A successful `/model` switch updates the current session’s badge; failed switches leave it unchanged. Changing the interface language affects future replies. Previously received replies, including their search and copy text, stay as written.

Command handlers emit result events. The receiving channel decides whether and how to display them; text channels use the request language by default. Clients use a shared ten-language catalog. On first send, the WebUI validates the selected preset before saving the chat; a rejection leaves the draft intact. Deferred Dream and restart notifications retry transient history writes without delivering to a replacement session. `/compact` retains its existing lifecycle, and Telegram and Discord use their native locale information. No history migration is required; the WebUI/gateway same-version policy is unchanged.

Verification covers command dispatch, text and WebSocket delivery, transcript replay, first-send rejection, and deferred notifications. Live Telegram and Discord services were not exercised.

prs.title: feat(webui): edit and resend messages in the same session
prs.body:
**Current head: `a51f1ea21`, based on `main` at `0c45c7441`.** [All 20 CI checks passed](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/45027140708), including `CI required`. The Windows benchmarks and CI run below apply to earlier snapshots, not the current head.

Related to [NAN-92](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-92/webui-支持编辑并重新发送已发送的用户消息).

## What users get

In a saved topic, select **Edit message** beside your message on desktop, or under **Message actions** on mobile, to open an inline draft. **Cancel** preserves the conversation and composer. **Resend** replaces the selected message and its suffix and generates a reply in the same topic. **Fork** still makes a separate topic. This does not undo external tool effects. Edit the text of ordinary messages, including captions on uploads and local file attachments. Resending reuses the original files rather than uploading them again. If a file is missing or access has been revoked, the conversation and draft stay intact. Quotes, mentions, commands and special inputs are not converted to plain text. [User guide](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/a51f1ea21be4420ea50e9728bc64777db8d6bb49/docs/webui.md#edit-a-sent-message).

## Current behavior and verification

Edit-and-resend is an in-place fork at the selected input. A normal fork copies the prefix to a new topic; resend keeps that prefix in the same topic and writes the replacement. Both use the same prefix and transactional persistence code. A later append is not a conflict: resending at B discards an already appended C. A normal message sent after the replacement continues the current topic; it has no history-version precondition. A genuinely missing fork point cannot select a different row. Other connected tabs receive the replacement over WebSocket.

The session transaction stores the replacement and the original attachment references in the existing durable input queue. The worker then handles that input exactly as it handles a normal send. The model loop has no edit/fork branch, and a retry does not generate a second reply. Local file access is checked again before truncating the conversation.

On `25d2bcdbf`, two Chromium tabs on the production-built local gateway verified both message ordering and attachment reuse with a real model. A text file was uploaded once; changing the question made the model retrieve a different value from that same file. The second tab updated without reloading and the file remained attached after refresh. The restart regression also exercises resuming an accepted, not yet executed replacement with an image. Focused Python, UI and browser checks, the production build, type checks and import boundaries passed. Two unrelated startup-language UI tests also fail on the preceding head. The earlier Windows benchmarks were not rerun.

## Earlier verification (`68c11eaf0`)

[Earlier CI](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/44917107465). Synced `main` at `0dc8679ed`. On desktop and a 390px viewport, opening the editor on a collapsed message exposes the full text and resend controls; cancel restores the original collapsed message and keyboard focus. Edit admission no longer decodes answer bodies to identify the discarded suffix. A concurrent SQLite writer test verifies that a history page and its ETag describe the same snapshot and an edit based on an obsolete page is rejected.

### Historical comparison: `0dc8679ed` vs `68c11eaf0`

Both snapshots were separately production-built on Windows and run against the same deterministic loopback model, fixture data, dependencies and browser. Eight fresh gateway pairs × 16 measured pairs per operation; startup and within-pair order were balanced. Differences are PR minus `main`, in ms. For all five shared operations the one-sided 95% upper bound on the paired median was below the existing margin. This measures typical latency on this runner, not every device or tail latency.

| Shared operation | Paired median Δ | One-sided 95% upper bound | Margin |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Latest history (8 turns) | -0.29 | +0.61 | 1.00 |
| Latest history (192 turns) | -0.83 | +0.25 | 1.00 |
| Ordinary input acknowledgement | -0.20 | +0.20 | 1.00 |
| Ordinary input → completed reply | -2.44 | +0.56 | 5.00 |
| Navigate → latest message painted | +0.60 | +4.90 | 5.00 |

`main` has no edit-and-resend operation, so it has no like-for-like timing for that new feature. Earlier results against an older integration parent and the previous edit implementation are [historical diagnostics](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-92#comment-59285eab-02f7-45da-bd22-d08700295c79), not the readiness gate. [Measurement plan, all 640 raw pairs and confidence intervals for the current comparison](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-92#comment-03da91ef-d8e0-464f-940a-7719408576c5).

## Correctness evidence on `e42f74689`

- One owner serializes ordinary input and edits. The SQLite transaction checks the page-independent source identity, original text, revision and retry receipt, then changes both model history and display history. Admission failure leaves the old histories intact. Once accepted, a model failure belongs to the new turn. A transport retry does not schedule a second model request.
- **White-box:** reviewed admission/dispatch, cancellation, storage/crash boundaries, outbound ownership, HTTP pagination and frontend draft/connection lifecycle. Fixed canonical `input_id` on replacement and a late idle event that could leave its original run marked active. The late event releases only that owner and does not publish into a replaced history. Final focused Python selection: 81 passed.
- **Black-box:** two Chromium clients, production-built UI, real local gateway/SQLite/WebSocket and a deterministic HTTP model. Mouse, keyboard and touch; cancel with an outstanding composer draft; middle, first and paginated edits; reload and actual disconnect/reconnect. The provider saw exactly 3, 0 and 174 retained user inputs respectively, followed only by the edited input, once per edit. Older retained rows remained pageable; the topic/identity did not change. Two editors of the same revision produced one winner; reconnect/retry, busy/stale source, provider refusal and ordinary fork were checked independently. No uncaught browser exceptions. No physical device or external model was used.
- **Formal concurrency check:** [two TLA+ models, assumptions and reproduction commands](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/tree/e42f74689b0e41915d0c7d52939092cd50f4b062/verification/history-edit). All invariants held over 484 admission states and 132 delayed-delivery/reconnect states, with no unexpected deadlock. Removing transactional source validation or the retired-generation fence gave the expected counterexamples. These are bounded single-owner models assuming atomic SQLite commits, not an exactly-once guarantee for external side effects.

## Historical CI and snapshots (`e42f74689`)

[Test Suite 44722331397](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/44722331397) passed, including `CI required`. PR head `e42f74689`; Actions checked out `5a0fd420d`, merging that head onto `db0306b40`. The local correctness and timing runs use the PR head; ordinary timing uses its frozen integration parent `cd75dbfaa`, not moving main. No check or size/coverage budget was relaxed. Attempt 1's Windows native upgrade/recovery test reached the second `metadata-loss` journey, then `inspect_profiles()` raised `ValueError` while checking readiness after the second restart. The exact target's push CI skipped native acceptance. The preceding PR candidate passed the same step. Only that Windows job and downstream aggregate were re-requested on the unchanged merge; the original failure is not attributed to the edit without evidence. [First attempt's failure report](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/44722331397/artifacts/14624090600).

<details><summary>Historical performance results and diagnosis on e42f74689 (superseded by the current table above)</summary>

### Performance

**At that snapshot, performance was not signed off:** Latest page, 8 turns, Latest page, 192 turns, Ordinary input → completed reply, Navigate → latest message painted, Edit → completed reply. Do not treat passing CI as performance approval.

Windows, real same-version gateway/WebUI with a deterministic loopback model. Ordinary operations vs `cd75dbfaa` (integration parent); edits vs `d06d326ad` (previous edit implementation). Four fresh gateway pairs, 16 measured pairs each, per metric. Snapshots on the same volume. AB/BA balanced at startup and randomized within adjacent pairs; warmups excluded, no other observations discarded. Reads decode eight real HTTP responses per observation. Render requires the expected message in view followed by an animation frame. Edit replaces turn 49 of 96, with one provider execution and the exact retained prefix. All durations are ms.

| Path | Baseline median | PR median | Paired Δ [two-sided 95% interval] | One-sided upper / margin | Gate |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Latest page, 8 turns | 13.21 | 14.36 | +0.88 [-0.28, +1.62] | +1.54 / 1.00 | Not established |
| Latest page, 192 turns | 14.70 | 15.27 | +0.64 [-0.51, +1.60] | +1.19 / 1.00 | Not established |
| Ordinary input ACK | 6.07 | 5.85 | +0.05 [-0.38, +0.53] | +0.48 / 1.00 | Pass |
| Ordinary input → completed reply | 70.04 | 72.48 | +1.91 [-1.51, +6.17] | +5.22 / 5.00 | Not established |
| Navigate → latest message painted | 99.65 | 95.45 | -0.15 [-7.80, +7.20] | +5.30 / 5.00 | Not established |
| Edit ACK | 13.19 | 10.79 | -1.57 [-2.25, -0.85] | -0.92 / 1.00 | Pass |
| Edit → completed reply | 86.31 | 100.96 | +9.27 [+3.27, +14.12] | +14.02 / 5.00 | Not established |

The gate is the one-sided 95% upper bound on the paired median delta (candidate minus baseline), strictly below max(5% of the baseline median, 1 ms for reads/ACKs or 5 ms for completed turns/render). Intervals use 12,000 deterministic stratified bootstrap draws across observations within the four blocks. Cross-block and machine-to-machine variability, tails, physical-device latency and the latency of an external model are not bounded by this test.

On the previous `aa18f9e45` snapshot (48 pairs; gateway blocks separated in time), short/long reads had paired medians +1.67/+2.24 ms and upper bounds +2.80/+3.43 ms vs a 1 ms margin. Ordinary ACK, paint and edit completion also failed to establish non-inferiority. Profiling identified a duplicate SQLite snapshot-header lookup. This candidate reuses immutable headers only within one transaction and sends the regular 40-event page after replacement, with a cursor for the rest. The previous samples were retained, not pooled.


| Path | Baseline / candidate block medians (ms), in measurement order | Min–max of all samples: baseline / candidate (ms) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Latest page, 8 turns | 19.14 / 20.84; 11.75 / 14.21; 13.03 / 12.07; 12.95 / 12.93 | 6.92–24.56 / 6.77–26.59 |
| Latest page, 192 turns | 22.50 / 17.84; 13.20 / 14.74; 12.98 / 12.78; 14.03 / 14.99 | 7.40–25.67 / 8.04–26.99 |
| Ordinary input ACK | 5.75 / 6.21; 7.06 / 7.07; 5.77 / 5.41; 5.77 / 5.77 | 4.70–24.72 / 4.66–37.74 |
| Ordinary input → completed reply | 66.80 / 70.06; 84.42 / 92.85; 68.16 / 69.86; 67.26 / 69.63 | 59.76–114.63 / 59.57–130.79 |
| Navigate → latest message painted | 90.60 / 90.45; 102.80 / 108.55; 102.30 / 100.40; 92.70 / 90.90 | 65.50–163.60 / 67.20–149.50 |
| Edit ACK | 11.10 / 10.02; 12.36 / 9.92; 16.95 / 13.63; 13.63 / 12.48 | 10.03–25.28 / 7.71–186.72 |
| Edit → completed reply | 74.88 / 87.17; 78.57 / 82.53; 114.81 / 123.42; 93.31 / 109.56 | 68.64–346.62 / 70.84–463.34 |

**Where to investigate next:** on an equal 48-input context, the interval between the fixture provider returning and the client receiving `turn_end` was 16.8–16.9 ms (old edit), 23.6–24.7 ms (candidate edit), and 22.6–24.6 ms (ordinary input on the integrated main baseline), as ranges of two diagnostic block medians. Independent tracing found prompt-context observation and four display-history appends on both current main and the candidate, versus two appends on the previous edit implementation. This explains a candidate path to optimize; it does not assign the full end-to-end difference to one function. Recheck the shared delivery path on a quiet runner without dropping context graphs, persistence or generation checks. In ordinary HTTP reads the candidate already makes fewer SQL statements (25/37 vs 27/39), selects the same 24/42 records, and does not load full model history. These diagnostics do not override the failed timing gates. [Raw paired timings and a relocatable Windows benchmark harness](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-92#comment-e64c8f32-6625-410f-b27e-ac69baf99db7).

prs.title: feat(webui): show desktop message actions in the side gutters
prs.body:
## Why

Copying a reply on desktop used to take two clicks: open the `…` menu, then choose Copy. The narrow layout already offered one-click copy. Desktop should be just as quick without putting a permanent toolbar in the reading column.

## What changed

- On wide screens with hover, show the available actions directly beside the active message on hover or keyboard focus. Outgoing messages use the right gutter; assistant replies and incoming agent-to-agent bubbles use the left. Copy, fork and activity no longer require opening a menu.
- Center the action icons on the first line of message text, even below an image or quote. Align the timestamp under the first icon, use the built-in hover hint for its full value, and keep source details available on click.
- Only offer “New chat from here” when the view can actually start a chat. This removes a nonfunctional button from read-only subagent transcripts.
- Remove unused menu attributes and CSS. Replace assertions about DOM nesting and pointer-event styles with browser checks of placement and an actual clipboard read.

## Scope

Narrow screens and devices without hover keep their existing touch controls. This is a WebUI change only; it does not change gateway behavior, data formats or the client/host contract.

## Verification

- 426 component tests passed across six affected suites, including fork availability, keyboard focus after collapsing activity, and timestamp hints.
- 80 Chromium tests passed across the five affected browser suites, covering both sides of the conversation, text and timestamp alignment, one-click copy, and the mobile action sheet.
- Browser TypeScript checks, WebUI lint and the production build passed.

Resolves [NAN-482](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-482).

Catalog admission rule 11 requires subscription-backed plugins to declare requires_auth and let Hermes send the request without exposing the token. The built-in request broker currently supports openai-codex but not copilot. Could Hermes and/or the github-copilot Labs provider expose a brokered request for the account-advertised POST /v1/images/generations endpoint?

Use case: https://github.com/xiaofeng-zheng/hermes-copilot-image registers an image-generation backend for image_generate. Its standalone implementation works, but resolves the token in plugin code, so we are holding back the catalog submission. We want to keep using the existing profile sign-in over HTTPS, without Copilot CLI, another token store, or handing a token to the image backend.

Ideally Hermes would choose the active account origin, attach the provider-owned headers, enforce the allowed path/method and refuse redirects; the backend would receive only the response. Is there an existing supported seam we should use instead?

issues.body:
## Summary

The managed local llama.cpp runtime is pinned to **b12144**, which predates the `inkling2` / `inkling2_loop` architectures (upstream llama.cpp #32694, first in **b12600**, 2026-11-20). Any Inkling 2 Mini GGUF therefore fails to load, and the desktop shows it as a message that never gets an answer.

Nothing in the UI says the engine is too old: the "engine is up to date" state is pin-relative only.

## Environment

- macOS 27.2.1, Apple Silicon (M4 Pro, 24 GB unified memory)
- Hermes desktop, managed runtime: `llamacpp-metal` **b12144**, commit `69ee2ecc0`
- Executable in use: `~/.hermes/tools/llamacpp-metal-12144-darwin-arm64/llama-server`
- Model added manually via Settings → Local models: `Inkling-2-Mini-UD-IQ4_XS.gguf`
  - header: `general.architecture = inkling2`, `inkling2.block_count = 48`, 734 tensors over blk 0..23

## Actual behavior

llama-server starts and listens, then exits during load:

```
E llama_model_load: error loading model: unknown model architecture: 'inkling2'
E llama_model_load_from_file_impl: failed to load model
E cmn  common_init_: failed to load model '/Users/brian/.hermes/models/Inkling-2-Mini-UD-IQ4_XS.gguf'
E srv  load_model: failed to load model, '/Users/brian/.hermes/models/Inkling-2-Mini-UD-IQ4_XS.gguf'
```

The client sees HTTP 500 and burns its whole retry budget on a deterministic failure:

```
WARNING agent.conversation_loop: API call failed (attempt 1/3) error_type=InternalServerError
        provider=custom model=Inkling-2-Mini-UD-IQ4_XS summary=HTTP 500: model name=... failed to load
...  attempt 2/3 ... attempt 3/3 ...
WARNING agent.conversation_loop: Provider unavailable (server_error) — auto-recovery cycle 1/5, retrying in 18s
```

So the user experience is "I sent a message and got nothing", with no diagnostic surfaced anywhere in the app.

## Why the UI cannot tell the user

`hermes_cli/web_routers/local_models.py`:

```python
"update_available": bool(section.get("enabled") and engine is not None and current is None),
```

This compares *installed tag vs pinned tag*. No code path compares the pin to upstream, so a pin that is hundreds of builds behind still renders as "up to date". The `min_engine` gate exists but only applies to catalog entries (`_engine_too_old(entry.min_engine)` inside `_download_target`), so a manually added GGUF gets no gate and no hint.

## Upstream state

- `inkling2` / `inkling2_loop` support: llama.cpp **#32694**, first tag **b12600**
- loop scale fix for the `inkling2_loop` layout: **#32704**, merged 2026-11-21 (`690b87d`); verified contained in **b12642** (`compare 690b87d...b12642` → `status: ahead`, `behind_by: 0`)
- `main` in this repo currently pins **b12144 for all five backends**; the last bump was #154258 (2026-11-12), and there is no open bump PR

**Asset gotcha for whoever bumps:** upstream does not publish a `macos-arm64` archive for every tag. Checked today: `b12607` (which is what `pm.update.llama_app_latest()` currently resolves to), `b12610` and `b12630` return **404**, while `b12144`, `b12600`, `b12620`, `b12633`, `b12635`, `b12640`, `b12641`, `b12642` return 200. A blind `hermes pm update` on macOS would resolve to b12607 and fail the download.

## Second-order finding (a bump alone does not fix most users)

Testing the pinned file against a locally built **b12642**, the architecture is accepted but the file is rejected on tensors:

```
E llama_model_load: error loading model: check_tensor_dims: tensor 'blk.24.attn_q.weight' not found
```

Reason: the popular Unsloth root-directory GGUFs (`unsloth/Inkling-2-Mini-GGUF`, incl. `UD-IQ4_XS` 15.7 GB) use a fork layout — `general.architecture = inkling2` with 48 visible layers. Mainline reads only the `Mainline_Support/` variants (`inkling2_loop`, `block_count = 24`, which also need #32704). So after a pin bump, users who grabbed the root file will hit a *different* opaque failure.

## Proposed fix

1. **Bump the five `llamacpp-*` pins to >= b12642**, choosing a tag that actually publishes per-target archives (see the 404 list above) — or make `latest_versions()` skip tags without the target's asset.
2. **Treat "engine too old" as a first-class state for manually added GGUFs**: read `general.architecture` from the file header, map known architectures to a minimum build, and surface "this model needs llama.cpp >= bXXXX — update the engine" in the model row, instead of a 500 plus retry storm.
3. **Catalog entry for Inkling 2 Mini** (mainline `inkling2_loop` layout only, mmproj asset declared) — and a warning when a user adds a `block_count > physical tensor layers` file, so the fork-layout trap is visible before download completes.
4. Optionally: when the pinned engine moves, do not silently skip the optional `llamacpp-*` package during `hermes update` — prompt or at least report it, since the runtime cannot use the new pin until the binary is reinstalled.

## Workaround today

Run an external `llama-server` from b12642 (or later) with a mainline-layout GGUF and add it as a custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Note #158619 hides external llama.cpp providers from the WebApp model selector when the managed runtime is disabled, which makes this workaround harder than it should be.

issues.body:
**Summary.** Hark Pro, OpenAI dots, Meta Muse and Grok Bot all pair user-scheduled jobs with a background "look for ways to help" pass. Users mostly complain about the background pass: noise, broad reads, late timing. Hermes keeps every proactive run as a job you approved, with a visible prompt and schedule. The next steps below make those jobs quieter, cheaper and easier to stop, without adding a background scanner.

- **Step 1 = PR #158289**: the model proposes jobs from conversation, and each new job asks on a "Schedule this job?" card.
- **Inbox = separate PR (in progress)**: a Desktop/Web feed of cron results you can reply to.
- Step 1 also measures unwanted proposals (past events, "don't remind me", hypotheticals, finished tasks) across three models.

Full research with sources is in the first comment below.

## How the others do it

| | Hark Pro | OpenAI dots | Grok Bot | Meta Muse |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Trigger** | Email + connected services + memory; scheduled and conditional tasks | "Proactive research" over connected apps; scheduled tasks; event monitors | User routines (clock, Slack, webhook, email); primary-Bot check-ins | Reminders, standing goals, connector pushes, location |
| **Cadence** | Not published | Not published; the dot picks its own wake times | Routines ≥5 min apart; check-ins on a platform clock | User-set; reported 30-min heartbeat |
| **Output lands** | Home: one-tap Action Buttons, Panels, one chat | The dot's chat, Slack, text; iOS reply-from-notification | Bot chat, push, Slack/Teams DM | Chat, Ideas tab, Feed, WhatsApp |
| **Approval** | Asks before spend/send/share unless you grant standing permission for that kind of task | 4-level Custom Rules + Auto-review model check | Draft cards; Allow once / Always / Deny | Approval cards (once / task / site / always) |
| **Unattended** | Within standing permission (e.g. top up a lunch card) | Background research is read-only, enforced in code | Writes become drafts | Pre-authorized acts |
| **Memory** | Learned; "forget" on request | ChatGPT memory + private notes (no per-item delete) | Chat transcript | Editable memory files |
| **Cost control** | Relative usage tiers | Delegated tasks count toward limits | Hourly run caps | Weekly limit; users move polling into scripts |
| **"Stop that"** | "quiet this" on a card; pause scheduled tasks | Pause, stop and cancel are three separate actions; Custom Rule "never…" | Per-routine pause; check-ins off only via admin toggle | "Turn it off / dial down"; 👍/👎 |

## Ranked next steps

| # | Idea | Builds on | Label |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Model proposes jobs from conversation; each asks on a card | cron + approval card | **STEP 1** (#158289) |
| 2 | Every recurring job states when it speaks and when it ends (dots' "only message me if…" recipe), and the card shows both | `[SILENT]`, card copy | STEP 2 |
| 3 | Recurring watch jobs use a change gate by default; docs say gate output should only grow | `monitor_script` / `monitor_url` | STEP 2 |
| 4 | "Don't suggest this again": a declined card or removed job writes one memory line the model sees next time | memory | STEP 2 |
| 5 | Same output N runs in a row → one "pause this job?" message, then stop repeating | cron run history | STEP 2 |
| 6 | A failed check is never silent: throttled "check failed: <source>", tested separately from "unchanged" | monitor gate, watchdog | STEP 2 |
| 7 | Edits to model-created jobs (prompt, script, schedule, delivery) ask again on a "Change this job?" card | approval card | **STEP 1** (#158289) |
| 8 | One lever: `cron.proactive: create\|offer\|off` (default `create`) | config | STEP 2 (own PR, next) |
| 8b | Damaged `[SILENT]` markers (`[SLENT]`, `[ SILENT ]`, a cut-off `[`) no longer reach the user | response filter | STEP 2 (own PR, in progress; consolidates ~10 community PRs) |
| 9 | Card shows what the job reads (`enabled_toolsets`), kept narrow | `enabled_toolsets`, card | STEP 2 |
| 10 | Pacing: one one-shot per step at the moment it matters; evals for lead time and for unwanted proposals | cron one-shot, evals | STEP 2 |
| 11 | Inbox items with one-tap Pause / Don't suggest / Open in chat | Inbox | Inbox PR |
| 12 | Reply-from-notification for Desktop/Web Inbox push (messaging platforms already have this) | Inbox, push | LATER |
| 13 | Named rules surface (allow / ask / block) | approvals config | LATER: cards + memory cover it today |
| 14 | Background read-only sweep of all connected sources | — | NO: it's an overnight scanner; users who want one can create it as an ordinary job |

## What users asked for in #158289

- **Per-job memory and change gates by default**: @askclaw-vesper (one ungated watcher: 1,219 runs, ~159M tokens, 402 repeats), @eyedeaco, @humphreyyy, @33hodl
- **Remember declined or removed subjects**: @mselcukozturk, @33hodl, @eddwithers
- **Measure unwanted proposals, not just helpful ones**: @yqecea, @eddwithers, @mselcukozturk (negative eval set offered), @Lapot300
- **Failed checks stay visible; broken gates get repaired**: @yqecea, @33hodl, @CommanderROR9
- **Card completeness, edits re-ask, offer-don't-create when no card can show**: @AtlasOmnia, @quotumorg, @eyedeaco, @kronos-socotek
- **Damaged `[SILENT]` markers leak (patch offered)**: @mselcukozturk
- **Commitment lifecycle (goal, next event, expiry)**: @Lapot300, @kronos-socotek
- **Verification of locale parity and CI**: @salch-cred

issues.body:
### Summary

With the sidebar's **Archived** filter on, the view is internally inconsistent: the **SESSIONS** list switches to the archived set, but the messaging platform sections (Telegram, etc.) keep listing **live** threads. An archived messaging conversation therefore shows up in the wrong place — it lands in the generic SESSIONS list instead of its own platform section, while that section displays live chats.

*Corrected after review: an earlier revision of this issue said the archived thread was "unreachable" and appeared in "neither" list. That was wrong — it is reachable from the archived SESSIONS list. The defect is misplacement plus a live/archived mismatch, not absence.*

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Have at least one archived `source=telegram` session and at least one live one in the same profile.
2. Open the sidebar filter menu and tick **Archived**.
3. The archived Telegram thread appears in the **SESSIONS** list, while the **Telegram** section above it lists only live chats.

### Expected Behavior

Archived is a view of its own, and it should be internally consistent: archived messaging threads belong in their platform section, and the generic SESSIONS list should hold the non-messaging archive. That mirrors how the live view already works — messaging-platform sessions are fetched as their own slice rather than mixed into recents.

### Actual Behavior

The platform sections keep their live-only list, and archived messaging rows stay in the SESSIONS list.

### Root cause

Two different pools with different source rules:

- `$archivedSessions` (`store/sidebar-archive.ts`) is fetched with **no source filter** — `listAllProfileSessions(500, 0, 'only', 'recent', 'all', {}, offset)` — so it contains archived messaging rows. The Archived SESSIONS list then renders them.
- The messaging sections always read their own live slice: `filterSessionsByProfileScope(messagingSessions, displayScope)`, where `messagingSessions` comes from sidebar slices requested with `archived=exclude`.

```ts
// apps/desktop/src/app/chat/sidebar/index.tsx
const pool = showArchived ? archivedSessions : sessions            // recents only
const visibleMessagingSessions = useMemo(
  () => filterSessionsByProfileScope(messagingSessions, displayScope),   // always live
  [messagingSessions, displayScope]
)
```

### Suggested fix

Split the archived set by source instead of pointing the messaging pool at all of it. Pointing the platform sections at `archivedSessions.filter(isMessagingSource)` — the obvious first attempt — **double-renders** every archived messaging row, because the archived SESSIONS list already contains it.

- messaging-source rows → their platform sections
- everything else → the SESSIONS list

Put the split in a helper under `src/lib` rather than inline, so `index.tsx` (already at its file-size cap, which may only shrink) gets shorter rather than longer. The per-platform "load more" affordance should stay off in this view, but not for the reason originally given here: `listEveryArchivedSession` pages until every archived row is loaded, so the archive is already complete rather than "one capped query".

### Environment

- v0.23.3+334, commit `aeb5a071069`
- Windows 11 desktop build (`win-unpacked`)

### Additional Context

Adjacent but distinct from #157368 (messaging sessions excluded from the Projects tree) — that one is about the Projects grouping.

issues.body:
<!-- agent-origin:v1 model: claude-opus-5-5 -->
**Summary.** A steer the user sent and the surface acknowledged can be lost without any trace. It happens when the turn it was aimed at ends in a content-policy refusal or a compression-exhausted reset. The gateway settles those two results by evicting the cached agent, and a steer still buffered on that agent is not carried over. This is on main today; #157529 does not introduce it.

This collects the follow-ups from the review of #157529 (found by @BearHuddleston). Related: #157525, #157529.

## 1. Steer lost when the gateway evicts the agent after a content-policy refusal or a compression-exhausted reset

**Where.** `gateway/run_turn_persistence.py`, where both settlement paths call `_evict_cached_agent`:
- `_hmwa_retain_content_policy_refused_turn`, after a confirmed rewind of the refused turn;
- `_hmwa_rotate_exhausted_session`, on the exhausted-session reset.

Eviction does not move a buffered steer (`_pending_steer`) to the rebuilt agent or onto the session queue.

**How it happens.**
- On main, a steer drained before the failing request goes into that request. The rewind or reset then removes it with the turn.
- A steer that arrives while that request is in flight stays buffered on the agent and is dropped at eviction.
- #157529 does not change either case: it adds no hand-back on these results.

**Impact.** The user is told the steer was delivered, and it is never run. There is no error and no trace in the transcript.

**Suggested fix (gateway side).**
- Before `_evict_cached_agent` on these two paths, take any buffered steer off the agent and queue it on the session, so that it runs once the turn is settled. Today `_defer_past_exhaustion_reset` (`gateway/run_busy.py`) carries a returned `pending_steer` past the reset only when another event is already queued, and the content-policy eviction carries nothing.
- Exporting it as `pending_steer` from the agent is not enough on its own. Some hosts ignore or replace the turn result (kanban recovery, ACP, a muted CLI turn), and a review of #157529 showed they lose it there.
- More generally: settle a failed turn (rewind, reset) before running any follow-up, whatever queued it. Main already reaches these paths when a queued message follows those failures.

This was found by reading the code; it has not been reproduced through the gateway yet.

## 1b. A requeued steer handed back at finalize is dropped by hosts that ignore `pending_steer`
When a steer cannot be placed after a tool result in the current turn, it is requeued. If the turn then ends text-only, `finalize_turn` hands it back as `pending_steer`. Hosts that ignore or replace that field drop it:
- the kanban goal loop and recovery (`gateway/session_kanban.py`);
- the quiet CLI recover (`hermes_cli/cli_single_query.py`);
- ACP;
- a muted CLI turn.

On main this already happens for a history with no tool row (checked on 6161a34). #157529 extends it to a text-only turn after an earlier turn that used a tool.

A steer requeued before a first call that then fails stays buffered on the agent until its next turn. Exporting it instead loses it in the same hosts.

Suggested direction: have those hosts consume `pending_steer` (run it as the next turn, as the messaging gateway does), or make the hand-back contract explicit for every host.

## 2. Smaller items from the same review (not regressions; optional)
- **Todo-fold re-anchor** (`agent/turn_context.py`, around line 329): after turn-start compaction folds the todo list into this turn's ask, an older identical ask can win the re-anchor. The helper has 13 call sites.
- **Requeue order** (`agent/interrupt_control.py`, `requeue_drained_steer`): a requeued steer goes back *behind* a steer that arrived after the drain. It also matches the last drain by text, so in a narrow case it can restore an already consumed ticket.
- **Finalizer hand-back** (`agent/turn_finalizer.py`, around line 882):
  - The leftover hand-back runs on an interrupted turn too, so a steer can outlive a Stop that lands during the model call.
  - In the classic CLI, an explicit `/steer /x` or `/steer !x` handed back this way is queued on `_pending_input` and runs as a command.

issues.title: [Bug]: test_kanban_cli_dispatch_passthrough leaks hermes_cli modules into sys.modules, failing ~130 unrelated tests with the real-home guard

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: comp/cli

labels.name: comp/cron
labels.description: Cron scheduler and job management
