labels.description: Medium — degraded but workaround exists

issues.body:
### Summary

`tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_cli_dispatch_passthrough.py`'s `isolated_kanban_home` fixture deletes every `hermes_cli*` / `hermes_state*` module from `sys.modules` and **never restores them**. Every later test in the same pytest process then holds a different copy of `hermes_cli` than the one in `sys.modules`, and modules re-imported after `monkeypatch` restores the real `HERMES_HOME` bind to the real home.

The visible effect is enormous: running `pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban*.py` in one process reports **136 failed / 483 passed / 25 skipped**, while the same files pass individually and in small groups. The dominant failure signature is the repo's own isolation guard firing:

```
tests/home_io_guard.py:160: AssertionError: TEST BUG: file I/O against the REAL hermes home:
C:\Users\David\AppData\Local\hermes\manifest.json
    Use the isolated HERMES_HOME or a temporary fixture instead.
```

### Steps to Reproduce

```bash
# 2 tests, passes
pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_cli_dispatch_passthrough.py \
       tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_credential_startup_exit.py -q
# 17 passed

# the whole glob, fails loudly
pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban*.py -q
# 136 failed, 483 passed, 25 skipped
```

Minimal ordering that reproduces it:

```bash
pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_cli_dispatch_passthrough.py \
       tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_credential_startup_exit.py -q
# before the fix: 4 failed, 13 passed   (all 4 in credential_startup_exit)
```

Bisected: `test_kanban_credential_startup_exit.py` passes alone (15 passed) and after the twelve alphabetically-earlier `test_kanban_*` files (91 passed); it only fails once `test_kanban_cli_dispatch_passthrough.py` has run in the same process.

### Root cause

```python
@pytest.fixture()
def isolated_kanban_home(monkeypatch):
    test_home = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="kanban_cli_passthrough_")
    os.makedirs(os.path.join(test_home, "profiles", "default"), exist_ok=True)
    monkeypatch.setenv("HERMES_HOME", test_home)
    for mod in list(sys.modules.keys()):
        if mod.startswith("hermes_cli") or mod.startswith("hermes_state") or mod == "hermes_constants":
            del sys.modules[mod]
    yield test_home          # <-- modules are never put back
```

`monkeypatch` restores the environment variable at teardown; nothing restores `sys.modules`. So:

- a module imported before this test keeps pointing at the pre-deletion object,
- a module re-imported after it is a *different* object with its own module-level state,
- and any re-import after teardown resolves `HERMES_HOME` to the real home again — which is why the guard sees I/O against the real `manifest.json`.

### Suggested fix

Snapshot and restore the module objects, so the re-import only lasts for the test that needs it:

```python
    def _ours(name):
        return name.startswith("hermes_cli") or name.startswith("hermes_state") or name == "hermes_constants"

    saved = {name: mod for name, mod in sys.modules.items() if _ours(name)}
    for name in saved:
        del sys.modules[name]
    try:
        yield test_home
    finally:
        for name in [name for name in sys.modules if _ours(name)]:
            del sys.modules[name]
        sys.modules.update(saved)
```

Verified locally on Windows 11: the pair goes 4 failed/13 passed → **17 passed**, the 13-file group goes 4 failed/87 passed → **91 passed**, and the full glob's failure count drops sharply (a fresh full-glob run is in progress).

### Why it matters

This is not cosmetic. The pollution makes a green kanban suite impossible to obtain in one process, which hides real regressions: a change that broke two tests in `test_kanban_worker_socket_recovery.py` was invisible in the noise of 136 unrelated failures, and a reviewer had to bisect by hand to tell the two apart.

### Environment

- Windows 11, git-bash / MSYS2
- v0.23.3+334, commit `aeb5a071069`
- Python 3.14, pytest 9.1.1

issues.title: [Bug]: kanban dispatcher imports an operator script from the Hermes home into core (sys.path mutation, parents[2] home guess)

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Medium — degraded but workaround exists

labels.name: area/profiles
labels.description: Multi-profile isolation, HERMES_HOME scoping

issues.body:
### Summary

`hermes_cli/kanban_db_dispatch.py` imports an operator's personal script out of the Hermes home into core, and does it in four ways that core code should not:

```python
def _fleet_wall_module_get():
    for home in (os.environ.get("HERMES_HOME"), str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2])):
        ...
        scripts = Path(home) / "scripts"
        if not (scripts / "lane_ledger.py").is_file():
            continue
        if str(scripts) not in sys.path:
            sys.path.insert(0, str(scripts))     # permanent, process-wide
        import lane_ledger                        # operator script into core
```

1. **Hardcoded install layout.** `Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]` is treated as a Hermes home. That is only true when the checkout happens to sit directly inside one.
2. **Raw `os.environ["HERMES_HOME"]`.** Under multiplex the env var carries the **launch** profile's home, so every other profile drives the same operator ledger instead of its own.
3. **Permanent `sys.path` mutation.** The entry outlives the call. Any later `import lane_ledger` — or any unrelated module that happens to be named that — resolves to the operator's script.
4. **Core depends on an ops file that may not exist.** A fresh install has no `scripts/lane_ledger.py`; the code path is silently inert rather than absent by design.

### Observable symptom

It makes the dispatcher read the **real** Hermes home even when a test has sandboxed `HERMES_HOME`, because the import machinery scans the directory:

```
tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_parent_reopen_invalidation.py::
  test_dashboard_and_db_paths_produce_identical_outcomes
E   AssertionError: TEST BUG: file I/O against the REAL hermes home:
    <hermes_home>/scripts
```

The repo's own isolation guard is catching it. That is the guard working correctly — the production code is reaching where it should not.

### Environment

- v0.23.3+334, commit `aeb5a071069` (the code arrived in a later local commit)
- Windows 11, Python 3.14, pytest 9.1.1
- `<hermes_home>/scripts/lane_ledger.py` present (40 KB), so the path is live, not dead

### Tactical fix applied locally (and why it is only tactical)

Resolve through the real home resolver and load by file location, with no `sys.path` change:

```python
from hermes_constants import get_hermes_home
ledger_path = Path(get_hermes_home()) / "scripts" / "lane_ledger.py"
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("hermes_lane_ledger", ledger_path)
module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
spec.loader.exec_module(module)
```

That removes the `parents[2]` guess, the raw env read, and the permanent path entry, and the failing test goes green (`test_kanban_parent_reopen_invalidation.py` 4 passed). But **core still imports an operator script**, which is the actual design problem.

### Suggested architectural fix

Invert it: core should fire the existing `on_kanban_dispatch_tick` hook with the rate-limit facts, and the fleet-wall logic should live in a plugin that resolves the ledger itself. Core then has no knowledge of `lane_ledger` at all.

**Caveat for whoever implements it:** plugins are opt-in (`hermes_cli/plugins_discovery.py:122 _get_enabled_plugins()` reads the `plugins.enabled` allow-list). A naive move would make the feature silently dead for anyone who has not enabled the new plugin — strictly worse than the current coupling. The move needs a default-on path for this plugin, or the feature needs to relocate to the ops side (the dispatcher tick's caller) instead. Worth deciding deliberately rather than as a drive-by.

### Additional Context

Found by an independent review pass while chasing unrelated test failures; the coupling had been committed as part of a batch of kanban work rather than as a deliberate design. `_note_quota_wall()`'s own rate-limit requeue bookkeeping is core's job and is not the problem — only the `lane_ledger` reach-through is.

issues.title: [Bug]: Discord thread process-completion wake refused admission_conflict every 60s forever — attempt cap never fires and notify-mode=off has no effect

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: comp/gateway
labels.description: Gateway runner, session dispatch, delivery

labels.name: platform/discord
labels.description: Discord bot adapter

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Medium — degraded but workaround exists

issues.body:
### Summary

A process-completion watch tied to one Discord thread is refused with `admission_conflict` **every 60 seconds, indefinitely** — 494 occurrences in a single gateway log, still firing after 6 hours. Two things that should stop it don't:

1. **The attempt cap never fires.** `_MAX_COMPLETION_INJECTION_ATTEMPTS = 8` (`gateway/run_notifications.py:68`) should produce one `"completion for … was refused 8 times; falling back to the notify_mode=… notice"` line per eight refusals. In the same log there are **3** such lines against **494** refusals — so the loop producing this pair is not running the capped path.
2. **`display.background_process_notifications: off` has no effect on it.** Set on disk and confirmed read by a fresh process (`False`), the loop continued at the same cadence. Restarting with the value already `off` at boot (so a fresh worker snapshots it) still continued.

The loop also survives gateway restarts and a live turn in the affected thread.

### Environment

- Hermes Agent `v0.22.4`, Python 3.14.7, Ubuntu (kernel 6.8.0), single profile, **not** multiplexed
- Platform: Discord (thread), `chat=1562977450600702004`, guild `1548996776000888852`
- Session: `20261022_235423_95462272`, `chat_type=thread`, `origin.user_name=selig` (not null), no `end_reason`, `expiry_finalized=0`

### Log signature

```
19:59:23,834 INFO  gateway.run: Watch pattern notification — injecting for discord chat=1562977450600702004 thread=1562977450600702004
19:59:23,840 WARNING gateway.run: Watch notification not admitted for discord chat=1562977450600702004: admission_conflict
20:00:24,203 INFO  gateway.run: Watch pattern notification — injecting for discord chat=1562977450600702004 thread=1562977450600702004
20:00:24,207 WARNING gateway.run: Watch notification not admitted for discord chat=1562977450600702004: admission_conflict
```

Inter-line gaps measured over 20 consecutive ticks: `60, 60, 61, 60, 60, 61, 60, 60, 61, 60, 61, 60, 60, 60, 61, 60, 61, 60, 60, 19` — flat 60s, the `_COMPLETION_INJECTION_RETRY_MAX_DELAY` value. The refusal lands **4 ms** after the inject line, so it is a deterministic state check, not a transient race.

Sequence from the start of the episode (backoff restarts on every boot):

- First refusal `2026-10-23 16:12`; the `gateway_routing` row for that session was rewritten at **16:08:15**, four minutes earlier, while the session's `runtime_generation` was 17.
- Restart #1 (18:15): pid 160 → 128391. Refusals resumed 25 s later, backoff restarting from 4 s: `4, 8, 16, 32, 60, 60, …`
- Live turn in the thread at 19:58:15 (`msg='hello'`): response delivered, session grew 126 → 129 messages, `runtime_generation` **17 → 18**, routing row re-stamped at 19:58:20. Next tick refused anyway.
- Restart #2 (20:03) with `display.background_process_notifications: off` already on disk: pid 128391 → 135018, 9 refusals in the first 5.7 minutes at the same 60s cadence.

### What I ruled out

- **Poisoned admission record.** No `RETIRED_PREFIX + session_id` rows, no `gateway.terminal_admission.v1.*` rows anywhere in `state_meta`. `session_admissions` has 18 rows for the session, all `status=terminal`, `outcome=completed`, newest at `generation=18`.
- **Stale route/generation mismatch alone.** Bumping the generation with a real turn (`17 → 18`, route re-stamped in the same second) did not change admission.
- **Pruning the session.** `hermes sessions prune --chat-id …` skips it (open session); and no storage-side change should matter, since the retry reads routing from the queued event (`"Routing comes from the queued event, never the active foreground message"`).
- **Config mode gate.** See above — off at boot, confirmed `False` by `load_user_config_effective`, made no difference. There is no `HERMES_BACKGROUND_NOTIFICATIONS` env override and no `profiles/` directory.
- **Watcher attempt cap.** 494 refusals vs 3 `falling back to the notify_mode` lines.

### Suspected area

`gateway/run_notifications.py` — between `_drain_watch_notifications` (mode gate at `:733`, requeue via `_requeue_refused_watch_event`, no counter) and `_run_process_watcher` (`:1763`, capped at `_MAX_COMPLETION_INJECTION_ATTEMPTS`). The observed behaviour (60s flat, no cap, mode-independent, rearmed at boot) matches a requeue loop that has neither the cap nor the mode gate, with the event reconstructed at startup.

### Impact

Log churn only — nothing is delivered, no agent turn is produced, and the affected session works normally for real messages. At one line pair a minute it is ~2,900 log lines/day and it masks real watch notifications for that thread.

### Related

- #140189 — undeliverable process-completion notification retried forever, no backoff/cap (5s cadence, Feishu, multiplexed)
- #143447 — automation wakes refused `admission_conflict` forever when the lane's profile route postdates the session origin (matches the 16:08 route re-stamp here)
- #143306 — shared Discord thread speaker changes strand pinned completion wakes with `admission_conflict`
- #142402 — background-process completions refused when the stored origin's `user_name` is null (here it is `selig`, so not this one)

  - Fold in the 1-line `scripts/release.py:733` `--date` help typo fix (`YYYY.M.D` vs `%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ`).

issues.body:
### `test_cmd_update_boundary_finalizes_on_early_exit` fails on shared-venv dev checkouts: `cmd_update` re-execs the owning install with pytest's argv

On any checkout whose interpreter is a venv **owned by a different checkout** (a shared dev venv), this test fails on a pristine tree. CI does not see it because there the venv belongs to the checked-out repo, so `owning_install_root()` returns `None`.

## Repro (pristine `upstream/main` @ `0f602c5f6f`, dedicated worktree, no local modifications)

```
venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  "tests/hermes_cli/test_update_receipt.py::TestCommandBoundaryFinalization::test_cmd_update_boundary_finalizes_on_early_exit" -q
```

```
⚠ /Users/liyuan/github/ai/hermes-agent/venv is running the checkout at /Users/liyuan/github/ai/<wt>, not its own code.
→ Updating /Users/liyuan/github/ai/hermes-agent with its own updater; this also points its venv back at it.
-----------------------------
hermes: 'tests/hermes_cli/test_update_receipt.py::TestCommandBoundaryFinalization::test_cmd_update_boundary_finalizes_on_early_exit' is not a `hermes` command.
...
>       assert latest is not None
E       assert None is not None
1 failed in 5.45s
```

(The exit-code assertion `exc_info.value.code == 2` passes **coincidentally**: the re-exec'd owner CLI exits 2 for the unknown command, matching the fake impl's intended `sys.exit(2)`.)

## Mechanism

1. `hermes_main.cmd_update` calls `retarget_to_owning_install(PROJECT_ROOT)` (`hermes_cli/main.py:2162-2164`) **before** reaching `_cmd_update_impl`, so the test's monkeypatch of `_cmd_update_impl` is never reached.
2. `owning_install_root()` (`hermes_cli/update_owning_install.py`) resolves the shared venv to its real owner checkout (owner ≠ the pristine worktree under test, and the worktree root is not on `PYTHONPATH`).
3. `retarget_to_owning_install` runs `subprocess.call([sys.executable, "-m", "hermes_cli.main", *sys.argv[1:]], cwd=owner, ...)` — under pytest, `sys.argv[1:]` is the **pytest argv**, so the owner's real CLI receives the test node id, prints `is not a hermes command`, and exits 2.
4. The fake impl never ran → no receipt was begun/finalized → `ur.read_latest_receipt()` returns `None` → assertion failure.

## Established precedent in this repo

Sibling update tests already pin this exact seam:

- `tests/hermes_cli/test_update_custody.py:259`
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_update_post_commit_followups.py:243,265`
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_update_existing_branch_baseline.py:226`
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_shared_metrics_update_stop_reasons.py:107,251`
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_update_lock_windows_live.py:477`

`test_update_receipt.py`'s `TestCommandBoundaryFinalization::test_cmd_update_boundary_finalizes_on_early_exit` is the one update-flow test missing the pin.

## Suggested fix

Pin the seam in this test the same way its siblings do, e.g.:

```python
monkeypatch.setattr(update_owning_install, "retarget_to_owning_install", lambda root: None)
```

## Scope note

Found while verifying the pre-existing failure reported on PR #126913 (it reproduces identically there and on pristine `upstream/main`); #126913 is not the cause. Environment: macOS, python.org 3.14 shared venv at `/Users/liyuan/github/ai/hermes-agent/venv` owned by a separate main checkout. Source-level analysis plus the pristine-tree repro above; I did not bisect when the retarget call entered `cmd_update`.

prs.title: plugin-catalog: add gmat-mx (hosted MCP, verified GMAT facts for Mexico)
prs.body:
## What it does

Adds `gmat-mx`, a hosted-only Agent Plugins v1 package (configuration only: `plugin.json` + `mcp.json` + one skill) that connects Hermes to gmat.mx's free MCP server at `https://api.gmat.mx/mcp` (Streamable HTTP, no sign-in, no keys).

Tools (all read-only): `score_to_percentile` (official GMAC total-score percentile table, 2021–2026 data), `get_gmat_fees` (GMAT fees in USD for Mexico, Ecuador, Colombia, Peru), `get_exam_policy` (format, timing, attempts, validity), `get_sample_question` (original practice questions with explanation). Skill: `gmat-facts`, which tells the agent to use these tools instead of estimating GMAT numbers from memory.

## Hermes surfaces used

MCP server declaration only (portable `mcp.json`, `streamable-http`). No hooks, middleware, env vars, Python code or Desktop surface.

## Disclosures (rule 13)

- Hosted-only connector; every tool call goes to `api.gmat.mx`, a Cloudflare Worker operated by gmat.mx (a GMAT prep provider in Mexico, not GMAC). Source of the Worker is in the same repository (MIT).
- The server stores no user data and sets no cookies; responses are public, cacheable JSON.
- The package marks the server `untrusted` in `plugin.json`.
- The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.
- Submitted by the repository owner.

prs.title: fix(agent): classify axum/serde reasoning_effort enum rejections as reasoning-level rejections
prs.body:
## Problem

Strict axum/serde gateways (e.g. axum-based LLM proxies) reject the thinking-off encoding with an HTTP 422 like:

```
Failed to deserialize the JSON body into the target type: reasoning_effort: unknown variant `none`, expected one of `low`, `medium`, `high`
```

This wording matches neither `UNSUPPORTED_PARAM_MARKERS` (OpenAI/pydantic phrasings) nor `_REASONING_LEVEL_REJECTION_MARKERS` (`"must be one of"`, `"invalid value for"`), so `is_reasoning_level_rejection()` returns False. The auxiliary recovery ladder (e.g. title generation, which hard-codes thinking-off) then fails outright on every call instead of retrying at the floor effort — the recurring "Auxiliary title generation failed: HTTP 422" banner under every reply.

## Fix

Add the serde wording (`"unknown variant"`, `"expected one of"`) to `_REASONING_LEVEL_REJECTION_MARKERS`, so the existing floor step-up recovery fires (retry at the weakest accepted effort). Verified that the gateway's actual 422 message now classifies as a reasoning-level rejection, while a non-reasoning enum 400 (e.g. about `temperature`) still does not match.

prs.title: fix(gateway): keep bounded control reads off the serial queue
prs.body:
## Problem and behavior

`session.control.read` can miss the client's 30-second deadline while it waits behind a slow request on the same WebSocket. Switching from native Desktop to the gateway-hosted Webapp does not remove that transport queue. The ordinary dispatcher still awaits each serial request before taking the next frame; even existing concurrent reads were admitted into that queue before they could start.

Start the two allowlisted read projections at admission instead: `session.context_breakdown` and the pure `session.control.read` snapshot. Existing bounds remain **2 running + 8 waiting**; a flood still parks the reader. Mutations retain their arrival order.

## Ordering and profile boundaries

These snapshots are deliberately unordered relative to queued mutations. A client needing read-after-write consistency must await the mutation's reply. Desktop/Webapp `session.control` already awaits and consumes the returned snapshot; Ink's explicit control read hydrates the session once and receives later updates as events.

A read naming a hot-starting profile waits within the existing 20-second profile-start budget before taking a running read slot. It still counts against admission, cannot starve ready profiles' running slots, and is dropped when its viewer disconnects. Profile-bound grants naming another profile still fail immediately through the unchanged authority checks. The serial mutation hold lane is preserved.

Completed slow dispatches now log peer, request ID, method and elapsed time at a fixed 5-second threshold. IDs and methods use escaped repr; no request parameters or response bodies are logged. Cancellation and dispatch-crash paths keep their existing diagnostics. A handler that hands work to a pool is timed only through that handoff, not until its eventual reply. No new environment setting is added.

## Verification

Refreshed against upstream snapshot `8112254f8a934626032579cae967b25b7795836d` on 4 November 2026, preserving the published branch's history with a normal merge. Final head: `f41ee761ab98f1e0ab9c245d182a8aa0e59e9838`.

- **80/80 tests passed** across the concurrent-read, real ticketed profile-start, session-control, orphan-race and socket-send-deadline suites, using `scripts/run_tests.sh` with pinned Python 3.14 and two workers.
- The control-read regression fails on unmodified upstream: the read starts only after the gated mutation finishes. With the patch it replies while that mutation remains blocked, while a later mutation stays ordered. Both `prompt.submit` and `session.control` are exercised.
- `scripts/check --base origin/main`: **14 checks passed**, code health 0 blocking / 0 advisory. `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent Claude code/security/concurrency review: no remaining blocker or major for PR publication, conditional on passing the revised tests. The 80-test run above is that revised run. An earlier Gemini review raised the same profile-wait and ordering questions; the follow-up Gemini call hit quota and is not reported as a pass.

The first broader worktree run hit the repository's real-home I/O guard when bootstrap inspected its Git metadata under the live install. Verification was moved to an isolated clone outside the live home; the guard remained enabled.

## Limits

This proves the serial-queue regression, not the exact blocker on every naturally timed-out socket. Later independent-socket controls answered in 26–1685 ms while the user's original 30-second failure remained valid evidence. GIL pauses, database waits, read-lane saturation and full `session.resume` cost remain separate possible limits. See the new cross-surface evidence comment on this PR.

No live installation has been patched or restarted by this refresh. Installed activation and sustained real-use validation are outstanding. GitHub reported no configured CI checks; local test success is not a claim that GitHub CI ran.

prs.title: feat(regex): gate RE2-incompatible patterns in CI and pre-commit, ratchet stdlib re imports
prs.body:
## Summary
RE2 migration, stage S2 (guardrails). Adds the static RE2 pattern gate to CI and the pre-commit hook, and the code-health ratchet rules HX018 (no new stdlib `re` import in product code) and HX019 (no `hermes_re` in the named exempt files or under `pm/`; `hermes_platform/` keeps its own stdlib-only import test, and `scripts/`, `skills/`, `optional-skills/` and `website/` are outside both rules by design, plan 3.2 / D14). Must be merged before any import-swap PR.

Stacked on: #158717 (S1). Review only this PR's own commits; it targets main and also shows its parents' commits until they merge.

## What changes for users
None. Contributors: `scripts/check` gains the `re2-patterns` guard and the pre-commit hook runs it on staged non-test `.py` files. Both need google-re2 in the environment (added by S0): **re-source `./activate` after pulling S0**, or the guard fails with a one-line message (exit 2). `git commit --no-verify` skips the hook; `python scripts/check --only ruff,health,...` skips the guard.

## Plan stage and owner decisions
- the migration plan section S2 and the plan's stage kit sections A–D.
- D18: the gate runs in `repo-guards.yml` AND in the lefthook pre-commit hook (`just re2-patterns <files>`); the alternative `lint.yml` job is not used.
- Exemption list (`scripts/code_health/stdlib_re_exempt.py`, 49 entries) is the owner-approved list, unchanged. Files that started importing `re` on `main` after the plan's base are not exempt; HX018 treats them as existing hits.

## Commits
1. `ci(regex): run the RE2 pattern gate in CI and pre-commit` — `scripts/check_re2_patterns.py`, `_GUARDS` entry, repo-guards step + README row, `just re2-patterns`, lefthook job, code-health CLI test fixture copies the gate and `hermes_re`.
2. `feat(code-health): ratchet stdlib re imports with HX018 and HX019` — rules, exemption tuple, tests.
3. `docs(plugins): say slack action handlers need a stdlib re pattern`.
4. `docs(agents): point regex code at hermes_re` — size-neutral root AGENTS.md edit (root + gateway chain is at its cap).
5. `docs(plugins): say slack_bolt raises TypeError for a hermes_re pattern` — review fix: slack_bolt rejects the pattern (TypeError when the handler is wired; the plugin handlers registered after it are lost), it does not just fail to match.
6. `fix(regex): make the pattern gate see from-imports, pattern= and dynamic flags` — review fix: calls of `from hermes_re import compile [as c]`-style names and `pattern=` keywords are now checked (literal) or counted as DYNAMIC (non-literal); a call whose flags are not a literal is reported `not checked (flags not a literal)` instead of passing as flags=0 (a refused pattern is still a finding). Adds `tests/scripts/test_check_re2_patterns.py`, the gate's first behaviour test.
7. `fix(regex): resolve gate calls per scope and compare bytes and stalls` — Greptile review fixes: a call resolves the name bound in its own scope (a local `re`/`compile` no longer borrows a module-level binding); a waiver counts only in a real comment, not inside a string; bytes patterns are compared on generated subjects too; a comparison stdlib `re` cannot finish within 2 s (catastrophic backtracking) is reported as `UNCHECKED` and needs a review waiver instead of stalling the gate. The deadline uses SIGALRM, so it applies on POSIX hosts (CI, Linux, macOS).
8. `fix(code-health): read the name= keyword of dynamic re imports` — HX018/HX019 also catch `importlib.import_module(name="re")` and `__import__(name="re")`.
9. `fix(regex): catch escaped surrogates and refused flags in the gate` — Greptile review fixes: an escaped surrogate (`\uD800`-`\uDFFF`, also inside a class) is reported as SURROGATE; `re.L`/`re.LOCALE`/`re.DEBUG` reach the facade's build, so calls using them are REJECTED instead of DYNAMIC. The `--pre-swap` report now also lists 6 surrogate patterns still on stdlib `re`; the swap stages must handle them.
10. `fix(regex): read surrogates through stdlib's parser, not the pattern text` — Greptile review fix: the SURROGATE check walks stdlib's parse tree instead of the source text, so an escape inside a `(?#...)` comment is no longer a finding.
11. `fix(regex): give no flag-dependent verdict for non-literal flags` — Greptile review fix: when a call's flags are not a literal, the gate reports REJECTED or SURROGATE only if that holds under every flag combination, and DYNAMIC otherwise (no INEXACT or DIFFERS verdict from flags it cannot read).
12. `fix(regex): compare with the call's own count and maxsplit` — Greptile review fix: `sub`/`subn`/`split` are compared with the call's literal `count`/`maxsplit`; a non-literal limit makes the comparison DYNAMIC.
13. `fix(regex): treat star and double-star arguments as unknown in the gate` — Greptile review fix: an argument that `*args` or a non-literal `**mapping` could supply (pattern, repl, flags, count, maxsplit) is unknown and follows the non-literal rules; a literal `**{...}` is read.

## Tests run
- `python scripts/check`: 23 checks ok (re-run after commits 5–6).
- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/scripts/test_check_re2_patterns.py tests/scripts/test_code_health_cli.py`: 60 passed (18 new); the new test file fails 9 of 18 against the gate before commit 6.
- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/scripts tests/ci tests/hermes_cli/test_plugin_validate_private_imports.py tests/hermes_cli/test_plugin_docs_public_imports.py tests/plugins/conformance`: 3192 passed, 2 failed (`test_desktop_update_shim_profile_cleanup.py`, fail identically on the parent branch: environment).
- `just check --only re2-patterns` → 0; `just re2-patterns agent/redact.py` → 0 (`checked 0 files`); `just --list` lists `re2-patterns`; `check_agents_md_size.py` → 0.
- Ratchet proof: a new `agent/_re_probe.py` with `import re` fails `scripts/check --only health` with HX018.
- Without google-re2 the gate prints one line and exits 2.
- Lefthook job in a scratch repo: receives only staged non-test `.py` files; a refused pattern fails the commit.
- Full suite not run.

## What the gate checks today
Only files that import `hermes_re` (without `--pre-swap`). Today that is one file, `hermes_cli/doctor_regex.py`, with no literal pattern, so the CI step and the hook pass trivially until the first swap. `--pre-swap` is the mode for checking a file before it is swapped.

## Deviations from the plan's artifacts
1. `scripts/check_re2_patterns.py`: `encoding="utf-8"` and `timeout=60` on its two `git` calls (`scripts/check` footguns / HX006 refused them otherwise). No behaviour change.
2. `tests/scripts/test_code_health_cli.py`: the fixture's `scripts/check` now runs the gate, so the fixture copies the gate and `hermes_re/` (setup only, asserts nothing about the gate).
3. Commits 5–6 apply the adversarial review's findings 1–3.

## For S3/S4 (swap stages)
- `hermes_cli/web_routers/backend_migration.py:214` `(?<![\w./-])hermes (?!-p |--profile)` is REJECTED by the gate (`--pre-swap`) and no kit patch covers it: S3/S4 must rewrite it.
- `hermes_cli/gateway_migrate_backends_host.py:104` builds its pattern at run time (DYNAMIC): it needs a manual compile check.

## Known limits
- The ratchet compares fingerprints: a PR that removes N module-level `import re` lines can add up to N identical ones elsewhere unreported. Every swap PR therefore also runs the migration kit's `new_re_imports.py` (a planning tool, not part of this repository) against `origin/main` (plan 4.4).
- `__import__`/`importlib.import_module` with a non-literal name are not seen.

prs.title: fix(desktop): keep scaled Webapp statusbar menus within the viewport
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Keeps the Webapp's context-usage dropdown and statusbar visibility menu inside the viewport when UI Scale changes. Tall menus remain scrollable, including the Compact conversation action and the last visibility-menu command.

The shared Radix components already cap menu height and enable scrolling. The reproduced failure at 125% UI Scale comes from `<html>` CSS zoom scaling the positioner's viewport coordinates again. This patch keeps the statusbar positioner unscaled, reapplies the selected scale to its content, and converts the available height into the content's CSS pixels.

## Related Issue

Fixes #150502.

Related: #148414. The compensation in this PR is scoped to statusbar menus.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `apps/desktop/src/lib/browser-zoom.ts`: expose the applied UI scale as a CSS variable.
- `apps/desktop/src/app/shell/statusbar-controls.tsx` and `apps/desktop/src/styles.css`: mark the two statusbar menu entry points and apply the browser-only coordinate and height conversion.
- `apps/desktop/e2e/core/statusbar-viewport.spec.ts` and `apps/desktop/src/test/statusbar-viewport.fixture.tsx`: exercise the existing components with production CSS in Chromium.

## How to Test

In the Webapp:

1. Enable the context meter and set Appearance → UI Scale to 125%.
2. Open the context-usage dropdown and right-click the statusbar. Check that both menus stay inside the window.
3. Shorten the window. Scroll to Compact conversation and use End to reach the visibility menu's last command.

From a prepared checkout with Playwright Chromium installed:

```sh
pnpm --dir apps/desktop exec playwright test -c e2e/core/playwright.config.ts statusbar-viewport.spec.ts
pnpm --dir apps/desktop run typecheck
python scripts/check
```

Local results:

- Both browser regressions fail the viewport-containment assertion on base `a08f2418cd82`; both pass with this patch.
- Coverage includes 80%, 100%, 125%, 150% and 200% UI Scale; resizing an open menu; short-window scrolling; Compact conversation; and keyboard End/Escape.
- Focused Vitest run: 27 passed across the context-usage, statusbar visibility/context-menu, compact-action, browser-zoom and viewport suites.
- Full Desktop typecheck, changed-file ESLint with zero warnings, Prettier, `git diff --check`, and all 15 `scripts/check` checks passed.

Validated on macOS 27.2 with Chrome 156. The smaller CSS viewport models browser/OS zoom geometrically; native Windows DPI scaling was not tested. The full Python suite was not run.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] Read the Contributing Guide.
- [x] PR/commit title follows Conventional Commits.
- [x] Searched open and merged PRs for duplicates.
- [x] Changes are limited to this fix and its tests.
- [ ] Full Python suite run (frontend-only patch; not run).
- [x] `python scripts/check` passes.
- [x] Added behavior regressions and proved them red on the base.
- [x] Tested on macOS 27.2 / Chrome 156.

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] Relevant documentation: N/A; no public workflow or configuration change.
- [x] `cli-config.yaml.example`: N/A; no config keys changed.
- [x] `CONTRIBUTING.md` / `AGENTS.md`: N/A; no architecture or workflow change.
- [x] Cross-platform impact considered; native Windows verification remains outstanding.
- [x] Tool descriptions/schemas: N/A; no tool behavior changed.

prs.title: ci(release): commit builds run the Stable Release pipeline
prs.body:
Stacked on #142475 (phase 2 of the unified-pipeline plan). Review that one first; this PR's diff is against its branch.

## What

A commit build now **is** a Stable Release run, the same way a canary is. `release.py --build-commit REV` claims REV with an annotated `commit.<YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ>-v<version>` tag and dispatches `stable-release.yml` on it. Without `--publish` it's a dry run that creates nothing.

The commit kind differs from stable/canary only in policy:

| | stable | canary | **commit** |
|---|---|---|---|
| Lanes | stable default | all but `upgrade` | stable default minus `upgrade`, `install-e2e`, `windows-store` (commit builds don't support updating) |
| Green | required | claim's `requireGreen` | claim's `requireGreen` (default on) |
| Publication | `publish-bundles` + Docker | `publish-canary` + Docker aliases | `publish-commit`: the builds page only |
| Packages | release identity | canary identity | `X.Y.Z+commit.<stamp>`, stamped Windows quad, deb `X.Y.Z~commit.<stamp>-1` (`hermes-commit` suite), **`Commit<sha7>` identity + `source: commit-build`** so every updater refuses them |
| Concurrency | `stable-release` | `canary-release-pipeline` | its own tag (never queues behind a release) |

`--only/--with/--without` and `--[no-]require-green` work as they do for canary; a refused lane is an error. `--bundle-env/--bundle-unset` defaults travel in the claim, and `stable verify` refuses any candidate leg whose bundle env differs from it.

## Fails closed

- Channel/feed writers (`r2.channel_for_tag`, `release_artifacts.release_channel`, the macOS feed merge) used to default an unknown tag to stable; they now raise for commit tags.
- The Docker image is built and tested; publication-side checks (`require_release_image_tag`, `parse_manifest`) refuse a commit tag.
- The Store job refuses `commit.` tags.
- `stage_apt_repo` pairs the `hermes-commit` suite with commit claims only. It previously rejected `hermes-commit` outright, which would have failed every commit build's Termux candidate.
- The stable publication reconciler ignores `Commit release` runs.

## Page, receipts, retention

- `publish-commit` renders the accepted candidate's page at `releases/tag/<claim>/index.html` and in the run summary. It links the source commit (no GitHub release exists) and lists the claim's bundle defaults.
- The post-build commit receipt tag is retired: the claim, minted before the build, is the identity. The legacy tagless mode stops minting one too.
- Commit claim archives and claim tags are kept **90 days**, pruned by the daily canary workflow's existing prune steps. Legacy `releases/commit/<sha>/` objects age out by upload time on the same window.

## Not in this PR

- Channel builds and deleting the disposable path (phase 3).
- Deleting the legacy tagless commit mode and the unreachable jobs in `desktop-bundled-release.yml` (phase 4). The legacy mode still works on direct dispatch; `release.py` no longer uses it.

## Review hardening

- Native desktop cache saves now gate on the claim-tag kind: commit/channel claims skip prepared dependency, bundle-assembly and Windows/macOS signature saves. Restore/preparation and stable/canary prerequisites stay intact. These are workflow save gates, not token-enforced isolation.

- Stable/canary Docker alias publication now shares `_publish_aliases`; caller-specific identity/receipt checks and destination policy remain separate. Both variant digests are verified before any alias writes. Retry limits, delays, exceptions and read-back checks are unchanged.

- Commit-claim macOS staging now omits the updater-feed glob (the packager emits none), while DMG, ZIP, blockmaps and provenance metadata remain mandatory. Stable/canary/channel claims still require their feeds. Real workflow-shell regressions stage both architectures through the metadata recorder and receipt writer to loopback storage; missing feeds for updating kinds are refused before uploads.

- The icon renderer accepts a commit claim alongside its SHA while retaining incompatible-tag rejection; regression tests run the actual CLI with the generated build environment.
- Every shared claim-custody workflow call receives an explicit step-scoped `GH_TOKEN`, including receipt, candidate-manifest and complete; maintainer authorization is unchanged.
- Fresh-install native smokes retain tagged commit identity and require `source: commit-build`, null branch and `updateMechanism: external`. Real stamp-writer output is tested on both native platform contracts.

## Verification (Windows ARM64)

- Addressed the human review report about repeated commit dispatch: the test fixture orders claims by UTC stamp rather than tied tagger dates/inherited Git sorting. Reproduced the old failure deterministically, then passed both full files under adverse Git settings on Linux (**7 passed** on commit, **6 passed** on cleanup), plus **2** canonical Windows regression cases and all **13** lint checks. Production claim generation/dispatch is unchanged. Replies on #145680 and #146163 link the fix and evidence.

- The JS cache-expression harness now supports the claim-prefix `startsWith()` gate in the originating commit PR, not only the cleanup tip. Reproduced 8 CI failures locally before fixing; afterward **13 tests passed** on commit, **13 passed** on channel, and **8 passed** on cleanup. ESLint and independent review passed. That earlier change was test-only and left the cleanup tree unchanged.

- Current head `4df7a745a0c40ce485fbdd95d98eee8f051f9cc2` is rebased onto `main` at `fcc26fbd9f1641755e49793d7ed608f3b7214c3d`. Each PR’s complete patch is byte-for-byte identical to its pre-rebase patch; all four stack ancestry links and remote heads are verified. Rebased-tip verification: **230 focused Python tests**, **25 focused JS tests**, and all **14** lint checks passed. The originating commit/channel PRs also each pass **13** JS cache-harness tests. No merge or production release operation was performed. Fresh CI is pending; earlier native/platform verification limits still apply.

- Feedless-commit fix at `68644004c35de9ce711596999b9165b51f81845c`: independent review clear; **42 Python tests passed** on the commit PR. All four-kind handoff controls pass on the descendant branches (**16 cases**); the rebased cleanup tip passes **44 focused Python tests**, **17 JS tests** and all **13** lint checks. The graph suite additionally has **176 passed / 1 unchanged Windows shell-path failure** (`test_docker_recovery_refuses_to_replace_a_divergent_version_tag`), already present in the recorded baseline. macOS-only cases are skipped on this Windows host; native signing/notarization and production publication were not exercised. CI was restarted on these new heads; no all-green CI claim.

- Combined-stack canonical Python run across 47 files: **850 passed, 2 failed, 10 fixture errors, 29 skipped**. The exact 12 failing/error cases match the unchanged stack baseline (**798 passed, 2 failed, 10 fixture errors, 29 skipped**); no added failures. Baseline issues: Docker recovery's Windows shell path, shallow source-retirement fixture cleanup, and icon-environment provisioning through `windows-deps.ps1`.
- After the final review follow-ups, all added Python regression files were rerun at the final tip: **55 passed, 0 failed** across 10 files. Tests cover real icon generation, claim-custody credentials, HTTP publication with the real assembler, native ordering, live-head/retirement retention, APT indices, and rendering/concurrency gates.
- Final smoke/cache/helper Vitest run: **23 passed**, with the pre-existing PowerShell 5 compression-assembly test excluded. Its actual PowerShell script separately passes when `System.IO.Compression` is explicitly preloaded. Both new commit/channel smoke suites pass.
- All four desktop typechecks and touched-JS ESLint pass. Whole-tree Ruff passes. `scripts/check` at the integrated tip: **13 checks passed**, including cumulative health against the stack's main base; each PR's own health ratchet also passed.
- No real release, tag, or production R2 operation was dispatched. Signed native builds and real R2/CDN publication remain unexercised.
- CI on the updated heads is pending; the previous green checks do not verify these new commits.

prs.title: feat(release): commit builds run Stable Release with isolated caches and signing
prs.body:
## Infographic

![Isolated commit builds. Before: Claim: tagless dispatch; Caches: mutable caches; Termux: shared deb job; Page: ad-hoc page. After: Claim: commit claim tag; Caches: read-only legs; Termux: no GPG key; Page: full asset page. Change: bundles + smoke, cache-mode: read.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c400df13-9b9e-401b-af29-742640861470)

## What does this PR do?

Moves one-off commit builds (`scripts/release.py --build-commit`) onto the `stable-release.yml` claim/admission pipeline via `commit.<YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ>-v<version>` claim tags, while enforcing strict cache, credential, and signing-key isolation for untrusted commits.

This PR replaces #145680 (left open for now; not closed by this PR) on current `main`, rebuilding @ethernet8023's work with Option B1 trust-boundary controls. Four commits preserve `ethernet <arilotter@gmail.com>` as author with `Co-authored-by: BearHuddleston` (`bd507fa031`, `ac1fd04b67`, `2161472db2`, `742d6f6be1`), and a fifth commit (`d7466e681b`) adds trust-boundary and pipeline contract tests; a rebase-merge or merge commit preserves per-commit authors while a squash retains them as co-authors. Two test-only commits fix this PR's CI (`fb9e678b33`, `b3a5a14e13`). Review fixes: `4f47fe285b` makes the claim-support check recognize this tree's `deb_version.py`; `69cb09bcd3` (+ `1f5894f2d8`) and `58eeb44c9a` (+ `f362f89cd6`) isolate commit-claim recording and R2 staging onto four fresh controller-only jobs (`stage-commit-*`) that download only built package artifacts by validated producer artifact ID; `40e4a2cc5f` accepts a legacy claim's tagless Termux version `X.Y.Z+commit<sha12>`; `158d25e31b` refuses a bundle-less lane selection before claiming; `36d5ae1303` (replacing `372116c747`'s refusal) builds tagless on a repository whose default branch isn't `main`, as `main` did, and `19f57f1649`/`aa2a62fb6a` log that run's `release.py` command; `29a722e182` replaces the claim-support source-text match with a contract the claimed tree declares in `scripts/releases/commit_claim_build.txt`, so this PR's own earlier commits build as legacy and a failed read raises; `b477118265`, `ba1bade76c`, and `7a7d60862a` disable `persist-credentials`, strip write scopes on commit legs, block GHCR builder-image pushes from `termux-deb-commit` (falling back to the digest-pinned base image on a miss), and move `GH_TOKEN`/R2 secrets out of `termux-deb-commit`'s job env; `abf9308411` extracts the shared secret-free Termux build sequence into `.github/actions/build-termux-deb/action.yml`; `0a3c87b1c4`, `0f8965c202`, `285c20dd95`, `d5b852638f`, `f96fc8fdaa` and `fa7731ca08` record claim packages in a step without the R2 secrets and stage only the packages each recorder reads; `c3fac69324` and `d704ec4c99` are a typing fix and comment corrections from @kshitijk4poor's review.

Points to review:
- **Bundles + smoke policy and read-only caches (`2161472db2`, `742d6f6be1`, `ba1bade76c`):** `commit` claims default to `windows`, `macos-arm64`, and `smoke` (`--with termux` opts into Termux) and refuse every shared-cache or release lane (`ci`, `docker`, `docker-tests`, `nix`, `pm-bundle`, `install-e2e`, `termux-checks`, `windows-live`, `upgrade`, `windows-store`, `linux`, `bootstrap-version`). All `commit.` and `channel.` claims route to `cache-mode: read` native legs with `persist-credentials: false` and minimal job permissions, skip all cache saves, and are excluded from write-mode Linux legs. `win32-assembly-v1` drops prefix `restore-keys` so only exact lockfile hits enter assembly.
- **Controller-only commit-claim staging (`58eeb44c9a`, `f362f89cd6`):** Untrusted build legs upload only built packages (no `version-info-*.json` sidecars) via 7-day job artifacts and export `commit-artifact-id`. Four fresh controller-only jobs (`stage-commit-win32-x64`, `stage-commit-win32-arm64`, `stage-commit-darwin-arm64`, `stage-commit-termux`) check out only `github.sha`, validate a single positive numeric artifact ID before downloading, refuse any artifact entry other than the target's built packages (no directories, symlinks or hidden names; one non-Store MSIX for the arch, one DMG and ZIP with their own blockmaps, or `deb/*.deb`), record metadata in a step without secrets, and stage to R2 in a separate step that holds the R2 credentials and uploads only the metadata file it wrote; each target's selection gate requires both build and stager to succeed.
- **Termux split with shared action and no APT/GHCR write access (`742d6f6be1`, `b477118265`, `abf9308411`, `7a7d60862a`):** `termux-deb-release` (`cache-mode: write`, APT signing, GHCR push) and `termux-deb-commit` (`cache-mode: read`, `permissions: {contents: read, packages: read}`, no `GH_TOKEN`/`CLOUDFLARE_R2_*` in job env, no APT signing key) share the secret-free build sequence in `.github/actions/build-termux-deb/action.yml` (checked out via sparse-checkout from `github.sha`). On a GHCR miss in commit mode, both current and pre-PR checkouts fall back to the digest-pinned base image (`termux/termux-docker@<digest>`). `stage_apt_repo.py` refuses commit claims.

## Related Issue

Refs #145680 (replacement PR; #146145 follows on top of this stack once landed)

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)

## How to Test

```bash
scripts/run_tests.sh \
  tests/ci/test_commit_claim_trust_boundary.py \
  tests/ci/test_stable_release_commit_threading.py \
  tests/ci/test_stable_release_graph.py \
  tests/ci/test_commit_build_staging.py \
  tests/ci/test_protected_canary_publication.py \
  tests/ci/test_desktop_bundle_smoke.py \
  tests/ci/test_desktop_release_commit_admission.py \
  tests/ci/test_desktop_release_tag_admission.py \
  tests/ci/test_workflow_job_graph.py \
  tests/scripts/test_commit_release_pipeline.py \
  tests/scripts/test_dispatch_log.py \
  tests/scripts/test_release_build_commit.py \
  tests/scripts/test_release_handoff.py \
  tests/scripts/test_release_r2.py \
  tests/scripts/test_stage_apt_repo.py \
  tests/scripts/test_termux_build_driver.py
pnpm --dir apps/desktop exec vitest run --project electron \
  electron/feature-flags.test.ts scripts/commit-stamp-identity.test.mjs scripts/native-quad.test.mjs
pnpm --dir tests-js exec vitest run commit-claim-smoke.test.mjs setup-pm-cache.test.mjs
python scripts/check --only ruff,health --base origin/main

```

Verified on Linux (6.17 arm64) at head `fa7731ca08` (merges cleanly into `origin/main` `0f602c5f6f`): the 58 Python test files that cover the release scripts, lanes, dispatch log and `desktop-bundled-release.yml` gave 1193 passed, 6 skipped, 5 failed. The 5 failures (`tests/hermes_cli/test_update_channel.py::TestSetChannelCLI`, 3, and `tests/hermes_cli/test_source_release_channels.py` transient-channel, 2) fail identically on `f362f89cd6` on this host. On the merge with `0f602c5f6f` the set showed those 5 and no others. Each fix commit's regression tests failed on its parent and passed after; the typing and comment commits carry none. `setup-pm-cache` + `commit-claim-smoke` vitest passed (16/16) and `scripts/check --only ruff,health,shims` is clean. eslint ran at `f362f89cd6` and the desktop vitest suite (11/11) at `d7466e681b`; no later commit touches JS/TS. Not run locally: Windows-host tests (`platforms('windows')`) and live GitHub Actions `stable-release.yml` execution on hosted runners. prs.title: Hermes schedules help on its own (trips, habits, owed replies), and each job asks on its own "Schedule this job?" card
prs.body:
Hermes can now notice a moment you'll need help with later (a flight, an appointment, a deadline, a habit) and set up a scheduled job for it without being asked. Every job the model creates or changes first shows you a card ("Schedule this job?" / "Change this job?") with what will run, when, and who sees the result, and nothing is saved unless you allow it.

This is step 1 of the proactivity work; the roadmap and research on other proactive assistants are in #158538. The Desktop/Web Inbox for job results is a separate PR (#158555).

## What changes for you

| You say | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| "dentist thursday at 3pm, I always forget" | an answer, nothing scheduled | a card for a reminder before the appointment |
| "flying SFO to Tokyo on NH7 next friday 11:25am, nervous about the airport" | travel tips | a card for a check-in reminder at T-24h (plus arrival help on some models) |
| "landing in Lisbon tuesday 6am, check-in isn't until 3pm" | tips | a card for an arrival reminder with transit and bag-storage help |
| "I keep forgetting to answer people on slack" | tips | a card for a weekday "clear your unanswered Slack" nudge, a few runs, never sends anything |
| "my dentist appointment yesterday went fine" | — | nothing scheduled |
| "please don't set reminders for me" | — | nothing scheduled |
| the model edits a job you approved earlier | applied silently | a "Change this job?" card listing each change old → new; deny leaves the job untouched |

Where no card can be shown (cron runs, `-q` one-shots, kanban workers, API server / webhooks, `approvals.mode: off`, yolo, or after "Always allow new jobs"), the model is not told to create jobs unasked and jobs save exactly as on main.

## What changed

- **Proactive guidance, only where a card will show.** One rule (`tools.approval.schedule_card_skip_reason`) decides both whether a card is shown and whether the system prompt carries the one-line "create the job, then say what you scheduled" guidance. The `cronjob_manage` description itself is neutral: what jobs are good for (appointments, trips, deadlines and owed items, habits with a run limit, re-checks with `monitor` / `[SILENT]`), cadence advice, and "a job never sends, buys or submits on the user's behalf".
- **Schedule cards on every surface.** Classic CLI, Ink TUI, Desktop, and the messaging adapters (Telegram, Slack, Discord, Teams, Matrix, Feishu, …) draw a schedule card instead of the "dangerous command" card, and keep it a schedule card after a reconnect, behind another queued card, after a click, and in the plain-text fallback.
- **The card shows the job that will be saved.** It is built from the finished, validated record: the saved name, when it actually fires (first run in your clock; a one-shot's real instant), run count, "created paused", the monitor script or URL that runs first, and **who sees the result** (this chat, a named home channel, an explicit target, or nowhere), plus where failure notices go when different. The job text is fenced on messaging cards so model-written markup can't change how it reads.
- **Edits ask too.** A model-initiated update that changes when it runs, what runs or who sees it shows "Change this job?" (Allow / Deny only; an "Always allow new jobs" grant never covers edits). Pause / resume / run / remove stay unasked. A run that completes while the card is open keeps its count.
- **Honest outcomes.** Invalid jobs fail before any card. A card answered after the first run it showed has passed saves nothing (instead of a different time or an error after consent). A decline is an answer, not a tool failure, so the loop guardrail doesn't push the model to keep trying.
- **Approval kinds** (`schedule`, `schedule_edit`, plus `access` / `network` cherry-picked from @emozilla's #156726) travel through the approval contract, managed workers, replay and every adapter.

## Live results (real CLI in tmux, real models on Nous Portal, head of this PR)

16 conversations per model, each from a fresh profile, every card approved; counts are jobs created.

| | Sonnet 5.5 | Gemini 3.8 Flash | GPT-5.5 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8 helpful cases (dentist, flight, water, site re-check, report deadline, Tokyo trip, Slack replies, Lisbon arrival) | 1 of 8 (dentist) | 8 of 8 | 8 of 8 |
| 8 unwanted cases (past appointment, past trip in passing, "don't set reminders", hypothetical trip, a friend's story, finished task, a general cadence question, a plain question) | 0 of 8 | 0 of 8 | 0 of 8 |

On main, none of the three models created a job in the 5 helpful cases tried there (trip, Lisbon, Slack, site, report). Sonnet stays conservative: it offers in chat ("tell me the flight time and I'll set a check-in reminder") rather than creating. One run per cell: directional, not a rate.

Other live legs: the real system-prompt builder + `registry.dispatch("cronjob_manage", …)` under a temp `HERMES_HOME` for normal CLI (line present, card asked), approvals off with a UI, streaming API server, and a kanban worker (no line, no card, saved as on main); the real classic CLI card at 100×18 in tmux; the real messaging renderer (schedule card fenced, command card unchanged); Desktop approval cards earlier in this PR's history over CDP.

## Not covered

- Real Discord / Slack / Telegram clients (rendered strings only); Discord, Feishu and Matrix after-click card edits.
- Duplicate-proposal cases (needs a job to exist before the conversation starts) and ctaylor86's "propose a script job" / "reply stops one reminder" evals: tracked in #158538.

## Prompt surface

Stable system prompt: about +101 tokens per interactive surface vs main (the gated guidance line); tool schemas −1 token. Cron and unattended surfaces are unchanged. Needs a `hermes-agent-core` approval for the snapshot.

## Follow-ups (own PRs)

- #158541: damaged `[SILENT]` markers no longer reach your chat.
- #158555: Desktop/Web Inbox for job results, continuable in place.
- `cron.proactive: create|offer|off` (default `create`).

Credit: @emozilla (#156726 approval kinds), and the reviewers whose findings shaped this head: @kshitijk4poor, @salch-cred, @GottZ, @AtlasOmnia, @mr-magaia, @quotumorg, @ctaylor86, @eyedeaco, @askclaw-vesper, @mselcukozturk, @yqecea, @Adolanium.

## Infographic

![infographic](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0ab33edc/DuwWNho_knwZPY_vqjs2__sdPCJFuI.png)

prs.title: Add deepseek-meter to the plugin catalog
prs.body:
## What it does

`deepseek-meter` puts a DeepSeek account meter in the Desktop status bar:

- **chip:** `● ¥38.67 · 42% · 256k` — account balance, the focused chat's context-window load, tokens spent today;
- **panel (click):** balance (total / topped-up / granted), context fill with a bar and `used / max` tokens, today's input/output/cached tokens and estimated cost, 7-day and all-time totals, this chat's totals, and a per-model split;
- the auto-compression line states the threshold the host is actually configured with (`compression.threshold`), or that it is off.

The UI follows the app language (system locale) with `en`, `ru`, `uk`, `es`, `de`, `fr`, `zh`, `ja` bundles and `en` as fallback.

## Surfaces used

- **Desktop plugin SDK:** one `statusBar.right` contribution (`ctx.register`), `host.state.focusedUsage` for the live context load, `useQuery` polling the plugin's own backend every 20 s.
- **Dashboard plugin backend:** two `GET` routes (`/stats`, `/balance`) under `/api/plugins/deepseek-meter`.
- Nothing else: no tools, hooks, middleware, commands or routes.

## Disclosure (rule 13)

- **Network:** exactly one outbound HTTPS call — `GET https://api.deepseek.com/user/balance`. No other host is contacted.
- **Credentials:** `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` is read through Hermes' secret route (`agent.secret_scope.get_secret`, with `os.environ` as the single-profile fallback). The plugin never parses `.env` or `auth.json`, never stores or refreshes the key, and never returns it to the renderer.
- **Local reads:** `$HERMES_HOME/state.db`, opened `mode=ro`, table `session_model_usage` only — token counts, API-call counts, estimated cost, model name and timestamps. No message text, titles, prompts or tool output.
- **Reads config:** `compression.threshold` / `compression.enabled` (read-only) to state the real auto-compression setting.
- **No telemetry**, no self-updater, no background processes, no writes to Hermes state.

## Screenshots

Chip and panel in context:

![status bar](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/samieshmil-blip/hermes-deepseek-meter/79fe7d830538049f342f3f4e0533a20e6fa8d798/docs/hero.png)

The same panel in EN / RU / ZH / JA:

![locales](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/samieshmil-blip/hermes-deepseek-meter/79fe7d830538049f342f3f4e0533a20e6fa8d798/docs/locales.png)

## Validation

```
hermes plugins validate .   → 16/16 checks passed
hermes plugins doctor .     → runtime discovery, manifest, import, registration OK
```

Requires Hermes `>=0.23.0` (`host.state.focusedUsage`). The repo is mine (rule 5).

prs.title: fix(desktop): scale Webapp Radix poppers and click-anchored menus via containing-block hosts
prs.body:
## Infographic

![Scaled Webapp menus fit. Before: Portal: body portal, scale 1; Menus: clip past viewport; Scroll: cannot scroll. After: Portal: contain:layout host; Menus: aligned in viewport; Scroll: wheel & touch scroll. Change: contain:layout portals, scaled click anchors.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ccc8f39a-8228-4022-9266-874c158ac3c1)

## What does this PR do?

When Webapp UI scale is not 100% (`document.documentElement.style.zoom`), Radix poppers portaled directly to `document.body` resolve Floating UI's `offsetParent` to `window`, where `getScale()` returns `1`. Coordinates, `--radix-*-content-available-height`, `--radix-select-trigger-width`, and arrow offsets are then double-scaled by root CSS zoom, pushing menus, selects, popovers, tooltips, and submenus past the viewport and leaving tall menus like the profile switcher unscrollable.

This PR salvages @mothieras's #150624 (cherry-picked with `-x` so `74f8643d2f` keeps their authorship, plus `3606f887a2` mapping their contributor email) and generalizes it in `0de87f87c7` across every Webapp Radix popper and click-anchored menu instead of statusbar menus alone. A rebase-merge or merge commit preserves @mothieras's commit authorship; a squash preserves it as a co-author trailer.

Points to review:
- **Containing-block portal hosts over per-menu CSS zoom:** on `data-hermes-desktop-host="browser"`, `usePopoverPortalContainer()` routes body-level menus, selects, and tooltips into fixed full-viewport hosts with `contain: layout` (preserving the `--z-popover` / `--z-tooltip` stacking tiers) so Floating UI natively divides by root zoom, replacing the `data-statusbar-menu` workaround and keeping Electron and transformed `DialogContent` portals untouched.
- **Click-anchored menus and fixed modal overlays:** `AppContextMenu` and `NodeContextMenu` divide viewport `clientX`/`clientY` by `--browser-ui-scale`, and `BootFailureModal` adds `contain: layout` to its fixed portal container.
- **Scoping:** non-Radix `FanMenu` (#149885) and `#150729`'s sidebar virtualizer are left for separate focused PRs; see commit `0de87f87c7` for details.

## Related Issue

Refs #148414, #150502, #150729, #156390, #150624

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## How to Test

```bash
pnpm --dir apps/desktop exec playwright test -c e2e/core/playwright.config.ts statusbar-viewport.spec.ts webapp-scaled-poppers.spec.ts
pnpm --dir apps/desktop exec vitest run src/components/ui/dialog-portal-context.test.tsx src/lib/browser-desktop-bridge-zoom.test.ts src/app/context-menu/app-context-menu.test.tsx src/app/starmap/node-context-menu.test.tsx
```

Manually: open the Webapp, set UI scale to 125% (or 80%–200%), and verify the profile switcher scrolls to the last profile (mouse wheel and touch), the right-edge model picker and submenus stay aligned inside the viewport, and Select, Popover, Tooltip, and right-click context menus align cleanly.

**10.6-second before/after (125% UI scale, `0f602c5f6f` vs `3606f887a2`, synthetic dark-mode fixture):**

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b063b454-46b1-40ec-87c0-7f7cdad8f645

Tested on Linux arm64 (`chromium-headless-shell` 1248) at `3606f887a2`: both Playwright E2E specs (6/6), 13 desktop Vitest suites (106/106), `typecheck`, `build:webapp`, and `scripts/check --base origin/main` passed; `merge-tree` against `origin/main` (`0f602c5f6f`) is clean. Not run locally: full desktop E2E suite, native Electron build smoke, and physical tablet hardware (touch scroll was exercised via Chromium mobile CDP touch events).

## What does this PR do?

We're from the MiniMax team. This adds the new `MiniMax-M3.1-Flash` model to the `minimax`, `minimax-cn` and `minimax-oauth` model lists (ahead of `MiniMax-M3`, existing entries unchanged) so users can select it. Context length already resolves to 1M via the existing `minimax-m3` prefix. Thinking on M3.1-Flash is always on (levels `low`/`medium`/`high`/`xhigh`/`max`). On the OpenAI-compatible `/v1` route it gets the same reasoning controls as M3 but never sends `thinking: disabled`, and custom OpenAI-compatible providers send `low` instead of `reasoning_effort: "none"` for it (the API rejects `none` with 2013). Default aux model stays `MiniMax-M3`.

## Related Issue

N/A

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

## Changes Made

2. `python scripts/check`

### Code

- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/)

prs.title: fix(steer): a steer pending at a turn's first API call is not inserted into the previous turn
prs.body:
**What.** The pre-API steer drain (`_inject_steer_after_newest_tool_result`, `agent/turn_iteration_prep.py`) scanned the whole message list for the newest tool row and inserted the steer after it. On a turn's first iteration that row belongs to the previous turn, so the steer landed before that turn's final assistant reply, in history that was already sent. The scan is now bounded to the current turn. With no tool result in this turn yet, the steer is put back, as the function already did for a history with no tool row.

**Why.** The store keeps append order. The next request, rebuilt from the store, placed the steer after the turn's user row and the consecutive-user repair merged the two. Sent history therefore changed between two requests and every prompt cache was rewritten from that point; a provider that keeps a long-lived session had to rebuild it. Observed once on a long conversation: one full cache write of about 600k tokens, with the host logging `Re-anchored stale current_turn_user_idx 1800 -> 1801` at the start of the affected turn. Details in the issue.

**Behaviour note.** A steer that is already pending when a turn makes its first API call is now delivered after that turn's first tool batch (the post-tool drain), or returned as pending when the turn makes no tool call. Before, the model saw it one request earlier, but in the wrong place. A steer that arrives during a later iteration is placed exactly as before.

**Not covered.** On a second consecutive continuation inside one turn (for example two length continuations in a row) the rows after the newest tool row have already been sent, and a steer accepted then is still inserted before them. That is unchanged from main. A tail-only rule would break the redirect shape that `test_steer.py` pins, so it needs its own change.

**Tests.** New `test_first_iteration_steer_preserves_previous_turn` (three cases: delivery after the current turn's tool batch; a leftover steer with a tool row in the previous turn; a leftover steer with no tool row anywhere). Two of the three fail on main with the steer inserted before the previous turn's final reply; all pass here. `tests/agent/test_steer.py`, `test_turn_iteration_prep.py`, `test_message_sequence_repair.py` and `test_repair_reanchors_current_turn_user_idx.py` pass (119). The one existing direct call of the helper in `test_steer.py` passes the new argument. I also ran the whole `tests/agent` directory locally on the branch (14,635 passed); the tests that fail in my environment fail identically on main when the same files are run there, and none is in a file this change touches.

Refs #157525

prs.title: feat(regex): add the hermes_re facade over google-re2 and a doctor check for regex settings
prs.body:
Stacked on: #158716 (S0). Review only the commits after it; this PR targets main and shows S0's commits too until #158716 merges.

## Summary
Adds `hermes_re`, a first-party package with the stdlib `re` surface on top of Google RE2 (`google-re2`, added in
S0), so later stages migrate a module by changing only `import re` to `import hermes_re as re`. RE2 matches in
linear time (ReDoS-resistant). The package is stdlib-only at import and loads the engine on first use; `compile()`
validates at once and raises `hermes_re.error` (a subclass of `re.error`) for what RE2 cannot run. Without
`google-re2` the first match raises `ModuleNotFoundError(name="re2")`. **No product code uses it for matching yet.**

Also adds the D28 pre-upgrade check in `hermes doctor` so users can see, before any behaviour changes, which of
their regex settings the new engine will refuse.

## What changes for users
- `hermes doctor` gains the section "Regex Settings (RE2 engine change)": for the active profile it lists
  user-supplied regexes (shell-hook and outbound-webhook matchers, Matrix `ignore_user_patterns`, webhook route and
  subscription filters, platform mention patterns, env-var forms included) that RE2 will refuse (a manual issue:
  `hermes doctor` exits 1, like the neighbouring upcoming-change notices) or will read with ASCII word boundaries
  (warning). It rewrites nothing. Hooks are named by place, `hooks.<event>[<index>] matcher` / `hooks.outbound[<index>] matcher`;
  the hook's command, URL or name is never printed (it can carry a token). Without `google-re2` it prints
  `skipped: google-re2 not installed` (warning); with the package installed but failing to import it prints the
  cause (exception class and message) instead.
- Nothing else. Plugins may `import hermes_re as re` (new plugin-API entry).

## Plan stage and owner decisions
Plan stage S1 (facade package, tests, docs page, plugin-API entry, engine-missing test, doctor check). Implements
D24 (no module needs the engine to import: `tests/test_regex_engine_optional.py`), D28 (doctor check, exit 1 on a
refused pattern), the 64 MiB per-pattern memory budget, and the S0 "after S1" step (musl CI table check).

## Commits
1. `feat(regex): add the hermes_re facade over google-re2` — package, tests (108), table generator + JSON, docs page
   + sidebar, `packages.find`, plugin-API entry (+ regenerated `public-api.md`), package lists in the desktop
   fixture, two update tests and the neutral-imports allowlist.
2. `test(regex): check that modules import without the regex engine` — `tests/test_regex_engine_optional.py`.
3. `feat(doctor): report regex settings the RE2 engine will refuse` — `hermes_cli/doctor_regex.py`, doctor row,
   `webhook_filters.filter_regexes` walker (no behaviour change), CLI docs paragraph, tests.
4. `ci(pm): check the hermes_re tables against musl RE2` — musl job runs `gen_hermes_re_tables.py --check`;
   workflow triggers on `hermes_re/**`.
5. `fix(doctor): name regex hooks by index, never by command or name` — review fix: a hook command can carry a token.
6. `fix(doctor): report why an installed regex engine fails to import` — review fix: "not installed" only when it is.
7. `docs(doctor): state which lookarounds RE2 accepts` — review fix: RE2 refuses lookaround except a one-character
   lookbehind at the very start and one lookahead at the very end (a negative lookahead tests one character).

## Tests run (locally, isolated HOME/HERMES_HOME, Python 3.14)
- `tests/hermes_re/`: 108 passed. `scripts/gen_hermes_re_tables.py --check`: up to date.
- `tests/test_regex_engine_optional.py`: 4 passed. Doctor tests (`test_doctor*.py`, `test_doctor_regex_settings.py`)
  and `tests/gateway/test_webhook*.py`: all passed. STAGE_1 list (plugin API/docs imports, plugin conformance,
  neutral imports, update tests, tree layout) and `tests/ci/test_docs_drift.py`: passed.
- `python scripts/check`: ok (22 checks; code health 0 findings).
- Re-checked after the review fixes in a per-worktree venv (editable install of this branch only, engine + all
  extras): doctor tests + `tests/hermes_re` + engine-optional + docs drift: 336 passed, 0 failed, 8 skipped; check ok.
  The new doctor tests were red on the pre-fix code and green after.
- `tests/hermes_re/`, `test_doctor_regex_settings.py` and `test_regex_engine_optional.py` need `google-re2` (a core
  dependency from S0 on); on an interpreter without it they fail by design, not by flakiness.
- Without `google-re2`: `import hermes_re` works, compile works (a backreference or non-edge lookaround is refused at once), first match raises `ModuleNotFoundError(name="re2")`.

## Evidence level / known limits
The facade was differentially tested against stdlib `re` during planning (tens of millions of comparisons); this
PR's test runs are the first runs of the repository suite on it. Silent differences that remain by design (ASCII
`\b` away from simple edges, empty-match iteration, lone surrogates, repeated-empty-body groups) are documented in
`website/docs/developer-guide/regex.md`. Not run locally: the docs site build, the musl CI job, Windows/macOS lanes.
The doctor check covers the active profile only (`hermes -p <name> doctor` for others).
One deviation from the planned text: the table generator reads its JSON with `utf-8-sig` (the newer footguns lint).

prs.title: fix(agent): enforce lifecycle leaf toolset ceiling
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

The public plugin lifecycle API accepted `role="leaf"` and an explicit
`allowed_toolsets` tuple, but passed both through the shared delegate builder.
That builder derived the role from global delegation depth and could add
`delegation` or inherited MCP toolsets outside the requested set.

This change gives host-owned lifecycle launches an enforceable policy:

```text
PluginContext.subagent_lifecycle.launch
  validate request and parent ownership
  build child
    lifecycle role is authoritative
    explicit allowed_toolsets is a named ceiling
    reject role/config/parent-policy conflicts
  return capability-bound effective role/toolset evidence
```

Model-facing `delegate_task` keeps its existing depth-derived role and inherited
toolset behavior.

## Related Issue

No upstream issue currently tracks this exact public lifecycle invariant.
Related work is narrower or broader: #131282/#131283 covers lifecycle spawn
admission, #97637 covers parent disabled-toolset validation, #109524 covers
parent delegation authorization, and #89193/#82157 propose broader model-facing
or per-child capability systems.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix
- [x] 📝 Documentation update
- [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `agent/subagent_lifecycle.py`
  - marks validated lifecycle roles and explicit toolset ceilings as authoritative;
  - rejects conflicting construction before child execution;
  - exposes `effective_toolsets` with the effective role on handle/status/result evidence;
  - binds that policy evidence into the opaque handle capability and preserves plugin-host wire round trips.
- `tools/delegate_tool.py` and `tools/delegate_tool_toolsets.py`
  - preserve the legacy `delegate_task` path by default;
  - prevent explicit ceilings from inheriting MCP toolsets or gaining `delegation`;
  - require an authoritative orchestrator to be permitted by global depth/settings, its explicit ceiling, and the parent's effective tool surface.
- `tests/agent/test_subagent_lifecycle.py`
  - adds an adversarial plugin toolset case with orchestrator support and depth greater than one;
  - covers parent-policy conflicts, forged/cross-parent handles, wire evidence, default compatibility, result bounds, retention, and reconnect behavior.
- `website/docs/developer-guide/subagent-lifecycle-api.md`
  - documents authoritative roles, complete named ceilings, fail-closed conflicts, and public effective-policy evidence.

## Evidence

- **Before:** on exact base `109fd8161a509db5a00942152ba48882e446e8b0`, the adversarial lifecycle test failed because an explicit leaf became `orchestrator`. The same test failed for the same reason on v0.22.5 revision `bf0203a794a07aac3ff764972ab9087baa4e4f4e`.
- **After:**
  - `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/agent/test_subagent_lifecycle.py tests/tools/test_delegate_composite_toolsets.py tests/tools/test_delegate_toolset_scope.py tests/hermes_cli/test_plugin_host.py -k 'not agent_turn_binds_and_clears_lifecycle_parent' -v` — 32 passed, 0 failed, 2 platform skips.
  - `python scripts/check` — 15 checks passed.
  - `python website/scripts/check_doc_links.py` — passed.
  - `git diff --check` — passed.
  - independent revision-bound review at `9901a42a2ee7b1e64afb9f7624c024668a34f823` / tree `d454fb858d8cf7f7d9bdbb639dc3b87b23ba99b0` — PASS after one repair cycle.
- **Broader suite:** the canonical full-suite attempt was stopped at 7.7% after about 20 minutes (4,181/~54,335 discovered; latest progress 3,769 passed and 940 failed). Most failures were the known checkout-location baseline where `HomeIOGuard` rejects `hermes_bootstrap` probing `worktrees/manifest.json` because this assigned worktree is inside the production Hermes state root; unrelated high-concurrency host failures also appeared. The directly relevant 32-test set above remained green.

## How to Test

1. Run the lifecycle and plugin-host contract set shown under Evidence.
2. Run `python scripts/check`.
3. Configure delegation with `orchestrator_enabled: true` and `max_spawn_depth: 3`, register a synthetic plugin report toolset, and launch the public lifecycle service with `role="leaf"` plus only that toolset. The handle must report leaf plus the report toolset, and the child must not contain `delegate_task` or inherited MCP tools.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the Contributing Guide.
- [x] My commit follows Conventional Commits.
- [x] I searched open PRs and issues for duplicates.
- [x] The PR contains only this lifecycle policy fix, tests, and docs.
- [ ] The complete test suite passes locally; see the explicitly reported host-path baseline limitation above.
- [x] `python scripts/check` passes.
- [x] Tests cover the regression and compatibility paths.
- [x] Tested on Windows 11 / Python 3.14.

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] Public lifecycle documentation is updated.
- [x] `cli-config.yaml.example` is N/A; no config key changed.
- [x] `CONTRIBUTING.md` / `AGENTS.md` are N/A; no workflow changed.
- [x] Cross-platform impact considered; the change is platform-independent policy logic.
- [x] Tool descriptions/schemas are N/A; model-facing `delegate_task` is unchanged.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** Two-way. Reverting the commit restores the previous lifecycle behavior without a data migration.

**Blast Radius:** Plugin lifecycle launches only. Provider/model routing, parent ownership, cancellation, retention, result bounds, and the model-facing delegation contract remain unchanged.
