prs.title: feat(desktop): report plugin notification handoff outcomes
prs.body:
## Summary

```diff
 ctx.os
   notify(input): void                 # unchanged legacy contract
+  notifyWithResult(input): Promise<{
+    status: accepted | suppressed | failed | unknown
+  }>
```

Adds an outcome-bearing native-notification method to the Desktop plugin SDK while preserving the existing synchronous `notify` contract. Both methods share the existing preference, startup, focus, throttle, payload, and activation path. Callback handlers are registered before pending IPC can activate them, removed on known failure, retained for unknown outcomes, and cleared on plugin unload.

`accepted` means only that the native bridge returned strict `true`; it is not proof of OS display or user activation.

Consumer context: https://github.com/siyuanling_microsoft/agent-dotfiles/issues/19

## Evidence

- **Before:** the public-seam regression failed because `notifyWithResult` did not exist.
  **After:** 3 focused Desktop files / 57 tests passed.
- Current SDK factory → production downstream plugin pump: 11/11 compatible cases passed.
- Actual old-host source projection: 1/1 passed and the consumer claimed no durable effect.
- Mutation controls failed as intended: old consumer behavior failed 9/11 composition cases; old backend behavior failed the unknown-expiry assertion.
- Touched ESLint and Prettier passed; renderer, Electron, and e2e TypeScript compilers passed directly.
- Independent cross-repository review: PASS for base `90d6b98fd86d20981ee06ddd5b7d93e4320f26a4`, head `14440cf7e88aa63381bf5d8f1bc20489f558d7cb`, tree `801da44f34e2995aced2d9181196668115ef549f`: https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/149969#issuecomment-6681967089

Full Desktop UI suite is not claimed green: this host has Node 22 while current `main` requires Node >=26, and the locked `pele` runtime dependency was unavailable from the package proxy. No Electron app, gateway, native notification, display, or click was exercised.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

The interface is additive and the legacy method remains compatible. Consumers must feature-detect the new method when supporting older hosts.

**Blast Radius:** Desktop plugin native notifications

The change affects renderer-side admission/outcome reporting and callback cleanup only. It adds no retry loop, persistent state, plugin-specific policy, profile/config change, or Electron IPC contract change.

prs.title: plugin-catalog: add manina (drive a real iPhone through an ESP32 Agent board)
prs.body:
Adds `plugin-catalog/manina.yaml` for [Manina AI](https://github.com/onehumanbeing/esp32-iphone-agent/tree/6af87ec7a5ad2f19e2d98d39222e19ca4fd1958b/integrations/hermes), submitted by the repository owner.

## What it does

Lets Hermes see and drive a real, non-jailbroken iPhone through an ESP32 Agent board. The board acts as the iPhone's Bluetooth/USB mouse and keyboard and receives its AirPlay screen mirroring. The agent gets `screenshot` (returned as an image), `tap`, `longpress`, `swipe`, `type_text`, `press_key`, `press_button`, `device_info`, `phone_audio`, plus saved intents and run history.

## Hermes surfaces

A portable Agent Plugins v1 package, configuration only (no Python):
- `mcp.json`: one stdio server, `npx -y esp32agent@0.1.5 mcp`, forwarding `ESP32AGENT_DEVICE` as `${ESP32AGENT_DEVICE}`.
- `plugin.json`: `extensions.com.nousresearch.hermes.servers.esp32agent.timeout: 120` (first-run download and video decode). That key needs Hermes ≥ 0.22.3, hence `requires_hermes: ">=0.22.3"`.
- `skills/manina/SKILL.md`: the `manina:manina` skill (see-act loop, saving what worked, safety rules).

`provides_tools` is empty, as with the other portable MCP entries: the tools come from the MCP server at runtime.

## Disclosure (rule 13)

- **Binary download at setup:** `npx` installs the `esp32agent` npm package (pinned to 0.1.5). Its postinstall downloads the matching CLI binary (v0.1.4) from the repository's own GitHub Release, built by that repository's GitHub Actions. It checks the SHA-256 against the release's `checksums.txt` before installing. The plugin never updates it. The CLI's own `esp32agent upgrade` runs only when a user types it and is not exposed as an MCP tool.
- **Background process:** the CLI starts an `esp32agent daemon` that holds the Bluetooth session and decodes the mirrored video. It listens on a unix socket in its config dir and exits after 10 minutes idle.
- **Stored keys:** pairing keys live in the CLI's config dir (mode 0600). The plugin reads no other credentials.
- **Network:** it talks only to the board, over Bluetooth LE or the local Wi-Fi (TCP 7202). No cloud service, no telemetry.
- **Approvals:** the tools act on a real phone, and the package keeps the server at full trust. The skill tells the agent to ask the user before payments, messages, calls, deletions and security changes. The README shows the `config.yaml` override with `trust: untrusted` for anyone who wants Hermes to ask before every call.
- **Requirements:** the board, Node.js 18+ and `ffmpeg`.

## Validation

Run locally against the pinned commit:
- `hermes plugins validate integrations/hermes --install-deps`: passes, security scan `safe`.
- `scripts/ci/catalog_validate_pinned_entries.py` with `CHANGED_FILES=plugin-catalog/manina.yaml`: `✅ PASS`.
- `hermes plugins install onehumanbeing/esp32-iphone-agent/integrations/hermes --enable` into a clean `HERMES_HOME`: the skill registers as `manina:manina`, and MCP discovery registers all 13 `mcp__esp32agent__*` tools.

prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Old `execute_code` results lose their execution outcome when compaction replaces them with a short stub. An exception, a timeout, and a successful run can all become ``[execute_code] `run_validation()` (1 lines output)``: the formatter reads the arguments but ignores the result. Phase-one pruning can remove the failure before the summary model sees it, and proactive pruning can persist that same stub into the active transcript.

Preserve bounded failure, interruption, inner-tool error, and kernel-lifecycle notes in the execute_code-specific stub. Healthy results retain their existing format. This changes compaction text, not tool execution or effect certainty.

For example:

```text
Before: [execute_code] `run_validation()` (1 lines output)
After:  [execute_code] `run_validation()` (1 lines output) FAILED: ValueError: invalid schema

After a session-kernel timeout:
[execute_code] `run_validation()` (1 lines output) TIMEOUT; kernel state lost: Cell exceeded its deadline
```

## Related Issue

Related to #131244 and #132141: this is a remaining gap in the execute_code-specific summarizer. #126226 established the `tool_errors` result contract that this change also retains during compaction.

Adjacent open PRs address different data: #122635 fixes output line counting, and #129226 retains persisted-output paths. This change leaves those concerns alone and continues using the supplied line count.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `agent/context_compressor_code.py`: owns execute_code summarization, following the facade/sibling layout and keeping the existing oversized compressor file below its baseline size.
  - Read only the result envelope, including JSON followed by a subdirectory hint; do not scan stdout or nested application data for errors.
  - Keep `error`, status-only errors, nonzero exit codes, timeouts and interruptions visible. Use the final line of ordinary Python tracebacks for the bounded reason.
  - Report `tool_errors` separately from the outer script outcome. A successful Python cell with a failed inner tool is not relabeled as a script that never executed.
  - Retain explicit kernel loss/reset/end information, including the local/remote session-kernel timeout contract.
  - Reuse the shared refusal and bounded-reason helpers; blocked and pending-approval results keep their not-run semantics.
  - Keep annotated stubs below the existing prune floor and preserve them when fallback anchor collection summarizes them again.
- `agent/context_compressor.py`: route the existing dispatch entry to the sibling formatter; remove the old outcome-blind formatter. Net reduction: five lines.
- `tests/agent/test_execute_code_compaction.py`: two parametrized behavior tests, covering result classification/negative controls and the prune, summary-input and real SQLite reopen paths.

## How to Test

The initial regression matrix, before the production change, produced **27 failed / 12 passed** on base `5fc490e2b34123212d73ef316086f939567a725a`. Failures were outcome assertions, not collection/import errors. The final test file also covers bounded long stubs and fallback re-summarization.

```bash
scripts/run_tests.sh \
  tests/agent/test_execute_code_compaction.py \
  tests/agent/test_context_compressor.py \
  tests/agent/test_summarize_tool_result_type_safety.py \
  tests/agent/test_proactive_tool_result_pruning.py \
  tests/agent/test_proactive_prune_restart_safety.py \
  -j 2 --tb=short

python scripts/check
git diff --check
```

Validation on submission commit `e88f9b2aa6995fadaf6b34bb3316aeddb253513a`, rebased onto main `77b446b6e148e53218853dea08acdd3a0349b592`: **382 passed, 0 failed** across the five files above, including the explicit archived-original assertion. Final `python scripts/check`: **12 checks OK**, zero blocking/advisory health findings. `git diff origin/main...HEAD --check` passed.

The pipeline test captures the summary generator's input deterministically; it does not call a model. The persistence test uses a temporary real SessionDB and verifies both the active stub after reopening and recoverable archived output. The formatter tests cover successful output containing an application-level `error`, malformed result fields, blocked/pending approval, and JSON with appended hints.

Validation environment: native Windows, Python 3.12.7 with existing dependencies through the canonical hermetic test runner; Ruff 0.15.10 for the repository checks. A default full-suite attempt discovered 6,475 files (approximately 49,024 tests), but was stopped after early ACP compatibility failures: the local environment has agent-client-protocol 0.8.0 whereas pyproject.toml pins 0.9.0; one observed error was a missing AuthMethodAgent import. This incomplete attempt establishes neither a passing full suite nor a regression caused by this patch. The PM-locked test environment, Linux/macOS execution and model continuation benchmarks have not been run. No claim is made that this patch alone proves a particular model task-success improvement.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the Contributing Guide and applicable AGENTS.md files.
- [x] My commit messages follow Conventional Commits (`fix(compression): preserve execute_code failure outcomes`).
- [x] I searched existing PRs/issues and disclosed adjacent work above.
- [x] The changes are limited to this bug and its regression coverage.
- [ ] The full repository test suite passes — attempted but stopped on environment compatibility failures; targeted validation is listed above.
- [x] `python scripts/check` passes: 12 checks, zero blocking/advisory health findings.
- [x] Regression tests are included and the initial matrix was proved red before the fix.
- [x] Tested on native Windows; Linux/macOS not run.

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] Documentation: N/A for user behavior/configuration; the sibling module documents its contract.
- [x] Configuration examples: N/A — no new configuration.
- [x] Architecture/workflow instructions: N/A — follows the existing sibling layout.
- [x] Cross-platform impact considered: pure result formatting; no process/backend changes.
- [x] Tool schemas/descriptions: N/A — execution behavior and input schema are unchanged.

prs.title: fix(gateway): prove a route-drifted wake refusal permanent so the drain cap drops it
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Ends the one refusal loop in #143720 that neither the attempt cap nor `display.background_process_notifications` could stop: a process-completion wake whose **queued routing snapshot no longer rebuilds the session key it is pinned to**.

That snapshot is the input to the admission identity check (`gateway/session_automation.py::_owner`), so the authority refuses it with `admission_conflict` on **every** redelivery — the mismatch is a property of the snapshot, not of the moment. `_requeue_refused_watch_event` counts toward `_MAX_COMPLETION_INJECTION_ATTEMPTS` only when `_refusal_permanent` is set, and `admission_conflict` is deliberately not in `PERMANENT_REFUSAL_REASONS` (d6635ffe03b), so the event rides the 60 s ceiling forever: 494 refusals in one six-hour log against 3 `falling back` lines in the report.

The fix proves the fatal sub-case instead of reclassifying the code: after the refusal, re-derive the session key from the source restored for the event and compare it with the key the event addresses. A mismatch cannot be healed by waiting, so the refusal is permanent and the existing 8-attempt cap drops the event with the `process(action='log')` pointer.

Two cases stay transient on purpose, because redelivery can still succeed:

- a snapshot that rebuilds its own key — the unowned/foreign-pinned class d6635ffe03b protects, where a `/resume` can still reopen the pinned session;
- any event whose key cannot be re-derived (`_watch_route_identity_drifted` fails closed).

Adding `admission_conflict` to `PERMANENT_REFUSAL_REASONS` would have ended the loop by breaking that transient class; this does not.

## Related Issue

Part of #143720 — the identity-drift lane (the reported 494-refusals-vs-3-fallbacks signature). **Not** the whole issue; see the live-data caveat below.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `gateway/run_notifications_ownership.py` — new `_watch_route_identity_drifted(evt, source)`: proves a notice's own snapshot rebuilds a different key than the one it addresses (the same comparison `_owner` makes), and fails closed on an unprovable one.
- `gateway/run_notifications.py` — `_inject_watch_notification`'s `WakeNotAccepted` handler folds that proof into `exc.permanent` for `admission_conflict`, so the drain cap, the async-delegation ledger (`refused = not exc.permanent`) and the watcher all converge.
- `tests/gateway/test_automation_notification_category.py` — three tests: the drift case (red on `main`, green here), a guard that drift is only ever proven from an agent-keyed event with a drift-proving snapshot, and a guard that a foreign pin with an undrifted snapshot stays transient.
- `gateway/run_notifications.py` — `_drain_watch_notifications` now applies the suppression and off-mode gates **before** the refusal-backoff hold, so a refused event is discarded when the owning profile's notifications are off instead of being re-offered until its retry deadline (0.22.x lane; counterexample and patch by @kvnloo, commit 84ad3855, rebased as `c727ee0a837`).
- `tests/gateway/test_background_process_notifications.py` — `test_post_turn_watch_drain_off_discards_backoff_retry`: red on the head before that commit, green after it (executed; see the PR comment).

## Live-data caveat (measured on the reporting install)

The install that filed this (Discord, v0.22.5) was measured twice; the second measurement corrects the first.

- Aggregate, un-instrumented: **3,551** `admission_conflict` refusals in 6.5 days of `gateway.log` against **3,559** `injecting` lines — a 1:1 loop, not a race — with **0** `dropping the queued event`, **0** `permanently gone`, and 29 watcher `refused 8 times; falling back` lines.
- Instrumented (the #147335 fields on the same install, 2026-11-01 20:22:46 → 2026-11-02 06:34:23): **625** refusals, **625/625** `admission_conflict`, **625/625** `permanent=False`, **625/625** `pinned == route_session`, **0** `pinned=none`, **0** `route_session=none`. One chat carried a single event whose `retry` climbed 0 → 592 at a median 61 s gap; an ordinary service restart dropped the loop to 0.

`pinned == route_session` on every line excludes `_owner`'s ownership comparison (`expected != entry.session_id`), which was the first reading's conclusion and was wrong. On that build, the `admission_conflict` sites that can fire when the pin **is** the routed session are the two route-rebuild comparisons — `session_automation._owner` (the producer source no longer rebuilding the route key) and `snapshot_automation` (the committed envelope's restored source carrying a different route identity). That is the class this PR proves permanent, so the fix does fire on the reporting install; the aggregate 1:1 numbers alone could not have shown it, which is why the diagnostic fields ship with #147335.

Limits, stated so the fix is not over-read: the warning still cannot say **which** of the two rebuilds failed (that needs both rebuilt identities logged); this is not a general fix for every `admission_conflict` loop — the deliberately transient unowned/foreign-pinned class stays transient, and the async-delegation delivery path has no `background_process_notifications` gate at all; and `PERMANENT_REFUSAL_REASONS` is untouched, because proven drift and "I could not prove ownership" are not the same refusal.

## How to Test

1. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/gateway/test_automation_notification_category.py -q` — 17 passed.
2. Sabotage check: revert only the two wiring lines in `_inject_watch_notification`; `test_route_drifted_wake_refusal_is_proven_permanent_and_the_cap_drops_it` fails on `assert evt['_refusal_permanent'] is True`, and passes with the wiring restored.
3. Family regression: `scripts/run_tests.sh` over `test_automation_wake_route`, `test_completion_delivery`, `test_completion_ownership_proof`, `test_completion_admission`, `test_completion_owner_retry`, `test_completion_session_boundary`, `test_automation_retry`, `test_background_process_notifications`, `test_watch_automation_identity`, `test_wake_delivery`, `test_authority_automation`, `test_busy_wake_admission`, `test_heartbeat_watch_lifecycle`, `test_diagnostic_wake_presentation`, `test_child_notice_profile_admission`, `test_active_session_refusal_completion`, `test_admission_results` — 296 test executions, 0 failed (env built with `--group dev --group test --extra messaging`).
4. `python scripts/check` — 14 checks, ok.

## Scope and exclusions

- Sibling paths checked, not changed: the watcher already caps **every** refusal at 8 (`_watch_process`) and then falls back to the `notify_mode` notice, so it was never the spinning loop; the relay adapter already treats `admission_conflict` as permanent for redelivery (`gateway/relay/adapter.py::_PERMANENT_REFUSALS`). This gate is the single place `_refusal_permanent` is set, so the class is fixed for all three consumers.
- The second observation in #143720 — `display.background_process_notifications: off` not stopping the loop — is addressed by the second commit: the drain applied the backoff hold **before** the owning profile's mode gate, so a suppressed event was re-offered until its retry deadline instead of being discarded ([`run_notifications.py#L706-L719`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/c727ee0a8377d7a0de5eaffad2a77a555ce65542/gateway/run_notifications.py#L706-L719)). It does not explain the separate off-at-boot report; the loop terminates under this PR either way.
- Root-cause rebuild paths (`_build_process_event_source` dropping `thread_id` / `parent_chat_id` on a pruned-origin rebuild) are addressed by open PRs #147185 and #145501. They make those wakes deliverable again; this PR is the backstop that ends the loop when the snapshot cannot be repaired, whichever drift produced it.
- Dropping after 8 proofs (~4 min at the 60 s ceiling) is deliberate: the wake is undeliverable by construction, the drop is logged with the `process(action='log')` pointer, and the durable async-delegation row keeps its delivery state for audit.

## Attribution

The analysis and the first patch are **@liuhao1024's** (issue comment of 2026-10-23, branch `liuhao1024:liuhao/cron-bugfix-143720`, commit `0356f8bd6a0`), which he could not open as a PR. This PR carries that approach with the repo's code-health gate satisfied (`BLE001` waiver with the fail-closed reason), a third precision guard for the d6635ffe03b transient class, and re-verified red/green on current `main`. @riccelso's production evidence in #143720 (2026-10-31) is the case this closes.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate — #147185/#145501 fix the source rebuild (deliverability), not the retry termination; #142115/#143282 are other wake-route lanes
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits)
- [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass — **not run locally**; the affected families above were run through the canonical runner instead, and CI covers the full suite
- [x] `python scripts/check` passes (the blocking lint and code-health checks CI runs)
- [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features)
- [x] I've tested on my platform: Ubuntu 24.04, Python 3.14.9

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] I've updated relevant documentation (README, `docs/`, docstrings) — docstrings only; no user-facing doc change
- [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys — N/A (no config keys)
- [x] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` if I changed architecture or workflows — N/A

---

Prepared by an AI assistant (Hermes) on behalf of @landcraft, who reviewed the diff and is accountable for it.

## Rebase onto `main` (2026-11-21)

`main` moved from `c419cf7` (the base this PR was cut on) to `aeb5a0710`, and the PR was `CONFLICTING`/`DIRTY`. Both commits are now rebased onto `aeb5a0710` and force-pushed with lease; **authorship is preserved** (`dc51b6c` → `79d12591307`, kvnloo's `86757f2` → `c727ee0a837`).

Four conflict resolutions, each verified by execution rather than by inspection:

1. **`_drain_watch_notifications` (both commits).** `main` re-shaped the loop and replaced `self._completion_event_scope(evt)` with `completion_event_scope_or_refuse(...)` returning a scope or `None`. The backoff hold is kept at the top for enabled notices only after the merge is replayed: the commit's actual intent — *suppression and off-mode gates run before the refusal-backoff hold* — is now expressed as `should_surface_notification` → `off` gate → backoff hold → delivery, inside the scope.

2. **Test teardown idiom.** `main` migrated the file to `authority.runner.session_store.close_all_db_handles()` (commit `723cc578d1f`); the new tests carry that idiom instead of `authority.db.close()`.

3. **`authority.db` no longer exists.** `SessionAuthority` now exposes `persistence`/`session_store` only. The "foreign pin, still open" guard now creates its unrelated conversation through `runner.session_store.get_or_create_session(adapter.build_source(**_SOURCE, thread_id='9'))` and pins the event to the returned `session_id`, which is what `_classify_completion_owner` actually consults.

4. **`SessionActor` rename (`9ad4a599183`)** and the `should_surface_notification` placement needed no edit — they auto-merged and are covered by the run below.

### Verification on the rebased head (`c727ee0a837`)

```
51 passed   tests/gateway/test_automation_notification_category.py
            tests/gateway/test_background_process_notifications.py
47 passed   same two files at origin/main aeb5a0710 (baseline)
ruff 0.15.22  clean on all four touched files
```

A 30-file sweep over every gateway test that touches the drain / admission path was run on both trees; the failure sets are byte-identical, so the rebase introduces no new breakage.

The "How to Test" commands above were run against the pre-rebase head; the two-file results quoted here are the post-rebase ones.

## Review status (2026-11-23)

@kvnloo re-read the rebased drain at `c727ee0` and confirmed the ordering the off-mode add-on needed, with no further findings — the scope acquisition per held event is inherent to a per-profile gate and was left as-is. Head is unchanged. GitHub reports `MERGEABLE` / `BLOCKED` with no checks on the branch and no approving review recorded yet; the fork's workflows are still awaiting approval, so the remaining gate is a maintainer review, not anything in the diff.

prs.title: feat(plugin-catalog): update gws-workspace to v0.10.0 with watch confirmation
prs.body:
## Summary

Submit **GWS Workspace (`gws-workspace`) v0.10.0** for review, pinned to the published release below. Short-command live tests covered Drive and Gmail (`same_session`) and Calendar (`new_session`), with the delivery-evidence limitations recorded below. The release was published before updating this catalog pin.

Release: https://github.com/anpicasso/hermes-gws-workspace/releases/tag/v0.10.0

Repository: https://github.com/anpicasso/hermes-gws-workspace

Merged source PR: https://github.com/anpicasso/hermes-gws-workspace/pull/6

- Released source pin: `05448155edf3decd892b3b122af8cb7f3cc78a73`
- Source delta from the reviewed release: https://github.com/anpicasso/hermes-gws-workspace/compare/fe83b8a32d0cad4a91ef1b189b999d34bef7fbfb...05448155edf3decd892b3b122af8cb7f3cc78a73
- 16 Workspace tools, two hooks, and explicit slash-command watch controls.
- This PR changes only `plugin-catalog/gws-workspace.yaml`; the unrelated `google-workspace` listing is untouched.

## Changes following review

The release **removes the three agent watch lifecycle tools and all private session-origin/delegation imports**. Watch origin now comes from the public `ctx.register_command` handler metadata: the originating messaging conversation, physical session, sender and registered profile/home. The plugin does not need or install a core patch. Operator-provisioned routes, native gws credential ownership, filtered subprocess environments and curated-tool approval handling remain.

Native `gws` owns storage, decryption and refresh; Python does not export OAuth credentials or refresh mailbox access tokens. The optional [remote-auth companion](https://github.com/anpicasso/hermes-gws-remote-auth) is separately installed, not submitted here, and not a public-plugin runtime dependency. Native-owned credentials are disclosed, not represented as Hermes-managed OAuth. This follows the native-gws alternative requested by the maintainer. In the [follow-up review](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/157482#pullrequestreview-6011213652), teknium1 explicitly confirmed credential ownership/refresh, operator-provisioned routes and the minimal child environment as fixed. Authentication is not an outstanding review blocker; the remaining origin-API request is addressed separately below. Final catalog acceptance still requires maintainer review.

## Slash watch flow on unchanged Hermes

Ask the agent normally to prepare what you want to watch. It resolves IDs with ordinary read tools when needed, then `gws_watch_prepare` stores a local draft with **zero Google I/O or subscription action**. Review the full summary and send the returned short command yourself:

```text
/gws-watch confirmar CODE
```

`confirm` is also accepted. Codes expire after 10 minutes, are scoped to the physical session/profile, and are single-use. Confirmation checks the actual command sender against the operator route; knowing a code is not authority. Authorized confirmation consumes it before Google I/O, so failed starts require a fresh draft. Storage is capped at 64 pending drafts; summaries above 1,600 serialized characters are rejected rather than truncated. Shared-session preparation does not establish requester identity: the configured confirming sender is the authority. No core patch is required.

Raw JSON remains an advanced alternative; status and stop keep their existing syntax.

In an existing supported messaging conversation, send:

```text
/gws-watch gmail {"action":"start","account":"person@example.com","target":{"mailbox":true},"delivery_mode":"same_session","minutes":30}
/gws-watch gmail {"action":"status"}
/gws-watch gmail {"action":"stop","watch_id":"EXACT_ID"}
```

`drive` and `calendar` select their respective service schemas; `new_session` uses the operator-configured native webhook route. Status lists ten watches per page; pass the returned `next_offset` as `offset`, or request an exact `watch_id` for bounded target/filter details. The handler accepts a confirmation code or strict raw JSON, **not natural-language instructions**. Natural-language interpretation happens in the preceding agent conversation; the user sends the final command. Command text cannot select or override its origin. Starting the watch explicitly authorizes bounded subscription operations, background reads, renewal and cleanup; slash commands are not agent calls through `pre_tool_call`.

For `same_session`, matched notifications are injected back toward the saved initiating session through the existing public host API. The command changes **how the origin is captured**, not the existing delivery mechanism. A new chat needs a normal message first to create its physical session. On the WhatsApp bridge, only explicitly non-shared DMs are supported; groups and unknown chat types are refused. Surface restrictions and operator setup are described in the pinned docs.

## What we would like to enable next

We would like a normal conversation such as “watch this calendar and tell me here” to let the agent invoke a watch tool safely, without requiring the user to send a slash command. That needs a public way to obtain the current tool call's bound, non-delegated messaging origin—not merely a session ID or inherited route values.

- Narrow public-origin API request: https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/159074
- Proposed core implementation and regression tests: https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/159075

These are **independent of this release**. The plugin works through the current command API and does not import the proposed API. This is a concrete consumer for the proposed seam, not a request to move Google integration into core.

## Verification

- Release suite against unchanged upstream Hermes `0f602c5f6f18615632535251d62a2db74ce93b69`: **231 passed, zero skipped**.
- Automated integration tests exercise real plugin loading and gateway command dispatch with fixture Google responses/transport. Separately, the runtime revision passed the live tests below; the released pin adds only documentation to that tested runtime.
- Exact-pinned fresh checkout: Doctor and Validate passed with 16 tools and two hooks. Hosted isolation replaces the live session store with a placeholder; same-session delivery requires that live store and injection consent. Use the documented supported deployment, not an isolation bypass. Scanner cautions are `context_exfil` on the skill paragraph returning the confirmation command in this conversation (not history export), and `py_read_secrets_file` on the synthetic empty dotenv fixture in `tests/test_account_cli.py` (not a real credential read).
- Catalog structural validation and `git diff --check` passed. GitHub’s exact PR commit list was checked for approved personal noreply authors/committers (the shallow worktree lacks a local merge base for the stock attribution script).
- Source CI passed on the final released commit `05448155edf3decd892b3b122af8cb7f3cc78a73`: https://github.com/anpicasso/hermes-gws-workspace/actions/runs/45115123243. Catalog checks are separate; no catalog checks were reported at this update.
- Historical v0.9.x live tests are documented separately and do not validate the new slash-command path.

### Live short-command verification

Runtime revision `f0fb307337a9baab8bda2ec472abff1f420ca852` was installed and tested on 2026-11-23. The released pin changes only release documentation afterward. Watches were prepared conversationally and activated by user-sent short confirmation commands.

- **Drive / same_session:** controlled disposable file rename was read back from Google; `renamed`/`updated` metadata reached the initiating Discord conversation and the user confirmed receipt.
- **Gmail / same_session:** authorized self-addressed test mail was read back; its `messageAdded` notification and subject reached the initiating conversation and received an acknowledgment.
- **Calendar / new_session:** disposable event title update was read back; a separate native agent session completed with the expected acknowledgment. Its native delivery obligation recorded `delivered` without error. Destination was the configured Discord conversation: new session means separate agent history, not a new Discord thread. No Discord permalink or independent visual readback was obtained; we do not claim the user located that message.
- All three one-shot watches matched and their Google sources stopped, with zero pending source cleanup. Same-session cleanup completed. The new-session binding remains retained because the plugin cannot observe native final delivery; the host delivery ledger was checked separately, rather than counting admission as delivery.
- Installed runtime matched all 53 tracked files and passed 231 tests, zero skips. The final source tree was rerun with the same result, and a fresh clone at the release SHA passed Doctor/Validate.

**Coverage limits:** three live service/mode combinations, not all six. Manual stop, expiry, long-duration renewal and expired-token recovery were not repeated in this run. Historical evidence remains separately scoped. These tests do not imply exactly-once delivery, exhaustive certification or catalog policy approval.

## Operational disclosure

Requires native gws, explicit account consent, an operator-supervised POSIX worker, public HTTPS ingress, Google API/IAM setup and operator-created Hermes webhook routes. Installation provisions or starts none of these. Workspace results and matched metadata can reach the model provider. One profile is one trusted operator, not per-chat account tenancy. Native subprocesses use host filesystem permissions, not a sandbox. Same-session injection retains a concurrent session-reset race; admission is not delivery confirmation and exactly-once delivery is not promised. Credentials, state and saved response files survive removal.

prs.title: feat(sessions): delete individual messages or exchanges without removing later conversation
prs.body:
## Summary

Implements per-message and per-exchange deletion across the session persistence store, CLI, and sessions Web/Desktop API without truncating or regenerating later messages.

Refs #142421

### Changes
- **Persistence contract & SQLite store** (`persistence/conversation/messages.py`, `persistence/sqlite/conversation/_store/messages.py`, `persistence/sqlite/conversation/messages.py`, `hermes_state.py`, `tests/contracts/_reference/conversation/messages_writes.py`):
  - Added `DeleteMessageScope` (`message` | `exchange`), `DeleteMessagesResult`, and `MessageRepository.delete_message(...)`.
  - `scope="message"` removes the targeted message while preserving tool-call integrity (deleting an assistant row with `tool_calls` or a `tool` result row removes the paired tool-call group so no dangling `tool_call_id` remains).
  - `scope="exchange"` removes the entire user-initiated exchange containing the targeted message (from the owning `user` row through all subsequent `assistant`/`tool` rows before the next `user` row), preserving `system`/`session_meta` rows and all later exchanges.
  - Also removes any compaction-archived copies in the same session sharing `message_uid` so display/search views never resurrect deleted content; SQLite triggers automatically clean `messages_fts`, `messages_fts_trigram`, and `display_order`.
  - Recomputes `sessions.message_count` / `tool_call_count`, increments `transcript_revision`, enforces transcript write guards (`TurnLeaseLost`, `CompressionInProgress`, `CompressionClosed`), and returns `has_compressed_summary` so callers/UI can disclose that earlier compressed summaries are not retroactively rewritten.
- **CLI** (`hermes_cli/subcommands/sessions.py`, `hermes_cli/sessions_cmd.py`):
  - Added `hermes sessions delete-message <session_id> <message_id> [--exchange] [--dry-run] [--yes] [--json]` with confirmation prompt and compressed-summary disclosure.
- **Web / Desktop API** (`hermes_cli/web_routers/sessions.py`):
  - Added `DELETE /api/sessions/{session_id}/messages/{message_id}?scope=message|exchange` (returns `404` for missing session/message, `409` if the session is actively guarded by a turn lease or compression lock).

### Scope Note
This PR implements the persistence store, CLI, and HTTP API backend that Desktop and Web UIs can call directly. Wiring the Desktop message-menu confirmation dialog to `DELETE /api/sessions/{session_id}/messages/{message_id}` can follow in a small frontend PR.

### Verification
- `tests/persistence_sqlite/conversation_store/test_delete_message.py`: **8/8 passed** (single-message delete + FTS cleanup, exchange delete + DB reopen, tool-call group cascade, compaction-archived `message_uid` cleanup + `has_compressed_summary`, active turn-lease refusal, missing message, CLI `--dry-run`/`--yes`/`--json`, FastAPI `DELETE /api/sessions/{id}/messages/{mid}`).
- `tests/contracts/conversation/` + `tests/persistence_sqlite/conversation_store/test_session_delete.py`: **2,192 passed, 0 failed** across 67 existing test files.

prs.title: plugin-catalog: re-pin mock-review to v2.4.0
prs.body:
Re-pins `plugin-catalog/mock-review.yaml` from v2.1.0 to v2.4.0. v2.1.1 through v2.3.0 were never merged here, so this covers all of them.

- sha: `2b425e13686a6095cba58051ff4e57dfcc9ccefb`, the v2.4.0 release commit (tag `v2.4.0`, https://github.com/apelabs-dev/hermes-mock-review/releases/tag/v2.4.0).
- version: `2.4.0`
- The image and screenshot raw URLs now point at the new sha. Both return 200.

**2.4.0**

- **Waking is owner-only.** Send, Build and `@Hermes` wake Hermes only when the owner asks, checked per request. The same request arriving through a public Tailscale Funnel is saved with a plain reason instead of waking. Members no longer have Send.
- **Reviewer wake is opt-in.** A Reviewer's `@Hermes` mention wakes Hermes only after the owner confirms it in a dialog; existing Reviewer links, grants and invites start unconfirmed, and the board marks them.
- **Nothing queued before the update wakes or sends** until the owner sends it again from private ingress.
- **Comment mode pins the mock's own controls.**
- **Windows fix:** an existing artifact page written with CRLF now gets the current board probe.

**2.3.0** (included)

- **Wake on every messaging platform, Hermes Desktop included.** A board now wakes the chat it was made in on every messaging platform Hermes hosts. `mock_review_create` reads that chat from the calling session, and an explicit `origin_*` argument still takes precedence. `hermes mockreview setup` creates the wake route and the notice route for every configured messaging platform, not only the first one.
- **How a Desktop chat is woken.** A Hermes Desktop chat has no webhook route. The board server inside the gateway instead queues the wake prompt into that chat's own session through Hermes's plugin `inject_message` API. Hermes allows this only with `plugins.entries.mock-review.allow_gateway_injection: true`. Setup asks for that consent and sets it with `hermes config set` only when the user answers yes at a terminal. Under `--yes` it only prints the command.
- **Desktop boards are gated.** The woken turn runs with that chat's own tools, so a Desktop board is refused while Send is not gated. Send counts as not gated when the server is on a non-loopback host, `public_url` is set, a Tailscale Funnel mapping exists, or the board is public.
- **Non-chat origins.** Origins that are not chats (`api_server`, `webhook`, and others) are refused at create, with the reason.
- **Resolved pins.** Resolved pins now stay on the board. The new setting `hide_resolved_pins` hides them.

**2.2.0** (included): the board shows live which pins Hermes is working on: a pulsing red dot on the pin, a chip on the block, a status row in the thread, a badge in the Comments list and a count in the header.

**2.1.1–2.1.4** (included): the board header shows the project's icon; the Desktop Mocks tab renders design-profile mocks with their CSS; plus docs, CI and test fixes.

**Entry text.** The description adds the 2.2, 2.3 and 2.4 features and the Desktop wake path (`inject_message`, the consent key and its gating). Setup's `hermes` subcommands are still covered by `config get/set/unset`. There are no new outbound hosts, secrets or dependencies.

`scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py plugin-catalog/mock-review.yaml` passes.

prs.title: plugin-catalog: re-pin hermes-pilot to 0.2.4 (69fef2b)
prs.body:
Hermes Pilot moves from the listed `v0.2.0` pin to `v0.2.4` — 108 commits, 328 files, +46,907 −17,325 over `5c82ba62..69fef2b`. `version:` follows the pinned code in the same change (`0.2.0` → `0.2.4`).

Data-mostly re-pin, but the disclosure grows: 0.2.1–0.2.4 added local gateway control, a write into the user's registered repositories, and reading `~/.hermes/state.db`. Those are listed first below so they can be read before the feature list.

## What the pinned code newly does beyond the listed disclosure

**New local powers (rule 13).** Each is stated in the entry's `description` at this pin:

- Gateway control: `drain`, `restart`, `stop`, `start` go to the dashboard API already running on `127.0.0.1:9119`; the emergency stop writes the `~/.hermes/ESTOP` sentinel through `hermes pause` and aborts running kanban tasks.
- **A write inside a repository the user registered**: archiving a spec appends one line (`- **Status**: archived`) to a `SPEC*.md` in that repo. Everything else the plugin does with repositories is read-only (`git log`/`git numstat`, `docs/SPEC*.md`, an optional `.hermes-coherence.json` at the repo root).
- Reads `~/.hermes/state.db` read-only (usage, cross-session search, live turns) and the kanban SQLite databases read-only.
- `client-errors.log` under the plugin data folder records browser-side crashes.
- A fresh install attaches to the gateway already running on the machine instead of starting its own.

The earlier disclosure still holds: local HTTP/WebSocket bridge on `127.0.0.1:4097`, 256-bit token stored `0600`, the paired device gets an interactive login shell outside Hermes' approval prompts (the reason the entry is `community` and not `verified`), `node bin/hermes-pilot.mjs init` copies three bundled skills and the dashboard files, `service install` writes a launchd/systemd unit only on explicit command, remote access left to the user (documented `serve`, never started), demo is a static mock, no telemetry, no third-party upload, no self-updater (the plugin never fetches and replaces its own files).

## What landed in the range (for the re-review)

- Review queue: the sheet queue now has four states the UI shows as tabs — `Drafting` / `Waiting` / `Applying` / `Done` (`review.tab.*` in the i18n dictionaries) — with a per-sheet progress line and a "waiting for a worker" state, instead of a flat list.
- Chat is per-profile (chips, header, profile picker) rather than one global stream.
- `check:coherence` (`scripts/check-coherence.mjs`, 14 rules) replaces the older doc lint: it compares a repository's declared conventions with its recent commits, plus event/storage namespaces, i18n key parity and `npm run <name>` parity in the docs.
- Layout/resilience fixes the mobile UI needed: memos list `⋯` collapsed to one line and pinned to the card edge; chat becomes two columns above 820 px; tablet-landscape two-pane goes full width with one shared master width across the task and review panes; the dashboard worker feed is a 2×2 grid so tool names and bodies stop overlapping; theme/Vibe colours consolidate onto shared tokens (no per-screen hex); a failed dynamic `import()` recovers automatically instead of leaving a blank screen.
- The abstract-role delegation contract (roles, native delegation, fallback order) is defined inside the three bundled skills.
- 0.2.3 added the `npm` install path to the docs and fixed the CLI to run through npm's `.bin` symlink; this pin adds the kanban board picker listing unboarded repositories and refreshing repositories on open.
- This pin also gates the cold-install path in `verify`, so CI exercises the real install (`hermes plugins install` → `enable` → `npm ci` → `init` → bridge auth) rather than only the working tree.

## Checks

- `npm run verify` at `69fef2b`: exit 0 — `node --test` 1275 tests / 0 failures, then `check:dashboard`, `check:pwa`, `check:oauth` (0 forbidden access points in 349 files), `build`, `audit:responsive`, `check:term-enter`, `check:coherence` (14 rules, 0 hard fail), `check:cold-install` (`install` → `enable + list` → `npm ci` → `init + skills` → `bridge + auth`, 30.2 s).
- `hermes plugins validate .` at the pinned commit: `Validation passed.` — `manifest fields`, `requires_hermes '>=0.23.0' parses`, `loadable`, `capability probe`, `declared tools/hooks/middleware match registrations`, **`security scan — safe`**, **`no core override`**. Isolation note: dashboard backend API is served through the plugin host (buffered responses).
- Real loader: `hermes_cli.plugin_catalog.load_catalog` reads the entry — `hermes-pilot 0.2.4 community automation ['macos','linux']`, description 2852 chars, sha `69fef2bf5cd3`.
- `scripts/ci/catalog_entry_fields.py`: `BAD` empty.
- The pinned commit and the `v0.2.4` tag both resolve on the public repo (`refs/tags/v0.2.4` → tag `18d45e822d` → commit `69fef2b`).

## Known constraints (new `known_issues`)

- The interface is English or Japanese only; task titles, chat and review content stay in whatever language you write them in.
- The terminal tab is a full login shell on a phone keyboard — use the snippet bar or a hardware keyboard beyond short commands.

English-first check at the pinned commit: set Language → English and the chrome carries no CJK — the ja/en dictionaries are key-for-key identical at 1232 keys each, and the only value in `en.json` matching CJK is `settings.languageJa: "日本語"`, the language picker naming Japanese in its own script (`settings.languageEn` is `English`).

`requires_hermes` is unchanged at `>=0.23.0`, and the pinned `plugin.yaml` declares the same floor.

prs.title: fix(desktop): an open prompt-edit box keeps its draft across a stored re-read
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Editing a sent prompt loses what you typed if a stored re-read lands while the edit box is open. With a live turn, clicking Stop makes the app re-read the session from storage (`hydrateStoredSessionTranscript`). That re-read gives the edited user row a new renderer id: the live `user-<uuid>` becomes a page-index id such as `200-2-user`. The thread runtime keeps the inline edit composer in a map keyed by that id, so it has no edit composer for the new id: the edit box closes, the row shows the original prompt and the typed text is gone. This path is the runtime's id-keyed state (`_editComposers` in `@assistant-ui/core`), not a remount: the React key already uses the durable row id (`row:${rowId}`).

A second path, reproduced by @1821746019 on Desktop v0.23.3, needs no re-read: if the edit box opens before the interrupted `message.complete` arrives, `bindStoppedTurnReceipt` adds the durable `rowId` to the live `user-<uuid>` message. Its id does not change, but `transcriptRowKey` flips from the live id to `row:<id>`, which remounts the row, closes the editor and drops focus. A message that is still unstored when its edit box opens now keeps its live React key until the box closes (`$liveKeyIds` in `store/editing-rows.ts`, read by `transcriptRowKey`); every other row, including each normally sent prompt, keys exactly as before. The first version of this commit kept the live key for every unstored row; review showed that delays the usual remount of a just-sent turn to the next stored re-read, so it was narrowed to the edit box.

`UserEditComposer` now holds its durable row id in a small store (`store/editing-rows.ts`) while it is open, and `preserveLocalPendingTurnMessages` keeps the previous id of a user row in that set. Only rows being edited are touched (see the last paragraph for the one scope caveat). The merge step moved into `mergePreservedRows` in a new `preserved-rows.ts` next to `utils.ts`, which is over its file-size cap and may only shrink (this PR takes it from 2345 to 2343 lines).

Not addressed: the issue also reports that the transcript jumps to the top on Stop. It may share this cause (the closing composer releases the edit viewport hold in `list.tsx`), but I did not reproduce or change it. A send whose receipt carried no `user_row_id` has no durable id and is not covered. Every stored re-read goes through `preserveLocalPendingTurnMessages` (resume, `hydrateStoredSessionTranscript`, background sync, the tile delegate); only the jump-to-message window in `history-window.ts` builds its own page. The set is keyed by row id alone, so a row in another profile's session with the same row id also keeps its previous renderer id during a re-read; that is that row's own earlier id and duplicate ids are guarded against.

## Related Issue

Refs #145872 (fixes the lost draft; the scroll jump is not addressed here)

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix (undisclosed vulnerabilities in [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/SECURITY.md) §3.1 scope go to [Security Advisories](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/security/advisories/new) first, not a public PR)
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `apps/desktop/src/store/editing-rows.ts`: new stores of durable row ids open in the edit composer and of unstored messages whose box is open (counted, so two panes can edit one row).
- `apps/desktop/src/components/assistant-ui/thread/user-edit-composer.tsx`: hold the row id while the composer is mounted, and the live key if the message had no row id when the box opened.
- `apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-session-actions/preserved-rows.ts`: `mergePreservedRows` (the existing splice step, moved) and `keepEditedRowIds`.
- `apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-session-actions/utils.ts`: call `mergePreservedRows`.
- `apps/desktop/src/components/assistant-ui/thread/list.tsx`: `transcriptRowKey` keeps the live id for a message in `$liveKeyIds` (read with `.get()`, so a row's key does not move when its box opens or closes).
- `apps/desktop/src/components/assistant-ui/thread/user-message-edit-reread.test.tsx`: two tests: a re-read that re-derives the edited row keeps the typed text in the open box, and binding the stored row id to the same live message keeps the same editor node, focus and draft.

## How to Test

1. `cd apps/desktop && npx vitest run src/components/assistant-ui/thread/user-message-edit-reread.test.tsx` (2 passed). `src/app/session` and `src/components/assistant-ui/thread` together: 457 files, 4365 tests passed (`src/app/session`, `src/components/assistant-ui/thread`, `src/store`).
2. With `utils.ts` and `user-edit-composer.tsx` reverted to `main` (`0f602c5f6f`) both tests fail (the "Edit message" textbox is gone after the re-read; the editor node is replaced); with `list.tsx` or `user-edit-composer.tsx` reverted the second fails (the editor node is replaced).

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate — issue has no comments and no linked PR; open #148917, #148274, #147911, #147835 and #147121 edit `use-session-actions/utils.ts` for other reasons (this branch is rebased on current `main`; one of them already conflicted on an import line)
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits)
- [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass — NOT run: no Python changed; only the Desktop vitest files named under How to Test were run
- [x] `python scripts/check` passes (the blocking lint and code-health checks CI runs)
- [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features)
- [x] I've tested on my platform: Ubuntu (Linux 7.0), Node 26.12.1. Unit level only; not clicked through in a running Desktop window

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] I've updated relevant documentation (README, `docs/`, docstrings) — or N/A
- [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys — or N/A
- [x] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` if I changed architecture or workflows — or N/A
- [x] I've considered cross-platform impact (Windows, macOS) per the [compatibility guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#cross-platform-compatibility) — or N/A (renderer-only state)
- [x] I've updated tool descriptions/schemas if I changed tool behavior — or N/A

## Screenshots / Logs

```
vitest (this branch):  user-message-edit-reread -> 2 passed;  session + thread + store -> 4365 passed
vitest (utils.ts + user-edit-composer.tsx reverted to main 0f602c5f6f): 2 failed; (list.tsx reverted): 1 failed, `expected <div> to be <div> // Object.is equality`
  TestingLibraryElementError: Unable to find role="textbox" and name "Edit message"
```
The re-read is simulated with the real merge functions on a stored page; the receipt binding is simulated by re-rendering the same message with a row id, not by calling `bindStoppedTurnReceipt`. I have not run a real Desktop window, a live gateway or a real Stop on a live turn, and the issue reporter did not measure the race either.

prs.title: feat(code-health): HX018 keeps utils/ free of product code
prs.body:
`just check` now fails when a module under `utils/` imports product code or looks a module up in `sys.modules`. A new `utils/AGENTS.md` says what belongs in `utils/`. Please read that file: its rules are the part to review.

<details>
<summary>Claude Fable 5 2[1m] Medium</summary>

**Why the change**

`utils/` is useful only while every package can import it without pulling the product in, and nothing enforced that; after the merge a blocking rule does, and the rules for adding a helper are written down beside the code.

**Special things to note**

- **`sys.modules` lookups count.** `sys.modules.get("agent.x")` reaches a module with no import statement, so an import rule alone would miss it.
- **Two existing imports are waived on their lines.** `utils/files.py` imports `hermes_cli.config` inside the two round-trip YAML writers. Each carries `# health: allow HX018 -- <why>`. There is no baseline file and no count to maintain.
- **"First-party" is derived, not listed.** A top-level name is first-party when the tracked tree has `NAME.py` or `NAME/__init__.py` at its root.
- **The root `AGENTS.md` gets no routing row.** Root plus `gateway/AGENTS.md` is 11 characters under the chain cap, so the root cannot grow. `utils/AGENTS.md` loads when an agent works in `utils/`, and the rule's fix text names it.

**Change outline**

What HX018 flags in any tracked file under `utils/`:

| Reach | Example |
|---|---|
| an import at any depth, including inside a function and under `TYPE_CHECKING` | `from agent import redact` |
| an import by name | `importlib.import_module("gateway.run")` |
| a `sys.modules` lookup of a literal name | `sys.modules.get("tools.registry")`, `"gateway.run" in sys.modules` |

Allowed first-party imports: other `utils` modules, `hermes_constants`, `hermes_platform` and `hermes_yaml`. `pm` is not allowed: it imports `hermes_cli.config` inside functions, and no `utils` module imports it.

```diff
 scripts/code_health/
+  py_rules_utils_imports.py   the HX018 checker
   config.py                   the rule and its fix text
   gitio.py                    first_party_names(repo, tree)
   measure.py, py_ast.py, py_rules.py, cli.py, replay.py   pass the first-party set to the checker
+utils/AGENTS.md               what belongs in utils/, the import rule, module shape, tests
 utils/__init__.py             docstring: new code imports from the submodule
 tests/AGENTS.md               utils tests live in tests/utils/, so utils leaves the root-module list
 utils/files.py                two waiver comments
+tests/scripts/test_code_health_utils_import_rule.py
```

`utils/AGENTS.md` sets three tests for a new helper: two or more top-level packages call it today, it fits a module named for a subject, and it knows nothing about Hermes as a product. It also lists the owner for code that fails one of them.

<!-- before-and-after:start -->
<!-- before-and-after:end -->

**Live verification**

On macOS at the branch head, a probe file `utils/_probe_rule.py` with `from agent import redact` and `sys.modules.get("gateway.run")` made `just check` fail with two HX018 lines and the fix text. With the probe removed, `just check` passes and lists the two waived lines in `utils/files.py`. The code-health test files pass.

On `c98871c07c`, rebased onto `main` at `611f0ab757`: a probe with `from pm.install_states import read_state` fails `just check` with HX018. The rule's test file fails when `first_party_names` is changed to skip root-level `NAME.py` modules, and passes unchanged. `tests/scripts/test_code_health.py` and the rule's test file pass (52 tests), and `just check` passes.

</details>

It is live on `/v1/models` for **both** the general (`api.z.ai/api/paas/v4`) and Coding Plan (`api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4`) endpoints (verified 2026-11-23) and answers chat completions — while models.dev and Z.ai's own docs still lag (no 5.4 entry on either as of the same date). Since `zai` is a curated-first provider, the newest flagship would stay hidden in the `/model` picker until the registry catches up.

Live-API evidence (all probed 2026-11-23):

| Probe | Result |
|---|---|
| `GET /v1/models` (both endpoints) | `glm-5.4` listed |
| chat completion, plain | 200, `model: glm-5.4`, correct content |
| `reasoning_effort` low / high / none / minimal | all 200; `high` raises reasoning_tokens 2 → 178 |
| `thinking: {"type": "disabled"}` | 200 (unlike GLM-5.3, which rejects it) |

## Changes

- `hermes_cli/models_catalog_static.py` — add `glm-5.4` (first) to the `zai` curated row, matching the "deliberately surfaced newest model stays on top" design for curated-first providers.
- `plugins/model-providers/zai/__init__.py` — map GLM-5.4 `reasoning_effort` with the GLM-5.3 vocabulary (`low`..`max`, `xhigh→max`), but keep it **out** of the force-enable branch since GLM-5.4 accepts `thinking: disabled`.
- `hermes_cli/auth_zai_kimi.py` — probe `glm-5.4` first when detecting the Coding Plan key tier (newer plans may only carry recent slugs).
- `agent/model_metadata.py` + `agent/bedrock_adapter.py` — 1M context window per Z.ai's launch tag `glm-5.4[1m]` (the API exposes a single `glm-5.4` id and no window metadata yet).

## BEFORE / AFTER — `/model` picker, Z.AI / GLM (Coding Plan endpoint)

| Base (before) | This branch (after) |
|---|---|
| ![Base (before)](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2d018700-b9e7-4723-8512-1777293e28ee) | ![After — glm-5.4 surfaced](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/76f772d5-788b-42c3-84ea-e56cb796bfbb) |

Both screenshots are the real `hermes model` picker TUI (isolated `HERMES_HOME`), driven to the same Z.AI Coding Plan model list; the base run has the change stashed.

## Tests

- `pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_model_catalog.py tests/hermes_cli/test_models_dev_preferred_merge.py tests/agent/test_model_metadata.py tests/agent/test_reasoning_effort_wire_translation.py tests/hermes_cli/test_provider_parity.py tests/agent/test_provider_parity.py` → 202 passed. (`test_every_hermes_model_provider_is_configurable_in_desktop` failed once when run inside that wide 6-file batch; it passes standalone and in pairwise runs, both with and without this change — pre-existing cross-test state, not touched by this diff.)
- Behavior check of the provider profile on the new code: `glm-5.4` + `medium → reasoning_effort: medium`, `xhigh → max`, `disabled → thinking:{"type":"disabled"}` with no forced enable; `glm-5.3` + disabled still force-enables at `low` (regression verified).

prs.title: feat(mcp): resolve ${latest:<glob>} in mcp_servers config — version-agnostic server paths (#153351)
prs.body:
## The problem

`mcp_servers.<name>` entries that launch a server from a **versioned install
path** break on every upgrade, silently. A Claude Code plugin installs into
`~/.claude/plugins/cache/<vendor>/<plugin>/<version>/` and **deletes the
previous version directory on upgrade** — so an entry pinned to
`15.13.0/scripts/mcp-server.cjs` stops spawning the day the plugin updates to
`15.16.0`: the MCP child fails, the session shows zero MCP tools, and no error
names the missing path. Observed live on 2026-11-11 after a claude-mem
15.13.0 → 15.15.x auto-upgrade (#153351).

The failure mode is not specific to one plugin: anything registered from a
version-keyed cache (plugin caches, vendored `node_modules`, toolchains under
`~/.local/lib/<pkg>/<version>/`) has it, and today every user maintains their
own hand-written wrapper script to survive it.

## The change

A new resolver sibling to the existing `${VAR}` / `${env:VAR}` / context-var
interpolation family in `_interpolate_env_vars`:

```yaml
mcp_servers:
  claude-mem:
    command: "/usr/bin/node"
    args:
      - "${latest:~/.claude/plugins/cache/thedotmack/claude-mem/*/scripts/mcp-server.cjs}"
    enabled: true
```

Semantics (as proposed in #153351):

- **Resolved at render time** — every config interpolation *and* the
  connect-time re-render, so each new connection picks up the currently
  installed version. No gateway-lifetime freeze, no per-user wrapper script;
  the config shows what actually runs.
- **Newest match wins**: when the candidates' digit runs differ, the highest
  version wins with `sort -V` semantics (`15.13.0 < 15.15.2 < 15.100.0`,
  `v2 < v10`; mtime only breaks ties within one version) — an installer
  touching an *old* directory cannot outrank a genuinely higher version.
  Non-versioned names are ordered by newest mtime, per the issue spec.
- **No match keeps today's failure** — the literal placeholder is kept so the
  spawn fails loudly, and the unresolved pattern is **logged explicitly** (once
  per process, naming the pattern) instead of the server silently vanishing
  from the toolset. Unresolved refs are retried on every connect-time
  re-render, so an install that lands later recovers without a restart.
- **No new trust surface**: patterns only expand inside `mcp_servers` config,
  which already spawns arbitrary commands (cf. #152774's trust model). One
  docs-level caveat, now written into
  `website/docs/reference/mcp-config-reference.md` (new `${latest:...}`
  section: syntax, ordering, tie-break, no-match behavior): when a `latest`
  pattern matches, it spawns whatever version the plugin/cache ecosystem last
  installed, **unsigned** — the same auto-update-to-newest pattern as #152774
  finding 1 (`hermes update` → origin's latest release, no signature), one hop
  downstream. The miss-warning log carries this note verbatim.

Tool names/schemas and everything downstream of interpolation are untouched —
this only changes what path text the config resolves to before spawn.

On the security gate: `validate_mcp_server_entry` (the IOC/shape blocklist in
`hermes_cli/mcp_security.py`) runs at config-write/doctor time and in
`_load_mcp_config()` **before** interpolation, on the RAW entry text — it never
sees resolved values for any `${...}` ref, so `${latest:...}` bypasses it no
more than `${VAR}` does. A test pins this.

## Test plan

`tests/tools/test_mcp_latest_resolver.py` (16 tests), covering:
- highest semver wins regardless of mtime (installer touching the old dir
  cannot outrank the higher version); numeric-vs-lexical order (`2.10.0 >
  2.9.9`, `v10 > v2`); **mtime fallback for non-versioned paths is real** —
  an older `zzz-old` must not beat a newer `aaa-new` just by sorting later;
  versioned directories beat lexically-later non-versioned ones;
- resolution inside `args` lists; re-render after an upgrade picks the new
  version (per-connection semantics, no stale path); composition with `${VAR}`
  refs in the same config;
- no-match keeps the literal placeholder, marks the render `missed`, and warns
  the pattern exactly once per process;
- exact (non-glob) paths resolve verbatim; plain `${VAR}` behavior unchanged;
  the resolver only ever sees text between `${` and `}`;
- **end-to-end through the real load and launch chain** (no spawn): a
  `config.yaml` entry written the way an agent or user writes it survives
  `_load_mcp_config()` rendering and reaches `_stdio_launch()`'s
  `(command, env, cwd)` tuple with the newest match resolved — and the
  security gate is confirmed to inspect raw entry text, not resolved paths.

The end-to-end tests follow the harness shape of @tespio's repro scripts
(shared privately with the author for this PR) — the spawn step is
deliberately omitted, asserting on the launch tuple instead.

Docs: new `${latest:...}` section in `website/docs/reference/mcp-config-reference.md`.

Regression: the existing interpolation/config suites pass
(test_mcp_config_whitespace_warning, test_mcp_stdio_env_unset_ref,
test_mcp_config_change_rebind, test_mcp_reconcile_with_config,
test_mcp_config — 59 passed).

Closes #153351

## What does this PR do?

Adds Electron end-to-end regressions for two Desktop session-lifecycle boundaries:

- interrupted output persists across a Desktop restart and saved-session hydration;
- a follow-up submitted while a normal turn runs **after automatic context compression** stays queued until that turn finishes.

## What does this PR do?

Tests now exercise Hermes behavior instead of parsing the text of production code. A gateway test failed when Desktop changed `CARD_TOOL_NAMES` from a Set to an array, although card delivery still worked. The replacement imports Desktop's real classifier and checks emitted gateway frames.

| Boundary | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Desktop and gateway cards | A Python regex required one TypeScript declaration shape. | A Desktop test imports the classifier and checks start/complete frames from the registered gateway tools. |
| Docker, installer, and packaging | Tests extracted shell fragments or inferred contents from source. | Tests boot the image, invoke installer capabilities, run migrations, and import modules from a built wheel. |
| Whole-tree policies | Pytest searched source for rules it could not exercise exhaustively. | Standalone CI lints enforce those rules; focused tests exercise real callers. |

## What does this PR do?

Two independent desktop improvements, one per commit:

1. **Ship sourcemaps** for the renderer (vite), electron main, and preload (esbuild). Crash reports and devtools stack traces now point at real TS/TSX source instead of minified bundles.

2. **Debug trace instrumentation** — a device-local toggle (Settings → Advanced → Debug trace logging) that, when enabled, dumps structured `console.debug` entries for every stateful event in the desktop app. Designed for reproducing bugs that only happen in long-lived real client sessions (state accumulation, compaction, rapid session switching, background profile events) and are hard to reproduce in e2e tests.

prs.title: feat(desktop): detect and surface gone branches for cleanup
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Detects when a branch's upstream tracking ref has been deleted on the remote (the `[gone]` state — typically a merged or manually deleted branch) and surfaces it in two places: the composer coding rail and the sidebar project tree. Adds a bulk archive action for sessions sitting on gone branches.

This addresses a real workflow gap: after merging a branch on GitHub, the local worktree and its Hermes sessions linger in the sidebar with no indication that the branch is stale. The user has to manually cross-reference `git branch -vv` to know which sessions are safe to clean up.

**Two parts, one shared detection primitive:**

### Part 1 — Composer "gone" indicator
- `_branch_gone()` in `web_git.py` (remote/REST path) and `branchGone()` in `git-review-ops.ts` (Electron local path) — both use `git for-each-ref --format=%(upstream:track)` to check the `[gone]` state.
- `gone: boolean` added to `HermesRepoStatus` type.
- Amber "gone" badge in `CodingStatusRow` next to the branch name.
- Rides the existing 5 repo-status refresh edges (cwd change, workspace change tick, busy→idle, window focus, worktree mutation) — **no new polling, no cache impact** (the probe is entirely renderer-side, outside the conversation/system-prompt path).

### Part 2a — Session DB staleness fix
The session DB's `git_branch` column was only written at session creation. Now it's re-probed at:
- **Turn-complete** — `_run_prompt_submit` finally block (catches `git checkout` the agent ran in the terminal).
- **Session resume** — both deferred and eager paths (catches branch changes while the session was inactive).

Uses the existing `_persist_session_git_meta` daemon-thread helper — **zero cache impact**, it's a DB write outside the model context.

### Part 2b — Sidebar gone-branch detection + cleanup UI
- `gone_branches()` in `git_probe.py` — one `for-each-ref` call per repo root returns all gone branches.
- `gone_fn` parameter on `project_tree.build_tree()` + `_annotate_gone()` helper marks branch lanes with `gone: True`.
- `_gone_branches_for_repo` wired into the gateway's `_build_project_tree`.
- `gone?: boolean` on `SidebarSessionGroup` (renderer type).
- Amber "gone" badge on sidebar branch lanes in `WorkspaceHeader`.
- **Bulk "Archive sessions" action** in `WorkspaceMenu` for gone lanes: confirms with the user, optimistically tombstones sessions, calls `setSessionArchived` per session, surfaces success/failure toasts.
- i18n strings for all 4 locales (en, ja, zh, zh-hant).

## Related Issue

N/A — feature request from user workflow.

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/web_git.py` — `_branch_gone()` helper + `gone` field in `repo_status()`
- `tui_gateway/git_probe.py` — `gone_branches()` helper
- `tui_gateway/project_tree.py` — `gone_fn` param + `_annotate_gone()` 
- `tui_gateway/server.py` — `_gone_branches_for_repo` + staleness re-probe at turn-complete and session resume
- `apps/desktop/electron/git-review-ops.ts` — `branchGone()` + wired into `repoStatus()`
- `apps/desktop/src/global.d.ts` — `gone: boolean` on `HermesRepoStatus`
- `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/composer/status-stack/coding-row.tsx` — amber "gone" badge
- `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/sidebar/projects/workspace-groups.ts` — `gone?: boolean` on `SidebarSessionGroup`
- `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/sidebar/projects/workspace-header.tsx` — `gone` prop + archive item in `WorkspaceMenu`
- `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/sidebar/projects/workspace-group.tsx` — `handleArchiveGone` bulk archive handler
- `apps/desktop/src/i18n/{en,ja,types,zh,zh-hant}.ts` — `gone` + `archiveSessions*` strings

## How to Test

1. **Composer indicator**: In a git repo, push a branch to a remote, then delete the remote branch and `git fetch --prune`. The composer coding rail should show an amber "gone" label next to the branch name.

prs.title: fix(desktop): keep tab bar visible when toggling bottom panel panes
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

When terminal and logs share a zone (the "bottom panel"), toggling one off
previously folded the **entire zone** — hiding the tab bar so the user could
no longer switch between terminal and logs. Now:

1. **Toggling one pane off switches to a still-open sibling** instead of
   minimizing the whole zone. The zone only folds when no sibling is open.
   This uses a new `paneOpenGetters` registry so `setPaneCollapsed` can query
   each collapse pane's owning store for its open/closed state.

2. **When the zone does collapse with ≥2 shown panes, the horizontal tab bar
   stays visible** (instead of degrading to a narrow vertical rail). The
   vertical rail is now only used for a lone pane where the strip adds no
   value. This applies to both the bottom panel (row split) and the right
   panel (column split) — the column case already showed the header when
   minimized, and now the row case matches.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `apps/desktop/src/components/pane-shell/tree/store.ts` — added
  `paneOpenGetters` registry + `registerPaneOpenGetter()`; fixed
  `setPaneCollapsed`'s shared-zone branch to check for an open sibling
  before calling `toggleTreeGroupMinimized`
- `apps/desktop/src/app/contrib/controller.tsx` — `bindPaneCollapse` now
  registers the open-state getter (`() => $open.get()`)
- `apps/desktop/src/components/pane-shell/tree/renderer/tree-group.tsx` —
  `verticalCollapse` now requires `shown.length <= 1`, so ≥2 panes keep the
  horizontal tab bar even when minimized

## How to Test

1. Open the desktop app with terminal + logs in the same zone (e.g. the Quad
   preset, or drag logs into the terminal zone)
2. Toggle the terminal off (⌃\` or statusbar button) — the zone should
   switch to the logs tab instead of collapsing
3. Toggle logs off too — the zone should now collapse, but the tab bar
   remains visible as a horizontal strip (not a vertical rail)
4. Click a tab in the collapsed strip — it should restore + activate that pane

## What does this PR do?

Adds an "Archive all threads" action to the branch/worktree lane kebab menu (the `⋮` dropdown) in the desktop sidebar. Previously the kebab only appeared on removable linked worktree lanes and offered reveal/copy-path/remove. Now it appears on **any** non-profile lane that has sessions — including the main/home checkout — and offers a bulk archive that sweeps every session in that lane.

The action archives each session sequentially through the existing per-session `onArchiveSession` path (the same one right-click → Archive uses), so optimistic state, rollback, pin cleanup, and tile closing all work per-session. Sequential (not parallel) prevents overlapping rollbacks from restoring stale sidebar/pin state when one request fails mid-batch.

- `sessions-section.tsx` — passes `onArchiveSession` to `EnteredProjectContent` and grouped `SidebarWorkspaceGroup` (workspace mode only).
