prs.title: feat(desktop): show aggregate status dots on branch, repo, and project rows
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

A collapsed branch lane hid the status of the sessions under it. The user could not see that a collapsed branch still did work.

This PR adds one aggregate status dot to branch lanes, repo headers, and project overview rows (Home included) in the desktop sidebar. The dot shows the loudest status bucket across the sessions under the row. The priority order is: needs-input, working, unread, draft, idle. When the aggregate is idle, or the row has no sessions, the row shows no dot. The dot is visual only. The row click keeps its toggle behavior.

Placement keeps the rows stable:

- Branch lanes and repo headers put the dot in the glyph slot. The slot is the same fixed lead cell, so the swap does not move the label. At idle, the glyph returns.
- Project overview rows keep the identity icon. Their dot sits in a reserved fixed-size cell beside the label, so a project that starts work does not shift the row.

The aggregate reads the unfiltered membership. It sees all rows of a lane, not the visible page. One helper, `laneStatusSessionIds()`, defines what a lane's aggregate covers. `excludeProjectSessions` records the ids of the rows it hides on `statusSessionIds`. The home-lane fold in `mergeRepoWorktreeGroups` and the Home overlay rebuild in `overlayHomeLane` carry these ids forward. A pinned or filtered-out session that does work still lights its branch.

The dot renders through the existing `DOT_VARIANTS` table, so a branch row can never disagree with the session rows inside it. No new state is computed. The aggregate folds each session state through the existing `sessionStatusBucket()` and ranks with the existing `STATUS_RANK` over `$sessionDotStateById`. `stalled` and `background` read as working, the same fold the sidebar's status filter uses. No new rank table exists.

## Related Issue

None. Ethie requested the feature directly.

## Type of Change

- [ ] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `apps/desktop/src/store/session-dot-state.ts` — `maxSessionDotState()`: a pure max that folds each state through `sessionStatusBucket()` and ranks with the existing `STATUS_RANK`. Absent and empty resolve to idle.
- `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/session-status-dot.tsx` — `GroupStatusDot`, the aggregate renderer. It uses the same `DOT_VARIANTS` table as `SessionStatusDot` and takes an `idle` fallback node. It resolves through a scalar selector, so a row repaints only when its own aggregate flips.
- `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/sidebar/projects/workspace-group.tsx` — the branch lane swaps its glyph for the dot when the aggregate is not idle.
- `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/sidebar/projects/entered-content.tsx` — the repo header (multi-repo projects) gets the same swap, aggregated over its lanes.
- `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/sidebar/projects/overview-row.tsx` — the project row gets a reserved status cell beside the label.
- `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/sidebar/projects/workspace-groups.ts` — `statusSessionIds` on `SidebarSessionGroup`, recorded by `excludeProjectSessions` and carried through the home-lane fold and `overlayHomeLane`; `laneStatusSessionIds()` as the one definition of a lane's covered ids; `projectStatusSessionIds()` builds the per-project id sets for the overview.
- `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/sidebar/sessions-section.tsx`, `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/sidebar/index.tsx` — thread the per-project sets from `scopedSessions` (only the profile scope narrows this list) to the overview rows.
- `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/sidebar/projects/index.ts` — export `projectStatusSessionIds`.
- Tests: `apps/desktop/src/store/session-dot-state.test.ts`, `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/group-status-dot.test.tsx` (new), `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/sidebar/projects/workspace-groups.test.ts`.

## How to Test

1. From `apps/desktop`, run `npx vitest run src/store/session-dot-state.test.ts src/app/chat/group-status-dot.test.tsx src/app/chat/sidebar/projects/workspace-groups.test.ts`. All pass (this branch: 9 sidebar-related test files, 125 tests, all green).
2. From `apps/desktop`, run `npx tsc -p . --noEmit`. No errors.
3. In the app: enter a project, start a turn in a session under a worktree lane, and collapse the lane. The lane's git-branch glyph becomes the working dot. Collapse the project: the overview row shows the same dot beside the label. When the turn needs input, the dot turns amber on both rows. When everything settles and is read, the dots disappear and the glyph returns.
4. Pin a working session: its branch lane still shows the working dot, because the aggregate reads the pre-exclusion membership.

## Notes for review

- The running arc stays on session rows only. The aggregate rows show the dot without the arc. This follows the agreed design.
- The dot is not a click target. The design considered a jump-to-session click and rejected it, because the dot lives inside the row's toggle button.
- The repo-header wiring in `entered-content.tsx` has no direct render test. The merge and exclusion seams that feed it are covered in `workspace-groups.test.ts`, and the dot component is covered in `group-status-dot.test.tsx`.
- A two-axis self-review (standards and spec, parallel subagents) ran before the final push. It found one real defect: `overlayHomeLane` rebuilt the Home lane and dropped `statusSessionIds`, so pinned work under Home went dark when a detached live session triggered the overlay. The fix carries the field through the rebuild, and a test pins the flow. The review also drove the `laneStatusSessionIds()` extraction and explicit return types on the new functions.
- Known narrow edge: the overview row's covering set unions the tree lanes, the previews, and the loaded session page. A working session older than the loaded page and outside the preview set is invisible to the project row. Such a session also has no entry in `$sessionDotStateById`, so no aggregate over that map can see it. The lane and repo rows inside an entered project do not share this edge.

prs.title: fix(desktop): render the sidebar PR badge on session rows and branch lanes
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

The desktop sidebar can badge a session with its pull request. The badge did not appear. This PR repairs the data that the badge needs, and adds the badge to project branch lanes.

There are two defects, one behind the other.

**1. The gateway did not record `git_branch` on desktop session rows.**

The sidebar joins pull requests on `git_repo_root` + `git_branch` from the persisted `sessions` row (`sessionPrKey`, `apps/desktop/src/store/pull-requests.ts`). The composer status line shows a PR for the same branch, because it probes git live. That difference is why the feature looked half broken: the status line was correct and the sidebar was empty.

In a real profile database, 146 of 156 rows with a `git_repo_root` had a NULL `git_branch`. Both arms of session start failed to run the enrichment:

- Create: `_ensure_session_db_row` inserted the row AFTER the only call to the enrichment scheduler. `update_session_cwd` claims a generation only for a row that exists, so the call returned None and the branch probe never started.
- Resume: `_init_session` adopted the `cwd` of an existing row and skipped enrichment. A row with no branch stayed that way.

**2. The project branch lanes never read the pull-request store.**

The `projects/` folder had no reference to it. "Show PR" badged the session rows under a lane, but not the lane itself, although the lane label IS the branch name.

## Related Issue

No existing issue. Related but separate: #79623 reports the same NULL columns for **cron and CLI** sessions. This PR repairs the **desktop gateway** path only. The cron path writes its row elsewhere and needs its own fix.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

## Changes Made

**Gateway (commit 1)**

- `tui_gateway/server.py` — `_ensure_session_db_row` claims a generation and starts the branch probe AFTER `create_session` inserts the row.
- `tui_gateway/server.py` — `_init_session` starts the same enrichment when the adopted row has no git metadata. Rows from before this fix repair themselves on the next resume. The generation guard in `publish_session_git_metadata` keeps a concurrent workspace move authoritative.
- `tests/tui_gateway/test_session_git_branch_persistence.py` — 3 tests against a real `SessionDB` on a temp path.

**Desktop (commit 2)**

- `apps/desktop/src/store/pull-requests.ts` — new `branchLanePrKey(repoRoot, branch)`, the trunk-guarded key. `sessionPrKey` now uses it, so both surfaces build the key one way.
- `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/sidebar/projects/workspace-group.tsx` — the lane reads the store behind the same `rowMeta.includes('pr')` toggle and requests its own branch.
- `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/sidebar/projects/workspace-header.tsx` — new `meta` slot. The chip is a SIBLING of the toggle button, because a button inside a button is invalid HTML and the keyboard cannot reach it.
- `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/sidebar/projects/entered-content.tsx` — passes `repoPath` to the lane.
- Tests: `apps/desktop/src/store/pull-requests.test.ts`, `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/sidebar/projects/workspace-group.test.tsx`.

Two store changes that a second caller made necessary:

- Staleness is now per lookup. A repo that is fresh for the branches of the last fetch still fetches for a branch it has not asked about. Without this, a lane that appears after the fetch waits 60 seconds for a badge.
- A narrow ask merges the lookups of the last fetch. The store replaces the pull requests of a repo wholesale, so a one-branch ask would otherwise delete the PRs that the session rows show.

## How to Test

Both screenshots below come from a real Electron run: a real git repository, four real linked worktrees, four real sessions built through the gateway and the agent loop, and a `gh` stand-in that answers the real GraphQL query shape.

**Session rows (the gateway fix).** Before this PR every row here had a NULL branch and no badge.

![Session rows with PR badges](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethernet8023/hermes-pr-assets/main/pr-89709/01-session-rows.png)

**Branch lanes (the new surface).** Each lane carries the PR for its branch: #8077 closed, #8140 draft, #8098 merged, #8123 open.

![Branch lanes with PR badges](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethernet8023/hermes-pr-assets/main/pr-89709/02-branch-lanes.png)

**Both at once.** An expanded lane: the lane header carries #8123 from its label, and the session row inside it carries the same #8123 from the branch its session recorded. The lane badge and the gateway fix, in one frame.

![Lane and session row with the same PR](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethernet8023/hermes-pr-assets/main/pr-89709/03-lane-expanded.png)

Manual steps:

1. Open a chat in a worktree on a branch that has an open PR.
2. Turn on Filters → Show → PR in the sidebar.
3. The session row shows the PR number.
4. Group by project and enter the project. The branch lane shows the same PR.

Automated:

```bash
nix develop -c scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tui_gateway/test_session_git_branch_persistence.py
cd apps/desktop && npx vitest run src/app/chat/sidebar/ src/store/pull-requests.test.ts
```

Results on this branch:

- Python: 36 tests pass (the new file plus every neighbour that touches this machinery).
- Desktop: 181 tests pass. `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npx eslint` are clean.

Fault detection, which is the part that matters:

- Remove the gateway change: the two regression tests fail, the guard test still passes.
- Remove the renderer change: the two badge tests fail, the three guard tests (toggle off, no PR, kanban) still pass.

## Notes for review

- Existing rows repair themselves lazily, on the next resume of each session. There is no migration. Say the word if you want one.
- The lane badge appears in the entered-project view. Profile and source groups have no single repository, so they take no badge.
- The kanban lane takes no badge. It collects many branches into one lane.
- The Playwright spec that produced the screenshots above is included (`apps/desktop/e2e/sidebar-pr-badges.spec.ts`). Every test body passes and writes its snapshot. The run then reports a per-test timeout during teardown. The untouched `worktree-branch-status.spec.ts` fails the same way on the same machine, so the cause is the harness or this host, not this spec. CI runs no Playwright lane, so this spec does not gate the merge. It is here for a maintainer who runs the suite locally.
- `RealSessionSpec` takes an optional `cwd` (`apps/desktop/e2e/real-session-builder.ts`). The builder placed every session at the repository root before. A session must start in a named worktree for this spec, and any later test that needs a specific checkout can now do the same.

prs.title: ci: run the full suite in the merge queue
prs.body:
Makes the merge queue the full-suite gate, so a push to main no longer re-runs CI. Nothing in `.github/` had a `merge_group` trigger, so with a queue enabled the required `All required checks pass (v2)` check would never report and every entry would time out.

## Triggers
- `ci.yaml`: add `merge_group`, drop `push: main`.
- `nix.yml`: add `merge_group`, drop `push: main`.
- `docker.yml`: add `merge_group`; `push: main` stays, because the publish jobs run only for a main push.

## Classifier
- `detect-changes` diffs a merge group against `merge_group.base_sha` (its parent: the previous queue entry, or the target tip), so each entry is classified on what it adds.
- `classify_changes.py` forces every slow lane on for a merge group (docker, nix, all e2e lanes), the same way the `run-e2e` label does. The other lanes follow the diff. It never looks up PR labels for a merge group.

## Caches
A merge group's cache writes are scoped to its own `gh-readonly-queue/...` ref, which no PR or main run can restore. Dropping the main pushes would therefore stop refreshing the caches every PR restores from (main scope is 4.3 GiB of a repo already at 10.9 GiB used).
- Cache saves key on `github.ref == main` (`ci.yaml` timing baseline, `tests.yml` duration cache) and skip `merge_group` (`docker.yml` `cache-to`, `nix.yml` `save`).
- `ci.yaml` and `nix.yml` gain a daily `schedule`. Scheduled runs on main can write the default-branch scope, which keeps it warm.

## Plugin catalog
`merge_group` does not support `paths:` filters, so `plugin-catalog-ci.yml` could not keep its trigger.
- It is now a `workflow_call` job in `ci.yaml`, gated by a new `plugin_catalog` classifier lane, and added to `all-checks-pass`. It therefore becomes part of the required check.
- On a merge group it diffs against `merge_group.base_sha`, so entries ahead in the queue are not re-admitted. It fails if that base is not an ancestor of HEAD. The PR path (merge commit's first parent) is unchanged.
- `pinned-source-validate` is skipped for events that are neither a pull request nor a merge group (a stable-release call has no candidate entry).

## Tests
- Classifier: merge group runs all slow lanes and follows the diff for the rest; never reads PR labels; `plugin_catalog` lane.
- Wiring: the action reads the group's SHAs; `ci.yaml`, `docker.yml`, `nix.yml` trigger on `merge_group`; `plugin-catalog` is in `all-checks-pass`.
- Catalog step: the existing cases re-run in merge-group shape, plus one where entry B's group contains entry A.

Verified locally: 358 pass, 1 skipped, 1 fail. The failure is `test_stable_release_graph.py::test_docker_recovery_refuses_to_replace_a_divergent_version_tag` (a `cd C:\Users\...` path mangled inside `bash -c` on Windows; the file is untouched here). The catalog step was also run for real against a throwaway repo shaped like a queue. Not verified: the Linux-only catalog harness tests skip on this host, `actionlint` was not available, and no real `merge_group` run has happened.

## Not changed
- `archive-inputs`, `deploy-site`, `js-autofix`, `skills-index`, `termux-verify` stay on `push: main` (they publish or auto-fix).
- `pm-bundle`, `install-e2e`, `sandbox-image`, `windows-bundle-sdk`, `termux-verify` stay on `pull_request` with `paths:`; they will not run in the queue.
- The `protect-main` ruleset. After this merges, add the "Require merge queue" rule; the required check name is unchanged.

prs.title: feat(desktop): unify every new-session gesture on openNewSessionTab
prs.body:
## What

The tab-strip "+" and the new-session shortcut were two different functions minting two different artifacts: `openNewSessionTab` created a real, unlisted session that fell back to `sessionTitle()`'s **"Untitled session"**, while `session.new` (⌘N / alt+N) was a pure view-reset draft reading the **"New session"** placeholder — and the "+"-created tab never painted the new-session splash because `shouldShowIntro` gated on `primary`.

One creation path now serves every "new chat" gesture:

- **`session.new` (⌘N / alt+N), the sidebar New Session row, the command palette and ⌘T all dispatch the same `openNewSessionTab`** — a real, unlisted session fronts the workspace as its own tab; the previously occupied chat survives as its own tab. The pure view-reset draft (`startFreshSessionDraft`) remains for the gateway-event fresh-session flows.
- **Minting from a workspace page (Settings, Profiles, …) leaves the page** for the primary chat's session route (or the new-chat route when no session is selected), so the new tab is never hidden behind an overlay route (`leaveWorkspacePageForChat`).
- **Draft title unified on "New session"**: unlisted draft stubs are stamped `NEW_SESSION_TITLE` client-side, so every surface resolving them via `ownerLookupSessionRows` (`tileTitle()`, the document header) reads "New session", not "Untitled session". The backend row stays untitled, so derived/llm auto-titling still lands on the first exchange. Stub helpers live in a topical sibling (`unlisted-owners.ts`); the sidebar handler in `select-sidebar-item.ts` — both their old homes sit on code-health ratchets that may only go down.
- **The splash paints for draft sessions too**, via a tested predicate (`isDraftSessionRow` in `draft-session.ts`): a row must positively exist and carry an explicit zero `message_count`, so a resumed-but-not-yet-loaded session never flashes the splash next to its loading spinner. Hidden rows (canonical Bot Chat, group plumbing) and bot-scoped chats are excluded — their empty state belongs to the owning plugin's `CHAT_EMPTY_AREA` contribution, not the Hermes splash.

## Notes / tradeoffs

- ⌘N now requires the gateway (it performs a real `session.create`); without one it surfaces the existing create-failure notification instead of an offline blank draft. Repeated presses reuse the one blank draft (`frontUntouchedDraftTab`), so no twin minting.
- `KeybindRuntimeDeps.startFreshSession` is removed — the keybind map no longer calls it; test mocks updated, and `tool-pane-toggle`'s ⌘N test models the unified flow (fronts the new session's tile pane; the terminal stays open behind its tab).

## Tests

- `intro-visibility.test.ts`: draft-session suite (tile + primary binding, emptiness, aux-window and toggle gates, non-draft bypass).
- `draft-session.test.ts`: the draft predicate — explicit-zero acceptance, unknown-session / undefined-count / hidden-row / bot-scoped rejections.
- `new-session-tab-route-leave.test.ts`: page-leave behavior (no-op off pages, session route on selection, new-chat fallback).
- `unlisted-draft-title.test.ts`: stub placeholder title, owner-lookup visibility, same-id replacement.
- `use-keybinds-browser.test.tsx`: alt+N and alt+T (and the ⌃⌘ defaults) assert the shared action.
- `npm run typecheck` green; `eslint` clean on all touched files; `python scripts/check --only health` green (ChatViewContent, ContribWiring and the session-actions ratchets all offset via topical-sibling moves).

prs.title: feat(desktop): ship renderer sourcemaps without vendor source text
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Ships sourcemaps for the desktop renderer, so DevTools shows the original app source in the packaged app.

Full maps would embed the text of every dependency (shiki grammars, mermaid, ...) and more than double the dist size. A small build plugin removes the embedded text for `node_modules` sources after the maps are written. App sources stay readable in DevTools. Vendor frames still map to file:line, because the mappings are unchanged.

The Electron main process and preloads are unchanged. Main-process maps did not load in the packaged app anyway: Node loads the bundle through its virtual `app.asar/...` path and cannot read the `.map` file from there.

Measured on a win-arm64 build:

| build | `dist/` | maps | maps, xz |
|---|---|---|---|
| no maps (main) | 44.2 MB | — | — |
| full maps | 114.0 MB | 69.8 MB | 10.4 MB |
| this PR | 68.6 MB | 24.4 MB | 4.6 MB |

`dist/**` is unpacked from the asar, so the uncompressed number is what lands on disk.

## Type of Change

<!-- Check the one that applies. -->

- [ ] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)

## Changes Made

- `apps/desktop/vite.config.ts`: `build.sourcemap: true`, plus the `hermes:vendor-sourcemap-content` plugin. It rewrites each chunk's map in `writeBundle`.
- `apps/desktop/scripts/sourcemap-vendor-content.mjs`: sets `sourcesContent` entries to `null` for sources under `node_modules`. `sources`, `mappings` and `names` are left as they are.
- `apps/desktop/scripts/sourcemap-vendor-content.test.mjs`: covers the vendor/app split (both `/` and `\` separators), that mappings are kept, a map with no `sourcesContent`, and the in-place file rewrite.

## How to Test

2. Check the maps: every `node_modules` source has `null` content, every app source has its text.

prs.title: Prepared tool trees and Windows ARM64 wheel-or-source installs
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Hermes's package manager (PM) can install ready-to-use tool trees on every supported target without relying on a host archive utility. On Windows ARM64, it prefers verified native Python wheels but builds an unavailable wheel from its locked source distribution, preparing compilers only if the first build fails.

**Status: draft; do not merge yet.** All 96 distinct prepared tool objects for 116 package/target pins answered HTTP 206 on public R2. All eight reviewed native wheels still return 404; the existing organization release has no assets.

CI on `4d9eb2f184` did not finish: 14 jobs were cancelled with zero steps and no runner after a long queue; three Nix/Docker jobs remained queued at readback. The protected `ci-reviewed` gate needs maintainer review; the aggregate gate failed on that result and the cancellations. No completed test job failed on this head.

Native Windows ARM64 run `36663851577` passed on PR code `6191a998aa`: cold locked-sdist install, recorded-generation repair, and a separate source-built test environment. It also exercised Windows TOML local-wheel path rebinding and rejected corrupt copied bytes. The preferred prebuilt-wheel download path remains unproven from production hosts until those eight objects are published.

| User path | Before | With this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Pinned tools | Raw archives could need host-specific extraction tools. | Use a hash-checked post-staging tree, then the original pinned input only if the tree is unavailable. |
| Windows ARM64 Python | A missing direct wheel URL stopped uv; core sync prepared compilers unconditionally. | Try an existing release asset and then R2 with one reviewed hash; use the same-version, hash-locked registry sdist if neither exists. Prepare build tools only after a classified backend failure. |
| Other hosts | Resolve Python dependencies through the universal registry lock. | Keep that registry resolution and the same dependency versions. |

The existing NousResearch release is a read-only download candidate. The archival jobs write immutable SHA-addressed objects to R2, never create or modify a GitHub release or tag, and verify public bytes before pinning.

## Related Issue

No issue — planned PM distribution work.

## Type of Change

- [x] New feature: prepared tool delivery and optional native wheel recovery.

## Changes Made

- `pm/lock.json` retains 116 verified prepared rows. CI validates native archives, tree digests and source identities before a bot commits the pins and installer fragments.
- `pm/wheel_sources.py` stages only hash-verified wheels in a private generation. A missing object retains the locked registry sdist; a downloaded hash mismatch stops. Repair verifies copied wheels and rebinds their local paths.
- The publisher and bootstrap URLs use the Nous Research mirror. The obsolete release writers are removed; `agent/proxy_sources/iron_proxy.py` remains unchanged relative to main.

## How to Test

- `scripts/run_tests.sh`: **132 focused tests** passed before the audit fixes, **68** on `e823456f7f`, and **44 affected tests** on `6191a998aa`. Three CI-failing files passed their Linux cases on `ecc4685f06`; a POSIX no-release corrupt-hash regression was red before the fix and green on `4d9eb2f184`. Linux skips are not native proof.
- `nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.python-lock-derived --no-link` and lock check passed on `6191a998aa`; actionlint, PowerShell parsing and Windows-footgun scan passed on `ecc4685f06`; Bash parse and bootstrap-pin check passed on `4d9eb2f184`.
- A real uv probe selected seven reviewed local wheels plus one locked registry sdist. Windows ARM64 frozen dry-runs passed for initial and repaired workspaces on `6191a998aa`. Native run `36663851577` passed cold source install, generation repair, and a fresh-cache side-environment build; its local-wheel fixture proved Windows path rebinding and hash-mismatch rejection.
- Native run `36670575157` on current code passed the raw CUDA pause/resume test (1 test, 0 failed in 58.4 seconds), including pinned artifacts and the engine's `--version` and `--list-devices` commands.
- PR CI run `36670453665`: OS-specific tests, lint, bootstrap and uv-lock checks passed. The Linux full suite, E2E, JS and Rust jobs were cancelled without runners; this is not an all-green verdict.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] Commits use Conventional Commits; the PR diff names no staging repository; all 116 prepared source identities and generated installer fragments match this head.
- [x] Corrupt downloaded wheels fail closed; R2 publication reads back public hashes.
- [x] Native ARM64 source/side-environment/repair passed on `6191a998aa`; x64 and ARM64 bootstrap routes passed on `ecc4685f06`.
- [x] Raw CUDA pause/resume and native engine commands passed on ARM64 at `4d9eb2f184` (run `36670575157`).
- [ ] All eight prebuilt wheel objects answer from the public production mirror.

- [x] Config keys and model tool schemas: N/A.

The current head's raw CUDA pause/resume and engine-command acceptance passed in `36670575157`. Public probes returned HTTP 206 for 96/96 prepared objects and HTTP 404 for all eight wheels. prs.title: ci(release): drop retired tag/claim shapes; version commit and channel builds after their stable ancestor
prs.body:
Drops the readers for retired tag and claim shapes, and versions commit/channel builds after the stable release they're built on, instead of `0.0.0`.

Stacked on #146949.

## What changes

- **Old canary tag shape (`v<stable>+canary.<stamp>`): every reader, matcher and prune path deleted.** That's `update_channel`'s legacy regex, `published_canary_timestamp` / `published_release_version`, the `release_channels` / `channels` / `darwin` / `render-builds-table` / `r2` matchers and the `v*+canary.*` prune. No live published record uses the old shape: the canary channel record, pointer and mac feed all return 404. The desktop matchers were already new-shape only.
- **Legacy stable-claim shapes:** every `rc.*` claim gets cheap identity checks (`stable.claim_identity`: schema, version, attempt, commit, epoch vs tagger). The full shape + lanes check (`validate_claim`, now current shape only: `lanes` + `lanesRevision 2`) is required for the unfinished attempt.
  - A finished attempt in an old shape (v0.21.6 rc.4, v0.21.7 rc.15, v0.22.0 rc.3 are pre-lanes) isn't refused; its record carries `lanes: None`. Publishing or advancing a `lanes: None` record is refused with a pinned message.
  - `lanes.claim_lanes` loses its legacy branch.
- **Commit and channel builds are versioned after the newest stable tag that's an ancestor of the commit** (`commit_build.version_at`: plain `vX.Y.Z` only, numeric max, never unfiltered `git describe`), not pyproject's always-`0.0.0`. So claims read `channel.<stamp>-v0.22.5`, not `-v0.0.0`.
  - It refuses clearly when no stable ancestor exists.
  - `--build-commit` fetches with `--tags`.
  - Tagless desktop/Termux commit builds share the rule.

## Manual cleanup at merge (by hand, not in this PR)

main still cuts an old-shape canary daily, so re-derive at merge: `git ls-remote --tags origin | grep '+canary'` and `gh release list -L 200 --json tagName,isDraft`. As of 2026-10-29:
- **20 tags:** `v0.21.4+canary.*` ×5, `v0.22.1+canary.*` ×1, `v0.22.2+canary.*` ×6, `v0.22.4+canary.*` ×1, `v0.22.5+canary.*` ×7
- **15 draft releases:** every one of those tags from v0.22.1 on
- **R2 archives:** `releases/tag/v*+canary.*/`. R2 prune no longer matches these, so delete them by hand.

## Verification (local, Windows arm64)

Before stacking: `tests/ci` + `tests/scripts` had no failures beyond the base's known Windows-environment ones. The `hermes_cli` files that failed locally (7 files incl. the 4 that touch release modules) fail the same way on the unmodified base: 93 failing ids at the tip vs 94 at base, 0 tip-only. After the rebase onto #146949 only an import line in `sequencer.py` conflicted. `ruff check .` clean; `scripts/check --only health` 0 blocking. The full suite is left to CI.

issues.title: QQ channel error 11241: resty v2.17.1 regression breaks botgo auth header (botgo v0.2.1 expects resty v2.6.0)
issues.body:
## QQ channel fails with error 11241 ("Authorization header format error") — caused by resty dependency version regression (botgo v0.2.1 + resty v2.17.1)

### Summary

The QQ channel fails to start with:

```
{"level":"error","component":"channels","channel":"qq",
 "error":"failed to get websocket info: code:401, text:{\"message\":\"请求头Authorization参数格式错误\",\"code\":11241,\"err_code\":40011005,\"trace_id\":\"c776393f8d926343fa1fad8d71f0777b\"}",
 "message":"Failed to start channel"}
```

The credentials (AppID/AppSecret) are valid — a freshly obtained `access_token` works when called manually with header `Authorization: QQBot <token>` (HTTP 200, gateway URL and C2C message send both succeed). The failure is **not** a config or credential problem. It is caused by a Go dependency version mismatch between botgo and resty.

### Root cause

`botgo v0.2.1` builds the auth header correctly. In `token_source.go` it sets `TokenType = "QQBot"` (uppercase B), and in `openapi/v1/openapi.go` its `OnBeforeRequest` hook calls:

```go
c.SetAuthScheme(tk.TokenType)   // client-level: c.AuthScheme = "QQBot"
c.SetAuthToken(tk.AccessToken)  // client-level: c.Token = <token>
```

botgo v0.2.1 declares a dependency on `resty/v2 v2.6.0`. In v2.6.0, the middleware builds the header like this:

```go
// resty v2.6.0 middleware.go
var authScheme string
if !IsStringEmpty(r.AuthScheme) {
    authScheme = r.AuthScheme
} else if !IsStringEmpty(c.AuthScheme) {
    authScheme = c.AuthScheme   // <-- picks up "QQBot" from the client
} else {
    authScheme = "Bearer"
}
Header.Set(c.HeaderAuthorizationKey, authScheme+" "+c.Token)  // "QQBot <token>"  ✅
```

However, picoclaw v0.3.1's `go.mod` contains:

```
github.com/go-resty/resty/v2 v2.17.1 // indirect
```

Go's Minimal Version Selection therefore upgrades resty to v2.17.1 (confirmed by the embedded build paths in the released binary):

```
/home/runner/go/pkg/mod/github.com/go-resty/resty/v2@v2.17.1/middleware.go
```

In resty v2.17.1 the header construction changed:

```go
// resty v2.17.1 middleware.go
if !IsStringEmpty(r.Token) {
    Header.Set(c.HeaderAuthorizationKey, strings.TrimSpace(r.AuthScheme+" "+r.Token))
} else if !IsStringEmpty(c.Token) {
    Header.Set(c.HeaderAuthorizationKey, strings.TrimSpace(r.AuthScheme+" "+c.Token))
    //                                                       ^^^^^^^^^^^^ request-level scheme
}
```

Here the scheme is taken from `r.AuthScheme` (the **request**), not `c.AuthScheme` (the client). A `Request` is created by `c.R()` with `AuthScheme: c.AuthScheme` copied at creation time — which happens **before** botgo's `OnBeforeRequest` hook runs. Since the hook only mutates the client value (`c.SetAuthScheme`), the request still holds resty's default `"Bearer"`. The resulting header is:

```
Authorization: Bearer <token>   ❌
```

QQ's API rejects this with `11241 — 请求头Authorization参数格式错误`. This also matches direct testing: `QQBot <token>` → 200, `QQbot <token>` → 11201, `Bearer <token>` / bare token → 11241.

### Proposed fix

Pin resty back to the version botgo was written against. In `go.mod`:

```
replace github.com/go-resty/resty/v2 => github.com/go-resty/resty/v2 v2.6.0
```

(or change the `require` to v2.6.0), then rebuild. No change to botgo or picoclaw application code is needed. Alternatively, upgrade resty to a version where client-level `SetAuthScheme` is honored again (needs confirmation), or bump botgo to a version compatible with newer resty.

Note: simply adding a "header stitching" hook in picoclaw will not work — the header is assembled inside botgo via resty, and picoclaw exposes no override point for it.

### Environment

- picoclaw v0.3.1 (git 2cf030d2), linux/arm64
- botgo v0.2.1 (declared resty v2.6.0)
- resty v2.17.1 actually compiled into the binary
- trace_id: c776393f8d926343fa1fad8d71f0777b
- Failing call: `WS()` / "failed to get websocket info"

issues.title: [Feature] Add LLMTR as an OpenAI-compatible provider
issues.body:
## 🎯 The Goal / Use Case

I'd like PicoClaw to ship a named `llmtr` provider in the model catalog.

LLMTR (https://llmtr.com) is an OpenAI-compatible gateway at https://llmtr.com/v1. One key reaches the models in its catalog. I can already point a custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint at it, but a built-in catalog entry would let me choose `llmtr` and use `https://llmtr.com/v1` without overwriting another provider's settings.

## 💡 Proposed Solution

Add `llmtr` to the provider metadata catalog (the same map as OpenRouter and LiteLLM): default API base `https://llmtr.com/v1`, creatable and usable as a default chat model, with `/models` fetch enabled. I am not proposing a built-in common-model list or a logo; catalog models should be pinned in `model_list`.

## 🛠 Potential Implementation (Optional)

The change is a new entry in `pkg/providers/provider_metadata.go`, plus the providers guide, README provider tables, and a comment in `pkg/config/defaults.go`. No new HTTP client is needed; `httpAPI: true` uses the existing OpenAI-compatible transport.

## 🚦 Impact & Roadmap Alignment
- [ ] This is a Core Feature
- [x] This is a Nice-to-Have / Enhancement
- [ ] This aligns with the current Roadmap

## 🔄 Alternatives Considered

A custom OpenAI-compatible model entry with `api_base` set to `https://llmtr.com/v1` already works. That is what I use today. A named `llmtr` provider would keep those settings separate, the same way the OpenRouter catalog entry does.

## 💬 Additional Context

I am ready to open a PR after this issue. The change does not include a provider logo; a public asset could not be retrieved from llmtr.com for this work.

issues.title: [capability] Network mailbox so session runners don't need a shared session dir
issues.body:
Session runners currently need the host's session directory mounted: the two session DBs, the heartbeat and the outbox. That rules out runners that can't see host paths: remote or hosted ones, Kubernetes, and sandbox runtimes like OpenShell.

The mailbox seam from August should make a second implementation possible. What I have in mind:

- The host would keep its SQLite DBs as they are. A small host service would expose the runner's `MailboxOperations` for one session, backed by the existing SQLite mailbox.
- On the runner, a remote mailbox would load a snapshot in `run()` and commit the changes when it resolves (the ops are sync inside `run()`).
- Each session would get its own credential at spawn, scoped to that session only.
- The heartbeat and outbox would use the same connection. The group folder would stay a mount for now.

It would be runtime-neutral, and I'd try it on plain Docker first. My use case is OpenShell, along the lines of OpenClaw's worker mode.

Is something like this already planned, maybe for a hosted setup? If so I'd rather align with it than build a parallel one. If not, I'm happy to prototype it.

issues.title: Signal channel: image/PDF attachments unreachable from agent container

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something is not working as expected

issues.body:
## Bug

Images and PDFs sent over Signal arrive at the host but the agent inside the container can't open them.

## Reproduce

1. Install Signal via `/add-signal` on a v2 install.
2. From your phone, send a DM with an image attached (e.g. `archetype.png`).
3. Ask the agent \"can you see this image?\".

Agent responds with something like *\"I see that an image came through (the path is showing) but I can't access the file from my container — the Signal attachments folder isn't mounted into my workspace\".*

Same behaviour for PDFs (`application/pdf`), except PDFs are dropped silently — there's no handler for them at all in `src/channels/signal.ts`.

## Root cause

`src/channels/signal.ts` (upstream/channels) builds the inbound message's structured `attachments` array as `{path: <host-path>, contentType}` and also emits a `[Image: <host-path>]` line in the text body. The host path points into `~/.local/share/signal-cli/attachments/<id>`, which is **never mounted into the agent container** — `src/container-runner.ts:buildMounts` only mounts `/workspace`, `/workspace/agent`, `/workspace/global`, `/app/CLAUDE.md`, `/app/src`, `/app/skills`, `/home/node/.claude`, plus any `additionalMounts` the operator configures per-group.

So the agent receives a path that doesn't resolve inside its filesystem. Vision-capable models never see images; PDFs are silently dropped.

## Fix

The host already has a complete pipeline for this: `src/session-manager.ts:extractAttachmentFiles` saves any `attachments[].data` base64 to `<sessionDir>/inbox/<msgId>/<filename>` and rewrites the entry as `localPath`. The container formatter renders `[image|document: <name> — saved to /workspace/inbox/.../...]`. The agent can then `Read` the file.

signal.ts just needs to read each image/PDF file off disk and inline it as base64 in the `attachments` array. No host changes, no new mount, no new dependency.

PR with the fix (image + PDF, refactored into a shared helper, tests updated): #2529 — will edit this issue with the link after creating it.

## Verified

Fix is running live on a downstream install since 2026-05-17. Images now render through to the agent; PDFs work end-to-end with original filename preserved.

issues.title: Cold-start transcript rotation silently drops a live conversation with no handover
issues.body:
### What happened

A long working session (about 14 h with several auto-compactions, many screenshots read) ended at a usage limit ("You've hit your 5-hour limit"). The container went idle. When the user wrote again 30 minutes later, the runner started a brand-new SDK session (SessionStart `startup`, not `resume`). The previous transcript was archived to `conversations/` at that exact minute. The agent answered with no memory of the task it was in the middle of and had to rebuild it from memory files, archived transcripts and GitHub.

Cause, confirmed: the pre-resume rotation in `poll-loop.ts` (`maybeRotateContinuation` → `decideContinuationRotation`). The transcript was 24.5 MB, over the 12 MB cap, and was renamed to `<id>.jsonl.rotated-<ts>` at the first message after the limit. The usage limit only stopped the container. Any cold start would have rotated it.

Checked on `nanocoai/nanoclaw@53099d2`.

### Why it's a problem

Rotation exists for a good reason: a transcript too big to cold-resume hangs the first turn. But today it is silent:

- The user gets no notice that context was reset, and assumes the agent remembers.
- The fresh session gets no pointer to what it just lost. The archive is written to `conversations/`, but nothing tells the agent "you were rotated; the last thread is in <file>".
- It hits exactly the sessions that matter most: long, busy, multi-step work.

### Proposal (small)

When rotation fires at cold start, prepend a system note to the first prompt of the new session, e.g. "Your previous session was rotated (transcript 12.4 MB > 12 MB cap). It was archived to conversations/<file>.md. Read its tail before answering if the message refers to earlier work." The archive path is already known to `archiveClaudeTranscript`.

Optional: tell the user once in the chat ("I started a fresh session; I'll catch up from my notes").

### Related

- #4173: lets an agent reset itself with a handover (on demand; this issue is about the forced path).
- #3871: rotate transcripts between warm turns (would make this more frequent).
- #3057: handoff recaps on quota fallback.

issues.title: [bug] add-onecli setup.ts exits 0 when the gateway readiness check fails (STATUS: failed)
issues.body:
### Affected NanoClaw version or commit

v2026.10.0. Same code in v2026.11.0-beta.3 and on main at 67335cdd. Line numbers below are from v2026.10.0. On main, the later lines in `setup.ts` are shifted by about 2.

### Host platform

Linux

### What happened?

`.claude/skills/add-onecli/scripts/setup.ts` reports a failed gateway readiness check in its status block, but the process can still exit 0.

- In all three paths of `run()` (remote 454-468, reuse 499-513, fresh install 563-583), a failed `/v1/health` check does this:
  1. It emits `STATUS: failed`, `ERROR: gateway_not_ready`.
  2. It then runs `throw new Error(readinessError)` (lines 468, 513, 583). `run()` is async, so the throw becomes a promise rejection.
- The entry point is `void run(process.argv.slice(2))` (lines 586-588). Nothing catches that rejection.
- `src/log.ts:94-96` registers `process.on('unhandledRejection', (reason) => { log.error('Unhandled rejection', { err: reason }); })`, and `setup.ts` imports `log` (line 21). Registering any `unhandledRejection` listener replaces Node's default behaviour of throwing, which would exit 1. The rejection is logged and the process exits 0.
- Every other failure branch in `run()` calls `process.exit(1)` (lines 425, 484, 495, 526, 536, 548). Only the readiness failure does not.

The skill is run through `pnpm exec tsx .claude/skills/add-onecli/scripts/setup.ts` as an `nc:run effect:external` directive (SKILL.md:46). `scripts/skill-apply.ts` runs that command through the injected exec (line 799). The default host exec, `hostExec` in `setup/lib/skill-driver.ts`, resolves on exit 0 and rejects only on a non-zero exit (line 300). `setup/gateways/install.ts:43-48` then writes `NANOCLAW_GATEWAY_PROVIDER` once the skill is fully applied, which matches SKILL.md:76 ("only after every directive above succeeds"). So a gateway with no usable `/v1` API (unreachable or pre-`/v1`) is recorded as successfully set up. Any other caller that trusts the exit code has the same problem.

This was found by reading source. I did not run the real script against a broken gateway. I did run a minimal script on Node 22.22.0 that has the same `unhandledRejection` listener and a `void run()` that throws. It printed the log line and exited with code 0.

### What did you expect?

When the readiness check fails and the script has printed `STATUS: failed`, the process exits non-zero, like the other failure paths in the same function.

### How can we reproduce it?

1. Point setup at a gateway whose `/v1/health` does not return OK. For example, reuse an install where the gateway is stopped or older than the `/v1` API, or use `NANOCLAW_ONECLI_API_HOST` with an unreachable or incompatible URL.
2. Run `pnpm exec tsx .claude/skills/add-onecli/scripts/setup.ts; echo "exit=$?"`.
3. The status block shows `STATUS: failed` and `ERROR: gateway_not_ready`, the log shows "Unhandled rejection", and the shell prints `exit=0`.

### Suggested fix

Make the entry point fail on a rejected `run()`:

```ts
run(process.argv.slice(2)).catch((err) => {
  log.error('onecli setup failed', { err });
  process.exit(1);
});
```

Alternatively, replace the `throw` after `emitStatus` with `process.exit(1)`, as the other failure branches do. Setting `process.exitCode = 1` in the `unhandledRejection` listener would also fix this script, but it changes the exit code of every process that imports `src/log.ts`, which is a wider change.

Related and not duplicates: #4303 changes the entry-point guard just above this call but keeps `void run(...)`. #4221 changes how the agent-runner prints a crash and leaves its exit code unchanged. Neither changes this exit code.

issues.title: [capability] Approvals that outlive the timeout: let the agent continue and act on a late click
issues.body:
### What problem are you trying to solve?

An approver is often away from their phone for an hour or two. Today a gateway (OneCLI) approval holds the agent's HTTP request for about 3 minutes, then denies it on timeout, and the Discord card dies with it. A click after that has no effect, so the agent has to ask again and someone has to be there at the right moment. `ask_user_question` behaves the same: after the timeout the answer is lost.

### What should be possible?

When the timeout passes, the request fails as today, but the card stays live for a configurable time (e.g. 24 h). If someone approves later, the agent is woken and its identical retry goes through once without a new card. If someone rejects, the agent is woken with the rejection. For `ask_user_question`, a timeout returns `PENDING` instead of no answer, and a late click reaches the agent as a delayed note.

### What kind of skill is this?

Core change (approval coordinator, OneCLI provider, interactive module); could be repackaged as a skill if preferred.

### Who benefits?

Anyone running agents unattended who approves from a phone and can't answer within minutes.

### What have you tried?

Longer timeouts block the agent for the whole wait, and the request still times out upstream.

### What would this change?

A working implementation with tests exists on my instance (8 files, about 540 lines including 164 lines of tests). On timeout it opens a late card valid `NANOCLAW_LATE_APPROVAL_HOURS` (default 24). Approving stores a one-shot grant bound to a retry key (agent, method, host, path, body hash), valid for 30 minutes and single use, and wakes the agent. I can rebase it on current `main` and open a PR if this direction fits.

prs.title: fix(signal): inline inbound attachments so the agent container can read them
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Lets the agent open images and files sent over Signal.

- **Problem**: signal-cli saves attachments under the host's `<SIGNAL_DATA_DIR>/attachments/`. The adapter handed the agent that host path as `[Image: /home/...]`. The container doesn't mount that directory, so the agent can't read it. Non-image files (PDFs etc.) were dropped entirely.
- **Fix**: read each saved file and attach it as base64 `data`, the same shape the chat-sdk bridge uses. `session-manager` then stages it into `/workspace/inbox/<msg>/` like Slack/Telegram/Discord attachments, and the formatter renders `[image: <name> — saved to /workspace/inbox/...]`.
- **Scope**: every attachment except a voice note that gets transcribed. Files over 25 MB, or missing on disk, become `[<type>: <name> - file not available]` instead of a dead path.
- **Out of scope**: mounting the signal-cli data dir into containers (it also holds account keys).

## Related work

Closes #2528

Overlaps open PRs #2695 (images only, same base64 approach), #2529 and #3837 (larger, bundled changes). This one is the small version that also covers PDFs and other files, with tests. Happy to close in favor of whichever a maintainer prefers.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `pnpm exec vitest run src/channels src/session-manager` → 92 files, 1012 passed, 20 skipped.
- `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit -p .` → clean.
- `eslint src/channels/signal*.ts` → no new errors (the two existing ones, `signal.test.ts` unused `args` and the empty `catch` in `signal.ts`, are already on `channels`).
- New `signal-attachments.test.ts`: inlines bytes, adds an extension from MIME when the id has none, marks missing/oversized files, refuses `../` ids.
- `signal.test.ts`: replaced the test that asserted the old `[Image: <host path>]` text with one that drives an image + PDF through the adapter and checks the `data` payload and that no host path appears in the text, plus a missing-file case.
- Manual: running this patch on a live v2026.11.0-rc.3 install. Before it, the agent replied that the attachments "never made it" to it. signal-cli had saved the JPEGs on the host the whole time.

- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [x] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
Signal: images, PDFs and other files sent to the agent now land in its inbox and can be opened, instead of arriving as an unreadable host path.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

Attachment ids come from signal-cli (sender-influenced). They are `basename()`d before joining onto the attachments dir, so an id can't read outside it. The written filename still goes through `session-manager`'s `isSafeAttachmentName` + `AnchoredDir` exclusive-create path. Bytes are capped at 25 MB per file before being inlined. No new mounts.

## Skill delivery

- [x] Not a skill

Channel code only; `/add-signal` already copies `src/channels/signal.ts` from `channels`. The new `signal-attachments.test.ts` isn't in the skill's copy list; I can add it to `add-signal/SKILL.md` on `main` if you want it shipped.

prs.title: feat(providers): add pi agent provider (/add-pi payload skill)
prs.body:
## Type of Change

- [x] **Feature skill** - adds a channel or integration (source code changes + SKILL.md)
- [ ] **Utility skill** - adds a standalone tool (code files in `.claude/skills/<name>/`, no source changes)
- [ ] **Operational/container skill** - adds a workflow or agent skill (SKILL.md only, no source changes)
- [ ] **Fix** - bug fix or security fix to source code
- [ ] **Simplification** - reduces or simplifies source code
- [ ] **Documentation** - README, CONTRIBUTING, or docs only

## Description

**What** — Adds [pi](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi) (pi Coding Agent) as an optional agent provider, installable with the `/add-pi` skill. This is the restructured version of #3857, which targeted the `providers` branch. It now ships the way `/add-opencode` does on `main`: the skill carries its provider as a payload and needs no separate branch.

**Why** — pi is a lightweight coding agent with server-side sessions and MCP support; this makes it a per-group provider choice alongside `claude` / `opencode` / `codex` (`ncl groups config update --provider pi`).

**How it works**

- `payload/container/agent-runner/src/providers/pi.ts` — `AgentProvider` over the in-process pi SDK (`@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`, pinned 1.3.0). No `pi serve` process and no SSE: the whole server-lifecycle complexity class of the OpenCode provider does not exist here. Continuation = pi session file path; activity on every SDK event; fail-closed memory hook; one-shot empty-resume fallback.
- `payload/container/agent-runner/src/providers/mcp-to-pi.ts` — bridges the core's MCP servers to pi `customTools` in process (stdio + Streamable HTTP, per-process lifecycle, lazy reconnect, `isError` → throw, JSON-Schema `pattern` stripped because some model APIs reject the regex dialects MCP servers ship).
- `payload/src/provider-contracts/pi.ts` (host) + `payload/container/agent-runner/src/provider-contracts/pi.ts` (runtime) — seam version 1. The host contract declares the `AGENTS.md` project document, the group's `.pi-shared` state volume mounted at the agentDir, pi's skill backings/views, and the `auth.json` stub file; the runtime contract declares the permission stance, `textDelivery: 'result'`, and XML slash-command formatting.
- `payload/setup/providers/pi.ts` — the setup picker entry, gateway auth hook, and install check.
- `payload/src/providers/pi.ts` — the host container-config adapter (`PI_AGENT_DIR`, plus optional `PI_GATEWAY_PROVIDERS` / `PI_DEFAULT_PROVIDER` / `PI_DEFAULT_MODEL`).

**How the review points from #3857 are handled**

1. **Payload skill on `main`.** The whole provider lives under `.claude/skills/add-pi/` (`SKILL.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `REMOVE.md`, `apply-fixtures.json`, `payload/`). `SKILL.md` is a parser-applyable set of `nc:` directives: copy the payload, append five barrel imports (host/container providers, host/container contracts, setup), install the pinned runner dependency, build, test. No branch fetch, no `PI_REF`, no per-group overlay propagation. `setup/providers/skill-descriptor.test.ts` lists the newly offered skill.
2. **Credentials come through the gateway.** No personal `~/.pi/agent/auth.json` is copied anywhere. The container writes fixed `gateway-managed` placeholders into the group's pi agentDir before each session open (`payload/container/agent-runner/src/providers/pi-auth.ts`), and the selected gateway replaces them on the wire by destination host. ChatGPT subscription auth is pi's `openai-codex` provider, which reuses the gateway's Codex/ChatGPT login; because pi decodes the access token for the account id, the placeholder is a syntactically valid JWT carrying the placeholder claim. API-key providers get a placeholder `api_key` entry, and `provider-auth pi` stores the real key through `getCredentialStore().connection(target)` (observing the entry first, as the seam requires), recording the provider ids in `PI_GATEWAY_PROVIDERS`. A real login already in the agentDir is never overwritten.
3. **`bun.lock` / npm registry.** The skill no longer commits `container/agent-runner/package.json` or `bun.lock`; the pinned dependency is installed at apply time by the `nc:dep` directive, and the pin is registered in `.github/skill-pins` so Dependabot tracks it and `skill-pins:sync` writes future bumps back into SKILL.md. Locally regenerating that install against the default npm registry produces a lock with zero `registry.npmmirror.com` URLs (the #3857 lock had 260).

**Model selection follows the SDK, not a hardcoded id.** Model ids change between pi releases (0.85.1 ships `deepseek-v4-flash`; 1.3.0 calls it `deepseek-flash`), so the provider resolves the start provider/model from pi's own runtime catalog (`getAvailableSnapshot` / `getModel`) and writes that into `settings.json`. Operator-authored values are never overwritten. Verified across both versions with no code change.

**Two things a reviewer should know**

- **The secret still has to be granted to the agent.** The credential seam stores secrets but never assigns them, and `/add-opencode` has the same manual step ("follow the selected gateway skill to grant it to agents"). OneCLI's `secretMode` is `selective`, so an ungranted key reaches the provider as `401 access restricted`. SKILL.md documents it.
- **Setup's own ping is not proof the model call worked.** It reports "Your assistant is ready" whenever the chat command exits 0 with any output, and a failed pi turn answers with the generic "The agent run failed" notice. Verify with a real reply and `continuation:pi` instead; SKILL.md says so explicitly.

**How it was tested**

- `scripts/provider-contract-verifier.ts --required-declared pi` — **passed** (host deps, runtime deps, host build, host provider-contract tests, runtime typecheck, runtime provider-contract tests, host/runtime contract inventories, runtime conformance test files).
- Container suite: **673 pass / 3 skip / 0 fail**. Host suite: **3613 pass / 1 skip / 0 fail**. `skill-pins:check` clean.
- End-to-end on a fresh clone of this branch: `bash nanoclaw.sh` → pick pi → DeepSeek key stored in the gateway → skill applied (14 files, 5 barrels, pin 1.3.0, image SDK 1.3.0) → group switched to pi → real reply, session continuation, and `continuation:pi` in the session's `outbound.db` `session_state`. A WeChat channel was installed onto the same install afterwards, so the channel/provider split was exercised too.
- Testing was done against a OneCLI gateway at 1.45.0 (newer than the 1.42.0 pin in `/add-onecli`), so the grant step used its `PUT /v1/agents/<id>/grants/secrets/<id>` API. This payload itself calls no gateway management API — only the credential seam — so the pinned 1.42.0 gateway is unaffected.

**Usage** — On an installed system: run `/add-pi`, then `ncl groups config update --provider pi` and `ncl groups restart` for the chosen group. Configure credentials with `pnpm exec tsx setup/index.ts --step provider-auth pi` (ChatGPT via the gateway's Codex login, or a stored API key), then grant the secret per the gateway's skill. Model selection lives in the group's `data/v2-sessions/<group>/.pi-shared/settings.json`.

Note for reviewers: the **Provider contract** workflow was stuck in `action_required` on #3857 (first-time contributor). It needs a maintainer approval click to run here too. #3857 is superseded by this PR; it can stay open until this one merges.

## Rebased onto current `main`

Rebased after #4104 (`/add-codex` payload), #4107 (`/add-cursor` payload), #4105, #4106 and #3980 landed. Two conflicts, both list-append in shared files: `setup/providers/skill-descriptor.test.ts` now expects `codex, cursor, opencode, pi`, and `.github/skill-pins/package.json` carries this branch's pin alongside upstream's.

Upstream changes that touch this work, checked rather than assumed:

- **#3980 (first-chat ping)** fixed the very problem SKILL.md used to warn about: a failed pi turn's notice is now scored as a failed first chat instead of a green result. The doc now states the post-#3980 behaviour.
- **#4105 (shared exchange archive)** is for providers whose harness keeps no on-disk transcript. pi's session JSONL *is* its transcript — the continuation token is that file's path — so it needs no archiver, unlike Codex.
- **#4106 (credential connection path)** is unnecessary here: pi's provider entry is a key on exactly one host, so host-scoped injection is what we want.
- **#4104 / #4107** moved Codex and Cursor to the same payload-skill shape this PR uses, so the structure now matches three siblings.

Verification on the rebased branch: container `bun run typecheck` clean and the pi suites at 65 pass; host `tsc --noEmit` clean; host `vitest run` has one failure in `setup/gateways/selection.test.ts` ("detects an installed gateway from inside a nested pnpm") that reproduces on a clean `upstream/main` tree with this payload removed — it is a pre-existing flake under parallel load, not a regression here.

## For Skills

- [x] SKILL.md contains instructions, not inline code (code goes in separate files)
- [x] SKILL.md is under 500 lines (274)
- [x] I tested this skill by applying it onto current `main`, running the provider-contract verifier, and completing a real end-to-end install on a fresh clone

prs.title: feat(skills): /add-hindsight — bundled MCP wrapper for Hindsight memory
prs.body:
## Summary

Adds an opt-in `/add-hindsight` skill that wires NanoClaw v2 agent groups to a [Hindsight](https://github.com/vectorize-io/hindsight) long-term memory engine. **The MCP wrapper that bridges Hindsight's HTTP API to MCP is bundled in this PR** (under `hindsight-mcp/`) — operators don't need to clone external repos to install the skill.

Each wired agent group gets a per-group memory bank with three MCP tools:

- `mcp__hindsight__memory_recall` — semantic search across past memories
- `mcp__hindsight__memory_retain` — persist a durable fact
- `mcp__hindsight__memory_reflect` — synthesise an answer with evidence

## Relationship to existing memory skills

`/add-mnemon` already exists for graph-based memory. This is a sibling option backed by [Vectorize.io's Hindsight](https://hindsight.vectorize.io/) engine — different backend, different operational characteristics (Hindsight extracts entities + links them into a queryable knowledge graph server-side).

Operators should pick one — running both is redundant. The skill mentions this in its Credits section.

## Structure

- **`.claude/skills/add-hindsight/SKILL.md`** — operator setup (5 phases: build wrapper, extract stdio binary to host path, register mount, wire each group via `ncl groups config add-mcp-server`, verify).
- **`container/skills/hindsight/SKILL.md`** — in-container memory discipline (when to recall, when to retain, anti-patterns).
- **`hindsight-mcp/`** — self-contained TypeScript wrapper. Two transports (HTTP + stdio), shared tool implementation. Wrapper-only docker-compose (engine deployment is out of scope; assumes operator already has Hindsight running).

## Prereq (out of scope for this skill)

The Hindsight engine itself is not deployed by this skill. Operator follows the upstream [Hindsight install](https://github.com/vectorize-io/hindsight) first, then points the wrapper at it via `HINDSIGHT_URL`.

This split mirrors `/add-gmail-tool`, `/add-gcal-tool` etc. — the skill handles the NanoClaw-side integration; the external service is the operator's responsibility.

## What's deliberately *not* in this PR

- **Auto-wiring at group-init.** Per CONTRIBUTING ("source code changes should only be things 90%+ of users need"), wiring is opt-in via `/add-hindsight`, not automatic for every new group.
- **`ncl groups config add-mount`.** The skill currently uses a direct sqlite UPDATE to add the wrapper-binary mount to a group's `container_configs.additional_mounts`. Happy to drop the SQL once `ncl` grows an `add-mount` verb (separate PR).
- **The Hindsight engine docker stack.** Wrapper-only — see Prereq above.

## Testing

Verified on a NanoClaw v2.0.56 install with a Hindsight engine reachable on `localhost:3850`:

- `cd hindsight-mcp && cp .env.example .env && [edit] && docker compose up -d` → wrapper healthy at `127.0.0.1:3852/health`
- `npm install && npm run build` inside `hindsight-mcp/` produces a clean `dist/`
- `ncl groups config add-mcp-server` + sqlite UPDATE for the mount → group respawn → agent sees `mcp__hindsight__*` tools in its allowlist
- Agent successfully calls `memory_retain`/`memory_recall`/`memory_reflect` against the engine
- Removing the skill (`config remove-mcp-server` + sqlite UPDATE to drop the mount + group restart) cleans up

## Test plan for reviewers

- [ ] Read `.claude/skills/add-hindsight/SKILL.md` end-to-end — confirm operator can follow without prior knowledge
- [ ] Read `container/skills/hindsight/SKILL.md` — confirm no install-specific examples
- [ ] `cd hindsight-mcp && npm install && npm run build` — confirm wrapper builds cleanly
- [ ] `cd hindsight-mcp && docker compose build` — confirm wrapper image builds
- [ ] Optional: dry-run setup against a local Hindsight engine

prs.title: fix(container-runner): compose the project doc from the gateway-adjusted skills
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Makes the composed `CLAUDE.md` follow the same skill selection as the skill links on the provider-contract spawn path, so the active gateway's resident instructions reach every agent.

- **Problem**: `spawnContainer` calls `resolveProviderContribution`, which realizes the provider surfaces once and passes them to `buildMounts`; `buildMounts`' own realization (`providerSurfaces ??=`) is then skipped. The composer call that runs passed no skill list, so `composeGroupProjectDoc` fell back to the *stored* selection, while the skill links in the same realization used `selectedSkillNames` (the list `selectGatewayAgentSkills` adjusts: the active gateway's agent skills added, any other gateway's dropped). A group with an explicit skill list that leaves out the gateway skill gets `onecli-gateway` linked but not its resident `instructions.md`, which carries "never ask the user for API keys or tokens". A stored selection naming another gateway's skill gets that skill's prose without its link.
- **Fix**: pass `context.selectedSkills` to the composer in `resolveProviderContribution`, as `buildMounts` and the default path already do.
- **Why it slipped**: 249bbe93 added the `runtimeSkills` parameter and passed it in `buildMounts` and the default path, but `resolveProviderContribution` (bc383a2a, earlier) is the call that runs on spawn. The parity test `realizes declared Claude surfaces identically to the legacy default path` calls `buildMounts` without surfaces, so it covers the branch spawn skips.
- **Who hits it**: groups with an explicit `skills` list (`ncl groups config update --skills …`), including an empty one. The default `"all"` already includes the installed gateway skill, so the section disappears silently the first time a group is moved from `"all"` to an explicit list.
- **Out of scope**: `composeGroupProjectDoc` still falls back to the stored selection when `runtimeSkills` is left out (for example the add-codex payload's `composeGroupAgentsMd`). Making it required would change a payload signature, so that belongs in a separate PR.

## Related work

No existing issue or PR (searched for `composeGroupProjectDoc`, `runtimeSkills` and gateway skill instructions).

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- New test in `src/provider-surfaces.test.ts` drives the real spawn order (`resolveProviderContribution`, then `buildMounts` with its surfaces), with a stored selection naming an installed but unselected gateway's skill. It asserts that the active gateway's skill is linked and composed, and that the inactive one is neither.
  - Against `main`: fails (active gateway's section missing).
  - With the fix: `vitest run src/provider-surfaces.test.ts` 31 pass.
- Checked on a live install with 39 agents: rendering every agent's document before and after, only the 4 agents whose explicit list lacks `onecli-gateway` (two `[]`, two `["proofcheck","old"]`) change, each gaining the gateway section (~197 tokens); all others are byte-identical. Two of the four had been switched from `"all"` the day before, so without the fix their next spawn would have dropped the section they had.
- CodeRabbit review in the author's fork (mirror PR drsmk238/nanoclaw#5, same head, base pinned to `main` 80ce34aa): one finding, fixed in 5780472e. The inactive-gateway check used `fs.existsSync`, which is always false here because skill links target container paths and dangle on the host; it now checks `readdirSync(skills)` (verified by planting a dangling link: the new assertion fails, the old one passed). Its re-review of 5780472e: no actionable comments. A local multi-pass review found no correctness issue; its points are addressed in 54bbae49 (the suite restores the previously selected gateway in `afterEach`; fixture comment corrected) plus the inactive-gateway drop assertion.
- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [x] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
Fixed: agents with an explicit skill list now get the credential gateway's standing instructions in their CLAUDE.md, matching the gateway skill that is already linked for them.
```

Takes effect at each group's next container spawn; no image rebuild.

## Security and trust boundaries

None widened. Both lists come from the same `container_configs` row; the composer still reads only host files. The change adds the gateway's credential prohibition to agents that lacked it and stops composing an inactive gateway's prose.

## Skill delivery

- [x] Not a skill
- [ ] Skill: apply/remove footprint and fresh-clone verification are described above

<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Make OneCLI setup exit non-zero when its gateway readiness check fails.

- **Problem**: `run()` rejects after emitting `STATUS: failed`, but the shared logger handles unhandled rejections without setting a failing exit code. Setup can therefore exit 0 and let the skill driver continue.
- **Fix**: catch rejections at the OneCLI CLI entry point, log the error, and set `process.exitCode = 1`.
- **Coverage**: launch the real setup CLI against loopback fixtures for a 404, a dropped `/v1/health` connection, and a healthy gateway. The tests use a disposable HOME and a fake OneCLI CLI.

## Related work

Closes #4408.

prs.title: fix: support rootless Docker for agent containers
prs.body:
Agent containers are unusable on a rootless Docker daemon. Two independent failures, both invisible when the host user is in the `docker` group — which is presumably why they haven't surfaced before.

I hit them because I deliberately kept the agent account out of the docker group: on my host that group is root-equivalent, and `docs/SECURITY.md` makes a point of non-root execution and OS-level isolation. Rootless seemed like the setup the security model is written for.

## 1. `--user` mapping is inverted under rootless

`buildContainerArgs` pushes `--user ${hostUid}:${hostGid}`. Under rootless the daemon runs in a user namespace where the invoking host user **is already container uid 0**, so passing the host uid resolves against the subuid range instead and owns none of the bind mounts.

```
[agent-runner] Fatal error: EACCES: permission denied, mkdir '/workspace/agent/memory'
```

Verified directly (host uid 1003):

```bash
docker run --rm --user 1003:1003 -v ~/nanoclaw-v2/groups:/workspace alpine touch /workspace/probe
# touch: /workspace/probe: Permission denied

docker run --rm --user 0:0 -v ~/nanoclaw-v2/groups:/workspace alpine touch /workspace/probe
# succeeds
```

`--user 0:0` is the identity mapping back to the host user here — not host root.

## 2. Claude Code refuses `bypassPermissions` as root

With (1) fixed, containers run as uid 0 and `providers/claude.ts` always passes `permissionMode: 'bypassPermissions'`:

```
--dangerously-skip-permissions cannot be used with root/sudo privileges for security reasons
```

The runner surfaces only `Claude Code process exited with code 1`, so this isn't visible from the logs — it took a manual `docker exec` to find. `IS_SANDBOX=1` is the documented escape, and the claim is accurate on this path: it is a container, on a rootless daemon, where container-root maps to an unprivileged host user.

I confirmed the confinement holds — a container running as namespace-root with `/` bind-mounted still cannot read the host user's home or `/etc/shadow`.

## Changes

- `isRootlessDocker(dockerHost)` — detection via `DOCKER_HOST` containing `/run/user/`
- `userMappingArgs(uid, gid, dockerHost)` — the whole decision, pure and testable
- Rootful behaviour is byte-identical
- Corrects the `hardeningArgs` comment: `cap-drop` / `no-new-privileges` are described as inert under the `--user` mapping, which stops being true on the rootless path where the uid is namespace-root — they carry real weight there

**Tests:** 1241 pass, 4 new covering both mappings and the detection.

## Known limitation

Detection is `DOCKER_HOST`-only. A rootless install where the socket comes from the Docker CLI context rather than the env var would still hit (1). Happy to extend it to `docker context inspect` if you'd prefer.

Also unaddressed: `setup/container.ts` duplicates the old inline mapping for the setup smoke-test container and will fail the same way under rootless. Left alone to keep this reviewable — glad to route it through `userMappingArgs` in the same PR if useful.

prs.title: feat(providers): add MartLLM as an OpenAI-compatible gateway
prs.body:
**Update (2026-11-22): UberLLM is now MartLLM.** Same service, same accounts and API keys; the new site is https://martllm.com and the API base URL is https://api.martllm.com/v1 (the old uberllm.dev addresses keep working). This PR now uses the new name and links.

## Summary

Adds MartLLM as an OpenAI-compatible gateway provider. It goes through `OpenAiCompatibleProvider` like the other gateways, no new provider implementation. One key reaches about 260 chat models (Anthropic, OpenAI, DeepSeek, Qwen, GLM, Kimi, Gemini) with `vendor/model` ids. The same key also works on MartLLM's Streamable HTTP MCP server (`https://api.martllm.com/mcp`), so it can go in `mcp_servers` with `transport: "http"`, but this PR does not touch MCP config.

Mirrors #990 (Eden AI): same files, same places. One difference in `onboard.zig`: MartLLM is not in models.dev, so instead of a `models_dev_providers` row it gets a native catalog entry like Atlas Cloud from #922. `https://api.martllm.com/v1/models` is public, so `needs_auth = false`, and `require_chat_modalities` keeps the onboarding list to chat models.

- `providers/factory.zig`: `martllm` in `compat_providers`, base `https://api.martllm.com/v1`.
- `providers/api_key.zig`: `MARTLLM_API_KEY`.
- `onboard.zig`: `known_providers` row (Tier 4, after Eden AI, default `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash`) and the native model catalog entry.
- `model_refs.zig`: `martllm` in `known_url_model_provider_namespaces`, since ids carry a vendor segment.
- `integrations.zig`, `config.example.json`, `README.md`, and `docs/en` + `docs/zh` configuration and architecture.

No alias in `provider_names.zig`: the name has no space or hyphen variant to normalise.

## Validation

zig 0.16.0:

- `zig fmt --check src/`: clean.
- `zig build test --summary all`: 13/13 steps, 7491/7500 tests passed (9 skipped). New assertions went into the existing classify/URL/env/default-model/native-catalog tests, plus one env-candidate test.
- Live, through the built binary with only `MARTLLM_API_KEY` in the environment (no key in config) and `agents.defaults.model.primary = "martllm/deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash"`:
  - `nullclaw --list-models --provider martllm` returned 260 model ids from the public catalog, `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash` among them.
  - `nullclaw agent -m "What is 17 + 25? Reply with the number only."` printed `42`.

Tested with deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash: `nullclaw agent -m` returned `42` for "What is 17 + 25?".

## Notes

- Keys: https://martllm.com/signup. Prices are usually below list price; per-model prices are at https://martllm.com/models.
- Like the other gateways, a `base_url` override still works per provider.

I work on MartLLM.

issues.title: [QA] Make PRIMARY_MODEL_CALL_IDLE_TIMEOUT configurable for slow local LLMs

labels.name: qa-bug
labels.description: Bug found during QA testing

issues.body:
### Environment

hosted-staging (crab shack)

### Version / Commit Hash

1.4.1

### QA Test Date

2026-11-15

### Feature Area

Agent loop → model call idle watchdog (HostManagedLoopModelPort / LLM provider timeout)

### Steps to Reproduce

1.Configure a local Ollama provider in providers.json pointing to a llama.cpp-backed model (e.g. NEMOTRON-BOLT-ironclaw:latest) with a large context (num_ctx ≥ 32k).
2.Set LLM_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECS=3000 in the environment and start ironclaw serve.
3.Open the WebChat at http://127.0.0.1:3000 and send a message that triggers an agent turn with a large prompt (~30k tokens: tool catalog schemas + history).
4.Observe the llama.cpp server log: prompt evaluation runs >75 s before the first token, then the request is cancelled — [GIN] ... | 500 | 1m10s | POST "/api/chat" followed by srv stop: cancel task.
In the IronClaw log, the complete_model_request span for that model_call=N ends with a retryable Unavailable / "model gateway timed out" error.

### Expected Behavior

A model call whose backend is slowly processing a large prompt (but not hung) should not be cancelled at 75 s. PRIMARY_MODEL_CALL_IDLE_TIMEOUT in crates/kernel/ironclaw_turns/src/host_managed_ports/model.rs should be configurable (e.g. via env var), or prompt-eval progress should count as progress so the watchdog only trips on a genuinely stalled stream — while preserving the invariant that it stays below DEFAULT_PROCESS_LEASE_DURATION (90 s).

### Actual Behavior

The hardcoded 75 s idle watchdog in await_with_progress_timeout cancels the gateway call because prompt evaluation emits no text deltas; the error maps to AgentLoopHostErrorKind::Unavailable ("model gateway timed out") and the client disconnect makes llama.cpp abort the task.

### Logs / Screenshots

_No response_

### Pre-submit checklist

- [x] Title is specific (not "fix Google Suite" but "Google Suite install throws invalid_grant on OAuth step")
- [x] Commit hash is filled in
- [x] Steps are numbered and reproducible

prs.body:
## Summary

- **Fix `lobster_enable_tools` output render contract**: `output.render` in `dsh-bundles/lobsterai-host/plugins/tool-disclosure.mjs` previously returned a raw `string` instead of DSH's required `ContentBlock[]` (`[{ type: 'text', text }]`), causing `dsh-spill-policy` to throw `TypeError: content.some is not a function` whenever a model unlocked progressive tool groups (`computer-use`, `browser`, `word`, `excel`, `ppt`).
